prs.title: fix(core): dispatch the final Code Assist SSE event at end of stream
prs.body:
## Summary

`CodeAssistServer.requestStreamingPost()` only dispatched a buffered SSE event when it saw a blank line. When the connection closed right after the last `data:` line, with no terminating blank line (truncation, or a non-conformant proxy), that event was dropped with no error and no log. That event is typically the chunk carrying `finishReason` and usage metadata, so the turn degraded silently.

## Details

- The end of the stream is now treated like a trailing blank line: a small generator yields every `readline` line, then `''`. The existing parse/yield/log path handles the pending event, so there is no duplicated parsing logic and no new type assertion.
- On the spec: the WHATWG SSE spec says a pending event at end-of-file is *discarded*. That rule exists because generic text events have no other completeness signal. Code Assist events are JSON objects, so `JSON.parse` already tells us whether the final event is complete:
  - a complete final event is yielded;
  - a truncated one fails to parse and is reported through the existing `InvalidChunkEvent` ("Malformed JSON chunk") logging, instead of disappearing silently.
- Breaking out of the stream early still closes the `readline` interface (`yield*` forwards `return()`). Normal `\n\n`-terminated streams behave exactly as before.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29059

## How to Validate

1. `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/code_assist/server.test.ts`
2. All tests pass, including two new ones:
   - `should yield the final event when the stream ends without a trailing blank line`
   - `robustness testing > should log InvalidChunkEvent when the stream ends mid-event`
3. Revert `packages/core/src/code_assist/server.ts`: both new tests fail (the final event is not yielded, and nothing is logged for the truncated event).

prs.title: fix(core): match include patterns when deciding if read-many-files assets were requested
prs.body:
## Summary

`read_many_files` only inlines images, PDFs and audio when they were explicitly requested "by name or extension", but it decided that with substring checks between the raw include-pattern string and the file's stem/extension. Any textual overlap counted, so binary assets the user never asked for were base64-inlined into the model context:

- `include: ["**/*report*/**"]` inlined `reports/report.png` (the stem `report` is a substring of the pattern).
- `include: ["assets/**", "src/logo.txt"]` inlined `assets/logo.png` (the stem `logo` appears in the unrelated `src/logo.txt` pattern).

## Details

An asset now counts as explicitly requested only when both hold for the same include pattern:

1. The pattern actually matches the file, relative to a workspace directory, using `picomatch` (already a dependency of `packages/core`) with `nocase` and `dot` to mirror the discovery `glob` options. A literal path equal to the pattern also matches, since discovery escapes existing file paths.
2. The pattern's last segment names the file's extension or name (e.g. `*.png`, `logo.png`, `assets/*.pdf`), so broad wildcards like `**` or `*` still don't opt binaries in.

The comparison is now case-insensitive throughout. Previously the extension check was case-insensitive but the stem check was not, and `path.basename(file, '.png')` didn't strip `.PNG`. Text-file handling, discovery and exclusions are unchanged.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29045

## How to Validate

1. `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/tools/read-many-files.test.ts`
2. All tests pass, including three new ones:
   - `should skip images whose name only overlaps a directory in the pattern`
   - `should skip images matched by a broad glob when another pattern names a different path`
   - `should include images requested by path regardless of case`
3. Revert `packages/core/src/tools/read-many-files.ts`: the first two new tests fail. The existing "explicitly requested by extension/name" tests keep passing with and without the change.

prs.title: fix(core): use null check for exit code in shell sandbox denial heuristic
prs.body:
## Summary

The shell tool's sandbox denial heuristic guarded the exit code with `result.exitCode !== undefined`, but `ExecutionResult.exitCode` is typed `number | null`. Since `null !== undefined` is `true`, any result with a `null` exit code always entered the denial-detection branch.

The concrete trigger is backgrounded commands: `ExecutionLifecycleService.background()` resolves the result with `exitCode: null` while the process is still running. Their partial output was then scanned by `parseDenials`, so a background dev server printing something like `ECONNREFUSED` or `permission denied` during startup could be misreported as a sandbox denial (`SANDBOX_EXPANSION_REQUIRED`).

## Details

- Change the guard to `result.exitCode !== null && result.exitCode !== 0`, matching the sibling checks in the same function (the `Exit Code:` content and the `returnDisplay` branch).
- Real failures still enter the heuristic: non-zero exit codes, `error`, `signal` and `aborted` are unchanged.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29043

## How to Validate

1. `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/tools/shell.test.ts`
2. All tests pass, including the new `sandbox heuristics > should NOT run sandbox denial detection for a backgrounded command`.
3. Revert the one-line change in `packages/core/src/tools/shell.ts`: the new test fails because `parseDenials` is called for the backgrounded result.

Note: `shellExecutionService.test.ts > Orphan PTY slave FD cleanup > synchronously closes the matching slave fd when platform is darwin` fails locally on macOS on unmodified `main` as well; it is unrelated to this change.

prs.title: feat(acp): let clients steer a running turn
prs.body:
## Summary

Lets ACP clients (Zed, JetBrains, VS Code extensions, and others that run `gemini --acp`) add a user message to a running `session/prompt` turn without cancelling it, the same way `experimental.modelSteering` works in the terminal.
Today an ACP client can only send `session/cancel` or a new prompt, and both throw away the work in progress. This is an opt-in protocol extension: a client that doesn't use it only sees one extra `_meta` key in the `initialize` response.

## Details

**Protocol** (constants in `acpUtils.ts`)

- `initialize` advertises the extension under `agentCapabilities._meta["geminicli.com"].steering` with `version`, `content: ["text"]`, `maxPending: 20`, `maxChars: 8000`, and `enabled`.
- Steering is enabled when the client sends `clientCapabilities._meta["geminicli.com"].steering: true`, or when the user has `experimental.modelSteering` on.
- New request `_geminicli.com/session/steer` with `{ sessionId, content }`. It returns `{ status: "queued", steerId, pending }`, or `{ status: "no_active_turn" }` when no model loop is running.
- When a message reaches the model, the client gets a `user_message_chunk` with the user's text and `_meta["geminicli.com"].steering = { steerId, state: "delivered" }`.
- Messages still queued when the turn ends (cancel, replacement prompt, or turn limit) come back in the `session/prompt` response as `_meta["geminicli.com"].undeliveredSteering`. If the turn throws, each one is sent as a `user_message_chunk` with `state: "undelivered"` before the error.

**Behavior in `Session.prompt()`**

- Queued messages are added at the start of each loop iteration, after the turn-limit and cancel checks, in front of the tool results.
- They're joined and wrapped with `buildUserSteeringHintPrompt`, the same as the terminal UI does for hints sent after tool calls (`useGeminiStream.ts`). Each message still gets its own `delivered` update on the client.
- If the model finishes without tool calls while a message is queued, the loop sends one more request in the same turn, like the terminal UI auto-submits leftover hints.
- Running tools and open permission requests are not interrupted. Slash commands get `no_active_turn`. A second `session/prompt` still cancels the first, and the replaced turn reports its queue as undelivered.
- Messages are also passed to `InjectionService` with source `user_steering`, so running local subagents see them, as in the terminal. This is a no-op unless `experimental.modelSteering` is on.
- Loading a session replays stored steering as the user's own text, not the wrapped prompt.

**Dispatcher**

- `GeminiAgent.extMethod` routes the steer method and returns `-32601` for unknown methods. `GeminiAgent.extNotification` ignores unknown notifications, as the ACP spec advises.

No core changes. Terminal behavior and the `experimental.modelSteering` default are unchanged. No breaking changes.

**Open questions for maintainers** (see #29900): the `_geminicli.com/` method prefix, gating on client opt-in or the setting, reporting undelivered messages in the response versus a notification, and whether a `session/unsteer` method is needed.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29900

## How to Validate

1. Unit tests:

   ```bash
   npm run build
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/acp/
   ```

For the full suite, run `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true npm run preflight`, as CI does. Without that variable, 9 tests in `gemini.test.tsx` fail on `main` too.

New cases in `acpSession.test.ts` cover delivery, ordering, continuation when the model ends, `no_active_turn`, cancel, open permission requests, turn limits, replacement prompts, errors, validation, injection, and history replay. `acpRpcDispatcher.test.ts` covers capability advertisement and routing.

2. Protocol smoke test against the built CLI (no model call needed): send `initialize` and check `agentCapabilities._meta["geminicli.com"].steering`; steer an unknown session and expect `-32602`; call an unknown `_` method and expect `-32601`.
3. End to end with an ACP client: start a prompt that runs a tool, send `_geminicli.com/session/steer` while it runs, then check that the next model request contains the hint, the client gets a `delivered` chunk, and the turn finishes without being cancelled.

prs.title: fix(cli): restore workspace directories only after a resumed chat succeeds
prs.body:
Fixes #29864.

## What

`loadHistoryForResume` added the session's saved directories to the current workspace context **before** `await resumeChat(...)`. When `resumeChat` threw, the catch path reported "Failed to resume session" but the directories were already in the workspace context and stayed there for the rest of the session. The restore now happens after the resume succeeds, so a failed resume leaves the workspace untouched — the simpler of the two transactional orderings the issue proposes, and `resumeChat` takes no input from the workspace context, so its contract is unaffected.

The issue's second observation — the comment claims stale directories are filtered but the saved array is passed directly — is already handled where it belongs: `WorkspaceContext.addDirectories` resolves and validates each path (`resolveAndValidateDir`) and skips unreadable ones into `result.failed`. The hook's comment now says that filtering happens there instead of implying it happens at the call site.

## Test

New hook case in `useSessionResume.test.ts`: a `resumeChat` that rejects with saved `directories: ['/restored/dir1', '/restored/dir2']` must not call `addDirectories` — the saved directories stay out of the current workspace. The existing restore cases (success path, no-directories path) are unchanged and still pass: `15/15` in the file.

Verified locally with `npm install` (workspaces) + a core build, then `vitest run src/ui/hooks/useSessionResume.test.ts` — 15 passed, 0 failed; ESLint and `tsc --noEmit` clean on the touched files.

prs.title: fix(cli): preserve structured API errors in headless mode
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #29892.

Headless mode now converts non-`Error` values emitted through `GeminiEventType.Error` into a real `Error` using `getErrorMessage`. This prevents structured API errors from being stringified as `[object Object]` by the top-level error handler while preserving the original message.

## Details

API failures can arrive as structured objects rather than `Error` instances. The previous code rethrew those values directly, so consumers that expect an `Error` lost the useful message.

The fix:
- leaves existing `Error` instances unchanged;
- wraps structured values with `new Error(getErrorMessage(error))`;
- adds a regression test that verifies the real message is retained.

prs.title: fix(core,cli): preserve selected model across transient fallback, cancel, and rewind
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes an issue where a manually selected model (such as `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` / `gemini-3.1-pro-preview-customtools`) silently reverts to `gemini-3-flash-preview` on subsequent turns—including after cancelling a turn and running `/rewind`—while the UI footer and `/model` dialog still display `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`.

## Details

    - **Capacity Error Classification (`errorClassification.ts`)**: Classify capacity exhaustion `TerminalQuotaError`s (`MODEL_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED`, `MODEL_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED`, capacity messages) as `'transient'` rather than `'terminal'` so temporary server capacity spikes do not permanently lock the model with a sticky `'quota'` unavailability state.
    - **Turn-Scoped `'retry_once'` Fallback (`fallback/handler.ts`)**: Only apply permanent policy availability transitions on `'retry_always'`. When the fallback handler returns `'retry_once'` (e.g. default low-verbosity silent retry), mark the failed model via `markRetryOncePerTurn` + `consumeStickyAttempt` so it falls back for the remainder of the current turn only and recovers automatically on `resetTurn()`.
    - **Retry Loop Model Re-Selection (`geminiChat.ts`, `client.ts`, `baseLlmClient.ts`)**: Re-select the model via `applyModelSelection` inside `retryWithBackoff` when `ModelAvailabilityService.snapshot(currentModel).available === false`, ensuring `'retry_once'` immediately switches to the fallback candidate instead of retrying the unavailable model.
    - **Cancel, Turn Reset & `/rewind` State Cleanup (`config.ts`, `client.ts`, `rewindCommand.tsx`)**:
      - Restore `_activeModel = model` in `Config.resetTurn()`.
      - Reset turn state and clear `currentSequenceModel` when `GeminiClient.sendMessageStream` is aborted or `setHistory` is called.
      - Clear `currentSequenceModel`, reset `ModelAvailabilityService`, and restore `activeModel` to `config.getModel()` in `rewindConversation`.
    - **Custom-Tools Model Resolution (`fallbackStrategy.ts`, `overrideStrategy.ts`, `defaultStrategy.ts`, `client.ts`, `geminiChat.ts`)**: Pass `useCustomToolModel` to `resolveModel` instead of hardcoding `false`.

## Related Issues

Fixes #23154

## How to Validate

  1. Run targeted unit and integration tests:
       ```bash
       npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/availability/errorClassification.test.ts src/fallback/handler.test.ts
       src/availability/autoRoutingFallback.integration.test.ts src/core/geminiChat.test.ts src/core/baseLlmClient.test.ts src/core/client.test.ts src/config/config.test.ts src/routing/strategies/fallbackStrategy.test.ts src/routing/strategies/overrideStrategy.test.ts src/routing/strategies/defaultStrategy.test.ts
       npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/ui/commands/rewindCommand.test.tsx

  2. Run lint and typecheck:
    npm run lint && npm run typecheck
  3. Manual validation: Select gemini-3.1-pro-preview via /model, trigger a transient/capacity error during a turn (with default ui.errorVerbosity: "low"), cancel (Esc) and /rewind to a prior prompt, and submit a new message; verify requests use gemini-3.1-pro-preview (or -customtools) rather than gemini-3-flash-preview.

prs.title: fix(cli): add missing active and focus keys to custom theme ui schema
prs.body:
## Summary

    Completes the `CustomTheme` settings validation schema, runtime focus-background derivation, and documentation fix by adding the missing `ui.active` and `ui.focus` properties—complementing PR #25822 (`text.response`) so the custom theme schema mismatch reported in #25689 (and #25610) is now resolved in full.
    
    ### How PR #25822 and This PR Complement Each Other
    
    1. **Shared Root Cause (#20745):** Commit `d25088956d11` introduced three new semantic tokens—`text.response`, `ui.active`, and `ui.focus`—into the runtime `CustomTheme` interface (`packages/core/src/config/config.ts`) and `createCustomTheme` (`packages/cli/src/ui/themes/theme.ts`), while removing `border.focused`, without updating `SETTINGS_SCHEMA_DEFINITIONS.CustomTheme` in `packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts` or `docs/cli/themes.md`. Because `settings-validation.ts` enforces `.strict()` (`additionalProperties: false`) on object schemas, configuring any of these three keys in `ui.customThemes` triggered `"Unrecognized key(s) in object"` validation errors at startup.
    2. **Part 1 — `text.response` (Fixed in PR #25822):** Issues #25610 and #25689 reported the validation error when setting `text.response` in a custom theme. PR #25822 added `text.response` to `CustomTheme.properties.text`, resolving `text.response` while #25689 remained open.
    3. **Part 2 — `ui.active` and `ui.focus` (Fixed in This PR):** Auditing #25689 against the original #20745 changes showed that the sibling `ui.active` and `ui.focus` keys still lacked schema definitions, full runtime `FocusBackground` precedence, and documentation. Adding them here completes 100% alignment across the TypeScript `CustomTheme` contract, Zod runtime validation, IDE JSON Schema (`schemas/settings.schema.json`), custom theme color derivation, and user documentation.

## Details

    - **Settings Validation & JSON Schema (`packages/cli/src/config/settingsSchema.ts`, `schemas/settings.schema.json`):**
      - Added `active: { type: 'string' }` and `focus: { type: 'string' }` to `SETTINGS_SCHEMA_DEFINITIONS.CustomTheme.properties.ui.properties` and regenerated `schemas/settings.schema.json`.
      - Retained `border.focused` in `settingsSchema.ts` for backwards compatibility so existing user `settings.json` files created from older docs do not fail strict validation.
    - **Custom Theme Runtime Consistency (`packages/cli/src/ui/themes/theme.ts`):**
      - Updated `FocusBackground` (`semanticColors.background.focus`) in `createCustomTheme` to prioritize `customTheme.ui?.focus` before falling back to `customTheme.status?.success ?? customTheme.AccentGreen ?? '#3CA84B'`, matching `Theme` and `ThemeManager.getColors()`.
    - **Documentation (`docs/cli/themes.md`):**
      - Documented `ui.active` and `ui.focus` under UI properties, added them to the custom theme JSON example, and removed the obsolete `border.focused` entry so users are guided to the supported keys.

prs.title: fix(core): honor nested .gitignore negations under dir/** patterns
prs.body:
## Summary

`GitIgnoreParser` ignored files that a nested `.gitignore` re-includes under a parent `dir/**` pattern. With `logs/**` at the root and `!keep.txt` in `logs/.gitignore`, git tracks `logs/keep.txt` but the parser reported it as ignored.

## Details

`expandWildcardDirectoryPatterns` adds `/dir/` for each `dir/**` so the parser can prune the whole subtree. It only checked negations in the same file, so `logs/` got pruned and `logs/.gitignore` was never read.

`expandWildcardDirectoryPatterns` now takes an optional `dirHasNestedNegations` callback. `GitIgnoreParser` passes one that checks whether `dir/.gitignore` contains a negation (read through the existing per-directory cache), and the expansion is skipped for that directory. Pruning still applies everywhere else, and subdirectories like `logs/sub/` stay ignored, matching git.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29826

## How to Validate

```
cd packages/core
npx vitest run src/utils/gitIgnoreParser.test.ts src/utils/ignorePathUtils.test.ts
```

Checked against git in a scratch repo with root `logs/**` and `logs/.gitignore` containing `!keep.txt`: `git check-ignore` reports `logs/keep.txt` as not ignored, while `logs/drop.txt` and `logs/sub/keep.txt` stay ignored. The new test asserts the same. The full `packages/core` suite passes.

prs.title: fix(core): resolve symlinked paths canonically in GlobTool
prs.body:
## Summary
This PR fixes `GlobToolInvocation.execute()` in `packages/core/src/tools/glob.ts` so that symlinked workspace roots and symlinked entries within the workspace are consistently resolved to canonical realpaths during filtering, workspace boundary validation, and output generation.

Key changes:
- Cache each entry's canonical path (`resolveToRealPath(entry.fullpath())`) in a `resolvedPathMap` during `relativePaths` construction so no extra filesystem calls are made.
- Resolve `filteredPaths` against `realTargetDir` (instead of raw `this.config.getTargetDir()`) and validate each candidate with `!this.config.validatePathAccess(p, "read")`.
- Filter `allEntries` using the entry's canonical path and deduplicate entries that resolve to the same canonical target.
- Map `sortedEntries` to canonical paths in `sortedAbsolutePaths` so the paths returned to the LLM match what `read_file`, `edit`, and `write_file` expect.

## Details
Previously, `GlobToolInvocation.execute()` resolved `realTargetDir` and each entry's `realFullPath` when building `relativePaths`, but then:
1. Reconstructed `filteredAbsolutePaths` using `path.resolve(this.config.getTargetDir(), p)` (unresolved target dir).
2. Checked `filteredAbsolutePaths.has(entry.fullpath())` (unresolved entry path from `glob`, which does not resolve symlinks when `follow: false`).
3. Returned `entry.fullpath()` in `sortedAbsolutePaths`.

Whenever `targetDir` or a matched entry involved a symlink (such as `/tmp` -> `/private/tmp` on macOS or a symlinked file/folder inside the workspace), `filteredAbsolutePaths` and `entry.fullpath()` mismatched, either dropping valid matches (`No files found`) or returning non-canonical paths.

## Related Issues
Fixes #28416

## How to Validate
1. Run the `GlobTool` unit tests (including symlinked workspace root, symlinked workspace files, and outside-workspace symlink filtering):
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/tools/glob.test.ts
   ```
2. Run lint and typecheck:
   ```bash
   npm run lint && npm run typecheck
   ```

prs.title: fix(cli): serialize concurrent extension installs with per-extension lock (#29036)
prs.body:
## Summary

`installOrUpdateExtension()` checked whether the destination directory existed and then ran several asynchronous steps (removing the previous version, prompting for settings, copying files, writing install metadata) before loading the extension. Two installs or updates of the same extension running at the same time, in one process or in separate CLI processes, could both pass the check and write into the same directory, leaving a mix of files and metadata from both sources.

This PR serializes installs and updates per extension with a `proper-lockfile` lock and re-checks the destination once the lock is held. The second install now fails with the existing "directory already exists" error instead of writing over the first one.

## Details

- **Per-extension lock** (`packages/cli/src/config/extension-manager.ts`): a new `acquireExtensionInstallLock()` helper locks `<extensionsDir>/<name>` using the lock directory `<extensionsDir>/<name>.lock` (`realpath: false`, because the install directory usually does not exist yet).
  - The lock is keyed on the extension's own directory rather than the shared extensions directory. `proper-lockfile` tracks held locks per key within a process, so a shared key would let locks for different extensions (for example from `gemini extensions update --all`, which updates extensions concurrently via `Promise.all`) release each other and leave lock directories behind.
  - `stale: 15000` lets a lock left behind by a terminated process be taken over. `retries: { retries: 15, minTimeout: 200, maxTimeout: 500 }` waits up to about 7 s for a concurrent install of the same extension to finish.
  - If the lock cannot be acquired in that window, the install stops before writing anything and reports: `Cannot install extension "<name>" because another installation or update of it is already in progress. Please try again later.`
  - The lock-loss callback logs a warning instead of using the library default, which throws from a timer.
- **Check, lock, re-check**: the existing destination check still runs first as a fast path and runs again after the lock is acquired. Its error message is unchanged. The lock is released in the existing `finally` block, and release errors are logged so they cannot mask the result of the install.
- **Loader**: `_buildExtension()`, used by both `loadExtensions()` and `loadExtension()`, skips `*.lock` files and directories, so lock directories are never parsed as extensions. Extension names cannot contain dots (`validateName`), so no installed extension is affected.
- **Tests**:
  - `extension-manager.test.ts`: four tests in a new `concurrent installs` block, using real filesystem locks:
    - two concurrent installs of the same extension: exactly one succeeds, the destination contains only that install's files and metadata, and no lock directory remains
    - concurrent installs of different extensions: both succeed, each with its own lock
    - a lock held elsewhere: friendly error, nothing written
    - lock artifacts: ignored by the loader
  - `extensionUpdates.test.ts`: this suite mocks the filesystem, so `proper-lockfile` is mocked as well (the same approach as `projectRegistry.test.ts` and `trust.test.ts` in core). The update test now also asserts that the lock is acquired and released.
- No new dependencies (`proper-lockfile@4.1.2` is already a dependency of `@google/gemini-cli`), no breaking changes, and no documentation changes needed.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29036

## How to Validate

1. Run the extension manager tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/config/extension-manager.test.ts
   ```
   *Expected result*: 39 tests pass, including the 4 tests in `concurrent installs`. On `main`, these 4 tests fail; for example, the same-extension test finds files from both sources in the destination directory.

2. Run the update tests:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/config/extensions/extensionUpdates.test.ts
   ```
   *Expected result*: 2 tests pass.

3. Run the full CLI package suite, lint, and type check:
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli
   npm run lint
   npm run typecheck -w @google/gemini-cli
   ```
   *Expected result*: 475 test files / 7588 tests pass (4 skipped), 0 lint errors or warnings, and no type errors.

4. Optional manual check: run `gemini extensions install <local-path>` for the same extension in two terminals at the same time.
   *Expected result*: one install succeeds. The other reports that the directory already exists (or that an installation is already in progress), and no `<name>.lock` directory remains in `~/.gemini/extensions`.

Verification run on macOS: `extension-manager.test.ts` passed 39/39, the `concurrent installs` block passed 10 consecutive runs, and the full `@google/gemini-cli` suite passed (7588 tests).

prs.title: fix(core): preserve explicit gemini-2.5-flash model in dynamic model resolution
prs.body:
When `gemini-2.5-flash` is explicitly specified (e.g. via `--model gemini-2.5-flash` or `/model`) with dynamic model configuration enabled and `useLatestFlash` active (such as on Vertex AI or Gemini API key authentication where `hasLatestFlashGAAccess()` returns `true`), `DEFAULT_MODEL_CONFIGS.modelIdResolutions['gemini-2.5-flash']` (`packages/core/src/config/defaultModelConfigs.ts`) previously rewrote `'gemini-2.5-flash'` to `LATEST_GEMINI_FLASH_MODEL`.

This caused explicit requests for `gemini-2.5-flash` in dynamic configuration mode to resolve to the latest Gemini 3 Flash model instead of preserving `gemini-2.5-flash`, diverging from the static resolution behavior in `models.ts` (`isPromotableFlashModel`) and deduplicating `gemini-2.5-flash` out of `ModelConfigService.getAvailableModelOptions()`.

This change removes the `useLatestFlash` promotion rule from `DEFAULT_MODEL_CONFIGS.modelIdResolutions['gemini-2.5-flash']` so that explicit `gemini-2.5-flash` selections are preserved consistently across both static and dynamic model configurations, while keeping generic `'flash'` alias and base Flash tier promotions intact.

## Details

- **`DEFAULT_MODEL_CONFIGS.modelIdResolutions['gemini-2.5-flash']` (`packages/core/src/config/defaultModelConfigs.ts`)**:
  - Removes the `contexts` entry that mapped `'gemini-2.5-flash'` to `LATEST_GEMINI_FLASH_MODEL` when `useLatestFlash: true`, preserving `'gemini-2.5-flash'` as its concrete model ID.
- **Generated Settings Schema & Documentation (`schemas/settings.schema.json`, `docs/reference/configuration.md`)**:
  - Regenerates the settings JSON schema and reference documentation (`npm run schema:settings` and `npm run docs:settings`) to stay in sync with `DEFAULT_MODEL_CONFIGS`.
- **Unit Test Coverage**:
  - `packages/core/src/config/models.test.ts`: Verifies that explicit versioned models (`gemini-2.5-flash`, `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`, `gemini-3.6-flash`, etc.) are preserved when `useLatestFlash` / `useGemini3_5Flash` is `true` in both static and dynamic configuration modes, and includes `gemini-2.5-flash` and `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` in dynamic configuration parity checks.
  - `packages/core/src/services/modelConfigService.test.ts`: Verifies `ModelConfigService.resolveModelId('gemini-2.5-flash', ...)` and `ModelConfigService.getAvailableModelOptions({ useLatestFlash: true })` preserve `gemini-2.5-flash` in `DEFAULT_MODEL_CONFIGS`.
  - `packages/core/src/availability/policyHelpers.test.ts`: Verifies `resolvePolicyChain` parity between static and dynamic configurations for `gemini-2.5-flash` with and without `useLatestFlash` enabled.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29213

1. **Automated Unit Tests**:

   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/config/models.test.ts src/services/modelConfigService.test.ts src/availability/policyHelpers.test.ts

prs.title: fix(core): handle Windows libuv zero-device stat reporting in readSecureFileBuffer
prs.body:
## Summary

<!-- Concisely describe what this PR changes and why. Focus on impact and
urgency. -->
On Windows environments running Node.js `22.12.0` through `22.16.x` (bundling `libuv` `1.49.x`–`1.50.0`), path-based `fs.promises.stat(filePath)` reports `dev: 0` while descriptor-based `fileHandle.stat()` reports the volume serial number (`dev !== 0`) alongside an identical `ino`. Because `readSecureFileBuffer` in `packages/core/src/utils/fileUtils.ts` required strict equality on both `dev` and `ino` between `initialStats` and `handleStats`, file reads on affected Windows runtimes consistently failed with `File device or inode changed during read`.

This PR updates the pre-read file identity comparison in `readSecureFileBuffer` to permit a `dev` discrepancy on `win32` when either `dev` value is `0` and `ino` matches, while preserving non-zero `dev` comparisons, `ino` identity verification on all platforms, and post-read `stat` consistency checks.

## Details

<!-- Add any extra context and design decisions. Keep it brief but complete. -->
1. **Windows zero-`dev` handling in pre-read identity validation (`packages/core/src/utils/fileUtils.ts`)**:
   - Updated the pre-read `initialStats` vs. `handleStats` comparison in `readSecureFileBuffer` to treat `dev` as unchanged when `process.platform === 'win32'` and either `initialStats.dev === 0` or `handleStats.dev === 0`.
   - Preserved unconditional `initialStats.ino !== handleStats.ino` validation, non-zero `dev` mismatch checks on `win32`, strict `dev` + `ino` checks on non-Windows platforms, and post-read `initialStats` vs. `postStats` verification.
2. **Unit test coverage (`packages/core/src/utils/fileUtils.test.ts`)**:
   - Added unit tests for `readSecureFileBuffer` verifying successful reads on `win32` when `stat.dev = 0` vs. `handle.stat.dev = 12345` (and vice versa) with matching `ino`.
   - Added negative test cases verifying that `readSecureFileBuffer` continues to reject `ino` mismatches on `win32` when `dev = 0`, non-zero `dev` mismatches on `win32`, and `dev = 0` mismatches on non-Windows platforms.

only related to an issue or is a partial fix, simply reference the issue number
without a keyword (Related to #123). -->

prs.title: fix(core): honor .git/info/exclude and core.excludesFile in shadow repo
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes an issue where `/restore` deletes or reverts files that should be ignored under Git configuration rules coming from `.git/info/exclude` or the user's global `core.excludesFile`.

## Details

When session checkpointing is enabled, `GitService` creates an isolated shadow Git repository in `<historyDir>`. Because the shadow repository isolates its global config (via `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`) and uses a distinct `.git` directory (`<historyDir>/.git`), it only observed working-tree `.gitignore` files, ignoring rules configured in `.git/info/exclude` and global `core.excludesFile`.

Consequently:
- Files excluded via `.git/info/exclude` or `core.excludesFile` created after a checkpoint were treated as unignored, untracked files and deleted by `git clean -f -d`.
- Files excluded via `.git/info/exclude` or `core.excludesFile` present before a checkpoint were staged and committed during snapshotting, causing `/restore` to overwrite recent changes with their previous content.

This fix:
1. Queries the user's global `core.excludesFile` via `git config --global --path --get core.excludesFile` and sets it in the shadow repository's `.gitconfig` (handling backslash sanitization on Windows). Setting this in `.gitconfig` preserves Git ignore precedence over `info/exclude`.
2. Locates the project's private exclude file using `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path info/exclude` (with fallbacks to `rev-parse --git-path` and default `.git/info/exclude`, supporting linked worktrees and subdirectories) and mirrors its contents into `<historyDir>/.git/info/exclude`.
3. Adds comprehensive unit tests in `packages/core/src/services/gitService.test.ts` and integration tests in `integration-tests/checkpointing.test.ts`.

## Related Issues

Fixes #29654

## How to Validate

1. Run unit tests:
```bash
npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/services/gitService.test.ts
```

2. Run integration tests:
```bash

```

prs.title: fix(core): flush pending SSE event buffer at stream EOF in CodeAssistServer
prs.body:
## Summary

  Flushes any remaining buffered `data:` lines at stream EOF in `CodeAssistServer.requestStreamingPost()` so that the final Server-Sent Event (SSE) is not silently discarded when a stream closes without a trailing blank line (`\n\n`).
Previously, if a proxy, gateway, or server closed the SSE connection immediately after emitting the final `data: {...}` line (or after a single `\n` / `\r\n`),Node's `readline` exited the `for await` loop without emitting `line === ''`. As a result, the final chunk—which in `generateContentStream()` carries `finishReason`, `usageMetadata`, and credit updates—was silently dropped, and streams truncated mid-JSON at EOF failed to log an `InvalidChunkEvent`.


## Details

  - Extracted a `flushBuffer()` generator helper in `CodeAssistServer.requestStreamingPost()` (`packages/core/src/code_assist/server.ts`) and invoked `yield*flushBuffer()` both on `line === ''` inside the loop and once at EOF after the `for await (const line of rl)` loop exits.
   - Tracked `parseSucceeded` via `markParsed()` before yielding so `JSON.parse()` failures log `InvalidChunkEvent('Malformed JSON chunk')` via `logInvalidChunk()`,while any errors thrown by downstream consumers during `yield` are re-thrown instead of swallowed.
   - Added unit tests in `packages/core/src/code_assist/server.test.ts` covering EOF without trailing newline, single `\n`, single `\r\n`, multi-event and multi-line JSON streams, trailing non-data SSE lines, `generateContentStream()` `finishReason`/`usageMetadata` preservation, `InvalidChunkEvent` logging at EOF, and consumer `SyntaxError` propagation.

## Related Issues

 Fixes #29059

## How to Validate

1. Run the targeted unit tests for 'CodeAssistServer':
       ```
       npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/code_assist/server.test.ts
       ```
    2. Run lint, typecheck, and build:

       npm run lint

       ```

prs.title: fix(cli): kill active shells and persist tool calls on headless interruption
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes an issue where stopping a headless run (`gemini -p ... --yolo`) with a signal (SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP) or Ctrl+C while `run_shell_command` is running causes:
1. The process to exit with code 0 instead of a standard signal exit code.
2. The shell command to survive in its detached process group and run to completion in the background.
3. The session file (`session-*.jsonl`) to omit the tool call, leaving `--resume latest` with no record that the command was started or interrupted.

## Details

- **Immediate Tool Call Persistence:** `geminiChat.ts` now records incoming tool calls with status `Scheduled` as soon as the model stream yields them, rather than waiting for `scheduler.schedule()` to complete.
- **Interrupted Response Synthesis on Resume:** `convertSessionToClientHistory()` synthesizes an interrupted `functionResponse` for any uncompleted tool call. This prevents Gemini API 400 errors (unpaired function calls) and informs the model that execution was interrupted so it can inspect state before re-running.
- **Process Group Termination:** Added `ShellExecutionService.cleanupAllActiveProcesses()` to `runExitCleanup()` to terminate active child processes and PTY process groups across platforms (via `taskkill` on Windows and group signals on POSIX).
- **Signal Exit Codes:** Wired SIGHUP handling into non-interactive CLI runners and ensured graceful shutdowns return standard POSIX exit codes (130 for SIGINT, 143 for SIGTERM, 129 for SIGHUP) instead of 0.
- **Shared Helpers:** Extracted `createCancelledToolCall` and `CANCELLED_TOOL_ERROR_MESSAGE` into `@google/gemini-cli-core` (`tool-utils.ts`) so both interactive and headless runners record cancellation consistently.

## Related Issues

Fixes #30007

## How to Validate

1. **Unit tests:**
   ```bash
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/nonInteractiveCli.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli -- src/utils/cleanup.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/utils/sessionUtils.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/core/geminiChat.test.ts
   npm test -w @google/gemini-cli-core -- src/services/shellExecutionService.test.ts

prs.title: fix(core): keep oversized and boundary lines in read_background_output
prs.body:
## Summary

`read_background_output` reads the last 64KB of a log and always dropped the first line of that window when it didn't start at byte 0. A log that is one line longer than 64KB came back as `Full Log Output:` with nothing after it, a complete first line was lost when the window started right after a newline, and truncated output was still labelled "Full Log Output".

## Details

- read one extra byte before the window to tell whether it starts mid line
- drop the partial first line only when other lines follow; when it's the only line, keep it as a fragment
- skip the continuation bytes of a UTF-8 character cut by the cap, so the fragment doesn't start with U+FFFD
- the header says when earlier output was truncated
- the read stays bounded at 64KB plus one byte, and the session ownership check is unchanged

## Related Issues

Fixes #29944

## How to Validate

```
cd packages/core
npx vitest run src/tools/shellBackgroundTools.test.ts
```

New tests cover a 70,000 character single line, a window that starts right after a newline, a partial first line followed by a full one, and an "é" split by the cap. Against main's source all 4 fail; with this change the file passes 14/14 (macOS, Node 25). I didn't run the CLI end to end.

issues.title: WSL: clipboard write via clip.exe fails (quoted path in cmd /c), mouse selection copies nothing

labels.name: area:input-keyboard
labels.description: Keyboard shortcuts, keybindings, copy/paste, clipboard, mouse, and text input

labels.name: area:platform-windows
labels.description: Windows-specific: PowerShell, cmd, Git Bash, WSL, Windows Terminal

issues.body:
**Version:** 1.0.105 (also seen on 1.0.104)
**Environment:** WSL2 (Ubuntu 26.04) + WSLg, GNOME Console (VTE, no OSC 52 support)

**Problem**
Selecting text with the mouse and copying leaves the clipboard empty. `/copy` works.

**Logs**
`writeToClipboard: clip.exe failed; relied on OSC 52: Error: clip.exe exited with code 1`

**Root cause**
On WSL the CLI spawns `cmd.exe /d /c 'chcp 65001 >nul & "<path>\clip.exe"'`. The quotes around the path get escaped when launched from WSL, and cmd reports:
`'\"C:\Windows\System32\clip.exe\"' is not recognized as an internal or external command`
so it exits with code 1. The CLI then falls back to OSC 52, which VTE terminals ignore, so nothing reaches the clipboard.

**Verification**
Running the same command without the quotes around the clip.exe path exits 0 and the text lands on the Windows clipboard.

**Workaround**
Remove the quotes around `${n}` in the `chcp 65001 >nul & "${n}"` template in `cli-main.js`.

**Suggested fix**
Don't quote the path (or escape it correctly for WSL interop), or invoke `clip.exe` directly instead of via `cmd /c`.

issues.title: `/keep-alive` in WSL2 does not prevent the Windows host from sleeping
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When Copilot CLI runs inside WSL2, `/keep-alive` does not prevent the Windows host from sleeping. WSL is treated as Linux, so the CLI attempts to use `systemd-inhibit`; that does not create a Windows host power request visible through `powercfg -requests`.

This means long-running Copilot tasks can be suspended when the Windows host sleeps, even though keep-alive is enabled.

### Affected version

1.0.105

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Run Copilot CLI inside WSL2 on Windows.
2. Enable `/keep-alive on` or the busy-mode equivalent.
3. From Windows, run `powercfg -requests`.
4. Observe that Copilot CLI has not registered a Windows host power request.
5. Allow the Windows host's configured idle timeout to expire.
6. Observe that the host can sleep and suspend the WSL2/Copilot workload.

### Expected behavior

Enabling `/keep-alive` inside WSL2 should prevent the Windows host from sleeping, just as running Copilot CLI natively on Windows does.

The implementation could detect WSL2 and invoke an appropriate Windows-host mechanism, or clearly expose a supported integration that creates and releases the host power request for the lifetime of the Copilot task.

### Additional context

The original implementation uses `systemd-inhibit` on Linux and Windows power APIs only for native Windows processes:
https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/5669

A later fix explicitly handles WSL as an environment where the Linux inhibitor may fail, but does not forward sleep inhibition to the Windows host:
https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/13161

WSL2 is important for file-heavy Rust, Go, and similar development because working on its Linux filesystem can be substantially faster than working directly on NTFS. Requiring a separate Windows keep-awake utility makes `/keep-alive` ineffective for this common workflow.

Originating discussion:
https://github.slack.com/archives/C093WSH3L8J/p1793378606869279

issues.title: ACP mode: expired MCP OAuth access token opens the browser authorization page instead of using the stored refresh token

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server configuration, discovery, connectivity, OAuth, policy, and registry

issues.body:
## Describe the bug

In ACP mode (`copilot --acp`), when a remote HTTP MCP server answers 401 because the stored access token has expired, the CLI goes straight to `[acp::mcp_oauth] opened the MCP OAuth authorization page`. It never tries a `refresh_token` grant, even though a refresh token is stored and works.

The same config, same Keychain entry and same machine, a minute apart:

- `copilot` (interactive) and `copilot -p`: 401, then silent refresh, server connected in ~200 ms, no browser.
- `copilot --acp`: 401, then the authorization page opens. Nothing in the log shows a refresh attempt.

ACP does read the stored token: right after the interactive CLI refreshed and persisted it, an ACP session connected to the server without a browser. It just never renews an expired one.

Server used: Sentry remote MCP (`https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp`), dynamic client registration (`clientId` `https://github.com/copilot/cli/client-metadata.json`), token in the macOS Keychain (service `copilot-mcp-oauth`).

## Affected version

- GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.102 (latest stable; 1.0.103-0 prerelease release notes mention nothing related)
- Same pattern in my logs going back to 2026-10-19 (1.0.100 and 1.0.101)
- macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), arm64

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a remote OAuth MCP server in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`:
   ```json
   { "mcpServers": { "sentry": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp" } } }
   ```
2. Sign in once from the interactive CLI so an access token and refresh token are stored.
3. Wait until the access token expires (about an hour for Sentry). Don't run the interactive CLI in between.
4. Start `copilot --acp` over stdio and send `initialize` then `session/new` (`cwd` set to any temp dir, `mcpServers: []`).
5. The browser opens the Sentry authorization page. Log: `opened the MCP OAuth authorization page`.
6. Close the ACP process, then run `copilot -p "reply with ok"` from the same directory. The server connects after a 401 with no browser.

Minimal driver used for step 4:

```js
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
const cwd = process.argv[2];
const child = spawn('copilot', ['--acp'], { cwd, stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'inherit'] });
const send = (id, method, params) => child.stdin.write(JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id, method, params }) + '\n');
let buf = '';
child.stdout.on('data', d => {
  buf += d; let i;
  while ((i = buf.indexOf('\n')) >= 0) {
    const m = JSON.parse(buf.slice(0, i)); buf = buf.slice(i + 1);
    if (m.id === 1) send(2, 'session/new', { cwd, mcpServers: [] });
  }
});
send(1, 'initialize', { protocolVersion: 1, clientCapabilities: {} });
setTimeout(() => child.kill('SIGTERM'), 45000);
```

## Expected behavior

On a 401 for a server with a stored refresh token, ACP does what the interactive CLI and `-p` already do: silently POST `grant_type=refresh_token`, persist the new tokens, reconnect. Only fall back to the authorization page if the refresh fails (`invalid_grant`, revoked, no refresh token).

## Actual behavior

### ACP, expired token (2026-10-22, live repro)

```
11:45:55.601Z [INFO] Starting ACP server (stdio)
11:45:56.976Z [ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(OAuthChallenge { www_authenticate_header: "******"OAuth\", resource_metadata=\"https://mcp.sentry.dev/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp\"", response: McpOAuthHttpResponse { status_code: 401, header_count: 10, has_body: true } })
11:45:57.315Z [INFO] [rust:acp::mcp_oauth] opened the MCP OAuth authorization page {"server_name":"sentry"}
11:45:57.315Z [WARNING] [rust:mcp_engine::agent_host] HTTP 401 challenge (WWW-Authenticate: ******"OAuth", resource_metadata="https://mcp.sentry.dev/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp") {"server":"sentry","error":"MCP OAuth authorization failed"}
11:45:57.414Z [ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(OAuthChallenge { ... status_code: 401 ... })
11:45:57.458Z [INFO] [rust:acp::mcp_oauth] opened the MCP OAuth authorization page {"server_name":"sentry"}
11:46:39.891Z [WARNING] [rust:mcp_client::session_authorizer] MCP OAuth login did not complete {"server_name":"sentry","error":"MCP OAuth was cancelled because its original requester or configuration changed."}
```

Two authorization pages per `session/new`, one per challenge. The ACP client got no `session/update` or request about auth; the CLI opened the browser on its own.

### `-p`, same token, 60 s later

```
11:46:50.753Z [ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(OAuthChallenge { ... status_code: 401 ... })
11:46:50.955Z [INFO] [rust:rmcp::service] Service initialized as client {"peer_info":"Some(ServerPeerInfo { ... name: \"Sentry MCP\" ... })"}
```

No browser, connected 200 ms after the 401.

### Interactive CLI, earlier the same day

```
07:54:03.670Z [ERROR] [rust:rmcp::transport::worker] worker quit with fatal: Transport channel closed, when Client(OAuthChallenge { ... status_code: 401 ... })
07:54:03.761Z [ERROR] Refreshing authentication for sentry...
07:54:04.340Z [ERROR] Successfully authenticated with sentry
07:54:04.413Z [INFO] [rust:rmcp::service] Service initialized as client {"peer_info":"Some(ServerPeerInfo { ... name: \"Sentry MCP\" ... })"}
```

The Keychain item's modification date is 07:54:04Z, so this refresh was persisted. An ACP process that had already opened the page at 07:53:30 and again at 07:54:29 finally connected to Sentry at 07:54:34, using the token the interactive CLI had just stored.

### Across all my logs

I went through every process log in `~/.copilot/logs` (2026-10-19 to 2026-10-22) that has a Sentry OAuth challenge:

| Mode | Processes | With a refresh attempt | Opened the authorization page |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--acp` | 32 | 0 | 30 (in the other 2 the client disconnected before the page opened) |
| interactive | 2 | 2 | 1, only after its refresh attempt failed (2026-10-21, `Refreshing authentication` then `Opening browser for sentry authentication`) |

No ACP log contains `Refreshing authentication`, `Successfully authenticated` or anything else showing a refresh attempt.

## Impact

ACP clients (Kepler, editors) spawn short-lived `copilot --acp` processes: one per new chat, plus background ones for titles, model lists and similar. Once the access token expires, which for Sentry is about an hour, every one of them:

- pops one or two Sentry authorization tabs the user didn't ask for, at session start, before any Sentry tool is used;
- cancels the flow a moment later when the process exits (`MCP OAuth was cancelled because its original requester or configuration changed.`), or leaves it hanging until `OAuth callback timeout` after 5 minutes;
- starts the session without the server's tools.

The only workaround is to open the interactive CLI now and then so it refreshes and persists the token for ACP to pick up.

## Possibly related: `-p` refresh is not persisted

The silent refresh in `-p` runs never updated the stored token. After two `-p` runs at 11:46 and 11:50 that both refreshed, the Keychain item's modification date was still 07:54:04Z and nothing under `~/.copilot` changed. So every `-p` run refreshes again from the stored refresh token. That works with Sentry, but against a server that rotates refresh tokens it would break the stored grant (same class of problem as #5079). It also means a `-p` refresh doesn't help ACP the way an interactive refresh does.

## Related issues

- #4203: generic "expired access token forces interactive re-auth instead of refresh_token grant" (1.0.71). On 1.0.102 the interactive CLI and `-p` refresh fine for me; ACP still doesn't, so what's left of #4203 may be this ACP path.
- #4994: the authorization page opens on every ACP session since 1.0.89, with a valid token and no refresh token. Different trigger (an expired token with a working refresh token), same ACP handler that goes straight to the browser.
- #5192: tokens from an ACP sign-in are never persisted. Here the token is persisted (by the interactive CLI) and ACP reads it, but never refreshes it.

issues.title: [Feature request] Authoritative foreground-session change hook for terminal integrations, including warm resume

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Problem

Terminal integrations need to associate a pane with the **currently foreground**
root conversation, rather than the last conversation that submitted a prompt.
Command `sessionStart` hooks do not appear to provide a complete foreground-change
stream when switching between already-loaded sessions.

### Isolated observation

Tested Copilot CLI **1.0.105 on Linux**, using an empty disposable project, separate
`HOME`/`COPILOT_HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, user-level command hooks for `sessionStart`,
`sessionEnd` and `userPromptSubmitted`, normal folder consent and Manual Approval.
No auto-approval, production hooks or existing conversations were used.

1. Start the interactive CLI and submit a synthetic prompt in session A.
   Observe `sessionStart(A, source=new)` and `userPromptSubmitted(A)`.
2. Run `/new` and submit another synthetic prompt in B.
   Observe `sessionStart(B, source=new)` and `userPromptSubmitted(B)`.
3. Run `/resume <A-id>`, then `/session id` to independently confirm A is foreground.
4. Repeat `/resume <B-id>`, `/session id`, then `/resume <A-id>`, `/session id`.

Across these warm A-B-A switches, there were **no additional Start, End or
Prompt hook invocations** within the bounded 5-8 second observation windows.
A file written only by Start hooks would still identify B while A is displayed.
New idle conversations likewise produced no Start until the first submitted
prompt in this run.

A same-version `/restart` changed the observed CLI owner PID/start identity.
After restart, the first submitted prompt emitted Start with `source=resume`.
This was not a cross-version handoff test.

**Limitation:** model requests were rejected by account billing-entity
configuration, so this observation does not establish successful-completion,
subagent, background-model or all-platform behavior. The foreground switches,
session IDs and hook events were nevertheless observed independently. Please
confirm whether this limitation affects the intended lifecycle contract.

### Requested capability

Please provide or document one supported identity-only integration surface:

- A complete, causally serialized **foreground-session-changed** event covering
  warm switches, startup, new/clear/no-current transitions, with ordering and
  failure/supersession semantics; or
- A read-only authenticated accessor for current root identity (or no-current),
  resolved session-store location and an activation revision/conditional-current
  operation suitable for safely publishing asynchronous identity records.

An equivalent supported in-process integration would also work. Explicit revision
fields are not essential if the API guarantees complete serialized publication.
Session-only snapshots or hook-arrival counters alone do not establish that
delayed work still belongs to the current activation, particularly A-B-A.

This is not a request for tool approval, busy/idle authority, a heartbeat service,
or access to transcript contents. The goal is to stop relying on diagnostic log
registration lines to identify the displayed conversation.

Related but different: #4365 discusses prompt-hook/new/clear behavior; this request
concerns **command-hook coverage of warm foreground switches**.

issues.title: `--available-tools` with an empty value exposes all tools instead of none
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`--available-tools` is documented to disable every tool not listed, but an empty value (`--available-tools=` or `--available-tools ''`) sends all 21 built-in tools, the same as omitting the flag. There's no documented way to run `copilot -p` with no tools.


| Flag | Tools sent to the model |
|---|---|
| `--available-tools=` | 21 |
| `--available-tools ''` | 21 |
| `--excluded-tools '*'` | 21 |
| `--available-tools __none__` (a name that matches no tool) | 0 |

The workaround in the last row works, but it relies on unknown tool names being silently ignored.


### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. In an empty directory, run:
   ```
   copilot -p "Reply with the word ok." -s --model claude-haiku-5.5 \
     --available-tools= --disable-builtin-mcps --no-custom-instructions --no-ask-user
   ```
2. Read the tool count from the newest session's events:
   ```
   EVENTS=$(ls -t ~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl | head -1)
   jq -rn 'first(inputs | select(.type == "session.usage_checkpoint"))
     | .data.promptCacheBreakState[0].models[]
     | "\(.model): tool_count=\(.tool_count) tool_tokens=\(.tool_tokens)"' "$EVENTS"
   ```
   Output: `claude-haiku-5.5: tool_count=21 tool_tokens=10439`
3. Repeat steps 1 and 2 with `--available-tools __none__`.
   ```
   copilot -p "Reply with the word ok." -s --model claude-haiku-5.5 \
     --available-tools='__none__' --disable-builtin-mcps --no-custom-instructions --no-ask-user
   ```
   Output: `claude-haiku-5.5: tool_count=0 tool_tokens=0`


### Expected behavior

An empty `--available-tools` exposes no tools, or there's a documented way to disable all tools and an empty value is rejected with an error.

### Additional context

For text-only `copilot -p` calls in CI, the unwanted tool definitions add about 10,000 tokens per call. Related: #4596 (system prompt still references removed tools), #407 (list available tools).

issues.title: Hook event for slash-command / skill invocation (like Claude Code's UserPromptExpansion), and async command hooks

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, improvement, or new functionality

issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

Add a hook event that fires when a slash command or skill is invoked, with a matcher on its name

### Proposed solution

We ship skills as plugins for both Claude Code and Copilot CLI and log their use from plugin hooks. A skill the user types (/my-skill) doesn't go through the model's skill tool, so the only way to see it today is a userPromptSubmitted hook. That hook starts a process on every prompt and blocks it (~0.3 s), just to check whether the prompt starts with /.
 
Claude Code solves this with a UserPromptExpansion event. It fires when a typed command expands, carries command_name (plugin:skill) and command_source, and supports a matcher on the command name, so the hook only runs for matching commands.

Requests:
1. A hook event (e.g. skillInvoked / userPromptExpansion) that fires when a typed slash command or skill expands, with the plugin and skill name in the payload and a matcher on the name.
2. Support for "async": true on command hooks, so a logging hook doesn't delay the prompt (Claude Code runs async hooks in the background; Copilot CLI 1.0.105 currently waits for them).

The skill name and plugin are already available as the github.copilot.skill.invoked OTel span and the SDK SKILL_INVOKED event; exposing the same to plugin hooks would cover it.

### Example prompts or workflows

 User types /my-plugin:my-skill (or /my-skill). A hook configured as "skillInvoked": [{ "type": "command", "command": "...", "matcher": "^my-plugin:" }] runs with { "skillName": "my-plugin:my-skill", "source": "slash_command"}; ordinary prompts run no hook.

### Additional context

Copilot CLI 1.0.105, Windows 11. Claude Code already offers this as UserPromptExpansion

issues.title: Autopilot: assistant says its answer is "above", but no text was output before task_complete
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In autopilot, the agent often ends a turn with `task_complete` whose summary refers to a deliverable "above" (e.g.
"The Discord post is above, ready to copy"). The user sees no such text, because none was output: the
`assistant.message` before the call has `content: ""`. The user has to ask again, and the agent then insists it
already wrote it.

From my local session logs (`~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl`, last 21 days, deduplicated by tool-call ID):

- 544 `task_complete` calls; 489 had no assistant text before the call (often fine, the summary is the answer).
- 31 summaries refer to something "above"; in 27 of them (12 sessions) no text was output in that turn. Some may
  point to an earlier turn, so 27 is an upper bound.

One verified example (session log, 2026-10-30T15:55:32Z): the summary says "The shorter, casual Discord post is
above". The message content is empty, and the post text appears nowhere in the log, not even in the stored
reasoning summary, which only says "I've drafted a short, casual forum post…". Non-reasoning output was 151 tokens
for 342 characters of tool-call arguments, so no separate draft was emitted as visible output.

This is not #5150 (ACP clients got the summary only as a tool call; fixed in 1.0.102). Here the TUI shows everything
it received; the referenced text was never output. A second model (GPT-6.1 Sol) checked the log independently and
confirmed the counts.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105, TUI (not ACP). Windows 11, PowerShell 7. Model claude-opus-5.5, autopilot mode on.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

Intermittent; it happens most when the deliverable is text the user will copy (a draft, an explanation):

1. Turn on autopilot (`/autopilot` or Shift+Tab).
2. Ask: `Draft a short, casual forum post asking how others keep their CMS sites updated.`
3. Then ask: `Make it shorter and less formal.`
4. Check the final message: often only the `task_complete` summary appears, saying the post is "above", with no
   post shown.
5. Confirm in `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl`: the `assistant.message` with the `task_complete` tool
   request has `"content": ""`, and the post text is not in the file.

### Expected behavior

When the agent ends a turn with `task_complete`, every deliverable the user asked for is visible: either as message
text before the call or inside the summary. The summary never refers to text ("above") that was not output in this
or an earlier turn. Possible guardrails:

- the `task_complete` tool description could say "put the deliverable in the summary, or output it before calling";
- the CLI could flag a summary that refers to "above" when the turn has no visible text.

### Additional context

- Workaround: an instruction in `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` to put every deliverable inside the
  `task_complete` summary. That shouldn't be needed for every autopilot user.
- I searched github/copilot-cli issues ("autopilot task_complete summary", "message not shown", "task_complete
  hides") and found only #5150, which is a different problem.
- Root cause not proven: the token counts show the text wasn't emitted as visible output, but the stored reasoning
  is a summary (`reasoningSummary: "detailed"`), so I can't tell whether the model wrote it only in its reasoning.

issues.title: Agent writes invalid PowerShell on Windows (recurring patterns)
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When running on Windows, the Copilot CLI agent often writes PowerShell commands that fail to parse or run, so it has to retry. Each retry is an extra tool call plus a model turn. From 3 weeks of my session logs (2,164 unique shell calls), these patterns recur:

- Substring with IndexOf = -1, no bounds check (7 calls / 4 sessions)
- "$var: text" in a double-quoted string → ParserError; needs "${var}: text" (4/3)
- multi-line if/else joined into "}; elseif" → 'elseif' is not recognized (2/2)
- ConvertFrom-Json on package-lock.json without -AsHashtable, which fails on the empty "" key (2/2)
- bash-style \" escaping inside a single-quoted jq filter → jq parse error (1/1)

Expected: the agent writes valid PowerShell 7 for the powershell tool: no bash-isms, braces around a variable before ":", if/elseif blocks on separate lines, IndexOf results checked before Substring, and -AsHashtable for package-lock.json.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105. Windows 11, PowerShell 7.6.9, model claude-opus-5.5.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior


Each line below is a command of the kind the agent generated. Run each one in `pwsh -NoProfile`:

1. `$s="x"; "$s: y"` → ParserError: Variable reference is not valid
2. `if ($false) { 1 }; elseif ($true) { 2 }` → 'elseif' is not recognized
3. `'{"":1}' | ConvertFrom-Json` → "property whose name is an empty string … only supported using the -AsHashTable switch"
4. `"abc".Substring(0, [Math]::Min("abc".IndexOf("z"), 10))` → ArgumentOutOfRangeException (length -1)

### Expected behavior

On Windows, the agent writes valid PowerShell 7 for the powershell tool: no bash-style escaping ("), braces around a variable before a colon ("${var}:"), if/elseif/else kept on one block instead of joined with ";", IndexOf results checked before Substring, and ConvertFrom-Json -AsHashtable for files such as package-lock.json. The command should work on the first try, without a retry turn.

### Additional context

 - Counts come from my local session logs (~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl), 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-30. Calls were deduplicated by tool-call ID, because resumed sessions copy their history.
 - 11% of shell calls were flagged with a shell_error_category, but most of those were environment issues or real build failures. The patterns above are the ones caused by the generated command itself.
 - I searched the github/copilot-cli issues and found no existing report for these patterns.
 - Workaround: I added PowerShell rules to ~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md. That shouldn't be needed for every Windows user.

issues.title: web_search fails with HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout at ~120s (remote GitHub MCP server gateway timeout)
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

The built-in `web_search` tool fails intermittently (more than half of calls over the last ~9 days) with:

```
MCP server 'github-mcp-server': MCP request failed: Transport send error: Transport [...StreamableHttpClientWorker<...RawCapturingReqwestClient>...] error: unexpected server response: HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout: [HTML error page omitted]
```

Every failure happens at **~121s**. Successful calls take between 32s and 115s. This points to a fixed **120s gateway timeout** in front of the remote MCP endpoint (`https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/mcp/readonly`). The web search backend (Bing searches plus answer synthesis) often runs longer than that limit.

### Evidence (from local `~/.copilot/session-state/*/events.jsonl`, `tool.execution_start` → `tool.execution_complete`)

| Start (UTC)              | Duration (s) | Result |
|--------------------------|-------------:|--------|
| 2026-10-22T00:53:58Z     | 42.7  | OK  |
| 2026-10-22T00:58:11Z     | 42.4  | OK  |
| 2026-10-22T12:39:50Z     | 121.2 | 504 |
| 2026-10-22T12:42:42Z     | 121.0 | 504 |
| 2026-10-23T18:04:13Z     | 109.2 | OK  |
| 2026-10-26T17:13:55Z     | 87.1  | OK  |
| 2026-10-27T17:06:36Z     | 120.9 | 504 |
| 2026-10-28T19:36:13Z     | 120.9 | 504 |
| 2026-10-28T19:38:52Z     | 114.8 | OK  |
| 2026-10-28T19:38:52Z     | 120.8 | 504 |
| 2026-10-28T19:40:56Z     | 120.9 | 504 |
| 2026-10-28T19:49:43Z     | 121.1 | 504 |
| 2026-10-28T19:57:28Z     | 42.3  | OK  |
| 2026-10-28T19:59:53Z     | 32.1  | OK  |
| 2026-10-29T17:59:24Z     | 120.9 | 504 |
| 2026-10-30T13:58:26Z     | 121.0 | 504 |

That is 9 failures out of 16 calls, all at 120.8–121.2s.

### Client-side causes ruled out

- No HTTP(S) proxy configured (env vars and `scutil --proxy` are empty).
- No TLS interception: the endpoint certificate is `CN=*.business.githubcopilot.com`, issued by Sectigo.
- Traffic is routed directly via the local network, not through the corporate VPN.
- The endpoint responds normally from the GitHub edge (`x-github-edge-region: iad`, `x-github-backend: Kubernetes`).
- Copilot CLI is on the latest version (1.0.105). It has no configurable timeout for this tool.

### Expected behavior

`web_search` should complete reliably. Possible fixes:
- Raise the gateway/proxy timeout for the `web_search` tool on the remote MCP server above 120s.
- Bound the backend search/synthesis time so it finishes and returns a (possibly partial) answer before the gateway limit.
- Stream progress or keep-alives over the streamable HTTP transport so the gateway does not close idle long-running requests.

### Environment

- Copilot CLI 1.0.105, macOS (Apple Silicon), installed via Homebrew cask
- Plan: Copilot Business (`api.business.githubcopilot.com`)
- Remote MCP endpoint: `https://api.business.githubcopilot.com/mcp/readonly`
- Frequency: started roughly 2026-10-22 and occurs every day since

issues.title: Windows: 'Select an app to open' (OpenWith) dialog on every message when profile path contains a space
issues.body:
**Problem**
On Windows, every message sent in the GitHub Copilot app triggers the Windows "Select an app to open 'X'" dialog (OpenWith). X is only the first word of my Windows profile folder name, which contains a space (`C:\Users\First Last`). The dialog appears hundreds of times. It does not happen with Microsoft Copilot.

**Evidence (process watcher, 30 Oct 2026)**
- 14:08:25 `OpenWith.exe -Embedding` started 3 times, parent `svchost.exe` (Windows launches it when an open request has no registered handler).
- Same instant: `copilot-runtime.exe` spawned `pwsh.exe -NoProfile -NoLogo -NonInteractive -Command ...` (the shell tool).
- Copilot runtime log has no open/shell/launch entries around the event.
- No instructions, MCP config, agents or plugins reference the word; the only matches are the profile path.

**Likely cause**
An unquoted path (or openPath/ShellExecute-style call) containing a space is split at the space, so Windows is asked to open only the first word, which has no file association.

**Expected**
No open request, or the path is quoted so it resolves correctly.

**Repro**
Windows user profile with a space in the name, open the Copilot app, send any message.

1.0.105 (latest on npm), Linux

issues.title: store_memory fails for repositories whose origin is not on github.com (e.g., Azure DevOps)

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
## Summary

The `store_memory` tool returns the following error for every write attempt in a repository whose `origin` remote points somewhere other than `github.com`:

> Unable to store memory. The repository may not exist or you may not have write access to it. You can continue with your task without storing this information.

Reads of previously-stored memories still succeed (they're surfaced in the system prompt as `Repository memories for owner/repo`), so the failure is write-only.

## Reproduction

1. Take any repo that has stored memories from when `origin` was on GitHub.
2. Migrate hosting (e.g., to Azure DevOps): rename the GitHub remote, set `origin` to the new host:
   ```bash
   git remote rename origin github-archive
   git remote add origin https://dev.azure.com/<org>/<project>/_git/<repo>
   ```
3. In a fresh `copilot` session, ask the agent to remember a fact (so it calls `store_memory`).

**Expected:** memory is stored.
**Actual:** every `store_memory` call returns the access-denied message above. Reads of the previously-stored memories continue to work.

## Diagnosis (best guess)

Memory is keyed by GitHub `owner/repo`. The CLI infers that identifier from the `origin` remote URL. After migration, `origin` is no longer a GitHub URL, so the backend can't resolve the identifier and the write is rejected with a permissions-shaped error.

Reads work because the memories were written when `origin` was still GitHub and persist server-side; the read path may key off a cached / historical identifier or off the system-prompt repository hint.

## Why this matters

Teams that host code outside GitHub but still use Copilot CLI lose all session-to-session persistence of standing rules and conventions. The error message also misleads users into investigating GitHub permissions when the real issue is the remote URL scheme.

## Suggestions

1. **Don't silently fail.** When `store_memory` is called against a non-GitHub repo, return a clear error (`"Memory store currently requires a GitHub origin; this repo's origin is <URL>."`) instead of "the repository may not exist or you may not have write access" — the latter sends users on a wild goose chase through GitHub permissions.
2. **Allow an explicit override**, e.g., a `--memory-repo owner/name` flag, an env var (`COPILOT_MEMORY_REPO`), or a config key so a project hosted on ADO/GitLab/Bitbucket can pin its memory namespace to a sibling GitHub repo (often a mirror or an "ops" repo).
3. **Document** the GitHub-origin requirement in the README/help so users know up front.
4. **Long term**, decouple the memory namespace from the host (key by canonical workspace ID, repo path, or user-chosen string).

## Workaround I'm using

`AGENTS.md` at the repo root, which the CLI auto-loads every session per its docs. Captures the same standing rules, persists in git, and doesn't depend on the memory backend. Works well, but it's a workaround — multi-repo / per-user nuance that `store_memory` could express isn't replicable in a checked-in file.

## Environment

- macOS (Darwin)
- Repo originally on GitHub, migrated to Azure DevOps
- Multiple `store_memory` calls in a row, all returned the same error
- `githubstatus.com` shows Copilot operational at the time (no incident)

Happy to provide more detail or test patches.

However, in the current CLI this still presents as a confusing and inconsistent experience:

- `/model` -> `GPT-5.4` only shows `Low / Medium / High`
- the picker gives no explanation that `Extra High` is being hidden because of plan-tier gating
- current client bundles still appear to contain `xhigh`-related labels/descriptions/handling paths, which makes this look like a silent UI filter rather than a clearly communicated product restriction

So the problem here is not "please add xhigh back", but rather:

- the restriction is silently applied in the picker
- the CLI does not clearly explain why the option is missing
- this is easy to interpret as a broken or inconsistent model selector

Related issues:
- #2725
- #2739

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.36

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start `copilot`
2. Run `/model`
3. Select `GPT-5.4`
4. Open the reasoning effort picker
5. Observe that only `Low / Medium / High` are shown
6. Observe that there is no inline explanation that `Extra High` is hidden due to plan-tier restrictions

### Expected behavior

If `Extra High` is intentionally unavailable for the current account tier, the CLI should make that explicit.

For example, any of these would be much clearer than silently omitting it:

- show `Extra High` as disabled with a short explanation
- show a short message in the picker that it is restricted by plan tier
- document the restriction in a place the CLI can point to
- ensure the UI/messaging is consistent with the actual supported-effort metadata exposed by the client

issues.title: Support repository-level, version-controlled command permissions (allow / ask / deny)
issues.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you'd like to solve

While preparing a developer workshop, I wanted to commit a shared set of Copilot CLI command permissions alongside the repository's instructions, skills, and agents. Everyone cloning the repository should be able to review and adopt the same defaults, without individually configuring their home directory, repeatedly approving identical commands, or copying CLI flags.

The missing capability is **repository-level, version-controlled allow / ask / deny rules for commands**, not just saving one user's approvals for a project on their own machine.

Copilot CLI already supports `.github/copilot/settings.json`, but the [documented repository settings](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-config-dir-reference#repository-settings-githubcopilotsettingsjson) do not include command permission rules. Saved project permissions under `~/.copilot/permissions-config.json` are local to each user, rather than a portable configuration shared through the repository.

### Proposed solution

Support a committed repository permission configuration, ideally by extending `.github/copilot/settings.json`, with:

- **Allow:** preapprove specific commands or command patterns without repeated prompts.
- **Ask:** require explicit approval for matching commands, even when a broader allow rule matches.
- **Deny:** block matching commands, with deny taking precedence over ask and allow.

Reuse Copilot CLI's existing permission pattern syntax where practical, and document matching and precedence. Rules should be repository-scoped and portable across collaborators' machines.

Repository-provided approvals should require explicit user review and opt-in, not silently apply just because a repository was cloned. Changes that expand approvals should be surfaced for review. Repository rules must not weaken organization restrictions or explicit user deny rules.

Named or switchable permission profiles are not required for this use case: a committed, team-shared permission file would be sufficient.

### Example prompts or workflows

1. **Workshop setup:** the organizer commits approvals for the workshop's test and lint commands. Participants review and accept those rules instead of configuring identical permissions individually.
2. **Team onboarding:** new contributors clone the repository and can adopt the same reviewed command defaults as the rest of the team.
3. **Team standards:** setting up team standards for permissions corresponding to committed instruction files and skills would allow better collaboration.
4. **Mixed approval levels:** allow `npm run test` and `npm run lint`, ask before `git push`, and deny `git reset --hard`.
5. **Reviewable permission changes:** a pull request adds a new command approval alongside the script or workflow that needs it.

This avoids requiring broad `--allow-all` access simply to reduce repetitive approvals.

### Additional context

Claude Code supports repository-level `.claude/settings.json` files with `permissions.allow`, `permissions.ask`, and `permissions.deny`. I would like an equivalent native Copilot CLI capability.

Related issues:

- #3176 proposes a broader system of named, switchable permission profiles, including per-repository profiles. This request focuses specifically on committed, team-shared rules without requiring a profile system.
- #2398 requests a default permission configuration file, primarily at the user level.
- #5083 requests remembering approvals across sessions.
- #2338 reports that permissions in `.claude/settings.json` are not applied.
