issues.title: ACP session/list: every page rescans all sessions, so listing thousands takes minutes

labels.name: area:sessions
labels.description: Session management, resume, history, session picker, and session state

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Over ACP (`copilot --acp --stdio`), every page of `session/list` takes about as long as a scan of the whole session store. With many sessions, following `nextCursor` to the end takes minutes, so an ACP client either waits minutes for the full list or shows a partial one.

On one machine with 6,660 folders (34 GB) in `~/.copilot/session-state`, Copilot CLI 1.0.95 on macOS:

- `session/list` without `cwd` returns 4,618 sessions in 93 pages of 50.
- Each page takes about 1.0–1.7 s, whether it's the first page or the 90th.
- Following every page took 172 s, and 131 s again right after in the same process, so nothing is cached between lists.
- A page filtered by `cwd` also takes about 1 s.
- `initialize` takes about 0.5 s.

The cost per page doesn't depend on the cursor, which suggests every page reads all sessions, then sorts and slices.

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.95

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Have a few thousand sessions in `~/.copilot/session-state`.
2. Start `copilot --acp --stdio`, send `initialize`, then `session/list` with `{}`.
3. Keep calling `session/list` with each `nextCursor` until there is none, and time each request.

Every request takes about the same time; the total grows with the number of pages times the size of the store.

### Expected behavior

Each page costs roughly what its own 50 sessions cost. For example:
- Keep the sorted index between pages of one listing, or across listings.
- Stop reading once the page is filled.

Also helpful:
- An `updatedAfter`-style filter, so a client can fetch only sessions that changed since its last list.
- A larger page size, so the client needs fewer requests.

### Additional context

Found while building an ACP client that shows every session on the computer. It now works around this: it shows each page as it arrives, saves the last list, and re-reads only the first pages that changed. A full list still costs minutes of CPU in the Copilot process.

issues.title: ACP: session/prompt response is held until an async bash shell exits, so clients appear stuck

labels.name: area:non-interactive
labels.description: Non-interactive mode (-p), CI/CD, ACP protocol, and headless automation

labels.name: area:tools
labels.description: Built-in tools: file editing, shell, search, LSP, git, and tool call behavior

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

In ACP mode (`copilot --acp`), when the agent starts a shell with the `bash` tool in `mode: "async"`, the `session/prompt` response is withheld until that shell exits, even though the agent's foreground work finished long before. If the async shell is a dev server or another long-running process, the prompt never completes. ACP clients have no other end-of-turn signal on protocol v1, so they show the session as busy indefinitely.

The same prompt with `detach: true` (bash args `{"mode":"async","detach":true}`) behaves as expected: `session/prompt` returns `end_turn` as soon as the foreground work ends, and the later shell-completion wake (`system.notification` → `read_bash` → new turn) still happens.

This makes ACP clients look stuck. It was reported downstream in T3 Code: https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/issues/27301

### Affected version

1.0.105

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Start `copilot --acp` and send `initialize` (protocolVersion 1; optionally subscribe to raw events with `clientCapabilities._meta["github.com/copilot"].events = ["assistant.turn_end", "session.usage_checkpoint", "system.notification"]`).
2. `session/new`, then `session/prompt` with: *Use the bash tool with mode "async" (NOT detached) to run `sleep 25`, do not wait or read its output, then immediately reply with just the word ok. Do nothing else.* Allow the permission request.
3. Note when the `session/prompt` response arrives.
4. Repeat asking for `detach: true` for comparison, and check the bash arguments in `~/.copilot/session-state/<sessionId>/events.jsonl`: the bug needs `{"mode":"async","detach":false}` or no `detach` field.

Observed (seconds from start):

```
async, not detached ({"mode":"async"}):
  3.22  tool_call bash "sleep 25"
  3.94  sessionEvent assistant.turn_end
  3.94  sessionEvent session.usage_checkpoint    <- foreground work done, "ok" already sent
 28.27  sessionEvent system.notification         <- shell completed
 28.27  tool_call read_bash
 29.41  sessionEvent assistant.turn_end
 29.42  session/prompt response {"stopReason":"end_turn"}    <- held ~25 s

async + detach ({"mode":"async","detach":true}):
  4.18  tool_call bash "sleep 25"
  5.17  sessionEvent assistant.turn_end
  5.18  sessionEvent session.usage_checkpoint
  5.18  session/prompt response {"stopReason":"end_turn"}    <- immediate
 29.87  sessionEvent system.notification         <- wake still delivered
```

In a real session the agent started a local dev server with `mode: "async"`. The client showed the session as busy for about 10 minutes after the agent finished. The response to the next prompt came 0.5 s after I killed the dev server. Sending `session/cancel` also releases the held prompt without killing the async shell.

### Expected behavior

`session/prompt` should resolve with `end_turn` when the agent's foreground work ends, as it does for detached shells, even if an async shell started in that prompt is still running. If async shells must keep the prompt open by design, please provide a documented signal that foreground work has ended, such as ACP `state_update` idle (protocol v2) or a documented `sessionEvent`, so clients can show the session as idle with background work running.

### Additional context

- macOS 27.0.1, arm64
- Client: ACP over stdio (T3 Code; also reproduced with a minimal standalone JSON-RPC client)
- Models: claude-sonnet-5.5 (repro), gpt-6.1-sol (original session)

Also reproduced inside T3 Code with `{"command":"sleep 90","mode":"async","detach":false}`: the agent replied "ok" and emitted `session.usage_checkpoint` 4.3 s after the prompt, but the `session/prompt` response arrived 100 s after the prompt, only after the shell exited and the agent ran a second internal turn.

issues.title: Automatic compaction repeatedly times out at 300s until sessions hit the hard context limit (1.0.91)

labels.name: area:context-memory
labels.description: Context window, memory, compaction, checkpoints, and instruction loading

issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Automatic compaction repeatedly fails with a 300-second summarizer timeout. The conversation keeps growing until Copilot CLI rejects requests because they exceed the model's context limit. The error recommends retrying compaction, but automatic compaction and the context-limit retry have both already timed out.

I have been encountering this across my Copilot sessions, not just once. The detailed counts below were verified in one affected long-running session; the cross-session recurrence is my user report, not a count of all sessions.

Exact blocking error:

```text
Execution failed: Automatic compaction timed out and the request still exceeds the model's context limit (555009 tokens; limit 553200). Reduce context or retry compaction before continuing.
```

### Affected version

GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.91. This version is recorded in the affected session's startup event and confirmed by `copilot --version`.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. Use a long-running interactive Copilot CLI session with a large context. The inspected session uses GPT-6.1 Sol (`gpt-6.1-sol`), `long_context`, and reasoning effort `max`; the footer reports a 1.1M context.
2. Continue normal work until automatic compaction triggers.
3. Observe repeated `session.compaction_complete` events with `success: false` and the error shown below.
4. Continue working/retrying. Eventually a request fails with the hard context-limit error above, leaving the session unable to continue that request without intervention.

This is an observed failure sequence from a real session, not a minimal synthetic reproducer.

### Expected behavior

Automatic compaction should reliably reduce the conversation before requests exceed their effective context budget. If summarization cannot finish within its time budget, the CLI should provide a viable non-destructive recovery path rather than repeatedly discarding summaries and eventually blocking the session. Compaction accounting and the effective request budget should be coordinated so the session does not require manual rescue.

### Additional context

Environment: Linux x86_64, bash, tmux 3.4. The affected session had been running for approximately eight days.

The initial diagnostic snapshot, before recovery was attempted, contained **192 completed compaction attempts: 15 successful and 177 failed**. Of the failures, **175** had exactly this error:

```text
automatic compaction summarizer did not settle within 300s of starting; pending summary discarded
```

The other two failures were a connection timeout and an authentication error, so they are not included in the 175 summarizer-timeout count.

Selected sanitized events, all on 2026-10-29 UTC:

```text
04:29:36.426 session.compaction_complete
  success=true, trigger=threshold
  preCompactionTokens=738110, postCompactionTokens=70850
  messagesRemoved=951, tokenLimit=922000

18:04:48.304 session.compaction_start
  trigger=threshold, currentTokens=882584, tokenLimit=922000
18:09:48.324 session.compaction_complete
  success=false, trigger=threshold, tokenLimit=922000
  error="automatic compaction summarizer did not settle within 300s of starting; pending summary discarded"
18:09:49.919 session.error
  errorType=query
  message="Execution failed: Automatic compaction timed out and the request still exceeds the model's context limit (555009 tokens; limit 553200). Reduce context or retry compaction before continuing."

18:15:18.083 session.compaction_start
  trigger=context_limit_retry, currentTokens=709698, tokenLimit=922000
18:20:18.139 session.compaction_complete
  success=false, trigger=context_limit_retry, tokenLimit=922000
  error="automatic compaction summarizer did not settle within 300s of starting; pending summary discarded"
```

The compaction events report `tokenLimit=922000`, while the blocking request reports `limit 553200`. These are the recorded values; I have not established why the budgets differ. Earlier failures in the same session also reported `553294 / 553200` and `646726 / 645400` tokens.

Related: https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/5054 describes the same 300-second timeout. This report adds a Linux reproduction with repeated hard context-limit failures, a failed `context_limit_retry` recovery, and a successful manual compaction that took longer than the automatic timeout.

### Manual recovery result

Once the active inference was cancelled and the session was idle, the built-in `/compact` command succeeded without changing the model or reasoning setting, restarting the process, or manually editing session history:

```text
18:29:34.652 session.compaction_start
  trigger=manual, currentTokens=718298
18:36:47.985 session.compaction_complete
  success=true, trigger=manual, tokenLimit=922000
  preCompactionTokens=687202, postCompactionTokens=15751
  messagesRemoved=1665, checkpointNumber=16
```

The successful manual compaction took **433.333 seconds (7 minutes 13 seconds)**, exceeding the automatic summarizer's 300-second deadline. Its checkpoint was persisted. Afterwards, `/context` showed **78k / 1050k tokens (7%)**, and the original process resumed its existing work. This is a recovery workaround, not a fix for the recurring automatic timeout.

No conversation contents, source code, credentials, private repository names, or full diagnostic logs are included in this report.

issues.title: plugin marketplace add fails entirely if any single plugin description exceeds 1024 chars

labels.name: area:plugins
labels.description: Plugin system, marketplace, hooks, skills, extensions, and custom agents

issues.body:
### Environment
- Copilot CLI: `1.0.88`
- OS: macOS

### Problem

`copilot plugin marketplace add <owner>/<repo>` performs strict Zod validation
of `marketplace.json` and rejects the **entire marketplace** if *any* plugin
entry has a `description` longer than 1024 characters. There is no partial
load, warning-and-skip, or truncation — a single non-conformant plugin entry
makes the whole marketplace (hundreds of otherwise-valid plugins) unusable.

This may be related to/duplicate work for #3494 (SKILL.md `description` >1024
chars silently dropped from `skills.list()`), but the failure mode here is the
opposite and arguably worse: instead of silently dropping the *SKILL.md* entry
in an *installed* plugin, the CLI hard-fails to *add* an entire marketplace
because of a handful of over-length `description` fields in `marketplace.json`.

### Reproducer

```
$ copilot plugin marketplace add Rippling/claude-marketplace
Failed to add marketplace: Error: Request plugins.marketplaces.add failed with message: Invalid marketplace.json: plugins.27.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s), plugins.89.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s), plugins.147.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s), plugins.171.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s), plugins.394.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s), plugins.406.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s), plugins.417.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s), plugins.439.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s), plugins.580.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s), plugins.610.description: String must contain at most 1024 character(s)
```

The referenced `marketplace.json` has 672 plugin entries; 10 of them have
`description` fields between 1084 and 6103 characters (one is nearly 6x the
cap). Trimming just those 10 descriptions to ≤1024 chars allows the
marketplace to be added successfully — every other field/entry is otherwise
valid.

### Impact

- A single contributor adding an overlong description (easy to do
  accidentally, e.g. via generated/templated descriptions) blocks marketplace
  adoption for the *entire org*, not just their plugin.
- The error message lists the offending indices but not plugin names, making
  it hard to locate/fix the entries without manually indexing into the JSON
  array.
- There's no `--force`/lenient mode to add the marketplace while skipping or
  truncating invalid entries.

### Suggested fix

- Validate per-plugin-entry and skip/warn on individual invalid entries
  (matching the description in #3494) instead of failing the whole
  marketplace add, OR
- Include the plugin `name`/`id` (not just array index) in the validation
  error so it's actionable, and/or
- Document the 1024-char `description` cap for `marketplace.json` plugin
  entries (currently not called out anywhere in
  https://docs.github.com/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/plugins-marketplace).

prs.title: Fix container smoke-test workspace permissions
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes the amd64 and arm64 smoke-test failures in [workflow run 41153798295](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/actions/runs/41153798295).

The temporary workspace is created with mode `0700`, preventing the image runtime user (UID 10001) from accessing it. Initializing Git as root also leaves files that the non-root Actions runner cannot remove, masking the original failure with a cleanup traceback.

- Make the temporary workspace traversable by the runtime user.
- Initialize Git with the host UID/GID so the runner owns and can remove the fixture. Use `/tmp/workspace` for initialization because the host UID cannot traverse the runtime user’s private home.
- Keep the actual Git check at `/home/copilot/workspace` under the unchanged runtime UID and exact-path `safe.directory` policy.
- Document the bind-mounted Git check.

## Validation

- Reproduced both original permission failures using the release 1.0.105 image and a non-root host identity (UID/GID 1001).
- All six smoke checks pass on `linux/amd64` as both a non-root host and root, including the real server handshake, incorrect-token rejection, and SIGTERM shutdown.
- Removing system Git trust still produces the expected dubious-ownership failure; the host-owned fixture is cleaned up even on that failure.
- `git diff --check` passes.

Arm64 was not run locally; the fixture fix is architecture-independent. No image, publishing behavior, or runtime permissions are changed.

prs.title: Publish a Copilot CLI server container image on release
prs.body:
**Recreated from #5307:** This PR retains the original two commits unchanged.

**Outstanding review feedback:** An existing `latest` or `prerelease` manifest without a version annotation can be mistaken for a missing tag and overwritten by an older release. See the [original review comment](https://github.com/github/copilot-cli/pull/5307#discussion_r4427479326). The other two findings were addressed in the original final commit.

**Historical validation:** The original fork was deleted, so the fork workflow runs and `fork-validation` branch linked below are no longer accessible. For this recreation, a native Linux arm64 image build and all five container smoke checks passed, as did ShellCheck, actionlint, and the Python syntax check.

## Why

#55 asks for a container image of the CLI. This adds a workflow that publishes one to `ghcr.io/github/copilot-cli` whenever a release is published. The image runs the CLI as a headless server, so a Copilot SDK client in another container, a CI job or an integration test (for example one that starts Copilot with Testcontainers) can connect to it over TCP. It generalizes the image that [copilot-sdk-integrations](https://github.com/brunoborges/copilot-sdk-integrations) builds for its Testcontainers module, without the Java and Testcontainers specifics.

It does not fully answer #55: the regular `copilot` binary is in the image, but interactive use is neither the goal nor tested.

The trigger and trust model follow #5000: `release: published` plus a manual dispatch from `main` with an explicit tag, scripts taken from `main` and never from the release tag, and validation that fails closed.

## What changed

- `.github/workflows/publish-container.yml`: the release workflow.
- `container/Dockerfile`, `container/entrypoint.sh`, `container/Dockerfile.dockerignore`: the image.
- `container/smoke_test.py`: the gate that runs before anything is pushed.
- `container/README.md`: usage, configuration, security, verification and publishing.
- `.github/dependabot.yml`: keeps the pinned base image digest current.

**Image.** `debian:trixie-slim` pinned by digest, plus the official `copilot-linux-{x64,arm64}.tar.gz` release asset, verified against the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt` during the build. It runs as a non-root user, listens on port 4321 and refuses to start unless `COPILOT_CONNECTION_TOKEN` is set. Auto-update is off. The image is built from the files on `main` when the workflow runs, never from the release tag, and `org.opencontainers.image.revision` records that commit.

**Workflow**, in three jobs:

1. **Validate release**: checks that the tag is `vX.Y.Z` or `vX.Y.Z-N`, that the release is published and not a draft, that its prerelease flag matches the version, and that `copilot-linux-x64.tar.gz`, `copilot-linux-arm64.tar.gz` and `SHA256SUMS.txt` are fully uploaded.
2. **Build amd64 / arm64**: builds each architecture on a native runner and runs `container/smoke_test.py` against it (five checks, including a real `connect` handshake with the server). Only then does it push by digest, and it verifies that the pushed image has the same layers as the one that was tested.
3. **Publish multi-platform image**: assembles the OCI index, tags it with the version, moves the channel tag and attests the index.

**Tags.** `X.Y.Z[-N]` for each release, `latest` for the newest stable release and `prerelease` for the newest prerelease. A channel tag never moves backwards, so publishing an older release (for example a patch for an older line) does not replace `latest`.

**Security.** Top-level `permissions: {}` with per-job least privilege (only the publish job gets `packages`, `id-token`, `attestations` and `artifact-metadata`), all actions pinned to commit SHAs, no secrets (GHCR via `GITHUB_TOKEN`), runs only in `github/copilot-cli`, dispatch only from `main`. The index gets SLSA build provenance, pushed to the registry next to the image.

## Validation

I can't run this workflow in `github/copilot-cli`, so I validated it in my fork, [brunoborges/copilot-cli](https://github.com/brunoborges/copilot-cli), with a real `release: published` event and real GHCR pushes. The fork's releases carried placeholder assets (the workflow only checks that they exist); the image downloads the real binaries from `github/copilot-cli`'s releases. The fork ran this PR's workflow with two lines changed to target the fork: the repository guard and the release lookup. The earlier runs below used earlier revisions that differ in small details (for example the digest artifact retention and the runner labels); the last run is this PR's code, and its exact commit is on the fork's [`fork-validation`](https://github.com/brunoborges/copilot-cli/tree/fork-validation) branch.

| What | Run |
| --- | --- |
| Dry run: build and smoke test on both native runners, nothing pushed | [41103805885](https://github.com/brunoborges/copilot-cli/actions/runs/41103805885) |
| First publish from a real `release: published` event (new package, `latest` created). `actions/attest` hit a transient Sigstore error (`error fetching tlog entry - (404) Not Found`); re-running the failed job completed it | [41105152382](https://github.com/brunoborges/copilot-cli/actions/runs/41105152382) |
| Older stable release (1.0.104 after 1.0.105), manual dispatch: version tag created, `latest` stays at 1.0.105 | [41106646123](https://github.com/brunoborges/copilot-cli/actions/runs/41106646123) |
| First prerelease (1.0.105-1), manual dispatch: `prerelease` created, `latest` untouched | [41106899190](https://github.com/brunoborges/copilot-cli/actions/runs/41106899190) |
| Older prerelease (1.0.105-0), manual dispatch: `prerelease` stays at 1.0.105-1 | [41107225135](https://github.com/brunoborges/copilot-cli/actions/runs/41107225135) |
| Final code on the pinned `ubuntu-24.04` runners, manual dispatch with a real publish | [41108477246](https://github.com/brunoborges/copilot-cli/actions/runs/41108477246) |

Checked from outside after publishing:

- the package pulls anonymously;
- `docker buildx imagetools inspect` shows an OCI index with `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` and the expected `org.opencontainers.image.*` annotations;
- `gh attestation verify oci://ghcr.io/brunoborges/copilot-cli:1.0.105 -R brunoborges/copilot-cli` passes (workflow `publish-container.yml` on `refs/tags/v1.0.105`, trigger `release`, GitHub-hosted runner);
- `container/smoke_test.py` passes 5/5 against the pulled image on arm64 and on amd64 under emulation.

Locally I built native arm64 and emulated amd64 images, exercised the release validation and tagging logic including the failure cases, connected with the Node.js SDK, and ran `actionlint` and `shellcheck`. I also checked every release of this repository (521): tags are always `vX.Y.Z` or `vX.Y.Z-N` with a matching prerelease flag, and all 449 releases since `v0.0.370-1` carry the three assets the workflow requires.

## Required setup

No secrets. After the first publish, please check that `ghcr.io/github/copilot-cli` is public and linked to this repository (package settings). The organization's package settings must allow this repository to publish a public package.

## Open questions

- **Server flags.** The entrypoint runs `copilot --headless --host 0.0.0.0 --port 4321` and reads `COPILOT_CONNECTION_TOKEN`. None of these are listed by `copilot --help` or `copilot help environment` (1.0.105). Are they stable enough to depend on?
- **`prerelease` semantics.** The image's `prerelease` tag is the newest prerelease, like npm. `install.sh` resolves `VERSION=prerelease` to the highest tag by version sort, which can also be a stable release. Which should the image follow?
- **Concurrency.** One global, non-cancelling group, so two runs never race to move a channel tag. A run waiting behind another one is replaced by a newer waiting run; the README says to dispatch the workflow with the release tag to publish a replaced release. Is that acceptable?
- **Attestation order.** The attestation runs after the tags move, so a Sigstore outage leaves a tagged image without an attestation until the failed job is re-run (documented in the README). I can attest before tagging instead if you prefer to fail closed.
- **Storage record.** In organization-owned repositories `actions/attest` also writes an artifact storage record. That can't be exercised from a user-owned fork. It only warns on failure, and the workflow grants `artifact-metadata: write` for it.
- **ARM runners.** The arm64 image is built on `ubuntu-24.04-arm`. If those runners aren't available to this repository, the build can fall back to QEMU.
- **Release assets.** Like `winget.yml`, the workflow fires when the release is published and expects the assets to be attached by then. If they aren't, the first job fails and the workflow can be dispatched once they are.

Left out on purpose, as easy follow-ups: CI for pull requests that touch `container/**` (build and smoke test without pushing) and a pointer in the root README.

issues.title: server: GET /api/vcs returns {"branch":{}} until the location's plugins activate, while /api/vcs/branch already answers
issues.body:
### Description The first `GET /api/vcs` for a directory that the server has not served yet returns `200 {"branch":{}}`. It keeps returning that for about 1 s, until the location's plugin activation registers the git provider and the cached summary refreshes. During that window, `GET /api/vcs/branch` for the same location already returns `["main"]`. A client that reads the summary once gets an answer that looks like "no branch" or "not a repository", with no signal that the answer is not final. ``` [ 311 ms] vcs.get {"branch":{}} vcs.branch.list [] [ 766 ms] vcs.get {"branch":{}} vcs.branch.list ["main"] [ 1061 ms] vcs.get {"provider":"git","branch":{"current":"main","default":"main"}} vcs.branch.list ["main"] ``` The window reopens for every directory that the server has not seen before, not only after a server start. What I found: - `vcs.get` returns a cached value ([handlers/vcs.ts#L11-L18](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6f3639d82ed0760091792189b78f8eeb44f699b1/packages/server/src/handlers/vcs.ts#L11-L18) → `info()`, [vcs.ts#L169-L171](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6f3639d82ed0760091792189b78f8eeb44f699b1/packages/core/src/vcs.ts#L169-L171)). The cache starts as `{ branch: {} }` ([L61](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6f3639d82ed0760091792189b78f8eeb44f699b1/packages/core/src/vcs.ts#L61)). - Only `refresh()` fills the cache ([L122-L143](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6f3639d82ed0760091792189b78f8eeb44f699b1/packages/core/src/vcs.ts#L122-L143)). `refresh()` runs from the state notify after a provider registers ([L84](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6f3639d82ed0760091792189b78f8eeb44f699b1/packages/core/src/vcs.ts#L84)), or on a `HEAD` change. The git provider registers during the location's asynchronous plugin activation ([plugin/vcs/git.ts#L34-L35](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6f3639d82ed0760091792189b78f8eeb44f699b1/packages/core/src/plugin/vcs/git.ts#L34-L35)). [plugin/service.ts#L29-L33](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6f3639d82ed0760091792189b78f8eeb44f699b1/packages/core/src/plugin/service.ts#L29-L33) describes this exact early-request case. The handler does not wait for activation. - `branches()` reads the provider on every call ([L177-L187](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/6f3639d82ed0760091792189b78f8eeb44f699b1/packages/core/src/vcs.ts#L177-L187)), so it answers as soon as the provider is registered. The summary waits for the deferred `refresh()` and the git calls that it runs. - During that window, the response has no `provider`. After a refresh, a detached HEAD is `{"provider":"git","branch":{"default":"main"}}`. So `provider` is the only thing that separates "not known yet" from a real answer, and that is not documented. This looks like the same class as #36117 (catalog reads return 200 with intermediate activation state), for a different route. Possible fixes, in order of preference: 1. In `vcs.get`, wait for plugin activation and for the first `refresh()` to finish before it answers, in the same way that `worktree` and the session entry points already wait on `Plugin.awaitActivation`. 2. Or compute `info()` from the provider when the cache has never been refreshed, as `branches()` already does. 3. At a minimum, document on `Vcs.Info` that an absent `provider` means "not determined yet". ### Plugins None (isolated config, `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT={}`). ### OpenCode version 2.0.15 (`opencode serve`). The relevant code is unchanged in v2.0.16 and on `v2` at `19a9e41c28`. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Start `opencode serve` with its working directory outside the repository. 2. Create a git repository with one commit on `main`. 3. Poll `GET /api/vcs?location[directory]=` and `GET /api/vcs/branch?location[directory]=` every 100 ms. 4. The first samples of `/api/vcs` are `{"branch":{}}`, while `/api/vcs/branch` already returns `["main"]`.
Script (bun; starts an isolated opencode serve) ```ts // bun vcs-cold-location.ts (starts an isolated `opencode serve`, then touches a git repo it has not seen yet) import { mkdirSync, mkdtempSync } from "node:fs" import { tmpdir } from "node:os" import { join } from "node:path" const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "oc-vcs-")) const repo = join(root, "repo") mkdirSync(repo) Bun.spawnSync(["git", "init", "-q", "-b", "main"], { cwd: repo }) Bun.spawnSync(["git", "-c", "user.name=r", "-c", "user.email=r@r", "commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", "init"], { cwd: repo }) const port = 20000 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 20000) const base = `http://127.0.0.1:${port}` const headers = { authorization: "Basic " + btoa("opencode:repro") } const server = Bun.spawn([process.env.OPENCODE_BIN ?? "opencode", "serve", "--hostname", "127.0.0.1", "--port", `${port}`], { cwd: root, // not the repo, so the repo's location is cold on first request stdout: "ignore", stderr: "ignore", env: { ...process.env, OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD: "repro", OPENCODE_DB: join(root, "opencode.db"), XDG_DATA_HOME: join(root, "data"), XDG_CONFIG_HOME: join(root, "config"), XDG_STATE_HOME: join(root, "state"), XDG_CACHE_HOME: join(root, "cache"), OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT: "{}", OPENCODE_DISABLE_MODELS_FETCH: "1", }, }) const get = (path: string) => fetch(`${base}${path}`, { headers }).then((r) => r.text()) while (!(await fetch(`${base}/api/info`, { headers }).then((r) => r.ok, () => false))) await Bun.sleep(100) const at = `location[directory]=${encodeURIComponent(repo)}` const t0 = performance.now() let last = "" for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) { const vcs = await get(`/api/vcs?${at}`) const branches = await get(`/api/vcs/branch?${at}`) const line = `vcs.get ${JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(vcs).data)} vcs.branch.list ${JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(branches).data)}` if (line !== last) console.log(`[${Math.round(performance.now() - t0).toString().padStart(5)} ms] ${line}`) last = line if (JSON.parse(vcs).data.provider) break await Bun.sleep(100) } server.kill() ```
### Screenshot and/or share link Not applicable (HTTP API). ### Operating System Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200. The same raw `{"branch":{}}` was seen on Linux with 2.0.2. ### Terminal Not applicable (HTTP API; the script runs under bun 1.3.8).

issues.title: Bug: stale event sequence permanently rejects new session events
issues.body:
## Description

A durable aggregate can become permanently unwritable when `event_sequence.seq` falls behind rows already present in `event`. The next local publish derives `seq = event_sequence.seq + 1`, updates the sequence row, then collides with the existing `(aggregate_id, seq)` unique index. The transaction rolls back, so every later prompt repeats the same collision.

The event log itself remains intact; the failure is the stale sequence cursor. New publishes should recover inside the existing immediate transaction by deriving the local high-water mark from both tables, then write the next contiguous sequence without changing owner-claim behavior.

Plugin developers commonly run and compare v1 and v2 while supporting both host generations. That is a normal development workflow, not an unsupported user mistake. If only `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` is isolated while the default data DB remains shared, cross-generation startup can leave an active v1 session damaged (see #42260). This defensive recovery is necessary for a legacy database already left in that state; it does not replace proper v1/v2 data isolation.

## Plugins

None

## OpenCode version

1.18.32 (observed); latest `dev` inspected for the fix

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create an aggregate and durable events through any normal OpenCode path.
2. In a stopped, disposable SQLite fixture, lower only that aggregate's `event_sequence.seq` below the highest `event.seq`; do not alter the event rows.
3. Start OpenCode and publish another durable event for the aggregate.
4. Observe `UNIQUE constraint failed: event.aggregate_id, event.seq`; retries use the same stale sequence and the session remains unusable.

This can be left behind by historical cross-version/shared-database migration scenarios. Related context: #42260, #42444, #42389, and the template-closed report #51316.

## Operating System

macOS 26 / Apple Silicon

## Terminal

iTerm2

issues.title: [BUG]: Message revert/undo frequently corrupts session state — conversations and file changes get scrambled
issues.body:
### Description

Reverting/undoing a message (undo stack, "revert this message", regenerate-after-edit paths) **frequently leaves the session in a scrambled state** — this happens often enough to be a serious daily-driver issue, not a rare edge case.

Observed symptoms across repeated undos (Windows 11, Desktop recent builds incl. 1.18.30-era):

- Conversation history gets out of order or messages are misplaced/duplicated after an undo; the visible thread no longer matches what actually happened.
- File changes do not line up with the reverted conversation: some edits stay applied, some are rolled back incorrectly, and later turns run against a file state that contradicts the visible messages.
- Sometimes the whole session view bricks or behaves inconsistently until the session is closed/reopened.

This is broader than the individual reports below — from our side it presents as "undo is usually wrong in some way" rather than one fixed repro. Severity: high — we rely on undo daily and it has repeatedly destroyed work-in-progress sessions.

Happy to capture concrete session logs/screenshots on the next occurrence — guidance on what to attach would help.

### Related (already-tracked individual symptoms of the same class)

- #42370 (open) — Changes don't discard when message is reverted
- #46783 (open) — Running UNDO command deletes a file that was just read
- #33940 (open) — Undo in one session reverts all sessions
- #39260 (open) — Aborting a generation then editing/resending leaves an orphaned parentID, bricking the session view with a 404
- #40574 (open) — File modifications from other sessions appear unexpectedly in current session
- #39656 (open) — V2 auto-revert leaves forked session without instruction checkpoint
- Closed historical context: #5474, #29520, #32529, #20315, #10287

### Plugins

oh-my-openagent (oh-my-openagent@latest)

### OpenCode version

Desktop 1.18.30-era (Windows 11 x64); reproduces across recent builds

### Operating System

Windows 11

### Terminal

OpenCode Desktop app (Electron)

issues.title: Windows: plugin installs leave orphaned <spec>.staging-* copies in the packages cache (~38 GB)
issues.body:
### Description
On Windows, the plugin package cache at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\opencode\packages` accumulates orphaned install copies and grew to ~38 GB.

Each plugin install/update attempt leaves a full copy named `<spec>.staging-<rand>` next to the real `<spec>@latest` directory, and nothing ever removes them:
- 197 orphaned dirs `.oh-my-opencode-slim@latest.staging-*`, ~261 MB / 12,376 files each.
- Each contains its own `package.json` (`{"private":true,"dependencies":{"oh-my-opencode-slim":"2.2.x"}}`), `bun.lock` and a full `node_modules`.
- New ones appear during runtime even when the installed version already equals `latest` (3 new dirs within ~3 min while already on 2.2.25).
- The CLI cleanup matcher is `^\.staging-(\d+)-`, but the real names are `<spec>.staging-<rand>`, so they are never cleaned (`failed to remove stale npm generation`).

Expected: staging dirs are removed after a successful install, or stale `<spec>.staging-*` dirs are garbage-collected.
Actual: they accumulate without bound.

### Plugins
oh-my-opencode-slim (declared unversioned)

### OpenCode version
Desktop app, bundled CLI 2.0.16

### Steps to reproduce
1. On Windows, run OpenCode (Desktop) with the `oh-my-opencode-slim` plugin declared in config.
2. Let it run / update the plugin a few times.
3. Inspect `%LOCALAPPDATA%\opencode\packages` — a new `.oh-my-opencode-slim@latest.staging-<rand>` dir appears per install attempt and is never removed.

issues.title: provider/streaming: reasoning degenerates into repetitive loop on long session
issues.body:
## Summary

In a long desktop session (heavy MCP tool usage while testing wincontrol desktop-control), the assistant's reasoning stream degenerated into a repetitive near-empty loop — dozens of consecutive lines of "好。", occasionally "我输出。", "(写)", "(执行)", "嗯。" — until the turn was abandoned. Possibly model-side behavior, but filing for triage since it coincided with compaction / MCP catalog changes in the session.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.18
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.26200 (win32 x64), OpenCode Desktop app
- Model: qwen3.8-flash (provider: alibaba-token-plan-cn, variant: xhigh)
- Active plugins: @prevalentware/opencode-goal-plugin, local handoff-on-compact plugin (fires on context compaction)

## Reproduction

1. Run a long session with many tool calls against an MCP server (wincontrol), including an MCP server restart / tool-catalog change mid-session.
2. Session grows long enough to trigger context compaction (handoff-on-compact plugin active).
3. On a subsequent turn, the reasoning part degenerates into a repetitive loop of "好。" and similar filler tokens, continuing indefinitely.

## Expected Behavior

Either coherent reasoning output, or the provider/stream erroring cleanly. Not an endless degenerate loop.

## Actual Behavior

The reasoning section rendered dozens of repeated short lines ("好。好。我输出。好。嗯。好。好。(写)好。好。...") in the desktop UI. Screenshot held by reporter; can attach on request.

## Additional Context

- Uncertain whether this is an opencode bug (streaming/retry/compaction handling) or purely provider/model degeneration; happy to provide session JSON / logs if maintainers can tell which layer it belongs to.
- The session also exhibited a separate transient issue (404 "Message not found" toast after revert + resubmit), filed separately.

issues.title: Free tier issues: read this first, then post your report here

labels.name: zen
labels.description: Relates to Zen

issues.body:
This is the **main issue for free tier problems**. If you see any of these, you're in the right place:

- `Free usage exceeded, subscribe to Go`
- `Free usage limit reached`
- `You've used today's free messages. They reset at ...` and the reset never happens
- `This version of OpenCode Desktop no longer supports free models`
- `OpenCode's free tier can only be used from within OpenCode`
- `OpenCode 1.18.0 or newer is required to use the free tier`

**Please comment here instead of opening a new issue.** We're closing duplicates and pointing them here so everything is in one place.

## 1. Make sure you're on the latest OpenCode v2

Most free tier reports come from **OpenCode v1** (versions `0.x` and `1.x`, for example Desktop or CLI `1.19.5`). v1 no longer supports free models and only gets fixes for critical bugs. Updating to v2 has fixed this for many people.

Check your version:

- **Terminal:** `opencode --version`
- **Desktop:** Settings → About

The latest v2 release is **2.2.1**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The v1 Desktop app's built-in updater keeps you on `1.x`. Download v2 manually from **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**.

### Desktop

Download v2 Desktop for macOS, Windows or Linux from **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**, or on macOS:

```sh
brew install --cask opencode-desktop
```

### Terminal (TUI / CLI)

All install options are listed at **https://opencode.ai/v2/docs**. The quickest on macOS and Linux:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash
```

Or use a package manager:

```sh
npm install -g @opencode/cli
bun install -g --trust @opencode/cli
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2
paru -S opencode-beta
```

v1 and v2 both use the `opencode` command. If you installed v1 with a package manager, remove it first, for example `npm uninstall -g opencode-ai`. Windows package managers (Chocolatey, Scoop) don't support v2. On Windows, use the Desktop app, npm, or a [standalone binary](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/).

### Useful docs

- [Install OpenCode v2](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/)
- [Migrate from v1](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1/)
- [Free models, limits and privacy](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/models/#free-models)
- [OpenCode Go](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go/)
- [Troubleshooting](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting/)

## 2. Other things to check

- **Free models only work inside OpenCode.** Other clients, proxies and direct API calls can't use them. Use a paid model or [Go](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go/) there instead.
- **Subscribed to Go but still seeing free limits?** Run `/connect`, sign in with **OpenCode Console** in your browser (make sure you authorize the workspace with your Go subscription, or choose **OpenCode Go** if you use a Go API key), then pick a Go model (`opencode-go/...`) with `/models` rather than a free model (`opencode/...-free`).
- **Hit the real daily limit?** Wait for the reset time shown, subscribe to [Go](https://opencode.ai/go), or connect another provider with `/connect`.

## 3. Still broken on the latest v2? Comment with:

- OpenCode version, and whether you use Desktop, TUI, CLI or web
- Operating system
- The free model you used
- The exact error message (a screenshot is fine)
- When it started and the reset time you were shown
- Whether you have Go or Console credits

> [!WARNING]
> Don't post email addresses, payment details or other account information here. This issue is public.

## 4. Still don't know what's going on?

If you're on the latest v2 and none of the above helps, or the problem is about your account, billing or Go subscription, email **help@anoma.ly** with the details from step 3. Billing and account issues can't be fixed in GitHub issues.

issues.title: providers: model overrides (limit, name, disabled, aliases) ignored for opencode/opencode-go
Prompt POSTed to session HTTP endpoint during config-reload window is persisted but excluded from assembled context; assistant re-emits previous reply byte-identically
issues.body:
### Description

Headless deployment (`opencode serve`, prompts delivered by HTTP POST to the session prompt endpoint from a local automation relay). A prompt POSTed while a configuration-reload wave was in progress was persisted to session storage (sequence number and timestamp assigned) but was not included in the context assembled for the model call. The assistant "reply" to it was a byte-identical duplicate of the reply given to the previous turn 40 minutes earlier. The caller received HTTP success with the wrong answer; nothing in the response or the log marked it as stale.

**Timeline (UTC; server log + session database)**

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 23:12:26 | Last normal turn completes (assistant reply A, seq 2241) |
| 23:12:49 | Session idle |
| 23:51:59–23:53:23 | Config-reload wave: burst of `configuration normalization diagnostic` WARN entries (80 log lines in this window) |
| 23:52:03.509 | Relay POSTs a new prompt to the session endpoint (logged) |
| 23:52:03.5xx | User message persisted (seq 2252); assistant message created same second (seq 2254) |
| — | seq 2254 text part: length 888, SHA-256 `99d2738f39eb9edb6042936b…` — identical to reply A |

**Evidence**

- Session database (`session_message`): user row seq 2252 and assistant row seq 2254, both at 23:52:03. No other turn between 23:12:49 and 23:52:03 — the session was idle, so a concurrent running turn cannot explain a reused response.
- SHA-256 of the seq 2254 text part equals the SHA-256 of the seq 2241 text part (the 23:12:26 reply): byte-identical duplicate, not a paraphrase.
- The POST timestamp falls inside the config-diagnostic burst. POSTs to the same endpoint outside reload windows, before and after, produced correct replies.
- Interpretation (the only one consistent with the above): the persisted prompt was not part of the context assembled for that model call, so the model re-answered the previous turn.

**Expected:** the POSTed prompt is included in the context assembled for the next model call, and the assistant answers the new prompt.

**Actual:** the prompt is persisted but skipped during context assembly. The assistant regenerates the previous reply byte-for-byte. The caller sees success carrying the wrong answer — a silent failure for headless/automated deployments; no error is surfaced anywhere, so callers must detect it themselves (e.g. by hashing consecutive replies).

### Plugins

None configured (no plugin entries in user config, no local plugin files) — the reload wave was pure config-file normalization.

### OpenCode version

v2.0.16 (npm `@opencode/cli`; upstream git tag `v2.0.16`, object sha `3a103fe0`)

### Steps to reproduce

Not yet reduced to a minimal script. Observed sequence:

1. `opencode serve` with a session that has at least one completed turn; let it go idle.
2. Trigger a config reload (rewrite the user config file).
3. Inside the reload window, POST a new prompt to the session prompt endpoint.
4. Observe: the user message is persisted with a sequence number; the assistant reply is identical to the previous turn's reply.

### Screenshot and/or share link

None — headless server deployment; the evidence above is taken from the server log and the session database.

### Operating System

Linux 7.2.5-3 x86_64 (Arch-based)

### Terminal

Not applicable — headless `opencode serve` bound to loopback; client is curl over loopback (shell: bash)

issues.title: desktop: file links send literal ellipsis (U+2026) to /api/fs/read and 404
issues.body:
## Summary

In the desktop app, clicking a file link whose displayed path is abbreviated with a
home-directory ellipsis (`…`) sends that abbreviated string **verbatim** to
`GET /api/fs/read/…`, so the request 404s. The real file exists and opens fine by its
full path. The ellipsis is `U+2026 HORIZONTAL ELLIPSIS` (`%E2%80%A6`), not `~`, and the
server does not expand it.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.15 (desktop app, `opencode-cli.version`); update to 2.0.18 staged
- OS: Windows_NT 10.0.26200 (win32 x64), Windows 11
- Terminal: Unavailable — OpenCode desktop app (Electron); `TERM=xterm-256color`, `TERM_PROGRAM` unset
- Shell: `C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe`
- Install/channel: latest — desktop installer (`@opencodedesktop`)
- Active plugins: none found in config (only an MCP `playwright` server configured)

## Reproduction

1. In a desktop session, have the assistant reference a file that lives **under the home
   directory but outside the project**, for example
   `C:\Users\<user>\.config\opencode\commands\grill-me.md`.
2. Click the file link in the chat.
3. The UI shows `Failed to load file` / `File not found`.
4. The server log shows the abridged path requested literally.

## Expected Behavior

The link opens the real file. Any home-prefix abbreviation or middle-truncation used for
display should be expanded back to the real absolute path before the `fs/read` request.

## Actual Behavior

The request path still contains the display ellipsis:

```text
GET /api/fs/read/%E2%80%A6/config/opencode/commands/grill-me.md   -> 404   (x2)
```

`%E2%80%A6` decodes to `…` (U+2026). The real path
`C:\Users\<user>\.config\opencode\commands\grill-me.md` exists (2041 bytes) and reads
successfully by full path, so only the link expansion is broken.

The same happens when the chat text itself used a shorthand ellipsis:

```text
GET /api/fs/read/%E2%80%A6/skills/engineering/prototype   -> 404   (x3)
```

## Additional Context

- The abbreviation seen in the UI is the home prefix (`C:\Users\<user>\.`) collapsed to
  `…/`; the click handler appears to use the *rendered* text as the path.
- Related but distinct: #50876 and #50881 cover **relative / basename** links resolving
  against `$HOME`; #50913 covers a URL-style path resolving to `C:\static`. This issue is
  specifically the literal `…` surviving into the request URL.
- Secondary symptom: the `skill` tool's supporting-file sample lists bare relative names
  (e.g. `SKILL.md`); clicking one requests `GET /api/fs/read/SKILL.md` -> 404, because the
  client has no base directory for the skill and does not resolve it against the skill
  root.
- Frequency: 100% reproducible on 2.0.15 across several clicks.
- Workaround: open the file from a terminal or editor instead of clicking the chat link.

### Description

Description
I am encountering repeated ECONNRESET errors when using a Custom Provider to connect to an OpenAI-compatible AI server. The error occurs during chat with the selected AI model and causes the response stream to terminate unexpectedly.

The app also seems unable to correctly detect or handle the custom provider endpoint. This does not appear to be a transient network issue because official providers (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic) work fine under the same network conditions.

Steps to Reproduce
Start an OpenAI-compatible server at http://<host>:<port>/v1 (e.g., vLLM, SGLang, Ollama, etc.).

Add a Custom Provider in the app with the server URL and model name.

Start a new chat session using this custom provider.

Send a chat request or upload files (without exceeding the model context limit).

After a few interactions, the response stops and the ECONNRESET error appears.

Repeat the same steps with an official provider to confirm the issue is specific to the custom provider.

Environment
OS: <e.g., Windows 11 / macOS 15 / Ubuntu 22.04>

App Version: <e.g., 1.18.25 or latest>

Terminal: <e.g., PowerShell / CMD / Bash / Zsh>

Custom Provider Type: <e.g., SGLang / vLLM / Ollama / OpenAI-compatible>

Model: <e.g., Qwen3.5-27B-FP8>

error={"error":{"code":"ECONNRESET","path":"http://<host>:<port>/v1/chat/completions","errno":0}}

Disabling reasoning-parser or reasoning features on the server side avoids the error, but this is not suitable for agentic use cases.

The problem seems to be in the transport/streaming client layer, possibly related to HTTP/2 or keep-alive connection handling.

issues.title: v1: repeated tool calls across assistant messages bypass doom_loop deny
issues.body:
### Description

In `v1`, identical tool calls across separate assistant messages bypass `doom_loop`, including an explicit session rule setting it to `deny`. The processor checks only the current assistant message, so a model issuing one tool per response never reaches the three-call threshold.

This is the maintained-client counterpart of the repeated-call problem in #45442. Open PR #53032 targets `dev` and its newer core implementation.

### OpenCode version

`v1` at `006d837c5022ea5278162307c04c78412cfae9f3` (1.19.5 source).

### Steps to reproduce

Use a local synthetic provider to return four identical tool calls in four assistant responses, followed by a terminal text response. Configure the session with an allowing general rule and `doom_loop: deny`.

Four identical failed edits still execute. A repeated shell command appending a marker in a disposable directory provides an observable execution count.

Expected: the existing permission gate applies on the third identical call across assistant messages. Deny must prevent that execution; allow must keep permitting it. A new user message resets the history, and `continue_loop_on_deny` retains its existing meaning.

### OS

macOS, arm64; bounded local-provider tests without paid API calls.

issues.title: snapshot: recover index contention without stale captures or stdin EPIPE
issues.body:
### Description

On the maintained `v1` branch, `Snapshot.track()` loses captures when another Git process briefly holds the shared snapshot index lock. Failed staging can also leave it returning the previous tree instead of reporting that the new files were not captured.

Retrying contention exposes a subprocess stdin failure: a child that exits before reading a small payload can emit an uncaught Node `EPIPE`. This reproduces through `AppProcess` without a snapshot or external lock holder.

### OpenCode version

`v1` at `006d837c5022ea5278162307c04c78412cfae9f3` (1.19.5 source), Bun 1.4.4.

### Steps to reproduce

In a disposable Git worktree, capture an initial snapshot, add a file, hold the snapshot index with a separate `git update-index --index-info` process, then call `Snapshot.track()`. Releasing the holder after 250 ms should allow capture; currently the operation does not recover.

A required Git clean filter that fails reproduces the stale-tree result after an initial successful snapshot. Separately, repeated `AppProcess.run` calls to a child that immediately exits 128, with a one-byte stdin payload, produce uncaught `EPIPE` errors.

Expected: bounded recovery from transient contention, no deletion of another process's lock, no successful capture result after failed staging, and ordinary subprocess exit/error reporting when a child closes stdin early.

### OS

macOS, arm64. Local synthetic reproductions; no user session database or installed runtime was modified.

issues.title: First prompt after start has no MCP tools: tool list does not wait for pending MCP connections
issues.body:
## Description

After `opencode serve` starts (or on `opencode run --standalone`), the **first prompt** sent for a directory is built without any MCP tools. From the second prompt on, the MCP tools are present.

As far as I can tell, the per-directory instance is booted lazily on first access and MCP servers connect in the background. Building the tool list (`MCP.tools()`) does not wait for connections that are still `pending` (unlike `callTool`), so the first request only contains built-in tools.

For `opencode run --standalone` this means a one-shot run **never** gets MCP tools, since there is no second prompt.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure one or more remote MCP servers (`type: remote`, `codemode: false`).
2. `opencode serve` (fresh start), then send the first prompt for a directory, or run `opencode run --standalone "..."`.
3. Inspect the request sent to the model: no MCP tools. `GET /api/mcp` right before the prompt shows the servers as `pending`.
4. Send a second prompt: MCP tools are included.

## Expected

The first prompt waits (with a timeout) for MCP servers that are still connecting, or the instance connects MCP eagerly on boot, so the first request gets the same tool set as later ones.

## Workaround

Poll `GET /api/mcp` (with `x-opencode-directory`) after start until no server is `pending`, then send the prompt. For `run`, start a private `opencode serve`, wait the same way, then `opencode run --server <url>`.

## Environment

- opencode 2.0.18 (Linux), `opencode serve --service` and `opencode run --standalone`
- Local model via an OpenAI-compatible provider
- Related but different: #45333 (V2 runner never includes MCP tools) and #38470 (MCP tools missing from sessions created via `POST /api/session`). Here the tools are missing only until MCP has finished connecting.

issues.title: ACP: first prompt can miss MCP tools supplied to session/new (2.0.18 / 2.0.22)
issues.body:
### Description

MCP tools supplied through ACP session/new can be absent from the first model-visible tool catalog, even after session/new has returned successfully. A later prompt in the same session sees them.

Reproduced on 2.0.18 and 2.0.22 on macOS arm64. Two independent 2.0.18 runs both showed: immediate prompt = tools absent; prompt after 500 ms = tools present. A diagnostic control that waits for actual tool registration makes the first prompt include them.

The diagnostic observer records tool registration and model context, then deliberately stops before provider dispatch. These observations do not require a model/API request. Native permissions were ask, with the test MCP namespace allowed.

Expected: the first prompt should use the tools supplied for that session without the ACP client needing an arbitrary sleep.

Suspected location in v2.0.22: packages/core/src/tool/mcp.ts debounces subsequent updates by 100 ms, but flush only awaits the initial registration. packages/core/src/session/context.ts then takes the tool snapshot. This appears to leave a readiness gap for MCP servers added by ACP; please confirm the diagnosis.

### Plugins

Custom diagnostic observer only; separate control adds a tool-readiness wait. No third-party plugin pack.

### OpenCode version

2.0.18 and 2.0.22

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start opencode acp with a clean runtime/config directory.
2. Complete ACP initialize.
3. Call session/new with an absolute cwd and a local stdio MCP server exposing two fixed tools. Allow this MCP namespace.
4. Wait for the successful session/new response, then immediately call session/prompt.
5. Inspect the model-visible tool catalog: the supplied MCP tools may be missing, while the registry logs show them arriving shortly afterward.
6. Send another prompt in the same session after 500 ms: the tools are now present.

Control: wait for the supplied tools to enter the registry before preparing the first prompt; the first context then includes them. This control is a diagnostic workaround, not an upstream fix.

### Screenshot and/or share link

_No response_

### Operating System

macOS, Darwin 27.0.0, Apple Silicon arm64

ACP stdio client launching opencode acp (not the TUI)

issues.title: desktop: browser pane launcher missing from side panel after update (gated on attached())
issues.body:
## Summary

On OpenCode Desktop 2.2.2 (Windows), the **Browser** entry disappeared from the session side panel's **+** (new tab) launcher after updating from 2.2.1. Only **Review**, **Terminal**, and **Open file** remain, and there is no launcher left that can open a browser pane for the first time.

The launcher is registered only when `attached(session)` is already `true`, so once the pane is not attached there is no path back to it through the UI.

## Environment

- opencode version: Desktop app `2.2.2` (bundled CLI `2.2.2`). A separate `opencode` on `PATH` reports `2.0.32`.
- OS: `Microsoft Windows [Version 10.0.26300.9550]` (win32 x64)
- Terminal: OpenCode Desktop (Electron app, `packaged: true`); `TERM=xterm-256color`, `TERM_PROGRAM` unset
- Shell: `C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe`
- Install/channel: OpenCode Desktop, channel `latest`, auto-updater, packaged build at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ai.opencode.desktop`
- Active plugins: `superpowers@git+https://github.com/obra/superpowers.git` (2ce8aa1), `rtk` (local `~/.config/opencode/plugins/rtk.ts`). MCP servers: `playwright`, `dev-workflow`, `clinic-helper`.

## Reproduction

1. On OpenCode Desktop 2.2.1, open a session and open the browser pane (or let it open from a `http://localhost:...` link in a message).
2. Update the app to 2.2.2 and restart. The main log records the server restart on the version change:
   ```text
   v2 CLI background service starting { reason: 'version-mismatch', previousVersion: '2.2.1' }
   ```
3. Open a session and click **+** in the session side panel to open the new-tab / launcher list.
4. Observe the launcher list.

## Expected Behavior

**Browser** appears in the side panel **+** launcher so the browser pane can be opened, as it did on 2.2.1.

## Actual Behavior

The launcher list only contains **Review**, **Terminal**, and **Open file**. There is no Browser entry, no browser tab, and no obvious way to open a browser pane from the UI.

## Additional Context

### Cause: the launcher is gated on `attached()`

`packages/gui-plugins/src/browser/renderer.tsx` registers the launcher only when the pane is already attached:

```tsx
ctx.add(MenuItem, (): MenuItem | undefined => {
  const view = sessions.current()
  const value = model()

  // Only once the desktop's pane answers.
  if (!view || !value?.available(view) || !value.attached(view)) return undefined

  // A launcher of the side panel's new tab view, between Review and Terminal.
  return {
    menu: "session.panel",
    id: "open",
    ...
  }
})
```

And `attached()` requires an existing registration or existing browser state — `packages/gui-plugins/src/browser/model.ts:358`:

```ts
const attached = (session: Session) => {
  const value = attachment(session)

  return value?.registration !== undefined || !!value?.browser
}
```

So the launcher is a function of "a browser pane is already attached", but its `run` is `open(session)` — the action that opens the browser pane in the first place. When the pane is not attached (fresh app start, server restart on update, or a failed registration), the launcher can never render, and the user has no launcher to attach it again. The **Open browser** command and its keybind still work, which confirms the pane itself is fine — only the discoverable entry point is gone.

### Contributing: the `unsupported` flag is sticky for the app's lifetime

`model.ts:225` sets a permanent per-server flag on a single failed registration, and nothing ever clears it:

```ts
change: (next, mirror, native) => {
  if (next.error === "browser.pane.unsupported") {
    setState("unsupported", ref.server.id, true)

    return close(id)
  }
```

`available()` then returns `false` forever (`model.ts:374`), which also disables the **Open browser** command:

```ts
const available = (session: SessionRef) =>
  !state.unsupported[session.server.id] && !!session.id && session.server.compatible && !layout.narrow()
```

`connection.ts:173` likewise latches `blocked = true` for `browser.pane.unsupported` **and** `browser.pane.replaced`, with no reset path. A server restart during an app update is exactly the situation where `browser.pane.replaced` can fire, after which the browser pane never comes back until the whole app is restarted.

### Workaround

- Command palette (`Ctrl+K`) → **Open browser**, or `Ctrl+Alt+B`. Once the pane opens, the launcher entry reappears for that session.
- Or fully quit and relaunch OpenCode Desktop, which resets the sticky `unsupported` state.

### Suggested fixes

1. Register the side-panel launcher on `available(session)` only, and let `run` perform the first attach (drop the `attached()` requirement), or keep the launcher visible but `enabled: false` until attached.
2. Clear `state.unsupported[server.id]` when the server reconnects, its version changes, or the pane's Ipc comes back, instead of latching it for the app's lifetime.

### Notes

- The browser pane itself is functional; this is a discoverability regression in the launcher, not a broken pane.
- `server.compatible` is `true` and `/api/info` reports `2.2.2` on the desktop's own server (`http://127.0.0.1:28894`), so this is not a version-mismatch gate.
- Unrelated but observed in the same session: the `playwright` MCP server exits with code 1 after a few minutes (`mcp transport error ... "MCP server process exited with code 1"`). Happy to file that separately if useful.

issues.title: desktop: question tool aborts with 'location shut down', owner decision controls never render
issues.body:
The `question` tool aborts with `Interaction cancelled because the location shut down` in the desktop app, making it impossible to collect a decision from the owner.

**Environment**
- Client: OpenCode desktop app (`ai.opencode.desktop`, bundle `/Applications/OpenCode.app`)
- Server: 2.0.16, pid 90359, `http://127.0.0.1:49374`
- CLI binary: 2.0.18
- macOS (darwin)

**Reproduction**
1. Run a session in the desktop app.
2. Call the `question` tool with any question and options.
3. Observe the tool result: `{"error":{"type":"aborted","message":"Interaction cancelled because the location shut down","content":[]}}`

The control never renders, so no answer can be given.

**Occurrences** — 2 consecutive, in the same session, with the server restarting between them:
- attempt 1, after the server had just restarted
- attempt 2, after a second server restart

**Impact**
Any workflow that relies on the `question` tool to present owner decision controls (Adopt/Adapt/Reject, A/B/C options) is unusable in the desktop app. The only fallback is plain prose in the assistant message, which loses the structured, nothing-pre-selected control that decision requests depend on.

**Suspected cause**
The abort message suggests the question's owning "location" is being torn down — plausibly a lifecycle/race issue between the question control's location and the desktop app's session or server lifecycle, rather than an owner cancellation. Note the two failures both coincided with a server restart, which may be relevant.

**Question**
Is this a known limitation of the desktop client, or a bug? If it is a race with server restart, it would be good to have it fail loudly (or retry) rather than silently aborting the interaction.

issues.title: compaction: after auto-compact, agent stops using top-level tools and reports it has none
issues.body:
## Summary

After an automatic context compaction, the agent in session
`ses_f16eb025affe3LdBxKli5Wz92x` never called a top-level tool again. It routed
all further work through code mode (`execute` -> `tools.shell`), which fails in
every session, concluded its tools were unregistered, and told the user
repeatedly — across four CLI restarts — that it had no usable tools.

## Environment

- opencode version: 2.0.18 (channel: latest)
- OS: Linux 7.2.7-zen1-1-zen (linux x64)
- Terminal: TERM_PROGRAM=tmux, TERM=tmux-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor
- Shell: /usr/bin/zsh
- Install/channel: release, latest
- Active plugins: none configured
- Session: `ses_f16eb025affe3LdBxKli5Wz92x`, agent `plan`,
  model `opencode/mimo-v2.6-flash-free`

## Reproduction

Not reliably reproducible — occurred once, in this session only. New sessions
were unaffected. Timeline (UTC, 2026-09-28):

1. Before 19:24:37 — 100+ direct `shell` calls, all successful; last successful
   ones at 19:24:34 and 19:24:36.
2. 19:24:37 — automatic compaction (`reason=auto`, `status=completed`).
3. 19:35:17 — first tool call after compaction: `execute` running
   `await tools.shell({...})` -> `Unknown tool 'shell'. Use search to find
   available tools.`
4. 19:35:20, 20:39:30, 20:41:14 — same failure, same path.
5. 19:35:32-19:37:33 — `search()` from inside `execute` returns only
   `tools.browser.*` and `tools.opencode.*`; `search({namespace:"tools"})`
   returns 0 items.
6. From 19:35 onward — no direct `shell`/`read`/`grep`/`glob` call is recorded
   in the session at all. Only `execute` and `skill`.
7. CLI restarts at 20:28:50, 20:41:02, 20:59:30, 21:08:19 (`--standalone`) did
   not change the behavior.

## Expected Behavior

Compaction summarizes context only. The agent's tool set and its ability to
call top-level `shell`/`read`/`grep` should be identical before and after.

## Actual Behavior

The agent's tool usage changed permanently at the compaction boundary: it
stopped issuing top-level tool calls entirely and only attempted shell through
the code-mode sandbox, where it fails by design. It then reported to the user,
repeatedly, that it had no tools it could use.

Session-provided tools were still being served — `skill` succeeded at 21:04:04
and `execute` at 21:09:24 — so the session was alive and the harness was
responding.

## Additional Context

- Two earlier compactions in the same session (18:21:22, 19:07:16) did not
  produce this; direct `shell` succeeded after both.
- No `config.updated` events on 2026-09-28 (last was 2026-09-25), so no config
  change preceded the failure.
- `opencode.log` contains no tool-resolution errors; last `spawning process` is
  19:24:37 UTC.
- Agent and model were unchanged across the compaction.
- Limitation: the session record stores calls, not the tool list presented to
  the model, and the agent never made a direct top-level tool call after the
  compaction. Whether top-level registration was actually lost, or the
  post-compaction context led it into the code-mode path and it never
  self-corrected, cannot be determined from persisted data alone.
- Separately reproducible: calling `tools.shell` inside `execute` fails with
  `Unknown tool 'shell'` in any session, healthy ones included, and the error's
  hint ("Use search to find available tools") is misleading because `search`
  never returns `shell`.

issues.title: read: varying out-of-range offsets evade doom-loop detection
issues.body:
### Description

Repeated reads beyond EOF evade `doom_loop` when the model changes the offset. Reads at offsets 636, 700 and 800 of the same unchanged 635-line file fail equivalently, but have different inputs. A valid read between those failures also prevents consecutive-call detection.

A bounded local fake-provider regression continues to another provider call instead of requesting the configured `doom_loop` permission. Expected: recognize equivalent range failures within one user turn, preserve explicit permission rules, and reset when the file changes.

Related: #45442 and #53032. This concerns varying invalid reads on maintained `v1`; that PR targets identical calls in the newer core.

### Plugins

None in the reproduction.

### OpenCode version

1.19.5 (`v1`, `006d837c5022ea5278162307c04c78412cfae9f3`)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a 635-line text fixture.
2. In one turn, use a local fake provider to request reads at offsets 700, 600, 900, 600 and 1100 (three failures interleaved with two valid reads).
3. Configure `doom_loop` to deny; queue those five tool responses followed by one terminal text response.
4. Observe that the third equivalent invalid read does not request `doom_loop`, so the loop makes a sixth provider call instead of stopping after five.

### Operating System

macOS arm64. Reproduced in the package tool and session test harnesses.

prs.title: refactor(ai): structured output via schema on generate, stream and loop
prs.body:
### Change

Structured output moves from a separate `generateObject` call to a `schema` option on `ai.generate`, `ai.stream` and `ai.loop`, in both the Promise and Effect clients. How it works doesn't change: the model still answers through the same forced hidden tool call on every protocol.

```ts
// Before
const { object } = await ai.generateObject({ model, prompt: "Pick a city", schema: City })

// After
const res = await ai.generate({ model, prompt: "Pick a city", schema: City })
res.object.city // typed from the schema
```

- `schema` takes an Effect Schema (typed `object`) or a raw JSON Schema object (`object: unknown`). The old `jsonSchema:` input is now `schema:`.
- The result is the normal `LLMResponse` plus `object`, so `res.response.*` becomes `res.*`.
- `stream`: the `finish` event carries `object`.
- `loop`: user tools run as usual. With tools present, the hidden tool is only `required`, not named, so the model can call user tools first. `loop` never runs the hidden tool itself. A step that calls it ends the loop, even if it also called other tools, and that step's `finish` carries `object`.
- Errors work as before: a missing call, the token limit or a decode failure is an `AIError` with the response in `partial`.
- `generateObject` is gone, along with its types, README section and tutorial step.

### Follow-up

- Native JSON modes (OpenAI `json_schema`, Gemini response schema, Anthropic output format) where the protocol supports them.
- Streaming partial objects.

### Verification

- `bun run test` in `packages/ai`: 2003 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun typecheck` and `typecheck:tsc` pass in `packages/ai` and `packages/core`.
- `bun run check` from the root passes.

prs.title: fix(core): scan zsh q flags without exponential backtracking
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Fixes #60721

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`ZSH_SAFE_FLAGS_RE` in `packages/core/src/shell/scan.ts` matched `q` twice: once in the flag character class and once through `q[-+]?`. Inside the `(...)*` repetition a run of `q` then has two parses per character, so rejecting `${(qqqq…!x}` backtracks exponentially — 28 `q` took ~4 s here, 40 `q` effectively hangs.

A bare `q` now matches only through the character class; the alternative is `q[-+]` for the two-character forms. The accepted language is unchanged: `q`, `q-` and `q+` still parse, everything else still fails. I verified the old and new regex agree on `${(q)`, `${(q-)`, `${(q+)`, `${(qqq)`, `${(q-q+)`, `${(Aq)` and non-matches like the pathological input above, and the new one rejects 28 `q` in ~10 ms instead of ~4 s.

The regression test scans 40 `q` with and without a closing `)` — on `dev` the first case does not finish in reasonable time.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun test test/shell-scan/` in `packages/core`: 3185 pass, 5 skip, 1 fail — the failure (`real-shell compound syntax`, a bash case) also fails on a clean `dev` checkout, unrelated to this change.
- `bun run typecheck` in `packages/core`: no errors.
- `oxlint` on the whole repo: clean.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: feat(ai): accept "provider/model" strings as models
prs.body:
I made `model` accept a `"provider/model"` string anywhere a text, image, or decision model is accepted, in both the Promise and Effect APIs. A model object still works for anything that needs settings.

```ts
await ai.generate({ model: "openai/gpt-5.4", prompt: "Hi" })
await ai.generate({ model: OpenAI.model("gpt-5.4", { baseURL }), prompt: "Hi" })
```

The text before the first `/` picks the provider and the rest is the model id, so `openrouter/openai/gpt-5.4` sends `openai/gpt-5.4` to OpenRouter. The string loads that provider's default `model`, `imageModel` or `decisionModel` with its env key and no settings. Each provider module is imported only when a string names it, inside the Effect, so failures are a typed `AIError`:

- unknown provider or no `/`: lists the known ids
- provider without that kind of model: `Provider "anthropic" has no image models`
- provider that needs settings, such as `azure/...`: the provider's own error (`requires resourceName or baseURL`)

Provider options for a string model are untyped. `ai.request` still needs a model object because it builds the request synchronously, and so does `compact`, which takes a built request. This is a stopgap until strings resolve through a bundled catalog.

Accepted ids are each provider module's `id`, plus these models.dev ids where ours differ:

| models.dev id | provider |
| --- | --- |
| `fireworks-ai` | `fireworks` |
| `vercel` | `vercel-ai-gateway` |
| `google-vertex-anthropic` | `google-vertex` (Messages API) |
