prs.title: fix(core): release location holders on shutdown
prs.body:
Part of https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/51003 and https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/52965. Related: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/50363, https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/51249, https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/37844, https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/58795

### Problem

`invalidate` (idle eviction, `opencode reload`, `vcs.init`, debug evict) drops a location from the cache, but the `RcMap` only closes it once nobody holds it. An open PTY websocket or a client-hosted MCP socket holds it for as long as it stays open, so the whole old location keeps running: MCP servers, watchers, shells. The next request boots a fresh location with its own set, so you end up with duplicate MCP server sets.

Running steps already handle this by checking `lifecycle.isClosed()` at step boundaries. Sockets never did.

### Change

```diff
 invalidate(location)
   drop from cache
   lifecycle.shutdown
+    -> awaitShutdown resolves
+       PTY / client MCP socket closes with 1012, client MCP reconnects to the new location
+       last holder gone -> location scope closes -> MCP servers, watchers, shells stop
+  still held after 30s: warn "location still held after shutdown"

 idle sweep
-  evict if no running session or job
+  evict if no running session or job, and no open PTY or client MCP socket
```

- `LocationLifecycle` gets `awaitShutdown` plus `retain`/`isRetained`. One server helper, `holdLocation`, does both for the PTY and client MCP sockets.
- The idle sweep skips retained locations. For a PTY, eviction would kill the shell. For client MCP, `connectClientMcp` reconnects within 500ms, so evicting would just boot a fresh location (and its MCP servers) right away.
- The 30s warning timer is forked into the held location's scope, so it stops as soon as the last holder lets go instead of hanging around.
- Explicit invalidations (reload, `vcs.init`, debug evict) still end location PTYs on purpose. The PTY service belongs to the location, so keeping the shell means keeping the stale location, which is the leak this fixes. The TUI and app terminals use the persistent PTY daemon (`/api/experimental/persistent-pty`), which isn't tied to a location, so they're unaffected. Only direct `/api/pty` users see the 1012 close, and reconnecting to the old PTY ID gets a 404.

### Verification

- `packages/core`: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run typecheck:tsc`, `bun run script/test.ts` on the location, mcp, pty and browser-idle tests: 200 pass.
- `packages/server`: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run typecheck:tsc`, `bun test`: 117 pass. `packages/client` `bun test test/mcp.test.ts`: 4 pass. Root `bun run check` passes.
- New tests, each fails on `dev`, and passes 5/5 with `--rerun-each 5`:
  - `core/test/location-retain.test.ts`: the idle sweep evicts an idle sibling but keeps a retained location, then evicts it once released.
  - `core/test/location-layer.test.ts`: warns when a borrower still holds an invalidated location after 30s, stays quiet when it lets go on shutdown.
  - `server/test/pty-transport.test.ts`: a held PTY socket gets 1012 on reload and the old shell process exits.
  - `server/test/client-mcp.test.ts`: a real `connectClientMcp` client gets 1012 on reload, the old location closes, and the client reattaches to the new one.
- Manual run on a local `serve` (isolated XDG dirs) with one stdio MCP server, a PTY socket and a client MCP socket on the same directory:
  - `dev`, after reload: 2 MCP processes, old shell still alive, sockets still on the old location
  - this branch, after reload: both sockets closed with 1012, client MCP reattached, 1 MCP process, old shell gone
  - this branch, after debug evict: client MCP closed with 1012 and reattached, 1 MCP process, no "still held" warnings

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="9">
  <style>
    .old{animation:old 4s ease-in-out infinite}
    .new{animation:new 4s ease-in-out infinite}
    .sock{animation:sock 4s ease-in-out infinite}
    @keyframes old{0%,40%{opacity:1}60%,100%{opacity:.12}}
```

prs.body: ### Issue for this PR Fixes #60772 ### Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [ ] Refactor / code improvement - [ ] Documentation ### What does this PR do? **Problem** On Windows, after maximizing and dragging the title bar, the console can end up with an inverted window: `srWindow.Left` is past `Right`. The width is negative, so the TUI draws nothing and the screen stays black. We don't know why conhost does this. The negative width reaches OpenTUI as a huge number: ``` width = Right - Left + 1 = -29 Bun: process.stdout.columns = 2^64 - 29 (prints as 18446744073709552000) ``` OpenTUI only checks `width > 0`, so the bad value passes and reaches the native renderer, which throws: ``` RangeError: Session renderer width exceeds native u32 length limit ``` **Fix** - On Windows, check the console viewport every 500 ms. - If it is inverted, restore it. On the alternate screen, if that does not work, restart the renderer with its own `suspend()` and `resume()`, which re-enters the alternate screen and repaints. - Once the viewport is valid, resize the renderer if the size changed, or restart it to repaint. - Drop bogus sizes before they reach OpenTUI. Non-Windows platforms and the Node build see no change in practice: the repair never runs there, and bogus sizes never occur. ### Notes for reviewers - The guard wraps `requestResize` only to drop bogus sizes, and it reads no private OpenTUI state. The proper fix belongs in OpenTUI, see anomalyco/opentui#1738. - Recovery uses `suspend()` and `resume()`, the same calls the external editor makes. `resume()` repaints everything. - The restart change is not yet tested on Windows. The alternate-screen case needs a live check. - Tested on conhost only. #60772 was reported in Windows Terminal, and that has not been tested. ### How did you verify your code works? - `bun test test/terminal-size-renderer.test.ts` in `packages/tui`: 3 pass. The tests use OpenTUI's `ManualClock` and spy on `suspend()` and `resume()`, so they don't sleep or touch the terminal. - `a bogus resize reading never reaches the native renderer` fails without the guard (`exceeds native u32 length limit`). - `a viewport the repair cannot fix restarts the renderer on the alternate screen` and `a viewport that recovers at the current size restarts the renderer once` fail without the guard. - `bun run typecheck` in `packages/tui`: clean. - `bun run check` from the repo root: passes. - Manual test on Windows 10 with conhost, on commit d5788ee: maximize, then drag the title bar. Before: black screen. After: screen redraws. - Not yet run on Windows for the restart change in f7d8e3c. ### Screenshots / recordings ### Checklist - [x] I have tested my changes locally - [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR --- _Added by the opencode bot (AI-generated)._ Related: #51167 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: fix(ai): handle stream errors without messages
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #60760

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

An OpenAI-compatible stream event can carry an `error` object without a `message`. The schema rejects such an event before the provider error handler runs, so the request fails with a stream validation error instead of the provider's failure.

Accept a missing or null `message`. When it is absent, the serialized `error` object becomes the message shown to the user. The raw body still goes to classification, so neither the fallback message nor the missing field changes how the failure is classified.

Kept to the fix this issue needs: no nested `errors[0]` extraction, no new `ProviderFailure` field. A readable message for nested provider errors is a separate change, where the extraction can reuse `providerErrorMessage`.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Added one regression test: an error event without `message` now surfaces as `ProviderInternal` with the serialized error object as its message, and the raw body keeps the original payload.

### What's new

A native trading dashboard driven by a real IBKR engine (verified live against a TWS demo account):

- **Trading panel** with the system pool: per-system run/pause, PID display, P/L, and position
  feed. The panel's dedicated chat session is excluded from the home history.
- **Trading engine (`core`)** with accounts, systems and tasks over SQLite, speaking to TWS
  (`@stoqey/ib`). Runs as children of the sidecar server, so a closed window does not kill them.
- **Experimental endpoints** (`experimental.trading.*`) with the generated Effect SDK
  (`snapshot`, system activate/pause, position close/closeAll, task list/add/cancel).
- **TUI palette panel** for the same pool.
- **Desktop-native close warning**: closing an app window while a bot is running stops on a
  native dialog first (bots keep trading headless behind the window otherwise). The guard lives
  in main — the sidecar credential is not exposed to the renderer — and answers quickly
  (1.5 s timeout) so a stalled engine can never block a close.
- First-open performance: the panel session resolves instantly via pointer-first chat boot,
  lazy route mount and an idle preload in the desktop shell.

prs.title: perf(core): rebuild providers on account switch only when a plugin's state changed
prs.body:
## Problem

On `Credential.Event.Switched`, five provider plugins re-ran their `load()` and then always called `ctx.provider.reload()`, which rebuilds the Location's whole provider and model catalog. Switching between two OpenAI API keys, for example, rebuilt every Location's providers even though nothing the OpenAI plugin applies had changed. Since https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59084 an identical rebuild publishes no events, so this is wasted CPU only.

## Change

Each `load()` now reports whether the state its transforms read changed, and the switch handler reloads only then. This follows the plugins migrated in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60082.

| Plugin | Compared |
| --- | --- |
| `openai` | whether a ChatGPT login is active, and its `accountID` |
| `chatgpt` | the token-sharing source connection (`Equal.equals`) |
| `gitlab` | discovered workflow models and their connection (`Equal.equals`) |
| `snowflake-cortex` | the normalized account |
| `openai-context-caps` | `signedIn` |

```diff
- load().pipe(Effect.andThen(ctx.provider.reload()))
+ load().pipe(Effect.flatMap((changed) => (changed ? ctx.provider.reload() : Effect.void)))
```

Session hooks read the same state at request time, so they are unaffected. GitLab's credential-derived `instanceUrl` setting already reloads on its own change through `credentialSettings`.

I added a test that switching between two OpenAI API keys does not rebuild providers, and switching to a ChatGPT login does.

prs.title: test(core): check models.dev entrypoints against native providers
prs.body:
Nothing in this PR deletes a subpath. Every duplicate `@opencode/ai/providers/*` path is still referenced by models.dev, by Core, or by both, so removing any of them would break saved configs or catalog entries. The PR only adds a test that protects this contract.

### The contract

- **models.dev**: each model API's `sdk.opencodeai` names a package entry point.
- **Core** loads that name through the `builtins` map in `packages/core/src/provider.ts`. Names missing from the map are skipped as unknown (`loadable()` in `models-dev.ts`). `variant.ts`, `aisdk-native.ts` and `plugin/verbosity.ts` also key on these paths.
- **The published package**: users' configs (`package: "..."`) and other apps import these paths directly.

An existing test already checks that the builtins map matches every package export that has a `model()`. The new test closes the remaining gap. Every `@opencode/ai/*` value in the bundled snapshot (`packages/core/src/models-dev/snapshot.txt`) must be a real package export and a loadable builtin. The only exception is an explicit list of protocol-only entry points.

### Duplicate paths

| Path | Same as | References found | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `providers/openai-compatible-responses` | `providers/openai-compatible/responses` | models.dev: 0. Core: `provider.ts` loader, `variant.ts`, and a `provider.test.ts` test that pins it for existing configs. ai tests import the source file. | kept |
| `providers/openai-compatible/responses` | ↑ | models.dev: 783. Core loader and `variant.ts`, README, www docs | kept |
| `providers/google-vertex-messages` | `providers/google-vertex/messages` | models.dev: 0. Core: `provider.ts` loader, `variant.ts`, and the same config test. `auth-options.types.ts` | kept |
| `providers/google-vertex/messages` | ↑ | models.dev: 18. Core loader, `variant.ts`, `models-dev.ts`, `aisdk-native.ts` (`@ai-sdk/google-vertex/anthropic` maps here), README, docs | kept |
| `providers/amazon-bedrock/mantle` | `providers/amazon-bedrock/mantle/responses` | models.dev: 0. Core: `aisdk-native.ts` returns it as a rewrite target. Also the loader, `variant.ts`, and tests | kept |
| `providers/amazon-bedrock/mantle/responses` | ↑ | models.dev: 17. Core loader, `variant.ts`, `plugin/verbosity.ts`, docs | kept |

Several `<provider>/chat`, `/responses` and `/messages` subpaths re-export the root's `model`: `alibaba/chat`, `moonshot/chat`, `minimax/messages`, `zai/chat`, `zai-coding-plan/chat`, `meta/responses`, `openai/responses` and `google-vertex/gemini`. These are not module duplicates, because each root is the provider's full module with more exports. models.dev uses every one of these subpaths, and Core loads every root. All are kept.

### Gap this surfaced

The snapshot points `openai/gpt-6-luna`'s `decisions` API at `@opencode/ai/protocols/openai-decisions`. That entry point has no `model()`, so Core skips that API. The test lists it explicitly. Any new non-loadable value fails the test until someone decides how to handle it. Current models.dev data also names `protocols/openai-speech`, `openai-transcription`, `google-speech` and similar paths. These will hit the same check when the snapshot is next refreshed.

### Verification

- The test fails when a snapshot-referenced export is removed. I checked this by temporarily dropping `providers/zai/chat`.
- `bun run check` passes. `bun typecheck` and `typecheck:tsc` pass in `packages/ai` and `packages/core`.

## Problem

`packages/cli/test/flag.test.ts` fails on `dev` in both "keeps the first of repeated flags" cases, which breaks CI on unrelated PRs.

The test came in with https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60712, whose CI ran against effect 4.0. The effect 4.1.0 upgrade in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60651 landed just before it and changed how repeated single-value flags parse:

```diff
  --model a --model b
- effect 4.0: model = "a"
+ effect 4.1: error, "2 occurrences, expected at most 1 value"
```

## Change

The test says `--worktree` should match every other single-value flag. Under effect 4.1 every other single-value flag rejects repeats, so I updated the expectation to match, and added the `--model a --model b` case so the comparison is checked directly. No source changes; the optional-value parsing from https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60712 is unchanged and its tests still pass.

## Out of scope

Whether repeated flags should be allowed again across the CLI. That would be a framework-level choice, not something to special-case for `--worktree`.

prs.title: docs: document the Windows Terminal ctrl+tab caveat
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Refs #55606

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [x] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`session.tab.next` and `session.tab.previous` default to `ctrl+tab` and `ctrl+shift+tab`. On a default Windows Terminal neither key ever reaches OpenCode, so the advertised default silently does nothing.

The cause is in the terminal, not in the TUI. Windows Terminal binds `ctrl+tab` and `ctrl+shift+tab` to its own `Terminal.NextTab` and `Terminal.PrevTab` actions, and a terminal key binding consumes the key before the client application sees it.

I measured this on Windows Terminal 1.24.12741 with a probe process that logged every byte the terminal delivered. Same terminal, same run, `ctrl+tab` / `ctrl+shift+tab` / `tab`:

| encoding | `ctrl+tab` | `ctrl+shift+tab` | `tab` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| default, no unbind | *(nothing)* | *(nothing)* | `0x09` |
| `ctrl+tab` unbound, legacy | `0x09` | `ESC [ Z` | `0x09` |
| `ctrl+tab` unbound, kitty requested | `0x09` | `ESC [ Z` | `0x09` |
| `ctrl+tab` unbound, `win32-input-mode` | `CSI 9 ; 15 ; 0 ; 1 ; 40 ; 1 _` | `CSI 9 ; 15 ; 0 ; 1 ; 56 ; 1 _` | `CSI 9 ; 1 ; 9 ; 1 ; 32 ; 1 _` |

Three things fall out of that:

- While the terminal holds the binding, the key never arrives at all.
- Unbinding it is not enough on its own. Windows Terminal ignores the kitty keyboard protocol, so the terminal keeps sending the legacy encoding, where `ctrl+tab` is the same byte as `tab` and `ctrl+shift+tab` is a plain `shift+tab`. The Ctrl is gone either way.
- The only encoding that carries the modifier is `win32-input-mode`, and the `win32-input-mode` row is the one where the key-down arrives at all.

`alt+down` and `alt+up` are not reserved by the terminal and do arrive: they come through as `CSI 1 ; 3 B` and `CSI 1 ; 3 A`, which the parser reads as `down` and `up` with the alt modifier.

This PR adds a `### Windows Terminal` subsection under `## Sessions` in `services/www/src/docs/content/cli/keybinds.mdx`, next to the table that lists the session tab bindings. It says that the terminal reserves `ctrl+tab` and `ctrl+shift+tab`, points at `alt+down` and `alt+up` as the ones that work, and explains that unbinding the terminal's binding only helps once `win32-input-mode` is on.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Measured the terminal behaviour rather than inferring it, with a probe process inside Windows Terminal 1.24 that logs every byte the terminal delivers. The comparison that carries the argument is the one in the same run: a key the terminal binds, against one it does not, in each of the three encodings.
- For the rows that need the terminal's binding released, the probe added `{ "command": "unbound", "keys": "ctrl+tab" }` to the `actions` array of the terminal's `settings.json`, took a byte-exact backup first, and restored the file afterwards.
- Fed the exact bytes Windows Terminal sends for `alt+down` and `alt+up` (`CSI 1 ; 3 B` and `CSI 1 ; 3 A`) through the TUI's key parser and confirmed they resolve to `down` and `up` with the alt modifier set, so the alternative the new subsection points at is one that actually works.
- Checked the `settings.json` shape against the Windows Terminal documentation: `keybindings` was replaced by `actions` in version 1.4, and `"unbound"` is the value that releases a default binding.
- Ran `bun typecheck` and `bun run check:generated` from `services/www`: 0 errors, 0 warnings and 0 hints over the 34 Astro files, and the generated-output check passes.
- Built the documentation site with `bun run build` from `services/www`.

### Screenshots / recordings

Not a UI change.

### Checklist

- [x] I have tested my changes locally
- [x] I have not included unrelated changes in this PR

prs.title: fix(core): wait briefly for starting MCP servers before a model call
prs.body:
The first model call after startup, or right after an MCP server is added or reconnected, gets built without that server's tools, since servers connect in the background and the tool list doesn't wait. `opencode run` one-shots never see MCP tools at all. And even after a server says `connected`, its tools only reach the registry about 100ms later through the debounced reload, so waiting on status alone isn't enough.

Fixes https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/51812

I changed `McpTool.flush`, which `SessionContext.select` already calls before building the tool list:

```diff
 flush:
   await initial registration
+  for each server still connecting (in parallel):
+    wait until it settles, or until 2s after its attempt started
+  if registry tools != current MCP catalog:
+    reconcile now instead of waiting for the debounce
```

Each server's 2s window starts when its connection attempt starts (initial boot, add, connect, reconnect, credential reconnect), so a server that has been hanging for a while never makes a prompt wait, and a second call after the window is free.

`tools()` used to wait for every server's startup with no cap, and https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/48937 removed that because one slow or hung server blocked every prompt. This wait is capped per server and only happens on the session's model call path, so Location and MCP boot stay async and a hung server costs at most 2s once.


---

Fixes #53299

prs.title: perf(core): ignore credential events for unrelated integrations
prs.body:
## Problem

Every Location runs two listeners that wake up on any credential event for any integration:

- `credentialSettings` (Bedrock, both Cloudflare plugins, GitLab) re-reads its integration's active credential on every `credential.updated` and `credential.switched`, even when the event is about some other integration. That's 4 listeners doing a list plus a get each, per Location, per event.
- `Provider` runs `notify` (snapshot plus `integrations.list()`, which reads every credential) on every `credential.updated`, even though that event can't change which providers are available.

## Change

`credential.updated` is only published for a create, a label rename or a remove. Any of those that changes the active credential also publishes `credential.switched`. So `updated` alone never changes the active credential's value, and never takes an integration from zero connections to some or back.

```diff
 credentialSettings
-  subscribe([Credential.Updated, Credential.Switched])
+  subscribe(Credential.Switched)
+  filter(event.integrationID === integrationID)

 Provider
-  subscribe([Integration.Updated, Credential.Updated, Credential.Switched])
+  subscribe([Integration.Updated, Credential.Switched])
```

What that buys per Location:

| event | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| add/switch/remove a credential for an unrelated integration | 4 settings reloads (x2 when `updated` also fires) | 0 |
| credential add or active remove | 2 provider notifies | 1 |
| label rename, inactive add or remove | 1 provider notify, 4 settings reloads | nothing |

I added a test that a Cloudflare Workers AI form login switch still updates the account ID, so the filter doesn't drop its own integration's events.

## Out of scope

- `Provider` still reacts to every `credential.switched`, including integrations it has no provider for. Filtering that would mean checking the provider records on each event, and the switch is rare enough that I left it.
- `google-vertex.ts` and `config/plugin/policy.ts` have the same unfiltered subscription shape.

prs.title: fix(vscode): emit V2 mention syntax (@path#37-42) instead of V1 #L prefix
prs.body:
## Problem

The VS Code SDK's "File Reference Shortcuts" feature (`Cmd+Option+K`) inserts at-mentions like `@path#L37-42` for selections. That `#L` prefix is **V1 syntax**. The V2 TUI expects `@path#37-42` — no `L`.

Evidence, from this repo's own source: `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/autocomplete.tsx` (line ~269) renders the mention as

```ts
`${item.path}#${lineRange.startLine}${lineRange.endLine ? `-${lineRange.endLine}` : ""}`
```

prs.title: perf(core): check MCP tools ourselves and skip the SDK tool cache
prs.body:
MCP tool listing did a lot of work we didn't need. The SDK zod-checked every listed tool (on legacy that walks every property schema), we checked each tool again with the SDK codec to skip bad ones, and the SDK cached the whole list as a JSON string that it parsed again on the first tools/call to compile an output validator for every tool. This PR folds in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60761.

What I changed:

- SDK patch: tools/list items are `z.array(z.unknown())` in the legacy, modern wire and modern lifted result schemas (mjs and cjs). The rest of the result is still checked. The SDK's modern header exclusion now reads `tool?.inputSchema` so a `null` entry can't throw.
- Our check lives in `connection.tools()`. Each listed item is skipped with one warning if it isn't an object, has no non-empty string `name`, has no object `inputSchema`, or has an `inputSchema.type` other than `"object"`. Everything else becomes a new tool: `name`, `title` and `description` if they are strings, `outputSchema`, `annotations`, `execution` and `_meta` if they are objects (kept by reference), and `inputSchema` with `type: "object"`, plus `properties`/`required` only when they are an object / string array. A field of the wrong type is left out and the tool stays. `icons` is dropped. Nested property schemas are left as sent. The server's objects are not mutated.
- Tool lists use `cacheMode: "bypass"` (prompt and resource lists still use the SDK cache), and each `callTool` passes our checked tool as `toolDefinition`, so the SDK compiles only that tool's output validator and modern `Mcp-Param-*` headers come from our copy. A tool we haven't listed gets a bare `{ name, inputSchema: { type: "object" } }` definition, so the SDK never lists and caches raw tools on its own. If a modern server answers HeaderMismatch (-32020), I relist through `connection.tools()` and retry once with the fresh definition.

```diff
- transport.onmessage: per-tool SDK codec check, mutate the message
+ tools(): client.listTools({ cacheMode: "bypass" })
+   result.tools.flatMap(tool => unusable ? (warn, []) : [{ name, title, description, inputSchema, outputSchema, annotations, execution, _meta }])
+   listed = Map(name -> tool)
  callTool(input):
+   client.callTool(params, { toolDefinition: listed.get(name) ?? { name, inputSchema: { type: "object" } } })
+     on -32020 (modern only): tools() then call again once
```

Paths I checked for raw tools reaching the SDK or a provider:
- initial list, list_changed refresh, attached servers and pagination all go through `connection.tools()`; the SDK only walks pages (`JSON.stringify` cycle check) and runs its header exclusion on raw items before that
- `callTool` output validation and modern header mirroring read our `toolDefinition`, never the SDK cache
- HeaderMismatch retry relists through our path, and since a definition is always passed the SDK's own relist (which caches the raw list and compiles every output schema) never runs
- a malformed `outputSchema` is dropped, so it can't make the call fail at compile time

Behavior changes:
- A tool with a malformed top-level `required` (like `required: "text"`) now loads in both eras without that field. Before it loaded only on modern, and kept the bad `required`.
- A tool with a bad optional field is kept without that field instead of being skipped.
- `icons` is no longer on listed tools. Nothing in opencode read it.
- Tool list TTLs: dev never relisted an expired list before a call either. `callTool` read the cached list without a freshness check (SDK `dist/index.mjs` 2260-2276, 2299-2316, 3905), and a `listTools` call was served from cache only inside a modern server's `ttlMs` (legacy defaults to 0, so never), while list_changed evicted the entry first (4108-4111). The only difference now is that a `tools()` call inside that window refetches, and opencode only calls it on connect, reconnect, list_changed and a stale header declaration.

| Catalog, era | tools/list CPU, dev → this PR | First tools/call CPU, dev → this PR | Heap per connection after list + call |
|---|---|---|---|
| 296 tools, legacy | 6.7 → 1.6 ms | 45.8 → 0.3 ms | 3.58 → 1.82 MiB |
| 296 tools, modern | 2.6 → 2.2 ms | 47.9 → 0.3 ms | 5.15 → 1.83 MiB |
| Cloudflare 3,763 tools, legacy | 17.0 → 6.2 ms | 2.7 → 0.3 ms | 8.25 → 4.13 MiB |
| Cloudflare 3,763 tools, modern | 10.1 → 7.4 ms | 6.7 → 0.4 ms | 12.12 → 4.14 MiB |

tools/list CPU is one in-process `listTools()`; the call and heap columns are the real `McpClient.connect` over stdio with 20 connections.

prs.title: chore: upgrade effect to 4.1.0 and fix a SQLite lock-up on interrupt
prs.body:
**Effect is upgraded to 4.1.0, and stopping a database write at the wrong moment can no longer lock every later database call forever.**
SQLite has one connection, guarded by a single permit. If a queued transaction was interrupted between taking the permit and registering its release, the permit leaked and every later query waited forever. Effect fixed this upstream ([Effect-TS/effect@2cb498e](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/commit/2cb498e0795ecabc491689cb298db966da24c8e7)); our two SQLite clients (Bun and workerd) copied the old code, so they get the same fix here.

❌ **Before**
1. A transaction waits for the connection's only permit.
2. It gets the permit, then registers "give it back when done" as a second step.
3. ❌ An interrupt landing between those two steps skips the release. The permit is gone and the database hangs.

✅ **After**
1. A transaction waits for the permit.
2. Taking the permit and registering its release happen as one step that can't be split (`Semaphore.takeScoped`, new in Effect 4.1).
3. An interrupt either lands before the take or after the release is registered. The permit always comes back.

```diff
- restore(take(1)) -> then addFinalizer(release(1))   // interruptible gap in between
+ restore(takeScoped(1))                              // take + finalizer, atomic
```

📊 **Proof**: interrupt a queued transaction at each of 31 timings, then check that the next query runs

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Bun client, `withTransaction` | ❌ 1/31 timings lock the DB | ✅ 0/31 |
| Bun client, `reserve` | ❌ 1/31 | ✅ 0/31 |
| workerd client, `reserve` | ❌ 1/31 | ✅ 0/31 |

The new `sqlite-interrupt.test.ts` fails all 3 cases without the fix and passes with it. The holder fiber keeps the connection across two yields, so the interrupted fiber is really parked in the permit's waiter queue. A 4th case covers workerd's `withTransaction`, which passes before and after (it was already safe through `withPermits`).

**What else the upgrade needed**
- `FileSystem.readDirectoryEntries` is now built into Effect and clashed with our own helper, so the helper is removed. Callers use Effect's entry types (`"File"`, `"Directory"`, `"SymbolicLink"`, …), with the same no-follow behavior.
- Command args and env can now be redacted values. Our cross-platform spawner now unwraps them, drops `undefined` env keys, hides redacted args in spawn errors, and supports the new `duplex` extra fds, all matching Effect's own Node spawner. It also ports two of that spawner's guards: an arg or env value containing a NUL byte fails with a typed `BadArgument` before spawning (and the redacted value never appears in the error), and a write error on stdin or a duplex fd surfaces as a stream failure instead of an uncaught error. Each has a test that failed first (a defect, and a 30s hang).
- Effect 4.1 rejects `Schema.Record` values whose encoded side is optional. The app's saved-state records wrap entries in a fallback that has one, so the web app failed at load. Record entries now decode from `unknown` through the new `Persistence.entry` and keep their per-entry recovery (bad entries still fall back or get dropped, as before). The persistence README no longer suggests `Persistence.optional` for record values.
- The recorded AI provider tests used the removed `NodeSocket.layerWebSocketConstructorWS`. They now use `NodeWS.layerWebSocketConstructor`.
- Small type fixes: the Node WebSocket import moved, an `Exit` needs narrowing before reading `.cause`, and request methods are now plain strings in the HTTP recorder.
- Free win, not measured on OpenCode: `Effect.fn` no longer leaks memory per call ([Effect-TS/effect#9878](https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/9878)).

**SDK consumers:** the generated client SDK has no diff. The paths and operation IDs in `openapi.json` don't change, and every request and response body refers to the same schemas as before. What does change:
- **Query parameters, 86 of 169 operations:** optional ones are now plain types, not `anyOf [T, null]`. Three of them now inline a type they used to reference: `Artifact.ProviderIDEncoded`, `Event.SeqEncoded` and `PersistentPty.ReadLinesEncoded`.
- **New schemas, 362 → 488:** JSON-encoded string fields such as SSE event payloads now declare their decoded shape with `contentSchema`. That adds component schemas like `V2Event` and `Event.ID`.
- **Event stream copies:** Effect 4.1 reaches some schemas twice, once through the REST JSON codec and once through the event stream, and names the second copy `<Name>_1`. `openapi-stabilize.ts` now folds a copy back into its original when the two are deeply equal, so 14 copies are gone, `Shell.Info_1` among them.
- **12 copies remain:** `Form.*_1` (11) and `Session.Inbox.MovePayload_1` are real differences. In the Form copies, `NaN` comes at a different spot in an enum. `MovePayload_1` refers to `Location.Ref` where the original refers to `Location.PublicRef`. Only event schemas refer to them; no REST operation does.
- **Version literals:** each event's version literal now gets a name from its content (`Event.VersionEncoded_<hash>`), not from encounter order (`_37`, `_47`).

👀 **Read:** `packages/core/src/database/sqlite.ts` and `sqlite.workerd.ts`, the `transactionAcquirer` lines. This is the actual bug fix, the same shape as upstream's. Workerd's own `withTransaction` uses `withPermits`, which was already safe. Also read `Persistence.entry` in `packages/app/src/runtime/persistence/schema.ts`, the one upgrade fix that touches saved user state. The rest is routine upgrade fallout.

<sub>🔍 Found while reviewing the Effect 4.1 changelog · no user reports · timings from the sweep test above</sub>

<details><summary>Checks run</summary>

- `bun turbo typecheck`: all packages pass
- `packages/core`: `bun run script/test.ts` on sqlite-interrupt, sqlite-workerd, database*, process, fs-util, filesystem, shell, session prompt/step/runner, skill, plugin, provider-azure, schedule, workspace, cross-spawn-spawner, environment, boot-work, tool-shell, session-shell: 691 pass, 2 fail. The 2 failures are `tool-shell` "conditional substitutions" cases, which need bash ≥ 4.4 (macOS ships 3.2, so `wait` on a process-substitution PID fails). They don't come from this change.
- `packages/app` `test:unit`: 945 pass · `packages/ai` `bun test`: 1990 pass · `packages/tui`: 1595 pass · `packages/server`: 115 pass · `packages/simulation`: 48 pass · `plugin`, `plugin-browser`, `client`: all pass
- `packages/util` `bun test`: 140 pass · `packages/http-recorder` `bun test`: 53 pass · `packages/cli` `test/updater-install.test.ts`: 30 pass
- `packages/protocol` and `packages/client` `check:generated`: pass
- After review fixes: `packages/core` cross-spawn-spawner, sqlite-interrupt, sqlite-workerd, shell, process: 47 pass · `packages/schema`: 90 pass · `packages/protocol`: 12 pass · `packages/util`: 140 pass · typecheck util, schema, protocol, core: pass

</details>

prs.title: feat(ai): apiKey: false for keyless providers
prs.body:
### Problem

A provider that needs no key (a local server, a gateway that authenticates by header) had no way to say so. Leaving the key out failed with `Missing auth credential: apiKey`, and passing `apiKey: false` crashed.

### Change

`apiKey: false` means "no key on purpose": no env lookup, no auth header from the package, no error. Omitted or `""` keeps today's behavior.

```ts
OpenAICompatible.model("local", { apiKey: false, baseURL: "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1" })
OpenAICompatible.configure({ apiKey: false, baseURL, headers: { "x-gateway-token": "t" } }) // sends only that header
```

```diff
 AuthOptions.apiKey(options, envVars, apply)   // new shared helper; bearer() wraps it
   auth override?        -> use it
+  apiKey === false      -> Auth.none
   else                  -> apiKey ?? env vars, rendered by apply
```

**Covered:** every provider on the shared helper (OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible chat/responses, xAI, Groq, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, Cloudflare Workers AI, Mistral, Cohere, Alibaba, Moonshot, MiniMax, Z.ai, Meta, Venice, etc.), plus Anthropic and Anthropic-compatible (`x-api-key`), Google (`x-goog-api-key`), Azure (`api-key`), Cloudflare AI Gateway, ElevenLabs, Deepgram and AssemblyAI. Image, decision and other media routes reuse the same auth, so they honor it too.

### Out of scope

- Amazon Bedrock (SigV4/bearer) and Google Vertex (ADC/express): auth unchanged, and their types still reject `apiKey: false`.
- Core config wiring: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/42790

### Verification

- New offline `test/keyless-auth.test.ts` against a local `Bun.serve` stub: omitted key still errors; `apiKey: false` succeeds with no `Authorization` (chat + image) and no `x-api-key` (Anthropic); custom header is the only one sent.
- Type tests in `test/auth-options.types.ts`.
- `bun test` in packages/ai (2000 pass), `bun typecheck` + `typecheck:tsc` in ai and core, `bun run check`.

prs.title: fix(core): lower interrupted streaming tool input to an object
prs.body:
## What

A tool call that is still `streaming` when a request is built is lowered to the provider with its **raw argument text** as `input`. When that text is empty, truncated, or valid JSON that is not an object (a quoted string, number, or array), the provider rejects the whole request and the session is permanently stuck on that history.

`toolInput` in `packages/core/src/session/runner/to-llm-message.ts` returned the raw text whenever `JSON.parse` failed, and returned whatever `JSON.parse` produced otherwise:

```ts
tool.state.status === "streaming"
  ? Option.getOrElse(decodeToolInput(tool.state.input), () => tool.state.input)
  : tool.state.input
```

So `input: "not-json"` stayed a string, and `input: '"just a string"'` became a string too. Protocol lowerers copy `part.input` onto the wire verbatim, which produces:

- Anthropic: `400 tool_use.input: Input should be an object`
- OpenAI-compatible gateways: `messages[N].tool_calls[0].function.arguments must be a JSON object encoded as a string (for example "{\"path\": \"src/app.ts\"}"); received string`

The second is what a RunInfra-backed OpenCode session reports as `Failed to drain Session`, and the index points at a tool call that was interrupted (server restart, mid-turn instructions refresh) and left in `streaming` state.

## Fix

Streaming parts now only surface a parsed **plain object**; anything else collapses to `{}`. The call was never executed, so there is no real input to lose, and the synthetic tool result already tells the model the call did not run. This matches what `session.tool.failed` already does when it normalizes `typeof input === "string" ? {} : input`.

## Test

New regression test in `packages/core/test/session-runner-message.test.ts` lowers four streaming parts through `toLLMMessages`:

| state.input | lowered input |
| --- | --- |
| `not-json` | `{}` |
| `"just a string"` | `{}` |
| `[1,2]` | `{}` |
| `{"command":"pwd"}` | `{"command":"pwd"}` |

It fails on `dev` and passes with the change.

Verification run locally:

- `bun test packages/core/test/session-runner-message.test.ts` — 30 pass
- `bunx tsc -b tsconfig.json tsconfig.tests.json` — clean
- `bunx oxlint <changed files>` — clean

## Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="240" height="72" viewBox="0 0 240 72" role="img" aria-label="An interrupted tool call's raw text becoming an empty object">

    .raw { fill: currentColor; font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-size: 10px; fill-opacity: .85; }
```

prs.title: fix(core): report every subagent result to its parent when it goes idle
prs.body:
**Subagents now report every real result to their parent whenever they go idle, including turns that finish after the initial run or across a server restart.**
A subagent is a child session launched to do a task; if a background command or plugin woke it for another turn after its first reply, the parent never received the follow-up result. Turns started by a user prompting an idle child directly, empty retries, and deliberate cancellations behave as before, while steering a running child still delivers its answer.

🔍 **Origin:** reported in #48826; replaces #58825 with one saved-marker path on the SQLite `job` table (#60491).

❌ **Before**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Parent session
    participant J as Background job
    participant C as Child session
    J->>C: run first turn
    C-->>J: first turn settles (or stops empty)
    J->>P: deliver once, then stop watching
    Note over C: Background shell or plugin wakes child
    C-->>C: ❌ finishes real result, parent never hears
```

✅ **After**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Parent session
    participant J as SQLite job row
    participant C as Child session
    Note over J,C: One job row per child tracks reported idle + dirty flag
    C->>J: turn 1 idle (text or error)
    J->>P: deliver <subagent ...> and advance reported
    Note over C: Later turn (or after server restart)
    C->>J: turn 2 idle (text or error)
    J->>P: ✅ deliver <subagent ...> in order and advance reported
```

```diff
- background job waits once -> reads last message -> delivers to parent
- later child turns after job exit are unwatched and lost
+ store one `job` row per child session (`pending`, `reported`, `dirty`)
+ session projector marks `dirty` on idle, cleans up on delete, and re-anchors `reported` on revert
+ whenever a child goes idle (and on startup recovery for dirty rows), scan new turns in order:
+   deliver text results and failures to parent; skip empty turns, interrupts, and user-started turns
+ subagent job only blocks foreground calls and reports explicit cancellations
```

📊 **Proof**

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Background or foreground child woken by a background shell or plugin after its first report | ❌ follow-up result dropped | ✅ parent receives `<subagent>` for each real turn in order |
| Empty initial step or repeated empty plugin continuations | ❌ parent woken with "completed without a text response" | ✅ silent until a turn produces text or fails |
| Server restarts between a child's first turn and a later continuation (or before delivery) | ❌ lost | ✅ saved `job` row survives restart; catches up in order and reconciles legacy notifications without duplicates |

prs.title: feat(cli): support flags with an optional value
prs.body:
### Problem

The Effect CLI parser gives a string flag the next token as its value, and never gives a boolean flag one. So we had no way to write a flag that works both bare and with a value. https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60703 wants `opencode run -w "fix it"` to create a worktree with a generated name, but with a plain string flag `-w` takes "fix it" as the worktree name and the message is lost.

### Change

I added `CliFlag.optionalValue(name, metavar)` in `packages/cli/src/framework/flag.ts`. It builds on `Flag.withOptionalValue`, which the effect version we already pin (4.0.6) ships, so no patch is needed and it stays on public API.

```ts
export function optionalValue(name: string, metavar: string) {
  return Flag.String(name).pipe(
    Flag.withOptionalValue(""),
    Flag.withMetavar(metavar),
    Flag.map((value): string | true => value || true),
    Flag.optional,
  )
}
```

The value only counts when it is attached with `=`, like git's `--color[=when]`. Taking a space-separated value would make `-w fix it` ambiguous with the variadic message, so the next token is never read.

| argv | flag | message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| (absent) | `None` | |
| `-w "fix it"` | `Some(true)` | `["fix it"]` |
| `--worktree=` | `Some(true)` | |
| `--worktree=feature fix it` | `Some("feature")` | `["fix", "it"]` |
| `-w=feature hi` | `Some("feature")` | `["hi"]` |
| `-w --model a/b hi` | `Some(true)` | `["hi"]`, model `a/b` |
| `-- -w hi` | `None` | `["-w", "hi"]` |

Help renders it as `--worktree, -w [=name]`. A repeated flag keeps the first value, the same as every other single-value flag.

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60703 can adopt it like this:

```diff
-worktree: Flag.String("worktree").pipe(
+worktree: CliFlag.optionalValue("worktree", "name").pipe(
   Flag.withAlias("w"),
   Flag.withDescription("Start a new session in a new git worktree"),
-  Flag.optional,
 ),
```

The handler then sends `name` only when the value is a string. `true` means the server generates the name.

### Visual

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 240 72" width="240" height="72" fill="none" font-family="ui-monospace,monospace" font-size="11">

    .val{animation:val 3s ease-in-out infinite}
    @keyframes drop{0%,20%{transform:translate(-56px,-36px)}55%,100%{transform:translate(0,0)}}
    @keyframes val{0%,45%{opacity:0}65%,100%{opacity:.55}}
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.pill,.val{animation:none}}
  </style>
  <text x="10" y="20" fill="currentColor" opacity=".55">opencode run</text>
  <rect x="96" y="8" width="26" height="17" rx="4" stroke="currentColor"/>
  <text x="102" y="20" fill="currentColor">-w</text>
  <text class="val" x="128" y="20" fill="currentColor" opacity=".55">= true</text>
  <text x="10" y="56" fill="currentColor" opacity=".55">message</text>

```

### Out of scope

prs.title: fix(ui): mount tooltips on first hover and render buttons natively
prs.body:
Every `Tooltip` built Kobalte's whole tooltip when it mounted: root, popper, presence, disclosure state, trigger, plus a `MutationObserver`. Every `Button` and `IconButton` ran Kobalte's polymorphic `Button.Root`. The timeline mounts several of each per row (message actions, a copy button on every code block), so scrolling built and threw away tens of thousands of computations for tooltips nobody hovered.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[row mounts] --> B["trigger div, as Kobalte renders it closed"]
  B -- "first pointerenter or focus" --> C["Kobalte tooltip mounts, its Trigger adopts the div"]
  C --> D["open delay, skip delay, presence, popper, dismiss: Kobalte, unchanged"]
```

- **Tooltip:** renders the trigger `<div>` exactly as Kobalte renders it while closed (`type="button"`, `data-closed`, the same class and `data-component`). The Kobalte tooltip mounts on the trigger's first `pointerenter` or `focus`, or as soon as a caller sets `forceOpen`. Its `Trigger` adopts the element that is already there, so mounting re-renders nothing and the trigger keeps focus and hover:

  ```tsx
  const adopt = (triggerProps: TriggerHandlers) => {
    handlers = triggerProps
    if (ref) spread(ref, triggerProps, false, true)
    return null
  }
  // ...
  <Show when={state.mounted}>
    <Root {...}>
      <Trigger as={adopt} />
  ```

  Kobalte attaches its listeners while the mounting event is dispatched, too late to receive it, so that one event goes straight to its handler.
- **Button, IconButton:** render a native `<button>` with the attributes `Button.Root` sets on one: `type` (default `button`), `disabled` and `data-disabled`. Kobalte triggers that render `as={Button}` still pass their props through.
- **Removed:** the tooltip's `onPointerDownCapture` and `onKeyDownCapture`. Passed to a component, Solid registers them as `pointerdowncapture` and `keydowncapture` events, which never fire, so their handler never ran.
- **DOM:** a serialized dump of the whole page (titlebar, sidebar, composer, timeline) matches `dev` except for generated ids.

### Benchmark

Production build, 320-turn session, Chromium 148. Medians of interleaved runs; intervals are 90% bootstrap intervals of the median change.

**Scroll** (300 wheel notches up, then down; 6 runs)

| Frames busy over 8 ms | 92 | **80** | -13% [-20, -2] |
| Solid computations created | 72,142 | **53,267** | -26% |

**Open a session** (reload until the timeline settles; 8 runs)

prs.title: feat(cli): add --worktree to opencode run
prs.body:
### Problem

Headless `opencode run` always starts in the current checkout, so parallel runs (cron jobs, Slack bots, scripts) share one working tree. The only way around it today is to create a worktree through the HTTP API and pass the session ID, or tell the agent to make one itself.

Requested in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/48272 (and earlier https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/35471, https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/21680).

### Change

`opencode run -w "..."` creates a git worktree through the existing `POST /api/worktree`, then starts the new session in it. The server picks a name; `--worktree=<name>` sets one. The value only counts with `=`, so `-w "fix it"` keeps "fix it" as the message.

Stacked on https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60712, which adds the optional-value flag helper.

```diff
 resolveSessionTarget
   resolve location (cwd)
+  if --worktree
+    POST /api/worktree {projectID, name}
+    use the returned directory
   create session at location
```

- Works with `--standalone` and `--server`: the server creates the worktree on its own disk, where the session runs.
- Uses the existing worktree behavior: detached at the HEAD of the checkout you run from (also when that's a linked worktree on another branch), `-2` suffix on name clashes, the project's `commands.start` setup script runs.
- Starts in the same subfolder of the new worktree (run from `packages/cli`, work in `packages/cli`), or at its root when that folder isn't checked in.
- Prints `worktree <root>` to stderr as soon as the worktree exists, so the path is known even if the run fails later, and keeps the worktree after the run.
- Rejects `--continue` / `--session`, since those resume a session that already has a directory.

- Clearer server error when the folder isn't a checkout: `Cannot create a worktree from <dir>: it is not a checkout of this project that supports worktrees, such as a git repository` (was `Worktree source not found: <dir>`).

### Out of scope

- A `--worktree-ref` base option, and a branch per worktree (worktrees stay detached, like the rest of the app).
- Removing the worktree after the run.
- The same flag on the TUI.

### Verification

- Full `packages/cli` suite: 380 tests, 0 fail. `packages/server` worktree tests pass. `bun typecheck` passes in both.
- `run --help` shows `--worktree, -w [=name]`.
- `bun run check`: passes.
- Manual, in a fresh temp repo: `run --standalone -w --auto "run pwd"` ran in a generated `jolly-falcon` worktree, and `run --server <live service> --worktree=named-one ...` ran in `named-one`. `git worktree list` showed both, main checkout untouched. From `packages/cli` the session ran in `<worktree>/packages/cli`; from an untracked `scratch/` it ran at the worktree root; from a linked worktree on `feat` the new worktree started at `feat`'s commit; in a non-git folder it failed with the new message, exit 1. `-w -c` fails with the error above.

### Visual

prs.title: feat(core): add goal round driver and goal verification
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Part of the goal/todo series. **Stacked on #55744** (the endpoints) and #54799 (the durable contracts) — review those first.

### Type of change

- [x] New feature
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Adds the goal round driver, the independent verification round, and the model-facing tools.

**No new loop.** A round is one synthetic inbox row plus one `SessionExecution.wake`. The only place a round is scheduled is the `session.execution.succeeded` subscription, and it re-checks before scheduling: the process-local arm, the durable phase, the verifier's verdict, the todo gate, `rounds < maxGoalRounds`, and no human item waiting. The upper bound is `maxGoalRounds` (default 8).

**The verifier is a second, independent LLM request** — the shape of `SessionTitle.generate`: no conversation history, its own prompt entry, its own `UsageRecorded{source:"goal-verify"}`. Its input is only three kinds of evidence: the session's file diff, the results of finished tool calls (exit code and output), and the todo rows' `acceptance` text. The assistant's prose never enters. The output is decoded from one `llm.stream`; anything that does not decode is `incomplete` (fail-closed).

**`completed` is the verifier's alone.** The model's todo tool cannot write `completed`, and the gate is in code: `todo.every(s => s === "completed" || s === "cancelled")`.

**The model cannot resume.** The goal tool's `action` set is `set|edit|pause|clear` — `resume` is not constructible.

**Fail-closed disarm list**: execution failure, shutdown interruption, a verifier throw, session move/fork, compaction failure. `armed` is process-local and never persisted, so a restart is always disarmed.

### Notes

- `SessionGoalVerify` is a global node with `verify(sessionID, context)` parameter injection — putting `SessionContext.node` in its requirements makes `Instance.Services` self-referential.
- The human-yield check uses `Session.inbox()` rather than `nextPromotable`, because `nextPromotable` only returns the head and would miss a user row queued behind a steer.
- Known limits: the verifier can be fooled by a model that edits tests or the diff; `armed` is process-local.
- If the loop should be reviewed on its own, this splits cleanly into the verifier + tools and the driver + disarm list.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun typecheck` in `packages/core`, `packages/protocol`, `packages/server`: exit 0.
- New tests (`session-goal-verify`, `tool-goal`, `session-goal-driver`): 29 pass.
- Regression (`session-goal`, `plugin/command`, `session-projector`, `session-title`): 48 pass.

The round driver, the verifier and the model tools land in a follow-up.

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Refs #27167. This is the first of four PRs; it does not close the request on its own.

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

The durable half of a session goal: a schema contract, `session_goal` / `session_todo` tables, four durable events, their projections and the read model. No endpoints, no UI, no round driver.

- `packages/schema/src/session-goal.ts` — `Phase` (`active | paused | blocked | complete`), `Snapshot` (with a `revision` CAS reference and `maxGoalRounds`), `TodoItem` / `TodoInput`, `Verdict`, and the `State` read model. The goal id is server-generated and validates the `goal_` prefix it emits.
- `session_goal` / `session_todo` follow the shape of `session_inbox` and `instruction_state`: `session_id` with `onDelete: "cascade"`, JSON columns, the shared timestamps.
- Four durable events: `session.goal.updated` / `.cleared`, `session.todo.updated` / `.verified`.
- Projections: the goal row is upserted with a revision guard (`excluded.revision > revision`), so replaying an event is idempotent; a clear deletes by `(session_id, goal_id)` and the id is never reused; the todo list is replaced wholesale in one transaction; a verification updates items by position and advances the round counter.

### Why it is split this way

The round driver is the only part with an autonomous loop, so it gets its own PR and can be rejected on its own. Even then, this PR plus the endpoints and the desktop indicator are a self-contained feature: a persisted goal, manual control, a todo list, and the indicator — and they already fix the class of defect in #48239, where the stop button did not stop the loop.

- `packages/core/test/session-goal.test.ts` covers the migration and projection idempotency (replaying an event leaves the same row; a stale revision does not overwrite a newer one).

prs.title: refactor(core): share provider discovery through a simple cache
prs.body:
Provider, model and integration state is per Location, so built-in provider plugins that fetch credential-scoped data redid the same fetch in every Location. With 30 Locations open, GitHub Copilot hit `/models` 30+ times at startup and again on every account switch, and DigitalOcean, Azure and Modal did the same.

I added a small internal global cache, `SharedCache`. It is not part of the plugin API.

```text
SharedCache.get({ key, load, interval?, force? })      interval defaults to 10 minutes
  result newer than interval (and no force) -> return it
  load for key already running              -> join it
  otherwise                                 -> run load once, retrying network errors, timeouts, 408/429/5xx 3 times
  load still fails                          -> keep the last good list if there is one, else return the failure
  either way the result is kept until the next interval or a force refresh; interrupts and defects are never kept
  entries nobody asked for in 24 hours (or two of their intervals, if longer) are dropped; never while loading
```

- Each Location's plugin loads in the background at startup, on an account switch and every interval (one value per plugin for both the timer and freshness, 10 minutes by default), calls `get`, and reloads providers only when the result differs from what it applied. That's one request per key per 10 minutes, however many Locations are open. Copilot, DigitalOcean and Modal share one small helper for this; Azure keeps its own discovery flow.
- On an account switch, a Location shows the account's cached list right away and runs a forced refresh in the background, applied if the list changed. Without a good cached list it waits for that forced refresh, so re-selecting an account whose load failed retries at once.
- Keys are the integration, the connection (credential ID or env name, never a token), a short sha256 fingerprint of static API keys and Copilot headers, and any config that changes the answer. Each load resolves the connection's current credential when it runs, so OAuth token refreshes keep their key and use the latest token.
- The cache logs one warning per failed attempt; plugins don't log their own.
- Copilot and Modal now load through Effect's `HttpClient` like DigitalOcean and Azure.
- Azure falls back from the management API to the resource's own list on any error, and reports the management error if the fallback fails too.
- DigitalOcean doesn't load with an expired token and keeps the routers it has.
- With no list, every plugin keeps its models.dev catalog (Copilot routes through its SDK fallback).

Requests to Copilot, DigitalOcean and Azure from server start through opening N Locations, and Copilot `/models` during an account switch (fake upstream from the location-duplication harness, 100 ms latency, measured on an earlier revision of this cache):

| Locations | Start + open: Copilot / DO / Azure | Copilot switch |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3 / 3 / 3 -> 1 / 1 / 1 | 2 -> 1 |
| 10 | 12 / 12 / 12 -> 1 / 1 / 1 | 11 -> 1 |
| 30 | 32 / 32 / 32 -> 1 / 1 / 1 | 31 -> 1 |

Out of scope: Console (it fits `get` with a 1 minute `maxAge`, follow-up), wellknown remote config, and local discovery, which already shares its fetch.

prs.title: perf(core): skip the MCP SDK tool cache and validate only the called tool
prs.body:
Stacked on https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60733. Review only the top commit until that one merges.

## Problem

The MCP SDK writes every tools/list into its response cache as a JSON string. On the first tools/call after a list, it parses that string again and compiles an output validator for every listed tool that has an `outputSchema`, even though only one tool is being called. On a 296-tool catalog where 1 in 3 tools has an output schema, that first call costs about 46 ms of CPU, and each connection keeps the cached string plus all the validators.

## Change

I use two public SDK options and no patch:

```diff
  catalog = { timeout, cacheMode: "bypass" }   // lists skip the SDK response cache
+ listed = Map<name, Tool>                    // refreshed by every tools()

  callTool(input):
-   client.callTool(params, options)
+   definition = listed.get(input.name)
+   if no definition: client.callTool(params, options)      // same as before
+   client.callTool(params, { ...options, toolDefinition: definition })
+     on HeaderMismatch (-32020): client.callTool(params, options)   // once, lets the SDK relist
```

- `toolDefinition` makes the SDK compile only the called tool's output validator. Output validation behaves as before: a structured content mismatch still fails the call.
- On a modern server, the SDK copies `x-mcp-header` arguments into headers from that definition. If the definition is stale, the server rejects the call before running the tool. I retry once without the definition, so the SDK's own relist and retry path runs. That costs one extra round trip in that rare case.
- Behavior change: list TTLs from modern servers are no longer used. opencode already relists only on list_changed or reconnect.

| Catalog, era | First tools/call CPU, before → after | Heap per connection after list + first call |
|---|---|---|
| 296 tools, legacy | 45.8 → 0.23 ms | 3.58 → 1.86 MiB |
| 296 tools, modern | 47.9 → 0.22 ms | 5.15 → 1.87 MiB |
| Cloudflare 3,763 tools, legacy | 2.7 → 0.21 ms | 8.25 → 4.18 MiB |
| Cloudflare 3,763 tools, modern | 6.7 → 0.25 ms | 12.12 → 4.19 MiB |

These numbers come from the real `McpClient.connect` over stdio against a canned server in a separate process, with 20 connections and the median of 5 runs. tools/list CPU also drops by 0.3 to 3 ms because the cache write is gone.

## Out of scope

The legacy deep walk of property schemas in the SDK's tools/list schema is already gone with https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60733, which stops the SDK checking list items one by one.

### Issue for this PR

Closes #39368

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Adds an opt-in screen reader mode. The full-screen interface redraws in place, which screen readers can't follow, so in this mode OpenCode uses the minimal interface (`opencode mini`), which appends to scrollback.

Turn it on with `--screen-reader` (`--no-screen-reader` forces it off), `OPENCODE_SCREEN_READER`, or `screen_reader` in `cli.json`. Plain `opencode` hands off to mini. It is never auto-detected.

- No splash, footer details, animation or color. `NO_COLOR` is also honored.
- Lines are labeled `you:`, `assistant:`, `tool:`, `tool error:`, `error:`, and `Working...` prints after your `you:` line when a turn starts.

- Menus, question lists and the permission prompt move the terminal cursor to the selected row, since screen readers read the line under the cursor. Digit keys in question lists select and Enter confirms.
- The terminal bell rings when a turn ends, when input is needed, and when a tool runs over 5 seconds.

prs.title: fix(gui-extensions): stop rapid toggles from duplicating the first terminal
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #55992

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

Toggling the terminal open again while the first `pty.create` is still in flight re-ran the "create a first terminal for an empty workspace" step, so two terminals could be created. When the two create replies resolved out of order, the pending focus request named a terminal that was no longer active and the panel's focus guard never fired, leaving the open terminal unfocused - typing did nothing until clicking into it.

The fix tracks the in-flight create on the workspace (`creating`, cleared in `finally`) and skips the automatic first-terminal creation while one is pending. Explicit "+" button creates and the "recreate after every terminal exited" behavior are unchanged. Rebased onto `dev` (supersedes #55994, which targeted `v2`).

### How did you verify your code works?

Added a keeper e2e case in `terminal-input.spec.ts` ("rapid repeated toggles create one terminal and keep focus in it"): three quick shortcut presses previously produced two terminals and focus outside the terminal; it now asserts exactly one created pty, one tab, and focus inside the terminal textarea. Ran the full file in built mode as CI does: 10 passed (42s). `packages/gui-extensions` unit tests pass (175), typecheck and `lint:changed` clean.

### Screenshots / recordings

Behavior-only change (focus), no visual layout change; the repro and fix are pinned by the new e2e case above.

prs.title: fix(core): preserve closed blocks on interrupt and retry cut streams cleanly
prs.body:
Interrupting a session or hitting a mid-stream network error previously blurred three different states into one `message.error` path:

1. Cancelling or declining a local tool after the model stream had already finished marked the assistant message `STEP_INTERRUPTED`, wiping valid reasoning signatures, encrypted reasoning items, and Gemini `thoughtSignature` metadata on the next turn.
2. Pressing `Esc` mid-stream discarded completed reasoning blocks from earlier in the same message and replayed half-streamed uncalled tool inputs as fabricated `tool_call(input: {})` + error `tool_result` pairs.
3. Mid-stream network or provider drops before any tool ran kept the broken partial fragment in model history and appended `"The previous response was interrupted. Continue from where you left off..."`, which confused follow-up generations and still tripped occasional `reasoning_extraction` blocks when a thinking-only turn was omitted.

I split step settlement and history lowering on whether the model stream finished and whether any tool ran:

```diff
 SessionStep.attempt (step.ts):
   local tool cancelled or permission declined:
-    failUnsettledTools + failAssistant(STEP_INTERRUPTED) -> Step.Failed
+    failUnsettledTools + Step.Ended when recorded.finish exists (preserves signatures & usage)

   mid-stream provider / transport error with retry:
     record.toolCalled == true  -> Outcome.Continue (keep ran tool + continuation prompt)
-    record.toolCalled == false -> Outcome.Continue (partial fragment + continuation prompt)
+    record.toolCalled == false -> Outcome.Retry (fresh assistant message, retry cleanly from prompt)

 toLLMMessages (to-llm-message.ts):
+  non-abort provider error with 0 ran tools -> omit broken partial attempt from model history
+  aborted mid-stream -> keep closed blocks (signed reasoning before kept output, closed text metadata, ran tools)
+                        and drop uncalled streaming tool inputs + orphaned trailing reasoning
```

| Interruption / failure point | Model history on next request |
| --- | --- |
| `Esc` or permission decline during local tool run (stream finished) | Keeps completed reasoning + signatures, `thoughtSignature`s, and cancelled/declined `tool_result`s |
| `Esc` mid-text after completed reasoning | Keeps completed signed reasoning + partial text (drops unfinalized trailing text metadata) |
| `Esc` mid-tool-input stream | Drops uncalled `streaming` tool input (keeps any earlier ran tool + signed reasoning in the same step) |
| Mid-stream network / provider failure (0 tools ran) | Drops broken partial attempt and retries cleanly from the prompt without `CONTINUE_AFTER_INCOMPLETE_STREAM` |
| Mid-stream failure after a tool ran, or server restart (`restart.ts`) | Keeps ran tool results and continuation / server-restart notice |

prs.title: fix(app): stop the browser pane jumping while resizing panels
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

On Linux (Wayland, high zoom), dragging a sidebar or panel edge made the side panel's browser page jump around on every move. It overlapped the chat, opened gaps, and fell out of line with its own tab strip.

The browser page is a native view. During a drag, `EmbedView` sent new bounds on every frame, and main applied them right away. The DOM around the view only reaches the screen a frame or more later, especially at a device pixel ratio of 4+, so the view and its panel drew from different frames. Panel open/close animations already avoid this: `panelsMoving()` hides native views and shows a still of the page in their place. Resize drags didn't count as movement.

- `ResizeHandle` takes an `onDraggingChange` callback. It gets `true` on the first move (so a plain click on the handle doesn't blink the page) and `false` on release.
- `panel-motion` adds `setPanelResizing`, and `panelsMoving()` is now true during a resize drag as well as during flights.
- The vertical tabs sidebar, the chat/side panel edge, the bottom pane and the side region split pass `setPanelResizing`.

During a drag the page shows as a still, cropped to its box, that moves exactly with the DOM. The live view comes back when you release. Each frame also does less work, because the child page no longer re-lays out on every move.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Reproduced in the packaged beta inside a nested niri (in a headless sway), using real Wayland pointer input from a virtual pointer, at zoom 2 (DPR 4), with a browser tab in the side panel. Recorded frames show the native view drawn about 30 px off its panel and over the chat for several frames per drag. With this branch's renderer in the same app, the still stays aligned on every frame and the live view returns on release.
- New component test in `browser-pane.spec.ts`, using the real `ResizeHandle`, panel motion and host embeds. It fails without the change.
- `bun run check`; `bun typecheck` and `typecheck:tsc` in app, ui and gui-plugins; built e2e `tabs`, `side-panels` and `panel-edges` (46 passed); app components suite run cold with no optimizer reloads. The one failure, `composer.spec.ts:3`, is an existing flake in prompt history (it also fails 1 in 3 on repeat) and unrelated to this change.

prs.title: fix(ai): keep an unencodable tool result from killing the session
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #58934

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

`toolResultText` called `encodeJson` on json tool results without a guard. `ToolOutput.toResultValue` produces `{ type: "json", value: undefined }` when a tool returns `undefined` with no content parts (`tool.ts:262`), and `Schema.encodeSync(Json)` rejects a top-level `undefined` with `Expected a JSON-serializable value`. It now goes through `Schema.encodeUnknownOption(Json)` and falls back to `String(value)` — the same guard `schema/messages.ts:123` already applies to text results. Values that are JSON still encode exactly as before, including the quoted form for strings.

`LLM.compile` had no `catchCause`, so that throw was a defect that unwound through `SessionStep.attempt` into `SessionRunner.drain`: nothing was sent, and the session never recovered. Compile now turns a non-interrupt cause into a typed `AIError` through the existing `streamError` helper, so one step fails instead of the whole session.

I cannot show that this is the same trigger as the large pasted-image reports in #58934, and there is no end-to-end reproduction here. What is shown is the lowering path above, and that a throw at compile time is currently fatal.

### How did you verify your code works?

From `packages/ai`: `bun run test` → 1992 pass / 28 skip / 0 fail (2020 tests, 154 files); `bun run typecheck` → no type errors on both tsconfigs.

The two new tests assert the lowered strings (`"undefined"`, `'{"a":1}'`, `'"abc"'`), not just "does not throw". Reverting the `shared.ts` line makes them fail with `Die(SchemaError(Expected a JSON-serializable value))`. Two existing tests still pass unchanged: `anthropic-messages.test.ts -t "prepares tool call and tool result messages"` (a json tool result still lowers to `'{"forecast":"sunny"}'`) and `media.test.ts -t "rejects local file references as request errors"` (a typed `AIError` is still surfaced, not swallowed).

prs.title: feat(cli): add opencode doctor
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds `opencode doctor`: a read-only report of the data directory and the failure modes that are hard to see from a normal session.

Motivated by a real incident. A v1 CLI and the v2 desktop app shared one `~/.local/share/opencode`; the database ended up with a stale schema (`table session_inbox has no column named type`), the directory had grown to 1.7 GB, and every question about what was actually wrong had to be answered by hand with `sqlite3` and `grep`. `doctor` answers them in one command.

## What it reports

- global paths (data, config, cache, state, log, bin, repos, tmp)
- data directory total, plus a per-child breakdown so you can see what is large
- database, `-wal`, and `-shm` sizes
- count of orphaned temp-then-rename leftovers (`<file>.<pid>.tmp`)
- how many `opencode` executables are on `PATH`, with a warning when more than one shares the data directory (the failure mode above)

## Design

- Measurement is separated from presentation: `handlers/diagnostics.ts` does the read-only filesystem work and is unit tested; `handlers/doctor.ts` is a thin formatter.
- Standard library only (`node:fs/promises`, `node:path`, `node:os`) — no database handle, no writes, nothing created if a path is missing.

## Verification

- `bun test src/commands/handlers/diagnostics.test.ts` → 5 pass, 0 fail (16 assertions, including real temp-directory walks).
- `bun run check` at repo root → 35/35 tasks, 0 errors.
- Exercised the measurement layer against a real 800 MB data directory:

prs.title: fix(app): stop the composer dropzone flickering and showing for text drags
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Regression from:** #37102 (v2 prompt input rewrite). It mapped every drag type to one `drag.enter` state, so the text drags that #12569 treated as @mention drags now opened the file dropzone. It also added the editor `dragleave` handler that clears the state.
- **Text drags showed the file dropzone.** The document `dragover` listener treated any drag that carried `text/plain` as a file drag. When you dragged a selection in the composer, "Drop images, PDFs, or files to add" covered the page.
- **File drags flickered over the composer.** The editor's `dragleave` cleared the drag state every time the pointer moved between the editor's own nodes. The next `dragover` set it again, so the dropzone unmounted, remounted, and restarted its fade on each move.
- **Fix:** The document `dragover` owns the drag state. The editor no longer sets or clears it. The dropzone opens only for drags that carry `Files` (from the system) or `text/uri-list` (file rows from the workspace tree).

**Before**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0bdf03c-8cb7-440b-b596-5bf079bdbc0e

**After**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d649b9ae-5e99-4003-b0a6-0dbec4e55054

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant D as document
  participant E as editor
  participant S as drag state
  Note over D,S: Before: pointer moves from the editor onto its text
  E->>S: dragleave GΓê⌐ΓöÉΓò£Γê⌐ΓöÉΓò£ idle (dropzone unmounts)
  D->>S: dragover GΓê⌐ΓöÉΓò£Γê⌐ΓöÉΓò£ active (dropzone remounts, fade restarts)
  Note over D,S: After
  D->>S: dragover GΓê⌐ΓöÉΓò£Γê⌐ΓöÉΓò£ active (no change)
```

## Implementation

- `attachments.ts`: `dragover` sets the state from the drag's types:

  ```ts
  function dragType(data: DataTransfer | null) {
    if (data?.types.includes("Files")) return "image"

    if (data?.types.includes("text/uri-list")) return "@mention"

    return null
  }
  ```

- `interaction.ts` / `editor.tsx`: The editor's `dragenter` only calls `preventDefault()`, and it has no `dragleave` handler. `onDragLeave` is now `clearDrag`. The session controller calls it when the composer becomes hidden.
- `composer.spec.ts`: A new keeper checks two things. A text drag shows no dropzone. When a file drag moves onto the editor's text, the dropzone element stays mounted and visible.

prs.title: fix(app): scroll settings natively from the sidebar and gutters
prs.body:
## Summary - **Regression from:** #57598 added the `onWheel` forwarding that this PR removes. #60504 then made the forwarding step aside for an overflowing page list, but did not change the stepped scroll. - **Problem:** Scrolling over the settings page list or the gutters jumped in steps. A `wheel` handler on `.settings-screen` caught the event and called `panel.scrollBy()` once per event. This skipped the browser's smooth wheel animation and trackpad momentum. - **Fix:** In the wide layout, the whole settings view (`.settings`) is now the scroll container, and the sidebar is `position: sticky`. A wheel anywhere on the screen scrolls the page natively, so it is smooth and has momentum. The JS forwarding is removed. - **Page list that overflows:** It still keeps the wheel at its edges. `overscroll-behavior: contain` now applies only while the list overflows. Chromium applies `contain` to a list that fits too, and that stopped a wheel over the tabs from reaching the page. - **Narrow layout (< 800px):** No change. Each page still scrolls inside its own panel. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Before W1[wheel over tabs] --> H[onWheel on .settings-screen] --> S["panel.scrollBy(deltaY)
instant jump per event"] end subgraph After W2[wheel over tabs] --> N["native scroll of .settings
(sidebar is sticky)"] end ``` ## Implementation - `settings.css` - `.settings` fills the screen and centers its 1048px layout with `padding-inline: max(0px, calc((100% - 1048px) / 2))`. The gutters are now inside the scroll container. - `@container settings-screen (min-width: 800px)`: `.settings` scrolls, the sidebar is sticky at `height: 100%`, and the panel grows with its content. The sticky page header now sticks to `.settings`. - The nav list's `overscroll-behavior: contain` comes from the same `scroll(self)` timeline as the edge fades. A list without overflow has no timeline, so it keeps `auto`: ```css @keyframes settings-nav-contain { from, to { overscroll-behavior: contain; } } ``` - `navigation.tsx`: In the wide layout, all pages share one scroller, so a page change resets it to the top. - `scroller.ts`: `settingsScroller(panel)` returns the element that scrolls a page: the panel in the narrow layout, `.settings` in the wide one. Search reveal and the Models provider jump use it. - `shell.tsx`: Removes the `onWheel` forwarding and `insideScroller`. ### Visual ```svg ```
