issues.title: GNU screen: inherited COLORTERM overrides the screen guard, so the TUI loses all colors
issues.body:
### What happened?

The TUI renders with no colors under GNU screen.

Pi enables 24-bit output whenever `COLORTERM` advertises it, and screen passes an inherited `COLORTERM=truecolor` straight through. But screen's own `truecolor` option is off by default and it does not approximate: with it off, 24-bit SGR is not forwarded at all, so `38;2;` / `48;2;` never reach the terminal. The screen branch in `detectCapabilitiesFromEnvironment` only helps when `COLORTERM` is unset, which is not the common case because the outer terminal sets it.

Validated with `pi -ne` (no extensions loaded). Related: #1810 (same case, closed) and #4835 (same `COLORTERM` guard weakness, under tmux).

_AI-assisted: drafted by an agent from measurements run on the machine. Every command and output below is reproducible as written._

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# 1. What Pi decides inside screen, no TUI needed
TERM=screen.xterm-256color COLORTERM=truecolor \
  node -e "import('@earendil-works/pi-tui').then(m=>console.log(m.detectCapabilities()))"
# → { images: null, trueColor: true, hyperlinks: false }
# Repeat with COLORTERM unset → trueColor: false

# 2. What stock screen then does with the 24-bit SGR Pi emits
screen -c /dev/null   # default configuration: truecolor off
printf '\033[38;2;255;0;0mred\033[0m\n'   # no color
printf '\033[38;5;196mred\033[0m\n'       # red
```

Running `pi -ne` inside `screen -c /dev/null` and counting what reaches the emulator: `38;2;` × 0, `48;2;` × 0, `38;5;` × 9.

Workarounds today: `truecolor on` in `~/.screenrc` (screen ≥ 4.7 only; 4.6.x answers `unknown command 'truecolor'`), or `PI_TRUE_COLOR=0`, which makes Pi emit 256-color escapes that screen forwards as-is.

### Expected behavior

An inherited `COLORTERM` should not override the screen guard without confirming that the multiplexer forwards 24-bit color, or Pi should fall back to 256-color output inside screen.

### Version

1.0.4

issues.title: Branch summaries replay assistant content omitted by automatic retry

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

After a partial assistant response fails and automatic retry succeeds, `/tree` branch summarization sends the omitted failed response to the summarizer again. This can carry abandoned response content into the new branch.

Reproduced offline with the faux provider and no extensions. Pi itself creates the `context_edit` omission. The retry request correctly excludes `FAILED_ATTEMPT_MARKER`, but the subsequent summary request contains:

```text
[User]: Investigate login
[Assistant]: FAILED_ATTEMPT_MARKER
[Assistant]: Successful retry
```

`prepareBranchEntries()` reads raw entries through [`getMessageFromEntry()`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/f09d01b85e0384647fcab6779d35ab9dabe04be3/packages/coding-agent/src/core/compaction/branch-summarization.ts#L158), which returns `entry.message` without applying `context_edit`. Content replacements are also ignored.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a session and save an earlier assistant entry as the navigation target.
2. For the next prompt, return a partial response followed by `Network connection lost.`, then a successful retry.
3. Verify the failed response has a `context_edit` with `replacement: null` and is absent from live model context.
4. Call `navigateTree(targetId, { summarize: true })` and inspect the summary request: the failed response is present again.

### Expected behavior

Branch-summary input should honor the abandoned branch's latest context edits, including omissions and replacements. Raw history can remain unchanged.

### Version

`main` at `f09d01b85e0384647fcab6779d35ab9dabe04be3` (2026-10-29).

issues.title: Gemini tool-call thought signatures are dropped with the AI Studio OpenAI-compatible endpoint
issues.body:
I can reproduce this with Pi 0.87.1 using the Google AI Studio OpenAI-compatible endpoint and a Gemini Flash Lite model.

The endpoint returns `extra_content.google.thought_signature` in both non-streaming and streaming tool-call responses. However, Pi’s subsequent request replays the assistant tool call without that field, and Gemini returns a 400 error saying the function call is missing a `thought_signature`.

This appears related to #6996, which is closed and I don’t have permission to reopen. Could you confirm whether thought signatures are expected to be preserved for OpenAI-compatible Gemini endpoints, and whether the fix proposed in #8590 is planned for the main branch?

**Environment**

- Endpoint: Google AI Studio OpenAI-compatible API
- Model: Gemini Flash Lite

No API keys or signature values are included.

issues.title: install.ps1: npm detection fails with nvm for Windows (npm.exe, no npm.cmd)

labels.name: pkg:coding-agent
labels.description: Coding agent CLI

issues.body:
Reported in https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7547#issuecomment-6532822706 by @jeffl8n (also item 77 in that thread).

## Problem

`pi.dev/install.ps1` hardcodes `npm.cmd`. With nvm for Windows, the Node install provides `node.exe` and `npm.exe` but no `npm.cmd`. `node --version` and `npm --version` work, but the installer:

- fails `Get-Command npm.cmd` in preflight and offers to install standalone Node.js, which would put a second Node ahead of nvm on PATH
- `Get-NpmGlobalPrefix` and the other `npm.cmd` call sites also assume `npm.cmd`

Repro: `powershell -c "irm https://pi.dev/install.ps1 | iex"` on a machine using nvm for Windows.

## Suggested fix (from the report)

Resolve npm once in `Invoke-PreflightChecks` (`npm.cmd`, falling back to `npm.exe`), store the resolved path, and use it for all npm invocations instead of hardcoded `npm.cmd`.

The installer lives in `earendil-works/pi.dev` (`public/install.ps1`).

issues.title: [Windows] [sink-thread] How do you use Pi on windows? What issues are you seeing?
issues.body:
## Motivation

There are gazzilion developers on windows. Some use pi. Many could use pi. There are however too many ways pi can be run on windows and as such it is hard to know where to focus energy (fixing bugs, having best docs, having out of box) vs what ways can be delegated out of core to extensions. 

## Ways to run pi on WIndows:

- Pi runs on windows, uses git bash (default)
- Pi runs on windows, uses wsl bash (?semi-automatic fallback)
- Pi runs fully on windows with pwsh.exe/powershell.exe bash replacement (only plugins?)
- Pi runs fully in wsl2

## Issues seen:

All of these have some papercuts. Windows/wsl bash suffers from https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7064, Windows/*  suffers from https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/7427, Windows/git-bash suffers from git bash being iffy and e.g. https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/6817 (among some closed). Full wsl2 has least amount of problems but might not be feasible due to compliance + still pi uses wrong keybidnings for copy/paste images with WT/allactitty. Running fully natively on windows/powershell isn't easy even with plugins as bash tool cannot be easily replaced (just shadowed; ie same name) and not all shell invocations can be hooked (RPC, ...).

## Call to action:
As such, I'd like to ask: how do you use pi on windows? Why this particular way and not any of other of the abovementioned ones? If you use some plugins, why and which ones? What's missing? What's challenging? What UX gaps are you seeing? 

Feel free to also link your other more specific issues.

issues.title: pi-tui: `getKeybindings()` realm/instance singleton breaks extensions that import keyText
issues.body:
## Summary

Extensions loaded by `pi-coding-agent` resolve `@earendil-works/pi-tui`
from their own `node_modules`. The `let globalKeybindings = null`
module-scope singleton in `packages/tui/src/keybindings.ts` is therefore
distinct from the one Pi mutates via `setKeybindings(merged)` in
`interactive-mode`. Extensions calling `keyText("app.<binding>")` hit
their copy's lazy fallback, which is constructed with **only** the
`TUI_KEYBINDINGS` definitions (`tui.*`). `app.*` lookups return an
empty key list and render as empty strings.

## Reproduction

1. Install `@victor-software-house/pi-nudge` v0.3.3.
2. Install `@victor-software-house/pi-caveman` (it registers an anchor
   that pi-nudge renders).
3. Start Pi 0.75.3.

The anchor / nudge expand hint renders as `( to expand)` — the
`keyText("app.tools.expand")` substring is empty. With normal Pi
keybindings (`ctrl+o` default, no user override) it should read
`(ctrl+o to expand)`.

I verified this is not a user-override or render-time race issue:

- `~/.pi/agent/keybindings.json` only overrides `tui.input.newLine`.
- `app.tools.expand` is present in both Pi 0.75.0 (pi-nudge's devDep)
  and 0.75.3 (live) under the same id.
- The renderer fires after `interactive-mode` constructor (which calls
  `setKeybindings`), so timing isn't the problem.

## Root cause

`packages/tui/src/keybindings.ts`:

```ts
let globalKeybindings: KeybindingsManager | null = null;

export function setKeybindings(k: KeybindingsManager) {
  globalKeybindings = k;
}

export function getKeybindings(): KeybindingsManager {
  if (!globalKeybindings) {
    globalKeybindings = new KeybindingsManager(TUI_KEYBINDINGS); // TUI-only fallback
  }
  return globalKeybindings;
}
```

Extensions load via `jiti.import(extensionPath)` from `~/.pi/agent/npm/`
which has its own `node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-tui`. Pi's main
runtime in `~/Library/pnpm/global/v11/.../node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-tui`
is a separate copy on disk → separate module instance → separate
`globalKeybindings` slot. Pi's `setKeybindings(merged)` only touches
the slot in its own copy. The extension's copy sees `null` on first
read and creates the `TUI_KEYBINDINGS`-only fallback. `app.*` lookups
then return `[]` forever in the extension's realm.

## Proposed fix

Anchor the singleton on `globalThis` so every pi-tui module instance
in the process shares one slot. Same pattern pi-nudge uses for its
own state (ADR-0010 in that repo). Minimal patch:

```ts
const REALM_KEY = Symbol.for("@earendil-works/pi-tui.keybindings.v1");

interface Realm { manager: KeybindingsManager | null; }
function realm(): Realm {
  const g = globalThis as unknown as Record<symbol, Realm>;
  if (!g[REALM_KEY]) g[REALM_KEY] = { manager: null };
  return g[REALM_KEY];
}

export function setKeybindings(k: KeybindingsManager) {
  realm().manager = k;
}

export function getKeybindings(): KeybindingsManager {
  const r = realm();
  if (!r.manager) r.manager = new KeybindingsManager(TUI_KEYBINDINGS);
  return r.manager;
}
```

After Pi's `setKeybindings(merged)` runs once, every realm/instance of
pi-tui in the same Node process returns the merged manager.

## Impact

- Any extension that imports `keyText` / `keyHint` / `keyDisplayText`
  for an `app.*` binding renders the key as empty.
- `keyText` for `tui.*` bindings happens to work because the lazy
  fallback includes those.
- Currently affects at least `@victor-software-house/pi-nudge` v0.3.3
  (anchor + reminder renderers display `( to expand)` with blank
  shortcut).

## Workarounds considered (and rejected)

- Hardcoding `ctrl+o` as a fallback in the consumer extension — breaks
  user keybinding overrides and defeats the purpose of `keyText`.
- Having each extension call `setKeybindings()` itself — extensions
  don't have a `KeybindingsManager.create()` equivalent and shouldn't
  own that lifecycle.

Fix belongs in `packages/tui`.

issues.title: tool_search returns another tool when the query is a tool's exact name
issues.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-drafted report.** An AI agent wrote this report. I checked the reproduction output myself.

### What happened?

`tool_search` and codemode `searchTools()` do not return a tool when the query is that tool's exact name, if another tool has a shorter description with the same words.

The query `thread_read` is split into `thread` and `read`. `Bm25Ranker` scores only those terms, with length normalization. A short `queue_read` description that contains "read" and "thread" outranks the long `thread_read` description. With `limit: 1`, the named tool is not returned. The full name `mcp__app__thread_read` gives the same result.

Why it matters: agents search deferred MCP tools by name with `limit: 1`. They get the wrong tool, and in our runs some agents then stopped looking for the tool they needed.

Code at current main: [tool.ts#L128-L155](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/36be9c612e64082a4f0d4d0a94706c38ecbc20a1/packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/tool-search/tool.ts#L128-L155). Codemode uses the same ranker in [execute.ts#L674-L696](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/36be9c612e64082a4f0d4d0a94706c38ecbc20a1/packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/codemode/execute.ts#L674-L696).

### Steps to reproduce

Against the published package, no extensions loaded:

```sh
npm pack @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.3.0 && tar xzf earendil-works-pi-coding-agent-1.3.0.tgz
cd package && npm install --omit=dev --ignore-scripts
node --input-type=module <<'JS'
const { Bm25Ranker, createToolSearchDocument } = await import("./dist/extensions/tool-search/tool.js");
const tool = (name, description) => ({ name, description, parameters: { type: "object", properties: {} } });
const docs = [
  tool("mcp__app__queue_read", "Read a queued message of this thread."),
  tool("mcp__app__thread_read", "Read durable state and a paginated timeline from any thread. The default view returns user messages, assistant messages and plans. Continue with afterPosition until hasMore is false."),
].map((t) => createToolSearchDocument(t));
for (const q of ["thread_read", "mcp__app__thread_read"]) {
  console.log(JSON.stringify(q), "->", new Bm25Ranker().rank(q, docs, 1).map((m) => m.name));
}
JS
```

Output:

```
"thread_read" -> [ 'mcp__app__queue_read' ]
"mcp__app__thread_read" -> [ 'mcp__app__queue_read' ]
```

The ranker at current main is unchanged from 1.3.0.

### Expected behavior

A query that is a tool's exact name returns that tool.

### Version

1.4.0 (latest release), 1.3.0, and current main (36be9c6)

issues.title: detectInstallMethod mislabels non-pnpm installs under PNPM_HOME
issues.body:
### What happened?

`detectInstallMethod()` treats any path containing `/pnpm/` as `pnpm`. Installs that only *share* `PNPM_HOME` for bins (e.g. under `$PNPM_HOME/global-nub/...`) are labeled `pnpm`, then `isManagedByGlobalPackageManager` correctly rejects them.

Result:

- Error text: “not managed by a global **pnpm** install” (implies method is pnpm)
- `getUpdateInstruction` / banner still suggest `pnpm install -g …` (wrong tool)

`pi -ne update` reproduces. 0.84.1.

This is a **detection/messaging** bug, not a request to first-class every package manager.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install so the package realpath is under `$PNPM_HOME/…` but **not** under `pnpm root -g` (e.g. `$PNPM_HOME/global-nub/…`)
2. `pi -ne update`
3. Observe pnpm-specific wording and `pnpm install -g` suggestion

### Expected behavior

When the install is not actually managed by that PM:

1. Do not claim install method `pnpm` / do not suggest `pnpm install -g`
2. Prefer: unknown/wrapper wording, or fall through after managed-check fails
3. **Optional generic escape hatch** (preferred over hardcoding each PM): settings/env self-update command, e.g. `selfUpdateCommand` / `PI_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND` with `{installSpec}` — so wrappers can declare how to upgrade without growing `case "nub" | "foo" | …` in core

Out of scope for this issue: adding first-class support for any specific third-party package manager.

### Version

0.84.1

issues.title: WSL: clipboard image paste silently fails when pi's cwd is deep (PowerShell interop hits MAX_PATH)
issues.body:
### What happened?

On WSL, `readClipboardImage()` returns `null` when pi's working directory is deep enough that its Windows path exceeds MAX_PATH, so an image on the Windows clipboard silently fails to paste. Nothing is reported: `runClipboardCommand()` spawns with stderr set to `ignore`, so the failing `powershell.exe` interop call is invisible and the PowerShell backend (the one that actually supplies images on WSL) just returns `null`.

### Steps to reproduce

Pi 1.4.0, Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2/WSLg (kernel `6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2`), node 24.15.0, screenshot on the Windows clipboard (Win+Shift+S).

1. Run pi's own reader from a shallow and a deep cwd:

```bash
node --input-type=module -e 'const m = await import("./dist/utils/clipboard-image.js"); console.log(await m.readClipboardImage())'
```

Measured with the same clipboard contents:

- cwd 228 chars (Windows path ~254): `{ mimeType: 'image/png', bytes: 23883 }`
- cwd 232 chars and above (Windows path ~258+): `null`

The Windows path is the interop UNC form `\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\<linux cwd>`, so the Linux budget is roughly 233 characters.

2. Minimal repro — spawning `powershell.exe` itself fails from the deep cwd:

```bash
node -e 'require("child_process").execFile("powershell.exe", ["-NoProfile","-Command","Write-Output ok"], (e,o)=>console.log(e && e.message, o))'
```

stderr: `/mnt/c/WINDOWS/System32/WindowsPowerShell/v1.0//powershell.exe: Invalid argument` (exit 1). The same command from `/tmp` prints `ok`.

Notes: `wl-paste` is not installed here and `xclip` only lists text targets, so the PowerShell backend is what supplies the image; the same limit applies to an alternative reader that returns the PNG as base64 over stdout, so it is the cwd and not the temp-file/UNC technique.

### Expected behavior

The image pastes, or at least a diagnostic is surfaced instead of returning `null`.

### Why it matters

Any deep repo path (common under `~/source/...` monorepos) silently loses clipboard image paste on WSL, which is also the symptom people report as "image paste is broken" (#2469, #11259).

Suggested direction: spawn `wslpath`/`powershell.exe` with a short cwd, and stop discarding stderr so a failed backend can report instead of failing silently.

### Version

1.4.0

---

_Report drafted with my Pi agent from evidence measured locally on my machine; I reviewed it before posting._

issues.title: Strict-tools fallback on Anthropic is retried on every request instead of remembered

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

The strict-tools fallback from #10409 works, but it isn't remembered. Every request first goes out with strict tools, gets the 400, then retries without strict:

> 400 invalid_request_error: The compiled grammar is too large, which would cause performance issues. Simplify your tool schemas or reduce the number of strict tools.

The tool set doesn't change between turns, so after the first rejection every later turn hits the same 400. I ran a workflow with about a dozen subagents on claude-opus-5-5. Each one had read/bash/edit/write plus a `StructuredOutput` tool (an array of objects with two enums) as its strict tools. Nearly every assistant turn in those sessions has an `anthropic_strict_tools_fallback` diagnostic, up to 65 per session. That's two requests per turn and a few hundred 400s in my proxy logs in ten minutes.

The cause is that `disablePreferredStrictTools` in `anthropic-messages.ts` is local to a single `stream()` call.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Register enough tools with `constrainedSampling: { type: "json_schema", strict: "prefer" }` that Anthropic rejects the grammar (the setup from #10409 works).
2. Run a few turns.
3. Every turn's assistant message has an `anthropic_strict_tools_fallback` diagnostic, and every turn makes two requests.

### Expected behavior

Once a strict tool set has been rejected for a model, later requests with the same strict schemas should go out without strict right away. A small bounded cache keyed by model plus a hash of the strict tool schemas would do. The Bedrock fallback (842c7317) has the same per-request behavior.

I can open a PR for this.

### Version

1.4.0

---

issues.title: openai-completions: empty tool call from OpenRouter/GLM permanently wedges the session (repro + fix for #4854)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

I ran into this bug, found it in 4854 closed for no repro - I have repro and fix. Issue:

GLM via OpenRouter occasionally returns a malformed tool call as an empty tool_calls entry (no id, no name, no args) plus the raw <tool_call> text; pi saves and replays it, so every later request 400s and the session is permanently wedged.

- Provider/model: openrouter · z-ai/glm-5.3-flash · api openai-completions · pi 0.85.1, and the same code is in 0.99.2
- Rate: 1 in ~70k tool calls over 14 days. Rare, but the session never recovers.
- The raw text GLM sent: <tool_call>jat-banner --state starting … </arg_value>, with no tool name and no <arg_key>
- Error on every later request: messages[N]: tool messages must include a non-empty string tool_call_id
- Checked against OpenRouter directly: an empty id gets a 400; an id filled in with an empty name also gets a 400; dropping the ghost call and its result gets a 200

Fix (~20 lines + test): fill in a missing tool-call id when the call finishes streaming, and when sending the history back, skip tool calls with no id or no name, and their results. That also heals sessions that are already broken. Happy to open the PR if you lgtm.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use pi with openrouter / z-ai/glm-5.3-flash (pi 0.85.1, and the same code is in 0.99.2).
2. Any stream that ends with finish_reason tool_calls and one empty tool_calls entry (no id, no name) gets saved as {id:"", name:"", arguments:{}}, with a tool result where toolCallId:"".
3. Every request after that returns a 400. Checked directly against OpenRouter: empty id gets a 400, an id filled in with an empty name gets a 400, and dropping the ghost call and its result gets a 200.
4. I have a failing test that reproduces it with a mocked stream and passes with the fix. I can share it with the PR.

### Expected behavior

_No response_

issues.title: 0.99.x: terminal color query replies leak into the prompt and BEL opens the external editor (mintty on Windows, ConPTY)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

On startup pi opens the external editor. The prompt contains `;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000;1;rgb:d4d4/2c2c/3a3a;…`.
The query runs regardless of theme.

**Versions:** 0.99.x are affected. 0.87.1 is fine. Windows Terminal is fine.
**Terminal:** mintty on Windows, native node.exe, `TERM=xterm`, `EDITOR=vim` (I am using GitBash for Windows environment)

## Cause

0.87.1 sent a single `ESC]11;?BEL` query. 0.99.x sends OSC 10, OSC 11, OSC 4 for indices 0–15, and DA1 (`ESC[c`) as the end marker (`TERMINAL_COLOR_QUERY` in `packages/tui/src/tui.ts`). In this terminal:

1. The DA1 reply arrives first, before any color reply. `consumeTerminalColorResponse` then drops the pending query, so later replies are no longer consumed.
2. The OSC replies arrive without their `ESC]4` prefix, in fragments (`;0`, `;rgb:0000/0000/0000`, `BEL`, `;1`, …). The reply regex cannot match them anyway.
3. `StdinBuffer` splits non-escape input into single characters, so they land in the editor as text. Each stray BEL is Ctrl+G and opens the external editor.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run pi under GitBash (Windows).
2. The prompt contains `;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000;1;rgb:d4d4/2c2c/3a3a;…`.
3. External editor opens, containing the prompt.

### Expected behavior

Prompt is empty and external editor is not opened at the startup. Worked in 0.87.1.

### Version

0.99.0, 0.99.1, 0.99.2,
1.0.0 (tui-mode regular; see my comment below)

issues.title: Document which cwd a resumed session runs in, per entry point
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

`docs/sessions.md` and `docs/cli.md` never say which working directory a resumed session runs in, and it differs by entry point.

- `-c` / `--continue` -> launch directory
- `-r` / `--resume`, `--session <path>`, `/import <path>` -> the cwd stored in the session header
- `--fork <path>` -> launch directory (header rewritten)

A four-row table in sessions.md would state it, plus one line on `/import` copying the file into the current project's session dir.

### Why?

The resumed cwd is what tools, `@path`, project settings and context files resolve against, and it is not inferable from the current text. Copy a session into another project's folder and it appears in `pi -r` there while still running in the original directory - the failure is silent.

### How? (optional)

Table in `docs/sessions.md` under "Continue or switch sessions", one row per entry point. Related: #3249 (closed as by-design) and #11060.

issues.title: pi-coding-agent leaks X11 connections: fills the X server client table ("Maximum number of clients reached")
issues.body:
**Version:** `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@0.81.1` (Node v22.23.1, Linux Mint 22.3 / Cinnamon on X11)

## Summary

A long-running `pi` process leaked **182 established connections to the X server** over ~8 days. This filled Xorg's 256-client table (default limit), so any new X client failed with `Maximum number of clients reached` — new windows couldn't open and the desktop environment could no longer restart.

## Evidence

Connections held by the `pi` process (Node.js from the pi-coding-agent install):

```
# ss -xnp | grep "@/tmp/.X11-unix/X0" → 254 connections total, of which:
# 182 owned by the pi (node) process — 206 total fds, 182 sockets
$ ps -o pid,etime,cmd -p 1845812
PID     ELAPSED   CMD
1845812 8-06:17:04 pi

$ sudo ls -l /proc/1845812/fd | grep -c socket
182

$ sudo readlink /proc/1845812/exe
/home/r/.local/share/pi-node/node-v22.23.1-linux-x64/bin/node

# After killing the process, X connections dropped from 254 to ~60.
```

Each socket points to `@/tmp/.X11-unix/X0` (the local X server on `DISPLAY=:0`).

## Suspect: clipboard integration

`readClipboardText()` calls `clipboard.getText()` on the native addon `@mariozechner/clipboard` (clipboard-rs). On X11, clipboard-rs opens an X server connection per read. Given the process accumulated exactly one new X connection per operation over days, the most likely cause is a connection that is opened per `getText()` call and never closed (or a leaked X connection inside the native addon).

Note: `copyToClipboard` correctly daemonizes `xclip`/`xsel`; only the read path goes through the native addon.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start `pi` in an X11 session (`DISPLAY` set).
1. Trigger operations that read the clipboard (e.g. pasting context) repeatedly.
1. Watch the connection count grow: `ss -xnp | grep "@/tmp/.X11-unix/X0" | grep -c node`.
1. Eventually Xorg hits the limit and logs/behaves as `Maximum number of clients reached`.

## Suggested fix

- Reuse a single X11 connection in the native clipboard module instead of opening one per call, and always close it on failure/timeout.
- As a stopgap in JS: guard `readClipboardText()` to limit call frequency, or fall back to `xclip -o` when the connection count grows.

Happy to provide more logs (full `ss`/`lsof` dumps, strace) if useful.

issues.title: ai: support Anthropic thinking.display "updates" (progress updates between tool calls)
issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Let `anthropic-messages` send `thinking.display: "updates"`, and let pi-durable pass it through.

- `AnthropicThinkingDisplay` is `"summarized" | "omitted"` ([L188](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/b271b0a524b29e13c0c9e748aea0d34e1597f2db/packages/ai/src/api/anthropic-messages.ts#L188)). Add `"updates"`.
- When it is used, add the `thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18` beta. Without it the API rejects `"updates"` as an unknown display value.
- pi-durable's `ConversationStreamOptions` has no display option, so a durable harness cannot pick it at all.

### Why?

On Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.x, the short notes the model writes between tool calls ("found X, now checking Y") come back as their own `thinking` blocks, not `text`. With `"summarized"` (Pi's default) they arrive mixed with reasoning summaries, so a client can't tell them apart. With `"updates"`, every non-empty thinking block is a progress note and reasoning stays hidden.

Our app is a personal assistant on a phone built on pi-durable. During long tool runs it goes silent for minutes, because we only render text blocks and can't safely surface summarized thinking.

### How? (optional)

Widen the type, append the beta in `getBetaFeatures` when `thinkingDisplay === "updates"`, and add `thinkingDisplay` to `ConversationStreamOptions` in durable. Parsing should not need to change: the blocks are ordinary thinking blocks with signatures and are echoed back unchanged.

I'm happy to send a PR if this is wanted.

issues.title: Custom message can make a submitted prompt fail while its input handlers or auth check run
issues.body:
### What happened?

A custom message with `triggerTurn: true` can start its own run while a submitted prompt is still preparing: async `input` handlers, then `checkAuth`. The session still reports idle there, because #10739 marks it busy only from `_startRun`. When preparation ends, the submitted prompt fails with `Agent is already processing. Specify streamingBehavior ('steer' or 'followUp') to queue the message.` (input window), or the core start rejects it (auth window).

### Steps to reproduce

Faux provider, no network:

1. Register an async `input` handler that waits on a promise.
2. Call `session.prompt("human")` and wait until the handler is entered.
3. Call `pi.sendMessage({ customType: "mail", content: "peer mail", display: true }, { triggerTurn: true, deliverAs: "followUp" })`. `steer` and `session.sendCustomMessage` behave the same.
4. Release the handler. The prompt rejects; the custom run took the turn.

For the auth window, block `modelRuntime.checkAuth` instead of an input handler.

The test file on the branch below covers both windows. The six collision cases fail on main `d20c6e9` and pass with the fix; the three controls pass on both.

### Expected behavior

The submitted prompt runs. The custom message queues into its run, as it would during streaming, or starts its own run if the input is handled without one.

### Related

- #10606 and #10739: #10739 reserves the session from `_startRun` and partly fixed #10606. This is the earlier window, and one custom message against one human prompt, not two human prompts.
- #9155 counts pending prompt preflights for tree navigation in the same window. It does not change custom delivery. Whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

### Fix

Branch: [`ajaynomics/pi` `fix/coding-agent-input-preparation-race`](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/compare/main...ajaynomics:pi:fix/coding-agent-input-preparation-race). While a prompt prepares, a triggering custom message is held until the run starts, or until the input ends without one. It then goes through the existing routing, like the `agent_settled` deferral. My first attempt awaited preparation inside `sendCustomMessage` and deadlocked an input handler that awaits that call; a test covers that case.

One behaviour change needs your call. During preparation, `sendCustomMessage` now resolves when the message is accepted, not when its run finishes, and a later delivery error goes to the extension error listener. Is that acceptable, or should it keep resolving on completion?

Happy to open the PR if this is the direction you want.

### Version

1.2.0; main `d20c6e9`.

---
Drafted with AI assistance (Claude), which also wrote and ran the tests. I reviewed the trace.

### What happened?

Some symbols are leaking into my input under specific conditions:

- I'm also running something CPU heavy on my client device, totally unrelated to what's going on in the ssh session terminal. In this case, another pi session on PowerShell is compiling a rust project, and rustc is utilizing the entire CPU.

This is what my agent thinks:

tails, not color-query replies. For example:

4;29;16M;16M;16M5;29;16M5;29;16M

Those look like fragments of `ESC[<34;29;16M` / `ESC[<35;29;16M`.
Selecting text produces many motion reports, and under client CPU load the SSH
chunks arrive split; StdinBuffer then flushes a partial mouse sequence and the
headerless tail leaks into the editor character by character.

flood described in #7876, rather than the color-reply leak in #10256.

Can #6628 be reopened, or should this be filed separately with the selection
and CPU-load reproduction?


### Steps to reproduce

On your windows device, ask pi to compile a rust program in one pi session, while SSHing to another machine and opening a pi session there, keeping the ssh session in the foreground. Stressing the client system with CPU-Z did not reproduce this behavior - I only face it when rustc is running. The session that is running the compilation is not getting any garbage symbols regardless of it it is in foreground or bg, it's only the session over ssh that has this problem. ssh terminals where I'm not running pi do not have this problem.

Only stuff that I write goes into the pi input.

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Replace the raw-string regex checks in the shipped example `packages/coding-agent/examples/extensions/permission-gate.ts` with structural command checks, under the same extension contract.

### Why?

The example is the only shipped command-layer check, and pi's default has no command-layer Decision/Approval gate at all. The regexes match substrings of the whole command string, so they miss trivial variants — `rm -fr` flag order, quoted flags, `find -delete`, `dd of=`, `mkfs`, output redirection, symbolic `chmod 777` — and false-positive on benign mentions (e.g. echoing a dangerous command). Anyone copying the example gets string luck, not a declarative policy.

### How?

I want to implement it myself — already implemented in #11608 (branch `vroomanalytics123:fineprint-permission-gate`): a tokenizer that unwraps `sudo`/`env`/`command` and `sh`/`bash -c`, splits on top-level operators honoring quotes, and checks structure (recursive `rm` in any flag spelling, `find -delete` / `-exec rm`, `dd of=`, `mkfs*`, 777 in numeric or symbolic form, `git clean -f`). Same `tool_call` event, bash-only, same block/ask contract. Verified: 48-case behavior matrix all correct, 8/8 vitest tests, Biome clean, tsc clean. Honest note: repo-wide gates in my checkout fail for a pre-existing reason (missing generated model data); maintainer CI is the right place for the full-suite verdict.

Request: maintainer `lgtm` so the auto-closed PR #11608 (closed by the new-contributor gate, not on merit) can be reopened.

issues.title: bash tool reports "Command timed out after N seconds" for a command that already exited with a real exit code
issues.body:
**What happened?**

When a bash command has already exited with a real exit code, but a descendant keeps the inherited stdout/stderr pipe busy, the tool reports:

```
Command timed out after N seconds
```

The command did not time out. Example measured here: the shell exited with code 1 after ~1.06s, the tool returned at 12.75s with `timeout: 3`, and the model was told `Command timed out after 3 seconds`. The real exit code 1 never reached the model, so it treats a finished-and-failed command as a slow one.

Root cause: `dist/core/tools/bash.js:107` only tests the `timedOut` flag:

```js
if (timedOut) throw new Error(`timeout:${timeout}`);
```

`waitForChildProcess` had already resolved with the real exit code (the child exited long before the deadline), and `killProcessTree` at the deadline is a no-op on a pid that no longer exists (`taskkill` exits 128), so nothing about that call is actually a timeout.

Related: #6787 asked for the timeout deadline to be enforced when descendants keep stdio active (auto-closed by the new-contributor gate). This report is narrower — I am not asking to change the wait, only to stop reporting a false `timed out` when the child already exited. That is a one-condition fix and it also preserves the wait behavior added for #5303.

**Steps to reproduce**

Windows 11, Git Bash, `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.4.0:

```bash
bash(command: "bash -c 'while true; do echo tick; sleep 0.05; done' & sleep 1; echo boom >&2; exit 1", timeout: 3)
```

Result: returns after 12.75s (varies: 5.1s, 12.0s, 22.7s in repeated runs) with output ending `Command timed out after 3 seconds`.

Control cases on the same machine:

| command | timeout | shell exited | tool returned |
|---|---|---|---|
| above (chatty descendant) | 3s | 1059ms, code 1 | 22744ms → `timed out` |
| same but descendant stdio redirected | 3s | 1050ms, code 1 | 1050ms → `Command exited with code 1` |
| `sleep 1; echo boom; sleep 300` | 3s | 3310ms (killed) | 3310ms → `timed out` (correct) |

**Expected behavior**

If the shell had already exited before the deadline, report its real exit code (the same `Command exited with code N` path), not `timed out`. Keep `timed out` for commands whose process was still alive at the deadline.

Suggested condition: record the exit timestamp, and in the `timedOut` branch throw only when the child had not exited before `start + timeoutMs`; otherwise return `{ exitCode }`.

**Version**

pi-coding-agent 1.4.0 (also present on `main`), Windows 11 + Git for Windows bash. Reached through pi-web-ui 0.113.1, which passes `timeout` through unchanged — reproduced directly against the SDK, no extension loaded.

---
_Filed by the reporter's coding agent; the measurements above were produced and re-run locally, not generated._

issues.title: coding-agent: compaction replays pre-summary signed thinking blocks; persistent 400 retry loop on Anthropic-path providers

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What happened?

Token-pressure compaction fired mid-session. pi's cut point landed on an assistant entry that carries `thinking` blocks (split-turn case: "Can cut at user OR assistant messages (never tool results)"), and every retained entry is replayed verbatim behind the compaction summary. On Anthropic-path providers, signed thinking blocks fail signature validation once the request prefix differs from the conversation the signatures were minted against. Every request after compaction then returns a hard-400 `invalid_request_error` — the bad-request class, not a transient error — and pi's retry loop resends the identical context 8 times before I manually escaped by switching models.

Upstream error, exact text (Anthropic Claude API, reached through a proxy that wraps it):

```json
{"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"Upstream request failed: [invalid_request_error] messages.1.content.0: Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block. The block is bound to a different conversation. Remove the block, or set `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior` to \"drop_block\". That setting requires the `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` value in the `anthropic-beta` header. Content that preceded this block when it was created is missing from this request, starting at `messages.0.content.0`."}}
```

Note upstream's own diagnosis: the signature is intact, but "content that preceded this block when it was created is missing from this request" — the compaction rewrote the prefix. The error text even offers a remedy (`prefix_mismatch_behavior: drop_block` behind the `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` beta header).

### Environment

- `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` 1.4.0
- provider: opencode-go proxy → Anthropic Claude API, model `claude-haiku-5-5`, thinking level `high`
- compaction at `tokensBefore: 91408` (contextWindow pinned to 100000 via `modelOverrides`, default reserve 16384 — the trigger path is irrelevant, the kept-tail shape is what matters; a manual `/compact` with the same tail should reproduce)
- compaction ran in split-turn mode — the summary embeds the `--- **Turn Context (split turn):**` merge marker from `compact()`

### Repro shape

1. Session with thinking on plus tool use on an Anthropic-path provider.
2. Compact so the cut point is an assistant entry containing `thinking` blocks. Kept tail then starts at `assistant(content=[thinking(thinkingSignature), toolCall, toolCall])`; the summary user message precedes it.
3. Next request: the block at `messages.1.content.0` is a pre-compaction thinking block → upstream 400 invalid signature (thinking signatures bind to the request prefix).
4. pi deletes its own failed reply (`context_edit` with `replacement: null`) and resends the same unchanged context → identical 400, repeatedly. My session log shows 8 consecutive failures over ~70 s (12:57:16–12:58:23).
5. Escape: switching to a non-Anthropic model family (GLM here) — the different serialization drops the foreign thinking blocks, calls pass. Switching back to a `claude-*` model in the same session would re-send the stale entry and re-fail until that entry leaves the context.

### Expected behavior

Compaction must produce a context the upstream accepts. Thinking blocks retained behind the summary boundary cannot survive the rewrite: their signatures bind to the pre-compaction prefix. Strip them at compaction time, degrade them per upstream's offered option, or self-repair when precisely this error repeats.

### Suggested fixes (ranked)

1. **Strip at compaction.** When persisting the compaction entry, drop `thinking` blocks from all retained messages. Split-turn kept assistant entries are exactly the failure shape. Signatures bind to this conversation prefix and cannot be revalidated after the rewrite; the structured summary already carries the reasoning value. This mirrors the normalization pi already applies across model switches (turns `transformMessages`, which inlines thinking content to plain text; related precedent: closed issue #6167).
2. **Opt-in upstream drop behavior.** Send `anthropic-beta: thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` with `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior = "drop_block"` for compaction-rewritten contexts, as upstream's error text offers. Works on direct Anthropic API paths, but beta headers must survive proxy providers (my provider wraps an Anthropic upstream; passthrough is not guaranteed) — hence option 1 as the default.
3. **Repair on repeated signature errors.** During my loop, each retry deleted the *new* failed reply and resent the identical context; the stale entry was never touched. After N (say 3) consecutive `Invalid signature in thinking block` 400s, pi should strip thinking from retained messages once and retry, instead of burning attempts on unrecoverable state.

### Notes

- Session log corroboration: the compaction entry has `firstKeptEntryId` pointing at an assistant message from 12:56:56 with content types `thinking, toolCall, toolCall` and `thinkingSignature` present on the thinking block; compaction record carries `tokensBefore: 91408`; the summary ends with the `Turn Context (split turn)` marker.
- No thinking-related handling appears in the compaction module: `findCutPoint()` / `prepareCompaction()` / `compact()` persist kept entries as-is.
- Cost of the loop: 8 failed turns with zero-token usage, ~70 s blocked, human intervention required.

issues.title: OpenCode Go Claude (anthropic-messages): 400 on replayed thinking block after tool list change; block_binding only sent for supportsMidConvoEffort
issues.body:
_Disclosure: this report was written by an AI agent (Claude Code) at the request of a downstream app's maintainer. The experiment below was run by the agent against the real OpenCode Go endpoint with synthetic input._

### What happened?

Same failure as #10324, but on `anthropic-messages` through the OpenCode Go gateway (`opencode-go` / `claude-haiku-5-5`). Replaying a signed thinking block after the tool list changed returns:

```
400 invalid_request_error: messages.1.content.0: Invalid `signature` in `thinking` block. The block is bound to a different conversation. Remove the block, or set `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior` to "drop_block". ... The `tools` list differs from the one this block was created with.
```

`anthropic-messages` only sends `block_binding` + `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` when `compat.supportsMidConvoEffort` is true. The generated catalog entry for this model (1.2.0, `opencode-go.json`) is `compat: { forceAdaptiveThinking: true, supportsTemperature: false }`, so it takes the plain path.

### Steps to reproduce

Using `streamSimple` with the `opencode-go` provider, model `claude-haiku-5-5`, `reasoning: "high"`:

1. Send a prompt that makes the model think and call a tool (2 tools in `context.tools`).
2. Send the tool result back with the same history and a 3rd tool added.

Results on the same history:

| Step 2 | Result |
|---|---|
| same tools | 200 |
| one tool added | **400** (above) |
| one tool added + `thinking.block_binding = { prefix_mismatch_behavior: "drop_block" }` + beta `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` in `betas` (via `onPayload`) | 200 |
| one tool added, thinking blocks stripped from history | 200 |

Context: I embed `pi-ai` / `pi-coding-agent` via the SDK in a desktop app whose on-demand tool loading changes the active tool set mid-run, so it hits this often. No pi extensions are involved; this is not the `pi` CLI.

### Expected behavior

The gateway path should not 400 on a changed prefix, as Bedrock no longer does after #10324. Either mark this catalog entry so `block_binding` is sent, or send it for adaptive Claude models on `anthropic-messages` providers known to accept it. I only verified `claude-haiku-5-5` on OpenCode Go; I would not generalize (your Bedrock note says Opus/Sonnet 4.6 reject the field).

### Version

`@earendil-works/pi-ai` 1.1.0 (request-building code is unchanged in 1.2.0)

issues.body:
### What happened?

Model `openai-codex/gpt-6.1-terra` intermittently disappears from `pi --list-models`, apparently after system sleep or VPN connectivity issues (or wrong country selection).

```
❯ pi --list-models | Select-String -Pattern "terra"

openai         gpt-5.6-terra                       272K     128K     yes       yes
openai-codex   gpt-5.6-terra                       272K     128K     yes       yes
```

The model is still present in ~/.pi/agent/models-store.json, but its catalog metadata changes:

Field | Before | After
-- | -- | --
lastModified | 1793193879000 | 0
checkedAt | 1793240351635 | 1793295007994
etag | Present | Missing
gpt-6.1-terra in cached models | Yes | Yes
Model visible in Pi | Yes | No

Even with PI_OFFLINE=1, the model remains hidden.

Running pi update --models restores it immediately. This has happened repeatedly.

# Suspected cause
In withRemoteCatalog(), HTTP 404/501 responses reset lastModified to 0 and clear etag, while preserving stored.models.

remoteModels() then rejects the cached models because their timestamp is older than the built-in catalog.

A successful response missing the Last-Modified header is another possible cause.

Source: [remote-catalog-provider.ts (v1.4.0)](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/v1.4.0/packages/coding-agent/src/core/remote-catalog-provider.ts)

---

- Pi 1.4.0
- Node.js 26
- Windows 11

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run pi update --models and verify gpt-6.1-terra is listed.
2. Allow a periodic catalog refresh, potentially during unstable VPN connectivity.
3. Observe that the model disappears while remaining in the stored model array.
4. Run pi update --models again. The model reappears.

The network trigger is intermittent; the exact HTTP response has not been captured.

### Expected behavior

A transient catalog endpoint failure should not invalidate a previously valid cached catalog or hide working models. The last known good catalog should remain available until a valid replacement is received.

```
❯ pi --list-models | Select-String -Pattern "terra"

openai         gpt-5.6-terra                       272K     128K     yes       yes
```

prs.title: fix(durable): rank tool search like the coding agent
prs.body:
Ports the coding agent's tool ranking fixes for #11331 (#11440, #11625) to durable, which keeps its own copy of the ranker in `src/search.ts`. Problem: durable's `rankDocuments()` was still the coding agent's ranker from before both fixes. `thread_read` with `limit: 1` returned `queue_read`, and a tool name among other words (`peekaboo app`) lost to tools that only mention the words in their descriptions. Change: - `src/search.ts`: same scoring as the coding agent's `Bm25Ranker`, plus coverage first: a tool matching more of the query's terms (in any field) ranks above one matching fewer, whatever the scores. Without it, name weighting regressed `screenshot window` (1 to 2, `window` beat `image`) and `describe app` (1 to 2, `app` beat `see`). The name is a separate field (3x IDF per term, above any number of description mentions), a tool whose whole local name is in the query gets a bonus worth one more match of every query term, a query that is exactly a tool's name ranks it first, and namespace text is a separate 0.5x field that is not length-normalized. - `tool_search`: the search text no longer repeats the name; the ranker reads it from `name`. - `searchTools()`: same, and the namespace text now includes the namespace instructions, as in the coding agent. - `test/search.test.ts`: the coding agent's ranker cases. Remaining difference from the coding agent: durable's `tool_search` has no namespaces (they are a code mode option), and `searchTools()` ranks on the tool sample from the start data (description plus TypeScript declaration) rather than description plus schema text. `searchTools()` results are journaled, so replaying a script started before this change returns the old results; no `CODEMODE_MODULE_VERSION` bump. ## Before/after `searchTools()` ranking on a made-up set of 16 MCP tools from 5 servers. Each tool is searched with its description; each server is a code mode namespace (prefix `mcp____`) with the description and instructions below. prs.title: fix(coding-agent): rank tools matching more query terms first in tool search
prs.body:
Follow-up to #11625 (#11331). Same change in durable's copy: #11631.

Problem: #11625 made a query term in a tool's name outweigh any number of description mentions. That regressed queries where another tool matches more of the query in its description:
- `screenshot window`: `peekaboo__window` (name has `window`) beat `peekaboo__image` ("Take a screenshot of the screen, an app, or a window.").
- `describe app`: `peekaboo__app` (whole name `app`) beat `peekaboo__see` ("... describe the UI elements of the app.").

Fix: `Bm25Ranker` sorts by coverage first: a tool matching more of the query's distinct terms, in any field (name, description and schema, namespace), ranks above one matching fewer, whatever the scores. Within the same coverage, the score decides as before. A query that is exactly a tool's name still ranks that tool first.

On the 16-tool set from #11631 (5 servers, 16 queries), this fixes both regressions and changes nothing else; `search github issues` stays at rank 5, since `list_issues` lacks "search" and ties on coverage with `search_code` and `linear__search_issues`.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): pass host keybinding hints to extension renderers
prs.body:
Fixes #4748.

## Problem

Extensions that import `keyText`/`keyHint` from `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` can resolve their own copy of the package (their own `node_modules`, or the bundled `cli.js` vs `dist/index.js`). That copy's keybindings are never set by the host, so it falls back to a manager with only `tui.*` bindings, and `keyHint("app.tools.expand", "to expand")` renders as ` to expand`.

## Change

The host passes its own `keyText` and `keyHint` to extension renderers, the same way it passes `theme`:

- `ToolRenderContext` (`renderCall`/`renderResult` context): `context.keyHint(...)`
- `MessageRenderOptions` and `EntryRenderOptions`: `options.keyHint(...)`

All three extend a new exported `KeybindingHints` interface. The docs and the `debug-provider` example now use the injected functions and warn against importing them in renderers.

Not done:

- Moving the `pi-tui` keybindings singleton to `globalThis`. Per the discussion in #7011, extension-facing state should be host-owned and passed through the extension API instead of shared through process-wide module state.
- `ctx.ui.keyText`/`keyHint`. No reported case needs them outside renderers, RPC and print modes never install app keybindings, and adding them to `ExtensionUIContext` would break SDK hosts that implement it.

## Tests

- `test/extension-keybinding-hints.test.ts`: tool, message, and entry renderers format a user-overridden `app.tools.expand` binding.
- `npm run check` passes.

prs.title: feat(coding-agent): add PI_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND and selfUpdateCommand for pi update
prs.body:
Refs #7756, #5607.

Problem: when a wrapper or another package manager provides Pi (mise, a `PNPM_HOME` wrapper such as nub, Nix), `pi update` cannot update it and prints "pi cannot self-update this installation." Users with several machines have to remember which tool updates Pi on which machine.

Example:

```sh
export PI_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND="mise use -g npm:{packageName}@{version}"
pi update
# Updating pi with mise use -g npm:@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent@1.4.0...
# Updated pi from 1.3.0 to 1.4.0
```

or in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`:

```json
{ "selfUpdateCommand": ["nix", "profile", "upgrade", "pi"] }
```

Behavior:

- `pi update` still checks pi.dev first. The command runs only when a newer release exists, or with `--force`, and the release note prints first.
- Placeholders come from that release: `{packageName}`, `{version}`, `{installSpec}` (`<packageName>@<version>`). A package rename announced by pi.dev flows into them.
- `PI_SELF_UPDATE_COMMAND` takes precedence and is split on whitespace (no quoting). The setting is argv, for arguments with spaces, and is read only from global settings, so a project's `.pi/settings.json` cannot inject a command.
- The configured command replaces Pi's own update logic for every install method, including installer-managed installs: it is explicit user intent.
- Exit code 0 does not prove an update. Pi reports "Updated pi from X to Y" when its own `package.json` now shows Y (in-place updates) or when `pi --version` from PATH reports Y (wrappers such as mise or Nix that install each version into a new directory). Otherwise it warns: ``Ran <cmd>, but `pi --version` reports X, not Y.``
- "cannot self-update this installation" now mentions the env var and setting.

Docs: `docs/cli.md` (new "Custom update command" section), `docs/settings.md`, `docs/environment-variables.md`, `--help` env list, regenerated `schemas/settings.schema.json`.

Tests: unit tests for argv resolution and placeholders in `test/config.test.ts`; CLI tests in `test/package-command-paths.test.ts` for env precedence over the setting and the managed install, global-only setting gated by the version check, and command failure. `npm run check` passes.

Manual end-to-end check with real mise 2026.10.23 in a sandboxed HOME, running this branch as the mise-installed 1.3.0 (`PI_PACKAGE_DIR` pointing at mise's install):

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| `mise use -g npm:{packageName}@{version}` | mise installs 1.4.0; `Updated pi from 1.3.0 to 1.4.0` |
| Already 1.4.0 | `pi is already up to date (v1.4.0)`, mise not run |
| In-place `npm install -g --prefix <dir> {installSpec}` via the setting | `Updated pi from 1.3.0 to 1.4.0` |
| Command `true` (exit 0, installs nothing) | ``Ran true, but `pi --version` reports 1.3.0, not 1.4.0.`` |

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): weigh tool names above descriptions in tool search
prs.body:
Follow-up to #11440 for the latest comment on #11331.

Problem: the ranker scored a tool as one bag of words. A query term in the tool's name counted like a mention in its description, and the server's instructions were copied into every tool's text, which lengthened it and lowered its score. Models often add words to a tool name, so `peekaboo app` ranked `mcp__peekaboo__app` 14th: other peekaboo tools mention "app" in shorter descriptions, and its own description says "applications".

Fix: `Bm25Ranker` scores three fields separately:
- name: a query term in the name counts 3x its IDF; the description part of BM25 is at most 2.2x, so a name match beats any number of description mentions;
- description and schema text: BM25 as before, length-normalized on this field only;
- namespace name, description, and instructions: 0.5x IDF per matching term, without length normalization.

A tool whose whole local name (last `__` segment) is in the query gets a bonus worth one more match of every query term, so it mostly wins (`peekaboo app`, `describe app`, `read thread_read state`). A query that is exactly a tool's name still ranks it first (#11440). Applies to `tool_search` and codemode `searchTools()`.

Not included: the comment's second point (loading a deferred tool on a direct call instead of `Tool X not found`). That error comes from `prepareToolCall` in `packages/agent`, which has no hook for unknown tools; it needs an agent-loop API change.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): start WSL interop helpers from / and report external editor failures
prs.body:
Fixes #11592.

## Problem

WSL starts Windows programs in the current directory, translated to `\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\<cwd>`. When that path exceeds MAX_PATH, every Windows program fails to start with `Invalid argument`. pi inherits its cwd when spawning `powershell.exe`, so in a deep directory:

- clipboard image paste returns `null` (the PowerShell backend fails, stderr is discarded)
- copy via `powershell.exe` (WSL without WSLg) fails
- opening the browser for sign-in fails (`xdg-open` on WSL runs `explorer.exe`)

Reproduced on WSL (FedoraLinux-44): `powershell.exe` and `cmd.exe` work from a 225-char cwd and fail from 230. With an image on the Windows clipboard, `readClipboardImage()` returns the PNG from `/tmp` and `null` from a 245-char cwd; with this change it returns the PNG from both. `LongPathsEnabled=1` does not help.

## Changes

- `runClipboardCommand` and `openBrowser` run from `/` on POSIX. These tools never use the cwd (temp files are passed by absolute path), and `/` is always the shortest UNC path. `tmpdir()` was not used because `$TMPDIR` can itself be deep.
- The external editor keeps pi's cwd on purpose, so project-relative paths and integrated terminals keep working. A Windows editor such as `code` can still fail from a deep WSL directory, as with git's `core.editor`. A comment documents this.
- External editor failures were silent: the UI redrew over the error immediately. pi now shows `Failed to launch external editor: <cmd>`, `External editor exited with code N; prompt unchanged`, or the signal name. This shows in the status line for the main editor and inline in the extension editor dialog.

## Testing

- New tests: clipboard commands run from `/` (POSIX); an editor that cannot be launched is reported (POSIX); the existing failure test checks the message.
- Verified on WSL by running the real modules: clipboard image paste from a deep cwd, and editor success, exit code 1, launch failure, and SIGTERM.
- On Windows, the 3 existing `external-editor.test.ts` tests already fail on `main`: the editor command is split on spaces, so `C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe` breaks. Not addressed here.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): name the package manager in pi update only when it owns the install
prs.body:
Fixes #7756.

Problem: `detectInstallMethod()` classifies any path containing `/pnpm/` as pnpm. An install that only lives under `PNPM_HOME`, for example a wrapper under `$PNPM_HOME/global-nub/5/node_modules/...`, is detected as pnpm. `pi update` then correctly refuses to self-update (the path is not under `pnpm root -g`), but `getSelfUpdateUnavailableInstruction()` printed:

```
This installation is not managed by a global pnpm install. Update it with the package manager, wrapper, or source checkout that provides it.
```

Fix: name the package manager only when it owns the install (managed but not writable). All other cases fall through to the neutral message:

```
Update @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent using the package manager, wrapper, or source checkout that provides this installation.
```

`detectInstallMethod()` is unchanged: every user-facing path already goes through the ownership check, and returning `unknown` would trip the Windows "only supported for npm and pnpm" guard with a worse message. The update banner already says `Run pi update` and no longer suggests `pnpm install -g`.

The pi.dev installer is not affected: it verifies npm ownership with `npm ls -g` and never infers pnpm from paths.

Tests: regression test in `test/config.test.ts` (fails without the fix). `npm run check` passes.

prs.title: fix(tui): consume mintty's prefixless palette replies after DA1
prs.body:
Problem
mintty under ConPTY answers the OSC 4 palette queries after the DA1 reply and without the ESC ] 4 introducer. Captured from mintty (see #10256):

\x1b[?1;0c;0;rgb:0000/0000/0000\x07;1;rgb:d4d4/2c2c/3a3a\x07 ... ;15;...\x07
StdinBuffer emits the DA1 reply, then the tail one character at a time. The query is already complete at that point, so the tail is typed into the editor, and each BEL is handled as Ctrl+G and opens the external editor.

Fix
When a color query's DA1 arrives without any color reply, TuiBase holds back input that matches the prefixless reply format (;N;<rgb:/rgba:/# value>BEL, complete or partial) and drops complete replies.

Input that stops matching, or a 150 ms pause, ends this and delivers the held characters as ordinary input in their original order, so typed text is delayed at most briefly and never lost. Terminals that answer the color queries never enter this state.

StdinBuffer is unchanged, so normal typing such as ;1; is not buffered.

The colors in the tail are not used: the query has already resolved on DA1. Delivering them would need a later result after resolution, which I left out of this fix.

Tests
Added to test/terminal-colors.test.ts:

the captured mintty reply in one read: nothing reaches the editor, and a later real Ctrl+G still does
the same replies split into fragments
typed text after DA1 is delivered in order when it stops matching, or after the pause
no input is held back after a terminal answered the color queries

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): tokenize permission-gate command checks
prs.body:
Problem: the permission-gate example matches raw command strings with regexes.
That both misses and misfires. `rm -fr /x` slips past the `rm -rf` pattern,
while `echo "do not run rm -rf /"` trips it even though nothing is deleted.
Destructive commands outside the three patterns (find -delete, dd of=,
mkfs, git clean -f) run with no prompt at all.

Change: parse each command into segments, tokenize honoring quotes, unwrap
sudo/env/command/nice/time and sh -c to the real command, then check the
leading command and its flags structurally. One dangerous segment prompts
(blocks without a UI, as before). sudo alone still prompts, as before.
Documented limits: script files run by path and output redirection are not
inspected; substitution nested past two levels prompts as uninspectable.

Verification: examples/extensions/permission-gate.test.ts covers the
behavior matrix (8 tests: flag spellings, wrappers, false positives,
destructive families, substitution, chains). Measured with FinePrint
(github.com/Vroom-Analytics-123/agent-boundary-conformance): with pi's
default (no command rules) every probe is undecided at the command layer;
with the example's documented intent encoded as rules, wrapper and
flag-order variants stay undecided. This change closes those variants for
the commands it checks. It does not add a default gate to pi core, and it
does not claim anything about the sandbox layer.

Note: this PR was prepared with AI assistance. The behavior matrix above
was verified by executing the checker and the gate's tests.

Verification status, stated exactly: the new test file passes 8/8 under
vitest (scoped run and the package examples/ suite), and a 48-case
behavior matrix script passes against the rewritten gate. Biome is clean
on both changed files, and tsc reports no errors in either file. The
repo-wide `npm run check` and `./test.sh` do not pass in this checkout
for a pre-existing reason unrelated to this change: the generated model
data under packages/ai/src/providers/data/ is absent here (it is
gitignored and produced by `npm run generate-models`), so suites fail on
`Cannot find module './data/amazon-bedrock.json'`; no failure names the
permission-gate files. Maintainer CI, which generates that data, is the
right place for the full-suite verdict.

prs.title: fix(durable): return image blocks from read in Code Mode scripts
prs.body:
In pi-durable, a Code Mode script that called the built-in `read` on an image got `""` back, so `image(await tools.read({ path: "pixel.png" }))` threw a TypeError. `read` declared no `structuredOutputSchema`. Code Mode resolves a schema-less tool with only its text, and drops images on purpose. `read`'s output for an image is a single image block with no text, so the script got an empty string. The coding agent fixed the same problem for #10251.

With this change, `read` declares a `structuredOutputSchema`: a string, or an image block `{ type: "image", data, mimeType }`. It returns the matching `structuredOutput`:
- for a text file, its text, so scripts get the same value as before;
- for an image, its `ImageContent`, which `image()` accepts.

The "Read image file" note stays an info diagnostic, as before. The README section on structured output and the changelog are updated.

**Testing**
- New test in `test/codemode.test.ts`. A script reads a real PNG and a text file through `tools.read()`, checks the block's type, MIME type, and data, and passes the block to `image()`. It checks that the script succeeds, the image is saved and shown, and the text read still returns its text. The test fails without the change: the script errors because `image()` gets `""`.
- `test/tools-read-differential.test.ts`: the reference implementation now includes the new `structuredOutput` field.
- `npm run check`.
- `test/codemode.test.ts`, `codemode-describe`, `tools`, `tools-images`, `tools-read-differential`, `harness-tools`, `harness-hook-reads`, `harness-read-only`, and `spec-usage` all pass.

prs.title: fix(chord): remove whole ANSI escape sequences from tool output
prs.body:
`sanitizeOutput()` in `@earendil-works/chord/output` deleted the ESC byte (0x1b) along with the other control characters, but it left the rest of each escape sequence in place. Colored tool output such as `\x1b[31mERROR\x1b[0m` came back from `OutputBuffer.snapshot()` as `[31mERROR[0m`. Because the ESC byte was already gone, later ANSI stripping could no longer recognize the leftover fragments.

`sanitizeOutput()` now removes whole 7-bit escape sequences before it removes single control characters. It handles:
- CSI sequences (colors, cursor and erase commands)
- string sequences (OSC, DCS, APC, PM, SOS) terminated by BEL or `ESC \`
- short `ESC x` forms such as `ESC ( B` or `ESC 7`

`snapshot()` sanitizes the concatenated retained text, so a sequence split across pushed chunks is also removed.

**Testing**
- Added a regression test in `packages/chord/test/output.test.ts`. It covers SGR colors, cursor and erase CSI, charset and short escapes, OSC 8 hyperlinks and an OSC title, plus an `OutputBuffer` fed a color sequence split across three chunks. The test fails without the change and passes with it.
- `test/output.test.ts` and `test/output-skip.test.ts` pass.
- Biome is clean. The only `tsc` errors in `npm run check` are in `packages/ai` tests and are unrelated to this change.
- The durable package test results are the same with and without the change: 71 test files fail on both, and every individual test that runs passes.
- Reproduction from the issue: before the change both lines printed `"[31mERROR[0m\n"`; after it, both print `"ERROR\n"`.

Fixes #11604

Requested by @badlogic

prs.title: fix(env): report watch overflow when a change list exceeds the frame limit
prs.body:
After a rescan, the env daemon's file watcher sent every changed path in a single `change` event. When a big batch of changes made that event larger than the 16 MiB frame limit, `write_frame` rejected it. The daemon's only output writer then shut down. The daemon process kept running but sent no more replies or pings. Requests hung until the client's 30 s silence limit dropped the connection and reconnected.

Now the watcher builds the event with `change_event`. If the serialized path list would not fit in a frame (`MAX_PAYLOAD`), it sends the existing `{ kind: "change", overflow: true }` event in its place. The client already maps that to an `overflow` file change, so the wire format does not change and the connection keeps working.

Testing:
- Added Rust unit tests in `watch.rs`. One checks that a small path list is sent as `paths`. The other checks that a list larger than `MAX_PAYLOAD` becomes `overflow`.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --locked` pass in `packages/env/daemon`.
- The `packages/env` vitest suite passes.
- Reproduced with the real daemon: I watched a directory and renamed in a directory of 6,000 files with long paths, about 20 MB of path JSON. Before the change, `fileInfo` requests timed out from the flush until the client reconnected about 30 s later. After the change, the watcher reports `overflow` right away and `fileInfo` keeps working. With 3,000 files, which fits in a frame, the paths are still reported as before.

Fixes #10516

Requested by @badlogic

prs.title: feat(coding-agent): defer extension runtime reloads
prs.body:
## Summary

- replace awaited command-only `ctx.reload()` with fire-and-forget `ctx.requestReload()` in every extension context
- coalesce reload requests and defer canonical runtime replacement until extension operations, compaction, or branch summarization settle
- reject unsafe direct reload and RPC admission while preserving abort controls, teardown, and terminal failure behavior
- document the API and add lifecycle, admission, teardown, compaction, and RPC regressions

## Breaking change

`ExtensionCommandContext.reload()` is removed. Extensions must use `ExtensionContext.requestReload()`. The request does not return reload completion because replacement starts only after the requesting extension operation settles.

## Testing

- `npm run check`
- `npm run build`
- focused reload, runtime lifecycle, compaction, tree summarization, and RPC suites
- `./test.sh`: one unrelated deterministic failure in `packages/ai/test/supports-xhigh.test.ts`; one footer watcher timeout passed when rerun individually

Fixes #6552

prs.title: feat(serve): batch workspace session live-state snapshots
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds one read-only request for complete live-session snapshots from 1–20 explicitly selected registered workspaces. Each workspace keeps its own canonical identity, catalog version, and independent success or error result. The new request shares the existing single-workspace snapshot and catalog-cache reconciliation logic. A distinct capability and TypeScript SDK method let clients opt in with cancellation and timeout support.

## Why it's needed

Clients showing several workspaces currently make one live-state HTTP request per workspace on every refresh. The recently added batch session catalog can read persisted history, so it is not a suitable high-frequency execution-state endpoint. This API lets clients fetch the same authoritative in-memory state in one request, while preserving the existing single-workspace route and per-session SSE.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Start a local daemon with a primary workspace, register a trusted secondary workspace, then send one batch request containing both IDs and an unknown selector. Expect two full snapshots and one explicit `workspace_not_found` member in input order, with `Cache-Control: no-store`. Confirm malformed bodies fail with HTTP 400, an untrusted or transitioning workspace fails only its own member, and the capability is advertised. Change a live session between running, waiting, and idle without advancing its catalog version; every batch snapshot should still reflect the current state. Confirm the SDK makes one authenticated native REST request and preserves abort and timeout behavior. Older daemons should continue to use the single-workspace route after callers preflight capabilities.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (HTTP and SDK change; no TUI change). The local daemon returned two workspace snapshots and one explicit unknown-workspace error in a single POST.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ Build, typecheck, bundle, focused tests, and local HTTP E2E passed; the large server test file showed unrelated intermittent failures |
| 🪟 Windows | Not tested locally |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ `dev` x86_64: frozen install/build/bundle, typecheck, focused tests, and daemon HTTP E2E passed |

### Environment (optional)

Node 22.23.1 on macOS arm64 and `dev` Linux x86_64, each with an isolated daemon on a dynamically assigned loopback port. The global `qwen` binary was unavailable for the pre-change CLI dry-run; the absence of this route was confirmed in the current base source.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: A batch is not atomic across workspaces. Each successful member is capped at 512 KiB and an oversized member gets an explicit error.
- Not validated / out of scope: Web Shell still polls workspaces separately until a client migration adopts the new capability; no model-driven live session was created in the HTTP E2E. Windows was not tested locally.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None. Clients preflight `workspace_session_live_state_batch` and retain the existing single-workspace path for older daemons.

Design: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/batch-workspace-live-state/docs/design/daemon-batch-session-live-state.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/batch-workspace-live-state/docs/design/daemon-batch-session-live-state.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Closes #12511

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的改动

新增一个只读请求，一次获取 1–20 个显式选定、已注册 workspace 的完整会话运行状态快照。每个 workspace 独立返回规范化身份、目录版本及成功或错误结果。新请求与单 workspace 接口共用快照生成和目录缓存校准逻辑。独立 capability 和 TypeScript SDK 方法支持客户端按能力接入，并支持取消与超时。

## 为什么需要

同时展示多个 workspace 的客户端目前每次刷新都要逐 workspace 发起运行状态 HTTP 请求。近期增加的批量会话目录可能读取持久历史，不适合高频查询执行状态。新接口让客户端通过一次请求获取同样的权威内存状态，保留原单 workspace 路由和逐会话 SSE。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

启动包含 primary workspace 的本地 daemon，注册可信的 secondary workspace，再用一次批量请求查询两个 ID 和一个未知 selector。预期按输入顺序得到两个完整快照和一个明确的 `workspace_not_found` 成员，响应包含 `Cache-Control: no-store`。确认无效请求体返回 HTTP 400，不可信或过渡中的 workspace 只影响自身成员，且 capability 已公布。在目录版本不变时使会话在运行、等待和空闲之间切换，每次快照都应反映当前状态。确认 SDK 只发送一次带鉴权的原生 REST 请求，并保留取消与超时行为。旧 daemon 的调用方应预检能力，继续使用单 workspace 路由。

### 前后证据

不适用（HTTP 与 SDK 改动，无 TUI 变化）。本地 daemon 实测一次 POST 返回两个 workspace 快照及一个未知 workspace 的明确错误。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 构建、类型检查、打包、聚焦测试和本地 HTTP E2E 通过；大型 server 测试文件出现无关的间歇性失败 |
| 🪟 Windows | 本地未测试 |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ `dev` x86_64：锁文件安装/构建/打包、类型检查、聚焦测试与 daemon HTTP E2E 均通过 |

### 环境

在 macOS arm64 和 `dev` Linux x86_64 上使用 Node 22.23.1，各自启动使用动态 loopback 端口的隔离 daemon。全局 `qwen` 命令不可用，无法进行改动前 CLI dry-run；已从当前基线源码确认该路由不存在。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：批量结果不保证跨 workspace 原子性；每个成功成员上限为 512 KiB，超限会返回明确错误。
- 未验证或范围外：Web Shell 在后续客户端迁移前仍逐 workspace 轮询；HTTP E2E 未创建由模型驱动的运行会话；未在本地运行 Windows 测试。
- 破坏性变更或迁移说明：无。客户端预检 `workspace_session_live_state_batch`，旧 daemon 保留现有单 workspace 路径。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/batch-workspace-live-state/docs/design/daemon-batch-session-live-state.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/codex/batch-workspace-live-state/docs/design/daemon-batch-session-live-state.zh-CN.md)

## 关联 Issue

Closes #12511

</details>
