prs.title: fix(acp-bridge): record channel-exit reason in daemon.log
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Channel-exit diagnostics now reach the daemon's persistent log as well as stderr, so companion users can see why an agent channel disappeared. Successful routine retirement is logged at info; unexpected exits, failed initialization, transport faults, timeout retirement, condemned channels and unsettled abandoned work are logged at warn. A clean stdout EOF observed during a successful daemon-initiated exit does not turn routine retirement into a warning.

The diagnostic reports the number of sessions actually removed. Logging failures cannot interrupt session teardown or prevent the stderr diagnostic. Transport handling and lifecycle telemetry retain their existing behavior.

## Why it's needed

The companion stops consuming the daemon's piped stderr after startup. An exit reason written only to that stream is therefore absent from the persistent log used to investigate #12416. This PR makes that existing diagnostic available there; it does not claim to fix the underlying session-creation failure in that issue.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Retire a session through the bridge with production pipe limits enabled. When the child closes stdout and exits successfully, expect one info exit record.
- Verify that an unexpected EOF, nonzero process exit, oversized frame, failed handshake, workspace timeout, condemned channel or unsettled abandoned request produces warn.
- Exercise timeout retirement both with an empty channel and with sessions that must drain. Starting a replacement while the previous channel is still exiting must remain possible.
- Verify that a throwing log sink or lifecycle listener does not strand session cleanup, and that tearing down a condemned managed channel leaves the other engine's live session available.

### Evidence

At the previous PR head c0f5f8c8, a real spawned protocol-fixture child with guarded pipes exited with code 0 during planned retirement, but its exit diagnostic was warn. The corrected real-process regression records info. Negative cases cover unexpected EOF, guarded nonzero exit, oversized frames, and nonzero exit without a transport-failure marker. The fixture waits for a transport-error acknowledgement before exiting; it does not use a scheduling delay to order EOF and process exit.

Two workspace-timeout assertions failed on the previous behavior with info instead of warn. They cover immediate retirement and retirement after sessions drain. The replacement-channel regression also passes with the final diagnostic-only timeout marker; drain scheduling is unchanged.

Mutation checks remove the EOF exception, known-bad process-exit guard, timeout diagnostic guard, and condemned-channel guard in separate runs. Each removal makes the relevant assertion fail; removing the condemned guard leaves the existing channel-exit tests passing and fails the newly added execution-engine assertion.

Local validation: 53 acp-bridge test files / 2572 tests passed, full repository build followed by a final acp-bridge rebuild, bundle generation, ESLint and Prettier on changed files, and bundled CLI version smoke. Full repository typecheck passed.

### Tested on

macOS arm64 / Node 22.22.3. The new real-process fixture uses POSIX signals and is skipped on Windows. Full real-agent/daemon E2E and Windows execution were not performed in this revision.

## Risk & Scope

One additional persistent diagnostic per channel exit. The existing bounded message fields are preserved. A per-channel timeout marker affects diagnostic severity only and is discarded with that channel; it does not affect scheduling or propagate to replacements. Workspace attribution and retirement-reason metadata remain follow-up work.

## Linked Issues

Refs #12416

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

本 PR 把通道退出诊断写入 daemon 持久日志，补上 companion 启动后停止读取 stderr 导致的诊断缺口。正常回收记 info；异常退出、初始化失败、传输故障、工作区超时、故障通道和未完成的废弃请求记 warn。主动回收时，子进程正常关闭 stdout 并以 0 退出，不会因 EOF 被误记为 warn。

退出记录中的会话数按完成清理的数量计算。日志回调或生命周期回调抛错不会中断剩余会话清理。传输处理和生命周期遥测保持原有行为。工作区超时使用通道自己的诊断标记，不改变调度标记和替换通道行为。

本轮在 macOS arm64 / Node 22.22.3 验证。真实进程测试使用实际 bridge、spawn factory 和管道，子进程为协议夹具；没有把它宣称为完整 qwen agent/daemon 端到端验证。Windows 信号测试跳过。工作区归属和退出原因元数据留作后续工作。本 PR 不声称修复 #12416 的会话创建根因。

</details>

prs.title: feat(qqbot): add opt-in forwardBotMessages for bot-authored messages
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a per-channel `forwardBotMessages` option (default `false`). When it is on, messages authored by another bot are delivered to the agent with a `[bot]` prefix on the sender line; the channel prompt explains that prefix and the model decides whether replying makes sense. When it is off — the default — bot-authored messages are still dropped before they reach the agent, exactly as today. User-supplied `[bot]` text is stripped either way, so the tag cannot be forged.

## Why it's needed

There is currently no way for an operator to let two bots in one group talk to each other: the inbound handlers drop bot-authored messages unconditionally, and the formatting path that was meant to tag them is unreachable. Hard-blocking was added as an infinite-loop defense, and unconditional forwarding would give that defense up for every operator. An opt-in switch keeps the default safe while giving operators who intentionally run bot-to-bot conversation a supported path (see #15903).

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Configure a QQ channel with `groupAllPolicy: "all"` and `groups: {"*": {"requireMention": false}}`.
2. With `forwardBotMessages` unset, have a second bot post in the group: stderr shows `Bot message dropped in group <group_openid>` and the message never reaches the session (unchanged default).
3. Set `forwardBotMessages: true` and restart. No drop line is logged; the session transcript shows the message with `[bot]` before the sender bracket, and the model answers or emits `<noreply>` on its own judgment.
4. As a human member, send `[bot] hello`: the literal token is stripped before the model sees it.
5. Direct chats follow the same switch for bot-authored messages.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Unit coverage: `packages/channels/qqbot` 719 passed across 8 files. The forwarding tests run with the switch on and assert the `[bot]` tag; three new tests pin the default drop for C2C, group and group-all; one pins that a member cannot forge the tag. `tsc --build`, ESLint and Prettier are clean on the touched files.

Runtime: a local QQ daemon deployment with `forwardBotMessages: true` logs 0 `Bot message dropped` lines since the restart, and the deployed bundle contains the `[bot]` prompt line gated on the switch. Before the switch existed, the same deployment logged 55 `Bot message dropped` lines in one hour while another bot was active in the group.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests plus a local daemon deployment of the QQ channel on Linux (aarch64). No platform-specific code is touched.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: with the switch on, two bots in one group can answer each other. The model's silence rules, `<noreply>`, and the operator's group policy are the brakes — this PR does not add a platform-level cycle cap. The switch defaults to off, so no existing deployment changes behavior.
- Not validated / out of scope: live delivery was verified against a deployment that receives other bots' messages; other QQ intents beyond group all-message mode were not separately exercised.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. New optional field; the default keeps today's drop behavior.

## Linked Issues

Closes #15903

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

新增每个 channel 的 `forwardBotMessages` 选项（默认 `false`）。开启后，其他机器人发来的消息会带着发送者行上的 `[bot]` 前缀交给 agent；channel 的提示词会解释这个前缀，是否回复由模型自行判断。关闭（默认）时，机器人消息仍像现在一样在到达 agent 之前被丢弃。无论开关如何，用户自己写的 `[bot]` 文本都会被剥离，因此该标签无法被伪造。

## 为什么需要

目前运营者没有办法让同一个群里的两个机器人互相说话：入站处理器会无条件丢弃其他机器人的消息，而本来用于给它们打标签的格式化路径根本不可达。硬拦截最初是作为无限循环的防御加的，而无条件转发又会让所有运营者都失去这层防御。可选开关让默认行为保持安全，同时给有意运行 bot-to-bot 对话的运营者一条受支持的路径（见 #15903）。

## Reviewer 验证计划

### 如何验证

1. 配置 QQ channel：`groupAllPolicy: "all"`，并在 `groups` 里设 `{"*": {"requireMention": false}}`。
2. 不设 `forwardBotMessages` 时，让另一个机器人在群里发消息：stderr 出现 `Bot message dropped in group <group_openid>`，消息不会进入会话（默认行为不变）。
3. 设置 `forwardBotMessages: true` 并重启：不再出现 drop 日志；会话记录里该消息的发送者括号前带 `[bot]`，模型自行决定回复或输出 `<noreply>`。
4. 由人类成员发送 `[bot] hello`：到达模型时该字面前缀已被移除。
5. 私聊中的机器人消息同样受这个开关控制。

### 证据（Before & After）

单测覆盖：`packages/channels/qqbot` 8 个文件 719 通过。转发测试在开关开启状态下运行并断言 `[bot]` 标签；三个新测试钉住 C2C、群消息、群全量消息的默认丢弃；一个测试钉住群成员无法伪造该标签。改动文件的 `tsc --build`、ESLint、Prettier 均干净。

运行期：一台本地 QQ daemon 部署设置了 `forwardBotMessages: true`，重启以来 `Bot message dropped` 记录为 0 条，且部署产物里包含受开关控制的 `[bot]` 提示词行。在该开关存在之前，同一部署在另一个机器人活跃的一小时内记录过 55 条 `Bot message dropped`。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

### 环境（可选）

单测，加一台 Linux（aarch64）上的 QQ channel 本地 daemon 部署。未触碰平台相关代码。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/取舍：开关开启时，同一个群里的两个机器人可能互相接话。刹车是模型的静默规则、`<noreply>` 以及运营者的群策略——本 PR 不引入平台级循环上限。开关默认关闭，因此现有部署行为不变。
- 未验证/超出范围：线上投递是在一个确实会收到其他机器人消息的部署上验证的；群全量消息模式之外的其他 QQ intent 没有单独覆盖。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：无。新增可选字段，默认保持当前的丢弃行为。

## 关联 Issue

Closes #15903

</details>

prs.title: Add DOCX generation through a local MCP extension
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds an optional local extension that creates Word documents from a title and paragraphs, then publishes the generated file as a downloadable session artifact. The extension includes a bundled MCP server, a companion skill, installation instructions, and automated tests.

The server creates real DOCX bytes, binds output to the session workspace, and refuses to replace existing files. The skill registers the exact generated path through Qwen's existing artifact tool. It reports a downloadable document only after registration succeeds.

The implementation and design are documented in [English](https://github.com/waybarrios/qwen-code/blob/docs/docx-generation-proposal/docs/design/native-document-generation.md) and [Simplified Chinese](https://github.com/waybarrios/qwen-code/blob/docs/docx-generation-proposal/docs/design/native-document-generation.zh-CN.md). Both versions cover the same decisions, constraints, and acceptance criteria.

## Why it's needed

Qwen can run a document-generation script, but users still need to assemble the library, instructions, and artifact publication themselves. A request for a Word contract should produce a file the user can download and open.

This implements that workflow through the existing extension system. Starting with DOCX and plain paragraphs gives reviewers a complete, testable result with a small document contract. Users can install it explicitly, and the existing core tool and artifact interfaces stay intact.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Build and link the extension using its installation instructions, then start Qwen in a separate workspace. Confirm that its document tool and companion skill are available.
2. Ask for a Word document containing a title, several agreement paragraphs, Chinese text, accented characters, and literal `<` and `&` characters. Confirm that the file appears in the workspace, registers once as a document artifact, and downloads with identical bytes. Open it in an Office application and check the title and paragraph order.
3. Request the same destination again. Confirm that generation reports the existing file and preserves its original bytes. Repeat with concurrent requests and confirm that only one creates the destination.
4. Try parent traversal, an absolute output path, and a symlink parent leading outside the workspace. Confirm that the tool rejects them without writing to the redirected location.
5. Generate a file with a 201-character basename. Confirm that artifact registration uses its bounded title fallback and retains the exact file path. If publication fails, retry registration against the existing generated file.
6. Extract a built extension archive and run its server without access to repository dependencies. Confirm that it still discovers the tool and generates a document using Node.js alone.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before, users had to supply the generator and coordinate publication themselves. After installing this extension, the companion skill has a documented generation and publication workflow backed by a packaged runtime.

- All 32 extension tests passed. They cover independently parsed OOXML content, Unicode, invalid input, unsafe paths, existing files and symlinks, concurrent writes, cancellation, real MCP calls, startup failures, and an extracted archive running with restricted filesystem reads.
- Repository build, typecheck, and CLI bundle passed. The affected workspace meta-tests passed with 112 tests and one existing skipped test. Scoped lint and formatting checks cover the changed files.
- LibreOffice 24.2.7.2 opened and saved a generated DOCX. Independent ZIP/XML inspection verified its title, title style, paragraph order, Unicode text, and literal XML characters after the round trip.
- Independent review generated a DOCX with an exact 201-character basename and registered it through Qwen's real artifact tool. Registration produced one artifact with the correct file size and the bounded title fallback.
- Two end-to-end runs used the real local Qwen daemon with deterministic model responses. They loaded the extension and skill, executed generation and registration, persisted exactly one available artifact per document, and downloaded identical bytes through the authenticated file API. Both downloaded documents also passed LibreOffice round trips and independent Unicode/XML checks, including the 201-character basename case.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :---: | :--- |
| 🍏 macOS | Not tested locally |
| 🪟 Windows | Not tested locally |
| 🐧 Linux | Build, typecheck, bundle, automated tests, packaged runtime, Qwen generation/publication/download workflow, and LibreOffice round trips passed |

### Environment (optional)

Repository-local worktree on Linux with Node.js 24 and the repository's pinned pnpm. The bundled extension targets Node.js 22. Generation uses local stdio and requires no converter, network access, or separately installed document library. The end-to-end harness used deterministic model responses because live credentials were unavailable. It exercised real Qwen tools and APIs, without a browser UI.

## Risk & Scope

- Artifact publication remains a separate call coordinated by the skill and model. A generated file stays available if registration fails, so publication can be retried without regenerating it.
- Output uses atomic hard-link creation to preserve existing destinations. The filesystem must support hard links. The MCP process runs with the user's permissions and expects a trusted workspace; path validation is not an OS sandbox against another process replacing directories concurrently.
- This change supports DOCX titles and plain paragraphs. Rich layouts, tables, images, templates, editing, conversion, XLSX, PPTX, PDF, automatic MCP artifact ingestion, and registry publication are outside its scope. macOS, Windows, Microsoft Word, and live-model reliability still need separate validation.
- There are no breaking changes or migration requirements. The extension is optional and private to the workspace release setup. It does not join automatic public package releases.

## Linked Issues

Related to #14616.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的内容

新增可选的本地扩展，根据标题和段落创建 Word 文档，再将生成文件发布为可下载的会话产物。扩展包含打包后的 MCP 服务器、配套 skill、安装说明和自动化测试。

服务器生成真正的 DOCX 字节，将输出绑定到会话工作区，并拒绝替换已有文件。skill 通过 Qwen 现有的产物工具登记实际生成路径。只有登记成功后，才报告文档可下载。

实现和设计提供[英文版](https://github.com/waybarrios/qwen-code/blob/docs/docx-generation-proposal/docs/design/native-document-generation.md)和[简体中文版](https://github.com/waybarrios/qwen-code/blob/docs/docx-generation-proposal/docs/design/native-document-generation.zh-CN.md)。两种语言涵盖相同的决定、约束和验收标准。

## 为什么需要

Qwen 可以运行文档生成脚本，但用户仍需自行组合文档库、操作说明和产物发布步骤。用户请求 Word 合同时，应当得到可以下载并打开的文件。

本改动通过现有扩展系统实现这一工作流。先支持 DOCX 和原样文本段落，可在较小的文档契约下，为评审者提供完整且可测试的结果。用户可以显式安装，现有 core 工具和产物接口保持完整。

## 评审者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 根据安装说明构建并链接扩展，然后在独立工作区启动 Qwen。确认文档工具及配套 skill 可用。
2. 请求包含标题、多个协议段落、中文、重音字符以及原样 `<` 和 `&` 字符的 Word 文档。确认文件出现在工作区中，仅登记一次文档产物，并且下载字节完全一致。在 Office 应用中打开，检查标题及段落顺序。
3. 再次请求相同目标。确认生成器报告文件已存在，并保留原始字节。通过并发请求重复验证，确认只有一次能够创建目标。
4. 尝试父目录穿越、绝对输出路径以及指向工作区外部的符号链接父目录。确认工具拒绝这些输入，且不写入重定向位置。
5. 生成基本文件名恰为 201 个字符的文件。确认产物登记使用有界的备用标题，并保留准确文件路径。发布失败时，针对已生成文件重试登记。
6. 解压已构建的扩展归档，并在无法访问仓库依赖的环境运行服务器。确认仅使用 Node.js 仍能发现工具并生成文档。

### 证据（前后对比）

此前，用户需要自行提供生成器并协调发布。安装此扩展后，配套 skill 具有已记录的生成与发布工作流，并由打包后的运行时支持。

- 扩展的 32 项测试全部通过，覆盖独立解析的 OOXML 内容、Unicode、非法输入、不安全路径、已有文件及符号链接、并发写入、取消、真实 MCP 调用、启动失败，以及限制文件读取范围后的解压归档运行。
- 仓库构建、类型检查和 CLI 打包均通过。受影响的 workspace 元测试共 112 项通过，另有一项现有跳过测试。针对改动文件执行了 lint 和格式检查。
- LibreOffice 24.2.7.2 成功打开并保存生成的 DOCX。独立 ZIP/XML 检查确认往返保存后，标题、标题样式、段落顺序、Unicode 文本和原样 XML 字符均得到保留。
- 独立评审生成了基本文件名恰为 201 个字符的 DOCX，并通过 Qwen 真实的产物工具登记。结果仅包含一个产物，文件大小正确，且使用有界的备用标题。
- 两次端到端运行使用真实的本地 Qwen daemon 和确定性模型响应。它们加载扩展及 skill，执行生成和登记，为每个文档持久化恰好一个可用产物，并通过经过身份验证的文件 API 下载完全一致的字节。两个下载后的文档也均通过 LibreOffice 往返保存和独立 Unicode/XML 检查，其中包括基本文件名为 201 个字符的情况。

### 测试平台

| 操作系统 | 状态 |
| :---: | :--- |
| 🍏 macOS | 未在本地测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | 未在本地测试 |
| 🐧 Linux | 构建、类型检查、打包、自动化测试、打包运行时、Qwen 生成与发布及下载链路和 LibreOffice 往返保存均通过 |

### 环境（可选）

Linux 上的仓库内 worktree，使用 Node.js 24 和仓库固定的 pnpm。打包后的扩展面向 Node.js 22。生成通过本地 stdio 运行，不需要转换器、网络访问或单独安装文档库。由于未配置真实凭据，端到端测试使用确定性模型响应；测试执行了真实的 Qwen 工具和 API，未使用浏览器界面。

## 风险与范围

- 产物发布仍是由 skill 和模型协调的独立调用。登记失败时保留已生成文件，可以重试发布而无需重新生成。

- 无破坏性改动或迁移要求。扩展可选，并在 workspace 发布设置中标记为私有，不会加入自动公开包发布。

prs.title: docs(managed-agent): point the server README at the configuration reference
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Makes the generated configuration reference the one place a Managed Agent server setting is described, and removes the copies the server README kept by hand:

- **Three settings tables become links.** The README's tables for the O3 tool-result settings (`qwen.managed-agent.artifacts`), the H6 automation settings (`qwen.managed-agent.automation`) and Runtime record retention (`qwen.managed-agent.runtime-broker.retention`) are replaced by a sentence naming the prefix and a link to that group in the [configuration reference](docs/users/managed-agent-configuration-reference.md). The prose around each table, which explains the feature rather than a setting, stays.
- **The commented Broker block becomes a link.** The `bash` block that set `QWEN_MANAGED_AGENT_RUNTIME_BROKER_ALLOW_NON_LOOPBACK` and `QWEN_MANAGED_AGENT_RUNTIME_BROKER_V3_RESULT_WINDOW` to their defaults, with a comment on each, now names the two settings and links to the Runtime Broker group.
- **The create-Session `curl` becomes a link.** The README had its own copy of the first-Session request, with another tenant and key. It now points at the deployment guide's "Run a first Session" step, which also reads the events and uses a fresh key per check (#15944). The README's Session lifecycle examples (rename, close, archive, delete) move from the `demo` tenant to that step's `default` tenant, so they find the Session it creates.
- **README-only facts move into the descriptions.** Before deleting a row, I compared it with the reference and checked each fact the reference lacked against the code. Seven descriptions in `configuration-descriptions.json` gain a sentence, in English and Chinese, and the two reference pages are regenerated:

| Setting | Added |
| --- | --- |
| `artifacts.enabled` | Committed tool receipts are still recorded for projection while it is false, so turning it on later projects them too. |
| `artifacts.read-timeout` | Whatever this value, a download also ends when one storage read receives nothing for 50 seconds (the OSS client's default socket timeout, which no setting changes), or when a gap between chunks lets its read lease lapse: more than 90 seconds can, two minutes always does. |
| `artifacts.read-revalidation-interval` | What a revocation still lets through: up to one window of a streaming download, or a whole Range response (at most 1 MiB, written in one piece after its last check); nothing after a check denies. |
| `automation.lease` | Once another node claims the lapsed lease, the earlier holder's writes are refused. |
| `automation.max-slots-per-tick` | The limit does not shorten the scan: every minute from where the previous tick stopped, up to the whole lookback window, is still checked. |
| `runtime-broker.v3-result-window` | A value above `30m` does nothing on the shipped path: the Hosted Harness waits for a Tool v3 execution for a fixed 30 minutes. |
| `runtime-broker.allow-non-loopback` | The listener has no per-tenant authorization, and restricting the network alone still sends its token in clear text. |

Two README claims about `read-timeout` change on the way:
- **"Capped by the fixed two-minute output read lease"** is dropped. The lease renews whenever a chunk check finds a quarter of it used, so a download that keeps moving may run past two minutes. What the lease does bound is the gap between chunks, which the new sentence states.
- **"Storage requests also use the storage client's timeouts"** becomes a number. The server configures no OSS timeout, so the SDK default applies: `ClientConfiguration.DEFAULT_SOCKET_TIMEOUT` is 50 000 ms in `aliyun-sdk-oss` 3.18.4. A read that times out fails the download through the same path as `read-timeout`.

The README keeps its duration-unit paragraph. It is a rule across many settings, and `ManagedAgentPropertiesTest` checks its two lists against the code. One test comment that cited the removed `projection-interval` row now cites the reference.

## Why it's needed

#15939 added a configuration reference generated from the server's metadata, which CI keeps current. The README's tables and comments are maintained by hand, so each one is a second description of the same setting that can drift; the reference rows were already more precise in places. For example, the reference says `v3-result-window` applies only to Tool v3 Shell and Monitor executions, and the README comment did not. The triage review of #15944 also noted that the create-Session request now existed in both the guide and the README, with different values, as a future sync obligation.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Regenerate the reference and confirm it is current, and that the only rows that changed are the seven above:
   ```bash
   mvn -f packages/sdk-java/qwencode/pom.xml -DskipTests -Dgpg.skip=true install
   mvn -f packages/managed-agent-server/pom.xml -DskipTests clean process-classes
   node scripts/generate-managed-agent-configuration-reference.mjs --check
   git diff origin/main -- docs/users/managed-agent-configuration-reference.md | grep -c '^+|'   # 7
   ```
2. Check the README tests that read its text:
   ```bash
   mvn -f packages/managed-agent-server/pom.xml -pl verification -am -Dtest='ManagedAgentPropertiesTest,RuntimeRetentionConfigurationTest' -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false test
   npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts scripts/tests/managed-agent-server-e2e.test.js scripts/tests/managed-agent-dev.test.js
   node --test scripts/tests/package-managed-agent-reference.test.mjs scripts/tests/managed-agent-upgrade.test.mjs scripts/tests/generate-managed-agent-configuration-reference.test.mjs
   ```
3. Read the seven new sentences against the code. The evidence for each:
   - `artifacts.enabled`: `ManagedSessionStore` calls `ManagedToolResultStore.captureEvents` on every journal commit, with no check of the setting; `ManagedToolResultProjector.tick` returns early when it is false, and the claim query has no age bound.
   - `read-timeout`: `ToolPublicationRetentionStore.ReadLease.check` renews the 120 s lease once a quarter of it has passed, so after the last check 90 to 120 s remain; `ManagedArtifactService.content` calls it around each chunk. `AliyunObjectStoreClient` builds its OSS client without a timeout, so the SDK's 50 s socket timeout applies, and the read failure reaches the same handler in `ManagedArtifactService.content`.
   - `read-revalidation-interval`: the guard in `ManagedArtifactService.content` re-checks access at most once per window, and the Range path writes its bytes in one call after the last check.
   - `automation.lease`: `AutomationLedgerStore` conditions every write on `lease_owner` and `fence`, and a claim increments `fence`.
   - `max-slots-per-tick`: `AutomationScanner` starts the window at the latest of the arming time, the lookback start and the watermark; `CronSlots.between` walks every minute of it, then keeps the newest `limit` slots.
   - `v3-result-window`: `packages/cli/src/serve/hosted-workspace-broker.ts` polls a Tool v3 execution until `Date.now() + 30 * 60_000`.
   - `allow-non-loopback`: `RuntimeBrokerHttpServer` authenticates its routes with the one configured bearer token, as its constructor comment and the [Broker hardening design](docs/design/2026-10-02-runtime-broker-hardening.md) say.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A, documentation only. Local results on this head:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `generate-managed-agent-configuration-reference.mjs --check` | passes; 7 rows changed per language |
| `ManagedAgentPropertiesTest`, `RuntimeRetentionConfigurationTest` | 33 and 15 passed |
| `managed-agent-server-e2e.test.js`, `managed-agent-dev.test.js` | 134 passed |
| packaging, upgrade and generator `node --test` suites | 93 passed |
| `classify-profile.test.mjs` | 24 passed |
| Prettier, `git diff --check` | clean |
| README links into the reference and the guide | all 6 anchors resolve |

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Maven build of the server with the Java SDK installed from this tree; Node 22 with a fresh `pnpm install`.

## Risk & Scope

- **Main risk or tradeoff:** a reader of the README now follows a link to see a setting's default. That is the point of the change, but the README is less self-contained. The links go to the group's anchor in the reference, and inside the archive the packager rewrites them to `docs/configuration.md` like the README's other links to shipped documents.
- **Not validated / out of scope:** other README passages still describe settings inside feature prose, such as the Session Store base URL and the credentials file. They are not tables and mix settings with behaviour, so they are left for a separate pass. The duration-unit paragraph stays, as explained above.
- **Breaking changes / migration notes:** none. No setting, default or behaviour changes.

## Linked Issues

Part of the deployment usability plan (#12380): item 12, follow-up to #15939 and #15944.

prs.title: fix(core): decode buffered shell output once on non-UTF-8 code pages
prs.body:
## What this PR does

On a system whose code page is not UTF-8, such as CP936, CP932 or CP866, the final result of a shell command run without a pseudo-terminal is no longer decoded with an encoding picked by the first chunk of output the command printed. The buffered result, which is what the shell tool returns in one-shot prompts (`qwen -p`), in sessions with `tools.shell.enableInteractiveShell` turned off, and in serve mode's managed shell results, whose raw-capture path always runs without a pseudo-terminal, is now decoded once from the complete output of each stream (stdout and stderr separately) with the existing detection: UTF-8 when the bytes are valid UTF-8, otherwise the system code page. The pseudo-terminal path already decodes its complete output this way when a command exits. Output that was cut off, by the capture limit, a cancel or a signal that ended the shell, can end partway through a UTF-8 character; that last character does not count against UTF-8 when the bytes before it are valid UTF-8 and hold at least one multibyte character. Output that ended on its own is judged as a whole, so complete output that is not valid UTF-8 decodes with the code page. Streamed output (background shells, the monitor tool), output after a running command is moved to the background, the snapshot taken at that move, and the progress snapshots sent while a buffered command runs are decoded exactly as on main, by the decoder the first chunk picked; making streamed output follow the complete output as well is left for a follow-up. On UTF-8 systems (Linux and macOS UTF-8 locales, Windows with `chcp 65001`), and when the system encoding is unknown or plain ASCII, decoding is unchanged; that covers code pages 437, 850 and 852, which have no decoder, glibc C and POSIX locales, which name no charset and so leave the system encoding unknown, and macOS with no locale set, which reports US-ASCII. The system encoding is read once per process through a new cached accessor that shares the existing detection cache.

## Why it's needed

On Windows with a code page that is not UTF-8, a command that first printed an ASCII line, such as `Loading...` or a path, and then printed localized text in the system code page had its whole output decoded as UTF-8, because the ASCII first chunk is valid UTF-8 and picked the decoder. Everything after that line came back in the tool result mostly as replacement characters: `C:\Users\管理员` arrived as `C:\Users\����Ա`. Programs that write the system code page to a pipe, such as Python or Java on a Chinese or Japanese Windows install, produce exactly this shape. The first-chunk choice also broke valid UTF-8 on these systems when the first chunk ended partway through a UTF-8 character: that chunk failed the UTF-8 check, the decoder was locked to the code page, and `你好` arrived as `浣犲ソ` on CP936. The buffered path serves one-shot prompts (`qwen -p` turns the interactive shell off unless the setting turns it on), every session with `tools.shell.enableInteractiveShell` turned off, serve mode's managed shell results, whose raw-capture path always runs without a pseudo-terminal, and the fallback when a pseudo-terminal cannot be started. The review of #7955 settled the direction for this fix: accumulate the raw bytes and decode the complete buffer once. #12731 already made the system code page take precedence over statistical detection for bytes that are not UTF-8 (#8278), so the first-chunk lock was what remained for the final result.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: on a system whose code page is not UTF-8, main kept UTF-8 for the whole output whenever the first chunk the command wrote was valid UTF-8, ASCII or not, and the buffered result now follows the complete output of each stream instead. When a stream's complete output is not valid UTF-8, it is decoded with the code page, the rule `getCachedEncodingForBuffer` already follows and the pseudo-terminal path applies to its complete output. So GBK, Shift-JIS or CP866 text decodes with the code page, including GBK whose characters partly form valid UTF-8 (`目录路径`). The cost is UTF-8 output with even one byte that is not UTF-8, such as a Latin-1 file name in a git log or grep across UTF-8 and Latin-1 files: main kept the UTF-8 decoder its first chunk picked and showed one replacement character, while this PR decodes it with the code page (the two Latin-1 real-process rows). Also different from main: UTF-8 that a program itself stopped partway through a character, or UTF-8 cut off when the shell is killed from outside rather than cancelled, can read as code page text (on Windows such a kill is reported as exit code 1, not a signal, and elsewhere the kill's own end events can arrive before the exit, so the streams look complete), and a GBK character whose two bytes also form a UTF-8 character, split after its lead byte, reads as UTF-8 when the whole output is valid UTF-8 (`目`, `C4 BF`, reads as `Ŀ`). Decoding the complete output is how the pseudo-terminal path already decodes its final result, and the direction the review of #7955 asked for. A cut-off last character only counts for UTF-8 when that stream was cut off: the capture limit dropped bytes from it, the post-exit drain stopped waiting for it, or a cancel or a signal stopped the shell while it was still open. Which streams were still open is recorded at the cancel, before the kill, because a kill makes the streams it cuts end before the exit is reported, and otherwise at the exit; a stream that had already ended, or a background promote that finds the shell already exited, cuts nothing. Output that ended on its own is judged as a whole, so short code page output that happens to read as UTF-8 cut partway, such as GBK `目浣`, still decodes with the code page, as it does on main when it arrives in one chunk. On these systems the final result costs one more decoding pass over the captured output and a copy of each stream's bytes: 60 MiB of GBK output on a CP936 console peaked at 349 MB on main and 472 MB with this PR (0.85 s and 1.1 s). When output that was cut off is not valid UTF-8, its bytes are checked in place, without another decode. The system encoding is now read by the time the first buffered command without a pseudo-terminal finishes (once per process; one `chcp` call on Windows), not only once output that is not UTF-8 arrives.
- Not validated / out of scope: streamed output, output after a command is moved to the background, the snapshot taken at that move, and the progress snapshots sent while a buffered command runs keep the decoder their first chunk picked, byte for byte as on main, because the code that decodes them is unchanged; the streaming and post-promote unit tests and every streaming and promote run above pin this for streamed output, output after a promote and the snapshot. Making streamed output follow the complete output too needs a different approach, because streamed text is sent as it arrives and cannot be decoded again, so it is left for a follow-up. The pseudo-terminal path is unchanged. Also unchanged are two other points raised in #7936, which the review of #7955 treated separately from the decoding fix: the `chcp 65001` prefix for cmd.exe and the CLI's own subprocess readers. Code pages without a WHATWG decoder (437, 850, 852) keep main's behaviour, as do UTF-8 systems, including main's handling of UTF-8 whose first chunk ends partway through its first non-ASCII character, which statistical detection still misreads there (`ASCII\nä˝ ĺĽ˝ä¸ç` on `chcp 65001` and 437, on main and with this PR). The CLI itself was not run end to end (no API key on this machine), so the steps above that go through `qwen -p` were checked one layer down: the evidence runs the built shell service directly with real child processes, the same calls `qwen -p` makes with the interactive shell off. The full core suite could not run to completion on this machine, because a libuv `fs.watch` assertion in unrelated tests aborts the vitest worker, so the related test files were run one by one instead.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No setting or output format changes. The encoding utilities gain one exported function, a cached read of the system encoding, which the core package re-exports.

## 本 PR 做了什么

在代码页不是 UTF-8 的系统上（例如 CP936、CP932 或 CP866），不经伪终端运行的 shell 命令，其最终结果不再按命令打印的第一个输出数据块所选定的编码来解码。缓冲结果，也就是 shell 工具在一次性提示（`qwen -p`）、关闭了 `tools.shell.enableInteractiveShell` 的会话以及 serve 模式下托管运行时捕获的 shell 结果（该原始捕获路径始终不使用伪终端）中返回的内容，现在会对每个流（stdout 和 stderr 分别）的完整输出用现有的检测逻辑一次性解码：字节是合法 UTF-8 就按 UTF-8，否则按系统代码页。伪终端路径在命令退出时本就这样解码其完整输出。因捕获上限、取消或结束 shell 的信号而被截断的输出，可能停在某个 UTF-8 字符的中间；只要这个最后字符之前的字节是合法 UTF-8 且至少包含一个多字节字符，它就不会被当作否定 UTF-8 的依据。自然结束的输出则作为整体判断，因此不是合法 UTF-8 的完整输出会按代码页解码。流式输出（后台 shell、monitor 工具）、运行中的命令被转入后台之后的输出、转入时取得的快照，以及缓冲命令运行期间发送的进度快照，都与 main 上完全一样，由第一个数据块选定的解码器解码；让流式输出也依据完整输出解码留作后续工作。在 UTF-8 系统上（Linux 和 macOS 的 UTF-8 locale、执行过 `chcp 65001` 的 Windows），以及系统编码未知或只是纯 ASCII 时，解码方式不变；这包括没有解码器的 437、850 和 852 代码页，没有指定字符集、因而系统编码未知的 glibc C 和 POSIX locale，以及未设置 locale、报告为 US-ASCII 的 macOS。系统编码通过一个新的带缓存的读取函数在每个进程中只读取一次，它与现有的检测共用同一份缓存。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：在代码页不是 UTF-8 的系统上，只要命令写出的第一个数据块是合法 UTF-8（无论是否为 ASCII），main 就对整个输出沿用 UTF-8；缓冲结果现在改为依据每个流的完整输出。当某个流的完整输出不是合法 UTF-8 时，按代码页解码，这正是 `getCachedEncodingForBuffer` 已有的规则，也是伪终端路径对其完整输出采用的规则。因此 GBK、Shift-JIS 或 CP866 文本按代码页解码，包括部分字符恰好构成合法 UTF-8 的 GBK 文本（`目录路径`）。代价是夹着哪怕一个非 UTF-8 字节的 UTF-8 输出，例如 git log 中的 Latin-1 文件名、跨 UTF-8 和 Latin-1 文件的 grep：main 沿用第一个数据块选定的 UTF-8 解码器，只显示一个替换字符，而本 PR 按代码页解码（见真实进程结果中的两行 Latin-1）。与 main 不同的还有：程序自己在某个字符中间停止输出的 UTF-8，以及 shell 被外部强制终止（而非取消）而截断的 UTF-8，可能被读成代码页文本（在 Windows 上这种终止报告为退出码 1，而非信号；在其他平台上，终止本身引起的 end 事件可能先于退出到达，流因此看起来是完整的）；两个字节同时也构成 UTF-8 字符、并在首字节后被拆开的 GBK 字符，在整个输出是合法 UTF-8 时按 UTF-8 读取（`目`，即 `C4 BF`，读作 `Ŀ`）。解码完整输出是伪终端路径本就采用的方式，这也是 #7955 评审要求的方向。只有当该流被截断时（捕获上限丢弃了它的字节、退出后的 drain 不再等待它，或者取消操作、信号在它仍未结束时终止了 shell），被截断的最后一个字符才会算作 UTF-8。哪些流仍未结束，是在取消时、发出终止之前记录的，因为终止会让被它截断的流先于退出报告而结束；没有取消时在退出时记录。已经结束的流不算截断，后台转入时发现 shell 已经退出也不算截断。自然结束的输出作为整体判断，因此恰好读起来像被截断的 UTF-8 的短代码页输出（例如 GBK `目浣`）仍按代码页解码，与 main 上它作为一个数据块到达时相同。在这类系统上，最终结果需要对捕获的输出多做一次解码，并复制一份每个流的字节：在 CP936 控制台上，60 MiB 的 GBK 输出在 main 上峰值内存为 349 MB，本 PR 为 472 MB（耗时 0.85 秒和 1.1 秒）。被截断的输出不是合法 UTF-8 时，直接检查其字节，不再额外解码。系统编码现在最迟在第一个不经伪终端的缓冲命令结束时读取（每个进程一次；在 Windows 上是一次 `chcp` 调用），而不再只在出现非 UTF-8 输出时才读取。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：流式输出、命令被转入后台之后的输出、转入时取得的快照，以及缓冲命令运行期间发送的进度快照，都沿用第一个数据块选定的解码器，与 main 逐字节相同，因为解码它们的代码没有改动；流式和后台转入的单元测试以及上面所有流式和转入运行，对流式输出、转入之后的输出和转入时的快照钉住了这一点。要让流式输出也依据完整输出解码需要另一种做法，因为流式文本随到随发，发出后无法再重新解码，所以留作后续工作。伪终端路径未改动。同样未改动的还有 #7936 中提到的另外两点，#7955 的评审把它们与解码修复分开处理：cmd.exe 的 `chcp 65001` 前缀，以及 CLI 自身的子进程读取代码。没有 WHATWG 解码器的代码页（437、850、852）保持 main 的行为，UTF-8 系统也一样，包括 main 对第一个数据块在首个非 ASCII 字符中间结束的 UTF-8 的处理，统计检测在那里仍会误判（在 `chcp 65001` 和 437 上，main 和本 PR 都得到 `ASCII\nä˝ ĺĽ˝ä¸ç`）。本机没有 API key，CLI 本身未做端到端运行，因此上面经由 `qwen -p` 的步骤是在下一层验证的：证据直接用真实子进程运行构建后的 shell 服务，也就是关闭交互式 shell 时 `qwen -p` 调用的同一组接口。完整的 core 测试套件无法在本机跑完，因为无关测试中一个 libuv `fs.watch` 断言会终止 vitest worker，所以改为逐个运行相关测试文件。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。没有设置或输出格式的变化。编码工具新增了一个导出函数（带缓存地读取系统编码），core 包会重新导出它。

## 关联 Issue

部分解决 #7936：不经伪终端运行的命令的缓冲结果。流式输出、cmd.exe 的 `chcp 65001` 前缀以及 CLI 自身的子进程读取代码仍待处理。

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): keep session-commit registration for an absolute cd into the same repo
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Makes the shell tool's "did this `cd` move us to a different repository?" check compare an absolute `cd`/`pushd` target against the directory the command actually runs in, instead of assuming any absolute path leaves the repo. A target that resolves to that directory or to a subdirectory of it is now treated as staying in the same repository; sibling and out-of-tree absolute targets still count as a shift, and relative targets behave exactly as before.

## Why it's needed

The product tells users to spell commits as `cd /abs/path/to/this/repo && git commit -m "..."`. For that spelling the agent's own commit was never registered as a session commit, so the very next `git commit --amend` was hard-blocked with the false reason "the target commit was not made by the agent in this session" (reported by @bainmariehk on 2026-10-07).

Root cause: `cdTargetMayChangeRepo` in `packages/core/src/tools/shell.ts` (now line 886, previously ~873) returned `true` for any target starting with `/`, with no reference to the shell cwd. That latched `cwdShifted` in `gitCommitContext`, so `attributableInCwd` became false, `trackSessionCommit` never ran, `sessionCommitShas` stayed empty, and `GIT_AMEND_PATTERN` in `packages/core/src/permissions/destructive-commands.ts` had nothing to exempt.

The fix resolves the target statically with `path.resolve(cwd, target)` and treats equality with `cwd`, or a prefix bounded by `path.sep`, as in-repo. It deliberately does not shell out to `git rev-parse`: the surrounding walk avoids a synchronous fs/exec call on purpose (see the comment at `gitCommitContext`).

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the session-commit tracking suite, which drives a real `git commit` through `ShellToolInvocation.execute()` in a real temp repo and then asks the guard whether the follow-up amend is allowed. The three new rows are:

1. `cd <absolute repo root> && git add feature.txt && git commit -m "feature"` → commit registered, amend exempt, `Co-authored-by: Qwen-Coder` trailer present.
2. `cd <repo>/sub && git add feature.txt && git commit -m "feature"` → same.
3. `cd <repo>-sibling && ...` (a sibling path that shares the repo path as a *string* prefix) → still not registered, amend still blocked, and no trailer stamped into the sibling repo. This row exists to reject the tempting one-line fix `target.startsWith(cwd)`, which would admit a foreign repository.

Relative-target rows are untouched and stay green.

**Before (fix stashed, tests applied) — RED:**

```
$ cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/tools/shell.session-commit-tracking.test.ts

      Tests  3 failed | 38 passed (41)
RED_EXIT=1
```

- `registers a commit after an absolute `cd` into the same repo root (issue #12514)`
- `registers a commit after an absolute `cd` into a subdirectory of the same repo (issue #12514)`
- `keeps the cwd-shift latch for an absolute `cd` into a sibling directory that shares the repo path prefix (issue #12514)`

**After — GREEN:**

```
$ cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/tools/shell.session-commit-tracking.test.ts

      Tests  41 passed (41)
GREEN_EXIT=0
```

**Typecheck and lint:**

```
$ NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 npx tsc -b packages/core    # exit 0
$ npx prettier --check packages/core/src/tools/shell.ts packages/core/src/tools/shell.session-commit-tracking.test.ts   # All matched files use Prettier code style!
$ npx eslint  packages/core/src/tools/shell.ts packages/core/src/tools/shell.session-commit-tracking.test.ts            # exit 0
```

**Environment note (honest disclosure):** this machine's only git is 2.19.1, but `initRepo()` in the suite calls `git init --initial-branch=main`, which needs git ≥ 2.28. On a stock run every row — not just the new ones — fails in `beforeEach` with `error: unknown option 'initial-branch=main'`, which is an environment limit and unrelated to this change. The runs above were therefore taken with a local PATH shim that only translates that one flag (`git init -q --initial-branch=X` → `init -q` followed by `symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/X`). The shim is not part of this patch, and it changes nothing about the code paths under test.

|     OS     | Status |

|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️ not tested (no Apple hardware available)   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️ not tested   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅ tested   |

### Environment (optional)

Node + `npx vitest` per-package run; no network, model, or credentials required — only the `git` binary.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the in-repo/sibling decision is made by string comparison after `path.resolve`, not by asking git for the toplevel. A path that is a symlink or otherwise resolves differently from its text form can still be classified conservatively (a miss, never a wrong-repo stamp), which matches the walk's existing "better miss than corrupt unrelated repos" stance.
- Not validated / out of scope: the execution-sandbox arm (issue comment "A.1") and the SSH arm ("A.2") are not addressed here, and `isAmendCommit`'s own strict `tokens[0]` walk (issue comment "C") is unchanged apart from inheriting the cwd-aware predicate. prs.title: test(managed-agent): anchor the A3 original-plan count pin and correct evidence prose
prs.body:
## What this PR does

This is a post-merge follow-up to #15945 (the A3 mixed-sibling approval crash arm). It closes the still-standing review evidence residual and the fast-tier pin gap (F1) recorded in that PR's post-merge verification, and corrects two prose inaccuracies in the bilingual design docs. Concretely: it adds a tightly anchored fast-tier contract pin for the original-plan call count, reclassifies the R1-4/R1-5 mutation reds to match what was actually observed, removes a claim that a deferred hook behavioral unit test already exists, and states that the captured plan order is request order rather than the model's part order. No production code changes.

## Why it's needed

After #15945 merged, three things remained outstanding. First, the fast-tier contract suite anchored only the `expectedExecutions` count ternary; the bare `? 2 : 1` pattern also matches the separate `expectedOriginalPlanCalls` site, so narrowing that site from 2 to 1 left all 46 contract tests green (finding F1) — the unit-speed gate did not catch a regression that the real-stack barrier still catches. Second, the design docs still listed R1-4/R1-5 as real-stack mutation reds that trip the new `decidedBefore` / `settled_at` assertions, but the author's own closure replies record that those real-stack witnesses red at *earlier* recovery guards (the load route's cancelled/expired guard; the adoption-stage digest conflict), so the new checks are defense in depth whose load-bearingness is proven by the fast-tier contract pins, not by a real-stack red at the new assertion. Third, the docs claimed a hook matching/non-matching behavioral unit test that is in fact deferred, and described the captured two-call plan as being in "model order" when plan order is request order. This PR makes the evidence prose match the recorded results so the acceptance ledger is accurate.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the fast-tier contract suite and confirm it is green, then confirm the new pin is load-bearing by mutating the original-plan count site. From the repository root: `npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts scripts/tests/managed-agent-server-e2e.test.js` should report 46 passed. Then change `expectedOriginalPlanCalls` in the E2E runner from `approvalFault === 'sibling-approval' ? 2 : 1` to `? 1 : 1` (leave the `expectedExecutions` site untouched) and re-run: the new anchored pin must red (1 failed | 45 passed). Restore the runner. The new pin uses a whitespace-only gap (`\s*`) rather than a spanning `[\s\S]*?` precisely so it cannot reach past its own site to the `expectedExecutions` ternary and mask the narrowed count — the spanning form was confirmed to stay green under the same mutation. The doc changes are prose-only; confirm the English and Chinese versions say the same thing and that Prettier passes on both.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — docs and a test pin, no user-visible/TUI surface. Mutation witness: with the runner unmutated the suite is 46 passed; with `expectedOriginalPlanCalls` narrowed to `? 1 : 1` the suite is 1 failed | 45 passed, the failure being the new `const expectedOriginalPlanCalls =\s*approvalFault === 'sibling-approval'\s*\?\s*2\s*:\s*1` pin. Prettier `--check` passes on all three changed files.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Local unit tests only (Node 22, vitest via the dedicated `scripts/tests` config). No real-stack run is needed: this PR changes no runner behavior, only a contract pin and design-doc prose.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: essentially none — the only executable change is an additional source-text contract pin; the rest is documentation prose. The new pin is strictly more discriminating than the bare `? 2` check it complements.
- Not validated / out of scope: the barrier per-member action ↔ call binding assertion (finding F2) and the deferred hook behavioral unit test are tracked separately in #15975 and #15976 and are intentionally not implemented here. No real-stack re-run was performed because no runner behavior changes.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Follow-up to #15945. Tracks the remaining suggestions in #15975 (barrier per-member binding) and #15976 (hook behavioral unit test); this PR itself closes the F1 pin gap and the design-doc evidence residual.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

这是 #15945（A3 混合兄弟审批崩溃臂）的合入后后续。它闭合该 PR 合入后验证中仍成立的评审证据残留与 fast-tier 钉缺口（F1），并更正双语设计文档中的两处表述不准。具体而言：为原始计划调用计数增加一个紧锚定的 fast-tier 契约钉；把 R1-4/R1-5 变异红重新归类为与实际观察一致；删除一句声称已存在（实则延期）的钩子行为单测；并说明捕获的 plan 顺序是 request 顺序而非模型的 part 顺序。不改任何生产代码。

## 为什么需要

#15945 合入后仍有三件事悬而未决。其一，fast-tier 契约套件只锚定了 `expectedExecutions` 计数三元；裸 `? 2 : 1` 模式同样匹配独立的 `expectedOriginalPlanCalls` 位置，因此把该位置从 2 收窄到 1 会让全部 46 个契约测试保持绿（发现 F1）——单测速度门禁没有抓住一个真机 barrier 仍能抓住的回归。其二，设计文档仍把 R1-4/R1-5 列为触发新 `decidedBefore` / `settled_at` 断言的真机变异红，但作者自己的闭合回复记录的是：那些真机见证在*更早的*恢复守卫处变红（load 路由的 cancelled/expired 守卫；采纳阶段的 digest 冲突），因此新检查是纵深防御，其承重性由 fast-tier 契约钉证明，而非真机在新断言处变红。其三，文档声称有一个实则延期的钩子匹配/不匹配行为单测，并把捕获的两调用 plan 描述为「模型顺序」，而 plan 顺序实为 request 顺序。本 PR 让证据表述与已记录的结果一致，使验收台账准确。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

跑 fast-tier 契约套件确认绿，再通过变异原始计划计数位置确认新钉承重。从仓库根：`npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts scripts/tests/managed-agent-server-e2e.test.js` 应报 46 passed。然后把 E2E runner 中的 `expectedOriginalPlanCalls` 从 `approvalFault === 'sibling-approval' ? 2 : 1` 改为 `? 1 : 1`（不要动 `expectedExecutions` 位置）并重跑：新锚定钉必须变红（1 failed | 45 passed）。恢复 runner。新钉使用仅空白间隔（`\s*`）而非跨段的 `[\s\S]*?`，正是为了不能越过自身位置到达 `expectedExecutions` 三元从而掩盖被收窄的计数——已确认跨段形式在同一变异下保持绿。文档改动仅为表述；确认中英文版本所述一致，且两者 Prettier 通过。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A —— 文档与一个测试钉，无用户可见/TUI 表面。变异见证：runner 未变异时套件 46 passed；把 `expectedOriginalPlanCalls` 收窄为 `? 1 : 1` 时套件 1 failed | 45 passed，失败项即新增的 `const expectedOriginalPlanCalls =\s*approvalFault === 'sibling-approval'\s*\?\s*2\s*:\s*1` 钉。三个改动文件 Prettier `--check` 均通过。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### 环境（可选）

仅本地单测（Node 22，经专用 `scripts/tests` 配置的 vitest）。无需真机运行：本 PR 不改 runner 行为，只改一个契约钉与设计文档表述。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/权衡：基本没有——唯一可执行改动是增加一个源码文本契约钉，其余为文档表述。新钉比它补充的裸 `? 2` 检查严格更具区分力。
- 未验证 / 范围外：barrier 逐成员 action ↔ call 绑定断言（发现 F2）与延期的钩子行为单测分别在 #15975 与 #15976 单独跟踪，刻意不在本 PR 实现。未做真机重跑，因为没有 runner 行为改动。
- 破坏性改动 / 迁移说明：无。

## 关联 Issue

#15945 的后续。剩余建议跟踪于 #15975（barrier 逐成员绑定）与 #15976（钩子行为单测）；本 PR 本身闭合 F1 钉缺口与设计文档证据残留。

prs.title: fix(core): queue same-process controller registry writers before the file lock
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Makes concurrent writes to the peer-controller registry from one process queue up in memory before they take the cross-process file lock. Writers in the same process now enter the `proper-lockfile` lock one at a time instead of all retrying against it at once. The file lock itself is unchanged and still guards writers in other processes, with the same retry budget.

This is the pattern the agent-team mailbox and task board already use for the same reason: a per-path `async-mutex` around the file lock.

## Why it's needed

#15581: `src/ipc/peer-controllers.test.ts > addPeerController > serializes concurrent additions` fails intermittently on CI with `Lock file is already being held`. It recurred on #15791, failing all three attempts in run 40685675129.

The test starts four `addPeerController` calls at once. Before this change, all four went straight for the file lock. The holder's critical section ends in an fsync, because `atomicWriteJSON` syncs the temp file before renaming it. The other three spun on the lock with a retry budget of about 0.65–1.3 s (`retries: 10, minTimeout: 5, maxTimeout: 100, factor: 2, randomize`). When the disk is slow, three serialized fsyncs outlast that budget, and the last waiter is rejected with `ELOCKED`.

Reproduced locally by delaying every `fsync` with strace fault injection:

| fsync delay | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none, or CPU contention only (one core shared with 4 busy loops) | 0 failures | 0 failures |
| 150 ms | 0 / 40 adds failed | 0 / 40 |
| 300 ms | **10 / 40 failed, one per round**, all `Lock file is already being held` | **0 / 40** |
| 1 s | — | 0 / 40 |

Pure CPU contention never reproduced it. Slow fsync did, deterministically. That fits a busy shared runner, and the failing CI case took 2234 ms.

The real callers write once per process: `qwen sessions controllers add/remove` and the TUI's `/peers remove`. So in-process contention happens only in the test. Cross-process contention between, for example, a CLI `add` and a TUI `remove` still goes through the unchanged file-lock retry budget.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

```
cd packages/core
npx vitest run src/ipc/peer-controllers.test.ts
```

The new case `lets one same-process writer reach the file lock at a time` wraps `lockfile.lock` and records how many same-process writers are trying for, or holding, the file lock at once. The peak must be 1. That does not depend on disk speed.

To reproduce the original failure, delay fsync while four adds race. This was done with a temporary witness test that is not part of the PR:

```
strace -f -qq -o /dev/null -e trace=fsync,fdatasync \
  -e inject=fsync:delay_exit=300000 -e inject=fdatasync:delay_exit=300000 \
  npx vitest run <witness test that runs Promise.all of 4 addPeerController calls per round>
```

### Evidence (Before & After)

- The new case is a negative control. With serialization disabled (every call gets a fresh mutex), it failed 5 out of 5 runs with `expected 4 to be 1`: all four writers on the file lock at once. With the fix it passes.
- `peer-controllers.test.ts`: 48/48 pass (47 existing + 1 new), including the stale-lock takeover case that mocks `lockfile.lock`.
- The slow-fsync results are in the table above.
- `eslint --max-warnings 0` and `prettier --check` are clean on both files. `tsc --noEmit -p packages/core` reports 0 errors.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

Only Linux was run locally. The change has no platform branch, and the new test uses only the real lock on a temp directory, so CI's macOS and Windows test lanes cover it.

### Environment (optional)

N/A, unit tests only (Node 22, Linux x86_64).

## Risk & Scope

- **Main risk or tradeoff.** Same-process writers are now strictly sequential. The critical section is one read and one atomic write of a file of a few kilobytes, so queuing costs nothing that matters. The mutex map is never evicted, as in `mailbox.ts` and `tasks.ts`, but it holds one entry per registry path, and there is one per Qwen home.
- **Not validated / out of scope.** The cross-process retry budget is unchanged. It is still shorter than the 5 s `stale` window, so a writer that meets a lock left by a crashed process gives up before the takeover would happen. That is a separate, pre-existing behaviour that this flake does not exercise.
- **Breaking changes / migration notes.** None. There is no API or on-disk format change.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15581.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

让同一进程内对 peer-controller 注册表的并发写入，先在内存里排队，再去拿跨进程的文件锁。同一进程的写入方现在一个接一个进入 `proper-lockfile` 锁，而不是同时对着文件锁反复重试。文件锁本身不变，仍然用来防其他进程的写入，重试预算也保持原样。

agent-team 的 mailbox 和任务板出于同样的原因已经在用这个做法：在文件锁外面套一层按路径区分的 `async-mutex`。

## 为什么需要

#15581：`src/ipc/peer-controllers.test.ts > addPeerController > serializes concurrent additions` 在 CI 上间歇性失败，报错 `Lock file is already being held`。它在 #15791 上又出现了一次，run 40685675129 中三次尝试全部失败。

这个用例同时发起 4 个 `addPeerController`。修改之前，4 个调用会直接去抢文件锁。持锁者的临界区以一次 fsync 结束，因为 `atomicWriteJSON` 会在 rename 前对临时文件做 fsync。另外三个在锁上反复重试，等待预算只有约 0.65–1.3 秒（`retries: 10, minTimeout: 5, maxTimeout: 100, factor: 2, randomize`）。磁盘一慢，三次串行的 fsync 就会超出这个预算，排在最后的那个就会被 `ELOCKED` 拒绝。

用 strace 故障注入给每次 `fsync` 加延迟，本机复现结果如下：

| fsync 延迟 | 修复前 | 修复后 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 无，或只有 CPU 争用（与 4 个空转进程共用一个核） | 0 失败 | 0 失败 |
| 150 ms | 40 次添加 0 失败 | 0 / 40 |
| 300 ms | **40 次中 10 次失败，每轮恰好 1 次**，全部为 `Lock file is already being held` | **0 / 40** |
| 1 s | — | 0 / 40 |

单纯的 CPU 争用始终复现不了，慢 fsync 则能稳定复现。这与繁忙的共享 runner 相符，CI 上失败的那次用例跑了 2234 ms。

实际调用方每个进程只写一次：`qwen sessions controllers add/remove` 命令，以及 TUI 的 `/peers remove`。所以进程内的争用只出现在测试里。跨进程的争用（例如 CLI 的 `add` 和 TUI 的 `remove` 同时发生）仍走文件锁原有的重试预算。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

```
cd packages/core
npx vitest run src/ipc/peer-controllers.test.ts
```

新增用例 `lets one same-process writer reach the file lock at a time` 包装了 `lockfile.lock`，记录同一进程里同时在申请或持有文件锁的写入方数量，峰值必须为 1。这个结论与磁盘快慢无关。

复现原始失败的方法：在 4 个添加并发时给 fsync 加延迟。这是用一个不包含在本 PR 中的临时见证测试做的：

```
strace -f -qq -o /dev/null -e trace=fsync,fdatasync \
  -e inject=fsync:delay_exit=300000 -e inject=fdatasync:delay_exit=300000 \
  npx vitest run <每轮 Promise.all 4 个 addPeerController 的见证测试>
```

### 证据（前后对比）

- 新用例本身就是负向对照。关掉排队（每次调用都新建一个 mutex）后，5 次运行全部失败，报 `expected 4 to be 1`：4 个写入方同时挤在文件锁上。加上修复后通过。
- `peer-controllers.test.ts`：48/48 通过（原有 47 个加新增 1 个），包括 mock 了 `lockfile.lock` 的 stale-lock 接管用例。
- 慢 fsync 的结果见上表。
- 两个文件的 `eslint --max-warnings 0` 和 `prettier --check` 都干净，`tsc --noEmit -p packages/core` 报告 0 错误。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

本机只在 Linux 上运行过。改动没有任何平台分支，新测试只用临时目录上的真实锁，CI 的 macOS 和 Windows 测试车道会覆盖到。

### 环境（可选）

N/A，仅单元测试（Node 22，Linux x86_64）。

## 风险与范围

- **主要风险或取舍。** 同一进程的写入现在严格串行。临界区只是对一个几 KB 文件的一次读加一次原子写，排队的代价可以忽略。mutex map 与 `mailbox.ts`、`tasks.ts` 一样从不回收，但每个注册表路径只占一项，而每个 Qwen home 只有一个注册表。
- **未验证 / 不在范围内。** 跨进程的重试预算没有改。它仍短于 5 秒的 `stale` 窗口，所以写入方遇到崩溃进程遗留的锁时，会在可以接管之前就放弃。这是早已存在的另一个行为，与这次的 flake 无关。
- **破坏性变更 / 迁移说明。** 无，不涉及 API 或磁盘格式变化。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #15581。

</details>

prs.title: feat(review): auto-verify a pull request whose review came back clean
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a built-in handoff from a clean pull-request review to a deep-verification round. When a review ends with no Critical findings and certified the scope it read, the running daemon starts a session in the same workspace that runs the maintainer verification round and publishes its evidence report, so the behavioural-evidence step no longer depends on someone noticing the verdict and starting it by hand.

The handoff is a durable, platform-neutral record rather than a hook inside one pipeline, and it has three entrances that all write the same record: the review pipeline records it automatically at the end of its own round; any external producer — another agent, a script, a CI job, a person — can record it with a new offline subcommand; and a registered watch lets the daemon observe the approval state the platform already holds, so a review performed by anyone at all hands off with no action from the reviewer. Every handoff belongs to a session and every verification round is that session's **sub-session**: the reviewing session for the tool's own rounds, the session an external producer was invoked from or names explicitly, or the session that owns a watch. A handoff naming no session is refused at the entrance rather than recorded, so no round is ever left attached to nothing. Every entrance passes the same gates, the same per-head dedupe and the same operator switch.

Ownership also gives the automation its lifetime. A watch is keyed by coordinates and owner, so two sessions watching one pull request are two watches rather than a transfer of ownership; the automation serves each owner only its own events and watches, and prunes a deleted owner's state. Liveness is decided by transcript presence, not residency, so an idle session keeps its watches and only deleting it ends them — and an owner whose state cannot be read is neither served nor cleaned up. Who reviewed and who owns the round are separate facts: the reviewer is recorded as attribution, the owner is the parent.

## Why it's needed

A clean review is exactly the moment when behavioural evidence is worth having, and exactly the moment a busy maintainer skips it. The two commands already exist; nothing connected them.

Two obvious shortcuts were rejected. Triggering from GitHub Actions after the bot approves is GitHub-only by construction, while the review pipeline already serves a second platform behind one provider registry and more are intended; a workflow also runs outside the operator's session and cannot create one. Welding the trigger to the review pipeline's own output was the first implementation here, and it was wrong for the same reason in miniature: the reviewer is frequently not this tool. Another agent, the CI bot, or a human leaves no artifact for that pipeline to emit from, so the contract had to be reachable from outside it — and the consumer had to be able to act on an event that names no local session, which the first cut silently dropped.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Build, then exercise the three entrances against a scratch workspace with the daemon's global directory redirected, so nothing publishes and no real PR is touched.

1. Internal entrance: stage a clean round's inputs (a findings report with zero Criticals, and a composed verdict whose body carries a ledger marker with its head anchor) and run `qwen review save-artifact … --workspace-root <scratch>`. Expect one event file under the host-trusted review-state directory, outside the repository, and a stderr line naming it. Withholding the marker's anchor — the state a fail-closed round persists — must produce no event while still saving the artifact.
2. External entrance: run `qwen review verify-event --pr <n> --repo <owner>/<repo> --head <sha> --reviewed-by codex --session-id <session> --workspace-root <scratch>`. Expect exit 0, one JSON object on stdout, and the same record naming that session as owner with no artifact path. With neither `--session-id` nor a session in the environment it must refuse and write nothing. A malformed head, repo, number, or a `REQUEST_CHANGES` verdict must exit 2 and write nothing.
3. Observation: run `qwen review verify-watch <n> --repo <owner>/<repo>`, then `qwen review verify-watch --once`. The judgement must refuse a dismissed approval (the aggregate is no longer approved even though the old review body still says "Approving"), any unresolved non-outdated thread, a draft, a closed PR, and a truncated thread page; a resolved or outdated thread must not block. A second `--once` at the same head must report `already-handed-off`.
4. Consumer: with the workspace carrying the verification skill, a pending event must produce exactly one sub-session of its owning session, whose prompt is `/verify-pr <n> --publish --repo <owner>/<repo>`, and the pending file must be gone afterwards. An event naming no owner must be dropped with a reason and spawn nothing. A deleted owner must spawn nothing and must have its watches and pending events pruned; an owner whose liveness cannot be read must be left untouched. Two clean rounds at one head must spawn once, whichever entrance wrote them.
5. Policy: `review.autoVerify: false` in user settings must stop spawning and stop observation while still recording events; the same key in a workspace settings file must be ignored in either direction.

Three harnesses driving the built output automate 1–4 and are recorded with their measured output in the E2E plan; they stub the platform reader and the session bridge, so they publish nothing.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-visible TUI change. The observable surfaces are a new daemon log line per handoff and the spawned session in the session list.

Measured on this branch: full build exit 0; the CLI package's type check exit 0; 200 tests across the eight touched suites plus 154 across the settings suites; ESLint and Prettier clean on every touched file. The three built-output harnesses report `SMOKE_OK true`, `EXTERNAL_OK true` and `E2_OK true`, the last including all four negative judgements and an attribution of `github:<approver>` with no session id.

One pre-existing red is worth flagging so it is not attributed here: the large server suite fails a different one or two tests on each full run on this machine. A pristine checkout of the base commit fails two tests in the same file, different ones again, and the failures from this branch pass when run in isolation. Three runs, three different failure sets, on both trees.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Local build and unit suites; the harnesses run the built modules directly with a stubbed platform reader and session bridge. No live daemon spawn and no real platform read were exercised.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the spawned session executes the pull request's code and publishes a comment. It is a sub-session of the owning session, so it inherits that session's workspace and counts against the launcher's per-caller and workspace concurrency caps and its one-level nesting limit — a verification round cannot itself start another. It inherits the isolation posture of a manually invoked verification round and adds no sandbox of its own. Dedupe is write-ahead per reviewed head, so a daemon that dies mid-handoff never replays a round that may already have published; the accepted cost is that a failed spawn is logged and not retried rather than risking a duplicate public report. An external producer's assertion that a round was clean is not independently re-checked — the caller runs with the operator's own authority, and the record names who asserted it.
- Not validated / out of scope: a live daemon spawn and drain, and the real platform read (both need a running daemon and credentials); observation on platforms other than GitHub, which is registered and declined with a reason; GitHub Enterprise targets, which the verification command cannot yet express because it has no host flag. A watch is an explicit operator registration, so the network spend is opt-in per pull request.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. One new operator-scoped setting, default on, which a repository cannot change in either direction; when settings cannot be read at all it degrades to off, preserving that loader's existing "a degrade writes nothing public" contract.

Design document: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/docs/design/review-clean-auto-verify.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/docs/design/review-clean-auto-verify.zh-CN.md) (both added by this PR, complete and synchronized).

## Linked Issues

None.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

新增一条内置交接：从一次干净的 PR 评审，到一轮深度验证。当一轮评审以零 Critical 结束、并且认证了它实际读过的范围时，运行中的 daemon 会在同一工作区起一个会话，执行维护者验证轮并发布其证据报告——行为证据这一步不再依赖有人注意到裁决并手工起轮。

这条交接是一份持久化、平台中立的记录，而不是焊在某一条管线里的钩子。它有三个入口，写的都是同一份记录：评审管线在自己那一轮结束时自动记录；任何外部生产者——别的 agent、脚本、CI job、人——都可以用一个新的离线子命令记录；登记一个 watch 后，daemon 会观测平台已经持有的批准态，于是无论谁做的评审都能在评审者毫不作为的情况下完成交接。每次交接都归属一个会话，每轮验证都是该会话的**子会话**：工具自己评审时是评审会话，外部生产者被调用时所在（或显式点名）的会话，或拥有某个 watch 的会话。不点名会话的交接在入口就被拒绝、不会被记录，因此不会出现不挂在任何工作之下的一轮。三个入口过同一套闸门、同一份按 head 的去重、同一个 operator 开关。

归属也给了自动化生命周期。watch 按坐标与归属者建键，因此两个会话 watch 同一个 PR 是两条 watch，而不是归属转移；自动化只为每个归属者处理它自己的事件与 watch，并剪掉已删除归属者的状态。存活性按 transcript 是否存在判定、而非是否驻留，因此空闲会话仍保有它的 watch，只有删除会话才终结它们——而读不出状态的归属者既不服务也不清理。谁评审与谁拥有这一轮是两件事：评审者作为归因记录，归属者才是父会话。

## 为什么需要

干净的评审恰恰是最值得补行为证据的时刻，也恰恰是忙碌的维护者最容易跳过的时刻。两个命令本来就存在，只是没有任何东西把它们接起来。

两条显而易见的捷径被否掉了。bot 批准后用 GitHub Actions 触发，在构造上就是 GitHub 专属，而评审管线早已在一个 provider 注册表后面服务第二个平台、且还打算接更多；工作流也跑在操作者会话之外，无法创建会话。把触发焊在评审管线自己的产出上，是这里的第一个实现，它因为同样的原因在更小尺度上错了：评审者经常不是这个工具。别的 agent、CI bot 或人不会留下让那条管线据以产出的产物，所以契约必须能从管线之外抵达——而且消费者必须能处理一条不指向本地会话的事件，第一版会把这类事件静默丢弃。

## 评审者验证计划

### 如何验证

先构建，然后在一个临时工作区上、把 daemon 的全局目录重定向之后，验证三个入口；这样不会发布任何东西，也不会碰到真实 PR。

1. 内部入口：备齐一轮干净评审的输入（零 Critical 的发现报告，以及 body 内 ledger 标记带有 head 锚点的 composed 裁决），跑 `qwen review save-artifact … --workspace-root <scratch>`。预期在宿主受信的 review-state 目录下、仓库之外，恰好一个事件文件，并在 stderr 点名它。把标记的锚点 withhold 掉——也就是 fail-closed 轮次持久化的那个状态——必须不产出事件，但仍然保存产物。
2. 外部入口：跑 `qwen review verify-event --pr <n> --repo <owner>/<repo> --head <sha> --reviewed-by codex --session-id <session> --workspace-root <scratch>`。预期退出 0、stdout 一个 JSON 对象、同一份记录且点名该会话为归属者、不带产物路径。既没有 `--session-id`、环境里也没有会话时，必须拒绝且什么都不写。畸形的 head、repo、编号，或 `REQUEST_CHANGES` 裁决，必须退出 2 且什么都不写。
3. 观测：跑 `qwen review verify-watch <n> --repo <owner>/<repo>`，再跑 `qwen review verify-watch --once`。判定必须拒绝：被 dismiss 的批准（聚合态已不再批准，尽管旧评审正文仍写着「Approving」）、任何未决且未过期的线程、draft、已关闭的 PR、以及被截断的线程页；已解决或已过期的线程不得算阻塞。同一 head 第二次 `--once` 必须报 `already-handed-off`。
4. 消费者：工作区带有验证 skill 时，一条待处理事件必须恰好产生一个归属会话的子会话，其 prompt 为 `/verify-pr <n> --publish --repo <owner>/<repo>`，且事后 pending 文件消失。不指向归属者的事件必须以原因丢弃、不派生任何东西。已删除的归属者不得派生，且其 watch 与待处理事件被剪枝；读不出存活性的归属者必须原样保留。同一 head 的两轮干净评审只派生一次，无论由哪个入口写入。
5. 策略：user 设置里的 `review.autoVerify: false` 必须停止派生并停止观测，但仍然记录事件；同一个键写在工作区设置文件里，无论 true 还是 false 都必须被忽略。

三个驱动构建产物的 harness 把 1–4 自动化了，其实测输出记录在 E2E 计划里；它们打桩了平台读取器与会话 bridge，因此不发布任何东西。

### 证据（改动前后）

N/A —— 没有用户可见的 TUI 变化。可观察面是每次交接一条新的 daemon 日志，以及会话列表里被派生的那个会话。

本分支实测：全量构建 exit 0；CLI 包类型检查 exit 0；八个受影响套件 200 个测试，加上设置相关套件 154 个；每个改动文件 ESLint 与 Prettier 干净。三个构建产物 harness 分别报 `SMOKE_OK true`、`EXTERNAL_OK true`、`E2_OK true`，最后一个包含全部四个否定判定，以及 `github:<批准者>` 的归因且不带会话 id。

有一处既有的红值得点名，以免被归到本 PR 头上：那个大型 server 套件在本机每次全量运行都会失败不同的一两个用例。基线提交的纯净检出在同一文件里失败两个、又是不同的用例，而本分支首轮那两个失败用例隔离运行时全过。三次运行、三套不同失败，两棵树都如此。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 运行环境（可选）

本地构建与单元测试；harness 直接运行构建后的模块，平台读取器与会话 bridge 均为桩。没有跑过活 daemon 的真实派生，也没有跑过真实的平台读取。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：被派生的会话会执行该 PR 的代码并发表评论。它是归属会话的子会话，因此继承该会话的工作区，并计入 launcher 的 per-caller 与工作区并发闸以及一级嵌套上限——验证轮自己不能再起下一层。它继承手工调用验证轮的隔离姿态，自身不新增沙箱。去重是按被评审 head 的 write-ahead，因此交接中途死掉的 daemon 绝不会重放一轮可能已经发布过的验证；接受的代价是派生失败只记日志、不重试，而不是冒重复发布公开报告的风险。外部生产者关于「本轮干净」的断言不会被独立复核——调用者与操作者同权限，且记录里点名了是谁断言的。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：活 daemon 的派生与 drain，以及真实的平台读取（两者都需要运行中的 daemon 与凭据）；GitHub 以外平台的观测，会被登记并以原因拒绝；GitHub Enterprise 目标，验证命令因为没有 host 旗标还无法表达。watch 是操作者的显式登记，因此网络开销按 PR 逐个 opt-in。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。新增一个 operator 作用域设置，默认开，仓库不能朝任何方向改它；当设置完全读不出来时降级为关，以保持该加载器既有的「降级不产生公开写入」契约。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/docs/design/review-clean-auto-verify.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/docs/design/review-clean-auto-verify.zh-CN.md)（均由本 PR 新增，完整且同步）。

## 关联 Issue

无。

</details>

prs.title: ci(release): only file issues on failure and reconcile stale ones
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Both fan-out release notifiers treated a cancelled run as a failure and filed an issue, and neither workflow had any path to close that issue once a later attempt shipped. Each notifier now reacts only to an actual failure of its build or publish job, and each workflow gains a success-gated sibling job that closes the bot-authored issue an earlier attempt filed. The shared release step behind that reconciliation now takes the issue-title prefix and the release version, so the CLI release and both fan-out workflows reuse one implementation instead of growing separate copies.

## Why it's needed

A shipped release could sit under an open failure report: release v0.26.3's VSCode companion run passed on attempt 2 while its failure issue stayed open until it was closed by hand. Cancellation also filed issues for runs that shipped nothing. Stale failure issues are picked up by the scheduled autofix agent and turned into PRs against releases that already landed, so the false report has a cost beyond noise.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

From the repository root, run `npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts scripts/tests/release-fanout-workflows.test.js scripts/tests/release-workflow.test.js`. The five new cases pin that neither notifier mentions `cancelled`, that each reconcile job is success-gated, checks out the workflow's own commit, calls the shared step with its own title prefix, and cannot turn a shipped release red. One case drives the script with a fake `gh` and two bot-authored issues whose titles differ only by workflow prefix, and asserts that only the matching issue is closed. The existing release.yml reconciliation cases keep passing unchanged.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before, a cancelled build or publish filed `VSCode IDE Companion Release Failed for …` / `Chrome extension release failed for …`, and a passing re-run left it open. After, cancellation files nothing and a passing re-run closes the workflow-owned issue with a comment. This is CI-only behaviour, so there is no UI before/after.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

The script is bash and both jobs run on `ubuntu-latest`; Windows is not a supported target. Linux was verified inside a `node:22-bookworm` container with `jq` installed.

### Environment (optional)

Unit and workflow-contract tests only; no release run was triggered.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: each successful release now runs one short reconciliation job, which comments on and closes only a `github-actions[bot]` issue whose title matches `<prefix><version> on ` exactly. A human filing the same title is never touched, and the step is `continue-on-error` so it cannot fail a shipped release.
- Not validated / out of scope: the notifier still has no dry-run guard and does not react to a `prepare` failure in the companion workflow; both predate this change and were left untouched.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The workflows grow by about 1.5 KB each, within the size-ratchet allowance, so no baseline update is needed.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15840

<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

两个发布下游通知器此前把「取消」也当成失败并创建 issue，而且两个 workflow 都没有在后续重跑成功后关闭该 issue 的路径。现在通知器只在 build 或 publish 真正失败时创建 issue，每个 workflow 新增一个成功才触发的兄弟作业，用于关闭上一次尝试创建的、由机器人提交的 issue。负责关闭的共用发布脚本现在接收 issue 标题前缀与发布版本，CLI 发布和两个下游 workflow 复用同一份实现，而不是各自再复制一份。

prs.title: test(managed-agent): cover local MCP reuse and close
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a public-API process acceptance test for two consecutive Managed MCP turns. It verifies reuse of the original local worker and MCP connection, durable tool results and physical effects, matching sanitized public and WebShell catalogs, and public close that releases ownership and stops both original processes before fixture cleanup. The change also documents the acceptance path in English and Chinese.

## Why it's needed

The existing combined extensions acceptance requires Linux Hook/cgroup setup. An MCP-only witness makes the complete public execution and close path verifiable on native macOS with the existing real MySQL, packaged Harness, durable worker and stdio MCP fixture. Production behavior and authorization remain unchanged.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Publish a pinned MCP definition, create a Session through the public API and submit two different inputs. Expect both turns to complete with their corresponding MCP results, one physical server start and initialization, two tool calls and two durable effects, and unchanged worker, Runtime and connection identities.
2. Query the public and WebShell catalogs. Expect the same nonempty committed catalog, no transport credentials or host paths, and no extra physical MCP requests caused by the catalog reads.
3. Close while both original processes are still alive. Expect a completed public close, released MCP and Runtime ownership, a drain receipt, all four storage-holder fields cleared, and both original processes gone before teardown. Missing physical effects or a retained storage holder must fail acceptance even when the model response looks successful.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A for UI screenshots: this PR changes tests and documentation. Local validation passed: root build/typecheck/bundle; all 70 Hosted CI budget contract tests; the four-case affected integration class; the final focused acceptance after strengthening the storage-owner assertion; and full Java verification with 5,095 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 18 skips, zero Checkstyle violations and zero SpotBugs instances/errors. A separate E2E comment records timings, negative witnesses and the installed-artifact baseline limitation.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :-- | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ Native arm64 process and MySQL acceptance |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ Not tested |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ Not tested locally in this change |

### Environment (optional)

Native macOS arm64, JDK 21, Node 22 and disposable MySQL 8.4.11, with a source-matched Core/CLI build and a deterministic loopback OpenAI-compatible model. The MCP server is a real stdio process; no upstream model is used. Test-owned processes have been stopped without touching existing deployments.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: one more process acceptance case adds startup variability. The measured four-case class took 113.7 seconds, fitting the existing 242-second allowance; CI timeout values are unchanged.
- Not validated / out of scope: upstream models, browser interaction, HTTP/SSE MCP transport, Windows, Linux Hook/cgroup combinations, SSH MCP and the dedicated resident file profile. User configuration management and WebShell resource/prompt operations remain separate work.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; this PR changes tests and documentation only.

The complete, synchronized design is available in [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/042337244d6356907b885fa0b983b1682e4913ba/docs/design/2026-10-21-managed-mcp-local-acceptance.md) and [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/042337244d6356907b885fa0b983b1682e4913ba/docs/design/2026-10-21-managed-mcp-local-acceptance.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

No closing issue. Related catalog/UI work: #14916 (merged).

<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 为什么需要

## 评审者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 发布固定版本的 MCP 定义，通过公开 API 创建 Session，提交两个不同输入。预期两轮均携带各自的 MCP 结果完成；实际服务启动和初始化各一次，工具调用与持久副作用各两次，worker、Runtime 及连接身份不变。

### 前后证据

不涉及 UI 截图：本 PR 修改测试与文档。本机已通过根构建、类型检查、打包、全部 70 项 Hosted CI 预算契约检查、四项受影响整类集成回归、加强存储 owner 断言后的最终定向验收，以及完整 Java 验证：5,095 项测试、0 失败、0 错误、18 跳过，Checkstyle 违规与 SpotBugs 实例/错误均为零。单独的 E2E 评论记录耗时、负向见证及安装版本基线限制。

### 测试平台

| :-- | :-- |
| 🍏 macOS | ✅ 原生 arm64 进程和 MySQL 验收 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未验证 |
| 🐧 Linux | ⚠️ 本次未在本机验证 |

### 环境

原生 macOS arm64、JDK 21、Node 22、一次性 MySQL 8.4.11，使用与源码匹配的 Core/CLI 构建和确定性的本机 OpenAI 兼容模型。MCP 服务是真实 stdio 进程，没有使用上游模型。测试自有进程已停止，未影响现有部署。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：增加一项进程验收会带来启动时间波动；四项整类实测耗时 113.7 秒，仍满足现有 242 秒预算，CI 超时值不变。
- 未验证或不在范围内：上游模型、浏览器交互、HTTP/SSE MCP 传输、Windows、Linux Hook/cgroup 组合、SSH MCP 和专用常驻文件 profile。用户配置管理及 WebShell 资源/prompt 操作仍是独立工作。
- 破坏性变更或迁移说明：无；本 PR 仅修改测试与文档。

完整同步的设计：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/042337244d6356907b885fa0b983b1682e4913ba/docs/design/2026-10-21-managed-mcp-local-acceptance.md) 与 [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/042337244d6356907b885fa0b983b1682e4913ba/docs/design/2026-10-21-managed-mcp-local-acceptance.zh-CN.md)。

不自动关闭 issue。相关目录/UI 工作：#14916（已合并）。
