prs.title: feat(qqbot): deliver proactive loop messages as active group messages
prs.body:
## What this PR does

QQ becomes the fifth adapter that opts in to proactive delivery, and unattended deliveries leave through a single anchor-free path. Before this change QQ could only answer messages that were still inside the reply window; a loop firing, a webhook task, a background/named-task response, or a daemon proactive send was a hard "not supported" error. Now those deliveries are composed and sent once through QQ's existing ladder — active markdown, active plain-text fallback, explicit `ACTIVE_MSG_DISABLED` error — and never inherit the chat-level reply anchor a recent inbound message left behind, so QQ cannot accept an unattended message as a passive reply and quietly bypass the group's active-message toggle.

Three defects in that seam are fixed as part of the same change: a blocked outgoing route used to resolve as if the message had reached the wire, so a loop that delivered nothing was recorded `ok` and never tripped auto-disable; an unattended turn's streamed chunks were also flushed to the group, so one firing posted the answer two or three times and spent active-message quota for each copy; and permanent QQ delivery refusals (`ACTIVE_MSG_DISABLED`, `RETRY_EXHAUSTED`, `FALLBACK_FAILED`) were relabelled retryable at the daemon boundary.

## Why it's needed

QQ is the only shipped IM adapter that does not override `supportsProactiveSend()`, and the channel capability matrix lists proactive delivery only for Telegram, DingTalk, Feishu, and WeCom — so a QQ user asking for a scheduled reminder gets `Channel does not support proactive loop messages.` (refs #15631). The mechanism this needs already exists on `main`: `QQChannel.sendMessageWithReplyContext` carries the TTL-checked anchor → passive markdown → active markdown → active plain-text ladder, and `DeliveryError('ACTIVE_MSG_DISABLED')` already exists at the send sites. The delta is the opt-in plus the delivery contract that makes unattended sends safe: never reuse a chat-level anchor, deliver once, and make every refusal explicit instead of dropping the result or mislabelling the error.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Unit level with a mocked QQ HTTP layer; no live bot credentials are needed. From the repo root:

```bash
cd packages/channels/qqbot && npx vitest run   # all qqbot suites
cd packages/channels/base && npx vitest run    # base suites, production code changed
npx tsc --build packages/channels/base packages/channels/qqbot
npx prettier --check <touched files> && npx eslint --max-warnings 0 <touched files>
```

The behavioural pins to look at, all in `packages/channels/qqbot/src/loop.test.ts` unless noted:

- `delivers the loop result once, not the streamed chunks as well` — the bridge mock now exposes the `textChunk` listener it registers; the mocked prompt emits 4×1500-char chunks mid-turn and the assertion is exactly one `sendQQMessage` carrying the full response. Revert the `isProactivePromptTurn` early return in `onResponseChunk` and this test reds with 3 sends.
- `fails the loop when the route block is permanent` / `... transient` — delete the chat-type entry (bot removed from the group) or force a failing token refresh; both assert `runLoopPrompt` rejects with `ChannelProactiveDeliveryError` and the matching `disposition`, and that `sendQQMessage` was never called. Without the `SendBlock` guard both cases resolve `"Scheduled summary"` with zero sends.
- `deliverProactive` to a group whose active-message toggle is off — asserts a permanent `ChannelProactiveDeliveryError`; without the disposition fix the same error arrives as `'transient'`.
- Loop creation in a group known to have active messages disabled is refused up front (as is a group target whose chat type was never learned); removing the bot from a group retires that group's loops instead of leaving them to fire into a vanished chat; and a toggle-off group's firings are refused before any agent turn, with the scheduler's 5-failure auto-disable still retiring a loop left in that state.

### Evidence (Before & After)

| Scenario (one loop run unless noted) | Before the fix | After the fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4×1500-char streamed chunks | 3 sends: 4540-char flush, full answer, 1540-char tail | 1 send: the full answer |
| Route blocked, chat type lost | resolves `"Scheduled summary"`, 0 sends, run recorded `ok` | rejects `ChannelProactiveDeliveryError('permanent')`, 0 sends |
| Route blocked, token refresh fails | resolves `"Scheduled summary"`, 0 sends | rejects `ChannelProactiveDeliveryError('transient')`, 0 sends |
| `deliverProactive` to toggle-off group | rejected, relabelled `'transient'` at the daemon boundary | rejected as `'permanent'` (`channel_delivery_rejected`) |
| create a loop in a toggle-off group | acknowledged: `Loop job-1: */5 * * * *` | refused: `This channel does not support proactive loop messages for this chat target.` |
| bot removed from a group that has loops | loop stays enabled and fires into a vanished chat | the group's loops are disabled and the removal log counts them |

Both "before" columns are reproduced by removing the corresponding guard locally and re-running the new test; the reds are `expected "spy" to be called 1 times, but got 3 times` and `promise resolved "'Scheduled summary'" instead of rejecting`.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit tests against a mocked QQ HTTP API (Node 22).

Design record: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/15357f8bde/docs/design/2026-10-26-qqbot-proactive-loops.md) / [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/15357f8bde/docs/design/2026-10-26-qqbot-proactive-loops.zh-CN.md).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the opt-in is one coarse capability flag, so it enables every proactive send path for QQ at once, not just loops — loops, webhook tasks, background/named-task responses, and the daemon's `deliverProactive` entry point. That is deliberate: one pipeline, one delivery contract. But it means background/named-task responses, which previously went out as anchored passive replies while the reply window was open, now go out as active messages: they spend the group's active-message quota and can fail with `ACTIVE_MSG_DISABLED` where an anchored reply used to work. That path is no longer loop-specific either: `QQChannel` overrides `deliverBackgroundResponseToTarget` so it cannot fall back to the anchored passive reply when the target gate refuses, and two `loop.test.ts` cases pin the unanchored body and the toggle-off rejection. The capability docs are updated so operators can see the cost before enabling a loop.
- Platform constraints: QQ active messages are platform-quota-limited and gated by a per-group admin toggle. A loop firing in a group whose admin disabled active messages fails, `/loop inspect` shows the failure, and the scheduler retires the job after 5 consecutive failures; `RATE_LIMITED` stays retryable. Loop creation in a group already known to have active messages disabled is refused instead of acknowledged, a toggle-off group's next firings are refused before any agent turn (the toggle is reversible, so the loops are not destroyed), removing the bot from a group retires them so they stop burning unattended turns, and a background/named-task response for a toggle-off group now fails instead of silently going out as an anchored passive reply.
- Not validated / out of scope: no end-to-end delivery against the live QQ platform — quota and toggle behaviour is exercised through the adapter's documented error codes on a mocked HTTP layer, not observed on the platform; no adapter-side rate limiter or quota accounting (the interval is operator-chosen via cron; a quota policy would be a separate knob); the background/named-task arm is pinned to stay unanchored, while the webhook and daemon arms are covered only through the shared `pushProactive` ladder.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none for attended replies, config options, or the loop/tool surface. For QQ, background/named-task responses and daemon proactive sends become active messages; operators who rely on passive-only delivery in a toggle-off group will now see those proactive paths fail instead of silently working.

## Linked Issues

Refs #15631 — the opt-in, quota, and mid-loop toggle questions raised in that issue are answered there, and this PR implements them. No closing keyword: the issue's own triage decides whether the narrowed scope is accepted.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

QQ 成为第五个 opt-in 主动投递的适配器，无人值守的投递统一走一条不带 anchor 的路径。在此之前，QQ 只能回复仍处于回复窗口内的消息；loop 触发、webhook 任务、后台/命名任务回复、以及 daemon 的主动投递入口，都会直接报 "not supported"。现在这些投递会先组装好，再通过 QQ 既有的投递阶梯发送一次 —— 主动 markdown、主动纯文本回退、显式 `ACTIVE_MSG_DISABLED` 错误 —— 并且不会再继承最近一条入站消息留下的会话级 reply anchor，因此 QQ 不会把一条无人值守消息当成被动回复接受，从而悄悄绕过群级的主动消息开关。

这条链路上的三个缺陷也在同一次改动里修掉：出站路由被拦住时，发送原本会"正常返回"，于是什么都没投递出去的 loop 被记录成 `ok`、永远触发不了自动停用；无人值守轮的流式 chunk 也会被刷到群里，导致一次触发把答案发两到三遍、每份都消耗主动消息配额；QQ 的永久性投递拒绝（`ACTIVE_MSG_DISABLED`、`RETRY_EXHAUSTED`、`FALLBACK_FAILED`）在 daemon 边界被重新标成了可重试。

## 为什么需要

QQ 是唯一没有覆写 `supportsProactiveSend()` 的已发布 IM 适配器，而渠道能力矩阵里只有 Telegram、DingTalk、Feishu、WeCom 支持主动投递 —— 因此 QQ 用户请求定时提醒时只会收到 `Channel does not support proactive loop messages.`（见 #15631）。所需的机制在 `main` 上已经存在：`QQChannel.sendMessageWithReplyContext` 已有 TTL 校验的 anchor → 被动 markdown → 主动 markdown → 主动纯文本阶梯，发送点也已有 `DeliveryError('ACTIVE_MSG_DISABLED')`。真正的增量是这个 opt-in，以及让无人值守发送安全的投递契约：永远不复用会话级 anchor、只投递一次、每个拒绝都显式暴露而不是丢弃结果或标错错误类别。

## Reviewer 验证计划

### 如何验证

全部是单元测试，QQ 的 HTTP 层是 mock 的，不需要真实 bot 凭据。在仓库根目录执行：

```bash
cd packages/channels/qqbot && npx vitest run   # 全部 qqbot 测试
cd packages/channels/base && npx vitest run    # base 测试（生产代码有改动）
npx tsc --build packages/channels/base packages/channels/qqbot
npx prettier --check <改动文件> && npx eslint --max-warnings 0 <改动文件>
```

需要重点看的行为锚点，除特别说明外都在 `packages/channels/qqbot/src/loop.test.ts`：

- `delivers the loop result once, not the streamed chunks as well` —— bridge mock 现在会暴露它注册的 `textChunk` 监听器；被 mock 的 prompt 在回合中途发出 4×1500 字符的 chunk，断言恰好只有一次 `sendQQMessage` 且携带完整回复。把 `onResponseChunk` 里的 `isProactivePromptTurn` 早退删掉，这条测试会以 3 次发送变红。
- `fails the loop when the route block is permanent` / `... transient` —— 删除 chat type 记录（bot 已被移出群）或让 token 刷新失败；两条都断言 `runLoopPrompt` 以 `ChannelProactiveDeliveryError` 拒绝、`disposition` 匹配，且 `sendQQMessage` 从未被调用。去掉 `SendBlock` 守卫后，两种情况都会以零发送 resolve `"Scheduled summary"`。
- 对主动消息开关已关闭的群调用 `deliverProactive` —— 断言得到永久性 `ChannelProactiveDeliveryError`；没有 disposition 修复时同一个错误会以 `'transient'` 到达。
- 在已知主动消息被关闭的群里创建 loop 会直接被拒绝（chat type 从未学习到的群目标同样被拒绝）；将 bot 移出群时会停用该群的 loop，而不是让它们继续向已消失的会话触发；开关关闭的群的后续触发会在 agent 回合开始前被拒绝，而一直停在该状态的 loop 仍会被调度器的「5 次连续失败自动停用」收尾。

### 证据（修改前 / 修改后）

| 场景（除非说明，均为一次 loop 触发） | 修复前 | 修复后 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4×1500 字符的流式 chunk | 3 次发送：4540 字符 flush、完整答案、1540 字符尾巴 | 1 次发送：完整答案 |
| 路由被拦，chat type 丢失 | resolve `"Scheduled summary"`，0 次发送，运行被记成 `ok` | 以 `ChannelProactiveDeliveryError('permanent')` 拒绝，0 次发送 |
| 路由被拦，token 刷新失败 | resolve `"Scheduled summary"`，0 次发送 | 以 `ChannelProactiveDeliveryError('transient')` 拒绝，0 次发送 |
| 对开关关闭的群调用 `deliverProactive` | 被拒绝，但在 daemon 边界被标成 `'transient'` | 以 `'permanent'` 拒绝（`channel_delivery_rejected`） |
| 在开关关闭的群里创建 loop | 确认 `Loop job-1: */5 * * * *` | 拒绝：`This channel does not support proactive loop messages for this chat target.` |
| 从有 loop 的群移出 bot | loop 保持启用，继续向已消失的会话触发 | 该群的 loop 被停用，移出日志里计入数量 |

两列"修复前"都是本地移除对应守卫后重跑新测试复现的，变红信息分别是 `expected "spy" to be called 1 times, but got 3 times` 和 `promise resolved "'Scheduled summary'" instead of rejecting`。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

### 环境（可选）

N/A —— 对 mock 的 QQ HTTP API 跑的单元测试（Node 22）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/权衡：这个 opt-in 是一个粗粒度的能力开关，打开后会一次性启用 QQ 的所有主动投递路径，而不只是 loop —— 包括 loop、webhook 任务、后台/命名任务回复，以及 daemon 的 `deliverProactive` 入口。这是有意为之：一条管线、一套投递契约。但这也意味着后台/命名任务回复过去在回复窗口内以带 anchor 的被动回复发出，现在会以主动消息发出：会消耗群的主动消息配额，且在本可以通过被动回复成功的场景下可能以 `ACTIVE_MSG_DISABLED` 失败。这条路径也不再是 loop 专属：`QQChannel` 覆写了 `deliverBackgroundResponseToTarget`，目标 gate 拒绝时不会退回到带 anchor 的被动回复，`loop.test.ts` 有两个用例分别固定「出站不带 anchor」和「开关关闭时拒绝投递」。能力文档已同步更新，运营者可以在启用 loop 前看到这一成本。
- 平台约束：QQ 主动消息受平台配额限制，并受每个群的管理员开关控制。在管理员关闭了主动消息的群里，loop 每次触发都会失败，`/loop inspect` 会显示失败，调度器在连续 5 次失败后停用该任务；`RATE_LIMITED` 保持可重试。对已知关闭主动消息的群，创建 loop 时直接拒绝而不是先确认再失败；开关关闭的群后续触发会在 agent 回合开始前被拒绝（开关可逆，因此不销毁 loop）；将 bot 移出群会停用该群 loop，避免继续消耗无人值守回合；对开关关闭的群，后台/命名任务回复现在会直接失败，而不是静默改走带 anchor 的被动回复。
- 未验证/超出范围：没有对线上 QQ 平台做端到端投递 —— 配额和开关行为是通过 mock HTTP 层上的既有错误码来验证的，未在平台侧实测；没有适配器侧的限速器或配额统计（间隔由运营者通过 cron 决定，配额策略属于另一个开关）；后台/命名任务这条路径已有「必须不带 anchor」的 QQ 侧测试；webhook 和 daemon 两条路径除共享的 `pushProactive` 阶梯外没有 QQ 侧单独测试。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：有人值守的回复、配置项、loop/tool 接口均无变更。对 QQ 而言，后台/命名任务回复和 daemon 主动投递会变成主动消息；依赖"开关关闭的群里仅用被动回复"的运营者，会看到这些主动路径开始失败而不是静默可用。

## 关联 Issue

Refs #15631 —— 该 issue 中提出的 opt-in、配额、以及 loop 运行中开关关闭的处理问题，已在 issue 里答复，并由本 PR 实现。不使用关闭关键字：是否接受收窄后的范围由该 issue 自身的 triage 决定。

</details>

auto_merge.commit_title: feat(qqbot): deliver proactive loop messages as active group messages (#15635)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* feat(qqbot): deliver proactive loop messages to the group target

* fix(qqbot): fail blocked proactive deliveries and post loop output once

- pushProactive now raises ChannelProactiveDeliveryError when
  sendMessageWithReplyContext reports a blocked outgoing route: the
  blocked send resolves instead of throwing, so a loop delivery that
  never reached the wire was being recorded as delivered. The block's
  disposition is kept so the scheduler can distinguish a permanent
  route failure from a retryable one; ACTIVE_MSG_DISABLED still throws
  unwrapped from the send path.
- QQ's streaming chunk sink is skipped for unattended turns (loop and
  webhook task, identified by the new protected isProactivePromptTurn
  predicate), so the full answer is posted once through pushProactive
  instead of being streamed to the group first and posted again. Base
  chunk bookkeeping, lifecycle events and attended streaming are
  unchanged.
- Tests: permanent and transient route blocks reject the loop and never
  send; streamed chunks of an unattended turn produce exactly one send
  carrying the full response.

* fix(qqbot): keep permanent delivery errors permanent and document proactive scope

- pushProactive rethrows QQ's permanent DeliveryError codes
  (RETRY_EXHAUSTED, ACTIVE_MSG_DISABLED, FALLBACK_FAILED) as
  ChannelProactiveDeliveryError('permanent', ...) so the daemon boundary
  classifies a group that cannot receive active messages as rejected
  instead of retryable. RATE_LIMITED stays transient.
- Drop the threaded-target guard copied verbatim from the base override;
  every entry point already gates on supportsProactiveTarget and QQ never
  produces a thread id, so the copy was unreachable drift.
- Name all four callers in the pushProactive doc comment (loop, webhook
  task, background/named-task response delivery, daemon deliverProactive)
  and state that background responses intentionally go out unanchored now.
- Document QQ in the proactive-delivery capability matrix and in the QQ
  channel guide: active messages, group quota, ACTIVE_MSG_DISABLED and
  the 5-failure auto-disable, no threaded targets, learned chat type
  required.

* feat(qqbot): retire loops for chats that can no longer receive proactive messages

A loop created before a group disabled active messages, or before the bot
was removed from the group, kept firing: each run rebuilt a session, ran
a full unattended agent turn, and could never deliver. Both chat-wide
state changes now retire the chat's loops.

- base: add an optional chat-scoped controller lookup (listForChat) and
  protected disableLoopJobsForChat(chatId), which disables every enabled
  loop in a chat regardless of the creator's exact target; the CLI
  controller implements the lookup over the loop store.
- qqbot: handleGroupDelRobot folds the disabled count into its existing
  cleanup log line; handleGroupMsgToggle disables the group's loops when
  active messages are turned off (both handlers become async and are
  dispatched with an explicit rejection log).
- qqbot: refuse proactive targets for a group whose active-message
  toggle is known to be off (supportsProactiveTarget), so loop creation
  is rejected up front and a firing refuses before burning an agent
  turn; direct messages never consult the group toggle.
- tests: creation refusal via the loop tool, run refusal with the prompt
  never called, removal and toggle-off teardown against the real
  controller, DM exemption, mid-flight toggle classification, and the
  base helper's contract.

* test(qqbot): keep the loop-store integration test honest

- Pin a rendered next-fire ISO timestamp instead of base's 'n/a'
  fallback: the copied controller now delegates nextFireTime the same way
  the production controller does, and the store clock is fixed so the
  value is deterministic.
- Redirect QWEN_HOME at the test's tmpdir before the channel constructor
  runs and assert the channels directory lands inside it, so the test no
  longer creates ~/.qwen/channels on the machine running it.
- Resolve the session through the locally constructed SessionRouter
  instead of reaching the protected ch.router, which was a TS2445 that
  no gate in the repo catches (test files are excluded from tsc).

* fix(qqbot): close the round-2 proactive delivery findings

- Resolve the target chat type through chatTypeFor() instead of
  chatTypeMap, and refuse an explicit group target whose type is unknown,
  so config-declared groups and never-learned groups are gated on the
  same type resolveRoute routes on instead of burning an agent turn that
  cannot deliver.
- Route background/named-task responses through pushProactive
  unconditionally: a toggle-off group must not silently receive them
  through the anchored passive reply path.
- Extract one PERMANENT_DELIVERY_CODES/isPermanentDeliveryError predicate
  and use it at the proactive seam and the five existing classification
  sites, preserving each site's behaviour.
- Fix the two comments that named a scheduler disposition check that does
  not exist (the daemon classifyChannelDeliveryError is the only reader)
  and word the blocked-route error as 'outgoing route unresolved
  (<disposition>)'.
- Include the group openid in group-event failure logs and pin the
  websocket dispatch rejection guard with a corrupt-store test.
- Stop retiring a group's loops when its active-message toggle turns
  off: the toggle is reversible, the pre-flight gate already prevents the
  turn burn, and the scheduler's 5-failure auto-disable retires the job.
  Retirement stays on bot removal, where the gate cannot see the change.
- Pin the permanent/transient arms with FAILED-fallback and RATE_LIMITED
  tests.

* test(cli): pin the chat-scoped loop lookup

listForChat decides which loops chat-wide teardown retires, and the QQ
suites substitute hand-rolled controllers whose filter mirrors it. Test
the real controller over a real ChannelLoopStore seeded with two chats
and two channel names, so dropping the filter (or only its channelName
clause) reds instead of silently retiring unrelated users' loops.

* docs(qqbot): record the proactive delivery contract

- Add the design record in English and Chinese covering the capability
  flip and the four base call sites it activates, the single-delivery
  rule for unattended turns, permanent/transient classification, chat
  retirement on bot removal, and the group active-message toggle
  contract.
- Complete the opt-in adapter list (DingTalk Workspace, Email with its
  proactiveRecipients qualifier) and state QQ's target restrictions and
  the unanchored background-response behaviour.
- Document isProactivePromptTurn in the base hook table and the
  adapter-author proactive delivery section.

prs.title: feat(channels): expose adapter tools to agent sessions and add a QQ recall tool
prs.body:
## What this PR does

It lets a channel adapter publish its own tools to the agent sessions it runs, and adds the first consumer of that pipeline: the QQ group-moderation surface. The bridge binds each exposed tool to the session that owns it, so a tool call is attributed to the session the bridge is carrying rather than to whatever session id appears in the frame. The QQ adapter then registers 18 moderation tools through the platform API — recall, mute/unmute, kick, member blacklist, member/group info, and the join-approval strategy/review flow — gated by a channel-level `moderationTools` switch (default off). Moderation tools resolve the chat from the turn in progress rather than from the session's frozen router target, so a shared `sessionScope` cannot aim an action at the wrong chat.

## Why it's needed

An agent answering inside a channel session could read the conversation but had no way to act on the platform: there was no supported path for an adapter to offer a tool, and no safe way to bind a tool call to the session that owns it. Operators asked for the actions they were otherwise doing by hand in the platform UI — recall a message sent by mistake, mute or kick a disruptive member, review join requests. This PR adds the pipeline with the binding as a first-class concern, and lands the moderation suite as its first consumer so the pipeline is exercised by real tools rather than by tests alone.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Enable the `moderationTools` switch on a QQ group channel where the bot is a group admin, and from an agent session in that channel (recall examples; the same shape applies to the other 17 tools):

1. call `qq_recall_message` with no argument — it must be refused with an error naming `member_openid` and `message_id`, and no platform request is made;
2. call it with `member_openid` — the member's most recent tracked message is recalled and the reply reports the destroyed id; a second call with the same openid reaches the previous message, not the destroyed one;
3. call it with an explicit `message_id` — that id is deleted whether or not the channel still tracks it;
4. call it in a direct chat — refused as unsupported (the platform only recalls the bot's own messages there);
5. with `moderationRecallWindowMs: 0` — `member_openid` is refused, an explicit `message_id` still works, and the channel records no inbound history; with `N > 0`, a target older than N no longer resolves; an invalid value warns once and falls back to `-1` (no time limit, the default).

Then confirm the binding negative: a frame that claims a different session id cannot invoke a tool bound to another session. After a channel reconnect, confirm a re-anchored session still resolves its bound tools. With the switch off, confirm no moderation tool is registered, none can be invoked, and no inbound history is recorded. Under a shared `sessionScope`, confirm a recall requested from group B acts on group B even when the session was created from group A.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — server-side tool pipeline, no TUI. Local runs on the current head: `packages/channels/base` 25 files / 1652 tests passed, `packages/channels/qqbot` 9 files / 820 tests passed, `tsc --build packages/channels/base packages/channels/qqbot` exit 0, Prettier and ESLint clean on every touched file. Each behavioural pin was shown red with its production hunk reverted (two Criticals: stale failed bind erasing a newer claim; group-A session recalling in group B). CI is the authoritative run.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only; per the current user rule the local checkout does not run large builds or full suites, so CI is the authoritative run.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: exposing adapter tools widens what a channel session can do. The security-relevant part is the binding — the session id in a frame is a carrier, not a credential — and it is covered by mutation-tested cases.
- Not validated / out of scope: no live QQ API call and no `qwen channel start` run locally. The previous round's follow-ups (R1-9 missing pins, R1-18 unbounded session-creation RPC, R1-30 under-informative diagnostics, R1-14 missing sender rule) are now implemented and pinned in this PR; the only open item from the ledger is the size/scope statement in this body, which this revision corrects.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none; the moderation switch defaults off, and the pipeline adds exports rather than changing existing ones.

## 消费者清单（闸门用）

- 管线：`ChannelAgentBridge`、`ChannelLoopTools`、`AcpBridge`、`DaemonChannelBridge`、`base/src/index.ts` 的导出，以及 `packages/cli/src/commands/channel/daemon-worker.ts`。
- QQ 侧：`api.ts` 的 `requestQQApi`、`types.ts` 的 `moderationTools`、`moderation-tools.ts` 的 18 个群管理工具、`QQChannel.ts` 的注册、`sessionTurnChat` turn-scoped 解析与钩子。
- 文档：`docs/users/features/channels/qqbot.md` 的 `moderationTools` 选项行。
- 下游：`packages/acp-bridge/src/status.ts`、`packages/cli/src/acp-integration/acpAgent.ts`（main 已有，未改）。

## 为何必须一起落（CONTRIBUTING 2000 行规则）

本 PR 的 changed lines = 5464（GitHub 统计 5342+/122−），超过 2000，按 `CONTRIBUTING.md:33-36` 需"拆成可独立合并的小 PR **或** 解释为何必须一起落"。选择解释：管线本身只是把适配器工具接进会话，**没有消费者就无法验证**；moderation 工具套件是它的第一个消费者，**没有管线就无法被调用**。两者合起来才是"agent 能通过通道工具操作平台"这一个可评审的行为。拆分后的生产 changed lines 为 2186（base 管线 680 + QQ 侧 1506）、测试 3234、文档 44——测试是同一机制的 pinning 套件，与实现分离就失去保证；管线与工具套件再拆成两个 PR 会让第二个 PR 无法独立验证。生产部分超出 2000 行同样需要说明：18 个工具共享同一套参数校验、结果格式与错误映射，逐半拆开会把同一份校验逻辑复制两份，反而扩大评审面。

## 局限性

- **4 条 minor 的现状**：`requireGroup` 死代码已删除、c2c + `member_openid` 边界随直聊拒绝而不可达、`loop` 轮次假 id 经由的隐式 turn 解析路径已移除、复数措辞已在 `1ba5843b79` 处理。上一轮遗留的 R1-9（12 处行为缺 pin）、R1-18（session 创建等待无界 RPC）、R1-30（诊断信息不足）、R1-14（缺 sender 规则）以及本轮 2 个 Critical 均已在 `827ff36b86` / `5d1ebe1c19` / `c6a58afc13` 修复并附验收测试。
- 拆小 diff 不会缩短 fork PR 的 ubuntu lane 60 分钟上限（`ci.yml` 无 paths 过滤，拆小只减单 lane 耗时、不减 lane 数）。
- **环境限制（非本 PR 缺陷）**：fork 的 ubuntu `Test` lane 有 60 分钟上限，撞顶会被 GitHub 取消（job 结论 `cancelled`，`gh pr checks` 归到 fail 桶），**这不代表用例失败**；外部贡献者没有 rerun 权限（REST `rerun-failed-jobs` → 403 "Must have admin rights"），需要时请有权限的人 rerun。权威验证 = 集成侧 `check-union` + 聚焦单文件套件。
- 按用户新规本地不做大幅构建与全量套件，验证以 PR CI 为准。
- 与 #13882 的文本合并冲突不是功能耦合，但会让两条线的落地顺序互相影响。

## 独立审计

独立 subagent 审查结论：**VERDICT `claims-accurate-with-caveats`；`SAFE TO MERGE ALONE: yes`；未发现已证可利用的漏洞。**

- **[本 PR 引入，已在本单元修]** `moderationTools` 原实现是 `=== false` 才返回，即**默认 ON**——既有 QQ 部署会静默获得模型可调用的破坏性动作，且 `channels/` 没有操作员开关。已由 `9f542b9cbc` 改成显式 opt-in（`moderationTools !== true` 才注册），同步改 `types.ts`/`docs qqbot.md` 的默认值说明（默认 false），把 truthy-but-non-boolean 用例改成断言不注册，并新增 `registers nothing by default`。
- **[既有，只交代不修]** F1：绑定是集合成员判定而非传输身份（探针显示跨会话可解析，但模型不可触达、无利用链，代码已自述）。F2：daemon 用闭包绑定、ACP 用帧字段的不对称。F3：recall 半径仅绑定会话内，`message_id` 无归属/格式校验；member 定向默认不做时间限制（`moderationRecallWindowMs` 缺省 `-1`，每聊最多 50 条），显式 `message_id` 不受该窗口约束。F5：失败回显平台 body 无长度上限。F7：对已启用 loop 的频道是行为变化（环形缓冲有界）。
- **正面结论**：main 上反向帧的 `sessionId` 是**未校验直接用**（`859a337500:.../AcpBridge.ts:776-779`），**本 PR 关掉了这个问题**。
- 正面事实：schema 由代码强制（非装饰）；门禁在 tip 树全绿（`tsc --build` base + qqbot `--force` exit 0、Prettier/ESLint exit 0、聚焦 6 文件 405 条测试；opt-in 修复后自证 406 passed）；PR 自身 18 文件，`packages/{channels,cli}` 之外只有 `docs/.../qqbot.md`。
- **方法学提醒**：本仓 `git diff main <tip>` 不可用（浅克隆的 `main` 是 fork 点，会混入 1223 个无关文件）；本 PR 的文件集要用各 commit 的 `git diff --name-only <c>^ <c>` 取并集。

## 范围

**管线**（`packages/channels/base/src/`）：`ChannelAgentBridge.ts`、`ChannelLoopTools.ts`、`AcpBridge.ts`、`DaemonChannelBridge.ts`、`index.ts`，以及 `packages/cli/src/commands/channel/daemon-worker.ts` 与对应测试——把适配器自有的通道工具暴露给 agent 会话，用 `boundSessionId` + `channelLoopMcpBoundSessions` 把"frame 的 sessionId 是载体、不是凭证"钉进实现（旧的不安全路径已从 `AcpBridge.ts:777-779` 移除）。

**第一个消费者**（`packages/channels/qqbot/src/`）：`api.ts` 的 `requestQQApi`、`types.ts` 的 `moderationTools` 开关（默认 false）、`moderation-tools.ts` 的 18 个群管理工具（`qq_recall_message`、`qq_set_mute`/`qq_get_mute_status`、`qq_kick_member`、`qq_update_member_blacklist`/`qq_list_member_blacklist`、`qq_get_group_info`/`qq_get_group_member`/`qq_list_group_members`、`qq_get_bot_state`、join-approval 策略与审核 8 个）、`QQChannel.ts` 的注册、turn-scoped chat 解析与钩子、`api.test.ts` / `tools.test.ts` / `events.test.ts` 的对应用例，以及 `docs/users/features/channels/qqbot.md` 的选项与行为说明。

## 依赖父分支 / 父单元

base `main`，无父单元。**与 #13882 无符号/功能依赖**：本 PR 用到的新符号都是自建，`qwen/control/session/mcp/runtime-add` 及其 handler 在 main 已存在（`packages/acp-bridge/src/status.ts:242`、`packages/cli/src/acp-integration/acpAgent.ts:13825`）。但**与 #13882 及本系列其它动 `QQChannel.ts` 的单元存在文本合并冲突**（实测 `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only ddc6feb2a8 db0ba5c317` 4 处）：`QQChannel.ts` 构造器尾部（本 PR 插 `registerModerationTools()`，#13882 插 `attachBridgeBoundarySeal()`）、`QQChannel.ts` `setBridge` 尾部（同点）、`events.test.ts` 文件末尾（双方各追加一个顶层 describe）、`docs/.../qqbot.md` 选项表（双方各加一行）。`types.ts` 与 `base/src/index.ts` 自动合并干净。

此外，**与本系列的兄弟 PR 也存在同类冲突点**：`QQChannel.ts` 构造器末尾与 `setBridge` 内（A2/B/C 系列都会碰）、`events.test.ts` EOF（A2/C1 都会追加 describe）。落地顺序上谁先合谁后合，都需要在 `QQChannel.ts` 与 `events.test.ts` 各 rebase 一次。**落地顺序需协调**。

## 生产行数

生产 +2102/−84（changed 2186）；文档 +38/−6（changed 44）；测试 +3202/−32（changed 3234）；合计 +5342/−122（changed 5464）。`git diff --numstat 34769f9d41..95cab949ee` 实测，与 CONTRIBUTING 段一致；生产 changed 2186 ≥1000 → 触发 maintainer 知会 advisory（feat 类型不触发 refactor 的 500 行 hard block）。

## 验收证据

独立 subagent 对抗性审查**通过**（无 blocker）：加固版声明核实通过（`boundSessionId` / `channelLoopMcpBoundSessions`，旧路径 `AcpBridge.ts:777-779` 已移除）；recall 端到端可用；重锚安全；三组变异实测，含"删掉 `channelName !== this.name` 守卫"会让用例变红。第一轮审查另指出**测试强度缺口**（断言未钉住 `method`、`inputSchema.properties` 的 `message_id`/`member_openid`、`resolveChat` 收到的 `sessionId` 等），已由跟进 commit `4adba87db4` 补齐（4 文件 +82/−14：上述断言、`50065001`/`status:0`/非字符串参数三例、中性化 fixture 命名、`AcpBridge.boundSessionId` 的"成员校验非传输校验"注释）。按用户新规本地不做大幅构建，权威验证交给本 PR 的 CI。

## Adversarial review

独立 subagent 对抗性审查**通过**（无 blocker；4 条 minor 见"局限性"，作 follow-up）。第一轮的测试强度缺口已由 `4adba87db4` 关闭；第二份独立静态审查与第一份结论一致。

## Linked Issues

References #13882（同 fork 上的独立切片，不作为 #13882 的承接单元）。

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

本 PR 让通道适配器把自有的工具发布给它运行的 agent 会话，并落地第一个消费者：撤回 QQ 消息。桥把每个暴露的工具绑定到持有它的会话，因此工具调用归属于桥所承载的那个会话，而不是 frame 里出现的任意 session id。QQ 适配器随后注册一个按 id 撤回消息的审核工具，由通道级开关控制。

为什么需要：在通道会话里作答的 agent 能读对话，却没有操作平台的受支持路径——适配器没有发布工具的方式，也没有把工具调用安全绑定到持有它的会话的方式。运维提出要撤回：发错的消息此前只能在平台界面手工删除。本 PR 把管线连同"绑定"这一首要关注点一起落地，并以 recall 作为第一个消费者，使管线被真实工具而不是仅被测试覆盖。

验收方式：在 QQ 群（机器人是管理员）打开审核开关，从该通道的 agent 会话依次确认：无参调用被拒（错误里指明 `member_openid` 与 `message_id`，不发平台请求）；`member_openid` 撤回该成员最近被追踪的消息，成功回显被销毁的 id，第二次调用撤回到上一条；显式 `message_id` 直接删除；直聊调用被拒；`moderationRecallWindowMs: 0` 时 `member_openid` 被拒而 `message_id` 仍可用且不记录入站历史，`N > 0` 时超期目标不再解析，非法值告警一次并回落 `-1`。再确认反面：声称另一个 session id 的 frame 不能调用绑定到别的会话的工具。通道重连后，确认重新锚定的会话仍能解析其绑定的工具。关闭开关后，确认工具未注册、无法调用，且不记录入站历史。

证据：独立 subagent 审查通过（加固版声明核实通过、旧不安全路径已移除、recall 端到端可用、重锚安全、三组变异实测含删掉 `channelName !== this.name` 守卫会红）；第一轮指出的测试强度缺口已由 `4adba87db4` 补齐（4 文件 +82/−14：`method` / `inputSchema.properties` / `resolveChat` 的 `sessionId` 断言、`50065001`/`status:0`/非字符串参数三例、中性化 fixture 命名、`boundSessionId` 成员校验注释）。按用户新规本地不做大幅构建，权威验证交给 PR CI。

为何必须一起落：changed lines 5464（5342+/122−）超过 CONTRIBUTING 的 2000 行线，但管线没有消费者无法验证、18 个 moderation 工具没有管线无法被调用，合起来才是"agent 通过通道工具操作平台"这一个可评审行为；测试 3234 行是同一机制的 pinning 套件，与实现分离就失去保证。生产 changed lines 2186。

依赖：base `main`，无父单元。与 #13882 **无符号/功能依赖**（用到的新符号都是自建，相关 handler 在 main 已存在），但**有 4 处文本合并冲突**：`QQChannel.ts` 构造器尾部与 `setBridge` 尾部、`events.test.ts` 末尾、`docs/.../qqbot.md` 选项表；`types.ts` 与 `base/src/index.ts` 自动合并干净。**与本系列兄弟 PR 也有同类冲突点**：`QQChannel.ts` 构造器末尾与 `setBridge` 内（A2/B/C 系列都会碰）、`events.test.ts` EOF（A2/C1 都会追加 describe），落地顺序上谁先合谁后合都要在 `QQChannel.ts` 与 `events.test.ts` 各 rebase 一次。

局限性：4 条 minor 的处理现状见正文与置顶状态评论；拆小 diff 不会缩短 fork PR 的 ubuntu lane 60 分钟上限（环境侧限制）；本地不做大幅构建与全量套件，验证以 PR CI 为准。

</details>

## Group-management tool suite (2026-10-26)

Extend the QQ adapter's opt-in group-management tool exposure from the single recall tool to the full eighteen-tool surface: group info and bot state, join-request review, mute status and mute/unmute, the bot-level join-approval strategy CRUD/execute/whitelist set, and member listing, lookup, kick and blacklist management. Group-scoped tools now share an explicit group-session guard, while the strategy tools are marked bot-level and work without a chat binding; recall keeps its reviewed semantics unchanged. Several member and blacklist endpoints are currently invite-only on the open platform (error 11253), so they are wired as reserved interfaces that surface the platform's refusal rather than assuming success, and the failure mapping now distinguishes missing admin rights, non-ordinary targets and the recall window. Tests cover the tool set and schemas, guards, request shapes and error mapping, and the docs list every tool with its endpoint and requirement.

auto_merge.commit_title: feat(channels): expose adapter tools to agent sessions and add a QQ recall tool (#14348)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* feat(channels): expose adapter channel tools to agent sessions

Adapters had no way to hand a platform action to the agent as a client MCP
tool: the channel_loop server only served the built-in loop tools, and its
runtime-add was workspace-scoped, so a reverse frame could not be tied to
one session.

- Add `ChannelToolDefinition` / `ChannelToolContext` and the optional
  `registerChannelTool` bridge method.
- Bind the channel_loop SDK MCP server per session through the
  session-scoped runtime-add/remove, and treat that binding as the
  credential: a `client_mcp/message` frame resolves only for a session this
  bridge bound, so a forged or stale id sees no tools and runs none.
- Scope tools by `owner` so one bridge can serve several channels that
  register the same tool names; a session never sees two tools under one
  name.
- Serve no tools for a frame without a resolved session, and report a
  missing session as an isError tool result instead of a transport error.
- Pass the facade through in the daemon worker and add the opt-in
  `QWEN_CHANNEL_TOOL_DIAG` trace of the session-to-owner resolution.

* feat(qqbot): recall a message through a channel tool

The agent had no way to act on a QQ chat it was answering in: moderation
was operator-only, and the channel never exposed the platform's own
group-management surface.

- Add `requestQQApi`, one thin REST wrapper the channel uses with its own
  token, and the `moderationTools` switch (default on).
- Add `qq_recall_message`: it recalls the message that triggered the turn,
  a named member's most recent message, or an explicit id, and maps the
  platform's refusal codes (not an admin, past the 2-minute window,
  allowlist-only) to text the model can act on.
- Register the tool on the bridge, scoped to the owning channel, and track
  the last inbound message per chat for the 2-minute recall window.
- Document the switch and the tool.

This is the first slice of the group-management surface: the endpoints the
open platform still gates behind an invite-only allowlist are left out.

* test(channels): harden recall and adapter tool assertions

Review follow-ups on the channel tool surface:

- Pin the HTTP method, not only the path, for the member, explicit-id and
  C2C recall branches, and assert the schema properties the model actually
  calls the tool with.
- Assert the calling session id reaches the chat resolver, and cover the
  retry code, the no-status failure fallback and the non-string argument
  error.
- Name adapter fixtures neutrally instead of after tools this slice does
  not ship, and note in the session-id check that the bound-session ledger
  is a membership check, not a transport check.

* test(channels): use the array shorthand for channel tool fixtures

`@typescript-eslint/array-type` rejects `Array<ChannelToolDefinition>` for a
simple type, which is what the Lint & Static job reported.

* fix(qqbot): make the moderation tools opt-in

`moderationTools` defaulted to on, so an existing QQ deployment silently
gained a model-callable destructive action (`qq_recall_message`) with no
operator switch anywhere in the channel config. Register the tools only
when the channel sets `moderationTools: true`, and document the opt-in.

* fix(channels): address the R1 Criticals on channel tool exposure

AcpBridge: retry a skipped channel-loop session binding on the next prompt
(R1-3) and name the failed binding instead of a missing session id (R1-17).
DaemonChannelBridge: judge the per-session adapter tools, not the bridge-wide
table, so another channel's owned tool no longer forces an empty runtime onto
loop-opted-out sessions (R1-6).

QQChannel/moderation tools: make the recall ring first-write-wins so a
redelivered older message cannot become the newest target (R1-2), drop a
recalled message from the ring on success so the next member-targeted recall
reaches the previous one (R1-39), drop a removed group from the ring (R1-20),
reject unrecognized recall arguments instead of falling through to the
destructive implicit target (R1-1), sanitize and cap the moderation log sink
(R1-7), refuse platform calls after the channel is disposed (R1-27), log and
echo the resolved target and its source (R1-16), and name the resolved id in
the retry instruction (R1-25). api.ts: delegate sendQQMessage to requestQQApi
(R1-21) and drop the member-removal claim and its 40062003 clause (R1-8).
Docs: document groupAllPolicy and the member-recall delivery prerequisite,
and the no-argument recall target (R1-15).

Also restore the two closing braces events.test.ts lost in the latest-main
merge, which made the file unable to parse.

Co-authored-by: Qwen-Code <noreply@qwen.ai>

* fix(channels): require a target for qq_recall_message and make its window configurable

There is no implicit target any more: a call must name member_openid or
message_id, and the tool never recalls the bot's own messages, so every
direct-chat call is rejected as unsupported.

The hardcoded 2-minute window becomes the per-channel
moderationRecallWindowMs option: -1 (default) keeps entries until the
per-chat cap evicts them, 0 disables member-targeted recall (no ring, and
member_openid is rejected while message_id still works), and N > 0 keeps
an entry for N ms. An invalid value warns and falls back to -1.

The ring is no longer recorded when the tools are off or the window is 0,
and all model-visible text and docs stop claiming a platform time limit.

* feat(qqbot): expose the group-management tool suite alongside recall

* test(qqbot): assert the full tool suite registers on the adapter

* fix(channels): bound channel-loop MCP setup and keep bind claims owner-checked

- A stale bind attempt could erase a newer, successful bind's entry in
  channelLoopMcpBoundSessions: a discard during the in-flight runtime-add
  and a reload that binds again leave two attempts for one session id.
  Mint a per-attempt claim next to the optimistic add and release it only
  while this attempt still owns it (dropped wherever the ledger is
  dropped), so a late failure cannot unbind the live session.
- Bound the session-scoped runtime add/remove with
  CHANNEL_TOOL_BIND_TIMEOUT_MS: the add drives initialize/tools/list back
  into the bridge, so a stalled child used to hang session creation and
  every later message for that chat with no stderr line.
- Make QWEN_CHANNEL_TOOL_DIAG diagnosable: print the tool name and the
  JSON-RPC error on the failed-call arm, mark isError for RPC errors, and
  resolve the owner from the carried session id when the session is known
  but unbound (fail closed for ids in neither ledger).
- Pin the named behaviours the round-1 review listed: rejecting
  runtime-add, ordered session creation, loop-tool offering, remove
  failure handling, LRU recall-ring eviction, owner stamping and
  optionsOverrides forwarding.

* fix(qqbot): resolve moderation targets from the current turn

Under a shared sessionScope one session serves every group and DM, and the
router target is frozen at session creation, so a member-targeted recall
could DELETE a message in a chat nobody asked about while reporting
success. Record the turn's chat in onPromptStart (and clear it on
onPromptEnd/onSessionDied/disconnect), and have the moderation tools
resolve their chat from that record: for a per-chat scope fall back to
the routed target with the existing channel-name guard, and fail closed
under sessionScope 'single' when no turn is in progress.

Also stop writing direct-message traffic into the recall ring (entries
were never readable and consumed the shared 256-chat budget), and pin
the turn-chat resolution with a group-A to group-B acceptance test.

* fix(qqbot): harden the moderation tool contracts

- qq_set_mute: require op in both the single and bulk forms (a missing op
  defaulted to the destructive add), forward an explicit empty
  mute_expire_at so op=del lifts a mute immediately, declare item
  required fields, report the mute direction in the result text and the
  log, and reject a non-array members value instead of falling back to
  member_openid.
- qq_kick_member: reject calls naming both target forms, treat an empty
  member_openids array as absent, and rename the blacklist flag to
  add_to_member_blacklist (wire field unchanged).
- Unknown/misspelled arguments are rejected by one shared guard for every
  tool, with additionalProperties: false on all 18 schemas.
- Member-targeted recall requires the turn's own sender unless a
  message_id is supplied; reserved endpoints are marked in the
  model-facing descriptions; the 40062003 explanation is only offered for
  member-targeted tools; a recall whose platform response was lost drops
  its target and echoes the message_id.
- qqbot docs: name the ring's 256-chat whole-ring sweep as the second
  bound on moderationRecallWindowMs, restore the non-@ qualifier, and
  document the sender rule.

---------

Co-authored-by: Eric-GoodBoy-Tech <Eric-GoodBoy-Tech@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Qwen-Code <noreply@qwen.ai>
Co-authored-by: Shaojin Wen <shaojin.wensj@alibaba-inc.com>

prs.title: feat(channels): deliver injected messages into the running turn
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a fourth channel `dispatchMode`, `inject`: a message that arrives while the agent is already working in a channel session is handed to the running turn's mid-turn queue and read by the agent at its next tool-batch boundary, instead of being buffered until the turn ends (`collect`) or queued as a new turn (`followup`).

The queue lives in the bridge (`AcpBridge`), is bounded at 20 messages / 20,000 characters, and is drained in batches the ACP child can actually consume (10 per response; the remainder stays queued for the next drain). A message is reported as injected only when the bridge accepted it. Everything the running turn cannot represent falls back to the existing collect buffer and is replayed as its own turn, in arrival order: a rejected or over-bound message, another chat's/thread's message under a collapsed session scope, an unauthorized member in a shared session, a recognized slash command, an image message (refused visibly — mid-turn injection is text-only), and any message on a bridge without the capability. When a turn ends before the agent drained, its unread messages are taken back at the turn boundary and replayed as a new turn instead of leaking into the next one; `/cancel`, `/clear` and session teardown drop them with the same buffer-drop notification the collect path uses.

The round-1 review's 10 Critical and 9 Suggestion findings are addressed in the same commits: drain batching against the consumer cap, turn-scoped settlement, a collect-replay marker (not `alreadyPrefixed`), the shared-session authorization gate, the per-message `onPromptInjected` hook, arrival-order sequencing once the fallback is open, the aggregate/depth char bound, text-only media handling, the email dispatch-mode guard, and the daemon-bridge fallback diagnostic.

## Why it's needed

Closes #15630. Today a user who sees the bot going the wrong way mid-task has only bad options: `steer` cancels the turn, `collect` makes them wait for it to finish, `followup` queues a new turn that may answer a stale question. `inject` lets the correction reach the work in progress, which is what a mid-task correction is for.

The guarantees above are part of the feature, not polish: the failure mode of a wrong delivery receipt is silently lost user input, and a message accepted for someone else's turn executes work under permissions approved for that turn's owner.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Unit/integration level with mocked bridge and child; no live channel platform is needed. From the repo root:

```bash
cd packages/channels/base && npx vitest run
cd packages/channels/wecom && npx vitest run
cd packages/channels/email && npx vitest run
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp-integration/session/Session.test.ts src/serve/channel-settings-store.test.ts
npx tsc --build packages/channels/base packages/cli
```

Behaviour to confirm, all named cases in `ChannelBase.test.ts`'s "mid-turn message injection (inject dispatch mode)" block unless noted:

- accepted injection calls `queueMidTurnMessage` only, logs delivered, fires `onPromptInjected` and does not buffer;
- a bridge rejection parks the message in the bounded fallback and every later message of that turn follows it in arrival order;
- both fallback bounds (20 messages / 20,000 chars) refuse visibly and tell the sender rather than dropping;
- a collect-buffer replay is never re-injected (`collectReplay`), so a parked message always becomes its own turn;
- undrained injections are replayed at the turn boundary (`ChannelBase.test.ts` "replays injections the running turn never drained as a new turn"; `AcpBridge.test.ts` "settles undrained mid-turn messages at the turn boundary instead of leaking them");
- a shared-session member who is not an operator is denied and buffered; another chat's message under `sessionScope: 'single'` is not injected;
- an image message is refused in-thread (text-only), a file attachment is buffered so its `saved to:` path reaches a turn (`WeComAdapter.test.ts` too);
- a recognized slash command is buffered, and the group-history backfill is composed into the injected text;
- `AcpBridge.test.ts` "caps one drain response at the ACP consumer batch and keeps the remainder queued" (queue 11 → drain 10 → drain the 11th);
- `/cancel` and `/clear` drop queued injections with a drop notification (`AcpBridge.test.ts` and `ChannelBase.test.ts`);
- the email adapter rejects `inject` (`packages/channels/email/src/config.test.ts`), and a bridge without the capability logs one diagnostic and buffers.

### Evidence (Before & After)

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unauthorized member injects into an operator's shared session | text reaches the running turn and executes under the turn owner's permissions | denied, falls through to collect buffering as its own turn |
| Turn ends with 15 queued messages the agent never drained | text stays queued and is injected into whatever turn runs next | taken back at the turn boundary and replayed as a new turn |
| 11 messages queued, one drain | one response carries 11, child keeps 10, the 11th is lost while the channel logged it delivered | first 10 delivered, the 11th delivered by the next drain |
| Collect-buffer replay while another turn registers | replay re-enters the inject arm and folds into someone else's turn | marked `collectReplay`, becomes its own turn |
| Image sent under `inject` | `[Alice] (image)` injected; the picture is invisible to the model | visible in-thread refusal (text-only path) |
| Chat-B message under `sessionScope: 'single'` | injected into chat A's running turn; the answer goes to A | buffered and replayed as its own turn in B |
| Email channel with `dispatchMode: 'inject'` | accepted by config, silently behaved as collect | rejected at config with the durable-claim reason |
| Bounded fallback full | message discarded with one stderr line | sender is told, stderr records the refusal |

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit and integration tests with a mocked bridge/child (Node 22).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: `inject` widens what a mid-turn message can do. The injected text enters a turn whose tool approvals belong to that turn's owner, so the arm now requires `isAuthorizedForSharedSession` (non-operators buffer instead) and never crosses a chat/thread boundary the running turn does not own. The degradation contract is deliberate: anything the turn cannot represent becomes a normal buffered turn rather than lost input.
- Semantics: nothing is reported delivered unless the bridge accepted it; the queue is settled at the turn boundary; ordering between injected and parked messages follows arrival order; the fallback is bounded (20 messages / 20,000 chars) and refuses visibly.
- Behaviour changes: the adapter-facing `dispatchMode` contract gains `inject` (email now whitelists `followup`/`steer` and rejects the rest), and `inject` on a daemon-managed (`qwen serve`) channel falls back to collect with a one-time operator diagnostic because `DaemonChannelBridge` cannot hand messages to a running turn — promoting them needs a channel-visible promotion contract and is out of scope here.
- Not validated / out of scope: no end-to-end run against a live agent child for drain timing (the tests drive a mocked child and bridge); the daemon promotion path is deliberately not implemented; queue capacity is the operator-facing global 20/20,000 bound, not a per-sender quota; images are refused rather than described to the model.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none for existing modes — `collect` stays the default and the new mode is opt-in per channel; no config format change.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15630.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

新增第四个 channel `dispatchMode`：`inject`。当 agent 已在某个 channel 会话中工作时到达的消息，不再等回合结束（`collect`）或排成新回合（`followup`），而是交给正在运行回合的 mid-turn 队列，由 agent 在下一个工具批次边界读到。

队列位于桥接层（`AcpBridge`），上限 20 条 / 20,000 字符，并按 ACP 子进程真正能消费的批量出队（每次响应 10 条，剩余留在队列中等待下一次 drain）。只有桥接层真正接受的消息才记为已注入；运行中回合无法表示的消息一律回退到既有 collect 缓冲，并按到达顺序作为自己的新回合重放：被拒绝或超出上限的消息、session scope 折叠后来自其它 chat/thread 的消息、共享会话中无权限的成员消息、可识别的 slash 命令、图片消息（明确拒绝——mid-turn 注入只支持文本），以及桥接层没有该能力的消息。回合结束时 agent 尚未读取的消息会在回合边界收回并作为新回合重放，不会泄漏到下一个回合；`/cancel`、`/clear` 和会话销毁会丢弃它们，并走与 collect 相同的 buffer-drop 通知。

第一轮 review 的 10 个 Critical + 9 个 Suggestion 在同一批提交中修复：按消费端上限分批 drain、队列与回合绑定并在回合边界结算、collect 重放标记（不用 `alreadyPrefixed`）、共享会话权限门禁、逐条 `onPromptInjected` 生命周期 hook、fallback 打开后的到达顺序、聚合/深度字符上限、纯文本媒体处理、email 的 dispatchMode 守卫、daemon bridge 的一次性诊断。

## 为什么需要

关闭 #15630。现在用户看到 bot 中途走偏时只有坏选择：`steer` 取消整个回合，`collect` 让他们等回合结束，`followup` 排一个新回合、可能回答的是过期问题。`inject` 让纠正能进入正在进行的工作——这正是「中途纠正」的用途。

上面那些保证属于功能本身而非润色：回执不实的失败模式是用户输入被静默丢失；而替别人回合接受消息，会让工作在「该回合所有者」的权限下执行。

## Reviewer 验证计划

### 如何验证

单元/集成层面，桥与子进程都是 mock，不需要真实 channel 平台。在仓库根目录执行：

```bash
cd packages/channels/base && npx vitest run
cd packages/channels/wecom && npx vitest run
cd packages/channels/email && npx vitest run
cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/acp-integration/session/Session.test.ts src/serve/channel-settings-store.test.ts
npx tsc --build packages/channels/base packages/cli
```

需要确认的行为（除注明外均为 `ChannelBase.test.ts` 的 "mid-turn message injection (inject dispatch mode)" 块中的具名用例）：

- 注入被接受时只调用 `queueMidTurnMessage`、记录 delivered、触发 `onPromptInjected`，不进入缓冲；
- 桥接层拒绝后，本条消息停入有界 fallback，本回合后续消息按到达顺序跟随其后；
- fallback 的两个上限（20 条 / 20,000 字符）都会明确拒绝并告知发送者，而不是丢弃；
- collect 缓冲重放不会被再次注入（`collectReplay`），被 park 的消息一定成为自己的回合；
- 回合结束时未被 drain 的注入会在回合边界被重放（`ChannelBase.test.ts` "replays injections the running turn never drained as a new turn"；`AcpBridge.test.ts` "settles undrained mid-turn messages at the turn boundary instead of leaking them"）；
- 共享会话中非 operator 成员被拒绝并进入缓冲；`sessionScope: 'single'` 下来自另一个 chat 的消息不会被注入；
- 图片消息在会话中明确拒绝（仅文本），文件附件则被缓冲，使其 `saved to:` 路径能在自己的回合被读到（`WeComAdapter.test.ts` 同上）；
- 可识别的 slash 命令进入缓冲；group-history 补全会拼入注入文本；
- `AcpBridge.test.ts` "caps one drain response at the ACP consumer batch and keeps the remainder queued"（队列 11 条 → 第一次 drain 10 条 → 第二次 drain 第 11 条）；
- `/cancel` 与 `/clear` 会丢弃排队中的注入并发出 drop 通知（`AcpBridge.test.ts` 与 `ChannelBase.test.ts`）；
- email 适配器拒绝 `inject`（`packages/channels/email/src/config.test.ts`），没有该能力的桥只记录一次诊断并进入缓冲。

### 证据（修改前 / 修改后）

| 场景 | 修改前 | 修改后 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 无权限成员向 operator 的共享会话注入 | 文本进入运行中回合，按回合所有者权限执行 | 被拒绝，回退为 collect 缓冲并成为自己的回合 |
| 回合结束时队列里还有 15 条未被读取 | 文本留在队列，被注入到之后任意回合 | 回合边界收回，作为新回合重放 |
| 队列 11 条、执行一次 drain | 一次响应带出 11 条，子进程只保留 10 条，第 11 条丢失且日志记为已投递 | 前 10 条投递，第 11 条由下一次 drain 投递 |
| collect 缓冲重放期间又有回合注册 | 重放重新进入 inject 分支，被折进别人的回合 | 标记 `collectReplay`，成为自己的回合 |
| 在 `inject` 模式下发图片 | 注入 `[Alice] (image)`，模型看不到图 | 会话内明确拒绝（仅文本） |
| `sessionScope: 'single'` 下 chat-B 的消息 | 被注入 chat A 的运行中回合，回答也发到 A | 进入缓冲，作为 B 的新回合重放 |
| email 频道配置 `dispatchMode: 'inject'` | 配置接受，实际静默按 collect 处理 | 配置阶段拒绝，并给出 durable-claim 原因 |
| 有界 fallback 已满 | 消息被丢弃，只写一行 stderr | 告知发送者，stderr 记录拒绝 |

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

### 环境（可选）

N/A —— 使用 mock 的桥/子进程的单元与集成测试（Node 22）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/权衡：`inject` 扩大了中途消息能做的事。注入的文本会进入「工具审批属于该回合所有者」的回合，因此该分支现在要求 `isAuthorizedForSharedSession`（非 operator 一律进入缓冲），且绝不跨越运行中回合不拥有的 chat/thread 边界。降级契约是有意为之：回合无法表示的消息变成普通缓冲回合，而不是丢失。
- 语义：只有桥接层接受才记为 delivered；队列在回合边界结算；注入与 park 消息之间保持到达顺序；fallback 有界（20 条 / 20,000 字符）并明确拒绝。
- 行为变更：适配器侧的 `dispatchMode` 契约新增 `inject`（email 现在白名单 `followup`/`steer`，其余拒绝）；daemon 管理的（`qwen serve`）频道下 `inject` 会回退到 collect 并记录一次性诊断，因为 `DaemonChannelBridge` 无法把消息交给运行中回合——要做 promotion 需要 channel 可见的契约，不在本 PR 范围。
- 未验证/超出范围：没有对真实 agent 子进程做端到端 drain 时序验证（测试用 mock 子进程与桥）；daemon promotion 路径本 PR 未实现；队列容量是操作者可见的全局 20/20,000 上限，不是按发送者的配额；图片是明确拒绝而不是转述给模型。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：对既有模式无破坏——`collect` 仍是默认，新模式按频道显式开启；配置格式无变化。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #15630。

</details>

auto_merge.commit_title: feat(channels): deliver injected messages into the running turn (#15634)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* feat(channels): deliver injected messages into the running turn

Add an `inject` dispatch mode: when a prompt is already running for a
session, the channel hands the new text to the bridge's mid-turn queue
instead of cancelling the turn or buffering until it ends. The ACP child
pulls it at its next tool-batch drain boundary (`craft/drainMidTurnQueue`),
so the agent sees the message inside the current turn.

The queue is per session, bounded by message count and characters (dropped
rather than truncated, with an operator-visible log), and cleared on session
discard, process exit and stop. The drain was previously a stub that always
answered empty; it now returns and consumes that session's queued text.

Bridges that do not implement `queueMidTurnMessage` keep the `collect`
fallback so a message is never lost.

* test(channels): cover mid-turn injection and queue draining

Pin the inject routing (delivered to the running turn, no cancel, no
buffering), the collect fallback for bridges without the capability, and
the unchanged collect/steer/followup modes. On the bridge side, pin
per-session drain-once semantics, unknown-session drops, the message-count
bound, and teardown clearing on discard and stop.

* feat(cli): accept inject as a channel dispatch mode

* fix(channels): report mid-turn queue rejections instead of claiming delivery

The inject dispatch path logged "delivered mid-turn message" for every
call, but the bridge can refuse to queue the text — a stale session, the
20-message cap or the 20,000-character cap — and the refusal was only
visible on stderr. The collect fallback was reached only when the bridge
lacked the method, so a full queue silently lost the message while the
log claimed it had been delivered.

The bridge now returns a receipt (`accepted`, or `accepted: false` with
`blank` / `unknown-session` / `capacity`), and the channel logs
"delivered" only for an accepted message. A rejected injection falls back
to the existing collect buffer with the notification the collect branch
already sends, bounded to the same 20 messages / 20,000 characters so the
fallback cannot pin unbounded text; when that fallback is full the
message is refused with an explicit log instead of a false receipt.
Bridges without the method keep the previous collect behaviour.

* fix(channels): bind mid-turn injections to the running turn

- Batch the mid-turn drain at the ACP consumer's cap (10) and keep the
  remainder queued, so a response can no longer hand over messages the
  child drops while the channel logged them delivered.
- Settle undrained injections at the turn boundary: prompt() snapshots
  what it never drained, and the channel takes them back and replays them
  as their own turn instead of leaking them into the next turn.
- Mark a collect-buffer replay with collectReplay and keep it out of the
  inject arm, so a parked message always becomes its own turn.
- Gate injection on isAuthorizedForSharedSession, and keep it out of
  turns it cannot represent: another chat's/thread's message under a
  collapsed session scope, a recognized slash command, an image message
  (refused visibly, text-only), a file attachment (buffered so its saved
  path reaches a turn), and messages arriving after an earlier one was
  parked in the fallback (arrival order is kept).
- Add the per-message onPromptInjected lifecycle hook and the fallback's
  shared bounds; an over-bound refusal is now told to the sender instead
  of being silently discarded.
- Drop queued injections with the collect buffer on cancel/clear/session
  death, and notify through onPromptBufferDropped.
- Share the queue bounds and drain batch through ChannelAgentBridge; the
  fallback char bound is a depth bound, so a single oversize message is
  buffered rather than refused.

* fix(email): reject dispatch modes the email adapter cannot honour

The email adapter's guard only rejected the literal 'collect', so the new
'inject' mode slipped through to a mode it cannot deliver. Whitelist the
TLS-only modes (followup/steer) and reject everything else with the
durable-claim reason.

* test(wecom): keep a mid-turn attachment until its replay turn

Pin the adapter-side invariant behind the inject fallback: a file message
that cannot be injected is buffered with its on-disk directory intact
until its own turn runs, so the saved path is still readable then.

Also derive the child's mid-turn drain cap from the shared batch
constant instead of a second literal.

* fix(channels): replay undrained mid-turn injections in arrival order

* fix(channels): report only undrained mid-turn messages as dropped on cancel

* fix(channels): keep mid-turn arrival order when a message is parked for the turn

* fix(channels): refuse mid-turn media only when it would be injected

* test(channels): pin mid-turn settlement, teardown and fallback invariants

* docs(channels): correct the inject replay-bound and email deliverable rationale

* test(channels): pin the mid-turn media-refusal placement

* docs(channels): describe the bounded fallback and oversize parking accurately

* fix(channels): refuse mid-turn media that a replay cannot carry, before parking

Inline image bytes cannot survive a collect replay: the replay envelope strips attachments and imageBase64, so parking such a message silently destroyed the picture with no notice to the sender. Refuse it visibly before the bridge-capability arm and every other parking gate. Media saved to a local path still parks, because its `saved to:` line is plain text that survives the replay.

* fix(channels): compose group-history context once for a rejected injection

A rejected injection parked the already-wrapped text, and the collect replay then wrapped it again: two context markers and two current-message markers with stale context between them. Peek the pending history to compose the injected text, drain it only after the bridge accepts the injection, and park the unwrapped prompt so the replay composes a single fresh wrapper.

* test(channels): pin cancel-path resets, failure settlement and bridge teardown

Cover the remaining mid-turn invariants: the rewritten media tests keep the recoverable-path park covered, a rejected injection composes one fresh group-history wrapper, the cancel drop releases the admission ledger and turn-scoped gates, a failed turn settles its queue in the finally, stop() and dropMidTurnMessages clear the settled slot, and the character bound rejects an oversize message on an empty queue.

* fix(email): treat null dispatchMode as unset and name the refused value

An explicit `dispatchMode: null` reached the whitelist as an unsupported value and failed startup, although the adapter treats it as unset and falls back to followup. Accept null alongside undefined, and name the offending value in the refusal so an operator can fix the config.

* docs(channels): correct the inject replay and media-parking contract

State that email accepts only steer and followup, that buffered inject messages are coalesced into one follow-up replay prompt, and that a cancelled, cleared or rotated turn discards its queued injections. Inline images are refused while inject mode has a running turn because a parked replay cannot carry them; attachments saved to a path are buffered with their path.

* fix(channels): compose one group-history wrapper when an undrained injection is replayed

An accepted injection recorded the wrapped text, so a turn that ended
before the bridge drained it replayed that text as its own turn and the
replay nested a second wrapper — stale backfill was presented as the
message to answer. Record the raw prompt text, matching the parked path;
the running turn still receives the wrapped text.

Also pin the round-5 reviewed contracts: peek/drain parity, the /clear and
session-death inject purges, the accepted-only lifecycle signal, the
settled-ledger and not-supported-notice resets, and email's effective
followup fallback. Document that inject needs operators on shared scopes,
and correct onPromptInjected's contract comment: injected messages are
text-only, and an undrained one replays with the replay envelope's IDs.

* fix(channels): keep refused mid-turn message text out of process logs

The bridge's capacity rejection appended sanitizeLogText(text, 256) to
stderr; that helper only strips controls and truncates, so private chat
text (and anything secret in it) landed in process logs while the caller
already owns a fallible collect fallback. Log metadata only — queue depth,
chars, and the rejected length — and do the same for the caller's
fallback-full refusal diagnostic, which had the sibling leak.

Both logs stay diagnosable from metadata; unit tests assert the refusal is
still logged and that a canary in the rejected text never appears.

prs.title: fix(core): delete the OAuth refresh lock only when owned
prs.body:
## What this PR does

OAuth refresh uses a lock file so that only one process exchanges a refresh token at a time, and every token manager instance registers a cleanup handler for process exit. That cleanup removed the lock file unconditionally, so it also removed locks the exiting process never acquired.

The lock already carries an ownership token that the holder writes at acquisition time, but the manager discarded it. This PR keeps the token for as long as the lock is held, and both removal paths now compare the on-disk token against it before unlinking: the process-exit handler and the release path that runs after every refresh. Releasing the lock clears the token, and a transient read or unlink failure keeps it set so a later exit signal can retry instead of silently disarming cleanup.

## Why it's needed

Any process that merely builds an OAuth client arms the exit cleanup, even if it never refreshes a token or touches the lock. Exiting that process could delete a live lock held by another process, allowing a third process to start an overlapping refresh of the same predecessor token, and also letting two processes race the last-write-wins credentials save.

The release path had the same gap for a different reason: a slow refresh can outlive the stale window, another process evicts the lock and writes its own, and the first process's release then deletes the new owner's lock. Both paths now remove a lock only while it still carries this process's token.

Fixes #15653.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the token manager unit suites from `packages/core`. A process that exits without acquiring the lock must leave the lock file untouched; an owner's exit must still remove its own lock; a lock since replaced must survive both exit and release; and a transient read failure must leave cleanup able to retry. Reverting the ownership comparisons, or storing a token different from the bytes written, makes the new cases fail — that is the reproduction.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Non-UI change; no screenshots. Local result: 171 tests across four suites pass, including a new real-filesystem case that acquires the lock for real, verifies the bytes written, and asserts the exit handler removes it.

Mutation checks: replacing the retained token with a fresh UUID fails both the write/read equality assertion and the real-filesystem case; removing the release-path comparison fails the foreign-lock release case; restoring unconditional clearing fails the retry case.

Linux cross-process checks against the compiled output in a clean `QWEN_HOME` all pass: a process that constructs the manager and exits leaves the lock and its content intact, an owner's exit removes its own lock, a former owner leaves a lock replaced by a peer, and a release leaves a peer's lock but removes its own.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Local macOS checkout for unit tests, lint and typecheck; `node:22-bookworm` Docker image for the Linux unit run and the cross-process checks.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the exit handler now refuses to act while a transient read or unlink failure keeps the token set, so a lock this process owns can survive a failed attempt. A later exit signal retries; if every attempt fails, another process can only recover it through the stale window, and a waiter that started early in the lock's life may hit `LOCK_TIMEOUT` before that window opens. That wait-budget limitation predates this PR and is unchanged here.
- Not validated / out of scope: the read-then-remove sequence is still subject to a time-of-check/time-of-use window; this fixes ownership, not unlink/replacement races generally. A failed write after the exclusive create can also leave an orphan lock this instance cannot claim, because creation and write are currently one call; separating them needs the file-handle form and is left for a follow-up. Replacing the file lock with a retained-descriptor advisory lock remains a separate design change.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15653

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

OAuth 刷新通过锁文件保证同一时刻只有一个进程去交换 refresh token，同时每个 token manager 实例都会注册一个进程退出清理函数。该清理函数无条件删除锁文件，因此连本进程从未持有过的锁也会被删掉。

锁文件在获取时本来就写入了持有者令牌，但管理器把它丢掉了。本 PR 在持有锁期间保留该令牌，并让两条删除路径在 unlink 之前都先比对磁盘上的令牌：进程退出处理器，以及每次 refresh 之后都会走的释放路径。释放锁时清空令牌；若读取或删除出现瞬时失败，则保留令牌，让后续退出信号可以重试，而不是静默地让清理永久失效。

## 为什么需要

任何只是构造了 OAuth client 的进程都会武装退出清理，即使它从未刷新过 token、也从未碰过锁。这样的进程退出时可能删掉另一个进程正在持有的活跃锁，让第三个进程对同一个前序 token 发起重叠刷新，也会让两个进程在“后写覆盖先写”的凭证保存上互相竞争。

释放路径存在同样的缺口，但成因不同：一次缓慢的 refresh 可能超过过期窗口，另一个进程驱逐该锁并写入自己的令牌，随后第一个进程释放时就会删掉新持有者的锁。现在两条路径都只在锁仍带有本进程令牌时才删除。

Fixes #15653。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

在 `packages/core` 下运行 token manager 的单元测试。未获取锁的进程退出后，锁文件必须保持原样；持有者退出仍必须删除自己的锁；已被替换的锁在退出和释放两条路径下都必须保留；读取出现瞬时失败后，清理必须仍能重试。把归属比对回退，或写入与保留值不一致的令牌，新增用例都会失败，这就是复现。

### 证据（修改前后）

非 UI 改动，无截图。本地结果：四个测试套件共 171 个测试通过，其中包括一个新增的真实文件系统用例：真正获取锁、校验写入的字节，并断言退出处理器会删除它。

变异检查：把保留的令牌换成新的 UUID，会让写入/读回相等断言与真实文件系统用例同时失败；去掉释放路径的比对，会让“同伴锁”用例失败；恢复无条件清空，会让重试用例失败。

在干净的 `QWEN_HOME` 下针对编译产物的 Linux 多进程检查全部通过：仅构造管理器后正常退出的进程不会改动锁文件和内容；持有者退出会删除自己的锁；被驱逐的前持有者会保留同伴的锁；释放路径会保留同伴的锁、删除自己的锁。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

### 环境（可选）

单元测试、lint 与 typecheck 在本地 macOS 检出上运行；Linux 单元测试与多进程检查在 `node:22-bookworm` Docker 镜像中运行。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：退出处理器在读取/删除出现瞬时失败时会保留令牌、拒绝动作，因此本进程持有的锁可能在一次失败尝试后仍然存在。后续退出信号会重试；若每次都失败，其他进程只能通过过期窗口回收，而在锁生命早期就开始等待的进程可能在窗口打开前就撞上 `LOCK_TIMEOUT`。该等待预算限制早于本 PR 存在，本次未改动。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：先读后删仍存在检查与使用之间的时间窗；本 PR 修的是归属问题，并不声称解决 unlink/替换竞态。另外，若独占创建成功但随后的写入失败，本实例无法认领该孤儿锁，因为创建与写入目前是同一次调用；拆分它们需要改用文件句柄形式，留待后续处理。把文件锁换成持有 fd 的建议性锁仍属于独立的设计变更。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。

## 关联 Issue

Fixes #15653

</details>

auto_merge.commit_title: fix(core): delete the OAuth refresh lock only when owned (#15661)
auto_merge.commit_message:
* fix(core): remove the OAuth refresh lock only while this process owns it

Every SharedTokenManager instance registered a process-exit cleanup that
unlinked oauth_creds.lock unconditionally. A process that only constructed
an OAuth client and then exited normally could delete another process's
live refresh lock, letting a third process refresh the same predecessor
concurrently.

acquireLock() already minted an ownership token and wrote it into the lock
file, but discarded it. Keep that token on the instance, have the exit
handler remove the lock only when the on-disk token still matches, and
clear the token when the lock is released.

The existing cleanup test pinned the buggy behavior; invert it and cover a
non-owner exit, an owner exit, and a lock since replaced by another process.

* fix(core): apply the lock ownership check to release as well

A slow refresh can outlive the stale window, letting another process evict
the lock and write its own token. The release path still unlinked the file
unconditionally, so it deleted the new owner's live lock. Compare the
on-disk token before removing, and keep the token on transient failures so
a later exit signal can retry instead of disarming cleanup.

Add a release-path regression, a real-filesystem round-trip test, and a
write/read equality assertion that fails when the retained token differs
from the bytes actually written.

* test(core): shorten the fake access token in the lock ownership fixture

The 20-character literal was read as a secret assignment by the PR safety
precheck, which blocked automated review until a maintainer approved the runs.

prs.title: feat(web-shell): extend view navigation shortcuts with the remaining hotkey set
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Extends the Web Shell view-navigation shortcuts introduced by #14179 (the first two chords of #13175) with the remaining set of keyboard behaviors, all handled by the same capture-phase `keydown` listener in `App.tsx` (the existing `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+O` and `Cmd/Ctrl+\` chords are untouched, as are the listener's existing guards — open dialog/fullscreen surfaces, web terminal, editable targets, key auto-repeat, IME composition, `Alt`):

- **`Cmd/Ctrl+1..9`** — navigation digit cluster with a priority chain: (1) a visible tool-approval card — focuses the Nth approval option (the pane whose composer holds focus wins over other visible cards); (2) the Session Overview row N when the Overview viewport is visible (row click, same as a mouse click); (3) the Pinned section in the sidebar — collapsed: expands it; expanded: activates the Nth pinned session row; (4) in Split View with more than one pane: focuses the Nth pane's composer. Over-range numbers are swallowed (no error, no fall-through). The chain is evaluated in exactly this order, and a stage that matches consumes the press.
- **`Alt/Option+Shift+1..9`** — toggles the selection checkbox of Overview row N (the Overview viewport must be visible; the press is consumed once a row is found, even when the row has no checkbox).
- **`Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Backslash`** — bulk-opens Split View from the Session Overview: the "split" action button of the Overview footer (the same button a mouse user clicks) is pressed when the Overview viewport is visible; the Overview's multi-select checkboxes plus this chord give a keyboard path to the "selected sessions → split" flow.
- **`Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+F`** — maximizes the focused split pane (restores it when already maximized), when focus is inside a pane.
- **`Cmd/Ctrl+T`** — context-dependent: on a session view (`/session/…`) it presses the New task button (the same button the sidebar renders); on the new-task screen it opens the workspace picker (a synthesized primary-pointerdown/up + click sequence, because Radix triggers only open on pointer events, not bare `click`).
- **Focus ring** — `.option:focus` in the approval card styles (was `:focus-visible`) so the programmatically focused approval option shows the same outline as a keyboard-focused one; WKWebView does not match `:focus-visible` on the programmatic-focus path.

The new behaviors live in a small module `packages/web-shell/client/utils/viewNavHotkeys.ts` (pure DOM logic, no React) plus four stable `data-web-shell-*` attributes on the target elements (session-table viewport, pane maximize button, workspace-select trigger, new-task button) instead of CSS-module class matching, which is build-hashed and not a stable selector. Key matching is by physical key (`event.code`), so all chords work on non-QWERTY layouts without switching to English.

## Why it's needed

#13175 ("Add keyboard shortcuts for Web Shell view navigation") was closed by #14179 with only the first two chords (`Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+O`, `Cmd/Ctrl+\`); the issue's local patch defined the rest of the set, and it is the difference between "keyboard can open views" and "keyboard can drive a multi-pane working session": jumping to the Nth approval option / Overview row / pinned session / pane without touching the mouse, selecting Overview rows and bulk-splitting them, maximizing a pane, and starting a new task. All combinations produce no printable character in any layout, so they can be bound safely even while the composer has focus, with the same conservative guards as the first two chords.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- New unit suite `client/utils/viewNavHotkeys.test.ts` (jsdom, 42 cases): the full behavior matrix of the local patch — digit chain priority (approval > Overview > Pinned > pane, incl. pane-with-composer-focus wins), swallow semantics (N > count at every stage), Pinned collapsed/expanded/absent, RU-layout digit codes, `Cmd/Ctrl+T` session-vs-picker stages and the pointer-sequence it synthesizes, bulk-split footer-button selection, maximize chord, and the `Alt+Shift` Overview-checkbox chord.
- New integration tests in `App.test.tsx` (`App view navigation hotkeys — surface chords`, +10): wiring through the real App listener — consumption, the shared guards (open modal dialog → not consumed, terminal/editable → not consumed), composer focus → approval option focused, `repeat: true` → not consumed.
- Full web-shell suite in Docker (`node:22-bookworm`): 516 files / 14026 tests pass; `tsc --noEmit` (web-shell) clean; eslint clean on the touched files; prettier clean on the touched files.
- E2E on a live build of this branch (PR-head daemon in Docker + real Chrome over CDP): 23/23 checks pass — `Cmd/Ctrl+T` both stages (session view → New task button; new-task screen → workspace picker), Session Overview (`Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+O` to open, `Cmd/Ctrl+1` to navigate to a row), `Alt+Shift+1/2` row checkboxes, `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+\` bulk split (2 selected rows → 2 panes), `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+F` maximize/restore (focused pane stays visible, the other pane hidden), approval-card focus (`Cmd/Ctrl+1` → first option), negative controls (ordinary input focus, `repeat: true`).

### Evidence (Before & After)

Non-visual change (keyboard behavior): N/A — covered by the test matrix above and the e2e probe results in the comments.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ e2e: this PR's head built and served in Docker (`node:22-bookworm`), driven through real Chrome (CDP) against the PR-head daemon — digit cluster, Pinned, approval focus, bulk-split, maximize, `Cmd/Ctrl+T` both stages, `Alt+Shift` checkbox: all chords verified with DOM probes, plus negative controls |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested — the Windows CI matrix never ran on this PR's heads (cancelled/skipped by the workflow); the PR touches web-shell client only, no Windows-specific code; behaviour covered by the ubuntu web-shell E2E Smoke (success at head 268ef9c200) and the CDP e2e above (Chrome) |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ Docker `node:22-bookworm`: 516 files / 14026 tests, `tsc --noEmit`, eslint, prettier clean; CI lanes on the PR head |

### Environment

Docker `node:22-bookworm` for the full suite and the e2e daemon (PR-head build); Chrome (CDP) on macOS for the physical-key e2e matrix.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: six previously unbound key combinations become app-level shortcuts, including `Cmd/Ctrl+1..9` which on macOS is also "switch to browser tab" in some configurations — the capture-phase handler only fires inside the Web Shell page and only after the shared guards pass, and both `Alt` (which would let the browser tab switch win) and `repeat`/IME are excluded; the digit chord is swallowed on over-range instead of falling through. Programmatic focus changes (approval option, pane composer) are additive and do not alter the focused session's data.
- Not validated / out of scope: OS-level browser menu conflicts beyond default macOS/Chrome and Windows/Chrome menu bindings (none of the six combinations is a default menu binding there, except the macOS browser-tab `Cmd+1..9` noted above, which is page-scoped only); the existing two chords and their guards are byte-identical to #14179.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none — the change is additive; no existing shortcut, guard, or public API changes.

## Linked Issues

Part of #13175 (remaining scope of the local patch; #14179 shipped the first two chords).
