issues.title: main does not compile: PersistRequest::ClearCheckpoint is now dead, and every PR's required checks fail on it
issues.body:
### What happened

`main` does not compile under the workspace's own lint policy. Every pull request's **required** checks now fail on the same error, so no external contribution can merge:

```
error: variant `ClearCheckpoint` is never constructed
  --> crates/tui/src/tui/persistence_actor.rs:80:5
```

Affected required checks on #7147: `Lint` (→ `Run clippy`), `Test (windows-latest)`, `npm wrapper smoke (ubuntu-latest)`. `Test (ubuntu-latest)` fails at `Build canonical executable for acceptance tests` and `MSRV check (1.89)` at `cargo +1.89 check`, same error.

The cause is a dead variant, not anything in the PRs: `PersistRequest::ClearCheckpoint` lost its last non-test constructor, every remaining construction sits inside `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (line 843 onwards), and `[workspace.lints.rust] warnings = "deny"` plus `RUSTFLAGS: -Dwarnings` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` turn that into a hard error.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
git fetch origin main
git checkout 6a08f0312      # current origin/main
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --lib --locked
# error: variant `ClearCheckpoint` is never constructed

git checkout c4a4f42e9      # its parent
scripts/dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-tui --lib --locked
# Finished — compiles
```

So the breakage is exactly one commit wide.

### Which commit

`6a08f0312 fix(session): retain recovery when reset snapshot fails [skip ci]`

It rewrote `persist_full_reset_snapshot` in `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/session_state.rs`; the replaced branch was the only production call site:

```diff
-    if let Some(session_id) = app.current_session_id.clone() {
-        persistence_actor::persist(PersistRequest::ClearCheckpoint { session_id });
-    }
+    let session = match session {
+        Ok(session) => session,
+        Err(err) => { /* ...add_message(Error)... */ return; }
+    };
```

That removal is intentional by the commit's own description ("retain recovery when reset snapshot fails" — the old branch cleared the checkpoint precisely when the replacement could not be built). What was missed is that the variant, its `PersistRequest` dispatch arms (lines 430/572/648), and its queue-coalescing paths are now unreachable from production code, and only the test module still names it.

### Why CI did not catch it

`ci.yml` triggers on `pull_request` and `workflow_dispatch` only — a push to `main` runs no build or test workflow at all (that is by design; CONTRIBUTING says the exhaustive gate runs once at release time via `gh workflow run ci.yml --expected_sha=…`). The commit also carries `[skip ci]`, which CONTRIBUTING explicitly forbids — but on a `main` push it is not what let this through, since nothing was scheduled either way.

The net effect is a window where `main` was red for its own lint gate and nobody could see it: the mirror/harvest workflows ran, the next PR did not.

### Suggested fix

One of:

1. **Delete the now-unused variant** — `ClearCheckpoint`, its `PersistRequest` match arms, its `PendingQueue`/`pending` handling, and its tests. Cleanest if the reset path genuinely never needs it again.
2. **Keep it with a stated reason** — `#[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]` on the variant plus a comment saying which future caller owns it. Cheap, but leaves a variant nobody constructs.
3. **Keep it and give it back its caller** — if clearing a stale checkpoint on a failed reset is still wanted (the removed comment argued it was: "Never let an older in-flight checkpoint resurrect the session the user just discarded"), reinstate the call instead of deleting the variant, which would also restore that behaviour.

I lean to (1) or (3) depending on which behaviour is correct; (2) only as a stop-gap to unblock the queue.

### For the process question

Two separate gaps, worth deciding on together:

- **The required checks are right, the invariant is not enforced where it broke.** `protect-main` already requires `Lint`, `Test (windows-latest)` and `npm wrapper smoke (ubuntu-latest)`, and the ruleset's `bypass_actors` is empty — yet `6a08f0312` and its four siblings landed as direct pushes with no PR and no CI. Whatever grants that (repository-admin role, or an org-level setting the ruleset does not expose) is what needs to change if direct pushes are meant to stay verified.
- **Nothing verifies `main` between releases.** With no `push` trigger, the only whole-workspace check is the manual pre-release dispatch. A cheap guard would be a `push: branches: [main]` job running just `cargo check`/`clippy` on the touched crates, or a scheduled run of the existing `Lint` job — minutes, and it would have caught this within the hour.

Cheap and durable: run the `Lint` job (or a `cargo check --workspace`) on every push to `main`, and require it alongside the PR checks. The release gate can stay as the exhaustive one.

### Environment

`main` at `6a08f0312`, macOS 26 (arm64), Rust per `rust-toolchain`. Reported while preparing #7147.

issues.title: main: three tests fail Test (ubuntu-latest) on every PR (stale providers golden, half-installed context-window fixtures)

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: New external report awaiting maintainer triage; repro, logs and version output help

issues.body:
### What happened

`Test (ubuntu-latest)` fails on every open PR with the same three tests, independent of what the PR changes:

```
route::export::tests::golden_providers_export_matches_registry                      (codewhale-config)
commands::config_policy_status_tests::tests::status_report_localizes_the_complete_japanese_surface  (codewhale-tui)
tui::app::tests::test_update_model_compaction_budget                                (codewhale-tui)
```

Seen on #7149, #7150 (run 41016661593) and #7151 (run 41019507563), all with PR base `6dd9af54c`. Nothing after that base on current `main` (`c96f4edc5`) touches the files involved, so the failures should still reproduce there.

The `main` compile error from #7148 is fixed by `7198de9` (Lint passes on these PRs again). These three test failures are separate from it.

### 1. `golden_providers_export_matches_registry`: golden file out of date

```
panicked at crates/config/src/route/export.rs:311:9:
assertion `left == right` failed: update providers-export.golden.json from ProvidersExport::from_registry
```

`0e3677b feat(catalog): pin kimi-k3.1-pro, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash and gpt-6.1-terra in the offline seed` added models to the bundled catalog but did not update `crates/config/src/route/providers-export.golden.json`. I compared the `left` and `right` values in the log route by route. The only differences are models that the registry lists and the golden file does not:

| route | missing from golden |
| --- | --- |
| `minimax`, `minimax-anthropic` | `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` |
| `moonshot` | `kimi-k3.1-pro`, `kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed` |
| `openai` | `gpt-6.1-terra` |

That commit verified with `cargo test -p codewhale-config --lib --locked catalog`, and that filter does not select `route::export::tests`.

Fix: regenerate with the existing helper,

```bash
WRITE_GOLDEN=1 scripts/dev-cargo.sh test -p codewhale-config --lib --locked \
  write_golden_providers_export_when_requested -- --ignored
```

### 2. `status_report_localizes_the_complete_japanese_surface`: fixture sets only the source

```
panicked at crates/tui/src/commands/config_policy_status_tests.rs:538:13:
missing StatusContextSourceProviderReported: ...
```

`da026a2 fix(tui): carry the resolved context window with its source ...` made `effective_context_window_source()` read the source from `active_context_window` when one is installed. The fixture at `config_policy_status_tests.rs:507` sets only

```rust
app.active_context_window_source = crate::route_runtime::ContextWindowSource::ProviderReported;
```

so `/status` shows a different provenance label and the Japanese provider-reported label is missing.

`5e9cefd` already fixed three fixtures for this reason, including `status_report_names_context_window_source_and_override_key` in the same file, but missed this one. Installing the window next to its source, as `5e9cefd` did, should fix it:

```rust
app.active_context_window = Some(crate::route_runtime::ContextWindowResolution {
    tokens: /* any window */,
    source: crate::route_runtime::ContextWindowSource::ProviderReported,
});
```

### 3. `test_update_model_compaction_budget`: probably the same change (not verified locally)

```
panicked at crates/tui/src/tui/app/tests.rs:4935:5:
a large-context model (61440) should budget more than an unknown model (62976)
```

The test at `app/tests.rs:4910` clears `active_route_limits` and `active_context_window_override`, then switches `app.model` between `deepseek-v4-pro` and `unknown-test-model`. It never clears `active_context_window`. After `da026a2`, `effective_budget_route()` prefers the installed window. If `App::new` leaves one installed, both models are budgeted against the same window and the per-model comparison no longer tests anything. I have not confirmed this by running the test. Clearing `app.active_context_window` in the fixture (or installing a window per model) is the likely fix.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
git checkout origin/main
scripts/dev-test.sh config golden_providers_export_matches_registry
scripts/dev-test.sh tui status_report_localizes_the_complete_japanese_surface
scripts/dev-test.sh tui test_update_model_compaction_budget
```

### Why this reached PRs

`ci.yml` does not run on pushes to `main`. `da026a2` also carries `[skip ci]`. Because of both, the first runs of these tests were on contributor PRs, where they look like regressions caused by the PR.

prs.title: test: repair three tests broken on main by catalog and context-window changes
prs.body:
Closes #7154

These three tests fail in `Test (ubuntu-latest)` on every open PR. This change fixes only the fixtures and the golden file. No production code changes.

- **`golden_providers_export_matches_registry`**: `0e3677b` added `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash`, `kimi-k3.1-pro`, `kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed` and `gpt-6.1-terra` to the bundled catalog but did not update `providers-export.golden.json`. Regenerated with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1 ... write_golden_providers_export_when_requested -- --ignored`. The diff adds only those model rows.
- **`status_report_localizes_the_complete_japanese_surface`**: the fixture set only `active_context_window_source`. Since `da026a2`, the source comes from `active_context_window`. The fixture now installs the window next to its source, the same fix `5e9cefd` made to three sibling fixtures.
- **`test_update_model_compaction_budget`**: `App::new` installs a resolved window for the default model, and `effective_budget_route()` prefers it, so `deepseek-v4-pro` and the unknown model were budgeted against the same window. In production, `/model` refreshes the window (`commands/groups/core/core.rs`). The test assigns `app.model` directly, so it now clears `active_context_window` along with the other pinned inputs.

### Verification

- Before the change, on `c96f4edc5`: both TUI tests fail (`0 passed; 2 failed`).
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --lib --locked -- config_policy_status_tests compaction_budget context_window`: `30 passed; 0 failed`
- `cargo test -p codewhale-config --lib --locked route::export`: `5 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean

prs.title: chore(deps): bump codewhale-hq/Codewhale/scripts/github-action/publish from c2a48723285c48978279f6c10672bbade49cc0cb to b92540d882b8e7c66389aa35e5fa0c3c178fe4ce
prs.body:
Bumps [codewhale-hq/Codewhale/scripts/github-action/publish](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/codewhale) from c2a48723285c48978279f6c10672bbade49cc0cb to b92540d882b8e7c66389aa35e5fa0c3c178fe4ce.
Changelog

Sourced from codewhale-hq/Codewhale/scripts/github-action/publish's changelog.

Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

[Unreleased]

Added

  • Runcrate is a bundled provider: runcrate reaches the OpenAI-compatible host at https://api.runcrate.ai/v1 with RUNCRATE_API_KEY, and model ids come from its public GET /v1/models listing. Thanks @​heydryft for the request and the vendor details. (#7085)

  • MCP connection status reaches the model: one existing history snapshot now records permitted configured, connecting, failed, authorization-required, unknown and connected servers, with bounded inert names and no raw errors. Stale status and server guidance are withdrawn on contention, configuration/scope changes and restore; observation does not connect servers or promise callable tools. (#6866)

  • Bundled-skill policy: [skills.bundled] separates automatic, authoritative and disabled installation from discovery, with per-name selection, disable and explicit-only controls. Aliases share policy; disabled shipped copies reveal user alternatives. Modified and managed files remain intact, and doctor plus /skills inspect show the effective policy. (#7066)

  • Configurable skill routing index: [skills] listing_max_description_chars and listing_budget_fraction control the shared parent/child catalogue. Defaults stay 400 characters and 5% of the route window, within the existing total bounds. Load warnings, localized inspect notes and /context explain shortening; full skill loading stays available. (#7073)

  • Compact approvals keep their authority visible: cards show three choices and default to Deny. An exact saved rule requires its scope preview on screen. Shortcuts for additional actions require opening Details; a hidden saved-rule choice never falls back to granting the session.

  • Quicker everyday navigation: top-level help separates everyday and advanced commands, doctor --all expands path/backend details, and the launch screen labels how to resume recent work. Up selects the newest recent session. Whale cameos stay out of transcript text.

  • Session-window diagnostics: the audit log records when a saved window starts a new journal root while retaining the previous branch, helping distinguish window replacement from lost durable history. session.window.rerooted now names a cause (engine_projection, session_restore or unattributed) and also fires when a journal with entries has no active path. (#7142)

  • Usage reporting counts models, tokens and tools: when usage reporting is on, each session now also reports, per provider and model, its turns by outcome, input, output and prompt-cache tokens, and turn-time buckets, plus how many times each built-in tool ran and failed. A model is named only when it is in Codewhale's bundled public model catalog; custom, local and fine-tuned names are sent as other, and MCP and plugin tools as mcp or other. No prompts, outputs, tool arguments or paths are sent. Runs under CI or the GitHub Action report the ci session source. The first-run notice is shown once more to describe this. DO_NOT_TRACK=1 now turns usage reporting off for that run, like CODEWHALE_TELEMETRY=0; codewhale config set telemetry false still turns it off for good. See docs/TELEMETRY.md.

  • exec and doctor follow the TUI onto local Ollama: with no cloud key and no explicit route, codewhale exec uses a running local Ollama chat model and says so, and codewhale doctor --probe-local checks that route. Nothing is saved. (#7115)

  • Thinking starts at auto: new configurations and the built-in default use reasoning_effort = "auto" instead of max; an effort you set is never changed.

  • DSH Git review scopes: the extension host brokers bounded, read-only Git metadata to reviewed DSH plugins through a new git_review_scope action (extension-host policy v8).

  • Safer uninstall: program removal never edits shell profiles; matching Codewhale PATH blocks are reported for manual cleanup. Data purge requires a receipted removal in the same confirmed run. Both Unix installers reject unsafe or managed destinations before creating them and keep shell profiles unchanged. Uninstall instructions now match the explicit-home purge scope in English and Chinese.

  • Nested and deletable threads (Runtime API): a fork (including a backtrack fork) records parent_thread_id, POST /v1/threads accepts one naming an existing thread, and GET /v1/threads/summary returns it so clients can nest child conversations. DELETE /v1/threads/{id} removes an idle thread with its turns, items, events and goal, and its saved session unless another thread shares it or a terminal holds it open; a running thread answers 409.

  • Hunk actions in Review (Runtime API): POST /v1/git/stage, /v1/git/unstage and /v1/git/discard take a patch holding hunks of the one path in paths and apply only those hunks through git apply, under the same expect preconditions as whole-path writes. A patch that no longer applies fails with git's message and writes nothing; renames, mode changes and binary patches are refused. The tasks tool can also suggest a task, shown as a Start/Hide card, without starting anything.

  • Live /models ceilings reach the route: a provider that states per-model context and output limits in its own /models body now keeps them instead of falling back to the legacy 128K window. OpenAI limit blocks, flat context_length / context_window / max_model_len / max_context_length fields, max_output_tokens / max_completion_tokens, and a relay metadata block (context_limit, context_budget, output_budget) are read; metadata.context_limit outranks context_budget because the first is the model capability and the second the share one deployment accepts. Each field is parsed on its own, so an unreadable one costs only its own candidate instead of hiding the readable fields below it.

  • Change mode and permissions while the agent works: Tab, Shift+Tab, /mode, the hotbar and /config mode no longer refuse while a turn is running. A response that is already streaming is not restarted; the change applies at the agent's next step in the same turn (before its next tool batch, at every approval gate, and before its next model request, which carries the new mode notice). The status line says so until it applies. A call still waiting for approval goes back to the model under the new posture, and a call you already approved runs only if the new posture is equal or broader. Model, thinking level and provider stay locked until the turn ends.

  • Steering interrupts thinking: a steer (Ctrl+Enter, or Enter twice after queueing) now closes the in-flight model request at once, whether the model is waiting on headers, reasoning, writing text or emitting a tool call, and continues the same turn with your message. Text already shown is kept as interrupted output; unfinished reasoning and partial tool calls are discarded, never run.

  • Modern MCP client: MCP servers now connect through the official MCP SDK (2.4) behind Codewhale's Rust broker by default (mcp_backend = "host"; "rust" stays available for one release). Servers that speak the 2026-07-28 revision are discovered with server/discover; other stdio and HTTP servers fall back to the legacy initialize handshake, and configured SSE servers keep theirs. Rust keeps process, network, credential, catalog, approval and cancellation authority.

  • DeepSeek Harness plugins: reviewed DSH plugins (definition API pinned to DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 in a shared compatibility table) run in the Native extension host. Tool output is validated against its declared schema, unsupported options are refused instead of ignored, and plugin commands can submit a prompt with visible plugin attribution. Terminal command receipts are kept in thread snapshots without entering model history. Changing the compatibility table invalidates earlier trust. A newly enabled plugin's tools are offered on the first turn: the turn waits up to 10 seconds for the plugin host to finish loading instead of adding them only from the next turn. Plugin UI views stay disabled, and the import receipt says why: WebKit's network restrictions do not stop WebRTC, so plugin UI waits for an isolated renderer. A plugin tool can call ctx.sessions.flush(exec.agent.session) to have the Engine save the conversation so far before it continues (Runtime, terminal and exec sessions); it reports failure instead of claiming a save. Installing a plugin whose bytes changed after review now returns a 409 conflict instead of a server error. A plugin tool can ask you a question with ctx.userQuestions.ask and gets back the options you picked, your own text, or a skip; the question shows like any other Codewhale question in the terminal and through the Runtime API. A plugin tool can start a child agent with ctx.subagents.startActivation (the spawn provider): the child runs through Codewhale's own sub-agent manager, needs the same approval as the model's agent tool, can carry an extra persona section and a narrower tool list set in its agent/created handler, and returns its result to the plugin.

  • MCP catalogs stay fresh: a server's tools, resources, prompts and skills are rediscovered on their own connection when an advertised ttlMs expires or the server sends a list-changed notice. A tool resolved against the old catalog is refused with "retry the call", a removed tool cannot run, and a failed refresh reconnects instead of serving stale entries. Catalogs are never shared across servers, credentials or reconnects.

  • MCP Skills extension: servers that advertise the published Skills extension have their skills listed in list_mcp_resources. Listing never activates a skill, and reading a skill file is refused unless its size and sha256 digest match the listing. MCP skills do not yet join /skills.

  • Updates install themselves: release-binary installs check for a new release every 6 hours (was 1), download and checksum-verify it in the background, and apply it the next time codewhale starts, never during a session. One line says Updated to v… · What's new: … · Undo: codewhale update --rollback. Until releases are signed, the download waits for your OK (one [y/N] question at the next start, or /update install); a release with a valid Ed25519 manifest signature applies on its own. codewhale update --rollback puts back the version the last update replaced and keeps the rolled-back version from returning automatically. Turn it down with codewhale config set update.mode notify (or off, or CODEWHALE_UPDATE_MODE); an organization's root-owned policy.toml overrides both. Offline and rate-limited checks retry about an hour later instead of on every launch. Package-manager and desktop-app copies only get their manager's command. Builds with the release key refuse a missing or invalid signature, and re-check the staged binary against the signed manifest at start. The checksum manifest now always comes from GitHub Releases; on Linux x64 the CNB mirror can still serve the binary, but only bytes that GitHub's manifest lists.

  • One view of every Codewhale on the machine: codewhale doctor has an Installations section and codewhale doctor --installs (--json, --brief) lists every codewhale, codew, codewhale-tui, deepseek and deepseek-tui with its owner: install receipt, package manager (with its exact removal command), the desktop app, a backup, or not ours. Nothing found is ever run. codewhale doctor --fix adds one plan to tidy them: old backups move to ~/.codewhale/recovery/<stamp>/ (kept 30 days, then deleted by a later --fix), an unreceipted codew is brought in line with codewhale, and the directory gets an install receipt; each move prints its undo and codewhale doctor --restore <stamp> reverses the lot. Package-managed, desktop-app, symlinked and foreign files are never touched, and neither is user data. codewhale uninstall now lists other copies with the same classification.

  • Uninstall guidance on every install route: codewhale uninstall previews receipt-owned release files and --yes removes only checked files, with the running command last. Both Unix installers and the Windows archive installer record command ownership; self-update renews existing receipts on both. On Windows the running codewhale.exe is renamed and deleted once the command exits. Package-managed copies are left alone, and the command prints their exact removal command: npm with its prefix, Cargo with its root, the Homebrew formula, scoop uninstall codewhale, winget uninstall --id HunterBown.CodeWhale, or the Windows setup's Uninstall.exe. Every other codewhale/codew still on PATH is listed. User data is kept unless you add --purge-data. With --yes it runs only after a receipted installation was removed in that same run, and then deletes only ~/.codewhale (or a CODEWHALE_HOME named .codewhale) and ~/.deepseek/snapshots, refusing symlinks, home ancestors and directories owned by another user. A copy from an older curl | sh installer that wrote no receipt is adopted on --yes when it sits in a known older curl-installer directory: the commands byte-identical to the running program get a receipt and are removed, anything else is preserved, and a symlink or hard link among them stops adoption before any receipt is written. Windows removal is compile-checked but not yet exercised on a Windows host. (Refs #7091)

  • GitHub Action reviews: analysis can export a structured Engine review for a separate trusted publisher job. The publisher checks the current PR revision and line anchors, deduplicates its findings, and keeps uncertain or preexisting claims out of inline comments.

  • DingTalk bridge: an optional internal-app Stream adapter reuses the same Engine, shared admission and approval helpers. Tenant/staff allowlists, durable acceptance before acknowledgement and retained uncertain deliveries protect recovery. Managed account linking is separate from this advanced self-hosted bridge.

  • Answerless output-limit recovery: opt into [reasoning_only] on_output_limit = true to request an answer again after a length stop with no answer or tool call, including hidden reasoning and ordinary Fleet workers. Retries share max_reprompts, retain existing output and control limits, and record request-scoped nudge receipts without adding them to resumed conversation context. RLM keeps its existing stop protocol. Thanks @​M-Maciej for the long-proof Fleet report. (#6990)

  • OrcaRouter recommendation: /provider and /model offer a shared partner recommendation with the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 30% top-up-match link, public referral disclosure and localized offer details. F7 or a click opens the existing pager while retaining the current route.

  • Per-scope instruction budgets: global and project standing instructions now have separate token budgets (100,000 estimated tokens each, capped at 25% of the usable context window), every trim, skip or refusal reaches the model and /context report, and [instruction_budget] policy = "refuse" stops a request before dispatch. Other tools' instruction files stay opt-in through project_instruction_imports or claude_fallback, and the table is user config only. Thanks @​7jrxt42BxFZo4iAnN4CX for the design and implementation. (#6526, #7086)

  • The TUI Terminal dock now also shows the model's shell commands for the session: each running or recent command is a read-only tab with its live output, beside the interactive shells. "No live terminals" appears only when there are neither.

  • Preview: dispatch --computer starts an account cloud conversation that can also be opened in desktop. --thread continues or inspects it; --stop, --approve and --deny control its current task. Explicit --key-stdin installs provider access in the running computer's memory. Retries retain one operation key and the account/VM binding. Existing Agent Work dispatch

... (truncated)

prs.body:
Bumps [actions/download-artifact](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact) from 7.0.0 to 8.0.2.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/download-artifact's releases.

v8.0.2

What's Changed

  • Update the readme by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#473
  • Improves artifact download retries when the service returns HTTP 429 (rate limiting), including honoring valid Retry-After headers.
  • Update @​actions/artifact to 6.3.1 by @​tunc-d in actions/download-artifact#492
  • Prepare download-artifact v8.0.2 by @​tunc-d in actions/download-artifact#493

New Contributors

  • @​tunc-d made their first contribution in actions/download-artifact#492

Full Changelog: https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/compare/v8.0.1...v8.0.2

v8.0.1

What's Changed

  • Support for CJK characters in the artifact name by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#471
  • Add a regression test for artifact name + content-type mismatches by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#472

Full Changelog: https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/compare/v8...v8.0.1

v8.0.0

v8 - What's new

[!IMPORTANT] actions/download-artifact@v8 has been migrated to an ESM module. This should be transparent to the caller but forks might need to make significant changes.

[!IMPORTANT] Hash mismatches will now error by default. Users can override this behavior with a setting change (see below).

Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the Content-Type header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new skip-decompress parameter to true.

Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the digest-mismatch parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to error which will fail the workflow run.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

What's Changed

  • Don't attempt to un-zip non-zipped downloads by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#460
  • Add a setting to specify what to do on hash mismatch and default it to error by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#461

prs.body:
Bumps [codewhale-hq/Codewhale](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/codewhale) from c2a48723285c48978279f6c10672bbade49cc0cb to b92540d882b8e7c66389aa35e5fa0c3c178fe4ce.
Changelog

Sourced from codewhale-hq/Codewhale's changelog.

Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

[Unreleased]

Added

  • Runcrate is a bundled provider: runcrate reaches the OpenAI-compatible host at https://api.runcrate.ai/v1 with RUNCRATE_API_KEY, and model ids come from its public GET /v1/models listing. Thanks @​heydryft for the request and the vendor details. (#7085)

  • MCP connection status reaches the model: one existing history snapshot now records permitted configured, connecting, failed, authorization-required, unknown and connected servers, with bounded inert names and no raw errors. Stale status and server guidance are withdrawn on contention, configuration/scope changes and restore; observation does not connect servers or promise callable tools. (#6866)

  • Bundled-skill policy: [skills.bundled] separates automatic, authoritative and disabled installation from discovery, with per-name selection, disable and explicit-only controls. Aliases share policy; disabled shipped copies reveal user alternatives. Modified and managed files remain intact, and doctor plus /skills inspect show the effective policy. (#7066)

  • Configurable skill routing index: [skills] listing_max_description_chars and listing_budget_fraction control the shared parent/child catalogue. Defaults stay 400 characters and 5% of the route window, within the existing total bounds. Load warnings, localized inspect notes and /context explain shortening; full skill loading stays available. (#7073)

  • Compact approvals keep their authority visible: cards show three choices and default to Deny. An exact saved rule requires its scope preview on screen. Shortcuts for additional actions require opening Details; a hidden saved-rule choice never falls back to granting the session.

  • Quicker everyday navigation: top-level help separates everyday and advanced commands, doctor --all expands path/backend details, and the launch screen labels how to resume recent work. Up selects the newest recent session. Whale cameos stay out of transcript text.

  • Session-window diagnostics: the audit log records when a saved window starts a new journal root while retaining the previous branch, helping distinguish window replacement from lost durable history. session.window.rerooted now names a cause (engine_projection, session_restore or unattributed) and also fires when a journal with entries has no active path. (#7142)

  • Usage reporting counts models, tokens and tools: when usage reporting is on, each session now also reports, per provider and model, its turns by outcome, input, output and prompt-cache tokens, and turn-time buckets, plus how many times each built-in tool ran and failed. A model is named only when it is in Codewhale's bundled public model catalog; custom, local and fine-tuned names are sent as other, and MCP and plugin tools as mcp or other. No prompts, outputs, tool arguments or paths are sent. Runs under CI or the GitHub Action report the ci session source. The first-run notice is shown once more to describe this. DO_NOT_TRACK=1 now turns usage reporting off for that run, like CODEWHALE_TELEMETRY=0; codewhale config set telemetry false still turns it off for good. See docs/TELEMETRY.md.

  • exec and doctor follow the TUI onto local Ollama: with no cloud key and no explicit route, codewhale exec uses a running local Ollama chat model and says so, and codewhale doctor --probe-local checks that route. Nothing is saved. (#7115)

  • Thinking starts at auto: new configurations and the built-in default use reasoning_effort = "auto" instead of max; an effort you set is never changed.

  • DSH Git review scopes: the extension host brokers bounded, read-only Git metadata to reviewed DSH plugins through a new git_review_scope action (extension-host policy v8).

  • Safer uninstall: program removal never edits shell profiles; matching Codewhale PATH blocks are reported for manual cleanup. Data purge requires a receipted removal in the same confirmed run. Both Unix installers reject unsafe or managed destinations before creating them and keep shell profiles unchanged. Uninstall instructions now match the explicit-home purge scope in English and Chinese.

  • Nested and deletable threads (Runtime API): a fork (including a backtrack fork) records parent_thread_id, POST /v1/threads accepts one naming an existing thread, and GET /v1/threads/summary returns it so clients can nest child conversations. DELETE /v1/threads/{id} removes an idle thread with its turns, items, events and goal, and its saved session unless another thread shares it or a terminal holds it open; a running thread answers 409.

  • Hunk actions in Review (Runtime API): POST /v1/git/stage, /v1/git/unstage and /v1/git/discard take a patch holding hunks of the one path in paths and apply only those hunks through git apply, under the same expect preconditions as whole-path writes. A patch that no longer applies fails with git's message and writes nothing; renames, mode changes and binary patches are refused. The tasks tool can also suggest a task, shown as a Start/Hide card, without starting anything.

  • Live /models ceilings reach the route: a provider that states per-model context and output limits in its own /models body now keeps them instead of falling back to the legacy 128K window. OpenAI limit blocks, flat context_length / context_window / max_model_len / max_context_length fields, max_output_tokens / max_completion_tokens, and a relay metadata block (context_limit, context_budget, output_budget) are read; metadata.context_limit outranks context_budget because the first is the model capability and the second the share one deployment accepts. Each field is parsed on its own, so an unreadable one costs only its own candidate instead of hiding the readable fields below it.

  • Change mode and permissions while the agent works: Tab, Shift+Tab, /mode, the hotbar and /config mode no longer refuse while a turn is running. A response that is already streaming is not restarted; the change applies at the agent's next step in the same turn (before its next tool batch, at every approval gate, and before its next model request, which carries the new mode notice). The status line says so until it applies. A call still waiting for approval goes back to the model under the new posture, and a call you already approved runs only if the new posture is equal or broader. Model, thinking level and provider stay locked until the turn ends.

  • Steering interrupts thinking: a steer (Ctrl+Enter, or Enter twice after queueing) now closes the in-flight model request at once, whether the model is waiting on headers, reasoning, writing text or emitting a tool call, and continues the same turn with your message. Text already shown is kept as interrupted output; unfinished reasoning and partial tool calls are discarded, never run.

  • Modern MCP client: MCP servers now connect through the official MCP SDK (2.4) behind Codewhale's Rust broker by default (mcp_backend = "host"; "rust" stays available for one release). Servers that speak the 2026-07-28 revision are discovered with server/discover; other stdio and HTTP servers fall back to the legacy initialize handshake, and configured SSE servers keep theirs. Rust keeps process, network, credential, catalog, approval and cancellation authority.

  • DeepSeek Harness plugins: reviewed DSH plugins (definition API pinned to DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 in a shared compatibility table) run in the Native extension host. Tool output is validated against its declared schema, unsupported options are refused instead of ignored, and plugin commands can submit a prompt with visible plugin attribution. Terminal command receipts are kept in thread snapshots without entering model history. Changing the compatibility table invalidates earlier trust. A newly enabled plugin's tools are offered on the first turn: the turn waits up to 10 seconds for the plugin host to finish loading instead of adding them only from the next turn. Plugin UI views stay disabled, and the import receipt says why: WebKit's network restrictions do not stop WebRTC, so plugin UI waits for an isolated renderer. A plugin tool can call ctx.sessions.flush(exec.agent.session) to have the Engine save the conversation so far before it continues (Runtime, terminal and exec sessions); it reports failure instead of claiming a save. Installing a plugin whose bytes changed after review now returns a 409 conflict instead of a server error. A plugin tool can ask you a question with ctx.userQuestions.ask and gets back the options you picked, your own text, or a skip; the question shows like any other Codewhale question in the terminal and through the Runtime API. A plugin tool can start a child agent with ctx.subagents.startActivation (the spawn provider): the child runs through Codewhale's own sub-agent manager, needs the same approval as the model's agent tool, can carry an extra persona section and a narrower tool list set in its agent/created handler, and returns its result to the plugin.

  • MCP catalogs stay fresh: a server's tools, resources, prompts and skills are rediscovered on their own connection when an advertised ttlMs expires or the server sends a list-changed notice. A tool resolved against the old catalog is refused with "retry the call", a removed tool cannot run, and a failed refresh reconnects instead of serving stale entries. Catalogs are never shared across servers, credentials or reconnects.

  • MCP Skills extension: servers that advertise the published Skills extension have their skills listed in list_mcp_resources. Listing never activates a skill, and reading a skill file is refused unless its size and sha256 digest match the listing. MCP skills do not yet join /skills.

  • Updates install themselves: release-binary installs check for a new release every 6 hours (was 1), download and checksum-verify it in the background, and apply it the next time codewhale starts, never during a session. One line says Updated to v… · What's new: … · Undo: codewhale update --rollback. Until releases are signed, the download waits for your OK (one [y/N] question at the next start, or /update install); a release with a valid Ed25519 manifest signature applies on its own. codewhale update --rollback puts back the version the last update replaced and keeps the rolled-back version from returning automatically. Turn it down with codewhale config set update.mode notify (or off, or CODEWHALE_UPDATE_MODE); an organization's root-owned policy.toml overrides both. Offline and rate-limited checks retry about an hour later instead of on every launch. Package-manager and desktop-app copies only get their manager's command. Builds with the release key refuse a missing or invalid signature, and re-check the staged binary against the signed manifest at start. The checksum manifest now always comes from GitHub Releases; on Linux x64 the CNB mirror can still serve the binary, but only bytes that GitHub's manifest lists.

  • One view of every Codewhale on the machine: codewhale doctor has an Installations section and codewhale doctor --installs (--json, --brief) lists every codewhale, codew, codewhale-tui, deepseek and deepseek-tui with its owner: install receipt, package manager (with its exact removal command), the desktop app, a backup, or not ours. Nothing found is ever run. codewhale doctor --fix adds one plan to tidy them: old backups move to ~/.codewhale/recovery/<stamp>/ (kept 30 days, then deleted by a later --fix), an unreceipted codew is brought in line with codewhale, and the directory gets an install receipt; each move prints its undo and codewhale doctor --restore <stamp> reverses the lot. Package-managed, desktop-app, symlinked and foreign files are never touched, and neither is user data. codewhale uninstall now lists other copies with the same classification.

  • Uninstall guidance on every install route: codewhale uninstall previews receipt-owned release files and --yes removes only checked files, with the running command last. Both Unix installers and the Windows archive installer record command ownership; self-update renews existing receipts on both. On Windows the running codewhale.exe is renamed and deleted once the command exits. Package-managed copies are left alone, and the command prints their exact removal command: npm with its prefix, Cargo with its root, the Homebrew formula, scoop uninstall codewhale, winget uninstall --id HunterBown.CodeWhale, or the Windows setup's Uninstall.exe. Every other codewhale/codew still on PATH is listed. User data is kept unless you add --purge-data. With --yes it runs only after a receipted installation was removed in that same run, and then deletes only ~/.codewhale (or a CODEWHALE_HOME named .codewhale) and ~/.deepseek/snapshots, refusing symlinks, home ancestors and directories owned by another user. A copy from an older curl | sh installer that wrote no receipt is adopted on --yes when it sits in a known older curl-installer directory: the commands byte-identical to the running program get a receipt and are removed, anything else is preserved, and a symlink or hard link among them stops adoption before any receipt is written. Windows removal is compile-checked but not yet exercised on a Windows host. (Refs #7091)

  • GitHub Action reviews: analysis can export a structured Engine review for a separate trusted publisher job. The publisher checks the current PR revision and line anchors, deduplicates its findings, and keeps uncertain or preexisting claims out of inline comments.

  • DingTalk bridge: an optional internal-app Stream adapter reuses the same Engine, shared admission and approval helpers. Tenant/staff allowlists, durable acceptance before acknowledgement and retained uncertain deliveries protect recovery. Managed account linking is separate from this advanced self-hosted bridge.

  • Answerless output-limit recovery: opt into [reasoning_only] on_output_limit = true to request an answer again after a length stop with no answer or tool call, including hidden reasoning and ordinary Fleet workers. Retries share max_reprompts, retain existing output and control limits, and record request-scoped nudge receipts without adding them to resumed conversation context. RLM keeps its existing stop protocol. Thanks @​M-Maciej for the long-proof Fleet report. (#6990)

  • OrcaRouter recommendation: /provider and /model offer a shared partner recommendation with the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 30% top-up-match link, public referral disclosure and localized offer details. F7 or a click opens the existing pager while retaining the current route.

  • Per-scope instruction budgets: global and project standing instructions now have separate token budgets (100,000 estimated tokens each, capped at 25% of the usable context window), every trim, skip or refusal reaches the model and /context report, and [instruction_budget] policy = "refuse" stops a request before dispatch. Other tools' instruction files stay opt-in through project_instruction_imports or claude_fallback, and the table is user config only. Thanks @​7jrxt42BxFZo4iAnN4CX for the design and implementation. (#6526, #7086)

  • The TUI Terminal dock now also shows the model's shell commands for the session: each running or recent command is a read-only tab with its live output, beside the interactive shells. "No live terminals" appears only when there are neither.

  • Preview: dispatch --computer starts an account cloud conversation that can also be opened in desktop. --thread continues or inspects it; --stop, --approve and --deny control its current task. Explicit --key-stdin installs provider access in the running computer's memory. Retries retain one operation key and the account/VM binding. Existing Agent Work dispatch

... (truncated)

prs.body:
Bumps [jsonwebtoken](https://github.com/Keats/jsonwebtoken) from 10.4.0 to 11.1.0.
Changelog

Sourced from jsonwebtoken's changelog.

11.1.0 (2026-09-16)

  • Add dangerous::insecure_decode_claims

11.0.0 (2026-07-24)

  • Add conversions between Algorithm and KeyAlgorithm
  • JWKs can now be created from DecodingKeys, creation from EncodingKey and DecodingKey now supports Ed25519 as well
  • JWKs with unknown key types are now deserializable
  • BREAKING: Algorithm, KeyAlgorithm, EllipticCurve and ThumbprintHash are now non_exhaustive
  • BREAKING: Jwk.thumbprint now returns a Result<_>
  • BREAKING: Header.extras is now a struct that allows for deserialization to any T
  • BREAKING: Implicit features resulting from optional crates have been removed
  • BREAKING: Validation.insecure_disable_signature_validation has been removed, use dangerous::insecure_decode instead
  • BREAKING: EncodingKey.inner has been renamed to as_bytes, try_get_hmac_secret has been removed
  • BREAKING: DecodingKey.as_bytes and try_get_hmac_secret have been removed, use try_get_as_bytes instead

Changes for CryptoProviders

  • When constructing HMAC signers, the algorithm family must now be verified on construction
  • JwkUtils has been renamed to KeyUtils
    • compute_digest now returns a Result<_>
    • extract_rsa_public_key_components has been renamed to rsa_pub_components_from_private_key
    • rsa_pub_components_from_public_key has been added
    • extract_ec_public_key_coordinates has been renamed to ec_pub_components_from_private_key
    • ed_pub_components_from_private_key has been added

prs.title: fix(tui): end a bare URL at full-width punctuation
prs.body:
## What and why

A bare URL runs to the next whitespace, and Chinese and Japanese text doesn't put a space after one. So the link takes in the punctuation and the words that follow, both on screen and in the OSC 8 target, which then points at a page that doesn't exist. This reply, at 80 columns:

```
● 项目地址：https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale。克隆后运行 cargo build
▏ 即可。
▏
▏ 文档在这里（https://docs.rs/ratatui/latest/ratatui/），先看 Buffer。
▏
▏ 维基条目 https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/北京，另外 https://example.com/a,
▏ then more.
▏
▏ 日本語：https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ジョン・レノン。続き。
▏
▏ 官网是“https://example.com/q”，另见‘https://example.com/s’。
```

left these hyperlink targets in the terminal once the reply finished, before:

```
https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale。克隆后运行
https://docs.rs/ratatui/latest/ratatui/），先看
https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/北京，另外
https://example.com/a
https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ジョン・レノン。続き。
https://example.com/q”，另见‘https://example.com/s’。
```

After:

```
https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale
https://docs.rs/ratatui/latest/ratatui/
https://zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/北京
https://example.com/a
https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/ジョン・レノン
https://example.com/q
https://example.com/s
```

The text drawn in the link style covers exactly the target in both runs, so before this `。克隆后运行` and `），先看` were styled as part of the link too, and the last line was one link that swallowed the second URL.

A bare URL now also ends at full-width sentence and clause punctuation and brackets (`。，、；：！？（）「」『』【】《》〈〉`) and at curly quotes (`“”‘’`). It doesn't stop at every CJK character: ideographs and kana can be part of a URL, so `北京` and `ジョン・レノン` stay in the link. Trailing ASCII punctuation is trimmed as before, and `[text](url)` links are unaffected. A URL followed by an ideograph with nothing in between (`https://example.com然后`) still runs on, since that can't be told apart from an ideograph in the path.

prs.title: fix(tui): keep asterisks that don't open emphasis
prs.body:
## What and why

`*` and `**` open emphasis wherever a matching run comes later on the line, so prose with spaced asterisks loses them, and the text between turns italic or bold. At 80 columns, before:

```
● Pass the rest through with args and *kwargs, like the base class does.
▏
▏ The timeout is 5  60  60 seconds, so 18000.
▏
▏ It runs on the schedule 0 9   1-5.
▏
▏ The formatter picks up .rs and .toml files.
▏
▏ Squares: x  2 + y  2.
▏
▏ Still styled: the real fix and this one.
```

The model wrote `*args and **kwargs`, `5 * 60 * 60`, the cron schedule `0 9 * * 1-5`, `*.rs and *.toml` and `x ** 2 + y ** 2`. After:

```
● Pass the rest through with *args and **kwargs, like the base class does.
▏
▏ The timeout is 5 * 60 * 60 seconds, so 18000.
▏
▏ It runs on the schedule 0 9 * * 1-5.
▏
▏ The formatter picks up *.rs and *.toml files.
▏
▏ Squares: x ** 2 + y ** 2.
▏
▏ Still styled: the real fix and this one.
```

An emphasis run now needs text right inside both delimiters, so it can't start or end with whitespace. That is the whitespace half of CommonMark's flanking rule. The `_` arm already checks it on the opening side (#6042); the asterisk arms didn't check it at all. The last line (`*real*`, `**this**`) renders as before, and a run with a space just inside a delimiter, like `** note **`, now shows its asterisks, as GitHub does. Punctuation next to a delimiter still doesn't matter, so `**注意：**后面` stays bold.

## Issue

No-Issue: spaced asterisks in prose open emphasis and disappear; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at 36f058c56 in a pseudo-terminal at 80x30 with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the six lines above; the rows above come from those runs. A second reply in Chinese checked that `**注意：**后面`, `这是*重点*` and `**关键**` still render as emphasis on both builds, and that `3 * 4 * 5` keeps its asterisks only with this change.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 13623 of 13625 passed, with the 139 tests whose names match `markdown`, `inline`, `emphasis`, `bold` or `italic` among them. The 2 failures (`status_report_localizes_the_complete_japanese_surface`, `test_update_model_compaction_budget`) also fail on `main` at 36f058c56 without this change.

prs.title: fix(tui): render ~~~ fences as code blocks
prs.body:
## What and why

The markdown renderer only knows backtick fences, so a code block opened with `~~~` renders as prose, although the rest of the codebase already treats `~~~` as a fence (memory import, the agent roster, the plan handoff title). `~~~` is a common way to wrap text that has backtick fences of its own, such as a README section. In prose, a `# comment` line becomes a heading with a rule under it, indentation is dropped, and `*all*` turns italic. At 80 columns, before:

```
● Here is the script:
▏
▏ ~~~python
▏ Count the lines in each file
▏ ────────────────────────────────────────
▏ import sys
▏
▏ for path in sys.argv[1:]:
▏ with open(path) as f:
▏ print(path, sum(1 for _ in f))  # all lines
▏ ~~~
▏
▏ And the README section, which has a fence of its own:
▏
▏ ~~~markdown
▏ Usage
▏
    python count.py *.txt
▏ ~~~
▏
▏ Done.
```

After:

````
● Here is the script:
▏
    # Count the lines in each file
    import sys

    for path in sys.argv[1:]:
        with open(path) as f:
            print(path, sum(1 for _ in f))  # *all* lines
▏
▏ And the README section, which has a fence of its own:
▏
    ## Usage

    ```bash
    python count.py *.txt
    ```
▏
▏ Done.
````

The parser's fence carry now records the fence character along with its length. A fence closes only on the same character and at least the opener's length, so a backtick fence inside a `~~~` block is code, and the other way round. Backtick fences parse as before. `streaming_preview_tail_source` in the thinking preview mirrors the parser's fence rule to pick a cut that isn't inside a code block (a review note on #6249 pointed out the two would drift if the parser learned tilde fences), so it gets the same change; without it, a cut could land inside a `~~~` block and the preview would render the rest of that block as prose.

This touches the same lines as #7146 (the parser's carry and `push_parsed_line`'s signature). If that one lands first, I'll merge `main` in and resolve it here.

## Issue

No-Issue: code blocks fenced with `~~~` render as prose in the transcript; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at 36f058c56 in a pseudo-terminal at 80x50 with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the message above; the rows above come from those runs. A second reply checked the edges: `~~~bash` and backtick `bash` blocks holding `echo "$HOME and $USER"` both render as code with the `$` left alone, a four-backtick block keeps a `~~~` line inside it as code, a `~~~~` block is not closed by `~~~`, and `~~struck~~` text still renders struck through. On `main` the `~~~bash` line shows as text and the `~~~~` block's `- inside` lines render as list items.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 13623 of 13625 passed, with the 266 tests whose names match `markdown`, `fence` or `thinking` among them. The 2 failures (`status_report_localizes_the_complete_japanese_surface`, `test_update_model_compaction_budget`) also fail on `main` at 36f058c56 without this change.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets`, `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` and `cargo doc -p codewhale-tui-kit --no-deps` with `-D warnings`: clean.

## Checklist

prs.title: feat: source navigation echoes and guarded fork-prefix inheritance
prs.body:
Index-free source-navigation echoes, bounded source reads and guarded fork-prefix inheritance on the existing Engine. Original contributor commits and credit are preserved; there is no replacement turn loop or indexing daemon.

**Current head:** [`70174cfd3`](https://github.com/AdityaVG13/CodeWhale/commit/70174cfd32c306f6c438812edd8cd723f691a778), following the history-preserving integration at [`40836d9e6`](https://github.com/AdityaVG13/CodeWhale/commit/40836d9e6f902ba7599132c8b21e1e3c9a7a953b) of upstream main [`96498ce2a`](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/96498ce2a7d12689275cea8a8feb5e0569b4431f). Website registries are regenerated from the merged source, not resolved by discarding either side's feature declarations or docs.

## Implemented slice

- Revision-qualified Rust function/method references carry a path, source window and revision, with stale-reference refusal rather than silently using old offsets. Guarded continuation/paging requires forward progress and retains the snapshot identity.
- Focused Rust grep results can supply bounded enclosing-function references and small complete bodies before a separate read. Declaration-line matches take priority across candidate files. Broad/truncated searches keep their ordinary output; this is syntax evidence, not macro expansion or name/type resolution.
- Native `grep_files` is eager beside file-name search, with explicit search argument schemas and aligned child/scout/workflow fixtures. Source whitespace survives tool-result projection.
- Bounded host observations remain separate from program-writable handles, current access authority and evidence delivered to a model. Program-internal reads do not count as delivery; only references surviving outbound projection enter the recipient's ledger.
- Source echoes remain in append-only tool/history evidence, not volatile additions to the pinned system/tool prefix. Making grep eager does grow the catalog; its actual contract is measured and budgeted in this change. Native read containment, deny rules and blocking-worker fences remain in place.
- Children retain the complete policy-allowed tool vector while preserving the current eager/deferred discovery and cache contracts. Fork-prefix inheritance stays gated by matching route/model/opaque receipt and supported dialect; unsupported or changed identities take the cold path.
- The skill index keeps eligible names enumerable without exposing mutable native skill paths. Workflow events retain task/workspace ownership.

## Current source-level verification

**224 selected `codewhale-tui` library tests passed: 0 failed, 0 ignored**, rerun on Linux from the existing RCH-built test executable. All 1,599 recorded source inputs match, and remote inputs were unchanged around execution. The selection covers search/navigation/read contracts, source-result projection and eager-tool/catalog behavior.

Four provider-free runtime metric tests passed separately. `scripts/check-runtime-contract-budget.py --receipt …` passes all 55 metrics exactly at the updated ceilings. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, touched-file `git diff --check`, web facts/cloud-facts/docs checks, and generated parity for all 90 feature rows and 25 documentation topics pass.

The native replay of the recorded search preserves its 11 raw hits and supplies the actual 564-byte definition, with exact guarded reading and same-size-edit refusal verified. This is diagnostic-client execution, not a model choosing or following the reference. Engine tests with injected model clients likewise establish host execution and projected request contents, not live-provider acceptance or completed-task improvement.

No full workspace suite, full web build, native macOS/Windows acceptance or packaged-release qualification is claimed. Historical receipts are not substituted for verification of the current source.

## Still draft: empirical qualification remains

This stays draft in accordance with [the contributor's scope decision](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6207193232). The earlier baseline, including its failed completion and incomplete pilot, remains in [the maintained progress record](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6185897898).

The six-attempt full/output-off/navigation-off comparison is complete but did not qualify an overall performance gain. The grouped-grep experiment was removed after smaller replay output did not translate into better fresh exploration. The latest smarter-exploration comparison stopped when its first control failed the frozen correctness rubric, without running a treatment or relaxing the rubric. See [the current findings and verification update](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/pull/6393#issuecomment-6524708140).

Remaining qualification is correctness-first completed tasks with a valid frozen control and contemporaneous ablations. No current-PR speedup, cost reduction, quality improvement, live-provider cache saving or independent quality review is claimed. Wider composition/impact-navigation work and release acceptance are not implied.

Refs #6393, CW-6439

prs.title: Native HarmonyOS: fix the documented build, and ship a signed arm64 release
prs.body:
## What and why

Two commits that make native HarmonyOS a target maintainers can document and a release can serve.

**1. `docs(ohos)`: the guide's commands now work, and the page says what the device actually does.**

Following `docs/HarmonyOS.md` from a clean checkout failed before producing a binary. Two independent causes, both reproduced on the base commit:

- The documented `cargo check --target aarch64-unknown-linux-ohos -p codewhale-cli` dies inside `aws-lc-sys`' build script with `Required build dependency is missing. Halting build.` — the message names neither cmake nor HarmonyOS. `scripts/ohos-env.sh` now puts the SDK's own `build-tools/cmake/bin` on `PATH` and exports `CMAKE`.
- With that fixed, the check then fails on the workspace's `warnings = "deny"`: `function sha256_hex is never used`. `crates/cli/src/lib.rs` compiled `hashing` unconditionally, but its only caller is `mod update`, which is already `#[cfg(not(target_env = "ohos"))]`. The module now carries the same gate.

The page also gained what it was missing, verified on hardware (HPR-W72, HarmonyOS 7.0.0.111, API 26, 2in1): only signed code runs at all (`chmod +x` is irrelevant); `hdc shell` cannot execute a binary under `/data/local/tmp` because of its security label, so a correctly signed binary still reports `Permission denied` there and must be run from HiShell; an emulator is more permissive than a retail device. Signing with the SDK's own `binary-sign-tool` is now part of the instructions, along with the two things a self-signature does *not* grant (permissions, JIT), and the credential-storage behaviour of the 2in1 user directory.

The capability table separates what was observed from what the target's `cfg` gates make unreachable, and states plainly that the interactive TUI has not been drawn on a device yet. I did not write claims I had not verified.

Chinese mirror updated in the same style; both pages have the same 13 sections.

**2. `feat(release)`: releases build, sign and publish a native HarmonyOS binary.**

Until now a release could not serve a native device at all, and `npm i -g codewhale` there installed the static Linux build, which a device refuses to start.

`aarch64-unknown-linux-ohos` becomes an eighth artifact target producing `codewhale-ohos-arm64`, `codew-ohos-arm64` and `codewhale-ohos-arm64.tar.gz`. The leg installs the published OpenHarmony 6.1 SDK (`native;toolchains`, `cache: false`), cross-compiles, signs with the SDK's `binary-sign-tool -selfSign 1`, and **fails unless `display-sign` reads back `code signature is self-sign`** — an unsigned ELF is refused at `execve`, so shipping one would be a dead download. It also asserts the file is an aarch64 ELF with the musl interpreter.

npm's `openharmony` platform now resolves to that native asset; `PLATFORM_ALIASES` was removed with it, and the OpenHarmony x64 branch of `assertCnbMirrorSupportedPlatform` now says it is x64-only rather than claiming to include OpenHarmony. Inventory stays exact and enforced (38 files / 8 targets), with the workflow, bundler, release-notes generator, runbook, checklist and `docs/features.toml` updated together.

## Issue

No-Issue: HarmonyOS support gaps found and fixed while building the native target; no tracking issue exists.

## How I tested it

Everything below was run on this branch after rebasing onto `origin/main` (`6dd9af54c`).

**The two documented failures, reproduced on base then fixed:**

```
# base 6dd9af54c, documented command, clean env
error: failed to run custom build command for `aws-lc-sys v0.46.0`   # "Missing dependency: cmake"

# base + only the ohos-env.sh change — proves the two bugs are independent
error: function `sha256_hex` is never used  -> crates/cli/src/hashing.rs:2
error: function `hex_bytes` is never used

# this branch, same command, bare PATH with no system cmake, no -A suppression
Finished `dev` profile [optimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 4m 58s
```

**Guards, all green:**

```
release-workflows.test.js            PASS   (8-target/38-asset contract)
assemble-release-assets.test.js      PASS
ensure-release-assets-absent.test.js PASS
verify-release-inventory.test.js     PASS
install-safety.test.js               PASS
compiled-host-delivery.test.js       PASS
npm-wrapper-smoke.test.js            PASS
npm codewhale suite                  PASS   (101/101)
generate-release-body.test.sh        PASS
prepare-release.test.sh              PASS
check-ohos-deps.sh                   PASS   (no-SDK dependency graph guard)
check-feature-release-notes.sh       PASS
feature_registry (cargo test)        PASS   (2/2 — covers the new row)
dev-test.sh secrets                  PASS   (46 passed)
dev-cargo.sh check -p codewhale-cli  PASS   (host profile)
```

**The release leg's own commands, replayed by hand against the real SDK and a real 120 MB binary**, which is how I caught a bug in my own step logic: `llvm-readelf | grep -q` cannot be used under `pipefail` — grep exits at the first match, readelf takes SIGPIPE and reports exit 74, so a *good* binary read as a failed verification. The step now captures and matches with `case`. Replayed:

```
OK signature     code signature is self-sign
OK arch          ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, ARM aarch64 … interpreter /lib/ld-musl-aarch64.so.1
OK interpreter
```

**Not verified:** the GitHub Actions run itself. The reuse of `components: 'native;toolchains'` and the assumption that `toolchains` lands beside `native` come from the local DevEco layout; if that is wrong the leg fails at `test -f "${signer}"`, which is a clear failure rather than a bad artifact. No device test of the *published* asset is possible until a release carrying it exists.

I also added a guard in `release-workflows.test.js` that every `- name:` in the three release workflows starts its own line: a `run:` block that loses its trailing newline glues the next step header onto the script text, which YAML accepts and which silently drops the step. I hit that while editing.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change per commit, started from current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and the changed behaviour is covered (feature registry test, npm suite, release invariants)
- [x] User-facing docs updated, and the new row added to `docs/features.toml`
- [x] No `CHANGELOG.md` hunks (per CONTRIBUTING.md: entries are written on `main` at merge time)

Every fleet change ends in `Op::SetFleetRoster`, and the engine answered each one with a status: "Fleet roster refreshed for subsequent turns".
```
Note Added openai/mock to the team My fleet (new personal team, now selected)
…
 ● ask   work (Tab)   Work bar (Ctrl+])                 Fleet roster refreshed for subsequent turns
```

```
…
```

```
Note Added openai/mock to the team My fleet (new personal team, now selected)
…
 ● ask  Shift+Tab to change   work (Tab)   Work bar (Ctrl+])
```

```
Note 已将 openai/mock 添加到 Fleet My fleet （新的个人 Fleet，已选中）
…
 ● ask  Shift+Tab 切换   work (Tab)   Work bar (Ctrl+])
```

The engine now stores the roster without sending a status. Nothing reads that message, and the TUI is the only sender of the op. 04de8eb67 fixed the same kind of ack replacing a host receipt for `SetCompaction`.

prs.title: fix(tui): detach recalled history when removing an attachment or deleting in vim
prs.body:
## What and why

After Up recalls an entry from prompt history, an edit is supposed to detach it: the note on `insert_str` explains that otherwise "the next Up/Down silently discards" the edit. Typing, Backspace and Delete, the word and line deletes, and kill and yank clear it, and e7e0a4da5 did the same for paste and the external editor. Among the edits that remove text, three don't: removing a selected attachment, and vim Normal-mode `x` and `dd`. After any of them, Up/Down carry on from the old index, and going back to that entry brings it back as it was saved.

Launch composer, `TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app`, one key at a time, with a history of `first entry` and a two-line entry that carries an image attachment. Type `draft`, Up to recall the attachment entry, Up, Home, Up to select the attachment, then Backspace (status: `Removed attachment: shots/a.png`). Before:

```
Backspace  ❯ what is in this picture
Up         ❯ first entry
Down         [Attached image: shots/a.png]
           ❯ what is in this picture
```

After:

```
Backspace  ❯ what is in this picture
Up           [Attached image: shots/a.png]
           ❯ what is in this picture
Down       ❯ what is in this picture
```

With `composer_vim_mode = "vim"` and a history of `first entry`, `second entry`: `k`, `0`, `x` gives `econd entry`. Then `k`, `j` showed `first entry` and `second entry` as saved; now `k` recalls `second entry` and `j` comes back to `econd entry`. `dd` on the second line of a recalled `two` / `lines` entry leaves `two`; `k`, `j` brought back `two` / `lines` and now come back to `two`.

Each of the three now calls `clear_input_history_navigation()` like the other deletes. For the attachment it goes after the check that one is selected, because every Backspace and Delete calls `remove_selected_composer_attachment` first. As with typing into a recalled entry, the draft from before the first Up (`draft` above) is no longer what Down returns to; the edited entry is.

## Issue

No-Issue: removing an attachment or vim `x`/`dd` on a recalled history entry is undone by the next Up/Down; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at 3690f9c4a in a pseudo-terminal with an empty HOME, a seeded `composer_history.jsonl` and `TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app`, sending one key at a time on the launch composer; the rows above come from those runs.
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui --lib`: 13908 of 13912 passed, with the 477 `vim`, `composer`, `attachment` and `history` tests among them. The 4 failures are plugin import tests (three in `plugins_dsh_tests`, plus `plugins_skill_tests::dsh_packages_import_through_the_reviewed_install_and_update_flow`, all "composition reviewer is unavailable"); the same 4 fail on `main` at 3690f9c4a without this change.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets --all-features` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui`: clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on 3690f9c4a; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

prs.title: fix(tui): fork a conversation by the history it carries, not the shape it stores
prs.body:
No-Issue: found while diagnosing a user report of `/undo` refusing with "Cannot identify an exact saved-history boundary" and "full history exceeds byte transport bound"; the report is reproduced and explained in this description.

## What this fixes

Two independent reasons `/undo` (and retry, and fork-at-turn) refused to cut a
conversation that was otherwise perfectly usable. Both were reported from the
VS Code client; the TUI hits the same code.

### 1. The fork was measured by its stored shape, not by its history

A saved session repeats its own conversation while it carries a journal:
`messages` and the journal's active branch hold the same turns, so the file on
disk is up to twice the history it holds. The reader that opens such a document
already knows this — `SessionManager::load_session_snapshot_with_limit` judges
an oversized file by `SavedSession::transport_form` — but the fork writer
measured the stored shape against the same 8 MiB canonical bound.

Concretely, on a 9.75 MiB conversation whose carried form was 5.2 MiB, the
runtime kept opening it, saving it and running new turns, while `patch-undo`
answered `400 full history exceeds byte transport bound; source retained`
before it touched a file. `/undo` is a fork, so the turn stayed in the
transcript.

`saved_document_digest` already measured `transport_form()`. Both now go
through one `ensure_history_transport_fits`, so the writer's rule and the
reader's cannot drift apart again.

### 2. The saved-history boundary counted engine traffic as user prompts

The boundary walk reads a saved transcript as "the prompts a person typed", so
it can align the transcript against the turn records. Two kinds of engine
message were counted as prompts, and neither is ever recorded on a turn:

- runtime-owned control messages — the MCP-server notice, shell-completion
  handoffs, the deferred-toolbox snapshot
- the `<image path=…>` / `</image>` tags that bracket an attachment

A conversation that had received any of them could not be cut at all: `/undo`
answered `Cannot identify an exact saved-history boundary`. Both are now
skipped. The runtime-owned check is the same recognition the session views
already use (`turn_classify::is_runtime_owned_user_message`) and keys off the
runtime provenance line in the `<turn_meta>` envelope — which a person's own
prompt does not carry, so a real turn is never swallowed.

## Tests

Two new tests, both in `crates/tui/src/runtime_threads/tests.rs`:

- `a_fork_measures_the_history_it_carries_not_the_shape_it_stores` builds a
  conversation whose file passes the bound while its carried form does not,
  asserts the fixture really is in that regime, then forks it. Reverting the
  production change makes it fail with the exact reported error.
- `runtime_traffic_and_attachment_tags_are_not_kept_prompts` builds the three
  shapes (MCP notice, screenshot prompt, toolbox snapshot) and asserts both
  walks a fork runs land where the records say.

Verified locally on `origin/main` (6a08f0312):

```
cargo fmt --check -p codewhale-tui                          clean
cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets (CI lint set)    clean
dev-test.sh ... recovery::                                  27 passed
```

Also exercised end to end against a copy of the real 9.75 MiB conversation:
`POST /v1/threads/{id}/patch-undo` returns `201` and the fork's own undo works
too.

## Not in this PR

`GET /v1/threads/{id}/history` still refuses a document over the bound, and
that one is not the same bug: the response body carries `session` in its stored
shape, so the bytes really would travel. Fixing it means changing the wire
payload to the carried form, which is a protocol change — worth its own
discussion rather than smuggling it in here.

## Note on the lint gate

`cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets` fails on `origin/main` at
`crates/tui/src/tui/persistence_actor.rs:80` (`variant ClearCheckpoint is never
constructed`) — pre-existing, untouched by this branch, from 4a974f0c6's
neighbourhood. I ran clippy with `-A dead_code` to get past it; everything else
is clean.

No changelog entries: CONTRIBUTING asks for them on `main` at merge time.
