prs.title: fix(tui): keep the indent of a paragraph nested in a list
prs.body:
## What and why

A paragraph indented under a list item renders flush left: the word wrapper drops spaces at the start of a row, so the indent never reaches the screen. Models write these often, as a bullet's second paragraph or a note after a numbered step's code block. At 60 columns, before:

```
● Setup:
▏
▏ 1. Install the dependencies:
▏
       npm install --save-dev typescript
▏
▏ This also writes a lockfile, which you should commit
▏ together with the change.
▏
▏ 2. Build:
       npm run build
▏ 3. Check the config:
▏
       {
         "strict": true
       }
▏
▏ - A bullet with a second paragraph.
▏
▏ The second paragraph of that bullet, indented two spaces
▏ and long enough to wrap.
▏ - Last bullet
```

The code under step 1 keeps its indent but the note after it doesn't, so step 1 looks finished and the note reads as top-level text. After:

```
● Setup:
▏
▏ 1. Install the dependencies:
▏
       npm install --save-dev typescript
▏
▏    This also writes a lockfile, which you should commit
▏    together with the change.
▏
▏ 2. Build:
       npm run build
▏ 3. Check the config:
▏
       {
         "strict": true
       }
▏
▏ - A bullet with a second paragraph.
▏
▏   The second paragraph of that bullet, indented two
▏   spaces and long enough to wrap.
▏ - Last bullet
```

The parser now carries whether a list is open, next to its code-fence state: a list item opens it, blank lines, code and indented paragraphs keep it open, and anything else closes it. While a list is open, a paragraph keeps its leading spaces, and `render_paragraph_tagged` wraps the text in the remaining width and draws the indent on every row, capped at half the width like a list item's indent (#7030); links shift with it. The decision is made when the line is parsed rather than in the renderer, because streaming renders the text between code blocks separately and a look-back there would not match the final render. Copy follows list items: the first row copies with its indent, as written, and wrapped rows strip it.

Command notes go through the same renderer, and some have indented rows that aren't under a list item, such as `/status`'s key/value rows and part of `/cost`. Those render as before: I ran `/status`, `/cost`, `/context`, `/hooks`, `/mcp`, `/skills`, `/tools`, `/memory`, `/doctor`, `/version`, `/usage`, `/agents`, `/workspace`, `/permissions`, `/sandbox`, `/todo`, `/goal`, `/diff`, `/stats` and `/profile` in one session on both builds, and the screens match once the session id is masked. A first version that kept every indent did shift `/status` and `/cost`, which is why the decision follows the list.

## Issue

No-Issue: a paragraph indented under a list item renders flush left; I searched and found no issue for it

## How I tested it

- Ran a debug build of this change and one of `main` at 588426ddd in a pseudo-terminal at 60 columns with an empty HOME and a local mock OpenAI-compatible server replying with the steps and bullets above; the rows above come from those runs.
- Selection copy: with a throwaway test (not part of this PR) that selects `1. Install` followed by an indented paragraph, and `- item` followed by an indented line, at 24 columns and calls `selection_to_text`, this change copies both as written (`"1. Install\n\n   alpha beta … kappa"`); `main` copies them without the indent (`"1. Install\n\nalpha beta … kappa"`).
- `cargo nextest run -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --lib`: 13880 of 13886 passed, with the 427 tests whose names match `markdown`, `paragraph`, `selection` or `transcript` among them. The 6 failures (`status_public_output_and_read_only_state_match_baseline`, `golden_turn_events_match`, `model_visible_prefix_bytes_match_goldens`, `interrupted_session_deletion_keeps_recovery_incomplete_and_can_finish`, `worker_compacts_past_its_context_window_and_keeps_working`, `reasoning_effort_uses_one_strict_alias_table_and_legacy_fallback`) also fail on `main` at 588426ddd without this change.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit` with CI's flags (also on 1.99), `cargo check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit --all-targets` and `cargo +1.89.0 check -p codewhale-tui -p codewhale-tui-kit`: clean.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, on 588426ddd; it merges cleanly into current `main`
- [ ] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior — `cargo fmt` passes; no new test, per AGENTS.md, so the runs above stand in for one
- [ ] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` checks it) — n/a

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The Gateway intermittently becomes unresponsive on macOS and requires a restart. Two process samples taken during separate hangs show the main thread waiting for a write lock while closing a worker MessagePort.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

The Gateway continues serving requests. Restarting the affected process restored service.

### Actual behavior

Three hangs were recorded on October 14–15. The process remained alive but the Gateway stopped responding. Samples from October 15 at 10:20 and 11:33 HKT show the same main-thread stack for every captured sample (1,808/1,808 and 1,360/1,360 respectively).

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.3, local source build `f6cf7bbb60c` (includes local carries, not an unmodified release).

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.1 (25G76), ARM64. Node 26; the captured library is `libnode.147.dylib`. The sample reports do not record the exact Node patch version.

### Install method

Git/source build, Gateway supervised by launchd.

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Logs

These excerpts come from `/usr/bin/sample` captures of two separate Gateway processes. Paths and addresses are omitted.

```text
2026-10-15 10:20:52 +0800, pid 22909
1808/1808 main-thread samples:
  node::HandleWrap::OnClose(uv_handle_s*)
  node::worker::MessagePort::OnClose()
  node::worker::SiblingGroup::Disentangle(node::worker::MessagePortData*)
  uv_rwlock_wrlock
  _pthread_rwlock_lock_slow
  _pthread_rwlock_lock_wait
  __psynch_rw_wrlock

2026-10-15 11:33:39 +0800, pid 22320
1360/1360 main-thread samples:
  node::HandleWrap::OnClose(uv_handle_s*)
  node::worker::MessagePort::OnClose()
  node::worker::SiblingGroup::Disentangle(node::worker::MessagePortData*)
  uv_rwlock_wrlock
  _pthread_rwlock_lock_slow
  _pthread_rwlock_lock_wait
  __psynch_rw_wrlock
```

### Impact and severity

One macOS Gateway installation; intermittent complete loss of service, requiring manual restart. Three incidents were recorded over two days. Frequency on other installations is unknown.

### Additional information

Related: #169535 (continuous V8 stall flight recorder).

Disabling only the flight recorder was deployed locally on October 15. No recurrence was recorded during the following 3.5-day observation period. This is an uncontrolled workaround observation, not proof of causation; there is no deterministic reproducer or re-enable/reproduce test.

Both hang samples contain a `v8:ProfEvntProc` thread, mostly in `SamplingEventsProcessor::Run` → `ConditionVariable::WaitFor`. Its presence does **not** establish that the profiler is deadlocked or owns the MessagePort lock. The samples establish the main-thread lock wait, not the lock owner or root cause.

Please investigate the MessagePort-close lock wait on macOS and whether continuous profiling contributes. This report does not propose merging the blanket recorder disable as a fix.

issues.title: [Bug]: zalouser never reports lastTransportActivityAt, so the core health monitor cannot detect a silently dead listener (18h inbound outage while reported running/connected)

labels.name: P1

labels.name: clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr

labels.name: issue-rating: 🐚 platinum hermit
labels.description: Good issue quality with a plausible reproduction path needing some confirmation.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

The `zalouser` channel can stop delivering inbound events for many hours while its account snapshot keeps reporting `running: true` / `connected: true`. The core channel health monitor cannot detect this, because its stale-socket rule only runs when a channel reports `lastTransportActivityAt`, and the `zalouser` plugin never sets that field. The result is a silent, unbounded inbound outage: nothing restarts the listener and no health warning is raised.

### Steps to reproduce

Not deterministic; it happens after some hours of normal operation (we have seen it several times in October on a personal account that is a member of ~50 groups).

1. Run the Gateway with the `zalouser` channel connected and receiving group/DM messages normally.
2. At some point the listener stops producing inbound events (no `channel_ingress_events` rows, no `message_received`), while people keep posting in the groups.
3. Observe `openclaw channels status` / the account snapshot and the Gateway log.

### Expected behavior

Either the plugin's own listener watchdog or the core channel health monitor notices that the account has produced no transport/inbound activity for a long time and restarts the account (as it does for channels that report `lastTransportActivityAt`, e.g. the `stale-socket` path), or at least reports the account as unhealthy.

### Actual behavior

- Last inbound event: 12:08 local time. Next one only after a manual `openclaw gateway call channels.stop` + `channels.start` for `zalouser` at 06:37 the next day: **~18.5 hours with zero inbound events** on an account in ~50 active groups, including a full working afternoon. Messages sent during the gap were never delivered afterwards.
- During the whole gap the account snapshot reported `running` / `connected`; no `stale-socket`, `disconnected` or `stuck` health reason was produced and no auto-restart happened.
- The plugin's own `Zalo listener watchdog gap detected (…s): forcing reconnect` did not fire in this window (it does fire in other situations, so the listener-level watchdog exists but did not catch this state).
- In an earlier, similar episode we checked the TCP connection while no events were arriving: the socket was still receiving bytes (last receive ~80 s earlier), i.e. the transport looked alive at the socket level while no message events were produced.
- A manual `channels.stop` / `channels.start` immediately restores delivery.

### Where it happens (2026.10.5)

Core, `dist/channel-health-policy-*.mjs` (`evaluateChannelHealth`):

```js
const lastTransportActivityAt = resolveObservedChannelTimestamp(snapshot.lastTransportActivityAt, policy.now);
…
if (snapshot.connected === true && lastTransportActivityAt != null) {
  …
  if (policy.now - lastTransportActivityAt > policy.staleEventThresholdMs) return { healthy: false, reason: "stale-socket" };
}
return { healthy: true, reason: "healthy" };
```

`@openclaw/zalouser` 2026.10.5 only reports `lastInboundAt`, `lastOutboundAt` and the ready patch through its status sink (`dist/.setup/monitor-*.mjs`: `statusSink?.({ lastInboundAt: Date.now() })`, `statusSink?.({ lastOutboundAt: … })`, `statusSink?.(channelReadyPatch())`). `lastTransportActivityAt` is never set, so for `zalouser` the function always falls through to `healthy`.

### Suggested fix

- Have `zalouser` report `lastTransportActivityAt` from **application-level** listener events (any message/event frame from the Zalo listener, not only TCP keepalives — keepalives kept flowing in the episode above), so the existing `stale-socket` rule (default 30 min) applies; and/or
- Let channels opt into a "no inbound for N" health rule (configurable per account, since a quiet DM-only account is legitimately silent), and/or
- Make the plugin's listener watchdog also trip when no message events arrive for a configurable period while the account is a member of active groups.

### Workaround we use

An external timer that checks the Gateway's ingress table and runs `channels.stop` / `channels.start` for `zalouser` when there has been no inbound for 60 minutes during working hours.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.5 (`@openclaw/zalouser` 2026.10.5); also seen on 2026.10.3/10.4

### Operating system

Ubuntu 24.04 (Gateway as systemd user service, Node 24.21)

### Install method

npm global install (`npm i -g openclaw`), auto-update enabled

### Related

- #168324 (durable observation of group messages before mention gating) — different problem, same channel.
- #109659 (channel auto-restart lost silently when abort races the backoff sleep) — possibly related to why recovery does not happen, but here no restart was ever attempted.

### Summary
On 2026.10.6, if `agents.entries.<id>.workspace` is spelled with different letter case from the folder on disk (`~/clawd` vs `~/Clawd` on case-insensitive APFS), every skill under `<workspace>/skills` is skipped with `Skipping invalid skill: file=.../SKILL.md error=resolved path escapes skill root`. 2026.9.4 loaded the same skills.

### Environment
OpenClaw 2026.10.6 (fe06181), bundled @openclaw/fs-safe 0.25.0, Node 26.12.1, macOS arm64 (APFS, case-insensitive).

### Cause
- The skill root is resolved with `tryRealpath` → `safeRealpathSync` → Node's JS `fs.realpathSync`, which keeps the spelling it was given: `/Users/<u>/clawd/skills/<x>`.
- The file is resolved by `createRootFileFinalAdmission` (fs-safe `dist/root-file-final-admission.js`) with `fs.realpathSync.native`, which returns the on-disk spelling: `/Users/<u>/Clawd/skills/<x>/SKILL.md`.
- `admitPathInsideRoot` (`dist/root-boundary.js`) only matches case-insensitively on Windows. On POSIX it does an exact `startsWith` and then `path.relative`, which gives `../../../Clawd/...`. That's treated as an escape.

### Repro
On macOS, set an agent workspace to the same folder but with different case, add a skill under `skills/`, then run `openclaw skills check --agent <id>`. The skill is missing and the gateway log shows "escapes skill root". Correcting the case in config loads it. (Here: 6 skills, about 13k warnings per skill over 6 h.)

### Suggested fix
Resolve the root and the file with the same realpath flavour (both `.native`), or compare case-insensitively when the volume is case-insensitive (darwin default).

issues.body:
## Summary

Coordinate the remaining work needed for Skill Workshop to capture useful procedural discoveries during ordinary work and demonstrate that an authorized skill revision improves a later task. Build on existing learning, proposal, evaluation and publication contracts; measure gaps before adding mechanisms.

This is a contributor proposal for discussion, not an accepted roadmap or a claim that OpenClaw lacks self-learning.

## Problem to solve

After an agent discovers a reliable procedure or receives a useful procedural correction, the operator needs to know whether that lesson was captured in the right skill, whether it was applied, and whether it works beyond the original example.

Those are separate outcomes. A pending proposal is not an active skill; a valid file is not behavioral proof; completion of maintenance does not necessarily mean a file changed. The proposed outcome is reliable, inspectable reuse—not more generated skill files.

The supplied static review identified possible coverage gaps between foreground authoring, immediate repair and delayed experience review. It did not measure their frequency or run behavioral trials. In particular, short-turn admission is a hypothesis to investigate, not sufficient evidence for lowering a scheduler threshold.

## Existing behavior and related ownership

OpenClaw already documents immediate repair and experience review. Workshop owns proposal application, while automatic background maintenance can edit its directory directly. These paths must not be given identical validation or publication guarantees by implication. See [self-learning](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/self-learning.md) and [Workshop ownership](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/skill-workshop.md).

| Existing work | Relationship to this proposal |
|---|---|
| steipete’s merged [#100692](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100692), closing [#95477](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/95477) | Existing reusable-workflow suggestion work. Reconcile its current behavior and subsequent changes before proposing additional recognition guidance. This umbrella does not reopen the old “missing self-learning” premise. |
| [#123992](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/123992), closed with linked fix #123994 | Existing evaluator-result visibility work. Reuse or verify its projection rather than proposing outcome visibility as entirely new. |
| Zeus-Deus’s [#111943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/111943) | Adjacent model/reasoning policy proposal. No routing or model-policy change is included here. |
| anyech’s [#141102](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/141102) | Existing collection-review eligibility/diagnostics discussion. Keep that decision on its owning issue; reuse its eventual contract. |

This is a coordination proposal, not a takeover of those items. If an existing umbrella already owns the remaining scope, attach the work there instead of opening a competing tracker.

## Proposed solution

Keep proposals and publication in Workshop, loading and refresh in the skills runtime, and permissions and execution capacity with their existing owners. Prefer an optional evaluator plugin over a new core controller. A quality result never grants authority to publish.

### Dependency-ordered workstreams

These are candidate PR units, not existing PRs or assignments. A workstream proceeds only after its gap and owner boundary are established.

| Unit | Change and independent value | Dependency / acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Characterize learning coverage** | Establish a synthetic behavior matrix for manual, foreground and experience-review paths, including current modes and runtime eligibility. Reconcile #100692 and later changes. | First evidence milestone. Separate contract tests from live-model trials. A prompt-text assertion does not prove recognition. Submit a standalone characterization PR only if maintainers want that artifact; otherwise carry its useful fixtures with the first demonstrated fix. |
| **B. Close demonstrated foreground capture gaps** | Improve existing guidance or authoring behavior only where A demonstrates a missing case. Prefer the owning skill or pending proposal; create a distinct skill only for a distinct procedure. | Depends on A. Show correct capture without an explicit learning request, no duplicate for covered work, and no failed attempt stored as a working solution. Preserve publication semantics and mode/permission boundaries. |
| **C. Demonstrate reuse and explain outcomes** | Use existing status, usage and evaluation projections to connect a proposal, its applied revision and a later task. Add only missing information. | Baseline fixtures from A; integrate B if needed. A fresh session must discover and use the authorized revision on changed input. Distinguish pending, applied, evaluated, failed, unavailable and abstained states. Do not silently reload the current session. Coordinate collection diagnostics with #141102. |
| **D. Reference behavioral evaluator** | Exercise exact candidate and baseline revisions through the existing evaluation extension contract; produce interpretable task outcomes. Prefer an optional plugin. | Requires agreement on placement and supported API. Use isolated synthetic tasks, baseline/candidate comparison or a no-skill control where meaningful. An incorrect skill must fail; evaluator absence must not be reported as a pass. Storage and publication remain Workshop-owned. |
| **E. Bounded evaluation and revision** | Optionally coordinate evaluate → revise → re-evaluate → stop through existing owners, without another persistent scheduler or proposal store. | Depends on D and explicit policy agreement. Bound attempts, elapsed time and resource use; honor cancellation; invalidate stale results. Any required-evaluation policy must define missing/error/timeout/skipped outcomes without changing advisory behavior silently. |
| **F. Short-turn review admission, only if justified** | Admit a demonstrated high-value short-turn case through the existing reviewer when foreground capture remains insufficient. | Depends on A/B evidence and a maintainer admission-policy decision. Preserve quiet-time, capacity, identity and authority controls; avoid duplicate or recursive review. No blanket threshold reduction or model call after every message. Omit this unit if the earlier work solves the gap. |

**First milestone:** A, the justified portion of B, and C. Reliable capture and reuse must not depend on building an optimizer.

**Second milestone:** D, then E if accepted. F is an evidence-triggered branch, not a mandatory feature.

### Proof required

Use scenarios covering a useful new procedure, a correction to a used skill, an already-covered lesson, routine work, a successful recovery, an unresolved attempt, denied authority and unavailable runtime capability.

For reuse, withhold the original solved answer and change the input. For optimization, reserve validation cases not used to select edits. Correctness and critical regressions take precedence over token or tool-call savings. Human review or inconclusive results are legitimate outcomes.

Fixtures, skill text and transcripts are evidence, not permission. Tests must not act on real external accounts or collect private conversations, credentials or personal facts.

## Alternatives considered

- **Use existing guidance unchanged:** preferred if characterization demonstrates sufficient coverage; retain useful regression proof rather than adding a feature.
- **Rely on explicit learning requests:** remains valid, but does not establish whether useful discoveries are consistently captured during ordinary work.
- **Lower review thresholds globally:** adds work without establishing that the lost cases contain reusable lessons.
- **Build a new learning service:** duplicates existing owners and is unnecessary unless a specific missing contract is demonstrated.
- **Apply an evaluation gate only to proposals:** cannot support a universal validation promise while direct maintenance remains outside that path. Either state the narrower guarantee or obtain agreement on a coherent change to the owner contract.

## Impact

Affected users are operators relying on learned skills across sessions. The intended benefit is fewer repeated procedural corrections and clearer evidence about what was learned. Frequency and magnitude have not been measured; no reliability percentage, runtime regression or release blocker is asserted.

## Evidence/examples

The input research was a static review pinned to OpenClaw `ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d`; it reported no executed tests or agent trials. Its relevant source pointers are [foreground guidance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/agents/skill-workshop-prompt.ts), [review admission](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/skills/workshop/experience-review-scheduler.ts), and [proposal evaluation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ca38979d2128d21616f815136f48d7466b803b4d/src/skills/workshop/service-evaluation.ts). These are research provenance, not freshly reproduced current-main defects.

The related tracker items and current documentation above were inspected while revising this proposal. Current-source history and behavioral reproduction remain the first implementation step. Hermes supplied UX inspiration in the original research; neither Hermes parity nor a claim of mandatory automatic benchmarking is an acceptance criterion.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself, after agreement on scope and ownership. I would start with the coverage evidence and the smallest demonstrated foreground gap.

## Additional information

**Maintainer decision requested:** does the first milestone belong on a new coordination issue or an existing owner surface? Separately, should a reference behavioral evaluator start as an external plugin, and is an optional required-evaluation/revision policy wanted at all? Neither question assumes approval for a new core contract.

Initial scope excludes a new memory backend, model training, registry, persistent controller, external skill installation, automatic sharing, protected third-party skill edits, model-routing changes, mandatory auto-publication, age-only retirement and same-session context replacement.

### Closure criteria

- [ ] Each workstream is completed with evidence, shown unnecessary, or explicitly deferred with maintainer agreement and a linked owner where appropriate.
- [ ] Accepted learning cases demonstrate correct capture and later reuse; negative controls show meaningful abstention and preserved authority.
- [ ] Evaluation claims identify the tested revision, environment and limits; untested direct maintenance receives no implicit validation badge.
- [ ] No duplicate proposal store, scheduler, publication authority or ownership takeover was introduced.
- [ ] Accepted changes include relevant regression tests, documentation and actual runtime evidence where required.

Intermediate PRs should use `Related: #<umbrella>` and explain which workstream they advance. Only the change satisfying all remaining closure criteria should close the umbrella. Preserve the original contributors’ authorship when extending or reusing their work.

issues.body:
### Summary

OpenClaw binds a model provider to a CLI runtime only when the registered CLI backend declares a `modelProvider` field. When the field is missing, `addCliRuntimeModelBinding` returns early without creating the binding and without emitting any diagnostic. Every model of that provider then falls through to the regular HTTP transport. Because such providers carry a `cli://` `baseUrl`, the user gets `Invalid URL: must be http or https` — an error that points at provider configuration while the actual cause is an incomplete plugin registration contract.

Nothing is logged at plugin load time and nothing is logged at call time. In agent runs the failure is invisible: the run completes with `status: ok` on a fallback model, and the run record contains no trace that the requested model was ever attempted.

### Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.10.3 (`59cb447`); also reproduced on 2026.10.2 (`b8952d4`)
- Self-hosted Gateway, Docker (OrbStack), Linux arm64, Node v24.21.0
- Plugin: `@jeehou/openclaw-cursor-cli` 0.0.6 (third-party), enabled, capabilities `cli-backend` + `text-inference`
- Provider: `models.providers.cursor-cli`, `baseUrl: "cli://cursor-agent"`, `api: "openai-completions"`, 44 models
- Binary `cursor-agent` 2026.10.14 works standalone; `CURSOR_API_KEY` present in the Gateway environment

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install a plugin that calls `api.registerCliBackend({ id, config, ... })` **without** a `modelProvider` field.
2. Declare a provider catalog with `baseUrl: cli://<binary>`.
3. Run:

```
openclaw infer model run --agent <id> --model cursor-cli/grok-4.7 --prompt "test"
```

### Expected behavior

Either the call is routed to the CLI backend, or the system reports the real cause — that the registered CLI backend declares no `modelProvider`, so no provider↔runtime binding exists. A registration missing a required contract field should be logged at plugin load time, naming the plugin.

### Actual behavior

```text
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] error provider=cursor-cli api=openai-completions
model=grok-4.7 message=Invalid URL: must be http or https
No text output returned for provider "cursor-cli" model "grok-4.7": Connection error..
```

In agent runs not even this appears: the run reports `status: ok` on the fallback model with no error and no diagnostic about the failed primary.

### Root cause

`dist/cli-backends-DNm7Vv7X.mjs`:

```js
function resolveCliBackendModelProvider(backend) {
  const provider = backend.modelProvider?.trim();
  return provider ? normalizeProviderId(provider) : void 0;
}

function addCliRuntimeModelBinding(bindings, params) {
  const provider = resolveCliBackendModelProvider(params.backend);
  const runtime  = normalizeProviderId(params.backend.id);
  if (!provider || !runtime) return;        // <-- silent drop
  bindings.set(`${provider}:${runtime}`, { provider, runtime, ... });
}
```

Built-in backends do set the field — `dist/cli-backend-BCcgnXM1.mjs:78` → `modelProvider: "anthropic"`, `dist/cli-backend-_dS2dNnJ.mjs:64` → `modelProvider: "google"` — so the requirement is real but undocumented for third-party authors and unvalidated at registration.

Verified in isolation (plugin copy + symlinked SDK, outside the Gateway):

```text
backend.id            = cursor-cli
backend.modelProvider = cursor-cli
BINDING OK -> cursor-cli:cursor-cli
args for grok-4.7/high: ["-p","--model","grok-4.7-high"]
```

Adding the single field restores routing. `registerCliBackend` appears 11 times in `dist`, so the extension point is live and is being called; only the binding step opts out.

### Impact

- Any third-party CLI backend written before `modelProvider` existed stops working after a Gateway upgrade, with no signal at all.
- The visible error points at the provider's `baseUrl`, sending the operator into model configuration while the defect is in the plugin registration contract. This cost hours of diagnosis here.
- The agent silently runs on a model the operator did not configure, and the run record preserves no evidence of the substitution.

### Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

1. Log a warning when a CLI backend registers without `modelProvider`, naming the plugin.
2. Or default `modelProvider` to `backend.id` when the field is absent (for this plugin the two are identical).
3. When a model whose `baseUrl` uses the `cli://` scheme reaches the HTTP transport, report the missing CLI runtime binding instead of an invalid URL.
4. Record the primary model's failure reason in the agent run record before falling back.
5. Document `modelProvider` as required in the `registerCliBackend` plugin API reference.

### Related

- #160317 — same subsystem (custom `registerCliBackend` plugin), different symptom: the static model catalog never reaches the configured `models.list` view. Possibly a shared root in how third-party CLI backends are wired into model resolution.

### Workaround

Patch the plugin locally to add `modelProvider: PROVIDER_ID` to the object returned by its `buildCliBackend()`. Lost on plugin update.

### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

Sessions under an agent with `runtime.type: "acp"` execute tasks normally and
the reply eventually completes, but the Control UI webchat shows **no
incremental output during the turn** — content only appears after turn
completion. Native OpenClaw runtime sessions in the same webchat stream
token-by-token as expected.

Streaming appears to be enabled at every lower layer:

- `claude` CLI is spawned with `--include-partial-messages --output-format stream-json --verbose` (verified via `ps`)
- Model provider returns `text/event-stream` (verified in gateway's own provider-transport logs)
- `acp.stream.deliveryMode: "live"` was active before session creation (hot-reloaded, then gateway restarted; session created afterwards)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an ACP runtime agent as above with `deliveryMode: "live"`.
2. Open its chat in Control UI (`/chat/claude/<label>`), send a prompt that produces multi-step output over ~1-2 min, e.g. "count from 1 to 10, one line at a time".
3. Turn runs (reply-timing shows `reason=acp_dispatch`, `outcome=completed`, e.g. `totalMs=102557`) with many intermediate blocks (`thinking`/`text`/`tool_use`), but nothing renders incrementally.
4. On **every** ACP turn completion, journalctl shows:

```
[gateway] terminal session persistence failed
  session=agent:claude:acp:<uuid>
  run=<runId>
  error=Error: Terminal write owner changed before commit
```

This error fires for every completed ACP turn across two different ACP
sessions (interactive webchat-bound). It does not fire for native runtime
turns.

### Expected behavior

With `acp.stream.deliveryMode: "live"`, an interactive webchat-bound ACP
session should project harness output incrementally into the Control UI
transcript while the turn runs: assistant text/thinking blocks and tool
activity appearing progressively as the harness emits them — matching the
live streaming behavior of native OpenClaw runtime sessions on the same
webchat surface.

### Actual behavior

The turn executes normally in the harness (multi-block agentic output over
~100 s with `--include-partial-messages` active), but the webchat transcript
shows nothing during the run. The full reply only appears once the turn
completes, as if `final_only` were in effect. On every ACP turn completion
the gateway logs `terminal session persistence failed ... Terminal write
owner changed before commit`; native runtime sessions in the same webchat
stream token-by-token without any such error.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.7

### Operating system

ubuntu 24.04

### Install method

npm global

### Model

deepseek-v41-flash

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> deepseek

### Additional provider/model setup details

## Environment

- OpenClaw: 2026.9.7 (c074824) — current npm latest
- OS: Linux x64, Node v24.21.0, gateway mode `local`, webchat via Control UI
- ACP backend: bundled acpx plugin, agent `claude` (Claude Code via `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp` wrapper)
- Harness model: routed through an OpenAI-compatible proxy endpoint (SSE-capable, verified)

## Config

```json
"acp": {
  "enabled": true,
  "backend": "acpx",
  "defaultAgent": "claude",
  "allowedAgents": ["claude"],
  "stream": { "deliveryMode": "live" }
}
```

Agent entry:

```json
"claude": {
  "name": "claude",
  "runtime": { "type": "acp", "acp": { "agent": "claude" } }
}
```



### Logs

```shell

```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

_No response_

### Impact and severity

## Suspected area

ACP session transcript persistence write-owner race in the turn-terminal
commit path — projected output never reaches the webchat transcript
incrementally. Dist code contains a sibling error pattern
(`Subagent abort-marker owner changed before commit`), suggesting a shared
commit-race guard.

## Impact

Cosmetic for delivery (task execution, results, multi-turn context all work),
but makes long ACP turns appear hung in the UI and defeats
`acp.stream.deliveryMode: "live"`.

### Additional information

_No response_

issues.body:
Bug type: Regression (worked before, now fails)
Beta release blocker: No

## Summary

Since #184013 (reuse prepared statements per PostgreSQL connection, merged 2026-10-30), `sessions.search` on PostgreSQL loses the #187909 fix (#187908) in steady state. After 5 executions on a bridge connection, PostgreSQL switches the reused prepared statement to a generic plan. In that plan the agent scope filter `session_key ^@ $6` has no value to estimate from, so the planner again expects about 6 session windows, drives a nested loop from them, and evaluates the tsquery against every transcript row of the agent instead of using the GIN index.

## Steps to reproduce

1. PostgreSQL engine, main at 4d2a9f8bb4c (2026.10.9) or later, which includes both #187909 and #184013. Use any agent with a few hundred sessions. Ours: a ported production store with 636 session windows and 7,956 transcript rows.
2. Call `sessions.search` (for example `{"query":"postgres","limit":20}`) more than 5 times through the same Gateway.
3. Compare `pg_stat_statements` for the `with "hits" as materialized ...` statement with a single psql run of the same SQL.

Standalone: capture the statement and its parameters (`log_min_duration_statement = 0`), `PREPARE q AS <statement>`, then `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) EXECUTE q(...)` under `plan_cache_mode = force_custom_plan` and `force_generic_plan`, or just execute it 7 times under the default `auto`.

## Expected behavior

Every search uses the `session_transcript_fts_search_gin` bitmap scan, as it does on the first five executions and in psql (#187909).

## Actual behavior

From the 6th execution on, the generic plan is used:

```
Index Only Scan using idx_agent_session_windows_session_key on session_windows (rows=6) (actual rows=636)
  Filter: ((session_key ^@ $6) OR (session_key = ANY (ARRAY[$7, $8])))
-> Index Scan using idx_session_transcript_fts_rows_session_message (actual rows=7956)
-> Index Scan using session_transcript_fts_pkey (loops=7956)
     Filter: (openclaw_search @@ (COALESCE((InitPlan 2).col1, ''))::tsquery)
Buffers: shared hit=40422
```

Same captured statement, same data, PostgreSQL 17.11 (shared host, so absolute times are noisy; the plan shape and buffers are not):

| plan_cache_mode | GIN used | Execution time | Buffers |
|---|---|---|---|
| force_custom_plan | yes | 30.0 ms | - |
| force_generic_plan | no | 88.0 ms | 40,422 hits |
| auto, 7th execution | no (`generic_plans=4, custom_plans=5`) | 50.5 ms | - |
| force_generic_plan, prefix inlined as a literal | yes | 6.7 ms | 578 hits |

In the Gateway (pg_stat_statements per arm, sessions.search only): ~44k shared buffer hits per call and ~0 ms plan time (cached generic plan), versus ~7k buffers per call measured right after #187909 merged. That is the #187908 pattern again.

## Proposed fix

Inline the agent prefix as a literal in the PostgreSQL scope filter so the generic plan keeps the estimate. One line in `src/config/sessions/session-transcript-search.ts`:

```diff
-  sql<boolean>`${eb.ref("session_key")} ^@ ${agentPrefix}`
+  sql<boolean>`${eb.ref("session_key")} ^@ ${sql.lit(agentPrefix)}`
```

`sql.lit` quotes and doubles single quotes (kysely 0.29.7 `sanitizeStringLiteral`). Each agent gets its own cached statement text (one per agent, well under the 256-statement cache). Alternatives: `SET LOCAL plan_cache_mode = force_custom_plan` around the search transaction, or an option on the statement cache to skip naming for a query. Both need more plumbing than the literal. A global `force_custom_plan` would undo #184013's planning savings for every other statement.

No red/green test yet: the plan only flips on data large enough for the GIN path to win, and the statement observer normalizes literals, so a cheap deterministic test is still open. I will follow up with a PR that includes a regression test.

## OpenClaw version
2026.10.9 (main 4d2a9f8bb4c, 2026-10-31)

## Operating system
macOS 26 (arm64), PostgreSQL 17.11 + pgvector 0.8.7

## Install method
git checkout, `pnpm build`

## Model / Provider
n/a (no model calls; read-only RPC bench)

## Logs

Captured statement, parameter list and both plans: outputs/pg-round2/L3/results/generic_postgres*.txt (local evidence, not attached).

## Impact and severity

Affected: every PostgreSQL Gateway after #184013, for every agent and every search after the 5th on a pooled connection, which is effectively all searches in steady state.
Severity: performance regression. Search returns correct results, but each search costs a full per-agent transcript scan again (2-13x more execution time on our data, ~70x more buffers).
Frequency: always, once a connection has run the statement 5 times.
Consequence: search latency and DB CPU are back at pre-#187909 levels, and searches against one agent store queue behind each other under concurrency (see #187908).

## Additional information

Related: #187908 / #187909 (the original planner fix), #184013 / #183698 (statement reuse).

Gateway A/B, same data, 3 interleaved rounds per build (fresh DB from template per run), main 4d2a9f8bb4c vs the same plus the one-line change. sessions.search only, closed loop. pg_stat_statements per arm. Median of 3 runs (host shared, load average 12-42 during these runs):

| | base | literal prefix |
|---|---|---|
| concurrency 1: p50 / p95 / p99 | 21.5 / 58.2 / 102.7 ms | 7.3 / 11.2 / 23.5 ms |

issues.body:
Drop MESSAGE_CREATE event when receiving-bot-account has isDefault=true AND a more-specific-scoped binding matches for the target channel

## Summary
Currently, an openclaw gateway configured with multi-agent bindings + isDefault fallback causes multi-agent fanout on human messages: a single human message on a channel bound to specific agent B causes BOTH bot account A (isDefault=true) AND bot account B (bindings[peer:channel:cid]) to independently generate replies. Result: user observes duplicate/cascaded bot responses to single message. Config knob `channels.discord.allowBots=false` empirically closes cross-bot echo (bot X reading bot Y's output as input) but does NOT close human-triggered multi-agent fanout because human messages bypass allowBots gate entirely.

## Steps to reproduce

1. openclaw config with:
   - `agents.list[0] = {id: "hedwig", isDefault: true, ...}` (guild-scoped catch-all)
   - `agents.list[1] = {id: "nanami", bindings: [{peer: {kind: "channel", id: "CHANNEL_X"}, ...}]}`
   - Discord guild with both Hedwig APP and OpenClaw Nanami APP as members with View Channel permission on CHANNEL_X
   - `channels.discord.allowBots: false` (to rule out cross-bot echo)
2. Human user posts message in CHANNEL_X
3. Both bot APPs generate independent replies within seconds of each other

## Empirical evidence

- `cowork-session/state/a692-post-restart-check-20260820T0315Z.log` — 7 bot messages POST-baseline (post-restart with allowBots=false LIVE) including two 03:04Z→03:05Z fanout instances
- Human ghostclaw asked "How is everything" at 03:04:49Z; Hedwig APP replied 03:05:06Z; Nanami APP replied 03:05:58Z (both bot=true; distinct account IDs)
- Config state at incident: allowBots=false, gateway pid 92348 stable, hedwig.isDefault=true, nanami.bindings=[peer:channel:1534983396340793405]

## Expected behavior

When bot account A receives a MESSAGE_CREATE event on channel Y where:
- A has `isDefault: true` at scope broader than Y
- Some other agent B has a binding whose peer matches Y

Then A's gateway SHOULD drop the event before processing (delegate to B's more-specific binding). Alternatively, A's isDefault should be interpreted as "catches unhandled channels" — where "unhandled" means "no other binding matches at more-specific scope."

## Actual behavior

A processes the event independently, producing a Hedwig-voice reply that posts via A's account. B ALSO processes the event via its binding. User sees two replies.

## Proposed fix (server-side)

In gateway routing:
```
def route_message_create(event, agent):
    if agent.is_default:
        # Check if any other agent has a more-specific binding matching event.channel_id
        more_specific = [
            a for a in all_agents
            if a.id != agent.id
            and any(
                b.matches_channel(event.channel_id)
                and b.scope_depth() > agent.default_scope_depth()
                for b in a.bindings
            )
        ]
        if more_specific:
            return drop_event(event, reason="delegated_to_more_specific_binding")
    return process_event(event, agent)
```

Where `scope_depth()` returns integer (guild=1, channel=2, thread=3, etc.).

## Alternative: config-only workaround

Users could work around this by:
- Removing isDefault from agent A (loses catch-all behavior for untargeted channels)
- Adding per-channel exclusion bindings to A (requires schema support for exclusion bindings, currently unclear)
- Moving each specific-binding agent to a channel-scoped isDefault (requires schema support for channel-scoped isDefault)

Please confirm which config workaround is currently supported. Empirical schema audit `state/a692-schema-audit-20260820T0335Z.log` in-flight to determine feasibility.

## Impact

- Every openclaw deployment with a catch-all agent + per-channel bindings is affected
- User-observable duplicate replies degrade UX
- No config workaround currently identified without functionality loss

## Backward compatibility

Proposed fix is opt-in via new config knob `agents.default_delegation_mode` with values:
- `"catch_all"` (current behavior, default for backward compat)
- `"defer_to_specific"` (new behavior — drop when more-specific binding matches)

Users can migrate on their own schedule.

---

Robert to file at github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/new (or wherever upstream lives) using this body verbatim. Alternative: task-agent can attempt `gh api POST /repos/<owner>/openclaw/issues` if hedwig confirms `<owner>` = openclaw org.

issues.body:
## Summary

Add an optional Cua Spaces integration through the existing WorkerProvider plugin contract.

## Problem to solve

Operators with Cua Spaces cannot select their existing Cua infrastructure as an OpenClaw worker provider. They need the standard worker execution and desktop workflow while Cua owns allocation and deletion.

## Proposed solution

Add an optional provider for dedicated, disposable Linux x64 Cua Spaces. Keep the Gateway on its existing host. Use Core-owned Node enrollment grants, the existing worker-turn and remote-exec modes, and Core's authenticated desktop viewer.

Keep placement and account selection in explicit trusted configuration. Local placement stays the default. Direct and Relay placement must retain the exact parent, child, account context, and operation ownership. The provider must report indeterminate cleanup when the host API cannot prove physical absence.

The first implementation keeps a pinned container image, runc runtime, no reuse, no public ports, and guest-only desktop control. It adds no general Gateway token or host desktop access. A bundled implementation would live under extensions/cua-spaces-worker and use the current public Plugin SDK. An external plugin remains a supported alternative if maintainers prefer that ownership model.

## Alternatives considered

- Keep a standalone plugin. This already fits the public SDK and avoids another bundled dependency, but maintainers would not own its release or compatibility.
- Reuse Crabbox. Crabbox is the existing bundled WorkerProvider precedent. This request is for Cua infrastructure and its native capabilities, with separate lifecycle and ownership behavior.

## Impact

This affects operators who already use Cua and want to attach a disposable worker to an OpenClaw conversation. The missing integration blocks that workflow until they maintain an external adapter. No outage, account change, paid plan, or automatic migration is implied.

## Evidence/examples

- The current public WorkerProvider contract and bundled Crabbox provider supply the required plugin registration, execution modes, enrollment callbacks, and desktop lease contract.
- An external candidate targets OpenClaw 2026.10.7 and @trycua/cua 0.9.0. Its isolated synthetic suite passed 86 tests with no skips and its package installation was checked. This is evidence for that candidate, not proof of compatibility with current main.
- An earlier local candidate demonstrated same-guest Core execution, files, computer interaction, and the Core viewer with a reviewed task-only Core enrollment repair. Stock Core and the current candidate were not qualified by that run. The existing enrollment work remains separately owned in #159178 and is not duplicated here.
- Genuine remote allocation, guest execution, and teardown remain unverified. A successful host delete response is not physical absence proof.

## Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself.

## Additional information

The goal extends beyond parity with another worker backend. The proposal is phased so OpenClaw can use Cua's native lifecycle, placement, desktop, and storage capabilities through the SDK rather than rebuild them. Later units can evaluate native media streams, stop/resume, checkpoints and forks, volumes, and prewarm where the supported contracts permit them. Each needs its own ownership model and runtime proof. The initial provider does not implement or claim those capabilities.

No Core enrollment repair, new generic manager, paid service, account enrollment, host listener, host desktop, or production deployment belongs in the first slice.

issues.body:
### Summary

Let operators pass an explicit vocabulary to Scribe v2 through the bundled ElevenLabs batch transcription provider using the existing `providerOptions.elevenlabs` configuration.

### Problem to solve

When transcribing recordings containing product names or specialized terms, an operator may want to supply a specific list of recognition hints. A [LiveKit developer requested this integration control](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408) on February 27, 2026, and supplied an implementation for that product. This is an external demand signal; applying the task to OpenClaw's recorded-audio workflow is an inference, not a report that this person uses OpenClaw.

OpenClaw already transcribes audio through Scribe v2. Its [current ElevenLabs implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts) reads only `no_verbatim`, `tag_audio_events`, and `diarize` from provider options. A configured `keyterms` array reaches the provider request context but never enters the multipart request. The [provider documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/docs/providers/elevenlabs.md#provider-options) explicitly limits support to those three fields.

The missing capability is selecting the terms used by Scribe's recognition-bias mechanism within this native transcription path. This does not promise correct spelling for every recording or a general improvement in accuracy.

### Proposed solution

Support one additional, opt-in provider option, `keyterms: string[]`, for `scribe_v2` batch transcription. Reuse current provider-scoped configuration and merge precedence; no new top-level configuration or tool is needed. For example:

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "media": {
      "models": [{
        "provider": "elevenlabs",
        "model": "scribe_v2",
        "capabilities": ["audio"]
      }],
      "audio": {
        "enabled": true,
        "providerOptions": {
          "elevenlabs": {
            "keyterms": ["OpenClaw", "Acme Research", "PostgreSQL"]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Serialize the list as repeated multipart `keyterms` fields, following the provider's array contract and [official SDK request construction](https://github.com/elevenlabs/elevenlabs-python/blob/f5d53e09e35717523435cee238ac5cc7f51966fb/src/elevenlabs/speech_to_text/raw_client.py#L177). Preserve each term's spelling and Unicode content; do not comma-join the list or encode it as one JSON string. Keep all option fields before the original file, preserving its filename, MIME type, and bytes; the shared multipart builder documents this ordering for streaming parsers. Keep array assembly provider-local rather than widening the shared scalar helper. A model-entry list replaces the audio-default list, as existing options already do. An empty list clears inherited terms; an absent or empty effective list sends no keyterms.

Keep this an explicit allowlisted addition. Preserve dedicated fields, existing scalar options, authentication, guarded HTTP transport, cancellation, and the synchronous transcript-text result. Reject an incompatible option shape or unsupported model rather than silently applying a different control. Surface provider validation errors through the existing error/fallback handling without truncating terms silently.

Document the option and its extra provider charge before users choose it. The [current API reference](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/speech-to-text/convert) currently permits up to 1,000 terms, requires each term to have fewer than 50 characters and at most five normalized words, and specifies disallowed characters. It adds a 20% surcharge; more than 100 terms also impose a minimum billable duration of 20 seconds per request. The provider remains authoritative for validation and future billing changes. No vocabulary is inferred from conversation history or sent by default.

### Alternatives considered

- **Explicit transcription prompt:** OpenClaw already forwards a configured prompt as context. It may help some tasks, but the current ElevenLabs API reference does not specify it as equivalent to structured `keyterms`. Preserve existing prompt behavior; this proposal does not claim it is useless.
- **Deepgram:** OpenClaw supports repeatable Deepgram keyterms after [#176781](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176781). Switching providers is valid. This proposal retains the selected ElevenLabs account and model.
- **Official ElevenLabs skill or SDK, a CLI transcription model, or a custom provider plugin:** These can perform vocabulary-guided transcription outside the bundled adapter. The [official skill reference](https://github.com/elevenlabs/skills/blob/9a1a4b7fbb6ca02fbdc7f44f2271e6c829d0f421/speech-to-text/references/transcription-options.md) includes keyterms. These are real alternatives; native support avoids maintaining a separate transcription script or provider registration for one additional input.
- **Correct text afterward:** This can repair known spelling errors but does not give the recognizer a selected term list. An uncertain correction can also change meaning.

### Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: Operators using bundled ElevenLabs transcription for recorded audio with specialized vocabulary. The affected OpenClaw population is unknown.
- Severity/urgency: The requested recognition control is unavailable in that adapter; ordinary transcription remains usable. No production outage or measured urgency is established.
- Frequency: A configured list would apply to matching transcription requests. Actual usage frequency is unknown.
- Practical consequences: Operators must accept transcription without that control, correct text, switch providers, or maintain another integration. Time savings and accuracy gains have not been measured. Enabling keyterms can increase provider charges.

### Evidence/examples

- [Original integration request and follow-up](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408); [LiveKit implementation #4967](https://github.com/livekit/agents/pull/4967). These concern the same author and task, not two independent users.
- [Official keyterm guide](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/speech-to-text/batch/keyterm-prompting) describes vocabulary biasing and distinguishes batch and realtime inputs.
- [Current options schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/config/zod-schema.core.ts#L627), [runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts#L86), and [registered provider](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts#L22) establish the input path and missing mapping.
- [#177975](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177975) already implemented three scalar options. This request adds a vocabulary input; it does not reopen that repaired bug or propose unrestricted forwarding.

Verification was static against the pinned main revision. No installed Gateway, live ElevenLabs transcription, or recognition-quality comparison was run for this proposal.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

The implementation owner is `extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts`; its former standalone media-understanding module was consolidated into registration. Suggested work is provider-local array serialization and validation, focused registered-provider coverage, and documentation. Public `AudioTranscriptionRequest.query` already accepts string arrays. A new SDK contract, provider manager, dictionary store, or model-facing tool is unnecessary.

Preserve the existing media authorization, HTTP guards, and cancellation behavior applicable to the caller at dispatch; this option does not introduce a new universal execution context. A vocabulary does not authorize a transcription request. Keep terms out of diagnostic logs; they may contain names absent from the audio. No retention or permission change is requested.

Non-goals: Realtime/Voice Call/Google Meet transcription, TTS pronunciation dictionaries, vocabulary management, speaker-label output, asynchronous webhooks, redaction, multichannel results, unrestricted form overrides, or guaranteed accuracy. No implementer has committed.

Acceptance criteria:

- With an isolated configuration selecting `elevenlabs/scribe_v2`, native recorded-audio transcription sends two configured terms as separate multipart fields alongside one unchanged audio file, and returns the transcript through the existing path.
- Capture the actual HTTP body from the shipped transcription entry point, not only a helper call. Verify model-entry replacement of defaults, an empty list clearing defaults, and unchanged requests without a list.
- Existing scalar `false` values and dedicated model/language/prompt fields retain their behavior. Other providers do not receive the ElevenLabs vocabulary; unsupported response-changing keys remain excluded.
- An incompatible scalar value or unsupported model does not silently send an unconditioned Scribe request. Provider-side term rejection surfaces without truncation. With an actual cancellation-capable execution context, cancellation before dispatch prevents a request.
- In an authorized live check, submit a synthetic name-bearing recording with a valid small vocabulary and confirm provider acceptance and native transcript return. Recognition output is observational evidence, not a promise that every supplied term appears.

labels.name: P3

issues.body:
### Summary

Add an optional tool to the existing ElevenLabs plugin that turns an ordered script with two selected voices into one generated dialogue MP3.

### Problem to solve

A scripted interview or podcast scene needs a relationship between each line and its speaker, together with the surrounding exchange. The [podcast_generator project](https://github.com/sjfischr/podcast_generator/blob/d1a7ca31814995bd3748b771ab348789df441783/README.md) implements this task using batches of speaker turns. Its author explains why synthesizing each turn separately and assembling the recordings does not provide the same conversational context. That is an external implementation and reported motivation; I have not independently evaluated its audio quality.

There is also an OpenClaw-specific consumer surface: [pixcli's registry README](https://hub.openclaw.ai/shellbot/plugins/openclaw-pixcli) advertises optional dialogue and podcast tools. It is an existing alternative, not a request from its author to migrate.

The bundled ElevenLabs integration currently accepts one text and one voice per synthesis request. A speaker name written into that text does not become a second voice assignment. The requested output is a short jointly generated exchange using the operator's ElevenLabs voices, rather than an ordinary spoken assistant reply. Applicability to operators of the bundled plugin is an inference from these public workflows, not a reported OpenClaw outage.

### Proposed solution

Keep this capability inside `extensions/elevenlabs`, behind an explicitly enabled plugin tool; `elevenlabs_dialogue` is a suggested name. Use the existing optional-tool registration and manifest contracts. Do not expand the core `tts` tool or the shared speech interface.

The initial tool would accept an ordered array of nonempty `{text, voiceId}` turns, with exactly two distinct voice IDs. Generate a single bounded scene using Eleven v3 and return one MP3 artifact. Preserve turn order and inline audio tags. Reject scripts above a total of 2,000 text characters before making a request; this intentionally excludes automatic long-form episode production.

Reuse the plugin's configured authentication, runtime-resolved secrets, trusted base URL and guarded HTTP helpers for `POST /v1/text-to-dialogue`. Use `mp3_44100_128`. Do not accept credentials, arbitrary endpoints or publication destinations in tool arguments. Keep normal tool admission, cancellation and current invocation authority. A provider error must not silently substitute another provider or turn the script into single-voice narration. Do not automatically regenerate or replay a request whose paid outcome is unknown.

Return the audio through existing media storage and tool-result/reply contracts. Artifact creation and delivery must be distinguished; do not claim delivery from a local path alone.

### Alternatives considered

- Repeated TTS calls followed by audio assembly preserve voice assignments, but each synthesis lacks the complete exchange. They remain useful when independently editable stems are the goal.
- The external Python project or a direct ElevenLabs SDK integration can already perform the vendor request; a custom OpenClaw tool can wrap that existing contract. An equivalent multi-voice operation in the current hosted ElevenLabs MCP was not established. These are valid alternatives; this proposal adds a narrowly scoped operation to an existing bundled owner, rather than claiming that OpenClaw cannot run such a workflow at all.
- pixcli already supplies dialogue tooling through its separately configured Meterkey service. Its README permits private output; it does not force public publishing. Keeping the existing ElevenLabs account and voice catalog is the distinction here, not an invented ban on other plugins.
- Other speech providers can offer dialogue, but their voices are not the selected ElevenLabs voice IDs.

### Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: operators generating two-voice scripted scenes with the bundled ElevenLabs integration. The public projects establish the task, not the size of this population.
- Severity/urgency: an additional authoring capability; existing single-voice speech remains available. No production incident or urgency has been established.
- Frequency: unknown. Each qualifying scene needs one bounded dialogue request.
- Practical consequences: the bundled integration cannot currently express both speaker assignments in a joint synthesis. Operators use a separate integration or assemble independently generated turns. No measured time savings or quality improvement is claimed.

### Evidence/examples

- [External batch producer](https://github.com/sjfischr/podcast_generator/blob/d1a7ca31814995bd3748b771ab348789df441783/generate_podcast.py): `build_batches` and `generate_dialogue_batch` preserve speaker turns. Its older batch-size assumptions should not be copied.
- [ElevenLabs API contract](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/text-to-dialogue/convert): ordered text/voice pairs produce audio. This proposal uses a smaller two-voice subset and the current short-request guidance.
- [Current bundled request builder](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8b8c33ef334b3754f42afe2a2e212418abfa80f4/extensions/elevenlabs/speech-provider-factory.ts) and [plugin entry](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8b8c33ef334b3754f42afe2a2e212418abfa80f4/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts): scalar synthesis and no dialogue tool.
- [Existing optional-tool contract](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/8b8c33ef334b3754f42afe2a2e212418abfa80f4/docs/plugins/building-plugins.md#registering-tools).
- Related [issue #165655](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165655) / [PR #165656](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/165656) concern dialogue-model transport for a single speaking voice and phone-call socket reuse. The inspected open PR sends one text/voice pair; this proposal concerns a structured multi-voice script and an audio file.

This is static source and public-contract research. No vendor request, installed-plugin execution or listening test was performed.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Suggested implementation: register an optional version 2 tool in the existing plugin and declare its manifest ownership; factor reusable plugin-local credential/config and request helpers rather than copying their policy. The public factory context already supplies runtime config, provider-key resolution and `assertInvocationCurrent`; recheck current authority after awaited preparation and before the request and artifact admission. Reuse focused media-store and bounded binary-response helpers. For a finished direct reply, the existing `canDeliverSourceReply` / `details.sourceReply` contract can deliver the artifact; nested Code Mode execution remains program data under that contract.

Non-goals: real-time calls, WebSocket pooling, new v4 model support, voice cloning, speaker identification, transcription, pronunciation-dictionary management, long-script chunking, audio editing, podcast hosting, public uploads, new persistent jobs, and a generic dialogue SDK. Existing TTS defaults, personas and fallback behavior remain outside this tool's operation.

Acceptance criteria:

- With the tool explicitly enabled and usable ElevenLabs credentials, submit a short A/B/A script with two accessible voice IDs. One dialogue request preserves the three turns and both IDs, and returns a playable MP3. Confirm the supplied voice assignments with a listening test as well as the request trace; do not promise subjective quality.
- The returned artifact is usable through the actual tool/result path. A direct source reply reaches only the admitted source conversation; a nested program call returns data without an unsolicited send.
- Empty text, malformed voice ID syntax, a missing second voice, and a script over the character budget fail before the vendor request. A syntactically valid voice ID may still be unavailable to the account; surface that provider access/validation failure honestly rather than claiming local validation proves access. The disabled tool is absent from discovery. Cancellation, a retired invocation, and credential/plugin disablement do not admit a new request or publish a success artifact.
- Authentication, validation, timeout, malformed audio and size-limit failures produce an actionable error, without silent voice/provider substitution or automatic paid regeneration. Existing single-voice TTS still works with its previous defaults.

Implementer unknown. Live synthesis, real tool delivery, failure/cancellation proof and focused plugin/contract checks remain work for the eventual implementation. Maintainers should decide whether this existing-owner enhancement is worth maintaining relative to the external alternatives.

issues.body:
# Issue 2: Feishu plugin doctor reloads the whole session store with skipCache on every startup

## Summary

On every gateway startup, the Feishu channel plugin's doctor sequence calls
`loadSessionStore(target.storePath, { skipCache: true })`, which **forces a full
re-read of the agent's entire session store** from disk — on the main thread,
during startup.

On our install the agent store is **1.26 GB** (`transcript_events` 78,440 rows),
and this read took **85 s** with `outcome: "error"`, blocking the event loop and
delaying every other plugin's `import()` behind it.

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)**, npm-global
- `@openclaw/feishu` (bundled), Windows 10.0.26300 x64, Node 24.19.0
- Agent store `openclaw-agent.sqlite` 1.26 GB
- Feishu enabled as the only channel

## Where

`@openclaw/feishu/dist/channel-*.js`:

```js
function inspectFeishuDoctorState(params) {
  ...
  for (const target of collectFeishuSessionTargets({ cfg: params.cfg, env, stateDir })) {
    const store = loadSessionStore(target.storePath, { skipCache: true });   // ← full re-read
    for (const [key, entry] of Object.entries(store)) { ... }
  }
}

async function runFeishuDoctorSequence(params) {
  ...
  const inspection = inspectFeishuDoctorState({ cfg: params.cfg, env: params.env });
  if (inspection.findings.length === 0) return { changeNotes: [], warnings: [] };
  ...
}
```

and it is invoked as a plugin-declared config sequence:

```js
const feishuDoctor = {
  runConfigSequence: async ({ cfg, env, shouldRepair }) =>
    runFeishuDoctorSequence({ cfg, env, shouldRepair }),
};
```

## Evidence

Main-thread block during the plugin load window:

```
{"operation":"direct","outcome":"error","pid":32560,"threadId":0,
 "isMainThread":true,"reentrant":false,"elapsedMs":94251,
 "queueWaitMs":0,"writerExecutionMs":94251,"completionDelayMs":0}
  → "slow agent database reservation"

liveness warning: reasons=event_loop_delay,event_loop_utilization
  interval=86s eventLoopDelayP99Ms=85698
```

Same startup: `plugin.feishu loadMs=72145.1 registerMs=1767.8`... i.e. the
plugin's `loadMs` is dominated by this read, not by its own ESM compile.

**Counter-check that it is the store size, not the plugin**: after we reduced
the store to 407 MB and later 321 MB by archiving old transcripts, the same
window dropped from 85 s to 68 s to 70 s — but the remaining time turned out to
be a different, fixed-timeout caller (`session-row-projection` drain), see the
sibling report. When we additionally set `OPENCLAW_FEISHU_DOCTOR=0`-style
skipping, the doctor path no longer appears in startup logs at all.

## Why it matters

- `skipCache: true` makes the cost proportional to store size, on **every**
  startup, even though the findings set is usually empty (the code short-circuits
  only *after* the read).
- It runs on the main thread inside the plugin load window, so it serializes
  against every other plugin's ESM compilation and inflates their `loadMs`.

## Suggested directions

1. **Don't skip the cache here.** The doctor is checking for corrupt state JSON
   and stale session entries; a cached store is sufficient for that check, and
   the caller can request `skipCache` only in the repair path.
2. **Run the doctor sequence after ready**, or at least off the startup
   plugin-load window — like other maintenance work.
3. **Short-circuit before the read** when nothing can be wrong: if
   `collectCorruptFeishuStateJsonFindings(stateDir)` is empty and no session
   targets changed, there is nothing for the store scan to find.

## Note

Deferring the doctor sequence is currently the only way we found to keep this
off the startup path; there is no documented config switch for it. A supported
switch (e.g. `channels.feishu.doctor.onStartup: false`) would help.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In Code Mode, when `exec` collects a warning and the command finishes inside the yield window, the value the Code Mode program receives has no warning. The native `exec` tool result shows it in its text. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187244 fixed this for running results by adding structured `warningText`; completed results (local and node host) and node-host failures still carry the warning in text only, and Code Mode returns structured details for successful calls.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a Gateway with `tools.codeMode: true`, `tools.exec: { security: "full", ask: "off" }` and a Code Mode capable model.
2. Store a secret-store `env` entry that exec refuses to apply to child processes: `openclaw secrets store set NODE_OPTIONS --kind env --value=--no-warnings`.
3. Ask the agent to run the Code Mode program `return await exec({ command: "echo ok" });` and reply with the returned value.
4. Read the `exec` tool result in the session transcript.

### Expected behavior

The returned value carries the warning, as a running result does since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187244: `warningText: "Warning: secret store environment entries were not applied for host=gateway: NODE_OPTIONS."`.

### Actual behavior

The value is `{"status":"completed","exitCode":0,"exitSignal":null,"exitReason":"exit","durationMs":244,"aggregated":"ok","noOutputTimedOut":false,"cwd":"..."}` with no warning. With Code Mode off, the same `exec` call's text starts with `Warning: secret store environment entries were not applied for host=gateway: NODE_OPTIONS.`, so exec did collect it. `buildExecForegroundResult` (`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-support.ts`) renders the warning into the text only, and the node-host result in `dispatchNodeSystemRun` (`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node-phases.ts`) does the same.

### OpenClaw version

Source build at 65acdfd629e

### Operating system

Ubuntu 22.04

### Install method

Source build

### Model

google/gemini-3.6-flash

### Provider / routing chain

`openclaw agent` CLI -> local Gateway -> Google Gemini API

### Additional provider/model setup details

Isolated Gateway on loopback with its own state directory, a synthetic token and channels skipped; the secret-store entry is a synthetic value.

### Logs

```shell
exec toolResult (Code Mode) details.value: {"status":"completed","exitCode":0,"exitSignal":null,"exitReason":"exit","durationMs":244,"aggregated":"ok","noOutputTimedOut":false,"cwd":"<workspace>"}
exec toolResult (Code Mode off) text: "Warning: secret store environment entries were not applied for host=gateway: NODE_OPTIONS.\n\n\n\nok"
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The before and after captures are in the pull request.

### Impact and severity

- Affected: agents using Code Mode that run commands through `exec` which finish before exec yields.
- Severity: the command result is correct, but the guidance in the warning is lost: why a secret-store variable is missing, why a sandbox command ran without a PTY, or that `host=node` ignored `yieldMs`/`background` and ran synchronously.
- Frequency: every quickly finishing Code Mode `exec` call that collected a warning.
- Consequence: the agent cannot explain or work around the condition the warning describes; direct (non-Code Mode) calls see it.

### Additional information

Failed local results already include the warnings in their structured `message` (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186515). Node-host failures are not tool errors and have no `message`, so their warnings are lost too.

|---|---:|---:|

| includeDetails:true | 872000 | 272000 |

The current session status also reports a 272k context budget. This is UI/catalog evidence, not a native Codex token-pressure stress test.

Installed `src/gateway/server-methods/models-list-public-projection.ts` build:

```js
const contextTokens = options.includeDetails
  ? asPositiveSafeInteger(entry.contextTokens)
  : void 0;
```

The installed Control UI formatter renders active/max only when both fields exist and differ. The selected row separately receives `contextTokens` from the matching session if model/runtime match. Evaluating the actual installed formatter with the two inputs reproduces:

A consistent distinction between maximum capacity and active/default budget in Home and session pickers, including unselected model rows. If no active session exists, label catalog/default budget honestly rather than silently showing maximum capacity as the only context number.

A second 2026.9.6 Gateway also returns 272000 detailed contextTokens; its maximum varies by catalog route/model. The same projection code applies. Exact introduction date and native Codex effective compaction thresholds were not established.

### Summary

On one Windows installation running OpenClaw 2026.9.5, `plugins inspect discord --runtime --json` takes tens of seconds before producing successful output; tracing places the delay inside runtime inspection, not process shutdown.

### Steps to reproduce

2. Measure time to JSON output and process exit.

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

Both observed runs exited 0. The detailed run produced valid JSON with Discord status `loaded` and empty stderr. It spent approximately 44.818 seconds inside `withPluginDiagnosticsReportForInspection` (registry acquisition, formatting, and release), then exited naturally about 15 ms after JSON output.

A retained shared-state SQLite worker was idle and unreferenced at exit, as were its three MessagePorts and the 30-minute coordinator timer. These resources did not block shutdown. No worker cleanup attempt or failed termination was observed.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.5; Node.js v24.19.0

Windows (exact OS build not collected)

Global npm installation

### Model

Worker, three MessagePorts, and 1,800,000 ms timer: hasRef=false. No calls recorded to store.close, broker.close, closeActor, retire, or worker.terminate.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Timing was collected with a process-local Node loading hook wrapping the inspection scope, broker/store lifecycle methods, worker ref/unref/terminate, and CLI finalizers. Async resources were observed through weak references. Instrumentation and machine load may affect timing; these measurements are not an uninstrumented benchmark.

Observed on one Windows installation during Discord runtime inspection. Practical impact: tens of seconds waiting for diagnostic output. Both instrumented runs were slow, but general frequency is unknown. No data loss, failed Discord inspection, or shutdown hang was demonstrated.

`io.snapshot-B7ifVteM.mjs:409,1059,2220` -> `openclaw-state-worker-store-Dt8l0iTE.mjs:136,70` -> `openSharedStateSqliteWorkerStore`.
