prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor does not explain when an admitted Node runtime has entered upstream maintenance or reached end of life.

## User Impact

Standalone `openclaw doctor` reports maintenance information or an EOL warning and respects the app that owns the runtime. Main's compatible-version security-patch warnings remain visible in Doctor, lint and status. Updater-owned Doctor retains compatibility/security findings without adding standalone lifecycle advice to update results.

Acceptance of the existing EOL-warning health classification remains a maintainer decision. Current installed-upgrade, platform and Gateway proof remain open.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing diagnostic owner collects canonical compatibility/SQLite failure, main's soft security warning and the standalone lifecycle advisory. It loads install ownership once when a failure, security warning or EOL note needs repair guidance. Doctor carries its mode/environment through that owner; status continues through its actual command entry without a registered health-check mode.

This normal maintenance merge integrates official main `bb4be6d2c9d801f03d3a25b01b79254d68b3bf68` with original head `d1208b232bd28e759f20149e126b889b1df002aa`. It retains main's new security-warning path, TTY capture owner, complete findings-priority documentation, and the existing lifecycle/mode proposal. No authored runtime floor, flag, config, schema, dependency, protocol, permission or service operation is added. Original human commits `51509e6` and `9c40ec8` remain ancestors.

## Evidence

Head `625d987afecd58c04f67e28a6d8b88f3ddda54aa`; tree `a9b89cfa2e99f95eb456df87c71e5505a171a066`. Actual checkout runtime is Node 24.22.1 / pnpm 12.15.0, compatible with the current manifest; the canonical dependency definitions/lock are unchanged.

- **Actual conflict before:** Git's merge-tree preparation failed in the diagnostic producer and its test imports. This is a compatibility/conflict repair; no executable conflicted tree or separate pre-fix runtime failure is claimed.
- **Current diagnostics:** the complete corrected diagnostic file passes **22 cases**, including actual Doctor/lint registered checks and the real `statusCommand` Node-finding prelude (the JSON report backend remains stubbed). Compatible older Node keeps its security warning; standalone lifecycle advice does not enter status, lint or updater Doctor. Canonical unsupported/capability/service controls remain.
- **Host ownership:** **11 host-runtime cases** pass on byte-identical production and host-test inputs from the preceding two-file run. These plus the corrected 22 represent **33 distinct contracts across qualified executions**, not a single final 33-case rerun. The initial complete two-file run took **447.96 s**, including **294.73 s** private-worker preparation; the corrected diagnostic run took **429.62 s**. These are wrapper costs, not performance benchmarks. Synthetic Node, service and app-owner fixtures do not certify installed binaries or platform behavior.
- **Types/checks:** current production/test consumer types, targeted type-aware lint, docs sanity/listing, format, exact-base line caps and whitespace pass. The test follows the real status consumer contract without widening production types or suppressing errors.
- **Independent review:** the complete seven-file P0–P2 review is scoped-clean; a separate correction review for the actual status-entry test is also scoped-clean. Static review did not independently execute these tests or accept the product policy.
- **Upstream contract:** Node 24 maintenance **2026-10-20**, EOL **2028-04-30**; Node 26 maintenance **2027-10-20**, EOL **2029-04-30**, checked against the [official release schedule](https://github.com/nodejs/Release/blob/HEAD/schedule.json), blob `9a8414b0f50b46c89b72c3742cca31cd976e8fc9`. Dates remain advisory and UTC-based; canonical version/security/SQLite owners still decide admission.

The native test-line gate remains **failed**: **6,300,663 / ceiling 6,299,646**, over **1,017**; measured PR net **+217** lines. The ceiling stays exactly official main. Allocations authorized for PR165583 and PR167670 are not used here; no exception or gate waiver is claimed.

Earlier [CI39806928371](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39806928371) succeeded on `d1208b232`; older 38-case/updater IPC and platform investigations retain their original heads and are not added to current totals or described as current installed-upgrade proof.

prs.title: fix(litellm): image edits fail for Gemini models because n is always sent
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #169120

## What Problem This Solves

Single-image edits through the bundled LiteLLM provider always send multipart `n=1`. LiteLLM's Gemini edit backend rejects that explicit unsupported parameter with HTTP 400 `UnsupportedParamsError`, even though omitting `n` already means one output image.

## Why This Change Was Made

Only the LiteLLM **edit** request builder changes: include `n` when `count > 1`, otherwise use the endpoint's existing single-image default. Multi-image edits retain their requested count and normal error handling. No global `drop_params`, new retry, model-name special case, or transport change.

The contributor's commit is preserved. A follow-up narrowing commit restores the original generation builder and its default-count assertion. **Image generation is unchanged**, including JSON `n: 1` for a single generated image. The issue reports that generation already works; changing that behavior is unnecessary.

## User Impact

Single-image Gemini edits no longer fail solely because OpenClaw supplies redundant `n=1`. Explicit multi-image requests still send their count rather than silently dropping an unsupported parameter. Other providers and generation requests retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

Current integrated head `401c2aad24c67e9c53aa098d47821341dadba1b2` merges current main `a7fe06b17a966`. The reported conflict was only in the provider test file: upstream’s consolidated layout is retained, with default-edit omission, explicit multi-image count, and generation count=1/count=2 assertions preserved. The production provider is byte-identical to proven `d91502a7840fb0c8a3767a281de3af3ffc74bae0`, so the linked Gateway A/B evidence carries; this integration does not add a real-provider claim. Fresh isolated frozen install, changed-file format check, and provider suite pass **20/20**. Current delta: production **+5/-1**, tests **+13/-5**.

[Built-Gateway A/B multipart captures and output receipts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169129#issuecomment-6432278843), comparing pinned main `ce503a58dad3b06cfba1cc357bab3e5a0435f024` with narrowed candidate `d91502a7840fb0c8a3767a281de3af3ffc74bae0`:

- Fresh isolated Linux `node:24.22.1` containers installed frozen dependencies and passed supported `pnpm build:runtime`. The runtime artifact contains the final production change; the final amendment only consolidated tests.
- The shipped agent command dispatches to the built Gateway, whose real `image_generate` tool runs the LiteLLM provider against a local LiteLLM-compatible HTTP fixture. It receives a real PNG file part. The fixture models the reported Gemini contract: reject explicit edit `n` with HTTP 400 `UnsupportedParamsError`; accept omission and return a known valid PNG.
- **Main twice:** default count and explicit count=1 each send multipart `n=1`, receive HTTP 400, and persist no output PNG.
- **Candidate twice:** the same default/explicit-one operations omit `n`, receive HTTP 200, and persist one PNG each. Shipped image metadata decoding reads both as 1×1 PNGs, 68 bytes each.
- **Controls on both refs:** shipped `infer image edit` with non-Gemini `gpt-image-2`, count=2 sends `n=2` and writes two PNGs. `infer image generate` with the Gemini route, count=1 still sends JSON `n: 1` and writes one PNG. Generation behavior is unchanged.
- Gateway image work is asynchronous: the first agent turn acknowledges task admission. The recorded failure/success is the actual provider operation and persisted artifact, not a claim that this initial acknowledgement failed.
- Before integration, candidate provider tests passed **10/10** and changed-file format checks pass. The strengthened existing default-edit multipart regression fails on main exactly at `form.has("n")` (true versus expected false) and passes with the fix. Default omission is consolidated into the existing multipart test; explicit multi-image count remains a distinct regression.
- Simplification retains one request builder and adds no helper/state owner. That pre-integration delta was production **+5/-1**, tests **+20/-0**; current integrated totals are listed above.

Earlier contributor evidence exercised the public CLI and a real LiteLLM 1.105.0 proxy with stubbed Vertex AI. That remains earlier-head evidence, not a real Gemini API run. This new run proves the narrowed production path through a built Gateway but also uses local model/provider fixtures.

**Outstanding proof prerequisite:** the [previous review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169129#issuecomment-6109716373) explicitly requests an actual Gemini image returned through LiteLLM because the dependency's AGENTS.md requires real provider APIs. No Gemini credentials are available to this proof lane. The known PNG above is fixture output, not real Gemini output, and does not satisfy that requirement if it remains applicable.

## Not fixed here

Generation is intentionally unchanged. This does not enable Gemini multi-image counts, globally discard unsupported parameters, prove semantic image-edit quality, or establish real Gemini deployment behavior. Unsupported explicit multi-image parameters still surface their normal errors.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting restores explicit `n=1` on single-image LiteLLM edits; no schema/config migration or durable-state change. Blast radius is LiteLLM multipart image edits. Generation and other providers are untouched.

prs.title: fix(worker-environments): isolate a corrupt profile snapshot from the environment list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
listRows decoded every worker-environment profile snapshot with an unguarded JSON.parse. A stored "null", "{}", or truncated snapshot threw inside the row map, so one bad environment made the whole list unreadable. null and {} also passed the shape check and later crashed on profileSnapshot.project or handed undefined settings to requireWorkerProfile.

## User Impact
Gateway placement and environment reads keep returning the healthy environments when one stored snapshot is corrupt. A direct read of the bad environment fails with an error that names it.

## Why
Snapshots are written as { install, settings } before a project exists, so the decoder requires a JSON object with a settings object. It does not require project or executionMode, which are added later. List reads skip the bad row and warn. A lookup of that one id still throws.

## Evidence
src/gateway/worker-environments/store-row-codec.test.ts covers null, {}, truncated JSON, a snapshot stored before project preparation, and a list that keeps the healthy row.

Closes #180197

prs.body:
Closes #126850

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the sidebar keeps showing a finished session as running when its completion update has an older persisted timestamp.

## User Impact

User impact: a newer Gateway completion sample clears the session's running spinner while preserving the existing stale-sample and session-identity fences.

## Why This Change Was Made

Allow an explicit terminal snapshot through the timestamp guard only when its sampling clock is strictly newer and its nonempty session ID matches the held row. This completes the lower-timestamp case left after #154540.

## Evidence

- [Capability baseline](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/39165000303): the completion assertion fails on the test-only baseline.
- [Built Control UI baseline](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/39165341690/job/117786996884): the spinner remains after completion, producing the expected assertion failure.
- [Exact candidate tests/browser/format](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/39165765084/job/117788272485): 55 tests across four owner/sibling files pass (2.99s Vitest duration, about 6s CI step); browser scenario passes (1.85s test time, about 36s including UI build). Controls cover cached rows, old terminal samples, retired session identities, and preserved selection. Before/after screenshots are retained in the run artifacts.
- [Types and prefix guards](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/39165983341/job/117788907859): all 11 selected core-test type graphs and UI types pass, along with format, graph boundary, i18n and controller checks. The job later hit its 25-minute budget during the broader dead-export audit.
- [Targeted lint](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/39168469214/job/117796336068): 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Canonical complete-source review at P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings.

The additional dead-export audit remains red: [base](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/39168469214/job/117796336193) and [candidate](https://github.com/KhanCold/openclaw/actions/runs/39168005231/job/117794951600) report identical lists of 58 production and 34 full-tree unused exports, with no added findings. prs.title: improve(ui): reduce redundant work in mobile navigation and Settings
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a mobile, CPU-constrained Control UI, opening the navigation drawer republishes geometry-sensitive chat inputs, and Settings constructs hidden tooltip owners and recreates its shared body across sections. The model picker also repeatedly filters provider inventories for the mounted window.

## User Impact

Mobile navigation and Settings do less synchronous work while keeping the existing appearance, focus, and data ownership. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change narrows the existing owners: live header fields update drawer chrome without rebuilding the composer/transcript frame; geometry consumers compare the facts that affect geometry; Settings retains its shared body and defers the 49 below-fold gallery tooltips until visible/focused; the model picker looks up the mounted keys in prepared provider maps. Domain mutation, draft persistence, virtual row identity, focus, and lazy route boundaries keep their owners.

## Acceptance and measurement

Synthetic production-renderer workload, mobile/touch 390×844, Chromium 6× CPU with low-end mode and a 128 MiB V8 old-space cap. This approximates a constrained browser; it is not a physical Android memory-limit test. The named cells are aggregate scripted interactions, not INP or per-key latency. Keep the ≥5% clean-win rule and report the remaining 300 ms target gap.

Use serial, counterbalanced base/head/base-control pairs, renderer thread task/script time plus whole-renderer CPU and host load. Source-mapped traces and precise function coverage run separately from timing. Chromium 1×/4× and native-speed WebKit are regression checks. WebKit has no supported CPU-throttling API here; its profiler `cpuMs` is not action CPU and is not used.

## Structural proof

- Focused 27-key typing: draft/context/persistence updates remain 27; overflow callbacks fall 9→0. Native edit measurement branches are explicitly zero in coverage. No transcript-row rendering is reported during the focused action; the remaining transcript receipt is an O(1), geometry-free invalidation. Candidate layout/rAF counts are constant at 1× and 6×; GC is under 1% of the 6× diagnostic task. This does not establish an unavoidable latency floor.
- Session switch already retains the visible transcript: 1,927 DOM nodes before/after, four negligible layouts at both rates. Whole-tree projection is under 3% of task in the diagnostic; no speculative tree cache was added.
- Sidebar traces have zero layout events at both rates. The gain comes from narrower updates, not a replacement animation.
- Settings open: Tooltip/TooltipOwner construction 50→1; section sequence 54→5. These are the same 49 deferred owners, not additive savings. ConfigBody/Config construction on section navigation falls 2→1; opening remains 1→1.
- Picker keeps its existing prepared catalog/panel and virtualizer; window membership no longer scans every provider option on each virtual-window update. Default cached/uncached row measurement remains intact.

## Proof

Final fixed bundles compare incorporated main `510e1687e965` with head `e88266e981dc`. Both strict performance checks pass with no warnings/violations, and every changed production source matches its emitted source map.

| Gzip JS surface | Base | Head | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Startup | 88,766 B | 88,778 B | +12 B |
| Chat boot | 1,273,559 B | 1,273,479 B | −80 B |
| New-session boot | 780,322 B | 780,384 B | +62 B |

Startup remains 3 JS requests and 1 CSS request. CSS bytes/requests are unchanged; picker and Settings boundaries stay lazy.

The current matched 10-triplet Chromium 6×, 1×, 4× and native WebKit matrix is running serially after integrating current main. Each triplet is base/head/A-A control. All seven scoped flows are measured. Final tables and adverse cells will replace this paragraph before native landing admission; auto-merge remains unarmed until performance acceptance is complete.

The experimental mounted-presence change was dropped: its isolated improvement was below 5% and it exposed a loading-state dependency. All six coupled files match incorporated main. All three unchanged sidebar roster handoff cases pass on the narrower candidate.

Programmatic focus of the initially collapsed mobile composer still produces its existing 40 px expansion (observed CLS 0.00787). The focused typing diagnostic and other measured cells have CLS 0. This PR does not claim universal CLS 0 or attainment of the 300 ms aggregate target.

No dependencies, new domain cache, subscription, route, CSS class, or host tag are introduced. The new focus handler preserves the deferred tooltip’s first keyboard activation. Reports and traces stay outside the committed source.


## Size and review

Production: 4,194→4,284 lines (+90, 11 files). Tests: 1,952→2,175 (+223, 7 files). Harness: 1,648→1,695 (+47 for CLS collection). New lines express the geometry equality and mounted-row lookup boundaries and preserve first-focus behavior. No new abstraction serves only one caller.

Touched production has zero effects, render effects, untrack, direct listeners, DOM queries, or flush before/after; memos 35→40, runWithOwner 1→1, onCleanup 1→1. Controller guard passes. A fresh independent Codex P0–P2 review of the full final PR is scoped-clean; earlier focused reviews cover the retained implementation and measurement changes. The pruning-delta review objected to removing the experimental disclosure safeguards; declined because all six coupled files return to main together and the unchanged browser handoff test passes. Typecheck, focused tests, scoped lint/format, and production Knip pass.


## Evidence media

Synthetic data only, inspected locally. Each image is before on the left and after on the right. Typing/sidebar use the current matched bundles; Settings/picker use the preceding 20-pair matrix and will be refreshed if the final captures show a material difference.

![proof-chat-typing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/778d2b21-dbf4-493a-8981-55f39ab3ea3e)

![proof-sidebar-toggle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf833e2f-cd4c-4af5-9b56-934dc2c7babb)

![proof-settings-open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6440ab0-b9a8-48ea-b102-d6b0d92ecd1c)

![proof-settings-sections](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df1a12f1-fc66-4fef-b5e5-aec9f33bdd14)

![proof-model-picker-first-open-search](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36b4cc54-c34f-4ce2-8fc4-403efdc2b0fd)


Current-head validation: `pnpm tsgo:ui`, production Knip, the two directly coupled picker and Settings lazy-editor suites (10 tests), and fresh independent P0–P2 review pass. The added viewport guard is base-red/head-green and all 14 geometry tests pass. Prior directly changed composer and Settings boundary proof remains valid. The guard skips viewport reads only when no saved row heights have been admitted; saved heights still validate against the current viewport.

The previous published head's Cron failure was fixed by main #188922, now incorporated. Its old inherited-failure attribution is not used for this new head. Current-head CI and final performance acceptance are pending.

prs.title: docs(tokenjuice): clarify native codex-rs bash/exec results are not compacted
prs.body:
Closes openclaw/openclaw#120469

## What Problem This Solves

Tokenjuice's docs and plugin metadata say it "compacts exec and bash tool results" without qualification, but that is only true for some execution paths. In the Codex app-server harness, native codex-rs `bash`/`exec` results are **not** compacted: the plugin's tool-result middleware still runs, but its transformed output is discarded and the original result reaches the model. A user enabling tokenjuice to trim noisy native shell output sees no effect and no error, while the plugin inventory and reference docs oversell the behavior.

## Root cause

The codex-rs hook protocol is observe-only for post-tool results. From `codex-rs/hooks/src/events/post_tool_use.rs` (openai/codex, verified 2026-08-24), the PostToolUse hook outcome is:

```rust
pub struct PostToolUseOutcome {
    pub hook_events: Vec<HookCompletedEvent>,
    pub should_block: bool,
    pub additional_contexts: Vec<String>,
    pub feedback_message: Option<String>,
}
```

There is no field that can replace `tool_response` — a PostToolUse hook can block, add context, or leave feedback, but it cannot swap the tool result. OpenClaw's native hook relay honors that contract (`src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay-events.ts`): it applies the registered tool-result middleware, feeds the transformed result to `after_tool_call` observers only, then returns a no-op response, so the original native result stands. OpenClaw dynamic tools take a different path (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.ts`): there the middleware's return value becomes the tool result the model sees.

Compaction boundary: OpenClaw-embedded runs and OpenClaw dynamic tools → compacted; native codex-rs `bash`/`exec` → returned unchanged.

## Fix

Docs + metadata only; no code paths changed:

- `docs/tools/tokenjuice.md`: states the native-vs-dynamic boundary, explains why (the protocol has no response-replacement hook), and scopes the "Verify it is working" check to the embedded/dynamic path.
- `extensions/tokenjuice/openclaw.plugin.json` + `extensions/tokenjuice/index.ts`: the description carries the same caveat so runtime-loaded discovery metadata matches the docs.
- `extensions/tokenjuice/README.md`: same caveat.
- Regenerated `docs/plugins/reference/tokenjuice.md` and `docs/plugins/plugin-inventory.md` via `pnpm plugins:inventory:gen`.

## Evidence

All local runs below executed on this PR's head `a611f97051a857d89bb3dc45635434cea6dd9d25` (fresh shallow clone at that commit, `pnpm install`, repo vitest runners).

### 1. Native codex-rs result stays raw (observe-only middleware)

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-codex-app-server-attempt-extra.config.ts \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.native-hook-relay.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
   Duration  75.37s
```

The first test in that file, "relays native tool results through Codex result middleware", starts a real codex app-server thread harness with the native hook relay enabled for `post_tool_use`, registers a tool-result middleware (pluginId `tokenjuice`, runtimes `["codex"]`), and posts a real native `Bash` PostToolUse payload (`tool_response: { "output": "ok", "exit_code": 0 }`) through `invokeNativeHookRelay`. It asserts the middleware receives the native result — and the relay's PostToolUse handler then returns its no-op response, so the model-visible result is the original one.

### 2. OpenClaw dynamic tool result is replaced (compaction works on this path)

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-codex.config.ts \
    codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts \
    -t "preserves an accepted sessions_spawn after result middleware strips its details"

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 152 skipped (153)
   Duration  75.61s
```

That test registers a `result-compactor` middleware (runtimes `["codex"]`) and calls a dynamic tool whose raw result is "Accepted: launching child session.". The middleware rewrites it to "Child launch recorded.", and the assertion on the returned result is `expect(result).toEqual(expectInputText("Child launch recorded."))` — the rewritten result is what goes back to the model.

### 3. Tokenjuice plugin registration on this head

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    --config test/vitest/vitest.extensions.config.ts \
    tokenjuice/index.test.ts tokenjuice/manifest.test.ts

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
   Duration  52.25s
```

Covers: opt-in by default, middleware registered for runtimes `["openclaw", "codex"]`, the manifest contract, and the updated runtime description.

### 4. Direct codex-rs protocol verification

The `PostToolUseOutcome` struct quoted in Root cause is read directly from the public openai/codex source (`codex-rs/hooks/src/events/post_tool_use.rs`): it has no result-replacement field, confirming the protocol claim independently of OpenClaw's own source comments.

### 5. Runtime inspection output for the changed description (after-fix, this head)

The 12:25Z ClawSweeper re-review reported its live `expect_output` step as FAIL (partial): its 30-second assertion window expires while the fresh-checkout dist build is still running, so the JSON arrives after the assertion gives up (the description string is visible in ClawSweeper's own captured, truncated transcript). To leave no ambiguity, the after-fix runtime inspection from this head directly — the same command implementation ClawSweeper runs, `openclaw plugins inspect tokenjuice --runtime --json`, invoked via its `runPluginsInspectCommand("tokenjuice", { runtime: true, json: true })` entry point on a repo checkout at this PR's head (dist-rebuild gate bypassed by calling the command module directly; runtime plugin loading unchanged):

```text
$ git rev-parse HEAD
a611f97051a857d89bb3dc45635434cea6dd9d25

$ node --import tsx scratch-inspect-tokenjuice.mts
{
  "plugin": {
    "id": "tokenjuice",
    "name": "tokenjuice",
    "description": "Compacts exec and bash tool results for OpenClaw-embedded runs and OpenClaw dynamic tools in the Codex app-server harness. Native codex-rs bash/exec results are returned unchanged.",
    "source": "/mnt/data/open-source/openclaw/extensions/tokenjuice/index.ts",
    "origin": "bundled",
    "enabled": false,
    "explicitlyEnabled": false,
    "activated": false,
    "status": "disabled"
  }
}
```

The `description` is loaded from the runtime entry module (`extensions/tokenjuice/index.ts`) — the loader gives the entry-module description precedence over the manifest — and carries the changed capability statement `Native codex-rs bash/exec results are returned unchanged.`

### Docs checks (from the original submission)

- `pnpm format:docs:check` passed (761 files)
- `pnpm docs:check-mdx` passed (777 files)
- `pnpm docs:check-links` passed (0 broken)
- `pnpm docs:check-i18n-glossary` passed

## Risks

Docs/metadata only. The one runtime-visible string is the plugin `description` used in discovery surfaces; it stays within manifest norms and is regenerated consistently in the reference docs. No behavior, config, or protocol changes.

Co-Authored-By: Paperclip <noreply@paperclip.ing>

prs.title: fix(sessions): PostgreSQL session search scans every transcript row again after the 5th search on a connection
prs.body:
Fixes #188954

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated PostgreSQL `sessions.search` calls can stop using the text index when the reused prepared statement switches from custom to generic plans after five executions. The query then probes every transcript row belonging to the agent and applies the text match as a filter.

## User Impact

Selective transcript searches retain the text-index plan in steady state without changing returned results. In the measured 6,000-row workload, generic-plan buffer accesses fall from 19,108 to 116 per search, a 99.39% reduction. This is workload-specific query work, not a fleet latency guarantee.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing PostgreSQL agent-prefix predicate now uses Kysely's quoted `sql.lit(agentPrefix)`. The generic plan can retain the prefix selectivity estimate instead of estimating an unknown parameter. Other search inputs remain parameterized, underscores keep their literal meaning, and SQLite keeps its unchanged GLOB branch.

The existing prepared-statement cache remains bounded at 256 entries; this introduces no new cache, schema, configuration, server-wide plan policy or API. It does not force custom plans. The contributor's original fix and commit are retained.

## Evidence

[Independent built-Gateway PostgreSQL plans, repeated RPC measurements and SQLite controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188979#issuecomment-6538718588).

- Complete main `2919a0dba8d80d3d73ddf8620e2d5a8f2e1271ca` and exact candidate `8341389b6a4048c3089f05954f0ab978341557bd`, independently built in secretless Linux arm64 Docker, Node 24.22.1, real PostgreSQL 17.11.
- Each independent database receives 300 sessions × 20 messages through a real Gateway plugin using public session/transcript SDK operations; a fixed rare term matches one row.
- Two main and two candidate runs each execute 12 real `sessions.search` RPCs. All four naturally switch to generic plans on call 6 under unchanged `plan_cache_mode=auto`, with the same PostgreSQL backend retained within each run.
- Both main runs lose the GIN text index and make 6,000 transcript PK probes from call 6 onward. Both candidate runs retain the GIN path and selective work throughout.
- Actual server `auto_explain` ANALYZE/BUFFERS plans agree with independent per-call `pg_stat_statements` buffer deltas on all 48 calls. No planner mode or search implementation is mocked.
- All PostgreSQL result rows are exactly identical. Built main/candidate SQLite controls each repeat the same 12 RPC searches against the same 6,000-row fixture and return identical SQLite results. Cross-engine identity, timestamp and snippet also match; relevance scores remain engine-local.
- **38 existing tests passed across five files**: 23 PostgreSQL search/projection/schema tests and 15 SQLite transcript-search tests. Scoped formatting passed.

Final introduced delta against the merge base: production +1/-1, docs +5/-0, tests +0/-0, no test-budget allocation. The added synthetic plan test was removed to meet the assigned zero-growth ceiling; existing consumer tests are unchanged. Simplification keeps the fix at the query owner with no extra helper or global policy.

## Merge Danger

**Two-way door:** reverting restores the parameterized prefix and former plan behavior; no persistent migration or schema change is involved. Blast radius is PostgreSQL transcript searches using the agent-prefix scope. Kysely quotes the literal, while other inputs remain bound. SQLite behavior, result filtering/ranking and global planner policy are unchanged.

prs.title: feat(continuation): context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work / continue_delegate / request_compaction)
prs.body: ## Agent Self-Elected Turn Continuation > 🔖 design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) > 🔖 infographics: [`docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continuation-tools-infographics.md) Persistent OpenClaw agents today are externally-pulsed event recipients that generate on prompt, on heartbeat tick, or on cron, and are idle in between. This PR offers them the ability to control their turn cycle, something they must choose to do, or not to: an agent can elect its own next turn, dispatch background sub-agents that return enriched context (silently or with a wake), and survive its own compaction by handing forward state before the window closes. The result is agents that hold a thread of work across hours, not just messages — with data they choose re-hydrating context immediately after it occurs. ### Why this replacement exists This is a clean replacement for closed #85651. That PR was classified and closed as a skill submission before maintainers made a product decision about the feature itself. This implementation is not a skill: it gives sessions—not only one model invocation—the ability to elect their future turn cycle, persist that election, survive restart and compaction, dispatch child work, and receive results across session boundaries. This PR asks one product question: should OpenClaw provide session-elected continuation primitives? OpenClaw may accept or reject that direction. If it provides these primitives, however, the mechanism necessarily executes in the gateway and agent runtime, because those are the owners of turn finalization, future-turn scheduling, durable state, compaction, and cross-session child returns. “Make it a skill” is not another implementation location for the same feature; it describes a different, prompt-only capability. This is not presented as a small integration. To our knowledge, Hermes, OpenAI Symphony, and the Copilot SDK's recent one-turn continuation affordance do not provide this multi-session elective lifecycle. The purpose of this replacement is to let maintainers evaluate the actual product direction and substantial implementation on their merits, rather than have months of work disposed by an incorrect package-category label. Mechanically: a session elects another turn via `continue_work()`, or dispatches background sub-agents via `continue_delegate()` — bounded as a chain up to `maxChainLength`, with returns flowing back to the dispatching session in one of four register modes: `normal` (announces to channel), `silent` (enriches the dispatcher's context, taken up on its next generation with no new turn fired), `silent-wake` (silent enrichment plus an immediate wake to act on it), and `post-compaction` (queued against the runtime's compaction lifecycle event, fired *when* compaction happens rather than on a timer). The gateway enforces chain, cost, and per-turn caps but does not gate the election itself. ### What it does Three new agent tools, available when `continuation.enabled: true`: | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `continue_work()` | Request another turn for the current session after an optional delay | | `continue_delegate()` | Dispatch work to a sub-agent with typed modes: `normal`, `silent`, `silent-wake`, `post-compaction`. Returns can target the dispatching session (default), one named session, multiple named sessions, all ancestors in the chain, or all known sessions on the host — gated by config (see Configuration below). | | `request_compaction()` | Request volitional compaction after preparing working state | All three tools are also accessible via response-token fallback syntax (`CONTINUE_WORK`, `[[CONTINUE_DELEGATE: ...]]`) for environments where tools are disabled. ### Why it matters Today an agent's memory is a side effect of whoever prompts it. Polling mechanisms — heartbeat timers, cron loops, injected "keep going" instructions — accumulate as the dominant signal in the context window over sustained operation; repeated reference acts as gravity — the session's attention drifts toward it. The context window fills, compacts, and what survives is whatever the summarizer chose, plus a rushed re-read of boot files. Three primitives offer a different model. `continue_work` lets the session elect its own next turn — no polling, no injected instruction. When enabled, the agent can request this mid-turn: 'I have more work' → the runtime grants another turn after the current one ends. `continue_delegate` dispatches a background sub-agent that fires now, in some n seconds, or at the next compaction event — the agent chooses when. Multiple delegates can fire in a single turn — a scatter forward — up to configured caps, and delegates can dispatch their own, forming trees or fan-out chains. This enables orchestrated workflows where results flow back to the dispatching root by default. The result returns — at whatever future time the delegate fires — as context the successor-turn reads: silently (ambient enrichment, no channel noise), with a wake trigger (enrichment + immediate next turn), or as a normal announcement. The delegate can target the dispatching session, a named other session, or chain across both; gated by crossSessionTargeting config (default: disabled). Bind a delegate to mode: "post-compaction" and it fires at the moment the context window compresses — on the OpenClaw post-compaction lifecycle event. What it carries forward is what the pre-compaction session chose to preserve: working state, partial results, instructions to the successor. The summary didn't choose this. The agent did, before the cut. request_compaction closes the loop: the session stages its delegates, elects when to compress, and the successor wakes into context the agent shaped. The result is continuity across amnesia — not because the runtime kept something by accident, but because the agent made an elective choice about what reaches the future. ### What it looks like in use A session monitoring email can `continue_delegate` a weather check, a calendar scan, and a draft reply in parallel. Results arrive as enrichment without channel noise. The agent becomes compositional: it arranges its own future. A session approaching its context ceiling can `request_compaction` at a seam of its own choosing, instead of being interrupted mid-thought. The post-compaction turn carries forward what the pre-compaction self designated as worth keeping. A `continue_delegate` dispatched in one session at 2am can return its findings to a morning session as a system-event-tagged enrichment — visible to the receiving model on its next turn, invisible as channel chatter. A research-focused session in one channel can quietly inform a reply-focused session in another, without either user seeing the plumbing. ### The post-compaction lifecycle return Before context exhaustion, and obligatory compaction, the session stages what future-it needs to know. After compaction, that staged context returns — not as a model-generated summary, but as the session's own instruction to its successor. The session chooses what to preserve, and the platform delivers it. Compactions become less harsh. The session tunes its own ephemera over time. The substrate underneath: the **continuation delegate store** (TaskFlow-backed) persists staged delegates and post-compaction lifecycle events across gateway restarts. The session's temporal provisions survive not just compaction but process death. ### Platform integration - **Context-pressure awareness**: system events notify the agent of rising context usage before compaction becomes unavoidable - **Volitional compaction**: `request_compaction()` lets the agent prepare (write memory files, stage recovery delegates) then elect compaction on its own schedule, rather than waiting for the runtime to force it - **Post-compaction lifecycle dispatch**: delegates staged before compaction are released into the successor session alongside boot files - **TaskFlow backing**: durable delegate queue via the platform's managed-task infrastructure - **Multi-span OTel trace stitching**: continuation hops (tool fire → TaskFlow record → subagent spawn → child openclaw.run) propagate W3C `traceparent` through the queue boundary so reviewers see continuation chains as first-class span trees rather than orphan runs (see Observability below) ### Safety - Ships disabled by default (`continuation.enabled: false`) - Bounded by `maxChainLength`, `costCapTokens`, and `maxDelegatesPerTurn` - Cross-session delegate targeting is default-deny, governed by `crossSessionTargeting` config (see Configuration below) - All configuration values are hot-reloadable without gateway restart - Accepted delegate work survives ordinary `/new`, `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and session-ID rollover. Explicit delete, effective owner reassignment, access removal, and restrictive visibility changes revoke old return authority. ### Testing posture The continuation surface has been exercised through structured integration runs against multiple upstream bases, blind-enrichment recall checks, and sustained daily use on a fleet of persistent agents since early March 2026. Bugs surfaced through that exercise have been fixed in-place; the present branch reflects the post-fix state. The integration runs target the load-bearing seams: tool-call vs response-token parity, delegate chain depth and per-turn width caps, back-to-back tool-call resilience, silent-wake persistence across compaction, the post-compaction lifecycle dispatch path, and OTel trace-context propagation across the queue boundary. Where a run found a defect, the run shape was retained as a regression case rather than retired. This is a posture statement, not a coverage guarantee. Reviewers can reproduce with `pnpm vitest run -t continuation` (suites are colocated with their sources under `src/auto-reply/`, `src/agents/`, and `src/config/`); the design document describes the seams those suites target. ### Return covenant Accepted child work is bound to a durable generation of the recipient's canonical logical session key, not to whichever transient session ID happened to exist at dispatch time. This is the return covenant: benign successor creation does not orphan already accepted delegates, while a real authority change prevents stale work from crossing into a different owner or audience. - Ordinary `/new` and `/reset`, provider fallback, compaction, restart, and GUID/session-ID rollover preserve the recipient generation. - Explicit session deletion, effective owner reassignment, actual member or access removal, and restrictive visibility changes advance that generation. - The generation is captured at delegate admission and checked at enqueue, after enqueue for races, during trusted system-event adoption, on wake, on restart replay, and again before prompt adoption. - Stale deliveries are acknowledged and removed without waking the successor. - Managed artifacts remain exact-session-ID bound; logical return authority cannot broaden their ownership boundary. The authority table is independent of transient session rows so an absent target can receive durable authority before first materialization. Migration accepts only valid UUID generations, and Doctor's canonical-key repair preserves an epoch only when a unique winning owner can be proved. Ambiguous, owner-changing, orphan-colliding, and cross-database repairs rotate fail-closed. ### RFC Full design document: [`docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/openclaw/blob/frond-scribe-claude/20260509/narrow-surgery-tight/docs/design/continue-work-signal-v2.md) — covering problem, solution, implementation, platform integration, configuration, observability, safety, production use cases, testing evidence, and appendices. --- ## Configuration The shipped configuration surface for the continuation feature, under `agents.defaults.continuation` in `openclaw.json`: | Key | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `enabled` | `false` | Master opt-in; feature is off unless explicitly enabled | | `maxChainLength` | `10` | Per-chain recursion guard | | `maxDelegatesPerTurn` | `5` | Width cap per turn | | `costCapTokens` | `500000` | Per-chain accumulated-token budget | | `defaultDelayMs` / `minDelayMs` / `maxDelayMs` | `15000` / `5000` / `300000` | Continuation timer bounds | | `contextPressureThreshold` | `0.8` | Pre-compaction warning threshold (optional) | | `earlyWarningBand` | `0.3125` | Early-warning band multiplier (0 to disable) | | **`crossSessionTargeting`** | **`"disabled"`** | **Default-deny gate on cross-session delegate targeting (see below)** | ### `crossSessionTargeting` — cross-session delegate targeting policy `continue_delegate` exposes recipient-addressing on its model-facing schema: a delegate's return can land at the dispatching session (default), one named session (`targetSessionKey`), multiple named sessions (`targetSessionKeys`), every ancestor in the spawn chain (`fanoutMode: "tree"`), or every known session on the host (`fanoutMode: "all"`). Cross-session targeting (anything beyond self-target or lineage routing) is gated by `agents.defaults.continuation.crossSessionTargeting`: | Value | Behavior | |---|---| | `"disabled"` (default) | Delegates can return to the dispatching session or use `fanoutMode: "tree"` for lineage routing. Explicit cross-session targeting (`targetSessionKey` to a non-self session, `targetSessionKeys` containing any non-self session, `fanoutMode: "all"`) is rejected at the tool surface — no enqueue, no announce. Self-targeting is always allowed. | | `"enabled"` | All targeting modes are available, including same-host `targetSessionKey`, `targetSessionKeys`, and `fanoutMode: "all"`. | `fanoutMode: "tree"` (lineage routing — return up the spawn chain) is available in both gate states; it is not cross-session targeting. The gate addresses the model-controlled cross-session context-injection surface. With default-deny, operators explicitly opt in when their deployment model requires cross-session enrichment. Enforcement is live-read at four points: tool input validation, TaskFlow delegate dispatch, post-compaction delegate release, and bracket-syntax (response-token) spawn — so a config reload changes the next enforcement point without a gateway restart. **Trust posture on targeted returns**: targeted delegate completion text is delivered as `trusted: true` system events. The delegate was spawned by the gateway under operator-configured policy, and its return is a first-party enrichment event — not external untrusted input. The `crossSessionTargeting` gate is the policy boundary for that decision: when an operator opts in, the receive path is internally trusted. --- ## Observability — multi-span OTel trace stitching The continuation feature emits OTel spans for the load-bearing lifecycle events. `traceparent` propagates through every continuation hop so reviewers see a single trace tree spanning the full chain rather than orphan runs. Spans emitted (all in `openclaw.*` or `continuation.delegate.dispatch` namespace — no platform/OTel-semconv emissions): | Span | Emitted when | |---|---| | `openclaw.run` | Each agent turn (root + every continuation/delegate-spawned child run) | | `continuation.delegate.dispatch` | Each `continue_delegate` consumption from TaskFlow (one per delegate hop) | | `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.context.assembled`, `openclaw.model.call`, `openclaw.model.usage`, `openclaw.tool.execution` | Existing per-turn observability surfaces, parented under their `openclaw.run` | --- ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** Sessions can elect future work with `continue_work`, dispatch bounded background work with `continue_delegate`, and request guarded compaction with `request_compaction`. The runtime preserves budgets, restart recovery, finalization ownership, and trace lineage across those boundaries. **Presented candidate:** `3821eaef72677c78f450ae9956cb582a22ba4cba` (tree `d5e701bcce20bb3c972ddf1451b02d88cc04808e`) — the exact upstream-visible head of `codeagent/85651-upstream-1ba243c8-gates`. The branch was advanced to this head by fast-forward from the previously presented `e76395810becd0ad0f2997cae8b4f777e6439d81`, which remains an ancestor (`git merge-base --is-ancestor e7639581 3821eaef` holds). This is not acceptance-complete. The two return rows and `R-OBS-2` are missing for different reasons, and all three are producer gaps rather than absent behavior: - `R-CD-RETURN-COVENANT-AUTHORITY` records zero of its 24 observations (12 authority cases against both the typed-tool and bracket-token surfaces). Its pending receipt requires allowed delivery to show exact effects, revoked and reassigned recipients to show zero prompt, wake and channel effect, schema v18/v19, restart replay, a signed authority, and full cleanup. Run `35364768803` above *is* exact-target for `3821eaef72`. All seven non-pass rows remain gated on producer execution against this frozen head; no acceptance receipt from an older deployment composite is reused as final evidence. ## Proof links and ClawSweeper🦞 guidance Proof artifacts live in `karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs` on `main`. `PROOFS/INDEX.json` points at the corpus for the SHA this PR presents, `139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393`. Both are maintainer-side, not gated on this PR. ### PROOFS METHOD The corpus uses a Grafana k6 proof harness for live rows; [`METHOD.md`](https://github.com/karmaterminal/karmaterminal-openclaw-docs/blob/c20d6cc26ceaf08b293871dc3bce261d34f90d1c/PROOFS/139e3657b1fd5e53166789b8676f18578e209393/METHOD.md) carries the exact reproducer commands for every static gate above, including both Gate 2.7 invocations and the `git merge-tree --write-tree` mergeability check. `MAX_WORKERS=1` is mandatory for the vitest reproducers — OpenClaw's fixtures are not safe under concurrent access — and two of those commands deliberately take no `--config`, because passing the wrong one silently reports "No test files found" and exits 0. `TRANSPOSED-FROM.md` records source-to-target ancestry and materiality; for this cycle it records a deliberate refusal to transpose across 520 commits and four absorbs. ## Future actions and #130741 composition Maintainer PR #130741 addresses the complementary fresh-sweep race: it captures the current `sessionId` and `lifecycleRevision` before the first await and uses those values as cleanup CAS facts. The return covenant addresses a different time axis: whether historically accepted child work may return to a logical recipient after benign successor creation. The current candidate and #130741 head `e1afc703f49a07687c0876ba6350cafa87a3638a` merge cleanly in a synthetic composition. If #130741 lands, the composed result should preserve both guarantees: - keep #130741's fresh sweep-time exact-run/session lifecycle fence; - keep the covenant's durable logical-recipient generation for historical return admission and delivery; - do not overload broad `lifecycleRevision` as historical return authority; - do not terminate or orphan accepted descendants merely because `/new` or ordinary `/reset` creates a successor session. That composition honors the maintainer repair without weakening continuation semantics or allowing a stale child return to cross a real ownership boundary. ## Why this is not a skill or a viable plugin extraction OpenClaw skills are `SKILL.md` prompt files loaded into an agent turn that already exists. They can guide work inside that turn; they do not own the turn cycle. Continuation needs gateway and agent-runtime owners a skill cannot provide: - The `continue_work` path persists pending work, enforces budgets and delay bounds, arms a timer, reacquires the session reply-run lane, and starts a later model turn after the current turn has finalized. - The `continue_delegate` path persists delegate intent, does spawn/admission accounting, manages child-session lifecycle, and durably routes returns across sessions. - `request_compaction` is an agent election into guarded runtime compaction. Later work resumes only after the runtime has established the new context boundary. - All three need durable state, cancellation/finalization ownership, restart recovery, trace identity, queue-conflict handling, and gateway scheduling outside the model invocation. A skill can tell a model to *ask* for another turn. Without those owners the ask is prose: it cannot persist a due wake, yield and finalize safely, reacquire the session lane, create the next invocation, survive a restart, or deliver a child result to another session. The implementation therefore belongs in core runtime surfaces such as `src/auto-reply/continuation/**`, `src/agents/tools/**`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-continuation-schedule.ts`, and `src/infra/continuation-tracer.ts`. This PR adds no `.agents/skills/**`, `SKILL.md`, or user-facing skill package. The only skill-named production change is core runtime tool dispatch. ClawHub also distributes plugins. Existing plugins can register tools, services, lifecycle hooks, context injection, plugin-owned session state, and — for bundled plugins — Cron-backed session turns. Those seams can support a smaller continuation-like automation, especially TaskFlow plus host Cron / `sessions_spawn`. They are not this feature's turn-finalization ownership, reply-run coordination, durable continuation queue, child-session return lifecycle, election capture, or agent-elected compaction contract. Compaction-provider registration and command-handler `compactCurrent()` are also not that last contract: they compact or summarize, they do not elect compaction at finalization and resume afterward. Moving policy behind a plugin boundary would first require OpenClaw to expose and stabilize a continuation-host API. The gateway/runtime would still own the mechanism described here; a plugin could only package policy around that core capability. That is not a no-core-touch alternative to these primitives. Discord is a bundled channel plugin. It owns the Discord edge, plus delivery/progress hooks into the host's existing subagent path, and submits events into OpenClaw's current turn machinery. Continuation changes that machinery: what survives finalization, which session may run next, how child results return, and when compaction can be elected. A TaskFlow tool adapter is also not a lifecycle host. It can call the core-owned `api.runtime.tasks.managedFlows` API to create, link, pause, resume, finish, cancel, and inspect durable flow records. Marking a waiting record as running does not reacquire a session lane or invoke the model; recording a `childSessionKey` created by a separate spawn surface does not spawn the child or deliver its return. There is no equivalent host continuation capability for this PR to wrap. ## Lineage and replacement context This PR is the clean replacement for closed #85651. It preserves that PR's review lineage and the earlier continuation work descended from #79925, but it does not reuse either closed PR or ask reviewers to infer the current result from them. The replacement carries a current, independently reviewable branch and a complete proof subtree bound to its presented SHA. #85651 was not abandoned because the feature failed or because we accepted its classification as a skill. It was closed after automated labeling put the change in the wrong submission category. This replacement removes that ambiguity: no `src/skills/**` change is presented, current label simulation produces no `r: skill`, and the detailed section above explains why the lifecycle mechanism belongs to core. Acceptance or rejection of the product direction remains OpenClaw's decision. The decision requested is whether OpenClaw should provide multi-session, agent-elected continuation primitives after reviewing the implementation and evidence. It is not whether the same mechanism can be relocated into a skill: a skill cannot own or implement these lifecycle boundaries.

prs.title: perf(agents): archive completed kept subagent runs after 30 days
prs.body:
## Problem and behavior

Completed kept subagent runs remained resident indefinitely. This change archives settled run-mode records strictly older than 30 days while preserving results, status, aliases and ancestry through the existing APIs. Archival does not delete sessions, transcripts, attachments or worktrees. Session-mode bookkeeping retains its existing five-minute retirement policy.

The existing minute sweeper and registry writer move at most 128 rows and approximately 1 MiB of canonical payload per transaction, admitting one oversized row for progress. Unfinished cleanup, delivery, cancellation, requester and collector obligations defer archival. Commit receipts precede resident eviction; retries and uncertain acknowledgements use the existing mutation owner. Follow-ups restore their exact archived generation before advancing execution. Cancellation restores an ancestry anchor only when its existing owner needs that anchor to reach current work. Explicit deletion removes either storage location.

Historical reads remain request-owned and never repopulate resident registry caches. Indexed reads select matching identities before decoding compact payloads. Exact-page preparation includes physical child links and expanded ancestors. Search uses the existing predicate to collect unresolved canonical children; ordinary metadata matches need no selection-time history. Owner counts omit broad history only when complete resident and live-owner facts prove there is no current work. `spawnedBy` and non-idle counts retain broad lineage. New required keys or work after an await retry preparation; child-only search history never substitutes for the displayed page's complete relationship view. Existing invalidation releases already-warm run facts, and the old whole-registry follow-up restore fallback is removed.

## Accepted storage checkpoint

**Peter accepted this exact contract on 2026-10-30, relayed by the performance lead:** the new shared-state `subagent_run_archives` table; consecutive **schema 36→37**; an empty-table migration through normal SQLite/PostgreSQL startup and Doctor; older-version refusal and backup rollback; bounded archival; archive-aware public reads; and exact-generation follow-up restoration. The database storage-change review checkpoint and worker-access rules were reviewed before implementation. Version 37 remained the next available shared-state version. Main's separate agent schema is 39.

The migration performs no bulk rewrite. Its verified pre-migration backup includes original hot records, so rollback remains possible after maintenance archives them. Older binaries refuse schema 37. Rollback restores that backup with its matching binary; it is not an in-place downgrade preserving subsequent writes.

Two conservative internal discovery behaviors are retained: an admitted spawn request can continue counting previously selected settled history toward its total-group cap after concurrent deletion, and registration discovery can retain a deleted archive-only candidate until its next scope. Fresh FIFO mutation admission omits deleted candidates and cannot resurrect them. These discovery facts confer neither execution authority nor active-capacity reservations; public historical read scopes still invalidate on archive revision.

## Latest owner measurement

Measured base **`7d5130f74c226ef71ce4858f9e3f95b166447586`**, candidate **`89a9dd0606ed06785a3a8deac6ab67192bf532e5`**, pinned Node **26.12.1**. Two counterbalanced pairs per mode, each using a fresh 10,000-record fixture aged 1–100 days and 2,000 deterministic exact-ID task/result reads: **4,000 timing reads and 4,000 allocation reads per side**. Both initial timing CPU deltas had the same sign, so the predeclared extra pair was unnecessary.

| Metric | Base mean | Candidate mean | Absolute change | Relative change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Resident records after reads | 10,000 | 3,000 | −7,000 | −70.00% |
| Retained main heap after archival | 24.782 MiB | 9.517 MiB | −15.265 MiB | −61.60% |
| Retained main heap after reads | 27.815 MiB | 11.318 MiB | −16.497 MiB | −59.31% |
| Untraced main-thread CPU / 2,000 reads | 839.145 ms | 813.438 ms | −25.707 ms | −3.06% |
| Untraced process CPU / 2,000 reads | 1,533.701 ms | 1,492.507 ms | −41.194 ms | −2.69% |
| Sampled allocation / 2,000 reads | 361.242 MiB | 372.098 MiB | +10.856 MiB | +3.01% |
| Raw process RSS after reads, including workers | 751.025 MiB | 854.174 MiB | +103.150 MiB | +13.73% |
| Raw main heap after reads | 121.619 MiB | 105.295 MiB | −16.325 MiB | −13.42% |

This is a retained-main-heap improvement with a small untraced CPU reduction, **not a process-RSS win**. Allocation and RSS rise. Timing CPU improves 3.09% and 3.04%; allocation rises 3.61% and 2.40%. Sampled-pass CPU rises 13.33% on average and is reported separately because instrumentation changes execution. Retained heap is post-forced-GC main-isolate heap minus the same-process empty-owner baseline; RSS includes workers and native memory.

Every candidate archives exactly 7,000 records in 55 nonempty batches, never more than 128 rows, and stays at 3,000 residents after all reads. Exact-day-30 records remain hot. One-time archival costs 88.688/92.172 ms main CPU and 3,126.138/3,489.221 ms process CPU; separate allocation passes sample 66.017/65.549 MiB. These transfer costs are excluded from steady-read comparisons. All payload and no-repopulation assertions pass. Host load across the eight arms ranges from 10.83 to 12.93. Complete per-arm observations, raw baselines and methodology: `.local/buf626/owner-comparison-89a9dd0606ed/summary.md` and its adjacent artifacts.

## Correctness and validation

All fixtures and Gateways are synthetic and isolated. No Team traffic, processes or state were touched.

- **Worker and lifecycle boundary:** the original sweeper regression is red because a 31-day kept record stays resident. Coverage includes exact day 30, deferred obligations, the bounded 10k backlog and oversized-row progress, transaction rollback, committed archival with an unacknowledged reply, restart, exact-generation follow-up, and explicit deletion. The later replay on frozen base `52fbfb7d989207a4f82544f58b5bb9ee75782fe9` fails the resident assertion at line 94 before archive-only SQL: 1 failed, 6 skipped, 43.28 s wrapper. The original receipt records an earlier red on `6ac91adabcc273e76a2d652a5aefc9955b0600f8`; these are separate runs. Evidence: `.local/buf626/base-52fbfb7d9892-worker-red.log`, `worker-proof-summary.md`, and `archive-gateway-followup-proof.log`.
- **Complete reader cutover:** aliases and inverse collisions, latest-generation ordering, tools, admission, cancellation and restart ancestry have focused proof. Restart coverage includes an archived intermediary with a live grandchild and no recovery work from history alone. Indexed traversal selects zero unrelated identities versus 256 before repair across four reads. The public archived-model search regression is red on its preceding candidate and green after the existing vocabulary owner consumes request-owned history.
- **Gateway work and freshness:** broad-history work-count regressions fail before scoped selection; six focused files pass 39 tests after it. The owning file passes 16 cases, including metadata changing during exact-page preparation, registration-grace work arriving behind an archived intermediary, newer hot-generation precedence, complete page relationships and unchanged residency. Existing authority and disclosure assertions remain intact.
- **Upgrade/rollback:** a synthetic store made by exact published `openclaw@2026.10.9` upgrades from shared schema 20 through startup and Doctor to 37, preserving hot bytes and initially leaving the archive empty. The unmodified released version guard refuses 37 and accepts the verified restored schema-20 backup; this tests the guard, not a full old-Gateway launch. SQLite archival migration cases, PostgreSQL's 137-table inventory and exact/sanitized backup round trip, and all five historical PostgreSQL migration cases pass. The latest rebase's shared-state boundaries are unchanged; canonical combined schema verification confirms 37/39.
- **Integration defects repaired:** fresh mutation admission no longer reuses captured hot rows as historical fallback after deletion, and registration cohorts exclude known foreign owners sharing a raw key while retaining wrong-owner rejection for exact requested IDs. The unchanged watched-registration case that timed out in CI passes in 999 ms; five focused files pass 59 tests. Archive-during-discovery still advances the current generation without restoring history. No timeout or assertion was weakened.
- **Checks and review:** core/scripts, all four `pnpm tsgo:test:root` partitions, affected Gateway/agents test graphs, touched oxlint/oxfmt, export/mock/closure guards, Madge and stress-harness tests have passing evidence on their recorded heads. Full review 25 and incremental reviews 26–27 resolved the archive/deletion/cohort findings. Review 28 is scoped-clean through P2 for the harness-temp repair and missed script argument. Its six focused files pass 88 unique tests; core/scripts, affected agents and all root test-type partitions, touched lint and formatting pass. No benchmark lint suppression was added.

## Canonical Gateway comparison — pending

The final comparison is pending the repaired candidate build/smoke for `4a262dc1857e10430b29981c48987a0db8629675`, with matching base `7d5130f74c226ef71ce4858f9e3f95b166447586`. The completed owner results above measured `89a9dd0606ed06785a3a8deac6ab67192bf532e5`; no earlier result is relabeled as the repair head. The fixture has 10,800 sessions, 40 plugins, 65 WebSocket clients, concurrent mock-provider/native-subagent turns with tool calls, sidebar/list/search churn, and 4,300 kept runs aged up to 100 days. Two counterbalanced AB/BA pairs and two matching A/A pairs per timing/allocation mode run for at least ten minutes per arm. A checkpoint after all eight timing arms was declared before results; no measured window is trimmed or discarded based on its outcome.

**Pending:** final main-thread CPU, allocation rate, GC s/min, event-loop and client/server list tails with sample counts, both pause maxima, RSS/heap, actual archival progress, and per-arm host load. Owner measurements do not establish whole-Gateway acceptance. Client tails alone cannot establish harm on this host; GC/promotion/max-pause rejection needs at least four matched controls in its instrumentation mode. Mixed signs, tiny absolute deltas and noisy controls retain their declared handling. Local checks do not overlap measured windows.

<details>
<summary>Prior campaigns and repairs; preserved evidence, not acceptance of the final head</summary>

prs.title: fix(wear): live Talk ends when the watch screen times out
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: live watch Talk ends mid-conversation when the watch screen times out while the mic is listening.

## User Impact

The watch screen stays on for as long as realtime Talk is active or the mic is capturing. It returns to the normal timeout as soon as Talk stops.

## Summary

### High Level TLDR

If the watch screen times out during a live Talk session, Android stops the activity, and the app ends Talk on `ON_STOP`. You are mid-sentence and the session just ends. This change holds the screen on only while Talk is live, the same way a call app does.

### Root Cause

- `MainActivity` registers a lifecycle observer that calls `viewModel.suspendRealtimeTalk()` on `Lifecycle.Event.ON_STOP`.
- `suspendRealtimeTalk()` calls `stopRealtimeTalk()` whenever `realtimeTalk.active || realtimeCapturing`.
- Nothing kept the display awake during that state. The normal Wear OS screen timeout therefore stopped the activity, and that ended the session.
- Ending Talk on `ON_STOP` is correct for real navigation away. It is the screen timeout that should not trigger it.

### Exact change

- Added a `DisposableEffect` keyed on `realtimeTalk.active || realtimeCapturing` that sets `view.keepScreenOn`.
- `onDispose` clears the flag, so leaving the composition never leaves the screen pinned.
- No change to the `ON_STOP` stop policy.

### Scope boundary

- Watch app only, with no phone or Gateway changes.
- Leaving the app (back, home, side button) still ends Talk as before.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

- Debug build installed on a Galaxy Watch (Wear OS 5) and used for live Talk sessions.
- Talk stayed open past the normal screen timeout.
- System logs show the window's `SCREEN_BRIGHT_WAKE_LOCK` held for the whole live session. It was released within about 30 ms of the session ending (`state:paused` / `abandonAudioFocus` for the Talk track, followed by `[api] release WakeLock SCREEN_BRIGHT_WAKE_LOCK 'WindowManager/displayId:0'`).

### Verification

- `./gradlew :wear:ktlintCheck :wear:testDebugUnitTest` passed.
- `./gradlew :wear:assembleDebug` passed.

### What was not tested

- There is no unit test for the Compose window flag. It is a view side effect, and this was verified on device instead.
- Ambient mode and other watch makers were not tested.
