prs.title: feat(workers): bind cleanup to recorded cloud resources
prs.body:
Related: #188796

## What Problem This Solves

Cloud worker recovery and cleanup need a durable binding to the original provider resource, rather than relying only on a reusable lease handle after a lost reply or restart.

Original work and design by @galiniliev; extracted and reimplemented at the contributor's request.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @galiniliev](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/1c21e0ea-e918-4f4d-a25f-a46256a029bd)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/9e5ce302-c947-42c1-9be1-a5254aa17cf2)

## User Impact

New Crabbox Azure Sandbox workers record exact resource identity before setup/enrollment. Restart recovery refuses replacement identities, unavailable observations preserve ownership, and Stop remains pending until exact-resource deletion is confirmed.

**This is a prerequisite, not retained-disk activation.** Gateway checkpoints, existing idle suspension, and workspace authority remain unchanged. It enables neither retained allocation nor pause/resume nor disk-authoritative workspaces. Legacy environments without receipts keep their fixed-lease cleanup contract and are not silently rebound.

Shared-state schema **36 → 37** preserves old rows with a null receipt and fences older binaries. Rollback requires settling new environments and pending cleanup, then restoring the matching pre-upgrade backup with its binary; a package-only downgrade is unsafe. PostgreSQL migration and generated predecessor descriptors are included.

## Why This Change Was Made

An optional generic provider receipt contract feeds the existing environment writer, provisioning, inspection, and teardown owners. The Crabbox plugin alone interprets Azure-specific identity and CLI flags. Receipt custody commits before subsequent setup effects; retries retain the original allocation and immutable identity. No separate manager, timer, queue, or state file is introduced.

Existing SSH bootstrap and Crabbox teardown phases are extracted without changing ownership to keep their modules bounded. Production delta is **+694/−143**, including relocations; tests are **+745/−38**. Generated files are separate. The **707-line** regression allocation is task-specific; the shared scalar is unchanged.

## Evidence

- **56 provider/recovery tests passed across 5 files** (79.85s wall time), including real environment-store recovery and Crabbox protocol fixtures.
- **10 real-worker store/migration tests passed**, covering reopening, immutability, live guards, corruption, runtime/Doctor upgrade, rollback, and PostgreSQL predecessor descriptors. All 10 passed again after main integration (60.61s wall time). Existing store/projection coverage also passed 25 cases in an earlier run.
- Three historical migration cases passed after deduplicating identical expectations for the line-cap gate. The final fixture-parameter rename is behavior-preserving and passes targeted lint.
- Targeted TypeScript, type-aware lint, formatting, canonical generator freshness, regression-budget and line-cap checks, and pre-commit passed. Initial committed SDK API comparison completed; acknowledgement digest **4a99ee35**.
- Independent autoreview against `18516599b1d417fee621b2fd2ceda21107bc038a`: four-pass **P0–P3 chunked scoped-clean**, with source verification. Generated catalog comparison was partition-limited; regeneration and migration tests supply cross-catalog evidence. Reviewed production snapshot: `b6057c7212706f64115b60c1947ab5617226d4ed`. Subsequent changes are historical-test deduplication/renaming and independent schema-metadata integration, not receipt behavior changes.
- Integrated main `7992b413a8b524c0a29c5b86e4e50c057a777a3a` to resolve the sole package metadata conflict, preserving this PR's state schema **37** and main's agent schema **39**. Published tree: `a998a5d347dcecef0f08c2985dd120cbb95ca132`.
- Production stop boundary negative control with a local fixture CLI: baseline deletes a simulated replacement; the changed implementation rejects it and leaves it intact.
- Managed Crabbox **0.80.0** advertises Linux Azure Sandbox **session-disk-retention-v1** and **pause-resume**. Exact-stop flags and the released provider implementation were inspected. This is protocol/source evidence, not authenticated controller readiness or live lifecycle proof.

No live provider allocation, real-model Gateway flow, latest-stable binary upgrade, or actual PostgreSQL server execution was performed. SQLite worker/migration tests and PostgreSQL generated-schema/descriptor checks are the available boundary proof; this host has no PostgreSQL or Docker executable.

At 04:19 UTC on October 31, head `13eb7612165f4cc805de5678e85e8cc115a6848f` had **18 pending, 7 passed, and 23 skipped/neutral checks**, with no failed checks. Dependency and security-sensitive gates passed; broad CI remains unqualified. The PR is mergeable, not merged or deployed. Prior-head checks are not current-head qualification.

## Worked on by

- @galiniliev

prs.title: fix(skills): selected project skills are missing from the $ picker and slash commands
prs.body:
Related: #187813

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: skills from a selected project's `skills/` and `.agents/skills/` are missing from the Control UI `$` picker and slash commands, both in the New session composer and in existing project sessions, even though the agent's runtime skill catalog includes them.

## User Impact

User impact: in the New session composer, selecting a registered project shows that project's eligible skills in `$` and `/`, switching projects or back to the agent workspace replaces the list, and a picked project skill is actually invoked on the first turn. Existing project sessions (Control UI, and channel sessions such as Telegram) list and invoke their project skills too. Precedence, allowlists, eligibility and sandbox containment are unchanged; clients that could not create a session in a project never see its skills.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **New session preview:** `commands.list` accepts an optional `projectId` (not combined with `sessionKey`). The Gateway resolves it through the project registry, admits the root with the same session-creation authorization and sandbox containment as `sessions.create`, repeats that admission right before responding, and passes the root to the existing skill loader as the execution root. The composer sends its selected project; the UI command cache and stale-request ownership are keyed by project, and a pending slash refresh is retired when agent, draft or project changes.
- **Invocation:** reply-path consumers (explicit `$` references, slash and tool dispatch) derive the session's execution skill root with the same resolver as the runtime catalog, so a listed project skill is also invocable.
- **Existing sessions:** a session with an execution root (spawned cwd or managed worktree) reads its own `commands.list` instead of the agent-scoped startup command catalog; sessions without a project keep the startup catalog. A republished catalog retires the session's cached copy.
- **File host:** one shared resolver keeps registered and cloned project roots Gateway-owned through preview, creation, invocation and the runtime snapshot, including for agents whose workspace is served by a paired node (File Transfer). The `workspace:<agent>` pseudo-project keeps the agent workspace's own host, using the registry's source classification.

Overlap: #187869 by @yy19971996 independently makes the same session invocation-root change in `chat-commands.ts`; this PR includes it because the preview-to-invocation flow needs it, and uses the same option names so either PR rebases cleanly onto the other. Credit to @yy19971996 for that work. #155867 is untouched.

## Evidence

Control UI New session with project **alpha** selected — both project roots listed:

![New session $ picker with project alpha selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/595a6a70-3327-4437-a45f-c24f2b47ac1a)

After switching to project **beta** — alpha entries gone:

![New session $ picker after switching to project beta](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44910848-9df9-493b-a4cd-75a196247f62)

Back to the agent workspace — project entries gone:

![New session $ picker back on the agent workspace](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18ddac3a-3606-4640-9673-1e4c9e68e3ce)

Existing alpha session `$` picker:

![Existing alpha session $ picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2925aaff-bfee-4799-9f0a-18b3d59502c3)

Project tool-dispatch slash command answered without a model turn:

![Project tool-dispatch slash command reply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/866d1e9c-df09-4e57-8b88-7a963a390bb8)

Cache retirement in the shipped Control UI (project session, Library activation succeeds, metadata refresh fails at the transport, a stale in-flight catalog read is released): reopening `$` fetches the fresh catalog once and shows the new pin, and an unrelated session keeps its cached catalog:

![Project session $ after Library activation shows the fresh pin](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6112db15-87aa-4d22-8846-f8d39c245aa3)

![Unrelated session $ still served from its own cached catalog](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3daff8ae-14f8-4877-9829-de357640839a)

- Focused unit/boundary suites: 250 passed across command discovery, the `commands.list` handler, protocol, runtime preparation and the New session/chat composer, plus the affected re-runs for each later change. Each fix has a regression that fails with the fix reverted, including a new one for invalidating every cached command variant of a session (Library activation, failed metadata refresh, late in-flight read, unrelated session unaffected).
- Real Control UI + Gateway flow (isolated Gateway, synthetic fixtures, fixture model): render and select both project roots, switch projects and back to the workspace, start a session and confirm the first turn carries the explicit skill instruction, open `$` in the created session, and run a project `command-dispatch: tool` slash command without a model turn.
- Shipped Control UI cache scenario (production bundle, visible Library controls, transport-level failures at a mock Gateway): see the screenshots above.
- Authority (real Gateway, trusted-proxy identities, `gateway.roles`, synthetic projects): `commands.list` with a `projectId` returned the project's skills to an administrator and to a member whose role allows the agent. A device granted only `operator.read`, and a role whose agents exclude the target agent, received only the agent catalog. While a slow discovery was in flight, removing the project returned `UNAVAILABLE` ("Project access changed while preparing its commands"), a config patch removing the role's agent access returned `UNAVAILABLE`, and revoking the operator's role closed the connection before any response; no project skills were disclosed. Tightening the agent's sandbox mode mid-discovery was not exercised because that setting requires a Gateway restart.
- Telegram Test Server DM bound to a synthetic registered project: `$skill` reached the agent turn with the explicit skill instruction, and a project tool-dispatch slash command replied directly with no model request.
- Separately launched, paired node with a File Transfer workspace: preview → `sessions.create` → `commands.list` → `chat.send` for a registered project and the workspace pseudo-project, red/green against the pseudo-project host fix. The no-Gateway-path-read claim rests on the node read policy and the observed catalogs, not a per-request node trace.
- Test-line allocation: `config/test-lines-allocations/project-skills-picker-187813.txt` grants exactly this PR's net +563 regression-test lines; the shared baseline is unchanged. They cover: project preview admission and the disclosure re-check before responding; the `workspace:<agent>` pseudo-project keeping the agent workspace's file host; registered-project roots staying Gateway-owned through preview, creation and invocation; existing project sessions reading their own command catalog; invalidation of every cached command variant of a session, including Library activation followed by a failed metadata refresh and a late in-flight read; New session project-keyed command cache and stale slash-refresh retirement; and the reply-path invocation root for `$` and `/` project skills. One duplicate node-workspace discovery case and one superseded scoped-invalidation block were folded first.
- Compatibility: `commands.list.projectId` is an optional additive parameter; requests without it behave as before. No persisted schema, config, user-state migration, protocol version or updater change, so no upgrade-path qualification applies.
- CI: earlier runs failed on checks inherited from main, not caused by this PR: a test-line ratchet over the shared ceiling (repaired on main in #188780), `skill-runtime.library-read.test.ts` expecting an older symlink error message (repaired in #188090), and `cron-descriptions.e2e.test.ts` expecting the pre-pause detail text (repaired in #188922). Those repairs are merged into this branch with no conflicts and this PR's own patch unchanged; the repaired tests pass locally on the current head. An earlier `server.chat-steer-direct-command.test.ts` failure (identical on main) and an artifact-download failure before lint did not recur. `pnpm check:changed` passes all lanes except the dead-export scan, which already fails on the base for two files this PR does not touch. CI passed on head fe7d994; all required checks are green.
- Not covered end to end: tool dispatch from a skill inside a managed-worktree project (unit-tested only).

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/aacbb42f-7202-412c-be3e-b04b536b3e36)

## Worked on by

- @hannesrudolph

prs.title: fix: refuse late plugin state work during Gateway shutdown
prs.body:
Related: #188920, #188976

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes plugin shared-state work continuing into worker retirement and retrying terminal state-admission errors after Gateway shutdown begins.

## User Impact

Gateway shutdown refuses new plugin shared-state work once, drains accepted operations before retirement, and preserves clean restart exits. Late background persistence is intentionally refused; no config or persisted-data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing SDK resource host now owns shared-state admission and drainage, using the existing Gateway shutdown signals. Keyed-store operations, retained worker leases, and fixed reads delegate to that owner; fixed reads enter admission before snapshot preparation. Accepted operations can finish their nested acquisitions, while completed operations cannot lend admission to later timers. Core shutdown persistence exits the initiating plugin invocation and retains its own existing authority.

The storage-error classifier marks invalidated admission and retiring workers terminal. Core retry runners enforce that decision even with a caller retry predicate, and Nostr's outer cursor-recovery loop consumes the documented SDK classifier. Existing command-lifecycle and read-reply helpers move to coherent sibling owners so capped files shrink. Production grows by 150 lines for admission/tracking and terminal classification; consolidated regression coverage and fixture ownership grow by 35 lines. A small leaf module carries admission wiring without importing the plugin runtime graph into state workers.

## Evidence

- Red on pinned main `983433f2187762a8788e06e004938f192d4a2668` under Node and Bun: late plugin state work was accepted, both terminal error forms made three channel attempts, and the model retry classifier accepted invalidated admission. Nostr also retried the terminal write.
- Green under Node and Bun: retry/channel/model/Nostr suites, shared-worker and retained-lease suites, existing Gateway close coverage, and the fixed-read snapshot/worker-lifecycle/retained suites. The actual restart-process test verifies exactly one terminal refusal, no retirement/open-failure diagnostics, and exit 0 for SIGTERM and managed restart.
- `node scripts/prepare-vitest-runtime.mjs --with-ai-package` passes on clean main and this branch, including the CLI bootstrap import guard. The unpublished draft's failure came from importing the database lifecycle error class into the CLI cleanup path; that pulled five forbidden filesystem-package edges into bootstrap. This patch uses the lightweight error code instead.
- Targeted lint, format, core and affected-test typechecks, SDK export synchronization, all baseline ratchets, the separate line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` pass. No cap, baseline, dependency, version, or config changes.
- SDK API diff completed successfully against pinned main: no entrypoints or exports removed. The report identifies the optional runtime retry predicate and ordering changes in an inferred declaration union (identical declaration-line contents).
- Independent local review found no actionable P0–P2 findings, including the final CI repair.
- Initial CI exposed a new static import cycle and a synthetic Memory Core fixture missing its SDK resource host. Both are repaired: `pnpm check:madge-import-cycles` reports zero cycles, and all 12 dreaming startup tests pass under Node and Bun. The held-process assertion in `src/gateway/server-startup-lifetime.test.ts` also fails on clean pinned main (expected one settlement, received zero); that failure is inherited and remains outside this change.

The PostgreSQL-only worker-view case remains skipped in these isolated SQLite proofs. No live Gateway or user state was used.


## Current CI Blocker

The repaired head `dbc931ead149d648a1d7b603a4a5ba69420624f2` is blocked. The new private admission module was omitted from `scripts/pr-lib/wrapper-components.txt`. Exact-head CI reports missing `src/plugins/plugin-shared-state-admission.ts` in wrapper import closure and extracted-runtime failures. This is attributable to this change; no claim of merge readiness is made.

Run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41165831153. Failed jobs: `checks-node-compact-small-1` (new wrapper closure failure), `checks-node-compact-small-2` (new wrapper closure failure plus private-store provisioning assertions), `checks-node-changed-compact-large-13` (private-store provisioning assertions, not separately proven inherited), and `checks-node-changed-compact-large-24` (the startup held-process assertion reproduced on clean pinned main). The final observation had 62 successful jobs, 23 skipped, 4 failed, and 3 PostgreSQL conformance jobs still running. The earlier import cycle and dreaming fixture failures are repaired.

The work order allows one repair push, which has been used. Stopping for coordinator review without further source edits, pushes, reruns, or merge. The remaining source correction is to include the new module in the extracted wrapper inventory and prove the failed wrapper/provisioning suites.

prs.title: fix(discord): channels named in non-Latin script resolve to a different channel
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/188126

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Discord channel configured or looked up by a name without ASCII letters or digits (for example "чат") resolves to a different channel, so its per-channel settings, including its tool policy, apply to the wrong channel.

## User Impact

User impact: guild channels named in Cyrillic, Japanese, Chinese, Korean and other non-Latin scripts now resolve to the channel with that name, at Gateway startup and in `openclaw channels resolve`. A name that matches no channel stays unresolved instead of taking another channel's ID, and so does a key made only of emoji or punctuation. The live directory search returns only matching channels for a non-Latin query. ASCII keys resolve exactly as before, to the same channel IDs, including `general` for a channel named "общий-general" and "alerts" for "⚠️-alerts". The channel label in agent context for an emoji-prefixed name such as "⚠️-alerts" becomes `#alerts` instead of keeping the emoji's variation selector.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord channel name matching used an ASCII-only slug, which turns every non-Latin name into an empty string, so all such names matched each other and the first one in API order won. At startup the configured entry (mention gating, system prompt, tool policy) is then bound to that channel's ID.

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187148 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188003 fixed the same class of problem for directory searches by comparing lowercase NFC text. Discord already has a Unicode-aware slug for channel labels, `normalizeDiscordDisplaySlug` (NFC, lowercase, keeps letters, marks and digits of any script). Channel resolution and the live directory search now use it for keys with letters outside ASCII, and resolution refuses an empty slug, as guild name matching already does.

For the review's Decision needed, this implements Preserve existing ASCII selection: ASCII keys keep the ASCII-only match (`extensions/discord/src/resolve-channels.ts:156-160`), so every existing ASCII key binds the same channel ID as before. A resolved name key is bound to its channel ID (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171829), and that binding is what keeps other channels and threads with the same name from using the key's policy; changing which channel an ASCII key binds, or leaving it unbound, would move or widen its policy on upgrade. A key with other letters (Japanese letters followed by `-ops`) never matches by its Latin part, which on the base bound it to a channel named `ops`.

The slug now drops emoji variation selectors and the keycap mark (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/allow-list.ts:88-91`). They are combining marks, so the slug kept them: emoji-only names such as "⚠️" and "❗️" both slugged to the selector and matched each other. Now they slug to "" and are refused.

## Evidence

Head `7a984a8f337` (base `upstream/main` `f9257898216`). The Gateway runs below are at `1fca9f16ee6`; the later commits change only tests and the test-line allocation. All data is synthetic: no real Discord account or token, no provider key.

### Real Gateway, message in, tool call, reply out

Each run started an isolated Gateway (`openclaw gateway run --allow-unconfigured`) with its own state directory, config and synthetic bot token, inside `unshare -rn` (loopback only). Discord was Crabline's local Discord server (REST and Gateway WebSocket) behind a small proxy that names its channels and lists the guild's channels for startup resolution. The model was a local OpenAI-compatible stand-in: on each turn it asks for `exec` with `echo tool-ran-<probe>`, whether or not `exec` was offered, and replies with the tool output once one arrives, so the Gateway's own tool gate decides. `tools.exec.mode` is `full` so a granted `exec` runs without a human approval; the only command ever run is that `echo`.

Guild: новости …10, чат …20, general …30, a thread named "чат" in новости …50 and one in general …60. Config: `groupPolicy: "allowlist"`, guild `tools.deny: ["exec"]`, key `чат` = `{ requireMention: false, tools: { allow: ["exec", "read"] } }`, key `general` = `{ requireMention: false }`. One message was sent into each channel or thread.

Startup log, base:

```text
[discord] channels resolved: 135000000000000011/135000000000000010 (guild:Synthetic Guild; channel:новости; aliases:135000000000000011/чат), 135000000000000011/135000000000000030 (guild:Synthetic Guild; channel:general; aliases:135000000000000011/general)
```

This PR:

```text
[discord] channels resolved: 135000000000000011/135000000000000020 (guild:Synthetic Guild; channel:чат; aliases:135000000000000011/чат), 135000000000000011/135000000000000030 (guild:Synthetic Guild; channel:general; aliases:135000000000000011/general)
```

| Target | Before (base) | After (this PR) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| чат …20 | admitted; `exec` not offered (13 tools); the turn stops on "unknown tool" | `exec` offered (5 tools) and run; reply `ack probe-chat tool-ran-probe-chat` |
| новости …10 | `exec` offered and run; reply `ack probe-news tool-ran-probe-news` | dropped, no model turn |
| general …30 | `exec` not offered; "unknown tool" | same |
| Thread "чат" in новости …50 | `exec` offered and run (inherits новости) | dropped |
| Thread "чат" in general …60 | `exec` not offered; "unknown tool" | same |
| Key `чат` removed | чат, новости and the новости thread dropped; general and its thread without `exec` | same |
| Policy moved to key `новости` | новости and its thread run `exec`; чат dropped | same |

With this PR, `exec` ran only in чат; no other channel or thread, including the two threads named "чат", got it. On the base it ran in новости and in the thread under it.

### Upgrade from 2026.10.9

The same config and guild ran on the latest stable release (`openclaw@2026.10.9` from npm with `@openclaw/discord@2026.10.9` installed by `openclaw plugins install`). It resolves чат to новости like the base. The thread rows differ from the base because 2026.10.9 predates https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171829, so threads still match keys by name:

| Target | 2026.10.9 |
| --- | --- |
| чат …20 | `exec` run |
| новости …10 | admitted (the `чат` key resolves to it), `exec` not offered |
| general …30 | `exec` not offered |
| Thread "чат" in новости …50 | `exec` run |
| Thread "чат" in general …60 | `exec` run |

The config hash was the same before and after the run. Then this branch ran on that state directory and config: `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` upgraded the agent database (schema 25 to 38) and changed no `channels.discord` setting. The Gateway (with the branch's bundled Discord plugin, which overrides the installed npm copy) logged the same "channels resolved" line as above and gave the same rows as "After": `exec` ran only in чат, and neither thread named "чат" got it.

### Tests

The case in `resolve-channels.test.ts` and the non-Latin query in `directory-live.test.ts` fail on the base and pass on this branch; the other 14 tests in the two files pass on both. In CI at `458bd869c7f` (run 41011581230) the two files took 50 ms and 25 ms of test time.

Checks at `7a984a8f337`: the two touched test files and `provider.allowlist.test.ts` (the startup channel-binding tests, with the resolver mocked), oxlint and format check on the changed files, and `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`. The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

The test-lines ratchet failed on the previous CI run because the base was already over its ceiling. This PR's net test lines (+40) are covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/discord-unicode-channel-resolution.txt`; they are the regression tests above.

<details>
<summary>Per-case test notes, CLI and directory search, local timing</summary>

`resolve-channels.test.ts` "matches channel names by their letters in any script" covers a non-Latin name, a missing non-Latin name, "alerts" for "⚠️-alerts", `general` for "общий-general", `ops` for the first channel whose ASCII letters are "ops" ("чат-ops", as on the base), a Japanese `-ops` key that stays unresolved, and an emoji-only key "⚠️" that stays unresolved next to a "❗️" channel. Without the selector strip the "⚠️" key binds "❗️" and the test fails.

CLI and directory search at `458bd869c7f`, same synthetic guild (новости …01, чат …02, general …03):

```text
$ openclaw channels resolve --channel discord --kind group --json "900000000000000001/чат"
before: "id": "910000000000000001", "name": "новости"
after:  "id": "910000000000000002", "name": "чат"

$ openclaw directory groups list --channel discord --query чат --json
after: channel:910000000000000002 "чат"   (новости and general are not returned)
```

A single local run with `--maxWorkers=1` at `7a984a8f337`:

| Test file | Tests | Wall (Vitest duration) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `extensions/discord/src/resolve-channels.test.ts` | 10 | 6.9 s (4.7 s) |
| `extensions/discord/src/directory-live.test.ts` | 6 | 7.0 s (4.8 s) |

</details>

Not covered: a real Discord guild. Messages went through Crabline's local Discord server, not Discord itself; the shared Discord end-to-end lane leases a QA guild with one fixed text channel and cannot hold the non-Latin channels this needs. The upgrade run used this branch from a source checkout on the 2026.10.9 state, not a packaged release.

Left for a follow-up: guild names are still matched on the ASCII-only slug, so a guild name that mixes scripts matches by its Latin part alone, and a guild name written only in non-Latin script does not resolve by name at all (it fails closed and never binds another guild). That behavior predates this change and is not touched here. A directory query made only of emoji or punctuation still returns every channel, as every non-Latin query did on the base.

Related: #188404

## What Problem This Solves

Fresh plugin lifecycle test children repeatedly load the source runtime, adding avoidable time to the same lease regression coverage.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. Developers retain all 19 lifecycle tests with less repeated child loading.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing invocation-prepared runtime entrypoints for the lease and installed-index owners, then run the fixture scripts as native ESM. This removes three tsx preloads, replaces nine source-owner imports with compiled-owner imports, and removes two temporary script writes while retaining all three fresh children. The registry change is additive.

## Evidence

Three successful serial runs before and three after, on frozen base `c993c8f2a51aba66a3b2be6fed3c68d00ae64bdb`, using the same worktree dependencies, pinned runtime, host, private temp directory, and caches:

`timeout 900 /usr/bin/time -v pnpm test src/plugins/plugin-lifecycle-lease.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose`

All three process boundaries, real SIGKILL recovery, stale loaded index, contention, ordered acquisition, merged records, captured output, ownership checks, and joined cleanup remain. The real 1.5-second synchronous stall is unchanged. No tests, assertions, mocks, timeout allowances, lease durations, or repetitions were removed or weakened. The removed optional environment parameter had no callers after #188404; each fixture still inherits the same isolated process environment.

Negative controls failed at the intended boundaries: retaining the dead owner's durable row prevents recovery with `OPENCLAW_STATE_LEASE_HELD`; reusing the process cache instead of a fresh lifecycle cache fails beta's `records:alpha` assertion. Both temporary production mutations were restored byte-for-byte. These intentional failures are preserved separately from the six passing measurements; no observed test flakes or discarded performance candidates.

Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/144969

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: setup stays unavailable on every device, with `OpenClaw setup is already in progress; try again when it finishes.`, after a client starts a setup or channel wizard and goes away without cancelling it. Only a Gateway restart clears it.

## User Impact

User impact: an abandoned setup wizard releases setup after 25 minutes without client activity, so another device (or the same one, after a reload) can start setup again without restarting the Gateway. A client that comes back to an expired wizard gets the same "not found" answer it already shows as an expired session.

## Why This Change Was Made

A `wizard.start` session holds setup admission until its runner settles, and nothing settles it when the starting client disappears: the session is intentionally not bound to its connection, and only that client knows the session id needed for `wizard.cancel`.

This change gives hosted `wizard.start` sessions a 25-minute idle window, reusing the session's existing expiry timer (`WizardSession` now takes either a fixed `timeoutMs` or a renewable `idleTimeoutMs`). Each `wizard.next` call restarts the window, and so does the step a waiting `wizard.next` receives. Expiry closes the wizard's input the same way closing the Control UI setup window does (`wizard.cancel` with `closeInput`). A configuration write already in progress still finishes, and a channel session left waiting on a prompt after its durable commit is released too. Other `WizardSession` users (provider sign-in, prepare) keep their fixed deadlines. An expired session is removed once its runner settles (when expiry ends it as cancelled), so a returning client gets `WIZARD_NOT_FOUND` rather than a generic "wizard not running".

Design note: I chose idle expiry over binding the session to its connection, because setup sessions are deliberately not connection-bound, so a reconnecting client can resume. 25 minutes matches the fixed deadline hosted provider sign-in already uses (`PROVIDER_AUTH_SESSION_TIMEOUT_MS`); here it renews on every `wizard.next`, so it is the looser of the two. The tradeoff: a tab left open on a prompt for 25 minutes also expires, and so does a client waiting on a step that takes more than 25 minutes with no progress output; the wizard then has to be started again. A pending `wizard.next` does not count as activity on purpose, because a long-poll left behind by a closed tab would otherwise hold setup forever. A busy-message cancel action, also suggested on the issue, would need UI and protocol changes and is left out of this change.

This builds on the approach of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/133848 by @SebTardif (renewable idle timeout on hosted wizards), which was closed for inactivity. Thanks to them for the original design.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175334 (channel setup stores tokens in the secret store) also edits the `wizard.start` handler, so whichever lands second needs a small merge there. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163527 (setup runner honors session cancellation), named here before, was closed without merging. Main's hosted runner still ignores the session's abort signal, so interrupting provider sign-in polling on expiry stays out of this change.

## Evidence

Re-run on 2026-10-30 at `226e4cf40d0`, the head of this PR after merging main `5ed4aa230f8`. The Before ran on main `5ed4aa230f8` itself. The two later commits change no production code: `6ed0e6a8b10` adds the test-line allocation described below, and `75e9295e0f8` rewrites the new handler test onto the file's existing helpers with the same assertions. So this run still covers the head.

A built Gateway ran on Linux (Node 24.22.1) with an isolated home and state, loopback only, inside its own network namespace, once per side, using the same steps on the channel setup flow the issue reports (`wizard.start` with `flow: "channels"`). Each line is a separate `callGateway` call (the Gateway client the CLI uses) with `operator.admin`, over a new WebSocket connection that closes when the call returns, which matches a Control UI tab closed mid-wizard. Client A opens channel setup and leaves, client B tries at once, nobody touches A's session for 26 minutes, then B tries again and A asks about its own session. The production 25-minute value was not shortened. Each line shows the call time, the method, and the answer reduced to its status or error fields.

Before (main `5ed4aa230f8`):

```text
2026-10-30T14:45:03.108Z wizard.start {"ok":true,"status":"running","done":false,"step":{"type":"note","title":"Channel setup"}}
2026-10-30T14:45:03.213Z wizard.start {"ok":false,"message":"OpenClaw setup is already in progress; try again when it finishes.","code":"UNAVAILABLE","detail":"SETUP_ADMISSION_BUSY"}
2026-10-30T15:11:03.331Z wizard.start {"ok":false,"message":"OpenClaw setup is already in progress; try again when it finishes.","code":"UNAVAILABLE","detail":"SETUP_ADMISSION_BUSY"}
2026-10-30T15:11:03.363Z wizard.status {"ok":true,"status":"running","done":null,"step":null}
```

After (this PR, `226e4cf40d0`):

```text
2026-10-30T15:18:19.224Z wizard.start {"ok":true,"status":"running","done":false,"step":{"type":"note","title":"Channel setup"}}
2026-10-30T15:18:19.364Z wizard.start {"ok":false,"message":"OpenClaw setup is already in progress; try again when it finishes.","code":"UNAVAILABLE","detail":"SETUP_ADMISSION_BUSY"}
2026-10-30T15:44:19.480Z wizard.start {"ok":true,"status":"running","done":false,"step":{"type":"note","title":"Channel setup"}}
2026-10-30T15:44:19.510Z wizard.status {"ok":false,"message":"wizard not found","code":"INVALID_REQUEST","detail":"WIZARD_NOT_FOUND"}
```

Observed result: on main, 26 minutes after client A left, client B is still refused with `SETUP_ADMISSION_BUSY`, and A's abandoned session still reports `running`. With this change, B starts channel setup, and A's expired session answers `WIZARD_NOT_FOUND`. While A's session is live, B is refused on both sides. The Gateway logs show no other wizard or setup-admission errors. The two earlier runs of this PR (`d762d1fbde3` and `a013647e3e1`, each against the main of its day) gave the same four answers on each side.

The merge follows main's https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183777, which moved `wizard.start` onto the shared `startGatewayWizard` runner. This PR keeps that runner and only adds two things to the `wizard.start` call: the `{ idleTimeoutMs }` option on `new WizardSession(...)` (`src/gateway/server-methods/wizard.ts:146`), and the expired-session cleanup, now inside `respondStarted` (`wizard.ts:153-161`). `startGatewayWizard` registers the session before it calls `respondStarted` (`setup-admission.ts:215-217`), so the cleanup sees the same registered session as before the merge.

Checks at `226e4cf40d0`: the two touched test files; a fail-to-pass run of both files on the base and here (below); type-aware `oxlint` (`scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`, as CI runs it) and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files; `tsgo` on the core and UI projects and every core test shard. At `75e9295e0f8`, the two test files, the fail-to-pass run, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` and the `tsgo` src test shards ran again. `pnpm test:ci-failed 170996` found no failed Vitest shards on the CI of `226e4cf40d0`; its only red was the test-line ratchet (see Test budget below). The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

| Test file | Wall time, this PR | CI at `226e4cf40d0` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/wizard.test.ts` | 6.4 s, 23 tests | 0.26 s of tests, in an 18.5 s shard of 8 files |
| `src/wizard/session.test.ts` | 0.6 s, 35 tests | 0.65 s, 35 tests |

Wall time is the Vitest duration of `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` with a warm cache, at `75e9295e0f8`. Most of the wizard.test.ts time is transform; the tests themselves take 3% of it. CI is the Vitest duration, or for a file in a multi-file shard the sum of its test times, in the run at `226e4cf40d0` (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41116378481: `checks-node-changed-compact-large-26` and `checks-node-changed-3`). The PR adds one test to wizard.test.ts and two to session.test.ts. All three use fake timers and take a few milliseconds each.

Test budget: `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (and `ci-gate` with it) failed at `226e4cf40d0` on this PR's test-line growth (`Test lines: 6307565; ceiling: 6307449; over by: 116; net delta: +116`, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41116378481/job/124272291972). The new handler test now uses the file's existing helpers and keeps every assertion, which brings the growth down to 90 lines. `config/test-lines-allocations/setup-wizard-abandoned-expiry.txt` records those 90 lines, and the shared scalar is unchanged. The remaining lines are needed, because each of the three tests catches a different failure. The ratchet passes on a local merge of `75e9295e0f8` into main `7992b413a8b`, compared the way CI does.

The three new tests fail on the base `5ed4aa230f8` and pass here, and the other 55 tests in the two files pass on both: the handler-level test in `wizard.test.ts` (polling renews, idle expiry releases admission, a returning client gets `WIZARD_NOT_FOUND`), and two `WizardSession` tests (the window restarts when a waiting `wizard.next` receives its step, and expiry releases a session parked after its durable commit).

Not covered: no Control UI browser run. The live run used Gateway client calls that disconnect after each request, which is the same server path a closed tab takes. The classic setup flow (`flow: "setup"`) shares the same expiry code and is covered by the handler test, not by this live run.

prs.title: feat(plugin-sdk): expose bounded status projections from command-status
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #76759. Plugin authors building status integrations had no public types for the gateway `/status` payload: an external plugin (`lossless-claw#516`) guessed the session-row shape from formatted output and navigated fields that do not exist (`sessions.byAgent[].entries[].usage.*` instead of `sessions.byAgent[].recent[]`), so its number extraction returned `null` on every field. Without a public type, this drift recurs for every status-consuming plugin.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous revision re-exported the host `StatusSummary`/`SessionStatus`/`HeartbeatStatus` types verbatim. ClawSweeper's review correctly rejected that: `StatusSummary` is a mutable host aggregate with transitive gateway, channel, task, audit, plugin, and degraded-secret details, and freezing it into the public SDK would make evolving host-owned nested shapes an implicit compatibility commitment (the old test even had to cast `tasks`/`taskAudit` through `unknown` to compile).

This revision defines **bounded SDK-owned projections** in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status` instead — the smallest shape status-consuming plugins actually need:

- `StatusSessionRow` — one session row: identity (`agentId`, `key`, `sessionId`, `updatedAt`) plus token usage (`inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `totalTokens`, `remainingTokens`, `percentUsed`, `contextTokens`, `model`, `flags`).
- `StatusSessionsProjection` — the session portion of a `/status` payload (`count`, `recent[]`, `byAgent[]`).
- `StatusHeartbeat` — per-agent heartbeat schedule state.

Drift protection runs in the other direction now: `src/plugin-sdk/command-status.types.test.ts` compiles projection functions from the real host types (`SessionStatus → StatusSessionRow`, `StatusSummary["sessions"] → StatusSessionsProjection`, `HeartbeatStatus → StatusHeartbeat`), so renaming a projected field on the host side breaks the build loudly — with zero `unknown` casts. Host-only fields stay free to evolve.

## User Impact

Third-party plugins can `import type { StatusSessionRow, StatusSessionsProjection, StatusHeartbeat } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status"` and bind the exact session/heartbeat data the `/status` RPC exposes, without copying host internals or acquiring an implicit contract over unrelated host aggregates. Types only — no runtime surface, no startup cost.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/command-status.types.test.ts` — green; the test is a compile-time assignability contract from real host types plus behavioral assertions on projected values.
- Plugin SDK surface gate `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mts --check` — green with the `+3` budget entry ("SDK-owned command-status projection types for plugin status consumers").
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` — green (format, oxlint, tsgo core + test shards, `api-baseline` test 22/22, boundary guards).
- Real consumer proof against the built package (fresh `pnpm build` on this head `e06332c90de`): a standalone strict `nodenext` TypeScript project outside the repo resolving `openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status` binds all three projections and compiles with **exit 0**:

  ```ts
  import type { StatusHeartbeat, StatusSessionRow, StatusSessionsProjection } from "openclaw/plugin-sdk/command-status";
  export function summarizeStatus(sessions: StatusSessionsProjection): string {
    const rows: StatusSessionRow[] = sessions.recent;
    return `${sessions.count} sessions\n` + rows.map((r) => `${r.key}: ${r.totalTokens ?? "?"} tokens`).join("\n");
  }
  ```

  Runtime probe of the built subpath: `import("dist/plugin-sdk/command-status.js")` exposes exactly `buildCommandsMessage`, `buildCommandsMessagePaginated`, `buildHelpMessage` — the projections are type-only and correctly absent at runtime.
- Branch was rebased onto current `main` (post pnpm-12 bump) and squashed to one commit carrying the projection design.

prs.title: fix(e2e): stabilize Windows Parallels validation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native Windows Parallels validation can abort on harmless npm stderr or lost SDK command results. A prepared guest can also pass verification without the Visual C++ runtime needed by the ARM64 native addons.

## User Impact

Fresh-install and update validation recover from the observed harness failures while retaining real command failures and phase deadlines.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Scope PowerShell `Continue` to npm and retain the explicit exit-code check.
- Retry the known Parallels rc255 SDK error once for opted-in reads and idempotent temporary-script staging. Staging writes identical bytes to the same unique path before execution; mutating commands are not replayed.
- Install the architecture-matched Microsoft Visual C++ runtime through the existing hash-verified, signed installer path. Reject baselines missing `vcruntime140.dll`.

The change removes an extraction-sensitive curl-count assertion. The 123-line test allocation covers npm stderr handling, read/staging recovery and refusal boundaries, and baseline rejection.

## Evidence

- Real Windows PowerShell 5.1: the original npm-notice/exit-0 script fails; the fixed script succeeds; npm exit 23 still fails.
- Fresh OpenClaw 2026.10.6 install, onboarding, gateway RPC, and a real OpenAI agent turn passed.
- Source-built package installation passed. Import inspection identified missing `VCRUNTIME140.dll`; the exact ARM64 fs-safe binary failed before Microsoft runtime installation and loaded afterward. Both installed fs-safe and proc-safe native addons now load.
- Baseline rejection, read recovery, and staging recovery regressions were red before their fixes and green afterward. Persistent transport errors and real guest failures remain failures; recovered staging executes the command once.
- All 130 focused harness tests passed. The two Windows-only npm cases skip on macOS; their generated production scripts were executed directly on Windows.
- Scoped typecheck, lint, formatting, Bash syntax, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent source review and local autoreview found no actionable findings.
- Final fresh/update live validation and exact-head CI are running at `5ec9a0c4ec2eea33be9cd85610f09aed9d18ce1b`.

## Remaining Validation Limits

Earlier source runs timed out during gateway restart or stopped on Parallels transport errors before the updater. The historical 2026.10.6 updater also timed out before package installation. Neither is recorded as a passing update.

Latest published 2026.10.9 was not used as the historical baseline because it is younger than the repository npm release-age policy. Source-built candidates use reviewed local artifacts without overriding that policy.

prs.title: feat: link Discord accounts from personal profiles
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

People need to connect their own Discord account to their signed-in OpenClaw profile without asking an administrator to attest the link, and retain their existing session permissions when requesting work from Discord.

## User Impact

User impact: Settings → Profile gains Discord account linking, verified linked-ID status, and disconnect directly below Linked emails and above GitHub account. Linked members keep their actual allowed operator scopes in channel runs; linking does not grant administrator or command-owner privileges.

Deployment requires the selected Discord application's existing OAuth client configuration and the Gateway callback URL registered with Discord. Live Discord OAuth deployment qualification has not been performed; this PR does not change live configuration or credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

The flow reuses the personal-profile authorization boundary, provider-browser callback owner, and canonical channel-identity store. Discord proves the immutable user ID with the `identify` scope; short-lived one-use state and an initiating-browser cookie bind the callback. The initiating profile, connection, scopes, plugin and account configuration are checked again before storing the link. Tokens are not persisted. Conflicting links are rejected, and administrative attestation endpoints remain administrator-only.

Channel run authority now derives independently from verified profile permissions rather than command-owner status, while retaining the existing access-grant, revocation and queued-recovery checks.

Requested by Vito. Co-authors recorded on the implementation commit: VACInc, obviyus, and hannesrudolph.

## Evidence

- Exact-head CI: [run 41163941917](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41163941917), attempt 1, completed successfully on `574e89cd9ae7b29b2f6614f284f775d0492b7656` (84 jobs passed, 23 skipped, no failures). The `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency-review and security-sensitive-review gates were independently verified successful on this head.
- Exact-head review: [ClawSweeper revision 2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188910#issuecomment-6537464725), completed October 31 at 04:14 UTC, reviewed `574e89cd9ae7b29b2f6614f284f775d0492b7656` against main `510e1687e965c1a5e2c372f6622704c88448fb5b`. It reports no findings, no before-merge items, no security concerns, sufficient proof, and readiness for maintainer review. This is review evidence, not merge authorization or a claim of live Discord qualification.
- Conflict integration: `adb5b7543405f13` incorporates main `d07273d4e319836cd461f65b02009e94418afb85` because the previous published head could not form a merge ref. The only conflict was the equivalent Cron Paused expectation; both Settings sidebar fixes are preserved. On the reconciled candidate, all 26 sidebar unit tests and 13 affected browser cases passed, along with scoped lint, UI types, formatting and whitespace checks.
- [CI run 41161841737](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41161841737) on `45978e2a33561a10e6321b1fd0afc14c932a011d` found a stale owner-selection expectation after adding the queued-recovery test. The exact missing-consumer failure reproduced locally; the one-line inventory correction in `232f91cd9345b4e` preserves strict selection assertions. All 54 owner-selection tests pass, with targeted types, lint and format checks. The same CI run also reported a synthetic Claude CLI child exiting before PATCH in the scheduled-message integration suite; all 9 scenarios passed the maintained failed-tests replay, including that 429 case. Its cause remains unproven and no fix is claimed.
- Registered Gateway RPC/callback suite: 7 passed using the real bundled Discord adapter and guarded HTTP transport against isolated loopback OAuth endpoints, followed by canonical SQLite writes. Covers wrong-browser rejection, replay, cross-profile conflicts, disconnect, and revocation before/during exchange. This is deterministic integration proof, not live Discord OAuth qualification.
- Real channel-tool regression: linked Discord member and Slack administrator both pass. The member can create work, cannot perform administrator operations or bypass shared-session participation, and cannot create a session after unlinking; canonical records remain unchanged.
- New queued-recovery proof: 2 passed. Persisted queue JSON and canonical SQLite close/reopen feed actual recovery and a harness-bound file-write tool. An allowed write succeeds; unlinking or reassignment after admission prevents the pending write and rejects stale recovery. File bytes and write count remain unchanged. Existing recovery suite: 40 passed, including the administrator close/reopen control.
- Red-on-base: the same two member cases fail on exact base `154cb5b28584507ab5897478bc3e3a478b02d438` because verified member authority is absent; the existing administrator close/reopen control passes. Local autoreview (Codex, P0–P3) found no actionable issues in the test-only delta from `32adf03cd60a98a506b8489fa51bf8a96bdace68` committed as `9f9a6a7b7e01a733bf7dceafda0496959af1b5ad`; this is not a fresh review of the entire branch. Targeted gateway types, lint, formatting, whitespace and staged test-line budget pass.
- Earlier CI repair proof retained: controlled browser tests were red before the query-reactivity and intentional Cron Paused-label repairs. Control UI types and selected plugin-sdk/gateway-methods graphs passed. The unchanged frame-budget suite passed targeted replay and prior-head CI; its earlier failure's cause remains unproven and no source fix is claimed.

### ClawSweeper review dispositions

These address all five items from the earlier review of `bb8844c`. The [completed revision 2 review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188910#issuecomment-6537464725) confirms the previous finding is resolved, accepts the supplied authority and compatibility proof, and identifies no new actionable defect.

1. **Real behavior proof:** [registered RPC/real-adapter tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9f9a6a7b7e01a733bf7dceafda0496959af1b5ad/src/gateway/server-methods/users-channel-identity.test.ts), [actual channel-tool effects](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9f9a6a7b7e01a733bf7dceafda0496959af1b5ad/src/channels/message-access/operator-authority.test.ts#L761), and [persisted queued final-I/O tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9f9a6a7b7e01a733bf7dceafda0496959af1b5ad/src/gateway/operator-run-recovery.channel.test.ts) cover the previously missing chain.
2. **P3 administrator negative control:** the valid `profileId` request now asserts `missing scope: operator.admin` and unchanged canonical identities. The incidental adapter authority-call-count assertion was removed.
3. **Security attention:** the review found no concrete bypass; its identified qualification gap is covered by allowed member effects, denied administrative/participation effects, callback revocation and the queued final-I/O controls above. No permission gate was weakened to make tests pass.
4. **Merge risk:** the queued tests revoke or reassign the canonical Discord identity while the real write is paused after admission. Resuming produces an inactive-authority rejection, no second file write, unchanged bytes, and refusal to recover the stale queue source. Reassignment to an administrator does not transfer authority to the queued member.
5. **Existing-data compatibility:** this PR changes no `src/state` storage implementation, persisted identity schema, queue-source shape/codec, configuration schema or migration relative to its base. Existing administrator identity and queued authority still recover after disk close/reopen on both the base and changed code; new member recovery uses the same unchanged persisted format. A full deployment upgrade from latest stable `v2026.10.9` was not run and is not claimed. There is no PR-specific storage migration to qualify; the bounded compatibility check instead exercises the changed consumer with existing-format persisted data.

The generated predicate diff is mechanical output from the repository's Gateway validator generator. The additional queued proof changes tests and their required database-worker lane registration only. Existing built-UI screenshots cover placement, linked/disconnected states and recoverable errors; no live configuration or credentials were changed.

## UI evidence

Real built Control UI; synthetic profile and mocked Gateway/Discord consent. Light theme, 1280 × 900 viewport, identity section cropped. Before: base `f8fe5864ab3a`; after: published implementation `7a6d1fd2925f`. This is deterministic UI proof, not live Discord OAuth qualification.

### Before

![Profile identity before Discord linking](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d8b13895-467d-4aea-8d12-75f96681596c)

### After

![Verified Discord identity and disconnect below Linked emails](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/eb85b8e6-a84e-4ba7-a360-18956bb3e3c7)

<details>
<summary>Disconnected and recoverable-error states</summary>

![Disconnected Discord identity](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d2b4cf01-3279-4ac1-a338-ba2cb30aa03d)

![Discord sign-in error with retry](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da99f144-b968-4d50-93ef-0939fb8dcfb0)

</details>

## Worked on by

- @obviyus
- @VACInc
- @hannesrudolph

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/3cba598f-a230-4270-97ac-8690b7b8f441)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/4f824400-bea7-455c-bf29-d897fab27825)

prs.title: fix(cron): keep admitted runs active during first-use audit setup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes admitted cron runs failing with “Session event agent is being deleted” when the first execution-identity audit binding initializes its optional table, even though no agent was deleted.

## User Impact

Scheduled turns remain admitted while unrelated first-use features initialize. Actual deletion still revokes only the affected agent; rollback, unknown-status refusal, terminal database failures, and explicit retirement retain their existing checks. No configuration, schema, or migration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deletion status is a journal-owned row fact, but it was classified as dependent on the shared database schema revision. First-use audit DDL therefore invalidated every agent's prepared status. The asynchronous reload for the current cron agent could not protect other agents or overlapping runs. Keep the row fact under journal-writer ownership and remove that caller-side reload: net **−6 production lines**.

## Evidence

The existing cron execution-identity regression fails on the original owner when audit is enabled: a different agent's prepared deletion check returns true. Disabled/default controls pass. All three modes pass with this fix, alongside lifecycle isolation/retirement and session-event handoff coverage: **44 focused tests**. The 12 added regression lines extend existing fixtures and have a dedicated test-line allocation.

Independent Codex autoreview of the complete local change and owning-source evidence: **scoped-clean, P0–P2**, no actionable findings. Synthetic first-use audit setup falsely blocks **4/4 prepared agents before, 0/4 after**. Five paired measurements (250,000 full guards/sample), with five A/A controls:

| Median owner metric | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ordinary CPU | 24.589 ms | 22.531 ms |
| Snapshot CPU | 34.867 ms | 32.433 ms |
| Snapshot sampled allocation | 14,157,976 B | 13,914,856 B |
| First-use CPU | 1.357 ms | 1.313 ms |
| First-use sampled allocation | 526,504 B | 480,752 B |

One contention sample worsened snapshot wall maximum/p95 (n=5): 36.540→124.474 ms. A/A snapshot CPU ranged 32.512–46.542 ms; the outlier used 44.707 ms CPU. A bounded two-pair comparison with two A/A controls and two million checks/sample found snapshot CPU 270.286→268.454 ms and wall maximum 273.109→317.648 ms. First-use timing moved in opposite directions between runs. These results establish the correctness gain and no repeatable warm overhead regression, not a speedup or a user-facing tail-latency guarantee. Ordinary allocation was below meaningful sampling resolution.

Reproduce with the existing `team-shape-fixture.ts` and extended `agent-deletion-blocked-measure.ts --prepared --first-use-audit --iterations 250000 --warmup 100000 --samples 1`. Baseline uses frozen original lifecycle/status modules via `--owner`, `--status-owner`, and `--expected-blocked 4`. Acceptance was recorded before measurement: zero false revocations after first-use DDL, preserved warm guards, and no repeatable CPU/allocation regression. Tooling grows by 67 lines.

`pnpm check:changed` completed: typechecks, lint, format, database and other guards passed; only the dead-export scan reported untouched baseline exports. The exact same six production findings and one full-tree finding reproduce on unchanged baseline `ece4ca85af0e`; the reviewed candidate was restored byte-for-byte. No failed gate was hidden or skipped.

The synthetic workload has 10,800 sessions, 4,300 settled runs and 62,000 workspace files (1.18 GB). Its agent database is approximately 475 MB; this is owner-boundary proof, not a 35 GiB database, btrfs, whole-Gateway, or live-model benchmark. The production journal does not record DDL, so the exact production first-use table remains inferred; the defective invalidation path is reproduced.

prs.title: test(ui): separate engine action and settle timings
prs.body:
Related: #188991

## What Problem This Solves

A WebKit census grouped unrelated actions around 255–266 ms. The engine harness exposed total automation wall time and a consecutive-frame interval, which could not distinguish driver/selector work, application work, and the final two-frame wait.

## User Impact

Developers can distinguish benchmark action time from the final frame wait. There is no user-visible application change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record `scenarioMs` and `settleWaitMs` alongside the unchanged `wallMs`, and summarize both phases. Traced, document-retaining actions also export native input and run-boundary User Timing marks. Boot/reload retain their existing navigation probes; their document replacement would discard a start mark. Hash the action and navigation scenario sources in the run manifest so timing changes can be attributed to the exact workload. Document the fields and their limits.

This changes benchmark diagnostics only. It does not change application scheduling, action assertions, input cadence, the final frame wait, or startup assets. The new fields do not claim input-to-paint latency or a product performance improvement.

## Investigation

The three representative WebKit traces do not contain a shared 250 ms timer. Cron schedules a zero-delay response; the picker has no installed timer; Settings schedules optional 500 ms idle work. Their gaps occur in different phases: Cron's native input arrives well into locator/focus delivery, whereas Settings receives its shortcut immediately and then renders. Bare native controls complete WebKit fills in about 8–11 ms and shortcuts in about 5 ms. The same unchanged application bundle produced warm mobile Settings samples of 180–195 ms, below the historical 259 ms cluster.

Completed 880/880 observations with zero failures: all 22 rows have 20 Chromium and 20 WebKit samples, with 10 observations per identical A/A slot. Phase accounting is valid in every observation. 14/22 refreshed rows remain above the 1.3× ratio target; no product latency optimization is claimed. Final-wait medians span 18.7–33.5 ms; WebKit settle-frame medians span 10.0–17.5 ms. Host one-minute load ranged 19.60–49.88. Wall time from first proof artifact: 41.2 minutes. Historical-to-current differences are observational: the historical census and this run differ in time/host state, and the UI already contains the separately landed model-search optimization. Both current slots serve identical bytes; these numbers do not establish a source A/B speedup. No speculative scheduler replacement or budget change is included.

## Evidence

| --- | --- |
| `pnpm tsgo:scripts` | Pass |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Pass |
| Scoped script lint, formatter, `git diff --check` | Pass |
| `pnpm ui:build` and strict `pnpm ui:check-performance` | Pass; startup 88,766 B gzip, one CSS request |
| Representative WebKit Timeline/native-mark traces | Cron search, Settings open, model-picker open/search passed |
| Untraced reproduction | 18/18 observations, Chromium + WebKit |
| Bare native input control | 100/100 observations, desktop + mobile, both engines |
| Corrected trace phase boundary | Settings: scenario 160.8 ms + final wait 29.1 ms = wall 189.9 ms |
| Full cluster rerun | 880/880 passed; 22 rows, 20 observations per engine per row; all phase sums valid |
| PR CI / native landing | Passed; merged exact reviewed head as `a78dc179ff413203923889dc5392a937f018060d` |

The UI source is unchanged; both census slots serve the same built bytes. No visual appearance change or new UI export is involved. The existing behavioral scenarios remain the proof rather than adding implementation-mirroring tests.

Independent Codex autoreview at P0–P2 found two diagnostic issues, both corrected: traced marker overhead belonged in the scenario phase, and marks cannot span document replacement. Final independent review of the complete change against `2919a0dba8d8` is scoped-clean at P0–P2.

LOC: harness 844 → 887; guide 781 → 788 (+53/−3 total). The growth is diagnostic fields/marks, source receipts, and their documentation; no new runtime abstraction.

## Refreshed cluster table

All timings are milliseconds (median/p95). “Census” is the earlier census; “Current” is the fresh A/A run. A/A columns are the median difference between the two identical build slots, not treatment effects. Where A/A moves beyond the acceptance band, the row remains noisy observational evidence; no performance gain is claimed.

prs.title: improve(ui): speed up Board tab navigation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large Board tab switches still spend work on unchanged card state and on document-wide appearance refresh. This revision keeps equal rectangle and session identities, uses explicit per-card bindings, stabilizes each provider's bound frame-URL callback, and keeps nonappearance preference updates out of theme application. Lightweight report shells remain eager; Menu reuses its machine’s accepted visibility notification instead of allocating a second per-menu projection and subscription; heavy report content still follows the existing visibility admission and retention owner.

**Round 4 performance qualification is running on `89c8c5517ae`. Do not land until navigation and scroll both qualify.** The previous revision improved navigation but regressed scroll scripting. That head is superseded. The revised desktop-scroll cohort has 20 counterbalanced A/A triplets: script CPU median 13.102 → 12.515 ms (−4.48%), p95 18.548 → 17.223 ms (−7.14%). Rendering/wall tails still need qualification, so no all-metrics claim is made. The 200 ms task target remains unmet; no performance floor is claimed.

## Evidence

Acceptance uses the existing 1,000-widget fixture (250 per tab), frozen current-main and candidate production bundles, serial base/head/base A/A controls, Chromium 4× desktop/mobile and WebKit desktop/mobile. Twenty Chromium pairs and ten WebKit pairs cover first render, switch, return and scroll. Every user-facing metric must hold or improve; an attributable regression blocks landing.

The residual investigation uses separate 100 µs source-mapped Chromium traces, temporary root/memo/bridge markers and a no-opt diagnostic. It found document appearance publication, redundant card bindings and native intersection/rendering work; the old residual was not pure Solid propagation. Temporary instrumentation is removed. Sorted profiler timestamps and exclusive rendering-phase accounting prevent double counting. Final before/after owner tables will replace this section after the measured run.

No dependency, cache, virtualizer, idle queue, or new lifecycle owner is added. Reports and traces remain uncommitted on the external disk. Final screenshots, LOC counts and full measured proof will be added before readiness.

prs.title: fix(codex): include relay conversation instructions in trajectory
prs.body:
Closes #188929

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing conversation instructions in the host trajectory when a managed Codex turn receives them through the inference relay.

## User Impact

Operators can inspect the current conversation guidance and callable-tool bindings alongside the other OpenClaw-managed instructions already recorded in `context.compiled`. This changes the diagnostic projection, not the instructions supplied to the model or native conversation history. Existing trajectory enablement and size limits still apply; previously stored records are not backfilled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The relay registration already assembled the instruction text, but the diagnostic renderer separately reconstructed only part of it. This change reuses the exact successfully registered relay text, combined with the thread-only developer policy. That includes the missing conversation block and avoids duplicating plugin hook context.

Conversation instructions here mean metadata interpretation, delivery/conduct guidance, activation and tool bindings - not conversation history. The combined view remains for observability and must not feed native thread requests. It is not a complete native/provider prompt dump.

## Evidence

### Retained live incident

A read-only extraction from the affected Gateway's real SQLite trajectory, recorded at `2026-10-31T00:28:17.959Z`, found a complete 25,716-character `systemPrompt` and 47 tool definitions:

```text
AGENT_SOUL                                 present
OpenClaw Skills                            present
Basic Memory                               present
Current OpenClaw conversation instructions  absent
openclaw.inbound_meta                       absent
Current OpenClaw tool bindings              absent
Be a good group participant                absent
```

This is a nontruncated instruction record, not a search over user quotations or native rollout text. The affected build was `5f6f15fed0d6`, with an unrelated local message-delivery patch disclosed in the issue. It is historical production evidence, not a controlled same-base live A/B run.

### Fixed-build live run

At `84e2d254916`, an isolated Gateway using bundled native Codex 0.164.0 completed two real model turns after a supported runtime build. The synthetic persona changed between turns; the replies were `RELAY-PERSONA-ONE` and `RELAY-PERSONA-TWO`, on the same native parent thread.

For both turns:

- SQLite retained a complete 14,129-character `context.compiled.systemPrompt`.
- The 8,302-character relay suffix had matching SHA-256 hashes in the outgoing WSS `send` body and SQLite projection.
- Conversation header, tool bindings, current persona and skill markers appeared exactly once. The old persona marker was absent after refresh.
- Native request `developerInstructions` and persisted native developer messages contained zero conversation-header, tool-binding or persona-marker copies.

All 186 stamped Codex plugin outputs matched their build provenance. The disposable fixture was cleaned up; production was untouched.

**Live-proof limit:** these were ordinary Gateway `agent` requests, without additional annotated channel instructions. They exercise the conversation wrapper, actual bindings and persona refresh, not a live Discord group/direct transition or plugin-hook scenario. Those richer cases are integration-test evidence below. The transport observer records the outgoing application boundary, not a server-side packet capture.

The attachment contains captured observations, hashes and reproduction instructions. Its reduced/formatted reproducer is explicitly distinguished from the executed source; successful live turns were not repeated for publication cleanup. Two preliminary fixture-only setup corrections are disclosed in the live-proof README.

### Focused regression coverage

The baseline regression reached actual relay preparation, then failed because the persisted trajectory lacked the conversation instructions. The fixed regression uses the production relay preparation and SQLite recorder to verify successive group/direct/removed instruction blocks, changed bindings, once-only sections, current-text parity and exclusion from native thread requests. Native RPCs/model completion are synthetic in this regression, separate from the live run above.

Implementation-time checks passed: 54 distinct focused tests across seven files, focused source/test typecheck, type-aware lint, formatting and the test-line ratchet. Selected log excerpts retain the baseline failure and explicit skipped-test count. These checks were not rerun for the final comment-only commit.

The accompanying 
[openclaw-188929-evidence.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34209192/openclaw-188929-evidence.zip)
 contains sanitized captured output, reproduction instructions and sources, and the retained baseline marker extractor. No production prompts, credentials or private model identifiers are included.

Related: #109436

Replaces #182511, which was auto-closed by the PR cap.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a long session overflows a small local fallback window after failover from a large-context primary.

## User Impact

User impact: they can use a llmman hybrid pair as the fallback instead.

## Why This Change Was Made

One paragraph and snippet in the existing hybrid section, plus a pointer from local-models. No new code. This is a workaround pointer, not a fix for #109436.

## Evidence

llmman 0.1.587, Qwen3.5 0.8B, OpenClaw `main` at 6ac91adabcc, `agent --local`, primary unreachable, `LLMMAN_CONTEXT_LENGTH=32768`, 125 kB prompt.

- Plain local fallback: `context_overflow`, run failed.
- Pair with `contextWindow` 131072: llmman routed the 196 kB request to the hosted half and the run succeeded.

The hosted half was a local mock, so a real hosted provider was not exercised. `format:docs:check`, `docs:check-mdx`, `lint:docs`, `docs:check-config-examples` and `git diff --check` pass. `docs:check-links` and `docs:check-links:anchors` fail only on entries in untouched files (ClawHub routes, same on `main`). `autoreview` is not installed here, so it was not run.
