prs.title: feat: preview Control UI themes before applying them
prs.body:
Related: #151479 (reuse of shared radio/option-card controls; this does not complete the consolidation tracker).

## What Problem This Solves

Choosing a Control UI theme needs a compact, keyboard-friendly way to try it across the window before saving, including matching colors in the embedded terminal.

## User Impact

Users can hover, focus, or tap a theme to preview the current window; Apply theme or Enter saves it, while Cancel, Escape, or leaving Appearance restores the current selection. Other windows and saved preferences are unchanged during preview. All 11 built-in names/IDs are preserved, with palette descriptions and Beacon identified as the high-contrast option.

Arrow keys browse, Home/End jump, and Space previews without saving. The visible keyboard guide is scoped to the picker, not text fields. Plugin and personal palettes use the existing catalog, including cancellation when a previewed plugin disappears.

Themes may optionally author 16 ANSI colors. Existing terminals and scrollback repaint without restarting the shell; explicit true-color output remains application-owned. No database migration or operator configuration change is required. The approved temporary ghostty-web 0.4.0 repair includes rebuilt embedded WASM and generated ESM/CJS/declarations, with pinned sources, hashes, rebuild instructions, and removal gates in patches/README.md and the packaged source patches.

This is Omarchy-inspired groundwork, not an official collaboration or an installed Catppuccin/Tokyo Night theme pack. New wallpapers, continuous animation, and external CLI theming are outside this PR.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing application theme owner now holds transient preview state separately from canonical preferences and rejects stale palette completion after cancellation. The picker reuses shared native radio navigation instead of adding a second keyboard model; the real window is the preview surface rather than a floating miniature. Preview and commit share the font/accent reset policy.

The terminal updates native color defaults directly rather than injecting OSC into the PTY parser, preserving split escape sequences and active-theme reset baselines. The canvas also paints literal-black cell backgrounds correctly. Existing clipboard-success and disposal repairs remain intact. Most patch bytes are reproducibly generated dependency output, not a second terminal implementation.

## Evidence

- Real Control UI browser flow: window preview, all scoped navigation keys, explicit Apply/Enter, Escape/Cancel/route exit, no writes before Apply, a second window retaining its selection, touch, plugin preview/withdrawal, and saved-profile persistence.
- Chromium Appearance consumer suite: 20 tests. Focused keyboard/preview consumer also passed in WebKit. Focused owner/preference/configuration suites: 169 tests, including late palette completion and Gateway-scope retirement. Contrast matrix retains AA, with Beacon AAA for the sampled text pairs.
- Full terminal browser suite: 6 cases, including cold authored palettes, live reload/fallback, clipboard outcomes, input, memory isolation, and disposal. Native regressions cover all 16 colors, scrollback, explicit RGB, cursor preservation, fragmented CSI/OSC, and reset defaults.
- The literal-black canvas regression was red before the renderer repair and green afterward: SGR 40 paints [0,0,0], while untouched default background remains [30,30,46]. A fresh-store frozen install reproduced both generated runtime formats and the native WASM hash.
- UI production typecheck, scoped lint/style/format, docs MDX, and i18n verification passed. Independent P0-P2 review is scoped-clean after resolving the black-background finding. PR CI provides the broad suite; no remote CI or whole-repository typecheck success is claimed.

- After GitHub reported an actual conflict, integrated main at `c64eaf54ad0b609a114d580e29135acd93433bfd`. Kept the new canonical Settings preference owner rather than restoring duplicate bindings. On that exact base, all 9 browser cases, affected Settings/preview owner regressions, UI production typecheck, scoped lint/format, and fresh P0-P2 review passed. The integrated After capture is byte-identical to the image below. Earlier unchanged-contract proof is retained, not relabeled as remote CI.

- Hosted-review follow-up: completed the remaining browser-only `ApplicationTheme` fixture and corrected the radio test callback's return contract. The UI-components test typecheck leaf now passes, along with that browser test and all 5 shared-radio tests. These follow-up edits are test-only; production behavior and the inspected images are unchanged.

Existing persisted preference and theme-definition shapes are unchanged, and ANSI tokens are optional. A full v2026.10.6-to-candidate upgrade run was not performed; it remains an explicit qualification gap rather than a claimed pass.

The earlier editor/test type graph (before base integration) reported errors in untouched native-desktop, quota-reset, and regexp declaration inputs. That broad graph was not rerun or claimed fixed; this is not a clean full-project gate run. No live Gateway was modified or deployed. Browser evidence uses synthetic Gateway fixtures.

### Visual walkthrough

**Revision provenance for every Before/After comparison below:**

- **Before = main at [d75915ee88343c26565b6855fde235525d112ba3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d75915ee88343c26565b6855fde235525d112ba3)**, fetched into an isolated, clean checkout for this recapture.
- **After = pushed PR head [da36d69fe3933fe1675201b26622972a7327b066](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/da36d69fe3933fe1675201b26622972a7327b066)**. The capture checkout's Git tree exactly matches the published commit tree (777b6ea8a27dab54d4656a994a92fe40f70177fc); it contains no unpublished product changes.

Both revisions ran the same scenario script and synthetic Gateway fixtures with matching viewport, locale, color scheme, and reduced-motion settings. Each used its own dependency installation and lockfile. These are real rendered Control UI captures, not design mockups or previous design iterations. Fixture footer version/build strings are synthetic; the source revisions above identify the code being compared. No code was pushed for this description/evidence update.

**How to read the picker:** the checkmark identifies the saved theme; the highlighted/focused radio identifies the preview target. “Previewing … — not saved” is an unsaved window-local state. “Current: …” and disabled Apply/Cancel mean there is no pending theme choice.

#### Main versus PR: hover Tide while Claw is saved

Identical action on both revisions: open Appearance with Claw selected, then hover Tide. Both use a 1440 × 1200 viewport.

**Before — main d75915ee: hover/tooltip only; the window stays Claw**

![Before on current-main snapshot d75915ee: hovering Tide leaves the window in Claw](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f2e11f8-783a-498c-880c-bfc786c8bffc)

**After — pushed PR da36d69: the whole window previews Tide, with Claw still saved**

![After on pushed PR da36d69: hovering Tide previews the whole window without saving](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/efeee2cf-26ea-48d6-b44d-74f88b96d688)

| Same action | Main d75915ee | Pushed PR da36d69 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hover Tide | Window remains Claw; 0 theme-selection requests | Window previews Tide; 0 theme-selection requests |
| Click Tide | Window changes to Tide and sends 1 theme-selection request | Window previews Tide but sends 0 theme-selection requests |
| Separate commit step | None: selecting the theme commits it | Apply/Enter commits the preview; Cancel/Escape restores the saved theme |

The comparison scenarios asserted these rendered states and request counts on both revisions. The PR preview includes typography as well as colors, so surrounding copy can rewrap; the captures do not normalize away that layout change.

#### PR-only state and persistence walkthrough

The following gallery and state sequence are **all from pushed PR head da36d69**. They illustrate individual PR interaction states, not additional main-versus-PR comparisons. This separate PR-state capture checked the rendered window, browser preference mirror, and outgoing **themes.set** requests:

| Action | Window displays | Saved theme | Theme-selection writes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Start | Claw | Claw | 0 |
| Hover/focus Tide | Tide, unsaved | Claw | 0 |
| Escape | Claw restored; focus retained | Claw | 0 |
| Preview Tide again, then Apply | Tide, current | Tide | 1 |
| End from the picker | Miami, unsaved | Tide | still 1 |
| Escape from that keyboard preview | Tide restored | Tide | still 1 |
| Tap Tide in a fresh mobile scenario | Tide, unsaved | Claw | 0 |

Cancel and leaving Appearance use the same saved-selection restoration path. Applying uses the existing preference owner; it does not create a separate theme engine. Other browser windows do not inherit the transient preview.

**Important scope distinction:** Light/Dark/System retain their existing immediate preference behavior; the new Apply button stages the **theme choice**, not every Appearance setting. The light-mode image below is after explicitly choosing Light, not a claim that Cancel rolls color mode back.

**Observed interaction edge for review (not fixed by this metadata-only update):** after Escape, leaving and returning to the exact previous pointer coordinates can leave the saved theme visible until another in-card movement, focus change, or click. The capture reproduced this, then explicitly clicked Tide to continue. It is not presented as repaired behavior.

<details>
<summary>PR-only gallery: saved, Cancel/Escape, and applied states</summary>

**New picker at rest — Claw saved, no pending choice**

![New picker at rest with Current Claw and Apply/Cancel disabled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d6a58fa5-acfd-44fc-97a9-44ca1a691949)

**Escape state on the PR — Claw restored, Tide still has keyboard focus**

The focus outline is not a saved-selection indicator. The Claw checkmark and “Current: Claw” remain authoritative; no theme-selection write occurred.

![Escape restores Claw while retaining focus on Tide](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c23b668-56ef-4534-bbef-9b9bd08b46c5)

**Applied state on the PR — saved checkmark moves to Tide**

“Current: Tide” replaces the unsaved-preview status. Apply/Cancel are disabled again. The capture observed one theme-selection request and the saved mirror changed to Tide.

![Applied Tide with saved checkmark and Current Tide status](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b8d31de4-37f6-4de2-98b2-cbb7f9950554)

</details>

<details>
<summary>PR-only gallery: keyboard navigation, light mode, and touch layout</summary>

**Keyboard — End previews Miami while Tide stays saved**

The actual window and typography change, the Miami focus/preview target is visible, and the saved checkmark remains on Tide. The same run exercised Home, ArrowRight, and Escape and verified no additional theme-selection request.

![Keyboard End previews Miami while saved selection remains Tide](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d17a31d-f249-42e5-b1db-5273a3d37d00)

| Key, with focus in the picker | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Arrow keys | Move through choices and preview |
| Home / End | First / last choice |
| Space | Preview without saving |
| Enter | Apply the focused choice |
| Escape | Restore the saved theme, retaining focus |
| Tab | Normal navigation into/out of the native radio group and actions |

These bindings do not intercept the import URL field or other text inputs; that boundary is exercised by the browser flow.

**Light mode — applied Tide, with real light palette swatches**

![Applied Tide in Light mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/168e1254-8cbf-483a-9df6-98c6daf51bd7)

**Touch — 390-pixel viewport, Tide preview with Claw still saved**

The choices form two columns and actions wrap below the status. One tap previews; Apply is still explicit. This is the actual responsive layout, including the keyboard hint that remains visible on mobile.

![Mobile Tide preview with Claw saved and explicit Apply and Cancel buttons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/69aee76a-e415-46a8-855f-f84ff9b8d89e)

</details>

#### Main versus PR: identical authored ANSI fixture

These are **two revision-specific captures**, not one PR implementation with its palette toggled. Both revisions received the same synthetic desired palette and the same four-row terminal output, in a 1280 × 900 viewport. The images crop the same header/output region without altering pixels.

**Before — main d75915ee: terminal retains its fallback indexed colors**

![Before on main d75915ee: identical ANSI fixture renders fallback indexed colors](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f83fae33-995b-4d93-866e-2e4196586c4c)

**After — pushed PR da36d69: terminal uses the authored ANSI colors**

![After on pushed PR da36d69: identical ANSI fixture renders the authored palette](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2f15d45b-55f8-44dc-87bc-fe9d9b59e5ed)

The sampled red background was RGB (255,107,107) on main and the authored RGB (243,139,168) on the PR. The synthetic UI fixture supplies the desired optional ANSI fields to both clients; it is not a claim that main's server accepts the new theme-import fields. Import/schema acceptance is tested separately.

Live-update behavior is also tested separately on the PR: the existing canvas/session is retained, terminal.open is called once, removing authored tokens restores defaults, and palette changes emit no terminal.input. Native checks cover all 16 indices, scrollback, explicit-RGB preservation, fragmented escape sequences, and reset baselines. The pictures above compare main with the pushed PR; they do not substitute two states of the same revision for a Before/After comparison.

Concept, UX direction, and feature request: Chris Eckert (@ceckert).

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/5c6bc88f-6d89-40f8-9bad-41b563880ac3)

## Worked on by

- @ceckert

prs.body:
## Summary
Revives #161383 (auto-closed for inactivity), re-applied on current `main`. The issue is still present on main.

- `transcripts list` counts only authorized rows, so a caller denied every capture never reaches the stop condition and pages through the whole store.
- Bound the walk to 20 pages of 200, and mark a truncated empty result so it isn't read as an empty store.
- Adapted to main's `listReadEntries` `{ entries, hasMore }` page shape.

Fixes #161327
Supersedes #161383

## Test plan
- [x] `vitest run src/agents/tools/transcripts-tool-read.test.ts`: 8 passed, including the denied-list page ceiling (the new test fails without the fix)
- [x] `oxlint` / `oxfmt --check` on changed files

prs.title: fix: configure, classic onboarding and agents add save new channel tokens as plaintext in openclaw.json
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/175333

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a channel token entered in `openclaw configure`, classic onboarding (and the Gateway's default `wizard.start` flow, which runs the same setup), `openclaw agents add` or the chat's channel setup in Control UI is saved as plaintext in `openclaw.json`. The same token entered through `openclaw channels add` goes to the protected secret store since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169732. Doctor then warns about plaintext secret-bearing fields, and the prompt's plaintext option says "Stores the credential directly in OpenClaw config".

## User Impact

User impact: a new or changed channel credential entered through any of these setup paths is saved as a protected entry in the shared secret store, and `openclaw.json` keeps a `store` SecretRef, as with `openclaw channels add`. The plaintext entry option now reads "Saves the credential in the protected secret store". Existing config is not rewritten: only credentials that differ from the config the setup started from are moved, so plaintext tokens, SecretRefs and env references saved by earlier releases stay as they are.

`--secret-input-mode plaintext` (the onboarding default) still means typing the value in. Channel credentials entered that way now go to the store as well, as they already do in `channels add`.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169732 put the protected-store step inside `persistChannelPluginConfig`, the save path of `channels add` and the Gateway's channels wizard. The other setup paths run the same `setupChannels` prompts but commit config through their own writers, so they never reached it.

What changes:
- The store loop moves unchanged out of `persistChannelPluginConfig` into `storeChannelSetupCredentials` in the same module. `persistChannelPluginConfig` calls it as before, so `channels add` keeps its retained-entry notice and its authority checks.
- `configure`, onboarding, `agents add` and `runHostedChannelSetup` call it at their config commit point, comparing against the config the channel step started from. The hosted chat setup passes its existing `beforePersistentApply` and live-owner assertion, so a stale chat session still cannot write.
- The Gateway's `wizard.start` setup flow passes the wizard session's cancellation lock and liveness check into that store write, as its channels flow already does: if the client cancels after the token prompt and before the store write, the write throws and nothing is saved; once the write has begun, cancellation is refused until the next prompt. Because setup keeps prompting after the channel step, it takes that preparation lock rather than the permanent one. A setup session cannot be replaced mid-flow: setup admission rejects a second setup session as busy.
- `wizard.ts` composes that liveness check with the `assertCurrent` callback `startGatewayWizard` gives the session. Since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183777, that callback checks the starting operator's retained grant, so a revoked device, a lost operator scope or a rotated shared credential now fails the check. Both `wizard.start` flows use it, so this also closes the same window in the existing channels flow.
- The check runs at the store writer's admission and inside the config writer's `assertBeforePublish`, the synchronous hook `config.patch` uses. Before, both flows checked once before awaiting the config commit, and an isolated Gateway showed the commit publishing after a device removal while it waited on locks. A store write already admitted settles; its entry then stays unreferenced (see the first accepted limit).
- The Control UI chat follows the same rule. `ChatWizardHost.forTurn` binds each queued chat turn to its Gateway request's `hasCurrentClientAuthority`, and the host's persistent-effect check, already used at the hosted store write, now also fails once that authority is gone. `runHostedSetup` runs the channel setup's check in the same `assertBeforePublish` hook. CLI chat has no request scope and passes no authority, as before.
- The plaintext option's hint and `docs/start/wizard-cli-reference.md` describe where the credential goes.

The store step runs where each path commits config, not inside `setupChannels`: a later prompt, a cancel or a failed check before the commit then leaves no store entries behind.

Accepted limits:
- If the config write fails after the store write (including a requester whose authority ends between the two), `configure`, onboarding, `agents add`, the Gateway setup flow and the hosted chat leave unreferenced store entries without the "retained" notice that `channels add` prints. The entries are unused and the config keeps its previous value; a retry stores the credential under a new name.
- Like `channels add`, the store step covers credential paths registered as channel secret-input targets. A plugin credential outside that registry is still saved as entered, under the same option hint.
- While the store write holds the preparation lock, `wizard.cancel` is refused and returns `status: "running"`; the cancel is not queued, so the client cancels again at the next prompt.

<details><summary>Writers and overlapping PRs</summary>

Writers that skipped the store step: `writeWizardConfigFile` in `configure` and the hosted chat setup, `commitSetupConfigFile` in onboarding and Gateway `wizard.start` setup, `createAgent` and `commitConfigWithPendingPluginInstalls` in `agents add`.

Open PRs touching the same files (none changes the channel save step):
- `src/wizard/setup.ts`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/127083, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163527, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166573
- `src/commands/configure.wizard.ts`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166573, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/131153
- `src/commands/agents.commands.add.ts`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174857, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/175069, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/168268
- Draft https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/121563 adds a shared credential-mode hint in `src/channels/plugins/setup-wizard-credential-mode.ts` that still says "Stores the credentials directly in OpenClaw config"; whichever lands second should use this PR's wording.

</details>

## Evidence

The CLI built from this branch and from the base `19c5e58c2e8`, each run in a fresh `HOME` and state directory under `env -i`, with synthetic tokens. The prompts were driven in a pseudo-terminal by the same step file on both sides. Runs that start the Gateway or the bundled Codex app-server were in a network namespace with only loopback.

Re-run on 2026-10-30 at the head `e268f2377da`, after merging `main` `885e57e9f9d`, with the same scripts on Node 24.22.1:
- `configure`: `botToken` is a `store` SecretRef, `openclaw.json` holds no copy of the token, the entry option says "Saves the credential in the protected secret store", and `secrets audit --check` exits 0, clean.
- Gateway `wizard.start`: the forbidden, cancel and complete scenarios match the first table below. With the answering device removed 2 to 100 ms after its last answer, 0 of 23 runs published the token to config. At 2 and 15 ms (10 runs) the removal cut off the answer before it reached the session, so nothing was written. From 25 ms on (13 runs) the session ended with one unreferenced store entry each (the first accepted limit above).
- Hosted chat: the forbidden and complete steps match the hosted chat table below. With the answering device removed at its last answer, 0 of 5 runs published config or stored an entry.

The hosted chat table no longer lists a second `operator.admin` device answering the admin's step. Since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176587, shared-token operator connections share the Gateway owner profile, so a second shared-token admin device is the same chat owner on `main` too. This PR does not change session ownership.

The tables below keep the commits they were first measured at.

`openclaw configure --section channels`, Telegram, "Enter Telegram bot token":

| Check | Before (`19c5e58c2e8`) | After (`dd48b4790aa`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| entry option hint | "Stores the credential directly in OpenClaw config" | "Saves the credential in the protected secret store" |
| `channels.telegram.botToken` in `openclaw.json` | **the token** | `{"source": "store", "provider": "default", "id": "CHANNEL_SETUP_…"}` |
| `doctor --lint` `core/doctor/security` plaintext warning (`Paths: channels.telegram.botToken`) | **present** | absent; the other five findings are unchanged |
| `secrets audit --check` | **exit 1, plaintext=1** | exit 0, clean, unresolved=0 |

`openclaw onboard --classic --flow quickstart --mode local --auth-choice skip --skip-…`, Telegram at "Select channel (QuickStart)", After at `6719dd19adc`:
- Before: exit 0; the token is in `openclaw.json` and `openclaw.json.bak`.
- After: exit 0; `botToken` is a `store` SecretRef and only the state database holds the token. `secrets audit --check` lists only `gateway.auth.token`, which onboarding generates and which this PR does not touch.

`openclaw agents add helper` on the onboarded state (After only, `6719dd19adc`), Discord at "Set up a chat channel now?": exit 0, "Agent "helper" ready.", `channels.discord.token` is a `store` SecretRef, resolves, and only the state database holds the token.

Gateway `wizard.start` setup, built at `786f6bc8daf` (the production code of the then-head `080097ce070`, which added one test-only commit): an isolated Gateway with token auth and a driver on the real `callGateway` client, answering each `wizard.next` step and reading the config file and `secrets.store.list` after each scenario.

| Scenario | Result | `channels.telegram.botToken` | Store entries |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| client with `[operator.write]` calls `wizard.start` | rejected: "missing scope: operator.admin" | absent | none |
| admin client enters the token, cancels at the next prompt | `cancelled` | absent | none |
| admin client completes QuickStart setup | `done` | `store` SecretRef | exactly the referenced entry |

The cancel above stops at a prompt, which the flow already honored. The new guard covers a cancel that lands after the last prompt and before the store write; the `wizard.test.ts` case below shows that window.

Device revoked after the last prompt, same Gateway setup: a client with its own paired device answers every step. At "Set up administration from your own chat account?", the last prompt before the store write, it sends its answer, and an admin client removes that device with `device.pair.remove` at once. Each run used a fresh state.

| Gateway build | Runs | Token stored after the removal | `wizard.status` after the answer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `6719dd19adc` (session hooks only) | 5 | **5** (config published 154–173 ms after the removal) | `running` |
| `fcc798f1332` (client check before the awaited commit) | 5 | **1** (config published 167 ms after the removal, after a lock wait) | `running` in the stored run, once `error` "Gateway caller authority is no longer active.", otherwise already ended |
| `3e378f75424`, a local build of `70078921176`'s production code before a test-only amend; it differs from `080097ce070` only in `src/system-agent` and `setup.test.ts` (check at publication) | 10 | 0 | already ended and collected |

Hosted chat in Control UI (`openclaw.chat`), the same isolated Gateway setup, built at `786f6bc8daf`, the production code of the then-head `080097ce070`. A chat session needs a verified model before it starts, so a loopback stand-in for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint answering "OK" was the default model; it was called once, for that check. The admin, a client with its own paired device, sent "connect telegram" and answered each hosted wizard step with `wizardAnswer`, as Control UI does.

| Step | Result | Config field | Store entries |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[operator.write]` client sends "connect telegram" | rejected: "missing scope: operator.admin" | absent | none |
| at the admin's token step, an `[operator.write]` client answers it | rejected: "missing scope: operator.admin" | absent | none |
| the admin answers through the last step | "Done — telegram is configured." | `store` SecretRef | exactly the referenced entry |

Hosted chat, answering device removed at its last chat answer ("Set up administration from your own chat account?"), a fresh state per run. Counted runs are those where the removal closed the answering request (4001); two `786f6bc8daf` runs where the request completed instead are listed in the proof file and excluded. In one, the answer's connection was silently re-paired on loopback after the removal. In the other, its handshake finished as the removal ran. `device.pair.remove` closes only registered connections, so a connection whose handshake completes during the removal keeps its capture, and loopback silent pairing can approve the device again; that is an existing Gateway race outside this PR.

| Gateway build | Removal | Counted runs | Config published after the removal | Store entry left |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before the hosted fix (`wizard.start` fixes only) | at once | 5 | **3** | 3 |
| `786f6bc8daf` | at once | 13 | 0 | 0 |
| `786f6bc8daf` | after 30 ms | 10 | 0 | 10, admitted before the removal; unreferenced (first accepted limit) |

Upgrade from the latest stable, v2026.10.6: the published package (`npm install openclaw@2026.10.6`, `fe06181`, empty HOME) wrote a state with a plaintext Telegram token, a Discord `env` SecretRef, a Slack `store` SecretRef and `env` SecretRef, a store entry, and gateway/model settings. On copies of it, the head `7b1c2db75d5` ran `doctor --fix --non-interactive` first: its `configure` refuses a state database that has not had the client credential migration from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/174599 (on `main` since 2026-10-19, not in v2026.10.6) and names `openclaw doctor --fix`; `openclaw update` runs that Doctor step after installing the candidate, so the run applied it by hand. Doctor migrated the state database and added five unrelated defaults without changing any release value. `configure` then added Zalo:
- Entered token: only `channels.zalo.*` and `plugins.entries.zalo.enabled` change; the other 26 config values, including the plaintext Telegram token, both env refs and the release store ref, are identical. The store keeps the release entry and gains one `CHANNEL_SETUP_…` entry.
- "Use external secret provider" → Environment variable: an `env` SecretRef, no store entry.
- `secrets audit --check`: `unresolved=0` after both runs; `plaintext=1` for the pre-existing Telegram token, as v2026.10.6 reports it on its own state.

An earlier run of the same steps from v2026.10.4 (`383c124`), with `configure` built at `6719dd19adc` and no Doctor step needed, kept the same values and store entries.

Tests:
- `src/cli/program/register.configure.persistence.test.ts` (new case): runs the registered `configure --section channels` command with a fixture channel plugin and checks that the file holds a `store` SecretRef and the store returns the token.
- `src/system-agent/hosted-setup.runtime.test.ts` "rejects stale hosted channel authority at config revision" now expects the `store` SecretRef in the hosted write, reads the token back from the store, and checks that a stale write phase leaves the store empty. Two new cases run the chat engine's turns in a Gateway request scope whose authority ends after the last answer, before the store write or while the config commit waits: the reply names "Gateway caller authority is no longer active.", nothing is published, and the store is empty or keeps only the admitted entry.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/wizard.test.ts` (new, four cases): the real `wizard.*` handlers and `WizardSession`; the `wizard.start` request carries a real device-revocation capture, which the session retains. The setup flow running, cancelled after the token prompt, and with the starting device revoked before the store write; the channels flow with the device revoked. Running: the store holds the token. Cancelled: `cancelled`. Revoked: `error` "Gateway requester authority changed". In the last three, no store entry and no config write.
- `src/wizard/setup.channel-authority.test.ts` (new, two cases): `runSetupWizard` with the real channel store step and a config-writer stand-in that runs `assertBeforePublish` as the real writer does. A rejecting `beforePersistentEffect` stops it before it saves the channel token; authority that ends once the channel config commit has started stops its publication. `setup.test.ts` is over its line cap, so the cases live in this sibling file and `setup.test.ts` is unchanged from `main`. Since `a7cf9a6d65c`, its migration, workspace, Gateway configuration and onboarding-helper mocks spread the real module through `importOriginal`; the channel registry mock keeps the process-global registry out of the fixture and says so in a `mock-isolation` comment, as `setup.test.ts` does.

Each changed test file, timed with `node scripts/test-projects.mts <file> --maxWorkers=1` (what `pnpm test` runs) and a warm transform cache, at the head `e268f2377da` on a loaded host (`setup.channel-authority.test.ts` at `a7cf9a6d65c`). With `main`'s additions, `src/system-agent/chat-engine.ts` and `src/wizard/setup.ts` passed their 700 counted lines; `e268f2377da` moves the turn's authority capture into `ChatWizardHost.forTurn` and shortens `setup.ts`. Related suites pass at the head `e268f2377da`: the changed test files and every test file that imports a changed production module (37 files), including `src/commands/channels.add.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/wizard.authority.test.ts`, the `system-agent` Gateway suites, the chat engine and turn router suites, and the onboarding and setup suites.

Checks at `886fd40bafa` (production code has not changed since `e268f2377da`, so the CLI and Gateway runs above still describe the head):

- At `86dc375851f`, `check-line-cap-ratchet --base upstream/main` and `check-test-timeout-race-ratchet` passed.

CI at `86dc375851f` (run 41137515051) failed three checks:

CI at `886fd40bafa` (run 41159636928) failed only `checks-node-changed-compact-large-16` (and `openclaw/ci-gate`, which aggregates it): `src/gateway/server-startup-lifetime.test.ts` "releases post-ready work and joins or bounds startup rollback (held-process)", where startup rollback had not settled after 10 s of fake time (line 510). Not covered:

That is pre-existing, and they write config only, not the team secret store, so it is outside this PR.
- `agents add` was run on this branch only.

<details><summary>Simplify pass</summary>

- Invariant: a channel credential typed into any interactive channel setup reaches config only as a `store` SecretRef, and a Gateway setup or Control UI chat setup whose session or answering client is no longer current writes no credential and publishes no config.
- One owner: the store step stays in `plugin-config-persistence.ts`; the four other save paths call it instead of copying it. `persistChannelPluginConfig` keeps its retained-entry notice and authority checks. Session liveness stays with `WizardSession` and caller authority with the Gateway (the grant `startGatewayWizard` retains, and the request scope); `wizard.ts` composes the two in one function both flows use; `ChatWizardHost.forTurn` binds each queued chat turn to its request's callback, which the host composes into its existing check. Publication-time admission stays with the config writer's `assertBeforePublish`.
- Against `main` `885e57e9f9d`: production +188/−88 in ten files (44 of the removed lines return unchanged in `storeChannelSetupCredentials`, and the channel step's nine options in `setup.ts` return re-indented inside the store call), tests +420/−3 in six files with a matching test-line allocation (+2), docs +1.
- The helper returns at once when the channel section is the same object as before: onboarding, `agents add` and the hosted chat skip secret-target discovery when the channel step changed nothing. `configure` always scans, because it compares against a clone of the base config.
- No new tests for onboarding and `agents add` beyond the CLI runs above: they call the same helper at their commit point.

</details>

prs.title: improve(ui): offer native video capture in Android composers
prs.body:
Part of #180298. ## What Problem This Solves The composer’s native Camera path only requests photos, and a delayed native return can begin attaching to a replacement draft. ## User Impact On the existing recognized Android browser route, Chat and New Session offer **Record video** alongside **Take photo**. A returned clip becomes a draft attachment and is sent only after an explicit send. Cancelled, detached, and replaced-draft camera returns are rejected. **This is a proposal for human review, not accepted picker policy or authorization to merge.** Desktop photo preview/capture/retake, other iOS photo routes, Safari’s **Photos & videos** and combined **Attach…** actions, image-only restrictions, upload safeguards, and unrestricted File selection remain unchanged. No custom recorder or microphone request is added by OpenClaw. Native browser/OS recording and permissions remain platform-owned. ## Why This Change Was Made A dedicated single-video capture input reuses the existing native-browser policy and attachment admission, preparation, preview and send owners. Explicit photo/video labels avoid implying that every platform has a video recorder. The native-return guard binds selection to the opening draft before asynchronous attachment reading starts. The merged existing-media contribution #180723 is incorporated through the refreshed main base: **Photos & videos**, Safari’s source-menu route, image-only restrictions and unrestricted File selection are preserved. Main’s lazy camera host is also preserved. Menu-heading proposal #180579, broader iOS capture policy and a desktop recorder remain outside this contribution. Proposed and directed by **Vitor Cepeda Lopes (@TheAngryPit)**. AI-assisted implementation. ## Work sessions - [Original discussion with @TheAngryPit](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/dfd1f162-7d1d-4dc0-a7e0-0a65c7817bd8) - [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/074b4e8e-6f15-40c7-9a31-e18ac3ab0f85) ## Evidence ### Current integration and CI repair — 2026-10-26 **Publication blocked; this PR is not yet merge-ready.** The tested, independently reviewed repair is preserved in the implementation session but has not reached this branch. The managed publisher rejected request `9ee1940f-f62d-4acd-8cf4-001375d7593d`: the requester needs full operator write authority for upstream workflow changes carried by the base refresh. The nine-file Camera delta against the verified refreshed base changes **no workflow files**. No workflow changes were removed to bypass the guard. A maintainer with full operator write access must publish the prepared update; then CI must pass on its exact head. Remote head was read back unchanged at `f36269109b8dbe32def219b35afd7828b5b5eb05` and remains conflicted with main. The original [UI-shard failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40086743010/job/120851466467) was reproduced: the Camera connected-input guard also rejected ordinary file-selection handoffs. The repair limits that guard to Camera returns; ordinary file/photo/media selection retains its existing handoff contract. Camera cancellation, opening-signal identity, detached-input rejection, disabled-state checks and image-only protection remain intact. Refreshed official-main base: `d46ce5ca6d6a067af0ab7a617750d082933e26c1`. Integrated candidate tree: `f57b2ecd842d77096474f17358d0bfc263c5fcb6`. Six shared-file conflicts were resolved with #180723 and main’s lazy camera host; the complete base-relative change remains nine files. No new recorder, picker-policy redesign or permission change was introduced. - **49 focused tests passed:** 27 native/desktop Camera and picker cases, plus all 22 isolated attachment-handoff cases, including both previously failing cases. - **18 production-browser behavior scenarios passed:** Chat/New Session video return, explicit exact-byte sending, cancellation/reselection, platform exclusions, preserved desktop photo capture, Safari picker behavior and mixed existing-media selection. One additional candidate screenshot scenario and one matched-base screenshot scenario passed. - Production UI types, affected Chat/browser-test typecheck leaves, scoped typed lint, stylesheet lint, i18n baseline/verification, formatting and lifecycle/controller guards passed. Both production UI builds passed. - The initial lifecycle/typecheck launch exceeded the sandbox thread capacity; rerunning those checks with bounded compiler concurrency passed without changing source, assertions or gates. Node 24.22.1 and the frozen dependency install retained integrity and release-age checks. - Test cost: component run 21.19 s total / about 0.5 s assertions; handoff run 8.63 s total / about 0.17 s assertions. The production-browser run took 71.92 s including build; the video-return file took 2.558 s. - Fresh independent P0–P3 review returned **scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. A first review had two status-only chunks; a follow-up supplied the complete 483-line base-relative diff, and all three passes explicitly confirmed coverage of every substantive hunk across all nine files. Tests were not independently rerun by the reviewer. Current-head CI remains the original failed run because publication of the repair was denied. Prior Android emulator evidence remains attached and explicitly belongs to the original head; no new Android run is claimed. **Actual integrated Before / After:** identical 390 × 844 light-theme synthetic Chat content and Android Chrome browser identity. Before uses the five affected production modules from the exact refreshed base; candidate modules were restored and byte-verified after capture. These are production UI screenshots, not native Android certification.
Before — refreshed mainAfter — integrated Camera proposal
### Original implementation proof - **Original published/tested-source head:** `f36269109b8dbe32def219b35afd7828b5b5eb05`, published by `roboclaw-bot`. All nine published files match the tested/reviewed source byte-for-byte; all three PR commits, including the managed base integrations, have the required TheAngryPit co-author trailer. - Prepared official-main base: `a6c561f954c41209124f7add70a13c59e883eda3`. Tested/reviewed candidate tree: `74ade09e50c17aaa58bc9968aeb76e4985ac10cb`; nine source/test/documentation files. - **25 focused unit cases passed** across native return, input ownership and existing photo capture. The two principal regressions fail on the exact prepared base: missing video action and native photo admission into a replacement draft. The corrected connected fixture was used for that base-red proof. - **27 production-browser scenarios passed across the initial run and focused correction.** Existing 25-case platform suite passed (Chat/New Session, native photo return, preview/retake, denied/unavailable preview, picker geometry, keyboard, Safari and embedded-host exclusions). The two new cases verify pointer/keyboard gesture admission, native video return, cancellation/reselection, no browser preview request, and exact attachment bytes at explicit `chat.send`/`sessions.create`. These run the actual built Control UI with synthetic Gateway responses, not a separate mock UI or live provider delivery. - Initial new-video browser attempt failed its test-only gesture probe: desktop Chromium does not expose the `input.capture` property used by the probe. Reading the actual capture attribute fixed the probe; no assertion was dropped, timeout raised, retry added or product safeguard weakened. Both cases then passed. Early unit-fixture connection/disposal mistakes and an unsupported icon choice were corrected before the final passing checks. - UI types, affected Chat and browser-test typecheck leaves, scoped typed lint, stylesheet lint, controller ratchets, i18n baseline/verification, format, changed-document MDX and whitespace checks passed. Production builds passed as part of browser verification. - Fresh independent Auto Review: **scoped-clean through P0–P3**, no actionable findings; OpenClaw engine, effective model `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`. It reviewed the complete base-relative candidate and supplied owners, did not independently rerun tests, and is not product acceptance. - Test cost: final focused unit run 1.14 s total; new browser file 7.888 s test time (two flows), combined video/capture run 44.71 s including setup. Initial 27-case run took 144.92 s with the two probe failures described above. At initial publication verification, hosted draft checks showed 7 passed and 70 skipped/neutral on this head; the broad CI gate and UI lanes are skipped while draft. These are not passing full-suite results. - Simplification: no new state store, recorder, policy owner or effect/listener ratchet allowance. Net production growth is 49 lines for the explicit input and opening-draft guard; regression coverage adds 248 lines net. Temporary capture code and generated media are excluded. ### Native Android verification — inspected Windows evidence The requester supplied the Windows handoff and a selected evidence bundle for the **original published head** `f36269109b8dbe32def219b35afd7828b5b5eb05`, against comparison merge-base `a6c561f954c41209124f7add70a13c59e883eda3`. These are Echo's retained emulator runs, **not Android tests rerun by Roboclaw**. Roboclaw has now inspected the supplied screenshots, recordings and return/ownership records, verified every one of the selected manifest's **33 files**, matched **29 included runtime originals** against the original 240-artifact manifest, and independently confirmed the captured MP4 is byte-for-byte identical to the decoded synthetic send payload. The other original artifacts were not supplied and were not reverified here. The archive passes CRC validation; its SHA-256 is `55357df3ddf4e781798013dd15190f605add88b29d2c1c0cbcc407962fb3ee6a`. The original manifest SHA-256 is `6d8a03785cb7ed0c19af729c8eeee3cc870f3b17a232e2a5a3e8055f23d0c958`. Curated synthetic media is embedded below. Raw reports, local host inventory/paths and human intervention quotations are not published. The observer source and all permission-control artifacts are not included in this selected bundle; their complete audit remains the Windows coordinator's report, not an independently repeated audit here. Reported environment: Windows 11; Google Android Emulator 37.2.12.0 with WHPX; Pixel 7 Google Play x86_64 AVD, Android 17/API 37; Chrome 156.0.8078.47; native `com.android.camera2` 2.0.002. The back camera was emulated, front camera absent and host audio disabled. Production Control UI components used the canonical synthetic Gateway fixture via localhost/`adb reverse`, with matching build identities and browser security/capability checks retained. No personal camera media or Google account was used. | Native scenario | Chat | New Session | | --- | --- | --- | | Genuine captured photo and recorded video returned as attachments | PASS | PASS | | Opening capture attaches/sends nothing; cancellation leaves no attachment/send | PASS | PASS | | Reopen and successful retry | PASS — photo | PASS — video | | Production video playback | PASS | Not separately tested | | Photo-only capture requests no microphone | PASS | Observed pass | | Denied camera permission preserves draft | PASS | Not separately tested | | Camera app unavailable; fallback cancelled without selecting a file | PASS — photo/video | Not separately tested | | Same-document replacement rejects late native photo/video returns | Not separately tested | PASS | The actual image-only Side chat menu also admitted a genuine photo without exposing video capture. On the matched base, photo capture worked and **Record video** was absent. Recorded Chat output: 75,545-byte JPEG with a decoded 1392 × 1856 preview; 1,228,950-byte MP4 lasting 13.444233 seconds. The Windows coordinator matched that captured MP4's hash to the decoded synthetic `chat.send` payload after explicit Send. Production playback reached 12.8214 seconds, readyState 4, with no reported error. Full FFmpeg decoding exited 0 with a duplicate-DTS warning (`271 >= 271`); it was not warning-free. New Session received a 75,051-byte JPEG and a 1,511,944-byte MP4. For the same-document negative control, browser Back/Forward replaced the New Session route while native Camera was foreground. The document, root and original connected input stayed unchanged; production route replacement aborted the opening read signal. Camera returned a real 71,741-byte JPEG and 1,468,016-byte MP4 to the original inputs, but neither attached, sent, or created a session in the replacement draft. A passive observer recorded metadata/hashes without assigning a File, signal or owner. Cancellation and a subsequent current-owner photo capture also succeeded. Whole-document navigation and ordinary text edits were correctly excluded as proof of this guard. The Windows coordinator reports checking all 240 retained artifact hashes/byte counts and inspecting the negative/positive captures. An independent native reviewer examined that evidence; its model metadata and full approval transcript were unavailable. This is additional runtime evidence, not maintainer approval or a blanket permission audit. No source changes or live deployment were made. ### Native Android media — inspected originals and one labeled viewing copy All six native-evidence assets below were fetched anonymously with HTTP 200 and matching inspected SHA-256/byte counts. The four screenshots decoded in the public PR at 300px widths; the Before/After images rendered side by side. Both embedded video players decoded and advanced without reported media errors. The rendered comparison was inspected. This is publication verification, not an additional Android run. **Photo capture → return → attachment (27.271789 seconds).** This is the real native **photo** flow, not a video-recording demonstration. Camera opens at roughly 15 seconds; the captured photo returns at roughly 22 seconds. Original recording, no audio track: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6eb3d640-9600-4c41-ad29-b4abf051607c
Original native video content and exact-byte send verification The original 1,228,950-byte recorded MP4 has SHA-256 `10a309ed7bc1b4bb2f0450d414a46bb55c4ba64985d5441e203281f52db9d2b7`. It matches both the native-return record and the decoded `chat.send` attachment byte-for-byte. The original was not changed. Independent local FFmpeg full decoding exited 0, retaining the duplicate-DTS warning; browser decoding also succeeded. The following **silent public viewing copy** removes audio and copies the original video stream without re-encoding. It is not the original file used for the byte-equality claim. prs.title: fix: prevent duplicate optional-question answers across viewers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes duplicate optional-question answer popups and submissions when several viewers share a conversation, including when the first answer is queued.

## User Impact

The first accepted answer is shared across panes and reloads as **Answer queued** or **Answer sent**. A stale second submit does not send another message. Normal typed corrections remain ordinary messages. Explicitly withdrawing a queued answer makes the question answerable again; interrupted custody does not release it. There are no new configuration options or database migrations.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the canonical question reference with the existing input and enforce uniqueness through its authoritative actor state before queued or direct custody. Incognito public staging applies the same guard at its storage-command effect. Shared presentation derives from accepted inputs, and confirmed withdrawal releases the submitting pane’s retained hint even when cancellation redacts the message. There is no separate question registry. The follow-up simplifies the SQL guard and consolidates repeated fixtures and scenarios.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original duplicate popup, retained-pane withdrawal, and previously missed public incognito staging path before fixing them. Two consolidated shared-state Chromium scenarios plus 15 existing scenarios passed: **17 total**, covering mounted viewers, confirmed queue removal, stale-submit reconciliation, outbox retirement, reload, and canonical confirmation.
- **65 focused backend/storage tests across five files passed.** Public durable/incognito active/idle cases race two answers, retry the actual winner, reject same or contradictory stale submits, distinguish cancellation from interruption, and preserve invalid-source rejection, ordinary corrections, and new same-worded questions. Existing authorization/replacement and memory-owner consumers passed.
- Reused real data produced by published `openclaw@2026.10.6` at commit `fe06181dc5ecc01cf8904abbfc26925925efefbc`. On the simplified kernel, an isolated copy again passed existing Doctor migration **schema 25→31**, cold SQLite reopening, legacy queued/saved duplicate rejection, explicit withdrawal, interrupted retention, and original transcript/message integrity. This is a storage compatibility rehearsal, **not** a full service install-over.
- Wrapper extraction/materialized-context checks passed **2 tests**. The worker inventory check and SQLite ratchet passed at **170→170**, compatibility **15→15**, without raising baselines. Affected production/test typechecks, targeted lint/format, controller guards, and diff checks passed. Fresh independent **P0–P2** review and originating-session review found no actionable issues.
- Browser proof uses the actual compiled Control UI with synthetic Gateway fixtures; two browser contexts simulate viewers. No live Codex/model execution or actual signed-in multi-profile browser run is claimed. Existing before/after images remain representative; this simplification changes no production rendering.

**Before**

**After**

![Shared queued answer shown without a duplicate optional-question popup](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9152c36-ff12-496f-94ee-bf50c8288d1e)

Thanks to @shakkernerd for reporting the issue and guiding the fix.

## User Impact

User impact: affected xAI turns retry once and then advance to the configured fallback instead of ending with an unclassified provider failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

prs.title: fix(talk): voice agent consults fail with PostgreSQL agent stores
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

With PostgreSQL selected for the agent database family, Talk connects and audio flows, but native GPT-Live delegations fail before starting the agent:

```
PostgreSQL connections must run in a worker; only synchronous admission, migrations, and CLI one-shots may run on the main thread
```

#188580 moved Talk entry initialization to its worker. Consult admission still synchronously read the voice-call record and session/model-lock state on the Gateway thread.

## Change

Use the existing voice writer's worker read for the open-call check and the existing asynchronous session reader for consult lifecycle/model-lock checks. Preserve ownership, open-state, model-lock, cancellation and final live-authority checks. Remove the unused synchronous call-facts reader. Keep the public synchronous SDK model-lock helper unchanged for its existing consumers.

Thanks to Chris Eckert (@ceckert) for the diagnosis and original fix; his commits are preserved. No configuration, authentication, schema, migration or threshold changes. #183586 is not changed. Active-consult steering and the voice-call extension's synchronous SDK helper are outside this change.

## Evidence

Exact-head maintainer runtime evidence: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188965#issuecomment-6538726082

Built Gateway, Node 24.22.1, isolated real PostgreSQL 17, authenticated public Talk RPCs. The GPT-Live WebSocket and Responses model are deterministic local loopback fixtures with synthetic credentials; no paid provider is called. The proof exercises relay readiness, appended PCM audio, provider transcript/delegation, an actual OpenClaw agent turn, returned commentary and persisted history. It does not claim real speech recognition or synthesis.

- Main `dda109cacbbefd3a6dfcc442ac97e2107b6c62c8`: PostgreSQL consultations fail twice with the worker-only guard; zero model calls and no assistant answer.
- Candidate: both consultations call the local Responses provider, return their distinct assistant markers and persist them. Direct PostgreSQL reads after Gateway shutdown independently find both assistant answers.
- SQLite control: main and candidate both complete twice.
- Focused Talk/native-control/worker/store suites: 41 passed. Real-storage entry/consult regression: PostgreSQL and SQLite pass on candidate; the same probe fails on main with the worker guard while SQLite passes.

The regression is consolidated in the existing `client-voice-session-entry.postgres.test-support.ts`, including both warm/cold entry initialization and the unchanged refusal of unrelated main-thread SQL. Against merge base `1f088d23a1ccf5eae60faed5225f1e366f1bc6ea`: production +71/-72 (net -1); tests and support +56/-69 (net -13). No new test suite/build entry remains.

Contributor's earlier shipped-Gateway proof: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188965#issuecomment-6537740084

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the old read paths; this change adds no schema or data-format migration. Blast radius is Talk consult admission and lifecycle reads on PostgreSQL and SQLite; incorrect ownership or cancellation handling could reject a valid consult or admit a stale one.

prs.title: fix: let maintainers prepare PRs in guest conversations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A maintainer helping in a guest's conversation can have permission to act there and still be refused when preparing its pull request. Preparation requires the conversation's creator and then requires the PR author to match the requester's linked GitHub account.

## User Impact

A current caller with full operator write permission can prepare or continue the verified PR without being its creator or author. The operation uses the configured publisher and the conversation's writable sandbox. Guests retain their identity, repository-access and action requirements.

A maintainer's update to an imported PR cannot make it eligible for later guest publication, even when its branch name matches the conversation's branch. Native-publication continuation and previously admitted bindings retain their behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The creator and author checks recognize the same current action authority, intersecting the admitted requester's permissions with the selected tool caller's capability. Both remain live across GitHub reads and workspace effects. Unbound preparation retains the selected requester through its existing handoff; the resumed conversation does not inherit the finished tool context.

The existing PR binding records whether the exact PR had a verified publication in this conversation before its first binding. Refresh and recovery preserve that fact. Imported-update receipts remain available for status and reconciliation but cannot establish guest authorship eligibility. Older bindings without the new field retain their existing checks. The field adds no permission or receipt-retention dependency.

## Evidence

The baseline registered public/private maintainer cases fail with the creator-only error. The focused owner suite passed 196 cases across 14 files, with formatting, lint and selected production/test type checks. It covers initial classification, matching and differing branch names, native and legacy continuation, refresh/restart/reset, workspace reuse and current-authority controls. The exact per-change allocation funds 221 net test/helper lines for these distinct regressions; the shared baseline is unchanged.

After resolving the base-branch conflict, the preparation and refresh suites passed all 53 cases with its locked dependencies. Formatting, lint, the selected gateway type graph and whitespace checks also passed. Integration required a one-line fixture correction so GitHub account reads work alongside repository reads.

Actual Guest Lab verification passed managed and unbound maintainer preparation, one update to the original foreign PR, refusal of the following genuine guest publication with pending work retained, explicit foreign-author refusal, legacy continuation after cold boot, protected inspection denial and second-guest chat admission denial. Configuration, profiles and identities remained unchanged.

The live build is the qualified P1/P2/R5/R6 composition shown below, not a claim that a standalone PR head was deployed. Same-profile scope narrowing, mid-call role/device revocation and the equal-branch edge remain native registered-test evidence. The second guest could not submit through the UI, so its deeper preparation guard was not exercised live. The unbound screenshot is final-state evidence only; that separate recording has a 16.499 second middle gap. A separate read-only inspection establishes the author refusal; the wrapped publication error is not presented as a captured inner stack.

prs.title: feat(ci): close issues older than 90 days and PRs older than 60 days
prs.body:
## Problem

The maintainer policy is that no issue stays open longer than 90 days and no PR longer than 60 days. The Barnacle lifecycle from #177120 only acts on inactivity, and it protects a wide set of labels and owners: `enhancement`, P0/P1, `security`/`impact:security`, maintainer authors and assignees, and active ClawSweeper work. Anything in that set can stay open indefinitely, and so can any item that keeps getting human comments. In practice, a manual sweep on 2026-10-20..23 had to close roughly 1,550 issues and PRs from February to August by hand.

This intentionally changes one documented rule from #177120 ("creation age does not override recent human activity"). cc @vincentkoc

## Change

The PR adds a creation-age lane to `scripts/github/stale-lifecycle.mjs`, the single owner of issue and PR lifecycle. It does not add a second owner or workflow job.

- Issues older than 90 days and PRs older than 60 days (by `created_at`) get an authenticated `lane=age-cap` notice. They close as `not_planned` after the grace: 7 days, or 14 days for `bug` issues, matching the bug-closure audit.
- Human comments do not cancel or restart age-cap grace. A hold added during the grace cancels it.
- Holds for the age cap are deliberately narrow: `pinned`, `no-stale`, `hold`, `in-progress`, `bad-barnacle`, the exact human `security` label, the confirmed-bug repair labels (`clawsweeper:source-repro`, `clawsweeper:queueable-fix`, `clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear`), locked items, and PR heads with a commit or push in the last 14 days.
- These do not hold an item past its age cap: `enhancement`, `bug`, P0/P1, `impact:security`, security-review and merge-risk labels, maintainer authors/assignees, executed CI, and active ClawSweeper reviews.
- If an inactivity or age-cap notice is already pending, that lane keeps its grace. One item never gets two notices in a run.
- The existing notice, receipt, readback and re-read-before-effect checks, the shared close cap, dry run and `item_numbers` targeting are all reused unchanged.
- `auditRecentBugClosures` accepts authenticated age-cap closures with the full 14-day grace. Its inactivity requirements for inactivity closures are unchanged.
- The close message thanks the author, says the close is not a claim that anything was fixed, and invites a fresh issue or PR that links back.
- Docs: the Barnacle section of `docs/ci/scheduled-workflows.md` is updated, and `pull-request-review-flow.md` now links to it instead of repeating old timings.

## Rollout note

On the first scheduled runs, every open item past its cap gets a notice. Closes follow 7 or 14 days later, bounded by the existing 50-close cap per run. To keep something open, a maintainer adds `no-stale` or `hold`; confirmed bugs should carry `clawsweeper:source-repro`. A `dry_run=true` dispatch of `stale.yml` shows the decisions before the first live run.

## Proof

- `node --test test/scripts/stale-lifecycle.node.mjs`: 299 passed, 0 failed. New clock-controlled cases cover these behaviors:
  - An over-age `enhancement` issue is noticed and closes even after a human comments.
  - An over-age maintainer-authored P1 PR closes, while the same PR with a head push 3 days ago is held.
  - `no-stale`, `clawsweeper:source-repro`, and a `hold` added during grace all prevent the close.
  - A `bug` issue's age-cap close uses the 14-day grace and passes the bug-closure audit.
  - Dry run performs no writes, and the shared close cap still applies.
- Production lint: 0 errors. Format and `git diff --check`: clean.
- An independent Codex review of the diff (P0–P2 scope) came back clean.
- Gap: the adjacent workflow and auto-response Vitest suites stalled at startup on the local host. PR CI covers them.

prs.title: fix(daemon): clarify launchd inspection failures over SSH
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The macOS service-inspection error currently asserts that the launchd GUI domain is unavailable and directs operators to manage the Gateway from a desktop session. The classifier uses that reason for native launchctl exits 1, 13, and 125, so this wording overstates the cause and can be read as an SSH-management restriction.

## User Impact

The error now says OpenClaw could not inspect the GUI domain and that it may be missing or inaccessible. It explicitly distinguishes this observation from SSH management being disabled, gives read-only account/domain checks, and makes desktop-login guidance conditional on a missing domain. For externally supervised Gateways, it retains a concise conditional link to the supported owner-managed recovery procedure.

No service-control, admission, ownership, error-classification, configuration, or database behavior changes. Existing detailed external-supervisor guidance remains unchanged for the other inspection reasons. This does not diagnose why a particular Mac's launchctl behavior changed or claim all SSH environments work.

## Why This Change Was Made

The failure is observed at the native service-inspection boundary; the message should describe that boundary rather than prescribe local-only management. Keep the existing safe refusal and offer diagnostics before recovery advice.

## Evidence

Original reviewed candidate: `45dc0ee76c54014b2402fc94aae80811791555d9`. The evidence below belongs to that revision; follow-up evidence is recorded separately below.

- Baseline: the new start/stop/restart CLI-boundary regressions fail on the old wording (3 failures; 34 existing tests pass).
- Candidate: lifecycle/status/launchd-membership suites report 94 passed and 16 skipped on Linux. These tests feed native exit fixtures through the real launchd probe/classifier/formatter and CLI lifecycle owners, and assert that service start/stop/restart mutations are not called.
- Independent review identified a Windows portability issue in the macOS fixture; explicitly pinning the fixture to Darwin fixed it. The affected lifecycle suite then passed 37/37. No production change was needed for that correction.
- Targeted lint, formatting, core and relevant test typechecks, and whitespace checks pass. Full supported build passed in 4m16s.
- Shared independent Auto Review completed scoped-clean for P0–P2; supplemental review verified the fixture correction. No remaining actionable findings.

## Original native macOS observation

An isolated-state, task-label, read-only invocation of the installed CLI reproduced the original service-inspection message. Native `launchctl print gui/$(id -u)` returned exit 125, `Domain does not support specified action`; the user-domain query succeeded. This proves the inspection failure, not the machine's historical root cause.

The exact candidate was built with the supported full build, then its complete build outputs were copied into a separate Mac checkout with Mac-installed dependencies. The normal built launcher ran successfully (exit 0) using isolated state, a task-specific service label, and `--no-probe`. The artifact checksum and production source hash were verified before execution. No live service was stopped, restarted, installed, or repaired.

Sanitized candidate output from `node openclaw.mjs gateway status --deep --no-probe --json`:

```json
{
  "inspectionReason": "launchd-gui-domain-unavailable",
  "loadState": {
    "status": "unknown",
    "detail": "ServiceInspectionError: OpenClaw could not inspect the macOS launchd GUI domain for this account; it may be missing or inaccessible. This does not mean SSH management is disabled. From the account that owns the Gateway, run id -un and launchctl print gui/$(id -u) to check the account and domain. If the domain is missing, log that account into the macOS desktop, then retry; you can still use SSH. Otherwise, check launchctl output for access errors.",
    "inspectionReason": "launchd-gui-domain-unavailable"
  },
  "runtime": {
    "status": "unknown",
    "detail": "Could not print domain: 125: Domain does not support specified action",
    "inspectionReason": "launchd-gui-domain-unavailable"
  },
  "targetRole": "diagnostic-only"
}
```

The installed CLI and candidate both report the same native exit-125 detail and `unknown` load state. Only the explanatory guidance changes. The old output directs management from the desktop and appends `OPENCLAW_SERVICE_REPAIR_POLICY=external`; the candidate offers account/domain diagnostics and does neither.

**Limits:** This is an actual non-GUI macOS CLI/native-launchctl observation, not an SSH transport end-to-end test or a successful service start/stop/restart. The lifecycle refusals and no-mutation behavior for all three actions are covered by deterministic CLI-boundary regressions. Linux skips are not counted as native Mac test passes. No claim is made about what originally changed on the reporting machine.

## Review follow-up: preserve recovery discoverability

The recovery route introduced in #145023 was intentional and reporter-confirmed. The GUI-domain diagnostic now retains a conditional documentation pointer: "If an external supervisor owns this Gateway, see https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway#existing-system-launchdaemons for owner-managed recovery." This follows the reviewer recommendation without prescribing Doctor repair merely because inspection failed. The documented recovery policy, state-owning account requirement, coordinator/lease checks, and owner-controlled shutdown/restart are unchanged.

Follow-up head: `60b9a0c815efdf6a9dffd7b356362e1076c387cc`.

- The three existing start/stop/restart cases now require the conditional recovery link. They fail on the previous head (3 failures, 34 passes) and pass after this change. All existing no-service-mutation checks remain.
- Lifecycle, status-gather and launchd-membership suites: 121 passed, 16 platform skips. CLI shard wall time 7.89s; daemon shard 30.69s, primarily cold compilation; fresh CI timing pending.
- Formatting, targeted lint, core typecheck and diff checks passed. Supported runtime build passed in 84.5s. Independent Auto Review: scoped-clean P0–P2 on the complete follow-up delta.
- Rebuilt runtime transferred to the Mac with SHA-256 verification. The normal built launcher again ran `gateway status --deep --no-probe --json` with isolated state and a task-specific label, exit 0. The native exit-125/unknown state is unchanged and the conditional recovery pointer is present. No live service mutation. This remains a non-GUI local macOS observation, not SSH service-control proof.

Current built CLI output:

```json
{
  "inspectionReason": "launchd-gui-domain-unavailable",
  "loadState": {
    "status": "unknown",
    "detail": "ServiceInspectionError: OpenClaw could not inspect the macOS launchd GUI domain for this account; it may be missing or inaccessible. This does not mean SSH management is disabled. From the account that owns the Gateway, run id -un and launchctl print gui/$(id -u) to check the account and domain. If the domain is missing, log that account into the macOS desktop, then retry; you can still use SSH. Otherwise, check launchctl output for access errors. If an external supervisor owns this Gateway, see https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway#existing-system-launchdaemons for owner-managed recovery.",
    "inspectionReason": "launchd-gui-domain-unavailable"
  },
  "runtime": {
    "status": "unknown",
    "detail": "Could not print domain: 125: Domain does not support specified action",
    "inspectionReason": "launchd-gui-domain-unavailable"
  }
}
```

prs.title: fix(ui): show the newest logs when the view opens
prs.body:
Related: #188617 (builds on the merged post-layout anchor fix).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Logs view opening around row 500 instead of showing the newest entries while Auto-follow is enabled.

## User Impact

Opening Logs follows the newest entries as the initial pages and wrapped row heights settle. The empty-state message stays visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first eleven rows can measure 73 px before later rows settle at 91 px. Their cached measurements account for an anchor 198 px short of the warm-metric position (`11 × (91 − 73)`): the reported 22468 becomes 22270 locally. Absolutely positioned rows can also extend the native scroll range ahead of the committed virtual spacer, leaving a stale clamped correction that overrides following. #188617 alone still strands the initial window at 22591.

Clip nonempty row overflow to the committed spacer height so the existing post-layout owner can settle measurements and append anchors consistently. Leave the zero-height empty fallback unclipped.

## Evidence

Initial-window failure rates through the unchanged browser test:

| Source | Alone | Original CI shard order | CPU load |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Original main | 16/20 | 0/1 | 3/5 |
| Main + exact #188617 diff | 20/20 | 1/1 | 5/5 |
| This fix | **0/20** | **0/9 target executions** | Remote proof pending |

The nine shard-order target executions include eight completed 136-file shards and a ninth stopped after the target completed during a host I/O emergency. The remaining eleven shard replays and twenty loaded runs are running on remote Blacksmith Testbox; those results are not yet claimed.

- All 27 Logs page tests, UI typecheck, scoped lint, format, and controller checks pass.
- All four Logs E2E files ran, including isolated real-Gateway lifecycle: **7/8 cases pass**. The pre-existing **:112 desktop WebKit wheel failure is separate and not addressed**. It failed in 17/20 original-main desktop cases and 18/20 fixed standalone cases; this is not a claim of green aggregate validation.
- Independent Codex autoreview of commit `9df278db107e74f9f04181571c6f36e5063dc5da`, P0–P2: **scoped-clean**, complete, no actionable findings.
- Fixed geometry trace: native scroll height matches the committed spacer/viewport in all 343 samples. Inspected synthetic screenshots show row 1999 fully visible at a zero-pixel bottom gap; the empty fallback remains fully visible.
- No test, retry, timeout, assertion, skip, dependency, or baseline changes.
