prs.title: fix(agents): Code Mode loses exec warnings when the command finishes before yielding
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/188803

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in Code Mode, a warning that `exec` collected (a secret-store `env` entry it refused to apply, no PTY in a sandbox, `host=node` running synchronously) never reaches the program when the command finishes before exec yields. The native tool result shows the warning; the Code Mode value does not.

## User Impact

User impact: Code Mode programs receive `warningText` on completed `exec` results, local and node host, and on node-host failures, as they already do on running results, so the agent can explain or work around the condition the warning names.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187244 added structured `warningText` to running exec results because Code Mode returns a successful call's structured details to the program, not its text. Completed results kept the warning in text only: the local foreground result builder, the node-host result builder and the node invoke-failure result render the warnings into the text and leave them out of the details. All three now also set `warningText` in the details, with the same shape as the running result (omitted when there are no warnings), and the `completed | failed` details type gains the optional field.

Local failed results already include the warnings in their structured `message` (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186515); they now also carry `warningText`, so a program can read the warning from one field whatever the status. Node-host failures (a non-zero exit or a failed node invoke) are not tool errors and have no `message`, so `warningText` is the only structured place their warnings reach. The node path now builds its warning list once for both branches.

Size: production +8/-3 lines in four files, docs 1 line (`docs/tools/exec.md` now says running, completed and failed results preserve warnings), tests +14/-16. No config, state or SDK surface changes.

## Evidence

[Fresh paired Node24 Linux Gateway/node proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188804#issuecomment-6538691661): separately built full main and candidate, a real second-container paired node, and actual CodeMode model continuation values. Main omits the existing synchronous-node warning twice; candidate preserves it twice. The no-warning control is unchanged. Provider responses are deterministic local fixtures, not a live-model claim. The local approval suite has one inherited allow-always persistence assertion that also fails on full main; the linked evidence distinguishes it from the passing warning regressions.

Tested at `d7928d7f9b3` (base `main` at `65acdfd629e`). `d7928d7f9b3` changes only tests: it folds the new Code Mode check into an existing test so the PR adds no test lines.

Both runs below start the checkout's `openclaw` CLI with `pnpm openclaw` on Ubuntu 22.04: an isolated Gateway (own state directory, loopback port, synthetic token, channels skipped) with `tools.codeMode: true`, `tools.exec: { security: "full", ask: "off" }` and the real Gemini API (`google/gemini-3.6-flash`). The Gateway log reports the repo's pinned Bun 1.4.4 (Node compatibility 26.12.1). Each turn is `openclaw agent --agent main --json` asking the agent to run one Code Mode program and reply with its value. The `exec` tool results are read from the stored session transcript.

### Local host

Program `return await exec({ command: "echo ok" });`, with one synthetic secret-store entry that exec refuses to apply to child processes (`openclaw secrets store set NODE_OPTIONS --kind env --value=--no-warnings`). After ran an earlier local build of this fix, differing only in the node invoke-failure line, which this run does not reach.

Observed result: before, exec collected the warning (a control with `tools.codeMode: false` shows it in the text) but the Code Mode value lacked it; after, the value carries it as `warningText`, and the model's reply quoted it.

<details>
<summary>Tool results (cwd and telemetry shortened)</summary>

Before (base):

```text
toolName=exec isError=false
value={"status":"completed","exitCode":0,"exitSignal":null,"exitReason":"exit","durationMs":244,
  "aggregated":"ok","noOutputTimedOut":false,"cwd":"<workspace>"}
```

Control on the same base with `tools.codeMode: false` (plain `exec` call, same command), tool result text:

```text
Warning: secret store environment entries were not applied for host=gateway: NODE_OPTIONS.\n\n\n\nok
```

After (this PR):

```text
toolName=exec isError=false
value={"status":"completed","exitCode":0,"exitSignal":null,"exitReason":"exit","durationMs":227,
  "aggregated":"ok","noOutputTimedOut":false,"cwd":"<workspace>",
  "warningText":"Warning: secret store environment entries were not applied for host=gateway: NODE_OPTIONS."}
```

</details>

### Paired node

Same Gateway setup with no secret-store entry, and a headless node host (`openclaw node run --host 127.0.0.1 --auth-from-env`, its own home directory, no provider keys, `tools.exec: { security: "full", ask: "off" }`) paired over loopback. `background: true` on `host=node` makes exec collect its "running synchronously" warning. After ran `d7928d7f9b3`. Two programs:

- Node completion: `return await exec({ command: "echo ok", host: "node", background: true });`
- Node invoke failure: `return await exec({ command: "sleep 47", host: "node", background: true });`, with the node host process stopped while `sleep 47` was running.

Observed result: on both node paths the program's value lacks the warning before and carries it as `warningText` after.

<details>
<summary>Tool results (node id and telemetry shortened)</summary>

Node completion:

```text
before value={"status":"completed","exitCode":0,"durationMs":41,"aggregated":"ok\n","nodeId":"<node-id>"}
after  value={"status":"completed","exitCode":0,"durationMs":28,"aggregated":"ok\n","nodeId":"<node-id>",
  "warningText":"Warning: continuation options are unavailable for host=node; running synchronously via remote system.run without a process session."}
```

Node invoke failure:

```text
before value={"status":"failed","exitCode":null,"failureKind":"outcome-unknown","reason":"outcome-unknown",
  "nodeInvokeFailure":{"failureCode":"DISCONNECTED","message":"node disconnected (system.run)","nodeCommandDispatched":true},
  "durationMs":1101,"aggregated":"Node command outcome is unknown for <node-id>.\n...\nDetails: node disconnected (system.run)"}
after  value={"status":"failed","exitCode":null,"failureKind":"outcome-unknown","reason":"outcome-unknown",
  "nodeInvokeFailure":{"failureCode":"DISCONNECTED","message":"node disconnected (system.run)","nodeCommandDispatched":true},
  "durationMs":1454,"aggregated":"Node command outcome is unknown for <node-id>.\n...\nDetails: node disconnected (system.run)",
  "warningText":"Warning: continuation options are unavailable for host=node; running synchronously via remote system.run without a process session."}
```

</details>

I could not produce a node-side refusal (`SYSTEM_RUN_DENIED`) or a missing-permission failure on a real node through this path. With `strictInlineEval` on the node, `node -e` is refused at `system.run.prepare`, and with an allowlist node policy the Gateway refuses before dispatch. Both surface as thrown tool errors, not as the node invoke-failure result. The disconnect above is a real invoke failure that reaches `formatNodeInvokeFailureToolResult`. The policy-denied and permission-missing reasons share that builder and are covered only by the focused test.

### Tests and checks

Regression tests, failing on the base and passing with the fix:

- `code-mode.agent-loop.test.ts:303`: the existing "preserves native exec refusal diagnostics" test now runs with the same synthetic secret-store entry and checks `warningText` on its completed results (exit 0 and exit 7) from real child processes through Code Mode. The secret-store warning string is one constant (line 45) shared with the running-result test.
- `bash-tools.exec.approval-id.test.ts:302`: the two node routes of "routes node=... host=... through node" now check `warningText` in the details beside the existing text check.
- `bash-tools.exec-host-node-phases.test.ts:79`: the existing node invoke-failure test passes a warning and checks `warningText`.

Checks: the touched tests (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, wall time per file in the table below); `bash-tools.exec-foreground-failures.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-host-node.integration.test.ts` and `session-tool-result-guard.test.ts`; oxlint and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files, `pnpm tsgo:test:src`; the broad suites run in this PR's CI. Vitest ran on Node 24.22.1.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall at `d7928d7f9b3` | CI seconds at `7cc63e3d46d` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/agents/code-mode.agent-loop.test.ts` | 16.6 s (17 tests) | 10.2 s (`checks-node-changed-16`) |
| `src/agents/bash-tools.exec.approval-id.test.ts` | 12.4 s (21 tests) | 10.9 s (`checks-node-changed-14`) |
| `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node-phases.test.ts` | 8.2 s (16 tests) | 7.8 s (`checks-node-changed-12`) |

The CI seconds come from the run on the previous head. `d7928d7f9b3` removes one Code Mode test and adds no test, so the new run should take the same time or less.

Test lines: the tree is already over the ratchet ceiling before this PR, so the checker accepts only a change whose net delta is zero or below. The previous head added 13 lines and failed `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (CI: 6,314,062 test lines against a ceiling of 6,313,024). `d7928d7f9b3` folds the Code Mode check into the existing refusal-diagnostics test and keeps the node checks inside existing tests. Run locally, `scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts` now reports "Test lines: 6311220; ceiling: 6310180; over by: 1040; net delta: -2. Tree is over the ceiling; this change does not add test lines." The two ceilings differ because the checker reads the baseline and allocations from the tree it runs on: locally the branch on `65acdfd629e`, in CI the PR merged into a later `main` (`961129f5dc5`).

Follow-ups, not in this PR: `process` poll results after a background start do not repeat `warningText` (the program already received it on the running result), and the warning text and `warningText` are assembled separately in each exec result builder.


## Merge Danger

Two-way door: revert restores prior structured-warning omission; no configuration, schema, execution-policy or published SDK migration. Blast radius is terminal exec result details consumed by CodeMode, on local and paired-node producers. Existing visible warning text and failure classification stay intact. Detached completion transport (#185436) is outside this change.

prs.title: fix: recover oversized reply attachments through Files
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an assistant saves a file successfully but its reply attachment exceeds the existing delivery limit, the chat can show a generic delivery failure and suggest trying again. The unchanged file will fail again, even when the user can already access the saved output through Files. The failure also loses the distinction between a size refusal and a transient delivery problem.

## User Impact

Oversized reply attachments get a native attachment card with the filename, the message “Too large to attach. Look for this file in Files.”, and a **Find in Files** action when the current chat supports it. The action opens the existing Files browser with a filename search. Users deliberately select a result, inspect its location, and use the existing preview or download action. A filename is a search aid; it is never treated as proof of a file's identity or location.

The action preserves open previews and unsaved drafts and is withheld for attachments attributed to another session or agent. Existing access checks still decide whether a file can be listed or read, including after permissions change. Size limits, file formats, saved bytes, and successful small attachments are unchanged. Older text clients retain a visible warning through the existing display-text fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

The media loaders did not consistently preserve typed size failures: the local byte-limit path threw a generic error, and the remote reader failed before returning enough information for the host to classify the refusal. The existing reply preparation owner now recognizes the existing typed size errors and emits a distinct attachment failure. An oversized remote file returns bounded metadata without reading its body; the host validates that response and issues the typed refusal. The existing finalization function shares the unoptimized image/document byte check and result construction, preserving image-specific limits and dimension validation without adding another layer.

The SSH workspace reader also preserves its actual bounded-read error without parsing diagnostic text. Older-client text fallback is projected by the Gateway, keeping server reply metadata out of the browser startup graph.

The Control UI uses the size distinction to offer the existing Files search instead of an identical retry. Search stays with the current session's Files owner, which checks the captured connection and workspace identity before loading results. Recovery does not add a download endpoint, a persistent file locator, or an access grant. The documentation describes the search and explicit selection step.

## Evidence

A native assistant produced a valid ZIP above the effective 5 MiB reply limit and a small sample ZIP. Before this change, the large attachment showed a generic failure while Files could download the original ZIP intact; the small sample delivered normally. A separate isolated reproduction traced the local failure through the byte-limit check and exercised the real remote workspace reader.

Changed-file formatting, lint, the UI catalog check, selected compiler graphs, and the test-line check passed. The 302 selected test files produced 301 passing file entries and 5,679 passing assertions; one platform-specific file and five tests were skipped. After simplifying the media finalization owner, its 29 related files were rerun: 529 assertions passed, with the same platform skip; unaffected earlier results remain applicable. The three regression cases fail on the original owners and pass with this change: typed remote rejection, real ZIP delivery with a healthy small-file control, and the unchanged text-client reader. UI tests cover the action, session attribution, stale connections, preserved drafts, ambiguous results, and deliberate file selection.

The aggregate test command retains one inherited failure: the uncaught Node 24.22.1 / Undici 7.30.1 data-URL abort error tracked in #188084. The unchanged attachment test reproduces the same error on the exact base and this candidate, with all 30 assertions passing in each run. Its fetch and cleanup owners are unchanged. No assertion or cleanup was suppressed, and this PR does not claim to fix that runtime error.

The first hosted build identified a startup regression: chat boot required 23 JavaScript requests versus 20 on the matched base. Moving the compatibility projection to the Gateway removes the extra browser imports. The corrected candidate passes `pnpm ui:check-performance:base 6fdd9aaf60cd92cdc967016ff419a029bbe716a3`: 20 chat boot requests, 1,272,942 gzip bytes, and every existing startup, JavaScript-byte and CSS budget intact. The native pair uses the declared Vite 8.3.4 toolchain; fresh hosted CI must also pass its merged toolchain. This is a deterministic build comparison, not a latency claim.

Independent review identified an additional SSH source-limit path. The real pinned Python reader and reply normalizer reproduced the generic failure at 25,165,825 bytes against a 25,165,824-byte source cap; the corrected path produces the size-specific warning while the small ZIP still delivers. The strengthened existing reader test fails on the original owners and passes on the correction. The correction batch passed 1,268 assertions across 63 executed test files, with 17 native skips; an opt-in live cron consumer was not run because its imported predicate and provider behavior are unchanged. SSH transport is source-qualified; this is not a newly executed SSH-network/model turn.

A real guest on the first published head used **Find in Files**, selected the saved ZIP, and downloaded all 80,000 rows with bytes matching the original. The healthy sample also matches its saved source. At 400px width, Tab reaches the filename-specific action and Enter opens the expected Files search. Current-head desktop/mobile media, draft preservation, independent recheck, required automated review, and hosted CI remain pending. This PR is not ready to land until those obligations are complete.

prs.title: fix(sqlite): size the worker store budget from the configured agent roster
prs.body:
Related: #162497

## What Problem This Solves

`SqliteWorkerBroker` caps concurrent SQLite worker stores at a hard-coded `MAX_STORES = 64`, and the broker is a **process-global singleton** (`resolveGlobalSingleton(Symbol.for("openclaw.sqliteWorkerBroker"), ...)`). Every agent in one Gateway process shares that single budget, and the count only grows with the number of distinct agents the Gateway has touched.

A Gateway with more than 64 agents therefore refuses new store opens for the tail of the fleet. The rejection is `SQLite worker store capacity reached` with code `overloaded`, so it is treated like a provider overload: the fallback chain runs and the user sees "The model provider returned a temporary internal error before replying". Nothing in the message points at the real cause, and the advice in the error text ("run openclaw doctor --fix ... and restart") names the wrong target - the agent databases are healthy.

There is also no knob. The cap is a literal in `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.ts`, and the same literal bounds the pending-open queue (`maxPendingOpens`), so a fleet larger than 64 is refused during startup preparation as well as during normal turns.

This change makes the store budget configurable and sizes the default from the configured agent roster, so a Gateway can serve a fleet larger than 64 without editing `dist/`.

## User Impact

- A Gateway with more than 64 configured agents stops refusing store opens for the tail of the fleet. The budget now defaults to `max(64, 2 * configured agent count)`.
- Operators can set an explicit bound with `database.sqlite.maxStores` when the automatic size is not what they want.
- A single-agent Gateway keeps the historical limit of 64, so resource use on small installs is unchanged.
- The budget is published from the runtime config and read by the broker on every open, so a config reload can raise it without restarting the Gateway. Lowering it stops new stores until the live count falls below the new value; stores that are already open are not force-closed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The merged reclamation fix (#164477) releases idle shared-state handles, and the startup retry candidate (#173994) stops a temporary rejection from becoming a terminal degradation. Neither of them changes the bound itself: the live store count still grows monotonically with the number of distinct agents touched inside one Gateway process, so the 65th distinct agent is refused no matter how many stores were reclaimed in between.

Deriving the budget from the configured roster removes the fleet-size cliff without removing the bound, and the explicit override gives operators a deterministic handle when the automatic size is wrong. The pending-open queue follows the same budget, because a fleet that cannot open stores cannot start its agents either.

## Evidence

- The budget is read from the same process-global broker that produces the failure: `MAX_STORES` gated both the store reservation (`reserveSqliteWorkerClient`) and the pending-open admission.
- New unit coverage in `src/config/sqlite-worker-max-stores.test.ts` pins the default (64 without config), the derived size (220 for a 110-agent roster), the explicit override (192), the rejection of invalid limits, and the published-budget round trip.
- New broker coverage in `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.capacity.test.ts` opens two stores against a published limit of two and asserts that the third open fails with `SQLite worker store capacity reached` / `overloaded`.
- New config coverage in `src/config/zod-schema.database.test.ts` accepts `database.sqlite.maxStores` and rejects out-of-range values.
- Focused tests: `pnpm test src/config/sqlite-worker-max-stores.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.capacity.test.ts src/config/zod-schema.database.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` - 43 tests across 3 files, all passing (13 infra + 30 runtime-config).
- `pnpm tsgo:core` - clean. Import-cycle check - 0 runtime value cycles.
- Scoped oxlint over the 10 changed files - 0 warnings, 0 errors; none of them appear in the `src/` failure list either.
- The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is not green on this repository and was not green before this change: `extensions/tlon`, `extensions/crabbox` and `ui/` carry pre-existing `max-lines`/unused-directive findings, and a scoped `src/` pass reports 7 pre-existing errors in files this diff does not touch (`src/agents/sessions/session-manager.ts`, `src/gateway/node-registry-private.ts` and 5 others).

## Notes

- The broker file already sat near the repository's `max-lines` budget (700 non-blank lines, 686 before this change), so the budget plumbing deliberately lives outside the class: the config layer publishes the resolved value and the broker only reads it.
- The `auto-response` CI job fails on this PR with a bot-side `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'owner')` in `scripts/github/barnacle-auto-response.mjs`. It is unrelated to this diff.

## What Problem This Solves

The one-shot CLI exit tests repeatedly load TypeScript source in fresh child processes; the proxy regression dominates this file's CI body time.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes. The same process-level regression coverage runs faster after the CI worker prepares its shared compiled graph.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing compiled one-shot finalizer and already registered runtime, snapshot, logging, and rejection-handler entries. Register only the missing argv and proxy owners through the existing declaration/build workflow, following #188977. Each probe still starts a fresh child, with the original environment isolation, timeout, output buffer, and assertions.

Simplification removes repeated source URL setup and turns the existing single-row default-success table into an equivalent direct test. All 18 cases remain. Production delta: 0 lines; native test LF delta: 0 (target 384→379, helper 245→250); build registry: +2 non-test lines. The scalar and every grant remain unchanged. Times are seconds. Import self/total is the runner's nested import breakdown, not an additional wall-time component. RSS is KiB.

The first candidate run includes 33.085 seconds of cold worker compilation, paid once per CI worker and shared with other compiled-process tests. No assertion, case, timeout, grace, or process boundary was removed. The default-success assertion remains in the direct test with `beforeEach` still resetting `process.exitCode`.

Temporary source-owner mutations failed at the intended assertions and were restored byte-for-byte:

- Replacing the recorded process failure with zero failed the real proxy status assertion.

Scoped typecheck of the target/helper/registry and their imports, type-aware core and registry lint, format, diff, line-cap/max-lines/test-LF, timeout, mock-export, and assertion-safety ratchets all passed. `pr-simplify` completed. prs.title: fix(feishu): accept the documented markdown table mode
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes gateway startup rejecting Feishu's documented `markdown.tables` option and applies the selected table mode across sends, replies, presentations, and previews.

## User Impact

Channel and account table settings are accepted, including the delivering/default account. Ordinary `off` table messages settle as authored rich-text posts. In `off`, presentations keep controls and show literal rows in card text and live previews. When idle close reuses a posted answer, missing reasoning follows it without duplicating it.

Accepted-prefix failures keep their receipts and do not replay accepted content. The unchanged post renderer still draws authored Markdown tables as grids.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu's strict schema gains the shared table option and keeps the legacy `markdown.mode` and `markdown.tableMode`. Formatting-aware delivery converts whole logical tables before chunking. Presentations and reasoning degrade undrawable block-mode tables to readable lists. For `off`, display-only delimiter escaping leaves authored fallback and deduplication text alone. The PR also declares `block` as Feishu's table default (see Table default).

The generated channel baseline gains two entries, `channels.feishu.markdown.tables` and `channels.feishu.accounts.*.markdown.tables`. Core and plugin counts stay unchanged. [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f659a3576b1/AGENTS.md#L96) permits narrow source-verified exceptions with a reason. This exception is not maintainer approval.

## Evidence

### Upgrade proof

Published stable `2026.10.2` (`b8952d477f0c`) seeded channel `markdown.mode: native` and `markdown.tableMode: ascii`, an account's `mode: escape` and `tableMode: simple`, and two accounts without Markdown settings. The proof head (`effbf8c7a8ab`) used that state, main (`29fc232d40be`) a copy. Both used fresh detached worktrees and separately packed Feishu plugins.

| Check | Stable | Proof head | Upstream main |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Legacy config validates, keys and overrides read back unchanged | Yes | Yes, before and after migration | Yes, before and after migration |
| Feishu config object on disk | Seed | Byte-identical | Byte-identical |
| Stored session loads with the same key and ID, and a label update survives restart | Created and patched here | Yes | Yes |
| Documented `markdown.tables` at channel and account scope | Rejected, exit 1 | Accepted, all four values | Rejected, exit 1 |
| Account override wins, unset accounts inherit the channel value | Key rejected | Yes | Key rejected |

Both builds refuse the schema 24 agent database (Gateway exit 78) until `openclaw doctor --fix` migrates it to 26. Repair and shutdown then exit 1 with `ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE`. The cause is undiagnosed and both databases stay readable. This is compatibility evidence, not a clean upgrade. Replacement was manual, not the published updater. Credentials were synthetic and Feishu accounts and transports disabled. Only the Feishu config object is byte-identical. Maintenance changed other config. The diff has no `src/state` change or database migration.

### Table default

Upgrade proof resolves `code` on stable and main and `block` on the proof head for unconfigured or legacy-only accounts. Legacy keys do not select the mode. In `auto`, stable and main route ordinary pipe-bordered tables to raw cards (`markdown.ts:25-27`, `outbound.ts:253-262`, `reply-dispatcher.ts:1289-1293` at main `29fc232d40be`, same logic at stable). Before captures show native grids. `block` retains them. Other modes convert before routing (`outbound-text-plan.ts:48-49`). Head lines use `948b2088919`.

Against main, standalone pipe-less and one-sided-pipe tables now get cards on `auto` sends and non-streamed replies. In chat text, blockquoted and list-opened tables take posts, but forced-card sends bypass that guard. Main sent these shapes to cards in streams or beside a fence or pipe table. Table messages needing multiple static cards also take posts. These posts use `code` unless fences cannot survive the cut. The five-table limit excludes streams. Direct post sends and edits still resolve `code`. Comments now convert raw rows to `code`. Explicit modes and size/fence safeguards apply.

A `code` default would fence those grids in cards (the `code` row at `outbound.markdown-tables.test.ts:640`, line 662 at `948b2088919`). `block` also drops "Avoid Markdown tables." from Feishu group prompts, even with account `code` or `bullets`, because `src/auto-reply/reply/groups.ts:126-131` reads the plugin default. Telegram and Matrix already declare `block`. Maintainers decide the default.

### Current repair verification

CI tested `cf49e1d3c83` merged with main `0858cc64613`. On that head 88 checks passed, none failed, 49 were skipped and CodeQL was neutral. In `checks-node-changed-1`, `telegram-ingress-coalescing.e2e.test.ts` passed 20 tests, and the shard's seven other targets, six contract tests and a gateway e2e test, passed 115. Locally at `cf49e1d3c83`, `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test`, four ratchets and five generated-file check scripts passed, and `extension-feishu` passed 1256 tests.

### Fresh Lark before/after rendering

[Comparison and limits](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-6093982920) cover four byte-identical synthetic fixture pairs through the production send, reply and streaming components with the real SDK. Captures compare plugin source `e7f29073f4dc` with rendering files published at `34f132a1bb49`, not whole deployments, and were not retaken at `effbf8c7a8ab`. Merges after `34f132a1bb49` left `presentation-card.ts`, `card-table-shapes.ts`, `markdown.ts` and `outbound.ts` unchanged, kept the off-mode projection in `streaming-update.ts`, and moved the reasoning formatter and close route into `reasoning-structure.ts` and `table-routing.ts` intact, so the three off-mode rows render through the same code. The idle row's settlement bookkeeping took upstream's latest-settlement shape, so that row rests on the proof head's regression tests, not the captures.

| State | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Off-mode presentation | ![Native table despite off mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff00b807-a9e6-465b-9f63-5829ea331710) | ![Literal rows and retained button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/96bf5ced-1f4e-4375-985f-cf0a9ab4132f) |
| Off-mode answer preview | ![Native answer-preview table](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e54aec3f-9a7c-41a7-886d-145522b8feed) | ![Literal answer-preview rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02c9e642-b5dd-4203-a3cf-87be4de7f7aa) |
| Off-mode reasoning preview | ![Reasoning-table rows missing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/325f6680-67b2-4de6-99f7-a93a0eb9afb1) | ![Reasoning-table rows visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c07ea2c4-df53-4628-9793-8e1946bbf661) |
| Idle reuse of accepted answer | ![Reasoning disappears after idle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4087a562-8abe-4253-8517-ac947981a16c) | ![One answer and separate reasoning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/430c18ca-2774-45cc-9055-44da9e169007) |

Both runs exited 0. Idle settlement adds exactly one reasoning-only post and keeps two actual receipts without replaying the accepted answer. All three dispatcher cases keep byte-identical authored final-post payloads. The button is retained, not clicked. All eight images were verified in the saved comment. The captures used no Gateway, model or mainland Feishu client. Lark still joins adjacent quoted paragraphs in the reasoning preview, not addressed here.

### Historical evidence

Pinned to the commits named, not current-head proof.

- CLI at `dbb422c85a5` (before) and `08c0c469de4` (after). Before, `config validate` rejected `tables` at channel and account scope (exit 1) and `gateway run` refused to start (exit 78). After, validation passed, the Gateway reached ready and shut down with child exit 0, and `doctor --fix --non-interactive` removed no `markdown` key.
- Gateway send RPC at `314ddb95`, HTTPS Feishu stub, real SDK, `renderMode` unset. Accounts resolved `code`, `bullets` and `off` as configured across full, reply and default-account sends, all exit 0.
- Authority proof at `c311d8a5d53` ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-5707888042)), registered sender, production components, real SDK. Allowed sent four of four with every receipt. Revoked after one of four was accepted, kept its receipt and exact content in the partial-delivery envelope, and the claim guard refused the pending terminal rather than replay it.
- Lark client round at `9d52663f11b` and `d0f6e3a3ba0` ([comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-5689525610)), real SDK, 62 captures. Blockquote and list-opened tables became readable fenced posts, and a mixed message kept both tables.
- Regression tests for schema acceptance, account selection, off-mode finals, comment delivery, block posts, preview dedupe and presentation cards each failed before the fix and passed after.

prs.title: feat: edit verified pull requests without preparing source
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Editing a pull request's title or description currently requires a prepared PR workspace or a completed publication in the conversation. The tool rejects an explicit PR URL before verification, so an unavailable or failed source preparation also blocks a metadata-only request.

## User Impact

The existing `github_publish` edit action accepts `pullRequestUrl` in a conversation with no workspace. Guests can edit a verified PR they own, and current authorized maintainers can help through the existing inspection policy. An explicit URL selects that PR for the request and preserves any existing conversation workspace or PR association.

Callers read the metadata first, then repeat the URL with the observed head commit and expected title or body. The existing concurrent-edit checks and attribution protection still apply. This action does not import source, commit changes, push a branch, or change the PR's state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The edit action now resolves an explicit target through the existing verified PR inspector and uses its observed details in the existing metadata-edit path. That keeps target identity, current-requester authorization, field preconditions and uncertain-response reconciliation together. Metadata edits can proceed when the source fork is gone or source-push permission is unavailable, provided the PR can still be verified and GitHub accepts the metadata operation.

This contribution builds on merged #188784 for current maintainer eligibility and the imported-PR receipt boundary. It adds no persistent PR association or separate permission policy. Canonical tool guidance and GitHub identity documentation describe the explicit read/write contract.

## Evidence

On the baseline, the regression exercised the real tool and registered Gateway action and failed at the explicit-URL rejection; all 16 existing owner cases passed. A real guest conversation with no workspace also reproduced that refusal for both an explicit read and a conditional body edit, with the PR and conversation unchanged.

Focused formatting, lint, the affected Gateway test-type graph, and all 78 cases in the action, adoption, tool and prompt-prefix files passed for the unchanged metadata implementation. These results remain qualified across the required prerequisite rebase. These checks exercise genuine workspace-free sessions, explicit target precedence, public/private maintainer edits followed by guest denial, unauthorized or stale targets, unavailable source repositories, and reconciliation after a lost write response. External GitHub I/O is synthetic in the owner tests; session and requester ownership use the real registered path. Unchanged schema and consumer checks retain their earlier passing results.

The single-worker action file passed 33 cases in 81.89 seconds; the adoption consumer passed four cases in 63.36 seconds. Both retain their existing real session/Gateway fixtures. The change funds its exact 230 net test lines. Earlier CI against the prior stacked base failed the aggregate test budget by 1,042 lines. The main rebase includes the upstream budget repair and the existing correction for a stale cron UI expectation seen in the previous run. Current-base CI remains required.

Live candidate proof and paired visual evidence, independent review, and hosted CI remain pending. The baseline media will be paired with the verified candidate result before landing.

prs.title: fix(android): make sidebar session parentage explicit
prs.body:
Related: #150054 — Android-specific context: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150054#issuecomment-5848447065

## What Problem This Solves

Android needs an unambiguous choice between starting a new root chat and creating a child of the selected chat. Previously, implicit Gateway parentage could make a supposedly independent chat a child, while explicit children and grandchildren could appear at root in Threads.

## User Impact

- The sidebar header **+** starts an independent root session. There is no second, competing independent-session button.
- The selected eligible session's overflow menu offers **New child session**. Children and grandchildren retain their hierarchy in Threads.
- Existing sessions are not migrated or reparented. Connection, busy-state, write-access, and selected-parent guards remain.
- These creation actions require a Gateway supporting the new intent fields. An older Gateway gets an update-required error; the app does not silently fall back to different parentage.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair carries explicit child intent through creation, persisted session metadata, reset preservation, list/describe/event projection, and Android rendering. Ordinary New sends `independent: true`; child creation sends `explicitChild: true` with the selected parent. Existing upstream standalone/direct-chat behavior and visibility admission remain intact.

The public API rejects conflicting independent/parent intent and adoption of existing keys. A review-discovered edge case is also fixed: explicit child creation without a key cannot take the main-session reset shortcut and reset its parent.

This is an Android proposal, not a web Control UI `/new` change. **Maintainer acceptance of the public `sessions.create` fields and Android product behavior remains separate from this repair.** No upstream merge is requested by this update.

## Evidence

Repair commit: `6a07b12ac85ece37ddaf80a002266969ddcd29eb`.
Integrated upstream: `54c3474691a6adc971056be145135d9146289394`. The update preserves the previously published head as its first parent; it is not a force push.

### Fresh focused validation

- **17 Gateway lifecycle tests passed**, including independent roots, explicit child/grandchild persistence and projection, reset retention, conflicting intent, and existing-key rejection. The new no-key child regression failed before the reset fix and passed afterward; it verifies a distinct child, unchanged parent entry, child metadata, and no parent-end hook.
- **2 inheritance-owner tests and 13 session-entry projection contract tests passed.**
- **69 Android tests passed**: controller creation (5), sidebar/Threads UI (2), grouping (24), and command controls (38). Production/test compilation and `:app:ktlintCheck` passed.
- Targeted TypeScript lint, Gateway-server typecheck, formatting, native-string inventory, canonical Gateway validator regeneration, and whitespace checks passed.
- Independent read-only code review covered the complete candidate. Its one actionable finding—the no-key child reset path—was fixed, regression-tested, and reviewed again. The standalone autoreview CLI could not authenticate; the independent review ran through the connected coding-agent session instead. No standalone-autoreview success is claimed.
- A normal hook-enabled merge commit was created in a secretless container, with exact tree and both parents verified. Merge-mode hook behavior is not a claim that all ordinary-commit checks ran.

Gateway checks used isolated repository harnesses and the repository-supported Node/oxlint fallback because the pinned Bun runtime could not be staged in the offline proof environment. Android dependency hydration/build used a task-owned secretless container. Full hosted CI is separate; earlier failed checks belong to the old head and are not represented as cleared by these local results.

### Before / after

Inspected synthetic Compose test renders, not connected-device screenshots. The historical before image shows the redundant root action and inline child action. The repaired sidebar uses one header New action plus the selected row's overflow menu. Minor speckling in the sidebar render is a test-raster artifact; incidental navigation ordering is not the claimed change.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: redundant independent action and inline child action](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/0e0a214538c4414432318b4ec46e251964e14696/20261031-before.png) | ![After: one header New action and selected-row overflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/0e0a214538c4414432318b4ec46e251964e14696/20261031-after.png) |

![Selected-row menu: New child session](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/0e0a214538c4414432318b4ec46e251964e14696/20261031-child-menu.png)

![Threads: Project, Child, and Grandchild remain nested; Ordinary New is a separate root](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/0e0a214538c4414432318b4ec46e251964e14696/20261031-threads.png)

### Scope and remaining limits

No new APK installation or live Android-to-Gateway device test was performed. Public-handler and rendering tests prove the scoped boundaries, not a full deployed-version upgrade matrix. [Earlier contributor-reported device evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/159159#issuecomment-5901361888) predates this candidate and is not exact-head proof. The full cross-platform suite was not rerun locally; current-head CI and maintainer review remain merge gates.

The repair uses the existing creation, lineage, projection, and reset owners rather than adding a parallel hierarchy manager. Its necessary growth is the explicit intent contract and boundary regressions; most generated-code churn is canonical predicate renumbering.

prs.title: fix(macos): run bundle copy off the main thread during self-install
prs.body:
## Problem

When OpenClaw is launched under **App Translocation** (the `com.apple.quarantine` xattr is still present on `/Applications/OpenClaw.app`), `handleLaunch()` falls into the `.offerInstall` path and calls `install()` **synchronously on the main thread**.

`copyItem()` on a 2 GB+ bundle blocks `applicationDidFinishLaunching` for minutes:
- No menu bar icon appears, no window opens
- CPU sits at 200–286 % continuously
- The process **cannot be terminated with SIGTERM** because the main thread is stuck in a kernel `write()` syscall — only `kill -9` works
- macOS generates a diagnostic report showing ~2.1 GB written in 40 s

Root cause and stack trace are documented in #134736.

## Changes

1. **`install()` is now `async`** — `copyItem` runs in a `Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated)` so the main thread can finish launching and present UI. `replaceItemAt` / `moveItem` stay on the main actor. Partial-copy and backup deletes are awaited off the main thread before exit.

2. **`.offerInstall` uses the existing activation-aware `confirmInstall`** (`AppActivation.shared.presentAlert`). When the confirm alert is answered before `handleLaunch` returns, the result is `.installing` and startup waits. If the copy fails, the failure alert is shown and the temporary app continues: menu, dock, and gateway start from that copy, matching a declined install. If the copy succeeds but the relaunch helper cannot be spawned, that process still quits, because the Applications copy is already installed and the alert tells the user to open it. A deferred `--no-activate` confirmation still returns `.continueLaunch` and does not terminate a session that already started.

3. **Relaunch** keeps the current activation-aware helper (`open` with `-g` / `--no-activate` when activation is disallowed).

4. **Progress copy** uses `String(localized:)` and is inventoried in `apps/.i18n/native-source.json` (catalog / locale JSON left to the native locale refresh).

## Testing

- Nesting-guard unit tests were removed with the unused staging containment surface (`isPath(_:nestedIn:)` / `UnsafeCopyDestinationError`); ClawSweeper withdrew that finding as unused surface when staging is under Applications.
- `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passed on Linux. `pnpm native:i18n:check` still reports untranslated locale rows for the two new progress strings; those catalogs belong to the native locale refresh.
- No Swift toolchain was available in the Linux agent environment, and no macOS offer-install recording is attached (fresh install / replacement / failure on a real Mac remain unproven).

## Risk

- Normal activation no longer blocks `applicationDidFinishLaunching` on the multi-GB copy. The transient bundle does not start gateway, menu, or onboarding while copying; the progress window stays up until relaunch or a failure alert (after which the temporary app continues launching).
- `FileManager.copyItem` work runs in a detached task with a task-local `FileManager()`; awaited cleanup avoids abandoning multi-GB staging/backup deletes on quit.
- A deferred `--no-activate` approval does not terminate an already-started session.

Fixes #134736

prs.title: fix: persist mock Gateway preferences across reloads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated preference migrations in Control UI performance fixtures after an acknowledged save or reload. The mock returned a static preference snapshot, accepted writes without storing them, and omitted the native preference-change notification.

## User Impact

There is no production UI behavior change. Readiness benchmarks and mock-Gateway tests now observe successful preference writes and the refresh work triggered by their notifications.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing serialized mock Gateway now owns preference state by admitted hello profile and normalized Gateway endpoint. Its immediate and deferred response paths share the same compare-and-set commit, persist accepted writes in session storage, and notify matching connections after the response. Explicit scripted responses and custom handlers retain their literal behavior.

The preference owner follows the existing serialized presence/reaction fixture pattern. The unchanged scenario normalizer and its type now live together, keeping the transport helper below its line cap without a circular type import. The theme-selection scenario explicitly retains its manually supplied profile snapshots instead of relying on the old unspecified-read fallback.

The team-scale fixture seeds its original rail preferences through the bootstrap input instead of static RPC responses. It does not seed a migration marker. This is a single-context server simulation; it does not model cross-tab sharing or canonical-profile aliases.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Serialized mock wire tests | 3 passed; 2.12 s file duration, 120 ms test execution; unchanged proof reused |
| Theme-selection E2E regression | 1 passed; 24.49 s file duration, 3.45 s test execution |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed |
| Targeted type-aware lint and format | Passed for all corrected TypeScript files |
| Madge import-cycle guard | Passed; 0 cycles |
| Staged test-line ratchet | Passed against original base; exact 474-line allocation |
| Independent review | Complete; no actionable P0–P2 findings in the full candidate and CI corrections |
| Full UI coverage | [41164750726](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41164750726) passed on `1f2714e4e62`: all 3 UI unit shards, all 7 UI E2E shards, both real-Gateway shards, architecture/guard checks, lint, and typechecks; `openclaw/ci-gate` passed |

Initial CI run [41159209533](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41159209533) passed UI units, typechecks, and lint. It caught the new type-import cycle and the theme fixture's old implicit-read assumption; both are corrected here. Two other initial failures match exact names and assertions in scheduled main run [41155320395](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41155320395):

- `Control UI cron saved descriptions E2E > configured duration precision: shows exact saved intervals in rows and details` — detail text includes `· Paused`.
- `Plugin settings keyboard dismissal > lets the Settings sidebar clear its search without closing plugin details` — Escape navigates to `/chat/main`.

The replacement run is fully green; no inherited-failure exception is needed.

The existing readiness captures independently demonstrated accepted migrations repeating because their marker never survived the fixture. The new tests cover read-after-write and reload persistence, compare-and-set conflicts, deletion, profile/endpoint event isolation, deferred success/rejection, and literal scripted outcomes. They do not prove browser readiness or a production performance improvement. The affected warm audit must be rerun with the corrected fixture.

No rendered styles, markup, route, startup import, or production bundle changed, so screenshots and startup-byte measurements are not applicable.

Touched test/support LOC: **3,640 → 4,114 (+474)**, including 215 lines of new wire tests. The transport helper shrinks **2,717 → 2,524 (−193)**. Production LOC: **unchanged**. The two-line allocation records only this change's growth.

prs.body:
Related: #180969

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on Windows, the built-plugin singleton smoke can pass its assertions and then exit 1 because its temporary home is deleted while source-capture SQLite leases remain open.

## User Impact

Developers can finish the smoke command with its temporary home removed. Assertion failures, cancellation exit codes and cleanup failures remain visible. Production Gateway and channel behavior are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The capture owner already retires process-owned leases at exit. Register fixture-home removal after the loader imports so it runs after that cleanup. Keep the existing synchronous removal and every smoke assertion.

Test tooling only: one file, +5/-1 lines; no production changes, retries, permission changes or new lifetime owner. The separate SDK prototype is excluded.

## Evidence

- **Native built smoke:** Windows 11 x64 build 26300, Node 26.12.0, isolated beta.3-based candidate `5b9a5c9b4d278ebe27f3fe4c7af5cd93d3efc26a`, unchanged runtime/build artifacts. Before: success marker, then cleanup EPERM, exit 1 (50.191 s). After: exit 0 (55.096 s). The existing SMS forced-retirement warning remained visible.
- **Supplemental native Windows subprocess fixture:** exact current-script controller/catch/finally code with real SQLite/filesystem operations. Base success/error/cancellation all failed with EPERM and retained the home. The patch returned 0/1/143 respectively, retained the intentional error diagnostic, and removed all three homes. Smoke-body/dist-wrapper substitution makes this supplemental lifecycle proof, not full-smoke E2E.
- **Source identity:** base `dfe89efb322f8e1983f7683c538ca5a4544bd4eb`; unpatched script blob `9e260e89094254328bc1b98b21995886ec00b40a` matches the retained failing script.
- **Independent review:** canonical autoreview of the byte-identical one-file source slice and complete related current-main owners found no actionable P0–P2 defects.
- **Current-main source checks, portable Node 26.12.1:** syntax, formatting, scoped typed lint (0 warnings/errors, one file, 292 rules), full scripts typecheck, and `git diff --check` all pass. Dependencies were installed independently with the frozen lockfile; the host's global Node and service were unchanged.

**Limits:** the full built-smoke observation uses retained beta.3-based artifacts rather than a fresh current-main build. Hosted exact-head CI is separate and is not claimed green here. No production configuration, credentials, business data or running service changed.

prs.title: fix: keep chat images readable when switching session stores
prs.body:
Closes #188582

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chat images becoming unavailable after healthy custom `session.store` switches A→B→A, including the first download after returning.

## User Impact

Retained image history keeps its originals and downloads without a reload. Already-deleted originals are not recovered.

Maintainer decision requested before merge: is it acceptable for an unknown, unreadable, or incompatible registered source to defer orphan reclamation indefinitely until resolved? This proposal consults exact references in registered retained stores; serving remains selected-source-only. This retention scope has not yet been accepted by a maintainer.

## Why This Change Was Made

Absence from the selected store does not establish that retained physical stores have no references. Cleanup uses existing owner-held readers on misses and pass-local results.

After awaited media work, consumers prepare the same captured read lease, then synchronously recheck the original physical/session identity and current visibility before effect. They do not adopt replacement targets, retry requests, or expand serving access. No schema or writer changes.

## Evidence

Tested source tree committed as `5c75029d0009173084f4e6c793c99cacd24eee5b`, integrating fixed upstream `83064b3ae1155f0c6c96081c863e7db4bd4451f4` to resolve an actual conflict, not merely main advancing.

- Current seven-file family: **91/91 passed**, zero failed or pending, 904.41s Vitest wall time. Includes all four managed-readiness cases and both upstream GitHub authorization purposes.
- Current secretless Gateway replay: **1/1 passed**, 80.71s case / 277.96s Vitest wall time. Five fresh HTTP200 downloads matched the expected PNGs; first return-A download passed without reload/retry/model resend, history matched, and A-under-B was denied. Only model responses were synthetic; Gateway, agent execution, persistence, GC, grants and HTTP were real.
- The exact final readiness fixture on base `68b8bf7113245f6207c508a23f3dabea3badaad2`, with the eight PR production paths stock, failed the selected unchanged case at the intended preparation checkpoint (98.44s case / 319.25s wall). Three negative cases were filtered, not passed; all four pass on the fix. This is not a pristine-whole-checkout claim.
- Current Gateway root/methods types, type-aware lint, format, test-line allocation and 1,421-file MDX checks passed. A separate 539-line allocation covers distinct GC, first-read and identity/visibility regressions; the shared scalar is unchanged.
- Two independent non-author narrative P0–P3 source reviews found no actionable findings. CLI review was unavailable and produced no report; it is not recorded as a CLI pass.

External-model evidence remains explicitly historical: the real Bailian replay on `270e634c1cbdb0c40c92ef2919468af72d0d59e1` had one HTTP200 physical request each for A/B, flow and Gateway closure passed, blocked=0, and usage **unknown**. Upstream preparation, grant and transport code changed; this is not exact-current-head LIVE proof. No further inference was used for the integration replay. [Current PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188584/checks) supplies broad proof; current-head CI completion is not claimed here.

<details>
<summary>Inspectable redacted terminal excerpts and proof boundaries</summary>

These are actual captures, not a manually filled result table. JSON fields were whitelisted and reserialized; paths, identifiers, headers and content were omitted. The supporting private Gateway fixture is not a committed CI test. The permanent GC/readiness regressions are included in this PR.

Current integrated Gateway, in emitted order:


## What Problem This Solves

Tool labels and icons import the complete native display catalog, including argument-detail keys and action metadata they never read. Generate compact identity data and complementary detail data from the existing canonical config, and let each browser consumer import only its projection. The native catalog is unchanged.

This draft is unqualified and must not be merged: the retained current-base cohort fails local readiness. No performance acceptance is claimed. The attempted runtime co-location did not remove its request and is not included in this diff.

### Qualification rule, recorded before the current-main cohort

Run 20 serial counterbalanced base/base-control/head triplets per profile (localhost and 100 ms RTT at 10,000 kbps), with fresh process and HTTP cache for every observation. Keep every observation. Report independent A/A and B/H median/p95/range, script and task CPU, long tasks, readiness, and host load. The timing band is at most 5% median regression and no worse p95 (sub-1% p95 movement is noise unless confirmed); an affected-path regression beyond 20% blocks acceptance. No filtering, A/A subtraction, extra file prewarming, or interpreting a preload as bytes not downloaded. Capture coverage and compiler diagnostics separately from ordinary timing.

prs.title: fix(update): enable process-tree termination and signal forwarding in runUpdateStep
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a CLI-driven update step (`runUpdateStep` in `src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:218`) spawns a package-manager child tree (such as `npm i -g --prefix <stage-dir> openclaw@<version>`) that hangs in `ep_poll` and ignores `SIGTERM`, timeout or operator cancellation previously did not enable `killProcessTree: true` and `runStep` (`src/infra/update-runner-command.ts:65`) did not forward `signal?: AbortSignal` to the underlying command runner. Unlike `buildUpdateCommandRunner` (`src/infra/update-runner-command.ts:223`), which already sets `killProcessTree: true`, `runUpdateStep` dropped explicit `AbortSignal` cancellation and left `SIGTERM`-ignoring child and descendant processes alive instead of escalating through `createCommandTerminationController` (`src/process/exec-termination.ts:22`) to force-kill the process group and wait for descendant settlement.

### Root Cause & Architectural Fix

- **Architectural owner**: `src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts` (`runUpdateStep`), `src/infra/update-runner-command.ts` (`runStep`), and `src/infra/update-runner-types.ts` (`RunStepOptions`).
- **Canonical fix**:
  - Enable `killProcessTree: true` in `runUpdateStep`'s default runner (`src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:230`) while preserving caller-supplied `runCommand` overrides.
  - Add `signal?: AbortSignal` to `RunStepOptions` (`src/infra/update-runner-types.ts:98`), forward `signal` in `runStep` (`src/infra/update-runner-command.ts:96`), and derive `runUpdateStep`'s parameter type directly from `Parameters<typeof runStep>[0]` (`src/cli/update-cli/shared.ts:219`) so `runUpdateStep` forwards `signal` and stays in sync with `RunStepOptions`.
  - Removed all unrelated layout/expression changes so 100% of touched production lines are inside `runUpdateStep`, `runStep`, and `RunStepOptions`.
- **Production LOC delta**: Net `-1` line across 3 production files (`+11 / -12`), plus `+69` test lines in `src/cli/update-cli/shared.command-runner.test.ts`.

## Evidence

### 1. Shipped CLI Update Flow: Timeout / Cancellation Stopping a `SIGTERM`-Ignoring Tree Before Recovery + Latest-Stable Upgrade Preserving Settings & Data

I executed the CLI package-update entrypoint (`runPackageInstallUpdate` in `src/cli/update-cli/update-command-package.ts:484`) against a global npm prefix initialized at `openclaw@2026.10.5` with `openclaw.json` (`gateway.port: 18789`, `agents.defaults.model.primary: "openai/gpt-5.4"`) and `state/openclaw.sqlite` (`kv` row `operator-setting = preserved-across-upgrade`):

1. **CLI timeout/cancellation on a `SIGTERM`-ignoring `npm` + worker descendant tree**: During `package-install`, the `npm` process and its spawned worker both ignore `SIGTERM` and hang. Under the CLI timeout, `runUpdateStep` force-terminates the entire process tree (`npmPidExitedBeforeRecovery: true`, `workerPidExitedBeforeRecovery: true`), discards the staging directory, and verifies recovery of the existing `2026.10.5` installation (`recovery: { serviceRestartSafe: true, version: "2026.10.5" }`).
2. **Transient hang auto-recovery (`package-install` hangs -> killed -> fallback `package-install-omit-optional` succeeds)**: When only the first `npm i` hangs, the timeout kills the hung `SIGTERM`-ignoring tree and the fallback install completes `2026.10.5 -> 2026.10.10` (`status: "ok"`).
3. **Latest-stable upgrade (`2026.10.5 -> 2026.10.10`) with settings and data intact**: Upgrading to `2026.10.10` completes with `status: "ok"`, updates `package.json` to `2026.10.10`, and preserves both `openclaw.json` (`configIntact: true`) and `state/openclaw.sqlite` (`sqliteDataIntact: [{ key: "operator-setting", value: "preserved-across-upgrade" }]`).

```text
=== 1. CLI Timeout / Cancellation on SIGTERM-Ignoring npm Tree ===
{
  "status": "error",
  "reason": "global-install-failed",
  "failedStep": {
    "name": "package-install-omit-optional",
    "termination": "timeout",
    "exitCode": 1
  },
  "npmPidExitedBeforeRecovery": true,
  "workerPidExitedBeforeRecovery": true,
  "recovery": {
    "serviceRestartSafe": true,
    "version": "2026.10.5"
  }
}
=== 2. Latest-Stable Upgrade Preserving Settings and Data ===
{
  "status": "ok",
  "mode": "npm",
  "beforeVersion": "2026.10.5",
  "afterVersion": "2026.10.10",
  "installedPackageJsonVersion": "2026.10.10",
  "configIntact": true,
  "sqliteDataIntact": [
    {
      "key": "operator-setting",
      "value": "preserved-across-upgrade"
    }
  ]
}
```

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins requesting approval for an automation need a supported way to prepare its default tools against the creating turn's executable permissions.

## User Impact

The optional `ctx.prepareCronToolSelection` callback prepares the concrete tool selection before approval. It preserves explicit empty/null/omitted selections, exact opt-out, aliases, plugin groups and execution-target restrictions. Preparation neither creates an automation nor grants execution; consumers still own approval and adoption.

**This remains a draft: native tool availability is not fully qualified.** A supported custom-model configuration can expose no shell while the existing native projection infers `read`/`exec`. Complete native executor/route evidence and live consumer qualification remain required before adoption. A partial native bridge list is not proof of the full callable tool set.

## Why This Change Was Made

The callback reuses default selection, creator authority, plugin admission and invocation lifetime. Discovery is followed by current authority checks; expired or unavailable authority is rejected. The branch also preserves offered exec schemas independently of per-turn execution restrictions.

The latest repair closes a specific async completeness hole: when configured MCP authority is unresolved, successful app discovery must not certify the remaining dynamic tools as a complete automation selection. The async resolver now reuses the startup incompleteness predicate and rejects before app capture can recertify that partial list. This adds no public API or configuration and does not fix the separate native executor-evidence gap.

## Evidence

- Current source: `c48c481ada5e04f2697d905b375736fcbe04c469`. Fresh independent Codex-agent review of the two-file repair found no P0–P2 findings. The unchanged commit hook applied assertion wrapping only; production logic retained the reviewed bytes.

External app eligibility/capture is mocked; the attempt and resolver are real. **These new runtime cases and type checks have not run locally** because the required runner environment is not qualified within the host's build reserve. Current-head CI must execute them.
- Previous head `5f0f3c0e0ee43e02859a850486ac20997709f24a` passed [CI 41157417689](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41157417689). That is prior-head evidence, not qualification of this repair. Earlier CI exercised preparation/factory and completion-turn cases; the inherited library-read assertions were repaired by main #188090.

Closes #188875

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: plugin/agent-runtime `sessions.create` with `idempotencyKey` always fails with a generic identity error that reads like caller misconfiguration, with no supported alternative named.

## User Impact

Identity-only callers (including agent-runtime plugin tools) still get `INVALID_REQUEST`, but the message now tells them to use a deterministic session `key` instead. Authenticated principal, operator-run authority, and device callers are unchanged. Omitting `idempotencyKey` keeps ordinary create behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main intentionally rejects idempotent creates without a principal, operator run authority, or device id. The previous message did not explain that identity-only paths can never satisfy that check. This is error-clarity and docs only: no acceptance path, scope, or dedupe key shape changes.

## Evidence

### Error message before/after

**Before** (base):
```
idempotent session creation requires an authenticated principal or device identity
```

**After** (this PR):
```
idempotent session creation requires an authenticated principal or device identity; identity-only callers (including agent-runtime plugin tools) should use a deterministic session key instead
```

prs.title: fix(skills): clarify that Workshop reads do not authorize foreground repair
prs.body:
Closes #152285

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Skill Workshop's guidance omits that reading a skill and preparing a patch do not, by themselves, authorize a foreground repair, which misleads the model into thinking an unused skill can be patched in place.

## User Impact

User impact: models authoring skills get accurate guidance — a skill genuinely used earlier in the run can be repaired in place, while an unused skill must be changed through a staged update (or edited directly when the user owns it). The enforcement error message now explains the correct path instead of failing obscurely.

## Why This Change Was Made

The foreground-patch path requires the skill to have been used earlier in the run (a run-usage receipt). Workshop `read`/`prepare_patch` only establish the content and patch-span prerequisites, never that receipt. The three model-facing surfaces now state this explicitly:

- tool description (after the repair policy),
- the `patch` action's schema description,
- the enforcement error message in the foreground-patch guard.

This is a prompt-text/guidance-only fix — no guard logic or security behavior changes. The existing tests that assert the enforcement behavior (including the substring "was not used in this run") remain intact and pass.

## Evidence

**Merge/rebase state:** The branch has been brought up to date with current `main` via a merge commit; GitHub reports this PR as **mergeable (no conflicts)**, with a clean diff of only the three intended files (+3/−3). The three files were reconciled against the latest upstream wording, so this PR carries exactly the three guidance clarifications and nothing else.

**Focused tests pass (21 total),** including the three "enforces foreground repair receipts" cases (off / propose / auto) in `src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool.test.ts` and the two skill-authoring-standards tests in `src/skills/workshop/skill-authoring-standards.test.ts`. prs.title: fix(process): ease agent exec IO throttling on solid-state disks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes excessive throttling of agent commands on non-rotational Linux storage when delegated exec isolation derives disk bandwidth from RAM. A 4 GiB exec memory allowance currently permits only 6.8 MiB/s, regardless of the backing device.

## User Impact

Non-rotational state devices get an aggregate agent-exec ceiling of 160 MiB/s in each direction and 40,960 IOPS per direction, applied at Gateway startup. Gateway IO remains outside the exec ceiling. Rotational or unidentified devices retain the existing conservative policy, and finite ancestor limits still reserve half of each corresponding rate for peers. No new configuration or deployment action is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Choose the budget at the existing startup owner using the logical device's kernel rotational attribute. Keep md/dm at their existing accounting boundary without traversing or separately charging member devices. This removes RAM/device-count coupling for solid-state storage without adding startup disk benchmarks, caches, or an unmeasured latency-controller target.

Related: #188379.

## Evidence

- Acceptance: non-rotational limits are independent of RAM and device count; inherited limits and Gateway placement remain intact. The selected ceiling is a conservative policy, not a bandwidth measurement or SQLite latency guarantee.
- The two new startup-owner regression cases fail on the original code and pass after the fix. The original two-device fixtures wrote 524,288 and 42,047,590 bytes/s respectively instead of 167,772,160 per device.
- `pnpm test src/process/linux-exec-cgroup.test.ts src/process/linux-exec-cgroup-device.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 20 passed; 1.92s wrapper wall time, 647ms Vitest duration. Mixed-media inherited-limit and existing btrfs/md/dm/partition tests pass.
- Independent Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2. Author simplification pass complete. Production net +1 line for startup-only media classification; tests net +17, with an exact scoped test-line allowance.
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed (format, typechecks, lint, dead exports and repository guards). Exact staged test-line ratchet also passed. Unchanged-file lint warnings remain advisory.
- No disposable NVMe/btrfs host was immediately available. No SQLite commit-latency, CPU, allocation, or A/A benchmark claim is made. The operator explicitly selected the existing-observation fallback; verification under load remains for the next deployment.

The GitHub publication guide promises automatic recovery retries at four, eight, sixteen, and thirty minutes even though the recovery owner stops GitHub effect recovery after three failed attempts. Operators could keep waiting for retries that will never happen.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recovery owner distinguishes attempts to recover GitHub effects from settling the failed receipt. Its attempt count and cooldown reset on Gateway restart, while the durable receipt age still bounds failed recovery. The corrected paragraph preserves per-request cooldown and same-worktree ordering guidance without promising retries beyond that boundary.

## Evidence

Compared the paragraph with the recovery owner, shared coordinator, executor, and existing runtime cases for fresh and old receipts, restart, and deferred settlement. The patch changes only this paragraph; the separate PR metadata-edit recovery guidance is unchanged. Product tests and runtime flows are not rerun for this prose-only correction.

Image-preparation tools need a supported way to export the installed OpenClaw worker runtime and install transferred archives without enrolling a node. Prerequisite #188651 is merged; this PR targets main.

## User Impact

Tool authors can use `openclaw/runtime-artifacts` to qualify bundled plugins and export canonical offline node/worker archives. Crabbox's lazy CLI API installs verified local archives without a logical lease, forwarded credentials, npm, lifecycle scripts, or plugin activation. Bundle enrollment needs matching Node and tar; explicit npm installations and repository setup retain npm/npx/Corepack where applicable. Existing remote npm installations retain their lock/reuse behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The public entrypoint composes existing artifact producers, joins both before cleanup, and returns build, archive and digest identities. Bundled qualification uses a detached inspection registry. Local transfer is an adapter in the existing installer, not a second installer. Only `./runtime-artifacts` is added to package exports; declarations and documentation are included.

History-preserving integration retains upstream root/Codex fs-safe 0.27.0 and the source-inspection worker-boundary fix in #188870. The lock was regenerated with pinned pnpm; dependency graph and integrity data match upstream, with canonical ordering differences only. The `/node-runtime-dependencies/` artifact ignore and accurate troubleshooting prerequisites are restored. Read-only cache verification remains separate in #188671.

## Evidence

### Source and actual package/install proof

- Published head **`ef8db05fbb68184e71f414dacdf280f4286b9a31`** is tree-identical to reviewed source `dfb8d790b6f10de01da64324a95a4a91ac99ba83` (tree `313ea3ea3186283ef6516f18b2da8a1ad527e800`). The latest correction contains only the coordinated shared-logger fixture repair and its seven-line regression allocation. Runtime API, installer, packaging sources and dependency manifests/lock are unchanged by that fixture correction.
- Real package proof retains source **`49968f58492355540037ef88abf2eeeeb4e9fdc2`** and build **`2026.10.9-49968f584923-2026-10-31T02-16-02.503Z`**. No new full package build is claimed for the fixture-only correction. Maintained runtime-only selected-Codex packaging passed on Linux x64 / Node 24.22.1: build 224.2s; tar/extraction, npm inventory and distribution import-graph checks 96s.
- Built public `openclaw/runtime-artifacts` exported both core-only and legitimately qualified bundled-Codex archives. The parent's own built installer—not descendant verifier code—cold-installed each into a fresh offline home. Both real CLIs printed `OpenClaw 2026.10.9 (49968f5)`; installed fs-safe was 0.27.0. Archive sizes/digests, installed manifest and worker archive digests matched producer receipts. Installation plus CLI: core 4.94s, Codex 15.39s.
- Proof used secretless, network-isolated bwrap and Node 24.22.1. No enrollment state, forwarded credentials or cloud allocation; owned installation homes were removed. Earlier d4b533 evidence retains its original identity.

<details>
<summary>Canonical archive identities</summary>

- Core node: `b81d6da09244c20adb7251cba3749c4ba9e1f0ea17dfe81c7da5a596dd65f117` — 125,714,787 bytes.
- Codex node: `cebf783e4347ab296f3617435d85806a681297c01a917cedf834b3b653470571` — 292,392,923 bytes.
- Worker: `35d53a13ca5fdeedd18c5b0996f2ccfbe6d4ef3070925d552ec92180da3f1787` — 34,750,971 bytes.

</details>

### Regression, static checks and review

- Retained source `49968f5`: **78 focused tests pass** across the original consuming bootstrap case, public API, source inspection, worker/admission, install-batch authority, rollout scanning and offline installation. Targeted types, 12-file lint, formatting, docs sanity and diff checks pass.
- Existing upstream `3ebb7807` (#188870) resolves the bootstrap boundary failure without weakening its allowlist: in-scope capture preserves worker publication context and host admission settlement. The original generated-graph case is green with **one case executed, 61 skipped**. The earlier all-skipped run was not passing proof; the cross-test-contamination claim remains withdrawn.
- The watcher test-owner repair preserves real filesystem operations and exact membership assertions. Withheld final notifications fail the original oracle; controlled delivery with constant directory timestamps proves invalidation and cached reuse. Its original 247-case Codex invocation and the 20 owner cases pass. Native kernel notification timing remains unobserved; no production fence, sleep or weaker assertion was added.
- [CI job 124416178578](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41160183562/job/124416178578) was reproduced exactly on `9d193015`: **2 failed / 283 passed** in the original eight-file invocation (247.49s), both terminal hooks rejecting on `log.isEnabled`. Only the existing authority owner's two-file repair from `5b08bece95307fb413f0d3db7248d5cb6c19ab42` was adopted. It uses the complete typed logger and explicitly enables/restores diagnostics while preserving all original closure, admission and card-list assertions.
- The identical repaired invocation passes **285/285 tests across eight files** (201.15s). A single-worker focused run passes **30 shared Gateway scope-consumer cases** (16.27s) and **both Workboard cases** (12.90s; case times 867ms/283ms), with 68.62s total wrapper time. Runtime: Node 24.22.1 and CI-pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1`, in secretless network isolation.

Existing API **332** and watcher **19** allocations remain unchanged; the fixture adds exactly **7** literal newline bytes and a separate seven-line allocation. Current local accounting: **6,318,417 / 6,350,276**. No scalar, checker or baseline waiver.

No actionable findings. Earlier incomplete I/O-stalled attempts were not counted; no review or test evidence is relabeled to a different source.
