prs.title: fix(gateway): paired-node Claude continuations retain Gateway context
prs.body:
Closes #145636

## What Problem This Solves

A Claude CLI continuation on a healthy paired node can fail with a Gateway-runtime or capability error after its originating request ends. Detached work retains a live Gateway resolver but deliberately does not retain the direct request context.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two paired-node readers now use the existing resolver-first `getInProcessGatewayRequestContext` in the current request-scope owner. This integrates with main's `PluginRuntimeExecutionFrame` storage instead of reintroducing the former AsyncLocalStorage owner or a second accessor. A resolver returning `undefined` remains authoritative: stale direct context cannot revive a retired owner.

The command policy, expected connection and pairing generation, dispatch-time authority, and skill/run/placement lifecycle checks remain intact. There are no configuration, protocol, database-schema, or public SDK changes.

## User Impact

A detached Claude continuation can use its still-live Gateway and connected paired node. A retired owner fails before any node lookup, policy check, or dispatch.

## Evidence

- Conflict refresh onto main `f76e79be6a8fc934afd0faf1315f0261cfc4bafe`; current head `eb7a861ea7c06c277806dd2c6d0dba6b0f9c0443` also checks the captured Gateway remains current at dispatch and skill authority use. [Remote focused tests](https://github.com/ZengWen-DT/openclaw/actions/runs/40626335729) passed 18 tests across both affected Gateway suites on a temporary child of this head. Full CI and refreshed real-node proof remain pending; earlier evidence below refers to the revisions identified there.

Reconciled against main `cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984`; candidate `2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d`. The production diff is two reader substitutions, plus focused regression coverage.

### Actual Gateway and signed-node boundary

The same temporary source-runtime fixture starts the actual Gateway with an isolated home, config and state, loads a startup plugin through the normal loader, and captures its real context in an authenticated RPC. A separately signed WebSocket node completes normal local device pairing and command approval, verified in the persisted pairing records. After the capture RPC finishes, the fixture invokes the production `invokeNodeClaudeCliRun` in a resolver-only scope and repeats with a retired resolver plus deliberately stale direct context.

Main before the fix, observed with clean shutdown:

```json
{"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":0,"ok":false,"error":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":1,"ok":true}}
```

Exact candidate after the fix:

```json
{"head":"2220ac4be308a06c58c1c1fc774bf8a83115414d","expectedFixed":true,"actualGateway":true,"signedNode":true,"devicePaired":true,"commandApproved":true,"resolverOnly":{"directContext":false,"dispatched":1,"result":{"ok":true,"payload":{"exitCode":0,"stderrTail":"","truncated":false},"payloadJSON":null,"error":null}},"retiredOwner":{"staleDirectContextPresent":true,"additionalDispatches":0,"result":{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"UNAVAILABLE","message":"Gateway node runtime unavailable"}}}}
```

The fixture exited 0, and the Gateway reported a clean shutdown.

This exercises real Gateway startup, plugin loading, authenticated RPC, signed WebSocket transport, persisted device/command pairing, NodeRegistry and the changed production invocation owner. The node returns a synthetic successful Claude-command payload. It does not establish live Claude model inference or a full terminal-close/Web-composer UI walkthrough.

The fixture uses synthetic data only. Update checks, telemetry and hosted catalog refresh are disabled with the documented config/environment opt-outs. Proof code and generated logs are temporary and are not committed.

### Regression coverage and checks

- Before the two reader substitutions: 13 failures / 3 passes across the invocation and paired-node skill suites. Detached dispatch failed unavailable; stale-context retirement incorrectly dispatched; skill preparation failed its Gateway/capability boundary.
- After, on the identical candidate tree: 27/27 tests across node invocation (5), paired-node skills (11), request-scope owner (7), and native Bash execution policy (4). Existing coverage for command denial, pairing-await authority retirement, capability requirements, skill delivery/authoring and publication retirement remains active under the resolver-only scope.
- Combined focused command: `pnpm test src/gateway/node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts src/gateway/node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/gateway-request-scope.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin-native-bash.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, 85.02s wall time including the first compiled-subprocess generation.
- Per-file exact-head cost using `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`: `node-agent-cli-runtime.test.ts` 5/5, 34.08s wall (21ms test bodies); `node-claude-skill-runtime.test.ts` 11/11, 65.68s wall (23901ms test bodies). The existing skill suite exercises real node-command subprocess/SQLite lifecycle boundaries; no new per-test Gateway boots, timers, or serial configuration were added. Hosted [changed-node CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37098465276/job/111133298553) passed both files separately: invocation 5/5 in 22.88s (15ms test bodies), skills 11/11 in 19.83s (9.768s test bodies).
- Independent `autoreview --engine codex --mode local --base cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984 --max-priority P2`: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Four-file type-aware lint (`node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json <changed files>`) passed in 22.70s. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed. The aggregate check passed conflict, line-cap, max-lines, assertion-safety, database-worker, timeout-race, dependency, config, plugin-boundary and other prerequisite guards, plus the core graph boundary and full production-core typecheck.
- Hosted [CI run 37098465276](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37098465276) passed on this exact head, including `openclaw/ci-gate`, production types, all selected test-type stripes, lint, selected tests and guards. The [fresh review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/145741#issuecomment-5644398815) resolves the previous integration concern and finds no actionable introduced issues: overall Platinum, proof Diamond.
- Full repository build/check/test is not claimed as locally passed. The bounded `check:changed --base cdfe6cf00705aa2f59dbbe8040d333cd7d597984 --head HEAD` attempt ran 605.19s and stopped at its 600s budget during the broad 27-graph test-typecheck lane: `agents-root` passed, `agents-other` was interrupted (143). Remaining test graphs and later aggregate checks were not completed locally. The separate changed-file type-aware lint passed; the subsequent hosted CI run completed successfully and covers the selected global verification gates.

### Historical CI failure

[The old head's native-Bash policy job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34680714684/job/103518938237) reported `allowlist/on-miss`: expected `allow`, received `deny`, after 7.764s with a 5s fixture run budget. That is consistent with timeout-sensitive authority rejection, but the historical assertion omitted the denial message and run outcome, so the exact denial reason cannot be established from that log.

The integrated main already contains [the Date-based watchdog change](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/62a8182e40d955ddcd509ba977badb37ea691d2a) and the independent [native-Bash fixture stabilization in #115184](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ce11e2e25c3b0ad6360b8c4e5bd7f17357f81c42), which freezes the policy matrix's Date clock and asserts a non-timeout exit. The local native-Bash matrix passes 4/4 on this candidate. No native-Bash production policy, test fixture, or CI configuration is changed by this PR; a passing replay is not being presented as proof of the old run's exact cause.

prs.title: feat(ui): offer European Portuguese in the Control UI
prs.body:
Part of #188793
Related: #3460

## What Problem This Solves

European Portuguese speakers cannot select their language in the Control UI; a `pt-PT` browser currently selects Brazilian Portuguese.

## User Impact

The language picker offers **Português (Portugal)** separately from Brazilian Portuguese. Explicit and saved preferences retain priority; bare `pt` continues selecting `pt-BR`.

The default main-session title and Workboard navigation label use their existing locale catalogs. The Workboard page registration uses the same catalog label; its landing content still says “All boards”. Saved names and internal IDs remain unchanged.

This PR is the source-only Control UI registration slice of the wider PT-PT request in #188793. It uses English source copy until the normal post-merge refresh generates its catalog. Native-app localization and the remaining user-visible surfaces stay tracked in that issue; this slice does not complete the full translation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The change follows the existing locale registry, lazy loaders and source-only contribution rules in `ui/AGENTS.md`. The regional match precedes the generic Portuguese match. Default titles use the existing catalog owners rather than another preference store or translation service.

The locale-refresh workflow already owns generated translations, as used by #62063 and repaired in #172689. Translation memory, locale metadata and generated foreign output are excluded from this PR.

Maintainer decision requested: should the Control UI add this separate source-only locale and use the existing catalogs for its default session and Workboard titles? No maintainer approval is claimed.

## Evidence

### Real Gateway behavior at `02e909f56837`

Two local qualification scenarios use the existing native standalone UI E2E project, synthetic state and Chrome 156.0.8078.79. They do not mock Gateway responses or make model/provider calls. The candidate scenario uses native Bun 1.4.4; the cross-version scenario uses Node 26.13.0 and each engine's own compiled CLI and bundled UI.

| --- | --- |
| Automatic regional detection | Official stable resolves a pt-PT browser to pt-BR with System selected, no saved override and no locale write. The candidate resolves the same browser locale to pt-PT, also without writing an override. |
| Selection and reload | The candidate exposes distinct pt-BR/pt-PT options, receives matching `config.patch` acknowledgements, and preserves pt-PT after reload. |
| Catalog-backed defaults | The actual native mobile header displays the main-session fallback and the native Pages pane displays the Workboard navigation label. This source-only artifact uses English bootstrap text. The Workboard landing heading remains “All boards”; the separate page-registration label is not claimed as runtime-visible text. |
| Existing language and session across upgrade | Stable saves French and a named, pinned synthetic session through its real Gateway. After stopping stable, verifying a native backup and running the candidate's native Doctor migration, the candidate serves the same state and origin. A fresh pt-PT browser retains French, the exact session ID, its human name and pinned value. The saved name is visible before and after; reload retains French and the new Portugal option is available. |

Both Gateway processes exit successfully and their process trees are joined before fixture cleanup. Bounded captures of the controls and labels were visually inspected locally; they have not been uploaded. The local qualification scenarios are not included in this PR.

This establishes the stated language/session compatibility through manual engine replacement plus native migration. It does not test the `openclaw update` command, arbitrary historical databases, backup restoration, model execution or every saved-data field. Native backup verification succeeded, with opaque-byte warnings for incidental SQLite backup/control files; no full-database or restore certification is claimed. Earlier setup/control/timeout failures are superseded by this complete run.

### Hosted CI and focused regression evidence

The complete [CI workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41152323786) and aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` pass on `02e909f56837`.

- Commit `c70e90fdc569` corrects the Workboard JSON mock's namespace type while preserving real exports, production behavior and assertions. The extension-test type graph, scoped native lint and eight Workboard owner tests pass; the hosted [check-test-types job passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41152323786/job/124392340341).
- A newer merge base exposed a separate CI provisioning gap: the composer picker suite launches WebKit but was missing from the workflow's browser-requirement registry. Commit `02e909f56837` adds that one suite to the existing registry. Native workflow validation, formatting and actual Vitest discovery pass. The current run installs WebKit and [passes all four composer picker cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41152323786/job/124392065390), now in shard 1/7. No assertions or thresholds were changed.
- After upstream integration, the affected session/Workboard owner files pass all 27 tests. The native mock-export guard, test-line ratchet and keyless i18n verification pass. Title-owner regressions failed with the original fixed-English titles. Upstream's test-budget correction #188780 is incorporated without a local waiver.
- Earlier source-only UI build comparison against `9f563700de04` measured startup JavaScript gzip growth of 27 B and unchanged CSS, including the baseline's 148 B absolute-cap excess. That is pre-integration comparison evidence, not a fresh performance measurement at the final head. Current hosted checks pass.

prs.body:
Closes #138251.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a channel `/reset` clears the conversation but also removes the custom icon and color an operator selected for that session.

## User Impact

User impact: the conversation can reset without requiring the operator to reapply its icon or color. Setting another value still works, and explicitly clearing appearance still clears it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add only `icon` and `color` to the channel rollover's existing explicit preservation list. The broader presentation-helper copy is removed, and the Gateway reset helper is unchanged.

**Visibility is deliberately left out because it is sharing policy, not appearance.** Its reset behavior remains identical to main. Board presentation, pinning, model/auth selections, permissions and send policy are also unchanged; this is not the earlier draft-visibility preservation proposal.

The contributor's commit is preserved, followed by a current-main refresh and the narrowing commit. Appearance coverage is consolidated into the existing reset-state table, including unchanged visibility/board behavior; duplicated counter assertions share the same expected state. Production **+2**, tests **−2**, with no test allocation or ceiling change.

## Evidence

[Full before/after evidence, native row results, replay command and all eight screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/138334#issuecomment-6538360787).

Built Gateway plus its matching built Control UI, official Node 24.22.1 Docker, real Chromium 156.0.8078.4, the canonical QA bus/channel, and a deterministic seed-model fixture. Inbound `/reset` takes the real channel/session initialization path; native rows are read after the completed reset reply and the UI reloads from the Gateway.

- Two rounds per ref: main drops `🦞`/blue and `🚀`/purple; candidate retains both pairs.
- All four resets keep main's visibility behavior: draft before reset, shared afterward.
- New `🧭`/orange values apply and explicit null clears work on both refs, in both rounds.
- Chromium checks the visible color indicator; icon preservation is checked in the persisted native row. All eight before/after screenshots were inspected. No Telegram-specific or authentication/security claim.
- Selected existing reset-state regression: candidate **1 passed / 91 skipped**; the same test bytes on main fail at the missing icon (**1 failed / 91 skipped**). Scoped type-aware lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass.

<details>
<summary>Round 1: built Control UI before and after channel reset</summary>

**Main: blue indicator is lost.**

![Main before channel reset](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed8a614f-1237-4da0-a57a-db9947d3866f)

![Main after channel reset](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/036f8489-afb1-4475-a01e-7a9ef5e9c3d8)

![Candidate before channel reset](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3fbfafb-4853-4d54-8ed0-7b54ef7e95ab)

</details>

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting removes the two retained fields, with no migration or new data format. Blast radius is icon/color carried by the existing channel-session rollover builder; other reset selections, sharing policy, public APIs and Gateway reset behavior remain unchanged.

prs.title: feat(workers): keep runtime image reserves ready without browser presence
prs.body:
Related: #188679. Stacked on `openclaw/p3a-runtime-image-reserves` at exact image prerequisite `a38be6547c3929041e8d3fbf27012d76e758bd9c`, including authority prerequisite `c6ceb4ae6a44bf244e381e3006ed986778f6a3a3`. Integration preserves published history; no retarget or landing was performed.

**Landing remains coordinator-owned:** current-head CI must be green and prerequisite qualification completed. Separate prerequisite CI/UI work is outside this slice; publication does not waive those gates.

## What Problem This Solves

Runtime-image integrations need ready capacity without a connected browser, without unavailable policy blocking cleanup or restart destroying and replacing existing ready workers.

## User Impact

The configured default profile keeps runtime-only workers ready and refills after claims. Restart preserves compatible reserve identities while demand is reconstructed. Disabling capacity drains unused workers without interrupting attached sessions or extending finite deadlines. Ready workers incur running-machine charges until deletion is confirmed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Standing demand reuses the existing pool and environment inventory. Image preparation contains runtime artifacts, not repository contents or credentials. Repository claim/startup and credential authority remain owned by #188679 and #188656. Browser-driven repository demand and empty-workspace activation retain their existing paths.

Demand observation cannot disable expiry or physical cleanup. Pending reconstruction preserves inventory but grants no provider I/O. Actual activation—not a restored reserve's creation timestamp—supplies independent refill demand, and allocation rechecks current authority and capacity after awaited preflight. Explicit repository builds remain request-owned.

The latest prerequisite correction changes only the required-session RPC fixture and reduces its test credit by one line: image allocation must remain credential-free; actual repository startup performs managed verification, Git and checkpoint work. The positive assertion and all four revocation controls remain. No parent production fix was duplicated here.

No new pool, schema, retained-disk feature, configuration option or live cloud change is included. The standing delta remains 190 production lines and 891 regression/support lines, with exactly matching test allocations.

## Evidence

### Current corrected propagation

Source commit `ee4ec18235d84ee2d90d5f166c55422a5af7558a`, tree `408f52d12fc1f325aa1dd8c2932328baa505bdff`. Published head `36471f906182d8b8cf96897d2d90160c201696af` has this identical tree:

- **10 tests across the actual required-repository RPC and automation sibling suites passed**, 36.32 seconds Vitest / 40.60 seconds wrapper. The previously failing allowed RPC case is green; policy, source, stop and caller revocation controls remain exercised.
- Before the fixture correction, the same RPC suite on `0367beeb` produced one failure and four passes: the fixture incorrectly requested repository identity during image preparation and received “Repository worker startup requires current GitHub dispatch admission.” This was a fixture/phase mismatch, not a new production authorization bypass.
- Affected native lint/types/core boundary, formatting, mock-export/assertion/test-line ratchets and diff checks passed. Test lines: **6,323,484 / 6,354,479**, slack **30,995**. The parent's one-line reduction is reflected in both tests and allocation; this slice changed no shared baseline.
- Source execution used secretless official Node 24.22.1 containers, networking disabled, read-only manifest-qualified dependencies including **fs-safe 0.27.0**, and private proof caches. Normal hooks were retained; no shared dependency mutation, live cloud allocation, or live credential/operator configuration change was performed.

### Retained standing proof and review

These results retain their original source identities; they were not rerun or relabeled solely for propagation:

- **24 standing lifecycle/production-adapter transport cases passed** at `0367beeb17840a3d762e6e935f8182c2f01e8637`, tree `6ef5e4b58e8b4d46095064c6f638caa0ecd247f3`, with fs-safe 0.27.0: 82.45 seconds Vitest / 85.16 seconds wrapper. They preserve original restart IDs while expiry/requested cleanup proceeds, protect finite deadlines/attached workers, and exercise the real Crabbox adapter/subprocess path with controlled local transport. Enabled fresh/recovered allocation succeeds; integration/profile withdrawal or replacement and zero capacity prevent allocation. Node/artifact responses remain synthetic; no live-provider qualification is claimed.
- **89 tests across all 13 pool suites passed** at published `152be64a` / source `2e562e6c`, tree `1df9ad396928409baf5edba2605cade954e6f02a`: 186.05 seconds Vitest / 188.72 seconds wrapper. The restart regression was red against `6b709d0`, where original ready workers were replaced.
- All **14 standing-delta files have byte-identical base and head blobs** through the latest integrations. The standing repair's independent P0–P2 scoped-clean review at `d706576e` remains source-bound; the corrected parent fixture received its own targeted independent review. No new standing logic or duplicate review request was introduced by this propagation.
- Stable `v2026.10.9` v1 payloads were persisted/reopened with settings, active ownership and finite expiry intact. This is preserved-data/model evidence, **not a released-binary install-over upgrade**. No full browser/model turn, live-provider upgrade or current-head broad CI approval is claimed. Prerequisite proof and remaining qualification are recorded in #188679; CI seconds remain pending.

<details>
<summary>Retained controlled-transport output at 0367beeb (not rerun for the fixture-only correction)</summary>

```text
PASS Crabbox transport: enabled standing policy (recovered=false) 1740ms
PASS Crabbox transport: withdrawn standing policy (recovered=false) 987ms
```

The real adapter reaches local configuration preflight. Enabled controls then reach its warmup subprocess and readiness; revoked/replaced policy, changed profile and zero-target controls record zero allocation commands after release.

</details>

Source implementation by @galiniliev, selectively extracted and adapted from `63fda88754e4b57b6893095c0dffc88a3ba1381f` and the required request-owned-build correction. The original source branch remains unchanged.

prs.title: perf(sessions): open cold history without restoring archives (schema 39)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening an archived conversation waits for its entire transcript to restore through the agent database writer, even when the client needs only one bounded page. A busy writer turns that unnecessary restoration into a visible session-open delay.

Archival now retains the existing navigation, identity, active-event and index facts. SQL selects the bounded page before the payload reader fetches verified archive chunks. History and subscription snapshots leave the archive intact; writes and explicit restoration retain the existing restoration owner. Branch, reset, cursor, visibility and ordered live-event delivery remain the contracts. Unsupported envelope/Unicode cases stay inline to preserve their payload semantics.

The material-change review checkpoint was completed before implementation against `docs/reference/database-schemas.md`, `docs/reference/database-schemas/worker-access.md`, the Doctor migration guide and the update implementation contract. Peter approved the retained-navigation design and schema change on 2026-10-30.

**Agent schema 38→39 was explicitly approved by Peter.** It adds a valid representation to the existing payload constraint, with no new table or column. SQLite/PostgreSQL, port/backup readers and historical repairs share that contract. Doctor backfill is best effort, resumable and commits one archive at a time; pending archives retain the existing restore path. Rollback requires the corresponding pre-migration backup and a compatible binary.

## Rebase note — 2026-10-30

Rebased onto `origin/main` **`9f14244a6067e9ca0e22d1a2b8c5150e9cb7c693`** at head **`35fcb7c494839a6cb389ea03e4e65f4a99f44f6b`**. Main #188090 already owns the fresh-only `usage.cost` cache predicate and its single-agent/all-agent regression, plus the supported final-symlink denial diagnostics. Dropped our superseded `cbee978ad238` commit rather than retaining a duplicate fix or test. The conflicted usage/skills files now match main. Main's newer direct-command steering assertions also remain intact; no steering-test delta is carried by this PR.

The cold-navigation patches are unchanged by the replay. Main's agent schema is still **38**, so this PR remains the next consecutive **39** (state schema stays 36). Runtime/schema production delta is now **+709 net lines**; the broad non-test/non-doc delta is **+1,636**.

All **33 touched/conflicting test files** were selected with `--maxWorkers=1`: **380 tests passed**, with the nine PostgreSQL cases initially skipped by the ordinary runner. Those **9/9 then passed** separately through the canonical conformance runner against a disposable local PostgreSQL 17 container with CI's pinned image and extensions. The first disposable attempt lacked those extensions and failed setup-dependent cases; that evidence is retained. Both owned containers were stopped and verified removed. No Team access occurred.

Scoped lint exposed the rebased schema coordinator at 703 code lines against the existing 700 limit. An unchanged memory-metadata migration helper moved beside its existing detection helper in `openclaw-agent-db-schema-helpers.ts`, leaving all three call sites and migration order intact and the coordinator at 698. No suppression or stored-shape change was added. Codex autoreview of this two-file move is scoped-clean with no accepted findings. After the move, **51 migration/subscription/closure tests**, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, scoped core oxlint, oxfmt and the export-name collision guard all passed. Script/extension oxlint and formatting of all other touched/conflicting files also passed in the initial check pass.

A final fetch advanced main to **`1bf930c8e40a547f0e2eda87f895b2a7a00e644a`**. A merge-tree preview of the final head against it is conflict-free, and its agent schema is still 38. The branch was force-pushed **once**. New-head PR CI is separate from the historical green run below.

Performance, storage and published-upgrade receipts below retain their original pinned revisions. The owner/upgrade measurements on `9ffaabf7` and its exact-head CI are historical evidence, not measurements or CI results for this rebased head. This rebase refresh does not rerun the stress campaign or published upgrade. Prior clean implementation review is reused for the unchanged stored-navigation patches; the small helper relocation received the fresh scoped review described above. The PR remains ready and **must not be merged by this lane**.

## Evidence before this rebase

Head **`9ffaabf7de6a48ebab4a271982ba702f2ec28052`**, comparison base **`f47669efcec232b35dc74ac2d5d89b60796e6540`**. Exact-head CI is green: **186 passed, 44 skipped, zero pending/failing**, primary run **41149130953**, attempt 1. Codex reviews have no accepted P0–P2 findings. The PR stays open for maintainer review; it has not been merged.

## Owner measurements on pre-rebase head `9ffaabf7`

The committed owner harness measures the real subscription handler with 256-message synthetic transcripts and an 80-message/256-KiB page. Baseline is `f47669ef`, candidate is `9ffaabf7`. The fixed-work campaign completed **4,128 measured subscriptions per revision**: 3,000 hot timing requests across AB/BA plus the predeclared extra AB pair, 1,000 hot allocation requests, and 32 timing plus 32 allocation requests for each cold/busy case. Allocation uses a separate 16-KiB main-isolate sampling pass. Total process CPU and main-thread CPU are reported separately; the remainder includes runtime helper/GC/compiler threads, not just JavaScript workers.

| Case | Subscribe p50 ms | Subscribe p99 ms | Total CPU ms/request | Main CPU ms/request | Sampled bytes/request |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Hot, synchronized AB/BA mean | 7.470 → 7.501 | 16.107 → 16.852 (n=1,000 per arm) | 13.035 → 13.135 | 2.264 → 2.260 | 1,725,278 → 1,715,513 |
| Cold | 139.372 → 12.578 | 154.054 → 17.346 (n=32) | 152.896 → 18.983 | 9.192 → 3.587 | 2,768,362 → 1,816,957 |
| Cold, writer held for one second | 1,165.632 → 10.090 | 1,202.393 → 15.046 (n=32) | 182.007 → 15.754 | 11.195 → 3.222 | 3,070,984 → 1,815,692 |

Cold/busy percentiles have 32 samples per arm and are context, not tail gates. Cold CPU falls **87.58%**, allocation **34.37%**; held-writer CPU falls **91.34%**, allocation **40.88%**. Both timing and allocation passes preserve **32/32 archives**, versus **0/32** on baseline. Every held-writer candidate reply finishes before release (**32/32**, baseline **0/32**). All page content checks pass. These deterministic work counts directly cover the original failure.

### Hot-session control and contention investigation

The sequential 1,000-session timing protocol produced a material adverse tail, which is retained here. Across all three pairs, mean run p99 was **32.406 → 91.936 ms** (+59.530 ms, +183.70%); mean wall time was **10.417 → 17.648 ms/request** (+69.41%). Total CPU was **13.693 → 14.616 ms/request** (+6.73%), main CPU **2.983 → 3.199** (+7.27%), and p50 **8.734 → 9.265 ms** (+6.08%). Hot sampled allocation was **1,725,278 → 1,715,513 bytes/request** (−0.57%, 1,000 requests per side).

Individual pair p99s were **37.566 → 18.718**, **41.632 → 41.586**, and **18.021 → 215.505 ms**, each with 1,000 observations per arm. Four matched identical-baseline A/A pairs followed. Neither counterbalanced control block crossed the declared adverse gate: p99 changes were **+1.495 ms/+9.29%** and **−36.577 ms/−68.98%**. These controls alone do not dismiss the candidate signal. No samples, pauses or arms were excluded.

The third sequential candidate was slower throughout the run while host one-minute load rose **25.46→39.00**, versus **14.32→14.69** during its earlier baseline arm. This motivated a separately declared simultaneous comparison, not exclusion or relabeling of the old result. Both revisions use independent synthetic state, the same warmup and measurement barriers, and wait for both measurements to finish before either writes diagnostics or cleans up. Fixture preparation order is counterbalanced AB/BA. Each arm opens 1,000 distinct sessions; no extra warmup or forced GC was added. Profiling is a separate diagnostic pair and never supplies acceptance timing.

The two synchronized **untraced** pairs completed another **2,000 hot requests per revision**, with successful content checks and stable build/tool hashes:

| Pair | Total CPU ms/request | Main CPU ms/request | p50 ms | p99 ms (1,000/arm) | Host load1m, shared before→after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| AB fixture order | 12.980 → 13.011 | 2.277 → 2.225 | 7.483 → 7.395 | 15.953 → 16.629 | 7.398 → 7.423 |
| BA fixture order | 13.090 → 13.258 | 2.251 → 2.296 | 7.457 → 7.607 | 16.262 → 17.074 | 7.101 → 7.373 |
| Paired mean | **13.035 → 13.135** | **2.264 → 2.260** | **7.470 → 7.501** | **16.107 → 16.852** | — |

Mean CPU change is **+0.100 ms/request (+0.77%)** total and **−0.0036 ms/request (−0.16%)** main-thread. Mean wall time is **7.866 → 7.948 ms/request** (+0.082 ms, +1.04%). Mean p99 change is **+0.744 ms (+4.62%)**; neither pair crosses the declared adverse thresholds. This controlled first-open comparison supports a small hot-path cost, not a hot-path speedup. It does not establish the cause of the earlier sequential anomaly or demonstrate equivalent behavior at that earlier higher host load.

Endpoint RSS was **1,602.2 → 1,883.7 MiB** in AB and **1,903.1 → 1,620.4 MiB** in BA: the higher value followed the second-prepared arm. Counterbalanced mean RSS was **1,752.7 → 1,752.0 MiB** (−0.63 MiB), and main heap was **572.14 → 571.97 MiB** (−0.16 MiB). These are ordinary endpoints, not forced-GC retained-memory measurements. No memory win is claimed. Full before/after memory, synchronization timestamps and every observation are retained in the local evidence.

The final decision uses these simultaneous, counterbalanced measurements to control shared-host timing while keeping the earlier adverse results visible. No extra A/A campaign was triggered by this non-adverse protocol. The eight sequential A/A arms and their limits remain reported above.

The diagnostic profile pair used another **1,000 requests per revision** and measured total CPU **13.115 → 13.128 ms/request** and main CPU **2.396 → 2.380**. It preserves full main-isolate profiles, request timelines, GC events and existing worker-request metrics. It does not provide nested-worker CPU stacks. Main profiles, GC and history-worker queue timings closely match: each arm completes 2,000 history operations, with summed worker elapsed time 5,995.406 → 5,998.948 ms. Both also show optional background writer/backfill activity after warmup. This overlap is not causal proof and does not explain the earlier 215.505-ms tail; no speculative production change was made from it.

The owner timing harness does not measure untraced GC or event-loop delay. The whole-Gateway stress below is explicitly pinned to earlier revisions and does not qualify the final runtime. All final-head owner builds/harnesses were hash-verified, and all owned measurement processes drained.

## Storage and code cost

The synthetic storage corpus contains **2,048 archived sessions × 1,024 events = 2,097,152 events**. Raw payloads total 3,577,628,672 bytes. Compressed archive bytes remain identical at **39,377,848 bytes**. These repetitive payloads compress about 91×: this is a harsh metadata-to-archive ratio, not a production storage estimate.

| Live database pages, all tables and indexes | Bytes |
| --- | ---: |
| Old archive-deletion policy | 3,026,944 |
| Retained navigation | 2,741,854,208 |
| Additional storage | **2,738,827,264** |
| Additional per archived session | **1,337,318** |

That is **1.275 MiB per archived session**, or **2.551 GiB** across this corpus. This all-catalog `dbstat` comparison applies the old deletion policy inside a rolled-back transaction on the same corpus. It is not an old-build physical-file comparison; allocated files do not shrink simply because rows are deleted. The unchanged stored representation makes this corpus applicable to the final head.

Runtime/schema production growth after this rebase is **+709 net lines**. The approved stored representation, resumable migration, bounded archive reader and SQLite/PostgreSQL parity require this growth. Duplicate archive replay and the restore-only read dependency are removed. Performance tooling is **+902 net lines** (888 in two owner scripts; native Doctor stress preparation and its guide account for the rest). The full non-test/non-doc diff, including tooling/configuration/generated outputs, is **+1,636 net lines**.

Tests and test support add **866 net lines** after removing the duplicate. The pre-rebase ratchet passed **6,316,939 / 6,348,041**, with **31,102** lines of headroom. This PR changes neither the shared test-line baseline nor allocation files.

## Correctness, integration and review

The initial subscription regression was red on baseline `97225ae1`: subscribing restored and removed the archive. Final baseline owner runs reproduce the same work-count failure. `sessions.messages-subscribe-cold.test.ts` proves archive preservation; snapshot/live-event proof covers exact ordering and exactly-once persisted delivery. Bounded history regressions cover branch/reset intervals, older/newer cursors, visibility, byte caps and placement metadata. `state-migrations.cold-navigation.test.ts` migrates a backed-up pre-change synthetic database, interrupts and resumes without restoring payloads; the scoped predecessor test preserves unrelated later writes.

The latest integration passed **81 focused tests** across Doctor, bounded/model context, subscription and lifecycle consumers. Core typechecking, `pnpm tsgo:test:root`, scoped oxlint/oxfmt and the ratchet passed. Broader proof is the exact-head CI run above, including all three PostgreSQL conformance jobs. Full implementation review and scoped follow-up Codex reviews are clean.

Main #188789 introduced a batched first-header scan that bypassed this PR's existing cold-session exclusion. The integration fix filters archive-marked sessions before aggregation and decoding. Its strengthened regression is red on the rebased pre-fix owner and green with the fix, including both navigation-only and exceptional inline cold rows; hot corruption assertions are unchanged.

Earlier CI exposed a `usage.cost` cache bug: transient `refreshing` results received the outer cache's 30-second TTL after the lower refresh settled. Main #188090 now owns the same fresh-only cache fix and broader scope coverage; this rebase drops our duplicate. The earlier handler regression was red before the fix and handler/lifetime tests passed **27/27**. Remaining fixture repairs use the existing complete Gateway logger and deterministic watcher notifications. Main owns the symlink-denial diagnostic adjustment. Production authority is unchanged. Earlier fallback, steering and workspace fixture repairs were also superseded by main and are absent from this diff.

A prior Android job built and verified its APK but failed when the emulator went offline during trust cleanup. Both Android jobs passed on the final head without rerunning that old attempt. No tests or assertions were weakened to obtain green.

## Latest-stable upgrade on pre-rebase measured head `9ffaabf7`

A fresh registry check confirmed latest stable **2026.10.9**. Its published driver upgraded a restored synthetic schema-25 database through the native updater to sealed **`9ffaabf7`**, on pinned base **`f47669ef`**, in **372,716 ms**. Terminal status was `ok`, run status `succeeded`, process exit was 0, and **all 19 recorded steps exited 0**. This covers agent schema **25→39**, native backup restore, Doctor, package swap, old-driver handoff and Gateway rehearsal.

Activation completion was verified against the retained operation journal after the updater exited: `anchor-retired`, `unlink-helper`, with matching helper identity. Repeat installed Doctor exited 0. The archived fixture gained 129 identity rows, 128 active-event rows, 128 cold-message markers and its navigation index, while retaining zero hot message payload rows. Its original generation, SHA-256 and **4,204 compressed bytes** were unchanged; SQLite `quick_check` passed.

The installed Gateway's initial 20-message subscription/history page and older 20-message cursor page matched exact order, role, timestamp, identity and synthetic content. Requests began only after listener readiness, without transport retries. Every owned build, updater, Doctor, client and Gateway process exited successfully and drained. Cleanup conservatively retained some temporary runtime artifacts when an unrelated process could not be classified; no unrelated process was signaled.

The native package owner validated tarball integrity and imports, then restored temporary manifest preparation. Package SHA-256 is `a9fa040a36d2934cbe9a338665ed768ae05087a58347cfbc8aa83770d523ec8c`. The baseline used supported `sourcePerformance` and candidate used supported runtime-only `package`; both share the runtime compiler/options, with source maps and private QA disabled. Their exact identities are retained. The full receipt is `.local/buf540/upgrade/final-f476-9ffaabf/published-9ffaabf-proof.md`.

This upgrade fixture contains ordinary user/assistant messages. Separate integration regressions cover background-result placement, branch/reset semantics and interrupted migration resume; the upgrade smoke does not claim those cases. Earlier `efecf020` and `f243711f` upgrades remain historical evidence, superseded here by fresh proof of the current package.

<details>
<summary>Earlier owner measurements and the short-window hot CPU signal</summary>

### Previous af8 → f243 owner measurements

These results belong to pinned base **`af8ab708`** → packaged runtime **`f243711f`**. Historical head **`bd361c59`** differed only in its test logger fixture; the final head integrates newer main and has separate results above. All 12 arms passed and their processes drained, with runtime/harness hashes verified before every arm and after completion. Each arm used **32 distinct sessions × 256 messages**, 80-message/256-KiB pages. Timing ran AB; a separate 16-KiB allocation-sampling pass ran BA. Each revision completed **192 measured subscriptions** (96 timing, 96 allocation).

| Case | Subscribe p50 ms | Subscribe p99 ms (n=32; context only) | CPU ms/request | Sampled main-thread bytes/request |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Hot | 10.304 → 9.328 | 18.877 → 13.467 | 18.849 → 21.054 | 1,800,139 → 1,871,920 |
| Cold | 157.206 → 10.602 | 703.890 → 23.480 | 182.070 → 19.202 | 2,697,082 → 1,806,783 |
| Cold, writer held for one second | 1,174.241 → 10.374 | 1,533.569 → 18.720 | 192.881 → 16.588 | 3,054,901 → 1,837,621 |

Cold CPU fell **89.45%**, sampled allocation **33.01%**; held-writer CPU fell **91.40%**, allocation **39.85%**. Cold/busy archive preservation improved **0/32 → 32/32** in both passes; busy replies before writer release improved **0/32 → 32/32**. These are deterministic behavior counts, independent of latency noise.

Hot CPU rose **2.205 ms/request (+11.70%)** and allocation **71,782 bytes/request (+3.99%)**, despite lower p50/p99. Those increases remain reported; older-head controls do not establish this head neutral. The predeclared swapped pair also raised CPU: **16.971 → 20.688 ms/request (+21.90%)**. Across both pairs, CPU was **17.910 → 20.871 ms/request (+2.961 ms, +16.53%)**, with both pairs above +10%. Four matched identical-baseline A/A pairs completed successfully. Their counterbalanced CPU blocks were **−3.99%** and **+2.32%**; neither tripped the paired gate. These controls do **not** dismiss the candidate CPU signal. Source inspection found no extra query, decoding, parsing or worker churn on this measured first-page path, but that does not resolve the measurement. The final-head fixed-work protocol above uses 1,000 distinct sessions per hot arm and separates main-thread from whole-process CPU; all short-window observations remain reported.

Host one-minute load ranged **10.36–35.54** across the 12 arms. Every arm's load, RSS/heap endpoints and raw observations remain in `.local/buf540/owner-f243711-af8ab70/`. This unchanged owner harness does not instrument GC or event-loop delay; the separately pinned prior-head whole-Gateway stress below must not be relabeled as final-runtime proof. No samples or arms were excluded.

### Earlier owner measurements and controls

The real subscription regression was red on baseline `97225ae1`: subscription restored and removed the archive. Previous isolated handler/WebSocket proof verified archive preservation and an exact snapshot followed by three ordered, exactly-once persisted live events. Matched owner measurements use baseline `c0c068e1` and candidate `ffbeb87c`, with 32 distinct 256-message sessions per case and arm, 80-message/256-KiB pages, timing AB and separate 16-KiB sampled-allocation BA. These measurements precede the later fallback/fixture CI repair; they are not relabeled as measurements of a later head:

| Case | Subscribe p50 ms, base → candidate | Subscribe p99 ms (n=32, context) | CPU ms/op | Sampled main-thread bytes/op |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Hot | 8.293 → 9.662 | 14.054 → 30.872 | 18.664 → 22.330 | 1,785,458 → 1,843,731 |
| Cold | 141.296 → 8.550 | 154.406 → 16.449 | 144.415 → 14.054 | 2,753,651 → 1,868,368 |
| Cold with writer held for one second | 1,142.224 → 9.557 | 1,177.507 → 15.058 | 163.971 → 15.639 | 3,086,395 → 1,846,324 |

Each revision completed 192 measured subscriptions across the timing and allocation cases. Cold archives survived **0/32 → 32/32** subscriptions in both passes. Held-writer replies completed before release **0/32 → 32/32**. All 12 processes exited successfully after isolated-state cleanup.

Hot results prompted further fixed-work measurements; none of the earlier results were discarded. A swapped 32-session pair left paired CPU **17.961 → 22.246 ms/op (+23.85%)**. Four identical-baseline 32-session controls had wide individual variation, but neither counterbalanced block met the paired rejection gate, so those controls alone do not explain away the CPU rise.

A longer, explicitly different workload revisited 32 warmed sessions for **2,048 subscriptions per arm**, AB/BA: CPU **11.301 → 11.400 ms/op (+0.88%)**, p99 **15.699 → 14.631 ms**, loop p99 **12.825 → 12.878 ms**, and GC **0.08384 → 0.09462 ms/op (+0.01079 ms)**. This supports the warm repeated path, not the first-open case.

The unchanged committed harness then measured **1,000 distinct sessions per arm**, AB/BA plus the one predeclared extra AB pair for mixed signs. All 6,000 pages were correct. Mean CPU was **11.761 → 12.228 ms/op (+3.97%)**; mean p50 **7.747 → 7.677 ms**. Mean run p99 was **17.025 → 36.995 ms**, including the first candidate's **76.449-ms** p99; the other candidate p99s were **16.652 and 17.884 ms**. That adverse first-open tail remains reported. Four matched identical-baseline A/A pairs completed with all eight processes successful and hashes unchanged. Their first counterbalanced block itself crossed the rejection gates: CPU **+1.206 ms/op (+11.94%)**, and p99 **+4.103 ms (+30.99%)**, with both pairs ≥10% adverse for each metric. The second block did not cross a gate; the four-pair signed means were CPU **+8.25%** and p99 **+15.03%**. First-open hot attribution is therefore **inconclusive**, not a demonstrated hot win or a discarded candidate tail. Host load is context only; no samples or arms were excluded.

The prior bounded-page microbenchmark also remains prior-head evidence; its earlier gains are not relabeled as current measurements.

</details>

## Prior-head canonical Gateway stress

The completed campaign is explicitly **prior-head evidence**: runtime base **`e3c85a81`**, runtime candidate **`60947404`**, tooling **`96a7dc75`**. It does not qualify the final rebased runtime.

Eight complete **≥10-minute arms** used timing AB/BA and separate sampled-allocation AB/BA, fresh 10,800-session fixtures, 40 plugins, 65 WebSocket clients, native mock-provider turns/tools/subagents and sidebar/list/search churn. **320 turns/tool pairs and 15,422 RPCs completed without errors.** All state and Gateways were synthetic and local; no Team access or load occurred. All owned processes/listeners drained.

| Natural post-major old generation | 413.5 → 421.6 MiB | +8.1 MiB |

No retained-heap improvement is claimed. Forced GC **after** measurement gave 405.287→405.296 MiB old generation, diagnostic only. Timing maximum GC pauses were 34.63→38.58 ms and 34.34→40.41 ms. No material adverse timing gate triggered; no A/A controls or extra pair were required. Client tails alone did not decide acceptance. Allocation-only event-loop maxima of 3,917 and 1,100 ms remain reported as diagnostics; sampled-pass timing/GC is not acceptance evidence. Promotion bytes were not measured.

Both arms were seeded at schema 38 by baseline tooling and ran their own built Doctor before readiness/warmup/measurement; candidate migrated to 39. The reviewed harness setup avoids service repair. Both setup-smoke arms preserved 108 sessions and 116 message identities. Fixed seed 1711, fixture clock 1793378753582 and 60-second warmup were identical. A private output root supplied safe temporary-directory ancestors without changing shared permissions. Earlier setup failures were preserved and excluded, not interpreted as performance results.

The corpus contains archived session-list flags, not deliberately cold payload archives. It proves mixed-workload compatibility on those prior heads. Subscriptions attach during setup, so it supplies no measured subscribe-handler percentile. The owner and upgrade proofs cover actual cold reads.

prs.title: feat(workers): preserve repository authority during dispatch and recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Optional repository policies need caller-bound admission throughout worker preparation, checkout, and authenticated recovery, regardless of the selected GitHub credential type or whether placement begins from chat or session creation.

## User Impact

Deployments opt in with `gateway.repositoryIntegration`. Missing or revoked admission refuses worker source access; omitting the integration preserves native behavior. Required repository placement now retains the original session-creation caller after acknowledgment instead of depending on a chat-only context. Automatic required placement does not request setup scripts, consistent with its existing worktree behavior.

Native owners retain credential issuance, managed-profile reading/rotation, and cleanup. This feature introduces no database-schema or checkpoint-format migration. Installed-release configuration and checkpoint preservation are qualified below; exact-head CI remains open.

## Why This Change Was Made

One lifetime-bound integration owner supplies policy; existing identity, dispatch, and worker owners enforce it. Managed PAT/OAuth profiles enter policy admission before refresh/profile reads without asking a plugin for their bearer. Native/App paths retain their issuer and guarded return value. Dispatch forwards the original reader; source owners compose caller, policy, and dispatch lifetime checks. The redundant reader wrapper was deleted, not extended.

Session creation passes its native caller-bound reader through an internal preparation option. Its existing retention owner and the coordinator's independent source custody remain responsible for post-acknowledgment work. No chat admission is fabricated, and no wire field or additional issuer is introduced. Host credential callbacks remain excluded from node transport.

Signed merge `82b2e5aee4612e606b9acf2280b5069c7e9f794d` integrates main `b5b02243a53b39bf8c3e838bce74eb7062df852a` without rewriting prior history. The sole conflict was a generated schema hash; canonical generation retained `repositoryBranchPrefix` and `gateway.repositoryIntegration` at 2585 core entries. No budget increase was added.

## Evidence

- **Actual session-creation regression:** `handleGatewayRequest` → `sessions.create` → required preparation → coordinator → actual dispatch reproduced missing repository admission after the RPC returned. Five controls now pass: post-acknowledgment activation with native Node/Git/checkpoint effects, policy revocation, caller-scope change, source replacement, and targeted controller Stop before credential effects. All five passed again on the combined source with frozen dependencies, including fs-safe 0.27.0. This is in-process RPC dispatch, not a WebSocket/model test. Stop coverage uses the real target-scoped controller owner, not public `sessions.abort`.
- **Released install-over preservation:** actual `v2026.10.9` (`8b18b5578f66eab1501cba4cef2310d88bfb9a41`) created a repository session, dispatched it to a paired local node, and accepted an editor mutation through public RPC. That produced a real revision-3 checkpoint containing content absent from the Git base. The canonical package built from exact head `c6ceb4ae6a44bf244e381e3006ed986778f6a3a3` passed tarball integrity checks and was installed over the same prefix/config/state. Installed Doctor performed the required agent-schema v25→v38 migration with backups. Gateway and model configuration, session identity, repository/base/manifest/checkpoint references, and the changed file bytes survived. With the node offline, the candidate's public `sessions.files.get` read those bytes from stored checkpoint artifacts; SHA-256 remained `823ca7b910bb25c9299516a968a823fb1b06f20a10cb685c33e2cd8ee66133cd`. Doctor's existing heartbeat migration removed the old `0m` field and produced a disabled heartbeat job, verified through `cron.list`. This proves installed configuration/checkpoint survival and offline checkpoint reads, not active-worker recovery or move-to-Gateway behavior.
- **Upgrade isolation:** the published baseline and candidate ran in disposable local containers with synthetic credentials and a TLS-validating, offline GitHub/Git fixture. There were no model turns or cloud allocations. The candidate tarball SHA-256 is `b0156d285bcbc8954252b1e3a28160cba0b7f329bb1ba71faa39b2dea6aa556a`; installed build identity was checked. Gateway/node processes were stopped through their lifecycle owners, and task containers were removed. No live Gateway, shared install, or real credential setup was changed.
- **Retained focused proof:** 28 managed/native dispatch cases, 17 existing required-profile cases, 2 Workboard terminal-hook cases, and 4 workflow-selection cases passed before the final RPC correction. Earlier 24-case dispatch proof and full-parent review remain prior-cut evidence, not rerun claims. Allocation, tunnel transport, HTTP responses, and policy decisions are synthetic in these source tests. The forwarding correction incorporates the [image-lane proof](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/c6d5c22f-133a-4a94-bbd5-51a4edb1ccfd).
- **Prior-head CI repairs:** [compact-small15](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41152484539/job/124392265988) tested merge `65b0c7ff40606d0f65f37a50fed509b73ba06323`; the Workboard logger fixture lacked the diagnostics contract. Canonical logger replacement was red/green through both hooks. [UI1/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41152484539/job/124392263962) lacked WebKit for the composer-layout suite. The installer inventory and existing workflow-selector regression were corrected red/green without skips or fallback; main subsequently contained the same inventory correction.
- **Fresh independent review:** local autoreview with Codex, P0–P2, reviewed the complete correction against `0f2cc377e276367afbb641f7c38dde1679459126`, including full creation callers, required-preparation owner, admission/coordinator contracts, and regressions. Final result: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The subsequent merge changed no reviewed authority module; its generated conflict and affected filesystem path were requalified. Source review is not CI approval.
- **Static/build checks:** targeted typecheck/lint/format, canonical schema generation/check, and diff checks passed. Canonical workflow validation passed actionlint, zizmor, Git-owner, and composite-run guards. Normal commit hooks ran without bypass using the verified private dependency checkout. Full canonical package build and tarball integrity checks passed. Published tree `3113778dde7c2fde7b002467eee2200f0ba0ac97` preserves both merge parents and prior-publication ancestry.
- **Remaining CI gate:** [current-head compact-small20](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41161544452/job/124420328494), tested merge `54717243` into `6fdd9aaf60cd92cdc967016ff419a029bbe716a3`, failed the `server-startup-lifetime.test.ts` held-process case at line 510: expected one settlement callback after advancing fake time, observed zero. The test blob matches this head and is unchanged by this PR from integrated main; its cause is not yet qualified. Other current-head checks were still pending at the last observation. Earlier materialization cases blocked by Git 2.39.5 are not claimed rerun. No CI waiver or merge-readiness claim is made.

Source implementation by @galiniliev, extracted and adapted from `63fda88754e4b57b6893095c0dffc88a3ba1381f` and the minimal required prerequisite slices. The original source branch was not changed.

## Worked on by

- @galiniliev

<!-- openclaw-publication:4abaa98c-2f3b-4712-af02-5afb8839a3bd -->

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/5195398f-32af-4571-9bc4-bf5c08341479)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/35d016ac-257e-44cd-8857-0beda59b9cee)
- [CI repair and final verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/5195398f-32af-4571-9bc4-bf5c08341479)

prs.title: fix(usage-bar): context budget shows 1000k instead of 1.0m
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the usage bar shows a context budget as `1000k` for one turn while the usage line beside it shows `1.0m` for the same number, when the context window is 999,500鈥?99,999 tokens.

## User Impact

User impact: the context budget in the usage bar now uses the same unit as every other token count in the same message, so `999950` reads `1.0m` instead of `1000k`. No other value changes; every band below 999,500 and at or above 1,000,000 renders exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The usage bar's `num` verb formatted the 1,000鈥?,000,000 band itself with `${Math.round(v)}k`, so values from 999,500 upward rounded to `1000k`. The shared token formatter already guards this exact case (`formatCompactTokenCount`, `Number(thousands) < 1_000`), and its own unit test asserts `999_950 -> "1.0m"`. That formatter already produces the surrounding usage line, so a single turn reported two different units for one count.

The verb now defers to `formatTokenCount` only when rounding crosses into the million band, which keeps the existing `k` formatting for every value that does not roll over. The prior test expectation `999_950 -> "1000k"` was asserting the defect, so it is replaced rather than kept.

**Owner decision requested.** PR #164684 deliberately preserved sub-million formatting, including a `999_950 -> "1000k"` assertion, while fixing the 鈮?,000,000 band. This PR proposes replacing that preserved boundary so the two units agree. The precise boundary measured here is **999,500** (not 999,950): `999_499 -> "999k"` and `999_500 -> "1.0m"`. If the owner prefers to keep the earlier boundary, this PR should be closed instead.

## Evidence

**Delivered footer through the shipped reply pipeline (not a translator unit test).** The proof script calls the production entry that the reply assembler uses 鈥?`buildReplyUsageState()` (`src/auto-reply/reply/reply-usage-state.ts`) into `resolveResponseUsageLine()` (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-usage-line.ts`), which is the exact function invoked at `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-result-payloads.ts:681` and `src/auto-reply/reply/followup-delivery.ts:359`. Only the provider-reported context window is injected (a real near-million model reports 999950); the usage projection, the usage contract, the default shipped usage-bar template, the declarative renderer and the `num` verb are all production code.

With the fix applied, the delivered footer per context window:

```
[PASS] 999,950 budget (reported defect)   footer: openai馃gpt-5-codex馃寳馃悓 | 馃摎[猓库？狻団爯鉅怾1.0m
[PASS] 999,949 budget (band floor)        footer: ...馃摎[猓库？狻団爯鉅怾1.0m
[PASS] 999,999 budget (band ceiling)      footer: ...馃摎[猓库？狻団爯鉅怾1.0m
[PASS] 999,499 budget (below band)        footer: ...馃摎[猓库？狻団爯鉅怾999k
[PASS] 500,000 budget (unchanged)         footer: ...馃摎[猓库？狻団爯鉅怾500k
[PASS] 1,000,000 budget (unchanged)       footer: ...馃摎[猓库？狻団爯鉅怾1.0m
[PASS] 200,000 budget (unchanged)         footer: ...馃摎[猓库？狻団爯鉅怾200k
cases: 7, failed: 0
RESULT: near-million context budget renders 1.0m through the shipped reply footer -> PASS
```

The same script against the base `translator.ts` (`git show 48eef4e~1:src/auto-reply/usage-bar/translator.ts` restored in place, nothing else changed) delivers the defect:

```
[FAIL] 999,950 budget (reported defect)   footer: ...馃摎[猓库？狻団爯鉅怾1000k   (expected 1.0m)
[FAIL] 999,949 budget (band floor)        footer: ...馃摎[猓库？狻団爯鉅怾1000k
[FAIL] 999,999 budget (band ceiling)      footer: ...馃摎[猓库？狻団爯鉅怾1000k
[PASS] 999,499 budget (below band)        footer: ...馃摎[猓库？狻団爯鉅怾999k
[PASS] 500,000 budget (unchanged)         footer: ...馃摎[猓库？狻団爯鉅怾500k
[PASS] 1,000,000 budget (unchanged)       footer: ...馃摎[猓库？狻団爯鉅怾1.0m
[PASS] 200,000 budget (unchanged)         footer: ...馃摎[猓库？狻団爯鉅怾200k
cases: 7, failed: 3
RESULT: shipped reply footer did not roll over -> FAIL
```

So the unit sent to the channel changes from `1000k` to `1.0m` for the affected band while four neighboring bands are byte-identical.

**Red on base, green with the fix** (test file updated to the measured boundary; base `translator.ts` restored):

```
FAIL  x|num formats {"x":999500} as 1.0m     expected '1000k' to be '1.0m'
FAIL  x|num formats {"x":999999} as 1.0m     expected '1000k' to be '1.0m'
FAIL  x|num formats {"x":-999600} as -1.0m   expected '-1000k' to be '-1.0m'
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  3 failed | 38 passed (41)
```

With the fix applied:

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  41 passed (41)
```

The rollover rows are now one positive per distinct behavior (999,499 stays `999k`, 999,500 and 999,999 roll over, -999,600 carries the sign) instead of three equivalent positives. A negative value at exactly `-999_500` still prints `-999k`, because `Math.round(-999.5)` rounds toward zero; that is pre-existing behavior outside this change, which is why the signed row uses `-999_600`.

**Checks run locally:** `oxfmt --check` clean on all three files; `oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json` clean on both source files; `tsc -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit` reports 14 errors, all pre-existing missing optional dependencies in this checkout (`@noble/hashes`, `fast-uri`, `@openclaw/fs-safe/advanced`, `darwin-process-inspection`, `local-repository-directory-policy`), with zero hits in `usage-bar` or `translator`.

**Environment note:** this run used Node v22.22.3 on Windows, driving the shipped helpers in-process (`--import tsx`). It exercises the real reply-side entry and the real default template, but it does not spin up a live Gateway against a channel; say so if a live-channel recording is required for this gate.

**Live Gateway attempt, and why it could not complete here.** Per the maintainer guidance to use isolated state and ports, I tried to boot a real Gateway on a separate state directory and port 19820 (`--bind loopback --auth none`), leaving the operator's running instances untouched. The server did bind the port and reach `gateway.server-start-import`, then aborted:

```
[gateway] sidecars failed to start: SyntaxError: The requested module
          '@openclaw/fs-safe/advanced' does not provide an export named
          'overwriteFileHandleWithAuthority'
Gateway failed to start: The requested module '@openclaw/fs-safe/advanced'
          does not provide an export named 'overwriteFileHandleWithAuthority'.
```

That is a dependency-version drift in this checkout, not anything this PR touches. `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` both pin `@openclaw/fs-safe` to `0.26.15`, but `node_modules/@openclaw/fs-safe/package.json` here is `0.26.7`. The pinned version exports the symbol and the installed one does not:

```
# installed 0.26.7  -> dist/advanced.js
export { overwriteFileHandle } from "./overwrite-file-handle.js";

# pinned 0.26.15 (downloaded from the registry and extracted to confirm)
export { overwriteFileHandle, overwriteFileHandleWithAuthority, type OverwriteFileHandleOptions } ...
```

`src/agents/host-file-write.ts:3` imports `overwriteFileHandleWithAuthority` from that subpath, which is why the Gateway aborts during sidecar startup. The same mismatch is already visible in a plain typecheck of this tree:

```
src/agents/host-file-write.ts(3,10): error TS2305: Module '"@openclaw/fs-safe/advanced"'
  has no exported member 'overwriteFileHandleWithAuthority'.
```

Reinstalling or reconciling the shared install is outside what a contributor PR may do (this checkout's `node_modules` serves other running jobs), so a channel-delivered footer is not obtainable from this machine without changing that dependency. If a maintainer can run this on a checkout whose `fs-safe` matches the lockfile, the same scenario is `messages.responseUsage="full"` plus a context window of 999950, and the footer should read `馃摎[...]1.0m`. Everything above stands on the production reply-side entry and the shipped default template; only the transport is missing. The isolated Gateway I started bound port 19820, reached `gateway.server-start-import`, then exited on the error above; the temporary state directory was removed and the operator's running Gateways were never touched.


**Documentation consistency.** `docs/concepts/usage-tracking.md` now states the same 999,500 boundary in both places it describes the footer: the `num` verb table note and the `/usage full` overview, which previously said only windows of one million tokens or more use `m` units.

Docs: `docs/concepts/usage-tracking.md` now states the `num` rollover and its 999,500 boundary next to the other verb notes.

prs.title: fix(skills): cancel experience review on explicit /stop
prs.body:
Closes #120558

## What Problem This Solves

An explicit Stop ends foreground work but leaves Skill Workshop Experience Review running independently. Its queued review can still start, and an in-flight review can continue making model calls or writing a skill. The stopped foreground run's own completion can also re-arm learning after a timer is cancelled.

## Summary

Preserve HeZ2z's fix at the existing review scheduler and accepted Stop boundaries:

- Cancel the selected session's queued review and its active review controller.
- Suppress the explicitly stopped run's completion once, without blocking later turns or general interrupted-turn learning (#115887).
- Bridge channel Stop, `chat.send /stop`, session `chat.abort`, and exact-run `chat.abort` only after their existing live-authority and owner checks. Maintenance and non-chat Stop contracts remain separate.
- Pass cancellation through the existing detached review admission and model run. Preserve independent cleanup failures rather than logging them as cancellation.

No new config, RPC/SDK contract, permission policy, persistent suppression, scheduler, or review prompt.

## Evidence

[Built Gateway / real Chromium before-after proof and inspected screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178145#issuecomment-6538191973).

At `17a43dbe566246b2027ee8494f50a20338e2aa91`, separately built Gateway and Control UI in secretless Node 24.22.1 Docker exercised the real shipped Stop RPC against an in-progress review. Only model responses came from a deterministic local provider.

Final head `0c81d38d0c56dab685f7cf1cce1db5ba17666425` changes only the scheduler test's braces and redundant timer cleanup/assertion from that runtime-proven revision; production, built artifacts, provider fixtures, and runtime inputs are unchanged. The final test was checked again in Docker: formatting clean, focused Oxlint 0 warnings/errors, and 11/11 passed.

- Frozen main twice: Stop was accepted, but the active review request remained alive and subsequently completed.
- Candidate twice: Stop closed the review request in 15 ms and 5 ms; neither review completed afterward.
- Both refs: a no-Stop review completed; non-explicit foreground interruption yielded the active review and later learning recovered; an authenticated non-owner Stop was rejected without cancelling foreground work or its queued review.
- Real Chromium session captures preserve the visible chat control; provider-observation captures show the hidden request cancellation. The screenshots do not claim that background reviews are shown in chat.
- Focused scheduler suite: 11/11 passed; changed-file formatting passed. On frozen main, the same suite fails the explicit Stop case because the cancellation operation is absent, alongside three expected signal-signature assertion differences.

## Simplification

Removed three forwarding wrappers and unused timestamp computation. Reused the existing scheduler suite for counters, queued cancellation, stopped-completion suppression, and interrupted learning instead of adding a standalone suite and repeated bridge-mock assertions. Existing baseline tests remain intact.

Against integrated main: production +249/-14 (263 gross, down from 288); tests +25/-25 (net 0); no added test/support files. Contributor commits are retained.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the former cancellation behavior; no schema/config migration or durable state is introduced. Blast radius is explicit Stop's connection to session-scoped Workshop review scheduling and active model cancellation. Rejected Stops, later turns, independent cleanup failures, and non-explicit interrupted learning must remain unchanged.

prs.title: perf(ui): speed up warm model searches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Warm model searches build temporary arrays and scoring objects for every catalog row, sort six fixed score classes, and read provider disclosure state even when the query ignores it.

## User Impact

The same search results, match priority, catalog-order ties, shortcuts, and disclosure state are preserved with less work. In 20 interleaved warm-search pairs, desktop Chromium median improved 8.8% and p95 improved 10.9%. WebKit desktop/mobile medians improved 4.1%/3.9%, with lower p95s. These are synthetic 1,000-model picker measurements, not live provider latency.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use six ordered buckets and assign final ranks in one pass. Query searches stop subscribing to unused disclosure state. The existing memo still filters identical results; no new state owner, cache, subscription, dependency, or eager import is introduced.

The benchmark additions retain the existing two-frame waits, record their frame intervals, and add explicit-only blank-frame and native-input controls. They distinguish cadence and input costs without subtracting them from wall time or treating them as universal latency floors. Default scenario selection stays unchanged.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Complete baseline census | 2,840/2,840 passed; 36 scenarios, 71 numeric desktop/mobile rows + one mobile split-pane N/A; 10 A/A pairs per numeric row |
| Picker comparison | 240/240 passed, then 120/120 warm-search confirmation observations; identical harness/bundle provenance checked before pooling |
| Search/ranking correctness | 10 tests passed across the existing search and picker suites |
| Type, lint, formatting | UI and scripts typechecks; targeted lint/format passed |
| Production build / strict asset check | Passed; startup JS 88,759 -> 88,756 B gzip (build variance), startup CSS unchanged at 33,559 B / 1 request |
| Production Knip / independent review | Passed; independent P0–P2 review reported no actionable findings |

All timings are headless on the same macOS host using Chromium 156.0.8078.4 and WebKit 27.2, production HTTP bundles, localhost synthetic Gateway, serial interleaved base/head/base runs. The paired baseline is the geometric mean of the two controls. Traces are excluded. No WebKit CPU claim is made. Chromium warm-search script CPU fell 24.0% desktop / 23.0% mobile; task CPU fell 12.5% / 13.4%.

| Engine | Viewport | Action | Pairs | Paired median change | Paired baseline / head p95 (ms) | A/A median drift |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| chromium | desktop | model-picker-first-open-search | 10 | -2.68% | 197.4 / 194.8 | +0.35% |
| chromium | desktop | model-picker-open-search | 20 | -8.79% | 146.9 / 130.9 | -0.51% |
| chromium | mobile | model-picker-first-open-search | 10 | -5.46% | 186.8 / 164.0 | -6.89% |
| chromium | mobile | model-picker-open-search | 20 | -2.20% | 144.8 / 130.8 | +0.15% |
| webkit | desktop | model-picker-first-open-search | 10 | -2.09% | 296.3 / 295.9 | +0.23% |
| webkit | desktop | model-picker-open-search | 20 | -4.06% | 220.6 / 215.2 | +1.70% |
| webkit | mobile | model-picker-first-open-search | 10 | -0.50% | 250.8 / 246.7 | +0.30% |
| webkit | mobile | model-picker-open-search | 20 | -3.85% | 203.1 / 198.1 | -0.70% |

The extra ten warm-search pairs resolve the initial tail outliers. Every final paired p95 is lower. The first-open mobile Chromium A/A drift was noisy, so its apparent improvement is not the primary win. The 20-pair Chromium CPU measurements support less actual work.

The census remains above target in 47 of 71 numeric rows; this PR does not claim to close every WebKit gap. Controlled replay identified the mobile Settings cost as the intentional spring timing in #188162 and the desktop fast-scroll regression as #188470's necessary deferred row measurement (+23.52% at its exact parent/head boundary). The prior positioning commit #186295 was not the cause (+1.88%). Existing resize-loop protection stays intact. Cron/Sessions ratio changes did not establish source regressions after controlled historical replay. Three other runtime experiments were rejected and are absent from this diff.

Simplification: production +23/-10 lines, benchmark/support scripts +158/-13; seven changed files total 6,372 -> 6,530 lines (+158 net). The added production lines replace per-row allocation and comparison sorting with explicit bounded buckets. Reactive-owner, listener, cleanup, async, and cache counts are unchanged. prs.title: fix(state): type the handle-adoption schema admission race for retry and replay
prs.body:
Fixes #188935

## What Problem This Solves

When a concurrent publisher revokes an agent database's schema proof during the worker's handle adoption, the guard in `adoptAgentValidationSchema` throws a plain `Error("Agent schema admission changed before handle adoption; retry the operation")`. In the report, the publisher is memory-core republishing after an index refresh. The same race at publication time throws the typed `AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError`, and that is the type the recovery code recognizes:
- `isReplayableWorkerTranscriptCommitError` treats it as a replayable worker transcript commit;
- the native open path treats it as `open-refused`, which leads to fresh admission;
- the bounded startup publication retry (#178577) retries it.

The plain error matches none of these. In the report, a completed 54-minute turn ended with only "OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply", even though the error text says "retry the operation".

## User Impact

Losing this race now goes through the existing retry and replay paths instead of discarding the turn's reply.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper's next step on the issue: "Fix handle-adoption error classification". The adoption site now throws `AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError` with an optional stage name, so the message still says "before handle adoption" and the publication message is unchanged. No classifier changes: every existing `instanceof` check now applies to the adoption race too.

## Evidence

Windows 11 / Node 26.12.1.
- **Setup:** the production `adoptAgentValidationSchema(…, reuseIntegrity=true, required=true)` is driven with a schema proof that a concurrent publisher revoked (valid flag 0).
- **Check:** the thrown error goes to the production `isReplayableWorkerTranscriptCommitError`. The native-open column mirrors the `instanceof AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError` check in `openclaw-agent-execution-native.ts`; the harness does not call that code.
- **Variable:** same harness; only `agent-database-admission-error.ts` and `openclaw-agent-db-validation-schema.ts` differ between main 2908f7a and this branch.

![proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/188935/proof-188935.png)

| | main 2908f7a | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| message | `Agent schema admission changed before handle adoption; retry the operation` | same text |
| type | plain `Error` | `AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError` |
| worker transcript commit replayable | false (terminal) | true |
| native open failure kind | `native` | `open-refused` (fresh admission) |

The regression is the existing case in `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-cache.test.ts`, "distinguishes raced publication from malformed receipts even after revocation" (race=schema). It now asserts the typed error instead of the message.
- **On main:** it fails with "expected error to be instance of SchemaAdmissionChangedError".
- **With this change:** it passes. The test line count goes down by one.

Other cases in that file: 47 pass. 4 fail on this Windows checkout with `EPERM` from `fs.renameSync` over an open SQLite file. Those cases replace the database file and are unrelated to this change. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-cache.test.ts`.

Not reproduced: the live memory-core publication race inside a long turn. It needs a publication to land inside the worker's adoption window, and the reporter saw it once.

Gates run locally: oxfmt, oxlint, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`.
