prs.title: fix(codex): don't resend a generated image already sent as a byte-identical copy
prs.body:
Fixes #186719.

## What Problem This Solves

A Codex turn can generate an image and then send it with `message(action=send, media=...)`. Sometimes the model sends a byte-identical copy of the image from another path, for example a workspace copy instead of the tool-image store file. In that case the end-of-turn channel final sends the same image a second time, without a caption. `CodexGeneratedMediaProjection.projectDelivery` maps a confirmed `message()` send back to the generated image only by path aliases (the gateway `mediaUrl` and Codex `savedPath`). It compares them with `normalizeMediaReferenceForComparison`, which deliberately does not resolve filesystem identity. A copy at another path therefore never counts as sent, and the generated image stays in `hostOwnedToolMediaUrls`. With `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"` it is then delivered despite source-reply suppression.

## User Impact

When the model has already sent the same bytes to the same chat through `message()`, the generated image is no longer sent again by the automatic final. Users see one photo, the captioned one, instead of the photo plus a captionless duplicate. A generated image that was **not** sent, including one where the model sent a different image of the same size, is still delivered exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper suggested extending the existing confirmed-media identity tracking rather than adding a Telegram-only hash or a filesystem-aware global normalizer. This change does that. Since `d9097a5`, the identity is taken from the bytes the send used. Since `642134e`, each confirmed delivery carries its own copy of that identity.

- `materializeImage` already has the decoded bytes when it saves a generated image to the gateway media store. It now records `{ bytes, sha256 }` for that file.
- For local workspaces, the existing `message()` argument preparation step now hashes each attachment **inside the agent workspace** before delivery reads it (`prepareCodexMessageMedia` in the new `message-media-identity.ts`). That step runs inside the tool call, under its abort signal. Since `67ccd00`, files are opened only through the workspace `root(…, { symlinks: "reject" })`, so links on any path component are rejected. Only regular files within the generated-image size cap are hashed, and **paths outside the workspace are never read**. This step runs before the message tool's media policy, so a denied host path (for example `/srv/private/report.png`) causes no filesystem I/O. Generated-image copies made by the agent live in its workspace.
- When a send is **confirmed**, `resolveConfirmedCodexMessageMedia` adds an immutable content alias for that send's own bytes (`codex-media-sha256:<bytes>:<sha256>`) to **that delivery's** `sourceUrls`. This happens in the existing `resolveMessagingMediaSourceUrls` callback, so `dynamic-tools.ts`, which is over its line cap, does not grow. There is no turn-wide or path-keyed state, so a later send of the same path to another chat cannot reassign an earlier receipt.
- `projectDelivery` registers each generated image's content alias next to its existing path aliases. A confirmed delivery whose alias matches therefore counts as that generated image for that delivery's target only. This is synchronous and does no I/O, and route, destination and source-reply semantics are unchanged.
- Finalize is untouched. Nothing awaits filesystem I/O outside the settlement races, so the intent of `4c18a682922` ("Bounded terminal settlement") is preserved.
- Out of scope: remote-workspace runs keep path-only matching, because their sources are staged copies. Relative `media` paths are skipped, since their meaning depends on the caller's cwd.

## Evidence

### Tests

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.media.test.ts` has one new case, "matches confirmed workspace copies of a generated image by the bytes each send used". It materializes a generated image G and sends three real `message()` dynamic-tool calls through `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` with `workspaceDir` set:

| send | file and bytes at send time | expected | main | previous head `d9097a5` | this branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `chat-a` | `<workspace>/copy.png` holding different bytes D | G not sent | not sent | **sent** (turn-wide map took G from the later overwrite) | not sent |
| `chat-b` | the same path, overwritten with G after `chat-a`'s send | G sent to `chat-b` only | **not sent** (bug) | sent | sent |
| `chat-c` | a byte-identical copy of G **outside** the workspace | not hashed, so G not sent | not sent | **sent** (outside the workspace and hashed) | not sent |

These results were measured by running this test against each version's source. On main it fails on `chat-b`, and on `d9097a5` it fails on `chat-a` and `chat-c`. It passes on this branch (`67ccd00`), and the file passes 12/12.

**Test-line ratchet:** the base tree is already over the repo-wide ceiling (6,310,615 > 6,310,000). The three earlier copy cases and the destination case are folded into this single table-driven case, and the PR now adds 37 net test lines, down from 68. One regression for a P2 duplicate send and a security-relevant scope check seems the minimum. The reviewed tree is 584 lines over the ceiling before this PR, so even a fully offset diff would only pass by deleting unrelated coverage. I would rather leave the remaining 37 lines to the next maintainer budget reserve, as in #186785, than trim other suites. If you prefer, I can drop the outside-workspace row instead.

oxfmt, oxlint, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` and `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet` are clean. In `dynamic-tools.test.ts`, "keeps Codex apply_patch containment diagnostics operator-only" fails both with and without this change on Windows. `run-attempt.test.ts` gives 118/119 here and on base `d5f7d57eff5`; the one failure is the same already-failing Windows case. `run-attempt.final-media.test.ts` passes 4/4.

### Live run (Windows 11, Node 26.12.1)

This is a real `openclaw gateway run` with Telegram (local Bot API stand-in) and the Codex harness, whose app-server is a local stand-in built on `scripts/e2e/lib/codex-app-server-fixture.mjs`. `messages.visibleReplies: "message_tool"` is set. The Telegram DM "Draw a lobster and send it to me." starts one Codex turn:

1. an `imageGeneration` item with an inline PNG (sha256 `de8fdd84…`);
2. an `item/tool/call` for `message` with `{ action: "send", message: "Here is your lobster.", media: "<workspace>/out/lobster-copy.png" }`;
3. a final `agentMessage`.

The Bot API stand-in logs every upload's caption, size and the sha256 of the PNG inside it.

![live run v2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/186719/proof-186719-v2.png)

| scenario | main `a74f408db7f` | this branch `d9097a5cd94` (re-run on `67ccd00b065` with workspace-scoped hashing: identical copy → 1 × `sendPhoto`; different image → 2 × `sendPhoto`, the unsent generated image still delivered) |
|---|---|---|
| `message()` sends a byte-identical copy | **2 × `sendPhoto`**: caption "Here is your lobster." and a captionless duplicate, both 7826 bytes, sha256 `de8fdd84…` | **1 × `sendPhoto`**: the captioned `message()` send only |
| `message()` sends a different image (`59d822ee…`) | not run on main | 2 × `sendPhoto`: the sent image plus the never-sent generated image `de8fdd84…` |
| a different image is sent, then the copy path is overwritten with the generated bytes before the turn ends | not run on main | 2 × `sendPhoto`: no false match, and the generated image is still delivered |

No code changed in `extensions/codex`, `extensions/telegram`, `src/auto-reply/reply` or `src/agents/harness` between `a74f408db7f` and this PR's base.

### Live run: no pre-policy reads outside the workspace (review's security / merge-risk items)

This uses the same real Gateway, Codex harness and Telegram rig. The model's `message(action=send)` attaches a byte-identical copy of the generated image, either **outside the workspace** (`proof-outside-dir/lobster.png`) or through a **workspace path that is a junction escaping to that directory** (`ws/proof-escape/lobster.png`). Windows junctions need no admin rights; plain symlinks do.

A `--require` preload wraps `fs.open`, `fs.openSync`, `fs.readFile`, `fs.readFileSync`, `fs.createReadStream`, `fs.promises.open` and `fs.promises.readFile`. It logs every call on those paths in the Gateway process tree, together with the calling OpenClaw frames.

![pre-policy read trace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/186719/proof-186719-v3.png)

| attachment | previous head `d9097a5` (hashed any absolute path) | this branch `67ccd00` (workspace root, links rejected) |
|---|---|---|
| copy outside the workspace | **1 read** by OpenClaw: `promises.readFile proof-outside-dir/lobster.png ← digestLocalMessageMedia` | **0** opens or reads by OpenClaw code |
| workspace junction → outside directory | **1 read through the junction**: `promises.readFile ws/proof-escape/lobster.png ← digestLocalMessageMedia` | **0** opens or reads by OpenClaw code |
| Telegram outcome (both heads) | the `message()` send of that path is refused, and the generated image is delivered once by the final reply | same |

The only other logged calls are the app-server stand-in writing its fixture, which have no OpenClaw frames. So the identity step no longer touches attachment content outside the workspace before the message tool's policy runs, including through a link.

### Not covered

The two-destination sequence is not shown in a live run. In `message_tool` mode, a non-final send to the source chat followed by a send to another chat makes the turn end without a final source reply, so the Gateway retries the turn. That makes the run unrepresentative. The bridge-level regression above covers this case through the real `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` and projector.


There is no run with a real Codex model and a real Telegram account. This environment has no Codex/OpenAI login or Telegram bot credentials. The app-server and Bot API stand-ins speak the real protocols, and the Gateway, Codex harness, Telegram plugin and outbound pipeline are the production code.

prs.title: fix(backup): truncated archive verification hangs before restore
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes backup verification hanging before restore when a PostgreSQL archive has a truncated gzip stream.

## User Impact

Damaged archives now fail promptly and close their temporary file handles. Archive verification keeps its existing single-pass behavior and corruption checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The streamed verification introduced in #188518 could throw while canceling an entry without an error listener, leaving another consumer waiting with an open file handle. Cancel every active consumer without re-emitting the error, then stop reading if cancellation occurs during a file write. The existing corruption test also checks that all opened handles close.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the original truncated-archive case timing out at 120 seconds before the fix. It now rejects in 81 ms on pinned Bun and 69 ms on Node 24.22.1.
- Pinned Bun: 101 tests passed across seven focused backup and startup-recovery files; one existing Windows-only long-path test skipped. Node 24.22.1: all 31 completeness tests passed.
- Scoped TypeScript, lint, format, test-line and line-cap ratchets, and diff checks passed. No timeout, retry, skip, assertion weakening or baseline increase.
- Fresh independent canonical autoreview of the accepted two-file patch: P0–P2, complete, no actionable findings. pr-simplify completed. Published source is verified against that accepted patch.
- Linux proof covers archive verification and staging restore; the existing Windows-only case was not exercised. Exact-head PR CI supplies broader proof.

Requested by @steipete
## Work sessions

[Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b5679712-7777-4ff7-a05a-81c1efab2069)

prs.title: fix(test): package extraction check fails on Windows
prs.body:
Related: #188661.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Windows CI failing the digest-bound package extraction test introduced by #188661 because Windows reports file mode `0666` rather than POSIX `0755`.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. Package validation tests can run on Windows while POSIX still requires exact `0755` executable permissions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the platform condition only to the executable-bit assertion. Keep manifest validation and all valid extraction, digest-mismatch and link-rejection variants on every platform.

## Evidence

- Reused the exact [Windows failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41151564335/job/124389364304) on `ac897d3b339ee8c91eac5dab2a853d48364eb808`; cached log integrity verified, no redownload.
- Node 24.22.1: all 84 owner cases pass (42.287s). Pinned Bun: 82 cases pass, and the two pnpm-produced fixture cases pass through the same installed pnpm 12.15.0 JavaScript entrypoint (3.951s), qualifying its shebang-less host launcher.
- A real POSIX extraction mutation still fails the exact `0755` assertion; restored production bytes and the focused valid/digest/link case pass. Scoped strict typecheck, typed lint, oxfmt/Bun parity and ratchets pass; no baseline or allocation growth.
- Fresh-context independent P0–P2 source review found no actionable issues. The canonical helper stalled at host Python startup; the explicitly authorized fallback lacks helper-owned isolation and validated machine status. It did not independently rerun tests.
- Native Windows proof belongs to PR CI `checks-windows-node-test-4` if that shard runs. The current exact-head PR run has a skipped Windows matrix and does not include that shard, so native Windows green remains unverified. Local Linux proof does not establish it.

## Worked on by

- @steipete
- @galiniliev

Requested by @steipete

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b5679712-7777-4ff7-a05a-81c1efab2069)

prs.title: fix(test): stabilize bounded context read counts after rewrites
prs.body:
Related: #187989

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a model-context CI test failing intermittently when transcript projection writes overlap its second read.

## User Impact

The fixture reliably checks the intended two-read contract. There is no user-visible runtime change.

## Why This Change Was Made

#187989 moved slow history reads outside writer admission and updated this test to expect refreshed messages after one retry. The native rewrite also schedules background projection reconciliation; those later writes can legitimately trigger the serialized fallback added by #188073. The fixture now joins that reconciliation before returning its first stale read. The exact two-call assertion and both refreshed-message checks remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- Directed scheduling reproduces the original expected-2/received-3 failure; the same qualifier passes with exactly two reads after the fix.
- 66 real-worker tests pass across the changed file and its two sibling suites on Node 24.22.1 and repository-pinned Bun.
- Scoped typecheck, lint, format, four ratchets and whitespace checks pass. Test count and test-line ceiling are unchanged.
- Fresh independent canonical P0–P2 autoreview: scoped-clean, no findings.
- Test-only change; production retries, timeouts and assertions are preserved. The historical CI scheduler interleave is unobserved; the controlled projection-write cause is proven.

Requested by @steipete

## Work sessions

[Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b5679712-7777-4ff7-a05a-81c1efab2069)

prs.body:

Related: #188335

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: npm plugins become unavailable when an update rolls core back after replacing them with plugins that require the newer core.

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

## User Impact

User impact: rollback restores the compatible plugin cohort and its settings, while preserving later independent plugin and config changes. This does not backport recovery into older released updater parents.

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain plugin install transactions until activation verification, and journal their owned artifact, record and config preimages in the existing update recovery owner. Reopened repair reacquires live custody and compares before restoring. Database restore retains only the exact recovery pair. The legacy reservation stays unchanged for released readers.

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

## Evidence

- Pinned main `edeae71308d8` RED through the registered updater: core rolled back while an incompatible npm plugin remained installed.
- Candidate source snapshot `1a2b2dd9c32b` (built before committing, stamped with base `edeae71308d8`) GREEN through registered rollback: exact prior plugin artifact/record/settings restored, old core reached ready and read-only RPC, and the verified backup stayed unchanged.
- Real foreground `update.run` GREEN: fresh ready successor, active plugin2, matching pending pair observed then committed/cleared, native custody released, settings and verified backup intact; all 16,826 installed payload files compared.
- Actual published 2026.10.9 (`8b18b5578f66`) → untouched candidate (`edeae71308d8`) upgrade GREEN: registered CLI exit0/statusok, exact loaded build and canonical payload (16,826/16,826 files), compatible plugin1/settings and backup preserved. Both packages report 10.9; distinct build IDs and the complete payload establish the upgrade. Canonical tar SHA-256: `1ce744571a21fde5bfc03ad714564e0f4aa16863be137eca9e6b5e7439270f4b`.
- Actual whole-container death/reopen/repeated settlement and later independent plugin/config preservation GREEN; success commit and failure after artifacts before index publication GREEN on unchanged recovery owners. Actual PostgreSQL 17 exact-pair restore/reopen and exact installed 10.9 reader/admission/old-cleanup checks passed. Prior proof is reused only where owner bytes are unchanged.
- Native regressions reproduced the foreground unwind and post-ready command-environment failures RED, then passed GREEN. Focused owner/consumer tests, targeted types, lint, format and the exact test-line ratchet pass. Final simplification is complete; fresh independent full-candidate Codex P0–P2 review completed scoped-clean (two complete passes, no accepted findings). prs.title: feat(sessions): protect selected conversations from automatic maintenance
prs.body:
## Current follow-through (October 30)

This remains an opt-in retention-contract proposal, not a merged or activated feature. The last published head is `5c54571a3aaacdf7bca44844c611d1dd1f831a52`; its test-type job and aggregate gate are still red. The obsolete fixture property identified in that job was repaired and type-checked in a retained local checkout, but that unpublished repair is not current-head CI evidence.

The outstanding behavior gate is isolated shipped-API retention across maintenance, restart, clearing and latest-stable upgrade; the earlier focused source tests do not replace that gate. Fresh GitHub readback on October 31 confirms this head now conflicts with main; integration and revalidation remain outstanding. Maintainer acceptance of the opt-in retention contract is still required. We are resuming this preparation within a shared-memory reserve and will not use a production Gateway as the experiment.

## What Problem This Solves

Long-lived nested project or course conversations can disappear through automatic maintenance, but cannot be pinned while preserving their sidebar hierarchy.

## User Impact

Operators can opt selected sessions out of automatic dashboard archiving, age pruning, entry caps, and disk-budget eviction with `maintenanceProtected: true` through the existing session patch API/tool. Discovery returns the flag. Existing defaults and sidebar placement are unchanged.

Protection includes historical transcript generations, survives reset/restart, and can be cleared with `false`. It requires the current `expectedSessionId`; batch targets carry their own identities. Manual archive/delete still work, and an existing archive is not automatically restored. Ancestors must be protected separately if they also need to remain visible. Protected data can exceed configured cleanup targets. Compaction, cold storage and managed-worktree GC are unchanged. No schema migration is needed; older versions ignore the field, so rollback also removes its protection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one optional field in the existing session entry and route it through the existing patch, discovery, lifecycle and maintenance owners. Pinning retains its current presentation constraints. No new retention service, database, global setting or UI state is introduced.

Author simplify pass retained only the existing-owner cutover and distinct regressions; removed a redundant standalone patch test. The feature extends the existing session owners; follow-up generated-validator changes are mechanical wrapper removal and regeneration. The remaining growth wires one persistent setting across all of its writers, readers and automatic cleanup paths. Maintainer review of this new opt-in retention contract is requested; this PR does not change defaults.

## Evidence

- 54 focused tests passed: maintenance writer (18), historical eviction preservation (7), patch expected-identity (15), and reset cleanup (14).
- Regression: a protected nested session survives each dashboard/age/cap phase while its unprotected sibling is archived; clearing protection restores normal maintenance.
- History regression first failed with 3 entries removed instead of 1, then passed after retaining every protected owner generation under physical disk pressure. Explicit reset/delete exclusions remain authoritative.
- Existing reset boundary test verifies retention survives lifecycle reset; patch boundary verifies identity admission, persistence, clearing and unchanged nesting.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm protocol:check` (registry, schema, native generation determinism, since guard), targeted typed lint, formatting and `git diff --check` passed.
- Measured local wall times with `--maxWorkers=1`: writer file 34.13s; patch file 128.11s (cold compiler); reset + history files 161.32s (cold compiler). History alone was 28.02s warm. Tests extend existing suites/fixtures; no new boot process or timer. CI timing is not yet available.
- Independent source reviews found and prompted fixes for historical-generation retention and PostgreSQL JSON-vs-JSONB handling. The standalone automatic reviewer could not start; no automatic clean-review result is claimed.

Not run locally: full repository suite and PostgreSQL runtime execution. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed upstream CI on 698f3b1bc7a. The predicate uses JSON-preserving extraction to avoid rejecting opaque entry strings during a JSONB conversion. No visual UI changes.



## CI follow-up

CI [39210419913](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39210419913) on `698f3b1bc7a` completed with 71 passed, 22 skipped, and 3 failed jobs. The two root causes were a redundant Boolean conversion in the new JSON test and New Session boot gzip 1,050,029 B against a 1,050,000 B ceiling (the measured base was already 1,050,021 B; candidate +8 B). The third failure was the aggregate gate. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards, database-dialect ratchet, generated-output checks, build, and previously failing node lanes passed on that head. A passing replay does not establish a root-cause fix for earlier chat-fixture failures.

Follow-up `c4113f94812` makes the SQLite assertion explicit about SQL 1 versus 0/NULL, and imports TypeBox's exact existing Unicode helper in the standalone-validator generator instead of its forwarding wrapper. All six owned outputs were regenerated. Validation logic, schemas, budgets, and gate enforcement are unchanged; no dependency version or installed dependency file was changed. The larger generated diff is helper-call renaming, redundant wrapper removal, and formatter/declaration-order effects.

All four JSON-owner tests pass (3.07s wrapper wall, 699ms test-run duration). All 23 canonical validator acceptance/rejection tests pass (6.98s wrapper wall, 4.46s test-run duration), including Unicode boundary coverage. Generator determinism, touched source formatting and diff checks pass. Native independent review found no P0-P2 findings and verified all six generated outputs preserve semantics. The standalone automatic reviewer remained unavailable; no automatic clean-review result is claimed. Isolated minified gzip estimates are not shipped-bundle proof.

[CI 39213084474](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39213084474) on `c4113f94812` completed with 77 passed, 22 skipped and two failures: UI performance plus the dependent gate. Main lint, all five core-lint stripes and PostgreSQL conformance passed. New Session boot was 1,050,294 B against 1,050,000 B (same-run base 1,050,257 B, head +37 B); failure classification was new, not an inherited-main exception. The Unicode wrapper removal alone was insufficient.

## Chat-only validator loading correction

Current follow-up `f3f40728171` separates the three goal-update, goal-clear and voice-event validators from shared `session-input` into generated `chat-input`. Only their two existing Chat consumers import the new group; New Session keeps its restriction and placement checks. There is no shared re-export, asynchronous event-admission change, schema change or validation removal. All owned outputs and the stock cold/warm boot manifest were regenerated. The manifest places the new group only in Chat; six additional reachable existing modules were captured by the canonical generator.

Same-machine, same-toolchain, frozen-build-identity stock UI builds measured:

| Route | Before | After | Delta | JS requests before/after | Fixed budget |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| New Session | 1,048,183 B gzip | 1,047,536 B | -647 B | 20 / 20 | 1,050,000 B |
| Chat | 1,487,825 B gzip | 1,487,955 B | +130 B | 25 / 25 | 1,490,000 B |

Both local product checks pass. These local absolute values differ from CI; actual exact-head upstream measurements remain required, not inferred. No budget, baseline, preload accounting or validation gate was weakened.

61 focused tests across canonical validator parity (23), Chat goals and Talk voice selection passed (9.30s wrapper wall, 6.34s test-run duration). Generator determinism, touched formatting and diff checks pass. Independent native review found no P0-P2 findings; all 11 moved/retained validator bodies and declaration signatures preserve semantics, all production imports are reconciled and the final boot manifest is consistent. The `transcript.js` follow-up is generated counter renaming only. Exact-head main CI had not started on f3f40728171 because the PR merge ref was stale and the generated boot manifest conflicted with current main. Earlier expensive host compiler/declaration checks remain incomplete rather than passing evidence; no live-gateway experiments were performed.


## Current upstream integration

Merged upstream `419653b638d8a53822d0c5ad919a6d05fb8e6c94` in `5c54571a3aa`. The only merge conflict was the generated boot manifest, resolved using the stock manifest generator with upstream loading rules. No budgets, baselines, chunking rules or gates changed. Dependencies were reconciled with the frozen lockfile.

All 65 affected tests pass after integration (four JSON-owner tests plus 61 validator/Chat/Talk tests; 12.38s wrapper wall). Generated-output determinism, touched formatting and diff checks pass. Independent native review of the effective feature diff against the new base found no actionable P0-P2 findings, including preservation, lifecycle, cleanup and generated loading paths.

The repository's strict same-machine comparison against exact upstream `419653b638d` passed with frozen build identity and canonical compression:

| Route | Upstream base | Candidate | Delta | JS requests base/candidate | Fixed budget |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| New Session | 1,050,423 B gzip | 1,049,473 B | -950 B | 20 / 19 | 1,050,000 B |
| Chat | 1,486,626 B gzip | 1,486,488 B | -138 B | 25 / 24 | 1,490,000 B |

The validator split remains necessary: current upstream alone still exceeds the New Session ceiling. Candidate headroom is 527 B. This is shipped-byte/request-count evidence, not a latency claim. Exact-head upstream CI remains required before local installation; no live changes have been made.

## Problem and change

First visits to Board, Usage, and Appearance wait through avoidable lazy-module discovery waves over remote Gateway connections. Appearance also acquires value-validation code although its display-only route does not validate values.

Start the two required Board presentation modules together at route activation, preload the measured page targets alongside their known dependency graphs, and group small Settings helpers already loaded together. The existing preload resolver uses Vite's chunk stylesheet metadata because Vite strips CSS before calling the dependency callback. Evaluation still follows Vite's stylesheet readiness; ordinary Chat, New Session, and optional artwork retain their existing lazy boundaries. Unchanged structural schema readers move to their traversal owner, leaving form edits with the existing validation owner.

No protocol, authorization, dependency, or configuration contract changes. The benchmark now distinguishes visible cached transcript, authoritative history, ready CPU, and CPU after its existing bounded settling tail.

## Current-head evidence

**Acceptance:** Board improves by 22.0% at 100 ms RTT and 35.9% at 250 ms RTT; Appearance improves by 20.0% and 11.3%. Both improve locally too. Usage improves by 12.8% at 250 ms, with a measured 4.3% readiness cost at 100 ms; its settled task/script CPU changes there are +2.1%/+0.7%, within the 5% noise band. This is accepted as a small scheduling tradeoff, not described as a universal Usage win. No startup growth or additional network contract is required.

Warm-visible targets are met at both RTTs. Switch targets miss by 14.2 ms and 416.8 ms; the remaining mobile response-delay source is not localized. | Cold Chat | D + max(A_chat, A_early + U + H + S [+ early approval handoff], max(A_route, A_early + U + H) + Q when uncached) + P. Initial history is already carried by S. | Same competing transport/render/resolution branches; no flat RTT sum or extra chat.history request. |
| Warm visible text / composer | D + max(cached chat/validator assets, local snapshot read/admission) + P. No awaited config HTTP, hello, or new history before cached display. Authority follows its separate U/H/S path, overlapping assets. | Same; config refresh is fire-and-forget and post-connect Q is not a cached-display gate. |
| Known-session switch | max(already-cached assets, one S) + P. Held roster avoids Q; old-observer release does not block the new pane. | Same; metadata and presence/viewer work remain concurrent decoration. |
| New Session | max(A_new, M if uncached) + P for plain /new. Selected model plus enabled textarea define readiness. | Same; models.list may gate readiness, sessions.catalog.list decoration does not. No session-create request until submission. |
| First Board | A_dashboard + P. Sidebar runtime precedes Board graph discovery and CSS delays entry requests; no required foreground Gateway RPC for the already-established fixture session. | Both existing runtime imports start at activation; measured target preloads with its graph. CSS evaluation order remains intact. Idle New Session imports are separate work. |

Clock starts at link restoration; cached text stays visible. | Same two-slot/foreground bootstrap scheduling. A successful periodic health probe can replace the client, adding its HTTP round trip and avatar refresh; ordinary retry can skip that mode. Do not count every prior RPC as a serial roster prerequisite. |

prs.title: fix(facetime): keep emoji whole at the transcript entry cap
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a FaceTime caller's transcript entry that ends with an emoji exactly at the 2,000-character cap leaves a lone UTF-16 surrogate in the text handed to the agent consult prompt.

## User Impact

User impact: emoji and other supplementary-plane characters at the FaceTime transcript cap are no longer split into invalid lone surrogates, so consult prompts always carry well-formed text.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript entry cap used a raw `slice(0, MAX_TRANSCRIPT_ENTRY_CHARS)`, which cuts by UTF-16 code units and can leave a lone high surrogate when an emoji straddles the cap. This was the one remaining naked text cap in the bundled FaceTime plugin; the rest of the repo was swept in the earlier "keep emoji whole at the cap" series (#186083, #181742, #182776, #101754). The cap now goes through the SDK facade `truncateUtf16Safe` (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`), the same pattern those merges used.

## Evidence

### Before fix
New regression test `keeps emoji whole when capping transcript entries for the consult prompt` failed: the transcript entry stored for the consult prompt was a 2,000-unit prefix ending in a lone U+D83D (cut emoji).

### After fix
Same test passes with the entry equal to a valid 1,999-unit prefix. Full file run: 20/20 tests pass (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/facetime/tests/talk-driver.test.ts`).

- oxlint (`--tsconfig extensions/tsconfig.json`): 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Format check: clean.
- Not verified locally: targeted tsgo typecheck — the tsgo native binary cannot run on this machine (glibc too old) and a full-graph `tsc` fallback exceeded the local time budget; CI covers the extensions type lanes.

Local diff review (openclaw-pr-review): PASSED, best-fix verdict, no findings.

### Real consult-prompt chain proof (added in response to review)

A temporary vitest probe (deleted after the runs; not part of the diff) drove the shipped module graph end to end. Only the inherently external seams were stubbed — the realtime provider transport (`createRealtimeVoiceBridgeSession`, `resolveConfiguredRealtimeVoiceProviderAsync`), the macOS audio pump, and the realtime bootstrap instructions builder. Everything in the transcript-cap → consult-prompt path ran as shipped: the PR's `startFaceTimeTalkDriver` cap code, the real SDK transcript recording, the real `openclaw_agent_consult` handling in the FaceTime consult controller, the real `consultRealtimeVoiceAgent` session machinery (session admission + fork against an isolated `createOpenClawTestState` store, real runtime agent), and the real `buildRealtimeVoiceAgentConsultPrompt`. The exact prompt handed to the model boundary (`runEmbeddedAgent`) was captured.

Input transcript delivered by the provider callback: 1,999 ASCII `x` + 😀 (U+1F600, surrogate pair D83D DE00) + `tail`, final.

Command:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extensions.config.ts --pool=forks facetime/tests/transcript-cap-consult-chain.proof.test.ts
```

(`--pool=forks` because the real consult session machinery opens a shared-state SQLite worker store that admits only from a main thread.)

**Before fix (current-main `slice` cap, same chain)** — the malformed entry reaches the real consult prompt:

```
[proof] MAX_TRANSCRIPT_ENTRY_CHARS = 2000
[proof] transcript block length = 2008
[proof] transcript block tail (JSON) = "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx\ud83d" code points: [120,120,120,120,120,55357]
[proof] lone surrogates in whole prompt = 1
```

(code point 55357 = U+D83D, a lone high surrogate.)

**After fix (this PR's `truncateUtf16Safe` cap, same chain)** — the boundary-crossing emoji is dropped whole; the prompt is valid:

```
[proof] MAX_TRANSCRIPT_ENTRY_CHARS = 2000
[proof] transcript block length = 2007
[proof] transcript block tail (JSON) = "xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx" code points: [120,120,120,120,120,120]
[proof] lone surrogates in whole prompt = 0
```

Full suite for the probe run: `Tests 2 passed (2)` on the PR head; on the unpatched cap the chain test fails exactly on the lone-surrogate assertion (`expected 'Caller: xxx…\uD83D' to be 'Caller: xxx…'`).

Relates to gap finding: facetime transcript cap splits emoji (free_text, evidence level B).

prs.title: fix #188929: record conversation turn instructions in the Codex trajectory projection
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: The Codex harness records its compiled-context trajectory event with only the rendered developer instructions, omitting the entire conversation-instruction component (`buildCodexConversationTurnInstructions`) that the same turn registers through the inference relay, leaving the host trajectory incomplete for instruction-level diagnosis (#188929).
- Solution: Include the same conversation-instruction component in the recorded `systemPrompt` projection, using the identical builder and arguments as the relay registration.
- What changed: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-turn-request.ts` (one component added to the recorded join); regression case and faithful `joinPresentSections` stub in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-turn-request.provider-review.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: The instructions actually sent to the model (the relay registration is untouched); the trajectory event shape and recorder API; the native rollout path; no instructions were added or removed at runtime.

Fixes #188929

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `context.compiled.data.systemPrompt` in the retained trajectory carried persona/skills/memory markers but not the conversation heading, inbound-metadata marker, source-conversation guidance, or current tool-bindings heading that the inference relay registered for the same turn.
- **Real environment tested:** This branch's worktree on Linux x64, Node v24.20.0, pnpm 12.15.0, driving the real `run-attempt-turn-request` turn-start path with the provider-review harness and asserting the recorded `developerInstructions` against the real `buildCodexConversationTurnInstructions` output.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  pnpm install
  OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/trajectory.test.ts \
    extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-turn-request.provider-review.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  before (production file restored to unmodified main, same regression case):
    × AssertionError: expected 'developer instructions' to contain
      'Current OpenClaw conversation instruc…'  (the recorded projection lacked the component)
  after (this patch):
    ✓ recorded systemPrompt contains "Current OpenClaw conversation instructions"
      and "Current OpenClaw tool bindings"
    ✓ run-attempt-turn-request.provider-review.test.ts: 15 passed (15)
    ✓ trajectory.test.ts: see suite result (all pass)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The recorded `context.compiled` projection now carries the same conversation-instruction component the relay registers (conversation heading plus current tool bindings), so instruction-level diagnosis sees the complete system prompt; runtime instructions are unchanged.
- **What was not tested:** A live Discord parent session was not re-run; the turn-start path is exercised through the repo's provider-review harness against the real builders, with only RPC transport and agent execution mocked. This host's `/` is world-writable without the sticky bit, so tests resolving the default rolling log path use the repo-supported `OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1` route, which CI does not need. tsgo could not run locally (GLIBC too old for the native binary); CI type lanes remain the guardrail.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt-turn-request.provider-review.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: a native acknowledged turn start records `context.compiled` whose `developerInstructions` contain the conversation-instructions heading and the tool-bindings heading produced by the real builder.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: it fails on unpatched main with the exact omission from the issue and pins parity between the relay-registered and trajectory-recorded instruction components without mocking the builder itself.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: the trajectory recording composed its `systemPrompt` from `buildRenderedCodexDeveloperInstructions()` (plus an optional MCP diagnostic notice) and never appended `buildCodexConversationTurnInstructions(...)`, while the inference-relay registration for the same turn composed a superset that includes it.
- Missing detection / guardrail: trajectory tests asserted the recorded prompt and event shape but never compared the recorded instruction components against the relay registration.

prs.title: fix(cron): bound runs before runner startup and retain cancellation
prs.body:
Related: #143624, #123419. Adjacent watchdog work: #184460 and #160804.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an automation can remain running indefinitely when its runner never reports startup, and disabling it can fail to cancel after run tracking is retired.

## User Impact

Finite automation deadlines now cover admission, setup, execution, and delivery. Disabling an active occurrence still cancels its exact runner after registry retirement, allowing another forced run after settlement. Busy-session waits now consume the configured job budget; unlimited jobs remain unlimited. Existing live-work and receipt fences remain in place.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deferred watchdog previously armed only its setup timer, which lane waiting clears; the wall-clock timer started only at `noteRunnerStarted`. Start that timer at entry instead. Bind marker cancellation directly to its captured handle rather than looking it up in a registry that teardown can clear. This removes the superseded lookup helper and introduces no new state or options.

A reported shared-session automation remained running past its 1700-second deadline after a Code Mode bridge error, with no active agent run or terminal cron record. The journal confirms that sequence, but does not establish where its agent promise stopped. The bridge catch already settles its failed reply; this repair targets the independently reproduced cron timeout and cancellation gaps rather than changing recoverable tool-error semantics.

## Evidence

- Base: `298546d88934bf05bc7e208d13bf6ce2c538e3f2`. Real cron timer/runner owners with held external runners: both no-start cases fail on base because no `TimeoutError` is raised; durable-disable-after-retirement fails because its controller remains un-aborted. Both pass after the fix, with terminal `timed_out` history, cleared `runningAtMs`, and successful forced re-admission after settlement.
- 43 tests pass, each run separately with `timeout 150`, an explicit `OPENCLAW_BUN_PATH`, `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun`, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`:
  - `timer.timeout-watchdog.test.ts`: 10 tests, 11.17 s command wall time.
  - `ops.disable-running.test.ts`: 1 test, 8.05 s.
  - `command-timeout.test.ts`: 10 tests, 8.57 s, including real child-process termination and retained output.
  - `session-run.test.ts`: 14 tests, 8.27 s.
  - `active-run-cancellation.test.ts`: 8 tests, 1.39 s, retaining shutdown/suspension visibility and sibling isolation.
- Touched-file core type-aware lint (`config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json`), formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. The initial lint invocation using `tsconfig.core.json` failed during unrelated plugin declaration preparation: installed `@openclaw/fs-safe` declarations lack `DirectoryMode` and reject string `dirMode`. The supported core-lint configuration avoids that package-boundary preparation. Full typecheck and broad proof are delegated to PR CI under the host IO emergency; no dependencies, operator state, or Gateway were changed.
- Fresh Codex autoreview of the complete local candidate against the base, with active-marker owner context: **P0–P2 scoped-clean**, no findings. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable on this host; the existing hosted ClawSweeper request was queued, so no duplicate request was posted.
- Simplification: production **−12 lines**, tests **−44 lines** against the base. Replaced the obsolete unbounded-wait cases with the wall-clock invariant and extended the existing disable regression; no test-line allowance. Exact-head [CI run 41161019407](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41161019407) passed at `f216d0ccfb772c214a50b3a0dada3b3379e27248` (530 s from run creation to completion). Security/dependency publication gates also passed.

Requested by @steipete

## Work sessions

[Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/06278ba2-46e2-491c-b138-d3f8848cbf45)

prs.title: improve(ui): reduce Usage model-filter tail latency
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large Usage histories rebuild analytics and session rows during model-filter refreshes, leaving the 4× main-thread task p95 above 200 ms after #188509 improved the worker path.

## User Impact

Model filters do less main-thread rendering work while preserving the existing layout, current totals, selection, pagination, exports, and error behavior. The final Chromium qualification puts both models below 200 ms p95 on localhost and with 100 ms added RTT.

## Why This Change Was Made

Retain analytics through the owner's existing strictly scoped snapshot while a text query is pending, keeping stale content hidden and inert. Preserve keyed session rows, remove callback identity from the mosaic computation, and retain cost-window cards and day columns across fresh data. The header, exports, and details still consume current query data; no new cache or query owner is introduced.

The benchmark now supports native WebKit, separates traced diagnostics from untraced timing, verifies generated package outputs, pins a common fixture date, and captures synthetic lower panels after timing.

## Evidence

The workload is 12,000 sessions, 180 days, 96 models, two model queries, localhost/100 ms RTT, and 20 serial interleaved observations per role/cell. A and B are independent identical main controls. All backend processes use frozen `047084bac58269ef67f36c162f8ec567f70ee62e`; only the frozen UI build varies. Traced diagnostics are excluded. Metric: Chromium renderer main-thread `TaskDuration`, not INP or automation wall time.

| 4× / model | Main A median/p95 | This PR median/p95 | Main B median/p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Localhost / 00 | 179.81 / 230.19 ms | 153.80 / 172.88 ms | 189.96 / 239.52 ms |
| Localhost / 01 | 194.00 / 222.54 ms | 170.28 / 184.91 ms | 180.72 / 206.08 ms |
| 100 ms RTT / 00 | 185.93 / 205.14 ms | 144.81 / 157.65 ms | 166.78 / 223.18 ms |
| 100 ms RTT / 01 | 177.30 / 184.05 ms | 155.69 / 173.85 ms | 173.74 / 196.90 ms |

264 observations, zero correctness failures. Host load ranged 32.60–41.86. Task medians and p95 improve against both controls. Script medians improve in every cell; layout is largely unchanged. All filters still dispatch one cohort operation with zero packed-row bytes. The ten visible session rows now survive refreshes, and cost-window cards/columns retain identity.

In the slowest final p95 cell (localhost/model-01), the 184.91 ms sample comprises 40.89 ms script, 36.81 ms style, 24.87 ms layout, and 82.34 ms other task work. Its near-median sample is 170.46 ms: 37.16/33.41/22.91/76.98 ms respectively. RPC elapsed time is separate and is not additive to browser CPU. The remaining tail is largely browser task time outside the script/style/layout counters. The separate localhost diagnostics record 14.7 ms of main-thread GC intervals for model-01 and none for model-00; these elapsed trace intervals cannot be assigned to the untraced p95 samples and do not establish an irreducible GC floor. Whole-renderer process CPU is noisy: the 100 ms/model-01 median is 411.88 ms versus 388.67/386.35 ms controls while its task and script CPU improve. This is not an all-metrics-win claim.

Native WebKit also completed 264 observations with zero correctness failures. Its untraced **automation wall time** is shown separately; these are not CPU measurements:

| Native WebKit / model | Main A median/p95 | This PR median/p95 | Main B median/p95 |

prs.title: fix(meta): Muse subscription sign-in cannot be finished from chat and turns are rejected after sign-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `/login meta` in chat can never start the Muse device-code subscription sign-in (it always hands off to Control UI guided setup), and even after a successful sign-in every turn on `meta/muse-spark-1.3` fails — first with missing-auth errors on the wrong runtime, then with `Requested agent harness "muse" does not support meta/muse-spark-1.3`.

## User Impact

User impact: users can add and authorize Meta Muse models end-to-end in Telegram (device-code in the browser, no API key or secret handling in chat), and signed-in models actually run. Control UI guided setup behavior is unchanged. Security boundaries are preserved: nothing starts in chat without the plugin's explicit `channelLogin` opt-in (the same mechanism GitHub Copilot, xAI, MiniMax, and Codex device-code already use), API-key entry still hands off to secure setup, and no credentials pass through chat.

## Why This Change Was Made

Four stacked gaps, each fixed at its layer:

1. The `muse-code` choice never declared `channelLogin`, so chat could not start it.
2. `projectChannelChoice` only computed a login kind for `credentialOnly` choices; harness-owned sign-ins (no credential profile saved — the credential lives in the Muse CLI) always projected to setup-only even with an explicit chat opt-in.
3. Credential-only login persistence dropped the auth result's declared `agentRuntimeId`, so the model kept resolving to the default API runtime. It now stages the same per-agent model runtime policy guided setup writes (`prepareSetupModelRuntime`), scoped to the signing-in agent and the login's own default model, ignored for the default `openclaw` runtime. The persistence owner (`runProviderAuthMethod`) reports the staging outcome (`stagedRuntimePolicy`) itself, so chat completion and model-access consent do not reconstruct it from result metadata that the credential-only path drops. Runtime-plugin repair after the write receives the login's agent and authority: before each package, marker, or install-record effect, it reruns the caller's `beforePersistentEffect` and `assertCurrent`.
4. Prepared native routes carry a blank `baseUrl`, which masked the configured official Meta endpoint in harness support facts while `endpointOverrides` was derived from that same config — the Muse harness therefore rejected every turn. Blank prepared baseUrls now fall back to the configured endpoint (live diagnostic before the fix: `rt=muse provider=meta transport=none endpoint=present baseUrl= api=openai-responses`).

## Evidence

Head `9366401038d` (merged current `main` at `fc64180eda0`; the merge was clean).

ClawSweeper findings fixed on this head (`src/commands/models/auth.test.ts`):

- **[P2] Return the persisted runtime-staging outcome to chat.** `runProviderAuthMethod` now returns `stagedRuntimePolicy` once the staged policy is persisted (or already present). `runModelsAuthLoginFlow` passes it through instead of re-deriving it from `result.agentRuntimeId`, which credential-only results drop. Regression "reports the persisted runtime staging to chat for credential-only harness sign-ins": without the fix, `expected undefined to be true`; with the fix it passes. (Red runs used this head's tests with only the fix reverted, before the module extraction, which is behavior-preserving.) The cross-provider test now also asserts that nothing is reported staged.
- **[P1]/[high] Carry login authority into runtime-plugin repair.** `repairModelSelectionRuntimePlugins` accepts `beforePersistentEffect`, and its internal repair chain already forwards that hook to its dependency-marker, payload-retirement, and install-record effects. The login passes a hook that reruns its own `beforePersistentEffect` and `assertCurrent`, plus the login's `agentId`, so the agent-scoped staged policy is the one the repair evaluates. Regression "rechecks login authority before runtime-plugin repair effects" revokes authority while repair is pending. Without the fix, the login resolves and the repair effect runs; with the fix, the login rejects with "Login authority ended." and no effect runs.

**Data-model compatibility.** New test "keeps an existing stored config intact and valid when a chat harness sign-in stages its runtime". It starts from a config shaped like those earlier releases persisted: an authored `agents.entries.main` with `workspace` and per-model `alias`/`params`, an `agents.defaults.model.primary`, and an unrelated enabled plugin. The test checks that config validates, runs a chat (credential-only) harness sign-in, then asserts:

- every pre-existing value is unchanged;
- only `agentRuntime` is added to the signed-in model's existing entry;
- the unrelated plugin entry is untouched;
- the result still passes `validateConfigObject`.

No schema or migration changes. Session rows and auth-profile stores are not touched by this PR. The test passes both before and after the finding fixes; it proves preservation and is not a regression for a bug.

Focused suites on this head (`node scripts/test-projects.mts <files> --maxWorkers=1`), 6 files, 209 tests, all passing:

- `src/commands/models/auth.test.ts` (47)
- `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-login.test.ts`
- `src/plugins/provider-login-options.test.ts`
- `src/agents/harness/selection.test.ts`
- `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth-login-flow-runtime.test.ts`
- `src/commands/promos/claim.test.ts` (the other `repairModelSelectionRuntimePlugins` caller)

`tsgo` core and the `commands` test project are clean. `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and the pre-commit line-cap ratchet pass. To stay within the line caps, the PR's runtime-staging computation moved unchanged from `auth.ts` into `src/commands/models/auth-runtime-staging.ts`, and its tests moved into `auth-runtime-staging.test-support.ts`, which `auth.test.ts` registers.

Live verification on a real Telegram + gateway install, before/after on the same account:

- Before: `/login meta` answered "Meta API key needs provider setup. Open Control UI…". After an out-of-band sign-in, turns failed with missing-auth on the API route, then with `Requested agent harness "muse" does not support meta/muse-spark-1.3`.
- After (earlier head, author's install): Muse Spark and Muse Wonder Full turns succeed with the session reporting the Muse runtime.

**Live proof pending (needs the author's real accounts and phone):**

1. A fresh Muse device approval started by the owner with `/login meta` in a Telegram private chat, reaching "login complete", the model-access consent prompt (with a restricted model list), and a working Muse turn.
2. A non-owner `/login meta` rejected before any process starts.
3. Owner revocation during a pending login, showing no config, package, or install-record effect afterwards.

The earlier `live-traces/` reference was not reachable by reviewers and is withdrawn; redacted captures will be attached to the PR.

**Needs a maintainer decision (ClawSweeper "Decision needed"):** should explicitly opted-in (`channelLogin`) profileless native sign-ins run from private chat and persist agent-scoped runtime routing without guided setup activation? This PR keeps runtime installation, native-permission consent, and current-authority checks in place for that path.

prs.title: fix(models): signed-in native runtime loses to a runtime preference pinned before sign-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after completing a native/CLI subscription sign-in (for example Muse), chats keep resolving the model to the default API runtime and fail with missing-auth errors, because a runtime preference stored while unauthenticated suppresses the signed-in runtime forever — and runtime-choice preparation never validated the stored preference at all.

## User Impact

On re-selection, the stored runtime preference is now validated against current availability:

- A stored preference that is still available always wins (unchanged behavior).
- A stored preference that no longer evaluates available (missing credential, expired sign-in, cooldown) makes selection fail with provider sign-in guidance for that runtime — it is **never silently replaced** by another runtime. This follows the no-silent-switching principle from #150224: re-selection validates the pin, it does not replace it. The user recovers by signing in (chat sign-in buttons / Control UI handoff) or by explicitly choosing a different runtime.
- Sessions without a stored preference keep existing discovery behavior: a claiming CLI/native runtime may be selected when available. Stored rows holding the "no preference" values `auto` or `default` (any casing) are read the same way and are never treated as a pin.
- A required `inference="worker"` profile keeps ownership of runtime selection (pinned or unpinned), so re-selection never validates worker-local credentials on the gateway.

Plain turns without re-selection are untouched; implicit runtime choices saved as pins at write time are a separate follow-up.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two stacked causes: session runtime overrides skipped CLI/native runtime discovery entirely, and dual-route models that list the API catalog row first skipped runtime-choice preparation even when a native variant exists. The change always discovers claiming runtimes, treats a native variant as requiring runtime choice, and passes a stored real runtime id (not `auto`/`default`) to runtime-choice preparation as a dedicated `pinnedRuntimeId`. Availability-filtered choices (`runtimeChoices` only contains runtimes that evaluated available) decide the outcome: pin available → pin wins; pin unavailable → selection returns the existing unavailable message with sign-in guidance instead of falling through to `choices[0]`.

## Evidence

Head `8a46c50e100` (merged current `main` at `fc64180eda0`). The only conflict was in `src/agents/model-runtime-choice.native.test.ts`: `main` added an independent native-only spawn `it.each`. Both sides were kept. The source files merged cleanly and their diff against `main` is only this PR's change.

**Data-model compatibility (new on this head).** No schema, config, or migration changes. Existing session rows are read as stored, not rewritten. A new stored-row test, "reads a stored runtime override … from an existing session row", feeds session rows shaped like those earlier releases persisted (`sessionId`, `updatedAt`, `providerOverride`, `modelOverride`, optional `agentRuntimeOverride`) through re-selection. Values covered: absent, `"auto"`, `"default"`, unnormalized `" Auto "`, legacy alias `"pi"`, and `"OpenClaw"`. This test found a real regression in the previous head: rows storing `auto`/`default` became a hard pin on a runtime id that is never a choice, so re-selection was rejected. Fixed in `8a46c50e100`; those rows now stay unpinned.

- Previous PR head `1e2a8b9438a`: `auto`, `default`, and `" Auto "` fail (`rejected`); the others pass.
- This head: 6/6 pass.

**Red on base.** These are this PR's regressions run against `main`'s `model-runtime-choice.ts` and `model-runtime-normalization.ts` with this branch's tests. All fail with assertion errors; on `main`, every case returns `ready` with the runtime `unchanged`, because API-first dual-route re-selection never reaches runtime-choice validation:

- "does not silently switch from a stored openclaw preference pinned while signed out…": expected `rejected`, got `ready`.
- "keeps a stored openclaw preference when its route is still signed in": expected `{ kind: "set", runtime: "openclaw" }`, got `{ kind: "unchanged" }`.
- All 6 stored-row cases fail.
- Base totals: 8 failed, 21 passed. This head: 29/29.

The two required-worker re-selection tests pass on both base and head. They guard the earlier P1 against regression and are not red-on-base proofs.

Focused suites on this head (`node scripts/test-projects.mts <files> --maxWorkers=1`), 5 files, 170 tests, all passing:

- `src/agents/model-runtime-choice.native.test.ts` (29)
- `src/auto-reply/reply/directive-handling.model.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-methods/agents-model-selection.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-mutations.sticky-model.test.ts`
- `src/model-picker/apply-session-model-selection.test.ts`

`tsgo` core and the `agents-other` test project are clean. `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on touched files.

Before the fix, on a real install: `meta/muse-spark-1.3` turns kept failing after a completed Muse subscription sign-in, because every turn resolved to the `openclaw` API route ("No API key found for provider meta").

**Live proof pending (needs the author's real accounts):** a redacted chat transcript plus gateway log covering (1) re-selecting the Muse model with a stored signed-out `openclaw` pin, which should be rejected with sign-in guidance; (2) the same with the API route signed in, which should keep the pin; (3) explicitly choosing the Muse runtime, which should give a working turn. Also pending: an upgrade from v2026.10.6 with existing sessions, showing runtime pins, account choices, and session settings preserved. The stored-row test above covers the session-row shapes in-process; it does not replace that upgrade run.

prs.title: fix(models): model picker switches chat to models the user cannot sign in to from chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: selecting a listed but unauthenticated model in the chat model picker (for example `meta/muse-spark-1.3` before Meta sign-in) reports success, pins the chat to a model that can only fail authentication, and then answers every message with a generic HTTP 401 that gives no direct way to authorize — forcing the user to switch back to another model and hunt for the sign-in flow.

## User Impact

Tapping a model whose provider has no working sign-in now keeps the current model and immediately shows how to connect that provider: a tappable sign-in button for OAuth/device-code providers, secure API-key entry instructions for API-key-only providers (for example OpenCode Go), and a deep link to Control UI → Settings → Model Providers (carrying `?provider=&agent=`) when the gateway advertises a public origin. Auth failures at run time name the provider and carry the same buttons instead of generic boilerplate.

Not blocked: ready, unconfirmed, and cooling-down models; reset-to-default and default selections; and selections on a gateway whose `cloudWorkers.requiredProfile` is a worker-inference device profile (provider credentials live on the node there, per #170132), unless the selection pins an explicit Gateway account. No secrets are requested or stored in chat, and no credential-bearing links are placed in chat.

## Why This Change Was Made

The picker already computed per-model readiness for display, but selection ignored it, and failure copy dropped the provider before rendering.

- The policy lives in the shared selection owner (`applySessionModelSelectionInternal`). Adapters opt in by passing the exact menu facts they rendered (`authReadinessMenu`); a rejection is a dedicated `reason: "auth"` result with a required `authBlock`. Telegram only renders the result. Typed `/model` and `sessions.patch` keep their current behavior and only gain the better failure guidance.
- Menu readiness describes Gateway credentials, so it cannot judge required worker-local inference. The #170132 exception is now one exported predicate in the runtime-normalization owner (`isProviderAuthOwnedByRequiredWorker`), used both by runtime preparation and by the picker gate. Gateway inference, optional placement, and explicit account pins stay gated.
- Each provider's concrete login route is resolved so recovery can tell API-key entry from OAuth sign-in. The provider is carried through failover facts, including typed auth errors buried in the cause graph. Provider ids are slug-validated before they are embedded in commands or guidance.

**Needs a maintainer decision (ClawSweeper "Decision needed"):** should Telegram reject unauthenticated picker selections through the new optional `authReadinessMenu` SDK parameter and `reason: "auth"` result variant, while other selection surfaces (Discord/Mattermost pickers, typed `/model`, `sessions.patch`) keep their current behavior? The PR is built so other adapters can opt in with the same contract later.

## Evidence

Head `484c1ad61fd` (merged current `main` at `fc64180eda0`).

Merge with `main`: conflicts in `failover-classification.corpus.test.ts` (upstream removed neighbouring tests; only this PR's 401 test is added), `user-copy.ts` (kept upstream `TLS_CERTIFICATE_ERROR_USER_TEXT` plus this PR's provider helpers), `commands-models-catalog.ts` (kept upstream's `loginProviders` placement and replaced its filter with the loop that also builds `providerLogins`), and `agent-runner-error-handler.ts` (`buildExternalRunFailureReply` no longer takes heartbeat options upstream; only `config` is passed). The Telegram loopback test now reads the session via `listSessionEntriesAsync`.

Regression for the worker-local finding (`src/model-picker/apply-session-model-selection.test.ts`, "shared auth gate defers Gateway readiness only to required worker inference"; cases `worker`, `gateway`, `optional`, `account`):

- Without the fix: `worker` fails (`Expected: "applied"`, `Received: "rejected"`); the other three pass.
- With the fix: 4/4 pass.

Focused suites on this head (`node scripts/test-projects.mts <files> --maxWorkers=1`), 10 files, 225 tests, all passing:

- `src/model-picker/apply-session-model-selection.test.ts`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-models-menu.test.ts`
- `src/agents/failover/user-copy.test.ts`, `src/agents/failover/failover-classification.corpus.test.ts`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-failure-reply.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-provider-failures.test.ts`
- `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth-login-flow-runtime.test.ts`
- `src/agents/model-runtime-choice.native.test.ts` (the #170132 worker/gateway/optional/account suite, still green after moving its predicate)
- `extensions/telegram/src/model-callback.loopback.integration.test.ts` (blocked selection keeps the current model and renders the Sign in button)
- `ui/src/pages/model-providers/route.test.ts`

Typecheck: `tsgo` core, extensions, UI, and the `messaging`, `other`, and extensions test projects are clean. `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on touched files.

Removed per review: the `buildModelsMenu` "exposes per-model readiness and login providers" case, which only checked copied input identity.

Before the fix, observed on a real Telegram + gateway install: selecting `meta/muse-spark-1.3` printed "✅ Model changed", then every message returned "⚠️ Authentication failed (provider returned HTTP 401)…", and `/login meta` answered with setup text and no link.

**Live proof pending:** redacted Telegram screenshots of (1) the blocked picker selection with the Sign in button, (2) the Control UI handoff opening Model Providers for the right agent, and (3) a run-time 401 reply carrying provider-specific buttons. These need the author's real accounts and device. The earlier "live-traces package" reference was not reachable by reviewers and is withdrawn. The required-worker case is covered by the regression above, not by a live two-machine run.

prs.title: fix(ui): show website identity in dashboard gallery (#178467)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Dashboards whose primary content is a session:website widget appear as empty boards in the Dashboards gallery with the message 'A clear board, ready for work'. This occurs because session:website is registered with previewSafe: false to prevent passive code execution, causing board-document.tsx to filter out the widget and leaving BoardView with zero active rectangles (view().empty === true).

## Solution
Rather than changing previewSafe: true (which would allow unisolated iframes in gallery thumbnails), this change computes a safe websiteIdentity from authorized snapshot metadata during passive rendering. When BoardView detects an empty layout rectangle set, it inspects websiteIdentity and renders a recognizable website preview card featuring the built-in globe icon, saved title, and localized Website badge.

## Invariants & Security
- previewSafe: false is strictly retained in CORE_BOARD_WIDGET_ELEMENTS.
- Exactly 0 iframes or executable website widgets are mounted in passive mode.
- 0 network requests are initiated.
- Truly empty boards continue to display the standard empty-board prompt.
- Other unsafe widgets (agent:node-browser, mcp-app) remain isolated and do not display a website card.
- Mixed boards with preview-safe widgets (HTML) continue to render normal widget previews.

## Evidence
- Focused unit & integration regression tests: 27/27 pass.
  - ui/src/components/board/board-document.test.ts (14/14 pass).
  - ui/src/pages/dashboards/dashboards-page.test.tsx (6/6 pass).
  - ui/src/lib/board/widgets/website.test.ts (5/5 pass).
  - ui/src/lib/board/widgets/index.test.ts (2/2 pass).

prs.title: fix(update): measure state sizes in bounded chunks
prs.body:
Fixes #188897

## What Problem This Solves

On a large state directory every retained update capture ends `incomplete` ("no sealed manifest is available"), so the update has no usable recovery set even though it succeeds. The metadata inventory handed the whole path list to one child process and parsed one JSON array from its stdout; once the inventory exceeded roughly 6,000 paths the child was killed with `output-limit` and the capture was abandoned.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readUpdateStateDatabaseSizes()` (`src/infra/update-candidate-state.sizes.ts`) builds one `{ files }` payload for a single child with `maxOutputBytes: { stdout: 1024 * 1024 }` and `terminateOnOutputLimit: { stdout: true }`. The result array itself (path + size per entry), not the progress channel, crosses the cap on real inventories (~640,000 paths in the report).

The inventory is now measured in bounded chunks of 1,000 paths. Each chunk keeps the existing per-source inspection budget (`resolveAggregateSqliteInspectionTimeoutMs` divided across chunks), the same child script, the same output cap and the same diagnostics owner, and the results are concatenated in order. An empty path list short-circuits. A chunk that still trips the cap fails the capture exactly as before, so the failure mode is not hidden.

## User Impact

Updates on large state directories regain a sealed recovery set instead of always reporting `incomplete`; small installs keep the single-child behaviour because their inventory fits in one chunk.

## Evidence

Head `a2dc13c69e`, Node 26.12.1.

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/infra/update-candidate-state.sizes-chunks.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
✓ measures a large metadata inventory in bounded chunks
1 passed

# same test with update-candidate-state.sizes.ts reverted to the branch base:
× measures a large metadata inventory in bounded chunks
  AssertionError: expected [ 2500 ] to deeply equal [ 1000, 1000, 500 ]
1 failed

$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run src/infra/update-candidate-state.budget.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
18 passed | 1 todo | 1 failed
```

The remaining budget-suite failure (`budgets schema inspection for configured cache`) reproduces on the branch base in this checkout (temp-dir ownership check: `relative.split(path.sep)[0]` is `..`); it is unrelated to this change.

## AI Assistance
This PR is AI-assisted. Traced the `output-limit` termination to the single-child inventory payload, chunked the payload inside the existing owner, and added a regression that asserts the chunk sizes and the concatenated result. The implementer understands the code: chunking bounds only the child payload, so the capture seals while a genuinely oversized single chunk still fails loudly.

prs.title: fix: worktree sessions load their own bootstrap instructions
prs.body:
Supersedes #129413, thanks @krell11

Fixes #129411

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes worktree sessions receiving bootstrap instructions from the shared agent checkout instead of their recorded workspace.

## User Impact

Recorded worktree sessions use their own bootstrap files, including `AGENTS.md` and `SOUL.md`, while skill discovery stays anchored to the configured agent workspace. Runs restricted by `workspaceOnly` use their execution workspace. A cwd override alone does not change bootstrap identity.

Missing files have **no fallback to the shared checkout or a packaged template**. A worktree without `AGENTS.md` behaves like running the harness directly in that directory: no project instructions. OpenClaw retains its normal missing-file diagnostics. Rejected symlink paths and workspace escapes are logged and treated as missing; guarded reads remain inside the selected root. Other read failures retain their unreadable diagnostics.

**Native Codex boundary:** native project-document discovery remains Codex's documented loader operating on its cwd and permissions, including native symlink behavior. A native session whose cwd is the worktree already loads that worktree's documents. This PR changes neither native configuration nor the native loader and adds no in-memory defaults.

**Needs deploy:** affects Team worktree sessions directly; deploy after landing. No live Gateway changes were made during development.

## Why This Change Was Made

One selector in `workspace-run.ts` chooses the bootstrap root for embedded and CLI preparation. Bootstrap loading retains its existing session filters, budgets, and guarded filesystem reads. Skills resolve their configured anchor independently, so changing bootstrap cannot move the agent skill tier when a reusable snapshot is absent.

Production delta is **+19 lines**: the selector and its callers establish the recorded boundary, the skills change preserves independent ownership, and the loader preserves its diagnostic while marking typed symlink/escape rejections missing. The orchestrator adds zero lines. Shared workspace input types and duplicate config guards were consolidated in the same owner; there is no registry lookup, new state, or native configuration path. The separate test-line allocation covers 100 net lines of regression/support coverage.

## Evidence

- All five bootstrap/CLI regressions fail on main before the fix, as does the snapshot-less configured-skills regression. All six pass with the fix.
- Consumer run: **258 passed**, including bootstrap privacy/remote/memory consumers, workspace reads/cache, CLI preparation, embedded runtime, configured skills, native workspace snapshots, and prompt-prefix stability. Three existing library-read assertions fail identically with all six changed production modules restored from main: they expect `/regular file/i`, while the maintained filesystem reader reports `symlink path component not allowed`. This is retained as an investigated baseline failure, not counted as a passing test.
- Targeted lint, targeted typecheck of changed tests and their production import graph, formatting, `git diff --check`, and both production/full-tree unused-file scans pass. No full live-model proof was run.
- Final changed-file runs pass: CLI preparation **112 tests / 87.83s wall**, bootstrap preparation **19 tests / 10.63s**, and skills preparation **6 tests / 7.30s**. Wall times include compiler/startup overhead. The existing CLI suite exercises auth, MCP, and session recovery; the new case reuses that boundary fixture. The broader consumer run took 200.46s. Hosted CI remains the broad proof gate; CI timing is available in the linked checks after publication.
- The first PR CI head (`9a30e14`) exposed three assertions caused by overly broad missing-file classification (hard links, permission failures, and two-link atomic publication). The correction recognizes only typed symlink/escape failures. The affected workspace/read/bootstrap suites pass **89 tests**, and atomic publication passes **7 tests**; targeted lint and typecheck pass again.
- Final exact-head [CI run 41160224530](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41160224530) completed successfully for `28bfbb481e9d236622381d2808a1295dd3adda35` (10m19s). The exact-head watcher reached GREEN with zero pending checks; dependency and security-sensitive review gates also passed. Landed through `scripts/pr` as `80dead1a1837f1d9155c164cc76d17f5f1fc47a5`.
- Shared autoreview was rerun with a **300-second wall timeout** and produced no report (exit 124). No provider/route configuration changed. The authorized fallback fresh-context P0–P2 security/correctness review of the final diff against `3e1dbed3b0de4f1138e229a0564674c56f4c923e` found **no material findings**. It inspected the selector, all three consumers, guarded reads, skills ownership, and regressions; it was source-only and did not independently rerun tests or claim live/native proof. A follow-up fresh-context review of the CI correction also found no material findings. This is not a clean autoreview machine result.

The contributor's code was read through PR metadata/diff only and was never checked out or run. Human credit: krell11 <11bobin.kiryusha@gmail.com>; every replacement commit preserves that Co-authored-by trailer and excludes the agent trailer.
