prs.title: fix(agents): worktree sessions inject shared AGENTS.md bootstrap instead of worktree files
prs.body:
Closes #129411
Related: #129404 #129405

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where managed worktree sessions would inject `AGENTS.md` / `SOUL.md` / `BOOTSTRAP.md` from the shared agent home into the system prompt. After one agent used `exec` to rewrite shared `AGENTS.md`, later worktree sessions inherited the poisoned shared bootstrap and stopped following their own checkout.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runEmbeddedAgent` always passed `bootstrapWorkspaceDir: canonicalWorkspace` even when the session workspace was a managed worktree. Bootstrap loading and prompt file headings therefore stayed on the shared home. This change binds bootstrap to the managed worktree checkout **only when the resolved session workspace itself is remounted inside that worktree**. A cwd-only worktree binding no longer steals bootstrap identity for a still-canonical session.

Related remount work for the Working directory / file-tool root: #129405. This PR owns the bootstrap source separately.

## User Impact

Managed worktree sessions now receive bootstrap context from their own checkout. Rewriting shared `.openclaw/workspace/AGENTS.md` no longer rewrites the injected identity for later worktree sessions. Canonical sessions whose cwd happens to sit inside a managed worktree keep agent-home bootstrap.

## Evidence

### Isolation fix (ClawSweeper P1)

- `resolveWorktreeIdForPath` candidate list is `[resolvedWorkspace]` only (no `params.cwd`).
- `resolveRunBootstrapWorkspaceDir` returns canonical when the session workspace is outside the managed worktree root.
- Regression: canonical session + managed worktree supplied (cwd-only case) keeps `/…/workspace` bootstrap, not `/…/worktrees/…`.

### After-fix redacted selector trace

```json
{
  "scenario_remounted": {
    "sessionWorkspace": "/home/USER/tmp/ID/worktrees/0746a04e/wt-demo",
    "toolWorkspaceRoot": "/home/USER/tmp/ID/worktrees/0746a04e/wt-demo",
    "bootstrapWorkspaceDir": "/home/USER/tmp/ID/worktrees/0746a04e/wt-demo",
    "bootstrapAgentsContent": "WORKTREE_ONLY"
  },
  "scenario_cwd_only_must_stay_canonical": {
    "sessionWorkspace": "/home/USER/tmp/ID/workspace",
    "cwdInsideWorktree": "/home/USER/tmp/ID/worktrees/0746a04e/wt-demo",
    "bootstrapWorkspaceDir": "/home/USER/tmp/ID/workspace",
    "bootstrapAgentsContent": "SHARED_HOME"
  }
}
```

### Focused tests

- `prepareEmbeddedAttemptBootstrap` regression: when `bootstrapWorkspaceDir` is the worktree, injected files are worktree-only and exclude shared home `AGENTS.md`/`SOUL.md`.
- Focused Vitest: `workspace-run` + `attempt-bootstrap-prepare` suites passed (16 + 3) after the isolation fix.

<!-- EVIDENCE DRAFT: current head is rejected for first-rich-arrival CPU regression. Redesign required before landing; no fresh push is claimed. -->

Cold Chat evaluated tool, question, activity, and work-context presentation before any visible row needed it. This change puts that family behind one lazy entry while fetching its bytes alongside the Chat route. Plain text and media rows remain immediately available. The existing transcript range owner admits rich presentation only when the visible range requires it; while preparation is pending or fails, accepted rows retain their geometry, identity, focus, and foreign DOM. Failed imports expose reload recovery.

Label/icon consumers now use a small generated tool-identity catalog instead of importing argument-detail data. Both catalogs remain owned by the existing generator. No new dependency, public tag, CSS class, route, or selector is introduced.

**The current head is not landable: the corrected rich cohort confirms a first-arrival script CPU regression.** The ordinary cohort shows no attributable readiness regression, and the bytes improve modestly, but neither offsets the affected-interaction CPU failure. This is not a demonstrated latency win, and it does not meet the lane's approximately 950 KB unused-at-boot reduction target. The implementation needs redesign before another landing attempt.

## Exact comparison

The remote PR remains at `2dcf713b7f5d2e5087864a3d37d14c63642af0f0`; the measured local candidate below has not been pushed. Auto-merge is not armed.

- Base UI: `a32d79a2c763d3dab52022027fce38c34c7b3dea`.
- Head UI: `a8a127228f0529365162e8ade94221c37d8c76d9`.
- Local candidate source and benchmark runner: `a2dc5c832f92eca58ef92df2fbabb7964e5525a8`. Its changes after the UI build are an unused test-import fix and opt-in diagnostics; production UI source is unchanged.
- Corrected canonical harness manifest SHA-256: `e1b2856149e8066433dea3d03521b4d67bd0e1a498ee6d87094b7daaafbae130`.

## Production bundle bytes

Same-machine production builds and their strict performance checks, using Node 26.12.1 and shipped compression sidecars:

| Surface | Raw JS base → head | Gzip JS base → head | JS + CSS requests, both |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Startup | 277,716 → 277,716 B | 88,758 → 88,754 B | 3 + 1 |
| Chat | 4,066,722 → 4,050,817 B | 1,272,959 → 1,267,215 B | 20 + 3 |
| New Session | 2,512,276 → 2,502,871 B | 780,049 → 777,854 B | 15 + 3 |

Chat saves 15,905 raw B and 5,744 gzip B. New Session saves 9,405 raw B and 2,195 gzip B. The 4 B startup gzip change is within the 64 B build-variance allowance. Startup CSS remains one request, 192,369 raw B / 33,568 gzip B. These route-envelope totals are distinct from the actual HTTP resources below.

## V8 coverage and actual downloads

One diagnostic capture per variant/profile. These captures use the exact UI builds above; the retained coverage harness differs from the corrected timing harness. Their source/range and resource observations are used as structural evidence, not as latency or CPU acceptance.

| Captured boot | Evaluated V8 source, base → head | Executed V8 ranges, base → head | Unused V8 ranges, base → head | HTTP JS raw, base → head |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Ordinary localhost | 4,469,870 → 4,417,575 B | 1,988,860 → 1,971,359 B | 2,481,010 → 2,446,216 B | 4,810,164 → 4,807,756 B |
| Ordinary 100 ms RTT | 4,469,870 → 4,417,575 B | 1,984,210 → 1,965,818 B | 2,485,660 → 2,451,757 B | 4,534,012 → 4,518,002 B |
| Mixed history localhost | 3,949,648 → 3,897,461 B | 1,401,649 → 1,401,601 B | 2,547,999 → 2,495,860 B | 4,081,660 → 4,065,755 B |
| Mixed history 100 ms RTT | 3,940,229 → 3,888,042 B | 1,394,811 → 1,396,594 B | 2,545,418 → 2,491,448 B | 4,081,660 → 4,065,755 B |

Ordinary unused evaluated source falls 33,903–34,794 B (1.36–1.40%); mixed-history unused source falls 52,139–53,970 B (2.05–2.12%). Ordinary evaluated source falls 52,295 B. This closes about 3.6–3.7% of the approximately 950 KB ordinary unused-source goal, leaving approximately 916 KB. It does not represent a 40% reduction or a 30% Chat-download reduction.

V8 coverage records source supplied to V8 and which instrumented ranges executed. It does not measure total downloaded bytes, total compiled bytes, or useful work. Its evaluated-source denominator must not be subtracted from the HTTP denominator. HTTP Resource Timing includes completed preload downloads even when their module never evaluates. Fetch timing can change which optional resources finish within a capture. A zero-hit function or initializer does not establish that a security check or every catalog key can be removed. Module and exclusive-function rankings below overlap and must not be added.

## Corrected ordinary timing

The production file-reader worker graph was rebuilt canonically before this cohort. There are 20 counterbalanced base/control/head triplets per profile: 120 observations, with control using the identical base UI. Fresh source/output, dependency, Chromium, and full UI seals were checked before and after. All 120 summary hashes match the aggregate receipts; no observations were removed. Statistics use aggregate medians and nearest-rank p95; the raw aggregate also retains per-pair deltas and ranges. A/A is reported separately and is not subtracted.

The shared host was loaded: localhost 1-minute load medians were 23.86/23.62/23.90 for base/control/head (full range 15.67–29.68). Local A/A route/transcript median drift exceeded 5%, so that cell cannot establish a latency gain or a simple wall-time pass. Its script/task CPU is effectively flat, and its long-task variation is also present in A/A. At 100 ms RTT the ordinary readiness metrics stay within band. Together these support no attributable ordinary-readiness regression, not faster startup.

prs.title: improve: Doctor flags cron failure alerts that could not be delivered
prs.body:
Related: #186990

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Doctor gap behind #186990: when a scheduled automation fails and its failure alert cannot be delivered (for example on a gateway with no messaging channel configured), the delivery failure was recorded only in the job's state fields, and `openclaw doctor` never surfaced it.

## User Impact

User impact: operators running `openclaw doctor` now see which automations have an undeliverable failure alert, the recorded reason (such as "Channel is required (no configured channels detected)"), and what to do next: configure a messaging channel for the Gateway or set an explicit delivery target on the job. No behavior changes outside Doctor output, and the check is read-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor already reports chronic failures, auto-disabled jobs, and in-flight markers, but it did not read the settled alert-delivery result. This adds a finding next to those, driven by `lastFailureNotificationDeliveryStatus` and `lastFailureNotificationDeliveryError`.

Scope follows the agreement in the issue thread:
- Only `not-delivered` warns. `delivered`, `not-requested`, `unknown`, and absent fields stay silent, so an unsettled delivery is never reported as a failure.
- The recorded reason is sanitized before display (control characters stripped, whitespace collapsed, capped at 200 characters).
- Repair-brief wording and deduplication of repair requests are deliberately untouched. Current source already has a repair-per-streak marker and an owner-directed fallback, and the reporter is running the bounded repro to settle those separately. This PR uses `Related:` rather than `Closes` for that reason.

<details>
<summary>Implementation notes</summary>

- Detection lives in `inspectCronJobHealth` and runs for enabled and disabled jobs, so it is placed before the early `continue` that only the auto-disabled path needs.
- Tests are in a new `index.failure-alert.test.ts` because `index.test.ts` is already at the repo's file-length cap.
- `docs/cli/doctor/checks.md` lists the new check beside the other cron reports.

</details>

## Evidence

- New tests (3 passed) cover: a channel-less failed alert produces the warning with job name, recorded reason, and fix hint; a delivered alert produces no warning; `not-requested`, `unknown`, and missing fields produce no warning. These match the verification criteria the maintainer set on the issue.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passes.
- Existing `index.test.ts`: 27 of 28 pass, and the one failure (`reports a moved partition, refuses --yes guessing...`) also fails on unmodified `upstream/main` on Windows. The message embeds the store path JSON-escaped, so the raw-path match fails. It is unrelated to this change.
- Docs file passes `oxfmt --check`.
- On my Windows machine the local pre-commit hook cannot launch `pnpm` (`spawn pnpm ENOENT`), so I ran the docs checks manually and relied on CI for the rest.

prs.title: improve: clarify prompt delivery and request intent
prs.body:
Related: #188740

## What Problem This Solves

Clarifies advisory prompt wording that can refuse a separately configured integration, turn a requested plan into implementation, treat compatibility wording as ACP execution intent, count retries as recurring work, or delegate despite excessive handoff overhead.

## User Impact

Follows the requested operation and delivery target more precisely while preserving identity, credential, enforced approval, tool-policy, sandbox, channel-isolation, and ACP boundaries. No runtime enforcement, configuration, or credential behavior changes.

## Scope and Review Follow-up

- Distinguish managed channel transport from separately configured services such as email; native-tool equivalence includes operation, destination, sender identity, attachments, and delivery semantics.
- Deliver the requested planning/audit/review/report artifact without unrequested implementation; change/build requests continue beyond a plan.
- Preserve stronger prefer-mode delegation for responsiveness, with small/tightly coupled work and excessive handoff cost as bounded exceptions. Preserve explicit user/model choices.
- Distinguish explicit ACP execution intent from compatibility/artifact-target wording.
- Exclude retries, corrections, and failed/incomplete follow-ups from recurring-job promotion.
- Treat explicit current-turn authorization as confirmation only within its bounded target/content/scope; runtime policy, enforced approvals, and missing safety decisions still govern.

Rebased on `71ab715e24240d9ae8e31efeed76f376f891fc6d`; candidate `41bc8f2a3d87fbd2b2b69091d6173d27f7133825`. Resolved snapshot conflicts by regeneration. Fixed attributable formatting and line-budget growth; removed a redundant negative assertion and unnecessary line allocation. The source diff retains prefer-mode responsiveness rather than flattening it into general delegation guidance.

## Evidence

Verification on exact candidate `41bc8f2a3d87fbd2b2b69091d6173d27f7133825`:

- Five affected test files: **108/108 passed** (43 unit-fast + 65 agents-core), pinned Vitest 5.0.5 and repository-selected configs.

- Max-lines, test-lines, and line-cap ratchets against the stated base: pass; no baseline weakening or new allocation.
- All six generated prompt snapshots: current.
- Clean isolated worktree; no installed OpenClaw/Gateway changes.

These are text-contract/unit and generated-prompt checks, **not real-model behavior proof**. Before/after shipped-agent scenario evidence requested by review remains outstanding; no full build or broad test-suite result is claimed. Prior setup failures were resolved with an isolated frozen-lockfile root-only dependency install; lifecycle scripts were disabled and shared dependencies were not modified. Remote source CI and the repository `openclaw/ci-gate` passed for this exact head ([CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41160400891)). ## What Problem This Solves

Each live Logs poll traverses the retained window separately for filtering and key indexing, allocating temporary tuples and row/index objects even when all filters are disabled.

## User Impact

Logs polling performs less preparation work. No visible behavior change is intended; the retained buffer remains capped at 2,000 lines, and filters, export order, row keys, and scroll following keep their existing contracts. No latency improvement is claimed.

## Why This Change Was Made

One existing view derivation now builds a fresh ordered row array and key-to-index map in one pass, with the default-filter decision made once per batch. This removes the separate mapped index without adding state or caching. Measured-window keys still resolve against the same current snapshot, including index zero; the virtualizer and post-commit scroll compensation are unchanged.

## Evidence

The exact mounted production Logs route/sidebar census driver and one identical Babel instrumenter ran on base `f5381735e51d366879d398db3c622fefa6e4a18a` and the candidate. I/O is an in-process Gateway fixture and layout is synthetic jsdom geometry. The workload seeds 2,000 rows, then follows 100 batches of 20 lines, plus scrolled-up, text/level-filtered, follow-off, status/presence/sidebar and empty-poll controls.

| Count over 100 following batches | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Retained source row visits | 400,000 | 200,000 |
| Default-path predicate calls | 200,000 | 0 |
| Temporary index tuple arrays | 200,000 | 0 |
| Temporary row/index value objects | 200,000 | 0 |
| Key-index entries written | 200,000 | 200,000 |
| New-line parses | 2,000 | 2,000 |
| Mounted row constructions | 1,597 | 1,597 |
| Virtual key calls | 603,040 | 603,040 |
| Logs scrollHeight reads | 970 | 970 |
| Logs DOM added / removed nodes | 13,943 / 13,948 | 13,943 / 13,948 |
| logs.tail RPCs | 100 | 100 |

Every preserved per-action parse/format, row/list/key, geometry, DOM and RPC count matches; visible rows, retained DOM identity, cursors and scroll offsets match for all controls. Active-search predicates and normalization bytes remain unchanged. Allocations above are observed source literal executions, not a VM allocation profile. The benefit is modest for a bounded window polled every two seconds.

- Regression is red on base (64 level reads instead of six) and green on the candidate; it also checks index zero and independently expected export order.
- Logs view/page/data: 28 tests pass across three files (3.19 s Vitest wall time). Formatting, diff checks and test-line ratchet pass; no test-line allocation is required.
- Production: +5 net lines; tests: +33. pr-simplify completed. Independent Codex autoreview (P0–P3, local candidate against `f5381735`) completed scoped-clean with no findings.
- Full lint is unavailable with the copied dependency set: `eslint-plugin-solid` is missing. Its first wrapper attempt entered package-artifact preparation and hit the 3 GB cap; the preparation-skipping scoped attempt exposed the missing plugin. No broad build proof is claimed.
- UI typecheck reports the same five core/dependency errors byte-for-byte on base and candidate (fs-safe exports and string/number mismatches); no changed-file diagnostic. These remain unresolved.
- Exact-head CI closes the local lint/typecheck and Logs browser gaps: all UI unit shards, lint, production/test UI types, performance budgets and ratchets pass. Logs autofollow (Chromium), scroll (Chromium/WebKit), layout, and real-Gateway lifecycle pass. Separate WebKit overlay unit steps were skipped as planned. No local native-layout or latency proof is claimed.

Exact-head CI: [CI run 41156864789](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41156864789), attempt 1, for `0c600789ee2341aabb56385070fbfa2b050c850d`, remains **failed**: 63 terminal jobs, 32 successful, 27 skipped, three direct E2E failures and the aggregate gate. The `ci:full` label was applied while draft before marking ready.

The scoped parent ruling authorizes the documented native pre-existing-failure exception for these unrelated failures. Each failing test, fixture and production owner is byte-identical between CI base `18516599b1d417fee621b2fd2ceda21107bc038a` and tested merge `c25252a02d7e42552d8def4e01241e33178f463c`; only the two Logs files differ, and these scenarios do not mount Logs.

- [Chat snapshot, shard 1/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41156864789/job/124405812914): the mismatch case times out waiting for the visible native pane session key after URL canonicalization. Its precise cause remains unresolved; no proven-flake or matching-main-signature claim is made.
- [Plugin Settings keyboard, shard 6/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41156864789/job/124405812926): the inherited lazy-search regression from #188884 makes Escape read an older committed query while the native input contains text. The owning regression is green before #188884, red on main, and green with the native-input fix already in #188922.

- [Aggregate gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41156864789/job/124407962303) names only `checks-ui-e2e` as failed; all other selected families pass.

Security Review [41156865018](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41156865018) and security-fast pass on this head. CI remains failed. Security, required reviews, and live writer authority remain unwaived; native admission independently verifies them.

prs.title: fix(auth): CLI clients refuse to start after a macOS reboot renumbers the state volume
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw node run` and other CLI clients stop with "Client credential migration is incomplete or stale; run openclaw doctor --fix" after a macOS reboot, even though the shared state database did not change.

## User Impact

User impact: clients keep working after a reboot that renumbers the data volume. A node under a service manager no longer crash-loops until someone runs `openclaw doctor --fix` by hand (we observed one restarted about 32,500 times over four days). A shared database that was really replaced (new inode or new path) is still refused, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The local client credential receipt binds itself to the shared `state/openclaw.sqlite` with `{path, dev, ino}`, and readiness refused any mismatch, including `st_dev`. On macOS APFS, `st_dev` is assigned at mount time and can change across reboots. Some Linux mounts do the same. In the observed case the device number changed while the database kept the same path and inode, and every client start failed closed.

Path plus inode is the stable part of that identity. It is what detects a replaced database (restore, rename-over, new file). This change compares only path and inode, and treats a changed `dev` as the same file:

- **Canonical receipts:** writable admission rewrites the recorded `dev`, so the receipt heals itself. Read-only admission accepts the file and writes nothing.
- **Independent native receipts:** their `source.identity` embeds `<dev>:<ino>`, so only the inode is compared. Before this change, a writable admission after a renumbering also wiped the local derived rows and rebuilt them from the native source, which dropped tokens refreshed since the copy. Now an unchanged source keeps its rows, and only the receipt's identity and binding are refreshed.
- **Migration paths** that compare the same binding (fresh bootstrap, recovery, independent→canonical cutover) use the same comparison. Recovery still rewrites the receipt when only `dev` changed, so `doctor --fix` records the current device.

The restore and rewrite flows in `client-credential-restore.ts` still compare their captured identities exactly. They run inside one Doctor operation and are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Why not a stronger identity signal, and what about the macOS app?</summary>

A generation stored inside the database would also survive a reboot. But canonical readiness deliberately does not open the shared database. A realpath'd path plus inode already distinguishes the replacement cases this guard exists for. What remains is a different filesystem, mounted at the same path, holding a file with the same inode. A whole-volume clone or restore is the realistic version of that, and it carries `client/credentials.sqlite` along with the shared database, so the pair stays consistent.

The macOS app's native check (`ClientCredentialReceipt.swift` `assertReady`) still compares the full binding. After this change, any CLI client admission on the profile refreshes the receipt, and that also clears the app's check. Relaxing the Swift comparison can follow separately.
</details>

## Evidence

The new tests fail on `origin/main` and pass with the fix. The inode-change guard tests pass on both.

- `client-credential-store.test.ts`: a receipt with a shifted `dev` and the same path and inode is admitted. Writable admission rewrites `dev`; read-only leaves the receipt untouched. A shifted inode still throws the `doctor --fix` error in both modes and leaves the receipt untouched.
- `client-credential-native-bootstrap.test.ts`: an independent receipt with a renumbered device keeps the locally refreshed token in both modes. Writable admission refreshes `source.identity` and `sharedFile`.
- `client-credential-bootstrap.test.ts`: rebinding the same anchor file after a `dev` change succeeds, records the current `dev`, and keeps local identities and tokens.
- `startup-client-credentials.test.ts` (the startup path `node run` uses): after a `dev` change, preparation finishes without entering Doctor maintenance, and credentials stay readable. Existing recovery tests that used a `dev` shift to force recovery now shift the inode, which still requires recovery.

Commands run locally:

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/infra/client-credential-*.test.ts src/infra/state-migrations.device-*.test.ts src/commands/startup-client-credentials*.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:core`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <touched files>` and `node scripts/run-format.mts --check <touched files>`

Results: 17 test files passed, 2 skipped (PostgreSQL-only suites with no local server). Typecheck, lint, and format are clean. An independent local review of the branch reported no actionable findings.

prs.title: fix(update): scale the metadata inventory output cap with its path list
prs.body:
Fixes #188897

Note: #188907 was opened while this was in progress; at the time of writing it contains only a planned `it.todo`. This PR has the implementation, the failing-then-passing regression and a live A/B run.

## What Problem This Solves

The update capture measures every state database through `readUpdateStateDatabaseSizes()`. That function sends the path list to the `updateStateSizes` child process and reads back one JSON array. The child's stdout was capped at a fixed 1 MiB with `terminateOnOutputLimit`. Each result entry repeats its path, so the cap is reached after roughly 6,000 to 7,000 databases (fewer when paths are long). The child is then killed with `output-limit` and the capture is never sealed. The reporter has about 640,000 inventory paths and 4 of 4 retained captures `incomplete` ("no sealed manifest is available").

## User Impact

Long-lived installs with many agent databases get a sealed recovery set again, instead of an update that succeeds with no usable rollback capture.

## Why This Change Was Made

The child's output is derived from its input: one entry per existing path, holding that same path plus a decimal `sizeBytes`. So the stdout cap is now computed from the request: input JSON bytes, plus 64 bytes per path for the size field and punctuation, plus 1 MiB of slack. This keeps output bounded (a misbehaving child still hits `output-limit`) without making the bound a fixed count that scales the wrong way. The child script, the timeout budget and the progress channel (stderr) are unchanged.

Not addressed here: the reporter's very large inventories still pass every path through one child request and one parsed array. That works at the measured sizes, but chunking could be a follow-up if maintainers prefer it.

## Evidence

Production `readUpdateStateDatabaseSizes()` with the real `updateStateSizes` child process, on Windows 11 / Node 26.12.1.
- **Setup:** N distinct agent databases (`<state>/agents/agent-NNNNNN/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`) created on disk.
- **Variable:** same harness and files; only `src/infra/update-candidate-state.sizes.ts` differs between main 2908f7a and this branch.

![proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/188897/proof-188897.png)

| databases | input JSON | main 2908f7a | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3,000 | 282 KB | 3,000 entries (238 ms) | 3,000 entries (234 ms) |
| 6,000 | 564 KB | 6,000 entries (371 ms) | 6,000 entries (372 ms) |
| 12,000 | 1.13 MB | `output-limit`: "State schema inventory failed (output-limit): Worker output exceeded its capture limit" (1.2 s) | 12,000 entries (710 ms) |
| 40,000 | 3.76 MB | `output-limit` (2.6 s) | 40,000 entries (2.1 s) |

The regression is a new case in `src/infra/update-candidate-state.budget.test.ts`, "inventories more paths than a fixed 1 MiB result would hold". It inventories 12,000 paths through the real child.
- **On main:** it fails with the same `output-limit` the reporter saw.
- **With this change:** it passes.
- **Existing cases:** the output-limit case (child output capped at 1 byte through the runner) and the metadata-budget cases still pass.

Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/update-candidate-state.budget.test.ts -t "inventor"`.

Gates run locally: oxfmt, oxlint, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet`. Not run: a full `openclaw update` on a large real state directory. The proof calls the inventory step directly.

prs.title: fix: prevent agent database reopen loops during shutdown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway shutdown repeatedly reopening agent databases for optional session previews after clean close, keeping the process alive until the watchdog kills it.

Related: #188402, #188496, #188920.

## User Impact

Shutdown stops optional preview work when restart drain begins. Queued previews can be dropped and rebuilt by the next Gateway; already-admitted database work keeps its existing settlement and drain. Marker-first persistence, snapshot abort, retirement order, required joins, and watchdog budgets stay intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The projection backfill queue outlived the close boundary. On the base, `src/gateway/session-row-projection-backfill.ts:79` calls writable execution at `src/gateway/session-row-transcript-backfill.ts:69`; every queued row can acquire and release the database again.

The queue now consumes the existing process drain/cleanup signals, stops scheduling, and checks cancellation after its readiness waits. That same signal reaches writer admission and the existing worker execution authority callback. The existing database drain owns accepted work. No lifecycle plumbing, plugin fence, retry change, new deadline, config, schema, or dependency is added. All three previously capped files are unchanged.

## Evidence

The reported r250 stop on 2026-10-31 UTC finished its close steps around 00:12:09.6, then wrote 205 clean-close receipts between 00:12:13.096 and 00:13:29.846, roughly every 350–400 ms, until watchdog SIGKILL. The independent plugin shared-state refusals failed fast and were not the process-retention cause.

The existing isolated held-finalizer scenario naturally reproduces queued projection work, without seeding a fake queue. Reservation diagnostics identify `session.rowTranscript.backfill`: first clean-close at 02:06:13.957Z, successful backfills at 02:06:14.395Z and .456Z, and another clean-close at .508Z. This proves the caller mechanism; it does not claim to reproduce all 205 production cycles.

- Pinned base `a825acc286e01fab2722471336f1a9523b12e28f`: the retained reopen assertion in `restart markers survive graceful shutdown (suspend/reopen and blocked store: false)` was red under Node 26.12.1 and pinned Bun 1.4.4 (`expected true to be false` for post-clean-close backfill).
- Narrowed build: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/prepare-vitest-runtime.mjs --with-ai-package` passed, including the CLI bootstrap import guard (3m25.8s).
- Backfill owner tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-row-projection.backfill.test.ts src/gateway/session-row-transcript-backfill.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passed 33 tests in two shards (92.94s including compilation; test files 36.75s and 23.65s).
- Core and root-E2E typechecks, targeted production/process-test lint, four-file format check, all nine baseline ratchets, the line-cap ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Isolated local autoreview against the pinned base, complete four-file snapshot, P0–P2: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper requires an existing exact issue/PR and clean committed target; this pre-PR candidate used autoreview. The ready PR's automatic hosted review remains advisory.

Full process regression command (each run uses its own ignored FS module cache):

```sh
OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Both passed 2/2 tests, including existing restart, held-finalizer, queued-input, blocked-store and crash cases, with no backfill operation after first clean-close. Node: 84.229s test time, 116.55s wrapper; shutdowns 2.377s (suspend/reopen), 6.725s (SIGTERM), 1.510s (managed). Bun: 61.67s total file time; shutdowns 1.508s, 6.895s, 1.072s respectively. All three measured close modes exited 0 under each runtime. Exact-head CI run [41160058115](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41160058115) passed: 41 successful jobs, 27 skipped, no failures; all observed required `openclaw/ci-gate` entries are SUCCESS. The successful-job envelope was 542 seconds; aggregate successful-job time was 6369 seconds. The exact-head watcher reported GREEN, ignoring 81 superseded aliases behind GitHub’s stale rollup. No CI reruns or repair pushes were needed.


Whole change: four files, production net +25 LOC, test net -18 LOC, docs +5 LOC. The only new machinery is cancellation at the existing optional-work owner; the wider proposed shutdown plumbing was removed.

### Deferred follow-up

Plugin shared-state admission remains separate: the SDK resource host's `track`/`drainWork` (`src/plugins/legacy-sdk-resource-host.ts:59–61,129`) does not currently fence all cached/worker state paths, and `src/state/openclaw-state-worker-owner.ts:364` reports retirement refusal. The earlier process-test variant's late plugin lookup was accepted after close; its red test was `restart markers survive graceful shutdown (suspend/reopen and blocked store: false)`. That assertion and the shared-state patch are preserved locally, outside this PR.

Retry classification is also deferred: `src/infra/retry-policy.ts:16–33` treats `closed`/`unavailable` as transient, and Nostr's stop at `extensions/nostr/src/nostr-bus.ts:491` awaits the unconditional recovery loop at `nostr-cursor.ts:140–151`. Red tests were `keeps OpenClaw state database read admission is closed terminal despite a transient wrapper`, `keeps Shared-state worker is retiring while its actor is in use; close its leases first terminal despite a transient wrapper` (three attempts instead of one), `does not retry terminal outcome STATE_DATABASE_READ_ADMISSION_INVALIDATED`, and `retries safety writes unless admission is closed (true)` (incorrectly recovered after four writes). Their fixes and tests are preserved in `.local/v2-followup.patch` and are not included here.

prs.title: feat(memory): let workspaces exclude generated files from search
prs.body:
Related: #101422 Supersedes #177868 by @CheekyHobson: their reviewed head `a2008ab09`, ported onto current main with co-author credit on the commit, plus the proof ClawSweeper asked for. ## What Problem This Solves Generated dreaming reports under `memory/dreaming/` are indexed like curated notes and crowd them out of memory search, and there is no setting to exclude paths inside the default memory folders. ## User Impact User impact: operators can set `memory.search.excludePaths` (globally or per agent), for example `["memory/dreaming/**", "memory/.dreams/**"]`, to keep matching workspace files out of memory search and file watching. - Unset or empty changes nothing. The index scope hash is identical to the one 2026.10.9 writes, so this setting adds no rebuild on upgrade. - Setting or changing the list is a scope change, like changing `extraPaths`: `openclaw memory status` reports it, vector search pauses, and `openclaw memory index` rebuilds and drops the excluded rows. - Search only: excluded files are not deleted, `memory_get` can still read them, `memory forget` still scrubs them, and short-term recall/promotion eligibility is unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made One workspace-relative glob check, next to the existing `extraPaths` glob matcher in the memory host SDK, is applied where search scope is decided: file discovery (local and remote workspace providers), watcher eligibility, and the index scope hash. Shared watchers include the exclusions in their selection keys, so agents with different exclusions on one workspace rebaseline when one joins or leaves (the P2 ClawSweeper found on #177868). Changes compared with #177868 at `a2008ab09`: - Rebased onto main: the scope hash goes through the single `resolveConfiguredMemoryScopeHash()` owner, and the matcher is exported from `plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-engine-fs`, the subpath #181891 narrowed the file worker to, instead of `engine-storage`. Both are private local-only subpaths, so this adds no third-party SDK contract. - The matcher lives in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts` beside `matchesExtraMemoryPathEntry` instead of core `src/memory/root-memory-files.ts`. - Added the config field label, corrected the docs about the rebuild step, and linked the setting from the dreaming docs. - Tests: replaced the 13 s CLI e2e case with a manager test of about 4 s that mirrors two unforced `openclaw memory index` runs (the real CLI run is below). Dropped a test that indexed an excluded file through a private method, a `selectionKeys` shape test covered by the join/leave behavior test, a worker integration test that still passed with the P2 fix reverted, and (after ClawSweeper's review) a test that only checked the worker request shape. Size against main: production +67/-8 in 15 files; tests +148/-3; docs +15/-4; generated baselines +3/-3. (#177868 was +439/-18 in 33 files.) ### Maintainer decision needed #101422 asks for both search exclusion and recall/promotion eligibility control. This PR is the narrow first stage: search discovery, watching, and index scope only, with defaults and promotion safeguards unchanged. ClawSweeper's review of #177868 recommended approving that narrow search stage and leaving recall inclusion and diagnostics to follow-up work; the alternative is one combined search+recall include/exclude design. An operator on #101422 said the search-only step covers their need. Config surface: `pnpm config:docs:gen` raises the core count by 4 (2584 -> 2588 on main `dfc3ce8`) for `memory.search.excludePaths` and `agents.entries.*.memory.search.excludePaths`, each with its `.*` item path. That is the new setting itself. ## Evidence Real runs on head `8eb4b7b` (on main `f980e01`). Synthetic workspace: 3 curated files (`MEMORY.md`, `memory/backups.md`, `memory/garden.md`) and 7 generated reports (5 light, 2 REM, one REM report containing only "No strong patterns surfaced."). Isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` under `env -i`, Node 26.12.1, and a local OpenAI-compatible embeddings stub on 127.0.0.1 (deterministic vectors, no provider calls). **Upgrade and CLI:** 2026.10.9 from npm builds the index; this branch keeps its scope hash with no `excludePaths` (the re-chunk comes from main's #168867), then drops the 7 reports after `excludePaths` plus `memory index`; the curated note stays first and an edit refreshes it.

Done. # memory_search tool result (from the stub's log): path: memory/backups.md # indexed memory/ rows before edits: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # wrote memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-29.md and edited memory/backups.md (02:30 -> 04:45); no CLI calls from here # after the Gateway watcher sync (~1s), plus 5s more: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 04:45 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # dreaming rows: {"dreamingRows":0} ```

prs.title: fix(update): keep repair refusal reason in update history
prs.body:
Closes #182054

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update repair` records only the generic `repair-failed` reason when Doctor refuses to stop a Gateway ancestor process.

## User Impact

User impact: update history keeps the actionable refusal code (for example, `inside-gateway-process-tree`) while reports still identify the failed operation as a repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor now carries the managed-service failure facts it already receives into the maintenance refusal. The report renderer derives repair operation identity from the existing retained `repairing` phase, keeping operation identity separate from the specific failure reason. Generic repair failures remain compatible, and ordinary update failures still render as update failures.

## Evidence

- Dependency-free source-path oracle reproduced the base failure: the producer and finalizer carried failure facts, but Doctor did not forward them.
- The same oracle passes at `a3a842fb584c112f0743d6735059724ded01887e`: Doctor forwards the facts, the retained `repairing` phase identifies a repair, and generic `repair-failed` compatibility remains.
- `git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check` passed.
- Exact-head autoreview completed with no findings (`patch_correctness_confidence: 0.99`), and an independent verifier reported CLEAN through P2 / best-fix.

## Summary

- preserve `blockFailureFacts` through the Doctor refusal boundary
- keep repair/update operation identity separate from the specific refusal code
- cover standalone repair history, ordinary Doctor callers, and renderer controls

## Issue

Closes #182054

## Root cause

`PreManagedServiceStop` recorded the authoritative failure facts and update finalization already collected them, but `assertDoctorMaintenanceInspection` rebuilt `DoctorMaintenanceRefusalError` without forwarding those facts. Once the specific reason was preserved, the report renderer also exposed a coupled assumption: it inferred repair identity only from `reason === "repair-failed"` instead of the retained repair phase.

## Verification

- Before-fix oracle: `doctorForwardsInspectionFacts=false`, exit 1.
- After-fix oracle: `doctorForwardsInspectionFacts=true`, `rendererUsesRepairIdentity=true`, `rendererUsesReasonOnly=false`, `genericRepairCompatibility=true`, exit 0.
- `git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check`: passed.
- Focused Vitest and changed checks were attempted but did not collect because dependencies were unavailable; details are in **Not tested**.

## Before / after

Before: the refusal was saved as `repair-failed`, losing the actionable `inside-gateway-process-tree` fact. A report could only identify repair from that generic reason.

After: the refusal's specific fact is saved, and the existing failed `repairing` phase independently preserves the operation identity. Generic repair failures continue to render as repair failures.

## Risk and scope

Low and bounded to update maintenance refusal propagation/reporting. This uses existing ledger fields and lifecycle phases; it adds no schema, config, protocol, or migration. Production delta is +8/-2 lines; tests are +110/-0 lines.

## Not tested

- Focused Vitest did not collect: `node_modules` was absent, and `pnpm install` failed twice because `@pnpm/macos-arm64@12.15.0` was unavailable from both the configured mirror and the official npm registry.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs ...` likewise stopped before checks because dependencies were absent.
- Blacksmith Testbox did not start because the host had no `blacksmith` binary.
- No packaged or live Gateway run was performed.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**

Preserve the concrete managed-service refusal code through Doctor into update finalization, while continuing to report standalone repair runs as repairs.

**Real environment tested**

An isolated macOS source checkout at exact head `a3a842fb584c112f0743d6735059724ded01887e`, using dependency-free source-path assertions. This was not a live Gateway environment.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**

```bash
node -e 'const fs=require("fs"); const report=fs.readFileSync("src/infra/update-run-report.ts","utf8"); const checks={specificReasonPreserved:/failureFacts:\\s*inspection\\.blockFailureFacts/.test(fs.readFileSync("src/commands/doctor-maintenance-inspection.ts","utf8")),repairIdentityRecorded:/this\\.ownsRepairRun\\s*\\?\\s*"repairing"/.test(fs.readFileSync("src/cli/update-cli/update-finalization-lifecycle.ts","utf8")),rendererUsesRepairIdentity:/steps\\.some\\([\\s\\S]{0,160}step\\.step === "repairing"/.test(report),rendererUsesReasonOnly:/run\\.reason === "repair-failed" \\? "repair" : "update"/.test(report),genericRepairCompatibility:/run\\.reason === "repair-failed" \\|\\|/.test(report)}; checks.fixed=checks.specificReasonPreserved&&checks.repairIdentityRecorded&&checks.rendererUsesRepairIdentity&&!checks.rendererUsesReasonOnly&&checks.genericRepairCompatibility; console.log(JSON.stringify(checks,null,2)); process.exit(checks.fixed?0:1);'
git diff HEAD^ HEAD --check
```

**Evidence after fix**

The oracle printed all required booleans as `true` and `fixed=true`, then exited 0. The diff check produced no output and exited 0. Exact-head autoreview returned `findings: []`.

**Observed result after fix**

The specific refusal code crosses the Doctor owner boundary, and the report derives repair identity from the retained `repairing` phase. The existing generic `repair-failed` path remains supported.

**What was not tested**

No focused Vitest, changed-check lane, Testbox run, packaged CLI run, or live Gateway run completed; the precise environment blockers are listed above.

## What Problem This Solves

The V1 and V2 plugin Decision methods separately implement the same registry, lifecycle, cancellation, and completion coordination.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior, configuration, or supported SDK export changes. Part 05 of the maintainer-directed Decision refactor stack, based on [part 04](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188223).

## Why This Change Was Made

Use one scoped execution path for both versions while retaining their typed operations. Completion still runs only after the caller's late lifecycle and cancellation checks; the wrappers return the shared promise directly so accepted usage is not followed by an extra rejecting guard.

## Evidence

- Independent fresh source review and local committed-range ClawSweeper review completed with no unresolved actionable findings. Corrective changes were reviewed separately; mechanical restacks were checked with `git range-diff`.
- [Exact-head ordinary CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41037174133) passed at `6d09b8fb9eb4f4b6ccc28f3d64a43220e68d1945`, including the configured runtime, type, lint and guard lanes.

Shared SDK source-audit evidence, the advisory API-report timeout and broader manual-campaign limitations are recorded in [part01](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188216).

## Landing update

Current head: `0ec7a48a15975537e672b7f51d66b54742e5b645`; current-head CI has an attributed baseline-only failure; native landing will retain failed CI and verify the scoped exception. After part04 landed, the remaining stack was replayed onto its actual protected-main commit `63dbee6a514580948082dc20cb930c7e748c019e` to resolve the named CI/base-context gap in part05. All 20 commit ranges remain patch-identical by `git range-diff`; the allocation guard passes. Earlier CI/build evidence above remains historical. Each slice lands through the native main-targeted review, preparation, and merge workflow after its predecessor.

That run used the former stacked part04 source head as its merge baseline, which is not a protected-main ancestor after squash. ### Earlier required-gate interruption

[CI41071226056](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41071226056) has 40 successful jobs and no failed test/lint/type shard in the inspected 71-job snapshot. The remaining `checks-node-changed-boundary` job124116418301 and its check-run still report `queued`, no runner, no steps, no completion and no annotations. The failure classifier says the jobs have not all completed. This selected shard is unproven; the initiating platform condition is unresolved. No CI rerun, inherited-failure exception or merge has been submitted for this head.

### Current baseline attribution

[CI41159448416](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41159448416) completed with two Workboard terminal-hook test failures (`agent_end` and `subagent_ended`), plus the downstream aggregate. Main [4811c39057d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4811c39057dd0ac994464db37b1fa7adc0f280b6) added `workboard.cards.list` diagnostics that call `log.isEnabled`; the existing context fixture supplies only `error` and `warn`. Classification is unknown because no matching job exists in the compared main run. prs.title: fix #188935: throw the typed schema-admission error at handle adoption
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: When an agent-database open loses the schema-admission race at handle adoption, the site throws an untyped `Error` ("Agent schema admission changed before handle adoption; retry the operation") instead of `AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError`, so no retry/replay path classifies it and a completed long turn ends with only "OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply" (#188935).
- Solution: Throw the existing typed `AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError` at the adoption site (keeping its exact message), so the transcript-commit replay classifier already in the tree treats the race as retryable.
- What changed: `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-schema.ts` (typed throw), `src/state/agent-database-admission-error.ts` (optional custom message, default unchanged), strengthened race assertions in `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-cache.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: The typed error's identity, default message, and all publication-path behavior; the admission/adoption verdicts themselves; no retry logic was added — the fix only connects the existing throw to the existing classifier.

Fixes #188935

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A session-turn Worker's agent-database open lost the publication race at handle adoption and threw an untyped `Error`, which `isReplayableWorkerTranscriptCommitError` could not classify, so the turn was terminated terminally instead of being retried.
- **Real environment tested:** This branch's worktree on Linux x64, Node v24.20.0, pnpm 12.15.0, driving the real `adoptOpenClawAgentDatabaseSchema` through the repo's concurrent-publication race fixture with a real SQLite agent database and the real replay classifier `isReplayableWorkerTranscriptCommitError`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  pnpm install
  OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-cache.test.ts
  ```
  (`OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1` keeps test file logs under the repo on this host; see "What was not tested".)
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  before (production files restored to unmodified main, same assertions):
    × schema: expected Error: Agent schema admission changed bef… to be an instance of SchemaAdmissionChangedError
    (the adoption race surfaced as a bare Error; the replay classifier did not own it)
  after (this patch):
    ✓ same race now throws AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError with the unchanged message
    ✓ isReplayableWorkerTranscriptCommitError(error) === true
    ✓ openclaw-agent-db-validation-cache.test.ts: 51 passed (51)
  worker transport replay (real session Worker, src/worker/worker.transcript-failure.test.ts):
    ✓ replays transient transcript failures and completes the run without duplicate messages
      — drives an actual AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError through the real worker
      transcript-commit transport: replayed requests equal the original, the run completes,
      and no duplicate messages are persisted (3 passed, exit 0)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** The adoption-race failure is now an instance of the typed error the transcript-commit replay path already classifies as retryable, so a raced open can be retried instead of discarding the turn; the same typed error is shown replaying through the real worker transcript transport to a clean completion without duplicate persisted messages (the pre-existing worker replay suite, re-run green on this head).
- **What was not tested:** The original 54-minute Feishu turn was not replayed (the race window requires a live long-running turn plus a concurrent memory-index publication; the repo's race fixture exercises the exact adoption path deterministically). The `core-runtime-infra-state` CI-like shard was attempted but this host's dist-fence guard refuses to run it (it cannot verify separation from managed Gateway artifacts; this is an environment restriction, not a test failure) — the affected validation-cache suite runs green standalone and CI lanes remain the shard guardrail. This host's `/` is world-writable without the sticky bit, so tests resolving the default rolling log path use the repo-supported `OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1` route, which CI does not need. tsgo could not run locally (GLIBC too old for the native binary); CI type lanes remain the guardrail.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: `src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-cache.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: the "schema" race in `distinguishes raced publication from malformed receipts even after revocation` now asserts the adoption failure is an `AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError` with the exact message and is classified replayable by the transcript-commit path.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: it fails on unpatched main with the precise defect from the issue (bare Error, unclassifiable) and pins both the type contract and the replay classification without touching unrelated races.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: the handle-adoption race site threw a bare `Error`, while the sibling publication-race site threw the typed `AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError`; the replay classifier keys on the type, so the adoption race fell through every retry path despite its message saying "retry the operation".
- Missing detection / guardrail: the race fixture asserted only the message text, never the error type or its replay classification, so the untyped throw compiled and passed review.

prs.title: fix(cli): preserve final replies after earlier message sends
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing final answers when a CLI-backed agent sends an earlier message, continues working, and then returns a different final answer.

## User Impact

Users receive the later result without asking again. Exact repeated answers, including short replies such as `Done` or a single emoji, are not sent twice to the same conversation. A terminal answer that confirms an earlier progress message completes normally instead of producing a false missing-reply notice.

Message-tool-only delivery, explicit delivery custody, other destinations, and internal source mirrors retain their existing behavior.

prs.title: fix(config): disabled mixed-case plugins are re-enabled by auto-enable and doctor --fix
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/188845

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a plugin whose manifest id has uppercase letters (for example `MyProv`) is enabled again by plugin auto-enable, and persisted by `openclaw doctor --fix`, after the user ran `openclaw plugins disable MyProv`.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw plugins disable`, `openclaw plugins enable` and `plugins.deny` hold for plugins with mixed-case manifest ids; auto-enable and `doctor --fix` no longer undo a disable, add a second raw-case entry, or report an auto-enable that did not happen. Lowercase ids behave as before.

A config this bug already rewrote keeps its extra `MyProv` entry; running `openclaw plugins disable MyProv` (or `enable`) once more collapses both spellings onto the canonical key. This PR adds no Doctor repair: the mixed-case key is a valid shape, and Doctor cannot tell a `true` the user wrote from one this bug wrote. On the latest stable (2026.10.9) the same steps make `doctor --fix` drop the `myprov` entry altogether; this change cannot restore a disable that was already lost there, so affected users disable the plugin again once.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180789 moved install persistence onto the canonical plugin id, the lowercase id that `plugins enable`/`disable`, config validation and the loader use (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/180071). Plugin auto-enable still read and wrote policy under the raw manifest spelling: it missed `plugins.entries.myprov.enabled: false`, appended `plugins.entries.MyProv.enabled: true`, and that later key won when the entries folded onto `myprov`.

All policy reads and writes in `src/config/plugin-auto-enable.materialize.ts` now go through `normalizePluginId` and the normalized plugin config, the same owners the loader uses: the explicit-disable, deny, allowlist and already-enabled checks, the explicit-selection check that guards the preferred-over path, and the entry and allowlist writes. Raw entries are still read where the normalized view drops fields (`apiKey`, `env`).

Size: production +28/-18 lines in one file; one 21-line regression test; one test-line allocation record. No config, state or SDK surface changes.

Follow-ups, not in this PR: candidate detection in `src/config/plugin-auto-enable.shared.ts` and `src/plugin-sdk/provider-enable-config.ts` still compare raw plugin ids.

## Evidence

Tested at `543dd536de5` (base `upstream/main` `24e37a12ddc`).

The built CLI (`pnpm openclaw`) on Ubuntu 22.04 with Node 24.22.1, with fresh isolated state, config and home directories for every run. The plugin is a synthetic local provider plugin with manifest id `MyProv`, provider `myprov` and `autoEnableWhenConfiguredProviders: ["myprov"]`; it is never called, and no network or credentials are involved. Same steps on both sides, with one policy step each:

```text
openclaw plugins install --force --accept-capabilities ./myprov
openclaw config set models.providers.myprov '{"baseUrl":"http://127.0.0.1:9/v1","api":"openai-completions","models":[{"id":"m1","name":"m1"}]}' --strict-json
<policy step: plugins disable MyProv | config set plugins.deny '["myprov"]' --strict-json | plugins enable MyProv>
openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive
openclaw plugins list --json
```

Before (base `24e37a12ddc`), `plugins.entries` without the two unrelated bundled entries:

```text
== plugins disable MyProv
before doctor: {"myprov":{"enabled":false}}
doctor:        myprov auth configured, enabled automatically.
after doctor:  {"myprov":{"enabled":false},"MyProv":{"enabled":true}}
plugins list:  MyProv: loaded

== config set plugins.deny ["myprov"]
before doctor: {"myprov":{"enabled":true}}
doctor:        myprov auth configured, enabled automatically.
after doctor:  {"myprov":{"enabled":true},"MyProv":{"enabled":true}}
plugins list:  MyProv: disabled

== plugins enable MyProv
before doctor: {"myprov":{"enabled":true}}
doctor:        myprov auth configured, enabled automatically.
after doctor:  {"myprov":{"enabled":true},"MyProv":{"enabled":true}}
plugins list:  MyProv: loaded
```

After (this PR):

```text
== plugins disable MyProv
before doctor: {"myprov":{"enabled":false}}
doctor:        (no auto-enable line)
after doctor:  {"myprov":{"enabled":false}}
plugins list:  MyProv: disabled

== config set plugins.deny ["myprov"]
before doctor: {"myprov":{"enabled":true}}
doctor:        (no auto-enable line)
after doctor:  {"myprov":{"enabled":true}}
plugins list:  MyProv: disabled

== plugins enable MyProv
before doctor: {"myprov":{"enabled":true}}
doctor:        (no auto-enable line)
after doctor:  {"myprov":{"enabled":true}}
plugins list:  MyProv: loaded
```

Observed result: before, `doctor --fix` re-enabled the disabled plugin (`plugins list` shows it loaded) and, in all three cases, saved a second `MyProv` entry and reported an auto-enable; after, `plugins.entries` is unchanged and nothing is reported.

### Upgrade from the latest stable

Settings written by the latest stable, then carried to this branch in the same state directory. Fresh isolated home, `env -i`, `unshare -rn` (no network), three synthetic provider plugins with mixed-case manifest ids `MyProv`, `OtherProv` and `OnProv`, no credentials.

On `openclaw@2026.10.9` from npm:

```text
openclaw plugins install --force --accept-capabilities ./myprov        # and ./otherprov, ./onprov
openclaw config set models.providers.<id> '{"baseUrl":"http://127.0.0.1:9/v1",...}' --strict-json   # each of the three
openclaw config set gateway.port 18999 --strict-json
openclaw config set agents.defaults.workspace <home>/workspace
openclaw plugins disable MyProv
openclaw config set plugins.deny '["otherprov"]' --strict-json
openclaw plugins enable OnProv
openclaw plugins list --json
```

Then, in the same home, this branch's CLI ran `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` and `openclaw plugins list --json`. For comparison, this branch rebuilt with the base `plugin-auto-enable.materialize.ts` (the PR's only production file) ran the same two commands in a second home set up the same way. `entries` below are shown without the two unrelated bundled entries:

```text
stable wrote:        entries {"otherprov":{"enabled":true},"myprov":{"enabled":false},"onprov":{"enabled":true}}, deny ["otherprov"]
stable plugins list: MyProv disabled, OtherProv disabled, OnProv loaded

base materializer (24e37a12ddc), after doctor --fix
  doctor:            myprov, onprov and otherprov "auth configured, enabled automatically."
  entries:           the three above plus "MyProv":{"enabled":true}, "OnProv":{"enabled":true}, "OtherProv":{"enabled":true}
  plugins list:      MyProv loaded, OtherProv disabled, OnProv loaded

this PR, after doctor --fix
  doctor:            (no auto-enable line)
  plugins section:   identical to what stable wrote (entries and deny)
  plugins list:      MyProv disabled, OtherProv disabled, OnProv loaded
```

Everything else Doctor changed is the same on the base and on this PR, so none of it comes from this change: the state database migrations (schema 20 to 36, with a pre-migration backup), the `meta.migrations.webhookListeners` marker, the `agents.entries.main` roster entry, the `wizard` run record, and the `skills.entries` Doctor disabled. `models` and `gateway` are unchanged on both sides. The three plugins installed by the stable release are still discovered from their stable install records, and their extension files are unchanged. Existing data needs no migration: this change adds no config, state or schema shape, and it reads `plugins.entries` and `plugins.deny` through the same id normalization the loader and config validation use, so any key stable accepted is read the same way.

Regression test, failing on the base and passing with the fix: "reads mixed-case plugin policy under the canonical lowercase key" in `plugin-auto-enable.materialize.test.ts` feeds `MyProv`, `OtherProv` and `OnProv` candidates against lowercase `entries.myprov.enabled: false`, `deny: ["otherprov"]` and `entries.onprov.enabled: true`, and expects no config change and no reported change.

Checks: the touched test (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, wall time below); the auto-enable suites `plugin-auto-enable.core.test.ts`, `plugin-auto-enable.channels.test.ts`, `plugin-auto-enable.providers.test.ts` and `plugin-auto-enable.materialize.test.ts` (66 tests); seven consumer suites of auto-enable (79 tests): `src/commands/doctor-legacy-config.migrations.test.ts`, `src/commands/doctor/shared/release-configured-plugin-installs.test.ts`, `src/commands/channel-setup/plugin-install.test.ts`, `src/commands/channels.list.inventory.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-startup-config.recovery.test.ts`, `src/gateway/plugin-activation-runtime-config.test.ts` and `src/config/official-external-channel-secret-schema.test.ts`; `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.config-cli.json`; oxlint and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files; the broad suites run in this PR's CI.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/config/plugin-auto-enable.materialize.test.ts` | 35.1 s (4 tests; the new test runs in under 1 ms, the rest is module transform on a cold cache) | 3.69 s (`checks-node-changed-1`; 5.71 s for its shard) |

Test lines: the allocation in `config/test-lines-allocations/auto-enable-mixed-case-disable.txt` is 22, exactly the regression test's 21 lines plus its separating blank line, the PR's whole net test-line delta. The test-line ratchet passes in this PR's CI (`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`: 6,315,943 lines, ceiling 6,347,938).

Not covered: the proof uses a provider-triggered auto-enable; channel, tool and model-reference candidates go through the same checks and writes. The preferred-over path was checked by direct calls in review, with no committed test. A hand-written mixed-case entry with config (`plugins.entries.MyProv: {config: …}`) that auto-enable enables gets the canonical `myprov: {enabled: true}` beside it instead of being folded in, as the base did; the merged result is correct, and `plugins enable` or `disable` folds it. Folding it here through the enable helper would also rewrite `plugins.allow` and `deny` aliases on every `doctor --fix`, so it was left out.

prs.title: fix(workers): reject new turns on unusable provider leases
prs.body:
Related: #188796

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a fresh worker or remote-exec turn can claim input using a still-attached local record after its provider lease has become unusable, before background reconciliation observes the loss.

## User Impact

New turns qualify the exact attached lease before taking a claim. Unavailable provider observations leave ownership intact and reject admission for retry; dormant paired devices retain their existing reconnect behavior. Confirmed loss uses existing cleanup and never starts the new input. This adds a bounded provider observation to fresh lease-backed admission; it adds no configuration, schema, or public provider API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider lifecycle shares one loss-settlement implementation between maintenance and turn admission. The service serializes inspection with the environment owner and retains accepted cleanup after caller cancellation. Admission rechecks the same lease at claim commit and after waiting for an earlier claim. Existing recorded-loss and runtime-refresh recovery remain with their current owners. This inspection does not allocate a replacement or replay input.

## Evidence

- Baseline `4a393be419f30ecfd65972fe3ea1416c6f707316`: the production preclaim function admitted synthetic fresh input with **1 claim / 0 provider inspections**. The same focused reproduction on the fix rejects it with **0 claims / 1 exact-lease inspection**.
- **CI repair:** [run 41154754160](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41154754160) and the [hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188914#issuecomment-6537279352) exposed an omitted Goal fixture method and read-order-dependent launcher fixtures. The repair supplies required inspection, moves proxy assertions to workspace preparation, checks admission/I/O outcomes instead of environment-read counts, and introduces simulated provider loss only after the stale-build rejection. Production inspection remains required and unchanged.
- **Fresh post-repair tests: 141 passed across eight complete files.** `pnpm test:ci-failed https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41154754160 --run` passed all six selected files: **119 tests**, three Vitest shards, 543.48 s. A separate full lease-admission and claim-admission run passed **22 tests**, 161.49 s including its wrapper. Both used the pinned Bun runtime. These replace the earlier partial repair receipts as current evidence.
- Coverage includes Gateway Goal promotion/continuation and claim revocation, independent worker-proxy scope, initial setup, retired lifecycle, stale-build/shared-node cleanup, active/dormant/unavailable/unknown/destroyed lease dispositions, and cancellation after accepted cleanup. SQLite and admission owners are real; provider, node and model I/O are fixture-backed. No live provider/model-driven proof is claimed.
- The missing Goal method was reproduced with the full production typecheck before repair. After repair, **full `tsconfig.core.json` and all 29 canonical changed-caller test type graphs passed**. Scoped type-aware lint, formatting, normal pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed. The unchanged documentation audit checked 16,190 internal links with zero broken.
- Fresh **autoreview / Codex GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P3** reviewed the complete candidate against the pinned base with complete ownership and affected fixture sources. It reported three **INDEX-only** omissions from the previously published snapshot, judged the working-tree repairs correct, and found no additional production defect. Those findings were resolved by staging the exact reviewed repairs; no source edit followed the review. This run was not labeled `scoped-clean`, and the reviewer did not execute tests. No extra hosted review was requested.
- Published repair head: `da87c635972f1cf8aada5fdd4410defc0012388d`. Its tree **`0b11684359e82523b6d856bed868548311371ba9`** is identical to reviewed local repair commit `83be13de1381d137144855fc1f95710c85cdeb4a`; normal hooks and managed attribution preserved it. Fresh exact-head hosted CI is running, not yet claimed green.

Staged ratchet: 6,316,185 / 6,348,174. No second lifecycle manager, persistence, resume API, retained-disk behavior, merge or deployment was added.

prs.title: fix(diagnostics): identify stalls during native child launches
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Slow native child launches can leave Gateway stall warnings unattributed when the CPU profiler has no samples for the blocked interval.

## User Impact

The process runner, direct command runner, and PTY helper now identify synchronous launch stalls using fixed task labels. This improves diagnosis; it does not claim to eliminate the underlying pause. No configuration or process-routing change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Linux libuv blocks SIGPROF around fork(), including allocator atfork hooks. Zero samples therefore do not prove that the entire process stopped. Reuse synchronous phases in the existing bounded main-thread task monitor at three launch owners, avoiding inherited diagnostic contexts in child callbacks; keep admission ordering, native descriptors, broker routing, cleanup, and child lifetime unchanged. Production growth is fourteen lines, with no new observer, timer, cache, or state.

See the [libuv spawn path](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v26.12.1/deps/uv/src/unix/process.c#L760-L875) and [V8 sampler](https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/v26.12.1/deps/v8/src/libsampler/sampler.cc#L568-L573). Other direct launch sites, synchronous credential commands, and broker bootstrap are outside this diagnostic's coverage.

## Evidence

- Regression fails on the original owner and passes with the change. It launches a real child and advances the monitor clock at Node's native launch boundary, proving that admission work and asynchronous child lifetime are excluded. Its 37 new test lines have a dedicated exact allocation; no shared ceiling was changed.
- Final synchronous-phase revision: 80 focused Node tests passed with no skips (38.87 s wall). Earlier validation: 83 passed under the default runtime; 12 existing Node-only broker cases skipped. Node follow-up: 63 passed, zero skipped. Wall times were 56.21 s including worker compilation, and 27.13 s respectively.
- Linux Node 26.12.1/libuv 1.52.1 with jemalloc background purging and 1-second decay: 1.77 GB heap and roughly 62 GB virtual address space. Three injected 1.5-second atfork waits produced zero samples while a worker continued ticking. Ordinary native waits and synchronous child sleeps produced 49–51 samples. An object-heavy 2.02 GB heap recorded ordinary GC frames during 329 ms median full collections. These controls establish diagnostic ambiguity, not a production root cause.
- Actual spawnProcess fault injection: before, 1,505.4 ms launch with no named stall; after, 1,510.8 ms launch with a 1,510.2 ms process:spawn:native stall. No speedup is claimed.
- Repeatable workload: node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/main-thread-stall-measure.mjs native-spawn 6 50. Five counterbalanced A/A/B or B/A/A groups with the first batch separated as cold. Median warm cost per 50 launches: wall 58.734 → 57.389 ms; main CPU 38.049 → 37.205 ms; V8 allocated bytes 7,742,344 → 7,625,560; per-launch p95 1.607 → 1.587 ms. Decreases are not claimed as optimizations because A/A variation is present. A preceding cold-only pilot had a 712.8 ms candidate burst outlier versus 224.5 ms baseline maximum; the warm run separates that startup variance.
- Calibration limits: paired mean changes against each pair's two baselines were wall +1.39%, CPU +1.63%, allocation -5.79%, p95 +4.25%. A/A wall and CPU changes reached +28.30% and +30.11%; allocation A/A reached +51.67%, and one candidate pair had +20.78% p95. These measurements do not qualify a speedup or precise overhead estimate; acceptance is the recovered attribution.
- Scope: isolated ARM64 Linux synthetic owner proof, not a complete Gateway/channel/model or x86/btrfs replay. No production data was used.
- Final staged Codex autoreview: scoped-clean through P2, with the unchanged monitor supplied as context. Review confirmed that the phase form preserves child callback context. Formatting, focused tests, targeted core/script lint, and line-cap checks passed. pnpm check:changed completed: production and test typechecks, core lint, import cycles, and database guards passed. Its optional broker-bootstrap line-cap failure was repaired by removing that change; the benchmark array lint failure was repaired and rechecked. The remaining unused export, prepareClientPluginNodeCapabilities, is unchanged from the pinned baseline, where it has no external production consumer; it is outside this PR scope and has since been fixed on main by #188839 (4a393be419f3). Full local gate is therefore recorded as failed, not green; unaffected local proof is reused.

prs.title: feat(pdf): add explicit OpenAI native document opt-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Platform users cannot explicitly choose native PDF document input through the PDF tool while preserving existing upload and model-selection behavior.

## User Impact

`agents.defaults.pdfNativeOpenai: true` opts an already-selected OpenAI vision model into complete-document input. **Unset or false preserves extraction and the existing provider order**, including saved configurations upgraded from the latest stable release. Selecting an OpenAI model alone does not authorize complete-document upload.

Page selection, passwords, unknown completeness, page/text/image truncation, size-limit violations, custom endpoints, Codex/ChatGPT transports and text-only models retain bounded extraction. Completeness checks still require the configured extractor. Existing Anthropic and Google paths are unchanged.

## Implementation

This replaces the earlier automatic-upload/provider-preference proposal with one default-off core boolean at the existing PDF configuration owner. The bundled OpenAI provider implements a narrow optional media-understanding hook using the official [PDF input contract](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/file-inputs): inline `input_file`, official Platform HTTPS `/v1/responses`, `store: false`, each PDF under 50 MB and combined PDF input at most 50 MB. There is no persistent Files upload, automatic provider preference or new dependency. The official configuration generator records the single additional core leaf; channel/plugin surfaces are unchanged.

Prepared credentials, headers and symbol-attached request/auth overrides use the existing scoped egress helpers. The native branch also reuses the host-owned `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` scope with `assertModelCurrent`, the **original model's** credential authority and the retained provider-resource assertion. The existing HTTP guard rechecks these synchronously immediately before dispatch after asynchronous preparation and on redirects. This closes the assert-only operator/credential retirement gap across lazy provider and DNS awaits without adding an authorization abstraction or changing shared HTTP behavior.

Capability adoption and the proposed setting placement remain normal maintainer product decisions. This branch provides a concrete default-preserving candidate for that decision.

prs.title: fix(state): throw the typed schema-admission error so retries classify it
prs.body:
Fixes #188935

## What Problem This Solves

`adoptAgentValidationSchema` rejected a stale receipt with a plain `Error`, while every retry and replay path classifies this fact through `AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError`. The message even asks the caller to retry, but nothing could act on it, so a completed turn ended with "OpenClaw couldn't finish this reply".

- Problem: one admission site reported a retryable fact as an untyped error.
- Solution: throw the typed error that other sites already use.
- Changed: `openclaw-agent-db-validation-schema.ts` throws `AgentDatabaseSchemaAdmissionChangedError`; that class accepts a message so the existing "handle adoption" wording is preserved.
- Not changed: the admission condition, the verdict, the message text, and the classification rules in `transcript-commit-failure.ts`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sibling receipt-publication path already throws this type (and the class documents "a receipt lost its publication race; fresh admission can obtain current proof"), so the two sites now agree on one signal instead of relying on the caller to match a string. The constructor's new optional message keeps this site's operator-facing wording identical, because the change is about classification, not about rephrasing a log line.

## User Impact

A turn that loses the schema-admission race can be retried or replayed instead of being discarded. The `rawErrorPreview` text an operator sees is unchanged.

## Evidence

Bidirectional, both runs real. The production throw reverted with the test kept:

```text
# reverted to the untyped Error
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-cache.test.ts
→ FAIL: AssertionError: expected error to be instance of SchemaAdmissionChangedError

# with the typed error
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/state/openclaw-agent-db-validation-cache.test.ts
→ 51 passed
```

The regression assertion sits in the existing schema-race case (`race === "schema"`), next to the message assertion that already covered this branch, so it proves the classification change rather than a new behavior path.

Not tested: the intermittent 54-minute-turn reproduction from the report (a concurrent memory-core publication landing inside the worker's schema adoption). That race needs the production timing window; the classified fact and its consumers are covered above.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used code tracing from the reported message to its single throw site, then compared it with the sibling site that already throws the typed error. The implementer understands the code: this error is a receipt race that fresh admission can resolve, so it must be the typed fact consumers classify, and the message is not the contract.
