prs.title: improve(ui): open large completed chat runs faster
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large completed chat runs make 2,000-message conversations slow to open and retain tens of thousands of rendered elements.

## User Impact

Long sessions become usable sooner and retain much less DOM and heap while preserving scrolling, transcript search, session switching, message controls, and streaming at the bottom. No migration or configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing virtualizer now materializes completed runs in bounded fragments instead of rendering their full contents up front. Incoming rows are prepared in small frame/idle budgets using cached geometry and scroll direction. Completed Markdown preparation survives DOM eviction; the retained DOM window stays bounded. Existing sanitization, media custody, and session authority remain with their current owners.

Footer disclosure also stops at the message-content boundary. Hovering one completed run no longer invalidates its entire Markdown subtree, and the original selector shape avoids per-scroll descendant invalidation.

Qualification repairs preserve neighboring behavior: Escape clears the Settings search input while asynchronous results still hold the previous query, instead of leaving plugin details; maintenance scrolling preserves the reader’s policy and does not publish a false new-messages affordance. Explicit reader takeover still works. Flushing a pending text-only run update now preserves its classification instead of waking non-text pane consumers; the existing publication regression moved to its focused suite to respect the line-cap ratchet.

## Evidence

Candidate `6e59b6c005c770f2bee585b9ac131548790b2e49`, compared with base `b70d9aa95d459d955955be1db6fb6ce71a8b4d7b`. Main was integrated by merge, preserving its resize-frame scheduling and this change’s cached table geometry. The current full CI run is [41159341793](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41159341793). Final committed builds, exact-source verification, and the complete V205 timing matrix are in progress. Prior-head results do not qualify this candidate.

Acceptance was fixed before measurement: mixed/direct-run × 400/2,000 messages × localhost/100 ms RTT at 10 Mbps, with 20 serial base/base/head triplets per cell. Up/down scroll frame-tail p95 must be ≤40.08 ms, with zero candidate tasks >50 ms, no sampled coverage below 90%, no corrections, and no endpoint misses >2 px. A/A, per-action CPU, and host load are retained. These synthetic-Gateway workloads measure renderer and simulated transport costs; they do not measure provider latency. Geometric coverage does not prove compositor paint completeness.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Independent review | Direct-provider Codex, scoped-clean P0–P2 on the text-only flush correction and the relocated regression. Earlier repair scopes also completed cleanly. |
| UI typecheck / targeted lint | Passed, including the relocated test. |
| Repair regression tests | The text-only flush assertion fails before the repair; 90 chat-state tests pass afterward, and all three tests in its final publication suite pass. Previous scroll and Settings regressions retain red/green evidence. |
| Focused stream E2E | All six current-source cases pass, including zero pane commits during the delta burst, bounded live tools, rich streaming, composer locality, and idle behavior. |
| Production Knip / strict bytes | Final checks in progress; no new ignores. |
| Timing matrix | Eight cells × 20 base/base/head triplets pending committed-head build; no final qualification claim. |
| Functional and memory proof | Pending final matrix. |
| Full CI | Run 41159341793 on current head with `ci:full`; no current-head green claim. |

Physical LOC across 165 changed files: 75,053 → 82,034 (+6,981). Production UI: 32,974 → 34,662 (+1,688); tests/helpers: 37,620 → 41,835 (+4,215); other: 4,459 → 5,537 (+1,078). The growth implements bounded preparation, fragment indexing, foreign-DOM lifecycle, and distinct geometry/scroll behavior proof. The latest flush repair removes one production line and reuses an existing test. Scoped Solid counts remain effects 8→8, untrack 2→2, listeners 0→0, DOM queries 19→18, flush 0→0, getOwner 2→2, runWithOwner 3→3, view cleanup 6→6, manual imports 1→1; retired/forbidden patterns 0.

### Inherited Cron assertion

The original [CI run 41153875940](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41153875940), [job 124396686094](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41153875940/job/124396686094), failed `Control UI cron saved descriptions E2E > configured duration precision: shows exact saved intervals in rows and details`: the row remained `Every 1m`, but detail was `Every 1m · Paused` instead of `Every 1m` (`cron-descriptions.e2e.test.ts:114`). ## Why This Change Was Made

## What Problem This Solves

The two worktree exact-state request flags can hang indefinitely on a FIFO or other blocking special file before reaching worktree owner admission.

prs.title: fix(memory-wiki): refuse special files during ingest
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Wiki ingestion can hang while holding its vault mutation lease when either the selected source or retained page is a blocking special file.

## User Impact

Both reads now reject nonregular files promptly with the selected filename and regular-UTF-8-file recovery guidance. Regular, symlink and hardlink source imports keep working, and correcting the path permits retry without losing handwritten Notes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the contributor's narrow repair in the shared ingest owner: use the existing regular-file reader after resolving the selected symlink, retain missing-page ENOENT recovery, and leave UTF-8 checks, Notes preservation and the write path intact. There is no new cap, schema, permission, default, dependency or SDK API.

Maintainer simplification extends the existing invalid-source test with directory admission and successful same-process retry, instead of adding FIFO writer/drainer subprocess fixtures. The necessary retained-page retry-fault migration remains. Whole-PR test-line delta is **0**; production remains **+21/-7**.

## Independent Maintainer Evidence

Fresh built Linux CLI proof in secretless `node:24.22.1` Docker: FIFO and no-input terminal character device at both source and retained-page boundaries, twice each. All eight main calls exceeded the 20-second guard and were killed/joined. All eight candidate calls rejected with a clear filename/recovery error in **1.51–2.46 seconds**, with no timeout. Each baseline attempt used a fresh vault/profile, ruling out abandoned-lock false positives.

Regular, symlink and hardlink imports exit 0 on both revisions and preserve Unicode and a real handwritten Notes block read back from disk. Source/config/protected-page bytes remain unchanged on refusal. After restoring a regular path, all eight candidate CLI retries exit 0 and preserve the note. The fast unit test separately proves same-process recovery after file-admission failure.

[Full independent commands, per-case timings, data hashes, controls and limits](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187621#issuecomment-6497802510).

Final focused suite: **3 files / 24 tests passed**, including 2,000,006-byte content, malformed UTF-8, CRLF/human Notes, mutation queuing and transient/persistent retained-page errors. The directory-admission negative control fails on main with EISDIR. Targeted format/lint passed. Runtime proof uses the freshly built production inputs from a29ce23a; the final maintainer commit changes only tests, whose final blobs were checked separately. Exact-head hosted CI/review are evaluated separately.

Merge danger: two-way door; the reader change can be reverted without a stored-format migration. Blast radius is the two local-file reads used by CLI/Gateway wiki ingestion. Successful writes remain unchanged, and rejection preserves the protected source/page content; whole-vault byte immutability, authenticated Gateway RPC, native Windows/macOS and a new release-upgrade run are not claimed.

A plugin-local helper gives them the same symlink handling and error context, while retaining the existing missing-page recovery. Remove the directory-as-absence branch now that directories are refused by file admission.

prs.title: fix: scheduled runs fail after unrelated channel reloads
prs.body:
Related: #188530 covers caller-turn custody separately; this change does not modify that boundary.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes scheduled work failing after unrelated channel configuration reloads, and known pre-effect policy refusals stranding an occurrence until a later slot.

## User Impact

Unrelated channel reloads leave valid scheduled work active. Relevant policy changes can re-admit genuinely unstarted work under fresh authority. Work that may already have performed effects, including model-resolution hooks, is not replayed by this policy retry.

## Why This Change Was Made

Scheduled events compare effective policy using canonical runtime/source snapshots for the selected agent, trusted creator and delivery channels, including shared channel policy and activation. Live source/job and per-effect authority checks remain. The existing event owner retains the same occurrence, with its existing two-readmission limit and 100/200 ms backoff. A typed lifecycle refusal before operation acquisition returns the existing mailbox receipt to the existing FIFO drain.

Execution and registered hook dispatch consume existing custody. This includes `before_model_resolve`, the only registered hook dispatched by the logical entry/setup modules before native candidate preparation, alongside the existing bootstrap and reply-hook barriers. Treating a registered model hook as possible work conservatively gives up policy retry even if that handler happened to be pure. No hook-runner semantics, second retry queue, persistence, configuration option or FIFO/coalescing behavior changed.

## Evidence

- Seven original regressions are red on integrated main `8034bb1fafbe83e5ce95fc985686bc2f95ff5ce1` and green with R6. The committed registered-hook regression is red on incoming `67533beaef03f344b1386afa081c1b5096919afa`, observing two persisted filesystem appends. Corrected `4607413216a54980402d55074ce7bedbaaf90279` produces one append, one preparation, no provider request and terminal error after the relevant policy publication.
- All **100 focused cases pass**: 28 native cron/preparation/model cases, 23 event-owner cases, 18 execution cases, 14 stable prompt/tool-prefix cases and 17 timer/session-custody cases. The final two hook cases were rerun after the mechanical test return-type alignment and pass. The unchanged setup/model-entry consumer suites also pass (43 + 7). Whole-PR test lines remain **−1**; all cases remain, and a redundant fixture setup readback is still covered before effect and after settlement.
- Targeted format, typecheck and correction-file lint pass. Full-PR local lint retains the handoff `max-lines` finding: 735/700, with unmodified integrated main also above the cap at 712/700. The existing GitHub Actions advisory size policy is unchanged; no cap, baseline or suppression changed. Focused suites used the pinned CI Bun runtime in isolated, network-disabled rootless Podman, limited to 4 CPUs/8 GiB and one test worker.
- Fresh independent [autoreview](https://github.com/openclaw/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/autoreview) of committed `4607413216a54980402d55074ce7bedbaaf90279` completed **scoped-clean at P0–P2**, with no findings. It assessed source and did not independently execute tests. The native correction review resolves `R6-HOOK-REPLAY` and retains the incoming NEEDS WORK evidence.
- Exact-head [CI 41157345030, attempt 1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41157345030) finished **failed**: 48 jobs succeeded, 27 skipped, and the Workboard job plus its aggregate failed. The only two failing cases, `agent_end survives closure` and `subagent_ended survives closure`, have the same `log.isEnabled` TypeError and assertion/diagnostic locations as [scheduled-main 41155320395](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41155320395/job/124400999286). Their test and diagnostic files are byte-identical in main, tested merge `6703bc567b47782bd99056ff07e794109d74b0cb`, and its first parent `21fd5cbb06b33b1c45daa2eb178843d014cd1b43`. The automatic failure table is unknown because job groupings differ; attribution uses the actual logs and Git objects. CI remains failed, and native inherited-failure admission must still enforce current review/security gates. No full-package, live external-model/channel or R3 external-owner proof is claimed.
- The observed 2526-second duration was active execution with prior Code Mode work, not a proven 42-minute queue/preparation wait. Its exact delay remains unidentified; natural occurrence ownership, slot deduplication and explicit forced runs are unchanged.

Requested by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/06278ba2-46e2-491c-b138-d3f8848cbf45)

prs.title: fix(workers): preserve setup inputs and inspect interrupted work
prs.body:
Fixes #180664

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes interrupted child-work inspection requiring new work even when the original publication receipt and worker placement are still retained.

## User Impact

Agents can inspect a visible child's original publication ID, recorded effects, and environment state without publishing, allocating a worker, running setup, or starting another model turn. An unpublishable parent gets status reads, not new write authority.

Worker setup also preserves the originally selected OS and machine class after restart, retains own prototype-named secret mappings, and rejects missing protected setup inputs before allocation. Stale setup documentation now points to protected store references and explicit destination bindings.

Historical setup-grant provenance remains explicitly `unknown`; current configuration is not evidence that a historical grant existed or was absent. No new configuration option, database schema, migration, or live deployment is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse native publication readers and descendant-lineage custody, applying current visibility to both parent and child before and after awaited reads. Project bounded diagnostics from the original epoch-correlated environment snapshot instead of reconstructing them from the current profile.

The setup fixes stay at their existing owners: carry the recorded selection to the provider, construct own-key-safe maps, and share secret-owner validation between preallocation checks and grant creation. Grant creation still rereads current protected entries.

The existing Windows interpreter repair in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180073 is preserved; selected-OS handoff is a separate missing boundary.

The separate tooling prerequisite lets code-only maintainer checkouts run their normal hooks using the existing qualified tooling owner. TSX and native protocol bundling retain current-checkout dependency pins, package containment and native executable binding; generator source and workspace aliases never come from the donor.
Qualification probes isolate Git's repository-local hook environment, so donor identity and sparse-checkout checks inspect the donor while the commit keeps its own index context.

## Evidence

- Exact-head CI on `22ffe462` exposed missing packaged tooling helpers, a projection type-import cycle, stale authority/policy/prompt fixtures, and optional setup-hook test typing. The correction keeps package resolution in the dependency leaf, packages only its two required helpers, and moves the existing pure profile reader out of service validation. No authority check or outcome assertion is weakened.
- Correction proof: 297 tests pass across 15 selected files; import cycles are zero; extension test types and targeted tooling/fixture lint pass. Core types and lint first caught one unused type import, then both pass after its removal. The initial aggregate exit remains 1; only those failed surfaces were rerun. The final optional-hook assertion syntax matches existing tests and has an identical runtime AST to the previously tested provider file. Evidence: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39817959819 (test command outcomes are separate from cancelled lease cleanup).
- Independent P0-P2 review of the CI owner-boundary correction found no actionable issue. Normal hooks pass for the signed correction commit with zero unstaged files and no check bypass.
- Red baselines on `1071fac6f6f42957a909bfc1809dfc71de7d9403`: selected OS, own secret keys, missing-input ordering, descendant reads, agent status, and placement passthrough.
- Native tool-to-Gateway receipt read after reopening real stores returns an incomplete child's original push effect, leaves the receipt unchanged, and starts no publication or agent turn.
- Interrupted provisioning retains the original environment and operation through store reopen; observation precedes recovery dispatch.
- Negative tests cover unrelated descendants, changed lineage, parent/child visibility, lifecycle, scope, profile, grant, connection and setup authority loss.
- Core and plugin production type checks, protocol generation/check and plugin inventory check passed.
- Fresh independent autoreview of the final corrected diff, default P0 scope: no accepted/actionable findings. The flat-schema correction also received a separate independent audit with no concrete regression.
- All 801 Crabbox plugin tests passed across 49 files. Corrected projection, assembled tool registration and `sentBeforeError` admission behavior passed.
- Targeted core/plugin lint and SDK strict smoke passed, including all 157 public SDK subpaths and 55 built control-plane modules.
- Final focused rerun passed all 54 selected tests, including restart selection, own secret keys, preparation/grant failures, publication actions and tool-prefix stability. Native Testbox command exited 0: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39794592263 (the Actions lease is cancelled during cleanup, independently of command results).
- Native bundler regression fails on the frozen generator with missing esbuild. The repaired real generator preserves current source and rejects mismatched packages, escaped entries/binaries, arbitrary binary overrides, foreign inputs, undeclared inputs and nondeterministic output.
- The final native qualification/loader batch passes 32 tests. The earlier native artifact/scope batch passes 26 tests and the selected declaration-closure guards pass six; these batches overlap and are not additive. Both tooling and script test typecheck leaves pass. Targeted production-script and native-test lint pass.
- Independent P0-P2 tooling review identified cached esbuild retaining an earlier unqualified binary. The failing programmatic-caller regression reproduced it; qualified acquisition now rejects an already-cached donor API. All 13 final native cases, targeted lint and script test typechecking pass: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39810542060 (command exit 0; lease cleanup is separate).
- Normal commit exposed inherited Git hook context affecting donor qualification. Three regressions fail before the correction; all 23 loader, 13 native, and 10 freshness cases pass afterward. The watcher fixture was updated for the new Git probe, then all 10 watcher cases and targeted lint passed. Tooling test typechecking passed. Independent P0-P2 review found no remaining actionable issue: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39813758512.
- Complete local `pnpm protocol:check` and the normal fully staged pre-commit hook pass, including protocol generation and the line-cap ratchet, without an installation, hook bypass or unstaged-input skip.
- Catalog test extraction preserves all six catalog cases and 20 assertion sites; 64 provider and six catalog tests pass.
- Prior tooling fixture lint retains 29 diagnostics verified identical against the frozen base. That command remains failed, not green; the existing fixture lint debt is a separate follow-up.

Production delta is +316 lines, including +173 tooling lines; tests +788; docs +40; source/workflow inventories +6. Pure helper moves retain one implementation and add only the imports needed to separate ownership. Runtime growth provides the read-only tool/protocol surface and bounded diagnostics. Tooling growth shares the existing resolver policy and adds the native executable/bundle ownership checks required to run unchanged hooks from code-only checkouts. No parallel store, dispatcher, permissive fallback or permission grant is added.

## Landing Status

Published-head CI on `fea8b216` completed with failure: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39820492885. All job rows and actual failure logs were inspected. The merge tested is `4f502762`, against base `488631c`. No required CI exception or landing clearance is claimed.

- The native-child fixture omitted `tooling-dependencies.mjs` after its importer changed. A one-line correction is committed locally, not pushed. Five isolated real-shim cases pass on the frozen base, reproduce the published missing-helper failure, and pass after the correction. Independent P0-P2 review and normal signed commit pass; actual Linux/Bun Vitest replay remains pending.
- Three prompt artifacts need native regeneration after the new `sessions_list` guidance. The focused Testbox queued and was stopped before execution, so no generated-byte proof or snapshot rewrite is claimed.
- Five updater test failures trace to the early engine-only gate introduced by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/37550409085cf78e3bf059f4de5e1cb5b05d943d in the newer CI base. They include lost recovery behavior, not merely diagnostic wording. The CLI tree is unchanged by this branch. No qualifying baseline execution was available, so these are not classified as inherited or waived.
- The browser job has 26 failed cases across executable/cache/platform discovery. Relevant owner and fixture blobs are unchanged, but a suspected filesystem mock/import-order leak still needs ordered baseline proof. No browser code, assertions or timing changed.
- The exact previously failing UI publication-lifetime case passes on this head: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39820492885/job/119971019663. The file's 12 tests and shard's 194 tests pass. This establishes the current outcome, not the historical cause.

Native PR provisioning remains separately blocked before checkout creation by the retained maintainer registry's backed-up migration custody gate. No registry or credential mutation, repeated failed provisioning, workflow-binding replacement or live rollout was performed. Native review/preparation and squash landing are not claimed. All task Testboxes are stopped; no blind rerun or replacement full CI was started.

## Review Disposition

The ClawSweeper review of `22ffe462` is addressed by the published `fea8b216` correction:

- Packaged preparation: the suggested lazy import was not used. The required two-helper closure is now included, and the configuration reader moved to its dependency leaf to avoid pulling in the CLI lifecycle chain. The existing source-less preparation no-op remains; eager-import and package-fixture tests pass in the focused proof.
- Optional setup hook: calls use the file's existing non-null call style. Missing implementations still fail at invocation; all outcome assertions remain. Strict extension test types pass.
- Explicit action policy: the inherited fixture expects only its permitted `publish` action; unrestricted status coverage remains separate.
- Session description: exact expected guidance was updated without weakening link-composition checks.
- Earlier child-selection refusal: diagnostics match the actual guard while zero-write assertions remain.

The new CI failures above remain separate required work. No review rating or green CI is inferred from these dispositions.

prs.title: fix(cron): prevent late background turns after job timeouts
prs.body:
Related: #176511, #143355, #137274.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes additional model turns and repeated work when a scheduled job times out after launching background commands.

## User Impact

Timeout, cancellation, and restart revoke the originating occurrence's background work and completion events. Retained process output remains inspectable. **Already accepted exec follow-ups survive normal successful teardown**, preserving the contract from #176511 and ordinary interactive completion behavior.

**Maintainer decision still required:** scheduler and native-command deadlines do not automatically replay a job after execution starts or a dispatched command's outcome remains unknown. Recurring jobs keep normal cadence; one-shots follow existing terminal-failure handling. Known pre-execution failures and provider transient retry classification retain recovery. This intentionally differs from the policy discussed in #137274; this PR remains a draft.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing active-job marker to capture one occurrence's cancellation lifetime beyond its first model invocation. Successful retirement transfers accepted follow-ups to the session controller without cancelling them; timeout/cancellation/generation changes still revoke the captured lifetime. A superseded occurrence cannot regain authority when its older cleanup runs.

Originating-run liveness is still checked until event acceptance. Current destination and policy checks remain active afterward. Existing occurrence admission and completion source-run attribution are preserved. #143355 covers complementary child timeout propagation.

No public API, configuration, dependency, or schema changes. Upstream integration removes its retired conversation-origin field while preserving both notification-lifetime cleanup fields. The retry documentation now distinguishes scheduled execution deadlines from provider failures and forced manual runs.

## Evidence

- Review regression reproduced red against the original PR source: a real exec completion was accepted while its source turn was held, then successful marker teardown cancelled it before model execution.
- **95 affected tests pass on the integrated head** across active-job authority, real process/session-controller follow-ups, producer cancellation/recovery, and native child effects. Cases cover normal success, timeout, operator cancellation, restart, retirement before/during acceptance, and supersession. The supersession case was also reproduced red before its repair.
- Current-head core types, targeted lint, oxfmt/Bun parity, documentation MDX sanity, and whitespace checks pass. Independent review found no remaining P0-P2 issues in the upstream integration and retry documentation. The maintained runtime build passes. Previous-head focused test type graphs, line-cap guard, and full build also passed; broad GitHub CI subsequently passed on that head.
- **Shipped CLI trace:** a separate Gateway process ran synthetic cron jobs through public CLI/RPC and a loopback Responses provider that actually requested background exec. No production profile or paid provider was used.

```text
timeout: provider requests=2; child stopped=true;
         late child effects=0; late inference=0; cron outcome=error
success: provider requests=3 (2 source + 1 exec completion);
         child effects=1; queued follow-ups=1; cron outcome=ok
```

The success trace holds the source response until the child completes and notification admission has time to finish; the third provider request must contain both the exec-completion notice and the child's output. The real queue regression separately proves explicit successful marker teardown before follow-up execution. An initial delivery:none fixture intentionally disabled wakes; a second fixture released the source before asynchronous acceptance. Those failed fixtures were diagnosed and retained, not reported as passes.

**Fresh-install and latest-stable state compatibility:** Separate foreground Gateways exercised both a fresh candidate and published `2026.10.6` followed by the candidate's documented manual runtime replacement (`doctor --fix`, then restart with the same isolated state). Existing one-shot/recurring settings and full successful run history were preserved. Actual scheduled model-started timeouts disabled the one-shot and advanced the daily recurring job to its normal future occurrence. Restart preserved those terminal histories, enablement, and exact next scheduled time, with zero new provider requests. Each lane made four job requests (two successes, two timeouts) and one separately identified, expected main-session auto-disable notice. This is runtime/state compatibility proof, not a published updater-driver activation test or qualification of every historical schema.

The private compatibility fixture first used forced manual runs, which intentionally preserve future slots; it was corrected to use real scheduled firing. An extra request was traced to the exact synthetic auto-disable notice, not counted as a job replay. The final proof rejects unexpected requests and checks persisted next-run times so a delayed replay cannot pass unnoticed.

**CI:** The complete GitHub CI run passed on `a0b68f6` ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39814796168)); the review of that head reported no code findings. That is prior-head evidence. This integrated head must receive its own CI/review results; draft status is preserved, so some lanes may skip. A separate aggregate status was pending when inspected. Earlier inherited local planner/root-budget and UI-suppression failures remain recorded as historical gaps, not current-head passing claims; no baselines were weakened.

<details>
<summary>Local test cost</summary>

The current six-file affected run passed 95 tests in 100.76 seconds with one worker across three shards, including compiled-subprocess preparation, real child processes, controller custody, and scheduler/native-command deadline handling. The earlier four-file repair run passed 67 tests in 63.60 seconds.

</details>

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. **Blast radius:** cron-owned child processes, completion admission, and deadline retry scheduling. Keep draft until maintainers accept the retry policy and required review/CI gates are satisfied.

prs.body:
Closes #180709

## What Problem This Solves

Document-heavy sessions can repeatedly overflow context when model replay uses the recorded document projection but compaction budgets and summarization see only the saved caption. Align those existing consumers with the frozen model-facing projection while leaving canonical messages and fallback contracts intact.

## Evidence

### Current budget-only follow-up

Current head `75541f60637a54a6ac690beae1e3971bdf9fd652`, tree
`ac92e4a2e8108a3e20c8e19e3c8f50ae40253824`, has the single published parent
`fd3035ef91adab6df940f1088a5ff5424e061571`. This changes only the existing
test-line ceiling, preserving every production/test blob and the checker.

[CI on that parent](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40755548771/job/123054273958)
measured **6,311,148 / 6,311,058 / delta +498 / over 90**, using prepared base
`953eba4bbeec1c8cf7b255cce1c8c3f1496aaf3b`. Nine other independent baseline
checks passed; the second failed job was the aggregate gate. That failure is
retained, not relabeled inherited or repaired by a green replay. No further main
integration was performed.

This PR and the two other scoped session PRs now share identical single-line
**6,313,000** ceilings. Their same-pattern Git numstat test sets are disjoint and
sum to **617 + 498 + 694 = 1,809** retained lines. Two actual CI totals minus
their respective PR deltas both imply 6,310,650. The explicit planning arithmetic
is **6,310,650 + 1,809 + 541 = 6,313,000**. This is not an independent main
measurement or combined-branch execution. The one-time 541 reserve is bounded,
supports the observed queue-time movement, and identical bytes avoid mutual
budget conflicts when these changes are considered together. It neither
automatically grows nor guarantees future main changes will fit. The budget
owner permits such a justified manual increase.

The unchanged counted corpus retains its actual native count **6,311,036**;
arithmetic slack under the new ceiling is **1,964**. Native scalar parsing,
identical-byte and unchanged-corpus checks, and whitespace checks passed. The
count was reused, not rerun. Normal commit hooks remained enabled. Complete
independent P0-P3 review of all three budget deltas and helpers found no
actionable issue (Codex-app narrative assessment, unverified inherited model
identity; not CLI/helper attestation). Current-head hosted CI is separate.

The real-model/persistence proof remains bound to `e7f2617` and the source
identities below: nine real requests, strict recall, actual client overflow and
compaction, summary provenance and unchanged canonical/full document inputs.
No new model run or equivalence of all transitive inputs is claimed for this
budget-only head. Earlier failed exercises remain preserved.

## Evidence

Integration follow-up (2026-10-29)

This addendum supplements the existing PR description and proof record; it does not replace or retract the previously recorded real-model failures.

The exact local integration candidate is e7f2617dc90c19f3682118f4eefb3bc0d2f42937, tree b24de1dafeec2fd08850b4b24c5e46d6b0efa48c. It is a normal merge with ordered parents fd453fed2b6f7a9fc3518dd78ab2ca3ef58263af and the pinned upstream main a1859e5195f6e74f1980192bdf291c0193e940a1. Relative to that pinned main, the candidate changes 15 files (+607/-47). The cache-diagnostic fixture change is already identical upstream and is no longer part of this PR's delta.

The only merge conflict was config/test-lines-baseline.txt. Resolution adopts main's 6,310,000 ceiling and its complete bounded-reserve comments, with no additional increase. The assertion baseline preserves upstream's shrink-only changes and this PR's safeguard count of 7.

Native checks completed for this integration candidate using Node 24.22.1 and the repository-pinned pnpm 12.15.0 after a frozen install:

- Test-line ratchet: 6,305,081 lines, ceiling 6,310,000, slack 4,919.
- Assertion-safety ratchet: 2,406 files and 5,475 grandfathered assertions; safeguard baseline 7.
- Single-page formatting and MDX validation passed for docs/concepts/compaction.md.
- git diff --check against the pinned main passed.

The original projection production and test inputs are unchanged by this integration. The earlier 29-test and 56-test results remain historical results, not fresh CI or newly rerun tests for this exact head. An independent full-candidate P0-P3 review found no actionable issues. That review is a narrative review from the current Codex app session; the inherited model identity is unverified, and it is not a separate CLI/helper attestation.

New real-model verification (2026-10-29)

One new isolated shipped-Gateway attempt on this exact head/tree passed the unchanged four-turn scenario with Qwen3.8-Flash: three 23,878-byte TXT documents, exact ACK DOCUMENT 1/2/3 replies without repeating the document facts, and strict final recall of all three requirement-ID/recovery-signature pairs. Both native build/runtime producer stamps name this exact source head; their signatures match the effective clean inputs, and the maintained preparation check required neither a build nor a runtime refresh. The driver used Node 24.22.1 and dist/index.js.

The recording contains nine physical HTTP 200 model requests: four conversation requests and five summarization requests, totaling 45,950 input and 1,826 output tokens in the observed usage. Every request has retained semantic SSE through [DONE] and valid usage. This is not a claim of complete HTTP-tail capture. The final request contains all three pairs only in messages[1], the user-role summary carrier; none of the original document-only records remains there, and the earlier ACK replies contain no document facts. The caller-visible final exactly matches the captured provider result and the committed final assistant message.

The 16,384-token client budget was genuinely exercised. Turn 3 recorded a local estimated-input overflow of 19,511 at transcript sequence 18, followed by committed compaction at sequence 19 (recorded tokensBefore 13,192 to tokensAfter 3,682), then ACK DOCUMENT 3 at sequence 23 and the all-three-pair final at sequence 26. Independent read-only inspection of the already-created stopped-state inspection copy confirmed same-branch compactions at sequences 7/14/19, all three pairs in the final committed summary, and firstKept sequence 17 beyond the original document user entries at sequences 1/8/15. All four canonical user prompts remain unchanged; each of the first three version-1 frozen model projections retains its complete original synthetic document. The maintained bounded transcript decoder was used, and the original inspector's before/after database, WAL and SHM hashes match.

The maintained native Windows instance verified provider-observation drainage, process termination and output joining with no cleanup errors or observed emergency kill. Its stopped process recorded exit code 1 under the supported Windows shutdown owner; this is not a claim of graceful zero-exit shutdown or global descendant extinction. No model call or Gateway restart was performed during the independent persistence inspection.

This establishes client-budget compaction recovery and strict recall for this one recorded attempt, not provider-context-window overflow, fleet-wide behavior, or perfect LLM recall. The original fourth-response omission of document 3 remains a failed proof, and the separately captured copied-state diagnostic remains a failed strict-recall result despite all three pairs being present in its transmitted summary. Both earlier failures and their evidence remain intact; the new successful attempt does not relabel them as passing.

Closes #180709

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated context-overflow failures and missing summary input when uploaded-document text is replayed to the model but compaction only sees the saved caption.

## User Impact

Document-heavy conversations can compact and continue without resetting the session. Summarization receives the frozen document text already used by the conversation, subject to the existing summary limits. No configuration or migration is required; canonical messages, direct recent-turn excerpts, and deterministic timeout fallback remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing recorded prompt projection for compaction budgets, retained-tail selection, and summary execution, without rereading attachments or changing the transcript. The safeguard also summarizes projected text when its short canonical caption would otherwise allow the preserved-excerpts-only shortcut.

Custom compaction providers now receive the model-facing frozen document text instead of only the persisted caption; non-text blocks remain intact. This intentionally aligns their input with foreground model replay. The custom-provider regression checks the delivered text, image block and content-block order, as well as the unchanged saved message. The contract is documented.

This complements #171258's canonical-excerpt truncation handling and is downstream of the ordinary prompt capture/replay work in #169237 and #179840; it does not replace those changes.

## Evidence

### Current CI comparison-budget alignment on `fd453fed2b6f7a9fc3518dd78ab2ca3ef58263af`

The [subsequent CI on 129d61fe](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40554135614/job/122366430088) used merge `4687632ec229046ace66c3005ac1aa3d553b6bd3` against base `d1cda17dde7fbd744d812cf7da80ee5aa20b03eb`. It measured 6,286,636 test lines against this branch's 6,286,444 ceiling, with the PR delta still +498. The other nine ratchets passed. This actual failed run is retained; no failure-report classification was available when diagnosed, and it is not labeled as inherited-only or a CI pass.

Only the budget scalar is now raised to **6,286,636**, exactly that observed CI total. There is no further main merge, test deletion, guard change or production change. This has zero arithmetic slack against the failed CI snapshot and 192 lines of slack against the unchanged, previously measured local fixed-`f39` tree (6,286,444). Those are different snapshots; this is not a claim that a new local counter measured the CI total. The repository permits a justified manual increase. Independent review verified the raw log, exact one-line metadata delta and unchanged test-count inputs; existing native local count evidence is reused, rather than starting another broad count or claiming a new passing counter run. New-head CI must still be evaluated.

### Retained CI fixture repair on `129d61feaae3c86156d0cd2c00e51ffd8bff5790`

[CI on 3aa1dfd](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40547663736/job/122343409010) passed the repaired test-line ratchet but failed one cache-observation assertion: the test expected `description: "read"`, while the diagnostic renderer intentionally emits `description: tool[1]`. The failure report classified that job as unknown because there was no comparable scheduled-main job; that classification is retained. Read-only contents from its actual comparison base `24e16034180f7a08eda5f17d2a2b573cde1868a5` show the same stale expectation and ordinal renderer, which is static attribution evidence, not a separate failing main run.

The repair changes only that expected string to the current anonymized tool label. It does not change production behavior or weaken the request-index, cache-usage, change-detection, compaction-skipping, pre-cache tool or authority assertions. Independent P0–P3 review of the full test and actual request-observation owners found no actionable issue. The original failed file now passes 2/2 cases through the native Windows/Node wrapper (304.53 seconds total, including 198.153 seconds of cold worker preparation; test bodies 60 ms and 12 ms). This is not a Bun/Linux replay. The original CI failure remains recorded, and the retained non-group Windows test namespace is not represented as globally certified cleanup. Minimal one-file type-aware lint, formatting and whitespace checks passed; lint's native prerequisite generated the required SDK boundary declarations.

This adds one existing-test-file 1+/1- change beyond the previous 16-file candidate, with no production or test-line-count increase. The original 15 document-compaction files and the justified zero-slack ceiling are unchanged; the existing relevant type and budget evidence is reused, not relabeled as a fresh full run. No additional main integration or live-model call was made. Exact new-head CI is evaluated separately.

### Previous budget repair on `3aa1dfd604cfa6fd483d5b460aef68077ee67433`

The previous repair, `86242d8622794edf7ee20a313aeda4d047c2401f`, exposed a test-line budget failure in [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40533987586/job/122298516812): 6,285,932 test lines against a 6,285,000 ceiling, with this PR adding 498 lines. The other nine ratchets passed. This failure is retained and is not described as inherited-only or waived.

First integrated the observed CI comparison snapshot `23b53fd33fcd0fbaaf62546db23fb032541c9bdc` normally in `9c1ddfba0771f442ec3a6b00a76f9833e58ce624`. The native checker measured 6,286,264 lines and passed after an explicit, zero-slack budget adjustment. Main subsequently changed the same scalar, creating a real one-file conflict. The final bounded integration uses snapshot `f39b480c874d8acdae73f3b1c060dbd6cfc7a052`; its sole conflict was that budget line. No history was rewritten or other conflict resolution required.

All original 15 PR files remain byte-identical to `86242d`; the only additional PR file is `config/test-lines-baseline.txt`. At the final fixed snapshot the native checker measured **6,286,444** lines and a **+498** PR delta. The deliberate ceiling adjustment is exactly 6,285,587 to 6,286,444, with zero slack: 498 lines of retained document regression coverage plus 359 lines already beyond the ceiling in that comparison tree. That decomposition is arithmetic, not a separate failing run of main. The repository's documented ratchet policy permits a manual increase with a PR justification; no tests were deleted and no guard was disabled. The native checker passed after the edit, as did whitespace validation.

An independent P0–P3 agent inspected the complete 16-file delta and the mechanical/budget increment, finding no actionable issue or generated/dependency drift. This is a narrative independent-agent assessment, not a CLI/helper attestation. The focused regression evidence below is reused for the unchanged PR code; it is not a newly executed live-model run. CI for the new exact head must be evaluated separately.

### Retained functional regression evidence

- Baseline: real embedded document ingestion/recording/recovery accepts two document turns, then returns `context_overflow` on the third and a short follow-up. A matched inline-text control continues all four turns. The regression fails at the expected overflow assertion on the unchanged base.
- Fix: the same production composition completes three projected-document turns and a short follow-up, feeds document text to summarization, retains all three document markers in the final model request, and leaves saved captions unchanged. No network calls occur.
- Five owner-boundary cases cover core summary execution, default recent-turn preservation in safeguard, a custom compaction provider, deterministic fallback, and manual retained-tail sizing.
- Pending-input tests cover historical projection costs and overlap credit, avoiding double-counting the admitted document.

Those regression checks use synthetic model I/O; they do not establish hosted-tokenizer accuracy or LLM summary quality. An earlier Gateway diagnostic timed out during startup before `chat.send` and is not product evidence. The real-model runs below cover the shipped Gateway path; each is labeled with its tested commit and limitations.

### Real Gateway/model evidence on `af783a8fe5cb1869ea150b10b284bafe51f947dc`

Using the standard CLI on Windows Node 24.22.1, isolated state, Bailian `qwen3.8-flash`, and the same 16,384-token client budget, sent three synthetic 23,878-byte TXT attachments and a follow-up. No tracked source changes, model fallback, tools, search, or thinking. Nine provider requests completed with HTTP 200, usage and `[DONE]` (four conversation and five summary requests).

The product recovered from a third-turn local context-budget overflow, committed actual model-backed compaction, and completed all four conversation turns. Real summary requests included document-only input; the latest persisted summary contains all three independently random ID/signature pairs. The initial ACKs are exactly `ACK DOCUMENT 1/2/3`, without leaking those values.

**Strict follow-up limitation:** the fourth response returned only document 1/2 pairs and omitted document 3, despite its pair being present in the committed summary. The live driver correctly exited 1; this run is not represented as a fully passing three-pair recall test. The original result and state remain unchanged. This establishes successful client-budget recovery and continued real-model responses, but does not establish flawless summary recall or, by itself, whether the omission occurred during replay or model generation.

```text
context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction for qwen/qwen3.8-flash
auto-compaction succeeded for qwen/qwen3.8-flash; retrying prompt
seq  7: committed compaction, 7643 -> 491 client tokens
seq 14: committed compaction, 8216 -> 6372 client tokens
seq 18: local context error, estimated input 18962 > client budget 16384, zero provider usage
seq 19: committed compaction, 12546 -> 3917 client tokens, all 3 ID/signature pairs in summary
seq 23: assistant stop, ACK DOCUMENT 3
seq 26: assistant stop, document 1/2 pairs only (strict recall assertion fails)
```

These are client accounting values, not the provider's context-window limit. The deterministic regression separately exercises provider-error recovery. No provider-window, channel-delivery, fleet-scale, or perfect LLM-quality claim is made.

One separately recorded diagnostic restarted a **copy** of that stopped state on the same head/model/config and issued one clearer follow-up containing none of the expected values. It made exactly one foreground request (HTTP 200, `[DONE]`, 3,925 input / 145 output tokens). Observation of the actual serialized request found all three ID/signature pairs in `messages[1]` (the summary); document 3's pair appeared there and not in the previous incomplete assistant reply. The model still returned only document 1/2, also persisted as a successful assistant response. This diagnostic also exits 1 under the strict recall assertion. It rules out loss of document 3 before transmission **for this diagnostic request**, not all prompt/context effects or the unobserved original fourth request. Original failed evidence and SQLite main/WAL/SHM hashes were unchanged. An independent reviewer checked the request observations, frozen usage ledger, copied database response, and original hashes. No additional model retries were attempted.

### Prior-head real Gateway/model behavior on `985c4cb00742a4c63e33cea3717c33db70eda041`

Ran the standard `node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run` CLI in isolated state with the OpenClaw runtime and Bailian `qwen3.8-flash` (OpenAI-compatible API). Sent three 23,878-byte synthetic TXT attachments through `chat.send`, then a follow-up through the same session. Client context budget: 16,384 tokens; thinking, tools, search, and model fallbacks disabled. Tracked source diff was empty.

Each document carried an independently random requirement ID and recovery signature. The first three replies were exactly `ACK DOCUMENT 1`, `ACK DOCUMENT 2`, and `ACK DOCUMENT 3`, without echoing any document facts. The final prompt did not contain the answers; the real model returned all three exact ID/signature pairs.

- Nine actual provider requests completed with HTTP 200, SSE usage, and `[DONE]`: four conversation requests and five summary requests. Read-only native transport observation did not rewrite request bytes or model responses.
- The actual summary requests included document-only text, including the first document's full unique requirement/signature sentence; its values appeared in the resulting persisted summary.
- Read-only SQLite verification found three committed compaction entries. The last advances the retained boundary past the original document 1/2 user entries, preserves all three pairs in its summary, and precedes the successful document-3 ACK and final follow-up.
- Third-turn local budget overflow was recovered by automatic compaction. This is **real model-backed client-budget recovery**, not a claim that the provider's much larger context window returned an overflow error. The deterministic regression separately covers provider-error recovery.

Redacted runtime and persisted-record evidence (token counts on compaction rows are the stored client accounting, not provider measurements):

```text
[agent/embedded] context overflow detected (attempt 1/3); attempting auto-compaction for qwen/qwen3.8-flash
[agent/embedded] auto-compaction succeeded for qwen/qwen3.8-flash; retrying prompt

transcript seq  7: compaction, tokensBefore=7615,  tokensAfter=634,  firstKeptSeq=5
transcript seq 12: compaction, tokensBefore=8328,  tokensAfter=6499, firstKeptSeq=8
transcript seq 17: compaction, tokensBefore=12673, tokensAfter=4068, firstKeptSeq=15
transcript seq 21: assistant stop, ACK DOCUMENT 3
transcript seq 24: assistant stop, all 3 exact random ID/signature pairs recovered
```

Observation limitation: the live driver exited 1 because its WebSocket compaction-event assertion received no matching event, despite all four conversation turns completing. That original failure is retained, not relabeled as a passing driver run. The completed compaction is verified separately from the actual persisted entries, real provider request/response observations, runtime recovery log, and subsequent assistant responses; an independent reviewer also read the SQLite records. No channel-delivery or fleet-wide reliability claim is made.

## Validation and review follow-up

On `af783a8fe5cb1869ea150b10b284bafe51f947dc`, four focused files passed all 56 tests: embedded continuation, projection consumers, request budget, and safeguard. The embedded case took 26.56 s; the two-shard wrapper took 203.38 s including worker preparation. Targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, documentation checks, assertion and line-cap ratchets, and PR-delta whitespace checks passed. Earlier focused sibling coverage includes prompt-prefix stability. These local checks used Windows Node 24.18.0; the real-model run used supported Node 24.22.1 after a successful standard CLI build.

[CI run 39990498846](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39990498846), for `af783a8fe5cb1869ea150b10b284bafe51f947dc`, completed successfully, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Its hosted logs show all five projection-owner cases passing. This CI result belongs to that commit; validation of the subsequent test-only refinement is recorded separately below.

The earlier SQLite fixture failure is resolved by running the real ingestion, recording, compaction and continuation composition in the existing child-main-process infrastructure. It preserves host-owned database admission and all behavior assertions. The longer integration test protects that composition; smaller owner tests cover its separate input contracts. The assertion-safety baseline shrinks from 9 to 7 to match two assertions removed by the text-helper extraction.

The merge at `af783a8fe5cb1869ea150b10b284bafe51f947dc` integrates pinned main snapshot `ca2ae0accb7481b9b3bb521f7eb38b534272638c`. The only manual conflict was adjacent baseline rows: safeguard count 7 and project-settings snapshot count 3. prs.title: improve(test): avoid repeated ACP client source loading
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The ACP client process test reloads the same TypeScript graph in each of its five independent client processes. This is a maintainer-requested test-health optimization.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Median warm focused-test wall time falls **22.48 → 15.62 seconds (30.5%)**. The tradeoff is higher preparation cost and memory: the first cold candidate invocation takes **53.03 seconds**, and median warm peak RSS rises **387.4 → 605.6 MiB**.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the client from the existing compiled subprocess generation during collection. Keep the JavaScript probe, pass its private directory and mode as arguments, and retain five separate clients and real stdio JSON-RPC servers. The existing registry supplies declaration, collection, compilation, and settlement; the CLI helper used by the concurrent logs lane is untouched.

All five cases, assertions, timeouts, cleanup grace periods, diagnostics, SIGTERM receipts, PID-death checks, and managed process-tree/output settlement remain. No production code changes or deleted behavior.

## Evidence

Frozen base: `21fd5cbb06b33b1c45daa2eb178843d014cd1b43`. Candidate: `d575e8324053a1a0c21b3652f3be6666b72df58f`.

`timeout 900 /usr/bin/time -v pnpm test src/acp/client.process.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose`

Three serial before and three serial after runs, all **5/5 passing**, with the same private frozen dependency installation, Node 26.12.1, pnpm 12.15.0, Vitest 5.0.5, host, temp paths, and cache paths. Import diagnostics were enabled for both series.

| Run | Wall s | Vitest s | Case sum s | Import self/total s | CPU user/sys s | Peak RSS MiB |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| before-1 | 23.54 | 21.20 | 19.770 | 0.214/4.46 | 15.50/2.65 | 408.7 |
| before-2 | 22.48 | 20.80 | 20.085 | 0.101/2.38 | 14.22/2.13 | 387.4 |
| before-3 | 21.19 | 19.67 | 19.090 | 0.076/1.58 | 13.28/1.82 | 364.9 |
| after-1 | 14.50 | 11.71 | 8.025 | 3.200/4.67 | 10.62/3.87 | 713.3 |
| after-2 | 16.19 | 13.40 | 8.063 | 4.760/6.55 | 11.65/4.81 | 560.0 |
| after-3 | 15.62 | 12.85 | 8.009 | 4.270/6.20 | 11.38/3.71 | 605.6 |

Median case sum: **19.770 → 8.025 seconds (59.4% lower)**. Case sums are verbose-reporter case durations, not wall time. Import self/total is Vitest's diagnostic; inclusive totals overlap and are not a separate elapsed phase.

The separate, retained cold candidate run passed 5/5: compiler preparation 39.508s, wall 53.03s, Vitest 50.31s, case sum 8.711s, import self/total 41.040/42.62s, CPU 151.21/29.60s, peak RSS 6174.7 MiB. This is a warm-run improvement with a disclosed first-preparation cost, not a cold-start improvement.

Discovery CI measured [18.092 seconds across five cases](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41144429846/job/124366403091). That is a historical CI case sum, not local wall time or a new candidate CI measurement.

<details>
<summary>Work counts, retained contracts, and validation</summary>

- Separate successful before/after syscall traces retain **five Node clients and five real servers**. Each client's TypeScript source opens fall **796 → 0**, or **3,980 → 0** total; source-loader client launches fall **5 → 0**. Compiler preparation is accounted for above.
- Existing cases still prove failed-handshake error structure and server death; spontaneous SIGTERM status 1; spontaneous exit status 0; client-owned quit preserving status 7 and its SIGTERM receipt; pending-prompt EOF preserving the final `[end_turn]`, one prompt, SIGTERM receipt, and SIGKILL diagnostic. All retain PID-death assertions and managed settlement. No assertions or behaviors were removed.
- Mutation checks: losing structured handshake details fails the RequestError assertion; forcing successful client status fails the SIGTERM and quit-7 outcome assertions; omitting the pending prompt's `[end_turn]` fails the EOF assertion. Temporary production mutations were restored byte-for-byte. Both intentionally failing runs are retained separately from benchmarks.
- Final focused proof: **33 passed, one existing Windows-only case skipped on Linux**, across `client.process`, `client`, `client.invocation`, and `infra/fs-safe-defaults`.
- Scoped typecheck, type-aware lint, format, diff, line-cap, max-lines, test-line budget, timeout-race, mock-export, and assertion-safety checks pass.
- Exact LF inventory: target **176 → 175**, existing helper **20 → 21**; **net test LF 0, production LF 0, effective cap delta 0**. Both native tracked snapshots count **6,319,265 test LF**. Scalar **6,320,000** and all **227 grants totaling 31,058** are byte-identical; effective ceiling **6,351,058** preserves exactly **31,793** inherited slack. No new grants, baseline growth, ignores, or exceptions.
- `pr-simplify` completed: one existing registry entry and the launch rewire; no new runtime owner, cache, wrapper, mock, or seam.
- Complete-source isolated Codex autoreview against the frozen base and final staged snapshot: **P0–P2, scoped-clean, exit 0, report_produced true**; one complete pass with 24 intact target/owner/helper/context files, 284,267 prompt bytes. The committed source matches the reviewed snapshot. No actionable findings; the reviewer did not independently rerun tests.

</details>

All six measurements, the separate cold run, and both profiling runs passed; no product flake was observed. An initial external scoped-typecheck config could not resolve Node's ambient types; explicitly binding the worktree's `@types` root fixed that setup. Auxiliary census/help tooling attempts (system Python stalled on host I/O; a Node census exceeded its output buffer) are retained as setup failures; the successful native budget checker supplies the inventory, and review used supported Python 3.12 on the same host. No test was retried for green.

No broad suite, SDK build, macOS/Windows execution, real Gateway change, or real-state operation was performed. PR CI supplies broad proof. Parent source review and native landing are complete.

### Native landing

Parent02:10 approved exact original source head d575e8324053a1a0c21b3652f3be6666b72df58f, including the disclosed cold preparation and warm RSS tradeoff. It merged as 5e407f5384f97a69d12761b51e3e48c9e50030c5 on 2026-10-31T02:17:32Z. Exact-head [CI41158498321](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41158498321) completed successfully. No executed attributable failure or extra platform run was used.

Native **COMPLETE** receipt 98cf0dee2e7bb076f782651c0753b59c6262fd54; original immediate squash attempt ff51809c-0880-4408-9c19-2afe02716280. Replaying the exact approved patch on actual parent 59bb137327fd40fed8011848f2f44e56b6c6dd5a reproduces the full landed tree 4a5f44449484510dad7dd08eaa88eaea84eda3ee. Original head, human coauthor trailer and authoritative main ancestry were verified. Native PR-owned checkout/branches were removed; parent-owned implementation checkout remains for its owner.

Native check-only comparison captured current main b70d9aa95d459d955955be1db6fb6ce71a8b4d7b: test LF **6319793 → 6319793 (0)**, cap **6351443 → 6351443 (0)**, slack **31650 → 31650**. Scalar and all current grants are unchanged. Actual landing-parent LF deltas are target **-1**, helper **+1**, net **0**, with effective-cap delta **0**. No funding, baseline/grant growth, extra census cut or new allocation. Frozen benchmark-base counts above remain historical.

All original six warm samples, the separate 53.03-second/6174.7-MiB cold run, warm RSS increase 387.4 → 605.6 MiB, both work-count traces, mutation results and setup/runtime/platform limitations remain above. No new integrated-main timing, memory gain, CI-seconds saving or independent reviewer test run is claimed. prs.title: feat(agents): expose configured descriptions in agents_list
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agent configuration accepts descriptions, but `agents_list` omits them. A requester choosing an allowed subagent cannot see the operator-authored capability summary. Fixes #7490.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expose bounded, nonblank descriptions only in on-demand discovery. Preserve the complete authorized roster, ordering, resolved model/runtime metadata, and existing child-agent restrictions. Each description is limited to 512 UTF-16 units without splitting a surrogate pair, with a shared 4096 CJK-aware weighted-unit budget. Later description text may be shortened or omitted; agent rows remain.

## User Impact

Names, descriptions and existing model/runtime metadata remain available together. Documentation at the current per-agent-entry and subagent-discovery owners describes model visibility and excludes secrets or tenant-sensitive material. There is no new configuration, authorization, persistence, provider, or automatic prompt-roster mechanism.

Existing nonblank descriptions would become model-visible to already-authorized discoverers after upgrade without an operator editing configuration. That disclosure choice requires the maintainer decision below; the spawn allowlist alone does not establish prior operator expectations.

prs.body:
Related: #182810, #176626

## What Problem This Solves

On the PostgreSQL engine, every read snapshot sends `BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY` as its own blocking bridge request before its first statement. Most snapshots run only one statement, so a one-row read costs three blocking requests (BEGIN, statement, ROLLBACK) instead of one.

## User Impact

PostgreSQL read paths (session lists, history, pending-input reads, workboard reads) spend less time blocked in `Atomics.wait`. A one-statement snapshot read drops from about 0.98 ms to 0.54 ms at p50 on our ported data. Results are unchanged. SQLite is unaffected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Under REPEATABLE READ, PostgreSQL takes the snapshot at the transaction's first statement, not at BEGIN. Sending BEGIN together with that first statement therefore leaves every snapshot's view unchanged. `PostgresSyncConnection` now holds a lone read-only BEGIN and attaches it to the next query request, and the bridge worker runs it just before the statement. A snapshot that ran no statement skips both BEGIN and ROLLBACK. `readRecoveryGeneration` sends a pending BEGIN first. Write transactions, savepoints and batched BEGINs are untouched.

Callers can't decide this up front: the hottest one (`session-pending-input-history.kernel.ts`) runs count-then-page and needs the snapshot only when the count is non-zero. So the deferral sits in the connection, not in a per-caller opt-out.

## Evidence

Setup: real Gateway data (13 stores: state, 11 agents, and a 336-card workboard), ported to PostgreSQL 17.11 over a Unix socket, on a shared Mac Studio. Base is main `00bfbf1f7ca`.

**How often this happens** (every statement logged, 120 s idle plus a 120 s read mix at concurrency 8, 17,988 RPCs): 20,545 read-only snapshots ran.

| Statements in the snapshot | Snapshots | Share |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 261 | 1.3% |
| 1 | 11,168 | 54.4% |
| 2 | 3,313 | 16.1% |
| 3 | 4,660 | 22.7% |
| 4+ | 1,143 | 5.6% |

The single-statement ones include all 5,704 `session_pending_inputs` counts, 3,744 of the 10,239 session window reads, and all `agent_provenance`, `user_profiles` and `update_runs` lookups. The read mix averages about 1.1 snapshots and 4.9 statements per RPC. This change removes about one of those ~4.9 blocking bridge requests per RPC.

**Cost per read** (microbenchmark through the real `PostgresSyncConnection` bridge, on the ported data): the hottest single-statement snapshot read (`session_pending_inputs` count), alternating 4 s phases of `runSqliteReadSnapshotSync(read)` and the bare statement. One connection per process, 3 interleaved rounds per arm. The host's load average was 22 to 67.

| Concurrency | Arm | Snapshot read p50 | Bare statement p50 | Wrapper cost | Snapshot reads/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | main | 0.98 ms | 0.31 ms | 0.67 ms | 452 |
| 1 | this PR | 0.54 ms | 0.28 ms | 0.26 ms | 1,111 |
| 8 | main | 3.81 ms | 1.35 ms | 2.47 ms | 662 |
| 8 | this PR | 1.50 ms | 1.08 ms | 0.42 ms | 1,216 |

On main the snapshot read costs 3.0 to 3.4x the bare statement at c1 (three requests). With this PR it costs 1.9 to 2.2x (two requests). The c8 rows are noisier: process start spread was 5 to 32 s on the shared host.

End to end, 3 interleaved Gateway runs per arm on the same read mix could not separate the arms on this host. At c1 the median was 75 vs 97 rps, at c8 196 vs 179 rps, and runs of the same arm varied 40 to 50%. I'm not claiming an end-to-end throughput number.

Tests:
- `src/infra/postgres-sync/connection.test.ts`: two new cases. One checks that a snapshot sends its first statement with `begin` and that an empty snapshot sends nothing. The other checks that a failing first statement still rolls back. Red on main (2 failed / 23 passed), green with the change (25 passed).
- PostgreSQL conformance (`scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres`): read-facts, reuse, session-publication, transcript-hydration, commit-receipts, session-accessor read-hold, state-read-admission and openclaw-agent-db postgres tests. 8 files / 52 tests pass on main and with the change.
- `pnpm check:changed`: everything passes except the Knip production unused-export scan, which flags `prepareClientPluginNodeCapabilities` in `src/gateway/plugin-node-capability.ts`. That file isn't touched here, and the export is already on main.

<details><summary>Not changed / follow-ups</summary>

- PostgreSQL still receives BEGIN as its own protocol message, because node-postgres sends one query at a time, so the server-side statement count is unchanged. What this saves is the blocking bridge round trip.
- The closing ROLLBACK of a non-empty snapshot is still a blocking request. Releasing it without waiting would save another round trip, but it needs ordering guarantees in the bridge and is left out of this change.

</details>

prs.title: feat(deepseek): add optional web fetch fallback
prs.body:
Related: #180680

## What Problem This Solves

Users who already use DeepSeek cannot currently select its standalone Fetch API behind OpenClaw's canonical `web_fetch` fallback without another retrieval provider or a separate MCP tool.

## User Impact

Operators can explicitly select `tools.web.fetch.provider: "deepseek"` and reuse their existing DeepSeek search credential. Local retrieval remains first; configuring DeepSeek inference or search alone does not opt users into paid URL delegation.

A one-off `openclaw infer web fetch --provider deepseek --url https://example.com/ --json` also works with no saved provider or a different saved provider, without rewriting that selection.

DeepSeek receives the requested public URL and can charge per successful fetch. Local request headers, browser cookies, and conversation history are not forwarded. Canonical fetching retains its target/redirect checks and output safety boundary; the adapter also rejects private/internal literals, credential-bearing URLs, and malformed requests.

**Product decision requested:** this remains a draft proposal for the existing official DeepSeek plugin. Official-plugin scope still requires maintainer sponsorship; the automated review is not a maintainer decision.

## Why This Change Was Made

Register a lazy `WebFetchProviderPlugin` that posts `{ url }` to the fixed official `https://api.deepseek.com/v1/tools/fetch` endpoint. Reuse existing prepared credential hooks, guarded HTTP, timeout/cancellation handling, text rendering, and canonical normalization/cache/spill ownership.

The review's P2 CLI finding is addressed at the existing selection owner: a per-call `providerId` is forwarded in the request's effective `fetchConfig`. The adapter consumes that effective selection before saved configuration. The saved config is neither mutated nor written, and automatic selection does not gain explicit consent.

No new model-facing tool, configuration key, SDK seam, credential store, cache, or default routing policy is introduced. Plugin metadata, catalog ownership, generated reference documentation, and operator documentation remain aligned.

## Evidence

### October 26 repair and real CLI execution

Repair commit: `c9cadc4d6bb2dca6b3a22fa1aee527bdd5139601`. Local validation used Node 24.22.1 on Windows, including the supported Node test-runner fallback.

- Added two selection-owner regressions covering absent and different saved providers. Both failed on the pre-repair code because no definition was resolved. After repair, all **16 web-fetch runtime tests** and **27 Fetch adapter/contract tests** pass (two targeted Vitest shards, 143.54s wall time).
- Re-ran the complete DeepSeek extension lane: **71 tests passed in 5 files**, including search, model, onboarding, and Fetch behavior (74.80s Vitest duration; source transformation dominates wall time).
- Production source typecheck, package-boundary DeepSeek typecheck, targeted typed lint, targeted formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Repository-supported candidate runtime build: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime` passed in **2m 3.2s**, including CLI, local external-plugin runtime artifacts, bootstrap import guard, and postbuild verification. This is a candidate runtime build, not a full release-package build.

The following controls ran through that build's **actual `dist/entry.js infer web fetch` CLI** and built DeepSeek plugin. HTTP and DNS were not mocked. A passive `node:diagnostics_channel` subscriber observed native Undici request creation and response status; it did not replace or redirect network operations. Each case used an isolated state directory and synthetic configuration; the existing key was supplied only in the child environment and was not saved in config, output, or this PR.

| Control | Saved provider | Command override | Observed DeepSeek Fetch POSTs | Fetch API response | Saved config SHA-256 unchanged |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Successful local retrieval | absent | none | 0 | not called | yes |
| Explicit CLI selection | absent | `--provider deepseek` | 1 | HTTP 200, nonempty page | yes |
| Explicit CLI override | `firecrawl` | `--provider deepseek` | 1 | HTTP 200, nonempty page | yes |
| Canonical configured fallback path | `deepseek`, `readability: false` | none | 1 | HTTP 200, nonempty page | yes |

<details>
<summary>Redacted live-run terminal summary</summary>

```jsonl
{"case":"local-first-without-selection","ok":true,"transport":"local","provider":"direct","extractor":"raw-html","nonemptyPage":true,"apiRequests":0,"apiHttpStatuses":[],"localHttpStatuses":[200],"configUnchanged":true,"elapsedSeconds":4.84}
{"case":"cli-explicit-without-saved-provider","ok":true,"transport":"local","provider":"deepseek","extractor":"deepseek","nonemptyPage":true,"apiRequests":1,"apiHttpStatuses":[200],"localHttpStatuses":[],"configUnchanged":true,"elapsedSeconds":4.53}
{"case":"cli-explicit-over-saved-firecrawl","ok":true,"transport":"local","provider":"deepseek","extractor":"deepseek","nonemptyPage":true,"apiRequests":1,"apiHttpStatuses":[200],"localHttpStatuses":[],"configUnchanged":true,"elapsedSeconds":4.58}
{"case":"canonical-selected-fallback-mode","ok":true,"transport":"local","provider":"deepseek","extractor":"deepseek","nonemptyPage":true,"apiRequests":1,"apiHttpStatuses":[200],"localHttpStatuses":[200],"configUnchanged":true,"elapsedSeconds":4.69}
```

</details>

The public target was `https://example.com/`. Local retrieval returned HTTP 200 with `extractor: raw-html`; provider cases returned `provider: deepseek` / `extractor: deepseek`. All four CLI envelopes were successful. Each completed in approximately 4.5–4.9 seconds. Exactly three authenticated Fetch requests were observed, without retries. The local machine uses trusted fake-IP DNS, so only the isolated canonical-fetch config enabled the documented RFC 2544 exemption; broad private-network access was not enabled.

The real canonical fallback control uses the existing `readability: false` mode after a successful local GET; it is **not** presented as a live HTTP-503 recovery demonstration. Local-503-to-DeepSeek fallback, normalization, and untrusted-content wrapping are covered separately by the canonical-tool integration test with fixed external HTTP/DNS fixtures.

### Scope of remaining proof

A running Gateway-plus-model E2E, full release build, and latest-stable package-upgrade exercise have not been performed. The real CLI controls prove preservation of saved settings during these calls, not preservation across an upgrade. This repair changes no persisted schema or migration. Broad CI and maintainer scope approval remain pending. No secondary-agent review was run under the task's no-delegation constraint.

Initial dependency/checkout setup failures and the original text-renderer expectation issue were resolved before the original passing extension lane. A combined follow-up check timed out while preparing/checking SDK artifacts; after verifying no associated compilers remained, the individual typed lint and source/package typechecks were rerun successfully. prs.title: fix(infra): keep the launchd recovery budget on elapsed time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The managed-service handoff recovery loop measured its budget on the wall clock:

```js
const deadline = Date.now() + params.recoveryTimeoutMs;
const run = (args) => runOwned("launchctl", args, undefined, deadline);
for (let inspection = enabled; enabled.code === 0 && Date.now() < deadline;) {
  ...
  await sleep(Math.min(500, Math.max(0, deadline - Date.now())));
}
```

Everything in that loop is local elapsed time, but it was seeded and consumed with `Date.now()`. A host clock correction during recovery (NTP step, VM pause/resume, manual change) either stretched the recovery wait past the configured timeout or expired it early, refusing a healthy `launchctl` restart during an update.

## Scope reduction (rebased onto current `main`)

This PR originally also converted the parent-exit path in `update-managed-service-handoff.ts`. Current `main` changed that contract: `params.parentExitDeadlineAt` is now created in the parent process (`parentExitDeadlineAt: Date.now() + owner.parentExitTimeoutMs`) and passed into the handoff script, so it is an epoch value that legitimately crosses a process boundary. Converting it to `performance.now()` would compare two unrelated clock domains, so that half is dropped — the remaining wall-clock dependency is the process-local recovery budget, fixed here.

Two deliberate boundaries in the reduced fix:

- **Spawn deadlines stay epoch-valued.** `runServiceCommand`'s `deadline` is shared with `params.parentExitDeadlineAt`, which comes from the parent process. Each local spawn therefore gets `Date.now() + remainingBudget()`; only the budget itself is monotonic.
- **Persisted timestamps keep `Date.now()`.** `serviceDowntimeMs` compares against the stored `serviceStoppedAtMs` epoch and is untouched.

This follows the owner established by #186484: `performance.now()` for process-local elapsed budgets, epoch for anything persisted or exchanged across processes. #186484 explicitly left managed-service handoff timing untouched, and this is that follow-up for the launchd recovery side.

## What Changed

```js
function createMonotonicBudget(timeoutMs) {
  const startedAt = performance.now();
  const remainingMs = () => Math.max(0, timeoutMs - (performance.now() - startedAt));
  return { remainingMs, commandDeadlineAt: () => Date.now() + remainingMs() };
}
```

## Evidence

`update-managed-service-handoff-command-source.test.ts` runs the embedded command source in a VM with injected `Date` and `performance`:

- Steps the wall clock **+1h** and then **−2h** mid-budget and asserts the remaining budget stays `180_000`ms while `commandDeadlineAt()` still tracks the live wall clock (`deadline − now === 180_000`).
- Asserts the recovery source drives its loop from that budget and no longer seeds it with `Date.now() + params.recoveryTimeoutMs`.

```
✓ src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-command-source.test.ts (12 tests)
```

`oxlint` clean on the three touched files.

### Known gap in this environment

`src/infra/update-managed-service-handoff-command.test.ts` (the end-to-end handoff suite) cannot run in this checkout: it needs the sealed `dist` runtime and fails with `Managed handoff requires its sealed runtime; use the repository test runner or the dist-backed pnpm openclaw CLI`. That is an environment limitation here, not a result of this change — CI runs it with the built runtime.
