prs.title: fix(ui): session New window/New tab always fails with "Allow pop-ups" in the macOS app
prs.body:
> **AI-assisted: yes**

Closes #144582

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users of the native macOS app choosing "New window" or "New tab" from the Control UI session tab menu would always see the toast "Allow pop-ups for this site, then try again." There is no way to allow pop-ups for the embedded WKWebView, so both actions were dead ends (the same actions work in a regular browser).

- **Related:** #144582 (labels: clawsweeper:queueable-fix, clawsweeper:fix-shape-clear, clawsweeper:source-repro).

## Why This Change Was Made

The web side reserves an inert `about:blank` popup via `window.open` and later redirects it to the session route. The macOS shell's `createWebViewWith` delegate classifies the `about:blank` request as ignorable and returns nil, so `window.open` returns null and the UI reports a blocked popup. The fix hands the final session URL to the existing native `openclawLink` bridge (already used by the Browser panel's external open) whenever that bridge is present, and keeps the previous `window.open` reservation as the browser fallback.

- **Intended outcome:** inside the macOS app, New window / New tab from the session menu hand the final session URL to the native link bridge instead of failing; no popup-blocked toast. The receiving default browser opens the Control UI session route; it needs its own gateway sign-in, so a previously paired browser renders the session directly while a never-paired browser lands on the Control UI login gate (an explicit sign-in surface) rather than the session.
- **Out of scope:** creating a native dashboard window/tab for the session (the shell has no such API today; whether to add one is flagged as a maintainer decision below); browser popup semantics are unchanged.
- **Highest-risk area:** routing the action through the native bridge hands a credential-free URL to the default browser, which does not inherit the app's WebKit credentials — a browser that never signed in to this gateway will not see the session.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The native receiver already validates main-frame + trusted same-origin source before opening; the posted URL intentionally carries no credentials (Gateway credentials must not be exposed in URLs), and an unauthenticated receiving browser is stopped at the login gate, which the E2E now asserts explicitly. Without the bridge (regular browsers), or if the post throws, the previous flow including the blocked-popup toast is preserved and covered by tests.

## User Impact

macOS app users can open a session from the session menu's New window / New tab items again: the session route now opens through the native link handoff in the default browser instead of failing with an impossible "Allow pop-ups" instruction. The receiving browser must be signed in to the gateway itself: an unpaired browser reaches the Control UI login gate (explicit sign-in) rather than the session; a browser that has already paired renders the session directly. Regular browser behavior is unchanged.

- **Success criteria:** with the native link bridge present, both menu actions post the final same-origin session URL and never call `window.open`; without the bridge, the previous reservation + toast flow is kept. The posted URL grants nothing on its own: a never-paired receiving browser stops at the login gate without rendering the session.
- **What should reviewers focus on?** `ui/src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.ts` (bridge handoff placed before the popup reservation); regression fixtures in `session-menu-navigation.test.ts` ("hands … to the native shell link bridge instead of a blocked popup", "falls back to the browser popup when the native link bridge rejects the post"); the real-Gateway E2E in `ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` (real Gateway + served Control UI + a page-level `openclawLink` bridge stand-in, covering both actions, the posted destination loaded verbatim in a paired isolated browser context, and the never-paired context stopping at the login gate).

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node 26, Playwright Chromium, a real Gateway child process built from this branch (`createOpenClawTestInstance`), and the Control UI served from this branch's source. The page-level `window.webkit.messageHandlers.openclawLink` bridge is installed through a browser init script before any page script runs — the same surface the macOS dashboard shell installs — and, like the native receiver, it does not open anything inside the source browser. The handoff destination is verified in isolated browser contexts that share no cookies, storage, or page state with the source page, modeling how an external default browser receives the `NSWorkspace.open` handoff: one context signs in to the gateway once through the Control UI's gateway confirmation surface (the analog of a previously paired default browser) and then navigates to the posted URL verbatim with no credential parameters appended; a second, never-paired context loads the same posted URL and must stop at the Control UI login gate. The macOS app itself is not runnable in this environment.
- **Exact steps or commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/lib/sessions/session-menu-navigation.test.ts ui/src/app/native-link-routing.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/vitest-ui-e2e-config.test.ts
  pnpm exec oxfmt --check ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  pnpm exec oxlint ui/src/e2e/session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts
  node scripts/run-tsgo.mts -b test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.ui-e2e.json --builders 1
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:** real-Gateway E2E (`session-menu-native-bridge.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`, head `d626215`) output:
  ```text
  ✓ hands session New window and New tab to the native link bridge instead of a popup 28328ms
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  1 passed (1)
  ```
  Both "New window" and "New tab" from the session menu post to the bridge:
  ```json
  [
    { "type": "open-link", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/chat/main/native-bridge-proof", "target": "external" },
    { "type": "open-link", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/chat/main/native-bridge-proof", "target": "external" }
  ]
  ```
  with zero `window.open` reservations from the menu code and no "Allow pop-ups" toast. The destination is then verified the way an external default browser receives it, in isolated contexts that share no state with the source page: the paired context first signs in once through the Control UI's gateway confirmation surface, then navigates to the exact posted URL verbatim — no `gatewayUrl` or token parameters appended — and renders the session's transcript, so the loaded session comes from the handed-off URL plus the receiving browser's own independent sign-in state. The never-paired context loads the same posted URL and stops at the `openclaw-login-gate` sign-in surface without ever rendering the session: the handoff grants nothing by itself, and an unauthenticated browser reaches an explicit sign-in flow instead of the session.
- **Observed result after fix:** with the `openclawLink` bridge present, `open-new-window`/`open-new-tab` hand the final same-origin session URL to the bridge and never touch `window.open`; the blocked-popup toast no longer fires. A receiving browser already signed in to the gateway renders the intended session from the posted URL; a never-paired receiving browser is stopped at the login gate. Without the bridge (regular browser), the previous reservation + fallback flow is preserved (covered by unit tests).
- **Before evidence:** with `session-menu-navigation.ts` restored to its pre-patch state (same worktree, patched E2E), the E2E fails — `AssertionError: expected undefined to deeply equal { type: 'open-link', …(2) }`, `Test Files 1 failed (1)` — the bridge never receives anything because every attempt goes through the `about:blank` popup reservation, matching the report (so the destination steps are never reached on unpatched code). At unit level the regression tests fail on main with `AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called … Number of calls: 0`.
- **What was not tested:** live macOS app / WKWebView runtime and the native Swift receiver (no macOS hardware in this environment); the native receiver path is unchanged and covered by existing native tests.
- **Proof tier:** L2 (real Gateway, real served Control UI, real browser; the WKWebView host bridge surface is installed at page level as the shell does, not mocked at module level; the handoff destination is verified in isolated browser contexts — one paired through the real sign-in surface, one never-paired — rather than a state-sharing same-browser tab).
- **Proof limitations:** no macOS environment available; the WKWebView message-handler transport and the Swift-side `NSWorkspace.open` handoff would need a reporter/maintainer repro on macOS. The bridge contract asserted in the E2E matches the existing native `DashboardWindowController.receiveLinkMessage` validation (main frame, trusted same-origin source, http(s) URL). The posted URL is credential-free by design: it grants session access only in a browser that already signed in to the gateway, and an unpaired browser lands on the login gate (now asserted explicitly). Whether the macOS session actions should instead open an app-owned authenticated destination (a new app window/tab that retains the app's WebKit credentials, as the ClawSweeper review recommends considering) is an open maintainer decision — this PR keeps the external-browser handoff and makes its sign-in requirement explicit and tested rather than building new native windowing unilaterally.
- **Review state:** Follow-up on the ClawSweeper review of `8d40173`: reworked the E2E destination step that previously appended `gatewayUrl` and token parameters before loading the posted URL (which overstated what an unpaired default browser receives) — the destination now signs in explicitly first and loads the posted URL verbatim, and a never-paired negative case asserts the login gate; the destination-access claim in this body is corrected accordingly. Rebased onto latest main (`d626215`). CI lanes pending on the updated head. Note: `checks-ui-e2e-real-gateway` previously failed on `quota-reset-status.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts` ("expected 'Signed in' to be 'Ready'") — a main-level failure unrelated to this PR's files (the same test fails identically on other current PRs, e.g. #146400) and not chased here.

prs.title: fix(telegram): keep progress and final replies after delegation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram can lose its progress card and final reply after an agent delegates work. A later user message can suppress an already accepted result, and retained cards can show an outdated plan. A yielded requester can also incorrectly treat consumed child input as fulfillment of its own final answer.

## User Impact

The conversation keeps one progress card while delegated work runs and the requester processes its results. A requester that yields while it still owes an answer must deliver its own final or a visible failure outcome. Ordinary child completion events can remain quiet, as intended by [#185388](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185388). Plan changes replace outdated steps; finished work disappears and explicit failures remain visible. Meaningful acknowledgments and streaming preferences are preserved.

Use `sessions_yield` with an acknowledgment for a waiting update when a final is still owed. A normal final “started” acknowledgment alone does not register a pending final. Progress remains process-local and is not restored after Gateway restart. Stop/reset and revoked authority prevent follow-up delivery; private child input is not automatically forwarded.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair follows the existing completion and delivery owners:

- Accepted results retain their original caller, conversation and session. A new message retires old automation privileges without discarding a still-authorized result or borrowing the new turn's privileges.
- Progress follows the pending result through waiting and requester processing. Updated plans replace old steps; closed owners retire their rows.
- Telegram confirms initial card delivery before taking it over. The additive `adoptProgressDraftWithReply` contract preserves a normal reply alongside the card; optional `updatePlan` keeps retained cards accurate.
- A yielded requester's final obligation remains until its own visible-final receipt is recorded. Silent/empty settled output uses the existing bounded tool-free finalizer; exhausted recovery uses the existing missing-answer notice. Completed actions are not replayed. Ordinary quiet child processing and Peter's later [visible-unsent fallback coverage (#185840)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185840) are both preserved.

No new queue, job store, polling loop, permission model or generic blocked-notice producer is introduced.

## Evidence

- **Conflict resolution and correlation diagnostics ([8acf8a32bb61](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/8acf8a32bb61893328dec71e4b782192cd065fdf)):** Integrated pinned main `ac0ca14148a7a30ff700e41b9d90b4b33a57f85f` after a confirmed conflict. Only the test-line ceiling required manual resolution; incoming test routing retains the existing PR route. All 81 other previous PR-owned files, including the eight final-answer runtime files, remain byte-identical to `5c990c`. Main measures 6,301,523 test lines; the combined tree measures 6,303,336, comprising the existing +1,770 coverage and 43 lines of bounded diagnostics. The exact ceiling is 6,303,336 with zero slack; no test or assertion was removed, and upstream baseline rationale remains. Native line accounting, Node syntax, formatting, diff and normal commit checks pass. Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable diagnostic issue; the committed file matches the reviewed hash. This integration does not claim a behavioral repair.
- **Process proof and scoped fixture correction:** [The failing isolated Gateway run on 982ca17747df](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40681647119/job/122794819479), synthetic merge ea1e01c1 with main 51420782, proves that the second input was committed with steerTargetRunId 8c468461-f551-45c7-a96d-6accaa970e08 and that the same recovery run wrote the sole matching final. It was adopted steering, not an independently queued turn. Recovery input has internal_system provenance and no second-message ID; an external-user followup retains its own currentMessageId for QA reply correlation. The documented queue contract permits steering active recovery, while followup creates a separate turn. The original fixture commit c28cf4fb7563732287b424c618ce56eaa73a5e48 specifically addressed new sends stuck behind a phantom active run. prs.title: test(ui): guard repeated WebKit picker dismissal
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related: #188810. Restores coverage of native composer-picker dismissal in WebKit; the previous test reloaded after each open and never exercised the reported freeze.

## User Impact

Keeps the existing mobile sheet behavior from #188810 and protects repeated picker closing in WebKit and Chromium. This follow-up changes tests, CI browser provisioning, and comments; the safe CSS is already on main.

## Why This Change Was Made

A single CSS ablation on base `a32d79a2c763` reproduced a native WebKit hang: adding `display:none` to the visibility-hidden `.chat-mobile-host` stalled on the third model close at 560 px. A two-second native sample remained in `Document::resolveStyle`, `Style::TreeResolver::resetStyleForNonRenderedDescendants`, and details slot assignment. Discrete display transitions were not required. Keeping the existing absolute flex box, transform, and visibility exit avoided that combination.

The initial historical-stylesheet overlay also reproduced a stall, but retained the current visibility rule, so it is not evidence that the exact historical source still fails. Removing clipping alone and restoring display-based hiding with visible contents did not reproduce it. No speculative runtime change is added.

The test now reuses its document for 50 Escape and 50 pointer closes per engine at 560 px, split equally between model and effort pickers, plus native close checks at 393, 320, 1100 and 1280 px. It retains the Files-narrows-composer setup and the existing varied press durations. The CSS comment and WebKit lesson record the minimal failing override and the ownership of the safe structure.

The first CI run (`41151623738`, head `14e48ae4ffc8`) exposed missing WebKit provisioning for this suite. The same missing-executable setup failure appears in scheduled main run `41151564335`. The workflow now includes this file in its existing per-shard WebKit requirements set, so selected shards install the browser before running it. Workflow validation and the focused CI-planning test passed.

That first run also failed `reveals draft and sent comments by touch before and after reload` in `chat-selection-to-main.e2e.test.ts`. One focused local replay against the unchanged production base passed (6.289 s test time), and this case passed in the next full CI run. No product fix or inherited-failure claim is made for that first failure.

The second full run (`41152942151`, head `e313355fd2bc`) passed the picker/WebKit shard, but failed `keeps the annotation-only bubble visible while its sent attachment is read`: `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded` retained a detached quote node during canonical message replacement. The test now checks the current quote and bubble geometry directly while the response remains blocked, including an explicit no-Loading assertion. It also handles an early response-wait rejection so a primary assertion failure cannot produce an unrelated teardown rejection. The unchanged-base replay and repaired case both passed locally; independent review confirmed the intended assertion remains covered. This is a test repair, with no runtime change.

The final run (`41154731426`, head `56474463c5b4`) passed the picker, lifecycle, and remaining selected jobs except UI shard 5. Its two failures match completed UI job `124400997116` in scheduled main run `41155320395` exactly:

prs.title: fix(gateway): preserve session state during slow shutdown
prs.body:
Related: #188402, #188496, #188413

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes terminal-session and pending-input persistence being invalidated during Gateway shutdown when accepted finalizers take longer than five seconds.

## User Impact

Deploys keep accepted session finalizers joined before releasing the Gateway lock and state admission. The existing shutdown deadline and hard-exit watchdog remain unchanged; a finalizer that never settles can still reach that deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

The required connection-work join treated its five-second diagnostic grace as permission to return. The run loop then released the Gateway owner lease, whose seal-on-close invalidated shared-state read admission while finalizers were still writing. Keeping the actual required join alive preserves the existing after-resources retirement ordering. Session shutdown also waits for all accepted persistence siblings before reporting a rejection, instead of abandoning them through a separate five-second race.

Marker persistence still precedes cancellation, the snapshot abort remains intact, and no timeout, config, schema, dependency, or run-loop change is included. This is the coordinator-prioritized persistence repair; the production agent-DB reopen caller and wider plugin-work fence remain follow-ups. Exec/spawn-broker cleanup is owned by a separate lane.

## Evidence

- Base `6f7b63cd95f27bd5c03df2b8a048087769708089`, with the final tests and production fix removed: the required-join regression is red under both Node and Bun (1 failed, 3 passed). The isolated SIGTERM process regression is also red under both runtimes: the process still has `exitCode === null` ten seconds after the held finalizer is released.
- Fixed candidate: restart process scenarios pass under Node and the pinned Bun fork, including suspend/reopen, SIGTERM, managed handoff, queued-input replay, and crash/restart. Deliberately delayed SIGTERM exits 0 in 6,728 ms on Node and 6,884 ms on Bun; marker/abort phases are 1,476/1,544 ms.
- Focused close-owner and run-loop process checks: 48 close-owner tests plus 2 run-loop process cases pass under both Node and Bun.
- Targeted production and test typecheck/lint/format pass. All changed-lane ratchets pass; SQLite T1 calls remain 168 and compatibility calls remain 15. Final test-line ratchet: 6,316,453 / 6,348,324. `git diff --check` passes. The initial changed-check run found three missing-brace lint errors in the fixture; they were corrected and the final targeted lint passed.
- Independent local Codex autoreview of the final candidate against the base above, including the lock-release/state-seal callers: scoped-clean at P0/P1, no accepted/actionable findings. Review did not execute the project tests. One earlier Bun attempt timed out in the unchanged SIGUSR2 retained-cleanup fixture at its 60-second limit. Baseline isolated, ordered-file, and original-shard comparisons passed; the unchanged fixed candidate then passed all 50 focused cases in the original shard sequence. The timeout was not reproduced or repaired, and remains an explicit follow-up rather than a claimed fix.

Exact focused commands (each test command uses `--maxWorkers=1`):

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'blocked store: false'
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 -t 'blocked store: true'
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=bun node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# Required-join red/green: execute once with each runtime on base and fixed production.
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-shutdown.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
# Focused green: execute with OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node and bun.
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-close.test.ts src/gateway/server-shutdown.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.plugin-state.test.ts src/cli/gateway-cli/run-loop.direct-stop-active-work.process.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 6f7b63cd95f27bd5c03df2b8a048087769708089
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs root
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.json test/gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts
pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet
git diff --check
```

The existing isolated restart process scenario now includes an active worktree-bound agent RPC run, another active tool run, a subagent, queued input, and a plugin scheduler touching shared cron state. A documented plugin hook holds the accepted finalizer beyond five seconds; the test then releases it, requires exit 0 within the existing ten-second assertion, checks that the worktree lease was released, rejects persistence-loss diagnostics, and verifies restart markers and queued-input replay. No live Gateway or real user state was used.

The production change removes 18 net lines. The process fixture and existing owner tests grow by 115 net lines to exercise the requested combined failure boundary without adding a separate Gateway fixture or new production test seam. No budget or baseline was raised.

<details>
<summary>Reported deployment timeline, 2026-10-31 UTC</summary>

The reported stop of release `797540497ae5` already contained #188402 and #188496:

- 00:12:02.917: SIGTERM after committed handoff; drain/shutdown budgets were 74,924/84,924 ms.
- 00:12:03.373: four restart markers persisted.
- 00:12:08.403–.495: session admission and received-connection cleanup exceeded five seconds.
- 00:12:08.865–.944: exec cleanup reported lost child identity and an unavailable spawn broker; this remains a separate investigation.
- 00:12:09.37–.57: slow state commit, three terminal-session persistence failures, pending-input completion failures, and three attempts per worktree lease release, with `STATE_DATABASE_READ_ADMISSION_INVALIDATED`.
- 00:12:13.096–00:13:29.846: 205 agent database clean-close receipts, roughly 350–400 ms apart. The exact reopening caller is not established by this PR.
- 00:12:17.947–00:12:52.959: audit, usage-cache, dreaming-cron, and Discord work encountered shared-state retirement while still in use.
- 00:13:27.915: shutdown deadline with no pending close steps; 00:13:29.914: watchdog SIGKILL. The next startup succeeded.

</details>

Follow-up source evidence: the concrete reopen-capable owner is optional transcript backfill: `src/gateway/session-row-projection-backfill.ts:57–79` drains queued rows until disposal, without a Gateway-close fence. Each row captures writable execution at `src/gateway/session-row-transcript-backfill.ts:69–76` with a no-op source guard and releases it at line 85; `src/state/openclaw-agent-execution-owner.ts:579–620` closes each native generation after the cleanup signal. Projection disposal belongs to the later request-runtime sidecar (`src/gateway/server-kernel-request-runtime.ts:86–101`), which the original required-join timeout skipped. This proves an unfenced reopen-capable owner, not that the reported production receipts came from this stack or that one row retried indefinitely; a large queue can also produce one receipt per row. `src/agents/worktrees/run-lease.ts:182–210` still retries deliberate admission invalidation. Plugin scheduling is already fenced at `src/gateway/server-lifecycle.ts:529` and joined through `src/plugins/service-scheduler.ts:33–51`; the reported plugin work needs separate ownership tracing.

prs.title: fix: prevent PostgreSQL connection exhaustion in multi-agent Gateways
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An idle multi-agent Gateway using PostgreSQL could exhaust a role's connection limit, breaking history reads, cron maintenance, usage refresh, and memory maintenance.

Fixes #184027

Thanks @etzelm for the report and measurements.

## User Impact

Idle reader retention no longer grows by one PostgreSQL backend per store per worker. A 13-store Gateway completed startup, six idle minutes, and all 130 history reads under `CONNECTION LIMIT 40`, with zero `53300` in both server and Gateway logs. SQLite retention, transaction exclusivity, and worker retirement remain unchanged. No configuration or schema change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Logical reader reuse and physical backend retention had the same lifetime. Each worker can retain [64 store scopes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3b410a688ebf75c59f6d41317e805110acb99a1c/src/config/sessions/session-transcript-worker-scopes.ts#L9-L16), while [seven reader lanes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3b410a688ebf75c59f6d41317e805110acb99a1c/src/config/sessions/session-transcript-worker-resources.ts#L118-L141) own independent pools. Each [retained scope](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3b410a688ebf75c59f6d41317e805110acb99a1c/src/state/openclaw-agent-db-readonly-scope.ts#L129-L142) pinned its [own physical connection](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3b410a688ebf75c59f6d41317e805110acb99a1c/src/infra/postgres-sync/connection.ts#L39-L42), outside the [four-entry returned-connection cache](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3b410a688ebf75c59f6d41317e805110acb99a1c/src/infra/postgres-sync/idle-bridges.ts#L3-L9). The 30-minute SQLite handle TTL was expensive when the handle represented a server backend. A capped control reproduced 209 server `53300` errors and only 42/130 successful history reads; instrumentation attributed the pressure to retained readers, not simultaneous query demand.

The existing scope now retains its admitted logical reader and returns its idle transport after the last borrower. The existing isolate cache retains at most two transports across stores, keyed by DSN and timeout settings. The next query lazily switches `search_path` when needed; prepared statements retain SQL-text identity and PostgreSQL re-analyzes them after a path change. Host-side transaction status allows local return with no checkout/release message. Failed or unknown status uses the existing worker guard. Active transactions stay exclusive; failed user statements are never replayed.

Reconnect-before-query is allowed only on the first request after taking a returned transport. A still-checked-out writer keeps its existing connection-loss behavior. A disconnect that races the next statement reports the existing error rather than replaying that statement.

**Accepted edge case:** Idle checkout no longer sends main's `SELECT 1` validation query. A server-closed socket (restart, `idle_session_timeout`, or termination) is still recovered before the borrower's first statement through the PostgreSQL `error` event and `reconnectIfIdle`. A socket that dies silently within the three-minute idle-cache window instead fails the borrower's first statement; for a writer's `BEGIN`, the caller sees an outcome-unknown error. This rare failure is visible and recoverable, and the cache window is shorter than typical NAT/load-balancer idle timeouts.

The physical budget is approximately the sum across isolates of **checked-out connections + up to two returned transports**. Dedicated writers and maintenance owners count as checked out even when PostgreSQL reports them idle. This bounds retention rather than introducing process-wide admission.

## Evidence

Synthetic state and agent families both used local PostgreSQL 17. Each store held four sessions with twelve messages, populated through normal store APIs. Real `gateway run --allow-unconfigured` processes used isolated state and task ports. A separate observer sampled the role every 500 ms. After ready +30 seconds, +3 minutes, and +6 minutes, the workload issued 130 history reads across all agents plus a usage refresh. Main ran uncapped at role limit 200 for usable latency and peak references; the candidate ran at 40.

| Stores | Main peak / startup peak | Candidate peak / startup peak | Main idle +30s / +3m / +6m | Candidate idle +30s / +3m / +6m |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 19 / 13 | 18 / 12 | 19 / 12 / 9 | 18 / 10 / 8 |
| 4 | 43 / 32 | 18 / 16 | 43 / 22 / 22 | 18 / 15 / 11 |
| 13 | 101 / 70 | 24 / 24 | 96 / 39 / 49 | 21 / 14 / 12 |

Zero candidate server/Gateway `53300`; all 390/390 reads succeeded in the final 1/13-store replays and the preceding 4-store run. Six-minute idle occupancy stayed at or below 12; the final 13-store burst reached 16 and overall peak 24. An earlier uncapped 13-store candidate peaked at 27. The final simplification restored normal background-worker retirement and repeated the 13-store capacity cell and one-store usage measurement.

| Stores | Main warm history p50 / p95 (ms) | Candidate warm p50 / p95 (ms) | Burst fresh connections, main → candidate | Candidate path switches |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 8.48 / 25.64 | 5.53 / 12.94 | 4 → 3 | 0 |
| 4 | 7.51 / 14.92 | 10.32 / 14.31 | 11 → 4 | 270 |
| 13 | 26.99 / 48.47 | 34.47 / 67.32 | 30 → 5 | 309 |

Warm percentiles exclude the first read wave. One- and four-store rows use interleaved runs on base `3b410a688ebf`; the 13-store main reference is from `3140acb54221` with unchanged connection owners, and the candidate is the final capacity-only replay on `3b410a688ebf`. The earlier one/four-store candidate used one-second background retirement; the final candidate restores normal retirement. These healthy-workload measurements precede the fault-only checkout recovery guard; its tests preserve the same healthy message/SQL counts. No healthy per-use checkout/release messages remain; data-query counts match main (1087/1133/1290). Final 13-store physical connect p50/p95 was 3.80/14.84 ms during the burst.

**Latency caveat and accepted tradeoff:** this shared 32-CPU host had materially different load between runs. Four-store load was 18.22 on main versus 36.99 on the candidate; main's own one-store p50 varied from 4.7 to 8.5 ms between iterations. The four-store p50 increase was 37.45% (+2.81 ms), while the candidate beat main at one store. Final 13-store warm p50/p95 was +27.7%/+38.9% with load 34.97 versus the reference's 24.86. These are observations, not established code-causal regressions. The maintainer accepted the latency result; the last replay was explicitly capacity-only. Main needed roughly 100 backends for its 13-store numbers.

Usage refresh (`usage.cost`): main/candidate was 0.885/1.535 s at one store before restoring retirement, and 0.874/0.772 s at four stores. Final one-store refresh was 0.819 s; final 13-store refresh was 1.476 s versus the 0.834 s reference. The final one-store time was 47% lower than the one-second-retirement candidate and within the main reference; host load still differs, so this is not a causal speedup claim. The final one-store replay also completed 130/130 reads with warm p50/p95 6.39/9.33 ms, three fresh burst connections, and no checkout/release messages.

<details>
<summary>Rejected alternatives and validation</summary>

- Immediate logical-reader release met capacity but lost admission/schema reuse and caused 13-store history p50/p95 of **6.57/12.51 seconds**.
- Short logical-scope TTLs and fallback-only release still hit the 40-connection startup cap (33 server errors in the final TTL experiment).
- Separating logical/physical ownership while keeping schema-bound transports met capacity, but caused **312 fresh burst connections versus 30**, and warm p50/p95 **144.23/232.65 ms versus 55.99/149.31 ms**.
- Schema-switching reuse cut the 13-store burst to five fresh connections. Removing the remaining per-use checkout/release messages then removed **359/358** bridge messages at 13 stores. The one-second retirement override was also removed after the final capacity check passed.

Regressions cover bounded physical backends while retaining logical scopes, no repeated admission, active borrower protection, fake-clock expiry, zero per-use control messages, unknown-status fallback after query failure, A→B→A rows/prepared statements/recovery namespace, terminated-idle recovery, and transaction exclusion. The bounded-backends regression failed on main; the no-message regression failed on the prior implementation.

Validation: the initial 137 focused unit tests passed (99.03 s wall). After the checkout recovery guard, 56 focused unit tests passed (82.01 s), and all 39 tests in the state-owner, agent-owner, reuse, and hydration PostgreSQL suites passed (198.29 s test runner). The unchanged state-owner loss cases caught an over-broad reconnect in the first CI run and now pass alongside cached recovery. Core and affected test typechecks, typed lint (193.53 s), format, local test-line and diff checks pass. The clean uninstrumented `qaRuntime` build passed in 213.93 s. The complete change passed a full-context isolated Codex review at P0–P2.

```sh
pnpm test src/state/openclaw-agent-db-readonly-scope.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-transcript-read-pools.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-transcript-worker-lanes.test.ts src/infra/postgres-sync/connection.test.ts src/infra/postgres-sync/bridge-prestart.test.ts src/infra/postgres-sync/protocol.test.ts src/infra/sql-connection.test.ts src/infra/sqlite-database-admission.retention.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-entry-publication-source.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection <isolated-dsn> -- src/state/openclaw-state-db.postgres.test.ts src/state/openclaw-agent-db.postgres.test.ts src/infra/postgres-sync/reuse.postgres.test.ts src/infra/postgres-sync/transcript-hydration.postgres.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:core
```

Test cost: `pnpm test src/infra/postgres-sync/connection.test.ts src/infra/postgres-sync/bridge-prestart.test.ts src/infra/postgres-sync/protocol.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 82.01 s wall on the same host. The change adds 234 net test lines. Simplification removed the extra retirement policy and timer-dependent test branches; the existing scope, transport, and cache owners carry the fix. Independent isolated Codex review: scoped-clean at P0–P2; no actionable findings.

</details>

## Exact-head CI

All three [PostgreSQL conformance shards](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41113824405), the UI E2E shards, and baseline ratchets passed on `6c199c986851715c6437325a7529353375ada918`. The effective `openclaw/ci-gate` is green.

The first `build-artifacts` attempt timed out after 120 seconds while generating bundled root help in `write-cli-startup-metadata`. The same head's isolated bundled root-help render passed in 3.81 seconds, and scheduled main passed the corresponding build step. One maintainer-authorized failed-job rerun passed the full artifact job and CI gate with no source change or timeout increase, consistent with the diagnosed runner-load flake.

prs.title: chore(test): avoid oversized stat-only fixture buffers
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two size-limit tests allocate and write more than 17 MiB of payload even though their readers reject oversized files before reading content.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. Tests retain oversized registry and snapshot rejection while avoiding unnecessary payload buffers.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use filesystem truncation at the existing fixture owner. Require the registry's exact size-limit classification so malformed sparse content cannot accidentally satisfy the test; retain the snapshot's exact byte-cap error.

## Evidence

- Actual Node26 probe with the pinned fs-safe0.26.14 reader: registry16777217 bytes and manifest1048577 bytes both rejected as too-large with zero content reads. Registry symlink resolution, inode/mode preservation and temporary fixture removal passed.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

iOS screenshot runners can spend substantial time waiting for CPU headroom between fresh simulators.

## User Impact

Reduces the measured simulator preparation cycle on disposable hosted runners. Normal CI capture, screenshot-only runs, and Store/TestFlight release capture use the same host Spotlight setting already used by release qualification. Local commands leave host indexing unchanged.

The optional `startup_probe` diagnostic keeps indexing enabled because its Spotlight experiment needs indexed positive controls. Existing runner sizes, deadlines, checks, screenshot inventory, and release admission remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Disable host indexing before checkout rather than changing simulator behavior, adding caches, or relaxing headroom checks. The production change is three existing-command workflow steps; temporary accounting scripts and benchmark inputs are excluded.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule agreed before the experiment: five interleaved fresh-runner baseline/disabled samples at one fixed source revision and runner class; lower median and tail total-cycle time with all existing checks passing, followed by a successful full screenshot capture. The total includes the final headroom wait after iPad cleanup.

All 10 samples passed all 25 commands, exclusivity assertions, cleanup, and final headroom. Each used `17d465f42d01b6075247d34feae64045c7b4ff5d`, `xcode-27-xlarge` with 5 available CPUs, image `xcode-27-arm64` version `20261026.0314.1`, macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), and Xcode 27.1 (27A9275). Both release jobs were skipped. Resource timelines and stack sampling were disabled.

| Total simulator cycle | Baseline | Host indexing disabled |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median | 336.5s | 226.5s |
| Observed p95 (linear interpolation, n=5) | 376.9s | 239.1s |
| Minimum | 196.4s | 195.8s |
| Maximum | 380.1s | 240.4s |

Median improved 32.7%; the slowest observed cycle improved 36.7%. Five samples per condition do not establish a reliable long-term tail estimate. Ranges overlap. This measures the stock simulator cycle, not whole screenshot-pipeline runtime, and does not identify the precise external service responsible.

Most savings came from waiting for headroom: median combined headroom waits fell from 132.0s to 36.0s. Active command totals slightly regressed (180.2s to 186.9s median). In particular, the first iPhone inventory median rose from 25.6s to 29.6s, and the later iPhone status-bar median rose from 1.1s to 3.8s. The complete table below retains these regressions; the accepted primary metric is the complete cycle with safety checks preserved.

prs.title: fix(plugins): keep Matrix and Copilot libc detection from blocking the Linux Gateway on slow DNS
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/188930

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: on Linux, the whole Gateway stops for seconds when the Matrix plugin prepares its crypto runtime for the first E2EE attachment, or when the Copilot harness captures or validates its runtime artifact, on a host whose DNS is slow or unreachable.

## User Impact

User impact: Matrix E2EE media and Copilot runtime artifact capture and validation no longer stall every other channel, the Control UI and RPC calls on Linux hosts with a slow resolver.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both plugins told glibc from musl with `process.report.getReport()`. Node builds that report synchronously and, unless `process.report.excludeNetwork` is set, reverse-resolves the peer of every open socket, so each socket can cost a full resolver timeout on the Gateway's main thread. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188521 replaced the same detection in the CUA plugin with a read of the loaded libc from `/proc/self/maps`.

- Matrix (`isMuslRuntime`) and Copilot (`runtimePlatform`) now read `/proc/self/maps`, as in the CUA fix, keeping each plugin's existing result shape.
- Matrix also loads `@matrix-org/matrix-sdk-crypto-nodejs`, whose native loader builds the same report once to pick its binding. `ensureMatrixCryptoRuntime` now sets `process.report.excludeNetwork` only for that synchronous `require` and restores the previous value afterwards (skipped when the runtime has no `process.report`). It is the package's first load in the process: the crypto bindings module is imported only after `ensureMatrixCryptoRuntime`, and `matrix-js-sdk` does not load the package.
- Matrix keeps its existing fallback: if `/proc/self/maps` cannot be read, it assumes musl, as it did when the report failed.
- Copilot has no fallback: if `/proc/self/maps` cannot be read (a heavily restricted procfs), the runtime artifact capture fails with the read error (validation reports the runtime as changed) instead of guessing a platform package. A Linux host without a readable `/proc` is rare and the failure is visible, so this is an accepted edge case.
- The obsolete assertion allowance for `deps.ts` is removed (2 to 1), as the assertion-safety ratchet asks.

## Evidence

Tested at `fb4e388d729d` (base `upstream/main` `cf83a69f74ee`).

The real QA Matrix lane on Ubuntu 22.04 with Node 24.22.1: a disposable local homeserver, a real Gateway child process, synthetic accounts and the mock model provider. Inside a private mount namespace only, `/etc/resolv.conf` points at an unreachable server (`nameserver 10.255.255.1`, `options timeout:1 attempts:1`). A preload wraps `process.report.getReport()` and logs each call's duration and caller. Same command on both sides:

```text
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm openclaw qa matrix --provider-mode mock-openai --scenario matrix-e2ee-media-image
```

Before (base `cf83a69f74ee`):

```text
gateway.stderr.log:
09:50:45.485 [spy] getReport took 27.4ms     at isMuslFromReport (@openclaw/fs-safe/dist/native.js:78:39)
09:51:22.571 [spy] getReport took 24.8ms     at isMuslFromReport (@openclaw/fs-safe/dist/native.js:78:39)
09:53:51.916 [spy] getReport took 4166.2ms   at isMuslRuntime (dist/extensions/matrix/.setup/deps-D-W_QQjz.mjs:38:39)
09:53:56.087 [spy] getReport took 4167.1ms   at isMusl (@matrix-org/matrix-sdk-crypto-nodejs/index.js:26:52)
09:53:56.105 [event-loop] main-thread stall: elapsedMs=6104 task=unattributed stallStartMs=1793408030001 stallEndMs=1793408036105
qa-suite-report.md:
- Passed: 0
- Failed: 1
- Details: QA scenario flow timed out after 180000ms
```

After (this PR):

```text
gateway.stderr.log:
09:59:39.388 [spy] getReport took 31.5ms     at isMuslFromReport (@openclaw/fs-safe/dist/native.js:78:39)
10:00:16.317 [spy] getReport took 24.4ms     at isMuslFromReport (@openclaw/fs-safe/dist/native.js:78:39)
10:00:58.796 [spy] getReport took 118.7ms    at isMusl (@matrix-org/matrix-sdk-crypto-nodejs/index.js:26:52)
10:01:34.246 [spy] getReport took 25.0ms     at isMuslFromReport (@openclaw/fs-safe/dist/native.js:78:39)
no "[event-loop] main-thread stall" line
qa-suite-report.md:
- Passed: 1
- Failed: 0
```

Observed result: on the base, preparing the Matrix crypto runtime for the first encrypted image builds the report twice in the Gateway, once in OpenClaw (4,166.2 ms) and once in the dependency's loader (4,167.1 ms), and the stall monitor logs a 6.1 s stall (it records a lower bound). The scenario times out because the QA driver, which loads the same plugin code and holds more sockets, blocks in the same two calls for 51,255.6 ms and 51,259.3 ms. On this branch OpenClaw's own call is gone, and the dependency's call runs without the network section (118.7 ms in the Gateway, 4.7 ms in the driver). The Gateway logs no stall and the scenario passes. The stall was observed with the Gateway on Node (`OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`); an earlier base run on the default Bun test runtime passed without it.

Timed directly, `ensureMatrixCryptoRuntime` from the built plugin, in a Node process holding 3 loopback sockets with the unreachable resolver: base 26,145.1 ms (two report calls, 13,068.7 ms and 13,067.5 ms), this branch 3.3 ms (one call, 1.3 ms).

Regression tests: the Copilot test "preserves native links across equivalent captures and invalidates changed bytes" asserts that no report is built; both Matrix "bootstraps a missing/truncated runtime once" tests assert that the crypto package is loaded with `excludeNetwork` set, that it is restored afterwards, and that OpenClaw builds no report. They fail on the base and pass on this branch; the other 6 tests in the two files pass on both.

Checks: the touched tests (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, wall time per file in the table below), `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxlint and format on the changed files, `pnpm check:assertion-safety`, and the test-lines ratchet (net delta 0; the tree at the base is already 1,033 lines over its ceiling: 6,313,571 lines, ceiling 6,312,538). The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

| Test file                                         | `--maxWorkers=1` wall |
| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `extensions/copilot/src/runtime-artifact.test.ts` | 30.2 s                |
| `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/deps.test.ts`       | 6.5 s                 |

Not covered:

- Copilot is proven by its unit test only (an end-to-end Copilot run needs a GitHub account).
- musl detection was checked by running the same pattern against `/proc/self/maps` in a `node:24-alpine` container, not through the Gateway.
- Core `src/infra/npm-managed-root.ts` still builds the report, during plugin install and uninstall only.
- `extensions/llama-cpp` still builds the report during server install; it needs the glibc version, which the map does not give.
- Copilot's SDK still builds the report itself when it starts its bundled runtime (plain Copilot runs and isolated completions); that needs a separate change.
- `@openclaw/fs-safe`, an external package, builds the report when it loads its native binding, starting at Gateway startup: about 25 ms per call in the Gateway above, about 39 s in the QA driver process, the same on both sides.

prs.title: fix: avoid oversized downloads during cold PR preparation
prs.body:
Closes #188764.

## What Problem This Solves

Cold preparation of an existing pull request downloads unrelated historical file versions before the workspace can use the PR's current files. On a large repository, this transfer can exhaust the fetch command's budget. A fork's separately fetched base can cause the same waste when it advances after the selected project snapshot.

## User Impact

Preparing a PR in an empty workspace or an existing project retains its history and required current files while avoiding unused historical blobs. Ancestry-dependent review, integration and publication continue to work. Command deadlines, retries, credentials and workspace authority are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing transport separates commit availability from current-file hydration. Every absent-commit fetch now requests blobless history, retaining commits and tree metadata for ancestry and workflow checks. Callers that need files continue through the existing explicit missing-object hydration. Keeping this selection in the shared owner also covers ancestry-only preparation callers without adding a new mode or downloading their unused tip contents.

The registered-action regression covers empty and selected-project sources with distinct fork/base URLs and an advanced base. It verifies that obsolete PR and base blobs stay absent while the required contents and history remain complete. The existing publication-history fixture now preserves the actual fetch arguments, and its normal publication case performs a native push from a cold metadata-only base with lazy fetching disabled. The 100 added test lines have an exact dedicated allocation; the shared baseline is unchanged.

## Evidence

The unchanged production baseline reproduced the cold fetch timeout at 60.034 seconds with no completed pack. The original registered-action regression failed because an obsolete PR blob was downloaded. A separate registered-action probe exposed the same problem in the cold fork-base path before the completed correction.

The final tree passed changed-file formatting and lint, all selected production/test/consumer type checks, and 268 tests across 17 files. One existing opt-in real Podman test was skipped. The cases include non-shallow ancestry, exact current-tree completeness, distinct fork/base histories, populated reuse without fetching, merge-base hydration, retry/cancellation, and native publication without implicitly fetching the target base's file contents. The affected-test runs took 472.8 seconds in total across six native test invocations, including their existing setup and transformation work; this is not the added cases' isolated cost.

Retained large-repository owner proof completed the identical contents-hydration path in 19.502 seconds for history and 39.591 seconds for current blobs: 122,203 reachable commits, no shallow boundary, and zero missing current objects. Populated reuse took 47 ms without a fetch. These are scoped reproductions, not a general latency benchmark. The final correction preserves that path's arguments and hydration behavior; the metadata-only callers have the separate final-tree proof above.

A real Gateway running the qualified combined source `0d70033ab4b8994471689cafeff9fe7a3c7b8879`, including this exact PR head `3fc5b0d02425dcbdf8271bad55434e189c17bb56`, also completed natural PR preparation in an existing guest conversation. A current maintainer prepared a foreign-authored fixture from the native empty source; the normal model/tool action returned `status: prepared` and `headChanged: false`. The guest's creator, sandbox requirement, original PR head and branch were preserved, and GitHub was unchanged.

A read-only observer identified the actual receiver before the fetch and tracked the same physical Git common directory through completion, with lazy fetching disabled and no alternates. Before fetching, the requested head, base and all five controlled file versions were absent. When the head and base first arrived, all five blobs were still absent. After preparation, all 12 ancestry commits and all 10 current-tree blobs were present; the current file version was hydrated, while all four obsolete versions remained absent. No objects were deleted and no delay or synthetic caller was introduced. This is direct cold-path evidence, separate from the large-repository timing above.

The live recording has a gap during the asynchronous handoff; a continuation captures the settled result, and no request was replayed. The native completion and physical object observations establish the transfer behavior. No visual latency comparison is claimed for this small fixture.

The independent recheck and current-head automated re-review are clean, and [exact-head hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41144698804) passed. On receiving main `ef2feab6ddae`, the original registered-action regression still failed specifically at obsolete-blob absence, with the other 22 tests passing. The exact proposed merge then passed 64 tests across preparation, native publication and refresh/hydration suites using that target's locked dependencies. The earlier large-repository timings remain scoped to their original execution environment.

prs.title: docs(plugins): fix unsupported exec policy guide reference
prs.body:
Related: #188833

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes SDK package contract checks failing because the tool-policy guide added in #188833 references a runtime without public TypeScript declarations.

## User Impact

Plugin authors are directed to the supported typed exec-policy resolver, with the global and per-agent policy inheritance guidance preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reference `execPolicy.resolveExecModePolicy` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime` and clarify that policy layering precedes resolution. The package export contract and typed-public-entrypoint guardrail remain unchanged.

## Evidence

- The existing typed-export guardrail fails before the edit with the exact main-CI error; all 18 tests in `plugin-sdk-package-contract-guardrails.test.ts` pass afterward under Node 24.22.1 orchestration and the repository-pinned Bun fork. Focused red/green wall times: 81.21 s including cold compilation, then 29.12 s.
- Target-page Markdown lint, MDX validation, oxfmt/Bun formatting parity, SDK export synchronization, line-cap ratchet, and diff checks pass. Canonical lane classification is docs-only; no runtime, export, test, ignore, or baseline changes.
- Fresh independent P0–P2 autoreview: scoped-clean, no findings. The one-file patch is unchanged from the accepted local review.

Requested by @steipete

## Work sessions

[Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/b5679712-7777-4ff7-a05a-81c1efab2069)

prs.title: feat(gateway): advertise chat input custody contract
prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:
fix(auth): login redirect loops when session cookie is expired

Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.
For fixes, describe the user-visible symptom and trigger:
fix: task list fails to load when user has no environments
Avoid implementation details such as:
fix: add null check to task query

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.
-->

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Independently versioned chat clients cannot discover the existing queue-mode and exact input-receipt contract without guessing from a protocol version or an unrelated capability.

**This is an additive compatibility-contract feature, not a fix for a demonstrated data-loss or model-steering bug.** The regression below proves missing discovery before the change and correct advertisement afterward; it does not prove that the marker itself repairs queue execution.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

Clients can check `hello-ok.features.capabilities` for `chat-input-custody-v1` before offering the existing `chat.send.queueMode` and `chat.history.inputRunIds` / `inputReceipts` contract. If absent, support is unknown and the client retains its existing send behavior.

The marker is **not permission, active-backend injection availability, acknowledgment-as-consumption, or permanent exactly-once delivery**. Requested scopes are not increased. No new RPC, protocol version, queue policy, backend, migration, bundled UI or consumer implementation is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

The existing server capability registry and hello owner are the discovery boundary. One constant and one hello-array entry expose the transport contract; the owner regression also checks unchanged read-only scopes. The handshake documentation explains pending versus consumed receipts, bounded idempotency, and retention of uncertain input.

At upstream main [`6c672d42f2dec42b7917f34dfe5ae8157b9b0abb`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6c672d42f2dec42b7917f34dfe5ae8157b9b0abb) (2026-10-29), both the capability registry and hello response still omit this marker. The existing `chat-send-routing-contract` is not this input-custody discovery contract. No current-main code was substituted for the tested historical base.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. For user-visible UI changes, follow the root
AGENTS.md "Product and validation" screenshot completion/landing gate; these other
forms of evidence do not replace the required screenshots in chat AND the PR.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

### Exact source and before/after regression

**Draft for review, not merge-approved.** Head remains `9c51b90ab5677c9fbae03a8a403d66d4df581c5b`, tree `4558ea5743235ed344de40d93145675eeb107fcd`; parent/tested production base is `776c8da8f06c6ed244b8ce22ea33165e4463f23b`. No code changed or runtime was restarted for this description refresh.

The **same** `advertises input custody without changing negotiated scopes` regression and command were used on both sides. Test-file SHA256 was `0FC3C374ABE9B8DE48513DE1492330E1E36A7A5FBAF0E822161542C281C5ACFC` in both runs and matches the committed head.

```powershell
node scripts\run-vitest.mjs run src\gateway\server\ws-connection\connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --testNamePattern "advertises input custody without changing negotiated scopes" --reporter=default --reporter="$HOOK_REPORTER"
```

`$HOOK_REPORTER` represents the same passive hook-timestamp reporter's private filesystem path, omitted from this public description; it changes no assertions.

| Source under test | Observed result |
|---|---|
| Base `776c8da8` production plus only the identical new test | **Expected RED:** exit 1, 1 failed / 47 skipped. The assertion at test line 205 reports capabilities missing `chat-input-custody-v1`; not a setup failure. |
| Base plus the exact four-file bytes later committed as `9c51b90a` | **GREEN:** exit 0, 1 passed / 47 skipped. Capability is present and `auth.scopes` remains `["operator.read"]`. This run preceded the commit; the recorded file hashes match the committed bytes. |

### Supporting validation at the fixed revision

| Recorded command / boundary | Result and limit |
|---|---|
| `node scripts\run-vitest.mjs run src\gateway\server\ws-connection\connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts packages\gateway-protocol\src\schema\logs-chat.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | **PASS:** 48 hello-owner + 7 schema tests. |
| `node scripts\run-tsgo.mjs -p test\tsconfig\tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json --noEmit --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile "$TASK_CACHE\marker-types.tsbuildinfo"` | **PASS:** owning Gateway-server test types; task cache path redacted. |
| `node scripts\run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.json packages\gateway-protocol\src\server-capabilities.ts src\gateway\server\ws-connection\connect-hello.ts src\gateway\server\ws-connection\connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts` | **PASS:** zero lint warnings/errors. |
| `pnpm exec oxfmt --check packages\gateway-protocol\src\server-capabilities.ts src\gateway\server\ws-connection\connect-hello.ts src\gateway\server\ws-connection\connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts docs\gateway\protocol\handshake.md` | **PASS.** |
| `pnpm run build ciArtifacts` | **PASS:** recorded Windows frozen-source build and subsequent Linux exact-head build. |
| Real built Gateway at exact `9c51b90a`, unsigned token-authenticated `test/backend` client (2026-10-26) | **PASS:** marker advertised, effective scopes empty, protected `users.self` rejected with `FORBIDDEN` / `MISSING_SCOPE`. This tests advertisement and the unchanged authorization boundary only. |
| Separate fresh live-05 at exact `9c51b90a` (2026-10-29) | **Bounded PASS, independently reviewed:** four immutable attachment-only `chat.send` cases passed hello/self/model, ack/matching final/history/provider and stored-byte length/SHA256 checks after verified quiescence. Input sizes: 3, 131, 2 and 68 bytes. This is supplementary actual behavior, not proof of backend steering or the marker's causal effect on storage. |

Live-05 used only task-owned resources and a synthetic loopback provider, with the original native request bytes preserved except five routing identities. All owned processes are gone and its one-use permission is revoked. Public-safe frozen proof digests: terminal `56C4FE039ECEDDA8597F2BFD7E742865DDB9E24053DCDE193AF5C009AD6ADA9E`, aggregate `4649B8E9BF754CCD19423ADB4ADBC0FF4374EDE232D3EC460F803C38D20786B6`, independent postcheck `A98115F9A1A1A881655B3D6622E4639D69EAAA5C45AA29B4830142EEC16E8D56`. No private logs, credentials or machine dumps are attached.

**Remaining limits and merge blockers:** no current-main integration/rebase execution, Windows UI/adopting-consumer proof, or live backend injection/exactly-once guarantee is claimed. Earlier deferred-custody attempts timed out or failed setup and remain failures; live-01 through live-04 remain BLOCKED, not retroactively upgraded. Live-05 does not replace those deferred-custody tests. The observed legacy `openclaw/security-sensitive-review` and aggregate status still require a maintainer's exact-head approval; normal CI successes do not replace that approval. A maintainer must also accept this stable transport-discovery contract. No merge, release or CI rerun is requested here.

<details>
<summary>Actual real-Gateway terminal output — exact PR head</summary>

The probe started the built production CLI with fresh isolated state and a task-generated token, waited for readiness, and made real WebSocket requests. prs.title: perf(gateway): reuse the primed Control UI file reader
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Rejected performance experiment; closing without merge.** A cold Control UI document primes one file-reader worker; the first parallel asset burst starts a second worker. This candidate used a singleton to avoid that second startup. The measured serialization cost exceeds the stated acceptance rule, so the two-worker production behavior remains.

## Evidence

The corrected production-faithful harness passed all four setup processes and all 60 measured processes, with ten counterbalanced base/control/head triplets per root kind. Three within-process repeats were collapsed; they were not treated as 30 independent observations. Both source/input after-censuses matched their original seals, and final aggregation is complete with no validation errors. The Node runtime was 26.12.1 on the same Mac, with host load recorded (median approximately 18).

The first identity burst's maximum file-worker run fell from 84.50 to 3.69 ms for bundled roots and 81.29 to 3.63 ms for mutable roots. But serialization slowed the already-warm gzip burst and mutable rereads. In particular, bundled gzip uncached median grew 37.81%, from 6.379 to 8.791 ms; the paired unchanged A/A median moved only +2.70%. Mutable gzip repeats grew 20.91%. These cross the 20% stop rule. The cold full HTTP timing also includes first-handler initialization and is not pure worker time.

| Root / encoding / temperature | Base HTTP median / p95 ms | Singleton median / p95 ms | Head change median / p95 | A/A change median / p95 | Process CPU median ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| bundled / identity / cold-assets | 402.308 / 615.511 | 445.638 / 515.624 | +10.77% / -16.23% | -18.35% / -9.49% | 537.487 → 465.892 |
| bundled / identity / repeat | 5.237 / 8.360 | 5.439 / 6.125 | +3.85% / -26.74% | -2.01% / -29.64% | 8.226 → 8.257 |
| bundled / gzip / cold-assets | 6.379 / 9.921 | 8.791 / 9.914 | +37.81% / -0.06% | +2.70% / -24.07% | 16.824 → 15.697 |
| bundled / gzip / repeat | 3.369 / 4.661 | 3.753 / 4.419 | +11.41% / -5.18% | +4.96% / -0.61% | 4.256 → 4.495 |
| resolved / identity / cold-assets | 420.446 / 652.551 | 409.731 / 530.097 | -2.55% / -18.77% | -21.17% / +13.11% | 571.678 → 429.594 |
| resolved / identity / repeat | 6.136 / 11.322 | 6.861 / 8.446 | +11.82% / -25.40% | +2.73% / -14.46% | 13.439 → 13.345 |
| resolved / identity / rewritten | 5.824 / 8.686 | 6.293 / 11.787 | +8.05% / +35.70% | +8.97% / +36.27% | 11.200 → 11.541 |
| resolved / gzip / cold-assets | 5.454 / 5.969 | 6.555 / 8.054 | +20.20% / +34.94% | +10.14% / +70.21% | 9.949 → 10.191 |
| resolved / gzip / repeat | 5.245 / 6.921 | 6.342 / 7.499 | +20.91% / +8.35% | +8.59% / +46.65% | 9.963 → 10.607 |
| resolved / gzip / rewritten | 5.898 / 8.967 | 6.731 / 9.041 | +14.14% / +0.83% | +5.30% / +31.79% | 9.878 → 11.113 |

Browser readiness was deliberately not run after this throughput rejection. There is no JavaScript byte saving, no readiness improvement claim, and no merge request. The full ten-cell data, all raw process reports, failed old setup, and before/after seals are retained as external campaign proof. Old diagnostics used a shared worker graph; their timing magnitude is explicitly superseded by this canonical standalone-worker cohort.

Acceptance was published before measurement: real HTTP burst of one 1 MiB plus seven 8 KiB assets, identity/gzip, bundled cache repeats and mutable root rewrites; reject real concurrency/CPU regressions and any material >20% regression. Each process has an index-only prime. Gzip generation and response hashing are outside the measured interval. CPU includes all fixture workers. No outlier filtering or A/A subtraction.

| Other proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Existing file owner tests | 15 passed |
| Core and scripts types | Passed |
| Independent source reviews | No actionable P0–P2 findings |
| HTTP body/status/encoding/tasks/worker counts | All 64 setup/measurement processes passed |
| Source/output/package/browser seals | Before/after matched |
| Browser readiness | Not run: throughput rejection |

The proposed production LOC change is +3, existing tests +3, and shared benchmark +150. No new dependency. All of these remain unmerged with the rejected experiment.

<details>
<summary>Boot coverage ranking retained from the paired UI investigation</summary>

The ranking below characterizes the exact immutable UI bundle used for the producer comparison. It is not a claim that the reader change removes JavaScript bytes.

## Exact-head top 30 unused-at-boot bytes — reviewed

Sealed source: head `a8a127228f0529365162e8ade94221c37d8c76d9`; base `a32d79a2c763d3dab52022027fce38c34c7b3dea`. Fresh module review and revalidated function source/caller judgments. Frequency describes source triggers, not population telemetry. Module and exclusive-function partitions overlap and must not be added.

† Corresponding source/entrypoint verified, but generated span bytes differ. Each value is that cohort’s own exclusive partition. This marker does not establish byte-for-byte emitted equivalence. The unmapped row is matched by its verified identical CSS literal and initializer role.

prs.title: fix(test): stream oversized generated-image responses
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The generated-image overflow test builds and serializes a 90 MiB string before exercising the response limit.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. The test retains the default 64 MiB generated-image download ceiling and its existing base64/envelope JSON allowance.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing finite oversized-response stream fixture. The same multipart edit request and exact overflow error remain, with explicit checks for early cancellation and dispatcher release.

## Evidence

- Actual Node 26 probe executed the real fixture and shared byte consumer: overflow at 87 MiB, cancellation observed, consumption stops before the finite 90-chunk limit. A separate uncapped control drains all 90 chunks from one immutable backing buffer.
- Personally traced the provider, image JSON allowance, bounded response reader and byte consumer. Overflow is rejected before contiguous copying, decoding or JSON parsing, so sparse zero contents cannot substitute a parse error for the existing exact size-error assertion.
- Independent full-source review: no actionable P0–P2 findings, confidence 0.96. Targeted pinned formatting and diff/privacy checks passed.
- Full dependency-backed provider tests have not run before publication; this managed source checkout is code-only. Exact-head PR CI is the validation route.
- Runtime production delta: zero. Tests: +10 lines, with a matching justified allocation for cancellation, early-stop and release coverage. Structural allocation reduction only; RSS, time and billed-minute savings remain unmeasured.

prs.title: fix(github-copilot): suggest refreshing unreadable usage data
prs.body:
Supersedes #131281, thanks @sunlit-deng.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Copilot usage report shows an internal JSON-reader diagnostic when GitHub returns malformed usage data with HTTP 200.

## User Impact

Operators see: “Copilot returned unreadable usage data. Try refreshing usage later.” Valid quota reporting and transport/size-limit diagnostics retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Pass recovery wording to the shared parser's existing `malformedResponseError` option, which already handles JSON parse and UTF-8 decode failures. Other usage providers use “Malformed usage response,” which lacks a next step; their shared catch-all helper would also change transport diagnostics.

Production change: +3/-1, net +2 lines. There is no dead or duplicate code in this small owner to remove without unrelated changes. Simplification removes the need for the proposed provider-local catch and error-message matching. No shared SDK changes, new options, or migrations.

## Evidence

- Regression through the registered Copilot usage hook: red on main base `3028168078eb3a43df1c37ffe3bc2dfa38a21ea0`, receiving `github-copilot-usage: malformed JSON response`; green with this change. The latest inspected main `90bbd65a8d3c07567f2d288ea965260d3a422730` has the identical Copilot usage source.
- Focused Copilot and shared HTTP-reader suites: 41 tests passed, including valid quotas, invalid UTF-8, and bounded reads. Final wall time: 18.19 seconds across both shards; Copilot file: 12.26 seconds (cold baseline run: 107.68 seconds including worker preparation). PR CI [run 41155531546](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41155531546) passed in 7m34s; its changed-node job including this regression took 300 seconds (file-only CI cost is not separately attributed).
- A separate synthetic transport fixture with external connections disabled exercised the registered provider through `loadProviderUsageSummary` and `formatUsageReportLines`, producing `Copilot: Copilot returned unreadable usage data. Try refreshing usage later.` This is fixture integration proof, not live Copilot service validation.
- Targeted type checking, lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and test-line ratchet passed. The eight added test lines have a dedicated allocation for this previously uncovered malformed-response guidance regression; the shared baseline is unchanged.
- Local autoreview (Codex, P0–P3) reviewed the complete change snapshot against the base above, subsequently committed as `603b8d3ab71ab038d27e1d73ae7370c25fd90504`: scoped-clean, no findings. Simplification pass completed.
- Reimplemented on main; the contributor's code was read via PR view/diff and was never checked out or executed. Contributor credit: `Co-authored-by: sunlit-deng <yang.jiajun1@xydigit.com>`.

prs.title: feat: allow scoped operators to manage their automations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Operators with write access cannot ask an agent to create and manage their own automations without Gateway administrator authority.

## User Impact

Adds `operator.cron` for authenticated agent-turn automation access, implied by `operator.write`. Users can schedule and manage jobs within the existing conversation/account ownership boundary without receiving `operator.admin`. Cron-only access does not grant chat, general write, or global scheduler administration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing requester grant and job ownership checks instead of treating every scheduler caller as an administrator. One runtime-method mapping covers creation, job management, history, and scratch access. Scheduled runs preserve the initiating operator scopes. Direct/global scheduler APIs, privileged binding, live revocation, and tool restrictions retain their existing checks.

Signed requester transports preserve private scoped-creation provenance without promoting it to local-owner or management authority. No new state owner or storage schema is introduced. The config baseline is regenerated for the accepted scope.

## Evidence

- Rebased onto main `f8fe5864ab3aab29ffeab8b98fef51d3014e5349`; current head is `01d2a7a7edda96784c97de77f5af43040223cfbc`. The only rebase conflict was the generated configuration checksum, regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`. `git range-diff` confirmed the feature and regression patches were unchanged by rebase. `pnpm config:docs:check` and `git diff --check` pass. All 145 focused post-rebase tests pass across scope implication, Gateway auth config, signed creator transports, Cron policy, and persisted scheduled continuation.
- [Rebased-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41152994878) exposed two failures, repaired in the current head: the contained-symlink test now accepts the earlier symlink refusal while still requiring denial; `usage.cost` no longer gives a freshness TTL to a refreshing lower-cache result. Two cost-handler regressions fail before the fix and pass after it for single-agent and all-agent reads, without increasing timeouts. The cost repair reuses the existing cache completeness predicate (production +2 lines; no new owner).
- CI repair validation: all 6 skill-read tests and all 44 cost/cache/consumer tests pass; formatting and diff checks pass. An independent P0–P2 review of all three repair files found no actionable issues. [Current-head CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41154293835) on `01d2a7a7edda96784c97de77f5af43040223cfbc`, including all Android and PostgreSQL lanes, changed Node shards, clean-install type/lint checks, and both required `openclaw/ci-gate` checks. The [real Gateway quarter-backfill regression](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41154293835/job/124398236592) passed in 10.809s on that head. Local full Gateway E2E setup, core typecheck, and lint preparation failed because the shared installation had fs-safe 0.26.13 versus lockfile 0.26.15 (missing native-asset pin/export); the shared installation was not modified. Those local environment failures are retained separately from the passing clean-install CI evidence.
- Red/green regressions for scoped creation and signed requester grants. Both `operator.cron` and `operator.write` pass real token mint/verification, production in-process dispatch, owned-job persistence, foreign-conversation/account refusal, and revocation during validation before persistence. Refused mutations leave storage unchanged; no local-owner or management authority is added.
- Reproduced the five stale CI consumer assertions and updated ingress/rejected-manager expectations without weakening their security checks. All 205 consumer tests and 9 transport tests pass. Scope implication, config, scheduled-scope preservation, grant/token, and prompt-stability suites also pass.
- Before this rebase, core/source-test typechecks, focused lint/format, config checks, line-cap/test-line ratchets, and diff checks passed. Main `f0586d2e3e0d73c` was integrated only for a generated-config conflict; affected checks were rerun. These are prior-head results, not current-head clean-install evidence.
- Pre-rebase local independent P0–P2 reviews of the implementation and the consumer/signed-effect repair found no actionable issues. The unchanged signed-token implementation was unavailable to the implementation reviewer; its changed regression tests and grant owner were reviewed.
