prs.title: fix(mcp): unreachable remote MCP server no longer blocks Doctor-gated Gateway startup
prs.body:
Related: #162228, #144911, #143070

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: standalone Doctor lint rejects an otherwise usable installation when a configured remote HTTP/SSE MCP service is unavailable, including a server that initializes but never answers its tool-catalog request.

## User Impact

Recognized remote connection, authentication and deadline failures become actionable warnings tagged `mcp-service-unavailable`. An error-threshold Doctor gate can proceed while the affected remote tools remain unavailable.

**Scope narrowed in response to review:** local stdio startup failures remain errors, including ambiguous `mcp-remote` proxy failures. Numeric JSON-RPC errors, unknown failures, invalid catalogs, pagination-integrity failures and cleanup failures also remain errors. This is a partial fix, not a resolution of every case in #162228; it no longer asks maintainers to accept broken local children as warnings. No config or stored-data migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing MCP owners now retain a typed availability classification through catalog collection and startup backoff. The pagination owner supplies a typed deadline error; classification uses transport provenance and structured error fields, never server-message text. Doctor preserves the strongest finding when different inspection contexts report the same server, so an earlier warning or deferred-auth notice cannot hide an error.

The repair is reconstructed on newer main at `f91bca9546f5`, reusing the existing catalog-projection owner rather than expanding the oversized runtime module. Current updater probe deferral, OAuth inspection ownership, last-good catalogs and retry behavior are preserved. A local merge check against `1e48ec3a9e3` succeeds; its newer enterprise-MCP capability preparation is not overwritten.

## Evidence

### Actual compiled CLI behavior — October 21

Ten independent ordinary standalone invocations used credential-free synthetic private config/state, real loopback MCP transports and the compiled CLI:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs doctor --lint --json \
  --only core/doctor/runtime-tool-schemas --severity-min warning
# Repeat each scenario with --severity-min error.
```

| Synthetic failure | Finding at warning threshold | Exit: warning threshold | Exit: error threshold |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Refused remote Streamable HTTP connection | warning; `mcp-service-unavailable` | 1 | 0 |
| Initialized remote server delays `tools/list` beyond the real 10-second deadline | warning; `mcp-service-unavailable` | 1 | 0 |
| Remote catalog repeats its pagination cursor | error; no availability code | 1 | 1 |
| Missing local executable | error; no availability code | 1 | 1 |
| Local stdio child exits during initialization | error; no availability code | 1 | 1 |

Every invocation reported `checksRun: 1`. At error threshold, remote-only warnings were filtered out (`findings: []`, exit0). Representative sanitized output projection:

```json
{"scenario":"refused-http","threshold":"warning","code":1,"checksRun":1,"severity":"warning","errorCode":"mcp-service-unavailable"}
{"scenario":"catalog-deadline","threshold":"error","code":0,"checksRun":1,"severity":"below-threshold","errorCode":null}
{"scenario":"closed-stdio","threshold":"error","code":1,"checksRun":1,"severity":"error","errorCode":null}
```

**Build provenance/limit:** this CLI proof ran on [assembled fork commit dda926bb935](https://github.com/Grynn/openclaw/commit/dda926bb93528517d02666179d4478579af6e4a9), which contains this exact repair plus separately reviewed immutable-launcher/runtime fixes and other local units. All 13 files in this PR are byte-identical there to `92b501e7e5af68ad01b829ff005739fe69ed45b1`. Its full `pnpm build` passed with the live-service safeguard enabled. This is real compiled CLI evidence, **not an exact standalone PR-head build, a production deployment or a full installed-release Doctor certification**. No serving credentials, user state or model calls were used. The older blocked CLI attempt remains historical evidence, not a success claim.

### Regression and cost evidence

- Production Doctor detector covers real refused HTTP, typed catalog deadline, remote auth and malformed/integrity controls. Same-server warning/error aggregation has genuine baseline failures and repaired passes. Stdio remains error without requesting a severity-policy exception.
- `pnpm test src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/flows/doctor-core-checks.runtime.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **60/60 pass**, measured wall **51.65s**, peak RSS **5,591,232 KiB** (includes compiler/bootstrap work; not a steady-state latency benchmark).
- After final owner extraction: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-start-backoff.test.ts src/flows/doctor-mcp-availability.test.ts src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-retirement-boundaries.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **32/32 pass**, measured wall **57.73s**, peak RSS **5,532,380 KiB**.
- Focused types, type-aware lint, formatting, scoped line-cap and diff checks pass. Final independent P0–P2 review of the full 13-file repair completed scoped-clean; its former compiled-CLI evidence gap is now addressed with the explicitly scoped proof above. Current-head PR CI remains separate from these local checks.
- Simplification: failure/retirement projection uses the existing catalog owner; the old duplicate retired-catalog literal is removed. Necessary growth is typed failure provenance and strongest-severity aggregation, plus distinct real transport/ordering regressions; no new manager, database schema or runtime policy option.

prs.title: fix(ci): avoid reaction runners for unrelated comments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary links, source paths and unrelated slash commands allocate an Ubuntu runner in Maintainer Command Reactions, then exit without doing work.

## User Impact

Internal CI allocation improves; tracked commands retain the same reactions and live maintainer authorization. Any nonempty custom command override keeps its full matcher, including commands without slashes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use a conservative necessary-condition filter for the default command prefixes before allocating a runner. The existing parser still owns exact command boundaries, multiline whitespace and issue-only autoclose behavior. False-positive prefixes such as `/landscape` remain safe no-ops.

Runtime LOC 0; workflow net +6; tests net +15 with matching allocation; docs net +1. No new config, dependency, permission or fallback.

## Evidence

- Signed head `f0d706a836e9980aa4d19a9195307396402fc2d4`; tree `8b0387a997ccd305d43008f2ae0bda30ce3a52c5`; frozen base `52fbfb7d989207a4f82544f58b5bb9ee75782fe9`.
- Dependency-free Node 26 probe executed the actual workflow condition and literal script across all 17 fixture rows: candidate passes; baseline incorrectly admits the link, path and untracked-command controls. Permission/reaction calls and bot admission assertions pass.
- All six defaults, CRLF multiline indentation, custom overrides, non-maintainer denial, issue autoclose versus PR-only commands and conservative prefix rejection are covered.
- [GitHub expression contract](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/expressions): substring and suffix functions are case-insensitive; the parser remains authoritative.
- Formatting, diff/privacy checks and signed hooks passed. Independent source review found no actionable P0–P2 issue (0.87), with unchanged surrounding-file inspection limited in its sandbox.

prs.title: fix(android): capitalize sentence starts in chat
prs.body:
Related: #139408, #152748 (closed broader Android proposals; this PR isolates sentence capitalization only).

## What Problem This Solves

The Android chat composer does not request automatic sentence capitalization from supporting keyboards. This proposal changes that input default; it is not a claim that the current default violates an established product contract.

## User Impact

Users can start messages and subsequent sentences with automatic capitalization, subject to their keyboard settings. No settings, migration, or changes to existing drafts are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The composer does not request sentence capitalization from Android's input method. This three-line change supplies `KeyboardCapitalization.Sentences` through `KeyboardOptions`, leaving autocorrection and all other keyboard defaults unchanged. It does not rewrite typed text or include the unrelated changes from the closed proposals above.

## Evidence

### Current review and CI — October 31

Published head: `40c67c2df5f03430376ae9098b945e8746b9708c`. GitHub reports the branch mergeable. The [current-head CI gate passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38503473608/job/115659038371). The [completed ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171601#issuecomment-6159892013) identifies no actionable code findings and accepts the recorded typing evidence.

**Area-owner decision requested:** should the Android chat composer request sentence capitalization by default, subject to the keyboard's settings? The review recommends acceptance without rewriting drafts or adding an app setting. Owner acceptance remains outstanding; passing checks and the advisory review do not supply it. No new implementation or device testing is claimed by this refresh.

- Real Android/Gboard reproduction using identical on-screen key positions, with no Shift taps or injected text: the GitHub v2026.10.3 baseline produced `h. h`; the repaired composer produced `H. H`. Android input flags changed from `0x228001` to `0x22c001`, adding only `TYPE_TEXT_FLAG_CAP_SENTENCES` (`0x4000`). Autocorrection was already enabled in both.
- The isolated candidate built from base `4a538d5fb3665c6af278e32026ae8fe4e722de69`, with the exact three-line patch submitted here, also produced `H. H` with actual Gboard taps. Only its test package identity differed. The test was offline; no message was sent, and the synthetic draft was cleared afterward.
- Passed `:app:compileThirdPartyDebugKotlin`, `:app:ktlintCheck`, and `:app:assembleThirdPartyDebug`, including Mermaid asset generation and package identity verification.
- Fresh independent review of the scoped patch reported no P2-or-higher findings. Repository commit hooks passed. No full cross-platform suite or alternate-keyboard coverage is claimed.

AI-assisted implementation and validation; the change is limited to the existing Android chat composer.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android commentary can render inconsistently: explicit commentary is italic, but unphased progress, live output, table headers, and disclosure summaries can remain upright. Users need temporary work/progress text to be distinguishable from the final answer.

## User Impact

- Commentary is italic across prose, headings, lists, bold text, tables, and disclosure summaries/bodies.
- Completed-work commentary uses the existing work-disclosure projection, including unphased messages that collapse after completion.
- Unlabelled live/unfinished assistant output is provisionally italic. Explicit final answers remain regular; settled unphased final answers return to normal formatting.
- Inline and fenced code stay upright. No settings, migration, transcript rewriting, or notification changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry assistant streaming phase through the controller and UI; reuse completed-work row classification rather than infer commentary from prose. Preserve inherited body styling in table headers and disclosure summaries. This intentionally broadens the original explicit-phase-only proposal; the area-owner decision on default styling is still required.

## Evidence

### Current review and CI — October 31

Published head: `341499417811aa6e14d8e095a54c9e8b8d1b4ef0`. GitHub reports the branch mergeable. The [current-head CI gate passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38722062857/job/116385724895). This supersedes the earlier pending-CI status; it is not maintainer approval.

**Area-owner decision requested:** should Android italicize completed-work commentary and all unlabelled unfinished assistant output by default, while keeping final answers and code upright? The review recommends accepting this distinction, but default-styling acceptance remains outstanding. No new code, tests, or device coverage are claimed by this status refresh.

### Streaming-phase follow-up — October 15

The Gateway can send a phased assistant event followed by an unphased chat mirror of the same text. The mirror previously cleared `final_answer`, briefly italicizing the live final answer. The repair retains phase only for identical text owned by the same run; changed text, a new unlabelled assistant item, another run, and terminal cleanup do not inherit stale phase.

The production-entry replay covers that agent→chat sequence. The new regression fails on the original controller with `expected:<commentary> but was:<null>` and passes with the repair.

Also removed an unnecessary optional default that triggered Compose `ModifierParameter` lint, and corrected two completed-work projection tests to expect intentional italic native commentary while preserving all other row data and visibility.

60 focused replay/completed-work tests passed; `:app:ktlintCheck` and `:app:lintPlayDebug` passed in the secretless validation environment. Scoped independent Astra/medium P0–P2 review found no actionable findings in this repair; subsequent test formatting changes were whitespace-only. This is incremental review, not whole-PR approval. Existing screenshot evidence remains applicable; no new APK/device capture.

The previous CI run also failed `WearChatEventFlowTest.appOwnAbortFollowsConfirmedOutcomeRatherThanTheRequest`, outside the changed commentary path. No Wear code was changed. The current-head CI gate is now successful; see the October 31 status above. Maintainer default-styling acceptance remains separate.

### Updated real-device coverage: custom V12.2

The user verified the real Gateway conversation on Pixel 9 Pro XL with custom V12.2 (`2026.10.20-cesura.v12.2-debug`, code `2026101404`). The screenshot shows italic prose, heading/list, bold+italic, table heading/body, disclosure summary/body, and tool-delivered progress, with upright inline/fenced code and regular final-answer control.

The user supplied the screenshot; only cropping removed app chrome/composer. The original volume overlay is retained and obscures part of the right edge.

![Custom V12.2 real-device commentary modes and final-answer control](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pestelence2k/openclaw/796589408cb73fe9d9988d1e615467643fa05b1e/pixel9-commentary-v12.2.png)

### Existing before/after baseline

Same real Gateway conversation on Pixel 6 Pro: GitHub-source v2026.10.3 (`59cb44796b0f1f0daa0e37af8b1495abb45d9bc1`) versus custom V12.1. This earlier capture demonstrates explicit-commentary styling and upright final/code, not the newly expanded V12.2 coverage.

prs.title: fix: cancel queued workspace binding promptly
prs.body:
Fixes #188771.

## What Problem This Solves

Cancelling workspace preparation can leave its final session update queued behind an unrelated writer. The final authority checks prevent a stale binding, but the cancelled update keeps waiting for a writer slot before those checks can run.

## User Impact

A cancelled final binding now withdraws from waiting admission promptly. Writes that have already started still settle before their owner releases custody, and an accepted workspace remains attached after cancellation. Existing ownership reconciliation and rollback remain awaited, so the overall operation can still wait for that recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The workspace preparation wrapper carried the source assertion into the commit callback but dropped its cancellation signal. Final binding now combines that signal with the caller's signal and forwards it through the existing canonical and shared-store admission paths. The native queue already removes cancelled waiters while retaining active work; no race against the complete commit promise is introduced.

The final-bind callers use the same contract, including preparation without a source wrapper. Existing authority checks, persisted session fields, and lease behavior are preserved.

Related draft #188843 also addresses this issue and credits Donnie Fi. This candidate additionally propagates caller cancellation and covers the separate repository-materialization binder and custom-target discovery. That comparison is source-only; the draft's head has not been executed here.

## Evidence

- On baseline 899e74744d88f39ea864d969d9bf204e9c18b9e4, the real final-bind integration case remained queued after cancellation until its unrelated writer was released. Recovery completed without a late binding.
- The changed owner file passes all nine cases, including caller/source cancellation, canonical/shared admission, normal binding, and cancellation after an effect has committed but before it settles. Measured file wall time: 52.69 seconds, including native worker preparation; CI timing is pending.
- Changed-file formatting/lint, all affected production/test compiler groups, and the runtime build passed. Across 407 related test files: 393 passed, 13 were conditionally skipped, and one baseline case failed; 4,930 cases passed.
- The dirty-checkout reset case in `server.sessions.create.workspace-policy.test.ts` reproduces the same `AgentDatabaseRegistryChangedError` on the unmodified baseline. Its reset-preparation path is unchanged and precedes final binding.
- The existing real-Gateway Stop button case passed on the [PR CI merge revision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f95b016cd30781cb6fdd7fb6d832fe6a35c7319c). It observed `chat.abort` returning `aborted: true`, parent and child cancellation, physical command cleanup, and a successful new instruction. The provider was scripted; the browser, Gateway, and exec were real. The changed files and checked Stop/signal owners match the PR head. This proves the input/cancellation hop; the held-writer cases above prove queued admission and settlement.
- [Hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41151549983) completed every selected row, including all three PostgreSQL conformance rows. The skill-resource read shard failed three contained-symlink diagnostic assertions, and the aggregate gate reports that failure. All three errors reproduced on its unmodified target parent, ac897d3b339ee8c91eac5dab2a853d48364eb808, using the same pinned Bun runtime. This PR does not change that read path or its dependencies; the failed statuses remain recorded.
- Auto Review (P0 scope) found no accepted findings against the baseline and candidate tree; commit 4dbf14e1afef7370dc96fbefe95ee201b9e59a17 retains that exact tree. A separate full independent engineering review concluded clean after inspecting the affected owners, callers, settlement paths, and raw execution evidence.

Live guest-session preparation remains pending. An exact queued-cancellation gesture has not been directly exercised in the deployed guest flow; ordinary successful preparation will not be presented as proof of that queue condition.

prs.title: fix(process): keep Gateway work outside agent exec limits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes chat startup and Git RPC timeouts when Linux agent-exec resource isolation also throttles Gateway-owned managed worktree preparation, base refresh, hydration, status and diff.

Related: #188379.

## User Impact

Gateway-owned commands retain the Gateway leaf's resource policy. Agent tool commands and their PTYs continue to use the separate agent-exec cgroup. No configuration or migration is required; restart into the fixed build through the deployment owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

Shared spawn/execa runners previously selected agent-exec for ordinary commands; the service-child anchor inferred placement from worker cleanup ownership. Callers now carry typed execution intent through the existing broker, supervisor, anchor and PTY transports. The default is Gateway-internal, and admitted agent tool paths opt in explicitly. Git and synchronization owners explicitly remain Gateway-internal. No executable-name inference, new cache, resource-budget change, or new state owner.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule: in a private Linux cgroup namespace with delegated CPU/IO/memory controls and agent-exec policy of CPU weight 10, memory.high 1 GiB, 84,095,180 B/s and 20,531 IOPS per direction, zero managed-worktree Git children may enter agent-exec, while admitted agent commands and descendants must enter it. Use a synthetic 62,000-file/1,116,000,000-byte repository; report owner elapsed time, host CPU, sampled allocations, interleaved comparisons and A/A controls separately. These measurements do not claim a whole-Gateway database workload or btrfs performance.

- PTY routing regression fails on the original implementation and passes with explicit intent. Node focused proof: 179 passed, 11 existing platform skips across 10 files (75.77 s wrapper wall). Additional Git, node PTY/workspace, and Gateway terminal suites passed.
The supported-runtime Linux comparison used Node 26.12.1 and five alternating baseline/candidate pairs, with fresh isolated state and the same warm synthetic repository. Baseline: `3ebb7807f489aef6b0e7eada2f7590d1ed9beb81`; candidate: `436cbd786124646e6f672fda51d108080b81ca16` (all 25 production files SHA256 matched the tested source).

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Managed preparation median | 18.839 s | 7.247 s |
| Managed preparation p95/max (n=5) | 22.086 s | 9.237 s |
| Managed preparation range | 13.382–22.086 s | 6.916–9.237 s |
| Checkout median | 16.054 s | 5.612 s |
| Host CPU median, managed creation | 1.255 s | 1.271 s |
| Whole-probe cgroup CPU median | 10.532 s | 10.436 s |
| Managed Git children incorrectly in agent-exec | 125/125 | 0/125 |
| A/A owner times | 21.669 / 23.531 s | 6.781 / 7.398 s |
| Host sampled allocated bytes, two separate passes | 14,249,032 / 14,001,168 | 10,060,976 / 10,555,504 |

Every accepted managed preparation made 25 real Git calls. All candidate agent command/PTY controls and real descendants remained in agent-exec, including the actual agent exec runtime, broker child/execa, native anchor, secret descriptor and extension exec routes. Generic Gateway controls stayed in gateway. Hydration median was 360 → 388 ms; this fix does not remove the unchanged Git census or claim a hydration speedup.

CPU scopes differ deliberately: host CPU excludes Git/workers; whole-probe cgroup CPU includes bootstrap, controls and all descendants. Allocation uses two 32 KiB-interval inspector samples of the host main isolate including collected objects, excluding workers/native Git. Five samples provide a maximum, not a reliable tail estimate. A/A spread was 8.6% baseline and 9.1% candidate, versus a 61.5% median owner-time reduction across revisions.

The Linux fixture uses overlayfs, not btrfs, and does not instantiate a 35 GiB agent database or thousands of sessions: those are outside this process-placement owner. The 1 GiB memory.high setting is below the 1.116 GB fixture content and magnifies reclaim; do not treat these timings as production latency predictions. No production data or live service was used. Earlier Node 26.11.1 exploratory measurements were excluded and replaced by this complete supported-runtime campaign. Two A/A attempts that reused state (16 Git calls) were excluded and replaced with fresh-state 25-call controls.

Reproduction: build the baseline and candidate with the repository runtime build, bundle the committed `scripts/perf/agent-exec-cgroup-proof.ts` with the canonical state-schema inline plugin and source-package dependency ownership, and execute it in an isolated delegated Linux cgroup namespace with `--device <whole-block-device> --repo <synthetic-repo> --samples 1` (`--allocation` for separate allocation passes). The script asserts kernel membership and exercises the real managed-worktree service and agent exec runtime.

- `pnpm check:changed` completed all gates. Initial line-cap, format and proof-script lint findings were repaired; their targeted reruns pass. All other gates passed, including production/test/script types, core lint, dead exports and repository guards. The complete final rerun passed.
- Codex autoreview P0–P2 scoped-clean after final check-driven cleanup, no actionable findings. Final broker/supervisor retest: 64 passed, 3 platform skips (51.04 s including compilation).

Production LOC: +38 (72 added, 34 removed), primarily typed intent plumbing across existing transports. The old worker placement exception is removed. The existing PTY table adds 14 regression lines, with a dedicated allocation record. Kernel placement remains covered by the committed Linux proof script.

Exact-head CI: 103 passed, 63 skipped; CI run [41154526132](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41154526132). No admin exception required.

prs.title: fix(memory-lancedb): reject compromised certificate chains
prs.body:
Related: #179898

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes compromised-certificate acceptance by the memory-lancedb native client when supported root-only verification is combined with an affected CA anchor.

## User Impact

Memory storage connections using affected keys are rejected while legitimate private-CA connections and existing stored memories remain usable in the demonstrated native macOS ARM64 and Linux x64/ARM64 GNU/musl scenarios. Windows qualification and its limitations are recorded separately below.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adopt authentic upstream LanceDB 0.41.0 for the wrapper and all seven advertised native packages, with the generated frozen lockfile. This uses the supplier's released fix without patches, overrides or vendoring.

The approved release-age exception covers only these eight exact 0.41.0 packages. The global `minimumReleaseAge: 10080` and `minimumReleaseAgeStrict: true` remain unchanged. Remove the temporary entries on or after **2026-11-05T09:36:54.156Z**, when all eight packages satisfy normal admission. Future versions are not exempted.

## Evidence

Exact candidate: `b477b1c6126ca93e1e53f805875928ccfb16bf02`; tested base: `77b37aca1f3aee1331e08a9eb796d5c95e1a12f0`. Local source and artifacts were independently reviewed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The patch changes only the plugin manifest, workspace admission exclusions and lockfile.

- **Supply chain:** all eight upstream tarball integrity values, npm signatures and publish/SLSA attestations verified against authenticated signing keys and the exact `v0.41.0` workflow identity. Tampered-payload and wrong-identity controls reject. Upstream source: `3936a8b3bcce8f8e073f3ec6a47e4ca4d3381b92`.
- **Admission:** actual full-workspace admission refuses 0.41.0 before the exception, succeeds afterward, and still refuses it with a wrong-version exclusion. Frozen isolated installation succeeds.
- **Native macOS ARM64 / Node 24.22.1:** actual released-plugin installation (native 0.39) replaced by candidate in the same installation preserves fields, vectors, scopes, timestamps, configuration and history. Separate native 0.40→0.41 comparison passes 22 assertions across four processes. Actual installed CLI, stats child, optimize/reopen and Gateway memory tools pass; old/new data remain usable after restart.
- **Causal TLS comparison:** same runtime, verified live DV-G3B incident chain, hostname, proxy and storage options. In supported `disable_system_certificates=true` root-only mode, native 0.40 accepts TLS and receives the site's HTTP body with either root or compromised-intermediate anchors. Native 0.41 rejects both with `InvalidCertificate(Other(OtherError(CertDistrusted)))`. Legitimate explicit private-CA controls pass on both. Installed candidate CLI reproduces rejection and legitimate recovery.
- **Other trust modes:** installed CLI and native probes reject the incident under default/system and additional-CA modes; legitimate HTTPS S3 passes through nonterminating CONNECT and imported guest OS trust. Actual Gateway store/recall/forget over private-CA HTTPS S3 passes. Default macOS rejection also occurs on 0.40 and is preserved protection, rather than attributed to this update. Exact guest trust/keychain baseline restored.
- **Checks:** seven focused memory suites / 30 tests, extension typecheck, runtime build, canonical host/plugin packaging and package-integrity/import-graph checks, dependency-pin guard, relevant formatting and diff checks pass. `pnpm peers check` fails on both base/candidate with the same pre-existing TypeScript/rolldown and OpenTelemetry/Mistral conflicts; candidate removes the old LanceDB/Arrow mismatch.

<details>
<summary>Artifact and incident identities</summary>

Canonical rebuilt host SHA256: `b24f71d24b4267c0ed8e20adc5c8ce662c9ae4019109ab4740db0e33825cb130`.

Rebuilt plugin SHA256: `fc29e52ffee8a83f7d554e9d58f6f9c2741c028cf0962f9b8b912a59b5ba0380`.

Actual loaded native 0.41.0 macOS ARM64 SHA256: `64575d55807ef1156afb1a92509a0cc3e4ec3bc90067529efab3478c78da4ece`.

Incident intermediate DER SHA256: `42c4accd12c4f59597925e1a08a7a90102608543809308d50ec427e118ba1493`; full DER SPKI SHA256: `ebed6475c2c2d80fcb199f3fe8dd6e6b3ce60b77eb15d4e42c3dec0c6f5b5105`. Fresh independent chain and hostname positive controls accept against historical roots. Endpoint failures, unknown issuer and hostname mismatch are not counted as key rejection.

All eight denied SPKIs are present in all seven authentic native binaries; one live incident key and its alternative anchors were dynamically tested on macOS, Linux and Windows x64/ARM64. Static coverage does not establish execution coverage of every key or OS.

Packages were built before the local commit: the host banner records the tested base. Exact reviewed patch SHA256 `93e28d2dbffdf687ac83c627c862b69597d55b49b1e5999239e60ddf7b4e4029` and candidate tracked tree `7eab30852da86c819b9816db5a6ee8b67c53771a` bind the artifacts to the candidate. Local package version metadata is not a new public release claim.

</details>

## Native platform follow-up

### Linux GNU/musl

Candidate `b477b1c6126ca93e1e53f805875928ccfb16bf02`, base `77b37aca1f3aee1331e08a9eb796d5c95e1a12f0`. Canonical rebuilt host archive SHA256 `b24f71d24b4267c0ed8e20adc5c8ce662c9ae4019109ab4740db0e33825cb130`; candidate plugin archive SHA256 `fc29e52ffee8a83f7d554e9d58f6f9c2741c028cf0962f9b8b912a59b5ba0380`. These are local qualification artifacts, not public releases.

All four native cells passed actual plugin installation, 22 same-store 0.40-to-0.41 data assertions, exact scoped CLI list/query readbacks, stats/optimize and 26 TLS/control scenarios each. GNU ran native Ubuntu 26.04.1 with official Node 24.22.1; musl used native official Node 24.22.1 Alpine containers inside the task guests, image digest `sha256:06d7adf3e0ef61a13f1d28682726366f97a15aa1888c934d3ecec86c33918b53`.

| Native cell | Actual product-loaded 0.41 binary SHA256 | Result |
|---|---|---|
| x64-gnu | `de260e0705b11e193c26b194e59f3a827fd175bae1d4a2ccf5a5e9aff828fd3e` | Passed |
| x64-musl | `ccc54214b5ae577d13f4001401a4e72c505c2b2914643003e9c083ef1a16562b` | Passed |
| arm64-gnu | `1d0c81094cc34790487267b175c51fa826b73b018293efcb25148d5a4979bb0f` | Passed |
| arm64-musl | `d290e3596da5aa95c7b3cb0d1f1f55c0463ceaab2703a73434c35eccd2b699c0` | Passed |

Actual `openclaw` process mappings identified the admitted `.node`, and every hash matched the authenticated supplier native manifest. The installed `ltm` path preserved legitimate private-CA HTTPS and rejected the verified live incident chain with **CertDistrusted** under default, explicit root/intermediate, root-only and imported OS trust modes, including importing the compromised intermediate itself. Legitimate requests succeeded afterward. Guest/container trust DER sets were exactly restored and fixture private keys removed.

The same-runtime baseline 0.40 reached the incident server’s explicit “Your client successfully connected to the site. That's bad!” body; candidate 0.41 rejected **CertDistrusted**. Fresh OpenSSL chain/hostname controls passed; the incident intermediate SPKI SHA256 was `ebed6475c2c2d80fcb199f3fe8dd6e6b3ce60b77eb15d4e42c3dec0c6f5b5105`, DER SHA256 `42c4accd12c4f59597925e1a08a7a90102608543809308d50ec427e118ba1493`. Generic parsing, unknown issuer, endpoint failure or hostname mismatch were never counted as revocation proof.

One initial harness control required OpenSSL `-partial_chain` because its explicit anchor was cross-signed; failed setup evidence was retained, corrected chain/hostname proof passed, and completed install/data work was reused. No attributable product regression or source repair was found. This is focused Linux evidence; older distro ABI, other incident keys, non-Linux platforms, fleet delivery and future public-release provenance are not established by it. Final PR gates remain separate.

### Windows x64

Tested candidate `b477b1c6126ca93e1e53f805875928ccfb16bf02` on native Windows Server 2025 x64 / Node 24.22.1. Actual released memory plugin (native 0.39.0) was installed, seeded and upgraded through the real `plugins install` command in the same installation. Installed candidate CLI list and stats retained scoped released rows/history. A separate 0.40 → 0.41 four-process native data comparison passed 22 assertions, including scoped writes/deletes, historical reads, optimization and reopen.

The actual Gateway completed `memory_store` → recall exact ID → forget → recall count 0 over private-CA HTTPS S3. Windows OS module observation bound that Gateway’s mapped admitted native binary to SHA256 `396993cde8f30011b689185a53698ae1655b186c5339f2418bb544e1117fbca0`, under Node executable SHA256 `d702daa815eabbff763c7d3808e235cf031cf2ca70211b56847bc72f51e240e5`.

Fresh chain/hostname control succeeded for the live G3B incident endpoint; intermediate SPKI SHA256 matched `ebed6475c2c2d80fcb199f3fe8dd6e6b3ce60b77eb15d4e42c3dec0c6f5b5105`.

| Actual boundary | Observed result |
|---|---|
| 0.40 root-only trust, explicit incident root or intermediate | TLS succeeded and returned actual HTTP body: `Your client successfully connected to the site. That's bad!` (then non-S3 response parse failure). |
| 0.41 same root-only trust/endpoint | Nested `InvalidCertificate(Other(OtherError(CertDistrusted)))`. |
| Actual installed 0.41 CLI root-only incident request | Same `CertDistrusted`; actual default incident list/custom-intermediate stats child returned nested `InvalidCertificate(Revoked)`. |
| Legitimate explicit private-CA HTTPS | Native and actual CLI succeeded; ordinary stats recovery succeeded after the incident requests. |
| Legitimate private CA imported into guest machine-root store, no extra bundle | Native and actual installed CLI succeeded; later stats recovery succeeded. After exact removal, `UnknownIssuer` returned. |
| Incident root and intermediate imported separately into guest machine-root store | Actual installed CLI and both native versions rejected this live chain with `Revoked`. |

**Scope:** Windows default/imported-store results are this served chain’s Windows-policy rejection, already present in 0.40. Source inspection shows OS delegation with end-certificate revocation and no second WebPKI denylist pass; these results do not prove unconditional rejection of all eight compromised keys or future leaves. No such universal claim is made. Noninteractive user-root import was unsupported and is recorded separately. Optional Doctor was interrupted after 128 seconds and remains unverified.

Candidate plugin archive SHA256: `fc29e52ffee8a83f7d554e9d58f6f9c2741c028cf0962f9b8b912a59b5ba0380`. Evidence archive SHA256: `e40a0c0b2f47c31d6180807c9779f1d84bd78ae843e7642c1680a7cebcf6f22f` (407,608 bytes). All four guest root/intermediate store inventories exactly restored; task processes/listeners/private keys removed; AWS worker release verified complete. No production artifacts published or PR source changed in this lane.

## CI and review status

The original hosted CI run settled at the candidate head. `build-artifacts` failed while rendering bundled root help at the existing120-second deadline; the required `openclaw/ci-gate` is red as a consequence. Other reported checks passed or were skipped. [Original failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41140788658/job/124354847586). prs.title: fix: bound reloadable chat history
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Long chat sessions retain an expanding transcript while readers page through history. This change bounds reloadable resident history and releases eligible bodies from projections and presentation caches.

The resident targets are **400 entries, 3,145,728 serialized JSON code units and eight source segments**. Actual reader ownership, one indivisible source group, and live/pending/error custody have explicit exceptions; one staged speculative packet is accounted separately. These are residency targets, not a whole-pane RAM guarantee.

Older/newer navigation retains authoritative opaque cursors. One bounded producer batches native packets into an atomic presentation admission, refines an unfit read through the same cursor, and reports a visible capacity pause. Latest restores the durable tail; semantic bookmarks survive pane retirement. Search states its loaded-window scope; export acquires complete history independently.

## Current head and landing status

Published production: `2ab4f7c17003650e0b433ba7c03ea94fcba70dee`, tree `91f562c96edebff7f924d40f21720909dd3240c1`; 100 changed paths against frozen actual base `803d7619edbb1460ab22589278f2d7ba3841a2d0`.

**Draft: the final timing gate failed. Merge is blocked pending explicit owner acceptance of the measured regression.** Production publication succeeded on resume after the earlier receive-pack errors. Exact-head CI and hosted review are pending; no timing acceptance or exception is recorded.

The [metadata](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187708), [creator](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187783), [workspace notice](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187830), [sharing/subagent copy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187943), and [inspector copy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187961) precursors landed separately. Combined fit was measured against the actual integrated base, not inferred by adding their savings.

## Executed proof

- **Strict assets passed:** Chat **1,276,572 gzip B**, unchanged cap **1,276,669 B**: **97 B headroom** (baseline 1,270,335 B). New: 782,115 B (+2,695); startup: 90,624 B (−18). Requests remain 20/15/3. Chat CSS: 126,037 B (+13); New/startup CSS unchanged. Total CSS: 308,438 gzip B (+13), 1,593,974 raw B (+51), 115 requests unchanged. Total JS: 12,581,226 gzip B (+8,592), 37,166,838 raw B (+24,085), one additional asset. Both precompressed checks passed; violations/warnings were empty. Caps and allowances are unchanged.
- Both asset arms used canonical capture, normal UI builds, matching Node 26.12.1, six dependency inputs, eight fixed build settings and the same three proof harnesses. Final source/index, full emitted UI and non-UI outputs were verified/restored exactly.

The startup catch-up row in the memory candidate repair test spends about 30 seconds waiting for the real session quiet period.

prs.title: fix(update): preserve unrelated notices during handoff recovery
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A detached managed update could rewrite an unrelated restart notice sharing its handoff ID, or borrow a failure reason from another installation.

## User Impact

Recovery preserves notices belonging to other runs and installations while the real updater and local lease continue to authorize restoration. No config, schema, protocol or public SDK change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Capture the canonical SQLite inspection and outcome writers before package replacement. Share outcome preparation with the PostgreSQL transport; remove duplicate SQLite policy and the PostgreSQL-only result-source module. Revision, consumed-notice, cancellation and terminal-settlement checks remain. The helper retains the shared launchd parser from [PR #188226](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188226).

Application runtime **−116 lines**; acceptance infrastructure/catalog/Knip/budget record **+644**; tests **+352**. The infrastructure supplies required packaged older-runtime proof. Its disposable service adapter reports observed Gateway identity but does not prove real transient systemd/cgroup custody.

The package fixture now runs published-runtime SDK, ledger and notice operations in separate processes. Loading two releases together reused incompatible process-global worker registries; the isolation regression reproduces that contamination on the old driver. Publication still uses the real canonical writer and precedes forwarding the updater's actual close event. Private child stderr stays piped; diagnostic failure exits promptly with bounded public source locations.

## Evidence

- Signed head `1c521369dd4b39ffd374e9d3c7e13e1e54da34b4`: [CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41155561142) and [Package Acceptance](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41155566709) pending. **Packaged rollback proof remains required.**
- Acceptance reuses the verified [package artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41098970982/artifacts/12997678329): source `f22a2670eaf09742beff52aeaa568705114356d7`, version `2026.10.9`, tarball SHA-256 `a5b09e9fb6620ef2ca3d1a012591a0565837f807388bd7e938f411994a6ed63b`. Application source is byte-identical; later commits touch excluded harness/tests/budget metadata only. The producer was cancelled after artifact publication.
- Both notice-ownership regressions failed on unchanged production: [RED job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41032357909/job/123985369051). Previous [green CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41103646731) passed 600 handoff cases across 34 suites, with 15 skips; all three general PostgreSQL stripes passed. It also covered the service fixture, recovery, activation, diagnostics and package/lane planners.
- Before process isolation, the [packaged failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41108584602/job/124251569904) exited 1 without a timeout and located worker construction before helper startup. The corrected local driver proves runtime isolation and both private-evidence paths in 108–110 ms; a failing child stderr-canary case passed in 88 ms. Independent source review, syntax, formatting, diff/privacy and signed hooks passed. No local dependency-backed suite ran.
- Previous-head [diagnostics CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41108582732/job/124245532604) passed 15 cases in 3262 ms, including the two added cases at 42/41 ms; scripts lint and scripts typecheck passed. Its only underlying CI failure was [test-line budget](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41108582732/job/124245531060): the immutable main base already exceeded its ceiling by 2664 lines, and this PR then added 332. The separate allocation now covers only this PR's final 352 justified regression lines; the shared scalar is unchanged. This preserves inherited debt rather than granting unrelated credit.

The packaged lane separately installs published `openclaw@2026.10.9` and runs a candidate-generated helper against its actual CLI. Required assertions cover exact candidate/restored payloads, settings/workspace/SQLite plugin data, the unrelated notice's full row/revision before consumption, fresh Gateway readiness, terminal rollback, lease release and sensitive-file cleanup. No parameters, lease history or recovery results are fabricated.

Five generated-helper PostgreSQL cases remain skipped; general conformance does not replace them. Follow-up: generated-helper PostgreSQL execution inventory. Prior [package validation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41074634084) passed published10.9 authenticated restart/full payload checks; its separate10.8 secondary UI specimen exceeded the deadline. Follow-up: isolate that specimen's receipt/phase timing. The new lane joins unfiltered Docker-all; explicit release profiles remain unchanged. No live operator update is claimed.

prs.title: fix: main-session automations fail before the model call when the main session is used from a DM
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/180602

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a `--session main` automation with no delivery config fails every run with `plugin delivery capability is no longer active`, before the model is called, when the main session is used from a channel DM with the default `session.dmScope`.

## User Impact

User impact: scheduled check-ins that continue the main conversation run again for people who talk to their agent in a DM. Before this change, every run failed silently, and each failed run was carried into later turns as interrupted input.

## Why This Change Was Made

Scheduled session turns minted their message-action turn capability under the execution session key (`agent:main:main`). Plugin tool delivery and the message tool look the capability up under the run's runtime policy key, which is peer-scoped for a DM-routed main session (`agent:main:<channel>:default:direct:<peer>`). The lookup missed, so the scheduled branch in plugin tool delivery was skipped, and tool construction threw.

The scheduled mint now binds the same key as ordinary replies: the turn's runtime policy key, falling back to the session key. The fix is at the producer, so every consumer keeps its single lookup key.

The scheduled path started minting this capability in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178764.

## Evidence

Tested at `69e2e6951b7`, which merges `upstream/main` `5ed4aa230f8` into this branch; the PR's own diff is unchanged. The checks and the authority-chain run below used the same tree as this head, built at `3c1257965ef` (the diff between the two commits is empty). The fail-to-pass run (base `5ed4aa230f8`) ran at this head. The Before/After and control runs are from the earlier head: base `b0d3cd303a0`, after-side build `7d1723c57be`. At the new head, the authority-chain run's first job shows the same After behavior: its scheduled send reached the provider and Alice's DM.

An isolated Gateway (Linux, Node 24.18.0), built from each side, ran in a loopback-only network namespace with its own state directory and no provider keys. It used a local IRC server for the DM (default `dmScope`) and a local OpenAI-compatible stub provider that records each request. The automation was created and run through the built CLI: `openclaw automations create --name checkin-main --every 1h --session main --message "…"` (no delivery config), then `openclaw automations run <id>` twice, with an ordinary DM before and after. The output below is the Gateway's error lines, the stub provider's request count per step, and the stored job state.

Before (base `b0d3cd303a0`):

```text
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=cron-nested error="plugin delivery capability is no longer active" errorName=Error taskKind=cron sessionKey=agent:main:main runId=<run>
Embedded agent failed before reply: plugin delivery capability is no longer active
[session-events] session event execution failed source=cron agentId=main sessionKey=agent:main:main eventId=<event> error="Session event execution failed"
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=cron-nested error="plugin delivery capability is no longer active" errorName=Error taskKind=cron sessionKey=agent:main:main runId=<run>
Embedded agent failed before reply: plugin delivery capability is no longer active
[session-events] session event execution failed source=cron agentId=main sessionKey=agent:main:main eventId=<event> error="Session event execution failed"
provider requests: 4 (alice 4)
job checkin-main: lastStatus=error lastError="Session event execution failed" consecutiveErrors=2
```

After (this PR):

```text
provider requests: 6 (alice 4, run-main 2)
job checkin-main: lastStatus=ok consecutiveErrors=0
```

Observed result: on the base both scheduled runs failed before the model call and only the DM turns reached the provider; with this PR both scheduled runs reached the provider, no errors were logged, and the job is `ok`.

Controls, unchanged on both sides: a main session started with `chat.send` (`provider requests: 5 (chat-1 1, chat-2 1, run-main 2, chat-3 1)`, job `ok`), and an owner-announce job on the DM-routed main session (`provider requests: 6 (alice 4, run-proactive 2)`, job `ok`).

Authority chain, with this PR, same isolated Gateway and IRC DM. The roster has two agents, `main` (bound to IRC) and `spare`. Two `--session main` jobs for `main` have no delivery config. The stub provider answers each job's turn at once with a `message` tool call (`action: "send"`, `channel: "irc"`, `target: "alice"`).

A proof-only plugin, loaded from a local path and not part of this change, registers a `before_tool_call` hook on `message`. The hook holds the second job's send after the model returned it and before the tool runs. While the send is held, the job's owner is retired through the built CLI: `openclaw config patch` removes `main` from `agents.entries` and moves the IRC binding and the system agent to `spare`. The Gateway applies this as a hot reload: no Gateway restart, no cron restart, and no cancellation of the run. Then the hook lets the call through unchanged. The hook only waits; it never blocks or edits the call.

The run key stays split from the policy key: the hook sees the run under `agent:main:main`, while the send's capability is bound to Alice's DM policy key, which is the only key the first send can redeem under.

The output below is:

- the stub's request log;
- the hook's lines;
- the CLI result;
- the Gateway's reload and tool lines;
- the two jobs' run receipts from the state database;
- every line the bot sent on IRC.

```text
provider request 1: alice DM, stub reply text
provider request 2: alice DM, stub reply text
provider request 3: send job run, stub reply tool:message
provider request 4: hook-held job run, stub reply tool:message-hook-held
hook: hold message send "HOOK_HELD_SEND 4" sessionKey=agent:main:main runId=<run>
hook: release message send "HOOK_HELD_SEND 4" (released, tool call aborted=false)
cli: openclaw config patch --file retire-main.patch.json -> Applied 3 config update(s). Change will apply without restarting the gateway.
[reload] config hot reload applied (agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId, agents.defaults.authInheritance, agents.entries.main, agents.entries.spare.workspace)
[tools] message failed:
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=cron-nested error="Session target preparation outlived its attempt: Error: admitted run authority is no longer active | cron job agent is unavailable: main" errorName=Error taskKind=cron sessionKey=agent:main:main runId=<run> modelFallbackCandidate=true
cron_run_receipts send job: status=ok delivery_attempt_state=started
cron_run_receipts hook-held job: status=error error_text="Session event execution failed" delivery_attempt_state=not-started
IRC bot -> alice: <ordinary reply>
IRC bot -> alice: <ordinary reply>
IRC bot -> alice: SCHEDULED_SEND 3
```

Observed result:

- The scheduled turn's `message` send reached Alice's DM (`SCHEDULED_SEND 3`). Its receipt shows the delivery attempt started.
- For the second job, the model had already returned the send when the owner was retired. The run was not cancelled: the hook released the call with `aborted=false`. The `message` tool then failed, and the run's admitted authority was refused (`cron job agent is unavailable: main`).
- The second job's receipt shows the delivery attempt was never started, and no `HOOK_HELD_SEND` line reached IRC.
- This scenario was run on the PR build only; on the base the same job shape fails before the model call, as in the Before run above.

Revocation does not depend on the key this PR changes. Closing the scheduled admission revokes the capability token from the store, and the capability's active check reads the store before each delivery attempt, so a revoked token is refused whatever session key it was bound to. This PR changes only the key used at mint.

Cross-peer redemption (Alice's grant under Bob's runtime identity) is not proven through a real transport client, because no product path produces it. A turn's capability token is carried only in its own run's signed runtime identity, and the Gateway redeems it under that run's id and session key: the `turnCapabilitySessionKey` lookup in `src/agents/tools/gateway.ts:535-541` and the identity check in `src/gateway/server-methods/message-action-context.ts:168-180`. Presenting Bob's identity with Alice's token would mean forging that signed identity, which no product path does, and a forged identity would not prove the real owners. So the regression test in `agent-runner-execution-session-events.test.ts` pins this at the owner instead, and this point is left to maintainer judgement. The scheduled grant redeems under the turn's own runtime policy key (`agent:main:irc:default:direct:alice`). It does not redeem under another peer's key (`…:direct:bob`), and it does not redeem under the shared execution key that the base used. The redeeming checks are unchanged: one lookup by agent, run, session key and session id, then the delivery-attempt fence before outbound I/O, which `src/agents/tools/message-tool.scheduled-lifetime.test.ts` covers for revocation during send.

Checks: the touched test (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, wall time in the table below); the nearby scheduled-turn and message-capability suites (`session-event-config-readmission`, `session-event-handoff`, `agent-runner-execution-message-authority`, `message-tool.scheduled-lifetime`; 87 passed together with the touched test); `tsgo` on `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.messaging.json`; `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files. The new test (`agent-runner-execution-session-events.test.ts:204-236`) fails on the base (`expected undefined to be defined` at line 233) and passes with the fix. The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-session-events.test.ts` | 17.2s on this head's tree (Vitest duration; 70.9s with a cold worker compile) | 14.6s at `ac947109e97` ([`checks-node-changed-1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39785814621/job/119849515354)); the new head's CI runs after this push |

Not covered: real Telegram, Discord or Slack DMs (the trigger is any direct chat route under the default `dmScope`; IRC was used here), live model providers, other owner retirements that leave the run alive (the run above retires the agent; job removal and cron config changes also cancel the run), cross-peer redemption through a real transport client (see above), and automations created by the agent's own cron tool.

prs.title: fix(media): normalize AVIF inbound images like HEIC before provider execution
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Channel plugins passing inbound AVIF images through the documented path (`runtime.channel.media.saveRemoteMedia` → `toInboundMediaFacts` → `MsgContext.media`) reached providers unchanged, and OpenAI-compatible providers that accept only PNG/JPEG/WebP rejected the request — while the same image as PNG/JPEG/WebP worked. HEIC/HEIF already gets normalized to JPEG before provider execution; AVIF (Chrome screenshots, Android camera captures) had no such path, so every channel would need its own image codec to handle it.

## What Changed

The HEIC/HEIF normalization path in `src/media-understanding/image-input-normalize.ts` now also covers **AVIF** (`image/avif` and the `.avif` extension), converting through the same shared pipeline (`normalizeInputImageBuffer` → `convertHeicToJpeg`) so every channel benefits. `CONVERT_TO_JPEG_INPUT_MIMES` in `src/media/input-files.ts` is extended to match.

## Evidence

**Real-behavior proof (codec-equipped runtime: macOS 27.2 arm64, Rastermill decode via the native sips backend).** A real 1×1 AVIF attachment (417 bytes) passed through the production `normalizeImageDescriptionInput`:

```
Input : mime=image/avif bytes=417 header=0000 0018 6674 7970 6176 6966  ("ftypavif")
Output: mime=image/jpeg bytes=543 header=ffd8 ffe0  ("JFIF", JPEG SOI)
```

**Behavioral regression, red on base / green on head.** The new `image-input-normalize.normalize.test.ts` embeds real AVIF/HEIC attachments and exercises the production Rastermill decode path with no module mocks:

```
PR head (16eeb10d):  ✓ 4 passed (4)
   - converts real AVIF bytes to JPEG before image description
   - converts AVIF declared only by the .avif file extension
   - still converts real HEIC bytes to JPEG
   - leaves common images untouched

main production files, same test file:
   × converts real AVIF bytes to JPEG before image description
       → expected 'image/avif' to be 'image/jpeg'
   × converts AVIF declared only by the .avif file extension
       → expected undefined to be 'image/jpeg'
   ✓ still converts real HEIC bytes to JPEG
   ✓ leaves common images untouched
   Tests  2 failed | 2 passed (4)
```

On main the AVIF bytes reach the provider unconverted (`image/avif`) — exactly the reported bug. The earlier mock-based suite was removed; these tests fail if AVIF ever forwards unchanged again.


**End-to-end through the shipped CLI** (`openclaw infer image describe --file proof64.avif --model zai/glm-5.3-flash`, a real 379-byte AVIF attachment, 64×64 solid red):

```
{
  "ok": true,
  "capability": "image.describe",
  "provider": "zai",
  "model": "glm-5.3-flash",
  "outputs": [
    {
      "path": "/tmp/proof64.avif",
      "text": "The image shows a solid red square — a uniform bright red color (approximately RGB 255, 0, 0) with no other details, patterns, or objects present.",
      "kind": "image.description"
    }
  ]
}
```

The shipped `infer image describe` entry point took the AVIF attachment through `prepareImageDescriptionInput` (this PR's normalization), sent the converted image to the provider, and the vision model described the actual pixel content — the AVIF was decoded and delivered as a real image, not forwarded raw.

## On the decoder prerequisite (owner decision)

This keeps the shared conversion policy (option 1). The runtime prerequisite is the same one the existing HEIC path already has: Rastermill decodes HEIC/AVIF through native OS codecs (macOS `sips`) and common formats in-process; no bundled codec is added or removed by this PR. On a host without a native AVIF/HEIC codec, conversion fails with a Rastermill error **before provider execution** — the channel gets a clear conversion failure instead of shipping bytes the provider rejects, which is the recovery path. This matches the shipped HEIC behavior (PR #86037) rather than introducing a new compatibility class.

## CI

- `pnpm tsgo:test` clean locally; check-test-types green on 42f70a8c.
- The 17 pre-existing failures in `image.resources.test.ts` (infra project) reproduce on clean `main` without this PR — unrelated.

Fixes #180508

prs.title: feat(claws): add offline packages from local build archives
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Recipients cannot use a Claw author's built `.tgz` to create an ordinary agent without manually unpacking it or publishing through ClawHub.

Closes #180518.

## User Impact

`openclaw claws inspect ./package.tgz` and `openclaw claws add ./package.tgz` accept local `.tgz` and `.tar.gz` packages, including after the author's project directory is unavailable. Directory and direct-manifest inputs remain supported.

Add keeps its existing Claws Labs admission, dependency checks, capability consent and one-way semantics. Local archives do not acquire ClawHub trust, and declared online dependencies can still require network access. Extraction is temporary; the operator's original archive remains unchanged. A running Gateway's ownership cannot be bypassed. No configuration/default, persistent source cache, database schema, dependency or protocol is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing installer extractor supplies bounded, staged extraction and unsafe-entry rejection. An operation-scoped disposable source feeds the canonical Claw reader and keeps extracted files alive until Inspect or Add finishes. Source identity remains the reader's selected-content snapshot, not registry attestation or archive-level trust.

ClawHub already supports registry distribution and manual extraction remains possible; neither provides this native offline handoff. This reuses the maintained fs-safe extractor rather than introducing an archive implementation.

The maintenance merge retains upstream `b3ba4d622638ac23f64c0cec415bf5bfe81f5cf5` and resolves only the adjacent introduction in `docs/cli/claws.md`: archive inputs and upstream UTF-8 admission/recovery guidance are both preserved. The offline delivery commands and trust/cleanup limits remain intact. No production or test change was needed for the conflict. Relative to that main commit: five files, production +70/-5, tests +87/-0, docs +20/-1. No lockfile, changelog, generated inventory or proof assets are committed.

## Evidence

Exact maintenance head `33a7d99d5aa50d4da84b2ba8396d964f58ea4008`, tested October 25: clean tree, normal merge preserving the original feature commits. `pnpm build sourcePerformance` passed in 308.32s wall (build-all 294.2s); `dist/build-info.json.commit` independently matches HEAD. The unchanged compiled-CLI native proof and a separate saved-stream/filesystem readback both pass on this head.

Linux, Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0. Current main pins fs-safe 0.26.13; the original proof used 0.26.8. The installed extractor's admission, staging, limits and cleanup contracts were inspected directly. This is not a claim that the dependencies or all downstream source are unchanged.

Historical baseline `212c35bc374d3eb2541a7ce1e65d20c79312c6cb`: actual CLI create, build and directory inspection succeeded; archive inspection exited 1 with `invalid_json`. This is dated RED evidence, not a fresh RED run against October 25 main. The same product entry points below pass against the exact maintenance head.

Reviewer-copyable product entry points, with isolated state/config and an unused output directory:

```sh
openclaw claws create <author-project> --agent-id offline-receipt --json
openclaw claws build <author-project> --out <delivery.tgz> --json
openclaw claws inspect <delivery.tgz> --json
openclaw claws add <delivery.tgz> --dry-run --workspace <recipient-workspace> --json
openclaw claws add <delivery.tgz> --workspace <recipient-workspace> --json
openclaw agents list --json
```

The retained native driver moves the author directory away before archive inspection, then checks corrupt-archive and Labs-disabled refusal, dry-run workspace absence, actual Add completion, `SOUL.md` contents, a new agent-list process, temporary-source removal and the original archive digest. It launches compiled CLI processes rather than importing source owners:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs ../claw-archive-live-proof-20261022.mts <new-isolated-run-dir>
```

Driver SHA-256: `8aab7b7bf12c45a763872079e79f9993cdffd922a3cfcd256b9044f25e1a1f84`. It ran with a clean PATH resolving Git to `/usr/bin/git`, after an independent assertion that HEAD equals `dist/build-info.json.commit`. The driver records both identities but does not itself assert equality. Its added negative controls follow the original baseline failure point.

Actual October 25 native result: 9 compiled-CLI processes, exits `0,0,0,0,1,1,0,0,0`. Directory/archive inspection and dry run pass; corrupt archive and Labs-disabled Add each refuse (2/2), creating 0/2 forbidden workspaces. Actual Add reports `status: complete`, `configCommitted: true`, and agent `offline-receipt`; the recipient `SOUL.md` contains `orchard-lantern-42`, and a separate `agents list --json` process returns that agent. The author directory is unavailable; both extraction roots are gone after Inspect/Add; the 306-byte original archive remains unchanged (SHA-256 `c14c90d87a6a2a034c8b5c2c4ada56a4bd0ea0db6b486b405030dfb17aa56bef`).

Saved native receipt SHA-256: `a909f8442ada0806babd6a19ad9f4e8cd45a82bad9f1f16d391b5016e4704fdf`. ```text

exit=1

The four production/test files are byte-identical to the prior feature head; only the conflicted documentation was edited during this maintenance pass. Runtime/build/native output identifies the final merge commit; no prior-head PASS is substituted.

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Fixes independent Canvas document clients being unable to honor the Gateway's effective embed ceiling when their paired-device/profile connection cannot use the separate Control UI HTTP bootstrap.

The observable defect is missing policy metadata: authenticated `canvas.document.view` and `canvas.document.preview` return document bytes and sandbox routing, but omit the active `strict | scripts | trusted` ceiling. This PR does not claim that a Windows renderer already consumed the field or that a permissive-rendering exploit was demonstrated.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

Independent clients can read optional `embedSandbox` alongside the document over their existing authenticated RPC connection, without adding an HTTP credential exchange or falling back to a shared token.

This value is a **ceiling, not a permission grant**. Clients must apply any stricter local/content/preview policy; missing or unknown values require strict fallback. Older Gateways remain usable with that fallback. No new RPC, protocol bump, authentication/scope change, origin/CSP relaxation, native renderer or Dashboard substitution is introduced. Client adoption remains separate work.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

The existing HTTP bootstrap knows the effective ceiling, but WebSocket profile/identity grants cannot simply be reused as HTTP admission. The narrow fix extends the shared Canvas response and uses the existing bootstrap presentation resolver. After the document/sandbox await, the existing owner revalidates authority and samples one active config snapshot for both sandbox origin and policy, including the default `scripts`.

The schema owns the optional three-mode type; the bootstrap type derives from it. Existing HTML byte limits, persisted-session receipt authorization, host isolation and returned HTML remain unchanged.

At upstream main [`6c672d42f2dec42b7917f34dfe5ae8157b9b0abb`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/6c672d42f2dec42b7917f34dfe5ae8157b9b0abb) (2026-10-29), `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/canvas.ts:21-26` and `src/gateway/server-methods/canvas.ts:78-86` still lack this field. The contract is not superseded there. Main's handler has since been refactored; these historical tests are not a claim that the branch has been rebased or tested against that new main.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. For user-visible UI changes, follow the root
AGENTS.md "Product and validation" screenshot completion/landing gate; these other
forms of evidence do not replace the required screenshots in chat AND the PR.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

### Review status — 2026-10-29

The PR is open and non-draft at the unchanged head below. [The previous full CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40377471791) passed on this head. [ClawSweeper’s completed re-review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180520#issuecomment-6339077137) accepted the real behavior and compatibility evidence and identified no actionable findings; acceptance of the optional independent-client contract remains a maintainer decision before merge. No source changes were made for this readiness refresh.

prs.title: fix(update): dev updates hang when local main is stale in a shallow clone
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update --channel dev` hanging in preflight, for 37 minutes before I stopped it, when a detached checkout has a stale local `main` and a shallow boundary hides its shared history with the target.

## User Impact

Dev-channel updates from that checkout shape now finish without manual repair. If the update skips replaying local `main`, it validates the upstream commit, reports a warning, and keeps any commits the candidate lacks at `refs/openclaw/update-preserved/main-<sha>`.

The rebase step now has a 10-minute deadline even without `--timeout`. The installed updater must contain this fix before it takes effect, so an affected checkout needs one update through its current path first. On that older updater, moving the stale local `main` up to the deployed commit avoids the hang.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preflight chose local `main` as the rebase source without checking how it relates to the target. With no visible merge base, Git treated all of `main` as unpublished work and tried to replay it. In a `blob:none` clone each patch-id comparison fetched a blob, about one fetch per second in the real run. No deadline reached the step unless `--timeout` was passed, and a deadline alone would only have failed each candidate in turn.

Preflight now checks the relation first. With no merge base, or more than 1000 commits to replay, it validates the upstream commit instead. Conflicts still walk back through older candidates. Once a conflict or expiry ends the replay, every candidate tried with it is retried clean, newest first. An interrupted rebase ends the attempt. If the preservation ref can't be written, the update activates on a detached HEAD and leaves `main` alone.

Tradeoffs: the preserved ref pins old commits until removed, and the warning gives the removal command. If every rebase succeeds and every build fails, the update ends with `preflight-no-good-commit` and the running version keeps serving. A shallow boundary hiding 1000 commits or fewer still replays.

## Evidence

The incident was on a real installation: partial and shallow clone, detached HEAD, local `main` 10,393 commits behind the deployed commit per GitHub compare, 111,287 commits of visible history with no merge base. `sample` showed git in `patch_id_neq` -> `diff_populate_filespec` -> `promisor_remote_get_direct`, with 2,400+ promisor packs.

Hypotheses tested with real Git:

| Hypothesis | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Partial clone alone causes it | Refuted: partial with full history fast-forwards in 21 ms |
| Shallow alone causes the hang | No hang, but it conflicts in under 1 s and ends `skipped/already-current` without moving, so the shallow history is the root cause |

Scale fixture, not committed: 3,000-commit stale `main`, `blob:none`, `--depth=100`, 60-second watchdog.

| Check | Base | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scale fixture | Still rebasing at 60 s, 447 promisor packs, `status=skipped` | No rebase, `status=ok`, `after` equals target, 0.9 s |
| `update-runner-git-local-replay.test.ts` (new) | 10 failed, 3 passed | 13 passed |
| `update-command-git-dry-run.test.ts` | 1 failed, 6 passed | 7 passed |
| 7 updater test files including the new one | Not run | 199 + 1 passed |
| `update-command-fresh-preview.test.ts` | 4 failed, 27 passed | Same 4 failed, 27 passed |

The 4 fresh-preview failures appear on base too in the isolated environment. I didn't chase their cause.

`codex-api-review` found 5 real P2 issues, all fixed, and its last P2 pass was clean. Four have regression tests shown red first. The reference-source interruption fix has no dedicated test.

Not verified:
- The full `openclaw update` CLI end to end. Proof stops at `updateGitCheckout` and the preview function with fake pnpm builds, because a live update was running on the test host.
- An upgrade from the latest stable, or a real 111k-commit history.
- The tests on this exact head. I rebased after they ran, and upstream changed none of the files this PR touches.
- Waiting out the real 10-minute deadline. The test checks the requested value, then shortens it to 1 second to prove the kill and fallback.
