prs.title: fix: prevent resize loops while chat responses stream
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes WebKit ResizeObserver loop errors while a response streams Markdown tables and code. Also removes synchronous composer layout measurement when a streaming pane update replaces callbacks without changing its geometry.

## User Impact

Streaming content, tool results, images, typing, and follow-to-end behavior stay available while overflow affordances settle on the next frame. There are no configuration or migration steps.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Markdown observers read overflow geometry during native resize delivery. Fresh main reproduced the WebKit loop in 1 of 3 traced mixed-stream runs. Deferring only class writes was insufficient: a later untraced run still failed with no synchronous DOM mutations inside any observer callback. The observers now queue affected blocks into the existing layout scheduler, which reads all geometry before applying the overflow classes. Release and hide cancel pending work; native horizontal scrolling updates its affordance immediately.

The composer width handle also treated new callback identities as geometry changes. Its measurement dependency now compares the saved width and transcript element. Actual measurements and resize actions still read live options, including late native element attachment. The domain owners, transcript row implementation, routes, and lazy boundaries stay intact.

## Evidence

The requested 40-run WebKit correctness check passed, followed by 20 more clean candidate WebKit comparison runs. Completed 20-triplet comparisons show no qualifying CPU win; this is a functional repair with fewer synchronous geometry reads.

Acceptance: the committed `streaming-mixed-fast` synthetic-Gateway workload runs headless against production bundles. The correctness target is zero ResizeObserver errors in 40 uninstrumented WebKit runs. Timing uses 20 serial, alternating base/head/base-control triplets in Chromium 1×, Chromium 4× and native WebKit, recording host load. A clean cell has median regression ≤5% and no worse p95; on this loaded host, A/A variability is reported and Chromium script/task counters over 20 pairs plus structural counts decide attributable CPU regressions. Traces are separate attribution evidence, never timing proof. No WebKit CPU claim or unsupported 4× throttle is made.

| Proof | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Current-main mixed-stream reproduction | 1/3 traced WebKit runs errored |
| Revised candidate, 40 uninstrumented WebKit runs | 40/40 passed, zero errors; all interaction/content assertions retained |
| Markdown code-block and table tests | 35 + 11 passed |
| Composer callback regression | Base fails with an unnecessary synchronous geometry read; candidate passes; 12 sibling width tests passed |
| UI typecheck, scoped lint, controller guard | Passed |
| Production Knip | Passed on final source |
| Startup JS gzip, refreshed after merging main | 88,758 B base; 88,752 B candidate (−6 B); raw startup JS identical after normalizing chunk hash names; strict check passes, one CSS request, 33,568 B |
| Native Chromium/WebKit, 20 base/head/A/A triplets each | Candidate 40/40 passed; WebKit base 19/20 and A/A 18/20 (ResizeObserver); all four fresh Chromium traces passed |

The timing and 60-run WebKit evidence below precedes the final merges of main (8034bb1fafb and 2d8b054eab1). The merges include #188810’s mobile-sheet target-stability fix, #188808’s shared syntax-color assertion repair, and dependency refreshes. The strict startup comparison and focused composer case were rerun on the combined head; these timing numbers are not relabeled as new-head measurements. Startup raw bytes and normalized startup code are identical across the refreshed comparison; the 6 B gzip reduction is hashed chunk-reference entropy.

Native results (median / p95 across runs):

| Metric | Chromium base | Chromium head | Chromium A/A | WebKit base | WebKit head | WebKit A/A |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Script CPU, ms | 737.28 / 752.64 | 713.84 / 751.14 | 735.13 / 762.49 | unavailable | unavailable | unavailable |
| Task CPU, ms | 1853.55 / 1908.24 | 1818.88 / 1895.77 | 1861.11 / 1909.12 | unavailable | unavailable | unavailable |
| Commit→rAF p95, ms | 17.07 / 20.49 | 17.33 / 24.18 | 17.54 / 18.95 | 32.27 / 38.00 | 31.50 / 38.80 | 32.22 / 35.30 |
| Composer input→rAF p95, ms | 15.38 / 18.05 | 16.84 / 24.42 | 15.56 / 25.12 | 28.77 / 54.80 | 34.20 / 53.15 | 35.55 / 64.00 |
| Sidebar click→rAF, ms | 48.80 / 50.60 | 48.00 / 49.90 | 47.75 / 50.00 | 97.00 / 169.00 | 91.50 / 157.00 | 98.50 / 198.00 |

Native script CPU improves 3.18%, below the ≥5% win threshold; no speedup claim. Loaded-host A/A composer timing also regresses, and tail movement is not a clean all-metrics win. Completed intervals with baseline browser errors remain in timing statistics and are explicitly failed correctness runs. The 1× longest-task maximum is 67 / 70 / 65 ms (base/head/A/A), still above the 50 ms target. Median host load is about 50–52, range 22.23–64.25.

Chromium 4× results, 20 runs per bundle (median / p95):

| Metric | Base | Head | A/A |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Script CPU, ms | 2944.06 / 3385.79 | 3022.94 / 3338.68 | 3000.22 / 3503.48 |
| Task CPU, ms | 6198.13 / 6887.75 | 6214.78 / 6681.98 | 6234.74 / 6849.64 |
| Commit→rAF p95, ms | 131.77 / 198.38 | 146.56 / 196.76 | 137.70 / 200.75 |
| Composer input→rAF p95, ms | 56.25 / 115.82 | 57.56 / 118.96 | 57.66 / 105.86 |
| Sidebar click→rAF, ms | 197.75 / 243.00 | 198.10 / 252.20 | 195.25 / 242.40 |
| Longest task, ms | 219 / 279 | 209 / 268 | 221 / 280 |
| Synchronous geometry reads | 55.5 / 57 | 35 / 37 | 55 / 59 |

All 60 throttled runs pass content and interaction assertions. Script/task medians move +2.68%/+0.27%, within the 5% band; no speedup is claimed. The head longest-task maximum is 311 ms versus 279 ms base and 291 ms A/A, so the ≤200 ms target remains unmet. Commit-to-frame median p95 increases 11.23% (A/A +4.50%) while its across-run p95 improves 0.82%; this mixed tail result is disclosed, not called a win. Host load spans 27.25–60.35, with medians 35.09–35.64. The native and 4× A/A variation and 20-pair CPU/structural counts are the loaded-host evidence; WebKit CPU remains unavailable.

Current source-mapped tail attribution (one fresh instrumented base/head capture at 1× and 4×; not timing proof): the longest 4× candidate task is composite tool publication, **242.94 ms wall / 240.99 ms CPU**, with no GC. Inclusive samples put transcript projection at 84.23 ms, cached grouping at 61.18 ms, the sessions observer at 28.82 ms, and streaming Markdown at 14.16 ms; these overlap and are not additive. The largest scroll task is 201.79 ms, with 64.72 ms style/layout in transcript anchoring. At 1× the 54.92 ms longest task has only 26.31 ms thread CPU; the largest app-heavy publication is 40.61 ms. This does not establish an irreducible floor or retrospectively identify Round 1's untraced 345 ms sample. Transcript rows/anchors remain the long-session lane's scope. The next distinct streaming candidate is the tool disclosure's obsolete overflow detector, which forces 21.35 ms style settlement in a live 4× input task; it needs separate CSS and performance proof.

CI follow-through: the first run exposed a directly coupled streaming-table browser assertion that expected synchronous ResizeObserver output. It now awaits visible overflow, and all 43 tests in that browser file pass. Two Logs WebKit cases also failed in that run; both pass on latest completed scheduled main (41138060956), in exact-base local reproduction (2 passed, 1 Chromium skipped), and in final-head run 41145842018. They are not classified as inherited. That final-head run instead found a detached-token race in the session-diff highlighting assertion. The assertion now polls the same color comparison after querying the current token inside its file; the exact focused Chromium test passes (1 passed, 7 unrelated cases skipped), and lint/format pass. Run 41147684856 then failed only `keeps independent model and effort controls within the chat composer` at the effort-slider visibility assertion. Exact head and base replays both passed; no inherited claim is made. The case now waits for mobile editing layout and its height animation before the real effort click, matching the existing mobile-browser test contract. The later main merge also brings #188810, which fixes picker targets moving during desktop/mobile transitions. The focused test passes on the combined head; independent review is clean. Main then landed #188808’s equivalent syntax-color fix, creating a real merge conflict. The shared main assertion was retained, our duplicate test hunk was removed, and that exact focused case passes. Fresh independent review is clean. Replacement-head run 41151093847 passed the other jobs and 135 files in its UI shard, but the composer-picker suite failed before assertions because its runner lacked Playwright’s WebKit executable (`webkit-2370/pw_run.sh`). This is a browser-installation failure, not an inherited-test claim. A single-job diagnostic rerun was requested. Source inspection then found the deterministic cause: the existing CI list of WebKit-dependent suites omitted this suite. Commit cde2d8367af adds it to that list. The actual requirement-discovery command with this suite selected returns no browser on the base and `webkit` on the fix. The focused workflow contract and workflow checker pass; independent review is clean. The exact replacement-head CI run [41152646795](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41152646795) passed. Native replacement recovery merged the reviewed head as `8f47a67d1ffe740b0873914416e29019b0c3705e`; the merge is verified on `origin/main` and native closeout completed.

Production LOC across the four touched owners: 1,032 → 1,077 (+45). Tests: 2,960 → 3,051 (+91) across five touched test files, including the directly coupled streaming browser file and corrected model-control assertion; the session-diff correction is now owned by main’s #188808. The added production work is the owner-scoped queue, cancellation and narrow geometry comparison. The required 91-line test allocation covers the observer lifecycle and composer geometry regressions; the shared scalar budget is unchanged. Refactor census: zero effects, render effects, untrack, direct listeners, flush, or owner API calls before/after; the 20 existing foreign-DOM queries remain unchanged.

Synthetic before/after captures were inspected in full. The appearance is intentionally unchanged after settlement.

prs.title: feat(browser): save rendered pages as offline MHTML archives
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #180472.

Operators cannot save an already-interacted browser tab as a reopenable offline page archive through OpenClaw. `openclaw browser archive --target-id <id>` captures the selected Chromium CDP tab as MHTML; JSON output reports the artifact path, target ID and URL.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse Chromium's existing `Page.captureSnapshot` serializer in the browser plugin, with the existing selected-tab, navigation-policy, CDP-session and media-publication owners. The node caller supplies current node/profile policy at final media publication, including a policy change during asynchronous preparation.

Existing-solutions preflight: current-document downloads fetch the original URL; screenshot/PDF/text produce different artifacts. The inspected SingleFile CLI CDP implementation creates a new target and navigates it, so it does not preserve this selected tab's already-interacted state. No new dependency or archive engine is needed. Related merged direction: browser-owned download artifacts in #101369; that merge is not approval of this proposal. The linked issue has a bot advisory requesting maintainer consideration; no human acceptance is claimed.

The final layout registers a bounded `agent.archive.ts` route through the canonical route index. Capture lives beside current snapshot operations in the browser owner; the node/media SDK retains admission and final-publication guards. No alternate dispatch, deleted debug-module restoration or compatibility route is added.

The October 25 maintenance merge preserves both the existing archive CLI regression and upstream's shared browser CLI test-runtime helper. This resolves the actual test-file conflict and retains the upstream helper-based test architecture.

## User Impact

Save the already-rendered tab and reopen its serialized DOM and resources offline. Browser media is temporary: copy archives requiring durable retention. Archives may contain private page content, are not sanitized, and do not back up application/server state. Capture retains the existing 5 MiB media limit. Existing-session Chrome MCP and Lightpanda profiles remain unsupported.

Twelve changed files versus integrated main: production **+135/-4**, tests **+64/-0**, docs **+11/-1**. Production growth supplies native capture, route/CLI discovery and the final node authority guard. No new config/default, dependency, database, channel or protocol-version surface; no generated, lock or proof assets in the PR delta.

## Evidence

Exact maintenance head **`31a508b87fa87f6a91060be56a62f978fd2eb05d`**, normal merge of main **`b3ba4d622638ac23f64c0cec415bf5bfe81f5cf5`**, clean working tree. Linux, Node 24.22.1, Google Chrome 152.0.7977.64, pinned Playwright 1.64.0. `pnpm build sourcePerformance` passed on this committed head in 300.13s wall (build-all 285.2s); `dist/build-info.json.commit` independently equals HEAD. Source-runtime proof, not installed-package or remote Testbox certification.

Actual public entry: `openclaw browser archive --target-id <id> --json`, against an isolated token-authenticated Gateway and real Chromium. The unchanged native driver exercises the compiled public CLI and production browser plugin, interacts with a page, then stops its origin and places Chromium offline before reopening the saved file:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs ../mhtml-live-proof-20261022.mts ../maintenance-180486-native-cli-20261025-run green --native-cli
```

Actual readback at `2026-10-25T12:58:17.318Z`:

```json
{
  "head": "31a508b87fa87f6a91060be56a62f978fd2eb05d",
  "buildCommit": "31a508b87fa87f6a91060be56a62f978fd2eb05d",
  "cliExit": 0,
  "realGateway": true,
  "authenticatedRpc": true,
  "artifact": {
    "bytes": 2101,
    "sha256": "bf8c5acc9ab3668743b8c6c41ba075bac9f3aa35271a66a3060f0398a2caefc2"
  },
  "offlineReadback": {
    "renderedText": true,
    "css": true,
    "image": true,
    "iframe": true,
    "originStopped": true,
    "browserOffline": true,
    "ordinaryHttpNavigationRejected": true
  },

```

Text inspection succeeded 1/1 before capture. Offline ordinary HTTP navigation succeeded 0/1, while the archive preserved 4/4 content checks. Logical MHTML resource-request events are not claimed as network egress. Native receipt SHA-256 `90886f396349c31d82b3a64dab8c979472712abb1b6ff5872175c2fe37cb74f9`; unchanged driver SHA-256 `33439a1996f03ffd28e76baf64912ac94ce69ba9b3229580e275f2f73114e53e`.

The unchanged authority scenario also ran on this exact source head:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs ../mhtml-authority-proof-20261022.mts ../maintenance-180486-authority-20261025-run
```

At `2026-10-25T12:59:34.315Z`, production `runBrowserProxyCommand`, the registered archive route, native Chromium and actual media store yielded:

| Scenario | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| Allowed profile | Saved 1, transferred 1; independently reopened in Chromium |
| Initially forbidden profile | Rejected 1; new archives 0 |
| Profile revoked when the actual temporary file appears | Watcher observed it; request rejected; retained archives 0 |

Revocation uses public runtime config-snapshot publication and a native filesystem watcher during asynchronous preparation. This is source-mode production node-owner proof, not paired-node WebSocket transport or a model turn. Receipt SHA-256 `8154a2079756c717cfdb7909c8e92856a7952c67c40b5fc309a8032ab4957562`; unchanged driver SHA-256 `5f7af1ab0c03151723748e00d3a089d47d7eacca85e98cd25f5999e0951d6b48`.

Those historical receipts are not new October 25 baseline executions. Both production paths were rerun after this merge; no ancestor GREEN substitutes for current-head proof.

Fresh maintenance gates, on source bytes identical to this commit:

- `OPENCLAW_BROWSER_CONTENT_E2E=1 PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/usr/bin/google-chrome OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/cli/browser-cli-actions-observe.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/agent.content.chromium.test.ts extensions/browser/src/node-host/invoke-browser.test.ts extensions/browser/src/node-host/invoke-browser.admission.test.ts extensions/browser/src/node-host/invoke-browser.lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **57 passed, 1 skipped**, 206.44s Vitest / 219.61s wrapper / 221.35s shell; native Chromium enabled.
- Real-source narrow `OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p .artifacts/tsconfig.mhtml-maintenance.json --incremental`: PASS, 114.50s wall, canonical source/ambient roots and no substitute SDK types.
- Typed lint on that same scope: 0 warnings/errors, 10 files, 293 rules, 89.8s tool / 205.95s wall (including artifact-lock wait). Existing SDK declarations prepared successfully.
- Scoped oxfmt: PASS, 12 files. Two changed MDX pages: PASS, 270ms. Existing publishing parser: 20 local destinations resolve; no full fragment-crawl claim. `git diff --check`: PASS. `docs:list` ran before this maintenance edit.

prs.title: fix(update): dev updates hang on disconnected local main
prs.body:
Supersedes #188857 (thanks @fuller-stack-dev)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw update --channel dev` can hang replaying stale local `main` when a shallow clone hides its shared history with the update target.

## User Impact

Dev updates validate upstream without replaying disconnected history. Commits outside the validated candidate remain reachable at `refs/openclaw/update-preserved/main-<sha>`, with inspection and removal commands in the warning. If preservation fails, activation uses a detached HEAD and leaves `main` unchanged.

The installed updater must contain this fix; candidate code cannot repair an older updater's already-running preflight. Preserved refs remain until the operator removes them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing preflight owner checks the relation before replay and limits optional local checkout/rebase to ten minutes per step, or a shorter caller timeout. Timeout gets one clean retry of the current candidate; ordinary conflicts retain the existing walk-back order. Interruption and unverified cleanup stop the attempt. Git state inspection distinguishes an active rebase from a timeout before rebase state exists.

This reduced takeover omits the 1000-commit cutoff, expanded retry queue, preview changes and return-field plumbing. It uses the existing preflight and native Git-step owners, with no new public options, config, protocol or schema.

## Evidence

- The trusted real-Git shallow `blob:none` regression was RED on `e765de67512f14a644f726372b0bb2b46e614a6c`: it resurrected a retired file and activated a different commit. It is GREEN with this fix and verifies the preserved original ref.
- All 14 replay scenarios pass: connected work, merge-only content, default/shorter/early timeout, failed active abort, conflict, replay/preservation interruption, detached fallback and rollback. The standalone file took 15.37s wall time. Real Git deadline tests shorten execution to one second; they verify the requested ten-minute or shorter budget.
- The initial consumer selection passed 214 tests plus both immutable-worker tests. After the review repair, all 81 affected tests passed; unchanged consumer evidence is retained. Services typecheck, typed lint, format, test-line ratchet and `git diff --check` passed. The separate 273-line regression allocation covers these native Git/process contracts without changing the shared baseline.
- Fresh independent Codex autoreview of the complete local diff against the base above, P0–P2: scoped-clean after fixing and reproducing the early-timeout finding. Final commit: 984b63709f0d8a2e65ad05011476ef2ef15f7c98.

- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41152259862) passed on `984b63709f0d8a2e65ad05011476ef2ef15f7c98` (attempt 1). The terminal PR rollup has 68 passing and 66 skipped checks, including a passing `openclaw/ci-gate`; no failures or pending checks.

Resolves #180453 

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: OpenClaw silently defaulting to the hardcoded `gpt-6-astra` model when a user enters an API key during onboarding, resulting in immediate Gateway crashes if the key lacks tier access or if a local provider like Ollama is used.

User impact: When a user links a provider account, they are now presented with an interactive dropdown strictly containing the models their account is actually authorized to use, preventing onboarding failures.

2. Hit the provider's live endpoint (`/v1/models`, `/api/tags`) via `loadPreparedModelCatalogView`.

- Verified setting up Ollama dynamically fetches and displays only locally downloaded `.gguf` tags.
- Verified TypeScript compilation (`tsc --noEmit`) passes cleanly with the new SDK imports.

prs.title: perf(ci): reuse database worker compiler symbol queries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Database-worker compatibility analysis asks the native TypeScript process for the same AST location in several graph phases. The existing access cache covers only one per-file fallback, so closure discovery, callback classification and reference analysis can repeat compiler queries.

## User Impact

CI reuses each location's raw compiler answer within one immutable source snapshot, including unresolved locations. Dynamic-import forwarding, exact callback arguments, declaration identity, source isolation, credential validation and all inventory classifications retain their owners.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the partial access cache with one invocation-local node-identity cache and the existing ordered array API for unique misses. Resolve mutable forwarded bindings when consuming raw symbols. Nothing persists across source snapshots. Tooling net +2 lines establishes that ownership boundary; tests net +65 add a real-compiler work-count regression without substituting compiler results. The separate allocation matches the regression.

## Evidence

- Signed head `da3769e27ff6443b8cd6b6e4cc5500eed220f520`; tree `f2f8ca5d1afe714d9c838c7b58360882ac1101a7`; frozen base `52fbfb7d989207a4f82544f58b5bb9ee75782fe9`.

- Inspected the pinned TypeScript 7.1.0-dev.20261016.1 public sync implementation: `getSymbolAtLocation` scalar/array results preserve order and missing symbols; `cacheGeneratorMethod` retains only the callable. Node and symbol interning make snapshot-local identity the correct key. Inspected installed source: typescript/dist/api/sync/api.js:2824–2858 and generatorSupport.js:1–5.
- Targeted pinned formatting, diff/privacy checks and signed hooks passed. Independent source review found no actionable P0–P2 issue; it did not execute tests.
- Initial-head [lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41102107511/job/124223197514) rejected two unbound method references in regression instrumentation. The descriptor getter now uses an explicit receiver and the generator delegate is bound. Production cache code is unchanged; the final exact-head CI passes as recorded below.
- The focused Testbox request queued before payload and was stopped. No baseline-negative-control, owner tests or typechecks ran there. Its exact lease cleanup settled after observed GitHub cancellation.

## Validation And Gaps

The real-compiler regression records actual queried nodes and aligned results, covering repeated successful and unresolved callbacks plus dynamic forwarding and escaped-callback rejection. Existing alias/barrel/namespace/generic receiver/public SDK fixtures remain.

Initial c03acfcc compact tests passed with owner alias, namespace, dynamic-import, shorthand-escape and typed-receiver cases observed in the log. That head also failed [core test types 3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41102107511/job/124223197480): Vitest deliberately excludes callable-valued properties from its getter-spy overload. The latest correction observes the real descriptor directly and restores it in try/finally, preserving actual compiler results and all assertions. Independent read-only review found this correction clean. Production code is unchanged. Final exact-head CI passes as recorded below. Separate native-TypeScript test execution and paired full-inventory parity/performance are not established. No numerical request reduction, elapsed-time saving, billed-minute saving or Windows result is claimed. The proposed change leaves type/member queries and graph propagation unchanged.

## Exact-head follow-through

CI41105274080 now passes at da3769e27ff: owner94/94 (795ms), new real-compiler work-count regression13ms, ratchet19/19 (1.814s), core script test types exit0, lint and script types passed. Normal GitHub gates are green.

[Latest ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188588#issuecomment-6530564901) covers this exact head with no findings and no before-merge requirement. Its optional rank-up move asks for a comparable baseline/candidate complete-inventory performance/parity run. That benchmark is deferred: the isolated proof request never started its payload and its cleanup is settled; the observed CI timings use different source/runner conditions. Existing correctness, work-count and inventory-ratchet checks pass. This narrow ownership refactor makes no numerical performance or billing claim; paired qualification remains a named follow-up. ## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing cache report deadline and projection owner. Remove the separate direct refresh, pricing-fingerprint and projection pipeline: production net **-13 lines**. Preserve selected-session ownership, cancellation and fresh results when refresh completes in time.

## Evidence

- Main owner files at `92e1a1bb115f2ea646e0b57b21d7c5cfa6649ca7`: the regression holds a real SQLite refresh lock, advances ten seconds of fake time, and fails because the direct report remains pending. The fix returns the previously committed 10 tokens / $1 with `staleSince` and `refreshing`, while owner work remains pending. No real ten-second sleep.
- 74 focused pricing, archive, incognito, worker-I/O and refresh tests passed (108.02 s runner / 111.57 s wall); the final organization reran all 24 refresh tests successfully (56.24 s runner / 59.30 s wall, including a cold worker compile). prs.title: fix(usage): cap session-cost busy refresh wait
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadSessionCostSummary` retries while another live writer holds the usage refresh lock. A worker projection after that wait can publish a checkpoint that lags the transcript. The direct summary now polls the lock for five seconds. If the lock is still held, it returns null and does not project that checkpoint.

## Evidence

On this worktree, production `prepareSessionCostUsageRefreshLock` acquired the real SQLite lock. Production `loadSessionCostSummary` then returned null in 5013 ms. There was no wait-budget override.

```console
$ node -v && uname -srm
v26.10.0
Darwin 27.0.0 arm64

$ cd /tmp/oc-132396 && node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs /tmp/oc-132396-proof.mts
stateDir /var/folders/7_/3g02szlx2h3_4pdqp0knlw740000gn/T/oc-132396-proof-ilfhCA
lock_acquired true
{"elapsed_ms":5013,"summary":null}
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A direct session-cost load waits at most five seconds for a held refresh lock, then returns null instead of a lagging checkpoint.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS Darwin 27.0.0 arm64, Node v26.10.0, worktree /tmp/oc-132396.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `cd /tmp/oc-132396 && node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs /tmp/oc-132396-proof.mts`
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from that command:

```console
lock_acquired true
{"elapsed_ms":5013,"summary":null}
```

- **Observed result after fix:** With the real refresh lock held, `loadSessionCostSummary` returned null after 5013 ms.
- **What was not tested:** A multi-process gateway `/usage` command against a long-running writer on a large transcript.

## Summary

Public path: `/usage` and session-cost commands via `loadSessionCostSummary`. The worker projection from the reporting move still runs after the lock is free. A held lock does not publish a partial total.

Returning no total after five seconds is the contract in this patch. It still needs the area owner to accept that a direct request may come back unavailable while a legitimate refresh is running.

Focused command on head `b18611a1d382f2ea77459a6df6e870b655d82e61`, macOS Darwin 27.0.0 arm64, Node v26.10.0:

```console
$ cd /tmp/oc-132396 && /usr/bin/time -p pnpm test src/infra/session-cost-usage-direct-refresh.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
real 7.77
```

The runner finished that file in 7.36 seconds. The two cases returned in 38 ms and 30 ms of test body, inside the five-second lock budget. CI job `checks-node-changed-1` on run 37801558429 ran the same file and completed in 239 seconds, including runner setup (2026-10-08T15:39:19Z to 2026-10-08T15:43:18Z).

prs.title: fix(sandbox): resolve literal remote-shell and ssh identity paths without trimming
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two path-selected inputs still trimmed their value before use.

- The remote-shell sandbox file bridge (`sandbox.backend: "ssh"` / remote shell) resolved `" note.txt"` to the sibling `note.txt`. A read returned the wrong file; a write overwrote it.
- The SSH tunnel (`openclaw gateway status`, client `gateway.remote.sshIdentity`) passed `gateway.remote.sshIdentity.trim()` to `ssh -i`, so a configured identity file whose name ends in whitespace loaded a different key.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the selected path literal at both owners; the trimming resolver still owns only the invocation base. The mount-containment guard is unchanged.

Precedent: #187777 (OpenShell mirror-mode renderer), #187554 (linked hook discovery paths). Original fix by @wangmiao0668000666.

## Evidence

Real built entry point on both refs, on an isolated Linux box: `startSshPortForward({ target: "me@example.com:2222", identity: "/keys/id test " })` resolves `/usr/bin/ssh` through `resolveSshClient()` (strict trusted dirs), spawns it, and the observed child argv carries:

- base `8034bb1fafb`: `{"cmd":"/usr/bin/ssh","identityArg":"/keys/id test"}` (trailing space dropped → different key file)
- head `3e023096ccb`: `{"cmd":"/usr/bin/ssh","identityArg":"/keys/id test "}` (literal identity)

Scenarios used `tsx` on the source tree with the production `ssh-tunnel.ts`; only the child-process table is observed, the resolver, port preflight and argv construction are real.

Focused tests (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <file> --maxWorkers=1`, Node 24.22.1, Linux):

- `src/infra/ssh-tunnel.test.ts`: 26 passed (whole file; new case `passes the configured identity to ssh without trimming its whitespace`). On base the new case fails with `expected [ '-i', '/keys/id test' ] to deeply equal [ '-i', '/keys/id test ' ]`.
- `src/agents/sandbox/remote-fs-bridge.test.ts`: 24 passed (whole file; new case `addresses literal whitespace-padded paths instead of their trimmed siblings`). On base it fails because `" note.txt"` returns the trimmed sibling's bytes.

Existing directory, mount-root, symlink-escape and read-only protections keep their assertions.

Not tested: real SSH host, Windows, macOS, mounted gateway flows, live gateway.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: revert restores the trimming. No stored format, migration or protocol change. Users who (unintentionally) relied on trailing whitespace being ignored in `gateway.remote.sshIdentity` or in remote-shell relative paths now address the literal value they supplied; that matches every file tool and the documented behavior of #187777.

prs.title: fix(doctor): prepare plugin contracts off the main thread
prs.body:
Related: #166526

Prerequisite #188760 merged as `ae01f1c113826d3ff41463e74da6c115e5b581ff`. This draft now targets main. The measured head is retained unchanged pending the performance-tradeoff decision; current-main integration and exact-head CI remain required before native landing.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor can stall its main event loop while capturing an external plugin's setup-contract source, even though runtime plugin preparation already has a worker.

## User Impact

Doctor prepares selected plugin sources through the existing worker before invoking synchronous setup contracts. Each phase still gets private module files and fresh callbacks; capture, receipt checks, native admission, authority checks and awaited cleanup remain required. This is a responsiveness change, not a claim that the reported Windows Doctor duration or separate `--fix` hang is resolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Doctor run retains one unexecuted source seed in the existing preparation owner and creates independently owned artifacts for its phases. Host callers recheck the selected inventory, cancellation and retirement after asynchronous work and before binding. Metadata-only declarations stay metadata-only. Explicit callers already running inside a worker can capture inline. The superseded host synchronous custody path is removed; no new worker pool or persistent cache is added.

## Evidence

The real admitted-file rendezvous failed first on the synchronous path. The prepared path keeps an independent main-thread timer running while worker I/O is paused, then preserves the captured digest, payload bytes, callback results and private instance state. The same boundary covers cancellation, retirement, lost authority and injected source failure. Existing custody, dependency-junction, native-companion, read-only and cleanup cases are retained.

Current-main integration passed 15 focused tests, core types, the flows and plugin-platform type graphs, targeted lint, formatting and diff checks. A three-pass independent review of the integration is clean. Earlier frozen implementation proof passed 113 focused tests and the production build; that evidence is reused only for unchanged inputs. Four existing test factories now preserve real exports while retaining their synthetic overrides; the corresponding obsolete mock-baseline entries are removed. The exact Doctor-only regression allocation is 1,063 net test lines. The final bounded extraction checks passed 61 state-migration tests, 19 integrity tests, core and state-logging type graphs, targeted lint, mock and line-budget guards. Final bounded extractions preserve the original directory resolution, migration selection and test assertions while keeping oversized owners within their existing limits; their independent review is clean. Final measurements and main-targeted CI are pending; this PR remains a draft until those and any required performance-tradeoff acceptance are settled.

### Final measurement rule (recorded before the final run)

Run the committed `scripts/perf/doctor-setup-preparation-measure.ts` with the pinned Bun against exact baseline `4d2a9f8bb4c47da0daae7fd820cab33fa450ef7b` and the final committed candidate. Use identical workload/probe/fixture bytes, a fresh process per sample, and the fixed serial order A,A,B,B,A,B,A,B,A,B. Keep all ten samples and record host load. The workload has 131 files / 597,689 bytes and three independent phase caches. Imports and fixture creation are outside the timing interval. Report first capture separately from custody-warm phases, plus median, nearest-rank p95, min/max, raw samples and matching work counts. Five samples per arm make empirical p95 the observed maximum, not a reliable population-tail estimate.

Acceptance requires lower main-thread filesystem calls and improved main-thread CPU/timer-delay medians, with identical captured bytes, digests, callbacks and lifetime behavior. Publish elapsed time, process CPU, host CPU, phase latency/delay, and host/worker calls and byte counters, including every wrong-way metric. Process CPU includes worker threads; host CPU is its overlapping main-thread subset. No total-work or zero-I/O reduction is assumed. Every worsened user-facing metric needs explicit owner acceptance; a 20% regression is a stop for review, not a within-spread exception. Earlier measurements are historical and do not constitute that acceptance.

The baseline-to-candidate comparison includes the integrated lane changes since that baseline; it does not isolate this final PR from its prerequisites. Separate profiles retain filesystem-probe overhead and do not enter the timing samples.

## Final committed measurement — landing held

Candidate `f0e181d69203812fe666a49427d40cadda0796d6`, baseline `4d2a9f8bb4c47da0daae7fd820cab33fa450ef7b`, pinned Bun 1.4.4. All ten runs completed with unchanged source/runtime fingerprints, identical bytes/digests/callback results, and completed private-directory cleanup.

| Metric | Baseline median / p95, ms | Candidate median / p95, ms | Median / p95 change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Three-phase elapsed | 964.7 / 1,111.5 | 1,500.8 / 3,444.0 | +55.6% / +209.9% |
| Total process CPU (includes workers) | 925.3 / 1,036.5 | 1,481.5 / 3,129.3 | +60.1% / +201.9% |
| Main-thread CPU (overlaps total) | 639.7 / 795.5 | 325.4 / 376.3 | -49.1% / -52.7% |
| Maximum phase timer delay | 544.8 / 670.0 | 215.4 / 312.3 | -60.5% / -53.4% |
| First phase elapsed | 558.8 / 684.3 | 1,048.0 / 2,983.6 | +87.6% / +336.0% |
| Second, custody-warm phase elapsed | 130.8 / 204.7 | 171.2 / 179.3 | +30.9% / -12.4% |
| Third, custody-warm phase elapsed | 138.9 / 164.8 | 158.7 / 174.9 | +14.3% / +6.1% |
| Second phase timer delay | 118.2 / 193.1 | 87.4 / 94.2 | -26.1% / -51.2% |
| Third phase timer delay | 124.1 / 143.6 | 70.8 / 77.3 | -43.0% / -46.2% |

All timing samples are retained below in execution order. Empirical p95 is the maximum of five runs per arm; these are descriptive loaded-host measurements, not population tail estimates. One-minute load was 33.7–38.3 around the timing processes. This task ran no other local builds, reviews or checkout operations during these samples.

| Sample | Arm | Elapsed ms | Process CPU ms | Main-thread CPU ms | Maximum phase timer delay ms |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | A | 1,042.3 | 1,035.4 | 795.5 | 597.9 |
| 2 | A | 694.2 | 754.9 | 541.0 | 358.4 |
| 3 | B | 3,444.0 | 3,129.3 | 376.3 | 288.8 |
| 4 | B | 1,251.4 | 1,320.6 | 310.3 | 201.9 |
| 5 | A | 964.7 | 925.3 | 639.7 | 544.8 |
| 6 | B | 1,827.0 | 1,589.7 | 325.4 | 215.4 |
| 7 | A | 773.9 | 818.0 | 587.9 | 422.9 |
| 8 | B | 1,500.8 | 1,481.5 | 358.9 | 312.3 |
| 9 | A | 1,111.5 | 1,036.5 | 784.7 | 670.0 |
| 10 | B | 1,101.6 | 1,232.4 | 281.4 | 182.1 |

The initial A/A elapsed control changed −33.4%; B/B changed −63.7%. Both remain included. Each arm had identical I/O counts across all five runs:

| Work count | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread synchronous JS filesystem calls | 33,595 | 15,221 |
| Worker synchronous JS filesystem calls | 0 | 18,445 |
| Total synchronous JS filesystem calls | 33,595 | 33,666 (+71, +0.21%) |
| readSync bytes, main / worker | 4,679,828 / 0 | 1,093,170 / 3,586,840 |
| Streamed write bytes, main / worker | 597,689 / 0 | 0 / 597,689 |
| Raw copyFile bytes, main / worker | 2,390,756 / 0 | 0 / 2,390,756 |

Candidate accounting reports four captures, three source reuses, 524 selected package-file entries, 597,689 original bytes, four receipt passes / 524 receipt reads / 2,390,756 receipt bytes, and 2,988,445 aggregate logical copied/hashed bytes. Aggregate copy includes the initial stream plus raw copies; these are JS/logical counts, not physical storage traffic. Worker time and host round-trip time overlap. No zero-I/O or total-copy reduction is claimed.

**Acceptance is pending.** Responsiveness improves in this synthetic flow, but elapsed time, total process CPU, phase latency and total filesystem calls regress. The ≥20% elapsed/CPU/phase cells stop landing under the written rule. This is not an overall speedup, and does not establish the Windows report or separate `--fix` hang as fixed. Any acceptance must cover the full table, including the worse empirical tail and small count increase.

Separate whole-process CPU profiles retained the same FS probes and include imports/fixture construction. Bun emitted one profile per arm; neither establishes worker-thread coverage. These profiles cannot attribute the additional total CPU, and are excluded from timing samples. Total observed readSync bytes increased by 182 bytes (4,679,828 → 4,680,010); streamed and raw-copy categories are unchanged. Across the published median/p95 table, 11 cells regress and seven exceed 20%.

prs.title: feat: onboard personal channel users without external sign-in
prs.body:
<!-- openclaw:attribution=off -->

## What Problem This Solves

A token/password-authenticated single-user Gateway cannot establish a personal channel identity when its only profile is shared Owner, leaving personal session creation dependent on an external sign-in provider.

## User Impact

An authenticated administrator can explicitly create a person and bind a verified channel sender without Tailscale, Cloudflare Access, or another proxy. Shared Owner stays separate. An explicitly assigned role can delegate session-only authority without granting channel-owner status or global operator write access.

This is a draft for local testing. Real channel end-to-end acceptance remains unverified; do not treat the passing local fixtures as live Discord or Slack evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add administrator-gated `users.create` using the existing profile writer, then reuse `users.linkChannelIdentity` for the exact `(channelId, accountId, senderId)` binding. Carry limited personal authority with the existing verified requester identity, independently of command ownership, and retain the original binding and current policy during queued recovery.

Default roles, display names, message text, and login-name role assignments do not delegate these session scopes. Conflict protection, account qualification, shared-Owner exclusion, access policies, and live revocation checks remain in place. No database schema change or automatic identity migration is introduced. Profile names are not unique keys, and repeated `users.create` calls create distinct people; setup and recovery are documented in [User model](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ccb547a8062a35564f527c87708ce9baf5b647ae/docs/concepts/user-model.md#onboard-without-an-external-sign-in-provider).

## Evidence

- Reproduced the missing onboarding method through registered Gateway dispatch before implementation: `users.create` returned `unknown method`.
- Onboarding/authority/recovery suites: **95 tests passed** in 139.14 seconds including compilation. They cover unauthorized creation, shared Owner exclusion, conflicting links, exact account matching, forged/asserted contexts, default-role non-escalation, multi-user behavior, demotion, unlinking, and queued recovery. The Discord and Slack host-ingress fixtures invoke the real `sessions_create` tool and verify persisted personal creator attribution, without owner fallback.
- Protocol/discovery/prompt-stability consumers: **56 tests passed** in 79.23 seconds. CI time is not yet available.
- Production and touched-test typechecks, touched TypeScript lint/format, protocol registry, generated-validator consistency, native protocol generation, documentation configuration examples/links, diff checks, and the scoped test-line allocation check passed.
- Independent Auto Review (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2) covered the local candidate against base `1d6f75fd`. No concrete implementation defect was reported; its outstanding P2 finding is the missing real-channel acceptance proof.
- **Pending:** real verified channel turn → model tool invocation → new session under the personal profile's session-write authority. The QA credential broker could not be reached through any existing authenticated Convex launcher. No live Discord or Slack test turn ran, and no production identities or permissions were changed. The requester explicitly asked to publish this draft for local testing.

### Local testing

1. Start an isolated token/password-authenticated Gateway whose profile directory initially contains only shared Owner. Add the explicit `sessionWriter` role from the documented setup; preserve any existing multi-user defaults.
2. From the authenticated administrator connection, call `users.create` with `{ "displayName": "Local tester", "role": "sessionWriter" }`; save the returned `profile.id`.
3. Independently verify the channel sender's immutable ID and configured account, then call `users.linkChannelIdentity` with that personal profile ID and the complete identity tuple. Do not bind shared Owner.
4. From that sender, submit a fresh, normally admitted channel turn explicitly requesting a new independent session. Verify the actual `sessions_create` trace and the stored human/profile creator ID. It must be the new person, not `gateway-owner`; administrator/global-write operations must remain unavailable.
5. Check a different account with the same sender ID, then unlink or demote the person. Confirm those paths cannot retain or regain the old session-write authority. Inspect existing profiles/links before retrying any uncertain creation or binding operation.

Requested by Jacqueline Henriksen.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/af7ce7b0-0fc4-4179-9e6e-9b3038d2dd2f)

## Worked on by

- @jjjhenriksen

prs.title: fix(exec): preserve command outcomes during failed Gateway shutdown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes lost command outcomes when Gateway shutdown retains connection work before reaching process cleanup. Exec finalization could receive `ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE` because the outer runtime cleanup disconnected its broker before the CLI fallback canceled and joined commands.

## User Impact

Ordinary supervised commands retain their result and final output during this shutdown path. The existing shutdown deadline still bounds the caller; incomplete cleanup remains visible. Durable processes and public configuration are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The broker retirement owner now joins the existing process supervisor before stopping admission or the broker. The supervisor already owns cancellation, output settlement, and service-child extinction. A failed or pending join retains the broker instead of disconnecting it. The healthy core join and CLI fallback remain necessary for their respective lifecycle paths.

Production change: **+4 lines**, including the ordering comment and lazy import. This connects two existing lifecycle owners without a new timer, registry, cache, config option, or schema. The 61-line regression allocation covers a real command, final-output receipt, and native extinction after core close fails.

## Evidence

The new process regression fails on the baseline with the reported lineage/broker-unavailable error and passes with the fix. Node: 10 tests pass on macOS and Linux. Bun: both applicable native-transport tests pass on macOS and Linux; its seven broker-only cases are skipped because Bun deliberately disables command pipe brokerage. The Linux Bun runtime was installed through the repository's pinned-runtime setup after the first attempt found no Bun executable.

Five serial Linux A/B pairs using the committed `scripts/perf/spawn-broker-shutdown-measure.ts`:

| Owner measurement | Baseline | Fixed |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Lost command outcomes | 5/5 | 0/5 |
| Median shutdown | 132.607 ms | 102.520 ms |
| p95 (maximum, n=5) | 137.794 ms | 120.454 ms |
| Median host CPU | 13.555 ms | 11.264 ms |
| Separate sampled allocations (two samples) | 743,360 / 1,198,672 B | 592,016 / 443,992 B |

A/A controls: baseline 122.784/118.211 ms, candidate 98.321/92.322 ms. CPU ranges overlap; allocation samples are sparse, so neither is presented as a general performance improvement. Every candidate preserved the final marker and confirmed extinction, within the unchanged five-second budget. Acceptance was zero lost outcomes or failed extinction joins, bounded cleanup, and no owner-time regression.

The fixture uses the actual Gateway runtime wrapper, supervisor, broker, and service-child owners, with a synthetic retained-core-cleanup error. It does not boot agents or scan databases/workspaces; it is **owner-level process proof, not a whole-Gateway large-database/btrfs benchmark**. Linux measurements used Node 24.22.1 on a Testbox with 4 observed CPUs and 15.4 GiB RAM. A separate macOS baseline smoke exhausted 5,001.8 ms, whereas the candidate smoke completed in 109.2 ms; these single samples are diagnostic only.

Codex autoreview at P0–P2 found no accepted/actionable findings, including a follow-up with the complete runtime wrapper supplied. Targeted test readiness and probe typecheck findings from the initial changed-check run were corrected. The corrected targeted typecheck, lint, formatting, timeout-policy and test-line checks pass; the production and full-tree unused-file scan also passes. The complete final `pnpm check:changed` rerun passes (exit 0), including all selected type, lint, dead-code and repository guards.

Exact-head CI [run 41152084103](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41152084103) passed for `de5f222feeadccd039c9f315bb94d0f7d98c2ae4` (57 successful jobs, no failed jobs). Both required `openclaw/ci-gate` checks passed, including applicable security review requirements. Landed as `a535fbc2d36f7cf0a2a645b4fd9a366a3063938e` through the native pinned squash auto-merge route. No inherited-failure exception or CI rerun was used.

prs.title: perf(gateway): release unrelated session index snapshots
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long-lived subagent registration readers retained an entire obsolete registry snapshot even when they needed only one child. Session topology also retained duplicate per-child arrays when the published and internal child groups contained identical entries.

## User Impact

Lower retained Gateway heap without changing session selection, visibility, ownership, or deletion behavior. No schema, configuration, or public API change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Registration readers now retain only their original selected child/run fallback. Each later read still merges the current registry, committed receipts, and live owners, so new competitors and deletions remain authoritative. The existing mutation owner still hydrates payloads before a write.

Topology publishes its canonical child bucket directly when no distinct live owner must be appended. A later durable mutation or transition to a distinct live overlay detaches that bucket before changing it, preserving already captured snapshots. This adds no cache and does not combine distinct viewer or source scopes.

Runtime production delta: **+12 lines** (+8 for snapshot detachment, +4 for the scoped fallback). The growth preserves the held-snapshot contract and removes whole-registry retention; measurement tooling is separate (+368 lines). Tests add 59 lines; the shared test-line ceiling is untouched.

## Evidence

Focused owner tests: **52 passed** (30 query cases, 22 worker cases), 44.98 s wrapper / 40.80 s Vitest including compilation. Baseline fails the zero-copy and unrelated-row collection regressions. The independent review found a memory-only overlay transition bug in the first candidate; the final regression reproduces that bug before the repair and passes afterward.

Synthetic owner measurements use 19,500 child/run entries; imports, fixture writes, forced GC and heap snapshots are outside CPU/allocation windows. Separate allocation passes include collected objects. These are owner measurements, not whole-Gateway throughput or RPC-tail claims. The requested fast-path proof applies to these bounded ownership repairs; no live server was touched.

| Owner metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Registration unrelated rows after cache retirement | 19,499 | 0 |
| Registration reader-held heap after GC | 28.67 MB | 0.12 MB |
| Registration CPU / capture + 3 reads | 2.178 ms | 2.009 ms |
| Registration sampled allocation / capture + 3 reads | 6.079 MB | 6.111 MB |
| Durable-only topology unique child arrays (heap census) | 39,000 | 19,500 |
| Durable-only topology retained heap after GC | 13.25 MB | 12.19 MB |
| Durable-only topology build CPU | 50.10 ms | 35.68 ms |
| Durable-only topology sampled build allocation | 70.36 MB | 71.91 MB |
| Durable-only topology patch CPU | 2.78 µs | 2.35 µs |
| Durable-only topology sampled patch allocation | 3,825 B | 3,785 B |

Registration CPU uses two swapped pairs, **6,000 operations per side**; individual reductions were 14.48% and 0.22%, so retention is the main claim. Its separate allocation pass uses 3,000 operations per side (+0.52%). Topology uses five counterbalanced pairs, **25 builds and 15,000 patches per side per mode**. Sampled build allocation rose 2.2%; patch allocation fell 1.0%. The distinct-live-owner control remains separate by design: build CPU 40.70→41.19 ms, patch CPU 2.75→2.49 µs, and retained heap approximately 22.16 MB on both arms. No whole-Gateway speedup is inferred.

Heap census confirms one internal and one published child Map in both arms; the saving is shared bucket arrays, not fewer topology owners. Broad/agent/configured selections and active-only sentinel semantics remain distinct, so this PR does not claim to collapse all observed winners maps. Host load is recorded per arm in both scripts.

Root script test typechecks, matching agent/session test typecheck, changed-file lint/format, export-name collision guard and both closure guard files pass. Closure guards: 38 passed. Test-line ratchet passed with more than 31,000 lines of headroom.

Independent subagent review (**autoreview route unavailable**): the configured provider selector failed the helper's configuration preflight because it did not match operator configuration. No configuration was changed. A fresh reviewer received only the diff and relevant source; the second pass is **scoped-clean at P2+**, with the accepted snapshot finding fixed. The first two CI runs exposed a Linux Bun weak-retention assertion failure for an active worker-reply object; completing the test setup frame alone did not resolve it. Direct real-owner Linux Bun probes released both active and completed unrelated rows. The regression now observes a completed run’s fresh compact registry object, independently of the original worker reply lifetime, matching the measured retention scenario. The original full-map reader still fails this assertion. Active selected/new-owner and deletion behavior remains covered. Production code and measurements are unchanged. PR CI provides broad validation.

Reproduce with `scripts/perf/session-topology-sharing-measure.ts` (five AB/BA pairs; 25 builds and 15,000 patches per side/mode) and `scripts/perf/subagent-registration-fallback-measure.ts` (3,000 preparation + three-read operations per arm); each script header documents pinned baseline loading and isolated state.

prs.title: fix(ui): unfinished map entries disappear when editing existing values
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an unfinished Settings map entry disappears when an existing entry's value is edited.

## User Impact

Users can keep typing a new entry while changing an existing value. External configuration replacement still clears the unfinished draft, including restoration to the original value. No migration or user action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep draft continuity only for the exact result of a local child edit, using the existing collection draft owner. Unmatched external values retain the existing reset behavior; matching acknowledgements remain indistinguishable from the local edit.

Simplification review retained the narrow map adapter rather than changing shared collection lifetime policy. Production delta: +40/-3 lines; regression: +81 lines. No new effects, listeners, DOM queries, or lifecycle owners.

prs.title: fix: start managed browsers with large macOS process listings
prs.body:
Fixes #188889

## What Problem This Solves

Managed browser startup on macOS can fail before launching a browser when unrelated host process command lines make the process listing exceed 1 MiB. A fresh, unused profile then reports that headless-shell ownership could not be verified, blocking a normal about:blank open.

## User Impact

Managed profiles can start on the observed host with a process listing of approximately 1.26 MB. The profile ownership checks, executable selection, default sandbox behavior, and navigation policy are unchanged. Discovery remains bounded and still refuses startup when the command fails, times out, or exceeds the new 4 MiB limit; this is not an unbounded process scan.

## Why This Change Was Made

The macOS profile census captures all process arguments before looking for headless-shell profile users. Its 1 MiB limit was smaller than the existing 4 MiB process-list budget used by browser MCP discovery. This change aligns that one capture budget while retaining the one-second timeout and every parser, live-process, duplicate-flag, and failure path.

A narrower executable census was evaluated on the affected host. It found 542 shell processes, so individual argument queries would be expensive; batching required two scans, captured roughly 278 KB plus 755 KB, and took 259–286 ms. The existing single scan completed the approximately 1.26 MB inventory in 168–177 ms when allowed a larger bounded capture. These diagnostics support the small correction, not a browser-start performance claim. The maximum permitted output rises by 3 MiB.

## Evidence

A fresh isolated macOS runtime on a3cfe952aa942765e7081226dcb1ff999691ca8c reproduced the failure through native browser.request → /tabs/open with about:blank. The profile was stopped and no browser was spawned. Five contemporaneous captures using the original command and limits failed with ENOBUFS; no raw host process arguments were retained.

The existing launch test now uses a real subprocess to produce synthetic output above 1 MiB, preserving the actual capture boundary. Its 2 MiB startup case failed with the original ownership error before the correction and passes afterward. A 5 MiB overflow still refuses launch before profile creation or spawning.

Remote formatting, lint, affected production/test type checks, and three related browser files passed: 96 tests, including existing ownership, foreign-profile, duplicate-flag, changed-port, and cleanup controls. The affected batch took 35.13 seconds in Vitest (mostly cold transform); the test runner took 37.22 seconds. The 49-line test allocation covers only the two distinct capture outcomes and their shared fixture.

On the exact PR head, the same isolated macOS environment started Chrome through the native managed-browser path, opened about:blank, and read Example Domain through a 38-node ARIA snapshot. A file: open remained blocked and did not create a tab. A second active managed profile retained its PID and tab while the first was used. The host still exceeded the old limit: the 1 MiB capture failed while the 4 MiB capture returned 1,282,985 bytes.

A real agent using the OpenClaw runtime then read IANA's Example Domains page through Browser, delivered the expected explanation, and left the page open. The second profile remained intact. No alternate manually launched browser or sandbox relaxation was used.

Independent engineering review is clean. Canonical AutoReview covered P0–P3 on a3cfe952aa942765e7081226dcb1ff999691ca8c → 79381cbaf3a17faa3d8820824e0f00e41d85c6a7 with the unchanged launch, cleanup, locking, and sibling census context, and returned scoped-clean. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41152824747) passed its selected jobs. ClawSweeper has not produced an accessible current verdict: the first workflow was superseded before review after the evidence update, the replacement dispatch was accepted, and the observer endpoint returned HTTP 403. No ClawSweeper rating is claimed.

There are no UI layout or rendering changes; native process, tab, page-content, and ownership assertions cover the changed contract.

prs.body:
## Problem and change

Gateway config preflight imports session migration execution/recovery although it only needs the migration-complete assertion. Keep that assertion as one leaf implementation and move the byte-identical execution body to its runtime owner. Move two shared helpers to their existing owners to remove eager backedges, and update callers/mocks without a compatibility reexport.

Plugin readiness reads all pending/deferred obligations first and returns when empty. Nonempty startup still reads pending status separately: decoded obligations do not retain status and cannot replace that query. Admitted live reads, leases, inspection, config publication, settlement, warnings, legacy/deferred receipts, ambiguity refusal and profile-aware Doctor guidance remain. No schema, integrity, identity, transaction, security or MAIN-floor change. C and E remain held.

## Acceptance and measured work

Acceptance was published before measurement: committed teamBoot workload, compiled isolated Gateway, eight synthetic agents / 10,000 sessions / at least 5 GiB of synthetic state on internal disk, real authenticated WebSocket reads, plugin post-bind and cleanup. Intended cohorts: cloned/unsealed and retained boots, with empty/pending/deferred obligations kept separate. Win: shrink the static eager graph with four heavy owners absent; empty readiness two reads→one, no attributable MAIN increase or extra nonempty request. Any adverse cell of at least 20% stops for attribution. Timing requires the shared lock, load1 <24 and at least five interleaved pairs on the same platform; otherwise counts only, no latency/CPU or percentile claim.

| Config-preflight static eager closure | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Source modules | 1,616 | 958 |
| Source bytes | 12,072,562 | 7,335,026 |
| Compiled chunks | 778 | 424 |
| Compiled bytes | 8,576,941 | 4,871,168 |

These are static graph counts, not evaluated imports or a latency measurement. Four heavy owners are absent: `session-accessor.sqlite-import.ts`, `deferred-plugin-session-empty.ts`, `deferred-plugin-session-verification.ts`, `openclaw-agent-db.ts`. Base is `bdb7d4ad4afb4b337e9908b752d663bcffa48624`; candidate graph was measured at `7b8bc57fc19e96a0dfb129749dc3ee690cc35216`, whose production/scripts match final `fe80c3bb52aea1aee49a3d8b85be7c61d8140596`.

Empty pending-only SELECTs fell **1→0 in both native states**; existing all-obligation reads remain unchanged. SQL shapes still select `id, report_json, status` from `migration_runs` with `id LIKE ?`, `status IN (?)` or `IN (?,?)`, ordered by `id`. Before: pending-only then all obligations. After: all obligations, then pending-only iff nonempty. No write intervenes; SQL text and write envelopes are unchanged.

### Adverse raw counts and attribution

The one-pair whole-flow cohort is **nonpassing and confounded**: fresh all-process SQL/requests 3,407/682→5,116/856, Gateway MAIN 1,151→1,153; retained SQL 4,047→6,866. These values are retained, not averaged away, and establish no total-work or retained-seal improvement.

Fresh MAIN adds two existing legacy scans: six→eight distinct agents, one scan each, no duplicates. Retained scans reached eight→five agents. All 3,234 retained-candidate shutdown payload reads come from unchanged usage-rollup backfill. The moved execution body and 13 relevant owner files are unchanged; plugin post-bind does not drain the independent canonical/transcript/usage owners. Two independent audits found no B/D-created invocation or added-work path.

The coordinator accepted qualification on the narrow import/read counts after this attribution. Separate native pending/deferred arms were **not run**; their behavior is covered by focused owner tests and PostgreSQL conformance. No total SQL, MAIN, CPU, latency or size-scaling improvement is claimed. An optional fixture-completion experiment was discarded without a production or benchmark commit and is not acceptance evidence.

## Behavior, review and size

Owner/runtime 214 + Doctor 49 tests passed. Three missing-import fixture errors were corrected and replayed; nine source-recovery, fourteen prefix, readiness/import regressions and four final benchmark cases passed. Read-count/import regressions fail on base. Two isolated production reviews plus correction/workload/CI-fixture delta reviews are clean. Assertions remain; mock-baseline change is shrink-only.

Production **+11 LOC**, tests/helpers **−3 LOC**, tooling **+195 LOC**, other **−1 LOC**. The module boundaries require modest production growth. Source-based worker and dialect ratchets remain active; unrelated generated Markdown drift was excluded. The benchmark adds two synthetic preparation transactions, not Gateway runtime work.

Fixes #187811

## What Problem This Solves

Workboard lifecycle processing read every card and all of its child rows before deciding which cards could match a session event or need reconciliation. On a long-lived board that cost grows with history (events, comments, logs, notifications), even though only active cards can change.

In plain terms: every event and every 60-second sweep reopened the whole board and all of its history just to find the few cards that still matter. This change asks the database for that short candidate list first, then hydrates only those cards.

- **Session events**: resolve cards from the event's session/run identity instead of loading the whole board.
- **Sweep**: use a conservative SQL candidate read covering active lifecycle work and terminal worktree cleanup; the existing JS reconciliation predicate remains the final authority.
- The second full-board reload at the end of the sweep is removed; worktree cleanup runs against the same candidate set.
- No schema, config, public RPC, or persistence contract change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The store already had scoped reads (`session-links`, `worker-context`, `page`), but `syncWorkboardLifecycleEvent` and the sweep did not use one. The new `lifecycle` and `lifecycle-event` read scopes keep the selection in SQL and preserve the existing full card/child shape for the cards that are actually loaded.

The event scope is a superset of the existing matcher: exact and execution-only `subagent:workboard-*` suffix keys, derived workboard keys, exact and provisional run IDs, and recorded attempt/event links. The unchanged `workboardCardMatchesLifecycleLink` predicate still decides the final match. Terminal worktree cleanup keeps its own archived-safe branch and requires both `path` and `sourcePath`, so a discharged cleanup is excluded. The selectors use the existing Kysely query owner, not raw `db.prepare`, and both list branches preserve an explicit `boardId` constraint when supplied.

## User Impact

Long-lived Workboard boards stop paying history-sized reads on every lifecycle event and on the periodic reconciliation. Active cards and terminal worktree cleanup behave as before; settled historical cards are no longer decoded.

## Evidence

Real SQLite read against the production store with 500 settled cards, 5,000 history child rows, and one active card:

```text
historyCards: 500
historyChildRows: 5000
fullList: { cards: 501, ms: 62.2 }
lifecycleCandidates: { cards: 1, ms: 5.4 }
```

Focused regression and behavior suite:

```text
pnpm test extensions/workboard/src/lifecycle-sync.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
✓ 48 passed
```

Bounded hydration is asserted directly: a settled historical card gets a child comment with an empty required body, which full hydration would reject; the lifecycle candidate read succeeds and returns only the active card. The sweep test also asserts that the background service calls `store.list({ lifecycle: true })`.

Base red check (production changes reverted, regressions kept): `3 failed | 40 passed` — the failing cases were the scoped event read, session-scoped list, and lifecycle candidate read. Full Workboard suite after the fix: `351 passed | 11 skipped`.

Gateway lifecycle-service proof against a real SQLite store with 500 settled cards and 5,000 history child rows, one of which has an empty required comment body (full hydration would throw):

```text
completionHook: { count: 1, status: "review" }
subagentHook: { count: 1, status: "review" }
sweepListScopes: [
  { sessionKey: "agent:main:active", runId: "run-active" },
  { sessionKey: "agent:alpha:subagent:workboard-service", runId: "run-subagent" },
  { lifecycle: true }
]
fullHydrationError: true
```

Both the completion hook and the real `subagent_ended` path settled their active cards through `syncWorkboardAgentEnded` / `syncWorkboardSubagentEnded`; the periodic service used the lifecycle candidate read. None decoded the invalid historical child row. This host has no PostgreSQL service; the PostgreSQL storage/conformance path is covered by CI.

Independent running-Gateway PostgreSQL benchmark by @etzelm (recovery sweep, this head, production-shaped 336-card board): rows returned `11,616 -> 1,358` (-88%), shared buffer hits `9,402 -> 1,404` (-85%), median DB exec `30.2 ms -> 6.5 ms`. The reporter notes the event path was not exercised; the subagent trace above covers that path at the service boundary.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used source inspection of the Workboard lifecycle service and SQLite read scopes to replace both unscoped reads, then verified the regression on base and the fix against a real SQLite store. The implementer understands the code: SQL selects a conservative candidate set, and the existing lifecycle matcher and worktree cleanup predicates still own the final decisions.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenShell mirror-mode file tools trimmed the supplied path before resolving mounts. Reading or writing literal `" x.txt"` silently addressed the distinct sibling `"x.txt"`, potentially overwriting the wrong file.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the literal `filePath` in `OpenShellFsBridge.resolveTarget`; keep the existing mount-containment guard and invocation-base normalization. Original fix by @wangmiao0668000666. Precedent: #187554; related: #172869.

## Evidence

[Independent built-Gateway proof with the real OpenShell server](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187777#issuecomment-6534999635).

In an isolated disposable Linux machine with its own Docker daemon, two main Gateway turns read the decoy and overwrote it; two candidate turns read/update the literal leading-space path and leave the decoy unchanged. Ordinary-path controls pass on both. Real remote sandbox files match the mirror after publication. No workstation socket, host credentials or paid provider used. The disposable machine was deleted after proof.

The consolidated existing owner suite passes 30 tests; its literal-path regression fails on main. Existing directory, max-byte and symlink boundaries remain. Test LOC does not grow. Documentation records literal-path behavior.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: revert restores prior normalization; no migration or stored-format change. Blast radius is OpenShell mirror-mode tools on paths with leading/trailing whitespace. Users who unintentionally relied on trimming now address the literal file they supplied. Mount containment and shell quoting are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(codex): keep literal node-adopted transcript cwd
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Adopting a Codex CLI session that was started in a directory whose name carries whitespace (a valid POSIX name, e.g. `"/tmp/job "`) rewrote the transcript header cwd to the trimmed sibling. The transcript importer and the session manager consume that header as the session's filesystem identity, so continued sessions resolved files against the wrong directory.

Precedent: #187554 ("The configured directory's whitespace belongs to its filesystem identity"). Sibling: #172869.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous head passed the literal cwd only to the transcript importer (`afterCreate`), but creation initializes the transcript header **before** `afterCreate` runs: `createGatewaySession` normalizes `spawnedCwd` into `runtimeCwd` with `normalizeOptionalString` (a trim) and persists that into the transcript header, and the importer's `ensureTranscriptHeader` then returns early because the header already exists. ClawSweeper's review of this PR caught exactly that: the persisted header kept the trimmed cwd, so the session manager still resolved the wrong directory.

This head fixes the whole path under the invariant "spawnedCwd is a filesystem identity; only blank counts as absent":

- `extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-node-adoption.ts` passes the literal record cwd as `spawnedCwd` (the guard still treats blank-after-trim as absent).
- The owning normalization in `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts` now resolves `spawnedCwd` via `resolveSpawnedCwd` (`src/gateway/session-cwd-identity.ts`): first defined source, non-blank read, **whitespace preserved** — so the literal value survives into `runtimeCwd`, the persisted session entry, and the transcript header.
- Initialization recovery in `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent-session-create.ts` matches the literal `spawnedCwd` plus the trimmed form rows persisted before this change, so crash recovery still finalizes old initializing entries (see Shipped-run proof below for the legacy-row recovery run).

The ACP adoption sibling already passed a literal cwd; with the gateway normalization fixed it now persists literally too. ACP session metadata (`acpMetaMatches`) is a separate contract and intentionally unchanged.

Classification: `behavior-completing` (extends the literal-path contract to the node-adoption transcript owner).

## User Impact

Continuing a node-hosted Codex session from a whitespace-named directory now records the literal directory in the transcript header, so subsequent turns resolve files in the directory the session actually started in. Existing stored sessions are untouched — old trimmed values keep loading as-is (data compatibility proven below).

## Evidence

### Real-creation test (mock assertion replaced per review)

- Test: `persists the adopted cwd in the transcript header (%s)` in `extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-node-home.test.ts` — the adopted session is created through the **real** `createOrReuseNodeAdoptedSession` / `createSessionEntry` path against a temp store, then the persisted transcript header is read back from the store via `readSessionTranscriptEvents` and asserted byte-for-byte (`cwd: "/tmp/job "` survives; trimmed-sibling control `cwd: "/tmp/job"` stays trimmed). The previous mock-call assertion was removed: it passed while the transcript-header bug remained.
- Remote run (10.54.159.54, `vitest run ... --maxWorkers=1`, repo root config):
  - `extensions/codex/src/session-catalog-node-home.test.ts` — 9/9 passed
  - `src/gateway/session-create-{atomic-initialization,collision,diagnostics,display-name,fork-entry,inheritance,initial-transcript,preparation,target}.test.ts` — 61/61 passed
  - `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent{,.acp-binding,-session-catalog,.session-list,.session-color}.test.ts` — 27/27 passed
  - Final staged code re-run: codex node-home + session-create-preparation + session-create-inheritance + session-create-atomic-initialization + runtime-agent — 58/58 passed
- Local static checks: `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` clean; `oxlint` on all 5 changed files clean.
- Not tested: live Codex CLI on a paired node (the wire protocol path is exercised with the repo's catalog fixture, which is the established boundary for this owner); Windows node transports.

## Shipped-run proof (2026-10-30)

Plain node script (`proof-816/proof-shipped.mjs` in the worktree) drives the **built dist** of each worktree end to end: it builds the real plugin runtime (`createPluginRuntime`), calls the real creation owner `runtime.agent.session.createSessionEntry` with the codex harness `initialEntry` and `spawnedCwd: "/tmp/job "` (literal trailing space; both `/tmp/job ` and its trimmed sibling exist on disk with different marker files), against an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, then reads the persisted transcript header bytes straight from the session-store SQLite (`transcript_events`).

- **RED on base** (`/media/vdc/oc-base1` @ `f0401d55f`, dist built once): `entry.spawnedCwd = "/tmp/job"`, transcript header cwd = `"/tmp/job"` — the literal directory was rewritten to the trimmed sibling.
- **GREEN on head** (`347699d55`, this PR): `entry.spawnedCwd = "/tmp/job "`, transcript header cwd = `"/tmp/job "` — literal trailing space persisted byte-for-byte; the trimmed sibling `/tmp/job` was not used.
- **Data-model compatibility**: the base-created store (trimmed values) opens cleanly on the fixed build — the entry resolves and both `entry.spawnedCwd` and the transcript header keep their original trimmed bytes; no migration, old rows untouched.
- **Legacy recovery**: a real crash was simulated on the base build (SIGKILL between commit and finalization), leaving a genuine `initializationPending` row with the pre-fix trimmed bytes; the fixed build's `recoverMatchingInitialEntry` retry with the literal cwd request recovered and finalized that row (`recovered sessionId f345d2d4…`, values unchanged). A head-created literal row crashed and recovered the same way, staying literal.
- CI on head `347699d55`: PR checks (Actions runs 41009346802–41009353275) — see check results on the PR.
