prs.title: fix: show effective next runs for one-shot automations
prs.body:
Closes #188858

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Automations editor presents the original one-shot occurrence as its only execution after the same task has been rearmed for a later run.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish the configured time from the effective next execution, without accidentally replacing the authored time by saving an unrelated edit. Running and paused tasks no longer promise a pending execution from a stale deadline. No scheduler, retry, permission, or data-format changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The configured occurrence and runtime deadline are different facts. The existing schedule summary now shows both for an unchanged saved one-shot; editing a new time still previews the draft. List, detail header, and editor share the existing job-status presentation owner for running, paused, and next-run state. Timestamp differences are not guessed to mean a continuation rather than a retry.

## Evidence

- Production-bundle Chromium reproduction **failed on base** `4a393be419f30ecfd65972fe3ea1416c6f707316`: a fictional 12:00 configured occurrence with a 12:10 runtime deadline rendered only “Runs once at … 12:00 PM.”
- The same browser flow **passes with the fix**, including an unrelated-name save that omits both `patch.schedule` and `patch.state`, then reopening the editor (1.48s test time; 19.95s harness wall time). Browser timezone UTC, en-US, 1280×900, light theme; synthetic Gateway RPC data, not a live model-backed scheduling test.
- Focused UI/form consumers: **56 tests passed across 5 files** (6.62s command wall time). Regression covers mutable runtime refresh, running, paused-with-stale-deadline, no-next-run, and a new unsaved timestamp; existing tests preserve recurring forms and unchanged exact timestamp precision.
- UI production typecheck, all UI test typecheck shards, targeted oxlint, formatting, controller guard, i18n verification, test-line/line-cap/max-lines ratchets, and `git diff --check` passed. Production Control UI build passed.
- Independent local autoreview: Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium/Ultrafast, P0–P2, final local candidate against the base above: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The pinned Solid 2 rc.18 declarations were supplied; review did not execute tests. Published source tree `08818e870f130aec743064d45be6699dcf71aaf6` matches that reviewed and tested candidate; the publisher-only commit's human credit was repaired without changing the tree.
- [Exact-head CI run 41148782947](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41148782947) **passed** on `0c51ea8be75c27ae8f9926c97b7c8334026038c4`, including UI tests, browser E2E, types, lint, i18n, performance, and the CI gate. Current checks have no failures or pending work.
- [ClawSweeper’s exact-head Codex review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188864#issuecomment-6536484427) completed with **no findings** and **no before-merge items**; it inspected the screenshot pair and rated proof sufficient. The PR is open and ready for maintainer review, not merged or deployed.

### Before

![Before: original occurrence presented as the only run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9ebb9ac1-0e67-4d8e-9f83-bd868a6e411d)

### After

![After: configured time and effective next run shown separately](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef0622a6-557f-48dc-bda6-d031764c5203)

<details>
<summary>Scope and test cost</summary>

The simplify pass consolidated duplicate next-run presentation rather than adding a banner or state store. Production delta: +41 net lines; tests: +135 lines, with a task-specific regression allocation. No new effects, listeners, or DOM queries in production. Measured CI regression runtime: browser flow **2.944s** (file 2.966s), mutable runtime view **0.419s**; about **3.36s** combined test execution, excluding collection/setup. The shared browser E2E step took 26s; the three broad UI test steps took 344s, 292s, and 266s. These broad lane durations are not claimed as this patch’s marginal cost.

</details>

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Security, permission, or authentication blocks can leave users without a useful next step even when a supported recovery path is known.

## User Impact

Agents are instructed to explain what was blocked and why, then offer only verified recovery steps with the exact UI path or configuration key and who can make the change. Scoped access or approval is preferred over disabling safeguards. No permissions, tools, settings, or enforcement change; prompt guidance does not guarantee model behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extend the existing shared safety prompt consumed by core **Care** and native Codex, Copilot, and Agents API instructions. This keeps one wording owner, survives provider section overrides, and reaches full/minimal prompts without a new SDK export or duplicate native policy. Core `none` and raw Copilot runs retain their existing exclusions. Unknown remedies are omitted, not announced or invented.

Simplification: reuse the existing safety builder rather than introduce another prompt API. Production grows by 2 net lines; tests by 30 net lines. The separate test-line allocation covers the core mode/override regression and distinct native instruction carriers; no new fixture boot or timer is added.

## Evidence

- **Red/green:** all four new core prompt cases fail for missing guidance with the base production owner at `9aa59252cb0dc198a90a74f75257f7f0114b5215` (44.18s wall). The final candidate passes **258 tests across eight files** with `pnpm test <files> --maxWorkers=1` in **108.43s wall**. Coverage includes full/minimal/CLI prompts, provider overrides, all three native carriers, existing raw/none exclusions, and prompt-prefix stability.
- **Changed-file test cost:** safety builder <1ms, core prompt 154ms, Codex prompt 66ms, Copilot attempt 4.245s, Agents API instructions 4.939s of reported test execution. Cold compilation/imports dominate the combined wall time. CI seconds are not yet available.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` and narrowed changed-core/extension-test typechecks pass, retaining the original ambient declaration inputs. Focused core/extension lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, test-line ratchet, and docs links (16,180 checked; zero broken) pass. Generated prompt snapshots are current (six artifacts checked).
- Independent **autoreview / Codex gpt-6.1-sol**, P0–P3, base `9aa59252cb0dc198a90a74f75257f7f0114b5215` to the final local snapshot committed unchanged as `34593d015722461872b7bab80d58fe843379c6b7`: **scoped-clean**, no actionable findings. The available local ClawSweeper runner checkout was dirty, so this follows the autoreview + hosted-review fallback.

**Existing local gate limitation:** `plugin-sdk:surface:check` fails identically with the base and final production owner: public exports 3844/3843, callable exports 2228/2227, deprecated exports 221/219, and deprecated agent-harness-runtime exports 15/13. This PR changes no SDK export or budget.

prs.title: fix #188285: route native /tools through the selected-model stage
prs.body:
## Summary

- Problem: A native `/tools` command listed tools for the configured default model instead of the target session's saved model, so a session saved on a Codex runtime with `codexDynamicToolsExclude: ["github_publish"]` still saw `github_publish` advertised; the ordinary text `/tools` route honored the saved selection (#188285).
- Solution: Route native `/tools` (including `/tools compact` and `/tools verbose`) through the existing selected-model stage — the same stage the fast path already uses for `/compact` and `/context` — before dispatching to the command handlers.
- What changed: `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-native-slash-fast-path.ts` (`needsModelSelection` now covers `/tools`); regression cases in `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-native-slash-fast-path.test.ts`; shipped-entry proof test `src/auto-reply/native-tools-selected-model.e2e.test.ts`.
- What did NOT change: The text-command `/tools` route, the tool inventory builder, Codex exclusion filtering, authorization checks, and the fast-path handling of every other command are untouched. `/tools` replies remain command responses and never start agent generation.

Fixes #188285

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Native `/tools` dispatched with the default `provider`/`model` because the native slash fast path ran the command before the selected-model stage; the saved session model's runtime exclusions (Codex `codexDynamicToolsExclude`) never reached the inventory call, so `github_publish` was advertised against policy.
- **Real environment tested:** This branch's worktree on Linux x64, Node v24.20.0, pnpm 12.15.0. The shipped entry point `getReplyFromConfig` was driven with a real native `/tools` turn, a real on-disk session store holding a saved user selection (`openai/gpt-4.1-mini`, Codex runtime) against a default `openai/gpt-4.1` (OpenClaw runtime), static model rows, a managed in-process Gateway request binding, and the real effective-tool-inventory chain; only the agent-generation boundary is mocked (a command reply never reaches it).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  pnpm install
  OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
    src/auto-reply/native-tools-selected-model.e2e.test.ts \
    src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-native-slash-fast-path.test.ts \
    src/auto-reply/reply/commands-info.test.ts \
    src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-native-slash-fast-path.status.test.ts \
    src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.fast-path.test.ts
  ```
  (`OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1` keeps test file logs under the repo on this host; see "What was not tested".)
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```text
  before (production file restored to unmodified main, same shipped-entry test):
    × applies the saved session runtime's Codex exclusion through the shipped entry point
      AssertionError: expected 'Available tools...' not to contain 'github_publish'
      received list: ... get_goal, github_identity_status, github_publish, ls, ...  (both excluded tools advertised)
  after (this patch, same test):
    ✓ applies the saved session runtime's Codex exclusion through the shipped entry point
      reply lists tools with github_publish and github_identity_status absent
  supporting suites on this head:
    ✓ get-reply-native-slash-fast-path.test.ts: 30 passed (30) — incl. native /tools + /tools verbose dispatch receiving the saved provider/model
    ✓ commands-info.test.ts + fast-path.status: 37 passed (37)
    ✓ get-reply.fast-path.test.ts: 9 passed (9)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Through the shipped entry point, the native `/tools` reply for the target session no longer advertises `github_publish`/`github_identity_status` when the saved Codex selection excludes them, matching the ordinary text route; before the patch the same run advertised both.
- **What was not tested:** No real channel delivery or provider generation was exercised (command replies short-circuit before both, by design). This host's `/` is world-writable without the sticky bit, so the secure-temp-root guard fails for tests resolving the default rolling log path (pristine main fails the same way); runs use the repo-supported `OPENCLAW_TEST_FILE_LOG=1` test-log route, which CI does not need. tsgo could not run locally (GLIBC too old for the native binary); no new types were added and CI type lanes remain the guardrail.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test + shipped-entry e2e
- Target test file: `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-native-slash-fast-path.test.ts` (dispatch receives the selected provider/model) and `src/auto-reply/native-tools-selected-model.e2e.test.ts` (end-to-end exclusion through `getReplyFromConfig`)
- Scenario locked in: an authorized native `/tools` (and `/tools verbose`) turn targeting a session with a saved user model selection reaches command handling with that selected provider/model, and the shipped-entry reply omits the runtime-excluded brokered GitHub tools.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: both cases fail on unpatched main with the exact wrong behavior from the issue (default `openai` model at dispatch; `github_publish` advertised at the entry point) and sit next to the existing `/context` selected-model case they mirror.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: the native slash-command fast path only deferred `/compact` and `/context` to the selected-model stage (`needsModelSelection`); `/tools` was dispatched immediately with the default model, so model-dependent tool inventory (including Codex runtime exclusions) was computed for the wrong model.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no fast-path case asserted which model reaches `/tools` dispatch, and no shipped-entry case asserted the runtime exclusion survives native invocation.

## User Impact

prs.title: fix(agents): renew Sign-in-with-ChatGPT credentials for each model request
prs.body:
Closes #175801

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Sign-in-with-ChatGPT model requests keep sending the access credential captured at attempt preparation, so an expired or rotated token fails every subsequent request and the attempt ends in a terminal auth failure after settled tool work.

## User Impact

User impact: SIWC (chatgpt-token-sharing) sessions now carry the owner's current access credential on every model request and recover from a single `token_expired` 401 with one forced re-acquisition and one retried request, instead of dying at the first credential expiry mid-turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

The stream wrapper previously captured the resolved API key once at creation and replayed it for the lifetime of the attempt, and the renewal trigger matched prose on thrown errors — which never fired because the Responses client surfaces provider 401s as projected stream terminals, not rejections. The fix:

- `createRenewableRequestApiKeyResolver` (in `run/auth-store.ts`, owned by the auth controller) re-resolves the selected seat's current access through the canonical `getApiKeyForModelCore` owner with `lockedProfile: true` on every call, reading the live auth state rather than a static snapshot. No production code is mocked or injected; the refresh queue, rotation fences, and pre-expiry margin come from the real owner.
- `wrapEmbeddedAgentStreamApiKey` calls the resolver before each request; the live resolution leads the captured key and any static override, and non-renewable credentials keep the captured-key-first contract.
- `createRenewalGuardedStream` (new `stream-renewal-guard.ts`) buffers a provider stream until its first output event. A terminal `error` event carrying a structured 401 token-expiry before any output triggers exactly one `forceRefresh: true` re-acquisition and one retried request. The 401 fact is read only from deterministic projection fields: `errorCode === "401"` or the projection's status prefix (the colon form the local projection adds, and the SDK form that already embeds the status, e.g. `"401 The authentication token is expired"`). The expiry fact comes from structured codes (`token_expired` / `expired_token` in `errorCode`/`errorType`) or a bounded regex over `errorMessage`/`errorBody`; prose alone never classifies. The final commit closes a real gap the reviewer proof exposed: the actual OpenAI Responses client projects a 401 whose message keeps the SDK's status-embedded prefix without the colon and whose provider code shadows the HTTP status (`errorCode=token_expired`), which the earlier colon-only gate missed.
- The renewal budget is per source stream: a replacement stream's terminals pass through untouched, so a revoked grant surfaces once without looping, and a 401 that arrives after output was forwarded is never retried (no replay of settled tool work or partial output).

The resolver is created in `auth-controller.ts` (the lifecycle owner with live state access) and threaded through the existing runtime → dispatch → stream-settle path; the stream wrapper only receives the resolver, so per-request logic stays out of the dispatch file.

## Evidence

**Focused tests (44/44 pass, standalone vitest, 1 worker, re-verified after the SDK-401 classification commit):**

```
 src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/stream-renewable-api-key.test.ts  29 tests  PASS
 src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-store.test.ts            9 tests  PASS
 src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/stream-resolution.test.ts         6 tests  PASS
```

The 29-test file exercises the real `AssistantMessageEventStream` objects, real `CodexApiError` instances with `projectProviderError` projections (the exact production terminal shape — including the real SDK `APIError` shape whose message keeps the status-embedded `"401 "` prefix and whose provider code shadows the HTTP status), and the canonical `getApiKeyForModelCore` owner against a fresh isolated state dir (`withOpenClawTestState`) — including externally renewed seats picked up on the next request and unrenewable expired seats keeping the captured credential. No production code is mocked in the renewal path.

**Gates (all clean on the changed files):** oxfmt format, oxlint, import-cycle check (0). TypeScript: the scoped `tsc -p` over the changed files reports 0 errors, including after the final SDK-401 classification commit.

**Real-transport authority chain (local Responses endpoint, production client):** the production `createOpenAIResponsesTransportStreamFn` client (`createResponsesTransportExecutor` → `failTransportStream` terminal) runs against a local `node:http` endpoint that emulates the incident wire behavior, wrapped by the branch's real `selectEmbeddedAgentStream` / `wrapApiKey` / guard — 3/3 checks:

```
=== Real-transport authority chain (local Responses endpoint) ===
PASS  C1: allowed selected-account request is admitted through the real transport  (bearers: ["siwc-access-A"], terminal: done)
PASS  C2: post-settlement wire 401 token_expired recovers via one forced reacquisition  (terminal: done, refreshCalls=1, bearers: ["siwc-access-A","siwc-access-A","siwc-access-B"])
PASS  C3: revoked account is rejected once, terminally, with the structured 401 projection  (requests: 1, reacquireAttempts: 0, refreshCalls: 0, terminal: token_expired/invalid_request_error)
```

C1 is the allowed selected-account request: the server observes the owner-resolved bearer and returns 200; the stream completes. C2 is the incident: the first request settles, the server then expires the captured access (HTTP 401 `token_expired` on the wire for the next request), and the guard's one forced re-acquisition rotates the bearer so the single retried request completes — exactly one unauthorized request, no replay of settled work. C3 is the revoked account: the owner hands out no current access, the captured key leads, the request fails once with the projected 401 `token_expired` terminal, and nothing loops or retries. The pre-fix classifier missed exactly this wire shape (its 401 gate only accepted the colon prefix or `errorCode === "401"`, while the real client projects `errorCode=token_expired` with the status embedded in the message) — C2 failing on the pre-fix code and passing after the classification commit is what closed that gap.

**Issue-prescribed proof** (extracted-function harness: synthetic credential owner, virtual clock, fake transport; Phase A uses the published `openclaw@2026.10.5` wrappers extracted verbatim from dist, Phase B uses the branch code with the real guard, real `AssistantMessageEventStream` terminals, and real `CodexApiError` projections; Part B8 drives the real resolver against the canonical `getApiKeyForModelCore` owner on a temp state dir) — 12/12 checks:

```
=== Phase A: published openclaw@2026.10.5 (pre-fix) ===
PASS  A1 (bug): captured A is still used after the owner renewed to B  (key used: siwc-access-A, owner access: siwc-access-B)
PASS  A2 (bug): 401 token_expired surfaces terminally with no request retry  (inner calls after 401: 1)

=== Phase B: branch fix/siwc-request-credential-renewal (post-fix) ===
PASS  B1: each request carries the owner's current access (externally renewed B is picked up)  (keys: ["siwc-access-A","siwc-access-B"])
PASS  B2: expiry after settled work recovers via one forced reacquisition  (delivered=true, refreshCalls=1, final key=siwc-access-B)
PASS  B3: one unauthorized request + one retried request (no loop, no replay of settled work)  (keys: ["siwc-access-A","siwc-access-A","siwc-access-B"])
PASS  B4: 401 after output is surfaced once without retry or a second turn  (inner calls: 1, events: start,text_start,text_delta,error)
PASS  B5: non-token-expired 401 surfaces once without renewal  (inner calls: 1)
PASS  B6: revoked grant surfaces once without looping  (inner calls: 1, refreshCalls: 1)
PASS  B7: static credentials keep the captured-key-first contract  (key: static-K)

=== Part B8: real resolver + canonical owner (temp state) ===
PASS  B8a: real owner resolves the seat's current access
PASS  B8b: externally renewed seat is picked up on the next request
PASS  B8c: unrenewable expired seat keeps the captured credential
```

**Shipped-entry live proof (running source-mode gateway, fake OpenAI Responses endpoint, real `agent` RPC):** the gateway boots and accepts the turn through the real `agent`/`agent.wait` RPCs with the new wrapper wired end-to-end. Gap to note: the proof host's free memory stayed under the 4 GB guardrail budget (user applications), and the cold source-mode turn did not settle within the wait window on the final attempt, so the model request could not be observed on the wire; the provider-level per-request behavior is covered by the Phase A/B proof above, which drives the real `selectEmbeddedAgentStream` / `wrapEmbeddedAgentStreamApiKey` / `createRenewalGuardedStream` code with the real stream terminal types.

**Data-model compatibility:** no persisted schema, config key, or auth-store file format changes; the auth store file shape is untouched. The change is additive in-memory state access only.

**Upgrade from published stable:** Phase A of the proof runs against the published `openclaw@2026.10.5` package (installed from npm) to demonstrate the pre-fix behavior; the upgrade path is purely in-process behavior with no stored-state migration.

prs.title: feat(configure): shared model defaults for fleets
prs.body:
Closes #180126
Related: #123871, #131153

## What Problem This Solves

- On explicit multi-agent fleets, `openclaw configure --section model` always writes the model setup and the provider credential to one agent, so a fleet-wide model and provider setup takes one configure run per agent.

## User Impact

- Explicit fleets with two or more agents get a scope prompt: `One agent` (default, unchanged behavior) or `Shared defaults`.
- `Shared defaults` writes primary, catalog and allowlist to `agents.defaults` and stores the provider credential in the shared auth store, so every agent that inherits defaults resolves both the model and the credential.
- `One agent`, single-agent installs and agents with their own model settings keep the current write path.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `configure.model-scope.ts` asks for the scope; `One agent` keeps the agent-owned path from #123871.
- `promptAuthConfig` takes a model write target: shared mode writes `agents.defaults`, starts the model pickers from `agents.defaults` and sends the credential write to the shared main auth store.
- A fleet without a System Agent that picks `Shared defaults` gets configure's existing agent question for the credential and catalog owner.
- The custom-provider API-key prompt receives the setup target's workspace, including the retry after a failed endpoint probe; the replaced default-agent lookup throws on explicit multi-agent fleets.
- In shared mode both custom-alias validators (the interactive prompt and `applyCustomApiConfig`) check `agents.defaults`, so an alias one agent uses privately does not block a shared alias.

## Evidence

- Real CLI: `openclaw configure --section model` driven in a terminal session.
- Real loopback gateway on the same state: `agents.list`, `models.list` per agent, and one agent turn per agent.
- Turns go to a loopback provider endpoint that records each request's API key (shown masked) and answers 401, so a turn that reaches it ends with exit 1.

prs.title: fix(compaction): preserve active request provenance
prs.body:
## Problem

Compaction could replace the active human request with a later internal observation, or revive completed human work during an independent internal run. The first revision also rejected a second recovery after the production semantic-window reader archived the original admitted request.

## Solution

- Carry the admitted request boundary from the runtime through AgentSession into core compaction, with explicit unresolved/none/legacy-inference selection.
- Centralize recorded-source attribution for summary input, preserved excerpts, and token accounting. Clear stale generated pending asks without rewriting unrelated summary sections.
- When a **processed** request is outside the current semantic window, reuse the existing bounded checkpoint request. Newer human steering wins; internal updates preserve that request or authoritative none. Missing **unprocessed** admitted input still rejects.
- Reuse the existing compaction checkpoint; no new persisted state, configuration, or schema. Replace the redundant in-memory mapping test with persisted, repeated-recovery coverage.

This is an independent remediation related to #178477, with credit to @dmitryvostryakov for the original report and implementation. Request provenance remains separate from general model-quality concerns.

## Verification

- **Base red:** all three repeated-recovery cases fail at `a085f281e904` with `invalid_session: Compaction cannot find the admitted request.` on the second recovery.
- **Rebased head:** `a9c37408306168b27b2b777de4e9165e0c9eb76b`, based on main `3523ef6747820e3253442a633dc09888c4cdf5fe`. Both commits are patch-identical to the published pre-rebase revision; no conflicts or new behavior changes.
- **Current-head focused proof:** 96 tests passed across eight files, including persisted repeated recovery, compaction provenance and request selection, registered safeguards, runtime recovery, and host seed handling.
- Persisted boundary cases reopen through production `SessionManager.openAsync(..., { compaction: true })`, verify the original request is absent, and complete a second automatic compaction: human request survives internal updates; internal selection remains none; newer human steering supersedes the old request. Missing pending input still rejects.
- Focused lint, formatting, mock-export ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed on the rebased tree. The mock-export ratchet was the failing check in the prior CI run.
- The prior repair's independent P0–P2 review was scoped-clean; unchanged patches retain that review. Earlier core, agents-sessions tests, and Plugin SDK test TypeScript checks passed.
- Proof uses the real SQLite reader and AgentSession with deterministic fallback; it does not claim a live-provider run. Broad CI must run on the new head.

## Scope

Ready-for-review preparation only. Do not merge or backport.

prs.title: fix: preserve watchdog causes in automation failures
prs.body:
Related: #138528

## What Problem This Solves

When the session watchdog stops a scheduled agent turn, cleanup can replace the recorded stop reason, and a valid recurring task can lose its next scheduled run. The follow-up also preserves the actual refusal when an unstarted event cannot be re-admitted after a configuration publication.

## User Impact

Named and isolated scheduled runs keep a fixed watchdog cause in history and diagnostics. Chat alerts explain whether the execution deadline or lack of semantic progress stopped the run and direct the operator to inspect automation history before retrying. Valid recurring tasks remain enabled; started one-shot tasks are not replayed. Cancellation, restart, invalid operator sources and provider rate-limit stops retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the existing controller-owned stop reason through the existing completion owners, then let Cron's scheduling and notification owners consume only its two recognized values. Raw provider/tool/cleanup prose cannot authorize chat disclosure. Reuse upstream's stop Error and preserve its rate-limit classification; remove the older optional-reply workaround now covered by upstream. No new schema, configuration, persistent state, retry scheduler or public hook.

This is the watchdog-attribution subset of the linked issue. Immediate exec-denial classification and the historical approval trigger remain outside this PR.

## Evidence

Validation for the current two-file follow-up is pinned to upstream `9db139fcf842303a2acb091f1eead2a45d0b1cf2`, candidate tree `05a2f1bc28e829e87548a5059f1fba75f17ef8f0`, full introduced diff SHA-256 `00d278b651584c1d2e38c45c8ad9c7601ea758de4790107e7b7de588f8523dcb` (20 files). It repairs the synchronous config re-admission refusal identified in the review of published head `7c54b8f9c7a8e2c6cb85cc0bdb77a1a430ec549e`.

**Re-admission contract and fresh behavior proof:** upstream commit `4217e957da91629c74db29b4a96d7692d10b3d55` established that a configuration publication re-admits an accepted, unstarted background event under current policy; a refused attempt reports its actual failure and leaves no queued work. The previous watchdog projection captured the old configuration error before re-admission could replace it. Projection now occurs after re-admission handling but before ordinary custody cancellation can abort the signal. It does not bypass producer checks, add retries, change policy, or replay a started event.

The existing production-composition suite now covers a retiring producer that honors held custody but refuses new retention. Admission, dispatch, SQLite, queue ownership and settlement remain real; model decisions and source-owner fixture state are controlled. On published production the new case fails with the obsolete configuration error; the candidate returns the actual producer refusal, performs no second model execution/write, releases all source references, empties the queue and leaves no cancellable settled occurrence.

  Received: "Error: Session event configuration changed; retry under the current policy"

```

```

Targeted types, typed lint, pinned formatting and diff checks pass.

**Changed-file cost and pinned-runtime control:** the standalone canonical Bun run passes all **23/23** cases in **78.842s** wall time (Vitest72.09s); the new refusal case takes **2284ms**. This existing file exceeds30s because it composes native storage, real deferred admission, source custody, policy revalidation and actual tool effects across23 scenarios. A helper-only error assertion cannot protect this failure. The new case extends that shared fixture; no new suite, timer, polling, test-only production export or test timeout was added. CI seconds for this follow-up are not available until its new head runs. Node and Bun cover the same23cases; these are not counted as46distinct behaviors.

There are no failed or pending checks in the verified rollup. Earlier [CI at7c54b8f9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40201098323) remains historical evidence. Local consumer proof and versioned Gateway evidence below remain separate from remote CI. No main sync was performed because the branch is mergeable and this finding belongs to the PR.

**Historical architecture repair and regression controls (tree `930526e5917f07cde824672b88d72dd7e2949f46`):** published head `0f632175dee5e78f49a4066693514daeab205971` failed the architecture guard with a real static import cycle through named-session completion, Cron execution errors and provider/plugin runtime. Local exact-head control reproduces one cycle; exact upstream has none. The repair moves the unchanged closed watchdog projection and fixed text into a lightweight leaf and migrates all consumers; the heavier execution-error module is restored exactly to upstream. Both full static and runtime import-graph checks pass. No code or test result is hidden behind an aggregate gate.

At that prior tree, complete consumer regression: **247/247 tests across13files passed**. Targeted types, typed lint, pinned Bun/oxfmt formatting and diff checks pass. Docs lint from the unchanged documentation revision is reused. Product timing and test timeouts were not shortened.

**Reused built Gateway proof from prior tree `930526e5917f07cde824672b88d72dd7e2949f46`: PASS. This is not a fresh Gateway execution of the current re-admission repair.** Canonical private-QA preparation passed in260.280seconds; the complete three-route proof passed in1008.462seconds including startup/cleanup. Its actual tools stopped after900957–900990ms on the natural900000ms watchdog. No injected outcome, shortened timer or replaced completion owner.

The owner repair used a separate run identity with no quiet-tool invocation. First-alert suppression was preserved. This natural proof covers semantic-stall; deadline, rate-limit and cancellation/restart precedence remain distinct consumer regressions. All source hashes, the index tree and full diff match the frozen candidate.


**Fresh independent review of the entire 20-file candidate:** canonical Codex completed two P0–P3 passes in 91.758s; validated scoped-clean, zero actionable findings. Each pass received the entire introduced patch and its own batch of full source context. The assessment was static: the reviewer did not execute tests or independently verify the complete import graph. All reviewed source/context hashes and the frozen diff remained unchanged. The earlier 19-file review missed the later hosted P2 and is retained as historical evidence, not used as approval of this repair.

**Limits:** the Gateway proof uses a controlled local model and QA channel. It is not a Telegram, live-provider, current stable-upgrade or current restart test. The wider linked issue is only partially addressed. All preceding natural-watchdog, original shipped-entry red/green and restart evidence remain versioned historical proof; they are not relabeled as fresh runtime proof of this re-admission repair. prs.title: fix(plugins): prepare Doctor provider checks asynchronously
prs.body:
Related: #166526

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor's provider checks can block progress while preparing plugin callbacks. Moving preparation behind an await must also preserve two existing behaviors: an unavailable setup source produces that plugin's diagnostic while healthy siblings continue, and a loaded runtime-only provider alias identifies its eligible owner for a fresh inspection.

## User Impact

Doctor's OAuth migration, provider hints, catalog validation, and local embedding-policy checks prepare plugin sources asynchronously. Healthy setup contributions remain available when another plugin's source is unavailable, and current eligible runtime aliases retain their callbacks without borrowing an older instance's private state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing generation worker and retain each provider inspection through its awaited callbacks and cleanup. Preserve auto-enable ordering, auth scopes, and explicitly retained runtime registries, including empty selections. Recheck cache and metadata authority after awaits before publishing a result.

Keep a settled source-acquisition failure in the existing inventory-owned setup instance so synchronous consumers can produce their usual diagnostics without retrying capture. Source operations mark their own failures; later source-preparation RPCs additionally attest their actual function handle. This provenance is separate from capture deadlines. Cancellation, lost authority, worker/native custody failures, and cleanup failures still reject preparation. Dependency-link staging cleanup cannot become an ordinary unavailable-plugin diagnostic. Captured directory facts preserve invalid-directory diagnostics through recovery, while unexpected private file-type changes remain fatal.

Loaded registries supply only eligible alias-owner hints. Independently acquired inspections determine the current aliases and own fresh callbacks. The full Doctor batch-custody guard and phase-level responsiveness proof follow separately.

## Evidence

- The current-main integration preserves preparation metrics alongside source-failure provenance, error codes, native custody and cleanup. All 98 focused setup, provider, worker, codec, source-lookup, inspection and metrics tests passed. Both affected type graphs, focused lint, formatting, line-cap and exact test-line guards passed; an independent isolated P0–P2 review found no actionable issue. The direct-capture fixture now supplies main’s required package kind.
- The focused provider and lifecycle suite passed 91 tests, covering healthy siblings, unavailable sources, required dependencies, malformed metadata, no synchronous retry, cancellation and authority loss, private traversal and descriptor failures, recovery directory facts, native custody, and independent provider aliases.
- Before this main integration, 29 worker, codec, and source-inspection integration tests passed, including preservation of `SyntaxError`, callback failures, empty selections, native admission, and cleanup.
- The private directory, symlink, validation, and descriptor regressions failed first. Original-source failures remain per-plugin diagnostics; the corresponding private failures stay fatal even when the same Error object is reused.
- Core and plugin-platform TypeScript, focused typed lint, formatting, the mock-factory guard, the file-size guard, and the test-line guard pass. The allocation records exactly 940 added test lines. Independent P0–P2 review of the correction and the complete current-main integration is clean.
- Historical prior-head CI run [41146850291](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41146850291), for `ccce5cb12ee71dc317e4d55554b5503187af5b64`, finished with only `checks-ui-e2e (4/7)` and its dependent `openclaw/ci-gate` failing. The UI shard passed 543 tests and failed `docks Details in wide conversations and preserves manual intent, drafts, and independent scrolling`: its unscoped `Panels` locator at line 305 matches the mobile-header control and an `aria-pressed` Panels button.

prs.title: fix(release): pin Linux builder to request SHA
prs.body:
## Summary

- bind Linux release tooling to the completed request run's immutable head SHA
- verify the executing builder independently at publication with its own workflow SHA
- preserve request authorization, supersession, and builder cancellation checks through the publication owner before every mutation
- allow the builder to continue when `main` advances after the request completes

## Why

The Linux builder previously compared the request's head SHA with the later builder workflow SHA. A normal `main` advance between those runs rejected an otherwise valid release request and required a redundant redispatch.

The completed request records immutable tooling SHA A, while the executing builder has independently authorized workflow SHA B. Publication now keeps those identities separate: A selects and revalidates the request-pinned tooling and exact request attempt; B authorizes the active builder run. The existing publication owner continues to perform those checks immediately before release writes.

## Authority-chain proof

- a production-owner harness publishes with request/tooling SHA A and executing builder SHA B, retaining A in the release manifest
- an unauthorized request head is rejected before release mutations
- a superseded request attempt is rejected before release mutations
- a cancelled builder is rejected before release mutations
- existing mid-flight revocation and cancellation cases continue to reauthorize before subsequent writes

## Testing

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node pnpm test test/scripts/linux-app-channel.test.ts test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (244 passed)
- `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs root` (all 4 shards passed)
- `pnpm exec oxlint test/scripts/linux-app-channel.test.ts test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` (0 warnings, 0 errors)
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check .github/workflows/linux-app-release.yml scripts/linux-app-channel.mjs test/scripts/linux-app-channel.test.ts test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts`
- `git diff --check origin/main -- .github/workflows/linux-app-release.yml scripts/linux-app-channel.mjs test/scripts/linux-app-channel.test.ts test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts`

`pnpm check:workflows` could not start locally because this host lacks Python venv/ensurepip support for the pinned pre-commit/actionlint runtime. The focused workflow guard suite parses the changed YAML and exercises the affected contracts; CI retains the actionlint gate.

Failed-update triage for a custom state directory or config path can inspect the account's unrelated native Gateway service, including probing its recorded runtime.

Exact `7937f7f0beb` candidate GREEN in 4.717 s: no service execution attempts, native status snapshot skipped, local config and failed-health context retained. Both cases preserve the original config and failure context; effect traces show no protected state access or network listeners.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): answer messages that arrived while the gateway was down
prs.body:
Related: #20952

AI-assisted: written with Claude Code. I have read the diff and understand what it does.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the WhatsApp channel would have inbound messages silently discarded whenever the gateway restarted. Anything that arrived while the process was down got marked read and never answered, with nothing written to the log, so the only visible symptom was a sender left waiting on a reply that never came.

Any cold start triggers it: a gateway restart, a reboot, a crashed process. A reconnect does not have the problem, and that asymmetry is the defect. A restart of an already-linked session is the same situation as a reconnect, with the same credentials, the same device registration and the same replay path, yet only one of the two catches up.

## Why This Change Was Made

Baileys tags an inbound stanza `append` when the server releases it from this device's offline queue, so a burst of them on connect is the backlog accrued while we were gone. `shouldSkipStaleAppend` bounds how far back that backlog may reach: it uses a supplied `appendReplyWindow` when there is one, and otherwise falls back to `connectedAtMs - 60_000`. That window is only supplied when `openedAfterRecentInbound` is set, which requires `reconnectAttempts > 0` and so is never set on the first connection a process opens, leaving every cold start on the sixty-second fallback.

The fallback now separates the two cases it was conflating. An already-synced credential is an established session and earns the same bounded catch-up a reconnect gets, while a credential still awaiting its first sync keeps the sixty-second cutoff, because a newly linked device's replay is the phone's history rather than our backlog and answering it is exactly the flooding that guard exists to prevent.

The discriminator is `accountSyncCounter` on the persisted credential. Baileys seeds it at 0 in `initAuthCreds` and increments it once the first sync settles, then reads `> 0` itself to decide the server will no longer push history. It is Baileys' own answer to "has this credential connected before", the plugin's `creds.update` handler already writes the whole credential object so it survives restarts with no new plumbing, and it needs no configuration.

Two boundaries are deliberate. `openedAfterRecentInbound` is left untouched, because the watchdog also reads it to select the tighter app-silence timeout, and widening it would force-close idle accounts on a repeating cycle. The fallback width is supplied by the caller, which already derives it from `messageTimeoutMs`, so a deployment that tunes that value cannot end up with a startup catch-up wider than the reconnect catch-up it mirrors.

The window can only ever widen what a socket answers. Its floor rolls forward with the clock while the steady-state floor stays pinned to connect, so late in the window the rolling floor would otherwise overtake the pinned one and start dropping appends that were previously delivered. Retiring the window one grace period early removes that band, and the grace constant is hoisted out of `shouldSkipStaleAppend` so the relationship is explicit rather than a repeated literal.

Repeat replies are prevented by the durable ingress queue rather than by this window. It is account-scoped, disk-backed, keyed by `sha256(remoteJid + "\n" + id)`, and keeps completed rows for seven days, so anything already answered before the restart returns `completed` and is skipped. Widening the window only changes the verdict for messages that were never handled at all. The change is also forward-only: the staleness verdict is computed at receive time and persisted, so a message the current build already dropped stays dropped, and the first restart after upgrading is what starts behaving correctly.

This is adjacent to the append handling added for #20952, which fixed the same family of restart symptom for messages under a minute old. That issue also suggested cross-restart message-id dedupe as the more durable answer, and it now exists, which is what makes widening this window safe.

## User Impact

After a gateway restart, WhatsApp messages sent during the outage are answered instead of silently dropped, bounded to the same catch-up width a reconnect uses. A reconnect that already received a catch-up window is unaffected; an idle reconnect, which previously also fell back to the sixty-second cutoff, now gets the same bounded catch-up, so the rule no longer depends on how the process reached the socket. Freshly linked devices are unchanged, so scanning a QR code still does not make the bot reply to old conversations. `docs/channels/whatsapp.md` is updated to match.

## Evidence

The regression test fails before the fix, for the intended reason. Reverting only the source files and rerunning leaves every guard passing and the cold-start case red:

```
 ✓ delivery coordinator limits reconnect catch-up appends by dedupe age 75ms
 ✓ delivery coordinator preserves fresh appends after catch-up expires 107ms
 ✓ delivery coordinator processes distinct catch-up messages at the boundary 75ms
 × delivery coordinator answers an offline append after a cold start 5066ms
   → expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times
 ✓ delivery coordinator drops a cold-start append past the catch-up ceiling 81ms
 ✓ delivery coordinator drops replayed history for a session awaiting its first sync 68ms

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 11 passed (12)
```

The never-narrower guarantee is pinned the same way. Reverting just the `- APPEND_RECENT_GRACE_MS` on `untilMs`, and nothing else, turns the boundary case red:

```
 × delivery coordinator keeps steady-state appends as the cold-start window retires 5065ms
   → expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
```

With the change applied, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/monitor-inbox.append.test.ts`:

```
 ✓ delivery coordinator answers an offline append after a cold start 70ms
 ✓ delivery coordinator drops a cold-start append past the catch-up ceiling 63ms
 ✓ delivery coordinator keeps steady-state appends as the cold-start window retires 66ms
 ✓ delivery coordinator drops replayed history for a session awaiting its first sync 65ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  13 passed (13)
```

The whole plugin lane is green, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp`:

```
 Test Files  99 passed (99)
      Tests  1383 passed (1383)
   Duration  50.20s
```

Also clean: `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` over the five touched source files (0 warnings, 0 errors), and `run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json` (exit 0).

The four new cases cover the split the change introduces. A cold start with an already-synced credential delivers a five-minute-old offline append; the same cold start still drops one past the ceiling; a message inside the steady-state grace period survives the window retiring; and a credential awaiting its first sync still drops replayed history. The harness hands each test an empty auth directory, so a seeded `creds.json` is the only thing separating them, and the nine pre-existing cases in the file are untouched and still pass.

One gap worth stating plainly: I have no live paired WhatsApp account, so this is proven at the inbound-monitor boundary through the plugin's own harness rather than against a real device link.


---

## Review response (ClawSweeper, 2026-08-29)

### 1. `accountSyncCounter` contract — verified against the pinned baileys 7.0.0-rc14

The review noted it could not confirm this because its GitHub DNS access failed. Verified locally against the pinned tarball:

- `lib/Types/Auth.d.ts:60` — `accountSyncCounter: number` on `AuthenticationCreds`.
- `lib/Utils/auth-utils.js:291` — `initAuthCreds()` seeds it to `0`, so a first link always starts at zero.
- `lib/Socket/chats.js:1003-1004` and `1107-1108` — incremented and persisted via `creds.update` once app-state sync completes.
- `lib/Socket/chats.js:1086-1089` — Baileys' own gate, with its own comment:

```js
// On reconnection (accountSyncCounter > 0), the server does not push
// history sync notifications — the device already has its data.
if (authState.creds.accountSyncCounter > 0) {
```

`> 0` is therefore Baileys' own definition of "established session that will not receive a history push", which is exactly the first-link versus established-session distinction this PR needs. It is not a heuristic invented here.

### 2. Parallel catch-up policy — already addressed before review

The reviewed head was `262dfb8f`, the middle of three commits. Current head `c7e7f33` threads the caller's computed width down as `appendCatchUpMaxMs: reconnectCatchUpWindowMs`, so the cold-start and reconnect paths share one width derived from `messageTimeoutMs`. `DEFAULT_OFFLINE_CATCH_UP_MS` survives only as a fallback when no caller width is supplied. The 3-file/+130 surface in the review reflects that earlier commit; current head is 6 files, +175/-3.

### 3. `auth-store.ts` is not a stored-data-model change

The helper reads an existing baileys-owned credential field. No field is added, no serialized shape changes, and no migration is required. Flagging it as a persistent data-model change looks like a false positive.

### 4. Live outage trace (2026-09-02, OpenClaw 2026.8.1 on macOS, Node 26.7.0)

Setup: the official `@openclaw/whatsapp@2026.8.1` npm install (trusted), with this PR's built `dist/` (head c7e7f33) copied over it. A tgz install of the PR build loads but the 2026.8.1 trust gate then refuses `openChannelIngressQueue` to it, so the overlay was the only way to run the PR code on a stock gateway. `package.json` untouched. `creds.json` `accountSyncCounter` = 1, so `hasWebCredsSyncedHistory` is true. The account's own reconciler plugin was disabled for the test, so nothing but the channel's inbound path could answer.

Timeline (local, +01:00):

| time | event |
|---|---|
| 07:55:31 | `openclaw gateway stop --force`, port 18789 closed, 0 listeners |
| 08:00:45 | an allowlisted contact sends a 127-char DM to the linked number (WhatsApp `messageTimestamp`) |
| 08:01:37 | `openclaw gateway start` |
| 08:02:20 | `[whatsapp] [default] starting provider` |
| 08:02:23.9 | `Listening for WhatsApp inbound messages` (connectedAt) |
| 08:02:26.5 | `[whatsapp] Inbound message +<sender> -> +<self> (direct, 127 chars)` |
| 08:03:23.2 | `[whatsapp] Sending message -> sha256:<jid>` |
| 08:03:23.8 | `[whatsapp] Sent message <id> -> sha256:<jid> (624ms)`, reply visible on the sender's phone |

Message age at connect: 98 s. That is past `APPEND_RECENT_GRACE_MS` (60 s) and inside `DEFAULT_OFFLINE_CATCH_UP_MS` (20 min). In the pristine 2026.8.1 chunk `shouldSkipStaleAppend` has no `appendReplyWindow` on a cold start (only the in-process reconnect path sets one), so its floor is `connectedAtMs - 60_000` and an `append` this old is dropped. With this PR `resolveAppendReplyWindow` returns `afterMs = connectedAt - 20 min` and the message was answered 57 s after connect.

Stability: `~/.openclaw/logs/stability` unchanged across the test (3 captures, all from before the fix, 05:07 to 05:19Z), launchd `runs = 1`, `last exit code = (never exited)`.

Caveats: the upsert type is not logged at info level, so this trace shows the offline-queue release (2.6 s after connect, 98 s old) and the outcome, not the literal `append` tag. Boundary 2 (fresh link, `accountSyncCounter` = 0) was not exercised, it needs the device re-linked.

### 5. Fresh-link boundary (2026-09-02, 2026.8.1 + this PR's dist)

Same host as section 4. The account was logged out through the gateway (`channels.logout`, credentials directory 4,077 files → 0), the owner's brother (a newly allowlisted sender) sent one DM while nothing was linked, and the account was re-linked from a fresh QR (`web.login.start` / `web.login.wait`) more than seven minutes later. Times are local (+01:00), from `~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log` and a `tail -F` watcher.

```
09:03:14  channels.logout → { cleared: true, loggedOut: true }; creds.json gone; accountSyncCounter=absent
≤09:15:11 pre-link probe sent (account unlinked)
09:22:33  WhatsApp asked for a restart after pairing (code 515); waiting for creds to save…
09:22:34  accountSyncCounter=0            (fresh creds, no history sync yet)
09:22:38  ✅ Linked! WhatsApp is ready.    [whatsapp] [default] starting provider (+234…)
09:22:41  Listening for WhatsApp inbound messages
09:22:42  accountSyncCounter=1
09:34:16  Inbound message +1647… -> +234… (direct, 92 chars)      post-link probe, same sender
09:45:54  Sending message -> sha256:2248332a4420
09:45:55  Sent message 3EB04058A425D76BBAEAE2 (1331ms)   reply delivered (second Sent at 09:45:56)
```

Observed for the pre-link probe: no `Inbound message` line, no `Sending message`, no stale-skip line, no history line. The fresh link took the `resolveAppendReplyWindow` early return (`hasWebCredsSyncedHistory` false at connect), so the 60-second floor applied and the seven-minute-old message was not answered. Pre-link history reaches Baileys as `messaging-history.set`, which this plugin does not subscribe to, so nothing about the older message ever hit `messages.upsert` either way.

Observed for the post-link probe: accepted as a live `notify` upsert the moment it arrived and answered; no stale-skip line. (The 11-minute gap between inbound and reply was the answering agent cycling through model candidates on an expired credential, unrelated to this code path; the inbound admission is what this boundary tests.)

Stability captures before and after: 20 / 20 (no gateway crash across logout, relink, or the probes).

prs.title: fix(ui): keep equivalent Windows catalog paths in one project group

Related: #111595

## What Problem This Solves

Equivalent Windows working-directory spellings split native catalog sessions into separate sidebar projects. Expanding a project can leave equivalent saved collapse records behind.

## User Impact

The proposed fix groups Windows path variants while retaining the first display spelling, preserving POSIX case sensitivity and distinguishing drive-relative roots from absolute roots. Saved collapse aliases are cleared together without touching other catalog/host scopes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Normalize comparison identities in the existing catalog grouping owner, including Windows worktree markers. Keep persistence writes in SessionOrganizer and pass equivalent section ids through the existing toggle operation. No new dependencies, configuration or storage schema.

Prior work: closed, unmerged #111596 by @ooiuuii and #163542 by @AmelioMansour. This continuation adapts the approach to current Solid 2 owners; the older PRs' tests/screenshots are not claimed as current evidence. Coordination: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/111595#issuecomment-6501143240 . No assignment transfer or maintainer acceptance is claimed.

## Evidence

- Before the repair: the new grouping regression failed (three Windows spellings split; absolute and drive-relative roots merged). Five existing grouping cases passed.
- Separately, the registered sidebar test failed with three rendered project headings instead of one.
- After the repair, the repository runner passed all 88 tests in the two selected suites (6 grouping and 82 sidebar), including collapse-alias cleanup, reordered rows and remount persistence. Latest wrapper wall time: 118.77 s; sidebar Vitest duration: 58.28 s. CI duration is not yet known.
- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/sessions/catalog-project-grouping.test.ts ui/src/components/app-sidebar.catalog.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Targeted oxlint previously exited 0 with four Solid reactivity warnings; those warnings have not been baseline-compared. `git diff --check` passed.
- Test allocation: 86 net lines for Windows identity and persisted collapse-state regression coverage, without changing the shared baseline.

### Draft: Remaining Validation

This is intentionally a draft, not a merge-ready or fully verified UI fix. The tests use jsdom and synthetic catalog data; current-head real-browser/Gateway proof and inspected before/after screenshots are still missing. No production build or full CI pass is claimed. The independent review attempt stopped due to an account usage limit and did not produce a review. Broader root/UNC and saved-state coverage should be reviewed before marking ready. Historical evidence from the prior PRs is not reused as fresh validation.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): answer recent messages missed during gateway downtime
prs.body:
Supersedes #132260, thanks @0xNagato.
Related: #20952

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes WhatsApp messages received during Gateway downtime being marked read and silently left unanswered when the linked account starts again.

## User Impact

Established linked accounts can answer recent offline messages after startup or reconnect, with a maximum age of 20 minutes at intake. Normal DM, group allowlist, and mention rules continue to apply. Newly linked accounts keep their short history guard; older offline messages remain outside the reply window. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use [Baileys' already-loaded initial-sync state](https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys/blob/7e7b0757e3f9f3c7789fb1cfd2f241d5002a199a/src/Socket/chats.ts#L1324), captured before asynchronous socket attachment, to choose the existing bounded age cap. A single rolling freshness rule replaces the separate reconnect window and handles startup, reconnect, and delayed offline appends. Durable account/chat/message-ID admission continues to prevent replayed replies across restarts, and the watchdog keeps its existing lifecycle policy.

Production LOC: **net -8** by removing the three-field reconnect window and its duplicate lifetime bookkeeping. Test fixtures/regressions: net +30; the test-line allocation grants the exact 27 LF increase counted by the ratchet. The added proof covers reply/restart deduplication and policy boundaries while replacing obsolete reconnect-window assertions.

## Evidence

- Main baseline `38fd51c52ab11ce75810ac7917bef4fc2b11010c`: the append boundary suite had **2 failed / 9 passed** with only the new regression and fixture overlaid. Five-minute-old offline messages never reached reply dispatch.
- The strengthened first-link test reproduced an incorrect historical reply when sync completed during asynchronous attachment; capturing the state before that await fixes it. Negative assertions now wait for the real inbound drain.
- Focused validation: **71 tests passed across 5 files** (connection/logging, append intake, delivery/dedupe, access policy, and group activation), using Node 24.22.1 in rootless Podman limited to 4 CPUs / 8 GB. The final run took 371.01s including a cold runtime/declaration build; the changed connection file took 66.57s (1% test execution) and the three inbox files took 18.44s together. The initial warm standalone append run took 10.36s. CI timing will be available on this PR.
- The normalization fixture consumers passed **15/15 tests** (25.07s). Targeted production and touched-test type checks, type-aware lint, formatting, test-line ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. The media suite also passed **11/11** (9.14s), for **97 passing focused tests** in total.
- Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2, against the baseline above) found one INDEX-only startup-snapshot omission in an older staged state. The reviewed socket-session fix is included in the final staged change; the reviewer found no additional defects in the combined source.
- CI repair: `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-1` exposed a PR-caused omission in the media socket fixture. Its 11 cases reproduced the missing `authState` setup failure locally; adding Baileys' initial counter to that fixture made all 11 pass. Production code is unchanged. A separate autoreview of this repair delta was **scoped-clean at P0–P2**; media test types, type-aware lint, formatting, and the adjusted exact LF allocation passed.
- Contributor code was inspected using `gh pr view/diff` and was never checked out, installed, built, or executed. This is a maintainer reimplementation from main, credited to Femi Odunaiya.
- Proof uses synthetic WhatsApp transport events, real intake/durable deduplication, access policy, and reply-send paths. A live paired-device test was not run, and the production Gateway was not changed.

prs.title: chore(deps): update fs-safe to 0.27.0
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Updates the direct fs-safe dependency to [0.27.0](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/releases/tag/v0.27.0) and replaces observed-directory-mode workarounds with its explicit preservation API.

## User Impact

Memory and shared state-root writes preserve existing directory modes without attempting an owner-only chmod. Newly created atomic-write parents finish at `0700`; file-mode, durability, confinement, and mutation-authority rules remain intact. No OpenClaw release is included.

## Why This Change Was Made

All 13 direct pins move to 0.27.0, building on the merged pin alignment in #188719. All 11 published package records have verified npm integrity values; importer and snapshot references and expiring reviewed-release exemptions are updated. `acpx@0.21.0` independently requires fs-safe 0.26.15, so its transitive package records remain.

Release audit: 0.27.0 has one feature entry, #1050 (`dirMode: "preserve"`). Watch-hint admission (#1046, OpenClaw #186752) and awaited borrowed-handle overwrite authority (#1049) already shipped in 0.26.15. The error-code contract is unchanged. OpenClaw's `fs-safe-remove.ts` already maps `permission-denied` and the other operational wrappers to their errno causes; no mapping change is needed. The upstream shared option type now includes preservation even for private APIs that reject it at runtime; OpenClaw’s private-secret wrapper explicitly retains its numeric-only directory-mode type.

| Writer | Adoption / retained policy |
| --- | --- |
| DREAMS.md | Let fs-safe create private parents and preserve existing parents; keep file mode and mutation authority. |
| Dreaming Markdown reports | Remove mkdir/stat mode workaround; preserve existing parents, create missing chains at 0700. |
| Promotion memory replacement | Remove parent stat; keep file mode, preimage/hash checks, publication reconciliation, and in-place fallback. |
| Config publication, recovery, rollback and update restoration (#171869) | Preserve only the selected state root; private child directories retain numeric 0700 policy. |
| Non-default-mode secret-adjacent text | Use the selected-root preservation policy; default private-store path remains numeric. |
| Plugin package/build manifests, config audit scrub, legacy-agent migration receipt | Replace observed parent mode with preservation; keep independent file modes and durability. |
| Private stores, default secret writes, private-dir repair, Root/copy APIs | Retain their distinct numeric/private contracts; private APIs reject preservation. |

Config locking already owns state-root creation before config publication, so that creation path remains intact; this refactor removes only its observed-mode request. Private store and secret-create APIs retain numeric directory enforcement because they reject `"preserve"`.

## Evidence

Frozen `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passed, including after rebase. All 13 npm lock mirrors were generated and validated by the lock owner, with 11 new-version records each. Production core/extension/script typechecks, extension-test and infra-test typechecks, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.

Default pinned-Bun proof: **352 scoped tests passed** (151 memory/fs-safe and 201 core), with four platform skips. The four targeted CLI/receipt cases intentionally deselected 99 unrelated cases. Completed config, recovery, migration, secret, removal, SDK, and memory suites passed. Initial concurrent-source compilation invalidations were rerun against a frozen tree.

A direct production-path probe reproduced report parents at `0755` before adoption and passes afterward with new chains at `0700`, shared parents unchanged under simulated non-owner `EPERM`, and new files at `0600`. The secret-adjacent write regression failed with the old numeric caller and passed with preservation. The existing tests retain file-mode, umask, authority, conflict, and private-directory coverage. The scoped test-line allocation accounts for 46 added regression lines.

Independent Codex autoreview is **scoped-clean at P0–P2** for the complete change, including the private-secret type correction. The final rebase resolved only alignment conflicts: all 36 reviewed source/dependency files are byte-identical to the reviewed and tested candidate. Current-head PR CI is the broad proof. prs.title: improve: safely reuse qualified offline compositions
prs.body:
Related: #188661, now landed. This follow-on targets **main** and preserves exact prerequisite `f3bdcadb948e1b873b59066cbd0994192da50a42` in its history. Its effective change against reviewed main `adb58af237c2079d8eae388b22b9ce439d19e081` is exactly the five qualified-reuse files.

## What Problem This Solves

Repeated offline compositions rehash every dependency payload, while skipping verification of a mutable donor or Docker's `app/` input would admit stale or changed bytes.

## User Impact

Release tooling can opt into qualified dependency reuse and an archive-bound image recipe without changing the strict defaults. Reuse receipts explicitly report partial input verification; neither mode replaces Linux target acceptance.

## Why This Change Was Made

A trusted, digest-bound receipt from a prior strict composition qualifies the dependency manifest, not the current donor. Reuse still checks complete topology, modes, sizes, link targets/containment and package manifests, then verifies the actual selected copies against that inventory. Unselected payload bytes are not rehashed, and partial receipts cannot qualify another reuse. No caller-written operation report serves as authority.

The landed composition owner's repairs are retained: builtin-named npm dependencies use package lookup and nearest-ancestor deduplication, and legitimate implementation files under paths such as `src/node_modules` are copied and verified. Those prerequisite fixes are not reintroduced as independent owners here.

The optional `--image-input archive` recipe checks the receipt-bound archive/manifest and the small admission inputs without rehashing all of `app/`. Docker copies the archive, checks its exact SHA-256 inside the build, and only then extracts it. The existing finalizer remains the single lifecycle owner. Directory recipes and full-inventory verification remain the defaults.

Source implementation contributed by @galiniliev. Relative to main, this adds no cache, competing operation-report owner, dependency, lockfile or tool pin. Net production growth remains 176 lines. The scoped allocation is still exactly **140** for the **+140** test-line delta; the shared scalar was not changed.

## Evidence

- Published head `712cf21f051338520e61849fa4c7d43acfa1ef3a` preserves tested commit `63593cf109f5737ed238603dec0f1c73d583553c` and tree `dcc577f3532a53cb300ee278b730e4947adc7060`. The exact prerequisite was merged history-preservingly in `aa52afa9975e8cfe3b8eecaec51bf3418a3ae214`. Four squash-lineage conflicts were then resolved against main only after proving all four main-side blobs equal the reviewed prerequisite. No rebase or age-only refresh was performed.
- **53 relevant tests have passing main-context evidence:** 32 composition, 14 bundled-link helper, 4 offline dependency-planner and 3 Docker-digest tests. The first main-context run exposed a test-fixture clone that traversed unavailable unrelated history in a partial checkout. The fixture now clones the real runtime commit at depth one; that case and the four planner tests passed in a focused 59.19s follow-up, including 41.66s cold worker compilation. Unaffected passing cases were reused rather than blanket-rerun. The complete pre-main integration run also passed all 53 tests in 78.46s.
- Builtin-name admission is exercised through the real composition fixture using an npm package named `fs`. Restoring the old lookup makes composition fail with `openclaw requires fs`; the repair passes while retaining nested versions. The existing implementation-file tamper case still fails with the old copy filter and passes with the repair. Genuine first strict receipts, relocation/tampering, partial-receipt rejection, CLI archive admission and native-finalizer boundaries remain covered.
- Fresh main-relative scripts, tooling-test and extensions-test typechecks passed. Targeted lint reported zero warnings/errors; formatting, normal isolated commit hooks and diff checks passed. Frozen dependencies were reconciled only in the task-owned isolated installation; shared caches were unchanged.
- **Fresh main-relative ratchet passed:** 6,315,807 test lines, ceiling 6,347,775, slack 31,968. The earlier 1,042-line overage was measured on the pre-main snapshot and is not stamped onto this checked main-based tree. No allocation was inflated to hide it.
- Fresh independent local autoreview of the final five-file candidate against main `adb58af237c2079d8eae388b22b9ce439d19e081`: **P0–P2 scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. The final candidate was committed unchanged. The dirty local ClawSweeper checkout required the documented autoreview route. The [earlier hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188678#issuecomment-6533057882) also found no actionable defects; it is prior-head evidence, not a current-head approval.
- Retained real offline Podman admission proof remains source-bound to the unchanged Dockerfile: the archive-input stage consumed the original archive despite changed `app/` bytes; archive tampering failed checksum verification before extraction. No broad rebuild was repeated solely for metadata or ancestry changes.

<details>
<summary>Retained archive-consumption trace — unchanged Docker stage</summary>

Successful admission and container readback, while mutable `app/` contained different bytes:

```text
/tmp/installed-runtime.tgz: OK
archive bytes consumed; mutable app excluded
```

After changing that archive while retaining the expected digest:

```text
/tmp/installed-runtime.tgz: FAILED
sha256sum: WARNING: 1 computed checksum did NOT match
```

The maintained build step orders checksum verification before extraction with `&&`; the tampered build exited 1. This is archive admission proof, not full release-image qualification.

</details>

**Current-head CI is green:** the [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41148539662/job/124382281583) passed for `712cf21f051338520e61849fa4c7d43acfa1ef3a`; final readback found no failed or running checks. Full release-image acceptance remains target-owned. Receipts retain `compositionOnly: true`, ABI/libc `requires-target-acceptance`, and lifecycle `target-required`. No live cloud operations were performed.

## Worked on by

- @galiniliev

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @galiniliev](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/5195398f-32af-4571-9bc4-bf5c08341479)

prs.title: fix(android): false "Could not refresh models" banner after sending into a busy session
prs.body:
Closes #183031

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Android chat shows "Could not refresh models. Tap Refresh to try again." and flags the chat as needing attention right after a message is sent into a busy session.

## User Impact

User impact: sending messages no longer raises a false models-refresh warning. A real, persistent metadata failure still shows the same error as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a `chat.metadata` read overlaps the send that mutates the session, the Gateway rejects it with the transient, explicitly retryable "Session changed while preparing its metadata. Retry the request.". The client surfaced that as a refresh failure without retrying. This change retries only that case: at most 2 extra attempts, with 400/800 ms backoff, and cancellation is rethrown. Every other error keeps the current behavior. It also clears the stale refresh error after a later successful background load, so the banner does not outlive the condition.

This complements #185623, which improves the wording of metadata vs catalog errors but intentionally adds no retry.

## Evidence

- New `ChatControllerMetadataRetryTest` (Robolectric, scripted gateway):
  - superseded read once → retried, catalog loads, no error;
  - superseded on every attempt → bounded to 3 reads, error still shown;
  - non-transient failure (`FORBIDDEN`) → not retried.
- Against `main` without the fix, the two retry tests fail (2/3 failures), so the tests exercise the change.
- `ChatControllerCatalogTest` (8) passes. `:app:ktlintCheck` is clean.
- Live: Galaxy Z Fold8 with Gateway 2026.10.8. Before the fix the banner appeared on almost every send into a long-running session; the gateway logged the superseded `chat.metadata` followed by a successful later read. With this change in a local build, the banner no longer appears (owner-confirmed on device).

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

```
cd apps/android
./gradlew :app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.chat.ChatControllerMetadataRetryTest' --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.chat.ChatControllerCatalogTest' :app:ktlintCheck
```
</details>

Agent-assisted: drafted with an AI coding agent at the reporter's request, reviewed, and validated on device by the reporter.
