prs.title: fix(plugins): align artifact review budget and activation guidance
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: task-authored plugin archives fail review above a special 512-entry cap, including a valid 1,479-entry archive the ordinary installer ceiling would allow.

## User Impact

User impact: review now uses the shared 50,000-entry ceiling (`DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRIES`), counting files and directory headers like the ordinary installer. The ceiling is not a guarantee. Unchanged controls can still reject an archive: 32 MiB archive and per-entry, 64 MiB expanded, 96 MiB decoded, 30-second extraction, path, link, and SHA checks, a 3,000-character metadata cap, the dependency ban, approval, lease, inference-owner checks, and the explicit UI opt-out. Other post-install scans still use 10,000 directories and depth 64. ClawHub's 10,000 regular-file limit is a different unit; this change invents no ratio.

Gateway-bound activation requests a live runtime callback. Standalone execution without that callback does not. Report installation, runtime outcome, `restartRequired`, and browser observation separately. There is no lifecycle change and no unconditional hot-reload claim.

A normal 1,479-entry registry artifact can pass the count and still be refused by the unchanged no-dependencies rule. This pull request does not make it eligible for task-authored activation, does not install Pstack, and does not deploy a runtime.

## Why This Change Was Made

The 512-entry special case is removed in favor of the existing shared installer constant, while the tighter artifact byte and time budgets stay. Entry 50,001 is refused before extraction output.

## Evidence

Samples, not a host guarantee: a new 1,479-entry fixture in 9.59s with no exec; 10,000 empty files in 11.03s; 50,000 directories still hit the unchanged 30-second timeout and were cleaned up. The check was red before the fix and green after. Sixty-seven focused tests, one isolated native reload integration, affected canonical typecheck shards, lint, format, and the exact 40-line allocation passed. Peer review and one canonical API pass reported no P0–P2 findings. Hosted CI has not run and is not claimed green.

Five files, +52/−8; production net is two lines. The full input binary is not included.

prs.title: fix(agents): ask_user from another agent's turn reaches that agent instead of the owner
prs.body:
Closes #179964
Related: #180140

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent answering another agent sends its `ask_user` question back to that agent instead of to the person who owns it, and the other agent's reply can then answer it. For example, a peer agent asks to book a meeting, the agent asks its owner "May Bob book Thursday?", and the question goes to the peer.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Routing.** The inbound sender's bot flag (`SenderIsBot`) now travels with the run, the way `senderIsOwner` already does. The shared question publisher (`question-prompt-send.ts`) uses it to choose the recipient: a bot sender's `ask_user` and `secrets` prompts go to the agent's owner, on the route proactive delivery already uses (`commands.ownerAllowFrom`, then the channel's `allowFrom`). This covers every publication path:
  - embedded runs;
  - the loopback tools that CLI backends use;
  - skill commands;
  - harness questions (Codex, Copilot, CLI plugins);
  - ACP elicitation;
  - queued turns.
- **Answering.** The owner's typed reply cannot answer a question created on the bot's turn, so the owner prompt links to the question's Control UI page, which takes every answer form, free text included. Option buttons stay where the owner's channel shows them. The prompt asks for no typed reply.
- **Current owner and question.** The owner route is read from the live config. Right before the prompt goes to delivery, and again at delivery's final handoff (`assertDirectAdapterHandoff`, `onPlatformSendDispatch`), the publisher confirms that the question is still pending and the config has not changed. Otherwise nothing is sent.
- **The bot can't answer.** A bot's message is never accepted as an answer: not in reply admission, not when steered into the run that asked (`allowPendingUserInputAnswer: false`), and not in ACP question claims. Harness secret input is not requested on a bot's turn.

Boundaries:
- This adds no new way to answer a question and changes no answer authority. Answers still come from the channel's question buttons or the Control UI.
- Which tools are offered is unchanged.
- No schema, stored state, config option or permission changes. Human senders' prompts are unchanged.
- Not in this PR: typed owner answers, and letting agent-only channel plugins offer `ask_user` (#180140).

**Submitted for maintainer acceptance:** the recipient policy (the proactive owner route) and the Control UI prerequisite. Without `gateway.publicOrigin`, a bot sender's question is cancelled, even a single-choice question on a channel with buttons, because the owner could not give a free-text answer.

## User Impact

An agent that needs its owner's decision while serving another agent now asks the owner, who answers on the linked Control UI page, or with buttons where their channel has them. The other agent can no longer answer for the owner. Without an owner route or `gateway.publicOrigin`, the question is cancelled and `ask_user` reports that the prompt could not be delivered; the error names the setting. Questions from people behave exactly as before.

## Evidence

Exact head `1992f5aa920`, based on `2b9dd45ec2b`. Runtime transcripts are in the PR comments.

| Check | `main` | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| QA: a bot sender's question (`runtime-tool-ask-user-bot-sender`) | Prompt goes to the bot's conversation | Owner gets it with the answer page; bot gets nothing. With `senderIsBot` removed from the embedded subscription in `attempt-stream-prepare.ts`, the scenario fails: the owner never receives the question. |
| QA: the owner answers in the Control UI (`control-ui-ask-user-owner-answer`, Chromium) | — | Linked page answered as the signed-in operator; run resumes with `Deploy: Staging (Recommended)` |
| QA: no `gateway.publicOrigin` (`runtime-tool-ask-user-bot-sender-no-answer-page`) | — | Person's prompt and answer unchanged; bot's question cancelled |
| A bot's text during a pending question (`dispatch.question-input.test.ts`) | `handled: true` (answers) | Refused |
| A bot's message steered into the asking run (`agent-runner-steer-adoption.worker.test.ts`) | Answer-eligible | Not an answer; a person's still is |
| Owner replaced or question ended during held durable delivery (`owner-question-prompt.integration.test.ts`, `ask_user` and `secrets`) | — | Adapter never called. With the handoff guards removed, both fail. |
| Upgrade: config and state from 2026.10.5 start on this head | — | Gateway health `ok`; config sha256 unchanged |

The three QA runs ran on `824a49c227e`; this head is that commit rebased onto `main`, with the test-line ceiling below and `main`'s ACP bridge sentence kept in `docs/tools/ask-user.md`. The upgrade check ran on `88d812e801d`. The QA runs use a real Gateway child, qa-channel and the mock OpenAI provider. The integration test runs `sendDurableMessageBatchCore` with a test channel whose send preparation is held. Owner routes come from the real resolver throughout; unit tests mock only the transport.

Local checks, Node 24.22.1:
- The 12 test files this PR changes pass on `824a49c227e`, including `attempt-stream-prepare.test.ts`, which checks that the embedded subscription receives `senderIsBot`.
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test` pass on `de827f2eb35`, which differs from this head only by that rebase.
- `oxfmt`, `oxlint` and `git diff --check` are clean; `check:import-cycles` and `check:madge-import-cycles` report no cycles.

Autoreview (Codex, P0–P2) was scoped-clean on `88d812e801d`.

```sh
pnpm openclaw qa suite --provider-mode mock-openai \
  --scenario runtime-tool-ask-user-bot-sender \
  --scenario control-ui-ask-user-owner-answer \
  --scenario runtime-tool-ask-user-bot-sender-no-answer-page
pnpm test src/agents/tools/question-prompt-send.test.ts \
  src/infra/outbound/owner-question-prompt.integration.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-steer-adoption.worker.test.ts \
  src/auto-reply/dispatch.question-input.test.ts \
  src/gateway/tool-resolution.bot-sender.test.ts
```

Not claimed:
- A native button tap on a live channel. QA Channel has no button interaction, and Telegram proof needs leased credentials. Taps use the existing callback authorization and `question.resolve`.
- A live Discord or Slack run with a bot author.
- A dedicated test for the ACP guard.

### Test-line allowance

`config/test-lines-baseline.txt`: **6,299,646 → 6,300,988** (**+1,342**). This PR adds 578 test lines net. Its base is already 764 lines over that ceiling. The new ceiling equals this head's measured 6,300,988 test lines, with no slack. No test, assertion or required check is removed or weakened to make room.

CI on `de827f2eb35`: the test-line ratchet passed; five test jobs failed outside this change. CI is running on `1992f5aa920`.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep composer picker targets stable during mobile transitions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes model and effort pickers missing a native press when Files narrows the composer and the layout crosses to mobile. Related: #188734.

## User Impact

Picker targets stay in place through a normal held press. The mobile sheet retains its slide-out animation without making the conversation scroll when focus moves.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hidden mobile sheet transitioned `display` from the desktop wrapper’s `contents` to `none`. Until that transition ended, its children occupied an implicit 52 px grid row. Removing that row moved the composer between pointerdown and pointerup.

Keep the sheet an absolutely positioned flex box and transition `visibility`. Clip its containing region so the translated hidden box cannot create a focus-scroll range. CI exposed that second requirement: the region scrolled 158–372 px and moved task-suggestion actions offscreen.

No new state, handlers, dependencies, or loading boundaries. The motion tests now assert visible during slide-out and hidden at rest, preserving the native gesture and reduced-motion checks.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original press on base `b39e2d09329c` | Reproduced at 560 px; pointerdown hit the effort summary, pointerup hit the textarea, composer moved 52 px |
| Chromium and WebKit repeated press proof | **Chromium 50/50 and WebKit 50/50 passed** with the original ten-file worker prefix; all 11 files / 35 tests passed. Each iteration covers 0, 16, 32, 64, and 100 ms presses at 560 px. Chromium retains native Escape coverage; WebKit isolates activation with a fresh navigation between presses |
| WebKit closing baseline | Separate Escape and pointer-close stalls reproduced on unchanged base. The native WebCore style resolver hangs even without a JavaScript style read; the unsuccessful resize-measurement experiment is removed from the final candidate |
| Coupled CI failures | Final build passes the two task-suggestion viewport cases, all seven mobile-sheet motion cases, and the streamed-burst case (10 selected checks) |
| UI and focused E2E typechecks; targeted lint/format | Pass |
| Production Knip | Pass; no new ignores |
| Production builds and strict performance checks | Pass; startup JS unchanged at 88,760 B gzip; CSS unchanged at one request / 33,568 B |
| Independent Codex autoreview | Final activation-only candidate, P0–P2, scoped-clean |

The first CI run is retained as [41141681335](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41141681335). Its motion assertions and task-suggestion failures drove the coupled corrections above. The streamed-burst assertion passed both the unchanged base and final-build local replay; no claim that a passing replay fixes an intermittent failure. prs.title: feat(auth): allow write access without personal credential enrollment
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Shared Gateway operators need ordinary write access without letting teammates enroll personal credentials outside their managed credential system.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-enterprise/pull/3049

## User Impact

Adds opt-in `operator.write.no-credential-enrollment`. It blocks personal model-provider API-key/token/OAuth enrollment and personal GitHub publication OAuth enrollment, including reconnects and pending credential installation after permission is withdrawn. Ordinary writes, saved-account use, account status, and disconnection remain available. Shared credential setup remains admin-only.

**GitHub identity/co-authorship is not a publication credential.** Verified GitHub identity from supported sign-in, profile editing, and the Git co-author credit preference remain available. This does not add a manual identity-linking/OAuth feature or make an arbitrary proxy username a verified GitHub account; OCE’s ingress must use an already-supported verified identity path.

Existing `operator.read`, `operator.write`, admin, and default grants retain their behavior. Legacy read permits personal GitHub enrollment, so restricted roles must not also grant it. Grant only the non-enrolling scope, and review unioned device grants or apply a role ceiling. Adding legacy read restores GitHub enrollment; adding full write/admin restores all enrollment. Already-saved credentials, their refresh, and existing session selections are not revoked. This is an API guardrail, not isolation from unrestricted host execution.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared scope owner keeps grant containment separate from action eligibility. Full write includes restricted write, never the reverse. Because legacy read includes GitHub enrollment, the `operator.read.no-credential-enrollment` subset represents ordinary reads when read authority is capped by restricted write. Without that representable subset, intersection, cookies, or synthetic calls could restore enrollment or lose ordinary read capabilities.

Enrollment retains its original full-write (model providers) or legacy-read (GitHub) authority through provider I/O and credential persistence. Existing Gateway, tool, UI/native, and bundled-plugin adapters consume ordinary action requirements without manufacturing broader grants. No new policy store, database migration, config switch, dependency, or protocol-version change. Simplification keeps one action/grant owner rather than a deny flag or parallel policy; ordinary-read adapters are necessary because legacy read itself enrolls GitHub credentials.

## Evidence

- **2026-10-22 review refresh — a7d517ce8456b9df0feaed8a817a21083745e3bb:** rebased onto `a68d0eb252586b11412bced0ef41e41e5fc6e798`, preserving the scope lattice and upstream self-profile/UI owner behavior. Addressed the production-effect proof request by reproducing four unwanted GitHub HTTP dispatches after authority withdrawal, then carrying the transport’s existing live-authority callback through personal and System/agent device flows. Existing credential-install/store guards remain intact.
- **New execution proof:** 10 GitHub final-effect cases pass through real lifecycle/parser/profile/SQLite owners using a synthetic loopback issuer; 3 shipped-provider/private-store cases pass, including successful real-WebSocket API-key enrollment and withdrawal at transaction/commit admission. This is not genuine external GitHub OAuth, remote provider key validity, or model inference. The final effect/lifecycle rerun passes 54 tests (108.24s); the profile cleanup rerun passes 31 tests (8.67s). The earlier 295-test focused run (162.32s) is separate, not an additional distinct-test count. Six conflict-resolution consumer files also pass 109 tests (48.20s).
- **Current local gates:** core and Control UI production types, Gateway root/server and profile-page test types, targeted typed lint, formatting, and whitespace pass. Independent canonical Auto Review of the complete integration and final repair found no actionable P0–P2 findings; review was static and limited to supplied source/delta, not reviewer execution. [Detailed review response](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179959#issuecomment-6353908519).
- **Still unverified:** genuine external OAuth, native builds/device execution, and the stable 2026.10.6 account/selection upgrade lane. The maintained upgrade runner requires Docker, unavailable here; a Podman substitution awaits Sally’s decision. No feature-owned schema migration is introduced, but an upgrade result is not inferred from that fact. Existing screenshots and the live recording below remain historical evidence, not captures of this refresh.

- [Live Gateway recording and result matrix](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179959#issuecomment-6346078709) on `3150e352715d`: real browser/WebSocket requests, profile/co-author preference API readback, and four direct enrollment denials under restricted write. Synthetic trusted-proxy principals; legacy controls intentionally stop at schema validation. This supplements screenshots, not external OAuth or OCE/OpenShell qualification.

- 2026-10-22 conflict rebase onto `c5650f3a5e59d6523c913a8ebfff2b787cf58435`: preserved upstream profile/GitHub owner refactors and web-push inlining. The 27-file focused matrix passes (577 tests), four additional profile/GitHub lifecycle files pass (35 tests), and both production-built browser grant scenarios pass. Core/UI/extension production types, affected UI/Gateway and extension test types, targeted lint, i18n, formatting, and whitespace pass. Fresh canonical independent Auto Review completed scoped-clean at P0–P2 across the supplied candidate delta; no reviewer test execution or unchanged-context qualification is claimed. Earlier evidence below remains historical.

- A red probe against the previous provider-only implementation showed restricted write reaching GitHub device authorization. The retained router, real-Gateway, and lifecycle regressions now cover start/poll denial, ordinary status/profile reads, legacy-grant compatibility, and in-flight role withdrawal before credential installation.
- Real Gateway coverage verifies broader grants attenuate to restricted write, ordinary profile changes succeed, and provider enrollment is denied. A GitHub-backed sign-in fixture verifies identity and co-author consent remain available while GitHub credential enrollment is forbidden.
- Grant intersection/projection and plugin-cookie/relay checks protect against restoring legacy read. Device normalization does not synthesize that enrollment-bearing grant.
- Production-built UI scenarios compare legacy full write with restricted write: provider and GitHub credential setup are disabled only for restricted access; verified identity, co-author preference edits, and saved-account selection/unlink remain available. Captures use synthetic profiles and compare grants on the same implementation, not two source revisions.
- Focused backend, UI, and plugin tests pass after correcting a profile fixture; the two affected files were rerun successfully. The two production-built browser scenarios also pass. The initial 37-file batch took 206s, the final two-file repair run 36s, and browser proof 30s (2 tests; 5.2s test execution), excluding its 23s production build. These timings include cold compilation; no CI-seconds claim is made.
- Core/UI/extension production types and focused Gateway/UI test types pass. Targeted lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. A direct lattice probe passed 4,648 implication/intersection checks. Canonical independent Auto Review completed scoped-clean at P0–P2; review was static and limited to the supplied delta/context, with no reviewer test execution claimed.
- Main integration was needed for one Workboard fixture conflict. The resolution keeps both write-scope cases and the current fixture owner. All four overlapping test files pass after integration (95 tests, 128s); extension test types, targeted lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. Earlier broad focused checks and browser captures are pre-integration evidence; the integration changes no feature UI or scope semantics.
- Retained qualification gaps: native Swift/Kotlin builds/device execution and real external OAuth were not run. Existing voice-call startup failures (21 cases) were reproduced on the original unchanged base `afa9bfdcf82a7e1bdc4f8baf1bd4cbaf3200a936`; the suite is not claimed green. Broad CI is not yet qualification of this draft.

### UI comparison

Actual production-built Control UI with a synthetic profile, light theme, 1280×1400 viewport; tight crops make the changed controls visible. These compare grants on the same implementation, not two source revisions.

**Before — existing operator.write**

![Full write permits personal GitHub credential enrollment](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/89ce5af8-30e1-427d-857a-5fb5acee1405)

**After — operator.write.no-credential-enrollment**

![Restricted write disables personal GitHub credential enrollment and explains that identity and co-author credit remain available](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90ceccd7-15da-4f7a-a57e-7693a0e03088)

**Preserved — verified identity and editable co-author credit under restricted write**

![Verified octocat identity and enabled co-author preference under restricted write](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/030b3c4e-84f9-4fb2-89c4-072efb797aea)

## Contributor credit

Co-designed with @sallyom.

## Worked on by

prs.title: fix(codex): saved user turn is reported as a failed write when prompt annotation is refused
prs.body:
Closes #179892

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a saved user turn is reported as a failed write, and its persisted-message notification is skipped, when Codex native prompt annotation is refused.

## User Impact

User impact: a refused prompt annotation no longer raises a false persistence error for a turn that was saved, and persistence listeners are still told the admitted turn was persisted. A refused annotation with no host admission still writes nothing, as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Annotation only adds provenance to an admission that is already durable. The fix catches and logs annotation failures inside the mirror promise instead of letting them reject the promise registered with `markRuntimePersistencePending`. Keeping the catch inside that promise preserves the existing ordering: persistence waiters still wait for annotation to settle. When annotation fails and there is no host admission, the function returns as it did before rather than falling back to the generic mirror writer.

## Evidence

- New admission test where `annotateCurrentUserTurn` rejects: no `onPersistenceError`, exactly one persisted-message notification, the admitted message unchanged, and no extra transcript writes. It fails on `main` without this change (`onPersistenceError` is called).
- The existing `transcript-mirror*.test.ts` suites pass (44 tests).
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.



## Real behavior proof (production Gateway, before and after)

These are redacted logs from a production Gateway running 2026.10.5 (source build). This change was deployed there on 2026-10-21. Run and session IDs are replaced with labels; timestamps are UTC.

**Before the fix (2026-10-20).** Annotation was refused at turn start. When the run settled, the Gateway reported a failed user-turn write:

```
18:00:08.001 [agent/embedded] failed to mirror codex app-server prompt at turn start error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence" runId=<run-A> sessionId=<session-A>
18:03:46.522 [gateway] agent user transcript persistence failed: Error: native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence
```

The user turn had been saved anyway. In the agent's session database, `<session-A>` holds the admitted user message at seq 1 (created 18:00:05). The session's last event is at 18:03:46, the same moment the false error was logged.

**After the fix (2026-10-21 to 2026-10-22).** The same refusal happened on five Codex turns. Each one logged only the new warning, with no persistence error:

```
2026-10-21 19:51:25.581 [agent/embedded] skipped codex app-server native prompt annotation error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence" runId=<run-B> sessionId=<session-B>
2026-10-22 02:35:56.558 [agent/embedded] skipped codex app-server native prompt annotation error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence" runId=<run-C> sessionId=<session-C>
2026-10-22 13:25:39.513 [agent/embedded] skipped codex app-server native prompt annotation error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence" runId=<run-D> sessionId=<session-D>
2026-10-22 13:27:28.648 [agent/embedded] skipped codex app-server native prompt annotation error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence" runId=<run-E> sessionId=<session-E>
2026-10-22 13:30:47.032 [agent/embedded] skipped codex app-server native prompt annotation error="native prompt annotation would restore redacted evidence" runId=<run-F> sessionId=<session-F>
```

From 2026-10-20 to 2026-10-27, the Gateway journal has 1 `agent user transcript persistence failed` line. It is the pre-fix one above. In each of the five post-fix sessions, seq 1 is the saved `role: "user"` message, with no provenance annotation written.

**A caveat about current `main`.** The refusal seen in production, "would restore redacted evidence", was removed from `main` in #169063. The bug itself is still there. In `extensions/codex/src/app-server/transcript-mirror.ts` (`main` at 1b1c96578f6), `annotateCurrentUserTurn` is still awaited without a catch inside the promise registered with `markRuntimePersistencePending`. The annotation binder still throws on its remaining guards: "cannot replace an edited admission", "conflicts with recorded provenance", "does not match admitted content" and "no longer available for native annotation". Any of these produces the same false persistence error and skipped notification. I haven't observed those remaining refusals in production.

I re-ran the added admission test against `main` at 2868c5448f7 today. Without this change, it fails at `expect(onPersistenceError).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`. With this change applied, the file passes (5/5).

prs.title: feat(plugins): expose source preparation work in startup diagnostics
prs.body:
Related: #187350

## What Problem This Solves

`runtimePluginMs` combines source acquisition, dependency copying and receipt validation, leaving operators unable to tell which work dominates plugin startup. Add preparation counters at those existing owners and expose them alongside the startup timing.

## User Impact

`pluginPreparation.*` reports captures and retained-source reuse, selected package/dependency files, original and copied byte volumes, receipt passes/reads/bytes, hash-read bytes, and worker/host duration. Worker replies preserve measurements on errors, and completed startup metrics are snapshotted so a task that inherits the preparation scope cannot later rewrite a reported result.

Original bytes exclude retained ordinary files. Copied bytes include successfully completed private-tree copies, excluding native links; partial failed tree copies are not included. Byte volumes are logical, so filesystem cloning may avoid physical transfers. Worker and host wall durations overlap and must not be added or interpreted as CPU time. Loading, native admission, receipt verification, callback ownership and registry borrowing retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Earlier CI runs exposed a missing PR-wrapper inventory entry and a missing SAFETY rationale for the metrics reducer’s typed key iteration. Both are corrected; the final exact-head CI run passes.

The branch also incorporates current main (`c4b5c0aae2613d0860f399b62c927081a71067f5`) after a worker inspection conflict prevented the PR merge ref from being created. The resolution preserves main’s source inspection and custody handling and wraps that existing execution with the metrics scope.

The runtime preparation owners now expose their work so follow-up optimization can target the measured cost. This provides measurement for the installed-generation snapshot proposal; persistent source snapshots remain a separate change.

## Evidence

- Failing-first real capture accounting, inherited-scope mutation and retained-source-copy probes, followed by matching content and receipt digests.
- Real custody probe: first acquisition uses 45 original bytes and 135 copied bytes (capture, custody seed and private fork); subsequent reuse uses 0 original bytes and 45 copied bytes. Both verify identical contents and digests in independent private paths.
- The runtime-group metrics/Gateway run passed 10 tests. The custody/streaming run passed 15 tests, covering changed retained bytes, escaping links, native streaming, replaced destinations and copy/cleanup failures.
- Targeted lint and the agents-other/plugins-platform test type graphs passed.
- CI corrections: all five wrapper closure/provisioning cases passed on Linux after the inventory fix. The assertion-safety ratchet reproduced the missing rationale locally before correction and passed afterward; the correction also passed independent review.
- The current-main conflict resolution passed 22 focused tests covering runtime metric snapshots, worker callback/lifetime behavior, source inspection, native admission, capture accounting and retained custody reuse. The two affected type graphs, focused lint, formatting and an independent isolated review also passed.
- Full `pnpm build` passed before the current-main merge, including declarations, plugin SDK exports, UI and startup metadata. The updated candidate passed the focused checks above and independent review with no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Final exact-head CI [41146285215](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41146285215), attempt 1, passed at `a1788dfd75659401e02f423b902a2a8214f9b732`, including baseline ratchets and the final CI gate.

Three separate-process controls used the real runtime-group preparation over 6,503 synthetic files (26,414,754 bytes), with metadata already prepared. Every run recorded one capture, no reuse, 3 package files, 6,500 dependency files, 26,414,754 original/copied/receipt-read bytes, and 52,829,508 hash-read bytes. Contents, digest and private callback state matched.

| Control | runtimePluginMs | Worker ms | Host ms | Event-loop p99 ms | Maximum delay ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| C1 | 138709.06 | 136037.48 | 136567.08 | 4.710 | 2134.098 |
| C2 | 81748.11 | 79107.09 | 79340.17 | 4.829 | 2468.994 |
| C3 | 88228.57 | 86279.54 | 86477.41 | 5.386 | 1937.760 |

All three observed 110,674 synchronous Node filesystem calls against originals and 208,496 against artifacts. The probe includes host and worker wrappers, excludes asynchronous/native calls that bypass those wrappers, and adds measurement overhead. These are A/A controls on a heavily loaded Mac; they support the work counts, not a speedup claim. Each run emitted the existing five-second retirement warning during physical cleanup, then exited successfully with no remaining capture files; C3 measured final cleanup at 37.59 seconds.

The 242 added test lines have matching allocation. Final exact-head CI passed the baseline ratchets; no inherited-failure exception is needed for this head. Earlier failed runs and their corrections are retained as historical evidence rather than described as current results.

prs.title: improve: speed up large-buffer test assertions
prs.body:
Related: #188777, #188823

## What Problem This Solves

RFB, borrowed-file-descriptor, and avatar-cache tests spend seconds recursively comparing large byte arrays.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. These focused tests run faster with complete-byte integrity and every existing lifecycle assertion retained.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use native `Buffer.equals` with failure labels at seven comparison sites. The avatar expectation uses an identically sized Buffer, which remains a Uint8Array, and native equality rejects missing or non-byte-array results. No new helper or production change.

## Evidence

Three successful serial before and three after runs **per file**, against frozen base `e279b64ffe86578edff6c72cd39f98893a0e5ff2`, with the same host, private frozen dependencies, runtime, task temp roots, and caches:

prs.title: feat(control-ui): reflect session access changes immediately
prs.body:
Related: #112760 (closed as not planned).

[steipete’s closing comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/112760#issuecomment-6380197979) says current main resolved the original list-absence symptom and an explicit access-revoked signal is an optional follow-up, requiring a concrete current UI failure for a fresh issue. This PR proposes that optional contract; whether to accept it remains a maintainer decision.

## What Problem This Solves

This PR proposes an explicit Control UI signal when a sharing change changes a viewer’s access to an open session. A missing row in a filtered session list is not an access decision.

## User Impact

The open composer immediately becomes unavailable after access is revoked or changes to read-only, and recovers when shared access returns. Suggest mode continues to allow a suggestion draft until access is revoked. Missing list rows remain neutral. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Publish a connection-specific `session.access.changed` event after a committed visibility or membership change. The closed payload contains only `agentId`, `sessionKey`, `sessionId`, and `access` (`revoked`, `read-only`, or `read-write`). Publication uses the canonical sharing target and current recipient authority; no-op, denied, stale, and unrelated-recipient changes do not publish an access fact.

Control UI stores restrictions for the admitted connection and exact session instance. A restoration retires the matching restriction; existing session-row and scope checks still decide whether an action is allowed. Composer, pending typing, Talk, read-marker, and dashboard-default writers consume that state. Disconnect or connection replacement retires it. This is additive: older clients may ignore the event; native composer behavior, authorization policy, persistent schema, and protocol version are unchanged.

## Evidence

Current source: `a5c6206e9a5ebfe2161c707e5b84ec29c25e1f71`, after resolving the actual upstream conflicts and a UI file-length check failure. [Immutable current proof packet](https://github.com/zhangguiping-xydt/openclaw/blob/b961bd67259fedcf8eb4e521526ec6242d36fa7e/README.md) contains eight exact production UI captures, their DOM observations, a case-by-case socket trace and original-evidence hashes. All fifteen public files were fetched into a separate empty repository and their hashes matched.

- **Checks:** all 31 changed paths passed formatting; all 17 changed UI paths passed type-aware lint. The affected reply/state/sharing owners and consumers passed **3 complete files / 176 tests** on the exact final candidate tree. The execution receipts retain their original pre-normalization HEAD; the source tree did not change when the two local tail commits were combined. All **seven affected core, protocol, Gateway-test and UI-test TypeScript graphs** passed on the final HEAD. The earlier integrated 13-file/256-test run retains its original source binding and is not counted as another run on this HEAD.
- **Normal builds:** a full scripts-enabled frozen install in this worktree at `ec9f0cb1dc00` completed normally. The final candidate retains all 235 manifest/lock/settings/patch inputs, module metadata and seven tool hashes; a new native audit confirmed the same physical module roots, all 5,309 symlinks and 451 executable helpers. Fresh normal `qaRuntime` and `pnpm ui:build` builds passed on the final HEAD. The default official-selector CLI admission required no build, runtime postbuild or immutable repair; no bypass flag or handwritten stamp was used.
- **Whole Gateway and browser:** separate current wire, public `users.setRole` revocation and production Chrome modes passed and naturally exited. The browser entered the selected session through its real initial-history subscription and description, observed seven access changes, and retained the draft through restriction/restoration. [All eight captures and observed states](https://github.com/zhangguiping-xydt/openclaw/blob/b961bd67259fedcf8eb4e521526ec6242d36fa7e/ui.projection.json) are bound to that exact session instance and personally inspected. No chat or suggestion was submitted in the browser. Each same-run import trace was checked against the normal build inventory and all four canonical emitted Gateway owner regions.
- **Recipient authority at final I/O:** the separate production sharing/storage/connection/WebSocket owner fixture exercised identity reassignment and write-scope withdrawal both before publication and at the owner-minted target Set. Every case kept the same socket open, sent/received zero stale-recipient access frames and delivered one matching control frame. [The four-case projection](https://github.com/zhangguiping-xydt/openclaw/blob/b961bd67259fedcf8eb4e521526ec6242d36fa7e/owner-transport.cases.projection.json) names each actual send/receive and FIFO row in [the redacted trace](https://github.com/zhangguiping-xydt/openclaw/blob/b961bd67259fedcf8eb4e521526ec6242d36fa7e/owner-transport.redacted.ndjson). Whole-run totals remain viewer 6/control 10 because they include permitted priming/restoration; they are not the four negative cases. Production storage resources retired normally, the whole Node process exited naturally, and final SQLite/frame checks passed after join.

| Boundary | Drift | Stale viewer send / receive | Control send → receive rows | Viewer FIFO rows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before publication | Identity | 0 / 0 | 34 → 39 | 43 → 45 |
| Before publication | Write scope | 0 / 0 | 64 → 69 | 73 → 75 |
| Owner-minted target Set | Identity | 0 / 0 | 95 → 100 | 104 → 106 |
| Owner-minted target Set | Write scope | 0 / 0 | 126 → 131 | 135 → 137 |

Read-only restriction:

![Current read-only composer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhangguiping-xydt/openclaw/b961bd67259fedcf8eb4e521526ec6242d36fa7e/images/02-read-only-disabled.png)

Draft access revoked:

![Current draft restriction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhangguiping-xydt/openclaw/b961bd67259fedcf8eb4e521526ec6242d36fa7e/images/04-draft-revoked-disabled.png)

Suggestion draft retained during restriction:

![Current suggestion restriction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhangguiping-xydt/openclaw/b961bd67259fedcf8eb4e521526ec6242d36fa7e/images/07-suggest-withdrawn-disabled.png)

Shared access restored:

![Current restored composer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zhangguiping-xydt/openclaw/b961bd67259fedcf8eb4e521526ec6242d36fa7e/images/08-shared-final-restored.png)

**Compatibility and risk.** This adds a closed four-field observation, not authority. The visibility-filter exception admits only the connection owner's minted payload for its captured recipient; current identity/scope/session checks still run at actual delivery. Restoring access only removes the matching transient restriction and does not override existing row or scope decisions. The public role-revocation lane uses the supported role RPC and actual connection closure. Silent identity/scope changes in the separate owner lane are explicit composition fixtures, not a public authentication API. The whole-Gateway lane uses a trusted loopback identity peer and a metadata-only model fixture; no external identity provider, real provider account or tenant is claimed. Native Swift/Android runtime remains untested.

The optional notification direction and visibility-filter exception remain maintainer decisions described in [the review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179661#issuecomment-6346166861); supplying proof does not settle that product decision. This feature changes no persistent schema, configuration format or protocol version. Current source declares state/agent schemas 34/37. The earlier [released-state/settings control](https://github.com/zhangguiping-xydt/openclaw/blob/800c95223c27dfcd78452de9c810e96f5720d761/README.md) remains historical 20/25 → 32/34 evidence for source `460d0939aa0e`; no new 20/25 → 34/37 migration or Doctor claim is made. Historical failures, pending inner observations and original receipts remain unchanged; the new outer qualifications are separate.

prs.title: fix(whatsapp): honor channels.whatsapp.implicitMentions in group gating
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp group gating never consulted the `implicitMentions` policy that core defines and Slack already honors, so `channels.whatsapp[.accounts.*].implicitMentions` (and `channels.defaults.implicitMentions`) was silently ignored on WhatsApp. Every reply/quote to a bot message counted as an implicit mention and satisfied `requireMention`, with no way to disable it. Under `selfChatMode` (bot on the operator's own number) this means any reply to the operator's own messages auto-triggers the bot with no `@mention`. Closes #127308.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveInboundMentionDecision` already derives an allow-list from `policy.implicitMentions`, and `resolveChannelImplicitMentions` resolves account/channel/defaults precedence. Slack passes `implicitMentions` into the decision; WhatsApp did not.

- **Gating:** `group-gating.ts` resolves `implicitMentions` and passes it into `resolveInboundMentionDecision`.
- **Per-key account-default inheritance:** WhatsApp named accounts inherit `accounts.default`. The resolver gains an opt-in `inheritAccountDefault` that layers `accounts.default` **per key** between the named account and channel/defaults, so a partial named override (e.g. `accounts.work.implicitMentions.replyToBot: false`) never clears a sibling flag set on `accounts.default` (e.g. `quotedBot: false`). Slack path unchanged.
- **Config contract:** `implicitMentions` declared on the typed WhatsApp config (`WhatsAppSharedConfig`, channel + account), the zod schema, and the WhatsApp UI hints. Additive/optional with backward-compatible defaults, so no migration is needed; generated channel-config metadata regenerated.

## User Impact

Operators set `channels.whatsapp.implicitMentions.quotedBot: false` (or `replyToBot`, `threadParticipation`), at channel or account scope, to require an explicit mention. Named accounts inherit `accounts.default` per flag. Defaults unchanged (all `true`), so existing behavior is preserved.

## Evidence

- **Boundary spec** `group-gating.implicit-mentions.test.ts` drives the real `applyGroupGating` decision with a constructed WhatsApp group inbound; four cases, each **failing on pre-fix code** and passing with the fix: reply-to-bot admitted by default; skipped when `quotedBot: false`; named account inherits `accounts.default`; and a **partial named override preserves the default's other flags** (this last one fails on the prior revision of this PR, confirming the per-key fix).
- **Schema** `config-schema.test.ts`: `implicitMentions` validates at channel and account scope (fails pre-fix).
- Core filter behavior covered by `src/channels/mention-gating.test.ts`.
- `pnpm check:changed` (format + typecheck + lint + all guards + generated-metadata) passes.
- **Runtime verdict (real resolution logic).** Running the production `resolveChannelImplicitMentions` over the scenario matrix (`inheritAccountDefault: true`, as WhatsApp calls it) yields the resolved policy each inbound is gated against. The partial-override case shows `quotedBot` staying `false` even though the named account only set `replyToBot`:

```json
{
  "proof": "whatsapp-implicit-mentions",
  "allPass": true,
  "cases": [
    { "case": "default (no config)", "resolvedPolicy": { "replyToBot": true,  "quotedBot": true,  "threadParticipation": true }, "quotedReplyTriggersTurn": true },
    { "case": "channel quotedBot:false", "resolvedPolicy": { "replyToBot": true,  "quotedBot": false, "threadParticipation": true }, "quotedReplyTriggersTurn": false },
    { "case": "named account inherits accounts.default.quotedBot:false", "accountId": "work", "resolvedPolicy": { "replyToBot": true,  "quotedBot": false, "threadParticipation": true }, "quotedReplyTriggersTurn": false },
    { "case": "partial named override keeps accounts.default.quotedBot:false", "accountId": "work", "resolvedPolicy": { "replyToBot": false, "quotedBot": false, "threadParticipation": true }, "quotedReplyTriggersTurn": false }
  ]
}
```
- **Inspectable after-fix run** — the boundary spec drives the production `applyGroupGating` decision (not a mock of the logic), so its output is the runtime admission decision for a WhatsApp group inbound:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/group-gating.implicit-mentions.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 ✓ applyGroupGating implicit-mention policy > admits a reply-to-bot message by default (quoted_bot implicit mention)
 ✓ applyGroupGating implicit-mention policy > skips a reply-to-bot message when implicitMentions.quotedBot is false
 ✓ applyGroupGating implicit-mention policy > inherits accounts.default.implicitMentions for a named account
 ✓ applyGroupGating implicit-mention policy > keeps accounts.default flags when a named account overrides a different flag
 Tests  4 passed (4)
```
The `quotedBot: false` case is the config-driven suppression; each case fails on pre-fix code.
- **Live observation (redacted).** On a live WhatsApp self-number gateway, suppressing the `quoted_bot` implicit mention stopped a group reply to the operator's own message from triggering a bot turn, while an explicit `@`-mention still triggered; bare text with neither did not. Group/number identifiers omitted. This validates the runtime decision the PR makes config-driven; the config resolution path itself is exercised by the boundary spec above.

prs.title: feature(system): add heartbeat status for cadence and activeHours
prs.body:
Implements #178015

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot see heartbeat cadence, activeHours membership, and a next-fire estimate in one place — today they must combine config diving with `system heartbeat last` / `automations show`.

## User Impact

User impact: `openclaw system heartbeat status` prints a Gateway-free JSON status backed by the selected agent's surviving proactive / migrated Automation job (cadence, activeHours, `withinActiveHours`, and a next-fire estimate from `job.state.nextRunAtMs` when present).

## Why This Change Was Made

After the Automations cutover, scheduling ownership lives on persisted Automation jobs — not `agents.defaults.heartbeat` (schemas reject those fields). This command consumes `readHeartbeatSummarySnapshot` / `projectHeartbeatSummary` plus the job's `activeHours` and scheduling state. No Gateway RPC and no scheduler ownership changes.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/infra/heartbeat-cli-status.ts` (+test), `src/cli/system-cli.ts`, `src/cli/system-cli.test.ts`, `src/cli/system-output-mode.ts`, `docs/cli/system.md`, `test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs`
- Unit (infra / database-worker): 7/7 pass; system-cli: 7/7 pass
- Packaged CLI: `node openclaw.mjs system heartbeat status --json` after `qaRuntime` build

## Real behavior proof

### Behavior or issue addressed

Status must project current Automation job state (fresh / migrated), not retired heartbeat config. Enabled, disabled, outside-active-hours, and ambiguous-agent cases must be visible on packaged CLI.

### Canonical reachability path

Packaged `openclaw system heartbeat status` → `resolveHeartbeatCliStatus` → `readHeartbeatSummarySnapshot` / `projectHeartbeatSummary` + job `activeHours` / `state.nextRunAtMs`.

### Shared helper / provider constraint check

Reuses existing heartbeat summary snapshot helpers and `isCronWithinActiveHours`. Does not change Gateway wake RPC or the heartbeat runner scheduler. Agent selection uses configured / ambient owners (no invented `main`).

### Real environment tested

Packaged CLI (`node openclaw.mjs`) after `qaRuntime` build; temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` with proactive jobs seeded via `createDefaultProactiveJob` + `saveProactiveJobsForTest` (same receipt pair setup/Doctor own).

### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# seed disabled / outside / enabled / ambiguous Automation fixtures under OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR
node openclaw.mjs system heartbeat status --json
node openclaw.mjs system heartbeat status --agent ops --json   # ambiguous fleet
```

### Evidence after fix

```text
# disabled job
{"agentId":"main","jobId":"1d3c26ed-…","enabled":false,"every":"disabled","nextFireSource":"disabled","nextFireAt":null,…}

# closed activeHours window (start==end)
{"agentId":"main","jobId":"9bfd00de-…","enabled":true,"every":"1800000ms","everyMs":1800000,"withinActiveHours":false,"nextFireSource":"outside-active-hours","nextFireAt":null,"activeHours":{"start":"12:00","end":"12:00","timezone":"UTC"},…}

# enabled inside window (job.state.nextRunAtMs)
```

prs.title: fix(infra): name the rejected artifact when snapshot reclamation skips
prs.body:
Related #188593

## What Problem This Solves

When the SQLite snapshot reclaimer finds an entry it doesn't recognize in an abandoned staging directory, it skips that directory with a fixed message: `Skipped SQLite snapshot reclamation: Unrecognized snapshot artifact`. The message (structured payload `{}`) does not say which file or directory caused the skip. In #188593 the warning fires about 14 times an hour and staging data is never reclaimed. Neither the operator nor a maintainer can tell from the log what the reclaimer rejected.

## User Impact

The skip warning now names the rejected entry relative to the staging directory, for example `Unrecognized snapshot artifact: stray-notes.txt` or `Unrecognized snapshot directory: openclaw/foo`. An operator can then find and remove the stray file, and a report can say exactly what was rejected. Reclamation policy is unchanged: unknown content is still never deleted.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper's next step on the issue: "Establish a failing worker-to-log regression for missing artifact context and obtain the rejected cache staging tree with timestamps before deciding whether payload recognition needs another repair." `beginSqliteSnapshotRetirement` is where the entry is rejected, so the name is added there. Both rejection errors carry the path relative to the staging root, with `/` separators, so no home directory or cache root reaches the log. The worker path forwards the same message string, so it carries the name too. Whether the reporter's Linux tree needs a recognition change can be decided once the warning names the artifact.

## Evidence

Real Gateway on Windows 11 / Node 26.12.1 with isolated state and a private cache (`XDG_CACHE_HOME`).
- **Setup:** before start, two abandoned staging directories aged 48 h are planted. `…-Valid1` holds `database.sqlite`; `…-Unkn01` holds `database.sqlite` plus `stray-notes.txt`.
- **Run:** the idle `maintenance:sqlite-snapshots` task runs about 30 s after ready. Lines come from the Gateway file log.
- **Variable:** same script; only `src/infra/sqlite-snapshot-retirement.ts` differs between main ab54786 and this branch.

Raw Gateway file-log lines from both runs, plus the cache tree after each run. `_meta` is trimmed to hostname/date/level, and the hostname is redacted:

![raw log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/188593/proof-188593-raw.png)

Summary:

![proof](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wr-web/openclaw/proof-assets/188593/proof-188593.png)

| | main ab54786 | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| skip warning for `Unkn01` | `Skipped SQLite snapshot reclamation: Unrecognized snapshot artifact` (payload `{}`, same line as the report) | `Skipped SQLite snapshot reclamation: Unrecognized snapshot artifact: stray-notes.txt` |
| valid abandoned `Valid1` | reclaimed (`Reclaimed 20 bytes …`) | reclaimed (`Reclaimed 20 bytes …`) |
| directory with the unknown file | kept | kept |

The regression is in `src/infra/sqlite-snapshot-staging.ownership.test.ts` ("reclaims only stale %s snapshots", covering worker, legacy, flat and nested layouts). The existing skip assertion now also requires the rejected entry name. It is a one-line change, so the test-line count is unchanged: `main` is currently above the test-line ceiling, and any net-positive test growth fails `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`. Against main's `sqlite-snapshot-retirement.ts` all 4 layouts fail. With this change all 4 pass (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/infra/sqlite-snapshot-staging.ownership.test.ts -t "reclaims only stale"`).

Gates run locally: oxfmt, oxlint, `pnpm check:line-cap-ratchet`.

prs.title: fix(macos): preserve the selected CLI when inspecting a managed install
prs.body:
Closes #140128

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS CLI selection changing when the app inspects a ready managed CLI while an external CLI is selected.

## User Impact

Inspecting installations no longer changes the selected CLI. A successful managed install or update still selects the verified managed CLI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed inspection returns status without persisting selection. Discovery retains its existing selection behavior, while installation and update record the managed CLI only after their success checks. No preference keys or formats changed, and no CLI is removed.

## Evidence

Current product head: `a2c6197e80d459f03b88b8de3030e8ca67e6ddda`. The GitHub web merge on 29 October combined prior head `4298606a9e38b4665dc014a71fd81bfb451d97af` with main `878e682ecc3228e7bb9a535254e0bddaa4d97e7f`. All earlier proof below remains pinned to its actual revision; it is not current-head execution.

- **Current PR CI:** [Run 40975271680](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40975271680) passed its selected preflight, security-fast, and native-i18n jobs. The preflight log records synthetic merge checkout `ada0f18fae53e97108a139c83ca5f708a73d7436`, merging current product `a2c6197` into main `878e682`. Its macOS Swift and macOS Node jobs were skipped. This is current PR composition evidence, not native runtime proof.

- **Prior-head native-owner proof:** [Hosted macOS run 38597006067](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/38597006067) passed with QA/workflow `4cf95ff77fae422b8b380f4a2c49c4101a8f38b1` and clean initial/final product `76ee71b`. macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.0, Swift 6.4 arm64: 56 Swift Testing declarations across four suites, expanding to 64 executed cases (50 single-case declarations plus 14 cases from six parameterized declarations). Selection, managed-update success/failure, and older/missing/revoked canonical-verification controls passed. These are executable fixtures, not real npm installations or signed-app proof.
- **Prior-head canonical CI:** [Run 38599555604](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38599555604) passed at exact product `76ee71b`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Its macOS Swift and macOS Node jobs were skipped, not executed; native proof comes from the separate owner run above.
- **Prior applicability:** Source review of then-current main `794d6500f382311cab58f5d474a9ef248598e5f2` still finds the ready `managedStatus` selection write. This is source evidence, not a new live reproduction.
- **Current-head review:** [ClawSweeper Revision 14](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) reviewed `a2c6197` on 29 October. It reports no findings, patch quality 4/6, and overall/proof 2/6. App-entry inspection and verified installation/update evidence, plus an existing-state upgrade from `v2026.10.9` preserving settings and data, remain required. The completed review does not establish a data-model defect.
- **Prior-head review:** [ClawSweeper's review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) at `76ee71b` identifies no code findings; app-entry and upgrade evidence remains outstanding. Revision 14 above supersedes that historical review.
- **Fixture follow-up:** [Commit `4298606`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/4298606a9e38b4665dc014a71fd81bfb451d97af) changes exactly two positive Node fixture literals, preserving all assertions, old-runtime controls, and production source. Whitespace and exact source-delta checks passed. [Previous-head canonical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121014753) passed, including its CI gate, native i18n, and security-fast. The prior [combined CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40121219433) also reports success at `4298606`. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed; no current-head native execution proof is claimed.

### Remaining qualification

- **App entry and update:** The owner tests and retained real-npm evidence cover the affected **unbundled** discovery/inspection path at their recorded revisions. Signed packaged-app proof is separate: it must establish the actual legacy-service inspection/update routing, selection preservation, and verified canonical selection. A fresh bundled no-op or forced override cannot stand in for the original bug. The 56 owner declarations do not directly cover `install(target:)` success/compatibility-failure selection paths. The discovery regression seeds the external tuple, so it proves preservation rather than independently proving first-discovery persistence.
- **Existing-state upgrade:** A disposable latest-stable-to-candidate app upgrade with existing settings/data retained remains unrun. No preference/schema format changed, and source review found no data-model incompatibility; the missing upgrade run is a proof gap, not an established migration defect.
- **Current composition:** The PR-added selection fixture and PR-extended stale-update fixture now emit Node `v24.22.1`, matching the inspected minimum and remaining supported by the original PR base. This two-line fixture-only repair is published at `4298606`; native execution of the current composition remains unverified. This does not relabel the pinned original-head result or establish a production incompatibility.

### Retained real coexisting-installation proof

[Run 37386979616](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616) compared earlier product `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b` with baseline `3b16db73c0b5209aad2ee7c3fb5ddfb12fb208f9`, governed by corrected QA workflow `b166bce6b7ee4fc86631cb491fd7c17990be6362`. The candidate preserved external selection through ready managed inspection and left initially unset executable/version preferences unset: one native test passed in 74.660 seconds. The baseline failed exactly the five expected selection assertions; its verifier rejected other failures.

Both jobs used two distinct real `openclaw@2026.9.8` npm installations with verified published SHA-512 integrity on disposable hosted macOS runners. [Candidate receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11380755806) and [baseline receipts](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/37386979616/artifacts/11379004102) contain selection cells, installation identities, logs, and strict verification summaries. This covers inspection only at the earlier revision, not current signed-app install/update or upgrade behavior. Preceding failed QA attempts do not establish this result.

<details>
<summary>Historical CI and source qualification</summary>

[CI 37194001816](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001816), including native Swift, [macOS Periphery 37194001640](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001640), and [shared OpenClawKit Periphery 37194001665](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37194001665) passed at earlier head `a38ed66158bd270bd45607411aadb5862b299b8b`. Previously reported formatting, whitespace checks, and scoped Codex AutoReview remain historical proof, not a fresh review of the current head.

</details>

Maintainer review remains separate. The fixture-only follow-up changed no production source. The current head also includes the later main merge. Swift owner tests, real installation, and app upgrade have not been executed for the current head in this Windows review.

prs.title: fix(feishu): retry transient message send failures
prs.body:
Related: #90804

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes dropped Feishu text, card, image, and file messages when message creation or reply encounters a short-lived connection or server failure. A lost response after acceptance must not produce a duplicate message.

## User Impact

Message sends recover from transient failures with at most two retries. Permanent API errors still fail immediately. Sender cancellation stops later attempts, and accepted streaming cards can still update and close when Feishu omits the optional message receipt.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each message create/reply operation uses one UUID across all attempts, including the initial streaming-card message and uploaded-media message. The existing Feishu request owner now opts those operations into network, HTTP 408/425/5xx, and message-in-progress (230049) recovery. Existing rate-limit handling, per-attempt sender authority, durable dispatch accounting, and withdrawn-reply fallback rules are preserved. Image/file uploads and CardKit entity creation do not opt into transient replay.

## Evidence

- Integrated current main `08229175e9b5d9133a6739d360a4fa1269ef3a2c` to resolve conflicts, preserving contributor history and current send/streaming owners.
- Added focused regressions for an accepted message with a lost response (direct and reply, stable UUID and one simulated visible message), cancellation during backoff, fulfilled/rejected 230049, opt-in HTTP/network recovery, media-message UUID reuse, image/file upload non-retry, and streaming retry followed by receipt-free update/close. Existing missing-receipt and withdrawn-target tests remain in place.
- Fresh independent static review completed; its actionable test findings were corrected. Isolated trusted-main autoreview of the exact final tree: scoped-clean through P2, with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Current head: `70b58575edd3edc60dde7ff25141f36be29bb77f`. [Exact-head secretless GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37470343988): **passed**. Extension production/test types, extension lint, formatting/guards, source contracts, package boundaries, security, and all seven selected Node rows passed.
- Feishu test shard: **31 files / 585 tests passed**, Vitest duration **55.45 s**. The bundled CI test step took **217 s**, including its separate selected sibling config. All five changed test files were selected: `send.retry.test.ts`, `send.reply-fallback.test.ts`, `media.retry.test.ts`, `send.test.ts`, and `streaming-card.test.ts`. Logs explicitly confirm the lost-response direct/reply, cancellation during backoff, image/file upload non-retry, and receipt-free streaming retry/update/close regressions passed.
- Fresh independent static review and isolated trusted-main autoreview: no remaining accepted/actionable findings through P2. The first CI candidate caught a missing-braces lint rule in a new test assertion; a mechanical braces-only correction was independently reviewed before the passing final run.
- Installed `oxfmt` and `git diff --check`: passed. Candidate code was not executed on the credentialed local host; no separate local one-worker timing is claimed. Current proof is isolated CI/harness evidence, not a new authenticated Feishu message test.
- Current dependency contract personally inspected: `@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk@1.74.0` declares `data.uuid?: string` on both create and reply, issues one POST per SDK invocation, and fulfills business-error bodies through its response interceptor. Official [create](https://larksuite.github.io/oapi-sdk-java/com/lark/oapi/service/im/v1/model/CreateMessageReqBody.Builder.html) and [reply](https://larksuite.github.io/oapi-sdk-java/com/lark/oapi/service/im/v1/model/ReplyMessageReqBody.Builder.html) contracts document that the same UUID succeeds at most once within one hour.

### Current-head real SDK transport proof (2026-10-07)

[Secretless transport-proof run](https://github.com/litang9/openclaw/actions/runs/37631147371/job/112825441075): **passed**. The standard GitHub-hosted Ubuntu runner anonymously fetched and checked the immutable candidate `70b58575edd3edc60dde7ff25141f36be29bb77f`; the supplemental workflow itself is commit `fc200e9c118d6db640c50f24b1c869b201dd4f2f`. [Reviewed harness](https://github.com/litang9/openclaw/blob/fc200e9c118d6db640c50f24b1c869b201dd4f2f/transport-proof.test.ts) SHA-256: `c11599908db632ef331432c6d080414d5d5719086b6d002bd7f5eb53344d316e`.

The harness calls the current `sendMessageFeishu` inside `withFeishuSendContext`, then traverses account/target resolution, the idempotent message owner, the shared request/retry owner, dispatch accounting, `createFeishuClient`, real `@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk@1.74.0`, Axios HTTP, and production receipt construction. SDK methods, the HTTP instance, retry scheduler, and send owner remain real. A transport-only request interceptor restricts requests to a loopback fixture, with synthetic account/token/message data, redirects disabled, and ambient proxy settings removed. The SDK performs its own token exchange and Bearer-header serialization.

prs.title: fix(workboard): keep completed artifacts after run cleanup
prs.body:
Related: #111496

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users completing Workboard tasks could lose locally referenced generated files when automatic cleanup removed their Git-clean managed worktree. The card keeps its artifact path, but the bytes disappear. Protecting only run-end cleanup merely defers that loss to idle, count, or size GC.

## Why This Change Was Made

Workboard owns artifact interpretation and its durable generation journal; core owns generic, exact-owner claims against immutable worktree IDs and enforces those claims at automatic-removal admission. This follows the [requested ownership boundary](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111497#issuecomment-5143059431), without a Workboard-specific core scan or process-local lock.

Preparation is durable before acquisition. A card publishes its new references only after protection is acquired; the card, active generation, and obsolete-generation release obligations commit together. Cancellation/release is terminal, and failed releases remain durably retryable. An exact owner-matched removed identity with an existing snapshot can enroll before restoration, so restore does not create an unprotected window. A startup reconciliation failure warns without disabling change events or the existing real maintenance timer.

The latest commit also fixes a boundary exposed by native POSIX proof: `kind: worktree` represents both a source-checkout request and a materialized managed workspace. Only the latter carries `sourcePath`. Retention now uses that existing discriminator, preserving exact-owner/identity checks while allowing cleanup to return the card to its source checkout. Same-path edits preserve protection.

## User Impact

- Enrolled local references survive automatic run-end, idle, count, and size cleanup, including process restart.
- Removing, externalizing, archiving, or deleting references leaves durable release obligations so ordinary collection can resume.
- URL-only and canonically outside-worktree references do not pin unrelated checkouts. Native inbound aliases still protect the actual referenced worktree.
- A claim is not a backup: explicit operator removal, snapshot contents, and removed-snapshot expiry are unchanged. Enrollment cannot recover already-lost bytes or turn ignored output into snapshot-backed content.

### Compatibility and scope

The two tables are lazy/same-version additive for stable pre-feature schemas. Older binaries do not enforce claims: readable storage does **not** make downgrade artifact-safe. Earlier unmerged preview table shapes are not automatically migrated; preserve artifacts and use a targeted migration or disposable test state, never delete a shared state database as a workaround.

The persistent SDK, snapshot-backed removed-identity enrollment, and upgrade/downgrade boundaries still require maintainer acceptance. The [specific decision request](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111497#issuecomment-5600556086) is open; neither tests nor this contributor's implementation choice constitute approval.

One artifact-reference lifecycle PR: **30 files, +2157/-87** against frozen base `20e0ed5`. The latest follow-up changes only two existing Workboard files (+65/-2), mostly regressions, with one production state discriminator. It adds no API, table, dependency, callback, configuration, or new subsystem. Generic enforcement and its first Workboard consumer remain together; the proof harness lives on a separate validation-only branch, outside this PR diff.

## Evidence

Candidate: **`849b9156c0d8ca5a9fe7d6252edff7a6b68edb16`**. Frozen pre-retention baseline: `20e0ed521c00fd38b1d4d003636fa4ddd3bf2066`.

The [public proof bundle](https://gist.github.com/ooiuuii/9e28d79c9b962ca5017a6e82f8644492) preserves the original baseline RED and historical receipts, with separate current-head Windows and POSIX/upgrade projections. Recorders, commands, immutable harness source, raw-receipt hashes, source identities, worker PIDs, checks, and timing are linked there. Only redacted synthetic evidence is published, never configuration, credentials, personal paths, transcripts, or application databases.

### Current-head real behavior

- **Windows:** all four fresh runs on clean committed `849b9156` pass: lifecycle **5/5**, legacy first-enrollment/restore **5/5**, startup-release **1/1**, and supplemental events **3/3**. Eight distinct workers exit successfully, with unchanged clean before/after source identities. Actual maintenance retries complete after **62,737 / 62,763 ms**, each with two attempts and one successful release; subsequent real GC removes the retired checkout.
- **Native POSIX containment:** the secretless [Ubuntu run 34347410012](https://github.com/ooiuuii/openclaw/actions/runs/34347410012) passes all three fresh, two-process lanes: idle **6/6**, count **6/6**, size **6/6**. Native inbound symlinks protect the actual artifact; URL-only, outside-path, and outbound-symlink controls retain their exact references/outside bytes while the unrelated checkout is actually removed. Each lane then externalizes the retained reference and requires real removal with that same lane's GC parameters. Count/size clocks are not aged, so idle GC cannot stand in for them.
- **Existing-database upgrade:** the same run creates a real database/card through baseline `20e0ed5`, then opens it through `849b9156` in another process. All **4/4** checks pass: complete card preserved, both retention tables added, core/Workboard `user_version` unchanged at **16/0**, then real run-end protection, count GC protection, and externalization/removal. This proves the documented stable-baseline upgrade, not preview-table migration or downgrade protection.
- The Linux job independently reproduces and strictly verifies baseline artifact/checkout loss with the card/reference still present. All five Linux receipts have successful separate workers and unchanged clean source identities; the downloaded redacted artifact was checked against the pinned head/base. Recorder/workflow source is immutable at [proof commit f036c9d](https://github.com/ooiuuii/openclaw/tree/f036c9daaa723d584e4e2b7a2caecacc80a357b6); it is outside this product PR.

These are production source-owner/lifecycle runs using real Git, SQLite, files, separate processes, and unmocked disk capacity in isolated synthetic state. No installed Gateway, channel, provider, UI, or production configuration is started. Event coverage observes the real service's output sink, not network/UI delivery. Idle eligibility advances the exported service clock; startup retry uses real wall time. The release outage is deliberately injected. Externalization uses `https://example.invalid/report.txt` and proves reference retirement, not remote upload.

### Focused checks and CI

- Both new source-request/cleanup regressions failed with the unavailable-source-repository error before the fix. The final current-head delta passes **25 tests across three files**, type-aware focused lint, formatting, and `git diff --check`.
- The Windows outbound-junction regression requires real registry removal, `.git` disappearance, source-checkout fallback, unchanged references, and intact outside bytes. Git for Windows can leave an ignored junction directory after deregistration; a pure Git probe reproduced that without this PR. That independent existing cleanup behavior is excluded, not counted as complete Windows directory removal. The POSIX standalone proof retains its strict whole-directory disappearance assertion.
- The earlier broader suite on `78a1e91` had 95 passes and three unchanged Windows baseline failures (CRLF, executable-bit fixture, path separators). Its [full upstream CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34338980894), including typecheck and required CI gate, passed. This is explicitly historical evidence, not a current-head CI pass.
- Current-head primary [upstream run 34347235499](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34347235499) failed at GitHub startup **before creating any test job**. Its annotation reports an unexpected GitHub error. Author retry was denied with “Must have admin rights to Repository”; a maintainer must retry it. Separate dependency and security guards passed. No workflow was weakened or empty commit added to manufacture green.

### Review closeout

The whole preceding candidate was reviewed against `20e0ed5`; the final two-file follow-up was then reviewed using the repository's structured Codex helper: `--mode local --engine codex --max-priority P2`, frozen lifecycle context, 5,440-byte delta. Final source verification completed; result **exit 0 / scoped-clean**, no P0–P2 findings. Focused tests passed, and the reviewed change was committed as `849b9156`. The Windows Git residual-directory issue is a separate follow-up; the persistence contract is a maintainer decision, not an invitation to expand this PR.

AI-assisted: yes. Maintainer edits remain enabled.

prs.title: fix(feishu): recover transient sends without duplicate messages
prs.body:
Supersedes #104322, thanks @litang9.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing Feishu messages when a create or reply request encounters a transient network or server failure, including a lost response after acceptance.

## User Impact

Text, cards, and uploaded-media messages recover with up to two retries using the same UUID, preventing duplicate posts within Feishu’s deduplication window. Uploads and CardKit entity creation retain their existing transient-failure behavior. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Message create/reply now share one request assembler that supplies a UUID before the first attempt. The existing Feishu request owner delegates scheduling and canonical network classification to `openclaw/plugin-sdk/retry-runtime`; transient recovery is opt-in only for these UUID-bearing requests. Existing rate-limit handling, sender authority on every attempt, durable dispatch accounting, withdrawn-reply fallback, and streaming without a message receipt remain covered.

The shared outbound delivery queue does not provide this per-request recovery: ambiguous sends require reconciliation before replay. The repair belongs at the UUID-bearing Feishu HTTP request boundary.

Production LOC: **net -2**. Consolidating duplicate create/reply assembly in ordinary and streaming sends and combining fulfilled/rejected business-error classification offsets the new behavior. Tests: **net +125**, allocated specifically for transport loss, cancellation, upload non-replay and retry policy. Documentation: +4 lines.

## Evidence

- Baseline `70134e42285b4214579faba8ac10ed7098550643`: four new registered-adapter/real-Lark-SDK loopback regressions failed on `ECONNRESET` after fixture acceptance (direct text, thread reply, card, uploaded media). The source owners remain unchanged on the newer main inspected before publication.
- Fixed: **120 tests across six focused files passed** using the repository wrapper with one worker. The final transport suite passed 29 tests, including stable serialized UUID/content over two HTTP attempts with exactly one fixture acceptance, per-attempt dispatch accounting, sender retirement preventing a second POST, and one failed upload followed by the existing link fallback. Retry policy covers HTTP 408/425/5xx, fulfilled/rejected 230049, canonical transport codes and permanent failures. Streaming still updates/closes after recovery without a message receipt.
- Local wall time: first consumer batch (five files, 91 tests) 21.09 s; final retry/transport batch (two files, 46 tests) 57.09 s, including 35.66 s of runtime-worker preparation. The transport test execution was about 8 s; real SDK HTTP and durable delivery settlement require this boundary. The exact-head [extension CI shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41146098127/job/124371966446) passed: test step **240 s**, whole job **329 s**. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41146098127) completed successfully.
- Feishu production typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, assertion safety, mock-export ratchet, exact test-line allocation, documentation link audit (0 broken links), and `git diff --check`: passed. Initial typecheck setup lacked generated SDK declarations; after preparation, the final check passed.
- `pr-simplify`: completed; one message request owner replaces the duplicate assembly paths.
- Final local **autoreview**, base `70134e42285b4214579faba8ac10ed7098550643`, complete local candidate, P0–P2: **scoped-clean**, no accepted/actionable findings. Review ran independently and did not execute project code.
- Dependency inspected: `@larksuiteoapi/node-sdk@1.76.0` accepts `data.uuid` for both create and reply and performs one POST per invocation. Official [create](https://larksuite.github.io/oapi-sdk-java/com/lark/oapi/service/im/v1/model/CreateMessageReqBody.Builder.html) and [reply](https://larksuite.github.io/oapi-sdk-java/com/lark/oapi/service/im/v1/model/ReplyMessageReqBody.Builder.html) contracts document at most one successful send per UUID within one hour.
- Proof limit: loopback simulates provider acceptance/deduplication; no new authenticated Feishu delivery was run. The original PR contains separately dated live-provider evidence. Contributor code was read only with `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff`; it was never checked out, installed, built or executed here.

Contributor credit is preserved for both commit-author identities from #104322: litang9 and Alex Tang.
