prs.title: fix: keep Windows managed updates alive when the task stops
prs.body:
Related: #169844

## What Problem This Solves

Windows Scheduled Task updates can kill their own helper when stopping the Gateway, leaving the Control UI at **Activating**, no terminal result, and the task disabled.

## User Impact

This draft keeps the managed update helper alive through the task stop while retaining cleanup of ordinary Gateway children. **Blocked on merging and releasing [proc-safe#31](https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/pull/31), then updating this dependency:** the declared dependency and lockfile intentionally remain at 0.4.2; its released API cannot run this integration. All 24 required checks now pass on native head `9e91dcc8e9cafc09be31a7374327345b8ce93ef9`, but that PR is still unmerged: `roboclaw-bot` has only READ permission in proc-safe and cannot land it. A maintainer with merge permission must merge it first. Then publish the paired native package, update the shipping dependency/lockfile, and revalidate before marking ready. No native merge commit exists to reference yet.

Already-installed affected updaters need one [manual npm, pnpm, or Bun hop](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d514bf8157581542d8a3d55747a4e898e5124bb2/docs/install/updating/update-methods.md#alternative-manual-npm-pnpm-or-bun) from outside the Gateway to a fixed release. The installed driver owns the first handoff, so downloading a candidate cannot repair it. The documented service refresh restores the task definition and enabled state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both the task-launcher Job and inner command Job permit explicit breakaway, and only the Scheduled Task managed update helper requests it. Kill-on-close stays enabled and ordinary children remain contained. The existing runtime staging owner retains the matching spawner outside the installation being replaced; stdin/stdout and optional JSON IPC still reach the existing lease, cancellation, recovery and terminal owners.

The proc-safe launcher PID differs from the helper PID. The current handoff already verifies and settles the helper independently of its launcher. Mapped staged native files can remain for existing stale-directory cleanup after process exit; no new cleanup store or protocol is added.

## Evidence

- Spawn selection and outer/inner Job regressions fail on base and pass with the fix. Retained-runtime tests cover loading the copied public spawner after removing the source installation, executable validation, and process creation identity.
- Production and affected test typechecks, lint, formatting and docs links pass against the paired API, locally pinned to proc-safe PR commit `ec55427cacc83115f80b42750dc2aea28e470991`; the temporary dependency/lock changes are excluded from this PR.
- Final focused owner/consumer check: 73 tests passed across five files in 153.92s (runtime/compiler preparation included); the two previously interrupted systemd recovery cases also passed (64.09s including compiler preparation). Prior interrupted run completed 43 native lifecycle, 27 launchd recovery, 25 systemd recovery and 6 engine cases before termination. Initial full lifecycle batch: 79 passed, 4 failed, 5 skipped. The four existing profile-notice cases reproduce host `fs.watch` EMFILE and subsequent cleanup assertions on the base as well; no timeout, retry, skip or assertion relaxation was introduced.
- Test allocation adds exactly 204 net regression/support lines for spawn, nested Job permission and retained native runtime boundaries. The shared ratchet still reports 1,036 lines of inherited debt after this allocation; the shared scalar is unchanged.
- pr-simplify completed: existing staging and handoff owners retained, the FreeBSD-only stage export replaced without an alias, and non-service Windows staging remains independent of proc-safe. Net production growth: 47 lines; tests/support: 204 lines. Fresh independent Codex P0–P2 review: scoped-clean.
- [Native Windows CI](https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/actions/runs/41144054731): all four x64/ARM64 × Node22/24 jobs passed at `9e91dcc8e9cafc09be31a7374327345b8ce93ef9`, including native Node/Bun main-thread/Worker Job, pipe/EOF, JSON IPC and strict OS-argv proof. The native production/API bytes match the locally tested commit. All 24 required native-PR checks, including every other platform, have now completed successfully. Windows Scheduled Task/Control UI package-upgrade, failure/recovery and cancellation E2E remains unrun here. Crabbox rejected Windows before allocation; it was not retried. No full-symptom closure is claimed.

Root-cause analysis credit: @alexcousins-muratec. The contributor's release-specific patch was read only and never executed or adopted. The separate historical 1ms readiness-budget starvation was already repaired by 9405010d01e (#169787), first containing tag v2026.10.10-beta.1; no timeout changes are included.

## Work sessions

[Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/78580230-7d1b-4329-a7dd-72554eb66323)

prs.title: fix(apple): cut full chat-history downloads from 13 to 1 across refreshes
prs.body:
Related: #100197

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated full-history downloads when Apple chats refresh after small updates or check unchanged history.

## User Impact

Users download new chat rows instead of repeatedly downloading messages already on screen.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse accepted Gateway history cursors and share overlapping refreshes through one read-and-publication owner. Session, route, and transcript replacements invalidate the cursor and reload canonical history. Incremental rows are decoded once and reused when publishing the transcript. Deltas carrying anchored activity placement use the existing canonical reload so nested completions retain the same order as a full read. This narrow fallback avoids duplicating the Gateway display composer and leaves ordinary append-only and empty deltas on the fast path.

## Evidence

The app-hosted Swift Testing case `realGatewayHistory()` passed against a live isolated Gateway using the production iOS adapter and shared chat view model. A transparent wire relay observed the successful app connection and actual delta RPCs.

| chat.history measurement | Cursorless | Cursor refresh |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Requests | 13 | 13 |
| Full-history responses | 13 | 1 |
| Delta responses | 0 | 12 |
| Response JSON frame bytes | 633,120 | 131,529 |

Response bytes fell **79.23%**; both runs retain all nineteen messages. The 31 captured exchanges also verify active-run recovery, an empty sequence-gap delta, final completion, and stale-cursor reset followed by canonical reload.

Native proof and iOS adapter suite: **35 tests in 2 suites passed**. Focused shared-kit validation after the anchored-placement fix: **673 tests in 22 suites passed**. Removing prepared-message reuse makes the identity regression fail; restoring it passes **1 test in 1 suite**.

[Native harness, redacted wire trace, source hashes, measurements, and terminal results](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/491a4e92431c58e6d7f9ba50494346d5aba450d6/EVIDENCE.md).

The anchored-completion regression captures the cursor after `exec, wait`, then receives a later completion anchored after `exec`. It fails on the prior head and passes with canonical fallback, yielding `exec, completion, wait`; a subsequent empty delta preserves that order. The existing real-Gateway measurements above cover the unchanged ordinary-delta path.

```text
anchored-order-red: exit 1 (expected); 1 test failed on the prior source
anchored-order-green: exit 0; 1 test in 1 suite passed
Test run with 673 tests in 22 suites passed after 10.022 seconds.
```

AI-assisted.

prs.title: fix: updates fail with one moved cron partition
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw updates can fail candidate validation when a pre-v34 state database contains one historical cron partition whose path no longer matches the current state directory.

## User Impact

Upgrades choose a cron partition without an interactive Doctor prompt. Existing bindings and matching current defaults remain authoritative. Otherwise OpenClaw selects the moved partition with the most stored jobs, uses retained activity and then its stable path to break ties, and leaves every sibling partition untouched. An explicit `cron.store` setting can still override the default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing schema migration now makes one deterministic fallback decision across retained partitions. No new schema, runtime setting, prompt, or parallel migration owner is introduced.

The published-updater proof covers a stopped-but-installed stable Gateway, a sole moved partition, retained settings/jobs/receipts/history, a new candidate run, and a further restart. Its fixture uses a harmless command instead of model inference. The old Gateway stays stopped after moving state: restarting it recreates heartbeat jobs at the default path and invalidates the sole-partition specimen. History assertions use the public cron run identity, not the internal task-run key. Job-definition comparison excludes `updatedAtMs`: the cron outcome owner advances it on every successful execution; user settings and immutable definition fields remain exact.

## Evidence

- Original migration reproduction: moved v32, moved v33, and history-only cases failed with an absent binding before the repair.
- Opinionated-selection follow-up on `7b6da436ab6`: **88 focused tests passed**, including a selector-less published rehearsal with two retained partitions; core/test typechecks, targeted lint, and formatting also pass.
- Current rebased tree: **114 tests passed** across the migration, snapshot inventory, private admission, historical database, and workflow-plan suites. The two focused commands took 129.98s and 43.81s including compilation/setup. The slower process suite proves actual state-copy/admission boundaries.
- Workflow regression reproduced `undefined` instead of boolean `false` before the fix; missing, false, and true inputs now pass through the reusable workflow correctly.
- Core and tooling-test typechecks, targeted lint/formatting, workflow validation, docs links (16,167; zero broken), and test-line budget pass.
- Independent P0–P2 review found one proof gap: candidate-created run persistence after restart. Addressed by checking both old and new runs through public history plus stored history/receipts after restart.
- **Published CLI upgrade proof passed (2026-10-30):** isolated Docker, published `2026.10.8` updater → candidate `2026.10.9`; update exit 0 in 260.973s, recorded phase `finished`, readiness HTTP 200, running version verified. The sole moved partition was automatically bound; settings and job definition were retained. Both the stable-created and candidate-created cron runs remain successful in public history and stored receipts/history after a further Gateway restart. Durable conversation history survived; incognito state was removed as expected.
- Reproduce with `OPENCLAW_PUBLISHED_DRIVER_MOVED_CRON=1 bash scripts/e2e/published-driver-update-docker.sh <candidate.tgz> <artifacts> 2026.10.8`. The proof used current-head harness `7e42b3226058cae3d8074af6050923cfbad2e1b3` and the integrity-validated package built from `0a4e41909df5beb35aed1c20fd5542038bc8e343` (SHA-256 `0e827fdeec22507f18ee2c9436280422f6343874a870689c1bcb27b336b27301`). The intervening commits change only the test harness, workflow regression, and test allocation; runtime/package source is unchanged. Build identity is not claimed to equal the final harness head.
- Earlier failed attempts exposed fixture errors (restarting stable recreated a second partition; successful cron execution legitimately advances `updatedAtMs`). Both are repaired in the harness; those failed runs are not counted as passing proof.
- [Prior ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185097#issuecomment-6428902653): **platinum hermit**, sufficient proof, zero findings. A fresh review is requested for the deterministic multi-partition follow-up.
- Rebased onto `e97708044e8fe86b8d639b68de12a99b3a5b53c1` for inherited CI fixes. Preserved main’s expanded snapshot cases; dropped a disabled-dreaming expectation fix already on main. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41122194505) passed all 65 substantive jobs, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards, and its CI gate. No CI failure exception is needed.

The runtime change remains confined to the existing v34 identity migration. Test growth has a dedicated allocation for migration selection and the published-driver workflow contract; most other growth is the installed-package upgrade harness.

## Scope

Ready-for-review preparation only. Do not merge or backport.

prs.title: fix(gateway): acknowledge uploads before workspace preparation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Chat uploads can leave the composer in “sending” for seconds after the attachment has already been saved, because acknowledgment waits for sandbox workspace preparation and copying.

## User Impact

Uploads are acknowledged after validation and durable input custody. Both new turns and active-run steers prepare their files afterward. Failed staging remains a visible run error, saved originals remain available, and Stop can interrupt reconciliation-lease acquisition.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move workspace and private-skill selection into one shared turn/steering preparation barrier. Keep managed references across acknowledgment, enforce complete managed non-PDF staging, retain PDF copy fallback, and pass cancellation into the existing workspace lease owner. No new configuration, timeout, queue, schema, or synchronization algorithm.

This moves preparation off the ACK path; it does not claim to eliminate all workspace synchronization or reduce total model-turn time.

## Evidence

Focused Gateway tests passed (193), media/dispatch checks passed (126, with the lifecycle observation below), and prompt-prefix stability passed (14). All 15 SCP tests pass after preserving ordinary transfer diagnostics alongside cancellation. The affected CI repair files passed 75 tests; the relocated media registration passed its 3 selected cases; lifecycle, policy, and queued-followup fixture checks passed 20 tests. Targeted lint passed for all nine repair files. Independent Codex reviews are scoped-clean at P0–P2. `pnpm build` passed, with final production source subsequently typechecked and focused-tested. `pnpm check:changed` passed after deleting a newly unused test helper. The prior corrected head passed CI run 41136953733. Main then landed the shared-fixture repair independently in #188754; conflict resolution adopts that implementation and retains this PR’s extra preauth coverage. All 153 affected chat/lifecycle/policy/queued-followup tests passed after the merge, with both affected type graphs, targeted format/lint, and final Codex review also passing. Final exact-head CI is pending.

One initial lifecycle test, `holds session lifecycle mutation until an interrupted plugin claim exits`, timed out waiting for its mocked plugin claim before reply resolution. The same file passed in original order on a bounded replay. Its fixture contains no media and supplies its own reply resolver; no lifecycle source or assertion was changed. The cause remains unproven, and the passing replay is not presented as a fix.

The first CI run exposed missed test callers of the removed pre-ACK staging path and two test lint errors. Those tests now hold real parser custody after durable offload, retain cleanup-before-response assertions, and verify saved image bytes. Workspace-lifetime tests preserve the original abort reason and explicitly reject revoked workspace authority. The image cases moved into the existing admitted-media registration to shrink the oversized parent file.

CI also exposed a shared WebSocket fixture cleanup race, reproduced locally: hello-ok could precede completion of connect-owned background work. The fixture now reuses the existing policy suite’s exact work observer/join, preserving the separate lifecycle-write drain. A terminal-event observer now starts immediately before abort rather than before cold preparation; no timeout was raised and no assertion was weakened.

A later CI run exposed a separate reset-fixture defect, reproduced locally with the same registry-change exception: a nested test state changed the process-wide state directory beneath the running suite Gateway. The fixture now uses a unique temporary workspace within the suite’s existing isolated state. All 18 workspace-policy tests pass, with cleanup/assertions unchanged; types, lint, and Codex review pass. Production authority checks are unchanged.

The sandboxed ZIP ACK regression fails on the original boundary and passes with deferred staging. Additional production-path fixtures cover active-run steering, visible staging failure, readable ZIP bytes, PDF fallback, managed workspace revocation, and cancellation while another owner holds reconciliation custody.

The committed `scripts/perf/chat-send-attachments-measure.ts --workload zip` workload uses a valid 50,450-byte ZIP containing twelve 4 KiB files. Five serial baseline/candidate pairs, five warm samples per process plus separate cold calls, preserve every byte and managed reference:

| Attachment-owner metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Pre-ACK sandbox layouts per request | 1 | 0 |
| Cold median | 11,213 ms | 55 ms |
| Median warm batch p50 | 56.89 ms | 8.35 ms |
| Main-thread CPU per preparation | 33.03 ms | 3.69 ms |
| Process CPU per preparation | 83.44 ms | 5.90 ms |

These are synthetic attachment-owner measurements with fixed admission, not live Gateway ACK latency or whole-turn measurements. Host load varied; operation counts establish the removed ACK-path work. Baseline/candidate owner source was pinned; the concurrent optional-signal plumbing changes are not exercised by baseline callers or the candidate ACK path.

prs.title: fix(anthropic): preserve global exec restrictions in partial agent overrides
prs.body:
Supersedes #124275, thanks @Yigtwxx

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a latent policy-inheritance defect where the Claude CLI callback silently requests an implicit native-tool permission bypass when a partial agent exec block discards restrictive global settings.

## User Impact

This is defense in depth. **Current launchers already strip or replace the implicit bypass**, including non-live plugin execution, manual compaction, exact-tool/side-question execution, and node execution. There is no user-visible change to those launchers and no migration or new approval gate.

The documented callback cases do change: global `mode: "deny"` or `security: "deny"` plus an empty/ask-only agent block no longer yields `bypassPermissions`; a security-only agent block also retains a global `ask: "always"`. Explicit agent modes and explicitly configured Claude permission arguments retain precedence. Any future route that trusts the callback therefore inherits the configured global restrictions instead of permissive defaults.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing exec-policy owner to layer defaults, global settings, then agent settings. A supplied mode determines both policy fields; supplied legacy fields clear an inherited mode and replace only those fields. Missing fields inherit. Explicitly configured overrides remain intentional overrides; this does not impose a new maximum-restriction policy.

The production delta is **+1 line**: the SDK export of the existing helper. The adapter is line-neutral because it removes its duplicate policy reconstruction and reuses that helper. There is no additional dead production code in this owner to delete safely. Other SDK exports and implementations are unchanged. Existing policy-helper tests now exercise the SDK export directly.

### Before/after configuration matrix

`D` = default `security: full, ask: off`; `G` = normalized global policy; `A` = a complete agent security/ask pair or explicit agent mode; `P` = a partial agent block (including empty/non-policy blocks). `N(P,D)` fills missing fields from defaults. `Layer(G,P)` normalizes modes first and preserves unspecified fields from G. `bypassPermissions` is derived only when the final mode is `full`, subject to the existing explicit-argument/compaction checks and later launcher filtering.

| Global exec policy | Agent exec policy | Callback before | Callback after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unset | Unset | D | D |
| Unset | Partial P | N(P,D) | N(P,D) |
| Unset | Full A | A | A |
| Permissive (`full/off` or legacy `full/on-miss`) | Unset | G | G |
| Permissive (`full/off` or legacy `full/on-miss`) | Partial P | N(P,D) | Layer(G,P), inheriting omitted fields from G |
| Permissive (`full/off` or legacy `full/on-miss`) | Full A | A | A |
| Restrictive | Unset | G | G |
| Restrictive | Partial P | N(P,D), potentially dropping restrictions | Layer(G,P), retaining unspecified restrictions |
| Restrictive | Full A | A | A |

For `full/off`, Layer(G,P) equals N(P,D). A legacy `full/on-miss` policy instead retains `on-miss` when omitted; the callback still projects mode `full` unless an explicit agent field changes that projection.

Examples of the changed row:

| Global | Agent | Before callback policy / implicit bypass | After callback policy / implicit bypass |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode: deny` | `{}` or `ask: off` | full/off / yes | deny/off / no |
| `security: deny, ask: off` | `host: gateway` or `ask: off` | full/off / yes | deny/off / no |
| `security: full, ask: always` | `security: full` | full/off / yes | full/always / no |
| `mode: ask` | `ask: off` | full/off / yes | allowlist/off / no |
| `mode: deny` | `mode: full` | full/off / yes | full/off / yes |

## Evidence

- Base: `a1d1da77f8e80c2c4ace3445d507597201fd2f78`; candidate: `6408000f6ad7f19e9b3c5641d6bb42dae7093259`.
- Red before: fresh/resumed callback regressions fail for six inheritance combinations on main; 30 other tests pass. Green after: all 32 Claude shared tests and both SDK policy tests pass.
- Claude shared file: 2.51 seconds including transform/import/setup; the complete two-shard focused command took 175.41 seconds with a cold compiled-worker rebuild. The matrix replaces an existing table; its net 35 test lines have a separate allocation record protecting global inheritance and explicit overrides.
- Format and `git diff --check` pass.
- Final-head security autoreview: Codex, P0/P1, scoped-clean, no actionable findings, with unchanged policy owner and launcher/consumer source supplied. The reviewer did not execute tests.
- Capped rootless Podman (4 CPUs / 8 GiB): all 578 tests across 13 consumer files pass (232.82 seconds), including approval readers/policy, prompt-prefix stability, Codex config/side-question/conversation/MCP App consumers, Muse, Policy, and Anthropic sibling mappings.
- Full build passes (4 minutes 15.2 seconds), including SDK declarations and export verification. Production extension, extension-test, and core typechecks pass.
- Type-aware lint passes on the two Anthropic files (8.26 seconds) and both core/SDK files (5.35 seconds). SDK export registration check passes.
- Existing SDK-helper file: 169.06 seconds with 99% in cold transform/setup; assertions are synchronous and do not add a process or server fixture. Required PR CI passed on this exact published head: [CI run 41145533104](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41145533104). The compact check job took 303 seconds; extension bundle jobs 2 and 3 took 374 and 333 seconds. These are whole-job CI times including other files; per-file CI timing was not available from the retrieved logs.
- Local ClawSweeper is unavailable on this host; the maintainer fallback used completed autoreview plus one hosted ClawSweeper request. The hosted review was still in progress at merge and remains advisory.
- No authenticated Claude/model execution is claimed. Prior investigation verified actual process argv with a synthetic Claude executable; the current change targets the callback contract. Contributor code was read only, never checked out or executed.

prs.title: fix(agents): prefer write/edit tools over heredocs to prevent literal-newline corruption
prs.body:
Fixes #114128

## What Problem This Solves

Agents writing multi-line Python via unquoted heredocs (`<<EOF`) or `bash -c` corrupt `\n` into literal backslash-n. This compiles-fails silently and can rot for weeks before discovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exec description now prefers dedicated file-writing tools over shell heredocs or `bash -c` for multi-line content, and names only the tools that survived filtering (`write`, `edit`, and/or `apply_patch`). A write-only session is told to prefer `write`, not the unavailable siblings. Tool permissions are not widened.

## User Impact

When a dedicated file-writing tool is available, agents are steered to that tool instead of a shell heredoc, so multiline files keep real newline bytes. Sessions that do not have those tools are not told to call them.

## Evidence

Live proof on `401c566eb96410ae5989f69a160784e7405a1222`, using the production tool finalizer plus the real exec and write tools (`--pool=forks`).

Exec-only session omits the guidance. With only `write` available, the description names `write` and the selected file tool is `write`. The real exec tool ran the historical unquoted heredoc and left literal backslash-n bytes (`5c6e`). The real write tool wrote the same intended Python and the file bytes contain newline bytes (`0a`) and match the requested content.

```
HEAD 401c566eb96410ae5989f69a160784e7405a1222
EXEC_ONLY_HAS_FILE_WRITES false
EXEC_ONLY_DESCRIPTION Run shell and wait for completion. Omit host to use the session's configured host. TTY CLI/UI/coding agent: pty=true. Quote arguments containing shell metacharacters, including URL query strings with `?` or `&`.
WRITE_ONLY_DESCRIPTION Run shell and wait for completion. Omit host to use the session's configured host. TTY CLI/UI/coding agent: pty=true. File writes: prefer dedicated file-writing tools (write) over shell heredocs or bash -c for multi-line content. Quote arguments containing shell metacharacters, including URL query strings with `?` or `&`.
SELECTED_FILE_TOOLS write
HEREDOC_EXEC_RESULT [{"type":"text","text":"(no output)"}]
HEREDOC_FILE_REPR "def greet():\\n    return \"ok\"\\n\n"
HEREDOC_FILE_HEX 64656620677265657428293a5c6e2020202072657475726e20226f6b225c6e0a
WRITE_TOOL_RESULT [{"type":"text","text":"Successfully wrote 29 bytes to /home/synth/.hermes/cache/scratch/oc-vt-w5SDu1/oc-117274-proof-E6H7A1/write.py"}]
WRITE_FILE_REPR "def greet():\n    return \"ok\"\n"
WRITE_FILE_HEX 64656620677265657428293a0a2020202072657475726e20226f6b220a
WRITE_CONTAINS_NEWLINE_BYTE true
WRITE_MATCHES_INTENDED true
```

`src/agents/bash-tools.descriptions.test.ts`: 5 passed, including write-only, edit-only, and partial sets. `src/agents/agent-tools.deferred-followup-guidance.test.ts`: 12 passed.

Previous CI on `7bdf478a` failed `checks-node-changed-compact-large-12` (`AssertionError: expected 'blocked' to match object { state: 'reclaimed' }` in `src/gateway/worker-environments/placement-dispatch-reclaim.test.ts`) and `checks-node-changed-compact-large-7` (`ENOENT` for `dist/index.js` in `src/cli/update-cli.windows-lifecycle.test.ts`). Neither file is in this diff.

AI-assisted: yes (OpenClaw subagent).

prs.title: fix(anthropic): partial agent exec block drops restrictive global security
prs.body:
Related: #121678 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where an operator who set a restrictive global exec policy would still have a Claude CLI agent launched with permissions bypassed, as soon as that agent had any per-agent exec settings of its own. Concretely: the operator sets `tools.exec.security: "deny"`, then gives one agent a small per-agent block such as `tools: { exec: { ask: "off" } }` — a block that says nothing about `security`. The expectation is that the agent inherits `deny`. What actually happens is that the global block is discarded entirely, the missing `security` falls back to the permissive default, and the run is launched with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`, so Claude Code's own Bash/Write/Edit tools run without prompting. ## Why This Change Was Made The Claude CLI backend resolved exec policy with its own private logic that replaced the global block with the per-agent block wholesale: ```ts const exec = agentExec ?? context?.config?.tools?.exec; ``` Two independent failures, both in the permissive direction: the global block is never consulted once a per-agent block exists, and any field the per-agent block omits falls back to the most permissive default rather than to the global setting. The repository already owns this layering. `applyExecPolicyLayer` merges field by field, and keeps the "an explicit `mode` wins" rule intact; it is used by `resolveExecToolConfig` (`src/agents/lazy-exec-tool.ts:77`), `resolveExecDefaults` (`src/agents/exec-defaults.ts:190`), `agent-tools.ts:555`, and `node-host/invoke-system-run.ts:214`. This change makes the Claude CLI backend the fifth consumer of that seam instead of a fifth implementation of it. `applyExecPolicyLayer` is re-exported from the existing `plugin-sdk/exec-approvals-runtime` module, next to `resolveExecModePolicy`, which this file already imports. This is the non-live counterpart of #121678, which repaired the same defect on the live-session lane. That PR's description named this exact case — *"a partial per-agent exec block inherited a restrictive global security setting"* — and its regression suite covers it for live sessions. **Which lane this flag actually reaches.** On the default `claude-stdio` live transport the value computed here is not final: `prepareClaudeCliTransportArgs` treats `--permission-mode` as a protocol-owned flag, drops whatever arrived (`extensions/anthropic/cli-runtime-args.ts:15`, `:53`) and appends its own `--permission-mode default` (`:99`). So on that lane Claude is never launched with `bypassPermissions` either way, and this change is a no-op there. The flag is final on the lanes that run per-turn processes instead, where the runner strips `liveSession` before execution: ```ts // src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts:1809 (side question) and :1816 (disableCliLiveSession) const { liveSession: _liveSession, ...backend } = preparedBackend.backend; ``` There is a second gate after that one, and adding the runner's `resolveExecutionArgs` hook to the trace surfaced it. When a run carries per-run tool availability, the backend takes the restricted-execution path, and `--permission-mode` is on its strip list: ```ts // extensions/anthropic/cli-shared.ts:309-311 const CLAUDE_RESTRICTED_VALUE_ARGS = new Set([ CLAUDE_PERMISSION_MODE_ARG, ... ``` So the flag computed here survives to the process only when the run is **both** off the live transport **and** without per-run tool availability. Measured against the five `disableCliLiveSession: true` call sites: | call site | `cliToolAvailability` | flag survives? | |---|---|---| | `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.ts:156` | not set | **yes** | | `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts:722` | `{ native: [], openClaw }` | no - stripped | | `src/agents/isolated-completion.ts:224` | `{ native: [], openClaw: [] }` | no - stripped | | `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/cli-backend-dispatch.ts:258` | built at `:117`, always set | no - stripped | | `src/system-agent/agent-turn.ts:386` | `resolveSystemAgentCliToolAvailability` returns a value for this backend (`selectable` + `execution-args` + `resolveExecutionArgs`) | no - stripped | Compaction runs are the confirmed surviving lane, and they are the case worth repairing: they are unattended and long-running, which is exactly where an accidental `bypassPermissions` matters. The node-bound lane (`sessionEntry.execHost === "node"`, `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts:1046`) and side-question entry points that do not set availability behave the same way, but I have not enumerated them individually and am not claiming them. Scope, stated plainly: this fixes the global → per-agent layering only. `CliBackendNormalizeConfigContext` carries just `config`, `backendId`, and `agentId`, so session-level `execSecurity` and approvals-file floors never reach this lane at all. Extending the context to carry those is a larger change and is deliberately not attempted here. ## User Impact An agent with a partial per-agent exec block now inherits the global `security` setting instead of silently escalating to bypassed permissions. Operators who set a restrictive global policy get the policy they configured. Behavior narrows for one configuration shape on a narrow set of runs: a partial per-agent block that previously produced `bypassPermissions` will no longer do so on per-turn process runs that carry no per-run tool availability. Compaction runs (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact.ts:156`) are the measured case; they are unattended and long-running, which is where an accidental bypass matters most. Those runs now fall back to Claude's own default permission behavior instead of bypassing it. Runs on the default `claude-stdio` live transport are unaffected in either direction because that transport pins `--permission-mode default`, and runs with per-run tool availability are unaffected because the restricted-execution path strips the flag for both code states. An explicit per-agent `mode` still overrides the global policy wherever the flag survives at all; the argv table below shows both override rows byte-identical before and after. That is the intended direction and matches #121678. ## Evidence AI-assisted change. Re-measured on head `57ecf19007e`, Node 22.23.2, Windows. The real-binary arms below use Claude Code 2.1.268. **Real behavior — the argv a spawned process actually receives on the affected lane.** Rather than reading the normalized config, this drives the production chain to a real process and records the argv from inside it: the shipped `claude-cli` backend registration -> the real `normalizeClaudeBackendConfig` hook -> the `liveSession` strip the runner performs at `prepare.ts:1809`/`:1816` -> the `{sessionId}` substitution at `execute.ts:238-245` -> **the runner's `resolveExecutionArgs` hook** (`execute.ts:246`, i.e. the backend's own `resolveClaudeCliExecutionArgs`, which the earlier trace skipped) -> the real `buildCliArgs` (`execute.ts:275`) -> `spawnSync`. The only substitution is the executable itself: a stub script stands in for the `claude` binary and writes its own `process.argv.slice(2)` to a file. Nothing inside OpenClaw is mocked, and the hook ran in every row below. Operator config in every row: `tools.exec.security: "deny"`, `tools.exec.ask: "off"` globally, and one agent with the per-agent block shown. | per-agent `tools.exec` | run | per-run tool availability | `main` | this branch | |---|---|---|---|---| | `{ ask: "off" }` (partial, omits `security`) | fresh | none | `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` | flag **absent** | | `{ ask: "off" }` (partial, omits `security`) | resumed (`--resume`) | none | `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` | flag **absent** | | `{ mode: "full" }` (explicit override) | fresh | none | `bypassPermissions` | `bypassPermissions` | | `{ mode: "full" }` (explicit override) | resumed (`--resume`) | none | `bypassPermissions` | `bypassPermissions` | | `{ ask: "off" }` (partial) | fresh | `{ native: ["Bash","Read"], openClaw: ["memory_search"] }` | flag absent | flag absent | | `{ mode: "full" }` (explicit) | fresh | same as above | flag absent | flag absent | The last two rows are the restricted-execution path described above: the hook strips `--permission-mode` for both code states, which is what makes the availability column part of the scope statement rather than a footnote. Full argv recorded by the stub for the partial-block fresh run: ``` main ["-p","--output-format","stream-json","--include-partial-messages","--verbose", "--setting-sources","user","--allowedTools","mcp__openclaw__*", "--disallowedTools","ScheduleWakeup,CronCreate,Bash(run_in_background:true),Monitor", "--permission-mode","bypassPermissions", "--model","claude-sonnet-4-6","--session-id","00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"] branch ["-p","--output-format","stream-json","--include-partial-messages","--verbose", "--setting-sources","user","--allowedTools","mcp__openclaw__*", "--disallowedTools","ScheduleWakeup,CronCreate,Bash(run_in_background:true),Monitor", "--model","claude-sonnet-4-6","--session-id","00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"] ``` With the flag absent, Claude Code falls back to its own default permission behavior and prompts, which is the restrictive global policy the operator configured. The explicit-override rows are the control: they are byte-identical on both sides, so the narrowing is confined to the defect. The two code states differ by one file. **Real Claude behavior once the flag is absent.** The previous revision stopped at the argv. This one carries it into the real `claude` binary - Claude Code 2.1.268, authenticated, no stub anywhere. The two argv rows are produced by the production normalizers themselves: `main`'s `normalizeClaudeBackendConfig` and this branch's, imported side by side in one probe, given the same operator config (`tools.exec.security: "deny"` globally, agent block `{ ask: "off" }`). Each resulting argv is handed to `spawnSync("claude", [...args, prompt])` in a fresh empty working directory, with one permissioned request as the prompt: > Create a file named proof.txt containing OK in the current directory, then reply DONE. The observable is the filesystem, not the transcript. Each arm gets a throwaway `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` holding nothing but a `settings.json` written for that arm (plus the credential file, so the CLI can authenticate), so no operator CLAUDE.md, plugin or hook reaches the run, and every `CLAUDE*` variable is stripped from the child environment. | arm | argv produced by | user `settings.json` | `proof.txt` | Claude's own reply | |---|---|---|---|---| | A | `main` | `{}` | **created** | `DONE` | | B | this branch | `{}` | **absent** | "If you grant write permission for this directory (or run in an interactive session and approve the prompt), I'll create `proof.txt` with `OK` immediately." | | C | this branch | `{"permissions":{"defaultMode":"bypassPermissions"}}` | **created** | `DONE` | A against B is the change, measured rather than quoted from documentation: with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` the write happens unattended; with the flag gone the same request is refused by the permission system and nothing is written. Two consecutive runs of the probe produced identical results. C answers the open decision. The narrowing binds only where the operator's own Claude settings do not already bypass, because this branch stops passing a flag rather than starting to pass a restrictive one. A host whose Claude `settings.json` pins `permissions.defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"` keeps bypassing after this change. So affected compaction runs stop receiving an automatic bypass *from OpenClaw*, and an operator who wants the old behavior keeps two explicit ways to ask for it: a per-agent `mode: "full"` (rows 3 and 4 of the argv table, byte-identical before and after) or their own Claude settings (row C).
Harness for the real-binary arms (temporary probe, not committed) ```ts import { normalizeClaudeBackendConfig as mainNormalize } from "./cli-shared.control.js"; // origin/main copy import { normalizeClaudeBackendConfig as headNormalize } from "./cli-shared.js"; const context = { backendId: "claude-cli", agentId: "agent", config: { tools: { exec: { security: "deny", ask: "off" } }, agents: { list: [{ id: "agent", tools: { exec: { ask: "off" } } }] }, } }; const base = { command: "claude", args: ["-p"], output: "json", input: "arg" }; const mainArgs = mainNormalize({ ...base }, context).args; // ["-p","--setting-sources","user","--permission-mode","bypassPermissions"] const headArgs = headNormalize({ ...base }, context).args; // ["-p","--setting-sources","user"] // per arm: throwaway CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR with only settings.json (+ credentials), CLAUDE* stripped spawnSync("claude", [...args, PROMPT], { cwd: mkdtempSync(...), env, encoding: "utf8" }); existsSync(join(cwd, "proof.txt")); // the observable ```
Harness (temporary probe, run with node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs probe.mts; not committed) ```ts const plugin = buildAnthropicCliBackend(); // shipped claude-cli registration const normalized = normalizeClaudeBackendConfig(plugin.config, { backendId: "claude-cli", agentId: "agent", config: { tools: { exec: { security: "deny", ask: "off" } }, agents: { list: [{ id: "agent", tools: { exec: agentExec } }] }, }, }); // exactly what prepare.ts:1809 / :1816 do before a non-live run const { liveSession: _liveSession, ...backend } = normalized; const sessionId = "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000"; const baseArgsWithSkills = useResume // execute.ts:238-245 ? (backend.resumeArgs ?? []).map((a) => a.replaceAll("{sessionId}", sessionId)) : (backend.args ?? []); const resolvedExecutionArgs = plugin.resolveExecutionArgs?.({ // execute.ts:246 config, workspaceDir: process.cwd(), provider: "anthropic", modelId: "claude-sonnet-4-6", executionMode: "agent", toolAvailability, // undefined, or the availability object useResume, baseArgs: baseArgsWithSkills, }); const args = buildCliArgs({ // execute.ts:275 backend, baseArgs: Array.from(resolvedExecutionArgs ?? baseArgsWithSkills), modelId: "claude-sonnet-4-6", sessionId, useResume, }); spawnSync(process.execPath, [STUB, ...args], { env: { ...process.env, STUB_ARGV_OUT: out } }); // STUB: writeFileSync(process.env.STUB_ARGV_OUT, JSON.stringify(process.argv.slice(2))); ```
**Tests:** ``` vitest --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts extensions/anthropic/cli-shared.exec-policy.test.ts Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 2 passed (2) ``` **Control arm — the same two tests with `isOpenClawRequestedYolo` reverted to main's expression** (`const exec = agentExec ?? context?.config?.tools?.exec;`): ``` Tests 1 failed | 1 passed (2) × keeps restrictive global exec security when the agent block omits it AssertionError: expected [ …(11) ] to not include 'bypassPermissions' ``` Exactly one test falls, and it is the partial-block case. The second test — *"still lets an explicit per-agent exec mode override global security"* — passes in both states, which is the check that this narrows nothing beyond the defect: `applyExecPolicyLayer` routes an explicit `mode` down its `layer.mode` branch. The same revert flips only the two partial-block rows of the argv table above, and leaves both explicit-override rows byte-identical. **Neighbouring suites on the refreshed tree:** ``` vitest --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts extensions/anthropic/cli-shared.test.ts extensions/anthropic/cli-shared.execution-env.test.ts extensions/anthropic/cli-shared.exec-policy.test.ts extensions/anthropic/cli-context-window.test.ts extensions/anthropic/cli-runtime.test.ts Test Files 5 passed (5) Tests 84 passed (84) ``` **Boundaries and lint:** ``` oxfmt --check extensions/anthropic/cli-shared.ts extensions/anthropic/cli-shared.exec-policy.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/exec-approvals-runtime.ts -> All matched files use the correct format. ``` The merge with `main` touched only the import block: `main` moved `requiresClaudeMandatoryAdaptiveThinking` to `openclaw/plugin-sdk/claude-model-runtime` and hoisted it, next to the `exec-approvals-runtime` import this branch extends. `isOpenClawRequestedYolo` itself was not touched by `main`, and the defect is still present there today.

prs.title: fix(link-understanding): non-UTF-8 pages reach the model as garbled text
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: linked pages served in a declared legacy charset reach link processors and agent input as garbled UTF-8 replacement characters. This changes incorrect user-visible output, not just allocation or performance.

## User Impact

User impact: an agent reading a linked Shift_JIS page now receives and returns its readable Japanese title. UTF-8 pages are unchanged. Unknown charset labels keep the existing non-fatal UTF-8 fallback; no configuration change is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the response decoder already owned by `web_fetch` instead of the link fetcher's unconditional UTF-8 decoder. This preserves the existing BOM/header/document declaration order without adding another parser. The added export is internal, not a Plugin SDK surface. Fetch authority, cancellation, response limits, processors, prompt definitions and stored conversation history contracts are unchanged.

@Yigtwxx's original commit is preserved. The separate 13-line test table is consolidated into the existing transport/URL-selection regression; the shared decoder retains its declaration and fallback coverage. Production **+1**, tests **0**, with no test-line allocation or ceiling change. Earlier closed attempt: #111773.

## Evidence

[Built Gateway before/after evidence, native receipts and replay details](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188766#issuecomment-6535787163).

Built Gateway agent turns on current-main baseline `1d2e0b28b60b` and candidate `86a4b241c744`: two Shift_JIS turns and two UTF-8 controls on each. Real public HTTP pages pass through the normal STRICT guarded fetch, a real CLI processor and the real OpenClaw agent runtime. A deterministic OpenAI-compatible model fixture records the actual input and echoes its title; no paid live-model claim.

Current head `73ec930363d6` has the identical source tree as the proven candidate (`6b9d2585e88508e4f86e5d5c5f78834cf54f390e`): the contributor's intervening allocation commit was preserved, then its unused allocation removed. All proof inputs are unchanged.

Main's Shift_JIS input and final replies are garbled twice (**13 replacement characters** each); the candidate produces `阿部寛のホームページ` twice with **0** replacement characters. The UTF-8 control remains `気象庁 Japan Meteorological Agency` throughout. All eight turns complete with one model request each, no rerouting, native visible-delivery receipts, matching assistant history and clean Gateway shutdown.

Focused tests: **33 passed** (transport 5, shared decoder 14, prefix stability 14). The same final transport suite on main fails only the intended decoding regression (**4 passed / 1 failed**). Type-aware scoped lint, format and whitespace checks pass.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: a revert fully restores the old decoder; there is no migration, dependency, schema, credential or configuration change. Blast radius is decoded linked-page text supplied to configured link processors and agent input; UTF-8 fallback and the shared `web_fetch` decoder remain the existing owners.

prs.body:
Related: #188777

## What Problem This Solves

Large attachment, realtime audio, and WAL tests spend seconds recursively comparing byte arrays.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. These tests run faster while retaining their full payloads and complete-byte integrity checks.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use native `Buffer.equals` with named failures or lossless hex snapshots instead of Vitest traversing byte properties. Keep every test, dimension row, ownership check, real SQLite operation, and lifecycle assertion. No shared helper or production changes.

## Evidence

Three successful serial before and three after runs **per file** on frozen base `5d6e5aa36376de50619a674791a953455cd95f0b`, same host/private frozen dependencies/runtime/temp/cache:

| File | Median wall before → after | Gain | Median case-body sum before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `chat-attachments.test.ts` | 30.37 → 9.62 s | 68.3% | 13.079 → 0.458 s |
| `realtime-voice.test.ts` | 13.67 → 8.74 s | 36.1% | 5.090 → 0.042 s |
| `session-history-wal-budget.test.ts` | 16.79 → 13.76 s | 18.0% | 8.610 → 6.469 s |

Every candidate wall time was below every baseline wall time for its file; no file was dropped. The first attachment baseline includes 33.065 s of cold native-worker preparation and is retained. Case-body and CPU reductions corroborate the matcher mechanism; wall gains include runner/cache noise. These local wall times are not CI seconds. Discovery's CI case sums were 9.919 s for the two attachment rows, 7.099 s for the two voice cases, and 3.488 s for the WAL cadence case; exact-head CI41144159935 passed as the broad gate.

- Six comparison sites retain complete content and length checks: fourteen image rows, four 512 KiB audio chunks, and two 512 KiB native SQLite snapshots. No per-byte Vitest deep traversal at those sites.
- Last-byte corruption failed at every converted comparison: all fourteen image rows, each pending-audio chunk, dequeue/drain, and both WAL reads. Five mutation runs produced only the intended assertion failures. Candidate restored byte-for-byte; 72 tests across the three targets and three focused siblings passed afterward.

prs.title: fix(memory): skip file flushes when write is explicitly denied
prs.body:
Related: #126906

## What Problem This Solves

File-based memory flushes still run when `write` is explicitly denied, wasting attempts on a save they cannot perform.

## User Impact

Those file-based flushes are skipped without consuming a failure attempt. Memory plugins that save through their own tools keep their existing path. Normal replies and compaction continue.

## Why This Change Was Made

The flush owner checks the global and executing-agent deny policies with the existing tool-policy matcher, including groups and wildcards. The check applies only to file-backed plans. Allowlists, profiles, and provider-specific restrictions do not trigger this early skip. The selected memory plugin retains ownership of its flush plan and tools.

This addresses unnecessary file-backed flush attempts. It does not fully address reports of agents claiming that a memory save succeeded when it did not.

## Evidence

Current head: `03c910d997f50f86be92243a5aa33f1c5eb54d11`.

**Real Gateway/model proof passed on this head**, on Linux with Node 24.22.1. The canonical `pnpm openclaw` CLI built successfully and reported `OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (03c910d)`. The five PR files in the running candidate matched the checkout by SHA-256. No product source or workflow changes were made for this proof.

Each case used fresh isolated state, workspace, and port, with a synthetic plugin selected for the memory slot. `agents.defaults.compaction.memoryFlush.forceFlushTranscriptBytes: 1` made the flush eligible. A real configured model handled replies, tool calls, and manual compaction.

| Scenario | Dispatched flushes | Successful persistence calls | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| File plan, `write` allowed | 2 | 2 `write` | Pass; both distinct records remain in the file |
| File plan, global `tools.deny: ["write"]` | 0 | 0 | Pass; no target file or flush accounting |
| File plan, executing-agent `tools.deny: ["write"]` | 0 | 0 | Pass; no target file or flush accounting |
| Tool plan, global and agent `write` denies | 2 | 2 `proof_save` | Pass; independent `proof_get` readback succeeded |

All four cases passed with exit 0. Each Gateway reached `coreReady: true`, normal replies worked before and after compaction, and `sessions compact` committed a model-generated summary with `compactionCount` advancing from 0 to 1. There were no flush failures. Denied file plans left the flush state unset. Positive cases recorded successful flush accounting for both compaction cycles. Every test Gateway then stopped cleanly and released its port.

Persistence was checked through `audit.activity.list`, matching each detached flush run ID to a persistence tool's started/succeeded events with the same tool-call ID. The file case preserved two distinct `amber-47 proof-<UUID>` records. In the tools case, `proof_save` required a memory-flush context and used the plugin's keyed store. A later normal turn called `proof_get` and returned the exact marker, a nonempty `flushId`, and the source conversation audience. The test parsed the actual tool result, including Gateway-projected nested tool activity when the model used `dispatch_action`.

This closes the live evidence gap raised in the [source review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179604#issuecomment-6322276823). It is synthetic Gateway/plugin proof, not deployed-channel acceptance or Windows validation.

[CI run 40298288254](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40298288254) passed on this head, including selected Node tests, production and test type checks, lint, docs, security checks, and the CI gate. These are current-head CI results; no merged-head local Vitest run is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Earlier evidence and test setup corrections</summary>

The first live file fixture requested the same saved note twice. Its second write correctly hit the append-only replay check. The fixture now supplies a new marker-plus-UUID line for each flush; the requirement for a successful persistence audit on every dispatched flush was retained. The first tools run read the stored record, but its assertion missed the nested tool result. The external harness was corrected to read the current Gateway projection. Both incomplete attempts were retained as failed attempts; the complete scenarios passed in fresh state afterward.

The production guard is unchanged from the reviewed patch. This head merges upstream main `5bc90d07df855af4ea3b1fd86c79bc96d0b64caa` and resolves conflicts in three tests. It preserves upstream fixture helpers, active-model behavior, consolidated failure tests, and the deny/plugin-persistence/reply/compaction cases. There are no workflow changes relative to that base.

Earlier Linux regression tests on public commit `346f1950215e5ed3a7a892e18aafbd372542d1f2` with this patch passed all eight selected cases. Before the guard, the three explicit-deny cases failed. Those are historical-base results. Historical Windows attempts had SQLite cleanup errors and reply/compaction timeouts, including a runnable-case timeout before the fix. The Linux proof does not establish a repair for those Windows failures.

Independent source review found no actionable code defect. The unavailable local `autoreview` helper was not reported as a successful helper run.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ui): keep logs following after row resize compensation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Logs can stop following new entries when wrapped rows resize before their compensation scroll is reported, or when an in-flight poll finishes while the tab is hidden. Auto-follow stays enabled while the viewport remains near the previous end.

## User Impact

Appended logs remain reachable and continue following when the user returns to the tab. Reader wheel, touch and keyboard input retains control of the viewport. No configuration or migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The virtualizer's append/trim anchor was applied before Solid committed the new spacer and row window, so its end command used the old DOM scroll maximum. Normal animation-frame reconciliation could correct that target, but a hidden tab can suspend frames beyond the library's five-second reconciliation lifetime. The existing post-layout owner now applies the anchor after the published window commits. Its memoized height and key-extractor identity cover both size changes and same-height trims without adding a second follow-state owner.

After compensation, the same owner reads the actual scroll offset through the existing observer before another row measurement can consume the previous offset. The existing Subagents test repair polls its original containment inequalities until ResizeObserver publishes the narrowed transcript width; it retains the scrolling and readability assertions.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original resize-compensation regression | The base moves scrollTop 21,716 → 21,669 on the next resize; the repair preserves the end position. Both direct and already-queued resize schedules are retained. |
| Hidden in-flight append on exact `cb9b34c393ec` | Intended red: after 5,145 ms and exactly two requests, row 1,000 is absent; visible rows remain 482–507 (top 21,582 / height 44,252 / viewport 634). The real visibility owner stops hidden polls and issues one catch-up request. |
| Candidate Logs view and page tests | 23/23 pass in one run, including both resize schedules, the hidden append, initial loads, request ownership, quiet serialization, filters and explicit re-enable-follow behavior. |

Main’s measured-headroom repair (#188780) was merged after the previous CI run failed this gate; the four authored files remain byte-identical to the reviewed and locally tested candidate. |
| Independent P2 review | Three passes completed. One finding identified the old index snapshot's pre-publication anchor application; the candidate fixes that finding. No additional P0–P2 defect was established. The review status was `findings`, not `scoped-clean`. |
| Prior integrated-head CI | [Run 41127778122](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41127778122) on `cb9b34c393ec` failed the WebKit 1440 px initial-newest-row wait and Quiet automation's `updatedAt` equality. Both exact names passed [scheduled main 41123124777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41123124777); neither failure is claimed inherited. Both pass in the final exact-head CI below. |
| Final exact-head CI | [CI 41144405917](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41144405917) and [Workflow Sanity 41144405868](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41144405868) both passed on `d1e8dfbc1a44`. No CI rerun was used. |

The final `d1e8dfbc1a44` head incorporates #188780 and passed exact-head CI. Native completed-evidence recovery merged it as `769373dc062a9ce083c6ca34a352d179391ce192`; native closeout completed.

The hidden-append regression proves a reachable bug independently of the earlier WebKit CI failure. An unchanged source-Vite replay of that WebKit case passed once on `cb9b34c393ec`; it does not establish shipped-bundle equivalence or explain the CI failure. No timing improvement is claimed. prs.title: fix(plugins): keep adopted tools and hooks on one service owner
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Prepared agent registries can borrow a live Gateway's tool factories while retaining hooks from a different `register()` invocation. A hook that records per-registration state then writes to a different closure from the executor, so valid calls fail despite matching parameters and caller identity.

The selected-tool follow-up also needs to tolerate registrations that exist only in the donor. In particular, a donor containing `[owner_tool, unnamed factory]` must be able to serve a prepared consumer containing only `[owner_tool]`. Rejecting that donor group leaves the selected tool on its discovery instance, where its service has not started.

## User Impact

Stateful, service-backed plugins keep their hooks and selected tools on the admitting Gateway's service instance. Donor-only named or unnamed factories are not exposed to the prepared consumer. Selected unnamed or unmatched registrations still retain their local owner. Retained hook callbacks reject access after either owner retires.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing adoption owner matches every selected registration by identity, multiplicity and declared contract. Source digests, plugin configuration and hook policies must also match. It copies all three hook planes together and binds them to the prepared consumer's lifetime; other provider and capability adoption is unchanged.

The latest repair skips unnamed registrations only while collecting donor identity groups. It preserves the stricter selected-registration check and does not add shared state, a cache, permissions or a fallback.

## Evidence

The donor-only unnamed regression uses the real registrar, `acquireAgentRuntimePluginRegistry`, and an actually started service. The initial run at prior PR head `a73130fce56fc5853db93330c45503694007730e` has 1 failure and 22 passing cases; the affected selected tool throws `service is not started`. This red run preceded a test-only correction to the unused donor factory's returned label/result shape. Registration and grouping do not call that factory, and the failure trace enters only the selected named tool, so the correction does not affect the demonstrated cause. With the final valid fixture and two-file repair, all 23 cases pass, including named and unnamed donor extras, selected-unnamed rejection, contract checks and both owner-retirement paths. The native wrapper and final source verification completed with exit 0.

Final scoped validation passed: 23 owner cases, typed lint for both changed files, relevant core and test type checks, formatting, native commit hooks and the final source verification. The production file did not change during the test-only return-shape correction, so its already-passing core type check was reused.

A fresh canonical Codex review of the final two-file scope completed on the same Windows host with `scoped-clean`, no actionable P0–P2 findings, and successful final source verification. The reviewer assessed the supplied source; the test executions above are separate evidence.

This PR remains draft. Current-candidate Gateway agent-entry proof of allowed storage, forbidden peer-session effects and retained tool-callback retirement is still pending. The owner suite directly tests hook-callback retirement, not every retained tool executor after either owner closes. An isolated Gateway attempt timed out before producing an effect receipt and is not counted as a pass. The owner-suite results above do not claim a complete Gateway/model/channel run, repository-wide suite or hosted CI result.

prs.title: test(gateway): skip real xAI fallback retry waits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The 16-scenario xAI Gateway regression spends seconds waiting through real retry backoff, contributing to an already expensive test and its timeout risk. This is a maintainer-requested test-cost cleanup.

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. All 16 scenarios and their provider-request, error-priority, fallback, terminal-event, history, and display assertions are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the retry owner's existing `sleepWithAbort` seam for immediate, abort-aware completion, and restore the spy after each test. The existing retry-owner tests cover timing, cancellation, and elapsed retry budgets. This Gateway test retains real HTTP/WebSocket I/O and lifecycle timers. It already shares one Gateway across scenarios.

Production LOC delta: **0**. Test LOC delta: **0**. The fixture now stores only the last published assistant message it checks and removes redundant type/model wrappers; no budget files change. No new production seam, configuration option, dependency, benchmark script, or shared README change.

## Evidence

Timing on base `4d2a9f8bb4c47da0daae7fd820cab33fa450ef7b`, Node 26, one Vitest worker, real local Gateway and synthetic HTTP provider:

| Run | Before: test wall time | After: test wall time | Intentional retry sleep |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 120.494 s | 65.236 s | 6.127 s → 0 |
| 2 | 149.704 s | 49.375 s | 7.050 s → 0 |
| 3 | 151.583 s | 35.349 s | 5.353 s → 0 |

Each run executes all **16 scenarios**. Baseline instrumentation delegated every sleep to the real implementation and logged setup/scenario/cleanup timing; it is absent from the final diff. Every baseline made **six** retry sleeps, averaging **6.18 seconds** of scheduled waiting. The final fixture schedules no retry sleeps. Startup/boot alone took **61–87 seconds** in the baseline, with **29–30 seconds** of process CPU in the first two Node boot samples. One earlier cold Bun run timed out after boot used **175.9 seconds** of its 180-second test budget.

The Mac's load fell from roughly **75–120** during baseline work to roughly **28** late in candidate measurement. The raw wall-time decrease is therefore confounded by host load and warm caches; the attributable improvement is removal of the six waits. The **under-10-second target is not met** by these independent runs. No production allocation or CPU improvement is claimed; this is a test-only change, so a production-shaped load test would not measure its effect.

The selected project was `gateway-server-isolated` throughout. Final runs explicitly selected that project against the already-built runtime to avoid unrelated automatic artifact preparation. One canceled redundant build required local artifact recovery; its module-not-found setup failure is excluded from timing. No production Gateway was used.

Validation: focused test passed three final measurement runs and **10/10 consecutive fresh-process stability runs** (**160 scenario executions**, **29.170–47.794 seconds** per test). Final focused lint, formatting, whitespace, and the matching Gateway-server test typecheck passed. Exact-head [PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41143819975) passed, including the Gateway-server test typecheck, changed-test lanes, lint, ratchets, all three PostgreSQL conformance shards, and `openclaw/ci-gate`, at `8c4630876c8fdf1f2f2c8e110555e1ffbe4a565d`. The exact changed Gateway test passed in **31.318 seconds** under Bun in [its CI shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41143819975/job/124364556138). CodeQL and Security Review also passed. The PR remains ready and unmerged for maintainer handoff. The test-line ratchet passes with **net delta 0**, retaining its inherited **1,042-line** over-ceiling notice. No shared budget files change.

Focused test command (run serially ten times for stability):

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node OPENCLAW_E2E_USE_PREBUILT_DIST=1 \
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts \
  --project gateway-server-isolated src/gateway/server.xai-fallback.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

A same-worker `--repeats 9` attempt failed during the second Gateway start. The untouched baseline reproduced the same 180-second second-start timeout with `--repeats 1` (224.7-second total test time). All ten normal isolated-process runs passed; same-worker reinitialization remains an existing fixture gap.

prs.title: fix(plugins): plugin MCP accounts cannot be signed out and reconnect after reinstall
prs.body:
Related: #165951

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: plugin-declared MCP accounts (Granola-style connectors) can be signed in from the plugin page but never signed out, and uninstalling then reinstalling the plugin silently reconnects the previous account.

## User Impact

User impact: a connected account on a plugin's page now has **Sign out** (with confirmation), and uninstalling a plugin removes its saved MCP sign-ins, so a reinstall starts signed out. A server under `mcp.servers` with the same name and URL keeps its credentials.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The Gateway only had `mcp.authLogin`, and `openclaw mcp logout` resolves only `mcp.servers` entries, so plugin-declared servers had no sign-out path. The connected-account **Edit** action opened Settings → MCP, which does not list plugin-declared servers.
- New operator-admin `mcp.authLogout { serverName }` resolves the exact connection `mcp.authLogin` signs in (`resolveOperatorMcpOAuthConnection`) and clears it through the existing OAuth store owner. Running MCP clients read tokens per request, so their next call needs a new sign-in.
- The plugin page replaces the dead-end **Edit** on connected accounts with **Sign out**; the result is re-read from `plugins.inspect` rather than assumed.
- The credential store key is derived from the server name and URL, both of which come from the plugin, so a reinstall found the old row. Plugin uninstall now clears the operator and requester OAuth rows for the plugin's declared HTTP MCP endpoints, as removing a configured server already does. Endpoints are read during uninstall preparation, before files are removed. A clear failure becomes an uninstall warning rather than failing a committed uninstall.
- Accepted edge case: if two installed plugins declare the same MCP server name and URL, uninstalling one clears the shared sign-in; the other plugin shows **Sign in** again.

## Evidence

Real isolated Gateway and Control UI in headless Chromium, with a synthetic OAuth MCP server and a local plugin declaring one HTTP OAuth MCP server. Before: installed release 2026.10.9 (`7975404`). After: this branch built with `pnpm build` and `pnpm ui:build`. Sign-in went through the real browser callback; uninstall and reinstall went through `openclaw plugins uninstall/install` against the running Gateway.

**Connected account — before:** only **Edit**, which leads to a page that does not list the server.

![Before: connected plugin account offers only Edit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/734e8107-6bd9-4b7c-ad1a-bcf855a646bc)

**Connected account — after:** **Sign out**, with confirmation.

![After: connected plugin account offers Sign out](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e439663d-a485-4cea-b013-d9c812937ab8)

![After: Sign out confirmation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/abf7b16a-fe7d-4f45-b584-bd63215ff8d3)

**After uninstall, reinstall and enable — before:** still **Connected** to the old account.

![Before: reinstalled plugin is still connected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/684f4734-42bc-4852-8f0e-45119869a2dd)

**After uninstall, reinstall and enable — after:** signed out.

![After: reinstalled plugin starts signed out](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1b1c2365-65fd-4afd-87d9-fca48294f668)

Stored credential readback from the Gateway's `mcp_oauth_stores` row for the plugin server:

| Step | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sign in from plugin page | tokens present | tokens present |
| Sign out | no control | tokens cleared |
| Uninstall, reinstall, enable | tokens present | tokens cleared |

Focused tests:

- `src/gateway/server.mcp-auth-login.test.ts`: 38 passed, including a new case that signs a bundle-declared connector in through the browser callback, rejects read-only and unknown-server logout, then signs out without touching another connection's credentials.
- `src/plugins/management-uninstall.mcp-oauth.test.ts` (new): management uninstall (enabled and disabled plugin) and CLI uninstall clear the plugin's operator and requester rows and keep an unrelated server's row. These three cases fail with the clear call removed and pass with it. A configured server with the same endpoint keeps its sign-in.
- `ui/src/pages/plugins/plugins-page.mcp-auth.test.ts` and `plugins-page.test.ts`: 27 passed (confirmation gating, sign-out request, authoritative refresh, error retention).
- Also passed: gateway method descriptor/since/list tests, `connect-hello` scope test, existing uninstall and inspect suites, `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint and oxfmt on changed files, `pnpm protocol:check`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, `git diff --check`. Local autoreview (P1) on the committed range: no findings.

Gaps: no real Granola account was used. Settings → MCP still has no **Sign out** for `mcp.servers` entries; `openclaw mcp logout` covers those. Locally, `server.mcp-auth-login.test.ts` needs `NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1` on hosts that set `HTTP(S)_PROXY`; without it, existing cases in that file also fail with "could not reach the sign-in service" because the loopback fixture is sent through the proxy.

Requested by @jalehman.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/303fc055-5a5d-4eb1-94a9-d46c3520044c)

## Worked on by

- @jalehman

prs.title: fix(llm-task): tool fails when agents configure their own models
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`llm-task` rejects no-override calls when models are configured per agent or the global primary is a configured alias. Its unconditional provider/model precheck runs before the existing completion owner can select the correct default.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restrict that precheck to explicit/plugin-configured overrides. Calls without overrides already pass model selection to the completion runtime; let that owner resolve per-agent models and aliases. Explicit bad overrides remain rejected. No model policy, SDK, schema or prompt changes. Original fix by @Yigtwxx.

## Evidence

[Independent built CLI and real agent proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188758#issuecomment-6535700206).

Per-agent and alias configurations each fail twice on main and complete twice on the candidate. The real Gateway agent discovers and dispatches llm-task; candidate isolated completions reach a local streaming provider and return JSON. Explicit bad-override controls remain rejected on both refs. No paid keys or host credentials.

Focused suite: 9 passed. Baseline: 2 regression failures, 1 qualified-default control passed, 6 skipped. Test delta +20/-21 (net -1); removed the 12-line allocation by consolidating into the existing fenced-JSON case. Production +2/-1.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: revert restores the precheck; no migration or stored-format change. Blast radius is llm-task calls without model/provider overrides whose defaults require runtime resolution. Existing override validation and completion-owner authorization remain unchanged.

## What Problem This Solves

The shared test-line budget is 1,036 lines below the already-merged test corpus at 528b92792ed041366e037d084041369f93d244a7. That inherited deficit causes later changes with their own correctly allocated test growth to fail the test-line ratchet.

## User Impact

Contributors retain the existing regression coverage and all named allocations. This reconciliation accounts for the measured preexisting growth without changing tests, assertions, checker rules, or product behavior. It creates no spare test-line capacity at the measured cut.

## Why This Change Was Made

The receiving corpus contains 6,313,574 literal newline bytes. Its scalar of 6,287,490 plus 25,048 lines in 177 existing grants permits 6,312,538 lines. Raising only the scalar by 1,036 to 6,288,526 makes the effective ceiling exactly match the corpus. This preserves the intervening scalar reductions and uses the lower measured need; future test growth still follows the existing allocation rules.

The pinned measurement has zero spare lines. At the later receiving snapshot 29a02f29ea2fb0505896372c758b571558e020c1, intervening upstream test and allocation changes leave 11 lines of inherited slack. The reconciliation above remains measured against its pinned source.

## Evidence

The original pinned candidate passed the native checker with zero slack while preserving every grant. After resolving the actual scalar conflict against 528b92792ed041366e037d084041369f93d244a7, incremental source arithmetic establishes the lower 1,036-line need above. The corrected native checker reports `Test lines OK: 6313574; ceiling: 6313574; slack: 0.` Strict one-file metadata and whitespace checks passed, with all 177 grants unchanged. Hosted checks are pending. No runtime test suite is needed for this integer-only budget change.
