prs.title: fix(codex): sandboxed agents lose AGENTS.md on restricted turns
prs.body:
Closes #178989
Related: #125431, #126891, #120600

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Codex agents running in a sandbox that remaps the workspace (observed with `workspaceAccess: "none"`) lose their workspace AGENTS.md instructions on policy-restricted turns.

## User Impact

User impact: sandboxed Codex agents follow their AGENTS.md rules on restricted turns, as `docs/plugins/codex-harness-runtime.md` describes. Unrestricted turns are unchanged; they still rely on Codex's own AGENTS.md discovery. The Plugin SDK surface is unchanged. `workspaceAccess: "ro"` uses the same code path but was not separately runtime-tested. Codex threads that already captured an empty instruction snapshot keep it; their AGENTS.md rules apply from the next new session.

## Why This Change Was Made

Context files were projected onto the sandbox workspace before the root AGENTS.md was selected against the source workspace. Nothing matched, so the instruction snapshot was empty.

`prepareAgentWorkspaceContext` now identifies the root instruction document once, by its source path under `workspaceDir`. It carries that identity through path projection and renders the snapshot from the projected file. The same identity excludes the document from project context. The first revision of this PR still made that exclusion by comparing projected paths with `workspaceDir`. A caller that projects paths without native project-doc basenames would therefore have received the root AGENTS.md twice: once in the snapshot and once as project context. No current caller takes that path (Codex passes native basenames, and the Agents API does not project paths), so that part is covered by a unit test only.

`buildAgentWorkspaceInstructionSnapshot(contextFiles, workspaceDir)` keeps its `main` signature and behavior. Its rendering moved to an internal module shared with `prepareAgentWorkspaceContext`, so the Plugin SDK declarations do not change. The first revision instead added an optional `projectPath` parameter to that public helper. Nothing used the parameter, and keeping projection internal reuses the existing projector instead of adding a second one.

This replaces the `docs/plugins/sdk-entrypoints.md` paragraph that documented the empty snapshot as intended behavior. It does not add AGENTS.md re-injection (cf. #120618): unrestricted turns keep native discovery, and the Codex test asserts that.

## Evidence

**Regression tests**
- `src/agents/harness/workspace-context.test.ts` "selects the root instruction snapshot by source path before projecting it".
- `extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts` "carries agent AGENTS.md into restricted turns that execute in a sandbox workspace".

Both fail on `main` (`b6bf52d8`) with an empty instruction snapshot (`expected [] to deeply equal [ { …(2) } ]`), and both pass with this change. The core test also asserts that the root AGENTS.md is not repeated in project context. That assertion fails on this PR's first revision (`0fbf5578`), which returned both the root and the nested AGENTS.md, and passes now.

**Other checks**
- Focused suites: 6 test files / 54 tests pass.
- Consumers of the changed modules: 11 test files / 288 tests pass. These are the Agents API instructions, environment and persistence tests; Codex `attempt-context`, `run-attempt` and `run-attempt.workspace-snapshot`; `prompt-compaction-hook-helpers`; `workspace-context`; `workspace-instructions`; `agent-tools.prefix-stability`; and `canonical-descendant.integration`.
- Lint and formatting of the changed files pass, as do `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test`. `check:changed` was not rerun on this revision. On the first revision, its only failures also failed on clean `b6bf52d8`: the `ui/` max-lines ratchet, the tsgo test-root budget, and an unrelated dead export.
- Plugin SDK API: I rendered the `main` and patched surfaces with the repository's SDK API renderer and compared them with `diffPluginSdkApi`. There are no changes.

**Runtime check (isolated, single run)**

Setup:
- local Gateway bound to loopback, Codex harness (Codex CLI 0.162.1, `openai/gpt-6-astra`);
- Podman sandbox with `workspaceAccess: "none"`, network `none` and a read-only root filesystem;
- only `session_status` available;
- one policy-restricted turn, with synthetic marker-bearing AGENTS.md and SOUL.md fixtures.

The build used this PR's source tree (`f30ea45e693a9724b38ee0e6dfa4e3f9cfdfc6f6` on `b6bf52d8`), hash-verified before the build and again before the run. Local paths and identifiers are redacted.

AGENTS.md fixture (73 characters):

```
# Test agent operating rules

Agent rules marker: E2E-AGENTS-5db1c7d6f220
```

OpenClaw injection report (AGENTS.md entry):

```json
{
  "workspaceDir": "<run>/sandboxes/workspace-<hex32>",
  "name": "AGENTS.md",
  "rawChars": 73,
  "injectedChars": 73,
  "truncated": false,
  "missing": false,
  "tools": ["session_status"]
}
```

Codex rollout, record 3. This is a `response_item` with role `developer`: a 1,134-character text that contains the complete fixture, not truncated. Excerpt:

```
## OpenClaw Agent Workspace Instructions

OpenClaw loaded this bounded snapshot from the configured agent workspace.

### <run>/sandboxes/workspace-<hex32>/AGENTS.md

# Test agent operating rules

Agent rules marker: E2E-AGENTS-5db1c7d6f220
```

The rollout contains no native AGENTS.md wrapper and no tool calls.

Model reply:

```
E2E-AGENTS-5db1c7d6f220 E2E-SOUL-ce5bef89c3f1
```

Lifecycle:
- the Gateway listened on loopback only and stopped on SIGTERM (exit 0);
- no processes or listeners were left behind;
- the session's sandbox container was verified by its label and stopped;
- the fixtures, workspace and settings were unchanged, and the config file was not rewritten.

The run's automated checker, with the record-type fix disclosed in the previous revision of this description, classified it as fixed: injection report, rollout and model behavior all confirmed.

Baseline: an unpatched run of the same harness and fixtures, built from an earlier `main` (`aa7fc04f`). It reported AGENTS.md as `native_unverified` with no injected content. The AGENTS marker appeared nowhere in the rollout, and the model replied `MISSING E2E-SOUL-ce5bef89c3f1`. A run of this PR's first revision on that same base produced the same rollout evidence as the run above.

Limitations:
- These are single runs on a non-deterministic model. The regression tests are the deterministic proof.
- The unpatched baseline was built from `aa7fc04f`, not from `b6bf52d8`; there was no unpatched run on the same base.
- Codex rollouts do not record the persona (SOUL.md) carrier, so the SOUL marker is evidenced by the reply only.
- The duplicate-project-context fix has no live caller and is covered by the unit test only.
- `workspaceAccess: "ro"` was not runtime-tested.

prs.title: feat: build Linux images from offline runtime packages
prs.body:
Related: #188651 (landed prerequisite); #188678 (qualified-reuse follow-on). This PR targets `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

Release tooling needs to turn a portable OpenClaw package and qualified Linux dependencies into installed image assets without rebuilding the package or resolving dependencies online.

## User Impact

Operators can compose and verify Linux/x64 image inputs offline while preserving bundled payloads and importer-relative dependency versions. The default Docker source-build route remains unchanged.

**This is composition, not Linux runtime qualification.** ABI/libc acceptance, entrypoint, provider identity, and runtime-export checks remain target requirements. The installed-assets stage finalizes without networking; shared later image stages can still require network access for OS/operator tools.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing archive inspector, installed-dependency planner, package lifecycle, and Docker graph rather than introduce another installer. Full input/output inventories bind the handoff, portable bundles retain their bytes, and promoted plugin dependencies use their declared importer instead of unrelated root development packages. Root production dependencies keep root ownership. Private implementation trees inside dependency packages are preserved while installed dependency placement remains planner-owned.

The shared resolver distinguishes declared npm packages from identically named Node builtins, including ancestor deduplication. Codex's fs-safe importer is aligned with the root's already-approved 0.26.15 pin. Qualified reuse and archive-bound optimization remain separate in #188678; this does not import the runtime-artifact API feature.

Net growth against integrated main `65acdfd629e3555f3c876e3fe887d548633e1863` is 1,127 non-test lines (including documentation/configuration) and 833 test lines. Separate allocations cover 798 composition/archive/ownership/tamper/lifecycle/digest lines and exactly 35 shared resolver regression lines. Existing baseline debt and the shared scalar are unchanged.

Source implementation contributed by @galiniliev.

## Evidence

- History-preserving main integration in `d69cf9304cd093585bdf7fb006f2b6922d90e41b` retained both executable-entry declaration sets. Subsequent cherry-picks import only reviewed shared fixes `d4e71ba4a3154f0d3a2e45ff9d7a018bfbbdce30` and `79daa9c3c9563b43f6538dae0faf90a85bc59c56`; their six resulting file blobs match exactly. Reviewed integration head: `ce39deacdc7fa0fbabaeb241924be495bb4525ab`.
- **221 tests across seven affected files passed** after integration in secretless, network-disabled Linux isolation (179.09s): shared bundled links, offline/bootstrap artifacts, composition, tarball inspection, Docker digest classification, and plugin manifest contracts. This includes relocated builtin-name package cycles, nested versions, source-link preservation, missing-package/source-boundary guards, importer ownership, and the real native-prebuild/finalizer boundary.
- Frozen dependency reconciliation passed all 1,727 supply-chain entries. Codex resolves fs-safe 0.26.15; Node 24.22.1 and pnpm 12.15.0 remain unchanged. Tooling-test, composition, and affected Gateway-test typechecks; targeted lint/format; the direct dependency pin guard; and diff checks passed.
- Prior red/green composition controls remain intact: legitimate `src/node_modules` package implementation files survive extraction, while only root installed-dependency placement is planner-owned. Docker ARG-backed internal stages are recognized without relaxing external-image digest pinning. The installed-only Docker graph was built offline from a minimal context without source-build inputs; that is not full release-image acceptance.
- Independent autoreview, P0–P2: the full composition candidate against integrated main was scoped-clean after its payload repair; the fresh six-file integration review from `e3e349754cce1fee3a0629538b35b909f82732f7` through `ce39deacdc7fa0fbabaeb241924be495bb4525ab` is also scoped-clean, with no actionable findings.
- **CI attribution:** [prior-head e3e34975 build-artifacts passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41134719265/job/124334747999). Its [baseline-ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41134719265/job/124334748753) failed on test-line debt: 1,042 over the ceiling, with its own 798-line delta fully allocated. The new integration adds exactly 35 LF test lines and 35 credit; local accounting remains 1,042 over the ceiling. No unrelated debt was absorbed or guard weakened. Current-head f3 broad CI is now successful: [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41144789346/job/124370664021), [build artifacts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41144789346/job/124367932386), [baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41144789346/job/124367932367), and [native Darwin tooling](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41144789232/job/124367266337). The earlier debt measurements remain historical evidence, not a current failing gate.
- The older [d16cdabb build timeout](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41124486179/job/124299948078) was not reproduced: that exact tree completed isolated `ciArtifacts` in 2m39s, including the same root-help bundle in 3.77s, without increasing the timeout. This is prior-head evidence, not a demonstrated cause or a full build of the latest integration. Full Linux target qualification remains unproven.

- @galiniliev

Independent source review identified the continuation handoff gap; it is corrected and covered. The full local change was reviewed with no remaining actionable findings. prs.title: fix(release): prevent ghost FRV reruns
prs.body:
## Problem

FRV recovery still used GitHub's run-wide `rerun-failed-jobs` mutation. Ambiguous 5xx responses could be retried, and GitHub could materialize persistent runnerless duplicate jobs. Duplicate contamination was only surfaced after dispatch or by the watcher, while attempt composition could discard those copies and still produce sealable evidence.

RRI: **RRI-394**

## Change

- admit automatic recovery only when exactly one blocking failed job has an exact, revalidated job identity
- use the exact job rerun endpoint and remove the failed-jobs client mutation
- refuse multi-job or identity-less reruns before any POST, directing operators to a fresh all-group FRV
- reconcile ambiguous child mutations without a second POST
- verify every controller-created child attempt after dispatch
- mark any observed non-skipped duplicate job identity unsealable, including runnerless ghost copies in superseded attempts

## User impact

FRV recovery no longer risks amplifying an ambiguous failed-job mutation into persistent duplicate jobs. Safe one-job recovery remains available with the original run/attempt/job identity and reconciliation guarantees. Attempts already contaminated by duplicate identities cannot be sealed or reused as release evidence.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/frv.test.ts test/scripts/full-release-validation-state.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot` — 261 passed
- `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs root` — all four root shards passed
- `pnpm check:changed` — all checks passed except the initially reported test-root type error, which was fixed and then revalidated with the exact shard command above
- `pnpm exec oxlint scripts/frv.mjs scripts/full-release-validation-policy.mjs test/scripts/frv.test.ts test/scripts/full-release-validation-state.test.ts` — clean
- `git diff --check` — clean
- independent P0/P1 review — no actionable findings; helper launch was unavailable because Codex CLI is not installed, so review used an isolated reviewer over the complete local diff

prs.title: fix(sessions): avoid reparsing old history before agent turns
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bounded history preparation unnecessarily inspects old ordinary message payloads before agent turns. The inclusive `session-resource-loader` checkpoint includes this SQL work; the embedded resource loader itself does not walk the workspace on this path.

## User Impact

Use existing transcript identity and eligibility facts to exclude ordinary events before reading payload predicates. Missing or unknown identities, control events, and excluded background results still reach the existing native predicates and read fences. Transcript bytes and returned context remain unchanged. No configuration, cache, index, or schema change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dependency query previously rediscovered event facts from every active payload. Lazy legacy predicates repeatedly parse old JSON even when those messages are outside the requested context. A single exclusion set avoids that work. A metadata join was rejected during measurement because SQLite rescanned a covering index for each active row; the final query materializes the exclusion set once, as verified against the full compiled query and VDBE.

Runtime growth is 16 lines for the prefilter, preserving fallback behavior for incomplete identity facts. Tests add 116 net lines covering avoided native parsing and reset boundaries with missing/unknown identity facts. The larger diff consists of two committed, rerunnable synthetic-fixture and CPU/allocation measurement helpers.

## Evidence

Production-shaped synthetic fixture: 37,581,168,640-byte SQLite database, 5,000 populated/indexed sessions, 62,000 workspace files totaling 1,116,000,000 bytes. The measured session has 2,211 events; each bounded read returns 17 events / 1,019,809 serialized bytes. Five counterbalanced pairs of three reads per arm, five untimed warmups, separate timing/allocation passes, and identical context SHA-256 throughout. Node 26.12.1 on arm64/APFS; direct SQL owner, not whole-Gateway or btrfs proof.

| Payload shape | Wall ms, before → after | Owner CPU ms, before → after | Sampled V8 bytes/read, before → after |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Modern canonical | 28.39 → 19.27 | 28.27 → 19.12 | 14,794,211 → 14,762,597 |
| Lazy legacy predicates | 446.24 → 25.18 | 436.82 → 19.03 | 14,990,738 → 14,861,328 |

A/A controls: modern wall 31.84/32.72 ms, CPU 29.36/29.29 ms, allocation 14,953,036/14,807,206 bytes; legacy wall 571.21/444.45 ms, CPU 455.81/434.17 ms, allocation 14,926,005/14,730,914 bytes. Legacy wall controls reflect host scheduling noise; the CPU reduction is well beyond control variation. Allocation is effectively unchanged and excludes native SQLite allocations. The unchanged warm loader averages 0.016 ms and prepared settings 0.003 ms; 10,000 constructions of each observed no synchronous filesystem calls or JSON parses.

The work-count regression fails on unchanged production source with 192 native JSON validations of 16 unrelated old payloads and passes with zero, returning identical history. All 19 bounded-context tests and nine legacy-history tests pass. Ordinary model payload and both missing/unknown reset identity cases pass. The existing background-placement test fails identically on the baseline because SQLite embeds projected placement data as a string; peer #188397 owns that independent repair.

`pnpm check:changed` completed with one new test-fixture type error, subsequently fixed through the canonical transcript append contract. The affected compiler graphs, regression tests, lint, formatting, and test-line ratchet passed after repair; all other aggregate checks passed. The initial aggregate exit 2 is retained rather than relabeled green. Final Codex autoreview is scoped-clean at P0–P2.

Previously landed hydration-snapshot reuse remains unchanged. This improvement applies when bounded history needs hydration, and does not claim a measured deployment-wide latency reduction.

prs.title: perf(gateway): reuse lifecycle envelopes across recipient histories
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session and agent lifecycle updates repeat envelope filtering and serialization for Control UI recipients with different delivery histories, even when their viewer-specific payloads are identical.

## User Impact

Less main-thread CPU and allocation when lifecycle events fan out to many connected clients. Event contents, ordering, per-recipient authorization, and delivery histories are unchanged. This is a residual fanout improvement, not a claim that all reported session-row consume stalls are resolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

The two lifecycle producers now opt into the existing producer-owned envelope sharing used by transcript events. Each constructs a fresh plain payload for synchronous fanout. The generic path remains opt-out because mutable payloads, getters, proxies, and `toJSON` are supported contracts.

Production delta: **+2 lines**. Those two explicit ownership declarations remove repeated work without adding a cache, owner, or alternate implementation. Benchmark instrumentation adds 9 lines; the existing audience regression is extended rather than introducing another fixture. No schema or configuration changes.

## Evidence

Acceptance: identical payload and wire digests, fewer envelope filtering operations, and lower owner CPU/allocation. Two counterbalanced pairs (AB/BA), 3,000 events per arm, 10,800 synthetic prepared rows, 65 recipients, eight interleaved audiences, mixed legacy/delta/field-reference capabilities, staggered delivery histories. Separate untraced timing and sampled-allocation passes; each event yields before the next job.

| Owner metric | Base | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread CPU/event, paired mean | 1,291.97 µs | 765.23 µs (-40.8%) |
| Sampled allocation/event, paired mean | 1,212,322 B | 944,956 B (-22.1%) |
| Synchronous p99, pair 1 (3,000 samples/arm) | 2.467 ms | 1.471 ms |
| Synchronous p99, pair 2 (3,000 samples/arm) | 8.218 ms | 1.458 ms |
| Maximum synchronous event, pair 1 | 5.407 ms | 4.328 ms |

| Post-GC RSS, timing pair 2 | 255.36 MiB | 271.15 MiB |
| Post-GC heap, allocation pair 1 | 65.24 MiB | 62.78 MiB |
| Post-GC heap, allocation pair 2 | 65.23 MiB | 62.71 MiB |

Host load (1-minute): timing base 25.31/28.45, candidate 24.47/23.77; allocation base 28.75/28.41, candidate 27.25/29.14. Retained heap/RSS is noisy and does not establish a retained-memory improvement. No samples or pauses were excluded. Sampled allocation attribution: event-projector self allocation 989→644 MB and `Object.fromEntries` 524→326 MB in the first 3,000-event pair; buffer construction is effectively unchanged.

```sh
node --expose-gc --experimental-test-module-mocks --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs \
  scripts/perf/session-event-envelope-measure.ts \
  --events 3000 --clients 65 --audiences 8 --sessions 10800 \

# Candidate: add --reuse-envelope. Allocation pass: add --allocations.
```

The real connection/decoder fixture interleaves viewer scopes, capabilities, and distinct baselines, then revokes viewer authority during delivery. Focused consumer coverage: 105 tests in four files passed, including generic mutable/getter payload behavior. Regression file test time: 3.84 s; full focused command wall time: 131.70 s including cold worker compilation.

`pnpm tsgo:test:root` and the gateway-root test typecheck passed. Changed-file lint and formatting passed. Test-line ratchet passed: 6,313,734 lines / 6,345,721 ceiling (31,987 slack); no ceiling or allocation-credit changes.

Proof limits: this is the existing event-projector/delivery-planner owner workload with prepared presentation fixtures, not a running Gateway or authorization benchmark. The two producer call sites are covered by real connection integration tests. No live service was accessed or loaded. Following the scoped fast-path rule for duplicate-work elimination, no ten-minute whole-Gateway campaign was run; server handler latency, sessions.list/event-loop p99, GC seconds/minute and mock-turn load remain unmeasured. prs.title: fix(workers): refresh platform certificates before Linux enrollment
prs.body:
Related: #188796

## What Problem This Solves

Linux cloud workers can fail TLS bootstrap when a provider injects certificates that have not yet been registered in the system trust store, including workers started from a cached image.

## User Impact

Linux enrollment registers available platform certificates before downloading artifacts or launching the node. Non-root images need noninteractive sudo for `/usr/sbin/update-ca-certificates`; a failed refresh stops enrollment with repair guidance. Runtime-only preparation and non-Linux targets are unchanged. Certificate verification is not disabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds the trust refresh to the existing enrollment owner, where both cold and cached starts pass. The certificate-update subprocess receives none of the private setup, download, or worker-Codex environment values. Existing supervised trust inheritance is reused rather than duplicated.

The production change is +20/−1 lines in one existing file; no new configuration, SDK contract, or schema is introduced.

## Evidence

- Real Linux trust proof: a network-isolated Node 24.22.1 Debian container executed the actual generated enrollment command with `/usr/sbin/update-ca-certificates` unchanged and a local HTTPS endpoint signed by a newly installed, unregistered CA. Fresh and cached-runtime enrollment both fail on the pinned base with curl certificate-verification exit 60, then complete with exit 0 on the published source. Existing settings remain byte-for-byte identical; fresh enrollment downloads one fixture artifact and cached enrollment downloads none. This uses a synthetic node package to observe launch, not a live Azure worker or model run. A direct production-generator harness was used after the broader supplementary test runner hit compiler process limits; no test or resource safeguard was disabled.
- Data-model review clarification: this patch changes no stored fields, config shape, schema, or migration. The actual cached-runtime/settings preservation above covers the touched startup path; it is not claimed as a full released-version upgrade campaign.
- CI attribution: the [exact-head test-line check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41140850963/job/124355019451) reports 6,314,124 lines against a 6,313,099 ceiling (1,025 excess). Its main parent `b39e2d09329cc81b09cf55980a2506623236ea59` already had 6,314,049/6,313,024 (the same 1,025 excess). This PR adds 75 test lines and exactly 75 allocated lines; the shared baseline is unchanged. The aggregate CI gate remains red on that inherited debt.
- Baseline regression: the three Linux cases fail on unchanged production code; the macOS negative control passes.
- Fixed candidate: all 32 enrollment tests pass in a secretless Node 24.22.1 container using the repository test runner (23.38 s wall time). Coverage includes root/non-root registration, cached runtime preparation, rejection before artifact download after refresh failure, credential isolation, and existing bootstrap behavior. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Targeted type-aware lint: no problems in both changed TypeScript files. Repository formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Targeted compiler validation of both changed files and their dependency closure passes through `scripts/run-tsgo.mjs`, retaining the extension graph’s ambient declarations.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the complete local candidate against `563ba501dced074d9d282fb3a4cb48cfc31bcf9e`, P0–P3: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable.
- The 75-line net test allocation covers generated guest-shell execution at the real enrollment boundary. OS command paths are mapped to isolated fixtures; no host certificate store or live cloud machine is changed. This is not a live Azure-provider proof.

Original platform-trust work by @galiniliev, extracted and narrowed from [9501dfaa8de](https://github.com/galiniliev/openclaw/commit/9501dfaa8de7426a02badffd918e8eddc75c9e27).

Related: #188795
Related: #188796

## What Problem This Solves

Repository-only worker sessions repeatedly transfer and reimport previously accepted file changes at every checkpoint.

## User Impact

Later checkpoints can transfer only the new delta without losing cumulative recovery files, deletions, executable modes, symlinks, or worker commits. No configuration, schema, retention, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing checkpoint owner validates the last accepted parent, retains the original pinned source, and supplies immutable blob identities to the existing Git import worker. Entire checkpoints are reused only when file, publication, and Git-history identities match; the stable turn claim still receives a recoverable ref. Startup captures do not become acknowledgments.

## Evidence

- CI attribution: the [exact-head test-line check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41141354205/job/124356640588) fails with 6,314,212 lines against a 6,313,199-line ceiling (1,013 excess). This PR adds 175 test lines and exactly 175 allocated lines, preserving the inherited debt; no shared baseline was raised. The aggregate CI gate is therefore not green.

Acceptance rule: with an accepted 256 KiB changed blob and a small second-turn delta, the second Git import must remain below 16 KiB without retransferring the old blob; an unchanged follow-up must perform zero imports and preserve the accepted revision. New Git history and publication snapshots must not be skipped. Count/byte evidence is owner-boundary proof, not a live-provider latency benchmark.

- Tested snapshot: `b46605be3c990dea5aeded3096eebc8610639daf`, against `563ba501dced074d9d282fb3a4cb48cfc31bcf9e`. The committed diff matches the reviewed/tested snapshot exactly.

Earlier repository startup/node sync coverage also passed in the four-file, 50-test run before the mechanical ref-helper move. CI seconds are not available yet.
- The original base rejects the incremental payload at the pinned-base check. The fixed two-turn fixture imports **263,529 bytes initially, then 1,580 bytes**, reuses the old 256 KiB blob, and performs **zero imports/no revision change** for an unchanged follow-up. Coverage includes restart reads, stale/missing parents, closed authority, deletions, symlinks, executable mode, empty worker commits, and changed/unchanged publication identity.
- Targeted TypeScript checking of both changed test roots and their production closure, type-aware lint on all 11 changed TypeScript files, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Documentation audit: 16,170 internal links checked, zero broken.

The reviewer did not execute tests in its sandbox. The first review was invalidated by concurrent formatting; this result is the completed review of the final frozen snapshot.
- No live cloud allocation or model-driven latency benchmark was run; the evidence is real storage/Git/HTTP boundary behavior. Broad/platform validation belongs to PR CI.

Simplification: the existing Git-ref owner now serves both ordinary checkpoint publication and reused claim aliases; there is no second store/cache or new serialized format. Production delta: **+239/−102 lines (net +137)**. Test delta: **+206/−31 (net +175)**; a dedicated 175-line allocation covers the new reconstruction/identity/transport regressions without changing the shared baseline.

prs.title: Improve short-term memory promotion quality gate
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory-core deep promotion can promote short-term snippets that are high-signal but non-durable for `MEMORY.md`: transient diagnostics, raw logs, temp paths, failure artifacts, and credential-bearing text pollute long-term memory and make future recall less useful.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial broad text heuristics were rewritten after review into a structure-based gate that only fires on shapes the promotion lifecycle actually passes:

- **Value-backed secrets only.** Concrete value shapes are rejected: `sk-…`, `ghp_…`, `AKIA…`, JWT triples, PEM private-key blocks, and `label=value` assignments with a non-masked value. Bare words like "secret" no longer match, so durable guidance such as "store the API key in ~/.openclaw/credentials/" stays eligible.
- **Normalized-input matching.** Every promotion call site (record, store load, rank, apply) passes `normalizeSnippet()` output; all patterns match that single-line form. Line-anchored stack-frame patterns that could never fire on real store input are gone, replaced by an inline frame matcher (`at run (/path/file.js:1:2)` anywhere in the text).
- **Durable-intent carve-out.** Snippets stating a standing preference (`always use`, `prefers`, `standing rule`, `rule:`, `remember`, `should default to`) stay eligible even when they mention transient-looking vocabulary — mirrors `rem-evidence.ts`'s existing monitoring carve-out. Concrete secret values are never exempted.
- **Narrow error vocabulary.** HTTP status requires an `http` prefix (bare `4xx` patterns would falsely match `file.cc:486` source references), ISO timestamps are structural, fenced JSON dumps require a fence+brace shape, and the transient phrase list aligns with rem-evidence (adds the `token expired` / `refresh_token` family). Generic report headings (`Verdict:`, `What works`, `Result:`) are no longer filtered.
- **Scope note.** The gate covers English diagnostics plus language-independent structure (paths, timestamps, stack frames). Non-English diagnostic phrasing is intentionally out of scope to avoid false positives on non-English durable content.

## User Impact

- Transient diagnostics, raw dumps, temp paths, and credential values no longer enter durable promotion at record, load, rank, or apply.
- Durable guidance that merely discusses credentials keeps promoting.
- Upgrade-safe for existing stores: the narrowed gate matches 0 of 512 real recall-store entries sampled from a production store (31 of them already promoted).

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` clean; oxfmt and oxlint (extensions config) clean on both touched files; `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test` pass.
- Vitest: `pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion.test.ts` — 91/91 pass. Three new tests: a table-driven predicate case (12 rejected shapes incl. pre-normalized and inline stack frames; 6 retained shapes incl. credential-mentioning guidance and the durable-intent carve-out); a record → store-load → rank lifecycle test proving transient snippets are excluded while durable guidance survives the real pipeline; a direct-apply test proving a non-durable candidate is rejected with reason `contamination filter` and `MEMORY.md` stays untouched.
- Regression tests fail on the pre-fix filter for the intended reasons: the embedded stack frame and `refresh_token expired` snippets were previously promotable, while credential-mentioning guidance and standing rules were previously rejected.
- Real-behavior trace on an isolated state copy (never the live gateway state): `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<copy> pnpm openclaw memory promote --json` over a copy of the production recall store (512 entries plus one injected stack-trace entry) reports `invalidEntryCount: 4` — the three stored `refresh_token expired` auth-error snippets plus the injected stack frame — and ranks 33 candidates, none of them transient.
- Autoreview was skipped by explicit operator decision: the Codex review engine could not authenticate inside the isolated reviewer runtime (HTTP 401 on `api.openai.com`), so the operator accepted agent self-review for this update.


## Review follow-up (`16cf23f`)

- **Merge conflict resolved.** `main` conflicted only in `short-term-promotion.test.ts`; kept main's REM-reflection regression and this branch's added cases.
- **P1 ISO timestamps:** removed timestamp-only rejection. A timestamp now rejects only alongside diagnostic context (`failed` / `failure` / `error` / `root cause` / `exception`). `The service launched at 2026-08-05T03:00:00Z with the new collector.` is retained and covered by the record → store-load → rank lifecycle test.
- **P1 credential templates:** the assignment matcher now captures the value and skips placeholders and scheme-only instructions (`<your-key>`, `${…}`, `{{…}}`, `your-…`, `redacted`, `…`, `Authorization: Bearer`). Concrete values such as `password=hunter2secret` still reject.
- **P2 `Rule:` marker:** the trailing word boundary now applies only to word-ended alternatives, so `Rule: when exit code 1 occurs, rerun the collector` reaches the durable-intent carve-out.
- **Data compatibility:** no schema or store-shape change. This revision retains strictly more existing entries (templates, timestamped facts, `Rule:` guidance); the lifecycle regression proves a timestamped fact survives write, reopen, and rank.
- **Verification:** `pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/short-term-promotion.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 101 passed. oxlint 0 warnings, oxfmt clean, `tsc -p extensions/memory-core/tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean (tsgo is blocked on this host by the prebuilt `tsrs` GLIBC requirement).
- **Remaining gap:** no live CLI apply/reopen against a production-state copy in this environment; the earlier preview trace in the body still covers the changed predicate, and call-site wiring is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(workers): recover interrupted stops without a Gateway restart
prs.body:
Related: #188796

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a cloud worker can remain stuck stopping until the Gateway restarts when Stop is interrupted before its final workspace-save claim is recorded.

## User Impact

User impact: background recovery can finish saving and releasing the same worker without a Gateway restart. Offline workers retain their final-save obligation until reconnection; recovery never replays input or allocates a replacement. Existing claims, moves, and replaced attachments remain protected. No configuration or schema changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Runtime sweeps previously skipped draining placements without a claim. Enroll those placements through the existing guarded workspace-recovery owner, then let normal pending-result recovery finish the save. Proven worker loss still records that unresolved changes are unverified.

This adapts the interrupted-drain portion of S4 to current main: `retainDrainingWorkspace` already owns the donor's proposed enrollment helper, so no second helper or recovery path is introduced. Retained-disk changes and provider-outage containment are deliberately excluded.

## Evidence

- CI attribution: the [exact-head test-line check](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41141200382/job/124356088673) fails with 6,314,125 lines against a 6,313,100-line ceiling (1,025 excess). Read-only counting of its main parent `3111c36da03ae2932fffbac605628cbc5b66d525` gives 6,314,049/6,313,024 (1,025 excess). This PR adds 76 test lines and exactly 76 allocated lines, preserving the inherited debt; no shared baseline was raised. The aggregate CI gate is therefore not green.

- Regression reproduced on base `563ba501dced074d9d282fb3a4cb48cfc31bcf9e`: no pending final-save claim after a runtime sweep; proven worker loss remained draining.
- Corrected recovery suite: 37 tests passed, including actual temporary-file apply through the real placement/pending-result owners, offline retry, unchanged claim ownership, stale/replaced attachments, no replay/allocation, and proven-loss reporting. File wall time: 65.23 seconds (67.57 seconds including wrapper); native-worker compilation dominates the cold run. CI seconds are not yet available.
- Final combined recovery, admission, Move, and targeted-recovery suites: **80/80 tests passed across 4 files** in 96.96 seconds (99.53 seconds including wrapper).
- Scoped typecheck, two-file lint, and three-file formatting passed in a task-isolated rootless container with frozen dependencies and normal supply-chain gates; `git diff --check` also passed. Provider/tunnel I/O is fixture-backed; no live cloud-provider or model run was performed.
- Fresh independent P0–P3 review found two test-fixture issues, both corrected. Local autoreview (Codex/GPT-6.1 Sol, P0–P3) reviewed the complete final local snapshot against the pinned base with the unchanged ownership contracts supplied: `scoped-clean`, no findings. Reviewed commit `53c250e17f5feabda51186b0731547c5796556bd` and managed publication head `96b6dd8017c43d3171b46bae82ffb5f94aabd46d` have identical trees; the latter adds publication attribution only. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable; [the hosted review is already queued](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188805#issuecomment-6535207498), so no duplicate request was posted.
- Simplification: reuse the current enrollment and pending-result owners; no new state, schema, replay logic, or provider machinery. Delta: production +21/−2; tests +92/−16 (net +76, separately allocated for these regressions); documentation +1/−1.

Contributor credit: adapted from Galin Iliev's S4 source commit `9501dfaa8de7426a02badffd918e8eddc75c9e27` at his request.

prs.title: chore: update mature dependencies without breaking compatibility
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw misses maintained dependency releases because several eligible upgrades fail existing build, approval, or native-artifact contracts.

## User Impact

Refresh compatible provider, browser, discovery, native, mail/media, and tooling dependencies without silently changing approval, desktop-permission, or telemetry behavior. No configuration migration is required. Native platform CI and the deliberate holds below remain explicit; this is not a vulnerability-free-graph claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

Fixed audit: **2026-10-30T15:45:38Z**. Inclusive publication cutoff: **2026-10-23T15:45:38Z**, including introduced transitives. Preserve inherited newer pins, existing exceptions, and supported contracts; no unapproved identity/edge downgrade.

The refresh covers direct npm, Cargo, Ruby, Swift, and tooling dependencies plus two targeted security transitives. Five candidate updates were deferred during CI repair (details below). Already-open Dependabot Action updates are not duplicated.

Eight updates needed deeper qualification: tsdown 0.23.2, Muse 1.4.12, CUA 0.37, Chrome MCP 1.12, Lobster 2026.10.1, Crabline 0.1.31, body-parser 2.4, and ctutils 0.4.4.

- Rolldown changed region labels to module-ID comments. Share the small reader across consumers while preserving real-comment/source-and-symbol provenance, ambiguity rejection, and all-mappings-before-write.
- Handle Muse's new approval-feedback error while retaining deny, interrupt, failure, and terminal cleanup.
- Refresh verified CUA native admission hashes with the SDK; preserve permissions and routing.
- Forwardport the three existing Chrome renderer/session, Lobster AOT-validator, and Crabline static-codec contracts instead of dropping patches. Patch count and behavior remain unchanged.

### Highlighted upstream changes

- **OpenAI 7.39 → 7.43:** Realtime large-message/reconnect and lifecycle fixes, plus reduced long-log processing work. Breaking-minor Decisions types were checked against actual consumers. [7.40](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/releases/tag/v7.40.0), [7.42](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/releases/tag/v7.42.0), [7.43](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/releases/tag/v7.43.0).
- **Google GenAI 2.30 → 2.31:** consistent mid-stream SSE/drop errors and additive Live-context/function-result support. [Notes](https://github.com/googleapis/js-genai/releases/tag/v2.31.0).
- **Anthropic 0.135 → 0.137; Vertex 0.21 → 0.22:** unknown-SSE-event passthrough, tool-definition compatibility, sensitive-header and literal-replacement fixes without the 1.x authentication migration. [0.136](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/releases/tag/sdk-v0.136.0), [0.137](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript/releases/tag/sdk-v0.137.0).
- **CUA 0.36 → 0.37:** target-focus, untitled-X11-window, sibling-menu refusal, and recovery-hint fixes. SDK and native artifacts were qualified together; no live desktop-control proof is claimed. [Notes](https://github.com/trycua/cua/releases/tag/cua-driver-rs-v0.37.0).
- **Chrome MCP 1.12:** upstream snapshot timeout/filtering, frame waits, and Lighthouse improvements with the existing ownership repair retained. Real Chromium/OOPIF and packaged stdio flows qualify the port.
- **Native runtime/discovery:** mdns-sd 0.21.6 fixes browse/resolve backpressure deadlocks and multicast retries; Tokio 1.54.1 and Tauri patches address I/O, timers, and Linux runtime errors. [mdns-sd](https://crates.io/crates/mdns-sd/0.21.6), [Tokio](https://github.com/tokio-rs/tokio/pull/8692), [Tauri opener](https://github.com/tauri-apps/plugins-workspace/pull/3565).
- **Compatible parsing/security transitives:** fast-uri 4.2.3, body-parser 2.4.0, ctutils 0.4.4, without a new override.

These are upstream claims unless consumer proof below demonstrates an OpenClaw effect; updating an SDK does not expose every new upstream feature automatically.

## Evidence

The following qualification was supplied by the dependency-updater loop before current-main reconciliation; the merge-head proof is recorded separately below.

- Full `pnpm build`, updater bridges, bundled assets, SDK declarations, Control UI, core/extension typechecks, targeted lint/format/budget checks: passed.
- Red/green updater-provenance and Muse approval-lifecycle regressions; installed wrapper/AOT/packaging, real isolated Chromium, CUA artifact/client/result, and actual HTTP middleware consumers: passed.
- Frozen pnpm/independent npm installs and native Cargo/Swift locked resolution; Ruby frozen installs and actual consumer imports: passed.
- Rust workspace 148 tests, Watch engine 13, Go readonly tests/build/vet/module verification, Fastlane 17, Swift protocol 7, Python skills 27: passed. Replays/duplicate shard summaries are not added to a grand total.
- Correct application-lock document, introduced publication dates, package identities and dependency edges audited. No age violation or unapproved downgrade; Cargo/Ruby/standalone npm audits also pass. No new override, freshness exception, public peer floor, or patch behavior.
- Independent local review covered the initial checkpoint and complete compatibility/port delta, scoped-clean P0–P2. All 114 final source hashes match reviewed bytes.

### Known gaps and deliberate holds

- Workflow guards: **186 passed, one inherited serial UI-inventory mismatch**, reproduced on the exact baseline. No unrelated assertion was relaxed; aggregate is not green.
- Native Apple/GTK/Windows application proof remains for platform CI. This host lacks desktop development libraries; locked metadata/protocol tests are not app-build proof.
- Chrome initial attachment can have empty loader IDs: old-UID reuse after recapture fails on both prior patched 1.11 and this 1.12 port. No weakened guard or forced reload.
- **Copilot stays 1.0.25:** 1.0.26 removes pre-create/pre-resume restrictions while native remote export/steering remains. No supported equivalent deny contract was established.
- **Coordinated migrations held:** Anthropic/Vertex 1.x changes authentication/API/request contracts; OTel 3 lacks a compatible Jaeger propagator; MXC 1.x replaces the consumed sandbox API/wire contract.
- Convex broker needs a supported credential-store review route. Exact Mailauth/Crabline pins retain older undici/nodemailer/re2js rows; MSAL 7 is outside the current Azure identity range. No blanket security override or vulnerability-free claim.

Requested and guided by @steipete.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @steipete](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/f22d8bdb-5b30-435f-b808-30f9c6f82102)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/7a0f5292-9b46-4ec0-b706-282f1ae3df96)

## Worked on by

- @steipete

<!-- openclaw-publication:a4dba18f-2922-4233-8711-a7cb0346b59e -->

## Maintainer reconciliation

Merged main `4e0c02b8fec276c628f2bfac67169b44d7dda2de` into the PR without rebasing or force-pushing. Merge commit: `b5f8583e022f7803bca62cb8730e9c9de661cbeb`. First published merge candidate: `64d05f8a8ed2ce94e71d1cd8a39806ee52bd64e7`. Subsequent CI repair is recorded below.

The sole textual conflict was `extensions/cua-computer/src/driver-artifacts-resolution.test.ts`. The resolution retains main's Linux registration/no-diagnostic-report coverage. Follow-up source history inspection showed main intentionally retired the old static artifact assertion in `79f0434c4379`; the final resolution follows main and removes that obsolete assertion. The bumped admitted native-artifact record remains in production metadata. No product behavior or permission decision was required. Package and lockfile changes merged cleanly; `pnpm install --lockfile-only` and the canonical gateway validator generator confirmed the merged outputs without manual lockfile/generated-code edits.

The loop's reviewed repair is retained. Deferred updates: npm 12.2.1 (retain 12.2.0), oxlint 1.89.0 (retain 1.88.0), tauri-plugin-deep-link 2.6.2 (retain 2.6.1), and tauri-plugin-single-instance 2.5.4 (retain 2.5.3). The maintainer additionally defers `@tanstack/virtual-core` 3.19.7, retaining 3.19.2: the changed viewport measurement contract breaks 16 existing Logs unit cases. See the single-bump counterfactual below.

Supply-chain policy is unchanged: no new override or release-age exception. The only newly introduced npm identities are `@acemir/cssom` via LinkeDOM, `@pierre/highlights` via Pierre Diffs, and `marked-cjk-friendly` via pi-tui; all belong to intended bumps. The frozen install's supply-chain verification passed for 1,749 entries. Existing patch contracts remain registered under the bumped versions.

Local proof on the first published merge candidate (reused where inputs remain unchanged):

- `pnpm install --lockfile-only` and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`: passed.
- `pnpm deps:npm-lock:check:changed --base origin/main --jobs 2`: passed, 110 package scopes.
- `pnpm tsgo` and `pnpm tsgo:ui`: passed.
- `pnpm gateway:validators:gen`: passed, no further generated changes.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/gateway-protocol/src extensions/cua-computer/src/driver-artifacts-resolution.test.ts extensions/muse/harness.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 746 protocol tests passed (37.50s), 51 CUA/Muse tests passed and four Linux-only cases skipped on macOS (101.40s including initial worker compilation).
- Focused UI model-picker/helper consumers through `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config ui/vitest.config.ts ... --maxWorkers=1`: eight files, 68 tests passed (11.50s).
- `pnpm build`: passed in 6m 54.3s, including plugin packaging, declarations, and Control UI. No `INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT` diagnostic.
- The interim CUA isolation follow-up passed its focused replay and review; its obsolete static assertion was subsequently removed to follow main. This historical replay is not additional final-tree coverage.
- Resolved CUA test formatting and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Codex autoreview against main `4e0c02b8fec2`, including the complete candidate and conflict resolution: P0–P2 scoped-clean, two completed passes, no accepted/actionable findings. This reviews repository evidence, not upstream artifact contents. The reconciliation adds no production machinery.

Cargo is unavailable on this maintainer host; the existing Cargo lockfile merged unchanged, and no hand-edited regeneration is claimed. Native application build coverage remains with exact-head platform CI.

### Inherited local lint failures

CI-engine core lint was run with `OPENCLAW_LINT_TOOL=oxlint node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mts --only=core --split-core --threads=2`. It completed with 12 `eslint(max-lines)` errors and no other errors. These files, the lint configuration, wrapper, and oxlint 1.88.0 pin are unchanged from merged main `4e0c02b8fec2`.

An isolated checkout of that main revision reproduces all 12 identical error signatures using the same oxlint binary and main configuration through the supported focused syntax-rule mode (`node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --openclaw-focused-config --config .oxlintrc.json <the 12 failed files> --threads=2`). This isolates the static line-count rule from the bumped type-aware peer. A normal type-aware baseline replay also reproduced the first five identified failures. The baseline uses the prepared task toolchain, not a separate frozen-main dependency installation. No limits or assertions were relaxed.

- `src/agents/sessions/session-manager.ts`: 705 / 700
- `src/agents/sessions/session-manager-core.ts`: 701 / 700
- `src/infra/sqlite-database-admission-record.ts`: 701 / 700
- `src/gateway/worker-environments/workspace-quiescence-scripts.ts`: 715 / 700

- `ui/src/components/solid/menu-runtime.ts`: 704 / 700
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-lifecycle.ts`: 702 / 700
- `ui/src/pages/new-session/draft-place-state.ts`: 707 / 700
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-sidebar-region.runtime.tsx`: 703 / 700
- `ui/src/app/bootstrap.ts`: 701 / 700
- `ui/src/pages/activity/activity-page.test.ts`: 1229 / 1000

Extension CI-engine lint also completed using `OPENCLAW_LINT_TOOL=oxlint node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mts --only=extensions --threads=2`. Its only errors are three inherited `eslint(max-lines)` violations. All three files match main byte-for-byte, and a focused static-rule replay of the exact main blobs under the unchanged main configuration reproduced identical signatures:

- `extensions/anthropic/cli.runtime.ts`: 710 / 700.
- `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/index.test.ts`: 1,028 / 1,000.
- `extensions/oc-path/src/cli.test.ts`: 1,004 / 1,000.

These 15 local static-lint failures remain failed evidence. They are unrelated to the dependency refresh; no rule, source limit, or assertion was weakened. All requested local commands completed. These local failures are retained honestly; exact-head CI results are recorded below.

### CI repair after the main merge

Initial exact-head CI run [41131309941](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41131309941), attempt 1, completed failed. No job was rerun. The 16 failures in `logs-page.test.tsx` and `view.test.tsx` reproduce locally with virtual-core 3.19.7. Its viewport observer now reads client dimensions; the existing Logs fixture supplies offset dimensions. Current main with its own frozen install passes the same 20 cases.

Retaining only virtual-core 3.19.2, with every other dependency bump unchanged, makes those cases pass. The corresponding model-picker geometry-fixture adaptation is also removed. The combined Logs and model-picker consumer replay passes 10 files / 88 tests. No production UI compatibility shim or test assertion relaxation was added. Browser replay of the initial dependency tree already passed all six composer/provider-picker and Logs scrolling scenarios, so this is a failed qualification hold, not a claim of a reproduced browser regression.

Removing the obsolete CUA assertion and restoring the helper removes 30 lines relative to the first published candidate. Net test growth is the existing justified 154-line allocation; `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 4e0c02b8fec276c628f2bfac67169b44d7dda2de --no-merge-base` passes with four lines of slack. No ceiling or allocation was raised. The pnpm lockfile was regenerated with `pnpm install --lockfile-only`; the frozen install and UI typecheck passed again.

The retained virtual-core tree also passes all six real Chromium/WebKit composition and scrolling scenarios (104.54s including a fresh production UI bundle), `pnpm tsgo:ui`, formatting, and `git diff --check`.

Current main `4d2a9f8bb4c47da0daae7fd820cab33fa450ef7b` independently has 1,042 test lines above its effective ceiling (6,313,400 / 6,312,358); its self-base ratchet reports net delta zero. Any corresponding debt in a newer CI merge tree remains inherited evidence, not a reason to raise this PR's allocation. The replacement exact-head CI result and failure attribution are recorded below.

Repair head: `b75a0934ac266583ea4147423b170f835b20ddbd`. Fresh Codex autoreview of the four-file repair is P0–P2 scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable findings; the pin, importer, package identity/integrity, and snapshot agree and no transitive package or release-age policy was added. The initial full candidate review remains the review of the rest of the refresh.

### Completed replacement CI

Exact head `b75a0934ac266583ea4147423b170f835b20ddbd`, [CI 41135782996](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41135782996), attempt 1, completed with 182 terminal jobs: six failed root jobs and the failed aggregate. No job was rerun. The actual CI checkout is merge `118c02c01601c11a224cdce1a80b087bec3baea6`, with ordered parents main `00bfbf1f7ca54b0da62a10cc0d33323f3559dc02` and the exact PR head. The retained Git object and independently reconstructed merge tree agree. `security-fast` passed.

| Failed check | Observed failure and qualification |
| --- | --- |
| `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` | Only test-lines: total 6,313,554 / ceiling 6,312,512; debt 1,042, net +154. Frozen main has exactly the same 1,042 debt; this PR adds 154 lines and 154 credit. No baseline is raised. |
| `checks-node-changed-19` | Terminal-empty expects `error` but gets `ok`; cloud P6 cannot stage `undici`. Both exact signatures reproduce against frozen main `4d2a9f8bb4c47da0daae7fd820cab33fa450ef7b` with its own install and built runtime. |

| `android-access-native (16384, google_apis_ps16k)` | Four platform-root TLS cases fail after Android kills fixture-mounted zygote 538 at 22:13:04.825Z and replaces it with 2869 at 22:13:05.331Z. The app starts at 22:21:57.539Z, after the injected trust namespace is gone. Pin cases pass; cleanup confirms old PID missing and destroys emulator/AVD. Test/app/Gradle/trust-script inputs are unchanged; Android's sole PR delta is the unused Ruby lock. This is an emulator fixture lifecycle failure outside the changed dependency graph, with logcat, namespace, and JUnit evidence in [artifact 13016783879](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41135782996/artifacts/13016783879). |

The failing state is identical: top 22,468; height 89,316; viewport 378; rows 485–501 of 2,000; 16 reads; no page errors. Chromium mobile and WebKit desktop pass. The previous Signal timeout passes both the final PR file replay (5 cases) and the frozen-main original group (46 cases); restart passes both frozen-main scenarios. The replacement CI does not fail either check. The final npm-lock recheck also passes all 110 scopes. No passing replay is represented as a fix to the earlier failed run.

All six failed root jobs have concrete baseline or infrastructure attribution. Native preparation and the protected inherited-failure landing completed: squash [`70134e42285b4214579faba8ac10ed7098550643`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/70134e42285b4214579faba8ac10ed7098550643) is verified on `origin/main`. No CI job was rerun, no baseline was raised, and no assertion was relaxed. The exact-main workspace control used Node 24.22.1 to launch the repository-pinned Bun runtime, the owning gateway-server config, and `--maxWorkers=2`; only `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.workspace-policy.test.ts` ran. The final Linux UI comparison used Node 24.22.1, the CI four-worker cap and 16 GiB memory limit, and both CI exclusions. prs.body:
Bumps the swift-deps group with 1 update in the /apps/macos directory: [github.com/openclaw/peekaboo](https://github.com/openclaw/Peekaboo). Updates `github.com/openclaw/peekaboo` from 4.9.6 to 4.9.7
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/openclaw/peekaboo's releases.

v4.9.7

4.9.7 - 2026-10-23

Highlights: Report window close through the daemon as closed when an app keeps the closed window alive; let see observe Chrome windows whose titles carry the app name or are elided; close apps that re-exec themselves with --foreground; and keep the Mac chat, menu bar and Inspector accurate.

  • Report window close through the daemon or Bridge as closed when the app keeps the closed NSWindow alive, instead of exiting 1 with an indeterminate postcondition: the Bridge readback now applies the same exact-window Accessibility presence check as the in-process path. Thanks @​goutamadwant! #1131, fixes #1129.
  • Let peekaboo see observe Chrome and other apps whose Accessibility window title appends the application name or whose WindowServer title is middle-elided, instead of failing with "inconsistent response evidence: window-context window title". Thanks @​L1uYun! #1130.
  • Close windows of apps that re-exec themselves with window close --foreground, whose frontmost PID AppKit reports as -1. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1124.
  • Classify Dock separators and the Trash from their Accessibility subroles, so peekaboo dock list hides separators unless --include-all is passed, reports included separators as separator instead of blank unknown items, and identifies a localized Trash (such as "Papierkorb") as trash. #1120.
  • Use the Mac app's saved Vision model for image analysis even when its provider does not report vision support (OpenRouter, OpenAI-compatible, LM Studio and many Ollama models), surfacing the provider's error instead of silently switching models. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1127.
  • Keep the Mac chat's streaming answer together when you queue a follow-up, and keep Retry on the prompt that failed. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1126.
  • Show a failed Mac agent tool as failed, not completed, in the menu bar, while cancelled tools stay cancelled. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1134.
  • Highlight the Inspector control in the front window under the pointer, including floating panels and popup items past their window, instead of the smallest control anywhere on screen; windows of untracked apps such as the Dock now stop the hover from reaching what they cover. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1133.
  • Place Inspector highlight boxes on the correct display when a display does not start at the primary display's origin. Thanks @​SebTardif! #1132.
  • Restore source builds after the pinned MCP Swift SDK commit became unreachable upstream when its pull request branch was rebased. #1135.
  • Remove the unused public DialogError.inputSuppressedUnderTests case from PeekabooAutomationKit along with the dead test-only dialog typing hook that threw it; release builds could never throw it, so only SwiftPM consumers that switch over every DialogError case need to drop that branch. #1123.

prs.title: fix(tlon): add opt-in to keep citations inside their source channel [AI]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Adds an opt-in restriction for Tlon citation expansion: an admitted sender can otherwise cite a post from another channel the bot ship can read, including one the sender cannot read, and add that text to the agent context. This is source-channel hardening beyond #186092; it preserves the default and does not implement per-sender membership filtering or claim complete remediation of GHSA-3pp8-23cm-2xc2. Advisory reassessment is deferred.

## User Impact

Operators can set `channels.tlon.crossChannelCitations: false` (or the same key per account) to keep citations inside the conversation they came from. A citation then expands only when it points at the channel the message was posted in. Citations in non-owner DMs and group DMs stay as opaque references. The owner's verified 1:1 DMs keep expanding citations from any channel the bot ship can read.

The default (`true`) keeps today's behavior, so nothing changes unless an operator opts in. Operators who opt in lose cross-channel citation previews for everyone except the owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bot reads cited posts with its own ship session, and Urbit does not check whether the citing sender could read them. Channel rules decide who can trigger the bot, not which posts a sender can pull into context. A same-channel citation is safe because the sender posted in that channel and can already read it.

`contextVisibility` does not cover this case. `allowlist_quote` keeps explicit quotes from any sender, and Tlon citations are explicit quotes. `allowlist` filters by the quoted author against the current channel's allowlist, which admits everyone in an open channel. The question here is which channel the quoted post came from, not who wrote it.

The citation scope check moves into `cites.ts` as `isCitedNestInScope`, and the monitor binds the source channel for each channel message. DMs bind no source channel, so with the setting off only the owner exemption expands citations there. Sender admission still happens before any citation is fetched.

Config surface: this adds two channel config entries (`crossChannelCitations` and `accounts.*.crossChannelCitations`), so the generated channel config budget increases by two entries. One boolean is the smallest surface for an opt-in that reuses the existing scope check.

Builds on #186092 (merged), which provides the explicit channel scope, the owner-DM exemption, and the pre-request scope recheck. Since `main` now includes it, this diff contains only the setting.

This pull request was prepared with AI assistance.

## Evidence

Current candidate: `d0ab83f05b46bfb970ee908559882398004b312e` (tree `96746d0bacb3f2f11128489bacfdf8d79758ad68`), incorporating captured main `4368b276f5a35ccd34770d11b83a6d57d471ea2b`. The three merge conflicts were the test-line scalar and two generated config-doc baselines. Canonical generators produced both config-doc resolutions. All Tlon production/test/docs/config-metadata blobs remain byte-identical to the independently reviewed and live-proven source. The final delta is 10 files, +81/-12. Auto-merge is disabled; merging is reserved to the maintainer.

Main's #188780 restored test-code headroom while the preceding candidate was in CI. This refresh therefore removes the earlier PR scalar adjustment and retains main's `6,320,000` scalar and all existing allocations unchanged. The measured combined tree has 6,313,723 test lines against the inherited 6,345,721 ceiling (31,998 slack); this PR still adds 26 regression-test lines and adds no budget credit.

[Current candidate proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_908f4ac9d86a85d08a2a19f559dd388c), secretless AWS Crabbox `cbx_79ac438b09fd`, exited 0: canonical channel/config-doc generation and checks, test-line ratchet, `git diff --cached --check`, and all 47 focused Tlon tests passed across four files. The fresh published source plus captured main and the exact conflict resolutions produced tree `96746d0bacb3f2f11128489bacfdf8d79758ad68`, identical to the native signed candidate. [Exact-head GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41143563331) passed, including baseline ratchets, generated metadata, typechecks, lint, changed-code tests and the changed-extensions bundle. The required `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency-review and security-sensitive-review statuses also passed in [final security reconciliation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41144349387). The earlier live observations and limitations below remain unchanged.

Fresh independent local ClawSweeper committed-range review of exact final head `d0ab83f05b46bfb970ee908559882398004b312e` against `4368b276f5a35ccd34770d11b83a6d57d471ea2b` completed 2026-10-30 23:14 UTC, covering all 10 paths without truncation. No actionable correctness/security findings; high confidence (0.91). It independently decoded the generated metadata and confirmed only the new root/account boolean fields and UI hints. This was source inspection; runtime validation is the separate passing AWS run above.

Independent local ClawSweeper committed-range review of the preceding candidate `9b8614a5cd09cb439ec0091ee90c22f648e50798` covered all 11 then-changed paths against captured main `2c157ed06dff5032da1093cbb6745efeff2b6f33`: no actionable correctness/security findings, high confidence (0.9). It independently decoded the generated metadata and counted test lines. That candidate's [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41140734022) and required CI/security status gates passed before main advanced and introduced these baseline conflicts. The final refresh changes only baseline integration and generated resolutions; unchanged Tlon source review and live proof are reused, not described as new current-head proof. Exact final-delta inspection confirms main's scalar is unchanged and config-doc counts differ only by the two Tlon channel entries.

Previously reviewed candidate: `86b2bbb8a85d7c0157b4020d4077240e9fcffe58` (tree `ed5a5b74b28ef279db1aeffd865e554a49c354cc`). Its native baseline refresh incorporates captured main `4d2a9f8bb4c47da0daae7fd820cab33fa450ef7b`; all Tlon production/test/docs/config-metadata blobs remain identical to the independently reviewed and live-proven `f39e60e92e18ee9ae498438cd9c505f6d1773127`. Both generator checks, `git diff --check`, and all 47 focused tests passed again on that exact tree in [refresh proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_40cccb5e9daa63d1db0649ebf9ae35a8). Prior-head live/build/static results below are reused evidence and are not claimed as current-head whole-Gateway proof. Captured main `73cd9bdd33b36a825d3a33a27200e894aa7928e0` was merged to repair the two generated config-baseline conflicts. Canonical generators produced the resolutions; the maintainer repair adds no product logic and preserves current-main reply threading. Independent ClawSweeper source review found no actionable correctness/security findings.

- All 47 focused Tlon tests and canonical generator checks passed on the candidate-equivalent tree: [focused proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_1e382f1cc29b8b28f1ef65f15092b719).
- Full `pnpm build` passed in [build run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_9385b61fbdf423ee3d52b779c2a658fb). Scoped production/test typechecks, six-file lint, and changed-file formatting passed in [static-check run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_e03b2149d563f79d13696a73ed0e3a83). Those overall runs failed later on separate initial typecheck/privacy-fixture setup steps; they are not described as green runs. Setup was corrected without source changes. `git diff --check` passed.
- Live proof ran secretlessly on AWS Crabbox `cbx_e05c6948740f` using three actual Vere v4.5 test ships, the production isolated Gateway and Tlon plugin, and real Ollama `qwen3:0.6b` inference. The sender belongs to the source group and cannot read the secret target group: its authenticated target-post read returned HTTP 404. [Fixture verification](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_0378737f73ecfd1f31fe3ea423b99a33).

| Actual live case | Cited-post reads | Cited sentinel in actual model request | Actual Urbit reply |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cross-channel, option omitted | 1 | Private sentinel present | Received |
| Cross-channel, `true` | 1 | Private sentinel present | Received |
| Cross-channel, `false` | 0 | Private sentinel absent | Received; private sentinel absent |
| Same-channel, `false` | 1 | Source sentinel present | Model selected `NO_REPLY` |
| Verified owner 1:1 DM, `false` | 1 | Private sentinel present | Received |

The first four observations are from [live matrix run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_ca7d0cf95c9ee420ea7d88f55a50e043); the owner control passed in [owner-DM run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_a9cd4fe7e516f976826b74d4cba6f378). Transparent observation proxies forwarded real Urbit/model requests and responses; ingress, agent dispatch, backend, and model responses were not mocked.

**Investigated failure retained:** the live matrix exited nonzero because the same-channel model response was `NO_REPLY`, despite correct citation fetch/context delivery. An [earlier attempt](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_2728a4993fc37666c760c67d892b38ee) also completed inference with `NO_REPLY`; a direct same-model control returned `ACK`. Fresh state and explicit test-bot instructions produced the three cross-channel replies above, while same-channel silence remained. No product repair is claimed for model silence, and a passing replay is not treated as a fix. General reply reliability of this small model remains unqualified.

Limits: real Urbit software ran deterministic test identities on an isolated fake Ames network; this is not hosted/mainnet qualification. Live proof uses auto-discovery enabled. Both discovery modes, non-owner/group DMs, forged-owner and scope/revocation controls have focused/synthetic coverage. Omitted/true proves private text reached model context; the model did not emit that sentinel in its replies, so this does not claim generated-reply exfiltration. Final-head GitHub CI/security gates passed as linked above; the original green CI below is historical prior-head evidence.

## Historical contributor evidence

The evidence and proof pack below describe the original incoming head and its then-known live-proof gap; they are preserved for provenance. The maintainer validation above adds actual Urbit/Gateway/model observations.


- New monitor test in `index.thread-mentions.test.ts` runs with `crossChannelCitations: false` under both auto-discovery modes:
  - A citation of the source channel expands, and its text reaches the agent input.
  - Citations of another listed channel, an unlisted Notebook, and a citation in a non-owner DM make no post request.
  - The owner's 1:1 DM citation of an unlisted Notebook still expands.
- Red check: with the monitor ignoring the setting, the new test fails because the listed other-channel citation is fetched (`/channels/v4/chat/~zod/announcements/posts/post/12345.json`).
- After merging `main` (which includes #186092), the four changed Tlon test files pass 47 tests. Per file with one worker on the earlier head: `cites.test.ts` 6 passed in 83.4 s wall (cold compile), `index.thread-mentions.test.ts` 20 passed in 24.4 s, `index.club-sender.test.ts` 15 passed in 25.2 s, `settings-helpers.test.ts` 5 passed in 5.1 s.
- `pnpm check:changed --base origin/main`: 41 of 42 lanes passed, including changed-file formatting, core and extension typechecks (production and tests), changed-file lint, the line-cap growth ratchet, bundled channel config metadata, and the config docs baseline. The dead-export scan failed only on exports in files this PR does not touch, inherited from `main`.
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base origin/main` passed (6,270,606 lines against a ceiling of 6,326,488), so no allocation record is needed. `git diff --check` passed.
- Exact-head CI: `openclaw/ci-gate` and the changed-extensions bundle passed.
- Known gaps: no live Urbit ship was used, and the agent's generated reply was not exercised. The Behavior Proof below runs the production monitor and real Urbit client against a local synthetic endpoint.

<!-- behavior-proof-pack-section:start -->
## Behavior Proof

Mandatory behavior proof for current head `8ddfcddb5f96d5163795dee00bb0ce4daa52daca`

<!-- behavior-proof-pack-v2 sha256=df118ffe989a17d11e37d2402c205e9e029944a307c37d0293f4f01e2136594d -->

Sourced from github.com/blaizzy/mlx-audio-swift's releases.

v0.1.7

What's Changed

  • VoxtralRealtime streaming encoder: write KV rows into preallocated storage by @​T0mSIlver in Blaizzy/mlx-audio-swift#272
  • Nemotron streaming: compute only new mel frames; keep MLX's buffer cache between steps by @​T0mSIlver in Blaizzy/mlx-audio-swift#274

  • Irodori-TTS: add v4.1 and v4.1-MF (MeanFlow) support by @​jonpol01 in Blaizzy/mlx-audio-swift#284
  • Fix partial model downloads returning as valid from the HF cache by @​lucasnewman in Blaizzy/mlx-audio-swift#291
  • Nemotron streaming: reuse decoder and encoder work that has not changed by @​T0mSIlver in Blaizzy/mlx-audio-swift#275
  • Build against mlx-swift main (#469): Parakeet and Qwen3-TTS compile calls by @​T0mSIlver in Blaizzy/mlx-audio-swift#292

prs.title: docs(gateway): clarify HTTP check gaps during lifecycle transitions
prs.body:
Related: #187171

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway supervisors can mistake expected HTTP-check gaps during startup, shutdown, or in-process restart for a wedged process.

## User Impact

Operators get an explicit contract for connection refusal before bind and after transport closure, including while the same PID remains alive. Combine HTTP checks with process/exit information, bounded startup/restart grace, and the process owner's shutdown budget; a living PID does not justify indefinite grace. No runtime or configuration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

This implements the documentation alternative explicitly offered in #187171 and recommended by [its review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/187171#issuecomment-6485949796): define pre-bind/post-close refusal windows and bounded supervisor grace. The documentation change is complete for that scope. It does not promise continuous HTTP availability or change listener ownership; any such runtime contract remains a separate maintainer decision.

The checks share the Gateway HTTP transport. The later listening summary is not the bind timestamp. Existing projection-startup guidance and endpoint semantics are preserved: health 200 means HTTP liveness, startup remains 503 while starting or draining, and startup 200 is not readiness. Traffic still uses readiness and normal admission. No universal numeric timeout is prescribed.

## Evidence

Source inspection at candidate base `00bfbf1f7ca54b0da62a10cc0d33323f3559dc02` confirms transport ownership, bind/close order, same-process restart, endpoint semantics, and delayed startup logging.

Isolated Debian 12 Bookworm / Node 24.22.1 measurements compared actual npm **2026.10.5** (`1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8`) with source-built main **2026.10.9** (`d3c0ab1fc65a0dc0350a2f661835b05e2ea0c0f2`). Matched stop-run fixture launches on 2026-10-30 UTC were **21:52:18.732Z** (release) and **21:52:10.654Z** (main).

| Observation, seconds after fixture launch | Release | Main at d3c0ab1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Socket bind observation interval | 4.637–4.657 | 4.357–4.377 |
| First completed HTTP responses: health 200 / startup 503 / ready 503 | 5.072 / 5.075 / 5.074 | 4.418 / 4.419 / 4.418 |
| Later `http server listening` summary | 5.306 | 5.688 |
| First completed startup 200 / ready 200 | 5.836 / 5.836 | 6.376 / 6.417 |
| Transport close interval / process exit (code 0) | 7.545–7.565 / 8.124 | 7.505–7.526 / 7.710 |

Kernel socket sampling was 20 ms and HTTP probe sampling 50 ms; intervals are observations, not exact syscall timestamps, and completed HTTP responses are distinct from socket binding. Config-reload runs also retained the same PID across no-LISTEN gaps bounded at **3.031–3.070 s** (release) and **2.647–2.687 s** (main), then rebound with startup/readiness 503 before 200. These runs establish lifecycle gaps, not an entire-boot outage.

Limits: this was a Debian 12 sandbox, not an exact digest-pinned `node:24-bookworm` reproduction. Production 60-second startup durations, restart loops, and systemd active/running behavior were not reproduced. Main timings apply only to `d3c0ab1`, not newer main. No runtime proof was rerun for this prose-only change.

- Exact-byte oxfmt 0.74.0 and one-file MDX checks passed on Node 24.22.1. Structural/link sanity and `git diff --check` also passed. Document SHA-256: `826f9e56a77190372b9dfeb5ff727b23008c5ca6c388bb6134b9a4c520a11713`; relevant checker/configuration inputs matched the candidate base. Full Markdown lint/global docs checks were not run locally.
- Current-head [check-docs CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41141141644/job/124355685869). This is a specific docs-check result, not a claim that every CI lane ran or passed.
- Independent review approved the exact candidate. The full `pr-simplify` pass required no further edits: documentation **+15/-0**, production code **0**, tests **0**; no machinery was added or removed.

Thanks to Donnie Fi for the investigation and direction.

🦞 Made with [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai)

## Worked on by

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin manifest integration tests repeatedly start npm to prepare a registry fixture.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

Pack the override-reload fixture's 12 registry packages in two native npm invocations instead of 12. Keep versions separate because npm 12 keys pack JSON by package name.
