All 52 cases and their native pack/unpack, npm lock/ci/install, retry, integrity, runtime-export, state-probe, rollback and cleanup contracts remain. Registry listeners remain ephemeral loopback servers settled in `finally`. No production code, mocks, timeout, repetition, or cache-policy changes.

## Evidence

- Three successful base runs and three successful runs of the final candidate, each 52/52 cases. The override-reload case median falls from 3.534s to 1.921s (45.6%).

One complete-source pass included the intact target, manifest/runtime/lock owners, npm runner/JSON helper, state probes, temp/server helpers and sibling consumers. Reviewed source snapshot is identical to this commit.
- Net test LF: **−1** (1502 → 1501); production LOC: **0**. Native tracked-test LF: 6,308,023 → 6,308,022. Scalar: 6,287,502 → 6,287,501; unchanged grants: 20,553; effective cap: 6,308,055 → 6,308,054. Inherited slack remains **32**. No new grants or allocations.

The earlier applicability hold is resolved by the parent’s explicit review of the upstream SHA1 normalizer, one current integrated proof run, and a fresh complete-source isolated P0–P2 review. Approved original head `e9e40b8aea8bec7c381cf77834bd95bf1c6669ce` was mechanically rebased once onto captured main `4e0c02b8fec276c628f2bfac67169b44d7dda2de` only for the actual scalar conflict. No extra cuts or funding. All original 3+3 timings and failed attempts remain historical original-base evidence; this functional qualification is not a new timing/CI-speed claim.

The existing PR branch received one exact leased update after proof and fresh review. Exact reviewed head `e086aa1dc0c879dd3622ae74030f0bc433828736` **merged** at `9f05fe6db582389fda0ebfed767fb9e20476e504` on 2026-10-30T21:09:41Z. prs.title: perf(doctor): batch first transcript header reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Doctor checks the first transcript event separately for every session, even when every session already has a valid header. Group the minimum sequence per session in one read per database, stream and parse the complete first events, and retain only candidate session IDs before opening any repair writer.

Full JSON parsing preserves last-duplicate-key semantics, nonzero minimum sequences, malformed-first skipping and pre-compression schemas. Corrupt compressed payloads remain isolated to their session. Positive repairs still read their full exact snapshot and use the existing maintenance authority, identity, backup, transaction and snapshot guards. No schema, cache, generation or receipt change.

## Acceptance rule (registered before measurement)

Flow: the compiled Doctor invoked by `runPackageUpdateDoctor`, with an adopted native update executor, original recovery capture and stopped database backup. Workload: generated four-agent, 4,096-session state of at least 1 GiB; independent fresh fixture copies for baseline and candidate, same macOS/arm64 host and Node runtime. Filesystem cache is warm from generation/copy; this is not a cold-disk claim.

Primary acceptance is work counts: clean first-header detection falls from 4,100 SQL statements to four across four databases, with no additional worker requests or runtime Gateway-main SQL. Compare whole Doctor and attributed header-owner SQL/requests/MAIN. One matched baseline/candidate count/profile pair is required by the lane order. Verify the frozen observer and collect CPU profiles per process/thread. Any timing claim requires the timing lock, load1 below 24, at least five alternating samples per variant, and median/p95/spread with cold and warm separate. A 20% adverse cell stops the change. Loaded-host diagnostic timings are not a latency or CPU speedup claim.

Behavior acceptance: same candidate identities and repair results, byte-preserving original backup, unchanged malformed/corrupt-row handling, no cursor across repair writes, and normal compiled-finalizer completion and receipts. Peak process RSS will be observed alongside counts; it is not additive across threads or simultaneous process peaks.

## Evidence

The production-path regression is red on the unmodified reader (two transcript reads instead of one) and green with grouping. Reader, header-repair and unchanged label suites pass all 23 tests. Cases cover nonzero sequence starts, duplicate JSON keys, malformed first events, legacy schemas, corrupt compressed payloads, exact snapshots and recovery copies, timestamp changes, duplicate event identities, and logical workspace selection. Test consolidation retains these behaviors with net zero test-source lines.

The generated 4,096-session fixture returns identical first rows through the grouped and original readers. SQLite uses the existing covering `(session_id, seq)` index plus keyed payload lookups, with no temporary B-tree or sorter. Underlying payload retrieval still occurs once per session; the removed work is statement/native-call overhead and separate enumeration.

Two isolated Codex reviews, a delta-only review of the test placement correction, and a CI-forced delta review of the final ordering correction are scoped-clean. The change adds 57 production lines and one RSS diagnostic line, and has zero net test-source growth; the extra code replaces per-session lookups with a portable streaming selection at the existing reader owner. Required PR CI, all three actual PostgreSQL shards, and the published-driver update cell have passed at `8969d086ab1d35869edd810ad53768fab95e8990` ([PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41141353923), [main-tier qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41141354446)). No latency or CPU speedup is claimed.

Indexed open-PR overlap proof compares the base and candidate against #188397 at `f243711f0384`, #187268 at `f03a5086ef0a0`, and #158723 at `69dc6bf27a16`. No new conflict paths or blocks: 0→0, 1,853→1,853, and 32→32 conflicted paths respectively. The prior indexed #188397 head `eda006e04e97` also had 0→0 conflicts. All nine existing test-conflict regions are unchanged. The existing scanner-versus-inline-loop production conflict in #158723 gains only the selector line (20→21 current-side lines, unchanged boundaries and 118-line peer side); retaining the existing shared scanner requires no additional resolution choice.

## Matched compiled Doctor evidence

One matched, warm-filesystem 1 GiB count/profile pair on macOS/arm64, Node 26.12.1: base `cf83a69f74eed57a3467bba3963d433e25d20743` versus production code at `c3b4e6ef408e2c9f7d719b05e32873f5e3d41efd`. Both use the same `sourcePerformance` build profile. The measured candidate runtime was built from the production sources at `c3b4e6ef`; that head differed from its predecessor only in tests. Canonical build-info was regenerated for that measured head. The later final-head `toSorted` correction is described below and was not included in this runtime measurement. Frozen observer verification: 37/37 hashes.

Command: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/doctor-config-measure.mts run --repo <built-repo> --fixture <fresh-synthetic-copy> --output <fresh-output> --observer-root <frozen-v3.1.5> --profile`, serialized through the campaign proof slot. Each independent fixture has 4,096 sessions, 1,408 messages and 1,087,377,408 database bytes. Both real compiled finalizers completed with accepted exit/receipts, six stopped backup records and no backup warning. Both original recovery captures had the same one existing plugin backup-inventory warning.

| Work per Doctor pass | Base | Candidate | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| First-header detection SQL | 4,100 | 4 | −4,096 |
| Whole Doctor SQL | 50,922 | 46,826 | −4,096 |
| CLI-main SQL | 50,279 | 46,183 | −4,096 |
| Worker SQL | 643 | 643 | 0 |
| Worker requests | 251 | 251 | 0 |

The exact changes are 4,096 `ORDER BY seq LIMIT 1` statements removed, four header session-ID enumeration queries removed, and four grouped statements added. Label enumeration is retained. All other SQL shapes and all original-capture, backup, parent-startup and receipt-verification phase counts are identical. This exercises the update finalizer, not a complete launchctl outage or Gateway turn; no Gateway-runtime measurement is claimed. No work moved to another thread.

Timing qualification failed: load1 was 32.46 and 24.44 (required below 24), and this is one count/profile pair, not five alternating timing samples. Diagnostic only: Doctor process elapsed 70.647→75.941 s; main-thread OS CPU 24.351→25.439 s; observed process-tree CPU 80.803→84.426 s; Doctor-process peak RSS 1,181,904→1,254,368 KiB. No cell increased 20%; these values do not establish latency, CPU or memory improvement. Median/p95/spread are not claimed from one ineligible pair. Native Node profiles cover 104 of 171 observed Doctor-tree threads in each run; missing worker exits make total CPU incomplete. The one invalid baseline Inspector profile belongs to the parent harness, outside the Doctor tree; all native profiles validate.

PostgreSQL semantic approval is recorded for exact final head `8969d086ab1d35869edd810ad53768fab95e8990`. The final one-line correction uses `toSorted` instead of `sort` with the same UTF-8 comparator to satisfy `unicorn/no-array-sort`; it changes neither the SQL nor the ordering result. The final reader suite passes 6/6 tests, basic lint/format pass, and its isolated CI-delta review is scoped-clean. The matched compiled measurement above remains evidence for its named earlier head; it is not relabeled as a final-head runtime measurement. Final-head compiled integration is covered by CI and the published-driver update cell. Local type-aware lint could not start because the mandated external checkout/internal virtual store violates declaration custody; exact-head CI supplies type-aware/static proof, without a local guard bypass.

Static baseline attribution: the earlier candidate check-dependencies failure reports only `src/gateway/plugin-node-capability.ts: prepareClientPluginNodeCapabilities`. Scheduled main [run 41138060956](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41138060956/job/124345653643) reports the identical unused-export failure. That owner is untouched. Final-head qualification job [124356495499](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41141354446/job/124356495499) repeats exactly that failure. Perf-driver unused-file, script-export and full-tree export scans passed; all five final-head type-aware core lint shards passed. No static failure caused by this PR is being waived.

Broader nonrequired qualification also reports the untouched Talk browser-disconnect case (`cancels a public provider that resolves after its browser disconnects without creating a chat`, cancellation spy zero versus one), [job 124356496165](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41141354446/job/124356496165). The selected scheduled-main large-15 shard passed, so this is disclosed without claiming a matching inherited failure. Required PR CI is green.

Final-head required PR CI: [41141353923](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41141353923) succeeded. Actual PostgreSQL shards [1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41141354446/job/124356494034), [2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41141354446/job/124356494138), and [3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41141354446/job/124356494082), plus the [published-driver update](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41141354446/job/124362517425), all succeeded. Source contracts, architecture, test/type ratchets and type-aware lint passed.

Additional broad-qualification failures are the untouched CLI group-help test (exit 2 versus 0, [job 124356501255](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41141354446/job/124356501255)) and the test runner retaining a temporary namespace because nested-writer completion was unverified ([jobs 124356496321](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41141354446/job/124356496321) and [124356496359](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41141354446/job/124356496359)). prs.title: improve(agents): cover ask_user answer settlement through the production wrapper (#174994)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Adds regression coverage for an `ask_user` answer arriving while its run is blocked, followed by the run persisting its tool result. Related: #174994.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. This PR changes one test file; production code is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The previous test constructed answer custody manually, so it could pass when the production wrapper lost its recorder. It now enters `withPreparedEmbeddedRunToolAuthority`, creates the real tool inside that scope, and claims the answer through a separate ingress scope. An unrelated subsequent user turn must still refuse settlement without changing the transcript.

Cleanup closes the question manager and releases the settlement gate before awaiting the run. A failed answer claim now reports the original assertion instead of waiting for the question timeout.

## Evidence

Validated source at `5d7c8fc5251f2ba497c126671dcbc3a5334a10bf` (test SHA256 `62453132e2cae21f7419c44df2654652dca35aae168d93e33f359ebf14335280`), Node `26.8.2`, frozen lockfile dependencies:

- The final two-file command exited `0`: 16 passed, 0 failed (8 settlement tests and 8 answer-custody tests), 2 completed shards in `151.07s`; outer elapsed time `153.28s`.
- [Hosted changed-test CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39319597457/job/118290501512) passed all 8 settlement tests with shard exit `0`; [boundary CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39319597457/job/118290501578) passed 134 tests in 11 files. These jobs executed merge `6dde34edbd3ef776471e29e94b8dbe37f8c6e972`, combining this head with base `7a1f8b2e5cb341cb0dc15348e535d572cbf60c81`. The local 16-test result above is on the PR head directly.
- The `core-test-agents-sessions` typecheck shard exited `0` in `158.1s`. Focused format, lint, and `git diff --check` exited `0`.
- A fresh scoped review found no actionable P0-P2 findings. That review inspected source; the test results above come from separate execution.
- The six pre-existing timeout/answer x own-before/own-in-flight/foreign cases are byte-identical to `519800ec34033d05f0bc41aa023058cd7ba8d6f9`. Their block SHA256 is `3690416796815808cb5c29eb69d1de1b6975da05a683cce0f5e56cde3cc87688`.

| Temporary control | Original test at `519800ec34033d05f0bc41aa023058cd7ba8d6f9` | Updated test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Replace the production wrapper's `attempt.userTurnTranscriptRecorder` argument with `undefined` | Exit `0`, 1 passed / 6 skipped | Exit `1`, 1 failed / 7 skipped; `SqliteTranscriptMutationConflictError` reaches the success assertion |
| Omit the production wrapper's `admitTranscriptAnswer` callback | Not run | Exit `1`, 1 failed / 7 skipped; same intended conflict assertion |
| Claim `agent:main:no-question` instead of the waiting session | Exit `1`; instrumented trace prints `refused claim reached false`, then times out at `30000ms` | Exit `1`, 1 failed / 7 skipped; `expected false to be true` at the claim assertion, no timeout |

All temporary edits were restored before the final positive run. The new `unrelated-user` case independently expects refusal and compares the entire transcript before and after attempted settlement.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/sessions/session-manager-ask-user-settlement.test.ts \
  src/config/sessions/session-accessor.question-answer-transcript.test.ts \
  --maxWorkers=1 --pool=forks
node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs \
  --ci-graphs-json '["core-test-agents-sessions"]'
```

For each temporary production mutation in the table, run the first file with `--testNamePattern 'production owner: answer'`. For the original test, restore that file from `519800ec34033d05f0bc41aa023058cd7ba8d6f9` and use `--testNamePattern 'answer settlement survives'`. The refused-claim control changes only `sessionKey` in `claimPendingAgentQuestionAnswer`; the original control also prints `claimed` before its assertion and uses `--testTimeout 30000`, while the updated control uses `--testTimeout 10000`.

The sibling suite opens a temporary loopback server. A sandbox-denied run failed on `listen EPERM: operation not permitted 127.0.0.1` before its assertions; the reported final result is the rerun with that fixture access. An earlier passing touched-suite run used `/usr/bin/time`, whose own sandboxed `sysctl` failed; its outer exit was `1`, so it is excluded from the passing command result above.

</details>

The tests above prove the in-process production owner, question claim, worker persistence and transcript fence. The shipped Gateway/TUI run below exercises the product entry points separately. Neither reproduces the historical Telegram incident.

### Shipped Gateway and TUI proof, October 19

Built and ran exact head `5d7c8fc5251f2ba497c126671dcbc3a5334a10bf`, tree `7250820b79bc3948dce396bf5354e2b8b6b06369`, on Linux x86_64 with Node `26.8.2` and pnpm `12.11.1`. The source archive SHA256 was `61a47f2c49ea6ecfbaf1ea100e16142851765f80e1171a1f9fabe60289f3d8ee`; lockfile SHA256 was `3df67ddf1ecb545432d017683909200a1b9c823d8dbb84232cf751be9c9132ff`. Tracked source remained unchanged after the build and proof.

`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` exited `0` in `16.204s`. The canonical build, `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime`, exited `0` in `92.895s`. Both used four CPUs and nice level 10. The built `dist/entry.js` SHA256 was `a96040cdbdbabcd0a6205a63dd0a8292c4c0646f85b7dcbdc74f7f685af2197a`.

The proof used fresh temporary HOME, config and state, a loopback-only Gateway, the shipped TUI and the repository's local OpenAI-compatible mock server. The fixture set the documented [`tools.toolSearch: false`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5d7c8fc5251f2ba497c126671dcbc3a5334a10bf/docs/tools/tool-search.md) option so the model received the direct `ask_user` schema. It used synthetic credentials and normal TUI Owner-profile admission, with no profile injection or production imports in the harness.

The first scripted model response requested `ask_user` with “Which target?”, options `Staging` and `Production`. The TUI displayed the real pending question. A three-second negative control observed exactly one provider request and no continuation. Escape collapsed the overlay without resolving the question; typing `Staging` and Return into the ordinary composer sent the answer through `chat.send`. The second provider request contained the real successful `ask_user` result with `Staging`.

The final proof exited `0` in `19.235s`. It explicitly waited for the TUI's terminal idle state after the continuation and before sending any cleanup signal. The persisted continuation also has `stopReason: "stop"`.

<details>
<summary>Terminal output from the final shipped proof</summary>

Selected contiguous output from the final harness run, before the cleanup summary. Full log SHA256: `d8f13344b7b74c2fcb33f6c5da4ba39f630d006af0e0c4651ec57e632a30ea1a`.

```text
PASS: Shipped TUI displays the real pending ask_user prompt
PASS: Exactly one model request reached the waiting question
PASS: Real ask_user schema was advertised to the model
PASS: Negative control: no model continuation during 3 seconds before answer
PASS: Shipped TUI shows the model continuation after ordinary Staging ingress
PASS: Shipped TUI reaches terminal idle after the continuation, before any cleanup signal
PASS: Exactly two model requests: ask_user and continuation
PASS: Continuation model request received the real ask_user Staging tool result
PASS: Persisted transcript captured without read or decompression errors
PASS: Persisted initial input, ask_user call, Staging input, tool result, and continuation each occur once
PASS: All proof transcript events belong to one session
PASS: Persisted ordering: initial input < ask_user call < Staging input < toolResult < continuation
PASS: Real ask_user toolResult parent is the persisted Staging user entry
PASS: Original ask_user call, settled toolResult, and continuation retain the same nonempty runId
PASS: Persisted same-run continuation has successful terminal stop reason
PASS: Persisted ask_user result succeeds with Staging
```

</details>

| Persisted event | Sequence | Run ID |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Initial TUI user input | 1 | Initial request idempotency key uses the run below |
| Real `ask_user` call | 4 | `8dfad649-2efd-4581-8126-1ee7079ea350` |
| Ordinary TUI user answer `Staging` | 5 | Separate inbound message |
| Successful `ask_user` tool result | 6 | `8dfad649-2efd-4581-8126-1ee7079ea350` |
| Assistant continuation, terminal `stop` | 8 | `8dfad649-2efd-4581-8126-1ee7079ea350` |

All five entries belong to session `99f1f8f0-494f-4817-b260-28d2c4e7a600` and occur once. The tool result's `parentId` equals the persisted answer entry ID, `95d2bf20-20fa-4f12-9fe8-4d6b4e39072e`. Both user entries record `openclaw-tui` / `ui` transport. Exactly two provider requests occurred. The continuation marker was `PR176070_SAME_RUN_CONTINUED`. Transcript extraction and identity/order assertions completed without read or decompression errors.

Reproduction entry points, with every process given the same isolated config and state:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts qaRuntime
# Start scripts/e2e/mock-openai-server.mjs on 127.0.0.1 with two scripted responses:
# an ask_user function call, then the continuation text.
node openclaw.mjs gateway run --port <private-port> --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured
node openclaw.mjs tui --session agent:main:pr176070-proof \
  --message 'Run the synthetic question proof.'
# Wait for the real question; verify no continuation before answering.
# Escape, then Staging + Return in the composer; wait for terminal idle.
```

The Python PTY harness SHA256 is `6276d2c392f8a7c092be85700992f2f1761dbb4ecab8bd293d880912e3f2ad85`. It launches these shipped commands, captures both model requests and terminal output, then reads only its own stopped synthetic database to assert the transcript witness above. Gateway and TUI exited `0`; the mock received planned SIGTERM. No forced kill or live descendant remained, both ports closed, and temporary runtime state was removed.

Earlier attempts are excluded from this passing result: the first omitted the direct-tool fixture option and received `Tool ask_user not found`; the second used a short-lived `gateway call` client and received `Session-scoped access requires a verified user profile`. The final proof uses the genuine shipped TUI and its normal admission path. An earlier TUI run already recorded the correct transcript; the final run adds the explicit pre-cleanup idle assertion. No live service or external model was used, and no Telegram transport was tested.

### Hosted CI and review

[CI run 39319597457](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39319597457), attempt 1, completed successfully: all 48 jobs terminal, 17 successful and 31 skipped. It is attached to the current head and executed merge `6dde34edbd3ef776471e29e94b8dbe37f8c6e972` into base `7a1f8b2e5cb341cb0dc15348e535d572cbf60c81`; the private build/proof above used the PR head directly.

The [previous exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176070#issuecomment-6245913703) found no actionable source findings and requested this shipped proof. Both addressed review threads are now resolved. This evidence update requests a fresh assessment of the proof; it does not assert maintainer approval or authorise a merge.

prs.title: fix(gateway): finish config save responses before restart
prs.body:
Related: #120408. The non-restart config response work from #129321 is already on main.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes config.patch/config.apply restart writes losing their success response during auth rotation, and an unfinished response preventing forced restart after the deferral deadline.

## User Impact

Restart-required writes acknowledge restart admission before the initiating connection closes. An unfinished response shares the existing bounded restart deferral; at the deadline, forced restart can proceed. Clients should reconnect and use config.get to confirm the running configuration. No migration or new configuration option is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed reloader now carries response settlement with the existing write receipt and counts it as pending work in the native restart coordinator. It does not await that response inside restart preparation, so the existing forced deadline remains effective. Superseded requests preserve outstanding responses, and stopping cancels the deferred restart. Auth revocation and successor-readiness checks retain their existing owners.

Integrated main at 72330e21dbf53dab4457014881a5e8cbcdd8d35a, resolved conflicts against the current reloader/dispatcher contracts, and removed superseded polling/test-support changes. Extracted the existing receipt lifecycle helpers to satisfy the source growth guard.

## Evidence

Pushed head: 0962faa2cbc70ac6d4ddf56d85f27566aedf58a3. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39363548855) is running; no merge or auto-merge was requested.

- Before: both stalled-response regressions fail against the unbounded preparation wait: no restart emission at 300,000 ms.
- After: 333 focused tests pass across nine suites. The fake-clock regressions verify forced emission at the deadline, ordinary response ordering, supersession, and cancellation. Real loopback WebSocket tests cover both config methods with simultaneous auth rotation.
- Final-source reruns: all six changed test files pass; the reloader's 133 tests pass after extraction. Unchanged-input restart infrastructure and reload-handler proof was retained.
- Built runtime profile qaRuntime passes (78.9 seconds). Through pnpm openclaw, both config.patch and config.apply with gateway.controlUi.basePath changes plus token rotation receive success before auth closure and production restart emission; the successor reaches ready and authenticated config.get confirms the final configuration. Temporary Gateway state/processes were cleaned up.
- Formatting, scoped lint (zero warnings/errors), core typecheck, whitespace, line-growth, and timeout-race guards pass. Independent full-candidate review and extraction-delta review are scoped-clean for P0-P2.
- Verification gap: an earlier isolated port-change probe acknowledged and restarted correctly, but the in-process CLI successor retained the original listener port; new-port reconnection failed. Port relocation is not claimed fixed by this PR.
- Full check:changed is not green: three UI max-lines suppressions and core test-shard root budgets (gateway-root 725; plugins-platform 726; cap 720) reproduce on clean pinned main. No baseline/suppression exceptions were added. The broad typegraph continuation was stopped after core and Gateway graphs passed; full PR CI remains separate evidence.

<details>
<summary>Changed-test cost measurements</summary>

Each file was run with pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=dot. Wall time includes runner/compiler setup; these are local measurements, not CI seconds.

| Test file | Tests passed | Wall seconds |

prs.title: fix(telegram): state the current message body inside the Current-message carrier block
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The separate "Current message:" carrier block on a Telegram quoted reply contains a bare `#<msg_id>:` header without the current body. The inline projection is completed later by its prompt joiner; the fragment-based carrier is sent separately and needs its own body.

This fixes the carrier projection. The reported `NO_REPLY` and re-asking behavior is a historical observation, not an established current-head causal result or a guarantee about the model's answer.

## User Impact

The carrier includes the canonical current body, preferring `agentText`, then `BodyForAgent`, then `Body`, with existing transcript sanitization. Bodyless turns retain the bare header; turns without a message ID can still state the body.

The inline projection retains main's bare header, so CLI consumers join the complete body once. Non-Telegram turns and sessions using the older text-based carrier remain unchanged.

## Implementation

`projectTelegramCurrentMessageCarrier` applies only to the conversation-data fragment in `get-reply-run-context.ts`. The current-message and shared text helpers are extracted from `inbound-meta.ts`. The inline formatter retains main's behavior.

Published head: `3a87c8e741af073a2edc7de25e9f998810fe78a7`. It merges main `2e7668b2eaad12171ef4421b68286de6063b7e77` into `3b4178085051d729816a2ffc259b349c8871fe17`. The single conflict was in `inbound-meta.ts`. Its resolution retains main's reply-chain/history rendering, active-goal refresh, requester context and prompt selection.

Fresh independent review covered the complete six-file diff, +299/-87, at tree `d38c500269203d8bf8a9da0a13669e6675fc7e6c` and found no new correctness issue. The published tree matches that reviewed tree exactly. The helpers remain identical to the preceding PR head; the caller's reset, room-event and runtime-instruction paths remain intact.

## Evidence

Exact-head CI on `3a87c8e741af` ran both changed test files in [checks-node-changed-3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40122253803/job/120956437056):

- `src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.current-message.test.ts`: 4 passed (4), the four `projectTelegramCurrentMessageCarrier` cases.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/prompt-prelude.test.ts`: 12 passed (12), including `states a quoted Telegram body exactly once in the CLI inline prompt` and `keeps the complete formatted body in the CLI prompt and the sanitized one in the carrier`.

Every other check on that head passed or was skipped (61 passed, 61 skipped, CodeQL neutral); the only red run was this PR-context check. These are fixture tests, not the live Telegram run listed under remaining gates.

## Validation and remaining gates

- The resolved owner module was formatted with oxfmt; the scoped staged diff passed `git diff --cached upstream/main --check`.
- No local runtime tests were run for this merge; the planned focused run was held because of host resource pressure. The current-head results are the CI runs above. Earlier test results do not validate this head.
- The diff retains four carrier regression cases in `inbound-meta.current-message.test.ts` and two CLI composition cases in `prompt-prelude.test.ts`. The CLI cases use reply preparation and the inline renderer, checking that the full body appears once while the carrier contains the sanitized body.
- Still required: a real Telegram quoted reply through an embedded session that consumes the fragments, with the populated carrier, final provider request and answer correlated to the same turn. No live capture or current-head provider result is claimed here.

The CLI duplicate-body review is addressed and its thread resolved. Earlier claims of repeated delivery and re-drive storms are withdrawn: this PR changes prompt projection and makes no message-delivery claim.

prs.title: perf(ci): cut full UI validation tail work
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Full UI CI still took 842 seconds in its slowest job after #188673 and #188685. The explicit full-UI selection path also re-added release-only Gateway compositions after filtering them out, contrary to the policy established in #168105.

## User Impact

Faster UI CI with the same ordinary user-contract tests and unchanged runner, shard, worker, and timeout budgets. Release compositions remain available in full manual/release validation and when their test files change directly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Apply the existing release-only filter to the full Gateway append, qualify seven isolated child-Gateway fixtures for the existing parallel pool, and start measured long files first within that pool. Refresh 40 Gateway timing weights through the native two-independent-run refitter; preserve other timing surfaces, overhead, and prices for changed fixtures.

Move real protocol-mismatch recovery into the existing prebuilt Gateway pool. It shares the built runtime and current UI assets, keeps its incompatible-protocol build and actual rejection/reload/reconnect assertions, and removes the separate runtime preparation from the mocked browser job. No test assertions are deleted. In-process global Gateway fixtures stay serial.

A separate shared-build producer was not selected: each Gateway build contains real runtime/UI preparation, while a new producer adds setup and a dependency barrier. The existing public artifact producer also builds SDK declarations. Sharing the stale-recovery consumer removes a measured redundant preparation without adding a job.

## Evidence

Baseline: [green full UI run 41134985714](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41134985714). Successful target-job samples from scheduled main runs 41123124777 and 41115244650 were also inspected; those workflows were not wholly green. Native file refitting uses successful jobs from 41123124777 and 41134985714 and excludes changed test sources.

| Baseline job | Other setup/teardown | Runtime/UI build or prebuild | Test phase | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Real-Gateway 1 | 62 s | 97 s | 589 s | 748 s |
| Real-Gateway 2 | 61 s | 101 s | 680 s | 842 s |
| Browser 1 | 84 s | 84 s | 560 s | 728 s |

The largest visible individual Gateway cases were quota recovery (53.21 s), guest groups (49.47 s), and quiet automation (46.95 s). They already reuse their Gateway within the suite. Browser 1's boot-boundary suite owns one intentionally ungrouped build across 18 cases; sharing the grouped production bundle would change its import-failure proof.

Round 1's 107.58-minute comparable total excludes the browser-extension job absent from its original comparison; all 12 UI jobs total 112.48 minutes. [Final-head run 41143209305](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41143209305), at `0b3ea9727e86126ed5a5609cbe44a032212f9d9d`, passed the entire workflow and all 12 UI jobs: 85.18 comparable minutes (−20.8%), 90.92 minutes including the extension (−19.2%), and a 580-second maximum (−31.1%, below the 660-second limit). The Gateway pair finishes within 1.1%. Both requested limits are met without new runners, shards, or workers.

| UI job | Round 1 seconds | Round 2 seconds |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Unit 1 | 405 | 357 |
| Unit 2 | 368 | 286 |
| Unit 3 | 323 | 327 |
| Browser 1 | 728 | 580 |
| Browser 2 | 635 | 539 |
| Browser 3 | 537 | 505 |
| Browser 4 | 625 | 536 |
| Browser 5 | 595 | 535 |
| Browser 6 | 649 | 515 |
| Extension | 294 | 344 |
| Real-Gateway 1 | 748 | 463 |
| Real-Gateway 2 | 842 | 468 |

The extension row grew 50 seconds on this sample; that test and its routing are unchanged. Savings are not attributed wholly to this patch: runner setup throughput also improved. Gateway test phases fell 589 → 328 and 680 → 340 seconds, while their builds changed 97 → 105 and 101 → 97 seconds. Their remaining overhead is 30 and 31 seconds. Browser 1 no longer has its separate 84-second production preparation; its remaining test phase fell 560 → 507 seconds, with 73 seconds of other overhead. Browser jobs 1–6 finish within 14.9% overall; their test phases are within 17.6%, so the original approximate 10% balance aim is not fully met, but every job clears the critical-path limit.

The first CI run found three stale ownership-test expectations and positive regression-test LOC against an already-over-budget tree. The follow-up repairs the expectations and consolidates duplicate planner coverage. The two affected files pass 171 tests in 124.92 seconds; ordering passes 8 tests in 2.92 seconds, and tooling typecheck passes. The next head found an intermittent annotation-attachment read timeout and a CLI-help build timeout before Gateway tests. The annotation test now explicitly scrolls its canonical quote into the viewport, matching the existing lazy attachment-admission contract without removing any assertions. Its focused headless replay passes in 19.83 seconds (2.09-second case); independent review is scoped-clean through P2. A single recovery run was requested for the Gateway build timeout. The final fresh CI run above passes every job, including both repairs. No inherited-failure exception is needed.

Local proof: scoped UI and tooling typechecks passed; the three directly coupled planner, ordering, and ownership test files passed (333 tests, 8 pre-existing skips); formatting and diff checks passed. Local E2E was limited to the single annotation test reproduction and fixed replay; its harness built the UI. Independent Codex autoreview of the complete local change against 528b92792ed041366e037d084041369f93d244a7 and subsequent repairs: scoped-clean through P2; no actionable findings. Review is static; CI owns broad runtime proof. No visual behavior changes.

LOC across the 13 touched files: 17,369 → 17,383 (+14); the planner is +2 lines, with the remainder in test/config/docs. Total tracked test lines decrease by 3; no budget allocation or scalar increase. No new production abstraction or dependency.

prs.title: fix(cron): remove memory-core dreaming jobs left behind by its unloaded sidecar
prs.body:
Fixes #156666.

## What Problem This Solves

Turning dreaming off for a third-party memory slot owner unloads Memory Core's sidecar but leaves its canonical promotion job scheduled, including after a Gateway restart.

## User Impact

The Gateway removes that orphaned schedule after an accepted plugin reload and during normal cron startup. Leaving dreaming enabled keeps its job. Authored look-alikes and historical job families remain untouched.

## Why This Change Was Made

This ports Cyb3rb1ade's fix to the current lifecycle rather than reviving the retired heartbeat/system-job reconciler. One private helper reuses the loader's existing sidecar-admission decision and removes only the exact `memory-core:memory-dreaming-promotion` declaration through the existing cron service.

Startup uses the existing cron reconciliation completion owner; reload cleanup runs after accepted configuration/plugin publication and retained-service settlement. Both capture the current configuration, registry and scheduler lifetime, recheck them after inventory, and pass a live commit guard into removal. Missing manifests, memory disabled, and Memory Core owning the slot do not open an inventory for this cleanup. Failed storage operations are reported without undoing accepted configuration.

No SDK exports, config options, schemas, Doctor behavior, history cleanup or public hook fields change. The fresh runtime diff is **+116/−1 lines (117 changed production lines)**, well below 300. Existing test assertions remain, with shared reload-fixture construction consolidated: test files −31 lines and shared test support +30, **−1 combined net test line**.

## Evidence

[Sanitized runtime capture, controls and native-case comparison](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/156667#issuecomment-6535115913).

Built unmodified main `9db820e3174a7e0ea21e57e2b24c04f64a321195` and candidate `8a5ce094ec4ca8f59f09a12c974af446286f8b5d` in secretless Docker on `node:24.22.1`. Used the shipped Gateway, a task-owned memory-kind plugin loaded through its normal manifest/API, authenticated `config.patch`, `plugins.list` and `cron.list`, and explicit isolated profiles/state/config/database paths.

Head `7168c5417ed2e9dfc3d93d074157155cc7c92481` only updates an omitted MCP test consumer of the extended internal constructor and reuses the same shared fixture defaults. All production files are identical to the built candidate above, so the runtime proof is reused. The initial head's `check-test-types-core-1` failure was this missing test input, not an inherited failure; its configuration, registry and logger inputs are now supplied without weakening the constructor contract. The MCP consumer suite passes **9/9**.

Each revision exercised both transitions:

| Operator action | Main | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dreaming on → off by hot reload | Sidecar disabled; canonical job still enabled; PID unchanged | Sidecar disabled; canonical job removed; PID unchanged |
| Dreaming on → off while stopped, then real process restart | Sidecar disabled; same orphan persisted | Sidecar disabled; canonical job removed during startup |

Both dreaming-left-on controls retained the same canonical job ID across an unrelated owner-config reload. Re-enabling after candidate cleanup created a new canonical job. Three disabled authored controls, including same-named and legacy-named look-alikes, retained their IDs across both transitions. No direct cleanup-helper invocation or manual job deletion was used in the runtime proof.

Focused checks: **132 passed / 1 failed** across five lifecycle/consumer files. The new accepted-metadata cases for on, off and superseded-at-commit all pass. Replaying those cases against main gives **1 failure / 2 passes**: main fails to remove the canonical job in the off case. Formatting and changed-file lint pass.

The one local failure is the existing `server-reload-handlers.test.ts` case “keeps a supervised on-exit child alive exactly once across lazy cron reload”: `service child cleanup identity lost: native owner closed without kernel descendant extinction`. The identical case and error reproduce on unmodified main in the same container. That cron-only reload uses mocked reconciliation and does not enter the new plugin-reload cleanup branch; no process-supervisor code changes are included.

The proof driver allowed up to five minutes for real cold Gateway readiness after an initial cold device-identity admission exceeded its default harness wait. Product readiness, cron timing and lifecycle thresholds were not changed, and all native listening/readiness probes remained required. Proof Gateways and fixture servers stopped after capture.

Merge danger: **one-way for an already-removed scheduled row**—reverting code does not resurrect it; turning dreaming on recreates the managed job through its existing owner. There is no stored-format migration. Blast radius is canonical Memory Core dreaming schedules left without their third-party-owner sidecar; other schedules and historical rows are not selected.

prs.title: fix(talk): voice confirmations repeat after conversational assent
prs.body:
## Current disposition — superseded

Closing in favor of merged #159697 (`f4f48684aa20b65359832f23a98fb9aa06e5f802`, merged October 11). That repair routes authenticated voice through ordinary text permissions and deletes the extra voice-confirmation policy, including this PR's `client-voice-confirmation.ts` owner and both affected test files. Current main no longer contains those paths.

The earlier isolated behavior evidence below remains historical evidence for the old gate, not proof that this patch belongs on current main. Reintroducing that retired policy merely to improve its assent matcher would conflict with the merged product behavior. No replacement PR or local activation is needed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: voice-assisted work asks for confirmation again when a user confirms with a short conversational reply such as “Okay, yes” instead of bare “yes.”

## User Impact

Users can confirm the pending action in natural speech without repeating an already explicit answer. Each confirmation still authorizes only one matching action; reported, conditional, qualified, and negative replies remain rejected. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Finalized speech often includes conversational padding and punctuation. The matcher now accepts bounded padding around an explicit whole-utterance confirmation and preserves punctuation as word boundaries. Challenge identity, final argument fingerprinting, call/agent scope, expiry, supersession, and one-shot consumption are unchanged.

## Evidence

- 67 tests passed across the confirmation, persisted-transcript, and lifecycle suites on this source branch and separately on an exact 2026.9.7 backport.
- Regression cases include conversational assent, punctuation with and without spaces, the repeated-confirmation utterance, transcript replay rejection, and one-shot consumption.
- Reported, hypothetical, conditional, qualified, and refusal cases remain rejected.
- Scoped lint, formatting, and diff checks passed; independent source review completed.
- A real microphone-to-execution run on the repaired package has not yet been verified. This does not exempt shell or other high-impact tools from confirmation.

Test command: `pnpm test src/talk/client-voice-confirmation.test.ts src/talk/client-voice-confirmation-transcript.test.ts src/talk/client-voice-confirmation-lifecycle.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`

prs.title: fix(discord): codex detach and rebind are lost after a Gateway restart
prs.body:
Fixes #178330. Related to #175379.

## What Problem This Solves

A Discord thread detached with a typed `/codex detach` can become bound again after the Gateway restarts. A typed `/codex bind` that moves a bound thread to a new workspace can also be undone by a restart.

## User impact

Detached threads stay detached, rebinds keep their new workspace, and later binding changes remain durable. A refused write from a retired or revoked runtime no longer disables persistence for its replacement owner, and a refused binding change reports a failure instead of success. A replacement Discord provider that starts after its predecessor retires gets its own thread binding manager, so its bind, idle timeout and detach writes persist. No config change or migration is needed.

A row left behind by an earlier detach is still loaded at startup. That thread needs one more `/codex detach` on this build.

The repair reaches core runtime-owned state stores, so the Telegram, ClickClack and `/codex` caller suites are included below. Matrix's separate no-instance repair is #177372.

## Cause and repair

Discord looked up its plugin runtime in the slot of the plugin instance currently running, and a typed detach starts in the `/codex` instance, where the Discord slot is empty. The write threw `Discord runtime not initialized`, the manager changed memory and disabled persistence for the process, and the command appeared to succeed until restart.

Each Discord manager now retains its creating runtime and passes it into async and synchronous store opens, and session-wide idle timeout, max age and unbind helpers read the same runtime from a private WeakMap through the account registry. Core now checks a runtime-owned synchronous store at open and before all seven mutators, update and deleteIf also after their callback. Already-open handle reads are unchanged.

The state runtime marks its authority refusal with `PLUGIN_STATE_RUNTIME_INACTIVE`, and the worker client preserves it. Discord tells it from a storage failure through the SDK facade it already imports, drops the uncommitted write and leaves persistence on. For a retired runtime, async unbind, bind, detach and the session-wide idle timeout, max age and unbind updates reject with it, send no unbound notification and publish no record. The check runs before every shared-memory publication, including a touch inside the 15 s persist interval and a manager with persistence off or latched off. It opens a data-only V2 handle with no store operation before the operation module source is captured. Synchronous compatibility calls still return null or an empty array, a retired owner's touches resolve null, and a deleted thread still closes its sessions after a refused unbind. Real storage failures still disable persistence and apply the change in memory.

`createThreadBindingManager` used to return the account's cached manager even after its owner retired, so a replacement provider's own bind, idle timeout and detach were refused, and after the old stop removed the adapter nothing recovered until a later acquisition. Now, when the cached manager's runtime is inactive, acquisition checks that the caller's runtime is active, starts the old stop without waiting for it, and registers a new manager that retains the caller's runtime. The old manager's runtime is never reassigned, and its late stop clears the slot and adapter only while it owns them. A live owner's manager is still reused, an inactive caller still gets the typed refusal, and a reference taken while its owner was live stays refused after retirement.

Reviewed through `8f1ef6c97eff`, manager method signatures, account queues and the runtime lookup for managers without a retained runtime are unchanged.

Public SDK semantics change for retired runtimes. New synchronous opens and writes through retained synchronous handles now refuse work, and async binding changes through a retired Discord manager now reject. An October 19 usage query found no resolved references to this member but covered only 2,047 of 2,432 eligible artifacts, so third-party impact is unknown. `createThreadBindingManager`, exported from the Discord runtime API, now also replaces the cached manager of a retired owner, and in that case it throws the typed refusal if the caller's runtime is inactive or missing.

## Evidence

At `6dc75714ca61`, six PR test files passed 207 tests, 15 plugin-state files passed 182 with one skipped, and ten baseline checks passed. My real Discord/model checks at `d1e4495644c5` are in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177691#issuecomment-6505159776. The checks passed, but the full runbook evidence remains inconclusive. Typed detach and rebind persisted across restart. These runs cover only the first half of the authority-chain item. Retirement and replacement writes ran in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177691#issuecomment-6507291299, a scripted driver over the built production modules at `d1e4495644c5` and not a Gateway reload. A checker's revoke run there covers revocation. Other results below ran at earlier heads.

### Tests at `22ea62d`

Head `6dc75714ca61` adds an occupied-claim retirement test and moves `publicationEffect` to the receipt input module atop merge `92232b744436`, reviewed through `8f1ef6c97eff`. Commit `22ea62d` adds `src/plugins/conversation-binding.discord-handoff.test.ts` with three cases. A live owner's retained manager refuses a candidate's writes after retirement until an explicit acquisition hands off. A replacement started after retirement gets a distinct manager whose bind, idle timeout, touch and detach persist, and the old manager's late stop leaves it registered. An inactive candidate cannot replace a retired owner. All three fail with the two production files from `56cd59f` and pass at `22ea62d`. Wrong versions that borrow the caller's runtime at call time, fall back to memory on the typed refusal, hand off over a live owner, or skip the candidate's activity check each fail one of them.

On a mocked clock, an uncommitted diagnostic found that at `56cd59f`, after the owner retired, the candidate's idle timeout write was refused at five points from +1 s to +1 h. At main `e2da41f` the idle writes, bind, touch and detach all succeeded before the old stop. A probe then stopped the old instance from accepting calls, started the replacement with the old manager unstopped, and ran each operation in the replacement.

| Operation | `56cd59f` production files | `22ea62d` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bind | Refused | Persisted |
| `/session idle` | Refused | Persisted |
| Touch | Null, no write | Row updated |
| `/codex detach` | Refused | Removed |
| After the late old stop | `BINDING_ADAPTER_UNAVAILABLE` | Bind persisted |

At `22ea62d` the 14 Discord binding, listener and manager caller files passed 206 tests and the 7 conversation binding and contract files passed 128. The extensions type check, the core plugin-platform test type check, formatting and typed lint on the three files it changes, and the mock-exports and line-cap ratchets also passed. At `22ea62d`, max-lines, the other ratchets, the SDK exports check, plugin inventory and config documentation were not rerun. At the `56cd59f` production code they passed except max-lines, which flagged three unchanged UI files, and 17 Telegram, ClickClack and `/codex` caller files passed 310 tests.

The 19 retired Discord cases fail at `d5f8321`, and the bound-source and core open cases fail at `ed59bdf`. Real SQLite trigger failures verify the memory fallback. The `/codex detach` command file checks the failure reply and the restored native binding. A 30-cell guard matrix from `95d9afe` through `ed59bdf`, a 45-cell probe and an uncommitted 153-cell probe of earlier heads found no durable difference and were not rerun.

### Prior-head Gateway evidence, not rerun

The earlier local Gateway record used a Discord stand-in and mock model. It compares main `89e77376ccb` with local merge `3a4095bc93d`, the earlier `de7639b` repair. It was not rerun on a later head, and its typed detach reply predates the refusal path above. After detach, stop and a fresh start, main held 1, 1, 1 rows and the old binding returned after restart, while the merge held 0, 0, 0. A typed rebind run kept the new workspace through restart on the merge, not on main.

### Remaining limits

The live runs did not cover a base build, a DM, Always allow or registry retirement, which the scripted driver ran. The full Discord extension project passed at `67b59f2ef60e` and was not rerun after main changed 96 Discord extension files through `8f1ef6c97eff`. #178330 holds its author's pre-fix reproduction on a real Discord bot, which was not rerun on this branch.

The typed detach failure reply and the real store's refusal were measured separately, not together in a Gateway. The reload ordering, with the old instance's calls stopped before the replacement provider starts, was read from source and modeled with an instance that no longer accepts calls. The time from retirement to the replacement's acquisition was not measured, and writes in it are still refused. The handoff for a caller with no runtime has no test. A channel restart inside the same plugin instance after a timed-out stop still shares one manager, so the old task's late stop removes its adapter until the next provider start, as on main. A session-wide call while no manager is registered still uses the ambient runtime lookup, whose failure still turns persistence off, as on main. A session-wide update across two accounts stops at the first refused row without rolling back earlier rows, startup reconciliation does not catch a refused stale unbind, and a refused thread-delete unbind leaves its row for the replacement owner's sweeper.

prs.title: fix: speed up Gateway startup with large state databases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes slow Gateway startup when the shared state database is large, even when no plugin data migration is pending.

## User Impact

Startup migration confirmation reads its small ledger through the existing admitted live reader instead of making two full shared-database backups. No configuration, schema, durability, or offline Doctor behavior changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway-only confirmation caller inherited an artifact-preserving default intended for offline inspection. Ordinary runtime plugin readiness already selects live reads. This change aligns the confirmation caller while retaining the order of pending and deferred reads, lifecycle authority, and transactional generation checks.

Production change: +1 line for shared read options; no new cache or reader. The benchmark additions provide a rerunnable scale fixture and owner measurements.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule, fixed before scaled measurement: native database backups must fall 2→0; owner median wall time, CPU and allocation must improve while migration behavior stays correct. Run serial A/A controls and at least five interleaved baseline/candidate samples. The isolated Gateway fixture uses 46 synthetic plugins, eight agents/10,000 sessions, 12 GiB shared state, 35 GiB agent state, and 62,000 workspace files. Record actual hardware/filesystem and median/p95/spread. Whole-Gateway improvement must be measured separately from owner improvement.

- The new regression fails on the base with exactly two native SQLite backups and passes with zero after the fix.
- Focused readiness, migration-generation, and Gateway startup tests: 55 passed.
- Existing startup-benchmark tests: 46 passed.
- Exactly 19 regression-test lines are allocated to cover the previously untested Gateway confirmation path.
- Codex autoreview: scoped-clean at P0–P2 on the final change.
- `pnpm check:changed` completed after the seed correction: every gate except the inherited production unused export `prepareClientPluginNodeCapabilities` passed. Its source, references, Knip configuration and scanner are identical on base/head. This local failure remains recorded.
- Five interleaved owner pairs completed on a 12,518,367,232-byte synthetic shared database. Median confirmation wall time: **36.395 s → 0.966 s**; process CPU: **21.036 s → 1.555 s**; main-isolate V8 allocation: **30.971 MB → 5.846 MB**; sampled peak RSS: **667.7 MiB → 533.0 MiB**. Every baseline makes two backups (25,036,734,464 bytes); every candidate makes zero. A/A wall controls differ by 2.11%. The full Gateway comparison is complete below; the first lease ended with an incomplete Gateway sample set and is excluded. The granted Linux runner lacks btrfs support; timings use ext4 and cannot establish a btrfs-specific or production outage reduction. No production restart was performed.

The only rebase conflict was an explicit Knip entry made redundant by #188691’s new performance-driver glob; the redundant entry was removed. The measured migration owner and read implementation are byte-identical on the updated base.

CI initially caught a benchmark-only statement type mismatch. The benchmark now narrows its database connection with the existing SQLite guard before using native statement disposal; the targeted script type check and Codex review pass.

## Full Gateway result and memory tradeoff

Five interleaved pairs on the production-shaped synthetic fixture, excluding warmups:

| Metric | Baseline median | Candidate median | Change | Baseline/candidate p95 | Baseline/candidate range |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Gateway ready | 50.803 s | 7.276 s | -85.68% | 54.173 / 7.885 | 50.625–54.173 / 6.299–7.885 |
| Late listening summary | 49.685 s | 6.113 s | -87.70% | 53.050 / 6.538 | 49.565–53.050 / 5.299–6.538 |
| Post-bind plugin phase | 44.173 s | 0.634 s | -98.56% | 47.725 / 0.698 | 43.976–47.725 / 0.565–0.698 |
| Process-tree CPU | 38.000 s | 11.000 s | -71.05% | 41.000 / 12.000 | 38.000–41.000 / 10.000–12.000 |
| Sampled peak Gateway RSS | 1553.281 MiB | 1882.727 MiB | +21.21% | 1581.754 / 1941.738 | 1549.160–1581.754 / 1840.059–1941.738 |
| RSS at actual ready | 1524.100 MiB | 1838.800 MiB | +20.65% | 1546.200 / 1938.400 | 1478.700–1546.200 / 1828.800–1938.400 |
| Main heap used at actual ready | 310.400 MiB | 379.100 MiB | +22.13% | 311.200 / 386.200 | 287.600–311.200 / 378.900–386.200 |
| HTTP bound (trace clock) | 3.995 s | 4.052 s | +1.44% | 4.281 / 4.486 | 3.982–4.281 / 3.509–4.486 |

Readiness improves **6.98×** and CPU drops 71.1%, while median peak RSS rises **329.4 MiB (+21.2%)**. Higher RSS is present at actual readiness, not only teardown. Its cause and steady-state duration are unproven. **Owner accepts +329 MiB transient startup peak RSS for 7× faster readiness; restart time is user-facing outage.**

Removing the long backup wait may let startup allocations overlap and leave less time for garbage collection before readiness; this is a plausible explanation, not a measured cause, and retained/steady-state memory was not measured.

Baseline A/A readiness differs 0.110% and RSS 0.377%. CPU uses whole-second process-tree accounting; sampled peak RSS covers Gateway PID plus worker threads through graceful shutdown. The separate main-isolate heap-profile pair estimates 2.931→2.882 GB cumulative allocation (−1.68%, 32 KiB sampling, n=1 per arm); this does not negate the RSS increase. All 16 runs return healthy/ready, load 46 plugins and shut down cleanly. Linux 4 CPUs/15,789 MiB, Node 26.12.1, ext4; btrfs and actual production restart remain unmeasured.

Current-head CI run 41139753880 passes all selected jobs except the test-line budget and aggregate. The exact CI base already has 1,026 lines of debt; this PR adds 19 regression lines and 19 allocation, keeping debt unchanged. The base is grandfathered at delta 0, while the PR fails the positive-delta rule; this is inherited debt, not an identical baseline failing command. The unchanged guard/baseline inputs and exact native counts are recorded for the authorized inherited-failure route.

prs.title: fix: require approval for dynamic shell predicates
prs.body:
## Summary

Require normal exec approval for predicates whose shell source can expand or be interpreted differently from parsed argv. This narrows the safe-builtin exemption introduced by #79363 and extended to predicates in the later builtin work, while retaining ordinary literal predicate checks. It complements the exact `-v` guard from #180880 and corrects the quote scanner added with the shared authorization planner in #84172.

## What Problem This Solves

### What this Problem Solves

In gateway `exec` allowlist mode, a predicate can appear harmless to `src/infra/exec-safe-builtins.ts` while Bash later synthesizes a different operand and runs an external command. `src/infra/exec-authorization-render.ts` can also miss a glob after an escaped quote in an ANSI-C string. Together, these mismatches can let a model supplied command cross the approval boundary without a matching allowlist entry or operator approval. The classifier now withholds automatic trust from ambiguous predicate source, and the renderer catches that escaped quote form before dispatch.

## What was wrong

1. `src/infra/exec-safe-builtins.ts` checked the parsed `test` or `[` argv for an exact `-v` token. Shell expansion could produce a different operand after that check.
2. `src/infra/exec-authorization-render.ts` treated an escaped single quote inside `$'...'` as the end of an ordinary single-quoted string, hiding a following glob from the enforced renderer.

The combined effect was automatic authorization of a command whose final Bash behavior exceeded the reviewed predicate.

## Why this design

- Grant the safe-builtin exemption only to predicate source with static operand syntax; route ambiguous forms through the existing approval policy.
- Track ANSI-C quoting and escaped quotes in the renderer so a later glob fails closed. Consume each `$$` PID parameter as a pair so the following ordinary single quote keeps Bash semantics.
- Keep literal `test -d` and `[ -d ]` checks, including quoted paths with spaces, on the existing automatic path.
- Use the existing policy modes and configuration surface.

## Why this does not conflict with related PRs

| PR | Governed layer | Relation to this PR |
|---|---|---|
| #79363 | Safe-builtin convenience | Retains automatic handling for static predicates and other closed builtins. |
| #84172 | Shared authorization planning and source scanning | Corrects one ANSI-C quote-state case in that scanner. |
| #119351 | Preserve shell builtin semantics during enforced rendering | Keeps builtins in the shell; changes whether a predicate is automatically trusted. |
| #180880 | Exact parsed `-v` rejection | Preserves that guard and closes the residual source/argv mismatch. |
| #188780 | Shared test-budget headroom | Integrates the already merged upstream repair that unblocks exactly allocated regression growth; this PR adds no separate shared-baseline change. |

These changes are based on `main` after those PRs and change only the predicate trust and renderer checks.

## Evidence of Fix

| Path and mode | Command or probe run | Before fix | After fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shared allowlist, no matching entry | `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs --input-type=module` source probe of the benign ANSI-C quote plus glob regression shape | `analysisOk=true`, `allowlistSatisfied=true`, `safeBuiltins`; new classifier test failed | `allowlistSatisfied=false`; classifier test passes |
| Enforced renderer | Same source probe and renderer regression test | Returned the unchanged command as `ok=true`; new renderer test failed | Returns `shell expansion in enforced arguments` |
| Renderer quote tracking after PID parameters | Real prompt-only plans for `eval git status $$'a\'?v` and the four-dollar variant, with null satisfaction metadata | At PR head `8bca86cd`, the renderer returned `ok=true` for both; the two new rejection cases failed. Ordinary direct `$$` arguments were already blocked upstream as `dynamic-argument` | The renderer rejects both with `shell expansion in enforced arguments`; one- and three-dollar ANSI-C quoted-glob controls remain accepted |
| Gateway allowlist, approval off | Real Gateway E2E command in Testing; benign dynamic `test -e *.txt` plus allowlisted `printf` | Full gateway baseline was not run; the direct evaluator and renderer results above show the prerequisite automatic authorization | Rejects with `exec denied: allowlist miss` before process launch |
| Gateway allowlist, allow-once | Same real Gateway E2E with operator `exec.approval.resolve` RPC | Baseline approved path was not run | Actual process completed with exit code 0 and output `approved` |
| Gateway policy changed while approval was pending | Same real Gateway E2E; operator `exec.approvals.set` changed security to deny before allow-once resolution | Baseline revocation path was not run | Rejects stale approval with `Exec approval changed before execution`; no process result |
| Model-planned agent turn through a separate Gateway process | Deterministic local mock provider sent `chat.send` turns with `test -e proof.txt && pwd` and `test -e *.txt && pwd` under the same real allowlist/off policy; observed the paired `exec` tool outputs | With the original classifier and renderer temporarily restored, the new QA case failed at its dynamic-denial assertion while the static control passed | Static predicate returned the workspace path; dynamic predicate returned `exec denied: allowlist miss` and no `pwd` output |
| Ordinary static predicates | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-safe-builtins.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | Existing literal checks passed | Literal `test` and `[` checks pass, including a quoted path with spaces |
| Published stable policy to patched head | Published `openclaw@2026.10.9` CLI `approvals set --file <synthetic-policy>`; patched `doctor --fix --non-interactive`, `approvals get --json`, then shared evaluator, all in isolated state | Stable CLI stored version-1 allowlist/on-miss policy with one agent allowlist entry | Doctor migration completed; patched CLI and canonical SQLite row retained defaults and allowlist. With that stored policy, `test -d .` remained automatic and `test -e *.txt` required approval |
| Focused suite | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-safe-builtins.test.ts src/infra/exec-authorization-render.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-authorization.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | New classifier and renderer tests failed red before the implementation: 4 failures, 31 passes, 1 skip in the two-file run | 57 passes, 2 skips in the final three-file run, including the upstream arithmetic/assignment regressions |

The real-owner gateway test exercises operator approval RPC and the process supervisor; its approved outcome is observed at the process output, and its denied and policy-changed outcomes stop before execution.

## SDK / caller upgrade contract

Callers using ordinary static predicates keep automatic execution. Predicates with dynamic or ambiguous source syntax require the existing allowlist or approval decision; with approval disabled, they are denied. A policy written by the latest published stable CLI remained readable after the patched runtime's supported doctor migration, with the same defaults and agent allowlist. The classifier and real Gateway boundary tests cover these outcomes.

## Boundary decision

1. **Accepted by repository maintainer `art22s`:** quoted literal filenames containing shell metacharacters, such as `[ -f 'report[v2].txt' ]`, use the existing allowlist/approval authority. With approval disabled and no matching entry, these forms are denied. Retain the current static-source gate; ordinary static predicates and quoted paths containing spaces remain automatic. The explicit decision is [recorded on this PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187884#issuecomment-6535185770).

## Testing

- Added classifier, renderer, and gateway boundary regressions; final focused run after integrating `main`: 57 passed, 2 skipped (10.47 s Vitest). The two new PID-prefixed quote rejection cases failed at the intended renderer assertion before the dollar-pair repair; both pass after it, and ANSI-C quoted-glob controls remain green.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-gateway-approval.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: all 3 tests passed on the final integrated candidate (17.42 s Vitest). The new predicate test uses the real Gateway and approval/process owners with no RPC or process mocks; the existing hook reload test now updates config through the Gateway's managed `config.patch` path to avoid a missed file-watcher event.
- Previously verified at `8bca86cd`, cross-process QA agent-turn E2E: focused case passed after matching each model-planned tool call to its result; the complete QA file passed 10/10 before that final assertion refinement (110.22 s Vitest, 127.03 s wrapper). The local provider is deterministic and does not represent a live model decision.
- Final candidate infra and agents-root TypeScript checks, targeted core oxlint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. The four-file validation wrapper took 338.64 s including a fresh 271.3 s runtime build required after integrating `main`.
- Existing literal predicate tests and gateway authorization integration tests remain green.
- Independent Codex review verified the source and regression contracts; the upstream integration retains every PR-owned blob byte-for-byte. Hosted Clawsweeper reviewed final head `640fd5d1ff47` with no findings or Before merge items, sufficient proof (4/6), and Ready for maintainer review. The quoted-literal authorization decision is explicitly accepted above.
- Test budget: `config/test-lines-allocations/static-predicate-approval.txt` allocates exactly the 221 added LF lines for distinct classifier, renderer, real approval/revocation, and agent-turn contracts; carry this reason into the squash body. Integrated canonical main commit `4368b276f5a3`, which includes the published budget repair [#188780](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188780). The eight PR-owned file blobs remain byte-identical to reviewed head `9f951bd673cf`, and the shared baseline matches canonical main exactly. The staged canonical test-line check now passes: 6,313,918 lines, effective ceiling 6,345,942, slack 32,024. Hosted [CI run 41143275791](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41143275791) completed successfully on `640fd5d1ff47`. The baseline check, aggregate CI gate, and required CI status all pass.
