prs.title: fix(slack): avoid shutdown stalls during Socket Mode retries
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gateway shutdown spending the full metadata-retirement grace period and reporting retained plugin resources when a Slack Socket Mode startup is stopped while retrying its connection URL.

## User Impact

Slack account stop and reload can finish releasing plugin custody instead of leaving an old monitor pending. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SDK clears its reconnect timer on disconnect, but OpenClaw's patched scheduler left the promise behind that timer unresolved. Startup awaited that promise, so the channel monitor never reached its custody-release `finally` block. Settle the pending retry on the SDK's existing disconnect event, and settle retries admitted after stop immediately. Preserve the SDK distinction between fire-and-forget native restarts and awaited URL retrieval; remove the listener when the timer runs normally.

The fix stays in the Slack owner and preserves core retirement checks. Runtime production delta is **+11 lines**, needed for promise settlement and listener cleanup. The regression delta is +38 lines: the installed SDK is exercised with stop before and after retry admission, and the existing native-restart test now checks settlement. A separate test-line allocation records that growth. The rerunnable synthetic benchmark adds 148 tooling lines.

## Evidence

- Both new real-SDK cases fail on the base because startup remains pending. All 26 focused tests pass across `provider.interop.test.ts`, `provider.reconnect-loop.test.ts`, and `provider.ingress-start-cleanup.test.ts`. The original local invocation took 198.90 s; the integrated candidate also passed all 26 tests in 214.41 s (mostly worker compilation). Exact-head CI ran for a 7m54s job span: 31 jobs succeeded, 27 skipped, and the test-line ratchet plus its aggregate gate failed (run 41140725084, attempt 1).
- `pnpm check:changed`: passed before the conflict-only integration (including extension/test/script typechecks, lint, exports, and repository-policy guards). The integration drops a redundant per-script Knip entry now covered by main’s existing performance-script glob; runtime and test changes are identical.
- Independent Codex autoreview of the complete final candidate against `528b92792ed041366e037d084041369f93d244a7`: **scoped-clean through P2**, no accepted/actionable findings. Simplification pass retains one scheduler owner and no new caches or retirement fallback.

The committed probe runs 44 real plugin instances and one real Slack SDK monitor with synthetic API responses through channel custody and cache retirement. Five serial A/B pairs on source base `77869fe2570c` with Node 26.12.1, after A/A controls:

| Owner measurement | Base | Fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Stop + retirement median | 5007.588 ms | 9.282 ms |
| Stop + retirement p95 (maximum, n=5) | 5029.424 ms | 46.861 ms |
| Retirement-only median | 5005.548 ms | 8.816 ms |
| Process CPU median | 33.664 ms | 24.161 ms |
| Retained consumers after grace | 1 in all runs | 0 in all runs |

A/A total timings were 5005.832/5004.519 ms before and 7.567/7.644 ms after. Separate sampled allocations were 2,641,112/2,568,288 bytes. CPU ranges overlap and the host was busy; no CPU or allocation reduction claim. The reliable result is elimination of the five-second wait and retained consumer. Separately, the updated generation owner on main `528b92792ed0` with Node 24.22.1 reproduces the failure at 5033.036 ms; the integrated fix retires cleanly at 7.688 ms with zero consumers. This single pair verifies integration and is not mixed into the earlier distribution.

Reproduce with `node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/slack-shutdown-retirement-measure.ts`; add `--allocations` separately. Timing excludes imports/setup. This owner does no database or workspace I/O, so this is lifecycle proof, not whole-Gateway state-scale performance. The synthetic failure matches the retained-resource signature, but does not establish the exact await point in an earlier production incident.

CI's tested merge `f12e8da20f926dcf74a40ee7e4c291904ff8e21d` used main base `b39e2d09329cc81b09cf55980a2506623236ea59`. Its only test-line delta is +38 LF lines with an equal +38 allocation. The ratchet reports 6,314,087 lines against 6,313,062 credit, an inherited 1,025-line overage. An exact Git-blob census of the CI base finds 6,314,049 test LF lines against 6,313,024 credit: the same 1,025-line debt before this PR. The checker and shared scalar are unchanged, and the PR’s +38 test/+38 allocation pair preserves that debt exactly. The scheduled-main comparison labeled this job new because its older main job passed; this exact-base attribution is stronger than that job-name comparison. The shared baseline remains unchanged. CI is recorded as failed, not green.

prs.title: fix: reduce managed session diff stalls after file stat changes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes long waits for session diffs in large managed worktrees after file timestamps change without content changes.

## User Impact

Managed session diffs avoid repeating a full tracked-content verification pass. Diff contents and user-owned checkout behavior are unchanged; no configuration or migration is needed. This improves a reproduced source of latency, rather than claiming a measured production p99 reduction.

## Why This Change Was Made

Revision validation used `git --no-optional-locks status` for every checkout. On a stat-stale index, status hashes unchanged files but cannot retain the verified stat data, so the following tracked diff reads them again. The existing session owner now carries its persisted managed-worktree fact to revision validation, allowing Git's native optional index refresh only for managed checkouts. Both existing cache identities include this fact. A held index lock still permits a correct read.

Production growth is **18 lines**, carrying ownership across the Gateway/worker/cache boundary instead of removing the protection for user-owned checkouts. Tests grow by **26 lines**, extending the existing handler and index-lock regressions. There is no new application cache. A path-restricted alternative was discarded because it prevented Git's incidental index refresh and made following polls repeatedly expensive.

## Evidence

A reproducible synthetic Linux btrfs fixture contains 62,001 tracked files and 1.1 GB of inventory content. Ten warm rounds alternate baseline A, identical-code A2, and managed refresh, restoring the same stale index before each arm. Timing is untraced; the separate Trace2 run establishes work counts.

| Native status + tracked diff | Baseline A | Baseline A2 | Managed refresh |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Median wall time | 5,999 ms | 6,075 ms | 2,680 ms |
| Wall p95 (nearest-rank, n=10) | 7,082 ms | 14,688 ms | 5,892 ms |
| Wall range | 5,392–7,082 ms | 5,271–14,688 ms | 2,166–5,892 ms |
| Median child CPU | 6,135 ms | 6,212 ms | 2,764 ms |
| Median following status | 24.3 ms | 21.6 ms | 19.9 ms |
| Following-status p95 | 43.6 ms | 74.6 ms | 42.4 ms |
| Trace2 index-refresh entries scanned | 124,002 | 124,002 | 62,001 |

Acceptance: remove the redundant full refresh scan, lower status-plus-diff CPU/latency, preserve output, and avoid a repeatable following-poll regression. Run `python3 scripts/perf/checkout-diff-index-measure.py --root <new-btrfs-directory> --output <new-json> --samples 10`; add `--trace <new-trace>` for work attribution. All response hashes match. Baseline median wall/CPU controls differ by about 1.3%; tail timing remains variable. Initial rounds are retained separately without claiming OS-cache-cold or production percentile evidence.

A preceding five-round traced replay measured status-plus-diff medians 12,202 / 8,769 → 3,115 ms, with material A/A variability. Its following-status p95 was worse (125 / 76 → 149 ms). Inspection attributed the candidate outlier to unchanged preload/directory walking with no index write. That observation prompted the ten-round untraced replay above, which did not reproduce the following-poll regression; the earlier result is retained rather than discarded. Trace2 consistently shows the second full refresh scan disappears.

The existing TypeScript owner fixture also exercises 62k files / 1.1 GB. Warm V8 allocation across A/B/A2/B2 (20 samples each) is effectively unchanged: 1,177,630 → 1,176,810 bytes/read; main-thread CPU is 9.730 → 9.074 ms/read. These exclude native Git memory/CPU. A complete Git read reproduced 144.9 s before versus 52.4 s after in single initial samples, with matching response hashes; noisy macOS controls preclude a general latency estimate. No production data was copied, and no production deployment was performed.

The managed `sessions.diff` handler regression fails on pre-fix production behavior and passes with the fix. Its fixture disables downstream raw-diff auto-refresh so that stage cannot mask the bug; the unowned revision check preserves the index. Initial focused proof passed 90 tests. After correcting the cross-platform fixture, the affected handler/revision suites passed all 59 tests under Bun, with a meaningful red replay at the managed-refresh assertion. The unchanged cache suite's 31-test proof is retained. Optional-lock contention also passes. Windows has no claimed revision speedup. Fresh Codex autoreview completed with no actionable findings.

`pnpm check:changed` passed on the initial head, including core/test/script typechecks, lint, dead exports, database and boundary guards. The test-only repair passed the affected typecheck, lint, format, and test-line allocation checks; production is unchanged.

First CI attempt [41138419486](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41138419486) caught the overstrong unowned full-diff assertion, now repaired as described above. It also reported a session-reset registry-discovery failure and inherited test-line debt. The reset case reproduces locally with `AgentDatabaseRegistryChangedError`; its test and owner stack are byte-identical to CI's exact main parent. The first merge added 14 test lines and 14 allocated lines, leaving main's existing 1,036-line ceiling deficit unchanged. This PR does not raise the shared baseline or allocate unrelated debt. The original failure and replay remain recorded; a passing retry is not claimed as a fix for the registry owner.

Current-head CI [41141038498](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41141038498), at `085defeb869263916d19df5f74fc6d6ff873f828`, passes the repaired diff shard. Its only failing roots are the same registry-witness case and the test-line guard. The exact tested merge retains main's **1,025-line** deficit: **26** added test lines are covered by exactly **26** allocated lines. Native pinned-head inherited-failure evidence records these reds, the unchanged owner blobs, the local registry replay, and the exact CI merge tree. No security or required-review gate is waived.

prs.title: fix: keep session catalog discovery responsive during startup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Session catalog discovery can wait behind unrelated reconnect preparations, and an empty catalog unnecessarily depends on session projection readiness.

## User Impact

Catalog reads can proceed while reconnect subscriptions are parked. An empty catalog returns without waiting for session storage to become ready.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the scheduler's existing independent-read category for this read-only RPC, and the existing metadata-only response path when no catalog is registered. Keep agent/catalog validation, preparation concurrency, mutation ordering, provider enumeration and visibility unchanged. No schema, config, cache, or worker changes.

## Evidence

Acceptance declared before measurement: invoke the real request-start owner and catalog-list handler with 5,000 persisted synthetic sessions. Compare five fresh processes per revision, interleaved, plus A/A controls. Separate initial, warm, queue and handler time; report CPU and sampled allocations. Require identical responses, zero projection acquisitions for empty lists, catalog admission independent of the held preparation duration, and no unexplained >20% CPU/allocation/event-loop regression. Provider and workspace scans are outside this zero-provider workload.

The scheduler regression fails on the original scheduler, and the empty-list readiness regression fails on the original handler. All 52 focused tests pass with the final consolidated coverage. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean P0–P2.

Five interleaved pairs plus A/A controls, 5,000 persisted synthetic sessions, Node 24.22.1/Linux:

| Median across processes | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Admission p50 under a 100 ms held preparation | 100.406 ms | 0.0116 ms |
| Warm empty handler p50 | 0.0412 ms | 0.00205 ms |
| Warm sampled allocation per call | 34.1 KB | 6.90 KB |
| Warm CPU per 1,000-call cycle | 201.6 ms | 139.5 ms |
| Dirty-projection handler p50 | 0.1998 ms | 0.0297 ms |
| Dirty full-cycle elapsed | 385.6 ms | 386.7 ms |

Responses match byte-for-byte after deterministic serialization. Empty catalog projection acquisitions fall from one per call to zero. Dirty mode includes later projection settling: allocation falls 7.8%, cycle time is +0.3%, CPU median is +16.6% with overlapping ranges and large A/A variation. No CPU improvement is claimed for that workload. These are owner-boundary measurements, not network/model timings.

Production code shrinks by one line. Benchmark additions separate admission, handler, CPU/allocation and settling costs; no schema/config/cache change.

A second 24-process campaign used a physically allocated 35.02 GiB SQLite database (34,688 synthetic transcript rows), 5,000 sessions and a 62,000-file/1.18 GB workspace. Five interleaved pairs plus A/A controls reproduced the result: warm handler p50 0.1241 → 0.0137 ms, allocation 33.2 → 6.8 KB/call, cycle CPU 482.9 → 334.3 ms; admission p50 100.423 → 0.0119 ms. All response hashes matched. This host uses ext4: a task-owned btrfs loop mount was refused by its kernel, so btrfs-specific behavior is not qualified. Cold transcript payloads are present in SQLite but are not decoded by this empty-provider workload.

`pnpm check:changed` completed every gate. Its only findings were two discarded promises in the benchmark; both were already retained and awaited through the `starts` array. Added explicit `void` annotations, reran the affected script lint successfully, and obtained a clean supplemental Codex review. All other changed-check gates passed, including core/scripts types, core lint, format, database guards and import cycles. The annotations do not change the measured behavior.

A real isolated Gateway passed three WebSocket `sessions.catalog.list` calls through the repository benchmark client against 5,000 synthetic sessions; each returned `{catalogs: []}`. The Gateway was stopped afterward.

The only non-aggregate failure in the first PR CI run was the test-line ratchet: the merge base was already over its ceiling, so the initial +13 test lines failed despite their matching allocation. Consolidated the readiness/CPU diagnostics coverage to zero net test-line growth and removed the allocation. The consolidated readiness test fails on the original handler and passes with the fix; its 52-test focused suite, targeted types/lint/format and test-line guard pass. Exact-head CI [41140844726](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41140844726) passed on `240585045e1d8c4327493aac8faf1328dfdb0d38`, including the repaired test-line ratchet and `openclaw/ci-gate`.

prs.title: fix: speed up public plugin category browsing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Selecting a plugin category takes seconds when a ClawHub token is saved, because the public request bypasses the CDN.

## User Impact

Public category browsing uses the same anonymous discovery policy as the overview. In 12 paired real-browser samples, Channels click-to-render p75 falls from **2658 to 177ms (15.0×)**. Explicit tokens, auth overrides, custom registries, search and other feeds keep their behavior. Category metadata follows ClawHub’s existing public snapshot freshness policy; install/release authorization is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawHub’s [public curated-category cache is deployed](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/4162#issuecomment-6535009907), but ambient authentication prevented the Plugins page from using it. Keep that decision in the existing HTTP catalog owner and extend its public-read auth regression table. No client cache, state or configuration is added.

## Evidence

Two isolated production-built Gateways, same saved ClawHub credential, real HTTP/WebSocket/browser transport, no response mocks. Base `4d2a9f8bb4c47da0daae7fd820cab33fa450ef7b`; 12 alternating AB/BA warm samples per variant, 1440×1000 Chromium for UI. Acceptance set before measurement: category p75 at least 2× faster and ≤1s, equal catalog identities, no material control regression.

| Journey | Before p50 /p75 /p95 | Candidate p50 /p75 /p95 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Real Gateway Channels RPC |2993 /3218 /4219ms|80 /116 /151ms|
| Real Channels click→content+2RAF |2412 /2658 /3452ms|154 /177 /283ms|
| Fresh navigation→usable catalog control, separate cohort |738 /850 /1098ms|759 /869 /1034ms|

All 26 first/warm RPC results have the same 102 ordered catalog identities (100 remote + 2 bundled). Browser: 48 navigation/category actions, zero page errors, equal category identity hash,30 rendered first-page cards. Saved-ambient Authorization headers go from 1 to 0 per curated request in the existing owner test; explicit-token/skipAuth/custom-registry controls stay correct. First RPC 4645→2087ms is one sample per variant and remains separate from warm percentiles. Warm RPC ranges2112–4219→43–151ms. This is the actual isolated product, not a deployment of the personal running Gateway.

An initial navigation control 689→963ms triggered investigation. CPU profiles/browser traces retained; compiled Control UI JS is identical except generated sw.js, and overview request policy is unchanged. The stricter fresh navigation→usable-content comparison above did not reproduce that 40% difference. The initial negative cohort remains retained; no navigation speedup claimed. Optional check:changed aborted at its default 4 GB Node heap; scoped validation below succeeded instead.

Validation: 79 focused owner/client/Gateway tests pass; scoped oxlint, core/scripts tsgo, oxfmt, and both production runtime builds pass. Red-on-base public-read auth regression. Reproduce the real RPC comparison against isolated builds:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-plugin-catalog.ts \
  --baseline-url ws://127.0.0.1:19080 --candidate-url ws://127.0.0.1:19081 \
  --samples 12 --output /absolute/catalog.json
```

prs.title: fix: time out stalled session branch reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes branch history requests waiting indefinitely when database admission or cold transcript restoration stalls. The missing deadline was outside the branch scan, before the handler's authorization/admission completes.

## User Impact

`sessions.branches.list` returns one retryable `UNAVAILABLE` error after a ten-second request deadline, including predispatch authorization time. The existing Control UI branch-query error state displays the failure and offers retry. Accepted work retains its owner until settlement; late success is suppressed. A blocked main event loop can still delay JavaScript timers.

## Why This Change Was Made

Branch listing reads indexed transcript navigation; it does not run Git or scan workspaces. The existing observation owner now starts the deadline and propagates cancellation to queued cold restoration and worker reads. Integrity checks remain intact. Cold restoration also skips a redundant worker read after the transcript is known to be archived, reducing three worker attempts to two.

No schema, configuration, or new cache is introduced. Production source grows by 31 lines for the missing deadline and cancellation ownership; regression coverage grows by 99 lines. Independently cancellable callers do not share another caller's pending cancellable read; retained summaries remain shared.

## Evidence

Four focused files passed (65 tests), covering dispatch admission, cancellation of actual queued cold restoration, retained-work cleanup and unchanged branches. Both regressions fail on unchanged baseline: no response at ten seconds, and queued cold restoration remains blocked after abort until the 120-second test limit. `pnpm check:changed` passed. Independent Codex review found no actionable findings through P2.

Thirty-four owner timing/profile runs used the same synthetic 35.06 GiB database, 10,000 session records, 82,180 messages, and 62,000-file / 1.116 GB workspace. The fixture contains 5,334 hot, 423 embedded-cold and 4,243 empty transcripts; a real archive restoration verified event/identity/index/FTS hashes. No production data was copied. Storage is APFS, not btrfs: this does not qualify filesystem-specific behavior.

Two A/A controls preceded five alternating pairs per shape; CPU/heap profiles were separate. Values are medians of five timing runs per arm:

| Owner metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Warm p50, ms | 0.086834 | 0.086958 |
| Warm p99, ms | 0.146334 | 0.260833 |
| Warm main CPU, ms / 2,048 reads | 187.260 | 195.414 |
| Uncached-summary p50, ms | 6.422959 | 6.316417 |
| Uncached main CPU, ms / 32 reads | 44.450 | 44.739 |

Warm A/A p50 was 0.086541/0.086375 ms, p99 0.169167/0.183291 ms, and main CPU 187.041/187.608 ms. Sampled main-plus-worker allocation stayed within A/A spread: warm 109.696/111.442 MB versus 110.896 MB; uncached 565.558/568.916 MB versus 568.287 MB. All response checksums matched; warm reads made zero worker requests, uncached reads one each.

The measured tradeoff is +4.35% warm main CPU and +0.1145 ms warm p99 (+78%), accepted for bounded cancellation; this is not a claim of universal latency improvement. Fresh source-process first reads remained seconds (median 2,770/2,390 ms), with substantial worker/esbuild startup and host variation. Node CPU excludes the external esbuild subprocess. These results do not establish a production p50 improvement.

Five separate archived reads reduced worker attempts **15 → 10** with identical response checksum. Their startup/copy costs were asymmetric, so no timing speedup is claimed for that smoke.

Actual CLI/WebSocket proof: **309/309 successful replies**, identical one-branch response checksum. Baseline A/A warm RTT p50/p99 was 3.057/4.713 ms and 4.326/14.137 ms; candidate 3.092/5.200 ms (100 measured calls each). Candidate falls within the A/A spread. First RPCs were 172/317/172 ms, separate from source-mode startup. Baseline A1 needed the benchmark's supported shutdown fallback for an existing session-cost-usage sidecar delay; baseline A2/candidate stopped gracefully, all drivers exited zero and the isolated listener was removed. The real route proves unchanged successful behavior; the dispatch regression proves the blocked-admission deadline.

## CI Attribution

Exact-head run [41135742861](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41135742861), attempt 1, remains failed. Local proof is green; the authorized native inherited-failure route retains these results rather than relabeling CI green:

- The exact CI baseline and tested merge both exceed the test-line ceiling by 1,042. This PR's +99 test lines have an equal +99 allocation; the inherited deficit does not increase.
- The dirty-checkout reset case reproduces the identical registry-change error on baseline, through an unchanged direct-handler path that bypasses this dispatch change. Candidate replay passed.
- The chat lifecycle failure is an outstanding detached `ws:preauth` connect-catalog task from unchanged producer/fixture code. The case passes on both local heads; this attribution is source ownership, not a claimed baseline reproduction. `agent.wait` gets no new deadline or race path.
- The observed `NO_REPLY` terminal-delivery case matches the specifically identified inherited failure and unchanged result owner.

The native evidence binds all three failed root jobs and their downstream aggregate to the exact head, tested merge, unchanged failure inputs and inspected logs. Security, required reviews and live merge authority remain separately enforced.

Incognito session commands allocate an unnecessary extra copy of committed session metadata while assembling their receipts.

## User Impact

## Why This Change Was Made

The private receipt builder only reads the actor-owned postimage. Pass that postimage directly into assembly and retain the existing copies where receipts cross the observer and caller boundaries. Extend the existing mutation test to cover both boundaries. Production LOC delta is zero (+1/−1); no new cache, configuration, or schema.

## Evidence

The real memory actor handled patches and transcript appends over 1,000 synthetic incognito sessions with approximately 32 KiB of skills metadata per entry. Five counterbalanced baseline/candidate/A/A rounds used 2,000 operations each, with separate clone-count, uninstrumented main-thread CPU, and collected-object allocation passes on Node 24.22.1.

| Median per command | Baseline | Candidate | Identical-baseline control |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Patch explicit clones | 7 | 6 | 7 |
| Patch sampled allocation | 261,357 B | 224,993 B (−13.91%) | 261,293 B |
| Append explicit clones | 6 | 5 | 6 |
| Append sampled allocation | 251,595 B | 215,521 B (−14.34%) | 251,797 B |
| Patch main-thread CPU | 99.84 µs | 97.76 µs | 98.63 µs |
| Append main-thread CPU | 153.08 µs | 148.57 µs | 135.00 µs |

CPU varied more than the median change: append p95 CPU rose 9.84% and elapsed p95 rose 6.43%; A/A append median CPU varied −11.81%. No CPU or whole-Gateway latency improvement is claimed. Median GC duration moved within the A/A spread. This memory-only owner does not access the persistent database or workspace; the fixture does not establish full Gateway turn or large-database performance.

The 14 focused memory-actor tests passed, including observer/caller mutation isolation. Mutation behavior is unchanged on the base; separate count passes expose the redundant copy there. The existing test now covers both mutation boundaries with zero net test-line growth; all prior assertions remain. The benchmark adds 88 tooling lines to make both owner paths reproducible.

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid automatic profiler hang risk on macOS
prs.body:
Related: #181120

## What Problem This Solves

Automatic continuous CPU profiling exposes macOS Gateways to a native lock-stall risk implicated in #181120.

## User Impact

macOS users no longer need a local patch to keep the automatic CPU flight recorder off. Callback attribution, stall warnings, event-loop delay/utilization, and CPU health metrics stay enabled. The tradeoff is losing automatic trailing CPU profiles on macOS. No configuration change is required; Linux and Windows recording and explicitly requested on-demand profiling are unchanged.

This removes the automatic profiler exposure; it does not fix Apple's lock implementation or claim every Gateway hang is resolved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gate the recorder at its existing owner, before the first native profile starts. Eligible macOS processes emit one explanatory warning per monitor. There is no new configuration, dependency, timer, or fallback profiler. Recording can be reconsidered once the native interaction is demonstrated safe.

Maintainer decision requested: @vincentkoc, could you review this macOS-only safety tradeoff promptly? The reported failure leaves the Gateway unresponsive; this change removes automatic CPU profiles while preserving non-profiling diagnostics, without claiming the native OS/Node bug is fixed.

## Evidence

### October 27 refresh and CI repair

- Refreshed against `main` at `7bce7a61639ae959406736876f2f0cf8cee991ce`; current PR head is `c5d431869fab9c7ad3aff4dc67b5da4d68c7bc35`. Resolved the recorder-test conflict while preserving main's interval-object sampling API, 25 ms interval, and timing-attribution tests. The production macOS exclusion is unchanged.
- The newly upstream real-native-profiler test excludes actual Darwin hosts, so its Linux platform mock cannot accidentally enable the unsafe native sampler there. Mocked macOS no-start and Linux/Windows rotation coverage remain active. This is an intentional platform eligibility limit, not a suppressed failure.
- The first refreshed head `e1c3921201ec3d4d5b1d092db5b5a9abcb306cd7` failed the [test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40512027532/job/122216871729) with a net addition of 27 test lines. This repair removes duplicate mock layers, a forwarding fixture, and repeated lifecycle/redaction setup without dropping scenarios or assertions. All six redaction cases remain; additional cases now also check later-sample recovery and shutdown. The complete PR now has **zero net additional test lines** against the refresh base (75 added / 75 removed); production remains +7/-1. The unchanged ratchet passes locally; no ceiling, baseline, or exemption was changed.
- **Linux / Node 26.12.1: 35 focused tests passed**, including the real native-profiler block test (19 Gateway + 16 recorder; wrapper 21.54 s). The preceding test-consolidation revision passed pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+807211511`: 34 passed / 1 skipped because its native V8 profiling API is unavailable (wrapper 12.05 s); the only subsequent source change restores the erased TypeScript cleanup contract. Removing only the macOS guard makes the consolidated macOS no-start regression fail; restoring it passes.
- CI confirmed the [test-line ratchet passes](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40515606710/job/122229495293) on `f6ac5a2bd09679ccd07b1e35a9a570feab6a8e33`, then exposed an [await-thenable lint error](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40515606710/job/122230905307). The final one-line repair restores the test table's `void | Promise<void>` cleanup contract: skill tracking drains asynchronous work, so removing `await` would be wrong. The exact CI type-aware lint configuration reproduced the error before this repair and passes afterward on all three changed TypeScript files. The gateway typecheck and all 35 Node tests were rerun successfully, and the local test-line delta remains zero.
- Both affected typecheck graphs (`state-logging`, `gateway-server`), targeted lint, formatting and diff whitespace checks passed on this candidate. Earlier MDX validation remains applicable to the unchanged documentation. **Current-head CI passed**: [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40519506734/job/122254287794) succeeded for `c5d431869fab9c7ad3aff4dc67b5da4d68c7bc35`, including all selected aggregate lanes, with no known-main-red waiver. The previously failing [type-aware lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40519506734/job/122244976210) and [baseline ratchets](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40519506734/job/122243448980) both passed. GitHub reported the PR cleanly mergeable; it remains open and unmerged.
- Fresh independent Auto Review of the complete final local candidate against the pinned refresh base returned `scoped-clean`, no P0–P2 findings. Its final patch pass covered all four files and explicitly checked the consolidated assertions and fixture semantics; earlier passes contained only the staged base-refresh inventory. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable. The [hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181551#issuecomment-6362662214) reported no findings or before-merge items for `e1c3921201ec3d4d5b1d092db5b5a9abcb306cd7`; that is prior-head review evidence, not a claim it reviewed this test-only repair.
- **Proof boundary:** the macOS Gateway A/B below remains evidence for the original head, not a new macOS execution of this refreshed revision. The guard is unchanged; updated sampling and Gateway consumers were checked by the current focused suites.

### Original revision validation

- **Actual macOS Gateway A/B supplied by @Marvinthebored:** [run report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181551#issuecomment-6367004169) and [pinned artifacts](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/aaf4683affe31fde5d83512918ef64610dd31133/PROOF.md) compare original head `00d27c442c5d8b8886f6e40c22b41b241f366c96` with `ded4d430df859f35599fbb4d0ef32d8dec31e3b5` on macOS 26.6.1 ARM64 / Node 26.12.1. Both isolated source-CLI Gateways reached readiness, retained named callback-stall and live event-loop health reporting after the same 1.5-second block, returned final readiness/liveness HTTP 200, and shut down cleanly with exit 0. Native samples before/after the block contain the V8 profiler thread in stock and none in patched; the patched recorder warning appears exactly once. The corrected comparison uses Gateway-PID-only SIGTERM. I inspected the harness, logs, health snapshots and complete native-sample thread inventories and verified all 40 artifact hashes against the pinned manifest; this is a review of the reporter's run, not a separate execution.
- **macOS-host red/green:** the same two suites pass 33/33 on that original head; restoring only stock recorder source gives 32 passed / 1 failed, specifically the new macOS exclusion test. These recorder tests mock native APIs; the separate Gateway A/B above supplies native-runtime evidence.
- CI: [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39935940769/job/120358914893) passed for head `00d27c442c5d8b8886f6e40c22b41b241f366c96`, with no failed or timed-out selected jobs. Native macOS runtime jobs were not selected.
- The reporter's macOS ARM64 reduction stalled with pthread read/write locks plus SIGPROF at both tested signal intervals. The no-signal rwlock control and signaled ordinary-mutex control completed. Repeated native samples showed the same blocked lock waiters.
- The new macOS regression failed before the guard and passes with it: startup, sampling, and shutdown never call the native profiler. Existing rotation/cleanup coverage now runs for both Linux and Windows runtime facts.
- **33 focused tests passed** across the recorder and Gateway event-loop health suites on Linux with Node 26.12.1. The Gateway tests preserve callback reports, health metrics, telemetry, idle sampling, and cleanup.
- Production TypeScript checking, the affected state/logging and Gateway-server test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, documentation MDX parsing, and `git diff --check` passed. Independent review found no actionable P0–P2 issues.
- **Limits:** the new successful macOS Gateway A/B supersedes the earlier readiness-timeout evidence gap. Both stock and patched complete this short scenario: it proves removal of automatic profiler exposure with working startup, health sampling and shutdown, not reproduction or repair of the original deadlock or long-term stability. Source execution with tsx does not cover a release distribution, channel/model traffic or manual profiling. Short Node port-churn controls also did not reproduce the native hang; manually requested profiling is not made safe by this change.

<details>
<summary>Original revision validation commands, cost, and broader-check gaps</summary>

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/logging/diagnostic-stall-flight-recorder.test.ts src/gateway/server/event-loop-health.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 33 passed; wrapper 39.19 s, including a 33.35 s cold worker build. Regression lives in existing fixtures; no new worker, server, or sleep is added.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`: passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --changed-paths-json '["src/logging/diagnostic-stall-flight-recorder.test.ts","src/gateway/server/event-loop-health.test.ts"]'`: overall failed. Existing Gateway-root/infra inventories exceed the 720-root budget (726/729); neither test file is new. The runner expanded to all graphs: state/logging and Gateway-server passed, while a later plugin-SDK compiler process exited 139. That compiler crash is unresolved and is not represented as a passing full test-typecheck run.
- Targeted `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`: 0 warnings/errors on the three changed TypeScript files. `scripts/run-format.mts --check`, `scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/gateway/health.md`, and diff whitespace checks passed.
- Simplification: one platform decision in the existing recorder owner; production delta +7/-1 lines. No parallel implementation or native patch is introduced.

</details>

Reported and reproduced by @Marvinthebored.

## Worked on by

- @Marvinthebored

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid slow group changes with unrelated stores
prs.body:
Closes #167716
Replaces #167717, closed by its author while this adoption was in progress.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: renaming or deleting a small session group waits for unnecessary writes to unrelated agent stores, including stores left by retired agents.

## User Impact

User impact: group rename and delete skip stores with no members to move; empty groups require no category-write sweep. No client, configuration, schema, or migration changes are required. A concurrent assignment in a skipped store retains the source group and returns a retryable partial-change error rather than losing membership.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the membership snapshot already produced by the existing owner to select the stores to update. Keep category-write authorization, session recency, and the independent all-store membership check before retirement unchanged. The original production change is preserved; its two regressions are adapted to the current shared fixtures.

Original fix and regression design by @Marvinthebored in #167717, adopted at the author's request. The local implementation commit retains Marvinthebored as author and includes the verified co-author trailer.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/dc37b418-938e-4ae6-a533-f3b93a91cde4)

## Evidence

### Current-head runtime proof acceptance (recorded before measurement)

Run the built Gateway CLI over an authenticated loopback WebSocket, with three configured agents: one group member in main and unrelated sessions in the other two stores. Compare base `79798ed63e1d974179c2bfd7960c04daa7f14dda` with the candidate production tree, in five serial ABAB pairs of fresh Gateway processes. Each boot records first-use rename, populated delete, and empty delete separately, followed by 20 warm samples per operation. Use identical synthetic state, Node 26.12.1, and host-load records; no model calls or production state.

Acceptance: all responses and category/catalog readbacks must be correct; unrelated categories and member recency must remain unchanged. Member-only store sweeps must remain covered by the existing count regressions (3-store fixture implies 3→1 populated, 3→0 empty). Warm rename/delete median should improve, with no 20% regression in median or p95 for the measured cases. Report sample counts, median/p95/range, first-use samples, and any regression rather than treating historical timings as current evidence. Separate diagnostic CPU profiling from the timing runs.

### Built-Gateway results — 2026-10-26

**Source binding:** baseline `79798ed63e1d974179c2bfd7960c04daa7f14dda`; candidate published head `c9a370084a10b150cdf607df2616457d32a4538e`. Candidate build commit `05bd96ed4cd4b1928c0bf209b89927c0777f429a` has exactly the same entire Git tree as the published head: `8009de56e41d9637bcd2a2ec0fa86cbaa15c7464` (verified against GitHub). This follow-up changes only the existing benchmark script; production code and regression tests are unchanged.

**Real entry point:** both arms ran their built `dist/entry.js gateway run`, not a test-server factory. A real loopback WebSocket client authenticated with a synthetic token and matching build identity. Three sessions were created through `sessions.create` in three stores. Mutation responses and `sessions.describe` readbacks checked affected counts, category updates/clearing and unchanged member `updatedAt`; per-cycle `sessions.groups.list` and bystander readbacks checked the final catalog and unchanged unrelated categories. No model call, provider credential, production Gateway, or UI was involved.

Five serial **base → candidate** pairs, fresh state/process per arm. Each case has **100 warm samples per arm** (20 per boot), plus **5 separate first-use samples**. All 630 measured mutation requests and their readbacks passed; all 10 timed Gateways shut down cleanly. Linux x64, Node 26.12.1, 128 available CPUs, no cgroup CPU quota; observed host 1-minute load 4.92–6.95. Startup/build time is excluded. These are local-loopback measurements, not WAN/UI latency.

| Warm RPC | Base median / p95 (ms) | Candidate median / p95 (ms) | Median change | Base range (ms) | Candidate range (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Rename one-member group | 10.76 / 14.73 | 7.09 / 10.29 | −34.1% | 8.64–20.32 | 6.11–13.56 |
| Delete one-member group | 10.55 / 13.37 | 6.86 / 10.25 | −35.0% | 8.36–14.51 | 6.02–20.89 |
| Delete empty group | 9.23 / 11.76 | 3.83 / 5.55 | −58.4% | 7.43–14.83 | 3.25–34.02 |

| First use in each fresh process (5/arm) | Base median [min–max] ms | Candidate median [min–max] ms |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rename | 66.04 [62.06–80.87] | 50.25 [46.83–58.39] |
| Populated delete | 16.09 [15.75–17.04] | 10.92 [10.61–11.67] |
| Empty delete | 12.64 [12.32–13.47] | 5.52 [5.27–6.78] |

**Acceptance:** every correctness assertion passed and all median/p95 cells improved. **Tail caveat:** populated-delete and empty-delete single-sample maxima worsened, as shown above; their cause is not established. This is not evidence that every tail metric improves. Five first-use samples are not a reliable tail estimate. Existing deterministic sweep-count tests remain the work-removal oracle; this real-Gateway run measures latency, not an instrumented count of every store write.

A separate `--cpu-profile` diagnostic pass completed on each arm (24 valid Node CPU profiles per arm, including worker isolates), with clean shutdown. Profiles contain the real SQLite admission/transaction and membership paths. Profiled timing is excluded from these tables; sampled hit counts are not operation counts.

**Rerun:** build each clean checkout with frozen dependencies and the same Node runtime:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts sourcePerformance
```

prs.title: fix: prevent background summarization from delaying replies to new messages
prs.body:
Closes #176944

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a new message waits for background summarization to finish when a context engine's host LLM request is still in flight.

## User Impact

User impact: new messages can interrupt a context engine's background summary preparation instead of waiting for the model request to finish. In an isolated Gateway the second turn was admitted after 0.235 to 0.315 s instead of 40.8 to 42.3 s, and the held request was aborted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deferred maintenance is optional work, so a foreground turn cancels it. The host combines maintenance cancellation with the request's existing abort signal, including for engines that do not wire cancellation themselves. Foreground admission waits for disposal to finish; aborted cleanup retains predecessor ordering but cannot publish transcript rewrites or start another host LLM call. Coalesced reruns are discarded, and requests that arrive during cleanup are refused for retry on the next turn.

## Evidence

Regression tests, run with the source changes reverted and with them:

| Test | Without the change | With the change |
|---|---|---|
| host LLM request carries maintenance and request cancellation (`context-engine-maintenance.resources.test.ts`) | `expected false to be true` | passes |
| foreground turn preempts a held host LLM request, joins disposal, discards the coalesced rerun (`context-engine-maintenance.resources.test.ts`) | times out after 120 s | passes |
| aborted cleanup re-enters ownership without publication authority (`coordinator.test.ts`) | times out after 120 s | passes |
| maintenance and cleanup run without the launching turn's caller or operator authority (`coordinator.test.ts`) | `owner.runCleanup is not a function` | passes |
| new deferred request is refused while preempted cleanup waits for an earlier writer (`context-engine-maintenance.resources.test.ts`) | the failure callback is never called | passes |

The host-cancellation assertion was also replayed with only `context-engine-capabilities.ts` restored to unpatched source: `expected false to be true` at `expect(passed.aborted).toBe(true)`. Restoring the fix makes the same assertion pass. The full suites check that foreground admission waits for actual disposal, coalesced work never runs, canceled cleanup cannot publish, and a later maintenance run still succeeds.

Test environment: macOS 26.6.1 (arm64), Node 26.12.1, repository-managed Bun 1.4.4 test runner. The Gateway reproduction uses the supplied background-maintenance context-engine plugin and a loopback OpenAI-compatible fixture model server.

Focused validation passes: 31 tests in the coordinator and context-engine maintenance resource suites, the eager-import closure and PR-worktree provisioning guards, formatting, type-aware lint, and type checks scoped to the changed source and test files.

Isolated Gateway run from source (own state directory, loopback fixture model server, a context-engine plugin whose `maintain()` calls `runtimeContext.llm.complete` with no abort handling; the server holds that request open and the script releases it after 40 s on the unpatched tree):

| Tree | Run | Second turn admitted after | Reply received after | Held request aborted |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| unpatched | 1 | 40.806 s | 40.894 s | no |
| unpatched | 2 | 42.263 s | 42.521 s | no |
| patched | 1 | 0.315 s | 0.376 s | yes, engine disposed before admission |
| patched | 2 | 0.235 s | 0.287 s | yes, engine disposed before admission |

The driver sends both turns through the Gateway's HTTP chat-completions endpoint, into the same session. The fixture deliberately supplies no maintenance abort listener or request signal. Both patched runs record the request disconnect and engine disposal before the second provider request; neither reaches the 40-second release cap.

[Gateway driver, source attribution and current traces](https://gist.github.com/Marvinthebored/bdafbbfa3d70a9969d75750b408b5705) · [Unpatched run 1](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/9395532733ad5c05106a937ecc1990093710e84b/maintenance-preemption/runs/red-1-summary.json) · [Unpatched run 2](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/9395532733ad5c05106a937ecc1990093710e84b/maintenance-preemption/runs/red-2-summary.json)

prs.title: fix(xai): keep Talk connected after interrupted response replacement
prs.body:
Closes #184207

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes xAI Talk disconnecting with “Realtime provider output has no live response owner” when server VAD interrupts a response and its successor arrives without the interrupted response’s terminal event.

## User Impact

The conversation can continue with the new answer instead of closing. Late output from the interrupted answer remains discarded. No configuration changes or migrations are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The xAI adapter now settles the interrupted response as canceled before admitting a distinct identified successor. This is restricted to an observed server-VAD interruption; ordinary overlapping responses still hit the existing relay guard. Pending user transcription survives the handover.

The change uses the existing response owner and completion callback rather than relaxing shared ownership rules. Production delta: +25/-1 lines; one integration regression exercises the real adapter, relay ownership, and session harness.

## Evidence

On upstream base `e83186f4e8343a4b37001d0e726ef34e02d10a2a` with this patch:

- **Red/green regression:** the new test fails on the unpatched bridge with the exact ownership error, then passes with the fix. It covers the missing A terminal, canceled A turn, distinct B turn, preserved user transcript, discarded late A audio/text/tools/terminal, successful B completion, and rejection of arbitrary overlap.
- **46 tests passed** across the xAI provider suite and new relay-ownership regression. Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/xai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts src/gateway/talk/relay/xai-ownership.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.
- Targeted typecheck, type-aware lint (including package-boundary declaration preparation), formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Two independent reviews found no actionable defects.
- **Separate live Gateway smoke:** two real xAI runs received generated PCM through `talk.session.appendAudio`, interrupted a counting response with a sky-color question, then asked an ordinary arithmetic question. Each returned three distinct turns; 608 and 527 audio frames, zero errors. Replies included “A clear daytime sky is blue” and “Two plus two is four.”

**Proof limits:** live smoke used the candidate xAI plugin with previously built core/UI at a different, carried base—not this upstream head. Both live runs received the predecessor’s normal terminal, so those earlier runs did not exercise the missing-terminal branch. The October 27 fault-injection proof below now exercises it through real transport. The earlier synthetic smoke did not test physical microphone/remote playback. A full upstream runtime build was not tested. The earlier carried-base full-runtime build attempt stopped on a missing dependency; it is not claimed as passing. The fix was subsequently deployed to production; the manual microphone test below is additional evidence, not a reproduction of the rare branch.

### Production microphone interruption test — October 26, 2026

The patched production Gateway completed a manual Web Talk session using the real xAI provider and physical microphone. The user rapidly changed requests while answers were being generated. Gateway diagnostics recorded eight response lifecycles: five completed and three canceled, with no session warning/error or ownership failure. The conversation continued after all three cancellations, and the user confirmed normal playback.

Redacted lifecycle excerpt (HKT; response IDs replaced with A–F):

```text
20:33:24.840 response.created A
20:33:30.058 client response.cancel A
20:33:30.283 response.outcome A cancelled; response.done A
20:33:30.516 response.created B
20:33:31.119 response.done B
20:33:33.034 response.created C
20:33:37.374 client response.cancel C
20:33:37.605 response.outcome C cancelled; response.done C
20:33:39.639 response.created D
20:33:43.350 client response.cancel D
20:33:43.587 response.outcome D cancelled; response.done D
20:33:45.655 response.created E
20:33:49.650 response.outcome E completed; response.done E
20:34:27.011 session.closed
```

This establishes production cancellation/recovery behavior with real microphone input. All three cancellations were client-triggered, and each predecessor terminal arrived before its successor. It does **not** establish that the server-VAD missing-terminal branch ran. The October 27 controlled real-transport fault injection below supplies the missing-terminal branch proof.

### Review fixes — `77127e9b`

Moved the ownership composition regression to the core relay test suite, obtaining the xAI provider through its public plugin registration entry and the harness through the plugin SDK. The socket mock preserves real-module exports. No production code changed in this follow-up.

The relocated regression fails on the original unpatched bridge and passes with the repair. Another 71 affected tests pass. Targeted typecheck, typed lint, formatting, plugin boundary checks, and the mock-export ratchet pass locally. Fresh PR CI and review remain pending. The production microphone evidence above remains smoke coverage, not a claim of live missing-terminal reproduction.

### Real-transport missing-terminal fault injection — October 27, 2026

**Passed through a real xAI WebSocket and an isolated Gateway running the production build** (`b891b0f0ba0312a8f3aabb627d0b4e0a4554aaaa`, carrying this adapter fix). A single-connection transport filter withheld A's real `response.done`, forwarded the next real speech/VAD event and response B, then replayed five captured A frames after B started. The Gateway settled A as canceled, admitted B, rejected late A output, completed B, and completed a third ordinary turn. The client received **932 audio frames, zero Talk errors, and no late A audio after B began**. Test processes were stopped afterward; production was not changed.

This is controlled production-boundary fault injection, not a claim that xAI naturally omitted a terminal during this run. A had completed upstream; its terminal was withheld before reaching the adapter. Real provider events and audio drove the Gateway's missing-terminal handover. The test used generated PCM, not a physical microphone. The runtime was a carried production build, not a fresh build of the PR head.

<summary>Redacted filter and Gateway trace (UTC filter timestamps; +08:00 Gateway timestamps)</summary>

### Final fixture and CI-boundary repair

Socket construction now resolves a fixture-owned promise instead of timer polling. The core regression loads the xAI public entry through the existing bundled-plugin facade loader, avoiding a static extension dependency in the core typecheck graph. Production behavior is unchanged by these fixture repairs.

Validation for the final fixture: regression passes (639 ms test time; 5.23 s total Vitest duration) and fails on the unpatched bridge at the ownership assertion. Scoped typecheck, typed lint, formatting, and diff checks pass. Compiler file-membership inspection of the changed test includes zero bundled extension source files. prs.body:
## What

Russian docs localization is wired up but nearly empty: `docs/.i18n/glossary.ru.json` was 21 entries (1.2 KB) against 107 KB for `zh-CN`, and `ru-navigation.json` did not exist at all, so the Russian sidebar fell back to English while the pages themselves were already 75% translated.

This PR fills in the two files that drive the Russian locale:

- `glossary.ru.json`: **21 → 250 entries** (1.2 KB → 18.6 KB). Existing entries and their order are preserved; 6 target terms were corrected for consistency with the pages: Compaction → Сжатие контекста, Gateway → Шлюз, Node → Нода, Plugin → Плагин, Skills → Скиллы, Webhook → Вебхук. Deliberately kept in English: Active Memory, Cron, Dreaming, Heartbeat, Loopback, Markdown, Self-hosted.
- `ru-navigation.json`: **created from scratch — 12 tabs, 55 groups** (8.6 KB), mirroring the English navigation structure.

No page content, no build scripts, no English strings touched: two data files only.

## Verification

- Every path in `ru-navigation.json` was checked against the repository tree (1,385 `.md` files): 0 broken links, 55 unique anchors.
- Rendered through the real `composeDocsConfig()` from `scripts/docs-sync-publish.mjs`: 12/12 Russian tabs, 55/55 groups, pages resolve as `ru/index…`.
- `glossary.ru.json` parses as valid JSON and keeps the original key order (`json.load` round-trip diff on the untouched prefix).
- Note: `check-docs-i18n-glossary.mts` only validates `zh-CN` today, so this file is not CI-gated — I verified it manually as described above.

## Why

The Russian locale is the largest non-English audience for OpenClaw docs and currently has English headings over Russian text. These two files are the smallest, highest-leverage change: no translation work, but the sidebar and the inline glossary switch to Russian immediately.

## Visual proof

Rendered through the real `composeDocsConfig()` from `scripts/docs-sync-publish.mjs`, locale `ru`, same tree, only `docs/.i18n/ru-navigation.json` added.

| Before (`main` — no ru overlay) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adamant064/openclaw/docs/ru-i18n-proof/proof/ru-sidebar-before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adamant064/openclaw/docs/ru-i18n-proof/proof/ru-sidebar-after.png) |

Behavioural comparison of the two composed configs:

```
before: tabs 12, groups 55, pages 308
after : tabs 12, groups 55, pages 308      # page inventory identical
before tabs: Get started | Install | Channels | Agents | Capabilities | Models |
             Platforms | Gateway & Ops | Reference | Releases | Contributing | Help

```

Only labels change; every route and its order is preserved, which is the guarantee the overlay functions (`applyLocaleNavLabelOverlay`) are supposed to give. Screenshots are generated from the composed `docs.json` (sidebar label tree), not from a live docs host, so nothing is redacted and no endpoint is involved.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor migration attribution tests repeatedly load TypeScript in each real Doctor child process.

## User Impact

No product behavior change. The focused test completes faster while retaining both native and worker parent contracts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve the four child modules from the existing compiled subprocess generation during collection. Each row still owns isolated state, runs the full Doctor/auth repair composition, and launches a separate Node Doctor that must acquire SQLite exclusion while its parent lives. All 20 cases, assertions, receipts, credential/config migration, retirement completion, and cleanup remain. The child timeout stays at 60 seconds.

## Evidence

Frozen base: `24e37a12ddcc50c399bd3effe8be94a148587add`. Candidate: `c043b12686f264d2d5990d655973a7b32c28eda3`.

`timeout 900 /usr/bin/time -v pnpm test src/infra/update-doctor-migration-attribution.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --reporter=verbose`

Three serial before and three serial after runs, all **20/20 passing**, on the same host, frozen private dependencies, Node 26.12.1, pinned OpenClaw Bun fork `openclaw-v1.4.4-20261026-191755ec11-webkit-b82bc917e9`, and private temp/cache paths. Both measured series used prepared compiler outputs.

Median wall: **72.72 → 55.31 seconds (23.9% lower)**. Median case sum: **64.685 → 45.434 seconds (29.8% lower)**. Import is the test module’s inclusive import timing; case sums are verbose-reporter case durations, not wall time.

<details>
<summary>Causal work counts, retained proof, and validation</summary>

- Actual child profiling: 834 initialization + 31 later TypeScript loads per mode become **zero**. Each mode retains **eight nested process launches** and its separate Doctor process. Native/worker child wall was 11.97/11.52s before and 2.09/2.18s after; initialization was 2.95/2.82s before and 0.40/0.39s after. Three synchronous child launches consumed 3.50/3.46s before and 0.60/0.69s after.
- The native/worker retirement rows were 30.893/25.784s, 29.506/25.586s, 27.081/28.959s before; 19.089/21.052s, 19.886/16.663s, 19.418/16.423s after.
- Mutation checks: removing the parent close makes the worker row fail with SQLite “database is locked”; the native row passes that mutation. Suppressing durable retirement completion, forcing a false receipt, and bypassing auth migration each fail both rows at their intended assertions. All temporary production mutations were restored byte-for-byte.
- Focused consumers: 29 tests pass across `node-sqlite.worker`, `openclaw-state-db-cache.retention`, `openclaw-state-db-async-lifecycle`, and `update-doctor-result`.
- Scoped typecheck, type-aware lint, format, diff, line-cap, max-lines, test-line budget, timeout, mock-export, and assertion ratchets pass.
- Exact LF inventory: target −3, existing declaration helpers +3; **net test LF 0, production LF 0, effective ceiling delta 0**. Both snapshots contain 6,313,577 tracked test LF. Scalar 6,287,490 and all 177 grants totaling 25,048 are unchanged; the 6,312,538 ceiling retains exactly 1,039 inherited LF debt. The native comparison gate passes with the unchanged debt notice.
- `pr-simplify` completed: three existing declarations and four import rewires; no new runtime owner, cache, mock, seam, or removed behavior.
- Isolated Codex autoreview against the frozen base and final staged snapshot: **P0–P2, scoped-clean, exit 0, report_produced true**, one complete pass with 25 intact target/owner/helper/context files (295,962 prompt bytes). The committed source matches that reviewed snapshot. The reviewer did not independently rerun tests.

</details>

Failed/discarded preparation is retained separately: the first baseline attempt failed because the private task temp directory inherited group write permission; only task-directory permissions were corrected before the successful series. The first temporary profiler had a quoting error, then was corrected. The candidate’s cold two-row diagnostic includes 30.55s of compiler preparation and took 74.40s wall; it is separate from the warm full-file comparison. prs.title: fix(plugins): inspect installation sources asynchronously
prs.body:
Related: #166526

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor update-candidate repair and deferred plugin installation can synchronously read, copy and hash plugin source on the serving thread while inspecting the exact execution inputs.

## User Impact

Source inspection uses the existing preparation worker, so the caller can keep making progress while filesystem work runs. Selected source bytes, dependency results, native admission receipts, warning callbacks and syntax-error behavior stay the same. There is no new cache, pool, persisted state, public option or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The worker now runs the existing source inspectors without evaluating plugin code. Every selected package keeps its admission owner and receipts; inspection resources settle before results return. Install and repair callers recheck their authority after awaiting inspection. The already-isolated update-candidate subprocess keeps its synchronous inspector.

The new import path also exposed a cleanup bundle boundary: source-capture cleanup is already asynchronous, so it loads its cleanup implementation there, before checking current native custody. Deletion still finishes before instance release. General worker startup and the Windows failure logger keep their existing lazy imports.

## Evidence

The failing-first source-inspection regression observed three original-entry reads on the caller thread where the requirement is zero. The worker implementation observes zero and returns the same selected graph and ancestor warnings without executing the plugin.

Focused proof passed 87 tests before the cleanup boundary adjustment. A refreshed run passed 37 tests in five files, including multi-owner native receipt persistence, syntax and callback failures, empty selections, post-await lease revocation, delayed worker retirement and cleanup ordering. Its wall time was 388 seconds, including 114 seconds to prepare the worker compiler cache on a loaded Mac; the three new worker tests took about 12 seconds and the added lease-revocation case about 1.5 seconds. These are behavioral/work-count results, not a claimed elapsed-time speedup. These local durations do not predict CI or end-to-end Doctor latency.

The final source-capture cleanup/recovery run passed 55 tests in three files (285 seconds wall time, including worker preparation). It covers live native retention, partial disposal, recovery after removed directories, and exact worker inspection results. The complete production build passed in 12 minutes 26 seconds, including native loading checks for 56 built plugin control-plane modules. Typed lint, formatting, assertion safety and diff checks passed. Source-complete independent review of the final boundary found no actionable P0–P2 issue.

Test-line allocation: 211 lines for the real-worker source/admission/error regression and the post-await lease-revocation case. The staged ratchet reports the existing 1,042-line repository debt; this change allocates its exact growth and adds no further debt. The shared scalar remains unchanged.

Exact-head [CI run 41139258096](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41139258096) has all 84 jobs completed. The only root failure is the inherited test-line budget, followed by the aggregate CI gate. Its exact baseline `563ba501dced074d9d282fb3a4cb48cfc31bcf9e` has 1,026 lines of absolute debt; the candidate adds 211 lines and 211 allocation credit, preserving the same debt. The tested merge is `ba117162d82ec8d658bd5176e6dbab04abaea79f`. The supported inherited-failure landing path retains the failed result; CI is not described as green.
