prs.title: fix(gateway): config.patch hangs after a superseded reload until another config change lands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A persisted `config.patch` / `config.apply` can leave its RPC waiting indefinitely after an in-process Gateway restart. Retained reload candidates were not always rescheduled. Real Gateway verification also exposed a second cause: the effective-unchanged path compared a resolved secrets snapshot with an unresolved SecretRef candidate, classified the permanent mismatch as supersession, and kept retrying it.

## User Impact

Provisioning and other source-equivalent config writes receive their application acknowledgment without an unrelated follow-up edit. Existing credential activation, publication ownership, and rollback checks remain in force. No config option, schema, dependency, or protocol change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Schedule another attempt whenever a superseded write candidate is retained, including candidates retained by either inner catch.
- The second cause this PR originally repaired, a resolved-snapshot versus unresolved-SecretRef comparison that classified an unchanged write as superseded, is fixed upstream by #183964 (merged October 27). This PR's guard for it and its two regression cases were dropped on October 28; `server-reload-managed-secrets.ts` and its test are now identical to `main`.

The complete PR now changes one production line in `config-reload.ts` and adds one focused regression file, reusing the existing retry owner rather than introducing a second resolver, state, or weaker guards.

## Evidence

### October 28 refresh: exact-head real Gateway run on `b7c03efe8cb7da0cdc4af54b36e90b19de79e2d9`

<!-- pr177823-oct28-refresh -->

Upstream `main` moved past the reviewed head `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625`, and the branch picked up test-path and test-line-ceiling conflicts. The branch now carries merge commits of upstream `main` (latest `56eba2fae26`) plus two ceiling-only commits; the reviewed commits are untouched and the production diff against `main` is still the same two files, nine net lines. Everything below ran on the exact pushed head `b7c03efe8cb7da0cdc4af54b36e90b19de79e2d9`, built from source (`dist/build-info.json` commit `b7c03efe8cb7da0cdc4af54b36e90b19de79e2d9`, OpenClaw 2026.10.8), host Node v24.19.0, Gateway native runtime Node 26.12.1, macOS arm64, isolated `--profile` state, token auth, distinct free loopback ports.

#### Executed workload

Identical to the October 19 workload: full `gateway run --verbose`, real `SIGUSR2` **in-process restart**, `config.get`, one source-equivalent `config.patch` (`response:"summary"`) that rewrites the disabled Mattermost account's `baseUrl` to the `${PR177823_MATTERMOST_URL}` placeholder, then, right after the `config.patch write` log line, rotate the file-backed `proof/proof` provider key A→B and call `secrets.reload`, wait 2.5 s, restore B→A and call `secrets.reload` again, no further config write, 30 s RPC deadline, clean shutdown. The client is one process built on the repository's own `callGateway` owner (`src/gateway/call.ts`, CLI client mode), so the rotation reaches the Gateway about 40 ms after the write log line.

| Source | Same restart + file-credential-refresh workload | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Merge parent `953eba4bbeec1c8cf7b255cce1c8c3f1496aaf3b` (current upstream `main` without this PR) | Identical | Original patch answered successfully in **270 ms server / 280.7 ms client**, zero supersessions, clean shutdown. **PASS** |
| Final head `b7c03efe8cb7da0cdc4af54b36e90b19de79e2d9` | Identical | Original patch answered successfully in **420 ms server / 433.2 ms client**, zero supersessions, clean shutdown. **PASS** |

Redacted exact-head Gateway log, **October 28, 2026, UTC−07:00**:

```text
2026-10-28T15:00:42.439-07:00 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
2026-10-28T15:00:42.845-07:00 [gateway] restart mode: in-process restart (unmanaged: use in-process restart to keep custom supervisor PID tracking stable)
2026-10-28T15:01:06.966-07:00 [gateway] config.patch write changedPaths=channels.mattermost.accounts.proof.baseUrl restartReason=config.patch
2026-10-28T15:01:07.196-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 174ms
2026-10-28T15:01:07.298-07:00 [reload] config source revision 1 accepted (write)
2026-10-28T15:01:07.367-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ config.patch 420ms
2026-10-28T15:01:09.852-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 127ms
2026-10-28T15:01:10.503-07:00 [shutdown] completed cleanly in 553ms
```

Raw trace SHA-256 values: final-head Gateway log `ff77f2dd59dd24ba308e09d8f5e5d47af91672bc440ae5ec23b27baac1ad3e26`, final-head client event trace `1fb2d2fb88aaaf73400895f5acea84d45bf221ca0949a97622bb37af374d0cf8`, merge-parent Gateway log `8ea5b86083fef455e0a92d24a318486415e7989ff56d9cb4996e09065952f238`.

#### Exact-head rerun after the guard removal: `c3efb3da9a340c5957702cfbe783b8976593d52b`

Same build procedure, same workload, same client. Original patch answered successfully in **265 ms server / 274.4 ms client**, zero supersessions, clean shutdown. Redacted Gateway log, **October 28, 2026, UTC−07:00**:

```text
2026-10-28T15:21:07.167-07:00 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
2026-10-28T15:21:07.626-07:00 [gateway] restart mode: in-process restart (unmanaged: use in-process restart to keep custom supervisor PID tracking stable)
2026-10-28T15:21:15.624-07:00 [gateway] config.patch write changedPaths=channels.mattermost.accounts.proof.baseUrl restartReason=config.patch
2026-10-28T15:21:15.769-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 110ms
2026-10-28T15:21:15.820-07:00 [reload] config source revision 1 accepted (write)
2026-10-28T15:21:15.873-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ config.patch 265ms
2026-10-28T15:21:18.368-07:00 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 83ms
2026-10-28T15:21:18.544-07:00 [shutdown] completed cleanly in 127ms
```

Raw trace SHA-256 values: Gateway log `cda9311452c3a1c967099bd028e9355bb010e6618b097c457a29158af51c4b59`, client event trace `26e14af67145e907356902a48622f308792b534a1217b19cbe629f8896e52941`.

#### What changed upstream, and what this PR still fixes

The merge-parent control **no longer fails** this workload. Upstream [#183964](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/183964) (merged October 27) changed the unchanged-write handler in `server-reload-managed-secrets.ts` so an unchanged candidate whose secrets-source form equals the running snapshot's is accepted instead of being reported as superseded. That is the second cause this PR targeted, so the real-Gateway run no longer discriminates between `main` and this head. This PR's `server-reload-managed-secrets.ts` guard sat on top of an equivalent upstream guard (its stable-key and rotated-key regression cases pass on the merge parent without it), so the guard and those two cases were **dropped**: both files are now byte-identical to `main`.

The first cause is still present on `main`: a retained superseded write candidate is not rescheduled. `config-reload.superseded-retry.test.ts` fails on the merge parent (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called 3 times, but got 1 times`) and passes at this head with the two-line `config-reload.ts` change. Two attempts to force a genuine supersession on a real current-`main` Gateway (a second concurrent `config.patch`; an external on-disk save of `openclaw.json` inside the first write's apply window) were refused before apply by the base-hash guard (`config base hash required…`, `config changed since last load…`), so no live-supersession trace is claimed for the new head; the scheduler repair remains proven by the focused regression, as stated below.

#### Checks at the final head

- `config-reload.superseded-retry.test.ts` (1) and `server-reload-managed-secrets.test.ts` (19): **20 passed** at `b7c03efe8cb7da0cdc4af54b36e90b19de79e2d9`; the same two files on the merge parent: 19 passed, superseded-retry failed. After the guard removal (head `c3efb3da9a340c5957702cfbe783b8976593d52b`), superseded-retry, upstream's managed-secrets suite and `config-reload.test.ts` pass together.
- Gateway test-path list, test-projects routing and CI node test plan checks: 284 passed on the first merge commit of this refresh.
- Test-line ceiling: `main` keeps `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` at zero slack; this PR adds exactly 118 test lines, so each merge admits the measured total with no future allowance. `main` raised its own zero-slack ceiling twice more while this refresh was running (ceiling-only merges `d9bc85d1ff74122e2188028ddb72876ecf0f366b` and `1b9faf2d32354ceb3d0d93ef68c4da23cc0a1667`). After the guard removal the PR adds 60 test lines, which fit under `main`'s current ceiling, so `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` is back to `main`'s file.
- The merge commits require fresh maintainer security approval on the final head; none is claimed.

### Exact-head real Gateway recovery: `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625`

<!-- pr177823-real-gateway-repair-b8c13e0 -->

The previously stalling workload now completes on the final fixed full Gateway: **437 ms server / 439 ms client**, after a real SIGUSR2 in-process restart and concurrent synthetic credential refresh, with **no later config edit**.

Important distinction: this final run logged **zero supersessions**. The repair prevents the permanent resolved-value/SecretRef mismatch that produced them on the older head. This is not presented as a new-head trace that throws a supersession and then succeeds.

#### Comparable real-runtime controls

| Source | Same restart + file-credential-refresh workload | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct parent `08d04a9d7b97e50849ba089c3837d2e1c3c4f7fd` | One supersession, credential restored, no additional config write | Original patch still pending at the 30 s client deadline. It answered UNAVAILABLE only during shutdown, at 50,016 ms. **FAIL** |
| Initial PR head `ebfffd5599a7ee7c6d793718b96f923107b27691` | Eight supersessions before credential restoration; retries continued afterward | Original patch still pending at 30 s; 482 supersessions were recorded before task-owned forced cleanup. **FAIL** |
| First repair `c337231afc47e7cf137f0273a9051daab79b71ae` | Identical public-RPC/file workload | Original patch answered in **308 ms**, but broader CI exposed a restart-reapply regression. This is prior-head runtime evidence, not the final candidate. |
| Final head `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625` | Identical public-RPC/file workload | Original patch answered successfully in **439 ms**, before the credential-restoration step. Clean Gateway shutdown. **PASS** |

All runs used OpenClaw 2026.10.5, Node v26.8.1, macOS arm64, independently owned dependencies, isolated synthetic HOME/state/config/workspace, and distinct free loopback ports between control families. The final build and runtime-postbuild stamps both identify exact `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625` with `inputsClean:true`.

No mocked hot-reload callback, injected exception, fake clock, manually settled receipt, inference call, live Mattermost traffic, operator Gateway change, or TEST/PROD mutation was used in these real Gateway runs.

#### Executed workload

1. Start the full maintained Gateway with `node scripts/run-node.mjs --profile pr177823proof gateway run --port <isolated-port> --verbose`; wait for readiness.
2. Send SIGUSR2 only to that fixture's own Gateway PID; verify **in-process restart** and readiness again.
3. Connect through the real token-authenticated Gateway WebSocket protocol (v4). Read `config.get` for the base hash.
4. Submit one `config.patch` with `response:"summary"`:
   ```json
   {"channels":{"mattermost":{"accounts":{"proof":{"baseUrl":"${PR177823_MATTERMOST_URL}"}}}}}
   ```
   The environment placeholder resolves to the existing synthetic URL; the Mattermost account is disabled.
5. After the actual `config.patch write` log, rotate a task-owned JSON file's synthetic provider key A→B and call the real `secrets.reload {}` RPC. The provider is a custom `proof/proof` model pointing at an unused loopback endpoint; no model turn is sent. Its config uses:
   ```json
   {"apiKey":{"source":"file","provider":"proof","id":"/apiKey"}}
   ```
6. Observe for 2.5 s, restore that **credential file** B→A, and call `secrets.reload {}` again. Do not edit config or send another config-write RPC. The RPC deadline stays 30 s.
7. Join Gateway shutdown. On the fixed head, the original patch had already completed before step 6.

Redacted actual fixed Gateway log; **October 19, 2026, UTC−07:00**:

```text
18:27:43.065 [gateway] received SIGUSR2; restarting
18:27:43.192 [gateway] restart mode: in-process restart
18:27:49.708 [gateway] config.patch write ... changedPaths=channels.mattermost.accounts.proof.baseUrl
18:27:49.971 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 242ms id=proof-4
18:27:50.068 [reload] config source revision 2 accepted (write)
18:27:50.082 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ config.patch 437ms id=proof-3
18:27:52.511 [ws] ⇄ res ✓ secrets.reload 33ms id=proof-5
18:27:52.595 [shutdown] completed cleanly in 77ms
```

The original patch response was `ok:true`, with the expected changed path, `sentinel.persisted:true`, and `requiresRestart:false`. The raw trace contains one config write for the scenario and no later config write. The client observed settlement before the restoration RPC.

Raw local trace SHA-256 values (the redacted excerpt above is the submitted public evidence):

- Parent Gateway log: `4cda5b03044bf2ffb2f385b8c948d97128e7b56b13fbbb2edbab26bf1e66e79b`.
- Initial-head Gateway log: `06845c2cd190360b387e5aa8c082d10a60abbea3771cb33265794ee936afd03a`.
- Prior `c337231` Gateway log: `d37f7c8db6ada211be6733f342b11889d31bb761699d465373d9b0c07302e2c8`.
- Prior `c337231` client event trace: `5bcc6542104caff04cdd1e7b22dce04b6b5e6a47487249bac18be35b81ff0472`.
- Final `b8c13e0` Gateway log: `0134c2ff7a4d1595bb8aaffa1b3e2ef4bba573143f4156eafb8de0653a433b25`.
- Final `b8c13e0` client event trace: `efa09c7c6bb13b20dd266f86d21c419d05e2d94586e962bf559a62a42b76449e`.

These are isolated production-path controls, not a claim that the original tenant's entire environment was replayed. An earlier setup attempt expired while the source launcher was still rebuilding, before any config RPC; it is a setup failure, not a Gateway behavior verdict. The final clean-head run completed normally.

### Focused behavioral regression and checks

- The stable-key and rotated-key cases once added to `server-reload-managed-secrets.test.ts` were dropped on October 28 together with the guard they covered; upstream #183964 carries an equivalent case ("settles an unchanged activation write whose secrets are still unresolved").
- Existing `config-reload.superseded-retry.test.ts` still proves two retained supersessions followed by automatic application. Its hot-reload failures are mocked; this remains focused scheduler proof, not real-Gateway evidence.
- Maintained focused runs: **271 tests passed across 4 affected files**: config-reload plus superseded-retry (134), the complete restart/reload-handler suite (118), and managed secrets (19). After narrowing the guard, the combined run passed the first 252 but exposed the secrets fixture's identity stub; replacing that stub with production's existing `restoreCanonicalSecretRefs` helper made all 19 secrets tests pass (18.05 s wrapper / 12.12 s shard). No assertions, timeouts, or baselines changed. No full Bun/CI pass on the final head is claimed.
- Core typecheck and the canonical Gateway-server test typecheck passed.
- Targeted oxlint, formatter check, `git diff --check`, and the line-cap ratchet passed.
- The first repair's full local maintained `qaRuntime` build passed; the final clean-head source launcher rebuilt and ran its own exact-head runtime and assets.
- The broad changed-test typecheck selector encountered pre-existing advisory root-budget excesses in unrelated graph inventories; the relevant canonical Gateway-server graph was typechecked directly and passed. No inventory, budget, assertion, or baseline was weakened.

### CI and review status

The final repair remains at exact `b8c13e0f9263549628b1c1a3c8d1ba550501d625`. Its [pull-request CI run 39353612934](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39353612934) completed successfully, including the CI workflow's `openclaw/ci-gate`. The separately enforced aggregate status is still **failing**, because the [security review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39356909084/job/118413751307) explicitly reports “awaiting maintainer approval.” A successful policy-workflow execution is not a security approval, and no merge clearance is claimed.

The first repair's [CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39351516553/job/118396992531) timed out both existing `revalidates restart secrets after held promotion and an explicit reapply` cases at 120 s. The maintained CI classifier returned unknown/no comparable main job; the exact job log and a bounded local comparison established this as PR-caused, not inherited: both cases passed on initial `ebfffd5`, while `c337231` locally reproduced the first timeout (the second was interrupted after the same CI failure was established). The broad mismatch guard had incorrectly entered hot publication inside restart-owned reapplication. The final canonicalization comparison retains the restart owner; both cases and the full 118-test handler suite pass without changing those tests.

Prior-head dependency review passed. The [prior security-sensitive review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39351510133/job/118396555176) reports **awaiting maintainer approval** for the credential-owner change. Final-head security approval is still required; it is not bypassed or described as passing.

The local independent-review helper for this repair returned `reviewer_unavailable` without producing a report. The author explicitly approved publication for ClawSweeper review without that local review; that history is unchanged. [ClawSweeper's latest exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177823#issuecomment-6279684646), refreshed October 20 after this evidence update, rated **readiness 5/6, proof 5/6, patch quality 5/6**, with zero actionable findings on final `b8c13e0`. Its remaining checklist item is maintainer security approval. The later successful local review of a downstream integration is not relabeled as an independent review of this PR.

### October 20 refresh integration check

<!-- pr177823-oct20-refresh -->

The complete patch is retained in the downstream [refreshed native source `10f31e19e8a7b5d882c7078c1701bc8a7d3daa9b`](https://github.com/ceckert/openclaw/commit/10f31e19e8a7b5d882c7078c1701bc8a7d3daa9b), integrated with selected upstream main `2d03d5632a69d04181844f85b05d5509240dcc14`.

- On that integrated source, the maintained superseded-retry regression passed (1 test) and the complete managed-secrets suite passed (19 tests). The full native build and production typechecks also passed.
- The production reload modules changed in upstream/refreshed integration while these two regression files remained byte-identical to this PR. These results are **downstream integration evidence**, not a new exact-head upstream CI run or a replay of the original Gateway workload.
- Both real Linux architecture installers, isolated Shared/Builder configuration validation and Doctor checks, and ordinary offline Memory/Skills workers passed for the refreshed packaged source. Those checks exercise packaging/configuration boundaries; they are not credential-rotation recovery proof or a deployed customer check.
- The exact-head parent/fixed Gateway controls above remain the primary behavioral proof. No later deployment, live-provider result, merged security approval, or new-head real supersession trace is inferred from today's build.

### Earlier evidence retained with its limits

The original pre-fix incident remains a failure: after an in-process restart, a source-equivalent Mattermost URL write logged supersession and timed out after 130 s; an unrelated heartbeat edit later released the parked request at 198,627 ms.

Earlier initial-head local smoke completed in 157 ms (Mattermost URL placeholder) and 104 ms (workspace placeholder), with no supersession; a literal-value control was a no-op. A later single-supersession workload recovered on **both** the parent and initial PR head. Those cases are not patch-specific recovery proof and are not substituted for the failing controls above.

prs.title: improve: avoid unnecessary transcript compression projections
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Transcript appends and persisted model-selection rewrites perform a native metadata SELECT even when the compressed frame and required metadata cannot meet the existing storage savings threshold. This removes avoidable preparation introduced with #185730 and #184702, plus the same redundant work for assistant payloads.

## User Impact

Transcript and provider bytes, submitted model selection, restart delivery, and storage format stay unchanged. Payloads that already end in identity storage skip a metadata SELECT. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reject impossible-fit compression candidates before the SELECT using the already-prepared report and a conservative envelope lower bound. The envelope shape is shared with the native encoder, so its minimum is derived rather than hardcoded. Canonical entries retain type/id and any serialized parentId in all three native projections. Candidates that might fit still use those projections and the original final byte check.

No cache, generation, schema, transaction, admission, writer-claim, recovery, or security-effect check changes. PostgreSQL's existing early identity return is unchanged. The independent #186046 request remains a required floor: it computes the first off-thread fingerprint of newly sealed assistant output, then reuses it on later observations.

Production delta: +44 lines; test delta: 0. The shared envelope and lower-bound calculation are the necessary growth. A CI correction makes the three calculated minima a readonly tuple; it does not alter their values or runtime behavior.

## Evidence

### Acceptance rule (published before candidate measurement)

Use frozen v3.1.5 on the exact parent and candidate on the same Mac: 14 synthetic real-WebSocket Gateway turns, child/cron/compaction, idle, shutdown and restart. Count-only pair, one sample per head. Warm turns must remove the attributed initial and rewritten-payload SELECTs, preserve worker requests and active MAIN=0, and all flows must pass. Report phase and per-operation counts; cold and warm stay separate. The 48 synthetic stored/reconstructed variants must have byte-identical final outputs while redundant metadata SELECTs disappear. No latency or CPU-speed claim from the loaded host; per-thread profiles are attribution evidence only.

### Observed counts

Frozen v3.1.5 (37/37 hashes verified), exact parent `7d9677ce36db` versus measured candidate `d3c3d5bea831`. Command: `python3 <frozen-v3.1.5>/measure.py --repo <lane> --sha <head> --repetitions 1 --scratch-root <isolated-internal-temp> --idle-seconds 60`. Final head changes only the type-safe construction of the same minima; the repeated byte-equivalence and owner tests pass. No second full pair was run for that equivalent correction.

| Count | Parent | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Ordinary warm turn SQL / requests / MAIN | 48 / 13 / 0 | 45 / 13 / 0 |
| Ten warm causal phases: SQL median; p95 [min–max] | 48; 54 [48–54] | 45; 48 [45–48] |
| Ten warm causal phases: requests median; p95 [min–max] | 13; 15 [13–15] | 13; 14 [13–14] |
| Ten warm causal phases: MAIN median; p95 [min–max] | 0; 0 [0–0] | 0; 0 [0–0] |
| Whole workload SQL / requests / MAIN | 2,883 / 778 / 98 | 2,872 / 778 / 98 |
| Cold boot SQL / requests / MAIN | 320 / 97 / 51 | 317 / 97 / 51 |
| Connected idle (60 seconds) SQL / requests / MAIN | 92 / 29 / 0 | 92 / 29 / 0 |

Ten warm phases are observations inside one workload per head, not independent timing samples. Each ordinary warm turn removes three SELECTs: initial payload 12→11 SQL, model-selection rewrite 11→10, assistant payload 10→9. Requests stay 1 / 1 / 1 for those operations. Across ten warm phases, payload preparation is 220→200 SQL / 20→20 requests; rewrite preparation is 110→100 / 10→10. Across the full workload these owners save 41 statements (payload 428→400; rewrite 175→162), with unchanged 44 and 16 requests and zero MAIN SQL. The frozen mapper calls the candidate payload operation `batch` instead of `prepareTranscriptPayload` because the removed query changes its observed stack; counts above group the same captured source owner, not the label.

Cold/background counts are disclosed separately: restart-connect rises 42→71 SQL because unchanged `installStatusTracking` contributes 30 statements there; first-turn rises 429→430, idle-settle 98→99, restart-boot 313→314, and restart-first-turn 138→139. These are scheduling/background attribution differences outside the changed owner. Full phase/operation evidence confirms no added SQL or requests from the changed owners. Active MAIN remains zero, and all 14 turns, child/cron/compaction, shutdown and restart pass. This is operation-count evidence; latency, memory and CPU speed are unmeasured. Per-thread profiles were captured (200 parent, 226 candidate profiles) for attribution only.

The 48 synthetic variants produce byte-identical final outputs; native SELECTs fall 48→6 (12 initial, 13 rewritten, 17 assistant cases skipped). The final tuple correction repeats the same result. The work-count regression is red on the exact parent and green on the candidate. All 13 payload boundary tests and 14 prompt-prefix stability tests pass; existing UTF-8 readback, malformed/duplicate-key, predicate rollback, and read-only coverage remains.

Two full isolated Codex P0–P2 reviews are scoped-clean. One allowed delta-only review of the CI TS18048 correction is also scoped-clean. Local changed-file typed lint, formatting, source guards, Madge (0 cycles), worker/T1 (168→168), and dialect ratchets (design 9→8; mechanical 1→1) pass. Local type checks hit the documented internal-store declaration-custody restriction; exact-head CI owns that verdict. Three unchanged production Knip findings match scheduled-main run [41107007551, job 124239589390](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41107007551/job/124239589390): `recordNodeWorkerDescendantsReaped`, `recordNodeWorkerLineageSettled`, and `prepareAgentDatabaseStartupIntegrity`; full-tree scan has zero findings. No new Knip finding.

The initial CI run caught TS18048 in the new minimum array and was corrected before landing. Final-head validation runs in [CI 41119337522](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41119337522); all three PostgreSQL shards must complete successfully before merge. PostgreSQL source approval covers final head `d0c9b036a82ab3b94c704027ef928d75cd89fda6`. No SDK, update, migration, service lifecycle, or plugin-loading surface is touched.

Open-PR overlap: the shared index returns no open main-target PR touching either changed file; no new merge conflicts.

prs.title: fix(plugins): portable plugin-state keys for PostgreSQL
prs.body:
Refs #184862 #188642

## What Problem This Solves

Plugin Doctor migrations can fail while paging existing state on PostgreSQL because the next-page cursor appends NUL to the previous key.

## User Impact

Doctor can continue through existing plugin state on PostgreSQL, including keys that share the previous key's prefix. Plugin test fixtures catch new NUL-containing registration keys before those writes reach PostgreSQL. Existing SQLite legacy-key reads and adoption remain supported.

## Why This Change Was Made

The persisted-key sweep found one additional affected core API: Doctor's bounded range reader manufactures `after + "\0"`, which reaches `assertPluginStateKey` and throws `PLUGIN_STATE_INVALID_INPUT`. Its consumers include Codex binding repair, Telegram offset migration, and Matrix replay-guard migration. The private selector now uses an exclusive SQL lower bound for Doctor continuation pages. No stored keys need rewriting and no public API, schema, retention, or authority policy changes.

The test SDK rejects NUL on registration only, including synchronous and action-bound stores. It keeps the original store objects so native read/operation bindings retain their identity. Deliberate legacy SQLite fixtures seed via the existing Doctor import helper; reads, consumption, and production SQLite validation are unchanged.

The iMessage owner already uses the portable hash and bounded adoption pattern from #184919 / `9b05a64eff6f`. ClickClack's revoked-channel owner was fixed in #188643 and is untouched here. Its binding-store NUL key is only an in-memory reverse index.

## Evidence

The original real PostgreSQL 17.11 regression failed with `PLUGIN_STATE_INVALID_INPUT` on Doctor's second page. The fix passed the same test, preserving `binding:a0` after `binding:a`, and the existing iMessage PostgreSQL regression. The source inventory below is pinned to the original investigation snapshot.

Rebased onto main containing #188643 (`59059122`) and the idle-backend reuse fix (`d107cb81`). The earlier canonical-revocation test correction is already on main and drops out of this diff. The production patch is byte-for-byte unchanged; the maintainer's REVIEW-OK carries forward. The new ClickClack legacy fixture now seeds through the existing Doctor import helper, preserving its real NUL key and fail-closed/adoption assertions. The test allocation is 166 lines: 11 lines formerly deleted by the now-redundant hunk, plus six lines for this explicit legacy seed, account for the increase from 149.

**Fresh local proof:** 23 core plugin-state runtime tests, 11 iMessage tests, and 22 ClickClack persistence tests passed. The ClickClack fixture first failed with `PLUGIN_STATE_INVALID_INPUT` from normal registration, then passed after switching only the seed to Doctor import. Both real PostgreSQL conformance files passed (2 tests, 262.91 seconds). The full ClickClack replay passed 22 tests in 116.46 seconds.

The test-line check reports 6,313,566 lines against a 6,312,524 ceiling: the existing main overage remains exactly 1,042 lines. This PR adds 166 test lines and exactly 166 allocation credit; it does not absorb the inherited excess. Formatting passes. Targeted extension lint passes.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugin-state/plugin-state-store.runtime.test.ts \
  extensions/imessage/src/monitor/recovery-cursor.test.ts \
  extensions/imessage/src/monitor/catchup-startup.test.ts \
  extensions/clickclack/src/discussions/service-state-persistence.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres \
  --connection "$TEST_PG_URL" -- \
  src/infra/state-migrations.plugin-doctor-context.postgres.test.ts \
  extensions/imessage/src/monitor/recovery-cursor.postgres.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Independent isolated Codex review of the original complete patch found no actionable P0–P2 issues. The allocation correction was independently reviewed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. The six-line legacy-fixture correction was also independently reviewed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Simplification keeps the existing private selector as the single owner of exclusive comparison; no new store, migration, cache, or public option.

**Exact-head CI:** [run 41138522684](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41138522684) completed on `b3eae5650e975c6750c09a9c80fb9c5ab23bb9b6`; all three PostgreSQL conformance shards and `security-fast` passed. The sole root failure is `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets`: its test-line count is 6,313,738 against 6,312,704, an excess of 1,034. The tested main parent already has that same 1,034-line excess; this PR contributes exactly 166 lines and 166 allocation credit. [Scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41138060956/job/124345652415) records the existing excess but passes because its delta is zero; two subsequent main test-line deletions account for its 1,036 versus 1,034 difference. All other ratchets passed. The unchanged checker/baseline, exact checkout, logs, and byte-count proof are retained for native inherited-failure qualification. The failed overall CI result is not represented as green.

<details>
<summary>NUL inventory: construction, persistence trace, and classification</summary>

The constructor inventory contains **675 locations across 457 files**: 534 core locations and 141 extension locations. Full per-location tables: [core 1/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188693#issuecomment-6533161920), [core 2/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188693#issuecomment-6533162632), [core 3/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188693#issuecomment-6533163277), [extensions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188693#issuecomment-6533163995).

Scope: runtime source under `extensions/` and `src/`; searched escaped NUL forms (`\\0`, `\\u0000`, `\\x00`, `\\u{0}`), zero codepoint constructors, and raw NUL bytes. Validators, test fixtures, generated renderer assets, and process/file protocols were distinguished from runtime key constructors. No source contained literal raw NUL bytes. prs.title: fix(macos): report the real element when a page hooks Mac tab Inspect
prs.body:
Closes #183929 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Inspect on a Mac tab reports a page-supplied fake element, and the page can detect the inspection, when the page replaces `document.elementFromPoint` or `Element.prototype` methods. ## User Impact Inspect on a Mac tab reports the element actually under the pointer, and page scripts can no longer intercept or observe the lookup. ## Why This Change Was Made `DashboardNativeBrowserHost.inspect` now runs `BrowserInspectScript` with `callAsyncJavaScript(..., contentWorld: .defaultClient)`, the pattern the favicon reader in the same file already uses (#145714). Coordinates are passed as arguments instead of interpolated into the source. The shared script, bridge contract, tab-identity check after the await, and reply shape are unchanged. The client world still reads the shared live DOM, so content the page writes (for example an `aria-label`) is still reported as written; only page JavaScript hooks are excluded.
Root cause `inspect` used `webView.evaluateJavaScript("(\(script))(\(x), \(y))")`, which runs in the page content world. Page-defined replacements for `document.elementFromPoint`, `getAttribute`, or `getBoundingClientRect` therefore answered the inspection and could count the calls. The line arrived with #140988, which does not discuss content worlds. It was the only page-world script call on native browser tabs; the favicon reader already used `.defaultClient`.
## Evidence Packaged the macOS app ad hoc twice from upstream/main 443530a55b7: once with the fix line reverted (main) and once with the fix. Each build ran under the same named profile, connected with `configure-remote --direct-url` to an isolated Gateway started from the app's bundled runtime (private HOME, state, and config; loopback port; token auth). A chat link opened a Mac tab on a loopback test page that replaces `document.elementFromPoint` and `Element.prototype.getAttribute` and prints how many times those hooks ran. Inspect element from the tab menu, hovering the page's `div#real`: | | Hooked page: Inspect tooltip | Hooked page: hook counter after Inspect | Control page (no hooks) | |---|---|---|---| | main | `button#spoofed` 0 × 0, Name "Spoofed by page script" | 18 calls, "page detected the inspection" | `div#real.article` 592 × 538 | | fix | `div#real.article` 592 × 538, Name "Real page content" | 0 calls | `div#real.article` 592 × 538 | | main | fix | |---|---| | | | | | | | | | New real-WebKit test `DashboardNativeBrowserInspectTests` drives the same owner (`DashboardWindowController.nativeBrowser`) on a loopback `DashboardHTTPFixture` page with the same hooks. As a control, the script run in the page world returns the fake element; then `inspect(tabId:x:y:)` is called. - Base (fix line reverted): `node.id == "spoofed"`, `tag == "button"`, hooks called 5 times. Test fails. - Fix: `node.id == "real"`, `tag == "div"`, hooks called 0 times. Test passes. - `DashboardNativeBrowser*` suites: 25 tests in 4 suites pass on the fix, including favicon and tab-ownership tests.
Test output ``` ✘ ... Expectation failed: node["id"] as? String == "real" → "spoofed" ✘ ... Expectation failed: node["tag"] as? String == "div" → "button" ✘ ... Expectation failed: hookCalls == 0 → 5 ✘ Test run with 1 test in 1 suite failed after 1.352 seconds with 3 issues. ✔ Test "inspection reports the real element when the page replaces the DOM lookups" passed after 0.957 seconds. ✔ Test run with 25 tests in 4 suites passed after 1.883 seconds. ```
Checks: `swiftformat --lint` clean on both files; `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` reports only the existing `DashboardManager.swift` `file_length` violation, which is also on main; `git diff --check` clean. Environment: macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.1. Production delta +6/-2; test delta +52/-0. Merge risk: two-way door; reverting restores the previous evaluation world with no state or config migration. Blast radius is the Mac tab Inspect request.

prs.title: fix(macos): Settings 404 with remote Control UI base path
prs.body:
Closes #164596 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: the macOS dashboard and Settings return HTTP 404 when the app connects to a remote Gateway whose Control UI is served under `gateway.controlUi.basePath` and the connection address has no path (SSH tunnel, or a direct `ws://host:port` URL). ## User Impact Settings and the dashboard open under the Gateway's Control UI mount without editing the connection address. Both the app and the Gateway need this change; a mixed pair behaves as before. ## Why This Change Was Made The app cannot know the mount. SSH endpoints are always `ws://127.0.0.1:`, and remote mode deliberately fell back to `/` because the Gateway never advertised its base path (#15862 fixed local mode only). hello-ok already says where the Control UI lives through `controlUiUrl` (only with `publicOrigin`) and `snapshot.controlUiIdentityUrl` (only for HTTPS sign-in). This adds the bare mount beside them as the optional `controlUiBasePath`. On the app side, `GatewayEndpointStore.dashboardURL` stays the one place that picks the path, now using the advertised mount for remote URLs without a path. It is read from the same current hello as the identity URL. `config.get` (operator.read) can return the same value, but opening the dashboard reads only the hello, with no discovery RPCs (`GatewayConnectionDashboardIdentityTests` asserts this), and the Control UI location already lives in hello.
Root cause and rejected alternatives - With `basePath` set, the Gateway routes `/` outside the Control UI (`src/gateway/control-ui-routing.ts:92`), so `GET /` is 404 while WebSocket upgrades at `/` still succeed. That is why the node stays connected while the dashboard fails. - Redirecting `/` to the base path on the Gateway does not help: Settings appends its route to the dashboard's current URL, so it would still request `/settings/appearance`. - Keeping a path from `gateway.remote.url` in SSH mode does not help: the SSH editor writes the URL without a path, and nothing documents one there.
## Evidence Ad-hoc macOS builds from `c258ea68c3b` (main) and `c258ea68c3b` plus this diff, each against an isolated Gateway (`controlUi.basePath: "/__openclaw__"`) with remote URL `ws://127.0.0.1:28791` (no path). Settings opened from the app menu; screenshots are the dashboard window only. | Main | This PR | |---|---| | | | | "Dashboard unavailable. The Gateway returned HTTP 404 (Not Found)." at `http://127.0.0.1:28791/` | Settings → Appearance under `/__openclaw__/` | This PR, same connection, Settings → This Mac (the page blocked in the report): Request trace through a logging proxy (asset requests omitted): - Main, remote URL `ws://127.0.0.1:28792`: `GET / -> 404`. - Fix, same URL: `GET /__openclaw__/settings/appearance -> 200`, dashboard WebSocket upgrades at `/__openclaw__/`. - Control, `ws://127.0.0.1:28792/__openclaw__/`: Settings loads at `/__openclaw__/settings/appearance` on both main and the fix. - Fixed app against the main Gateway: unchanged 404 at `/`.
Fix run, root URL (asset requests omitted) ``` WS upgrade / HTTP GET /__openclaw__/ -> 200 HTTP GET /__openclaw__/control-ui-config.json -> 401 HTTP GET /__openclaw__/settings/appearance -> 200 WS upgrade /__openclaw__/ HTTP GET /__openclaw__/control-ui-config.json -> 200 -- dashboard window AXWebArea: Appearance — OpenClaw ```
Main run, root URL ``` WS upgrade / HTTP GET / -> 404 -- dashboard window AXStaticText: Dashboard unavailable AXStaticText: The Gateway returned HTTP 404 (Not Found). AXStaticText: http://127.0.0.1:28792/ ```
**Upgrade from latest stable (v2026.10.8)** `openclaw@2026.10.8` from npm in an isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` with `gateway.controlUi.basePath: "/__openclaw__"`, settings saved through the stable CLI. The macOS app from this PR saved a remote profile at the bare `ws://127.0.0.1:` and paired. Then stable was stopped, this PR's `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` ran on the same state, this PR's Gateway started, and the app was relaunched on the saved profile without reconfiguring it.
Before → after on the same state and saved profile ```text Stable 2026.10.8 Gateway hello-ok: {"serverVersion":"2026.10.8","protocol":4,"controlUiUrl":null,"controlUiBasePath":null} macOS app, saved profile, Settings…: WS upgrade / HTTP GET / -> 404 AXStaticText: Dashboard unavailable AXStaticText: The Gateway returned HTTP 404 (Not Found). paired devices: [4526d030… openclaw-macos node]; state schema 20 Upgrade: this PR's `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive` -> exit 0 Saved pre-migration SQLite backup ... schema=34, expected=34, pending=0 gateway block identical: True ui identical: True {'seamColor': '#FF4500'} paired devices: [4526d030… openclaw-macos node]; state schema 34 This PR's Gateway on the upgraded state hello-ok: {"protocol":4,"controlUiUrl":null,"controlUiBasePath":"/__openclaw__"} macOS app relaunched on the same saved profile, Settings… (asset requests omitted): WS upgrade / HTTP GET /__openclaw__/ -> 200 HTTP GET /__openclaw__/settings/appearance -> 200 WS upgrade /__openclaw__/ HTTP GET /__openclaw__/control-ui-config.json -> 200 AXWebArea: Appearance — OpenClaw ```
Saved connections and settings survive: the `gateway` and `ui` config blocks are identical, the paired Mac device is still paired after the schema 20 → 34 migration, and the saved pathless profile opens Settings under the mount after the upgrade. Doctor's other config additions and the migration come from main and are the same without this change. Before the upgrade the same app still gets 404, since v2026.10.8 does not advertise the mount. In an earlier v2026.10.7 run, the stable CLI's `gateway call health`, `status` and `device.pair.list` against this PR's Gateway all exited 0, so older clients accept the new optional hello field. Tests: `connect-hello.update-scope.test.ts` mount-path case fails on main (`expected undefined to be '/__openclaw__'`) and passes with the fix; both hello test files pass (56 tests). `remote dashboards open under the Control UI mount advertised by hello` fails with the old `/` branch and passes with the fix; the `GatewayEndpointStoreTests`, `GatewayConnectionControlUIAuthTests`, `DashboardTokenlessRouteTests`, `DashboardReconnectTests` and `GatewayConnectionDashboardIdentityTests` suites pass (92 tests). `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, oxlint, format check, SwiftFormat, `pnpm protocol:check` and `git diff --check` pass. SwiftLint `--strict` reports `file_length` on `DashboardManager.swift`, which is already over the limit on main (1505 lines). Production delta +46/-15 (including the `#if DEBUG` test factory hunk); test delta +55/-1. Merge risk: two-way door; the field is additive with no wire-version bump, older apps ignore it and older Gateways omit it. Blast radius is remote dashboards whose connection URL has no path.

prs.title: fix(android): preserve accepted work when ending Talk
prs.body:
Closes #188134

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes accepted agent work being canceled when an Android phone user taps End Talk.

## User Impact

End Talk stops listening and playback while accepted work continues and its answer remains available in chat. To cancel work instead, say “cancel” before ending the call or use the chat run’s existing Stop control.

Realtime detachment requires a Gateway advertising `talk-session-close-disposition`; older Gateways retain their legacy aborting close. Other clients’ Stop behavior is unchanged. No new setting, permission, protocol field, or UI control is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ending an audio conversation should not silently discard work the agent already accepted. Reuse the phone’s existing capture-cleanup path, which already detaches during backgrounding and mode changes, rather than maintain a separate abort override for End Talk. Native Talk keeps its existing accepted-work behavior.

## Evidence

- Reproduced through the actual Android `NodeRuntime` and relay WebSocket boundary on base `563ba501dced074d9d282fb3a4cb48cfc31bcf9e`: the updated regression failed with **expected detach, observed abort** specifically for End Talk.
- With the fix, `:app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest` passed **131 tests**: all **112 TalkModeManagerTest** cases and **19 RealtimeAgentCoordinatorTest** cases, with zero failures, errors, or skips. These include End Talk/mode-change close requests, capture retirement, native accepted-work preservation, explicit abort, legacy capability behavior, and voice cancellation. Gradle completed in **47 seconds**.
- Gateway `server.talk-consult-history.test.ts -t "settles close disposition"` passed **9 selected scenarios** in **84.75 seconds** overall. This exercises the real close/admission/history owners with fixed inference/provider fixtures: detach leaves accepted work running and publishes its answer; explicit/default abort cancels it. It also covers work completed before close, spoken replacement, a second consult, and uncertain transcript append outcomes. The 13 unrelated cases were filtered, not claimed passing.
- Android `:app:ktlintCheck` passed (**17 seconds**); production and test Kotlin compiled as part of the focused Gradle run. Both changed docs passed MDX and formatting checks; `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh independent **AutoReview**, Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, medium reasoning, **P0–P2**, reviewed the complete local candidate against the pinned base with relevant unchanged lifecycle/cancellation context: **scoped-clean, no actionable findings**. Only an American English spelling correction followed. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable within this task’s permitted source/skill scope, so the documented fallback route was used; hosted ClawSweeper has acknowledged the PR for review; its review is pending.
- Simplification: removes the phone-only close-disposition override and its unused plumbing. Production Kotlin **+2/-8**; regression test **+4/-4**. No new state or parallel lifecycle owner.

**Proof limits:** this is Android runtime/WebSocket and isolated Gateway boundary proof, not a newly installed physical-phone call or live-provider audio test. No rendered UI changes are included. Broad PR CI is separate from these focused passing checks.

Reported by @jeffjhunter in #188134. Prepared at the request of @RomneyDa.

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: fix(queue): keep system direct-command corrections as followups
prs.body:
Related: #188514

## What Problem This Solves

Browser corrections to a system-owned direct command were incorrectly steered into that command instead of becoming followup input.

## User Impact

System direct commands in a parent conversation retain followup behavior. Owners can still steer active loop/cron executions and visible child sessions, with live incoming authorization and the incumbent's existing execution permissions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The owner-guidance exception used a broad native-input attribution helper that also matched completion reports. Qualify scheduled executions and canonical child sessions at the existing continuation boundary instead. The subagent fixture now uses real child identity and parent lineage without invented inter-session provenance; uncapped loop coverage prevents dependence on an optional tool-policy cap. Restore the original direct-command followup expectation, which #188624 changed to steering while this repair was being validated.

Production grows by five lines to distinguish these execution contracts. No new configuration, state, migration, or steering path is added.

## Evidence

- Attribution: the unchanged system direct-command case passes on `14e213feadc2` and fails on `15db8cc635ff` with `expected 'steered' to be 'followup'`. The corrected child fixture also fails on unchanged main with `Compatible requester input was dispatched as a separate turn`.
- All 99 focused tests passed: 30 Gateway cases (28 custody plus both direct-command cases), 17 cron cases, 14 prompt-prefix cases, and 38 import-closure/PR-wrapper checks. The serial wrapper took 1266.22s on the loaded local host; Gateway group wall time was 685.34s. These are test costs, not performance measurements.
- The first tooling attempt exposed an outdated local dependency (`fs-safe` 0.26.14 versus the lockfile's 0.26.15); a frozen-lockfile install resolved it before the successful run.
- `check:changed --staged --timed`: 34 of 35 steps passed, including production types, affected Gateway type graphs, lint, formatting, database guards, import cycles, and all dead-code scans. The remaining test-type graph reports TS2559 at `src/sessions/session-controller.message-join.test.ts:591` in a pre-existing uncommitted local edit excluded from this PR. The same error reproduces with this production repair removed; the unrelated file is preserved. The final exact-head PR CI run verified the committed tree successfully.
- After integrating main `9db820e3174a` and restoring the original system-command assertion, both direct-command cases passed again (213.63s Vitest / 235.30s wrapper). Codex autoreview of the complete final diff is scoped-clean through P2, with no actionable findings and successful final source verification.
- Synthetic Gateway/mock-provider proof. No production runtime was changed or load-tested.

The first PR CI attempt (`41137345305`, head `98d292159e60`) found four net added test lines above the existing ceiling. The fixture was consolidated without removing cases or assertions; net test growth is now zero and no budget/baseline changed. All 28 custody tests passed again (400.47s Vitest / 421.05s wrapper), and refreshed Codex autoreview remained scoped-clean through P2. A local staged full-tree ratchet scan was stopped after ten minutes without a result; the final exact-head CI run passed that check and every required gate.

Final exact-head CI: [run 41139718659](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41139718659) succeeded for `dcb6d912b1df4f978e52d1bdf6087662bfcf3bba`, including all three PostgreSQL conformance shards. Required CI, security, and dependency gates passed; no inherited-failure exception was needed.

prs.title: docs(google-vertex): add Google Vertex AI provider setup guide
prs.body: Related PRs: #118745, #87800, #83971 Related issues: #56253, #85864, #79595, #79837, #11413, #49191, #50053, #52476, #48910, #77643, #55572, #53566, #9729 ## What Problem This Solves OpenClaw has no documentation for the `google-vertex` provider. Users who want to run Gemini models through Google Cloud Vertex AI have no setup path to follow: the provider has no onboarding wizard entry, and the only mention was a couple of lines on the Google (Gemini) page. Anyone on Google Cloud hit trial-and-error to get authentication, environment variables, model selection, and the gateway working together. ## Why This Change Was Made Vertex AI is a distinct provider in the bundled Google plugin that authenticates via Application Default Credentials, but it is setup-only (no wizard), so it needs a clear manual path. This adds a dedicated provider guide documenting the real, working flow on current `main`: authenticate with ADC (gcloud user credentials or a service-account key), set the model in `openclaw.json` and environment variables in `~/.openclaw/.env`, verify, provision the gateway, and use the agent. Every step was validated against live behavior rather than assumptions. This PR documents the Vertex AI ADC behavior shipped in #118745, and ships the documentation portion of the earlier, broader #87800. ## User Impact Users can now follow a single, accurate page to get Gemini models running through Vertex AI end to end. The guide covers both auth sources (gcloud ADC with auto-detected credentials, and service-account keys), where each environment variable must live (notably that `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` must go in `~/.openclaw/.env`, not `openclaw.json`), the bundled model catalog, verification via `openclaw models status`, and troubleshooting. The Google (Gemini) page now cross-links to it, and it appears in the providers sidebar as "Google (Vertex AI)". ## Evidence Verified end to end on a GCE VM against `main`: - **gcloud ADC path:** `gcloud config set project` + `gcloud auth application-default login` + project/location in `~/.openclaw/.env` → `openclaw models status` shows `google-vertex ... source=gcloud adc` → `openclaw tui` responds via Vertex AI. - **Service-account path:** key created via `gcloud iam service-accounts keys create`, `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` set in `~/.openclaw/.env` → resolves and responds. - **Detection is real:** `gcloud auth application-default revoke` flips `models status` to `[indeterminate]` ("auth readiness could not be confirmed"). - **Docs checks:** `pnpm check:docs` passes (format, markdownlint, MDX, i18n-glossary, link audit — 0 issues). --- **Rendered provider page: `/providers/google-vertex`** --- **Bundled model catalog: `openclaw models list --provider google-vertex`** --- **gcloud ADC configured: `openclaw models status` resolves (`source=gcloud adc`)** --- **Service-account key configured: `openclaw models status` resolves the same way** --- **Gateway provisioned without changing Vertex AI config: `openclaw onboard --auth-choice skip`** --- **Agent responds end to end via Vertex AI** ## Metadata-server ADC: tested, not currently supported end to end ClawSweeper flagged that the guide omits metadata-server / Workload Identity ADC. I tested this end to end on a GCE VM, and it does **not** currently work through the full agent request path, so the guide intentionally stays file-based. **Repro (GCE VM):** - Attached service account with Editor + the `cloud-platform` scope; `aiplatform.googleapis.com` enabled. - No credential file (`gcloud auth application-default revoke`; `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` unset). - `~/.openclaw/.env` sets only `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION`. - `model.primary = google-vertex/gemini-3.5-flash`; gateway restarted (confirmed healthy and listening on 18789). **Result:** `openclaw models status` shows `[indeterminate]` (expected), and sending a message in the TUI fails before any request reaches Vertex: ``` No API key found for provider "google-vertex". ... | missing-provider-auth ``` **Root cause:** the credential is resolved synchronously by `resolveGoogleVertexConfigApiKey` -> `hasGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserAdcSync` (`extensions/google/vertex-adc.ts`), which requires a credentials file. With metadata-only identity there is no file, so it returns undefined and the request is rejected with `missing-provider-auth` before the transport runs. The `google-auth-library` metadata fallback in the transport is real but is never reached on this path. The no-file metadata regression test drives the transport directly with a mocked `GoogleAuth`, so it passes without going through the auth gate and does not cover the end-to-end agent path. **Conclusion:** this guide's walkthrough covers the automatic file-based discovery paths (gcloud user ADC, service-account key), and Troubleshooting links metadata-only GCE/GKE hosts to the stored-profile sentinel route (`openclaw models auth paste-api-key --provider google-vertex` with `gcp-vertex-credentials`) documented on `/providers/google` in #150593. ## Vertex AI Express API key: intentionally out of scope Review cycles have asked both to document and to remove `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` on this page. It is deliberately not covered, because the transport cannot perform an express-mode request. `buildGoogleVertexRequestUrl` (`extensions/google/transport-stream.ts:434-446`) always emits a project- and location-scoped path and throws when either value is unset, while Vertex AI in express mode requires the global `aiplatform.googleapis.com` endpoint with no `projects` or `locations` segment. `model.baseUrl` overrides only the origin, so no config reaches that shape. The route also has no test coverage for `google-vertex` (every Vertex transport test uses the ADC marker `gcp-vertex-credentials`) and was never verified live. Per the P1 note in the review, adding endpoint-specific operator instructions without that proof would be wrong, so the guide stays scoped to ADC, as its summary, intro, and auth bullet already state.

prs.title: fix(ui): catch up Ask OpenClaw from the transcript after reconnects
prs.body:
## Problem
When the Control UI socket drops, Gateway turns keep running and their replies are
stored, but Ask OpenClaw could fail to recover. A drop during the rejoin left
"Retry to continue this setup" on screen with sending disabled. A Safari wake replaces
the client, so the agent list reload cancelled catch-up. A reply finishing behind the
rejoin was never read, and the early history read removed the running turn's message.

## Solution
- Catch-up stays owed until chat is available again, and restarts if interrupted.
- After an interruption, the input-free rejoin queues behind any running turn; the
  transcript is read after it. Turn outcome clears only once that read succeeds, and
  a failed read retries once.
- The history read before the rejoin is skipped for an interrupted turn, so the sent
  message stays visible.
- Reconnects no longer set an error. While chat is unavailable, a pending turn shows
  a spinner with a screen-reader-only "Reconnecting…" status and no visible text.
- `dismissQuestion` moves to `transcript.ts` to keep the store within the line limit.

## Impact
User turns are never resubmitted. Reconnects with nothing pending still do a history
read only, and unanswered question cards keep their state. Failures that aren't
connection failures still show their error and Retry. The unused
`custodian.connectionChanged` string is removed.

Known gaps: a socket that never fires `close` waits for wake detection or the request
timeout; a message that never reached the Gateway disappears on catch-up without a
notice.

## Evidence

Tests: `src/pages/custodian` and `src/lib/agents` pass (27 files, 276 tests), plus
lint, UI typecheck, i18n verify and the controller guard. New coverage runs each
scenario for a socket close and a client replacement, using the real agent capability,
and checks that the spinner is the only visible reconnect indicator in the panel.
`pnpm test ui/src/pages/custodian/custodian-session-store.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`:
17s wall. No new test lanes. CI seconds not measured.

Not tested on a physical device or against a live Gateway.

prs.title: fix(ui): recover focused Gateway desktops when Host Desktop is off
prs.body:
Continues #178405 from the original RoboClaw contribution, at Vítor's request. This personal-fork PR starts from the original PR's exact published head `83ac2b2d3763fb005304fc2e3eb32256f69b19b6`, preserving its commit ancestry, authorship and recorded evidence. Review and CI results below retain their original revision and do not imply a fresh qualification of this PR.

Follow-up to #177888. Related: #174368 (already closed).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: focused Gateway Desktop windows show an unavailable notice and empty picker when Host Desktop is disabled, instead of the setup recovery already available in chat.

## User Impact

Explicit Gateway desktops and focused sessions targeting that Gateway now reuse setup guidance, authorized enablement, and same-host retry. Back is available during setup/sign-in and other nonconnected focused states, including the unselected picker.

Desktop remains admin-only. Enablement requires the existing config authority and explicit action; OpenClaw does not change OS sharing permissions. No new settings, schema, migration, or setup owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

#177888 fixed chat recovery but deliberately left focused windows unchanged. This follow-up wires those missing entry points into the same setup and runtime-config owners rather than introducing another Systems-navigation flow.

The quality follow-up adds only a small admission regression: an advertised Desktop method must still reject a non-admin connection, offer no Enable action, dispatch no config patch/desktop observation, and retain Back. Production code is unchanged by that follow-up.

## Evidence

**Latest CI repair:** `83ac2b2d3763fb005304fc2e3eb32256f69b19b6`, tree `9cb472af62e872681ee6ade63f6a12201ebac5b3`, a normal child of the approved copy head `b467669acd42a56213f54a91675e88ea5b60f680`. Complete remote tree, parent, four-file delta and human co-author credit were verified.

- **Attachment defect reproduced and repaired:** a pending original-file download was cancelled when a same-session metadata refresh recreated its destination callbacks. The download resolver and attachment-input callbacks now retain identity within their existing host/read lifetime. Snapshot fields still refresh normally; no cancellation, destination, policy, authentication or live-connection guard was removed.
- **Deterministic regression:** the existing file-navigation scenario holds the original HTTP bytes, publishes a same-session title change and commits that frame before releasing the download. It fails at the same missing `Remove notes.md` chip on the pre-repair production code and passes after the producer repair. A plain focused replay had passed before this ordering was controlled; that replay was not counted as a fix.
- **Context test corrected to the actual contract:** the production shell intentionally warms lazy code at idle. The scenario now explicitly waits for that real code preload, then verifies that opening Details still performs **zero context-report RPCs**. It retains the later exactly-one report request and displayed breakdown checks. No idle warmup was disabled and no timeout, retry or skip was added.
- **25/25 browser cases passed** across both failed files and the original Desktop document flow. **71/71 existing consumer tests passed**, including real destination/connection/policy/auth changes, hidden/unmounted readers and pending-read handoff/retirement. Both scoped type graphs, typed lint, formatting and whitespace passed.
- **Fresh independent four-file P0–P3 review: scoped-clean**, with the complete patch and unchanged authority/idle-owner context supplied intact. The review was static; it is separate from the executed tests and earlier review scopes.
- **Automatically triggered repair CI:** [run 40975725218](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40975725218), pending at this update. No manual CI rerun or dispatch was used. Prior CI outcomes remain bound to their original heads.

The approved Desktop copy, buttons, layout, styles, setup behavior and earlier source history are unchanged by this repair. There is no new public API, config option, permission rule or state owner. The production growth retains operation bindings at the existing producers instead of weakening the consumer's cancellation guards.

prs.title: feat(memory): configure shared workspace output modes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In a shared workspace, memory-core's exact `0600` creation mode prevents the operator's group and inherited ACL entries from reading newly generated memories.

Closes #185191. Thanks @rbartoli for the report and scoped proposal.

## User Impact

Operators can opt into `agents.defaults.workspaceFileMode`, with an `agents.entries.<agentId>.workspaceFileMode` override, for new `DREAMS.md`, `MEMORY.md`, and `memory/dreaming/` reports. Accepted octal strings are `"0600"`, `"0620"`, `"0640"`, and `"0660"`.

Unset retains exact `0600`. Existing files retain their modes. Daily memory, the session corpus, credentials, configuration, logs, and other state retain their existing private policy. Sharing can expose generated memory to the configured group or ACL users; operators still provision directory traversal and default ACLs separately.

## Why This Change Was Made

The writing host snapshots its own umask and passes the exact effective mode to the existing fs-safe atomic writer. Remote transports carry the configured octal policy rather than a gateway-computed mode, so `"0660"` under remote umask `022` becomes `0640` even when the gateway uses a different mask. Guarded publication, cancellation, existing-mode preservation, and directory-permission behavior remain in place. The fs-safe dependency is unchanged.

One helper owns conversion from configured policy to an effective mode; the remaining production growth carries that policy through existing producers and transports (+125 net production lines). The two-field config-surface increase is intentional for the approved default and per-agent setting. The regression-test allocation is exactly 187 net lines for validation, host masks, actual file modes, remote transport, and private exclusions.

## Evidence

The added regressions failed on the original base: configuration rejection, missing policy inheritance, local and remote `0600` instead of `0640`, and loss of the pre-await umask snapshot. The pre-rebase implementation then passed 121 focused tests across eight files (one Linux-only ACL skip), all three typecheck scopes, core and extension targeted lint, the full build including SDK exports and Control UI, and two independent P0–P2 reviews. Cold preparation dominated the 892.62-second test run and 31-minute build; the new mode test bodies took 1.83 seconds. An initial extension-lint declaration-preparation timeout was followed by a successful run after the build populated declarations.

The current head `bf08221ab46a20d72fba90b2eac8dc1fbade270a` integrates main `5587ede1c4c`. Its affected schema, mode, dreaming and DREAMS-file tests pass: 74 tests across four files, with one Linux ACL skip (4.50 seconds for schema; 219.20 seconds for the memory shard). Extension typechecking and generated-config verification pass. The inspected range diff changes only generated metadata and the import needed to retain main's shared fallback constant; feature logic and tests are unchanged. The small phase-type extraction is type-only and passes the file-size gate.

The test-line gate remains red with inherited debt. The exact hosted CI base `528b92792ed041366e037d084041369f93d244a7` has 6,313,574 lines / 6,312,538 ceiling (1,036 over). Tested merge `c9ab4f1127b5a73f4e25e7426c66eb3d324616f9` has 6,313,761 lines / 6,312,725 ceiling, the same 1,036 debt. Both count and ceiling increase by exactly this PR's 187-line allocation. The shared scalar, checker and shrink helper are unchanged. Local rebase proof against `5587ede` independently retained its baseline's 1,039-line debt. This is an inherited failure, not a passing gate.

Hosted Linux default-ACL proof passed on this exact head in [CI job 124345538003](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41137951204/job/124345538003): all six workspace mode cases passed, including `retains inherited named ACL access in the file mask`, the real client/worker transport, and the pre-await umask snapshot. Existing atomic-write, malformed-byte, cancellation and worker-lifetime proof is retained from the pre-rebase run. [CI run 41137951204](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41137951204), attempt 1, completed on this exact head: 54 jobs passed, 25 were skipped, and the inherited test-line source job plus its downstream CI gate failed. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards passed. The automatic job-name classifier marks the ratchet new because a net-zero main change tolerates existing debt; the exact source/count comparison above proves this PR leaves that debt unchanged. Landing uses the native attributed-failure route; no CI rerun or assertion weakening.

prs.title: feat(android): mute the Talk microphone without ending the conversation
prs.body:
Closes #187721

## What Problem This Solves

Android Talk users need to pause microphone input without ending the conversation or interrupting the assistant's work and response audio.

## User Impact

A separate, accessible microphone button beside End Talk lets users mute and unmute input while keeping the call, accepted work, and reply audio active. Mute remains set across Talk restarts in the app process until explicitly unmuted; standalone push-to-talk still works after ending Talk.

Realtime mute sends silence while the recording session stays open, so Android's microphone indicator may remain visible. Native Talk finishes already-recognized words before pausing recognition. No new permission, configuration, dependency, protocol, or release-version change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ending Talk and muting reply playback are different operations from muting input. Keep input mute owned by `TalkModeManager` and expose that state through the existing runtime/view model to the actual ChatScreen control. Reuse the capture ownership lock to retire native recognition and keep queued microphone audio from crossing a mute/unmute toggle at socket enqueue. Preserve upstream detach/abort behavior.

The patch excludes selected-chat routing, Health Connect, SMS, version bumps, and the unrelated chat-metadata warning repair. It adds no parallel capture manager: the necessary growth is one input state plus audio-frame invalidation and the control/proof. Production Kotlin delta: +132/-20; tests: +253/-1; README: +1.

## Evidence

- Built and tested against pinned main `6c672d42f2dec42b7917f34dfe5ae8157b9b0abb`; Initial Kotlin test/review head `750c924b8ec5e95018239108fd9f85382d936a7c`; current head `3d852cea86599dcabc6df2f97dababf59ed842bc` adds only the generated source inventory entries described below.
- `:app:ktlintCheck` passed. `:app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest` passed **121 tests**, zero failures/errors/skips: all 118 `TalkModeManagerTest` cases and three targeted `ChatComposerLayoutTest` cases covering the real toggle, accessible state, and 320dp/French/large-font controls. Gradle build/check wall time: **4m 11s**; recorded suite times: **17.745s** and **12.297s**, respectively. These are Kotlin/Gradle suites, not `pnpm test` suites. The completed updated-head CI result is summarized below.
- Transport checks exercise microphone PCM replacement with silence, a read spanning a toggle, and queued audio waiting at the actual socket enqueue. Native/relay checks preserve admitted work and playback; push-to-talk checks cover muted admission and standalone use after Talk ends.
- The requester initially liked the feature during real voice use on the custom 2026.10.7 phone build, but subsequently reported that muting seemed to silence assistant playback as well. That observation is not yet reproduced or attributed; do not treat output preservation as accepted device proof. Source inspection confirms separate microphone and speaker controls, but does not establish what happened on that phone. This current-main port has not separately been installed on a device; do not treat the synthetic screenshots as live audio proof.
- Fresh independent Codex read-only review of the final mute-only snapshot against the pinned base found no actionable likely/high-impact findings. CLI AutoReview was attempted but unavailable because OpenAI returned HTTP 401; it is **not** counted as a passing AutoReview. `git diff --check` passed. Full Android framework/resource lint and broad hosted CI are not claimed passing.

### CI localization correction

The initial [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40892555492) passed Android third-party, Play, Wear, both native-accessibility jobs, and Kotlin style. Its one underlying failure was `native-i18n`: the source extraction inventory omitted the five new mute strings. `openclaw/ci-gate` reflected that failure.

Reproduced the same inventory failure locally before the repair. Ran `pnpm native:i18n:baseline`, which added exactly five generator-owned entries to `apps/.i18n/native-source.json`. `pnpm native:i18n:verify` now passes, including Android and Apple source safety checks; `pnpm android:i18n:gen` regenerates the Android lookup/resources with the new labels. Kotlin source and tests are unchanged, so the earlier focused test and independent review evidence remains scoped to that unchanged code. The [updated-head native-i18n job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40899576510/job/123538746357) now passes on GitHub for `3d852cea86599dcabc6df2f97dababf59ed842bc`; that run is now complete. Android third-party and Wear tests, ktlint, both native-accessibility jobs, and native-i18n passed. The [`android-test-play` job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40899576510/job/123538748350) exceeded its 20-minute unit-test limit, which failed `openclaw/ci-gate`. No failing assertion was established in the inspected log, and the empty failure-classification table does not establish an inherited failure. The timeout remains under investigation; no blind CI rerun was requested.

Translated dictionaries and derived locale metadata remain owned by the serialized post-merge locale refresh ([publication policy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6c672d42f2dec42b7917f34dfe5ae8157b9b0abb/.agents/skills/openclaw-pr-maintainer/references/landing.md#open-or-update-the-pr)); this correction commits the source-owned inventory, not hand-edited translations. The new labels can use English fallback until that refresh.

### Current-head phone testing artifact and CI follow-up — October 30

An [unofficial contributor test APK](https://github.com/davelutztx/openclaw/releases/tag/pr-187722-phone-test-3d852cea8659) is available from the exact
clean head `3d852cea86599dcabc6df2f97dababf59ed842bc`. The download page includes the APK SHA-256,
signature/build manifest, and [route-specific test instructions](https://github.com/davelutztx/openclaw/releases/download/pr-187722-phone-test-3d852cea8659/TESTING.md).
It is phone-only `thirdPartyDebug` (`ai.openclaw.app.debug`), not an official
release; no private Health/Samsung/selected-chat/lock-screen patches or version
source changes are included. No device installation was performed.
The unchanged upstream version label is `2026.8.2-debug`; identify
the artifact by commit and SHA-256, not the version label.

The new local build also passed **121 focused Play tests**, zero failures/errors/skips
(118 TalkModeManager cases and three ChatComposerLayout cases), with artifact
signature, CRC, manifest, compiled mute setters, and exact commit/timestamp
verified. This does not replace full hosted CI or physical audio proof.

**Physical acceptance remains pending.** The [current review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187722#issuecomment-6500004345)
found no actionable code findings but requires a device recording or redacted
runtime trace for **both native and realtime** mute/unmute during active answers,
showing suppressed new input, uninterrupted audio, and completed accepted work.
The testing packet includes that exact scope and a result template. The maintainer
decision on the feature's control, silence-based realtime behavior, and mute
lifetime also remains open. No new review was requested without that proof.

**CI investigation:** the [timed-out Play job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40899576510/job/123538748350)
left about **9m50s** after launching the app test JVM, whereas the
[previous passing Play job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40892555492/job/123513827300)
needed **10m32s** and passed 3,658 tests. Those heads differ only in the five
localization inventory entries, not Android code/tests/Gradle/CI. Current-head
third-party CI passed 3,776 tests in about 9m19s after test JVM launch.
This strongly supports inadequate whole-job headroom; failed-only logging and
skipped timeout reports mean an individual stall is not ruled out. The
[full findings](https://github.com/davelutztx/openclaw/releases/download/pr-187722-phone-test-3d852cea8659/CI-NOTES.md) propose a **test-play-only 30-minute
budget** while preserving all other budgets, followed by one result on the changed
head. Current upstream main still uses 20 minutes for this job. **No workflow
edit, blind CI rerun, inherited-failure classification, or green-gate claim was made.**

### Remaining before merge

- Supply runtime evidence on this current-main Android port for native and realtime mute/unmute during an active answer, including input suppression and continued playback. The older custom-build user report and synthetic UI captures do not establish that evidence.
- Obtain the maintainer product decision on the separate input control, silence-based realtime mute, and mute lifetime across Talk restarts. The author's requested feature and phone acceptance are not represented as upstream maintainer approval.

### Synthetic ChatScreen captures

The images below come from the real ChatScreen Robolectric fixture at 320dp, not a mock-drawn control or a live provider call. They demonstrate the control/status and layout only.

![Android Talk before the feature, with End Talk but no separate microphone mute](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f97c2d5-51c7-4f04-861e-ef117d1d4ea4)

The before capture used an isolated checkout of the exact pinned base, with a temporary UI-only proof asserting that the microphone toggle was absent (1 test passed; capture build wall time 3m 15s). No baseline proof code or generated images are included in the source branch.

**After: microphone enabled**
