prs.title: fix(tools): keep MCP tool names unique for non-ASCII inputs
prs.body:
## Problem
 
`_sanitize_name` replaces every character outside `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` with `_`.
A fully non-ASCII name such as `"获取天气"` collapses to `"_"` after sanitization,
causing silent name collisions when multiple such tools are registered from the
same MCP server.
 
## Changes
 
- Extract `_short_digest(value, length)` to consolidate the repeated
  `hashlib.sha1` pattern shared by `_limit_tool_name` and the new fallback path.
- Add a fallback in `_sanitize_mcp_tool_name`: when sanitization produces an
  all-underscore result, return `tool_<8-char sha1 hex>` instead.
- `_sanitize_name` and `_limit_tool_name` are unchanged.
 
## Behavior
 
| Input | Before | After |
|-------|--------|-------|
| `"获取天气"` | `"_"` | `"tool_a3f9c21b"` |
| `"日本語ツール"` | `"_"` | `"tool_8704490a"` |
| `"get_weather"` | `"get_weather"` | `"get_weather"` |
| `"My Tool"` | `"My_Tool"` | `"My_Tool"` |
 
## Related
 
Touches the same area as #3468 (spaces in MCP resource/prompt names), but
addresses a distinct failure mode: fully non-ASCII names that sanitize to
a single underscore rather than an invalid character.

prs.title: fix(memory): ignore runtime files inside tracked workspace dirs
prs.body:
## Summary

Keep runtime files inside the memory directory out of the workspace's untracked-file list, while preserving versioned memory files and user-owned ignore rules.

- Generate per-directory exclusions with explicit exceptions for tracked memory files and the Dream cursor.
- Backfill recognized legacy `.gitignore` prefixes when MemoryStore starts, placing the new rules before appended user overrides.
- Leave unknown, non-UTF-8, missing, and symlinked ignore policies untouched. An undecodable policy no longer prevents memory startup.
- Write backfills atomically and let memory startup continue when the optional repair encounters a filesystem error.
- Include `memory/.dream_cursor` in newly scaffolded memory repositories.

Fixes #5246.

## Compatibility

No memory files, history records, Git objects, or index entries are deleted or migrated. Existing indexed runtime files remain tracked; this change does not automatically untrack them. Custom ignore policies remain user-owned and may need their own runtime-file exclusions. The behavior is documented in `docs/memory.md`.

## Validation

- Integrated current main (`f744652b`).
- Reproduced startup failure with both a non-UTF-8 custom ignore file and a generated prefix followed by a non-UTF-8 comment, then verified both are byte-preserved across repeated startup.
- GitStore, MemoryStore, Dream, Dream commands, and helper suites: **176 passed**.
- Coverage includes fresh/legacy repositories, override precedence, repeated startup, symlink preservation, failed atomic replacement and retry, existing indexed runtime files, unchanged history/index/HEAD during backfill, and subsequent memory commit/diff/restore.
- Scoped Ruff and `git diff --check` passed.

Local verification uses synthetic temporary workspaces, not user memory or session data. Hosted CI provides the supported Python/platform matrix.

prs.title: feat(a2a): Add A2A Protocol support for agent-to-agent communication
prs.body:
## Summary

This PR adds full [A2A Protocol](https://a2a-protocol.org) support to nanobot, enabling agent-to-agent communication.

## Features

### 1. A2A Server (`channels/a2a.py`)
- Exposes nanobot as an A2A-compatible agent
- Agent Card served at `/.well-known/agent.json`
- JSON-RPC endpoint for `message/send` and `message/stream`
- Integrates with nanobot's message bus and agent loop

### 2. A2A Client Tool (`agent/tools/a2a_client.py`)
- `call_a2a_agent` tool for calling external A2A agents
- Agent discovery and capability inspection
- Message sending with response extraction

### 3. Configuration (`config/schema.py`)
- `A2AConfig` with host, port, streaming, skills
- Optional `public_host` for Agent Card URL
- Request timeout configuration

## Installation

```bash
pip install "nanobot-ai[a2a]"
```

## Configuration

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "a2a": {
      "enabled": true,
      "port": 8080,
      "publicHost": "https://my-agent.example.com"
    }
  }
}
```

## Usage

### As an A2A Server
```bash
nanobot gateway
# Agent Card: http://localhost:8080/.well-known/agent.json
```

### Calling Other A2A Agents
The agent can use the `call_a2a_agent` tool to communicate with other A2A-compatible agents:

```
User: Ask the travel agent at https://travel.example.com to book a flight to Paris
```

## Architecture

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   nanobot                     │
│                                               │
│  channels/                                    │
│    telegram.py  discord.py  a2a.py  ← NEW    │
│              │                                │
│              ↓                                │
│  bus/ → agent/loop.py → tools/               │
│                           a2a_client.py ← NEW │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

External A2A Agent ←→ a2a.py (server)
nanobot ←→ a2a_client.py (tool) ←→ External A2A Agent
```

## Testing

```bash
# Start nanobot with A2A
nanobot gateway

# Verify Agent Card
curl http://localhost:8080/.well-known/agent.json

# Test with A2A Inspector
git clone https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-inspector.git
cd a2a-inspector
uv run . --agent-url http://localhost:8080
```

## References

- [A2A Protocol Specification](https://a2a-protocol.org/latest/specification/)
- [A2A Python SDK](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-python)
- [A2A Samples](https://github.com/a2aproject/a2a-samples)

prs.title: feat(webui): notify when a background chat finishes
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds **opt-in desktop notifications** that fire when an agent turn completes in a chat that is **not** the currently focused, active conversation — so you can kick off background work, switch tabs, and get pinged when a reply is ready.

## What changed

- **`webui/src/lib/notifications.ts`** (new): thin wrapper over the browser `Notification` API. Gated by a `localStorage` preference **and** the granted permission, with graceful fallbacks when notifications are `unsupported`/`denied`. Notifications are tagged per `chatId` so repeated completions of the same chat re-alert rather than stack.
- **`nanobot-client.ts`**: `emitRunStatus` now carries a `completed` flag, and `turn_end` always reports completion. This surfaces runs that started *before* the client attached (missed-`running` case). The start-emit call signature is left as 2-arg to preserve existing subscriber contracts.
- **`App.tsx`**: on completion, suppresses the notification when the finished chat is visible, focused **and** active; otherwise shows one titled with the chat's display title.
- **`SettingsView.tsx`**: new "Turn notifications" toggle under Appearance that requests permission on enable, reflects `denied`/`unsupported` state in its help text, and fires a confirmation notification when granted.
- **`tests/setup.ts`**: hardened the test `localStorage` shim to install when the global is absent.

## Notes on correctness

- On **disconnect** the client emits `null` *without* `completed`, so no false "finished" notifications when the socket drops.
- On **(re)subscribe** the server only replays `goal_status: running` (never `turn_end`), so reconnecting does not spuriously notify for already-finished chats.
- New strings use i18n `defaultValue` fallbacks (English), consistent with how not-yet-translated UI strings are staged in this codebase (avoids breaking the locale key-parity test).

## Testing

- `bun run lint` — clean
- `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --noEmit` — clean
- `vitest run` — **436 passed**, including two new App-layout tests (inactive session finishes; active session finishes without focus) and a client test for the missed-`running` case.

prs.title: fix(mcp): reconnect on ClosedResourceError for HTTP transports
prs.body:
## Problem

When an MCP server using `streamable-http` or `sse` transport restarts (e.g. Docker with `restart: unless-stopped`), nanobot holds a cached `ClientSession` whose underlying anyio `MemoryObjectSendStream` channels are already closed. The next tool call raises:

```
anyio.ClosedResourceError: Attempted to send to a closed MemoryObjectSendStream
open_send_channels=0
```

There is no reconnect path, so **all MCP tools for that server silently fail** for the lifetime of the nanobot process.

## Root cause

`connect_mcp_servers()` in `mcp.py` creates one `ClientSession` per server at startup and stores it in an `AsyncExitStack`. If the MCP server process restarts the HTTP transport closes on the server side, but nanobot's `ClientSession` still holds a reference to the now-closed anyio `MemoryObjectSendStream`. The next `session.call_tool()` / `session.list_resources()` / etc. hits the closed channel and raises `ClosedResourceError`. Nothing in the call path catches this or attempts to reconnect.

## Fix

Added `MCPConnectionContext` — a small wrapper that owns the `AsyncExitStack` and `ClientSession` for one MCP server and exposes an async `reconnect()` method (mutex-protected so concurrent tool calls don't stomp each other).

All three wrapper classes (`MCPToolWrapper`, `MCPResourceWrapper`, `MCPPromptWrapper`) now hold a `conn: MCPConnectionContext` instead of a bare `session`. Each `execute()` method uses a **two-attempt retry loop**: on `ClosedResourceError`, call `conn.reconnect()` and retry once. If reconnect itself fails, a human-readable error string is returned rather than raising (so the agent can report the issue to the user instead of crashing).

`connect_mcp_servers` return type changes from `dict[str, AsyncExitStack]` to `dict[str, MCPConnectionContext]`. `MCPConnectionContext.aclose()` delegates to its inner stack, so the cleanup in `loop.py` continues to work unchanged. The `loop.py` type annotation for `_mcp_stacks` is updated accordingly.

Transports that don't support hot-reconnect (`stdio`) fall through gracefully with a warning rather than attempting a reconnect.

## Behaviour unchanged

- Startup logic, `enabled_tools` filtering, schema normalisation, tool/resource/prompt registration
- Session cleanup on agent shutdown
- stdio transport handling

## Testing

Verified locally by:
1. Starting nanobot with an MCP server configured over `streamable-http`
2. Restarting the MCP server container (`docker compose restart <mcp-service>`)
3. Issuing a tool call — nanobot transparently reconnects and the call succeeds on the retry

Without the patch the same scenario produces `ClosedResourceError` and the tool fails permanently until nanobot itself is restarted.

prs.body:
## Summary

A message polled from IMAP was marked `\Seen` as soon as it passed the channel's filters (self-sent, SPF/DKIM, allow-list), *before* it was actually delivered to the agent. This meant:

- A message rejected by a filter (self-sent, SPF/DKIM failure, not allow-listed) was still marked `\Seen`, even though the bot never acted on it — a human checking the mailbox couldn't tell what the bot actually handled from the unread state.
- A message could be marked `\Seen` and then fail delivery to the agent right afterward, silently dropping it.

This PR defers marking `\Seen` until a message has passed every filter **and** been successfully handed off to the agent — mirroring the existing `post_action` (delete/move) gate, which already only applies after successful delivery.

Three related bugs fixed along the way:
- A UID that failed delivery was left in the in-memory dedup cache (marked "already processed") even though it was never marked `\Seen`, so it silently never got retried on a later poll. It's now evicted from that cache on failure.
- A mark-`\Seen` batch failure (e.g. a dropped IMAP connection) could suppress a configured `post_action` for the same successfully-delivered messages. The two are now isolated from each other.
- A mark-`\Seen` batch failure otherwise left the affected UIDs unmarked with no retry, which would redeliver them as duplicates after a restart (the dedup cache is in-memory only). Failed UIDs are now retried on the next poll without re-delivering the message.

No behavior change to filter outcomes or message content — only when `\Seen` gets set.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest nanobot/channels/email/tests/` — 54 passed
- [x] Full suite: `pytest` — 6792 passed, 12 skipped (one pre-existing, unrelated failure in `tests/cli/test_tui_launcher.py` reproduces identically against unmodified `upstream/main`)
- [x] `ruff check nanobot/channels/email/`
- [x] `uv run --no-sync basedpyright` (strict type check, per CONTRIBUTING.md) — 0 errors

prs.title: fix(providers): keep parallel tool calls apart when the stream omits index
prs.body:
Gemini's OpenAI-compatible API streams parallel tool calls without `tool_calls[].index`: each call arrives whole (id, name and arguments) in its own chunk, and the turn ends with `finish_reason: "stop"`. `_parse_chunks` falls back to the call's position inside its chunk when `index` is missing. That's 0 for every one of these chunks, so all the calls of a turn land in one buffer: the id and name of the last call win, and the arguments are concatenated.

Replaying a captured `gemini-3.5-flash` stream with two parallel `get_weather` calls through the `openai` client and `_parse_chunks`:

```
before: call_4234487 get_weather '{"city":"Paris"}{"city":"Tokyo"}'
after:  call_4234484 get_weather {'city': 'Paris'}
        call_4234487 get_weather {'city': 'Tokyo'}
```

### Change

A delta without `index` now starts a new call when it carries an id different from the current call's id, or a name on an id-less call that already has one. Anything else is appended to the current call, so providers that stream unindexed argument fragments keep working. Deltas that do carry `index` are handled as before.

### Tests

- `test_parse_chunks_keeps_parallel_calls_without_index_apart`: the two-call Gemini shape from the capture (thought signature shortened). It fails on `main` and passes with the fix.
- `test_parse_chunks_appends_unindexed_fragments_to_the_last_call`: id-less argument fragments still join the current call.
- `tests/providers` plus `tests/agent/test_gemini_thought_signature.py`: 1464 passed.
- `ruff check nanobot/`: clean.

This change was made with Claude Code; the tests above were run on the branch to check it.

prs.body:
## Why

The active-queue admission path in `AgentLoop` hardcodes WebSocket eligibility even though `RecoveryCoordinator.admit()` already owns that policy. This duplicates channel knowledge in core and differs from the existing worker-dispatch admission path.

## What changed

- Delegate active-queue admission to the injected policy without a concrete channel filter.
- Document effective session keys, repeated admission, and queue ownership changes caused by cancellation.
- Extend the existing unified-session and active-recovery tests to cover ordinary Discord input alongside WebSocket input.

## Scope

Retain both admission points: early admission protects mid-turn injection, while worker admission revalidates queued recoveries. Keep Continue / Dismiss, recovery-task ownership, persisted state, and wire contracts unchanged; this does not add recovery support to other channels.

## Blast Radius

Incoming messages targeting an active session queue now reach the policy regardless of channel. The current coordinator still passes ordinary non-WebSocket input through without superseding recovery, including when channels share a unified session.

- Source review covered queue cancellation handoff, effective-session routing, and the unchanged worker revalidation path.

prs.title: fix(agent): add size guardrails to Dream memory files and requests
prs.body:
## Summary

PR #5622 fixed Dream's system-prompt duplication bug, but as a side effect
removed the only existing size cap on SOUL.md / USER.md / memory/MEMORY.md
(the old `_DREAM_FILE_EMBED_CAP = 8000` mechanism). Since then these
Dream-managed files can grow unbounded and get injected into every regular
turn's system prompt with no limit, and Dream's own consolidation request
has no check against the model's context window either.

This adds two related guardrails:

**Per-file display cap** (`nanobot/agent/context.py`, `nanobot/agent/memory.py`)
- Regular turns: SOUL.md/USER.md/MEMORY.md are truncated at markdown `## `
  section boundaries when they exceed `max_file_chars` (default 8000,
  configurable via `agents.defaults.memory.maxFileChars`) — trailing
  complete sections are kept, a note tells the model to call `read_file`
  for the full content. A single section that alone exceeds the budget
  (e.g. a large file under one heading) is hard-truncated by character
  count so the limit always holds.
- Dream turns are exempt: Dream is the sole writer of these files and needs
  the full view to avoid overwriting content it can't see. Detected via the
  existing `session_key.startswith("dream:")` convention.
- Writes (`write_memory`/`write_soul`/`write_user`) warn once per file when
  oversize but never block or truncate — Dream stays free to write, pruning
  stays Dream's own MECE responsibility.

**Dream request token budget** (`nanobot/agent/memory.py`, wired into the
`/dream` command and the periodic cron job)
- `dream_prompt_within_budget()` estimates the assembled Dream request
  (mirroring `Consolidator._input_token_budget`, and sharing its safety
  buffer constant) and, if it's over budget, halves the history batch and
  retries down to 1 entry. Estimates against the actual restricted Dream
  tool set (`store.build_dream_tools()`), not the caller's full tool
  registry, so the estimate matches the real request size.
- Distinguishes "no history to process" from "history exists but doesn't
  fit even at the minimum batch" so the user gets an accurate diagnostic
  instead of a misleading one.

## Why

Without these, a long-running Dream deployment could grow these files
without any pressure toward the context window, since #5622 removed the
only cap and never added a replacement. This restores an equivalent
safety net at both points where these files matter: display (regular
turns) and the Dream request itself.

## Test plan

- [x] New tests for section-boundary capping (including the case where a
  single section alone exceeds the budget) and Dream-turn bypass, in
  `tests/agent/test_context_builder.py`
- [x] New tests for write-side warnings in `tests/agent/test_memory_store.py`
- [x] New tests for the budget check (fits/shrinks/over-budget/zero-window,
  and that the estimate uses the real restricted Dream tools) in
  `tests/agent/test_dream.py`, including an end-to-end test driving a real
  `dream:` session through `AgentLoop.process_direct`
- [x] Full test suite passes (`pytest`), `ruff check`, `basedpyright`

prs.title: feat(email): add Microsoft delegated OAuth for Office365/Outlook
prs.body:
## Summary

Office365/Outlook is moving away from basic auth (IMAP/SMTP username+password) toward mandatory OAuth2 for mailbox access. This adds a Microsoft identity platform delegated-user OAuth flow (authorization code grant, confidential client) as an alternative to password auth for the email channel, so it keeps working against tenants that have disabled basic auth.

- `nanobot channels login email` opens a browser for Microsoft sign-in and completes the flow via a local loopback callback server (`http://localhost:<port>/callback`), or lets a headless user paste the final callback URL if no browser could be opened.
- Access/refresh tokens are persisted per `(tenant, app, mailbox)` fingerprint (so a stored token isn't silently reused after reconfiguring for a different tenant/app/mailbox) and refreshed transparently; IMAP/SMTP authenticate via XOAUTH2 when OAuth is configured instead of a password.
- WebUI: new tenant ID / client ID / client secret fields, mutually exclusive with password auth — mirroring the existing `matrix` channel's password-or-token pattern — plus a sign-in status/action control.
- No PKCE: this is a confidential client (it has a client secret), and Azure AD validates `redirect_uri` against a different registered-URI bucket when PKCE parameters are present (public/native client flow) than when they're absent (confidential/web client flow); the OAuth `state` parameter is the forgery defense instead, required and verified on every callback.
- The callback listener treats a request with a missing/mismatched `state` as non-terminal — it responds with an error page but keeps listening, since the legitimate Microsoft redirect may still be in flight (a stray probe or forged request must not be able to kill a pending sign-in).

Leaving OAuth fields unset preserves current behavior exactly — IMAP/SMTP password auth works as before.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest nanobot/channels/email/` — all passing, including new coverage for the OAuth module (token fingerprinting/refresh, XOAUTH2 wiring, callback-server state validation, headless paste rejection of a bare code) and WebUI validation
- [x] Full suite: `pytest` — one pre-existing, unrelated failure in `tests/cli/test_tui_launcher.py` reproduces identically against unmodified `upstream/main`
- [x] `ruff check nanobot/channels/email/`

- [x] Verified live against a real Exchange Online mailbox (IMAP + SMTP XOAUTH2, full sign-in flow through Azure AD consent)

prs.title: feat(email): filter by recipient alias
prs.body:
## Summary

A mailbox is sometimes shared across multiple addresses (aliases that all deliver to the same inbox — e.g. `assistant@example.com` and `team@example.com` landing in the same mailbox). Today the email channel processes every message it receives regardless of which address it was actually sent to, so a bot configured against a shared mailbox ends up acting on mail that wasn't meant for it.

This adds an `alias_address` config option: when set, only messages actually addressed to that alias are processed. Everything else is skipped — logged, deduped, added to `skipped_uids` — exactly like the existing self-sent/SPF/DKIM/allow-list filters already do, so it's never marked `\Seen` either (per #5605).

The match checks `To`/`Cc` (multiple comma-separated recipients handled via `email.utils.getaddresses`), plus `Delivered-To`/`X-Original-To`/`Envelope-To` as a bonus for providers that set them (Exchange Online does not, but Postfix/Gmail-style servers often do).

Leaving `alias_address` unset preserves current behavior exactly — the mailbox processes everything it receives, as before.

This is stacked on top of #5605 (deferred mark-`\Seen`) since the filter's skip path relies on that behavior. Until #5605 merges, this diff will also show that commit — it'll collapse to just the alias filter once #5605 lands.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest nanobot/channels/email/tests/` — 60 passed (6 new: accepts alias match, rejects non-match without marking `\Seen`, matches via Cc, case-insensitive match, matches via `Delivered-To`, no-op when unset)

prs.title: fix(provider): serialize half-open fallback probes
prs.body:
## Problem

After the primary circuit cooldown elapses, `FallbackProvider` is intended to enter half-open state and allow one probe request. The availability check only compared the cooldown timestamp, however, so concurrent requests could all reach the recovering primary before any of them completed. That defeats the circuit breaker during the endpoint's most fragile recovery window.

## Changes

- Reserve the half-open primary probe synchronously before yielding to the provider call; concurrent requests keep using the configured fallback chain.
- Keep the reservation through stream-recovery evaluation, then clear it on a successful probe, cancellation, non-fallbackable/streamed early return, or fallbackable probe failure.
- Add async regressions for concurrent admission, failed-probe re-opening, successful recovery, provider-call cancellation, and cancellation during stream recovery.

## Validation

Base: `origin/main@499bf903022f429dd4501fdfbeeccadcb99dd51f`

```text
uv run pytest tests/agent/test_runner_fallback.py -q
79 passed

uv run pytest tests/agent/test_runner_fallback.py tests/agent/test_runner_errors.py -q
92 passed

uv run ruff check nanobot tests conftest.py
All checks passed!

uv run basedpyright
0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes
```

The full repository test suite is running separately. No dependencies, configuration, retry policy, or fallback ordering changed. The reservation is a boolean because its check-and-set contains no `await`, so competing coroutines cannot interleave within that operation on the same event loop.

prs.title: feat(telegram): per-chat and per-topic group policy overrides
prs.body:
## Summary

Telegram's `groupPolicy` is channel-wide, so one bot serving a busy supergroup has a single behavior everywhere. With forum topics that is a real limitation: a team group usually wants the bot active in project topics but quiet in announcement topics, and today that cannot be expressed.

Napcat already exposes per-group overrides, so this ports the same idea to Telegram, adapted to its topic model.

Refs #5972.

## The Telegram-specific detail

Telegram forum topics **do not have their own chat id**. Every topic shares the parent supergroup's `chat_id` and is distinguished only by `message_thread_id`. A group-scoped key like Napcat's `str(group_id)` therefore cannot address a single topic; the key needs both parts.

## Changes

`channels.telegram.groupPolicyOverrides` accepts:

- `"<chat_id>"` — a whole chat
- `"<chat_id>:<thread_id>"` — one forum topic (most specific, wins)

Unlisted scopes fall back to `groupPolicy`. Resolution is a small helper so the precedence order is explicit and testable:

```python
def _effective_group_policy(self, message) -> Literal["open", "mention"]:
    # topic key → chat key → channel-wide group_policy
```

`_is_group_message_for_bot()` now consults that helper instead of comparing `group_policy` directly.

Example — channel-wide `open`, one announcement topic silenced:

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "telegram": {
      "groupPolicy": "open",
      "groupPolicyOverrides": {
        "-1001668715626": "open",
        "-1001668715626:7819": "mention"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Design notes

- **No new policy value.** With the channel at `"open"`, a topic set to `"mention"` already means "don't jump into the conversation, but answer when called" — the usual intent for a muted topic. Keeping the set at `{mention, open}` keeps the change small and matches Napcat's `GroupPolicy`.
- **No hard-coded thread ids.** The `chat_id:` prefix prevents a topic override from leaking into another chat that happens to reuse the same thread id.
- Follows Napcat's existing naming (`groupPolicyOverrides`) rather than inventing a Telegram-only key.

## Tests

New `tests/channels/test_telegram_group_policy_overrides.py` (7 tests) covering precedence directly, plus the two behaviors that matter end to end:

- chat-level override beats the channel default
- topic override beats the chat-level override
- a topic override does **not** leak to another chat with the same thread id
- chat override still applies to a non-forum group message (no thread id)
- a silenced topic ignores plain chatter (`_is_group_message_for_bot` is `False`)
- an unsilenced sibling topic still answers plain chatter (`True`)

```
$ pytest tests/channels/ -q
296 passed
```

With `runtime.py` reverted, 6 of the 7 new tests fail (the remaining one asserts the pre-existing default), so the tests genuinely pin the new behavior.

I also added the field to the channel manifest together with the ten `webui/locales` entries, because `test_channel_setup.py` requires every writable setup field to have locale copy. Wording follows the existing Napcat translations for the same field.

## Notes for Reviewers

- `ruff check` passes. I did not run `ruff format` since the surrounding tree predates it (per CONTRIBUTING) and it would add unrelated churn.
- The full suite has 4 pre-existing failures in this environment (`tests/tools/test_rg_tool.py`, `test_search_tools.py`) caused by missing local `rg`/`poppler` binaries, not by this change — verified identically on `main`.
- A follow-up PR adds a `/group` command to manage these overrides from chat without editing config; it layers on top of this one.

prs.title: fix(webui): paint the cached app shell immediately on PWA cold start
prs.body:
Fixes #5773.

The service worker served the app shell ("/" and navigate-mode requests) network-first, so an installed PWA blocked first paint on a full network round trip on every cold start even though the shell is already precached at install — on a high-latency link that is the long blank screen from the issue.

Shell navigations now go through a stale-while-revalidate handler: the cached shell paints immediately, while a background refresh overwrites it, refreshes the asset manifest, and prunes unreferenced build assets, so deployed updates still land on the next launch. First launch with an empty cache and the offline fallback keep the previous network-first behavior; manifest and brand-icon paths are unchanged. The iOS apple-touch-startup-image half of the issue needs per-device artwork and is left as a follow-up.

Verification: the service worker test file passes 20/20 (rewrote the navigation test for the SWR semantics, added an empty-cache first-launch case, and made the test fake snapshot cached bodies the way real CacheStorage does — the old fake let a read consume the body, which the new prune-then-read flow exposed). eslint --max-warnings 0 clean, tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --noEmit clean, and the pre-existing flaky UI test failures were verified identical against a stashed baseline.

prs.title: fix(agent): preserve finish reasons when dropping malformed tool calls
prs.body:
## Summary

Preserve truncated-response recovery when all tool calls in a model response have invalid names.

Previously, removing those calls could make the runner return a partial answer as completed or retry an empty response without requesting continuation.

## Root Cause

`_drop_malformed_tool_calls()` unconditionally changed `finish_reason` to `stop` when no valid calls remained.

This erased the provider's `length` signal before the runner selected its recovery path. It also overwrote error, refusal, and content-filter reasons.

## Changes

- Normalize the finish reason only when its original value is `tool_calls` or `function_call`.
- Preserve truncation and other terminal reasons.
- Add regression coverage for blank and partial-text truncated responses.
- Verify malformed calls are neither executed nor retained in message history.

## Result

Truncated responses enter the existing bounded continuation flow and assemble the recovered answer. Existing malformed tool-call retry behavior is preserved.

## Test

- Confirmed six regression cases failed before the fix.
- 173 related runner tests passed after the fix, covering governance, core, errors, goal continuation, hooks, injections, progress deltas, and reasoning.
- Ruff passed for both changed files.
- BasedPyright passed for `nanobot/agent/runner.py`.

prs.title: fix(providers): preserve Chat Completions refusal responses
prs.body:
## Summary

Fix the Chat Completions adapter ignoring refusal fields, which loses the model's refusal explanation and can trigger empty-response retries.

Preserve refusal text in both non-streaming and streaming responses, and map it to nanobot's existing internal `refusal` finish reason. The change is limited to the provider adapter and its regression tests.

## Root Cause

The Chat Completions API exposes refusal text separately through `message.refusal` for non-streaming responses and `delta.refusal` for streaming responses. A refusal can still arrive with `finish_reason: "stop"`, so forwarding the upstream finish reason alone does not identify it as a refusal.

For example, the [official Structured Outputs guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/structured-outputs), with **Chat Completions** selected, shows a refusal response whose message contains `role` and `refusal`, with no `content` field:

    {
      "choices": [{
        "index": 0,
        "message": {
          "role": "assistant",
          "refusal": "I'm sorry, I cannot assist with that request."
        },
        "finish_reason": "stop"
      }]
    }

nanobot already recognizes `"refusal"` as an internal finish reason, but the Chat Completions adapter did not translate these refusal fields into that internal representation. It also omitted the refusal text when collecting response content.

Consequently, a response containing refusal text but no ordinary content—whether `content` was absent or explicitly null—could be parsed as:

    LLMResponse(content=None, finish_reason="stop")

The runner can treat this result as an empty response and retry, even though the model has already returned a refusal explanation.

The existing handling of `"content_filter"` does not cover this case: content filtering and a model-generated refusal are distinct API outcomes. This issue concerns Chat Completions; the Responses API uses a different refusal content-block format.

## Changes

- Preserve non-streaming `message.refusal` text in the returned `LLMResponse`.
- Accumulate streaming `delta.refusal` fragments and forward them through the existing content callback.
- Set the internal finish reason to `"refusal"` when refusal text is present, including when the final stream chunk reports `"stop"`.
- Add parameterized JSON and SSE regression tests using the real OpenAI SDK with an HTTPX mock transport.
- Include ordinary-content controls and verify final text, streaming deltas, finish reasons, token usage, and absence of tool calls.

Production changes are limited to `nanobot/providers/openai_compat_provider.py`. The fix reuses existing downstream refusal handling without changing the runner, retry policy, configuration, or Responses API.

## Result

Refusal explanations remain visible to callers instead of being discarded. Streaming callers receive the refusal fragments as they arrive, and the final response preserves the complete text with `finish_reason="refusal"`.

For the example above, the adapter now returns:

    LLMResponse(
        content="I'm sorry, I cannot assist with that request.",
        finish_reason="refusal"
    )

This allows downstream code to distinguish a refusal from an empty response with a normal `"stop"` finish reason. Ordinary text responses retain their existing behavior, and token usage remains available.

## Test

Before the fix, both refusal regression cases failed: JSON and SSE responses returned `content=None` with `finish_reason="stop"`. Both ordinary-content controls passed.

After the fix:

- **362 tests passed** across custom-provider parsing, OpenAI compatibility, Responses parsing, LLM response contracts, and runner error handling.
- Ruff passed for both modified files.
- BasedPyright reported **0 errors and 0 warnings** for the modified provider.
- `git diff --check` passed.

The regression tests exercise real SDK JSON and SSE parsing with controlled HTTP responses. The non-streaming refusal fixture uses `content: null`; the streaming fixture supplies refusal fragments without ordinary content. These tests verify adapter output and streaming callbacks.

prs.title: fix(channels): deliver provider retry waits through an opt-in hook
prs.body:
Fixes #5585

## Problem
When a provider call backs off, core publishes `RetryWaitEvent` ("Model request failed, retry in {n}s (attempt {k}).") but `ChannelManager._dispatch_outbound_loop` dropped it unconditionally, before any channel hook and outside the `sendProgress` gate. Only the interactive CLI ever rendered it, so chat channels looked hung for the whole backoff.

## Change
I went with the less intrusive option from the issue: a default no-op `BaseChannel.send_retry_wait(...)` hook, following the same pattern as `send_delta` / `send_reasoning*`.
- `ChannelManager` now forwards `RetryWaitEvent` to `send_retry_wait` and never falls through to `send()`. Channels that don't override the hook stay silent, so there's no new config key and no extra chat messages by default.
- I didn't route it through `sendProgress`: that defaults to on, so every progress-enabled channel would get a permanent chat line. This matches the precedent in #5799 (compaction notices).
- Linear already built an ephemeral thought for this event inside `send()`, but that code was unreachable because of the drop. It now lives in `LinearChannel.send_retry_wait`, and `send()` delegates to it, so direct sends behave the same.
- WebSocket/WebUI is unchanged (it uses the structured `RetryStatusEvent`).
- `docs/channel-package-guide.md` documents the hook.

## Tests
- New `tests/channels/test_channel_manager_retry_wait.py` covers two cases: a channel that implements the hook receives the notice even with `send_progress` false, and default channels don't get it through `send()`. The hook test failed before the fix.
- A Linear test covers the ephemeral thought and direct `send()` delegation.

## Verification (Linux, Python 3.11, GH tokens unset)
- `uv sync --all-extras --dev`, channel dependency install, `uv pip check`: exit 0
- `uv run --no-sync ruff check nanobot tests conftest.py`: exit 0
- `uv run --no-sync basedpyright`: exit 0 (0 errors)
- `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest -n 2 --dist loadfile --ignore=tests/cli/test_commands.py`: exit 0 (9220 passed, 48 skipped)
- `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/cli/test_commands.py`: exit 0 (160 passed)

prs.body:
## Summary

The WeCom channel drops inbound video messages and quoted replies.

The WeCom SDK dispatches a generic `message` event for every inbound frame and only adds per-type events (`message.text`, `message.image`, `message.mixed`, `message.voice`, `message.file`) for the message types it knows about. `video` is not among them, so a video frame only ever fires the generic event — and the channel subscribed to the per-type events alone, so videos were never processed.

This change subscribes to the generic `message` event and dispatches on the payload's `msgtype`. That covers every message type the platform can currently deliver, plus any type added later, without another subscription per type.

On top of that:

- **Video messages** are downloaded and decrypted like the other inbound media, and forwarded as an attachment.
- **Quoted replies** pass the quoted text to the model as reply context (`[Reply to: ...]`), matching how the QQ and Feishu channels surface quoted messages. Quoted text is capped at 200 characters.

## Verification

- `pytest nanobot/channels/wecom` — 65 passed.
- `ruff check nanobot/channels/wecom/` — clean.
- `basedpyright nanobot/channels/wecom/` — no new findings (the 3 remaining errors are the pre-existing unresolved optional `wecom_aibot_sdk` import).
- `python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries` — passed.

New tests cover the SDK dispatch contract (a video frame reaches the generic `message` event), video download, quoted-text context, and quote truncation.

## Notes

- The event registration change is behaviour-preserving for the message types that already worked: the SDK fires the generic `message` event for those types as well, so nothing is delivered twice.
- Media download keeps using the existing `WECOM_DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` (200 MB) limit and the shared filename sanitizer.

## Related

The WeCom protocol and SDK surface referenced here (message types, `quote` payload, media download/decrypt) are documented in [WecomTeam/aibot-node-sdk](https://github.com/WecomTeam/aibot-node-sdk) and mirrored in [dividduang/aibot-python-sdk](https://github.com/dividduang/aibot-python-sdk).

prs.title: feat(heartbeat): add heartbeat-specific model override
prs.body:
## Problem

The heartbeat cron job runs on the main agent model for both the execution turn and the post-run notification evaluation. Heartbeat can run frequently (default every 30 minutes) and usually only makes a lightweight decision, so deployments using a premium or auto-routed model pay that cost for routine background checks. `agents.defaults.dream.modelOverride` already lets Dream run on a different model, but heartbeat has no equivalent setting.

## Solution

Add an optional `gateway.heartbeat.modelOverride`. For each heartbeat run, resolve an immutable runtime via `runtime_resolver.resolve_override(model=..., config=...)` (which also resolves the correct provider for the requested model); when the override is unset, snapshot the current default via `runtime_resolver.current()`. The same resolved provider/model is used for both the heartbeat turn and the notification evaluation. The main agent model and provider are never mutated, and unsetting the field keeps today's behaviour exactly.

## Changes

- `nanobot/config/schema.py` — add `model_override` to `HeartbeatConfig` with `modelOverride` / `model` aliases.
- `nanobot/cli/gateway_runtime.py` — resolve the heartbeat runtime and pass it to `process_direct`; use its provider/model for `evaluate_response`; startup output shows the effective heartbeat model.
- `docs/configuration.md` — document the new option with an example.
- Tests: config alias/serialization cases and a runtime case (default + override) asserting both the execution and evaluation use the resolved model while the main agent model is unchanged.

## Testing

**Environment**
- Runtime: Python 3.13.16
- OS: Windows NT 10.0.26200.0
- Arch: AMD64

**Test Commands & Results**
1. `pytest tests/cli/test_commands.py tests/config/test_gateway_config.py -k heartbeat`
   -> 20 passed, 150 deselected
2. `pytest tests/config tests/cli tests/agent`
   -> 2781 passed, 30 skipped, 0 failed (baseline: 2776 passed, 30 skipped, 1 flaky timing failure; the 4 added tests account for the count difference)
3. `ruff check nanobot tests`
   -> all checks passed
4. `basedpyright nanobot/config/schema.py nanobot/cli/gateway_runtime.py`
   -> 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes

**Pre-existing Failures**
- `tests/agent/test_runner_injections.py::test_websocket_followup_is_admitted_before_recovery_queue` raised an asyncio `TimeoutError` once during the baseline full run. It passes in isolation and passed in the post-change full run; it has no file intersection with this PR and is a pre-existing flaky timing test.

## Notes for Reviewer

- The earlier attempt #4549 was withdrawn without the feature landing; this re-implements the same requested behaviour against the current code, using the side-effect-free `runtime_resolver.current()` for the default case.
- Kept this PR to a model override only (no separate provider override) to match the issue scope.

Closes #4431

prs.title: fix(providers): sanitize decoded tool arguments during history replay
prs.body:
### Summary
Reuse the existing surrogate sanitizer after decoding or repairing tool arguments for history replay, and for dictionary-form replay input. Keep execution-time tool arguments unchanged and preserve the original input objects.

### Why
A JSON escape such as `\ud800` contains no surrogate until it is decoded. The earlier message sanitizer therefore misses it, and provider history conversion can reintroduce a lone surrogate that causes HTTP UTF-8 encoding to fail. This fixes the replay-specific gap in #4952; it does not claim to normalize arbitrary dictionary keys.

### Validation
- Reproduced failures on the unchanged source, including actual Anthropic request construction and httpx JSON encoding without sending a request.
- Added regressions for decoded/repaired inputs, input preservation and request encoding.
- Complete provider tests: 1,482 passed, 2 warnings, with `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on PYTHONPATH=tests .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/providers -q`.

- Full configured Ruff, strict BasedPyright, import-boundary checks and git diff --check passed.

The complete repository suite and live model API integrations were not run. Upstream CI results are pending.

prs.title: fix(api): release session locks after requests finish
prs.body:
## Summary
The OpenAI-compatible API kept one lock for every `session_id`, including sessions whose requests had already finished. Sending requests with many distinct session ids made the process retain those locks without bound.

Store the locks in a weak map, matching the agent session-lock lifecycle. A lock stays while a request holds it or another request for that session is waiting, then it can be collected.

## Test
On base `83b6112`:

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_openai_api.py::test_completed_api_session_lock_is_released -q --tb=line
```

Before: 1 failed. After both requests returned 200, `api:temporary-session` was still in the lock map.

After `84a2af799043adb51992053c325d071a71d2c2ba`: 1 passed. The two overlapping requests share one lock, and the entry is gone after they finish. `tests/test_openai_api.py`: 51 passed.

The OpenAI-compatible API kept per-session `asyncio.Lock` objects in a regular dictionary. Because `session_id` is caller-controlled and completed locks were never removed, each new session permanently increased the registry size.

prs.title: fix(cron): prevent overlapping executions of the same job
prs.body:
## Problem

`CronService.run_job()` can enter the callback for a job that is already suspended in another manual run or in the scheduler. The WebUI's Run action creates a new `run_job()` task on each request, and a manual run can also overlap a due timer. Both invocations execute the agent callback and append a successful run record. This can duplicate model/tool work for one automation.

This was found by source inspection and reproduced offline on `main` at `fbb61a373f47769734a0d47d8f61935ffca84b84`; it is not a claimed production incident.

## Change

- Claim the job ID before awaiting its callback, shared by manual and timer entry points; release it in `finally`, including cancellation.
- Return `False` from an overlapping manual run, including `force=True`. Other jobs remain concurrent, and a later intentional run of the same job still works.
- Add event-coordinated regressions for manual/manual, timer/manual, manual/timer, cancellation, and persisted run history.

The guard is local to one `CronService` instance. It does not provide distributed locking or crash-safe exactly-once execution. Related #3245 proposes a persisted cross-instance claim; this patch does not implement that. Historical #961 was closed by its author in February; the current manual-run paths still reproduce the problem.

## Verification

- New regression file against unchanged main: **3 failed, 1 passed**. All three overlapping cases execute the callback twice; the cancellation control already passes.
- `python -m pytest tests/cron -q`: **181 passed** after the fix.
- `ruff check nanobot/cron/service.py tests/cron/test_cron_single_flight.py`: passed.
- `basedpyright nanobot/cron/service.py`: **0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes**.
- `python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries`: passed (13 rules, 216 files).
- `git diff --cached --check`: passed.

Tests ran on Windows with Python 3.12.14 and workspace-local temporary directories. The restricted sandbox initially blocked Windows asyncio's local socketpair during event-loop creation; rerunning the offline checks with local socket access allowed produced the results above. No real model/provider requests, channel delivery, full-repository suite, or browser end-to-end run were performed.

## AI assistance and review status

Codex inspected the source and related contributions, wrote and ran the before/after tests, implemented the fix, and reviewed the complete diff under LJK-ikun's direction. This PR is ready for maintainer review. The validation above is automated local validation; independent human testing or approval is not asserted.

prs.title: fix(webui): retain temporary chats across navigation
prs.body:
## Summary

Temporary chats could lose their messages and show the new-chat welcome screen after switching to another conversation, especially while a reply was running or when a compact workbench unmounted the original pane.

- Keep the in-memory message cache at the app-session level and pass the temporary-chat retention list to both workbench paths.
- Save all received messages before detaching a chat subscription, including unpainted deltas and completed replies that have not committed to React yet.
- Retain background events for open temporary chats instead of truncating them to the replay tail used by disk-backed chats.
- Preserve cleanup on explicit close and connection loss, without persisting temporary messages.

## Validation

- Full WebUI suite: **1,736 tests passed across 106 files**.
- WebUI lint and production TypeScript/Vite build passed.
- Added real App/client integration regressions with synthetic network responses for navigation during/after generation, background completion, compact pane unmounting, multiple temporary chats, close/disconnect cleanup, and long background replies.
- Reproduced and fixed `stream_end`, `turn_end`, and direct replies arriving immediately before compact-pane unmount. Also verified all three detach/restore paths in a real browser using an isolated hook/client harness with synthetic messages.
- Verified ordinary-chat replay remains bounded and temporary messages are not written to browser storage or fetched from persisted history.

## Compatibility

No breaking API, protocol, configuration, or storage changes. Reloading, closing, or losing the connection still ends temporary chats.

Long-running offscreen temporary chats retain more events in memory because they have no persisted history to recover from. These events are consumed on resubscription and released on close or disconnect; ordinary-chat buffer limits are unchanged.

prs.title: feat(images): reuse named connections and image request settings
prs.body:
## Problem

Image settings list only fixed provider names. Users cannot select a named connection created in Models. Image-only request parameters must be placed in shared provider settings.

## Changes

- Select an image provider by its saved connection ID. Named custom connections use the OpenAI Images API. A chat endpoint does not imply image support.
- Reuse the saved key, URL, and proxy. Keep built-in adapters and the legacy `custom` connection.
- Add image-only headers and body parameters. Empty fields inherit provider settings. Secret values stay masked.
- Clear image-only overrides when the provider changes. Do not replace a missing connection with another provider.
- Reuse the existing parameter editor and request validation. Include all ten locales and failed-save recovery.

## Runtime integration

#6172 has merged into `main`. This branch now includes that main commit, `105b7722037bcae7fdd204d757690403ace22467`.

The application runtime owns image-tool registration and live reload. This PR supplies named connections and image request settings to that path. Provider discovery uses the same rules for the settings list, startup, and reload. No image-specific state or control-message branch is added to `AgentLoop`.

The final diff also reuses the shared editor and validation from #6159. It preserves the Codex Images API and `gpt-image-2` default from #6177.

## Compatibility

Existing saved configurations and high-level SDK, CLI, and WebUI entrypoints need no migration. Missing image-only fields retain the prior behavior. Reload reads the explicit gateway config path. A failed load retains the working tool. Clients created before reload retain their request settings.

This PR adds no further low-level constructor change beyond #6172. Direct `AgentLoop` callers must use the application composition described there.

Older releases do not support named custom image connections or the new image-only fields. Before a downgrade, select a provider supported by that release and check required request settings. See `docs/image-generation.md`.

Chat prompts, history, and tool schemas are unchanged. Updating image request settings does not change tool definitions or their order. Enabling or disabling a tool still changes its availability.

## Verification

prs.title: fix(feishu): restore assistant creation and pairing recovery
prs.body:
## Summary

- Restore **Add another assistant** after a Feishu assistant is configured. Reuse the existing QR flow with `mode=create`. Keep existing assistants and their credentials unchanged.
- Record pairing reply delivery separately from sender approval. Show a recoverable failure when a reply cannot be sent, instead of only showing empty code slots. A new private message retries the same unexpired code. Keep code entry available if a delivery receipt could not be saved.
- Send Feishu pairing replies as plain text. Report an uninitialized client as a send failure. Do not require rich-text/card permissions for pairing.
- Report saved Feishu credentials as **Configured**, not **Connected**, in field-only validation.
- Add localized recovery copy and update the Feishu setup guide.
- Show a recovered pairing request even if its failure notice was dismissed. A failed approval stays idle until the user retries; polling does not submit it again.

## Cause

PR #5356 removed the create-another-assistant action. The server still supports this operation.

Pairing generated a pending code before sending it. A send failure left the pending request visible, but no delivery outcome reached WebUI. The screenshot alone does not identify the user's specific Feishu API error. This change fixes the observable failure path and reduces pairing's message-format dependencies; it does not bypass platform permissions.

## Verification

- Python: 263 tests passed across the Feishu suite, pairing store, base channel, and settings system. Two existing optional-dependency guards skipped tests.
- Frontend: 160 tests passed across QR flows, channel settings, pairing UI, and localization. The two new recovery tests reproduced both failures before the review fix.
- WebUI production build, frontend lint, scoped Ruff, and scoped strict basedpyright passed.
- Browser checks used the actual components with isolated synthetic data: existing assistants → QR creation → cancel → retry → simulated authorization → another assistant; failure recovery and code entry at 375px; Chinese/English and light/dark states.
- A Feishu handler test exercises failed send → plain-text retry → approval, including a named assistant and cross-assistant isolation. Delivery callbacks cannot revive expired/approved requests or replace a successful receipt with a failed concurrent retry.
- Review verification reran 130 related Python tests. An isolated compatibility probe used the actual pre-change store implementation to create records, read them through the current settings DTO, add delivery status, and then approve/delete them with the old implementation. Existing approvals remained intact.
- The browser review used the current popup with simulated responses. At 375px in Chinese, one failed approval stayed idle and the Retry button completed the second attempt. All ten locales include the Retry label.
- Integration checks after updating the branch to the current main: 163 focused frontend tests and 130 related Python tests passed. The earlier CI failure was in an existing Linear cancellation test. It now waits for the input to become enabled after the cancellation effect, without changing production behavior or weakening the assertion.

The browser authorization callback and Feishu transport were simulated. No live Feishu authorization or user account configuration was changed. This is not a claim that the reported user's live environment has passed E2E testing.

## Compatibility and scope

**Breaking changes: none.** `delivery_status` is optional. Old pending records and old gateways retain code entry. Pairing codes, TTLs, approval rules, config paths, and assistant identities are unchanged. Direct code generators that do not track delivery remain compatible. No new API operation or capability is required.

Repository guide: updated in this PR. Release notes and published website instructions: follow up with the release; no external site changes here. No deployment, release, or merge is included.

prs.body:
## Scope and status

Prepare 0.4.0 from already-merged main `32ee2810a1ae563a3c3430e979f9b8e34129a85c`, including the Windows idle-memory fix in #6507 and obsolete upgrade-wizard cleanup in #6508. Open Dock window-reuse #6377 and retry redesign #6367 remain separate.

**The post-#6507/#6508 exact-source CI, five-platform candidate and retained-byte verification have passed. Independent review and publication approval remain pending.** Current head is `74cffe2bf923de35cf51f141d8ea6f253eb3bfd3`, containing main `32ee2810a1ae563a3c3430e979f9b8e34129a85c`. Previous files are historical evidence, not the final upload set. Both this PR and [website PR #35](https://github.com/Re-bin/nanobot-web/pull/35) remain Draft and must wait for the maintainer's release command before merge. No tag, Release, PyPI upload, deployment, public feed, signing switch or branch-protection change is part of preparation.

## Changes

- Set the Python release declarations to 0.4.0. Add release notes for merged features, the original-installation upgrade from 0.3.5, SQLite migration and recovery limits.
- Reuse the candidate builder and exact-source manifest. Keep Preview and stable preparation explicit. Add five-platform native acceptance without adding scheduled releases or a second publisher.
- Preserve a usable source repository through file-only CI artifact transport. Verify the downloaded handoff, exact source, manifest and all retained files before acceptance.
- Fix the real source-upgrade build failure: Bun's incremental frozen install could omit Streamdown's nested dependency. The existing build helper now uses `--frozen-lockfile --force`; the lazy-feature guard and lockfile remain authoritative.
- Update `@xmldom/xmldom` to 0.8.15 and align runtime/extras on pypdf >=6.21.3,<7, Pillow >=13,<14 and Dulwich >=1.2.20,<2. Dependency advisories prompted compatibility checks; an advisory entry alone does not establish an exploitable nanobot vulnerability.
- Add real retained-volume Docker upgrade acceptance. Extend installed native acceptance with terminal input, resize, exit and font/render-worker checks.
- Repair macOS test setup and terminal output draining, Windows durable-write test synchronization, and actual historical-wheel dependency resolution. Keep production guards and observable acceptance assertions intact.
- Resolve real macOS diagram fonts through CoreText using installed Heiti SC outline fonts. macOS 15 can map PingFang names to private HVGL-only faces unreadable by fontkit. Normalize fontkit's legacy ASCII PostScript-name records without accepting a different face. The packaged native probe now exercises Chinese C4 labels and generated Latin punctuation; no glyph or font guard is skipped.
- Provision `fonts-noto-cjk` on disposable Linux acceptance runners for those Chinese labels. Document platform font requirements; do not bundle system fonts in the product or treat DejaVu Sans as Chinese coverage.

- Include #6507 with its author and co-author preserved. Run the existing focused Windows process job on Python 3.12 with gateway runtime regression tests; retain the full Windows suite on Python 3.14 and exact-wheel native acceptance on Python 3.11. Check the affected ctypes runtime family, not only the latest interpreter.

## Current verification

- [Current-head CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40647115985) passed all 15 jobs. The [complete retained candidate](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40647141602) passed all five platforms and Candidate required for `74cffe2bf923de35cf51f141d8ea6f253eb3bfd3`; no old manifest or package hash is relabelled.
- Final manifest is `c7d2112431f52221e30bbac31b61bd0ed9c1ad9e8f0c08657cc9534a578865db`. Each exact wheel passed installed startup, 388 WebUI assets without frontend build tools or TUI download, five terminal samples, Chinese C4 rendering/worker restart, and nine upgrade/recovery scenarios with fifteen journeys. Configuration, authenticated canonical/display history, SQLite/outbox, continued writes, second start and cleanup passed. Windows explicitly enforced `LongPathsEnabled=0`.
- Accepted artifact `installable-candidate-14-1` (12799196609) is bound to the prepared artifact 12798213302 verified by the required gate. One matching local handoff/source repository is preserved. The transport digest, independent `--no-local` clone and `git fsck --full`, complete 16-asset verifier, six-file RECORD/tag/content/size/hash inventory and Twine 7.0.0 `check --strict` all passed. Final wheels are 33.74–52.80 MiB (+10.04–17.07% versus actual 0.3.5); sdist is 6.78 MiB (+57.12%). Windows/Linux x64 binaries remain below 135 MiB. The replacement manual upload instructions name exactly five wheels and one sdist, but are not upload permission.
- Latest native process job used actual Windows CPython 3.12.10: 112 passed / three unrelated skips, including pointer-type reuse. Latest Docker test merge `b2440d664964bbe9c4cb21dc6193d6ea73f1abe7` has parents current main and head, and tree `6eb581407e2baf09621d005c3ad3da89dc27bac4` equals head. Its actual 0.3.5 retained-volume upgrade preserved config/history, continued writes and second start, with cleanup; not in-container automatic rollback.

Its fresh Docker old-image upgrade passed retained configuration/history, continued writes, second start and cleanup against a test-merge tree identical to da965.
- That run's full Windows 3.14 suite had one model-start readiness timeout before the follow-up recovery assertions (10,798 other tests passed /139 skipped). Under six workers, adjacent real-persistence cases took over ten seconds. The 85d delta bounds Windows concurrency at four workers without changing tests, timeouts or assertions; its fresh Windows suite passed. The old failure remains recorded, not relabelled as a pass.
- Local focused runtime/process/workflow checks: 132 passed /10 platform skips. Full session-inbox controls:31passed. CI selection/workflow checks:81passed. Ruff and diff checks passed. Mac skips are not native Windows evidence.
- The da965 [exact candidate](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40643523616) passed all five platforms and Candidate required: each exact wheel passed installation, terminal/C4 rendering, nine scenarios/fifteen upgrade/recovery journeys, protected data, continued writes, restart and cleanup. Windows explicitly enforced `LongPathsEnabled=0`. Original reports retain da965 source and manifest `e4e82f8627919bdb6e366a68aa655452ba511ce75106382ddeda604dd3a59736`; they do not certify the final 74cffe bytes. The old upload command remains withdrawn until the new exact six-file set is accepted.
- #6508 removes the obsolete bundled wizard without modifying user-workspace skills or the current updater. Local skill-loader/CI checks: 102 passed; focused WebUI skill-ranking test: one passed, 195 unselected. Website 0.4.0 contains no obsolete wizard instructions, so its unchanged ten-language evidence is retained.
- Release notes and the private article include the Windows polling fix and preserve live identity/PID-reuse checks, handle cleanup and both contributors' attribution.

## Historical b4 verification — superseded upload set

The following results belong to `b4c3f8f5e85485806c016f1387f6886db7c4f6e4`, before #6507. They remain useful historical evidence, not current-head acceptance or permission to upload those files.

- [b4 PR CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40565642306) passed all 15 jobs, including Python 3.11/3.14, Windows Python/installers/process compatibility, WebUI/browser, TUI, Docker and Linux/Windows native recovery.
- [b4 exact candidate acceptance](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/40565872061) passed all five platforms and **Candidate required**: macOS arm64/x64, Linux arm64/x64 and Windows x64. Each exact manifest-bound wheel passed clean installed startup, 388 WebUI assets, five terminal input/resize/exit samples, Chinese C4 rendering and render-worker restart, plus nine update/recovery scenarios with fifteen journeys. Configuration, authenticated canonical/display history, SQLite/outbox, continued writes, second start and cleanup passed. The Windows job explicitly set and checked `LongPathsEnabled=0`.
- Historical b4 candidate/source; manifest SHA-256 is `c9214b0e451751ae451857519ce394fbcdb9c852a93021436a909eecb0c5e7e7`. Accepted artifact `installable-candidate-12-1` and its matching bytes/source are retained locally beyond CI expiry. An independent `--no-local` clone, `git fsck --full`, the complete repository candidate verifier, archive/RECORD/tag/content audit and Twine 7.0.0 `check --strict` passed. No public package was uploaded.
- The historical b4 PyPI set is five platform wheels plus one sdist. Wheels are 33.74–52.80 MiB, 10.05–17.08% larger than actual PyPI 0.3.5; sdist is 6.78 MiB, 57.15% larger. Windows/Linux x64 uncompressed TUI binaries are 128.18/122.88 MiB, below the 135 MiB budget; other targets are below 150 MiB. The growth is measured, not assumed unchanged. No intermediate universal wheel, test environment, private configuration or database is in the upload set.
- Earlier failed candidates remain failed historical evidence, not retroactive passes. They exposed macOS 15's private PingFang faces, the missing Linux CJK fixture prerequisite and Windows test synchronization. Those causes were fixed without weakening glyph, batching, ordering or data-preservation assertions; the final exact native execution above confirms the affected paths.
- Website PR #35 at `b9169498eeaa51f7371a27d659a72424ae4a8cfd` completes all ten 55-page manuals. Full local build, documentation/route/site/SEO/AI audits, TypeScript, 22 Bun/six Node tests, mobile/desktop browser samples and Lighthouse mobile pass. [Current remote CI](https://github.com/Re-bin/nanobot-web/actions/runs/40563408993) passed; deployment was skipped. It remains unmerged and undeployed.
- Full source evidence at `9ed984294…`: 8,915 Python tests passed / 53 platform or environment skips; channels 2,208 / 2; CLI 252 / 1; installer suite 80 / 1; dependency-impact checks 428 passed; strict Python types passed. Subsequent affected build checks passed 21 / 1. These retain their actual source identities under `.agent/workflow.md`.
- Earlier frontend evidence: TUI 310 tests / 1,986 assertions, native rendering 19 / 127, WebUI lint/types/build and dependency audit. These retain their original identities; current native package execution is separately recorded above.

## Upgrade and data-preservation evidence

The exact CI-produced f43 macOS arm64 wheel has SHA-256 `8ecc5bc425a43f8f3a31da5bcbee33d2dae2fbe5eb91f7d3ed7ce8f022b5b66c`.

- Genuine public 0.3.5 installations through pip, uv tool and pipx upgraded through their original owners to f43. Configuration and retained legacy bytes, authenticated canonical/display history, continued writes, second start and cleanup passed. This is not a one-click claim for 0.3.5, which lacks the new updater.
- A genuine tagged 0.3.5 source installation upgraded in the same clone through the fixed build hook. The same preservation and second-start checks passed. The actual baseline commit is `1bb712d3488915ca4ed9ccc1a93067ff722f5ab9`, not its annotated tag object.

These are private historical packages and a controlled feed, not public signature/catalogue validation.
- A real isolated source-installed WebUI/Gateway passed check-update feedback, stable/Preview preference persistence, refusal to downgrade an ahead-of-stable candidate, real restart/reconnect, retained authentication, migrated test conversation and exact unsent draft. No intercepted API or daily data was used. This is restart UI coverage, not a browser-driven package replacement.
- The five-platform 6407 candidate previously passed nine recovery scenarios/fifteen journeys per platform, with Windows `LongPathsEnabled=0`. It predates the new terminal/font gate and does not override its failure. Prepared artifacts and independent source handoffs retain their original hashes.

Historical b4 Docker acceptance used test-merge `4ee9d0c28c5266477e7f9bb007fd1c7f6b7699a8`, whose parents are main b07 and b4 and whose tree equals b4. The actual 0.3.5 baseline image was replaced on the same isolated volume by target image SHA-256 `ad12e47dfe632be4f251ce8bceb05695a74e7ebd828bf5c2dea8d17f971ff2dd`. Configuration/legacy bytes, authenticated canonical/display history, continued writes, second start, non-root operation and cleanup passed without external network. This is deployment-owner image replacement, **not** in-container updating or automatic Docker rollback. Report artifact: `docker-upgrade-40565642306-1`.

Installed-startup reports deliberately retain `interactive_ui_e2e=false`; Windows records process cleanup but `gateway_graceful_shutdown=false`. They are not browser interaction or Windows graceful-stop proofs. Genuine old-package and browser evidence above is inherited for their unchanged macOS/Linux and data/browser contracts. The #6507 delta affects Windows process identity, so Windows lifecycle and recovery need fresh exact-package evidence. Native fault-injection fixtures are not relabelled as previously published packages.

Both f43 source-installed and native-wheel runtime audits examined 110 distributions with no reported advisories; only unpublished nanobot-ai 0.4.0 could not be looked up on PyPI. This does not guarantee absence of vulnerabilities. Unchanged evidence is inherited with its original identity; it is never relabelled as a new package run.

## Remaining pre-merge gates

- [x] Fix and verify macOS 15 packaged font/rendering failure on both architectures; full current-candidate update/recovery is a separate gate below.
- [x] Finish the post-#6507/#6508 current-head CI and all five exact-byte native acceptance reports; preserve accepted new bytes and source before CI artifact expiry.
- [x] Complete website translations, full local build/audits/rendered review and current remote CI in website PR #35. Final-source reconciliation remains required; do not deploy early.
- [x] Recheck new package/license/source contents and replace the hash-locked manual PyPI instructions after acceptance. The Release article is updated in the previous release's style, including #6507/#6508 and their contributors; final merged range and tag links must be reconciled at publication.
- [ ] Obtain independent review and the maintainer's merge/publication decision. Current GitHub review decision remains `REVIEW_REQUIRED`; no unresolved review threads were present at the final check.

## Publication gates — require a later command

1. Merge the reviewed preparation only after explicit approval. Compare the actual merge result to the accepted candidate and rebuild/rebind/reverify changed source or package identity. Do not tag an unchecked later main tip.
2. Confirm the maintainer's at-least-three-year corresponding-source retention commitment and required signing/protected-environment approvals.
3. With publication authorization, tag the exact verified commit, publish complete immutable GitHub assets before PyPI, and verify actual public downloads.
4. Validate release signatures and complete public stable/Preview catalogue assets before advancing the update feed. The public Preview catalogue returned HTTP 404 during preparation; private controlled-feed tests do not prove public updates are available.
5. Merge/deploy the verified website and publish announcements when the promised downloads and links are live.

`docs/releasing.md` remains authoritative. Legacy goal-history collisions are not repaired by preventing new collisions; release notes retain that limitation. Daily checkouts, configuration and conversations remain untouched.

prs.title: fix(gateway): reduce lease writes and use Windows-safe I/O
prs.body:
## Why

Gateway status queries and the local-client monitor currently rewrite the lease JSON even when nothing changes, performing unnecessary file synchronization and atomic replacement. Necessary lease I/O also bypasses the Windows-safe atomic file helpers already used by gateway process records.

## What changed

- Keep lease snapshots read-only while still reporting only live clients, including PID-reuse detection.
- Persist monitor cleanup only when client records change; continue committing orphan shutdown under the existing lifecycle locks.
- Reuse `read_atomic_bytes()` and `replace_atomic()` for lease I/O, preserving UTF-8 decoding and allowing existing snapshot readers to retain the previous file during replacement on supported Windows filesystems.

## Scope

Keep the existing JSON format, cross-process locks, and lifecycle behavior. No database or retry policy is added. External handles that deny the required sharing can still block writes; this does not claim to resolve every cause of #6514. Process-record cleanup outside the lease is unchanged.

Related to #6514. Thanks to @BBTAN-bot for the report, and @balabommablock-cpu (B Rishabh Rao) for the Windows-safe I/O proposal and [patch](https://github.com/balabommablock-cpu/nanobot/commit/8d671457935e44579f37ceffe6dbaf61b36b00be), adapted here with a real snapshot-replacement regression test. Both contributors are credited in the commit history.

Resolves NAN-385

## Tradeoffs

Status queries filter stale clients in memory rather than cleaning the lease on disk. The monitor and lifecycle mutations remain responsible for persisted cleanup.

## Blast Radius

Local TUI/WebUI gateway status and lease monitoring on all platforms. Registration, release, and shutdown coordination retain their existing lock order. Windows uses the shared atomic-file implementation; POSIX continues to use ordinary reads and `os.replace()`.

## Verification

- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Regression coverage checks unchanged lease bytes/mtime during queries and steady polling, stale-client cleanup, and explicit versus on-demand lifetimes; existing lifecycle-race tests retained.
- Added a deterministic test that opens a real snapshot through the lease read path, performs an actual replacement before closing it, and verifies that the old reader sees the old state while a subsequent reader sees the new state. This test is included in the existing Windows and Linux Python CI suites.
- Local lint, type checking, and tests were not run; validation of the updated head is delegated to this PR's GitHub Actions.
