prs.title: fix(retry): prevent replay amplification and isolate backoff (NAN-313)
prs.body:
## Why

Nested retry owners multiply physical requests, replay already-delivered Telegram prefixes, and let failing destinations hold every outbound send slot while sleeping. Keep replay decisions with the domain owner, release resources before backoff, and remove duplicated recovery mechanics without adding a retry framework or dependency.

Fixes [NAN-313](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-313)

## What changed

- Hold outbound permits only for an adapter invocation, retaining bounded admission, destination FIFO, scheduled claim ordering, and pre-submission deadlines; add equal jitter to local manager/LLM backoff without changing server-hint rules.
- Prevent Telegram whole-message replay after per-part failures, disable nested SDK retries for internally created Bedrock clients, and close StepFun SSE response contexts before retry waits.
- Share request-only recovery across MCP wrappers and keep LLM stream/image/persistent recovery in an explicit domain loop; consolidate regression coverage into existing fixtures. No Tenacity dependency remains.

## Scope

Python outbound delivery, model-request retries, MCP wrapper recovery, and StepFun transcription resource lifetime. Preserve configured admission, scheduled unknown-result handling, provider continuation, cancellation, and public return shapes. Persistent-task recovery, other adapters' delivery policies, UI, configuration schemas, and dependency versions are unchanged.

## Tradeoffs

Removing nested retry budgets intentionally reaches exhaustion sooner; it does not promise equal success probability for every external fault sequence. Adapter-internal waits still occupy one invocation permit, and Telegram transport retries do not provide exactly-once delivery. Local jitter uses `[base / 2, base]`; provider/server Retry-After buffer and cap rules remain intact.

The final diff is production -77 lines and tests +668 lines, net +591. The proposed library adaptation was withdrawn because it added callbacks/state and maintenance cost without sufficient simplification.

## Blast Radius

ChannelManager scheduling affects ordinary outbound sends; Telegram and internally created Bedrock clients have intentional retry-policy changes. MCP tools/resources/prompts share one recovery owner, while rendering remains outside the replay boundary. Review focus: partial delivery, independent recovery budgets, active-permit release, cancellation, and response closure before sleep.

## Verification

Local checks ran on the exact published source delta against base `73a55e0b2fac17ae70641f028448201c4a0cb710`; commit preparation changes no source content. The current target branch is newer, so these local results are not merge-result CI results.

- **FAIL:** CI-scope Windows Python suite, isolated HOME, `-n 2 --dist loadfile`, the existing three CLI/native/WSL files excluded for serial execution, and `--cov=nanobot`: **9989 passed, 130 skipped, 5 failed; coverage 85.43%** (75% threshold unchanged). Four failures reproduce on the baseline environment: copied Scoop rg shim companion, Windows symlink permission, and two missing-USERNAME cases. The fifth is an unchanged shell-test marker-write race: normal focused runs pass on both snapshots; exposing the existing non-atomic marker window reproduces the same empty-content assertion on both. The full run remains FAIL.
- **PASS:** excluded serial CLI/native/WSL files: **222 passed, 1 skipped**. Ruff, import boundaries, dependency consistency, `git diff --check HEAD`, and strict typechecking of affected production files pass.
- **FAIL:** full-project BasedPyright retains the same two baseline `setproctitle` diagnostics; no affected-production diagnostics.
- **PASS:** real FastMCP stdio/connect/registry/reconnect/timeout/cancel/aclose comparison; five balanced fresh-process loopback SDK/MessageBus pairs preserve work/error/result counts; real unread-response SSE closure and cancellation regressions. These use deterministic local services, not production accounts or public models.

Performance evidence distinguishes the policy comparison from the final simplification rerun: before/after retry-policy probes measured Telegram 9→3 HTTP requests, successful-prefix submissions 3→1, and Bedrock continuous-503 requests 20→4. Final-source reruns preserve the reduced counts. An equal-work public-MessageBus fixture (65 sends, 33 completed destinations) reduces healthy-destination queueing under 32 sleeping retries from about 1009ms to 0.1ms. These are fault-isolation/request-count results, not general model throughput claims.

Seven new original-base/final bookkeeping pairs show transient→success p50 16.4→16.1µs, p99 31.7→33.5µs, and worst-run p99 37.7→43.1µs; provider-import medians are 101.7→107.5ms with overlapping ranges. No general speedup or zero-tail-regression claim. The issue records scope, acceptance criteria, measurements, and local evidence identifiers; raw local logs remain outside tracked source.

issues.body:
### Bug Description

Running `npm audit fix --workspaces=false` in `~/.hermes/hermes-agent` successfully resolves the agent-browser npm vulnerabilities reported by `hermes doctor` — confirmed via `hermes doctor` showing "no known vulnerabilities" immediately afterward. However, the same vulnerabilities reliably reappear after the next `hermes update`, because the update's Node dependency step reinstalls fresh from the upstream `package-lock.json`, which still pins the vulnerable package versions. This has now been observed and independently verified across two full cycles.


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `hermes doctor` and note agent-browser flagged with npm vulnerabilities (e.g., "0 critical, 1 high, 1 moderate")
2. Run `cd ~/.hermes/hermes-agent && npm audit fix --workspaces=false`
3. Run `hermes doctor` again — confirm agent-browser now shows "no known vulnerabilities"
4. Run `hermes update` (any update that reinstalls Node dependencies fresh — visible in the update log as "added 550 packages")
5. Run `hermes doctor` again — observe agent-browser's vulnerabilities have returned, identical to step 1


### Expected Behavior

Once `npm audit fix` resolves a vulnerability locally, a subsequent `hermes update` should not silently reintroduce it — either by preserving the fixed lockfile state where compatible, or by re-running the audit fix as part of the update's own Node dependency step.


### Actual Behavior

Confirmed across two independent cycles (Sept 14 → Sept 18, and Sept 18 → Sept 19): each time, `npm audit fix --workspaces=false` cleanly resolved agent-browser's vulnerabilities (confirmed via `hermes doctor`), and each time, the very next `hermes update` reintroduced the identical vulnerability set (1 high, 1 moderate) after reinstalling Node dependencies fresh.

issues.title: Request: add niubuhui818-oss to the pull request limit bypass list
issues.body:
Hello,

Since 2026-10-30 this account (`niubuhui818-oss`) has been unable to open new pull requests against `NousResearch/hermes-agent`:

- REST `POST /repos/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls` → `404 {"message":"Not Found","documentation_url":".../create-a-pull-request"}`
- GraphQL `createPullRequest` → `FORBIDDEN: niubuhui818-oss does not have the correct permissions to execute 'CreatePullRequest'`
- Pushing branches and opening issues still work (this issue is being opened by the same token).

This matches the repository's pull request creation limit for users without write access, as reported in #144873 (and #143992 / #144309 before it). I measured the boundary for our account with a zero-side-effect probe — `head` points at a branch that does not exist, so the request can never create anything:

| open PRs by us | probe result |
|:--|:--|
| 5 | `404 Not Found` (write path rejected before `head` is validated) |
| 4 | `422 Validation Failed (head invalid)` — request format is fine |
| 5 again (after opening #147075) | `404 Not Found` |

The same probe against `cli/cli` returns `422 head invalid`, so the request itself is well-formed, and `draft=true` is rejected here too (drafts count toward the limit). So the limit for this account is 5 open pull requests. I cannot read the configured value itself — `GET /interaction-limits/pulls/creation-cap` returns 403 for non-maintainers — the number above is inferred from behaviour, not read from config.

Current state:

- 5 open PRs: #146541, #146688, #146697, #146701, #147075
- #147075 stacks #146688 and #146701 plus three further secret-leak fixes; if it is accepted, both of those can be closed, which would bring us back to 3.
- To open #147075 we closed #146518 (a 17-line i18n string fix); it can be reopened if you would rather keep that one than the security fix.
- One finished, locally tested fix is waiting on the pushed branch `fix/cron-lazy-tick-import` (single file, `cron/__init__.py`) and cannot be opened as a PR.

Could a maintainer add `niubuhui818-oss` to the pull request limit bypass list? If you would rather we keep the count low, tell us which PRs to close or consolidate and we will. We will not use another account to work around the limit.

Thank you.

issues.body:
## Summary

Short CJK `session_search` queries can enter the LIKE fallback and scan a large message corpus even with `after='24h'` and a small output limit. In a long-lived installation this produced a tool timeout at about 420 seconds; diagnostic log excerpts recorded the underlying `like_scan` finishing after about 720 seconds. The latter is saved observational evidence, not a fresh end-to-end replay; rotated logs are no longer at their original file/line positions.

This report is about the SQL access path and cancellation boundary, not the older auxiliary-LLM summarization hang in #7725. #64559 and #129146 address adjacent LIKE matching/sort contracts; this report does not propose competing fixes for those contracts.

## Source and scope

- Tested installed baseline: `808520532cf7c48c3eccb09476fb3cde379b02e9`.
- Current upstream inspected: `c538ec5f402e8078248becacd474e47a08c6e79a`. Its `_search_cjk` implementation still contains the same relevant LIKE construction. The full candidate test suite was NOT rebased/run on this newer head.
- SQLite 3.53.1; approximately 41 GB state database; bigram CJK search unavailable for the affected route. No database dump, message text, credentials, or private infrastructure details are included.

## Affected path

`tools/session_search_tool.py` discovery -> `SessionDB.search_messages` -> `hermes_state_search.py::_search_cjk` -> `_like_rows`.

A representative input is `query='"留言" "格式"', after='24h', limit=3, sort='newest'`. In this configuration two-character terms do not qualify for trigram matching and fall through to LIKE. The tool internally requests up to 300 matching rows before grouping, despite the public result limit of 3. The time predicate is on `sessions.started_at`, not message timestamps.

The executed fallback plan was:

```text
SCAN m USING INDEX idx_messages_display_page
SEARCH s USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_sessions_1 (id=?)
USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY
```

The existing session-time index is not used to narrow the message scan first. A read-only replay with a SQLite progress handler was interrupted after 10 seconds. **Interrupted is not an empty successful result.** An indexed session-window candidate completed two SELECT measurements in approximately 3.17 and 2.83 seconds (five rows each), but these are candidate-only measurements on live data, not same-snapshot baseline/candidate speedups or full-tool timings.

## Experimental patch and correctness limitation

We prepared a narrowly gated candidate: only the time-filtered CJK LIKE path, preserve all existing matching/filtering/output behavior, retain the original message index traversal, and add a redundant indexed session-window predicate. No schema change, index creation, archive, cleanup, or live-runtime patch was performed.

Independent local fixture tests: **21 cases passed**, including 300 randomized fixtures with zero differences against the baseline. They cover nonempty results, role/source/inactive filters, time boundaries, offset/limit, quoted short CJK terms, ordinary LIKE, missing-index fallback, and cross-session timestamp ties.

**This is NOT a merge-ready fix.** A naive sessions-first rewrite was rejected because equal-timestamp pagination changed (`[6,16,3]` vs `[6,8,15]` in a synthetic fixture). The attached candidate preserves observed index visitation order on the tested SQLite version but still relies on implementation-specific equal-key sort behavior and exact EXPLAIN text. The implementation comment claiming unchanged ordering is an unproven assertion, not an acceptance result. Maintainer guidance on an explicit deterministic secondary ordering would enable a simpler, robust optimization without promising to preserve accidental historical ordering.

Separately, cancellation should interrupt SQLite work, not merely time out the waiting caller. This has not yet been fixed or end-to-end tested. Existing quote/operator and sort semantics should remain a separate change coordinated with #64559 / #129146.

## Requested direction

1. Review a selective session-window SQL path for the LIKE fallback, with an explicit stable tie-order contract rather than planner-specific ordering assumptions.
2. Ensure a tool timeout/cancellation can terminate the outstanding SQLite scan and report cancellation rather than an empty search.
3. Keep semantic corrections and the performance/cancellation fix independently reviewable.

We are supplying the experimental diff below for review, not requesting a blind merge. The local runtime remains unmodified.

<details>
<summary>Experimental diff against the tested baseline (not merge-ready)</summary>

```diff
--- a/hermes_state_search.py	2026-10-07 19:28:20.670330963 +0000
+++ b/hermes_state_search.py	2026-10-07 19:28:20.672330994 +0000
@@ -961,9 +961,10 @@
                 fail_open, exc)
             return None
 
-    def _like_rows(self, where: List[str], params: list, *, order_by: str, limit_sql: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
+    def _like_rows(self, where: List[str], params: list, *, order_by: str, limit_sql: str,
+                   from_sql: str = "messages m") -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
         """Canonical-table LIKE scan; ``params[0]`` is the snippet anchor term."""
-        sql = _search_select_sql(_LIKE_SNIPPET_SQL, "messages m", where, order_by, limit_sql)
+        sql = _search_select_sql(_LIKE_SNIPPET_SQL, from_sql, where, order_by, limit_sql)
         return [dict(row) for row in self._read_all(sql, params)]
 
     @staticmethod
@@ -1214,8 +1215,45 @@
```

labels.name: tool/memory

labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

issues.body:
## What happens

`build_memory_context_block` (agent/memory_manager.py, `main` f86276d) stamps the composed recall block into the
user row's `api_content`, and that row is replayed on every later request while it stays in the window. The
docstring of `_drop_repeated_recall_lines` (lines 326–333) says so: *"each duplicate is paid once per turn, forever"*.

That function removes repeats **inside one block**. Repeats **across turns** are not removed: when a conversation
stays on a topic, the provider returns the same facts turn after turn, and each turn stamps another full copy. With
a provider that injects five one-line facts (~60 tokens each), a 20-turn on-topic conversation carries 20 copies of
the same ~300 tokens until compression — about 6k tokens of repeated recall replayed on every request, growing
quadratically in total cost.

## Why core is the right place

Only core knows which rows are still in the window and when compression or `/new` removes them. A provider can only
approximate that (I ship a per-session "don't repeat for N turns" window in the `holographic` provider as a
stopgap: itpartypattaya/hermes-plugin-holographic 0.3.0), and every provider would have to reimplement it.

## Proposal

Keep, per session, the set of recall lines (the same normalised self-contained bullets `_drop_repeated_recall_lines`
already recognises) that are present in the rows currently in the window. When composing a new block, drop bullets
already in that set. Clear the entries of rows that compression removes, and on session switch / reset. Bullets with
continuation lines keep today's behaviour (never dropped).

Happy to open a PR if this direction is acceptable.

issues.body:
## Summary
The terminal lifecycle guard falsely blocks benign commands that invoke Node.js CLI bundles (e.g. `obsidian-headless`' `ob` CLI) with:

> Blocked: command or referenced script cannot restart, stop, or uninstall the gateway from inside the gateway process.

The block is caused by the **64 remote-read cap** introduced in the Sep 3 scan-budget commits (`d99eed7d83`, `e4c1e56d5d`) interacting with the recursive referenced-script walk.

## Regression range
- Works on: **2026-08-28** (before budget cap)
- Broken on: **2026-09-08** (`main` at `d4d4ecfae0c135b7bb52ff4f782ffef17bbc90c7`)
- Introducing commits: `d99eed7d83` "perf(cron): bound the lifecycle guard's whole-walk scan work" and `e4c1e56d5d` "perf(cron): 1 MiB walk budget".

## Reproduction

```python
# /home/gilad/.npm-global/bin/ob is obsidian-headless v0.0.13, a 216 KB minified Node bundle
from cron.lifecycle_guard import contains_gateway_lifecycle_command_or_referenced_script

contains_gateway_lifecycle_command_or_referenced_script(
    "/home/gilad/.npm-global/bin/ob --version",
    cwd="/home/gilad/.npm-global/bin",
    read_remote_script=lambda p: None,  # terminal guard supplies a real callback
)
# Returns True (blocked) because the remote-read budget exhausts.
```

With `read_remote_script=None` the function returns `False`, confirming the block depends on the remote-read path.

## Root cause

1. The command's executable is `/home/gilad/.npm-global/bin/ob`.
2. `_iter_referenced_shell_scripts` yields this path as a "referenced script".
3. The guard reads the file successfully (it is text, not binary).
4. It then **shell-tokenizes the entire minified JavaScript bundle** to look for nested scripts.
5. The bundle contains **152 slash-containing tokens** from regex literals and strings, e.g. `/^[x00-x19s,[]{}]/`, `/n+/g`, `/usr/bin/env`.
6. Each bogus token is treated as a candidate script path; when `read_remote_script` is provided, the guard tries to read it remotely.
7. After **64 remote reads** the budget is exhausted and the guard **fails closed**, blocking the command.

Before `d99eed7d83` there was no `_MAX_LIFECYCLE_SCAN_REMOTE_READS` cap, so the walk could finish and return `False`.

## Why this is a bug class, not a one-off

The recursive walk is only meaningful for **POSIX shell source**. Feeding non-shell interpreters (Node, Python, Ruby, etc.) to `shlex` produces path-shaped garbage and burns the scan budget without improving security. Any sufficiently large interpreted-executable bundle with regex literals or URL strings will trigger this.

## Suggested fix

Only recurse into referenced scripts whose first line indicates a POSIX shell shebang (`#!/bin/sh`, `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, etc.). This preserves the budget's DoS intent while avoiding false positives on non-shell bundles.

## Environment

- Host: Debian 13 VPS
- Hermes: `main` at `d4d4ecfae0c135b7bb52ff4f782ffef17bbc90c7`
- Obsidian CLI: `obsidian-headless` v0.0.13
- File: `cron/lifecycle_guard.py`, `_contains_unsafe_gateway_action` (recursive walk)

## Related commits/PRs

- `d99eed7d83` perf(cron): bound the lifecycle guard's whole-walk scan work (#78398)
- `e1a791b9f6` refactor(cron): fold review findings into the lifecycle scan budget
- `e4c1e56d5d` perf(cron): 1 MiB walk budget
- `2fe6fd9b6c` refactor(terminal): lifted script reader (provided the callback that now exhausts the cap)

issues.title: `hermes chat -r` on a messaging-platform session, then a clean CLI exit, permanently detaches the channel — the next inbound message lands in a brand-new empty session (`cli_close` is not recoverable)
issues.body:
## The problem, plainly

A messaging session (verified on Feishu) keeps its channel routing as long as only the gateway
touches it. But when the session is opened once from the classic CLI via `hermes chat -r
<session>` and then exited with a normal exit command (`/exit`, `/quit`, EOF — all of them), the
CLI teardown stamps the session row with `end_reason='cli_close'`.

`cli_close` is on neither side of the gateway's stale-route contract: it is not in the
reopenable whitelist (`_RECOVERABLE_END_REASONS` = `agent_close`, `ws_orphan_reap`,
`superseded_by_resume`, `startup_orphan_reap`), and it is not a user-facing reset boundary
either. So the next message from the channel takes the stale-route self-heal, fails to recover
the original session, and **silently starts a brand-new empty session** — the channel's whole
history is orphaned while the original row still sits in state.db with all its messages.

This is the same failure shape as #118196 (CLI→Slack `/handoff`), but on a path that fix does
not reach: `chat -r` attach leaves no `handoff_state` marker on the row.

## Reproduce (field-tested on Feishu; the mechanism is platform-independent)

Deterministic on v0.22.5; the four steps below were reproduced on a live deployment:

1. A Feishu-bound conversation `X` exists and is healthy (messages answered in-channel).
2. Open it from a shell with `hermes chat -r X`, chat or just look, then exit with a normal
   exit command. The row for `X` now carries `end_reason='cli_close'`
   (`cli_tui_runtime_mixin.py`, `_tui_shutdown`: `end_session(_closing_sid, "cli_close")` —
   unconditional at that call site).
3. Send another message from Feishu. The gateway logs the stale-route self-heal, drops the
   routing entry, cannot recover `X` (see predicate below), and the reply comes from a
   **brand-new session `Y`** with no memory of the conversation. The channel now routes to `Y`.
4. Recovery of `X` is possible but takes two conditions together: delete `Y` (which drops the
   routing entry that now points at it), **and** re-activate `X` through a client connection
   that writes new chat messages (which clears `ended_at` via `reopen_session`). After both,
   the next Feishu message finds `X` again through peer recovery and the original conversation
   continues.

Boundary note: deleting `Y` alone did not restore routing on the deployment where this was
observed — by the recovery predicate below, that is expected, since `X` is still ended with a
non-recoverable reason and no routing entry names it; only the row-level predicate was checked
here, so treat the exact one-condition-vs-two-conditions line as verified only to the extent
described.

## Root cause — two subsystem contracts, again

1. **The self-heal's reopen whitelist.** Routing recovery adopts a row only when
   `ended_at IS NULL OR end_reason IN (recoverable set)` (the peer-recovery queries in
   `hermes_state_gateway.py`; the tuple in `hermes_state_common.py`). `gateway/session.py`
   says it outright: stale-route recovery *"reopens agent_close / ws_orphan_reap rows, fresh
   session for other end_reasons"*.
2. **The CLI teardown's stamp.** `_tui_shutdown` ends the closing session with `cli_close`
   for every exit path, with no exemption at that call site for a session the CLI merely
   *resumed* rather than created. Notably, other steps in the same shutdown flow (the
   interrupt step and the finalize step) do carry `_gateway_owns_session_end` /
   `_handed_off_session_ids` exemptions — the `end_session` call is the one step without one.

Net effect: a messaging session that a CLI has merely *viewed* becomes un-recoverable for its
own channel the moment the CLI exits cleanly.

## Why the existing fix doesn't reach this path

#118196 fixed the `/handoff` variant in 61274a100b ("fix(gateway): recover a session a
completed handoff owns") by widening the recovery predicate for rows carrying
`handoff_state='completed'`. That marker is written by `/handoff` — `hermes chat -r` attach
writes nothing equivalent, so the widened predicate never matches. Verified:

- the deployment where this reproduced runs v0.22.5, which contains 61274a100b — the failure
  still occurs on the `chat -r` path;
- current `upstream/main` (f30105a0b4) still has the unconditional
  `end_session(_closing_sid, "cli_close")` in `_tui_shutdown`.

## Suggested fix (either side; not prescriptive)

- **A (CLI side, narrowest):** in `_tui_shutdown`, skip the `cli_close` stamp when the closing
  session is a messaging-platform row the CLI resumed (`source` is a messaging platform, or the
  row carries a gateway `session_key`) — a viewer exiting is not a conversation ending.
- **B (reason semantics):** stamp such rows with a reason the recovery treats as reopenable
  (e.g. `superseded_by_resume`, or a new `viewer_detach`) instead of `cli_close`, so the
  channel's next inbound reopens the row exactly as the gateway would after a restart.

Either keeps deliberate CLI-session closes (`/exit` on a CLI-born session) unchanged; the
distinction is only about sessions whose lifecycle another surface owns.

issues.title: Multi-branch `anyOf` on `terminal.notify` rejected by Vertex-backed OpenAI-compatible endpoints (400 on all agent turns)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/tools
labels.description: Tool registry, model_tools, toolsets

labels.name: tool/terminal
labels.description: Terminal execution and process management

labels.name: provider/gemini
labels.description: Google Gemini (AI Studio, Cloud Code)

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

issues.body:
## Bug description

Hermes' `terminal` tool schema makes every tool-bearing request fail with HTTP 400 on Vertex-backed OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Google's OpenAI→FunctionDeclaration translation cannot represent the multi-branch `anyOf` union declared on the `notify` parameter, and Vertex rejects the entire request:

```text
HTTP 400: {"error":{"code":400,"message":"Unable to submit request because `terminal`
functionDeclaration `parameters.notify` schema specified incorrect schema type field.
For schema with items, schema type should be ARRAY.
Learn more: https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/multimodal/function-calling",
"status":"INVALID_ARGUMENT"}}
```

Because `terminal` is included in every agent turn's tool list, all agent turns fail on such endpoints (model-agnostic; requests without tools pass). Flagging as family-adjacent to #71804 — same story of Gemini/Vertex strict schema validation rejecting Hermes' tool declarations, different root cause (union vs missing `items`).

## Root cause

`tools/terminal_tool.py` declares `notify` as a multi-branch union:

```python
"notify": {
    "description": "With background=true: notify=true fires exactly one notification ...",
    "anyOf": [
        {"type": "boolean"},
        {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
    ]
}
```

This is valid OpenAI-style/JSON Schema, but Google's OpenAI→FunctionDeclaration translator merges the union branches into a single node carrying `items` under a non-array type, which Vertex's schema validation rejects.

## Reproduction / isolation (verified 2026-09-12, Hermes v0.21.1)

A/B test with the identical real tool list (the full 34 tools from a standard agent turn in this install), toggling ONLY the `notify` node:

| Variant | Result |
|---|---|
| `notify` as `anyOf: [boolean, array<string>]` | HTTP 400 — error above, every model |
| `notify` as `{"type": "boolean"}` | HTTP 200; a tool-triggering round then returns a normal `tool_calls: terminal {...}` |

Same endpoint, same credential, same payload except one schema node ⇒ schema-shape causality.

## Suggested fix

Split the union into two single-typed parameters. The dispatcher already supports both forms (`_handle_terminal` maps a list-valued `notify` onto the legacy `watch_patterns` arg and still accepts `notify_on_complete`), so this is an API-surface-only change:

```python
"notify": {
    "type": "boolean",
    "description": "With background=true: notify=true fires exactly one notification ...",
    "default": False
},
"watch_patterns": {
    "type": "array",
    "items": {"type": "string"},
    "description": "With background=true: notify when a line matches any of these patterns ..."
}
```

Alternatively (defense in depth): collapse multi-branch unions for strict backends at the request-building layer, so future union additions degrade instead of failing the provider.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.21.1 (2026.9.7), upstream `b0c383cd`
- Still present in `origin/main` @ `3e09e5a15` (checked 2026-09-12)
- OS: Windows 10

issues.title: `_recover_rate_limit` sleeps up to 600s on `Retry-After` before rotating the credential pool on an Anthropic account rate limit
issues.body:
On v0.22.5, `_recover_rate_limit` in `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py` declines pool rotation on the first HTTP 429 of a turn (`not has_retried_429`) unless `usage_limit_reached` is `True`. `usage_limit_reached` checks only `"usage_limit_reached"`, `"gousagelimit"`, `"usage limit reached"`, and `"usage limit has been reached"`.

Anthropic's account rate-limit 429 returns `type: "rate_limit_error"` and `message: "This request would exceed your account's rate limit. Please try again later."` with a long `Retry-After` header. Because that phrasing matches neither token tuple, `_recover_rate_limit` returns `(False, True)` without calling `mark_exhausted_and_rotate`, and `compute_error_backoff` sleeps for `min(Retry-After, RETRY_AFTER_CAP_S)` (600 seconds) on the exhausted credential before attempt 2 can rotate to the next healthy pool entry.

Treating `"exceed your account's rate limit"` and any `reset_at` beyond `LIVE_RETRY_WAIT_CAP_S` (60 seconds) as `usage_limit_reached` lets multi-credential pools rotate immediately on the first 429 while keeping the single retry for short transient throttles.

issues.title: Switching a new Desktop/TUI session's model before the first prompt fails to persist the rebuilt system prompt and the `model_switch` marker
issues.body:
On v0.22.5, when a user switches the model on a freshly created session before sending the first message, `_set_model` builds the in-process `AIAgent` (which has `agent._session_db` bound, while `agent._session_db_created` is still `False` because `session.create` defers row creation to `prompt.submit`) and calls `_commit_agent_switch`.

1. `_persist_live_session_system_prompt` sets `agent._cached_system_prompt` in memory and calls `db.update_system_prompt(...)`, whose `UPDATE sessions SET system_prompt_hash = ...` touches 0 rows because the session row does not exist yet. When the first prompt is then submitted, `_ensure_session_db_row` inserts the row with `system_prompt_hash = NULL`, and `build_turn_context` sees `agent._cached_system_prompt is not None` and skips `_restore_or_build_system_prompt`, leaving `system_prompt_hash` `NULL` on the row.
2. `_append_model_switch_marker` checks `if db is None: _ensure_session_db_row(session)`. Because `agent._session_db` is not `None`, it skips `_ensure_session_db_row` and calls `db.append_message(...)`, which raises `sqlite3.IntegrityError: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed`.

Calling `_ensure_session_db_row(session)` in both helpers whenever `not getattr(agent, "_session_db_created", False)` fixes both paths.

issues.title: [Bug]: Termux canary omits the MCP SDK; configured HTTP MCP servers register no tools

labels.name: type/bug

labels.name: tool/mcp

labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

issues.body:
## Bug Description

The published self-contained aarch64 Termux package `0.21.7~canary.20261013T070740Z-1` starts successfully and passes its own installed-bundle gates, but its Python environment has no `mcp` SDK or `rpds`. A configured HTTP MCP server therefore registers no tools. This is a packaging/support request for MCP users, not a claim that the minimal CLI/TUI package is generally broken. If core+acp is intentionally the default, a supported tested optional-install procedure with Android native-wheel availability would also meet the need.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Obtain the package from the [official Termux canary Packages index](https://hermes-assets.nousresearch.com/releases/termux/canary/dists/hermes-canary/main/binary-aarch64/Packages). SHA256: `aa4755349b1d6d9edcf989755aaa017ed628c39fab5c576aacb47978a61521df`. Rechecked before filing: this is still the package listed in that index.
2. Install in a disposable Termux environment, or mount the unpacked payload at `$PREFIX/lib/hermes-agent` and run its normal launcher. Our verification used the unpacked artifact, mounted read-only in the pinned termux-docker ARM64 image; it was NOT installed on a production phone.
3. Under the launcher's Python environment, run `import mcp.client.streamable_http` and `import rpds`.
4. Call the real Hermes registration path with a test server:

       from tools.mcp_tool_discovery import register_mcp_servers
       print(register_mcp_servers({'probe': {'url': 'http://127.0.0.1:1/mcp'}}))

   The localhost URL avoids contacting a remote server. SDK absence stops registration before transport; this is not a connection-failure report.

## Expected Behavior

Users who configure MCP on the Termux package can enable its client through a working native install path, without modifying Hermes source or manually injecting site-packages. Including the MCP extra in the payload would provide that path without compiling dependencies on the phone.

## Actual Behavior

    IMPORT_FAIL mcp.client.streamable_http ModuleNotFoundError No module named 'mcp'
    IMPORT_FAIL rpds ModuleNotFoundError No module named 'rpds'
    MCP_SDK_AVAILABLE False
    MCP_REGISTRATION []

Adjacent cases that are NOT broken: the unmodified vendor validator passed CLI_AND_STDLIB_IMPORTS_OK, FFMPEG_MEDIA_CONVERSION_OK, PM_RUNTIME_TOOLS_OK, APT_UPDATE_REFUSAL_OK, TUI_SETUP_SCREEN_OK and INSTALLED_BUNDLE_VALIDATION_OK. The Termux package can run the base CLI/TUI.

## Affected Component

Setup / Installation; Tools (MCP).

## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A (packaging / direct registration).

## Debug Report

Isolated package verification, not a production profile dump. No shared debug upload was made. Interpreter: Python 3.14.6, sys.platform=android. Image: termux/termux-docker@sha256:c14ffb703abf44f2d3bf7fdffdcc50df7d1454d09c705be190e0342a0b47f303, ARM64 under emulation. Payload SHA256 above. Launcher init used unchanged; a separate test string replaced only the final exec to run the probe, with no edits to package files.

## Operating System

Android/Bionic userspace in pinned termux-docker, emulated on Linux x86-64.

## Python Version

3.14.6 (package bundled interpreter).

## Hermes Version

0.21.7+canary.20261013T070740Z; package version `0.21.7~canary.20261013T070740Z-1`.

## Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

With Git, clang, make and pkg-config installed in the pinned Termux container, `hermes pm install --extra mcp` proceeds to rebuilding the complete core dependency generation, then fails on `pillow-heif==1.6.0`: `The headers or library files could not be found for libheif`. `UV_FIND_LINKS=/wheels hermes pm install --extra mcp` fails identically even though that directory contains a matching Android pillow-heif wheel. The PM worker uses `uv sync --frozen`; the shipped lock does not record those local Android artifacts. No application generation was committed.

The lock pins rpds-py 2026.6.3. As a separate PM API control, `pm.ensure_environment(name, ["rpds-py==2026.6.3"], explicit=True)` fails without Rust (`Target triple not supported by rustup: aarch64-unknown-linux-android`). With UV_FIND_LINKS pointing at a matching cp314 Android wheel, the same PM API succeeds and its interpreter imports rpds and performs a HashTrieMap lookup. This proves that wheel and PM forwarding work for a newly resolved isolated environment, NOT that the frozen application MCP install works. No raw pip/uv mutation was used. A larger native-toolchain installation remains untested.

## Root Cause Analysis (optional)

At current main `e06df9c2eae6901f4c88f464e0ae6e753c0428b8`, scripts/termux/termux_build.sh's requirements export selects `--extra acp` only. pyproject declares MCP separately. The published native-wheels list excludes rpds-py. `tools/mcp_tool.py` probes find_spec('mcp') and discovery returns [] if the SDK is unavailable. Current-main packaging consequence is inferred from the export/source, not a new full package build or a tested PR.

Open PR #89232 changes inclusion of MCP through the all extra; it does not add MCP to the Termux core+acp export. Open PR #123773 preserves already-installed MCP during legacy venv migration; it does not add MCP to the self-contained Termux payload. Neither is a competing implementation of this request.

## Proposed Fix (optional)

Consider exporting `--extra mcp` for Termux, mapping rpds-py to its actual import module `rpds` in the native-wheel gate, and adding an installed-bundle check for `mcp.client.streamable_http`. A downstream build of the older 0.21.4 base has successfully built the native rpds dependency and shipped these imports. That is prior evidence, NOT a tested patch against current main; the older patch also carries wake extras and is not submitted verbatim. Alternatively document/provide a tested PM extras lane for the Android native dependency closure. Priority and default package-size tradeoffs belong to the maintainer.

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

Yes, after agreeing the intended packaging shape and verifying current-main regression/build tests. No untested patch is presented as a working fix.

AI-assisted investigation and draft; commands were exercised against the published artifact. No production configuration, credentials or private endpoints are included.

issues.title: Gateway freezes every session at startup while it checks retained API images

labels.name: type/perf
labels.description: Performance improvement or optimization

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: area/sessions
labels.description: Session lifecycle, resume, persistence, history

issues.body:
With the API server enabled, the gateway checks at every start which retained API images a session still references. The check runs on the owner loop and costs messages × images, so a heavy image user of an OpenAI-compatible client freezes every session on that gateway for seconds to minutes. It runs again on every API adapter reconnect, profile hot-serve and API session delete.

**Steps** (`main` at `ccc6956350`)
1. Enable the API server, on a `state.db` with about 20,000 messages and 1,000 images sent through `/v1/chat/completions` in chats that still exist.
2. Restart the gateway, then message the bot from any platform.

**Expected:** messages are served right away; images a live chat holds need no transcript check; the check costs about messages + images.

**Actual:** the loop is blocked for about 8 s at 1,000 images and 47 s at 5,000. Every API session delete pays the same scan again.

Also: if SQLite raises in the retired-media pass after `delete_session` commits (locked or corrupt store), the delete raises although the session is gone. `DELETE /api/sessions/{id}` answers 500 and skips removing its routing entries.

**Cause**
- Boot ([`run_startup.py:1342`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/ccc695635094d7615373db267b77f894d978b1a0/gateway/run_startup.py#L1342)), reconnect ([`run_adapters.py:910`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/ccc695635094d7615373db267b77f894d978b1a0/gateway/run_adapters.py#L910)) and hot-serve ([`run_runtime.py:380`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/ccc695635094d7615373db267b77f894d978b1a0/gateway/run_runtime.py#L380)) call `collect_unheld_api_images` synchronously on the loop ([`session_api_turn.py:330`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/ccc695635094d7615373db267b77f894d978b1a0/gateway/session_api_turn.py#L330)).
- Every on-disk API image is a candidate, held or not: the history scan runs for all of them ([`session_ingress_media.py:528`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/ccc695635094d7615373db267b77f894d978b1a0/gateway/session_ingress_media.py#L528)) before holders are checked under the write lock (line 536).
- `_history_mentions` runs `instr` per row × digest (line 497), then tests every needle against every matched row (line 502).
- `collect_retired_media` ([`hermes_state_media.py:55`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/ccc695635094d7615373db267b77f894d978b1a0/hermes_state_media.py#L55)) has no storage-error boundary, and every delete and prune path calls it after its commit ([`hermes_state_sessions.py:1757`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/ccc695635094d7615373db267b77f894d978b1a0/hermes_state_sessions.py#L1757)).

Listed in #140297 (Smaller follow-ups). Still reproduces at `ccc6956350`.

Fix: #140906 (reopened 29 Oct, rebased onto `main` `ef75bc7088` as `5ef5ed4540`).

Follow-up to #140090, which #140233 fixed (delete and startup recovery no longer fail at 1,000+ images).

Refs #134889
Refs #140297

issues.title: [Bug]: copilot-acp loads by directory presence and emits BrokenPipeError traceback when no credentials are configured
issues.body:
### Bug Description

The optional copilot-acp model provider plugin loads and runs its handler solely because the directory plugins/model-providers/copilot-acp/ exists in the hermes-agent tree. There is no configuration key, environment variable, or feature flag to disable it.When no Copilot credentials are present (the normal case for users who do not use this provider), the plugin’s handler raises BrokenPipeError during gateway startup / provider discovery. The full traceback is written to the logs on every start.Impact:
Persistent log noise on every gateway start.
Interferes with automated update review and shadow processes that parse logs or expect clean startup.
Users who do not want the plugin cannot silence it without deleting the directory.
Deleting the directory marks tracked files as deleted, which dirties the working tree. This can cause update-policy checks that treat any dirty tracked files as BLOCK to fire incorrectly. Subsequent hermes update or git checkout operations restore the directory, reintroducing the noise.
Steps to reproduce:
Fresh or existing install of hermes-agent that includes plugins/model-providers/copilot-acp/.
Do not set any Copilot credentials in config.yaml, .env, or the environment.
Start or restart the gateway (hermes gateway run or systemd unit).
Observe BrokenPipeError traceback from the copilot-acp handler in the gateway log.
Expected:
Optional providers that require credentials should either:
Remain unloaded unless explicitly enabled, or
Detect missing credentials and exit silently (no traceback, no error-level log), or
Provide a documented config key (e.g. providers.copilot_acp.enabled: false) that prevents the handler from running.
Actual:
Directory presence alone is sufficient to load and execute the handler. Missing credentials produce a BrokenPipeError traceback on every startup.Environment (observed):
Hermes Agent versions through at least v2026.9.14 / v0.21.x
Plugin path: plugins/model-providers/copilot-acp/
Error: BrokenPipeError in the plugin handler during init/discovery
No disable mechanism present in config or code
This behavior forces users who do not use Copilot into a choice between permanent log noise or a permanently dirty working tree. A proper opt-in or silent-skip path would eliminate the issue.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install or use a hermes-agent checkout that contains plugins/model-providers/copilot-acp/.
2. Ensure no Copilot credentials are set in ~/.hermes/config.yaml, ~/.hermes/.env, or the environment.
3. Start or restart the gateway (hermes gateway run, or systemctl --user restart hermes-gateway.service).
4. Check the gateway log.
5. Observe BrokenPipeError traceback from the copilot-acp handler during provider discovery/startup.

### Expected Behavior

Optional model-provider plugins that require external credentials should not run their handlers unless explicitly enabled, or should detect missing credentials and exit silently with no traceback and no error-level log.

Directory presence alone must not be sufficient to load and execute the handler. A configuration key (for example providers.copilot_acp.enabled: false) or an equivalent documented disable mechanism should exist so users who do not use the provider can silence it without deleting tracked files.

### Actual Behavior

The copilot-acp plugin loads and executes its handler solely because the directory plugins/model-providers/copilot-acp/ exists in the tree. No configuration key, environment variable, or feature flag exists to disable it.

When no Copilot credentials are configured (the normal case for users who do not use this provider), the handler raises BrokenPipeError during gateway startup / provider discovery. The full traceback is written to the logs on every start.

Users cannot silence the noise without deleting the directory. Deleting it marks tracked files as deleted, which dirties the working tree. Updates restore the directory and reintroduce the noise. This forces a choice between permanent log noise or a permanently dirty working tree that can trip update-policy BLOCK rules.

prs.title: fix(session_search): honour query when session_id is set
prs.body:
## What

`session_search(query=..., session_id=...)` ignored `query` and returned the whole session (or its head/tail). The context compressor's recovery footer tells the model to call exactly that shape to get compacted detail back, so models following it got a transcript dump instead of matches.

Now `query` + `session_id` searches inside that session's compression lineage:

- `search_messages()` takes a `session_ids` scope. It is applied in SQL on every search route (FTS5, CJK, trigram, LIKE fallback, rebuild-gap top-up), so hits in other sessions can't fill the LIMIT.
- You get one result per matching message, each with a `match_message_id` that works with `session_search(session_id=..., around_message_id=...)`.
- Rows still in the caller's live context are skipped, using the same rule the scroll guard uses, so every returned id can be scrolled. Compaction-archived rows and compression-ended ancestors can still be searched.
- `session_id` alone still reads the session, and `session_id` + `around_message_id` still scrolls. The schema text now documents the new shape.

## Tests

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tools/test_session_search.py tests/tools/test_session_search_readonly.py tests/tools/test_session_search_worker_store.py -q
```

- On main: `8 failed, 70 passed`. All 8 failures are the new `TestSearchWithinSession` cases, including one that feeds the compressor's footer shape straight into the tool.
- On this branch: `78 passed`.
- Mutation check: turning off the SQL scope fails 4 of the new tests, and turning off the live-context filter fails 1.
- `scripts/check` passes. In the wider session/FTS/compaction test files (691 tests), 2 fail, and both fail the same way on unmodified main.

prs.title: feat(cli): add explicit no-tools mode
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Hermes has no supported way to start or resume a conversation with an empty model tool surface.

Programmatic evaluation, simulation, judging, and participant workflows sometimes need ordinary conversational responses without allowing the model to inspect or modify its environment. `--safe-mode` removes user configuration, rules, plugins, hooks, and MCP servers, but intentionally retains native tools. `--max-turns 1` bounds the tool loop but does not remove those tools from the model request.

The existing workaround is to pass a nonexistent toolset name. Current tool resolution happens to turn that invalid allowlist into zero schemas, but this is undocumented behavior. It emits an invalid-toolset warning, can contaminate programmatic output and timing, and could silently regain tools if unknown-toolset handling changes.

This PR adds an explicit, invocation-scoped option:

```bash
hermes chat --no-tools -q "Respond without tools"
```

For an isolated, bounded model turn:

```bash
hermes chat --safe-mode --no-tools --max-turns 1 -q "Respond without tools"
```

The flag fixes the tool surface when the conversation process is constructed. It does not change tool availability between turns, mutate prior context, or rebuild the system prompt mid-conversation. A later resumed invocation must supply --no-tools again.

### Prior design precedent

Related PRs [#65908](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/65908) and [#56093](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/56093) were closed under the `tools-disabled` policy cited in those reviews.

This proposal avoids the mid-conversation tool-surface and prompt-cache concern raised on #65908 by selecting the empty tool surface when the process constructs the conversation and keeping it stable for the invocation. It still asks maintainers to reconsider the broader policy for an explicit, invocation-scoped CLI contract.

Today, callers can approximate this behavior by passing a nonexistent toolset, for example `--toolsets __none__`. An explicit toolset allowlist starts resolution from an empty set, and the unknown name contributes no tool schemas, so an ordinary chat request ends up with no model tools after emitting an unknown-toolset warning. This is an incidental consequence of current resolution behavior, not a supported contract. This PR formalizes that existing but undocumented resolution outcome as an explicit CLI contract users can depend on.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

Add hermes chat --no-tools, which:

- Rejects --no-tools combined with --toolsets.
- Preserves an explicit empty tool selection through the classic CLI and TUI.
- Applies the override before consulting the tool-definition cache.
- Prevents special worker tools from being injected.
- Excludes native, MCP, plugin, memory-provider, and context-engine tool schemas from the model request.
- Works with resumed conversations when the flag is supplied again.
- Documents the option in the CLI command reference.

The flag is invocation-scoped, like other CLI overrides. It does not change default agent behavior, imply safe mode, or disable non-tool behavior such as session persistence unless another option does so.

## How to Test

1. Run the focused and adjacent regression suites:

   ```bash
   ./scripts/run_tests.sh \
     tests/hermes_cli/test_no_tools.py \
     tests/hermes_cli/test_safe_mode.py \
     tests/hermes_cli/test_argparse_flag_propagation.py \
     tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_worker_spawn_toolsets.py \
     -q
   ```

   Expected result: 18 tests pass.

2. Start a bounded tool-free conversation, note the session ID printed on exit, and resume it with the flag supplied again:

   ```bash
   hermes chat --safe-mode --no-tools --max-turns 1 \
     -q "Reply with exactly NO_TOOLS_OK"

   hermes chat --safe-mode --no-tools --max-turns 1 \
     --resume <SESSION_ID> \
     -q "Reply with exactly RESUME_OK"
   ```

   Verify that both invocations return normally without tool progress, unknown-toolset warnings, or tool calls.

3. Verify that conflicting options fail before starting a conversation:

   ```bash
   hermes chat --no-tools --toolsets terminal -q "test"
   ```

   Expected result:

   ```text
   --no-tools cannot be used with --toolsets
   ```

4. Verify that the flag is exposed in CLI help:

   ```bash
   hermes chat --help
   ```

   Expected help entry:

   ```text
   --no-tools    Disable all model tools for this session
   ```

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits (https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (fix(scope):, feat(scope):, etc.)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs (https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this feature
- [ ] I've run pytest tests/ -q and all tests pass
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested the focused CLI paths on Fedora Linux 43

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated the relevant CLI reference documentation
- [x] cli-config.yaml.example update is N/A because no config key was added
- [x] CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md updates are N/A because no architecture or workflow contract changed
- [x] I've considered cross-platform impact; the implementation uses existing argparse and process-environment propagation paths without OS-specific behavior
- [x] Tool description/schema updates are N/A because no individual tool behavior or schema changed

## Screenshots / Logs

prs.body:
The agent can now wait on a background process until it prints a given line (a server saying "listening on", a build saying "Compiled"), instead of holding the whole timeout or guessing a `sleep`.

## What changes

`process_manage(action="wait", session_id=..., until="listening on")`:

| Case | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Server prints "listening" after 3 s, wait timeout 45 | holds the full **45 s**, `status: timeout` | returns after **3 s**, `status: matched`, process still running |
| Text already printed before the wait started | holds the full timeout | `matched` at once (no race between start and wait) |
| Watch-mode rebuild: second wait for `Compiled` | n/a | matches only the **next** `Compiled`, not the old one (each match uses up the output before it) |
| Coloured output (`\e[32mre\e[0mady`) | n/a | still matches `ready` (ANSI ignored) |
| Process exits before the text appears | `exited` | `exited` (unchanged) |
| Timeout with `until` set | n/a | normal timeout result, note adds "'X' has not appeared in its output yet" |
| No `until` | unchanged | unchanged |

**Live repro (real `hermes chat -q`, `openai/gpt-6-luna` via Nous, isolated probe homes, read back from each run's `state.db`):** same prompt ("start `sleep 3; echo Server listening on :8765; sleep 60` in the background, then wait until it is listening"):
- main: `process_manage {"action":"wait","timeout":45}` → `status: timeout` after 45 s (run 68 s wall)
- head: the model picked up `until` from the schema by itself: `{"action":"wait","timeout":45,"until":"Server listening on :8765"}` → `status: matched` after 3 s (run 27 s wall)

Direct E2E on real subprocesses (no model): server 2.26 s matched; repeat wait for consumed text → timeout; pre-printed text → 0.0 s; rebuild loop 0.0 s then 1.75 s; ANSI 1.25 s; exits first → `exited`.

## How

- New sibling `tools/process_registry_wait_until.py`: `until_match()` tracks a per-session "consumed up to" position over `total_output_chars` (the buffer is a rolling tail), plus the timeout-result builder moved out of `ProcessRegistry.wait`, so `process_registry.py` shrinks by 10 lines and `wait()` loses branches.
- `wait()` checks `until` each tick and ticks every 0.25 s instead of 1 s while `until` is set.
- Schema: one `until` property; `wait:` description mentions it. **Schema delta: +124 chars (~30 tokens)** on `process_manage`, which is in the tool-search deferrable set.
- Docs: `user-guide/features/tools.md` § "Waiting for a line of output".
- Tests: 2 invariants in `tests/tools/test_process_wait_clarity.py` (red on main, green here); 142 passed across the process-registry test files.

## Inspired by Cursor

Cursor IDE 3.27 (Oct 22, 2026, [release notes](https://cursor.com/docs/release-notes/ide)): "When the agent waits on a terminal command, it stops as soon as the command finishes or its output matches what it is waiting for, instead of always running out the full timeout." Hermes already returned on exit; the gap was the output match. `watch_patterns` is the asynchronous cousin (rate-limited notifications meant for rare one-shot signals); `until` is the synchronous "block until ready" the model actually wants after starting a server. Hermes adds the consumed-mark so repeated waits on rebuild output do not match stale lines.

## Infographic

![infographic](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0ab08a9e/2z5d8kjgEY8BDQDsnpXQR_CPC6o8sH.png)

prs.title: fix(redact): per-line URL gate, recursive searches, argv dumps
prs.body:
## Summary

Three secret-leak shapes found while auditing the redaction work in #146688 / #146701.
All three are leaks (a secret that should have been masked printed verbatim), not false
positives.

This branch stacks on top of both: it contains #146688, #146701 and the three fixes below,
because the fixes depend on the `secret_file` pass-through that #146688 adds to
`redact_terminal_output`. If this lands, #146688 and #146701 can be closed.

## 1. The `://` gate was whole-text, so one URL disabled masking for every other line

`_redact_assignments` gated its lowercase-ENV, dotted-config and YAML passes on
`if "://" not in text`. That is a property of a *line*, not of the whole dump: any output
that also held a relay URL skipped those passes entirely.

```
network_secret = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"   ← printed verbatim
ET_PEERS=wss://relay.example:11011/x
```

The same shape hit YAML (`password: …` next to `url: https://…`). Measured before the fix:
plain TOML masked, TOML + a URL line **not** masked, TOML + a non-URL line masked,
URL-first **not** masked.

Fix: `_sub_skipping_url_lines()` applies each pass per line and skips only the lines that
carry `://`. The gate exists so web-URL query params (`?token=`, `?api_key=`) survive, and
that is preserved — verified on three query-string shapes.

## 2. Recursive searches were never classified as secret-file reads

`_command_reads_secret_file` inspects the positional operands of a file-read command.
`grep -r password .` takes a **directory**, so no operand ever looks like a secret file, and
the output — `file:content` lines — printed through the lenient path:

```
a.env:DB_PASSWORD=Zx9Qm2Lp7Rt4Wv8N
```

Fix: a recursive `grep` (`-r` / `-R` / `--recursive`, including bundled short flags like
`-rn`) counts as a secret-file read, and so do `rg` / `ag` / `ack`, which recurse by
default. Flag scanning stops at `--`, so `grep -- -r file` (a pattern that looks like a
flag) is not misread. Non-recursive `grep -i password readme.md` stays lenient.

## 3. `ps` / `top` / `env` output skipped the strict pass

These print other processes' argv or the environment verbatim — no file is read, so
`_command_reads_secret_file` stays False and the strict pass never ran. A relay-URL path
token survived:

```
ET_PEERS=wss://relay.example:11011/et-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef   ← verbatim
```

Fix: `_command_dumps_argv()` detects `ps` / `top` / `pgrep` segments and routes those dumps
through the strict pass, alongside env dumps.

## Verification

- **240 unit tests pass** in `tests/agent/test_redact.py` + `tests/tools/test_terminal_error_redaction.py`
  (includes 12 new regression tests covering all three shapes plus their benign controls).
- **e2e not re-run on this branch.** `tests/e2e/core/security/test_secret_redaction.py` passed 23/23
  before these changes, but on this machine it now OOMs before reaching an assertion:
  `collect()` in `tests/e2e/core/security/_redact.py:213` walks the whole temporary `$HOME/.hermes`
  with `rglob("*")` and reads every file into memory, and that temporary home now also receives an
  auto-installed toolchain (`tools/node`, `tools/ffmpeg*`, `tools/python-3.14`, `installs/…/venv` —
  1.6 GB on disk). Reading it as text pushed the pytest process to ~20 GB and the kernel killed it.
  That code path is unchanged by this branch (`collect()` is identical on `origin/main`) and none of
  the changes here touch the e2e harness, so this is a pre-existing harness limitation on hosts that
  provision tools into a fresh `$HOME`, not a regression from these fixes.
- All three leaks verified fixed on this branch, and the earlier capabilities still hold
  (`cat .env`, `cat prod.env`, `--network-secret`, multi-line scripts, prefixed keys).
- **Zero false positives** across 9 benign shapes: multi-line YAML block, Python source,
  doc URLs, `git log` commit sha, JSON, timestamps, URL query params, plain `ps` output,
  plain `env` output.
- No perf regression: 804K chars in 0.05s, 5000-line env dump in 0.05s.

prs.title: fix(i18n): correct context-file cap tips to reflect the window-scaled limit
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the `tips.t179` startup tip in all 17 bundled locales. It currently claims context files are capped at **20,000 characters**, which has not been the whole truth since the cap became window-scaled.

`agent/prompt_builder.py` computes the per-file cap as:

```python
_CONTEXT_FILE_WINDOW_FRACTION = 0.06
_CONTEXT_FILE_DYNAMIC_CEILING = 500_000

def _dynamic_context_file_max_chars(context_length):
    budget = int(context_length * CHARS_PER_TOKEN * _CONTEXT_FILE_WINDOW_FRACTION)
    return max(CONTEXT_FILE_MAX_CHARS, min(budget, _CONTEXT_FILE_DYNAMIC_CEILING))
```

So 20,000 is now the **floor**, not the cap. A 1M-token model is allowed 240,000 characters.

This matters because the tip is what a user reads while debugging a truncation warning. The warning itself says:

> trim the file, pin a larger `context_file_max_chars`, or use a larger-context model!

Against a tip that claims the limit is 20,000, that advice is incoherent: the user is told to raise a limit that the tip says is already the limit. On a 1M-window model the real headroom is 12x larger than the tip suggests, so the tip sends people to trim files that would have fit.

Reproduced on 0.22.5 (same constants on `main`) by loading a 30,014-char `CLAUDE.md` through the real code path:

| `context_length` | result |
|---|---|
| `None` | `TRUNCATED: 30014 chars exceeds limit of 20000` |
| `1_000_000` | kept in full, no truncation |

The `None` branch is the only case where 20,000 is the whole story — and it is exactly the case the tip describes as if it were universal.

## Related Issue

No existing issue — I searched open and merged PRs/issues for `context file cap`, `20,000 characters`, and `t179` and found only adjacent work (#118005, #121244 scale *child* caps in `delegate_task`), nothing about the tip text. Happy to file an issue first if you'd prefer that for the paper trail.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

One line in each of the 17 `locales/*.yaml` files, under `tips:`:

- `locales/en.yaml`
- `locales/zh.yaml`, `locales/zh-hant.yaml`
- `locales/ja.yaml`, `locales/ko.yaml`
- `locales/de.yaml`, `locales/es.yaml`, `locales/fr.yaml`, `locales/it.yaml`, `locales/pt.yaml`
- `locales/ru.yaml`, `locales/uk.yaml`
- `locales/ar.yaml`, `locales/ga.yaml`, `locales/af.yaml`, `locales/hu.yaml`, `locales/tr.yaml`

Each new string states the real rule — **6% of the model's context window, floor 20,000 / ceiling 500,000 characters** — while keeping the existing head/tail-truncation clause. The 20,000 figure is retained as one bound of the range rather than dropped, since it is still the floor.

No code, no config keys, no TUI key packs (`t179` is not in `_keys.tui.json`, so `*.tui.yaml` is untouched).

**Translation caveat:** I am confident in the en/zh/zh-hant/ja/ko strings. The other twelve are careful but machine-assisted; a native speaker's pass would be welcome and I'd be glad to fold corrections into this PR rather than have them block it.

## How to Test

1. Check the string parses and carries all three bounds in every locale:

```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, ".")
import hermes_yaml as yaml
from pathlib import Path
langs = "af ar de en es fr ga hu it ja ko pt ru tr uk zh zh-hant".split()
for l in langs:
    v = yaml.safe_load(Path(f"locales/{l}.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["tips"]["t179"]
    assert "6" in v and "20" in v and "500" in v, (l, v)
print(f"{len(langs)} locales OK")
EOF
```

2. See it in the banner after a restart (locale catalogs are `lru_cache`d in-process):

```bash
hermes --lang en   # ✦ tip now reads "capped at 6% of the model's context window (20,000–500,000 characters)"
```

3. Confirm the cap itself is unchanged — this PR touches no code:

```bash
python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.'); from agent.prompt_builder import _get_context_file_max_chars as g; print(g(None), g(1_000_000))"
# 20000 240000
```

prs.title: feat(discord): DISCORD_THREAD_IGNORE_NO_MENTION — extend the no-mention drop into bot threads
prs.body:
Closes #142739.

Implementation by @kouyichi (commit c1aec83, 4 files); pushed verbatim from his fork and opened here so the change runs under the repo's CI and review flow.

## What it does

A thread the bot already participates in is exempt from the mention gate: it is its own conversation, not someone else's (#116568 / PR #116581). In multi-bot or human+bot threads that exemption is broader than operators expect — `@OtherBot do X` or `@person do X` reaches this bot verbatim while the same message in the channel is dropped.

`DISCORD_THREAD_IGNORE_NO_MENTION` (YAML `thread_ignore_no_mention`, default off) closes exactly that shape: inside an otherwise-exempt bot thread, a message that mentions someone other than the bot is dropped, and no-mention follow-ups are still answered. It is a no-op under `DISCORD_THREAD_REQUIRE_MENTION=true` (strict mode already demotes every non-typed mention) and in free-response channels, which keep their explicit "answer everything here" meaning.

## Notes

- The predicate lives in a topical sibling (adapter.py is at its line count); the adapter change is line-neutral.
- Author reports 43/43 tests and 12/12 checks passing locally.
- Default-off behavior change gated behind a new opt-in flag; no effect on existing installs.

prs.body:
## Problem
`tools/code_execution_env.py::_resolve_child_cwd` calls a bare `os.getcwd()`. Once the process cwd has been deleted (removed git worktree, pruned temp dir), it raises `FileNotFoundError`, so every `execute_code` call fails until the process restarts. ## Fix
- New `agent.runtime_cwd.process_cwd()` returns `""` when the cwd is gone or unreadable (`FileNotFoundError`/`PermissionError`); other `OSError`s still propagate.
- Every bare `os.getcwd()` under `tools/` that could hit this goes through it, falling back to the existing fallback chain (staging dir for execute_code, home elsewhere).

## Tests
`tests/tools/test_deleted_process_cwd.py`: 6 regressions (deleted cwd for execute_code, file tools base dir, mcp, search, process registry, local env) plus an AST guard that fails on a new unguarded `os.getcwd()` under `tools/`. They fail before the change and pass after. The neighbouring cwd suites (54 tests) pass. `test_code_execution.py`/`test_process_registry.py` show the same 16 failures on unmodified upstream/main in my environment, so they are unrelated.

prs.title: fix(auxiliary): preserve key_cmd credentials for auto vision
prs.body:
## Summary

When an auto-vision auxiliary request uses a custom provider whose `key_cmd` resolves to a callable token source, `_resolve_custom_runtime()` currently treats that non-string value as missing and replaces it with `no-key-required`. The placeholder is then forwarded as an explicit key to the named-custom client, overriding the provider's working `key_cmd` authentication. Authenticated OpenAI-compatible gateways reject the request.

- Preserve callable bearer-token providers in `_resolve_custom_runtime()` using the same `_normalize_api_key()` behavior as the auxiliary client router.
- Keep `no-key-required` only when no usable credential was resolved, preserving keyless local-server behavior.
- Add regression tests covering callable preservation and a named custom provider's actual `Authorization` header during auto-vision resolution when the live runtime has no endpoint recorded.

## Reproduction

Configure `model.provider: custom:litellm` and `model.base_url` for an authenticated gateway, with `providers.litellm.key_cmd` supplying its credential. Call auto-vision resolution without a live endpoint snapshot. Before this change, the generated client sends `Bearer no-key-required` despite the valid provider-level `key_cmd`.

## Validation

- Before the fix: both new regression tests failed (credential replaced and incorrect Authorization header).
- After the fix: `285 passed` for `tests/agent/test_auxiliary_named_custom_providers.py`, `tests/agent/test_auxiliary_main_first.py`, and `tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client.py`.
- `ruff check agent/auxiliary_client.py tests/agent/test_auxiliary_named_custom_providers.py` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

No changes to unrelated routing, provider selection, or service configuration.

prs.title: feat(google-workspace): named Google accounts with --account
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Lets one Hermes profile use more than one Google account (personal + work) through the bundled `google-workspace` skill. Today the skill reads a single `<HERMES_HOME>/google_token.json`, so the only way to reach a second account is a whole second Hermes profile, which also splits memory, sessions and config.

`--account EMAIL` on `setup.py`, `google_api.py` and `gws_bridge.py` selects a token of its own at `<HERMES_HOME>/google_tokens/<email>.json`. Leaving the flag out changes nothing: same token path, same output, same gws environment.

This is deliberately the small core the triage on #15602 asked for when it pointed at the closed #30686 ("split out the core multi-account token resolution and CLI plumbing that can be reviewed independently"): no migration, no default-account pointer, no aliases, no new env var, no new scope logic.

### Design decisions

- **No fallback for a named account.** `--account work@x.com` with no token for it exits 1 with the setup command to run. It never reads the default token, because that would answer a request about one account with another account's mail (the data-boundary concern raised in #15602).
- **Wrong-account guard at consent time.** `--auth-url` passes `login_hint`, and `--auth-code` asks Google which account actually granted the token (Gmail `users.getProfile`, or the primary Calendar id when only Calendar was granted). If it differs from `--account`, the token is not written and the message names both accounts. If the granted scopes can't reveal the account, the token is saved with a warning.
- **Separate gws config dir per named account.** gws caches access tokens per config dir without keying on `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLI_CREDENTIALS_FILE` (googleworkspace/cli#572, #134966), so two accounts sharing the default dir would silently run as whichever filled the cache first. Named accounts get `<HERMES_HOME>/google_tokens/gws/<email>` (0700); an explicit `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_CLI_CONFIG_DIR` from the caller wins. The default-token path is untouched, so this doesn't conflict with #134967's fix for that path.
- **Account names are validated as plain email addresses** (lowercased, no path separators), so `--account` can't escape `google_tokens/`.
- **No new `HERMES_*` env var**, per the contribution rubric; selection is by flag only.

## Related Issue

Fixes #15602

Related: #30686 (closed, larger version of this), #44057 (auth contexts: broader, overlaps in intent), #134967 (gws cache for the default token).

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `skills/productivity/google-workspace/scripts/_google_account.py` (new): account validation, `--account` argument, per-account token / pending-session / gws config paths, `list_accounts()`.
- `scripts/setup.py`: `--account` for `--check`, `--check-live`, `--auth-url`, `--auth-code`, `--revoke`; `--list-accounts`; `login_hint`; identity check before saving a named token.
- `scripts/google_api.py`: global `--account` (before the service); per-account gws config dir; setup hint names the account.
- `scripts/gws_bridge.py`: optional leading `--account EMAIL`; refreshes and writes only that account's token.
- `SKILL.md`: "More than one Google account" section, agent rule to ask which account when ambiguous, remote-backend note (`terminal.credential_files`); version 1.3.0. Website page regenerated with `website/scripts/generate-skill-docs.py`.
- `tests/skills/test_google_workspace_accounts.py` (new): 10 behaviour tests.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/skills/test_google_workspace_accounts.py tests/skills/test_google_workspace_api.py tests/skills/test_google_workspace_setup.py tests/skills/test_google_workspace_setup_deps.py tests/skills/test_google_workspace_credential_files.py -q` → 28 passed.
2. Manual, with a second Google account added as a test user on the OAuth client:
   ```bash
   setup.py --account work@example.com --auth-url      # consent screen pre-selects work@example.com
   setup.py --account work@example.com --auth-code "<redirect URL>"
   setup.py --list-accounts
   google_api.py --account work@example.com gmail search "is:unread" --max 3
   google_api.py gmail search "is:unread" --max 3      # still the default account
   ```
3. Approve with the wrong account on step 1 → `--auth-code` prints `ERROR: You authorized ..., but --account is ...` and writes no token.

The tests cover: named account uses its own token and gws cache; omitting `--account` leaves the env exactly as before; a missing named token fails instead of using the default; path-like `--account` values are rejected before anything is created; the bridge refreshes only the named token; `--auth-url` hints the account and keeps the default pending session untouched; a token granted by a different account is never saved.

prs.title: fix(secrets): move secret caches and the Photon token to the profile home root
prs.body:
## Summary

The Bitwarden and 1Password secret caches and the Photon sidecar token now live at the top of the profile home, where a sandbox can hide them by path, and every credential guard lists them, including the 1Password cache that no guard covered before.

A sandbox that hides files by path (MXC `deniedPaths` on Windows, used by the OpenShell plugin) can only protect a file that sits directly in the granted home. The sandboxed agent can rename a folder it writes, such as `cache/` or `runtime/`, together with a hidden file below it, and read that file at the new path (measured on MXC 1.0.0 and 1.0.1).

| Store | Old path | New path |
|---|---|---|
| Bitwarden plaintext cache | `cache/bws_cache.json` | `bws_cache.json` |
| Bitwarden encrypted cache | `cache/bws_cache.enc.json` | `bws_cache.enc.json` |
| 1Password cache | `cache/op_cache.json` | `op_cache.json` |
| Photon sidecar record (port, token, pid) | `runtime/photon-sidecar.json` | `photon-sidecar.json` |

## Changes

- `agent/secret_sources/_cache.py`, `bitwarden.py`: the disk caches read and write only `<home>/<name>`. A copy at the old `cache/<name>` path is deleted on first use without being read, because the agent can write that folder; clearing removes both locations.
- `plugins/platforms/photon/adapter.py`: the record lives at `<home>/photon-sidecar.json`. A record at the old `runtime/` path is deleted unread on first use; delete removes both.
- `hermes_cli/home_data_layout`: `SECRET_CACHE_FILES` (the four top-level names) and `LEGACY_SECRET_CACHE_PATHS` (the old paths); `SECRET_CACHE_STORES` is both, used by `PROFILE_CREDENTIAL_PATHS`, `agent/file_safety` (read and write denies) and the gateway's media-delivery deny. Backups leave out the top-level names. The dashboard Files API takes its hidden names from the same list; the flat-install `.gitignore` ignores the four top-level names.
- Docs: the Bitwarden, 1Password, Photon and security pages name the new paths.

All four stores are regenerated on use, so deleting an old copy costs at most one extra Bitwarden or 1Password fetch after the upgrade, or a Photon record until the gateway restarts. A profile that never uses its Bitwarden or 1Password source again keeps the old file in `cache/`, still covered by every guard; a sandbox plugin can delete `LEGACY_SECRET_CACHE_PATHS` before it starts a sandbox, as the OpenShell plugin will.

## Validation

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| New and changed tests (`test_secret_cache_location.py`, `test_credential_store_lists.py`, Photon runtime record, Files API, flat-install `.gitignore`) | fail at `main` (23) and at the first commit (8, for deleting old copies) | all pass |
| 95 related test files on Windows | 15 failures that this Windows host has without these changes | the same 15 |
| `scripts/check --base main` | | passes |

`test_credential_store_lists.py` takes each store's path from its writer and checks every guard against the current and the old location.
