prs.title: fix(slack): render multi-select clarify as checkboxes + Submit
prs.body:
## Problem

`SlackAdapter.send_clarify` overrides the base implementation with **one Block Kit button per choice**, and a click calls `resolve_gateway_clarify` immediately. The override never looks at `multi_select`, so a `clarify(multi_select=true)` question silently degrades to single-select on Slack: the card offers no way to pick two options, and the base adapter's numbered-list hint ("Multiple selections allowed - reply with the numbers...") never runs.

Reproduced live: a two-question multi-select batch rendered 4 buttons + "Other..." per question; one click per question answered `["Ramen / tsukemen"]` and `["Unagi"]` and both clarifys resolved. Telegram, Discord and Google Chat overrides have the same shape.

## Fix

A multi-select entry (the `multi_select` flag on the pending `_ClarifyEntry`, same probe the base adapter already uses) now renders:

- a `checkboxes` element in an `actions` block with a fixed `block_id`, option values packing `clarify_id|idx` exactly like the choice buttons;
- a **Submit** button (`hermes_clarify_submit`, value `clarify_id|submit`);
- the existing "Other..." button, so typed-text capture still works.

Checkbox toggles are acked and ignored (`_handle_clarify_multi_toggle`); nothing resolves until Submit, which reads `body["state"]["values"][block_id][action_id]["selected_options"]`, maps the packed indices back to canonical labels through the pending entry, and resolves with the JSON array `clarify_gateway` already parses into a label list.

Edge cases: an empty selection is not an answer - the card is rewritten with "select at least one option, then Submit" and stays live (the double-click guard is only consumed by a real resolution); a submit after eviction/expiry shows the usual expired notice rather than a misleading tick.

## Tests

`tests/gateway/test_slack_clarify_buttons.py::TestSlackClarifyMultiSelect` (4 new tests): checkboxes render instead of `hermes_clarify_choice_*` buttons, toggles do not resolve, Submit returns every ticked label, empty Submit keeps the card live.

- `tests/gateway/test_slack_clarify_buttons.py` - 11 passed
- `tests/gateway/ -k "slack or clarify"` - 812 passed, 2 skipped

prs.title: fix(telegram): replay replies after polling recovery
prs.body:
## Summary

Fix final Telegram replies stranded in the existing Delivery Ledger after a degraded send path recovers **without replacing the adapter**.

- When an in-place Telegram `getUpdates` polling generation proves healthy after degradation, invoke the existing platform/profile-scoped runtime failed-obligation sweep.
- Close the lost-wakeup race: if the health sweep occurs before the asynchronous `mark_failed` commit, the post-write path can replay via the **same** adapter only with confirmed Telegram polling health. Preserve the existing replacement-adapter behavior for every platform.
- Retain the replay task through the Gateway's existing background-task lifecycle and log failures. Reuse atomic ledger claims and existing attempt limits; no new delivery store or scheduler.

## Production incident (2026-10-30)

Two Telegram messages (IDs `1763` and `1764`) entered the same live session and completed model turns and GitHub writes. Their final answers were generated and persisted to SessionDB, but both sends returned `send_path_degraded`, with no Telegram acknowledgement/message ID. Ledger rows remained `failed` because the adapter's polling-health path cleared degradation without triggering the failed-obligation replay after the transport became usable.

The historical replies are **not** claimed delivered by this PR. The change has not been deployed.

## Regression coverage (exact PR HEAD `208ea188529a972b049cc2202e02ad44e13c9110`)

- Real isolated SQLite ledger with a controlled `mark_failed` delay: health sweep first finds zero; the delayed failure commits; post-write catch-up replays **exactly once**, transitions to `delivered`, and a repeated sweep cannot duplicate the message.
- Disconnected Discord/no-client negative regression: no same-adapter retry or extra claim before real reconnect.
- Telegram polling generation/recovery, send-path health, existing delivery lifecycle and replay-task ownership/error logging.
- Clean non-worktree exact-HEAD local validation: **72 passed, 1 pre-existing skip, 0 failed** (executor report; not independently rerun by Main Control). `git diff --check` and compilation passed.
- Worktree-local home-I/O guard failures were isolated to `hermes-update-pull` bootstrap path access and did not reproduce in the clean checkout.

## Review and CI status

- Main Control independently inspected the exact-head GitHub patch and marked source-level feedback resolved: [final review summary](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/146731#issuecomment-6519906317). This is **not a formal maintainer GitHub APPROVE**.
- Separate external exact-HEAD reviewer attempt returned **NO_VERDICT** (host IPC failure), not CLEAN/PASS.
- GitHub Actions workflows are currently **`action_required`** for this fork PR; they have **not** run to PASS. Upstream maintainer workflow approval and code review are requested.
- Keep open for normal upstream review and merge. No auto-merge, Gateway restart, credential/config change, or real bot traffic has been performed.

The original implementation task `t_b5a76261` and its separate uncommitted worktree were not touched.

prs.title: fix(skills-hub): git tree entries are directories, not symlink escapes
prs.body:
## Problem
`hermes skills install tradermonty/claude-trading-skills/skills/crypto-regime-analyzer` fails with

> Error: '…' is listed in the skills-sh index, but its files no longer exist upstream. Stale index entry …

even though all 25 files fetch fine (verified with an authenticated token). The real cause is logged at WARNING level only:

> Rejected non-regular referenced file in skill bundle: skills/crypto-regime-analyzer/scripts/calculators

The SKILL.md mentions the directory `scripts/calculators` in prose. `_referenced_support_paths` picks it up as a referenced path; `_tree_members` reports every non-`blob` tree entry as `is_regular_blob=False`, so `_collect_tree_files` puts the *directory* into `symlinked` and rejects the bundle as a symlink escape. `fetch()` returns `None`, and the CLI, seeing index metadata without a bundle and no rate limit, prints the misleading "stale index entry" message.

## Fix
Skip `type == "tree"` entries in `_tree_members`. Directories are never fetched anyway; a referenced directory now falls through to the existing "Referenced skill support file is missing; continuing without it" warning. Symlinks (mode 120000) are still rejected — `test_github_source_rejects_symlink_in_referenced_directory` still passes.

## Test
`tests/tools/test_skill_bundle_provenance.py::test_github_source_accepts_referenced_directory_path` — fails before the fix, passes after. `test_skill_bundle_provenance.py` + `test_skills_hub_github_fetch.py`: 23 passed.

Any community skill whose SKILL.md names a sub-directory (`scripts/<pkg>`, `references/<topic>/`) is affected, so this likely explains other "stale index entry" reports.

prs.title: fix(copilot-acp): catch BrokenPipeError on write and allow disabling via config (#147051)
prs.body:
## Summary
Fixes #147051

When copilot-acp is present in plugins/model-providers/copilot-acp/ and the copilot binary is unauthenticated or exits immediately on startup, attempting to write to proc.stdin in CopilotACPClient._request could raise an unhandled BrokenPipeError traceback.

Additionally, this adds the ability to explicitly disable copilot-acp in config.yaml under providers.copilot-acp.enabled: false (or copilot_acp).

## Changes
1. agent/copilot_acp_client.py: Catch OSError (including BrokenPipeError) on proc.stdin.write/flush, wait briefly for child process termination if proc.poll() has not yet updated, and report a clean RuntimeError (_exited_early) with stderr rather than bubbling raw BrokenPipeError.
2. plugins/model-providers/copilot-acp/__init__.py: Check is_provider_enabled in fetch_models() so setting providers.copilot-acp.enabled: false silences model discovery completely without launching external processes.
3. Tests:
   - Added test_stdin_broken_pipe_is_reported_as_a_clean_crash in tests/agent/test_copilot_acp_client.py.

## What does this PR do?

Adds one catalog entry, `plugin-catalog/cadence.yaml`, for a local usage page. Cadence shows a year heatmap, streaks from days a chat was actually used, model and place breakdowns, a 30 day / 90 day / all time range, this week against last week, and the busiest weekday and hour.

Days come from message timestamps, so a continued chat counts on the day it continued. Model totals come from `session_model_usage`, so a mid-chat model switch is not collapsed onto one model. prs.title: feat(dashboard): add fullscreen toggle and universal focus mode
prs.body:
## Summary

- Add a native fullscreen toggle to the shared Dashboard header.
- Add universal CSS-based Focus Mode as a safe alternative to native fullscreen.
- Provide an Exit Focus control to restore the normal Dashboard.
- Fix page-header action registration during navigation, including Files → Channels.

## Motivation

Some browsers have unreliable native fullscreen behavior. On an Amazon Fire HD 8 running Firefox 152.0.6, invoking native fullscreen caused Firefox to exit.

Firefox also reported a Linux desktop user-agent to Dashboard JavaScript despite running on Android, making user-agent-based detection unreliable.

Universal Focus Mode avoids both problems without disabling native fullscreen for other users.

prs.title: feat(signal): approve or deny a pending approval by reacting 👍/👎
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

On Signal you can now answer a dangerous-command approval prompt by reacting to it: 👍/✅ approves once, 👎/❌ denies. It works exactly like typing "👍"/"👎" (or `/approve` / `/deny`). Signal has no inline buttons, so before this a reaction, the most natural reply, did nothing and the command waited until the approval timed out.

How it works:
- `send()` records the wire timestamp of every chunk of an `is_approval_prompt` send. Records are TTL-bound to `approvals.timeout` + 60s and capped at 128.
- An inbound reaction whose `targetSentTimestamp` matches one of those records is turned into the approval word and dispatched through `handle_message()`. From there it goes down the gateway's existing plaintext-approval path (`run_busy._route_plaintext_approval_while_busy`), which only acts while `has_blocking_approval()` is true. No new resolution logic, and a stray reaction can never start a turn.
- Each record is used up on the first reaction. Removals, other emoji and reactions on non-prompt messages are dropped.

signal-cli delivers a reaction as `dataMessage.reaction` (`JsonReaction`: `emoji`, `targetAuthor`, `targetSentTimestamp`, `isRemove`), or as `syncMessage.sentMessage.reaction` for Note to Self, with no message text. So the reaction is picked up after the sync unwrap and **before** the empty-message skip and the group `require_mention` gate. Either of those would otherwise drop it, since a reaction never carries an @mention.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `plugins/platforms/signal/adapter.py`: approval-prompt timestamp registry populated in `send()`, plus `_handle_reaction_envelope()` that maps 👍/✅ → "👍" and 👎/❌ → "👎", reached from `_handle_envelope` via `dataMessage.reaction`.
- `tests/gateway/test_signal_approval_reactions.py`: behaviour tests using signal-cli's real envelope shape. They cover DM approve/deny for all four emoji, a reaction being used up once, removals, other emoji and non-prompt targets being ignored, reactions on a non-approval send not being routed, a group with `require_mention`, and Note to Self.
- `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/signal.md`: documents approving by reaction.

prs.title: fix(tui): adaptive flush for reasoning and streaming to reduce CPU during thinking
prs.body:
## Summary

TUI's `scheduleReasoning()` and `scheduleStreaming()` used a fixed `STREAM_BATCH_MS=16ms`
with no adaptive throttling. Under load — long reasoning text, many concurrent timers, large
transcript re-renders — each flush cost grows but the interval never stretches, creating a
positive feedback loop: more work → slower flushes → more frequent flushes → more work.
Desktop already has an adaptive delta flush mechanism but it was never backported to TUI.

This ports the same adaptive formula to TUI's `turnController.ts` singleton.

## Root cause

- `turnController.ts` scheduled flushes at a fixed 16ms interval regardless of how expensive
  the actual `patchTurnState` → React commit → Ink render cycle was
- Desktop solved this with `adaptiveFloor = min(max(base, lastFlushCost*3), cap)` in
  `use-message-stream/index.ts:351-445` (PR #72504), but TUI was never backported

## Fix

- Module-level `lastFlushCost` tracks the measured cost of `patchTurnState` via
  `performance.now()` — a standard Node.js API already used by `fpsStore.ts` in the TUI
- `adaptiveFloor()` computes the next flush gap from `lastFlushCost`, mirroring Desktop's
  formula exactly: `min(max(STREAM_BATCH_MS, lastFlushCost * 3), MAX_STREAM_FLUSH_GAP_MS)`
- `scheduleReasoning()` uses `adaptiveFloor()` directly
- `scheduleStreaming()` uses `Math.max(streamDelay, adaptiveFloor())` to preserve existing
  boost/relax semantics (scroll/typing delays still take priority)
- `reset()` resets `lastFlushCost = 0` so each turn starts from the baseline

## Measurement caveat

Desktop measures flush cost in two layers: a synchronous `performance.now()` around the
store write, plus a `requestAnimationFrame` callback that adds the actual React commit +
render frame time. TUI runs on Node.js (no rAF), so it measures only the synchronous layer
(store write + React scheduling trigger). This means `lastFlushCost` in TUI is systematically
lower than Desktop's equivalent metric — the actual render cost is not captured. The `×3`
multiplier and 250ms cap provide headroom, but on extreme load the TUI adaptive floor may be
less aggressive than Desktop's. This is a known limitation, not a bug: the cap guarantees
visible text still updates at ~4fps regardless.

## Behavior

| Flush cost | Before | After |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| ~0ms (idle) | 16ms fixed | 16ms — unchanged |
| ~5ms (light) | 16ms fixed | 16ms — unchanged |
| ~50ms (loaded) | 16ms → runaway | ~150ms — breathing room |
| ~100ms+ (contended) | 16ms → runaway | 250ms cap — ~4fps visible |

The mechanism is host-agnostic: it measures actual `performance.now()` cost on whatever
machine it runs on and adapts automatically. No environment variables, no hardware
detection, no host-specific configuration. On fast machines the floor stays at 16ms;
on slow or contended machines it stretches up to the 250ms cap.

## Testing

- `turnControllerNotice.test.ts` and `turnControllerTodos.test.ts` pass (6/6)
- `tsc --noEmit` passes clean
- ESLint passes clean
- Note: existing tests do not cover the adaptive flush logic itself. The `adaptiveFloor()`
  function is pure (no I/O, no side effects) and trivially unit-testable, but no test
  currently exercises it. A follow-up PR adding `adaptiveFloor()` boundary tests
  (`lastFlushCost=0` → 16ms, `lastFlushCost=100` → 250ms cap) is recommended.

## Risk

- Under light load: zero behavior change (`adaptiveFloor = 16ms` when `lastFlushCost` is
  near zero)
- `lastFlushCost` is module-level (singleton-safe since `turnController` is a singleton)
- No new dependencies, no rAF, no changes to `turnStore.ts` or Ink rendering
- `performance.now()` measurement omits the render frame cost (see Measurement caveat);
  the 250ms cap bounds the worst case

prs.title: catalog: bump agent-hint to 0.6.0 (sha 2eb5a09)
prs.body:
Bump the pinned commit for `agent-hint` from `5601d23` (0.5.1) to `2eb5a09` (0.6.0).

Upstream change: https://github.com/dachaimahogany/hermes-agent-hint/pull/1 (merged by the repository owner).

## What changed in the plugin

1. **One `cache_control` entry instead of two.** 0.5.1 sent `[pin, ephemeral]`; a consumer that reads the first entry (as MindIE-Motor does) gets the bare `pin` — no TTL — and silently drops the retention request. 0.6.0 sends a single `ephemeral` with an explicit TTL.
2. **`pin` retired on the wire.** The type never reached the engine and never changed behaviour; the value is still accepted by consumers that send it.
3. **Tool duration measured instead of hardcoded.** 0.5.1 used a constant 5 s, so the derived TTL always landed on the 60 s floor and any tool wait longer than a minute lost the cache. Now measured per tool (p90), with the constant only as a fallback.
4. **Prefixes below one cache block are not declared** (the engine hashes whole 128-token blocks).

## Disclosure (rule 13)

No change to what the plugin touches:

- The only outbound traffic is the `X-Agent-Hint` header on LLM requests to the configured provider (already disclosed in the entry).
- `status_sink: http` still POSTs session events to the operator-configured `status_url`; `ndjson` writes under `$HERMES_HOME`. Both remain off by default.
- No credential reads, no shell commands, no background processes, no self-updater, no new dependencies.

## Compatibility

- `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.6"` unchanged.
- Config keys unchanged (`cache_pin_end` now means the position of the single breakpoint; `cache_ttl_s` semantics unchanged).
- Capability block unchanged: 10 hooks + `llm_request` middleware, matching what `__init__.py` registers.

prs.body:
HTML-only emails now reach the agent with every entity decoded exactly once: an escaped `<APIKEY>` stays the literal text `<APIKEY>` instead of turning into ``, and `'` / `’` / `—` arrive as real characters instead of raw markup. Fixes #68704. Salvages #68707 (@ooiuuii, commit kept with authorship). Ported from paradigmxyz/centaur#2055, which fixed the same ordering bug in Centaur's Slack text normalizer. ## Changes - @ooiuuii's commit: decode `<`/`>` before `&` in the email HTML fallback, plus the regression test (rebased onto main's `_HTML_SUBS` table). - Our commit: replace the per-entity regexes with one `html.unescape` pass after tag removal, so the fix covers every named/numeric entity, not just the three it listed. ` ` still becomes a plain space. ## Before / after (real `EmailAdapter._parse_fetched_message`, HTML-only RFC 822 message) Input body: `

Use the literal placeholder <APIKEY> in the config.

Don't paste the real one — thanks!

` | tree | body the agent receives | |---|---| | main `f30105a0` | `Use the literal placeholder in the config.`
`Don't paste the real one — thanks!` | | this PR | `Use the literal placeholder <APIKEY> in the config.`
`Don't paste the real one — thanks!` | **Live repro:** above, via a real `EmailAdapter` built from `PlatformConfig` parsing raw message bytes on both trees. The IMAP transport itself was not exercised (no IMAP server in the probe); the change is confined to body parsing after fetch. Root cause: sequential replaces decoded `&` first, so its output was decoded again by the `<`/`>` passes; and only three entities were handled at all. ## Ours vs Centaur - Centaur (#2055) moved `&` to the end of a sequential `.replace` chain in its Slack normalizer. - Hermes' Slack adapter already decodes in one regex pass (`_unescape_slack_entities`), so nothing to port there; the email adapter was the surviving instance of the class in hermes. We use `html.unescape`, which is single-pass by construction and also handles numeric/named entities Centaur's chain still leaves raw. ## Tests `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_email.py`: 45 passed. prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Anthropic reports an empty credit balance as HTTP 400:

```
Error code: 400 - {'type': 'error', 'error': {'type': 'invalid_request_error', 'message': 'Your credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API. Please go to Plans & Billing to upgrade or purchase credits.'}}
```

The main loop handles this already. `classify_api_error` matches "credit balance" in `_BILLING_PATTERNS` through `_400_TAIL_RULES` and returns `billing` with `should_fallback=True`.

The auxiliary ladder does not. `_is_payment_error` in `agent/auxiliary_client.py` only looks at 402, or at a billing body on 403/404/429/no-status. A 400 never matches, so none of the `_FALLBACK_REASONS` predicates accept the error. An auxiliary task (compression, vision, titles and so on) running on an exhausted Anthropic key raises instead of moving on to `auxiliary.<task>.fallback_chain`.

With this change a 400 counts as a payment error when its body matches the main classifier's `_BILLING_PATTERNS`. I did not use the wider aux-only list (`_PAYMENT_KEYWORDS`) for 400. It contains words like "billing" and "credits" that can show up in an ordinary request-shape 400, such as an unknown `billing_tag` parameter.

## Related Issue

Refs #139285. That report hit the same error body in the main loop. As the comment there shows, the main classifier already gets it right. This PR fixes the auxiliary path, which had the same gap and no fallback.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/auxiliary_client.py`: `_is_payment_error` accepts a 400 whose body matches `_BILLING_PATTERNS`. The function stays the same length, so the file does not grow.
- `tests/agent/test_auxiliary_error_classification.py`:
  - `test_anthropic_credit_balance_400_walks_the_aux_fallback_chain`: the Anthropic body is `billing` for the main classifier and a payment error for the aux ladder, and the first matching `_FALLBACK_REASONS` label is "payment error".
  - `test_non_billing_400_is_not_a_payment_error`: three request-shape 400s stay non-payment, including two that mention "billing" or "credits".

## How to Test

1. On main, `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/agent/test_auxiliary_error_classification.py` with the new tests fails at `assert ac._is_payment_error(exc)`.
2. With the fix, the same file passes (10 tests).
3. `scripts/run_tests.sh` over every `tests/agent/*auxiliary*`, `*aux_*` and `*error_classif*` file: 66 files, 963 passed, 0 failed.
4. `python scripts/check`: 14 checks ok, code health 0 blocking.

prs.title: fix(kanban): active_pr lifts on a deliberate unblock, not only a dependency (stacked on #146075)
prs.body:
**Stacked on #146075** — review only this commit: `git diff 95448c94da..71ea7662da`. The PR diff shows both commits until #146075 lands.

## Symptom

`check_respawn_guard` step 4 lifts `active_pr` only for a `dependency_wait` hand-back. A conductor card whose own worker named the PR it was **gating** (`author == assignee`) and then blocked with any *other* kind came back from an unblock still guarded — `status ready`, guard `active_pr` — so it stayed unspawnable for the whole `_RESPAWN_GUARD_PR_WINDOW` (24 h) and the answer the human unblocked it with reached no worker.

Measured on the parent commit with a real `block_task` + `unblock` + `recompute_ready` round trip:

```
needs_input  -> blocked (active_pr) -> unblocked/recompute -> ready (active_pr)
transient    -> blocked (active_pr) -> unblocked/recompute -> ready (active_pr)
capability   -> blocked (active_pr) -> unblocked/recompute -> ready (active_pr)
```

After this commit the same replay prints `guard None` for all three, while still printing `active_pr` at block time.

## Fix

Lift on an `unblocked` event **strictly after** the worker's newest own-PR comment (same strict "after" / fail-closed same-second tie as the dependency lift).

The discriminator is the deliberate act, not the block kind:

* `unblocked` is written only by an unblock — `hermes kanban unblock`, the dashboard, or an agent's `kanban_unblock` tool — never by the dispatcher's retry path (that writes `reclaimed`/failure evidence). It is the same "deliberate re-run" reasoning step 3 already applies to `recent_success`.
* The block kind is the wrong key: the identical shape appears one block kind over, and the payload's `reason` is free text with nothing structural to match on.
* Not "pass the PR URL into the resume context": `build_worker_context` already renders the 10 newest prior attempts and the 30 newest comments, so a respawned worker reads back its own "Opened <PR>" note. A test pins that instead of adding a second prompt channel.

Automatic re-queues (crash, reclaim, claim timeout, failure retry) are deliberately **not** in the lift set: re-spawning the worker that already opened the PR is the duplicate-PR risk the guard exists for (#111910). A test pins that boundary.

## Tests

`tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_review_lifecycle.py`:

* `test_active_pr_guard_lifts_when_a_deliberate_unblock_returns_the_card[needs_input|transient|capability]` — full round trip, guard `None`, card claimable.
* `test_active_pr_guard_still_holds_for_an_automatic_requeue_after_the_pr` — a reclaim re-queues the card and the guard stands.
* `test_respawn_context_carries_the_workers_own_pr_url` — the mitigation for a respawned implementer.

Red proofs (each mutation restored afterwards): removing the lift turns the three parametrised cases red and leaves the rest green; adding `reclaimed` to the lift set turns the boundary test red.

Gate: `pytest` on `test_kanban_db.py`, `test_kanban_review_lifecycle.py`, `test_kanban_review_lifecycle_complete.py`, `test_kanban_block_kinds.py` -> 2 failed, 118 passed; both failures are environmental and fail identically at the base commit `95448c94da` (`test_infrastructure_spawn_refusal_never_charges_the_card`, `test_worktree_workspace_explicit_target_materializes_linked_worktree`). `ruff check` clean on both changed files.

prs.title: fix(ssh): keep ControlMaster sockets under sun_path for deep profile temp dirs
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

A profile whose scratch `TMPDIR` sits under a long `HERMES_HOME` puts the SSH ControlMaster socket past Linux's 108-byte `sun_path`. Every command on that profile's ssh backend then fails before it runs:

```
SSH connection failed: unix_listener: path "/home/demi/data/brain/.hermes/profiles/hermes-pc2/cache/scratch/hermes-ssh/368d00edfbf86ea7.sock.AWDFvvro2YxGTe00" too long for Unix domain socket
```

`$TMPDIR/hermes-ssh/<16 hex>.sock` plus ssh's 17-byte master suffix adds 39 bytes to the temp root. So any temp root longer than 57 bytes breaks on Linux (53 on macOS). A profile scratch dir is `<HERMES_HOME>/profiles/<name>/cache/scratch`, which crosses that limit as soon as `HERMES_HOME` resolves anywhere deeper than `~/.hermes`. The default profile one level up still fits, which is why this shows up only on named profiles.

The control dir stays `$TMPDIR/hermes-ssh` whenever its sockets fit, so nothing changes for existing setups. When it doesn't fit, it moves to a private `hermes-ssh-<uid>` dir:
- first choice is under `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, then `socket_safe_tmpdir()`;
- the dir is claimed with the browser harness's existing `claim_private_dir`: created 0700, or accepted only if it is a real directory (not a symlink) owned by this uid and closed to group/other, so another local user cannot plant it in a shared `/tmp`;
- the old dir remains the last resort.

Windows (no ControlMaster, `_SSH_MULTIPLEX` false) is untouched.

## Related Issue

No existing issue or PR found. I searched open and merged PRs and issues for "ControlPath socket path too long", "ssh control socket profile" and "ssh socket too long". This extends the macOS sun_path fix from #11840 to deep Linux temp roots.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `tools/environments/ssh.py`: `_control_dir()` and the `_CONTROL_DIR_MAX` budget (sun_path minus the socket name and ssh's master suffix); `SSHEnvironment.__init__` uses it.
- `tests/tools/test_ssh_environment.py`:
  - a budget test that ties `_CONTROL_DIR_MAX` to the 103/107-byte usable `sun_path`;
  - a temp root exactly at the limit is kept, even when a shorter private dir exists;
  - a deep temp root moves to a 0700 private dir at an exact-fit length;
  - a planted (symlinked) private dir is skipped for the next root.

## How to Test

1. Use a profile whose scratch dir is long (here `HERMES_HOME` resolves to `/home/demi/data/brain/.hermes`, a 63-byte profile scratch dir), with `terminal.backend: ssh`.
2. On main: `SSHEnvironment(...)` with `TMPDIR` set to that scratch dir fails with the `unix_listener ... too long` error above. I reproduced this on two profiles against two hosts.
3. With this branch, the socket is `/run/user/1000/hermes-ssh-1000/368d00edfbf86ea7.sock` (69 bytes with the suffix), `hostname` runs on both hosts, the dir is 0700, and cleanup removes the socket.

Results on Arch Linux (kernel 7.2, OpenSSH client, Python 3.11):
- `scripts/run_tests.sh` on `tests/tools/test_ssh_environment.py`, `test_ssh_bulk_upload.py`, `test_ssh_remote_cwd.py` and `test_ssh_session_cwd.py`: 43 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed.
- Mutation check: each guard was removed one at a time and a new test fails for every one (6 of 6): the fit-boundary comparison, the fallback, the private-dir length boundary, the ownership claim, the root order, and the ssh suffix in the budget.
- `python scripts/check --staged`: 14 checks, ok.

- Full `tests/tools/` on this head versus base `f30105a`, same interpreter: no new failures. Head: 10430 passed, 488 failed, 25 errors. Re-running the 129 failing files on base gives the identical failure set except one test, `test_browser_use_cli_owned_daemon.py::test_a_daemon_another_live_hermes_started_on_the_same_name_is_never_registered`. It touches no SSH code and passes 3/3 alone on both head and base, so it is load-flaky. The pre-existing failures come from running with a dev install whose venv `.pth` points into a live Hermes home: the home-I/O guard refuses those paths (`TEST BUG: file I/O against the REAL hermes home`). CI's isolated env is the authoritative full-suite gate.

prs.title: fix(desktop): honor focused chat tiles for preview and tour ownership
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes Desktop's foreground guard when chat A remains the route-driven primary while chat tile B is focused. B's preview/tour requests should operate on B's own page; A's background requests must not gain foreground control merely because A remains primary.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Changes Made

Only `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event/server-requests.ts` and its existing test file:

- Resolve foreground identity through the existing focused-tile stores, then use the existing runtime/stored/lineage conversation matcher.
- Preserve requesting-session preview ownership and the window-host routing gate; do not redirect operations to an arbitrary active tab.
- Recompute foreground status on reconnect replay, and pass live focus into the real built-in tour's post-eligibility-wait check.
- Make scoped, hosted-but-unfocused preview/tour/theme handlers **decline**, not return a terminal refusal that could win the first-response race against a focused owner in another window. Tours decline before evaluating the bystander's local enabled setting. Unscoped requests retain their immediate refusal.
- Retain upstream browser-host handling and existing profile/preview isolation.

## Related / Overlapping Work

Overlaps #133448 (andrexibiza) and #133437 (liuhao1024), which address the same foreground-guard problem. This is an alternative extracted from the user's existing local patch, with explicit decline, replay, theme, and post-wait regressions; **these overlapping dispatcher fixes should be reconciled, not stacked blindly**. Those PRs/branches were not modified. #145366 addresses the related but separate preview-profile-bucket problem and is not included here.

## How to Test / Observed Evidence

From `apps/desktop`, using installed dependencies:

```sh
npm exec -- vitest run --project ui \
  src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event/server-requests.test.ts \
  src/app/session/hooks/use-message-stream/gateway-event/theme-requests.test.ts
```

**48 tests passed** on the branch based on fetched upstream `main`. Scoped ESLint and whitespace checks passed. Commit hooks remain enabled.

Regressions cover focused B acting on its own preview, background A declining, hosted-but-unfocused bystander declines even with tours disabled, replay revalidation, theme scoping, and both retained/changed focus during the real built-in tour's deferred eligibility wait. Existing foreign-window and compression-identity cases remain covered.

## Limitations

Tests exercise renderer dispatch, real focus/session stores, session-owned preview navigation, and the real built-in tour wait. Pop-out transport, eligibility responses, and final tour rendering are substituted; this is not live multi-window WebSocket settlement or native Electron verification. No Desktop/gateway restart, full suite, packaged click-through, or CI pass is claimed.

prs.title: fix(desktop): preserve successful preview clicks across navigation
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes `drive_preview` reporting a successful click as a missed click when the click replaces the document and the new page answers the follow-up inventory read.

The pointer witness belongs to the old document. A navigation, including a same-URL reload, removes that witness; a genuinely missed click leaves the armed property present but null. Treating both cases as a missed click can encourage the agent to repeat an action that already happened.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Changes Made

Only `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-act.ts` and its existing test file:

- Report whether the post-input readback is running in a document without the armed witness property.
- Preserve the missed-input failure when the witness remains present but empty.
- Return a navigation note and the new document's inventory when document replacement is detected.
- Add a paired regression for document replacement versus lost input.

No session routing, permissions, providers, dependencies, or browser-opening policies change.

## How to Test / Observed Evidence

From `apps/desktop`, using the installed dependencies:

```sh
npm exec -- vitest run --project ui src/app/chat/right-rail/preview-act.test.ts
```

**29 tests passed** on the branch based on fetched upstream `main`. Scoped ESLint passed with one non-blocking whitespace warning; whitespace checks passed. Commit hooks remain enabled.

For manual verification, click a page control that performs a navigation or same-URL reload. The action should succeed with a navigation note. Input that never reaches an unchanged document must still fail.

## Limitations

The added regression substitutes iframe documents and input delivery in jsdom. It is not evidence of a native Electron webview navigation or a successful third-party login. No live Desktop/gateway restart, packaged click-through, full suite, or CI pass is claimed.

SHA-bump PR for the existing `birkin-mnemosyne` catalog entry, following the
published core release `v0.9.0` (PyPI `birkin-mnemosyne==0.9.0`):
`4b78ff476b655bccb8f68b2a50a967919d178175` -> `63a34526973fc9ad0e5a030a474c67a5fca873e7`.

The entry keeps a full 40-character commit pin. `version` is the Hermes plugin
manifest version at the pinned commit (`0.8.0` -> `0.9.0`); `0.9.0` is
the core package version the plugin depends on.

## Changes Made

- Only `plugin-catalog/birkin-mnemosyne.yaml`: `sha`, the pinned `docs_url`, `version`, the core
  version named in `description`, and one disclosure sentence in `description`.
  Capabilities and every other field are unchanged.

## Disclosure change (rule 13)

This range adds two write tools to the memory provider, `birkin_memory_forget` and
`birkin_memory_restore`, so "Create-only writes" is no longer accurate. The description now says
writes are limited to primary agent contexts: create-only notes plus preview-by-default archive and
restore, which never delete files. Forgetting moves a note to `_archive/` and only when
`confirm=true`. The provider still makes no network calls and needs no API key. `capabilities` stays
`provides_tools: []`: these are memory-provider tools, the same kind as the existing remember and
search tools the entry already lists that way.

prs.title: fix(desktop): the dead-session prune never re-asks a profile the gateway does not serve
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The renderer's dead-session prune (`apps/desktop/src/store/dead-session-prune.ts`) probes every stored chat
reference (pins, drafts, queued prompts, interrupted sends) on the active profile and then on every other
known profile. When a profile is **not served** by the gateway (parked with `hermes -p <name> gateway stop`,
or `gateway.standalone: true`), its probe is refused with a non-404 error. `sessionVerdict` returns
`'unknown'`, which is neither cached nor backed off, and the sweep re-runs on every sidebar refresh. So a
parked profile with saved chats is asked again roughly every 10 s, forever.

On one Linux v0.22.5 install this produced 840 `Invalid gateway ticket response` errors in `desktop.log` and
17 re-ensures of the shared gateway descriptor; switching to other profiles timed out until the parked
profile was started again (`hermes -p qa gateway start`), after which there were 0 errors in 10.7 hours.
The prune is byte-identical in v0.22.2 and v0.22.5; the ticket gate added between them is what turned
those probes into refusals.

This PR makes the prune stop asking:

1. **It uses the gateway's served list.** `/api/status` already reports `gateway_shared_with`, and
   `useStatusSnapshot` already polls it every 60 s. The hook now hands that list to the prune
   (`noteServedProfiles`). A profile not on the list is never probed. A chat that only such a profile could
   own gets a new verdict, `'unreachable'`: not alive, not dead, so it is never pruned, and it is not probed
   again until that profile is back on the list.
2. **Without a list it remembers refusals.** A standalone gateway or an older backend reports no list
   (`null`), and then every profile counts as served, as before. If the active profile answered (so the
   gateway is up) but another profile refused, that profile is skipped for 30 s, then 1, 2, 4… minutes,
   capped at 10. Several refusals in one sweep count once. Any real answer clears the record; a profile
   newly on the served list is asked again at once.
3. **Gateway down stays as it is.** If the active profile's probe itself fails, the verdict is still
   `'unknown'` and the next sweep retries, exactly as the existing test "defers on non-404 probe failures
   instead of dropping, and retries later" requires.
4. A gateway switch (`resetDeadSessionPrune`) forgets the served list and all refusals.

It never matches on error wording. Today a refusal reads `Invalid gateway ticket response`; with #142911 it
reads `The gateway does not serve profile '<name>'`. Both are covered by tests.

The hook loads the prune lazily (`await import`), as `src/api/mcp.ts` does, because the prune's store graph
reads the `@/hermes` barrel at load time and `use-status-snapshot.test.ts` mocks that barrel narrowly.

**What it does not do.** It does not touch `electron/local-gateway.ts`. Each refusal that still happens
(the first one, then one per backoff step, or a user opening the profile) still goes through the mint path
that reads a refusal as a dead owner. #142911 fixes that half; the two PRs are independent and both are
needed. This PR also adds no UI (no message telling the user to start the profile).

## Related Issue

No dedicated issue. Related: #142911 (a refusal for an unserved profile is not a stale owner),
#145224 and #132873 (other changes to the same prune), #140907 / #140908 (automatic parks that heal), the
Webapp's served set (`src/lib/browser-served-profiles.ts`, 8bfff4e27 / 562d95142).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/src/store/dead-session-prune.ts`: `noteServedProfiles()`; per-profile refusal records with
  capped backoff; the `'unreachable'` verdict and its candidate gate; reset clears the new state.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/shell/hooks/use-status-snapshot.ts`: passes `gateway_shared_with` from each accepted
  status to the prune.
- `apps/desktop/src/store/dead-session-prune-unserved.test.ts` (new, 11 tests): no re-ask on the next sweep
  for both refusal wordings; 30 s then 1 min backoff; several chats refused in one sweep start one wait;
  gateway-down still retries; gateway switch forgets; unserved profiles never probed; a returning profile is
  asked at once; full served list still prunes; `null` list behaves as before.
- `apps/desktop/src/app/shell/hooks/use-status-snapshot-served.test.ts` (new, 3 tests): the list is passed
  through, `null` for a standalone gateway, nothing from a signed-out body.

## How to Test

1. `cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run src/store/dead-session-prune-unserved.test.ts`. On `main` the
   refusal tests fail (`expected 1 to be +0`: the second sweep asks the refusing profile again).
2. Same command on this branch: 11 passed. Also `src/store/dead-session-prune.test.ts` (unchanged, 14 passed)
   and `src/app/shell/hooks/use-status-snapshot*.test.ts`.
3. Manual (not done by me): park a secondary profile that has a pinned chat (`hermes -p <name> gateway stop`),
   open Desktop on another profile, and watch `desktop.log`. Before: an `Invalid gateway ticket response`
   about every 10 s. After: none while the served list is known.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide
- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this fix
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass — not run: the change has no Python and my checkout has no
      Python environment
- [ ] `python scripts/check` passes — 11 of 13 checks run and ok (`--only` every guard plus `blob-size`);
      `ruff` and `health` not run (pinned ruff not installed; the change has no Python)
- [x] I've added tests for my changes
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Linux (Omarchy), unit tests only. Full `apps/desktop` vitest: 16,499
      tests, 10 failed, all 10 also failing on unmodified `main` in this environment (`mac-sign`,
      `ui-preferences`, `local-gateway` socket-path length, `source-backend`, `updater/checkout-source`);
      0 new failures. `tsc -p . --noEmit`: clean.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Documentation — module header comment updated; N/A otherwise
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example` — N/A
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md` — N/A
- [x] Cross-platform impact — N/A (renderer logic only)
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas — N/A

prs.title: feat(desktop): add managed oMLX alongside llama.cpp
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds a managed **oMLX** alternative in **Hermes Desktop → Settings → Local Models**, alongside llama.cpp. Users can choose an engine, install oMLX, start/stop its server, download MLX models from Hugging Face, and select a model for new chats.

The choice is offered only on **Apple Silicon (arm64), macOS 15+ backend hosts**. Intel Macs with Metal, Windows, and Linux do not see the selector. The API rejects unsupported oMLX selection without changing config, and stale preferences cannot expose unsupported controls. The CLI’s Local Models setup remains llama.cpp-based.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature

## Changes Made

- Add `hermes_cli/local_runtime/omlx.py`: download the SHA-256-pinned oMLX **0.7.2** DMG through PM’s downloader and privately extract its self-contained bundle. This avoids modifying `/Applications` or installing incompatible Python dependencies into Hermes’s environment.
- Serve only on `127.0.0.1:18081` with a stable private API key. Verify process incarnation and executable ownership before stopping; refuse unrelated listeners and servers owned by another live Hermes process. Refresh process identity across the launcher’s shell-to-Python exec.
- Keep MLX snapshots separate from GGUFs, hide incomplete downloads, and validate generation before applying the existing profile-safe custom-provider assignment. Engine browsing alone never switches the current provider/model. Preserve llama.cpp’s settings, downloads, and explicit-provider boot behavior.
- Add authenticated `/api/local-models/omlx` routes, defaults, bootstrap/provider integration, and the `macos_version()` support-detection helper.
- Add Desktop controls, typed API calls, localized copy, and owner-scoped queries. Electron forwards profile-sensitive operations with explicit profile scope; machine-wide install/download jobs share the backend used for job polling.
- Update Local Models documentation and behavioral regressions. Keep the existing Providers destination-routing fix in its own PR.

## Verification Performed

On this branch, based on the fetched upstream `main`, using existing installed dependencies:

- oMLX backend tests through `scripts/run_tests.sh`: **17 passed**.
- Desktop engine-selector/Local Models surface tests: **14 passed**.
- Electron connection-routing tests: **128 passed**. The runner emitted an unavailable packaged-PM interpreter warning; these routing assertions passed without Python execution.
- Commit-time Ruff and ESLint hooks passed; ESLint reported non-blocking whitespace warnings. Staged scope and committed trees were checked.

Earlier implementation-checkout evidence, before rebasing onto current `main`:

- **Native smoke, not mocks:** installed the bundle, downloaded `mlx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-4bit`, started the server, received `READY` from inference, and stopped it. All four reported native-kernel groups were available.
- Exercised actual REST handlers through TestClient with an isolated config scope: select, start, activate, assignment readback, stop, and switch back. Original profile config and credentials were unchanged.
- Renderer TypeScript check, Desktop build, and signed local packaging passed before the final eligibility-gating change. Packaged renderer/main bytes matched those build outputs; the package was not notarized.

## Limitations / Remaining Verification

- UI tests mock backend responses. Native inference/REST smoke is not a packaged-Desktop click-through. The final eligibility change has not been repackaged; the running Desktop/gateway were not restarted or activated.
- MLX model downloads expose phase/status only, without byte-level progress or pause/resume. llama.cpp’s fit/context-growth guarantees do not apply to oMLX. Port 18081 is fixed; an occupied port fails explicitly.
- No full-suite or current CI pass is claimed. An earlier existing local-model route run had **21 passes / 7 failures** at the PM manifest real-home isolation guard; that broader qualification remains unresolved.

prs.title: fix(skills): compare guard findings against pre-write baseline
prs.body:
## Summary

Fix opt-in `skills.guard_agent_created=true` rejecting unrelated safe updates solely because an existing skill contains a legacy critical heuristic finding. Compare pre/post critical findings for existing-skill writes. Apply the exception **only to an `ask` (`allowed is None`) verdict**, never an explicit denial (`False`). Newly introduced critical findings remain blocked and the write is rolled back. New-skill creation retains its existing full scan.

## Current revision and merge scope

- Verified upstream base: `f30105a0b4b3d0c1baa6c464189755ccdbc1ac7f`.
- Updated PR head: `e863ef322c87f5d549e017ae4e3b869f463f6513`.
- Refreshed on main, preserving upstream `utf-8-sig` handling and SKILL.md description-budget checks; baseline scanning occurs after those pre-write checks.
- **Only implementation + maintained regression tests are proposed upstream (2 files).** Independent reproduction assets are on a separate fork verification branch, not in this PR's ancestry.

## Behavior and safety boundary

Before mutating an existing skill, snapshot critical findings. Compare after the write as a multiset keyed by pattern ID, severity, category, relative file, and matched content. Ignore line numbers so unrelated insertions do not manufacture new findings; file/content/count changes still count as new.

An unchanged legacy finding does not certify that content as safe. This is a narrow write-delta policy, not a human-approval override. If the baseline scan fails, no delta exception is available and the normal post-write decision remains in force. This PR does not change upstream's existing post-scan exception behavior or other approval/config defaults.

## Fresh verification

Against the head/base above:

```sh
scripts/run_tests.sh -j 1 tests/tools/test_skills_guard.py tests/tools/test_skill_manager_tool.py
# 191 passed, 0 failed (86 skill-manager + 105 scanner tests)
ruff check tools/skill_manager_tool.py tests/tools/test_skill_manager_tool.py
# All checks passed!
```

The canonical runner used the checkout's isolated pm test environment. Ruff was executed via `uv tool run ruff` (the pm runtime did not expose a ruff executable). No production checkout, settings, gateway, or personal skills were modified.

Added regressions cover:
- Existing critical + unrelated safe patch succeeds.
- Newly introduced critical is blocked and restored.
- An explicit hard denial is never overridden by the baseline exception.
- Duplicate / moved / altered critical constructs are detected as new.
- A failed baseline scan does not permit an otherwise blocked legacy edit.
- Full edit and supporting-file write work with an unchanged flagged reference.

Existing upstream description-budget tests also passed in the targeted suite.

## Agent-friendly independent reproduction (fork-only)

Use a disposable checkout. No model call, credentials, private skills/config, or scanner mocks are required. The probe executes the real tool/config/filesystem path in temporary HOME/HERMES_HOME; the suspicious fixture is inert text with `example.invalid` and a literal variable name, not a secret or executed command.

- [Guide (commit-pinned)](https://github.com/omoi0kane/hermes-agent/blob/4e6b444ef84dc1617d9f30e09176db58153efd2c/scripts/repro_skill_guard_delta.md)
- [Probe source (commit-pinned)](https://github.com/omoi0kane/hermes-agent/blob/4e6b444ef84dc1617d9f30e09176db58153efd2c/scripts/repro_skill_guard_delta.py)
- SHA256: `f373474a5624cbc09911ead922d4b6474bfc63c7bd4e53dac15b08eb2382903c`

The pinned older guide includes a historical baseline. **Use the current base below for this revision.** Fetch the evidence commit without merging/cherry-picking it:

```sh
KIT=4e6b444ef84dc1617d9f30e09176db58153efd2c
KIT_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
REPRO="$KIT_DIR/repro_skill_guard_delta.py"
git fetch https://github.com/omoi0kane/hermes-agent.git "$KIT"
git show "$KIT:scripts/repro_skill_guard_delta.py" > "$REPRO"
# Set PY to an actual dependency-venv interpreter (absolute path).
# A wrapper relying only on PYTHONPATH is insufficient: the probe intentionally
# clears inherited environment variables before importing Hermes modules.
PY=/absolute/path/to/hermes-dependency-venv/bin/python
"$PY" "$REPRO" --repo "$PWD" --expect fixed
```

Expected: `PASS: expectation=fixed; cases=4; failures=0`, exit 0.

```sh
BASE=f30105a0b4b3d0c1baa6c464189755ccdbc1ac7f
git fetch https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git "$BASE"
git worktree add --detach ../skill-guard-baseline-116091 "$BASE"
"$PY" "$REPRO" --repo ../skill-guard-baseline-116091 --expect baseline
```

Expected: `PASS: expectation=baseline; cases=4; failures=0`, exit 0. This proves the bug, not correctness. Choose an unused worktree destination.

Negative controls (execute separately if shell is fail-fast):

```sh
"$PY" "$REPRO" --repo ../skill-guard-baseline-116091 --expect fixed
"$PY" "$REPRO" --repo "$PWD" --expect baseline
```

Both must FAIL with exit 1. Setup/import failures do not count as successful security rejection tests.

Fresh independent probe results on macOS / Python 3.14.9: current base baseline PASS/0, fixed FAIL/1; refreshed PR fixed PASS/0, baseline FAIL/1. Four cases: clean control, legacy single edit, legacy batch edit, new-critical rejection + original-byte restoration. All were actually executed.

## Remaining review scope

Not a full model/Discord/TUI end-to-end test, full repository suite, or cross-platform certification. Existing critical content is not endorsed as safe. Maintainer policy decision requested: allow unrelated safe edits when legacy critical findings are unchanged, while preserving explicit denials and blocking new findings?

Addresses #53491. Related to #94353; complementary to #94358 (explicit human approval path), not a replacement for it.

prs.title: feat(plugin-catalog): add hermesvault
prs.body:
xf## What does this PR do?

Adds `plugin-catalog/hermesvault.yaml`, a catalog entry for **hermesvault**: a secret-source plugin that keeps secrets out of plaintext `.env` files.

It resolves `secrets.hermesvault.env` entries (`ENV_VAR: hv:<item>[:field]`) at startup from a local [FloorVault](https://github.com/Guerilla-ops/floorvault) store (AES-256-SIV, context-bound records). It also adds a `hermes hvault` CLI to add, update, show, list and remove items.

The plugin lives in the FloorVault repository under `plugins/hermesvault`, pinned at `1fcb5988225b981fd0b28320c02a9ae607e7ab11`. This entry is submitted by the repository owner.

**Hermes surfaces used:**
- `ctx.register_secret_source()`, using `SecretSource` from `agent.secret_sources.base`.
  - Mapped shape, scheme `hv`.
  - The fetch never raises and never prompts.
  - The bootstrap key is read through `get_source_environment()` and declared via `token_env_key`, so it is protected from being overwritten.
- `ctx.register_cli_command()` for `hermes hvault`. The hermes hvault CLI command is skipped under plugins.isolation: host. The secret source works there as of NousResearch/hermes-agent#144430: before that fix a hosted fetch() result crossed the plugin-host wire as a generic record and apply_all applied nothing. That case was found by the maintainer during this review, not by my testing, which ran the source in-process.
- No tools, hooks, middleware or core overrides.

**Disclosure (rule 13):**
- **Reads and writes** an encrypted store under `<HERMES_HOME>/agent-vault`, or `secrets.hermesvault.dir`.
- **Reads its own master key** from the OS key store (macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service or Windows DPAPI; service `floor-vault`), or from the environment variable named by `token_env` (default `HERMES_VAULT_KEY`).
  - It reads only its own key entry; it never reads `.env`, `auth.json`, or other tools' credentials.
  - The listed `hermes-wincred` and `hermes-dpapi-secrets` sources read the OS key store in the same way.
- **Resolved values** become environment variables of the Hermes process and its children, like `.env` entries.
- **Installs** `floorvault>=0.2.1,<0.3` from PyPI, plus `secretstorage` on Linux and `pyobjc-framework-Security` on macOS. Every dependency has an upper bound. `floorvault`'s runtime dependency is `cryptography>=50.0.0`, which is compatible with Hermes' pin `cryptography==50.0.1`.
- No network calls, no subprocesses, no telemetry, no self-update. The plugin directory (5 text files) contains no binaries or bytecode.
- **Interactive input:** `hermes hvault put` prompts for a value with `getpass`. That is an interactive CLI command; the startup fetch path never prompts.
- **Protection** is at rest (backups, sync, copied files), not against code already running as the same user.

## Related Issue

None. This is a catalog submission.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/hermesvault.yaml`: new entry. `tier: community`, `category: tools`, `requires_hermes: ">=0.21.2"`, `version: "0.2.0"`, with a 2:1 banner image pinned to the same commit.

## How to Test

1. `python3 scripts/validate_plugin_catalog.py plugin-catalog/` prints `OK` for every file, including this one.
2. At the pinned commit, `hermes plugins validate plugins/hermesvault --install-deps` passes, including `security scan — safe` and `no core override`. Dependencies resolve from PyPI.
3. End to end, on a scratch `HERMES_HOME`:
   1. `hermes plugins install Guerilla-ops/floorvault/plugins/hermesvault`
   2. `hermes plugins enable hermesvault`
   3. `printf 'value=test\n' | hermes hvault add "Test" --id vault_test --stdin`
   4. Map `OPENROUTER_API_KEY: hv:vault_test` under `secrets.hermesvault.env`.
   5. `hermes status` should print `FloorVault: applied 1 secret`.

Results in the submitter's runs:
- **Catalog checks:** the catalog validator and `scan_plugin_payloads.py` pass.
- **Conformance:** Hermes' `SecretSourceConformance` kit passes (10/10) against releases 0.21.2, 0.21.3, 0.21.4 and 0.21.5, and against main `fab9b01`.
- **End to end:** the steps above pass on main `fab9b01`, with `floorvault` 0.2.1 installed from PyPI.
- **Not tested end to end:** Keychain, Secret Service and DPAPI custody, which need a desktop session. The `token_env` path was exercised.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Submitting to the Plugin Catalog](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/developer-guide/plugins/catalog-submission)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/)
- [x] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate
- [x] My PR contains **only** changes related to this entry
- [ ] I've run `pytest tests/ -q` and all tests pass: N/A (catalog-only change; catalog validator run instead)
- [ ] `python scripts/check` passes: N/A (no code)
- [x] I've tested on my platform: Linux (Ubuntu container), Hermes main `fab9b01` and releases 0.21.2–0.21.5

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Documentation: N/A (the plugin README renders on the catalog page)
- [x] `cli-config.yaml.example`: N/A
- [x] `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md`: N/A
- [x] Cross-platform impact: the plugin supports Linux, macOS and Windows; only Linux was tested end to end

## Summary
- ignore readable sibling `kanban.db` placeholders that do not have a `tasks` table

Workspace cleanup scans every sibling board DB before deleting a completed scratch workspace. A readable but uninitialized `kanban.db` raises `no such table: tasks`; the caller maps that to `reason=unknown` and defers cleanup forever. This can accumulate completed scratch workspaces over time.

prs.title: fix(gateway): guard null-origin completion preflight
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Avoid an `AttributeError` in completion preflight when a serialized routing entry has `SessionEntry.origin = None`. The optional-origin guard preserves the existing LOCAL chat-ID special case when an origin is present and the existing logical-owner lookup otherwise.

The messaging regression covers Telegram forum topics and Discord DMs **with an already populated inbound source cache**. This fixes the null-origin preflight crash on that path; it does not establish that a LOCAL chat owner and a transcript's logical owner are equivalent, or repair messaging delivery after a cold boot without cached source information.

## Related Issue

Related to #146696: addresses the reported `NoneType.platform` preflight exception only. Full cold-start route recovery and live adapter delivery remain unverified; this PR does not automatically close the broader issue.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/session_automation.py`: guard the optional origin before the LOCAL special case.
- `tests/gateway/test_completion_missing_origin.py`: retain the eight messaging positive controls (Telegram/Discord × direct/compressed × valid/null origin), including durable acknowledgement and replay.
- Add two LOCAL null-origin negative controls, using a real local-session reset to make the admission owner **different** from `authority.logical_owner(entry.session_id)`, with direct and compression-tip variants. Save and deserialize the null origin, assert there is no inbound source cache, and retry delivery twice. Both attempts defer: no admission under the true local owner, the incorrect transcript owner or compression tip; the durable completion stays `pending` with zero attempts, and no in-memory delivered acknowledgement is recorded.

These tests use real adapters, session serialization and SQLite ledgers, stopping before model execution. The LOCAL cases pin the existing deferral boundary when the source cannot prove local admission ownership; they do not add a new route-recovery policy or claim general cold-start delivery support.

## How to Test

Ubuntu 24.04.3 / Python 3.14.9, using the canonical runner:

```bash
HERMES_PYTHON=$PWD/.venv/bin/python HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0 \
  scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_completion_missing_origin.py -q
# With fix: 10 passed.
# Same final test file with the production guard removed:
# 4 passed, 6 failed with AttributeError (four messaging and two LOCAL null-origin cases).

HERMES_PYTHON=$PWD/.venv/bin/python HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES=0 \
  scripts/run_tests.sh \
  tests/gateway/test_completion_missing_origin.py \
  tests/gateway/test_completion_admission.py \
  tests/gateway/test_automation_compression_media.py \
  tests/gateway/test_automation_retry.py \
  tests/gateway/test_completion_ownership_proof.py \
  tests/gateway/test_completion_admission_compression_race.py \
  tests/gateway/test_local_chat_delivery.py \
  tests/gateway/test_local_automation.py \
  tests/gateway/test_automation_wake_route.py -j 4 -q
# 48 passed, 5 failed.
# All five failures are test_local_automation.py subprocess tests:
# Unix control socket denied (Errno 1: Operation not permitted).
# Re-running that file with the production guard removed gives the same five failures.

.venv/bin/python scripts/check --base HEAD
# Review delta against a local snapshot of b5e9b471:
# 14 checks passed; code health: 0 blocking, 0 advisory.
git diff --cached --check
# passed
```

Upstream base: `088f657ecf77674c7b8e2ededf4e3576d82e042c`. The production change remains the single guard from `b5e9b471`; this review follow-up only adds the LOCAL test. The full repository suite, a true messaging cold boot without source cache, and live platform/model delivery were not run.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the Contributing Guide.
- [x] My commit message follows Conventional Commits.
- [x] I searched existing open and closed PRs and the issue timeline for duplicates.
- [x] This PR contains only changes related to this fix.
- [ ] I've run the entire test suite and all tests pass (targeted results and baseline environment failures are documented above).
- [x] `python scripts/check` passes.
- [x] I've added tests for my changes.
- [x] Tested on Ubuntu 24.04.3 / Python 3.14.9.

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] Documentation: N/A; no public API or configuration contract changes.
- [x] Configuration example: N/A; no config keys changed.
- [x] Contributing/architecture instructions: N/A; no workflow changes.
- [x] Cross-platform impact considered: pure Python optional-value check, no platform-specific operations added.
- [x] Tool descriptions/schemas: N/A.

prs.title: feat(slack): add read-only Slack channel history tool
prs.body: Adds an opt-in, service-gated, read-only `slack` tool for bounded Slack history using the selected profile’s existing live Slack adapter and SDK client. Actions: - `list_channels` — list bounded public/private channels that the bot belongs to; - `fetch_history` — read a bounded channel or DM timeline; - `fetch_thread` — read a thread parent and replies, including from a validated Slack permalink; - `find_messages` — scan bounded pages using text and URL-domain filters. The tool provides explicit continuation metadata when Slack pagination, match limits, or local serialization limits leave more data. ## Authorization model By default, the tool can read only the active Slack conversation. An optional cross-channel exception is available only when all of these conditions hold: 1. the inbound turn came directly from the local Slack adapter; 2. the active conversation is a 1:1 `D…` DM; 3. the actor’s Slack member ID is explicitly configured in `history_cross_channel_user_ids` for the selected profile; 4. the target belongs to the same single connected workspace; 5. the authenticated credential is proven by `auth.test` to be a bot token; 6. the bot is a member of the target channel; 7. the target passes the selected profile’s `allowed_channels` policy, when configured; 8. the target is not another DM or an MPIM/group DM. Shared channels and threads cannot use the owner exception, preventing private cross-channel results from being disclosed to other participants. ## Security and privacy boundaries - Direct-Slack provenance is a wire-invisible, per-turn capability stamped only by the live adapter. - Queued recursive turns rebind the complete actor/session identity, preventing a later participant from inheriting a previous owner’s authorization. - Synthetic, restored, relayed, and background turns cannot borrow local Slack history authority. - Multiplex authorization resolves through the selected profile’s adapter and workspace. - YAML `allowed_channels` remains profile-local rather than flowing through a process-global environment bridge. - Missing or explicitly empty channel allowlists remain unrestricted; malformed allowlist types or channel IDs fail closed before history APIs and deny normal channel intake. - User-token installations may still connect with a warning for existing gateway behavior, but cannot expose the agent-facing history tool or call history/list APIs. - Multi-workspace adapters are ineligible; use one bot workspace per served profile. - Disallowed targets fail before Slack metadata, list, history, or replies API calls. - Permalinks are parsed locally and never fetched as URLs. - Returned Slack text is treated as untrusted external data and best-effort redacted. - Per-field, per-item, page-count, match-count, collection, and final serialized-response budgets are enforced. - Local truncation never advances a remote cursor past omitted items; `find_messages` fails safely if no match can fit. - Slack history results never enter the tool-result persistence backend. - The tool exposes no post, reaction, edit, delete, or other Slack mutation action. ## Tool and service gating `slack_history` is an explicit Slack platform toolset. The model schema is exposed only when the selected profile's running adapter has exactly one authenticated bot workspace and both history entry points are available. Profile identity and live eligibility are part of the availability-cache key, so one eligible sibling profile or stale connect/disconnect state cannot advertise a dead capability. Example toolset opt-in: ```yaml platform_toolsets: slack: [hermes-slack, slack_history] ``` Optional owner-only cross-channel configuration: ```yaml slack: history_cross_channel_user_ids: - "U01ABC2DEF3" ``` The owner list is profile-local and has no environment fallback. No new credential is introduced. ## Related Issue Fixes #6345 Partially addresses #35291 by adding a read-only Slack history tool and documentation. It does not implement that issue's broader setup wizard, OAuth scope manifest, or event-subscription work. ## CI and compatibility repairs included - Adds the original contributor’s `nmh9097@gmail.com` attribution mapping. - Corrects the quick-command fixture so a bare `MagicMock` does not accidentally become an internal message. - Initializes `_primary_profile_name` in the bare multiplex runner fixture. - Rebinds queued-turn identity with stack-safe ContextVar tokens. - Preserves pagination integrity across remote cursors and local output truncation. - Keeps Slack YAML channel allowlists profile-local under multiplex operation. - Makes dynamic tool-availability caches profile- and lifecycle-aware while preserving the existing zero-argument registry check contract. - Stabilizes dynamic availability snapshots across computation races and bounds contextual result/last-good caches. - Binds each contextual availability verdict to the same immutable sample used by its outer cache key, including ABA lifecycle transitions. - Validates loaded Slack channel allowlists and fails closed on malformed mapping, numeric, mixed, or invalid-ID values. - Validates history-owner settings atomically so a valid owner mixed with malformed input cannot retain cross-channel authority. ## Related and overlapping work Duplicate/overlap search was performed before finalization: - #29489 is the closest direct overlap: it also proposes scoped Slack history, but uses a separate token path and does not provide this PR’s live-adapter reuse, per-turn provenance, multiplex profile/workspace isolation, DM-only owner boundary, aggregate response budget, or no-persistence contract. - #63868 overlaps permalink parsing, but hydrates linked Slack content into inbound context; this PR accepts a permalink only as an explicit read-tool target. - #62135 overlaps capability-aware Slack platform guidance, not the read path. - #22061 requests platform-specific context access more generally. - #44430 requested automatic full-channel context; this PR instead keeps reads explicit and bounded. ## Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) - [X] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality) - [X] 🔒 Security fix - [X] 📝 Documentation update - [X] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage) - [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change) - [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub) ## Changes Made ### Slack history tool and toolset - `tools/slack_tool.py` - Adds the service-gated, read-only `slack` tool with `list_channels`, `fetch_history`, `fetch_thread`, and `find_messages` actions. - Reuses the selected profile's live Slack adapter/client instead of introducing another token path. - Enforces bounded pagination, query/domain filtering, permalink parsing, redaction, continuation metadata, and final response-size limits. - `toolsets.py` and `hermes_cli/tools_config.py` - Add the explicit `slack_history` platform toolset and keep it opt-in alongside `hermes-slack`. ### Authorization, identity, and adapter boundaries - `plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py` - Proves bot-token identity with `auth.test`, binds reads to a single authenticated workspace, and denies user-token or multi-workspace history access. - Enforces active-conversation access by default and the narrow direct-1:1-DM owner exception before Slack list, metadata, history, or replies API calls. - Applies bot membership and profile-local channel allowlists, rejects cross-DM/MPIM targets, clears principal capability on disconnect, and atomically rejects malformed owner/allowlist configuration. - `gateway/authz_mixin.py`, `gateway/session_context.py`, and `gateway/run.py` - Stamp trusted direct-Slack provenance, resolve authorization through the selected profile, and rebind/restore complete actor identity for queued or recursive turns. - Keep synthetic, restored, relayed, background, and mismatched-profile turns fail closed. - `gateway/session.py` - Adds capability-aware Slack prompt context while preserving conservative limitations when the history tool is unavailable. ### Configuration and service availability - `gateway/config.py`, `hermes_cli/config.py`, and `cli-config.yaml.example` - Add profile-local `history_cross_channel_user_ids` configuration and preserve profile-local `allowed_channels` values without a process-global environment fallback. - `model_tools.py` and `tools/registry.py` - Scope model-facing tool availability to the selected profile and live adapter lifecycle. - Bind availability verdicts to the exact sampled context used by cache keys, prevent cross-profile and ABA lifecycle cache errors, and bound contextual caches. ### Output and persistence safety - `tools/tool_result_storage.py` and `agent/tool_dispatch_helpers.py` - Prevent Slack history results from entering the tool-result persistence backend while preserving aggregate tool-result naming. ### Tests, documentation, and attribution - `tests/tools/test_slack_tool.py` and the changed gateway, session, multiplex, registry, cache, configuration, CLI, and persistence tests - Cover action behavior, pagination/truncation integrity, provenance, bot-principal enforcement, profile/workspace isolation, direct-DM owner boundaries, malformed configuration, queued identity, cache lifecycle/ABA behavior, and no-persistence guarantees. - `website/docs/reference/tools-reference.md`, `website/docs/reference/toolsets-reference.md`, and `website/docs/user-guide/messaging/slack.md` - Document setup, actions, access boundaries, configuration, pagination, and limitations. - `scripts/release.py` - Preserves the original hardening contributor's GitHub attribution. ## How to Test ```bash scripts/run_tests.sh \ tests/tools/test_slack_tool.py \ tests/gateway/test_slack.py \ tests/gateway/test_session.py \ tests/gateway/test_session_env.py \ tests/gateway/test_slack_history_config.py \ tests/gateway/test_slack_history_cross_channel.py \ tests/gateway/test_multiplex_profile_authz.py \ tests/gateway/test_multiplex_pairing_stores.py \ tests/gateway/test_background_process_notifications.py \ tests/gateway/test_run_progress_topics.py \ tests/gateway/test_relay_upstream_authz.py \ tests/agent/test_tool_dispatch_helpers.py \ tests/tools/test_tool_result_storage.py \ tests/tools/test_registry.py \ tests/tools/test_terminal_tool_requirements.py \ tests/test_get_tool_definitions_cache_isolation.py \ tests/hermes_cli/test_tools_config.py \ tests/cli/test_quick_commands.py \ -q ``` ## Checklist ### Code - prs.title: feat(slack): add per-channel reply modes
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds deterministic per-channel Slack reply modes through `platforms.slack.extra.channel_reply_modes`.

A workspace can keep the historical global `reply_in_thread` default while selecting individual channels that should use either:

- `channel`: top-level messages share one channel-scoped session and all progress, prompts, attachments, and final replies stay in the channel timeline.
- `thread`: top-level messages keep the existing thread-per-message behavior.

Replies inside a genuine existing Slack thread always remain thread-scoped in either mode.

This addresses mixed Slack workspaces where long-running project channels need continuous top-level conversation while task-oriented channels should remain thread-isolated. The existing global boolean cannot express both behaviors at once.

This is distinct from #73070, which proposes adaptive per-message classification, and #73851, which changes per-channel mention gating rather than reply placement/session scope.

## Related Issue

No linked issue.

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [x] 📝 Documentation update
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- Add `SlackAdapter._reply_in_thread_for_channel()` with global fallback.
- Apply the resolved mode to inbound session scope and every Slack outbound thread resolver call path.
- Make progress/status routing use the same channel-aware decision.
- Preserve existing-thread isolation regardless of the configured top-level mode.
- Document the new YAML map in the config example and English/Chinese Slack guides.
- Add regression coverage for both override directions, genuine threads, invalid-value fallback, and progress routing.
- Assert actual Slack API payloads for final text, status, attachment, and interactive-prompt delivery.

## How to Test

1. Configure a flat project channel while keeping the global thread default:

   ```yaml
   platforms:
     slack:
       extra:
         reply_in_thread: true
         channel_reply_modes:
           C0123456789: channel
   ```

2. Send two top-level messages in `C0123456789`; confirm both use the same channel-scoped session and all progress/final output stays top-level.
3. Reply inside an existing thread in the same channel; confirm the response stays in that thread.
4. Configure another channel as `thread` with global `reply_in_thread: false`; confirm that channel still opens a thread per top-level message.
5. Run:

   ```bash
   pytest tests/gateway/test_slack*.py tests/gateway/test_run_progress_topics.py tests/gateway/relay/test_relay_slack*.py -q
   ```

- Focused per-channel routing and payload suite: **31 passed**.
