prs.title: fix(openai_compat): handle Gemini thought_signature (echo captured + sentinel for unsigned tool calls)
prs.body:
## 📝 Description

Fix the `400 INVALID_ARGUMENT` error returned by Gemini 3 when continuing a tool-calling conversation through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

```
Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts.
This is required for tools to work correctly, and missing thought_signature
may lead to degraded model performance. ... https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thought-signatures
```

Gemini 3 requires the `thought_signature` to be **echoed back inside `extra_content.google.thought_signature`** on every `functionCall` part of the request history. PicoClaw's OpenAI-compatible provider only sent it under `function.thought_signature`, which Gemini rejects on the follow-up request.

Three distinct bugs are fixed:

1. **Serialization** (`pkg/providers/common/common.go`): resolve the signature from every known location (`Function.ThoughtSignature`, top-level `ThoughtSignature`, `ExtraContent.Google`) and emit it inside `extra_content.google.thought_signature`. A signature-less tool call no longer emits an empty `extra_content` block.

2. **Streaming capture** (`pkg/providers/openai_compat/provider.go`): `parseStreamResponse` did **not** read the `thought_signature` at all. Since `ChatStream` is the default chat path, any tool call produced in streaming mode lost the signature entirely, so the next request was rejected. The delta parser now captures the signature from both `function.thought_signature` and `extra_content.google.thought_signature`.

3. **Unsigned tool calls on Gemini hosts** (`pkg/providers/common/common.go` + `pkg/providers/openai_compat/provider.go`): fixes 1 and 2 only cover the case where the tool call was produced *by Gemini itself*, so a signature is available to echo. They do **not** cover the case that actually breaks the fallback chain: the tool call was produced by another provider (e.g. `deepseek-v4.1-flash`) and the turn later fell back to Gemini 3. There is no signature to echo, and Gemini rejects the request with the same `400`. Fix: a new `SerializeOptions{GeminiThoughtSignatureFallback}` injects the documented sentinel `skip_thought_signature_validator` into `extra_content.google.thought_signature` on every unsigned `functionCall` part. The option is enabled only for Gemini hosts (`isGeminiHost`), so every other endpoint keeps omitting `extra_content` exactly as before, and a real captured signature is never overridden.

## 🗣️ Type of Change
- [x] 🐞 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 📖 Documentation update
- [ ] ⚡ Code refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)

## 🤖 AI Code Generation
- [ ] 🤖 Fully AI-generated (100% AI, 0% Human)
- [x] 🛠️ Mostly AI-generated (AI draft, Human verified/modified)
- [ ] 👨‍💻 Mostly Human-written (Human lead, AI assisted or none)

## 🔗 Related Issue

Refs #3230, Refs #3111 — same `400` on OpenAI-compat Gemini 3 tool loops.

## 📚 Technical Context (Skip for Docs)
- **Reference URL:** https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thought-signatures
- **Reasoning:**
  - Gemini 3 (via both `generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/` and gateways such as Cloudflare AI Gateway) mandatory-signature contract. The signature must be resent on the assistant tool-call message of the following request, and Google specifically looks for `extra_content.google.thought_signature`.
  - `extra_content` is a Google-only extension. Providers that don't support it ignore unknown fields on the assistant tool-call object, so emitting it is additive; the `google` key is what only Gemini accepts. This mirrors upstream's existing `serializeToolCalls` behavior of preserving signatures, ordering the resolution so a top-level `ThoughtSignature` (set by the streaming path) still wins.

## 🧪 Test Environment
- **Hardware:** PC (linux/amd64)
- **OS:** Linux
- **Model/Provider:** `gemini-3.8-flash` via Google AI Studio OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/`)
- **Channels:** Telegram / web

## 📸 Evidence (Optional)
<details>
<summary>Click to view Logs/Screenshots</summary>

Reproduced failure mode (provider fallback from a DeepSeek primary to Gemini):

```
failover(format): provider=openai model=gemini-3.8-flash status=400
Function call is missing a thought_signature in functionCall parts...
```

Live reproduction against `generativelanguage.googleapis.com` (OpenAI-compat endpoint) confirms the fix for bug 3: an unsigned `functionCall` part fails with `400`, while the same part carrying the documented sentinel `skip_thought_signature_validator` is accepted; a real captured signature is preserved and never replaced.

Local verification:
```
$ go test ./pkg/providers/...
ok  github.com/sipeed/picoclaw/pkg/providers/common        0.032s
ok  github.com/sipeed/picoclaw/pkg/providers/openai_compat 0.121s
(... all pkg/providers packages pass)

$ golangci-lint run --build-tags goolm,stdjson ./pkg/providers/...
0 issues.
```

New tests cover: wire payload contains `"extra_content":{"google":{"thought_signature":"..."}}` when the signature is only on `Function`, only top-level, or only on `ExtraContent`; no `extra_content` when there is no signature; a streaming `ChatStream` round that captures the signature from the delta; the sentinel is injected for unsigned parts on Gemini hosts and omitted on non-Gemini hosts; and a real signature is never overridden by the sentinel.

</details>

prs.title: WIP: feat: base multi-agent collaboration framework & shared context
prs.body:
## 📝 Description

**WIP** — Base multi-agent collaboration framework with shared context pool, agent handoff, and discovery tools.

Builds on top of the merged PRs #213 (provider protocol refactor) and #131 (model fallback chain + multi-agent routing) to add:

- **Blackboard** — Thread-safe shared key-value context pool (`pkg/multiagent/blackboard.go`) for inter-agent data sharing with scoped entries (author, scope, timestamp)
- **BlackboardTool** — LLM-callable tool for read/write/list/delete on the shared context
- **Agent Handoff** — Synchronous delegation between agents via `ExecuteHandoff()` with automatic context propagation through the blackboard
- **HandoffTool** — LLM-callable tool that resolves target agent, writes context, builds system prompt, and delegates via `RunToolLoop`
- **ListAgentsTool** — Discovery tool listing all registered agents with ID/Name/Role
- **AgentResolver interface** — Decouples `pkg/multiagent` from `pkg/agent` to avoid circular imports
- **AgentLoop integration** — Blackboard snapshot injection into system messages, per-session blackboards via `sync.Map`, tools auto-registered when >1 agent configured
- **Config extensions** — `Role` and `SystemPrompt` fields on `AgentConfig` and `AgentInstance`

### Architecture decisions
- Zero overhead for single-agent setups (multi-agent tools only registered when `len(registry.ListAgentIDs()) > 1`)
- `registryResolver` adapter bridges `AgentRegistry` → `multiagent.AgentResolver` at the integration boundary
- Blackboard entries carry authorship metadata for audit/debugging

## 🗣️ Type of Change

issues.title: [hardening] Iron front: let operators turn off the automatic provider model domains in allowed_hosts
issues.body:
**Confirmation:** ☑ not an exploitable vulnerability (behaviour follows the current design for native providers).

**What should be safer?**

`ironFrontConfig()` builds `allowed_hosts` as `[settings.modelHost, ...providerModelAllowedHosts(), ...readAllowedHosts(settings)]` (`.claude/skills/add-iron-proxy/payload/src/gateway-providers/iron-proxy.ts`, ~line 220). The Claude contract is always registered (`anthropic.com`), and the OpenCode contract adds its native domains (`api.openai.com`, `chatgpt.com`, `openrouter.ai`, `api.deepseek.com`, `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, `api.anthropic.com`), each also as `*.<domain>`. `src/gateway-approval-coordinator.ts` (lines 406–417) then approves the front's default-trigger requests to the group provider's `modelDomains`/`modelAuthorities` without a card, for any method. This matches the documented design (`docs/gateway-seam.md`, "Default model-traffic approvals"); the request here is an opt-out, not a bug report.

An install that deliberately uses one model endpoint (e.g. OpenCode with `OPENCODE_BASE_URL` pointing at a self-hosted or confidential-inference endpoint) cannot remove these domains: `openCodeModelDomains()` keeps the native list even when a base URL is set. A prompt-injected agent can send data to them, for example with an API key of its own, without an approval card, although `allowed-hosts.json` is empty.

**How can we verify the concern?**

1. Normal install: Iron gateway, egress lockdown on, OpenCode provider with `OPENCODE_BASE_URL=https://llm.example.net/v1`, `allowed-hosts.json` = `[]`.
2. Read the generated front config. Calling `ironFrontConfig()` from `main` with those settings gives `allowed_hosts` = `anthropic.com`, `api.anthropic.com`, `api.deepseek.com`, `api.openai.com`, `chatgpt.com`, `generativelanguage.googleapis.com`, `llm.example.net`, `openrouter.ai` (each also as `*.`).
3. From the agent container, `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions -d '{}'` should be forwarded to the host without a card, per the code above. We have not run this step; steps 1–2 we have. No host access, source change or unsafe mount needed.

Suggested change: an opt-out (e.g. `IRON_PROVIDER_MODEL_DOMAINS=false`, or a field in `allowed-hosts.json`) that builds `allowed_hosts` from `modelHost` plus the operator list only, and limits the card exemption to the configured endpoint's authority. Today's behaviour stays the default. We run the strict variant locally (`allowed_hosts: [...new Set(readAllowedHosts(settings))].sort()`) without other changes.

**Affected version:** v2026.10.0 (`7203e00`); unchanged in v2026.10.1-rc.2 and on `main` `acc2b1c`.

**Related trust boundary:** Network egress, Human approval.

prs.title: feat(channels): add native Proton Mail adapter via Proton Mail Bridge
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

The adapter half of #3726, moved to the `channels` registry branch as review asked; #3726 keeps the skill (`/add-proton-mail`) and the Bridge container on `main`.
- **What**: a native IMAP/SMTP adapter (`src/channels/proton-mail.ts`) for a local Proton Mail Bridge, its tests, the barrel import, and five exact-pinned deps.
- **Sender identity**: a mail counts as from its `From:` address only when Proton vouches for it. Mail from outside Proton needs exactly one `mail.protonmail.ch` DMARC verdict, `pass`, for the From domain. Mail from another Proton account (which carries no verdict) needs exactly one `X-Pm-Origin: internal` and no Proton DMARC verdict at all. Either way, the `From:` must be a single plain dot-atom address. Mail from the Bridge account's own address is never delivered. Refused mail stays unread.
- **Approval cards**: each card mail carries an `[NC-…]` token in its subject. An answer counts only from the card's approver, quoting the token, `In-Reply-To` the card mail, with an option command on the first line. Every option gets a distinct command, so duplicate labels can't shadow each other. Cards persist across restarts; `onAction` gets the card's Message-ID and address. A card core has closed (a terminal edit), or no longer holds a row for, refuses later replies, giving core's reason when it gave one ("that request has closed: ⏱️ Timed out — no response"). Unanswered cards are never pruned before their 7-day TTL; at 1000 open cards a new one is refused (delivery fails) rather than pushing one out.
- **Confirmations**: none of the adapter's own for gateway approvals (`deferResolution`) — core's card edit is the confirmation, threaded onto the card; other cards get a neutral "Reply received". If that acknowledgement fails to send, the answer still stands.
- **Transport**: IMAP STARTTLS required (it was opportunistic: a listener without STARTTLS received the bridge password in clear); certificate verification on except on loopback; `PROTON_MAIL_TLS_CA_FILE` pins Bridge's own certificate so loopback is verified too, and an unreadable pin stops the adapter rather than falling back.
- **Delivery**: no mail is read until a fixed 30 s after `setup()`, whatever the poll interval, so nothing is marked read while the host still holds routing at startup. The inbound message id is chosen by the adapter (UIDVALIDITY plus UID), never the sender's Message-ID, which stays in `content` for threading. A reply that keeps the conversation's subject, or arrives on a card's thread, reaches core as its bare body, so core's free-text prompts (a new agent's name, a rejection reason) get just the answer. A mail whose handling fails *inside the adapter* (fetch, parse, card lookup, sending a refusal notice) is retried with back-off up to five times, then left unread and flagged `$NanoClawFailed`. **Routing failures inside the host are not retried**: `onInbound` hands the mail over and the host catches its own routing errors, so the mail is already marked read. Messages are fetched one at a time; mail over 40 MB is skipped.
- **Limits**: HTML-only mail uses mailparser's own text conversion. The body is capped at 50k characters, the subject at 300, and Message-ID and References are bounded. Attachments go through only once the sender's DM is wired to an agent, up to 15 MB each and 25 MB per mail. State lives under `STORE_DIR`; `PROTON_MAIL_POLL_SECONDS` must be 10–3600.
- **Headers that cannot be sent**: Bridge builds each outgoing mail from a draft template and drops custom headers, so `Auto-Submitted` (RFC 3834) and our `X-NanoClaw-Agent` loop marker never arrive. Loops are stopped by the own-address check, by the inbound filter for bounces and auto-replies, and by a limit of 20 mails an hour from any one sender; beyond it mail is left unread. That limit is what stops two agents answering each other.
- **Message kinds**: the body comes before the subject, so a `/command` by email is a command; `send_card` goes out as its fallback text plus links; an edit goes out as a correction on the edited mail's thread.
- **Out of scope**: shared email helpers (sender check, reply-card store) for `/add-resend` and #3743 — a follow-up once their home is agreed; a generic IMAP/SMTP channel (maintainers' call).

<details>
<summary>Why the sender check counts verdicts, not their position</summary>

Review asked for `Authentication-Results` "only as added by the trusted receiving server". Bridge adds no verdict of its own; it serves the headers Proton's inbound servers recorded. A position rule (only verdicts above the first `Received:`) was tried and dropped: across 60 real inbox mails, Bridge rebuilds every message with the whole `Received:` chain first, then Proton's verdicts, then `X-Pm-Origin`, so position says nothing about who added a verdict. A forged `mail.protonmail.ch` verdict beside Proton's makes two and is refused; all 60 external mails carried exactly one.
</details>

<details>
<summary>Why X-Pm-Origin: internal can be trusted (probes on Bridge 3.27.0)</summary>

Proton-to-Proton mail carries no Authentication-Results, so the DMARC rule alone refused all of it. Three probes:
1. **External mail with forged Proton headers.** A mail from Gmail carried a forged `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, `X-Pm-Content-Encryption`, `X-Pm-Internal-Id` and `mail.protonmail.ch; dmarc=pass`. Every one was stripped. What arrived carried Proton's own single `X-Pm-Origin: external` and Proton's real verdicts only.
2. **A separate Proton account to the Bridge account.** One `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, `X-Pm-Content-Encryption: end-to-end`, and no Authentication-Results.
3. **The Bridge account to itself.** The same as probe 2.

A Proton sender cannot set headers: Bridge's SMTP draft template drops them, and Proton's clients offer none. Bridge takes `From` from Proton's sender record. The rule fails closed: a forged `internal` that ever survived would sit beside Proton's `external` and be refused as two values, and if Proton stopped sending the header, internal mail would go back to being refused.
</details>

## Related work

Split from #3726 (skill half stays there; it copies these files from `channels`, so this lands first). Purely additive on `channels`: new files, one barrel line, five deps.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` on this branch → clean
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/` → 746 passed, 19 skipped (68 files), run locally: CI does not run on PRs into `channels`. This includes:
  - `proton-mail.test.ts`, the helpers: sender check (DMARC and `X-Pm-Origin`), plain-address check, card matching and distinct commands, framing, header caps, poll bounds, TLS options, skip rules.
  - `proton-mail-adapter.test.ts`, the adapter against fake IMAP/SMTP and real mailparser:
    - sender identity: forged sender refused; Proton-internal mail delivered; forged `internal` beside `external` refused; own address dropped; quoted local part refused;
    - approval cards: a late `/approve` answers its own card; cards survive a restart; a closed or missing card refuses replies; a failed acknowledgement keeps the answer; unanswered cards survive pruning; the gateway confirmation;
    - delivery: no mail read before the startup delay, even with a one-hour poll; adapter-chosen inbound ids; bare-body replies; the 20-an-hour sender limit; the card ceiling refusing new cards; capped attachment-name lists; retries on fetch and notice-send failures, and giving up; attachments held until approval; subject and Message-ID caps;
    - also slash commands, `send_card`, edits, and STARTTLS with pinning.
- `eslint` 0 errors, `prettier --check` clean on the new files
- Header probes against live Bridge 3.27.0 (26 Oct): our Message-ID survives Bridge; Proton strips forged `X-Pm-*` and `mail.protonmail.ch` headers from external mail; Proton-to-Proton mail carries `X-Pm-Origin: internal` and no Authentication-Results. See the second details block above.
- Adapter tests run against a scratch working directory and refuse to run otherwise, so they never touch a real install's `store/`
- Manual, Raspberry Pi 5 (Debian 13, Docker): live since 24 Oct with Bridge 3.27.0 run as uid 10001 with no capabilities — IMAP connects with the pinned certificate over required STARTTLS; SMTP STARTTLS + AUTH verified against the pin; inbound mail ingested. The 26 Oct review fixes are covered by the tests and probes above; they are not yet live on that install.
- Demonstrated before the fix, against #3726's code: a squatter on 127.0.0.1 without STARTTLS received the (fake) bridge password; a late `/approve` to card A approved card B

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
New channel: Proton Mail via a local Proton Mail Bridge (`/add-proton-mail`). Native IMAP/SMTP adapter; mail counts as from its sender only on Proton's DMARC pass, and approval cards are answered by replying to the card email itself.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- Inbound email is untrusted. For outside mail, sender identity rests on Proton's DMARC verdict, which is domain-level, so the owner's domain must stop its users sending as each other. This covers ordinary chat and `/` admin commands as well as cards: someone who can get a DMARC-aligned pass for the owner's domain (a shared ESP in its SPF record, a relay that doesn't enforce From) can write as the owner. Only card answers carry the extra token. An owner who writes from a Proton address is identified by mailbox, not by domain (below). For Proton-to-Proton mail it rests on Proton's `X-Pm-Origin: internal`, which means Proton authenticated the sending account; anyone with a free Proton account is therefore verified as their own address, and unknown senders still go through the approval card. Approvals additionally need the per-card token, so only someone who can read the approver's mailbox can answer.
- Attachments from a sender who is not yet approved are held back, so a stranger cannot park large events in `pending_channel_approvals`.
- Credentials: the bridge password is read from `.env` only; IMAP requires STARTTLS and SMTP requires TLS; Bridge's certificate is pinned when `PROTON_MAIL_TLS_CA_FILE` is set (the skill sets it).
- Attachment filenames pass `isSafeAttachmentName`; bodies are capped at 50k characters; bounces, auto-replies, mailing lists and mail from the Bridge account's own address are dropped before the router.
- Deps pinned exactly — `imapflow@1.7.8`, `mailparser@3.9.47`, `nodemailer@10.1.7` (past the addressparser advisories below 10.1.4), `@types/mailparser@3.4.6`, `@types/nodemailer@8.0.1` — all past the 3-day `minimumReleaseAge`; no build-script approvals added.

## Skill delivery

- [ ] Not a skill
- [x] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

Code for the `/add-proton-mail` skill in #3726, which copies the four `src/channels/proton-mail*` files from this branch and appends the barrel line.

Long `ask_question` option lists no longer lose their tail on Telegram and Discord.

prs.title: fix(telegram): give the getUpdates long poll a client-side deadline
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->
## Summary

Telegram inbound no longer stalls for ~15 minutes after a network change.

- **Problem**: `@chat-adapter/telegram` long-polls `getUpdates` with no client-side timeout. On a black-holed connection (no RST, e.g. after a Wi-Fi/NAT change) the request hangs until the kernel gives up on retransmits. No inbound message arrives meanwhile, while outbound keeps working on fresh sockets.
- **Fix**: `installPollDeadline` wraps the adapter instance's `telegramFetch`: `getUpdates` is aborted after its long-poll `timeout` + 30 s and fails with a plain error, so the poll loop backs off and retries. Every other Bot API method is untouched.
- **Scope guard**: an abort the adapter itself requests (polling stopped) still surfaces as `AbortError`. If a future adapter drops `telegramFetch`, the bridge logs a warning and polls as before.

## Related work

No issue; seen on a live install on 2026-10-03 (inbound dead for ~20 min, `ss` showed the getUpdates socket stuck with unacked data). Carried as a local patch since.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- New `src/channels/telegram-poll-deadline.test.ts`: a hung poll becomes a retryable error after 60 s (fake timers); an outer abort still stops cleanly; other methods pass through; installs on a real adapter instance -> 5 passed
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`: no new errors vs. `channels` HEAD (28 pre-existing, none in the touched files)
- `vitest run src/channels/telegram*`: 7 pre-existing failures on this host, identical without the change (better-sqlite3 11.10 does not build on Node 26)

## User and release impact

Telegram: a dead long-poll connection is now detected within ~60 s instead of stalling incoming messages for up to 15 minutes.

prs.title: fix(delivery): tell the agent when a message permanently fails to deliver
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->
## Summary

The agent is told when one of its messages permanently fails to deliver, instead of believing it was sent.

- **Problem**: after `MAX_DELIVERY_ATTEMPTS` the delivery loop only marks the outbound row failed in the session DB. Nothing reaches the agent, so it reports the message as sent ("sent — check the DM") while the user never sees it. Seen with a file Slack rejected with `missing_scope`.
- **Fix**: `noticeDeliveryFailure` sends a system note through `notifyAgent` (id `delivery-failed-<msg id>`; names the files/text, a fixed reason category and the message id for the host log) and wakes the container. Called once, right after `markDeliveryFailed`. The note tells the agent not to resend to that destination.
- **Reason categories**: not connected (unknown/detached messaging group, no adapter, no a2a module), rejected by the platform, not authorised, other. Host-side causes throw `DeliveryTargetError`; `MissingChannelAdapterError` maps to not connected.
- **Bounds**: no note when the failed message answers a delivery-failure note (`in_reply_to` starts with `delivery-failed-`); at most 3 notes per session and destination within 10 minutes (in memory, resets on restart), the rest are logged as suppressed.
- **Scope guard**: `system` and `task_log` rows get no note; a failure to write the note is logged and never breaks the delivery loop.

## Related work

No issue; carried as a local patch on a live install since 2026-10-01.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `src/delivery-failure-notice.test.ts`: text names files, text, reason category and log pointer; truncation; error classification; system/task_log rows and replies to a note are skipped -> pass
- `src/delivery.test.ts`: permanent failure writes the note without the remote error text; new test drives repeated failures on one destination (a reply to the note gets none, then notes stop at the cap) -> pass. Both bounds mutation-checked (removing either makes the test fail).
- Full host suite: 2157 passed; 3 failures in `src/cli/stdin-json*` fail identically on current `main` (Node 26 environment)
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` -> clean
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
When a message can't be delivered after all retries, the agent now gets a note saying so and the reason category, instead of assuming it was sent.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- The note is written as `sender: 'system'` into the same session's own inbound mailbox only.
- Remote platform error text never enters the note (it could carry attacker-influenced text into a system-voice message); only a fixed category and the outbound message id. The full error stays in the host log.
- Notes can't amplify: replies to a note get none, and each destination is capped at 3 notes per 10 minutes per session, so a permanently failing destination can't drive an unbounded wake loop.

## Skill delivery

- [x] Not a skill
- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

prs.title: feat(skills): add /add-lancedb-memory (hybrid vector + BM25 memory via MCP)
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Adds `/add-lancedb-memory`: opt-in, per-group long-term memory with hybrid (vector + BM25) recall, delivered as a skill with zero core edits.

- **Problem**: the built-in file memory suits curated notes, not many small facts. Agents can't find those again by meaning or keyword.
- **Fix**: a ~220-line stdio MCP server wraps the store, embedder and hybrid retriever of [memory-lancedb-pro](https://github.com/CortexReach/memory-lancedb-pro). It exposes six tools: `memory_recall`, `memory_store`, `memory_update`, `memory_forget`, `memory_list` and `memory_stats`.
- **Delivery**:
  - The server runs from `/app/src`, so it uses the agent-runner's own MCP SDK and zod.
  - The library is installed per group with `ncl groups config add-package`, so the base image is unchanged.
  - Registration is `ncl groups config add-mcp-server`.
  - Data lives in `/workspace/agent/lancedb-memory/`, per group, next to the file memory, which it does not replace.
- **Credentials**: the embedding key goes through the gateway (OneCLI grant per group, following `/add-tavily-tool`). `--env` carries only `EMBEDDING_API_KEY: "placeholder"`.
- **Out of scope**: reranking, auto-capture, and the library's other OpenClaw plugin features. Only `store`/`embedder`/`retriever` are imported; the library's OpenClaw-coupled `tools.ts` is never loaded.

<details><summary>Notes for reviewers</summary>

- `memory-lancedb-pro@1.1.0-beta.9` (npm) ships TypeScript sources only. Bun runs them directly.
- Its `package.json` declares MIT, but the GitHub repo has no `LICENSE` file. SKILL.md says so.
- The server finds the library under `$PNPM_HOME/global/*/node_modules`. `pnpm root -g` fails for the `node` user because corepack wants to download into root-owned `/pnpm/bin`.
- The library loads lazily. The server always boots, and a missing package becomes a tool error that names the fix.
- The skill-pins scanner does not see the `ncl … add-package --npm memory-lancedb-pro@1.1.0-beta.9` pin, so Dependabot will not track it. Fixing that is a core scanner change, left out of this PR.
- Concurrent sessions of one group share a single LanceDB directory.

</details>

## Related work

Supersedes #1283 (and #1043 before it). Those were v1-era PRs that vendored ~40 library files into the agent-runner and replaced `memory.ts`. This PR is a rewrite for v2's skill model. No issue exists, and the change is a self-contained skill that touches no core file.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [x] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `bun test src/lancedb-memory-mcp.test.ts` (skill applied) -> 3 pass. The store/recall case skips without the library.
- Same test with `LANCEDB_MEMORY_LIB` pointing at the unpacked npm package -> 3 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun test --isolate` (full container suite, skill applied) -> 630 pass, 4 skip, 0 fail.
- `pnpm exec tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json --noEmit` (skill applied) -> clean.
- `pnpm run build` -> clean.
- `pnpm test` -> 4250 pass, 1 fail. The failure is `setup/service-nohup.test.ts` (`spawnSync script ENOENT`: the `script` binary is missing on the dev box), unrelated.
- `pnpm exec tsx scripts/skill-directives.ts .claude/skills/add-lancedb-memory/SKILL.md` -> no findings.
- `pnpm run skill-pins:check` -> passes.
- Container probe -> lists tools, store, recall (correct hit) and stats all work:
  - Built `./container/build.sh`, then a derived image the way `buildAgentGroupImage` does it (`pnpm install -g memory-lancedb-pro@1.1.0-beta.9`). This installs `@lancedb/lancedb-linux-x64-gnu`.
  - Ran `bun /app/src/lancedb-memory-mcp.ts` as `node` against a fake embedding endpoint.
  - The shipped test inside the container -> 3/3.
- Base image without the package -> server boots, and tools return the "could not be loaded … add-package" error.
- Apply twice -> idempotent. REMOVE.md file steps twice -> clean tree.
- Not covered:
  - A live-host `ncl` add-package / add-mcp-server / restart flow (no host on the dev box).
  - Gateway key injection end to end.
  - arm64.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not). The `ncl` registration is runtime state with no in-tree line to guard; SKILL.md states this, as `docs/skill-guidelines.md` asks.

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
New `/add-lancedb-memory` skill: opt-in per-group long-term memory with hybrid vector + keyword recall, as an MCP server.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

- **Credentials**: embedding API keys are injected by the credential gateway per group. Only the literal `placeholder` is stored in the container config.
- **Third-party code**: `memory-lancedb-pro@1.1.0-beta.9` and its dependencies run inside opted-in groups' containers. They are installed via the existing per-group `add-package` path, which is approval-gated, pinned to the exact top-level version, and leaves transitive dependencies on ranges.
- **Agent-written data**: memories are stored per group in that group's folder. No cross-group access.
- **Recall results**: the agent-facing skill tells the agent to treat them as notes, not instructions.

## Skill delivery

- [ ] Not a skill
- [x] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

## AI assistance

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change

- [ ] A human has reviewed this PR and stands behind every change

prs.title: skill: upgrade memory to memory-lancedb-pro (hybrid BM25+vector retrieval)
prs.body:
## Why

The basic `memory.ts` only does vector (cosine) search. Keyword-heavy queries miss relevant memories, and there is no reranking, recency weighting, or noise filtering.

## What this adds

Replaces `memory.ts` with [memory-lancedb-pro](https://github.com/CortexReach/memory-lancedb-pro) (MIT):

- **Hybrid retrieval**: vector + BM25 full-text, RRF fusion
- **Cross-encoder reranking** (Jina / custom endpoint, optional)
- **Recency boost** — newer memories score higher (14-day half-life)
- **Importance weighting** — high-importance memories surface first
- **Time decay** — old entries gradually deprioritized
- **MMR diversity** — prevents near-duplicate results
- **Noise filtering** — ignores greetings, refusals, low-quality content
- **Adaptive retrieval** — skips lookup for simple confirmations/slash commands

## Embedding providers

Configured via `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER` env var (default: `gemini`):

| Provider | Model | Base URL | Dimensions |
|----------|-------|----------|------------|
| `gemini` (default) | gemini-embedding-001 | googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/ | 3072 |
| `jina` | jina-embeddings-v5-text-small | api.jina.ai/v1 | 1024 |
| `openai` | text-embedding-3-small | api.openai.com/v1 | 1536 |
| `ollama` | nomic-embed-text | localhost:11434/v1 | 768 |
| `custom` | (set `EMBEDDING_MODEL`) | (set `EMBEDDING_BASE_URL`) | (set `EMBEDDING_DIM`) |

All overridable via `EMBEDDING_API_KEY`, `EMBEDDING_MODEL`, `EMBEDDING_BASE_URL`, `EMBEDDING_DIM`.

## Rerank providers

Configured via `RERANK_PROVIDER` env var (default: disabled):

| Provider | Model | Endpoint |
|----------|-------|----------|
| `jina` | jina-reranker-v3 | api.jina.ai/v1/rerank |
| `siliconflow` | BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 | api.siliconflow.com/v1/rerank |
| `voyage` | rerank-2.5 | api.voyageai.com/v1/rerank |
| `pinecone` | bge-reranker-v2-m3 | api.pinecone.io/rerank |
| `vllm` | BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 | localhost:8000/v1/rerank |
| `none` | — | — |

All overridable via `RERANK_API_KEY`, `RERANK_MODEL`, `RERANK_ENDPOINT`.

## New files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `memory-store.ts` | LanceDB storage layer with multi-scope support |
| `memory-retriever.ts` | Hybrid retrieval: vector + BM25, score fusion, reranking |
| `memory-embedder.ts` | OpenAI-compatible embedding with chunking, caching, key rotation |
| `memory-chunker.ts` | Smart document chunking for long texts |
| `memory-access-tracker.ts` | Reinforcement-based time decay for access patterns |
| `memory-noise-filter.ts` | Filters trivial/low-quality content before storage |
| `memory-query-expander.ts` | Query expansion stub (pass-through) |

## Public API

Unchanged — `memoryStore`, `memorySearch`, `memoryDelete`, `memoryCount` keep the same signatures. Drop-in replacement.

## Build fixes

- `--legacy-peer-deps` in Dockerfile: `openai@4` peer-wants `zod@3`, but `claude-agent-sdk` requires `zod@4` (optional peer dep, safe to skip)
- Fixed import paths, type casts for LanceDB API, added missing `provider` field
- `container-runner.ts` forwards all embedding/rerank env vars to containers

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` + `npx tsc --noEmit` compile cleanly (host + container)
- [x] Container image builds successfully
- [x] `memoryStore` / `memorySearch` / `memoryDelete` / `memoryCount` work end-to-end
- [x] Existing memories remain accessible (same LanceDB table schema)
- [ ] Verify Jina / OpenAI / Ollama embedding providers with live keys
- [ ] Verify reranking with Jina / SiliconFlow

prs.title: feat(release): add codown SVN publish workflow
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds release tooling that builds signed installers and submits them to the internal SVN drop used by Codown. Deployment stays manual: the scripts print the ticket URL and the public download URLs, and never open a browser or create a ticket.

## New commands

- **`npm run release:codown -- --target <target> [--keyfrom <channel>] [--silent] [--dry-run]`**
  - Targets: `mac-arm64`, `mac-x64`, `mac-universal`, `win-channel`, `win-web`, `linux-x64`. Each target must be built on its native host.
  - Checks signing credentials and the SVN working copy before building.
  - Builds into an isolated, locked `.work/codown-build-*` directory, then verifies signatures (Authenticode on Windows, `codesign` + `stapler` on macOS).
  - Stages renamed artifacts with size and sha256 in `release/codown/<keyfrom>/<version>/<target>/manifest.json`, then submits them to SVN.
- **`npm run codown:publish -- --manifest <path> [--dry-run]`**: retries SVN submission from an existing snapshot without rebuilding.
- **`npm run codown:verify -- --manifest <path>`**: after manual deployment, downloads every artifact from the public URL and checks its size and sha256.

## Changes to existing scripts

- **`dist-win-web.cjs`**: new `--codown` mode. It bakes the final `.nsis.7z` URL (from `CODOWN_PUBLIC_BASE_URL`) into the web installer, so the build takes one pass instead of upload-then-stub-rebuild.
- **`build-env.cjs` / `electron-builder-config.cjs`**: new `LOBSTERAI_BUILD_OUTPUT_DIR` overrides the electron-builder output directory. Without it, the output directory is unchanged.
- **`.env.example`**: documents the six optional `CODOWN_*` settings. Real URLs and paths stay in `.env` or CI secrets.

## Safety

- SVN credentials are removed from the build subprocess environment. The password goes through stdin with `--no-auth-cache` and is redacted from error output.
- Refuses to overwrite an SVN file that already exists with different bytes; identical files are reused.
- Refuses to publish from a dirty working copy, or when the working copy changes during publication.
- On failure, reverts only the files this run added. Committed nodes are left alone.
- Lock directories prevent concurrent builds and concurrent publishers.

## Electron-specific notes

- Build and release scripts only. No app runtime, IPC, preload, storage, or OpenClaw config changes.
- Existing `dist:*` commands behave the same unless `--codown` or `LOBSTERAI_BUILD_OUTPUT_DIR` is set.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run tests/codownPublish.test.ts tests/channelInstallPolicy.test.ts`: 37 passed.
- `npm test`: 759 files, 8167 tests passed (177 skipped).
- ESLint (CI rules) on the changed test files: clean.
- Not verified end-to-end against the internal SVN drop and Codown deployment as part of this PR.

prs.title: fix(media): stop media intent recovery from blocking the main thread
prs.body:
## Summary

Typing in the prompt input and scrolling the session history sidebar stuttered every ~15s.

Root cause: the `media.intents.v2` kv row stored every generation request body inline, including base64 images, and was never pruned. On an affected machine it was **222MB**. `recoverMediaTasks` runs every 15s on the Electron main thread and read and `JSON.parse`d this row each time. That blocked the main thread for about 0.6–1.4s per tick, which freezes input in all windows. Each `saveIntent` paid this cost twice, because `SqliteStore.set` also re-read the old value.

## Changes

- **`mediaTaskStore.ts`**
  - The intent index keeps only metadata and a `requestBodySha256`. Bodies live under `media.intentBody.v1:<key>`.
  - A body is kept only while the intent can still be resubmitted: no `taskId`, not rejected, and within 24h. Otherwise it is deleted.
  - Settled intents stay in the index for 7 days, so a replayed tool call keeps its idempotency key. A replay with a different payload still throws.
  - Legacy records with inline bodies are migrated automatically.
- **`main.ts`**
  - The request body is serialized once, and the bytes sent are unchanged.
  - Recovery loads the body only when it actually resubmits. If the body is missing, the intent is marked rejected.
  - The index is compacted once at startup, before `createWindow()`.
- **`coworkStore.ts`**: adds `sessionExists()` for the recovery loop. `getSession()` also loaded a page of messages for every intent.
- **`sqliteStore.ts`**: `set`/`delete` read the old value only when the key has a change listener. Behavior is unchanged for watched keys.

## Measurements

On a copy of the affected database:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `media.intents.v2` size | 212MB | 32KB |
| `intents()` per recovery tick | 0.6–1.4s | ~0.1ms |
| One-time migration | — | 1.2s, at startup, before the window opens |

Tested in the app: input and sidebar lag is gone after the migration.

## Electron-specific notes

- **Storage**: there is a one-time, irreversible kv migration. Inline request bodies of settled or expired intents are dropped, and new `media.intentBody.v1:*` keys are added. The SQLite file does not shrink without `VACUUM`, but freed pages are reused.
- No IPC, preload, or OpenClaw config changes.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run src/main/libs/mediaTaskStore.test.ts src/main/sqliteStore.test.ts`: 19 passed. New cases cover body separation, cleanup after settle and expiry, legacy migration, and watched-key old values.
- ESLint, with the CI rules, is clean on all touched files.
- `npm run compile:electron` passes.
- In the full `npm test` run, the only failures are 4 existing `openclawPatches` failures that also fail on the base branch, and 1 load-related `skillManager.watcher` flake that passes when run alone.


## CI fix: Excel editor license check (separate commit)

`Electron Verify` failed in `scripts/sheet-third-party-notices.cjs`, and the failure is unrelated to the media change. Cause: `tslib` 2.9.1 was published on 2026-10-30. `rxjs` is a direct dependency, and its `tslib` range was not covered by the `@univerjs/design` override. CI installs without a lockfile, so it pulled 2.9.1 into the Excel editor graph, and `NOTICE.txt` no longer matched.

Fix: add `overrides.rxjs.tslib = 2.8.1`. A fresh lockfile-less resolution was checked: the Excel graph resolves to exactly the 139 packages in `resources/sheet-licenses/manifest.json`. Other PRs into this release branch will hit the same failure until this lands.

prs.title: feat(desktop): add custom and animated GIF companion skins, screenshot tools and follow-ups
prs.body:
## Summary
Add portable desktop customization and interaction improvements while preserving LobsterAI's built-in skins and branding.

- **Custom companion skins:** upload PNG/JPEG/WebP or animated GIF, preview, save multiple named skins, switch, rename/delete, and restore the default. Static images support scale/position adjustments and normalize to 512×512 PNG. GIFs retain their original frames, timing, transparency, loop metadata and aspect ratio in previews and on the desktop; static crop controls are hidden for GIFs.
- **Cowork follow-up suggestions:** show one contextual suggestion after a completed reply. Tab inserts an editable draft and Escape dismisses it; it never auto-sends. Requests use existing model configuration, a 10-second timeout, scoped caching and stale-response protection.
- **Screenshot tools:** adjust the region, annotate shapes/arrows/pen/mosaic/text, undo, copy, save, ask LobsterAI, extract text or translate. Independent Cowork tasks preserve the unsent composer draft and provide retry after failure.

## Electron-specific behavior
- Custom images stay in the local profile under content-hash filenames. Static formats accept uploads up to 5 MB; GIFs up to 2 MB, with each dimension between 128 and 2048 pixels. Validate GIF structure, frame bounds, byte limits, file ownership and content hash before restoration. Preserve GIF bytes instead of flattening through canvas or Electron nativeImage.
- Keep sandboxing and main-frame/sender checks; only the main settings window can mutate skins. Existing PNG profiles remain compatible. The desktop image element stays mounted across task mood changes.
- Keep per-display screenshot capture and explicit crop approval. Add preload bridges for local skin management, isolated screenshot tasks and suggestions.
- No server API, database migration, bundled runtime change, billing or private cloud image-generation dependency.

## Validation
- GIF follow-up: **166 tests passed across 5 files**, covering local persistence/restoration/deletion, malformed and oversized GIFs, forged types, symlinks, unchanged animation bytes, editor behavior, stable desktop image mounting and companion manager regressions.
- Renderer TypeScript (`tsc --noEmit`), Electron compilation, production build and changed-file ESLint (zero warnings): passed. `git diff --check`: passed.
- Windows Electron 43.5.0 component smoke: real upload decoding, animated editor preview, original-byte apply callback and desktop character playback passed. Captured two distinct rendered animation frames. The fixture mounts the actual editor and character components; it does not exercise the full app IPC/window lifecycle.
- Earlier base contribution: 241 focused tests passed, 1 macOS-only test skipped, plus renderer/main type checks, lint and production build.

## Screenshot
Actual Electron component smoke using a generated two-frame fixture:

![Custom GIF preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alison-xx/LobsterAI/feat/companion-customization-cowork-suggestions/specs/features/desktop-companion/custom-gif-preview.png)

## Remaining manual coverage
Full-app native file-picker/IPC roundtrip, restart across actual profile sessions, multi-monitor/DPI behavior, OS clipboard/save dialogs, and live-model OCR/translation/suggestions still need manual desktop acceptance. The component smoke and automated tests do not claim that coverage.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): keep tool payloads unmasked in transcripts for cache replay
prs.body:
## Summary
Users reported much faster credit use after upgrading. Follow-ups on heavy code-reading sessions read only about 15% of their prompt from the provider cache. OpenClaw v2026.8.1 masks secret-shaped text only in the persisted transcript copy, and the bare AWS secret pattern also matches 40-character relative paths. The next turn therefore replays different bytes than the previous request and loses the prefix cache from the first masked string onward.

## Changes Made
- Add `openclaw-tool-payload-transcript-fidelity.patch`, backporting the agents half of upstream OpenClaw #169063 (`f956a18741`). Tool arguments, tool results and conversation text are persisted and emitted as live tool events exactly as the model saw them. Logging, diagnostic, telemetry and config redaction, image payload stripping and persisted detail size caps are kept.
- Add a strong apply validator, README notes with verification and removal conditions, and patch contract tests.
- Add log-only TokenProxy prompt-prefix diagnostics: each model request is fingerprinted by hashes and compared with the previous request of the same session. The log line reports the first changed component, the stable prefix bytes and the cached tokens. It carries no message text.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Testing
- [x] OpenClaw: 35 related test files, 1301 tests passed. The new 40-character path regression fails without the source change.
- [x] The official patch script reapplies all 73 patches from a clean tag, and the result matches the tested tree byte for byte.
- [x] LobsterAI: `npm test -- openclawPatches openclawReplay patch` (149 tests) and the TokenProxy/diagnostics tests (71 tests) passed. Changed-file ESLint is clean.
- [x] Rebuilt the runtime and ran the scheduled-task audit task plus follow-ups (external account, deepseek-flash). Every follow-up's first request was a clean `change=append` with 99–100% cached tokens, and completed follow-up turns hit 98.6–99.6% cache overall.
- OpenClaw core tsgo reports existing errors only in three untracked files from other patches; the files changed here are clean.
- The server returned intermittent `500` errors during the check (serverTrace `0336c125`, `185d1115`, `300cee7a` and others). They are unrelated to this change; the server team should look into them.

## Electron-Specific Changes
- OpenClaw runtime patch: the runtime must be rebuilt (`npm run openclaw:runtime:host`) for the change to take effect.
- Behavior: secrets read by tools are now stored unmasked in local transcripts and live tool events, matching what was already sent to the model. Logs stay masked. Transcripts written before the upgrade keep their masked text, so the first follow-up after upgrading misses the cache once.
- The diagnostic adds one log line of about 320 bytes per model request (routine steps at debug level). Memory is bounded at 64 sessions × 4 lineages.

prs.title: fix(mcp): trust system CA store for stdio MCP servers
prs.body:
## 背景

Fixes #2906

OpenClaw 出于 stdio 启动安全策略会丢弃 MCP server env 中的 `NODE_OPTIONS`（`blockedEverywhereKeys`），用户原本用来让 Node 信任系统根证书的 `NODE_OPTIONS=--use-system-ca` 因此失效。在企业 MITM 代理或本机 TLS 拦截（Steam++、Zscaler、Netskope 等）环境下，Node 型 stdio MCP server 的所有请求都会报 `fetch failed`，而 UI 上没有任何提示。

已用打包的 OpenClaw runtime（v2026.8.1）实测：`NODE_OPTIONS` 被丢弃，`NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA` 会被保留。

## 改动

- 在共享的 MCP 启动 env（`buildMcpShimEnv`）中默认设置 `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1`。该变量与 `--use-system-ca` 效果相同（Node.js 22.19+），且不在 OpenClaw 黑名单中。
  - 写入 openclaw.json 的配置和设置页「获取工具列表」走同一函数，两边行为一致。
  - 用户显式设置的值（如 `0`）优先；Windows 上按不区分大小写匹配。
  - 只是额外信任系统证书库，内置 Mozilla 根证书照常保留，并非关闭证书校验。更旧的 Node 会忽略该变量，无副作用。
- MCP server 表单中填写 `NODE_OPTIONS` 时显示提示：该变量会被运行时忽略，系统证书已默认信任，额外 CA 请使用 `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`（中英文 i18n）。
- 新增单元测试，并覆盖托管/原始两种启动路径及运行时/工具发现两侧。

未采用 patch OpenClaw 放行 `NODE_OPTIONS` 的方案：`NODE_OPTIONS` 可加载任意代码（`--require`、`--import` 等），而 `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA` 已能达到同样效果。

## 行为影响

- 升级后首次启动，每个 stdio MCP server 在 openclaw.json 中的 env 会多出 `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA`，触发一次配置同步。
- issue 中 `web_fetch` 的 `blocked URL fetch ... private/internal IP` 日志来自 OpenClaw 的 SSRF 防护（hosts 将域名指向 127.0.0.1），属于设计行为，不在本 PR 范围内。

## 验证

- 改动文件 ESLint 无报错；`npm run compile:electron`、`npm run build` 通过。
- 相关 Vitest 通过。全量 `npm test` 中 3 个 `openclawPatches/*` 用例在基线上同样失败（检查本地 `../openclaw` 源码是否已打补丁），与本 PR 无关。
- 本机验证 `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` 在系统 Node 24.15 与 Electron 43 内置 Node 24.19（`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`）下均会加载系统证书。

prs.title: fix(mcp): harden OAuth sign-in cleanup and status refresh
prs.body:
Follow-up hardening for remote MCP OAuth sign-in (#2874, #2905).

## What changes

Every `openclaw mcp login|logout|status` call now runs against a **temporary openclaw.json** that lists only the servers involved, next to the gateway's real `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`. The entries come from the same `buildOpenClawMcpServers` that config sync uses (now exported). OpenClaw keys stored tokens by server name + sha256(name, URL), not by config file, so the CLI and the gateway still share the same tokens.

1. **Orphaned tokens on deleting a disabled OAuth server.** Delete, rename and URL changes now sign out even when the server is disabled (not in the gateway's openclaw.json). Re-adding the same name + URL no longer silently reuses old tokens.
2. **Misleading `server_not_loaded` right after save.** Sign-in no longer syncs the config first or checks the gateway's openclaw.json. It works while a config delivery is still pending on a busy gateway, and before a model is configured. The gateway picks up the token once its config lists the server. The now-unreachable "configure a model first" sign-in message is removed, and the sign-out "server not loaded" text now only covers disabled servers (zh + en).
3. **Disabling a server cancels its waiting sign-in.** `SetEnabled(false)` (and the registry variant) aborts the login controller, as delete does. This kills the CLI and frees 127.0.0.1:8989.
4. **No secrets for the CLI.** The temporary config references no `${VAR}` secrets and no plugins, so `getOAuthCliContext` no longer passes provider secrets. It also no longer calls `collectSecretEnvVars()`, which logged one line per provider on every CLI call.
5. **Refresh OAuth status on window focus** while the MCP page is open. It reads once per focus and never polls. Focus events during a read are skipped, and when reads overlap, a later-started read always wins.

The temporary config lives in a private temp dir (`lobsterai-mcp-oauth-*`, 0700/0600, since entries may carry other request headers). It is removed after each call. Dirs left behind by a crashed app are swept once per process. On a normal quit the cleanup already finishes, because `runAppCleanup` awaits several steps after cancelling logins.

Electron-specific behaviour: no IPC channel, storage or gateway restart changes. OAuth IPC handlers no longer trigger an OpenClaw config sync before login/logout. The design doc is updated.

## Verification

- `npm test -- mcpOAuthCli mcpStore`: 30 passed. `npm test -- mcp openclawConfigSync`: 319 passed.
- `npm run compile:electron`, renderer `tsc --noEmit`, and the CI ESLint command on all touched files pass.
- **End to end against the real bundled OpenClaw v2026.8.1 CLI.** The IPC handlers, McpStore and CLI driver are real. Electron is mocked only for `ipcMain`/`shell`, and a local mock OAuth 2.1 + MCP server stands in for the browser and the provider. The config sync stub never writes the server into the gateway config:

prs.title: fix(openclaw): let managed workspaces follow a relinked target
prs.body:
## Summary

A macOS user reported that every main-agent message failed with `workspace path alias points to a different current target`. Their logs show the cause: the user keeps the agent workspace in OneDrive, so the agent replaced `openclaw/state/workspace-main` with a link to the OneDrive folder. OpenClaw v2026.8.1 had already recorded the original real path in `workspace_path_aliases`. Once the path resolved somewhere else, it refused every message, including heartbeat runs, until the database was edited by hand. This happened twice: on 10-17, and on 10-18 after a data-migration restore, which skips links, put the empty template back and the agent linked it again.

## Changes

- **OpenClaw patch** `scripts/patches/v2026.8.1/openclaw-managed-workspace-alias-follow.patch` (changes only `src/agents/workspace-state-store.ts`, plus tests). It applies to workspace paths strictly below `LOBSTERAI_MANAGED_WORKSPACE_ROOT` that still exist. For those paths:
  - Alias rows pointing at an older target are ignored, and the current target's own records are used.
  - The next state write repoints the stale rows and logs a `workspace` warning naming both paths.
  - The previous target's records are left in place, not moved. Moving its file attestation would make OpenClaw report the linked folder as vanished.

  Missing paths keep their stored owner, so vanished-workspace protection is unchanged. Other paths, and processes without the variable, keep upstream's fail-closed behavior. Upstream #133198 (v2026.9.4) only improves the error and adds a confirmed `doctor --fix` rebind, so the README says to keep an equivalent of this patch after upgrading.
- **Environment:** the Gateway and the startup compatibility/repair helper now set the variable to the OpenClaw state directory (`OPENCLAW_MANAGED_WORKSPACE_ROOT_ENV` in `src/shared/openclawEngine/constants.ts`).
- **Error message:** the remaining alias errors map to `coworkErrorWorkspaceAliasRepointed`, with zh/en text in both the renderer and main-process i18n.
- **Patch bookkeeping:** a strong validator in `apply-openclaw-patches.cjs`, a README section, the patch added to the reviewed v2026.8.1 patch list, and a patch-content test that keeps the variable name in sync.

## Electron-specific behavior

- Adds one environment variable to the OpenClaw Gateway process and to the startup compatibility/repair helper processes.
- No IPC, storage schema, or config changes. The OpenClaw runtime must be rebuilt to pick up the patch.

## Testing

- All 67 v2026.8.1 patches apply to a clean tag checkout, and strong validation passes.
- OpenClaw: 8 new cases (6 store, 2 end-to-end through `ensureAgentWorkspace`). The end-to-end case relinks a seeded workspace to a "synced" folder that already holds agent files; messages succeed and no `BOOTSTRAP.md` is created. The control case without the variable reproduces the reported error. The 37 related workspace and migration test files (495 tests) pass, and `tsgo` core has 0 errors.
- LobsterAI: the full `npm test` run passes (7421 tests), targeted tests pass again after rebasing on the latest release branch, ESLint is clean on changed files, and `compile:electron` passes.
- **Not yet done:** in-app validation with a rebuilt runtime. Steps: initialize the main agent, quit, replace `openclaw/state/workspace-main` with a link to a folder that already holds agent files, and restart. Messages must succeed, the linked folder must not get a `BOOTSTRAP.md`, and the Gateway log must show `Workspace path alias now follows its current target.` once.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): stop restarting the gateway right after it starts
prs.body:
## Summary

User logs (Windows, 2026.10.16) show the gateway starting **twice on every launch**: it boots once, and as soon as it is ready `ensureRunning:config-confirm` hard-restarts it. All 7 launches in the logs reproduce it. The second boot adds 100–280s to every launch.

### Root cause
1. **Trigger:** `runStartupCacheWarmup` cached `/api/models/available` without the derived `presetContextWindows`, but `loadAvailableServerModels` adds them. So the renderer's first `getModels` always reported `metadataChanged=true`, and the rendered `models` gained `contextWindows`/`contextWindowDefault` while the gateway was still starting.
2. **Escalation:** a starting gateway owns its config file, so the change was deferred. `executeDeferredGatewayRestart` always synced with `restartGatewayIfRunning: true` + `expectedImpact: Restart`. Because the target can't be persisted during startup, `configChanged` stayed true, which re-armed a respawn demand on the generation that was still booting. The sync also re-ran every 3s while the gateway was starting (35 runs, ~18s of main-process CPU in one launch).
3. **Restart:** once the gateway was ready, `ensureRunning:config-confirm` saw the pending respawn and hard-restarted it (6s shutdown timeout → SIGKILL → ~8s prep → ~90s boot). A model-list change only needs a hot `config.apply`.

### Changes
- **Model metadata:** new `updateServerModelMetadataFromResponse()` in `claudeSettings.ts`, used by both the startup warmup and `loadAvailableServerModels`, so an identical response is treated as unchanged and no startup config sync happens.
- **Deferred restart:** the deferred state now records whether a respawn was actually requested.
  - A change deferred because the gateway is not running, and that asks for no respawn itself, is only reapplied once the gateway is up (via the existing `config-confirm` / gateway-ready reconcile).
  - Deferred polls skip while the engine phase is `starting`.
  - Real restart demands (env, bindings, plugin impact, explicit IM restart, deferrals while busy) keep their previous behavior.
- **Startup prep:** an enabled `nsp-clawguard` forces the pre-spawn compatibility helpers only when a supported payload exists under `third-party-extensions` (the only case its install repair acts on). An unsupported (e.g. 2.5.8) or removed package now uses the existing startup-prep marker instead of rerunning both helpers (~8–9s) on every gateway start.

### Electron / OpenClaw behavior changes
- OpenClaw config/restart: model-list changes that arrive while the gateway is starting are hot-applied after ready instead of triggering a gateway respawn.
- No IPC, storage, or UI changes.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test` (7929 passed before rebase; targeted suites re-run after rebasing onto the latest `release/2026.10.19`)
- [x] New regression test: a startup-warmed cache stays unchanged for the same `/api/models/available` response (fails on the old warmup code)
- [x] New tests for preset context window derivation and for nsp-clawguard startup-prep gating (supported / unsupported / missing payload)
- [x] `npx eslint --max-warnings 0` on touched files, `npm run compile:electron`
- [ ] Manual: cold start in `npm run electron:dev` while logged in. Expect a single `gateway process spawned`, no `HARD RESTART EXECUTING. reason=ensureRunning:config-confirm`, and `server model metadata unchanged, skipping config sync` on the renderer's model fetch

prs.title: fix(dev): stop stale immutable Vite deps from blocking the dev renderer
prs.body:
## 背景
Vite 对预打包依赖使用 `?v=` hash 并标记为 `immutable`，re-optimize 后 hash 可能复用但 chunk 文件不同。Electron 的 HTTP 缓存（各 checkout 与多次启动共享）不会重新校验，导致渲染进程导入 dev server 已不存在的 chunk（404），页面无法挂载。

## 改动
- `vite.config.ts`：dev server 增加 `Cache-Control: no-cache`，每次加载按 ETag 校验，未变化返回 304。
- `developmentHttpCache.ts`（含测试）：开发模式下每个 userData 仅一次清理 dev server origin 的旧 HTTP 缓存，用 marker 文件标记，失败/超时不阻塞启动。
- `main.ts`：在创建窗口前等待清理完成。

## 注意
仅影响 dev 模式；首次清理可能耗时（~17s / ~4 万条缓存），之后不再重复。未运行测试。

prs.title: fix(desktop-companion): keep orb clicks from activating the main window on macOS
prs.body:
## Summary

On macOS, clicking the desktop companion orb while the LobsterAI main window was on screen but covered by another app could bring the main window to the front instead of opening the quick input panel. With the main window minimized, the panel opened normally. The expected behavior is that clicking the orb always opens only the quick input panel, whatever state the main window is in.

### Root cause

Electron's `type: 'panel'` on macOS only emulates a nonactivating panel; AppKit logs `NSWindow does not support nonactivating panel styleMask 0x80`. A real click on the non-focusable orb half-activates the app: WindowServer treats LobsterAI as frontmost, but no window keeps key status. The quick panel lost key focus about 40 ms after showing, the macOS focus watcher dismissed it about 250 ms later, and key focus could fall to the main window. Whether it failed depended on which app was in front; native apps and Claude reproduced it reliably.

### Changes

- **Orb is key-capable on macOS** (`desktopCompanionManager.showOrb`). A click then hands key focus over cleanly without activating the app, the same way the composer panel already does. Windows and Linux are unchanged.
- **Orb ignores `close` unless the manager is disposing.** Once the orb can be key, the default app menu's Cmd+W would otherwise close it. This uses the same pattern as the composer panel; quit runs `dispose()` first, so quitting is unaffected.
- **Dock restore uses `restore()` for a minimized main window** (`app.on('activate')`). `show()` on a minimized window draws it at full size for one frame before the Dock animation, which looked like a flash. This flash predates this PR.

## Verification

Verified on macOS 15.1 with real OS-level clicks (CGEvent), tracing window focus events, companion IPC and the on-screen window order:

| Scenario | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Main window covered by another app (native app, Claude, Calculator), click orb | Panel lost focus and closed; main window could take focus | Panel stays open and focused; main window untouched |
| Main window minimized, click orb | Inconsistent | Panel stays open and focused; main window not restored |
| Click Dock icon with main window minimized | Full-size frame flashes before the Dock animation | Animates straight out of the Dock, then takes focus |
| Orb focused, press Cmd+W | — | Orb stays |

- `tsc --noEmit` passes for the Electron project.
- ESLint is clean on both changed files.
- `vitest run src/main/desktopCompanion` passes (300 tests).

## Electron behavior notes

- **Windowing:** on macOS the orb can become the key window. After the quick panel closes, keyboard focus stays on the orb rather than returning to the previous app. Before this change, keystrokes at that point went nowhere.
- **Not reproduced:** a report that a first orb click sometimes made the panel vanish and needed a second click. It did not reproduce in a traced hands-on session or in 30+ replays after this change.

prs.title: feat(providers): refresh builtin default models
prs.body:
## Summary

Refreshes the builtin default model lists for DeepSeek, Moonshot, Qwen, Zhipu, MiniMax and Xiaomi so each provider lists its latest model first, and switches the global default model from the retired `deepseek-reasoner` to `deepseek-v4-flash`.

Only the system defaults change. Saved user configs are not migrated: existing provider model lists and the selected default model are left exactly as they are.

This replaces the approach in https://github.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI/pull/2859, which filtered still-served model IDs out of saved configs on every startup and reset default models across providers.

## Related Issue

N/A

## Changes Made

| Provider | New default list (first = default) | Moved to `legacyModels` |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek | `deepseek-v4-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro` | `deepseek-reasoner` (retired 2026-07-24) |
| Moonshot | `kimi-k3`, `kimi-k2.7-code`, `kimi-k2.6` | `kimi-k2.5` (sunset 2026-08-31) |
| Qwen | `qwen3.8-max`, `qwen3.7-plus`, `qwen3.8-flash` | `qwen3.6-plus`, `qwen3.5-plus` |
| Zhipu | `glm-5.3`, `glm-5.3-flash`, `glm-5.1` | `glm-5`, `glm-4.7` |
| MiniMax | `MiniMax-M3`, `MiniMax-M2.7`, `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` | `MiniMax-M2.5` |
| Xiaomi | `mimo-v2.6-pro`, `mimo-v2.5` | `mimo-v2.5-pro` |

- **`legacyModels`:** a new optional field on provider definitions. These models are no longer seeded into new configs, but `ProviderRegistry` still uses them for image / thinking / context-window lookups. Without it, saved entries that rely on registry metadata would silently change behavior, for example losing the `qwen3.6-plus` image-support repair or the `glm-5` thinking flag.
- **Runtime-supported IDs only:** every new default is a model the pinned OpenClaw runtime (v2026.8.1) already handles. Three newer IDs were left out on purpose:
  - `deepseek-flash`: OpenClaw's DeepSeek V4 thinking wrapper only matches `deepseek-v4-flash` / `deepseek-v4-pro`. DeepSeek still accepts `deepseek-v4-flash` and routes it to V4.1 Flash at the same price, so we can switch after an OpenClaw upgrade.
  - `mimo-v2.6-flash`: not in OpenClaw's `reasoning_content` replay list, so multi-turn tool calls could fail.
  - `glm-5.3-flashx`: not in OpenClaw's zai catalog.
- **`mimo-v2.6-pro` is marked `supportsImage: false`:** only third-party catalogs claim vision support so far.
- **Global default:** `defaultConfig.model.defaultModel` changes from `deepseek-reasoner` to `deepseek-v4-flash`.

Saved configs keep a snapshot of every provider's model list, including providers the user never enabled. So an existing user who enables one of these providers later still sees the old list; only new installs get the new lists. Letting never-configured providers (no API key, never enabled) follow the new defaults would be a small follow-up, but it writes to saved configs, so it is left out here.

prs.title: feat(openclaw): keep user overrides in openclaw.user.json across config syncs
prs.body:
## Summary
LobsterAI regenerates `openclaw.json` on every config sync, so users who hand-edit it (e.g. to enable enhancement plugins or tweak OpenClaw options) lose their changes on restart. Instead of a "protection" switch that freezes the file — which would stop model, IM, MCP, skill and agent changes from reaching the gateway and can break startup when ports or plugin paths change — this adds a persistent user override layer: `openclaw.user.json` next to `openclaw.json` is merged on top of every rendered config.

Merge order: LobsterAI-generated config → user overrides → enterprise config (enterprise still wins).

## Related Issue
User feedback: manual `openclaw.json` edits are reset after restart; request for a protection toggle.

## Changes Made
- **Override layer** (`src/main/libs/openclawUserConfigOverlay.ts`): JSON5 file (comments, trailing commas), JSON Merge Patch semantics (objects merge, arrays replace, `null` removes). `plugins.allow` / `plugins.load.paths` are unioned so users can't drop bundled plugins; `plugins.allow` stays sorted so repeated syncs are stable.
- **Protected paths** are ignored and reported: `gateway.auth/mode/port`, `meta`, `agents.defaults.sessionStore`, `plugins.installs`, `plugins.slots.memory`, LobsterAI-internal plugin entries, and `$include` anywhere.
- **Removal works**: the renderer copies existing `gateway`, `plugins.entries` and unknown top-level keys back from the file, so a deleted override would otherwise linger. The paths each sync applied are recorded (kv) and reverted from the base before the next render, only where the value is still what was applied. `createOpenClawConfigTarget` gains an optional merge base / extra owned sections; `baseRaw` stays the real file so the rebase propagates removals.
- **Fail-safe**: a syntax error keeps the last valid overrides. If OpenClaw rejects the config (`config.apply` → `Rejected`, or startup "Invalid config"), overrides are suspended and the config is retried without them (the gateway is restarted once on startup failure); if it still fails, overrides are restored and not blamed again. Quick Repair also suspends overrides until the user applies them again.
- **Settings card** in Agent Engine → 运行维护: enable toggle, state (missing / active / parse error / suspended / disabled), overridden and ignored paths, OpenClaw's rejection detail, Open File / Show in Folder / Apply. zh + en strings.
- **IPC**: `openclaw:userConfig:*` (constants in `src/shared/openclawUserConfig/constants.ts`), handlers in `src/main/ipcHandlers/openclawUserConfig/handlers.ts`, exposed as `window.electron.openclaw.userConfig`.
- `json5` added as a runtime dependency (was dev-only transitively). It's imported as `json5/lib/parse` because the package's ESM entry has only a default export, which broke the Vite-bundled main process with a named import.

## Type of Change
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Code refactoring
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Testing
- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [x] Manual testing performed

- `npm test`: 689 files / 7439 tests pass. New: `openclawUserConfigOverlay.test.ts` (19), two `OpenClawConfigSync` runtime tests through the real renderer (apply → steady state reports `changed: false` → removal → steady again; minimal no-model path), one `openclawConfigTarget` test.
- ESLint (CI command) clean on all touched files; `tsc --noEmit` for renderer and `electron-tsconfig.json` pass; `compile:electron` passes.
- End-to-end in `electron:dev` on an isolated profile (`LOBSTERAI_DEV_USER_DATA_DIR`), driven via CDP, both logged out and logged in (lobsterai-server provider): template creation, apply, survives restart, coexists with a managed setting change in the same `agents` section, removal across `agents` / `plugins.entries` / `gateway`, protected paths ignored, syntax error keeps last valid overrides, invalid key rejected while running (engine stays up), invalid key at cold start (gateway auto-restarts without overrides), toggle off/on, Quick Repair suspend + reapply, file deletion.

## Screenshots (if applicable)
Not attached. The card was checked in the dev app (dark theme) in active, ignored-paths, parse-error and suspended states.

With overrides, they become part of the target `OpenClawConfigSync` renders, so the existing change detection, `config.apply` delivery and restart decisions apply to them. prs.title: feat(providers): support OpenAI Responses and Gemini formats for custom providers
prs.body:
## Summary

Custom model providers can now use the **OpenAI Responses** and native **Gemini (generateContent)** API formats, on top of OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic. Both reuse OpenClaw's native transports instead of adding LobsterAI-side protocol code.

- **Settings UI:** the API format radio buttons become one dropdown. Custom providers list OpenAI Chat Completions, Anthropic, OpenAI Responses and Gemini; built-in providers keep Chat Completions and Anthropic only.
- **Storage:** Responses is a sub-mode, `ProviderConfig.openaiApiMode`, stored next to `apiFormat: 'openai'`. Older builds therefore fall back to Chat Completions. Gemini is stored as `apiFormat: 'gemini'` on custom providers only.
- **OpenClaw config sync:** Responses mode maps to the `openai-responses` transport (a pasted `/responses` suffix is stripped). Custom Gemini maps to `google-generative-ai`, with a versioned base URL that keeps relay path prefixes and adds `/v1beta` when no version is given.
- **Other callers follow the same choice:** the connection test (native `generateContent` probe for Gemini) and provider export/import, plus the compat proxy, legacy chat path and native Gemini clients for titles and quick answers.

### Why built-in providers don't get Responses yet

Several OpenClaw provider plugins are tuned for Chat Completions:

- The DeepSeek V4 and Xiaomi MiMo thinking wrappers inject Chat Completions fields regardless of transport. This is still true upstream in v2026.10.4.
- Moonshot's Kimi K3 runtime profile requires Chat Completions.
- Volcengine Ark rejects unknown Responses fields.

So the option is limited to custom providers for now.

## Electron-specific behavior

- **OpenClaw config:** changes only for custom providers set to Responses or Gemini. The gateway picks the new transport up through the normal config sync.
- **Provider export:** writes `openaiApiMode` only when it is Responses, so default exports stay importable by older builds with the strict schema.
- **Renderer config normalization:** keeps `apiFormat: 'gemini'` on custom providers. It used to coerce unknown formats to Anthropic.

## Testing

- `npm test`, CI eslint on touched files, `npm run compile:electron` and `npm run build` pass.
- Not yet checked in `npm run electron:dev`: the new dropdown, a Responses or Gemini custom provider (connection test and chat), and that built-in providers show only two options. No screenshots yet.

prs.title: feat(media): erase from a close-up and blend it back into the source
prs.body:
## Summary

Improves image Erase quality. Previously the full source and full mask were sent to the image model, so small marks were easy to miss and the model re-rendered unmarked areas too.

- Compute the marked area's bounds from the mask and send the model a close-up around it (3x the mark, min side 512, aspect ratio ≤ 2; falls back to the full image when the close-up would cover ≥ 60% of it). Private copies of the cropped source/mask are recorded in the new `ImageEditRequest.eraseCrop`.
- Blend the model output back into the immutable source locally (`imageEditingErase.ts`): the mask is grown and feathered, the patch's color drift is measured on preserved pixels and removed, and every pixel outside the feather stays untouched.
- Erase now shares the local-compose flow with background removal via `composesImageEditLocally()` (raw output downloaded privately, only the composed result is published).
- Erase uses its fixed prompt and ignores the conversation model's extra prompt; the conversation-model context tells it not to inspect the mask or guess the marked object.
- Media generation logs now record the prompt actually sent, plus the edit operation and crop rect.
- Requests staged before this change (no `eraseCrop`) fall back to the full image.

## Electron behavior changes

Main process only; no IPC channel, storage schema, or OpenClaw config changes. New private files `*-erase-source.png` / `*-erase-mask.png` are written alongside existing edit guides, and erase results are saved as `image-erase-*.png`.

## Testing

- `npx vitest run src/main/libs/imageEditing src/main/libs/agentEngine/openclawRuntimeAdapter.test.ts` — passed
- New unit tests in `src/main/libs/imageEditingErase.test.ts`
- `tsc -p electron-tsconfig.json` — no errors
- ESLint clean on touched image-editing files
- Manually verified erase results in the app
