prs.title: fix(runtime): keep personality files stable per session so edits don't bust the prompt cache
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `Agent` renders the `## Project Context` block (the personality files: `AGENTS.md`, `SOUL.md`, `TOOLS.md`, `IDENTITY.md`, `USER.md`, `HEARTBEAT.md`, `BOOTSTRAP.md`, `MEMORY.md` when injected) once, on its first system-prompt build, and reuses that text every turn. Before this, `IdentitySection` re-read the files on every turn's rebuild. The system prompt heads the provider's cached prefix, so any edit to one of those files made the next request of every live session of that agent miss the prompt cache for the whole conversation (#11696).
  - New `PromptContext::identity_snapshot` carries the pre-rendered text. `prompt::render_identity_section` is the shared renderer, and `None` keeps today's read-now behavior for other builders.
  - New `Agent::reload_personality` re-reads the files on purpose and rebuilds the system prompt. It's exposed as `session/reload_context` (RPC, `sessions:update` grant, owner-only, refused with `SESSION_BUSY` while a turn holds the agent) and as the ZeroCode `/reload-context` command. After its session lookups, the handler re-resolves the caller's current grants and holds it to ownership of the admitted record right before the reload, as `session/append` and `session/abort` do. ZeroCode says whether anything changed and that the changed prompt may reduce cache reuse on the next request.
  - A turn now makes sure the history starts with a system prompt. A resumed session whose snapshot failed (for example a broken `identity.json`) used to keep its history with no system message, and later turns never added one. Now each turn inserts it once the snapshot succeeds; until then the turn fails with the load error.
- **Scope boundary:** this doesn't touch the CLI `loop_::run` path or the channel orchestrator (the channel path already builds once). It also doesn't touch the `tool_search` deferred-tools section, which still changes the prompt when a tool is activated (noted in #11696). No config switch.
- **Blast radius:** long-lived `Agent` sessions (ZeroCode/ACP, gateway WS). **Behavior change:** an agent that edits its own rules mid-session no longer sees the new text in its system prompt on the next turn. It already has the edit in its conversation context, and other live sessions get it on `/reload-context` or in a new session.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11696. Related #8321.
- **Holding-crate exception:** every `zeroclaw-runtime` file this PR changes (`src/agent/{agent,prompt}.rs`, `src/tools/delegate.rs`, `src/rpc/{dispatch,types}.rs`) is inside the merged personality-snapshot row from #11697 (ADR-016). Since `eb4822217`, `src/agent/personality.rs` is unchanged from `master`: the snapshot path calls the existing `load_personality_files` and rereads only the files it reported missing. If a reread finds text that the first read missed (a file saved mid-read), it captures again, up to 3 times, and then fails rather than pin a partial snapshot. Any read error other than not-found also fails. So no amendment to that row is needed.

### What this does, simply

Each agent has a few notes files that are pasted into the start of every conversation. ZeroClaw re-read those files before every turn. If anything in them changed, even one line, the provider couldn't reuse its cached copy of the conversation, and the next request was billed at full price. That happened for every open session of that agent, not just the one that edited the file. With long sessions this cost about $1–2 per session per edit.

Now a session reads the notes once and keeps that copy. New sessions see edits right away. An open session picks them up when you type `/reload-context`. Its prompt then changes, so the next request may get less use out of the provider's cache; you choose when that happens.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `tui` (ZeroCode Code pane over RPC)
- **Setup / preconditions:** a provider that reports cached input tokens. Two ZeroCode sessions of the same agent, each a few turns in.
- **Steps to run:** append a line to the agent's workspace `AGENTS.md`. Send one message in each session. Check `cached_input_tokens` in the cost ledger. Then run `/reload-context` in one session and send one more message.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the first request after the edit stays cached in both sessions. `/reload-context` shows "Context reloaded…", and only that session's next request reads less from the cache. A second `/reload-context` says "Context unchanged".
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the first request after the edit is uncached (`cached_input_tokens` null/0) in both sessions.

### How I tested

- **AIEOS failure path (head `51e26a3c3564`):** a configured `identity.json` that can't be read or parsed now fails the snapshot capture with `Could not load AIEOS identity: …` instead of silently falling back to the Markdown files. A failed `/reload-context` keeps the previous snapshot and system prompt, and a failed first capture isn't pinned, so the next build after the file is fixed captures the full identity. The non-snapshot renderer stays lenient. New tests: `mixed_aieos_markdown_reload_failure_keeps_previous_snapshot` and `mixed_aieos_markdown_failed_first_capture_is_not_pinned` (each covers malformed JSON, a directory in place of the file, and a missing file, with `AGENTS.md` still present, then recovery after repair), plus `legacy_identity_renderer_tolerates_aieos_load_failure`. With only the test commit applied to `19c478e3b0`, both mixed tests fail (`0 passed; 2 failed`: the old renderer accepts the degraded render). On this head, through the local cargo wrapper: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` → `5889 passed; 2 failed`, the two being `relay::local_dial_tests::a_closed_route_releases_a_dial_parked_on_a_stalled_listener` and `a_dial_that_never_connects_ends_on_its_own_budget`, which fail the same way on `19c478e3b0`; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --test '*'` → all 15 integration binaries pass.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the Rust test/clippy jobs for `zeroclaw-runtime` and `zerocode`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none known.
- **Current head `650ab4b2a761`** (`de9462e2f` plus the fixes for Greptile 4429288963 and 4429288973), Linux x86_64:
  - `cargo +1.98.0 test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --no-fail-fast` → `5914 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored`, including the new `resumed_history_gets_its_system_prompt_once_the_identity_loads`, `personality_capture_rereads_a_file_that_gained_text_during_the_read`, `personality_capture_fails_when_a_file_keeps_changing` and `personality_capture_accepts_files_that_are_really_missing_or_empty`.
  - `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → clean.
  - CI for this head is pending. The Security job fails on every current PR run because of new wasmtime advisories (RUSTSEC-2026-0420 to 0424) until #12129 lands. This PR doesn't touch wasmtime.
- **Earlier head `de9462e2f8ec`** (`eb4822217` plus a clean merge of `master` `1c1cd118a`): `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- agent:: rpc:: tools::delegate` → `2547 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored`. Clippy and fmt clean.
- **Earlier head `51e26a3c3564`:** CI Required Gate green.
- **Commands run and tail output** at `3794bcf4a254` (rebased onto `ee2f5f58f7d7`), through the remote cargo wrapper:
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- reload_context a_reload_` → `4 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib` → `5811 passed; 2 failed`. The two failures are `relay::local_dial_tests::a_closed_route_releases_a_dial_parked_on_a_stalled_listener` and `a_dial_that_never_connects_ends_on_its_own_budget`, which fail the same way on `ee2f5f58f7d7` in a clean detached worktree. This PR doesn't touch `relay`.
  - `cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode` → `1550 passed; 2 failed`. `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` and `app::tests::input_wait_returns_early_for_pending_transport_events` also fail on `ee2f5f58f7d7` (the second is timing-sensitive; it passed once and failed three times there).
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` and `scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` → clean.
- **Earlier runs** at `f0fd4f895a78`, before the rebase:
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- personality_edit_mid_session session_reload_context new_session_methods_are_classified remote_dispatch_rejects_every_foreign build_system_prompt_omits_memory_md method_all_no_duplicates method_from_wire_roundtrip agent::prompt::` → `test result: ok. 35 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- agent:: rpc::dispatch tools::delegate` → `2149 passed; 1 failed`. The failure is `new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants`, which fails the same way on the base `f12da7462a0f` in a clean detached worktree (`0 passed; 1 failed`). It isn't caused by this change.
  - `cargo test -p zerocode -- input_bar chat::tests::old_daemon reload` → `160 passed; 0 failed`
  - `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → clean. `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` → clean. `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the changed files → clean.
- **Regression guard:** `personality_edit_mid_session_keeps_system_prompt_byte_stable` runs two streamed turns with an `AGENTS.md` edit between them and asserts the provider-visible system prompts are byte-identical. It then checks that `reload_personality` reports the change and that turn 3 carries the new text. With the snapshot disabled (render every turn) it fails: `assertion left == right failed: a mid-session AGENTS.md edit must not change the cached system prompt`.
- **Authority regression guard:** `a_reload_is_refused_when_its_grant_is_revoked_while_it_waits` and `a_reload_by_a_demoted_administrator_is_held_to_ownership` pause the reload after its gate, republish the policy, then release it. Both expect `FORBIDDEN` and an agent that still holds its first snapshot. `a_reload_of_an_own_session_survives_an_unrelated_policy_change` is the permitted control. With the recheck removed, the first two fail and the control still passes.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** No live provider cache check on this head. Real screenshots of the `/reload-context` outcomes, built from `725dcbbf69`, are linked under Screenshots below.
### Screenshots

Real screenshots: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11698#issuecomment-6514495140 (macOS Terminal.app captures of `725dcbbf69`).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. The new RPC re-reads the same workspace files the prompt already read, for the session's own agent, and needs `sessions:update` plus session ownership like `session/rename`.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. It's the same text as before; only the time it's read changes.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: n/a

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes on the wire: the new method is additive, and an old daemon returns method-not-found to `/reload-context`, which ZeroCode shows as an error line. The behavior change is described under Blast radius.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No config. The RPC method `session/reload_context` and the ZeroCode command `/reload-context` are new.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After squash merge, `git revert <squash-commit>`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** an agent ignoring a personality-file edit in an already-open session (expected until `/reload-context`). Report it if a new session doesn't see the edit.

prs.title: fix(rpc): judge queued session ownership by current authority
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Current head: `90baa4e0b822dbee54e51d870e3f902c1143f073`, integrating master through `5d4b18d335780af8bf15979b2f45e541f91c5eb9` with an additive merge. The PR's eight-file security patch is unchanged by this refresh. The [prepared canonical repair](https://github.com/Aarlington/zeroclaw/commit/677961e7d73f17c36a7d21742095ea0292d605d8) and all existing contributor commits remain in the ancestry, including the merged #10246 and #11222 behavior.
  - Commits since `d72bab13cd`, the head Aarlington reviewed on 2026-10-18:
    - `68c8228891` (JordanTheJet, 2026-10-21): `test(rpc): cover a TUI rebind during the transcript capacity wait`. Adds `messages_frame_capacity_wait_rechecks_remote_tui_owner` to `rpc/dispatch.rs`.
    - `b350fcec00` (JordanTheJet, 2026-10-21): `fix(rpc): recheck the remote TUI owner before committing the transcript`. A seven-line addition in `commit_session_messages` that, after the writer capacity wait and under the session-map guard, refuses a remote caller whose `tui_id` no longer matches the live session's `owner_tui_id`, the same fence `replay_session_plan` uses. This answers the transcript finding from Aarlington's 2026-10-18 review.
    - `1688a026cb` (JordanTheJet, 2026-10-22): merge of master through `7820b366ec` into the branch.
    - `90baa4e0b8` (IftekharUddin, 2026-10-26): merge of master through `5d4b18d335` (the v0.8.7 version bump) into the branch.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Session operations that wait (for the session admission permit, the config writer gate, a pending provider binding or the provider-update lock) decided ownership with the administrator bypass stamped on the connection before the wait. `recheck_authority_after_admission` re-resolved the grants afterwards but never updated that stamp, so an administrator demoted while queued still reached another principal's session. A new `scoped_principal_id_from(grants)` derives the ownership scope from a given grant set; `scoped_principal_id()` delegates to it with the stamped grants and remains the pre-wait check. `revalidate_admitted_session`, `authorize_session_owner_for_mode` and `resolve_session_record_for_mode` now take the scope as a parameter instead of reading the stamp, so those post-admission ownership decisions and refusals use freshly resolved grants.
  - `session/close`, `session/kill` and `session/delete` recheck authority right after the permit and revalidate with the scope those grants give. Kill and delete also fall back to the durable record when a hard-cancelled turn removed the live incarnation during the wait; that fallback now requires the record to be the caller's under the same scope. Without it, a demoted administrator whose target's live incarnation disappeared while it waited still tombstoned or deleted another principal's durable row.
  - `session/prompt` derives ownership from fresh grants after admission and provider waits. Final preparation runs inside the execution task after it acquires the canonical Agent lock. It checks the exact Agent and current owner/binding/environment permissions, narrows tools, and authorizes the checkpoint or running-state write under the storage lock before execution. Refused preparation ends the client turn through `refuse_admitted_prompt` without calling the provider. Rehydration uses guarded recovery and seed-trim persistence so a storage-lock wait cannot retain earlier authority.
  - `session/new`: `SessionStore::resume_existing_authorized` hands the session's owner to its authorize closure, and the new `authorize_resumed_incarnation` judges that owner with the same authority it resolves for the agent/workspace binding and the retained environment, under the store lock. A connection whose stamp still carries a revoked bypass therefore cannot rebind another principal's live session. After the permit, authority is re-resolved before anything else and the scope derived from it judges the record found under the permit (so a demoted administrator no longer leaves a cross-principal audit record for a request refused a few lines later, and a principal promoted while waiting is honoured), the post-admission resume, the cross-mode replacement and the ACP restore preload. After the config writer gate wait it is re-derived again: the owner of the session being restored or replaced must match, and whether a failed owner-stamp write aborts creation follows that scope.
  - `session/configure` and the queued (reaped) branch of `session/messages` also act after a wait and call `revalidate_admitted_session`, so they recheck authority and pass the fresh scope as well.
  - Live cancellation, publication and deferred approval-channel installation reauthorize under the live-session boundary. `session/messages` and plan replay reserve outbound capacity before their final ownership/authority check and send synchronously while guarded. The shared plan helper covers live resume, restored `session/new`, and prompt rehydration.
  - `session/append` passes the current ownership scope into its admitted lookup, then resolves authority again after that awaited lookup and before either transcript write. Its regression covers a demoted administrator targeting a foreign session, an owner whose update grant was revoked, and a demoted owner whose update grant remains valid.
- **Scope boundary:** The request gate, durable owner identity (`owner_principal_id`), wire, config and CLI shapes are unchanged. Ownership after the covered waits follows current authority. The guards authorize individual effects; this does not add continuous revocation of an already-admitted running turn or roll back effects authorized before demotion.
- **Blast radius:** RPC dispatch, execution-task preparation, live-session synchronization, outbound frame reservation, and guarded ACP/Chat persistence. New authorization callbacks run after storage locks or transactions are acquired and retain authority through synchronous effects. History helpers acquire the Agent before the session map and recheck incarnation identity. Unsupported guarded backend reads and deletes fail closed. Permitted own-session operations retain positive-control coverage.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11126. Related #11222 (merged prerequisite). Related #10412.

### What this does, simply

Named local principals can hold an administrator bypass that lets them act on other principals' sessions. Several session requests wait before they act: behind a turn that holds the session, behind a configuration change, or behind a provider update. The daemon did recheck the caller's permissions after that wait, but it kept deciding who owns what from the administrator flag recorded when the request arrived. If an administrator lost that role while their request waited, the request still went through: it could delete another person's saved session, kill it, send it a prompt, change its settings, read it, or restore it.

After this change, the covered effects decide ownership from the permissions in force after their final wait. A demoted administrator receives the same "not found or not owned" refusal as any other principal before that effect executes, changes saved data, or discloses a foreign transcript or plan. Permitted operations on the caller's own sessions keep working.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: reproducing it needs a principal roster and a demotion that lands while a request is queued, which the dispatcher-level regressions below drive deterministically.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** On `90baa4e0b822dbee54e51d870e3f902c1143f073`, [Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914/job/121823900690), [Parallel Runtime Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914/job/121824145930), [Lint](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914/job/121823900780) and the [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914/job/121833369379) pass in [Quality Gate run 40394518914](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914). Test covers the RPC and storage regressions, including the remote-TUI transcript fence; Parallel Runtime Test checks concurrent runtime execution, and the required gate aggregates the selected jobs. [Windows compile](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914/job/121824410202), [Windows Service Smoke](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914/job/121824410236), [macOS compile](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914/job/121823900711), [MSRV](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914/job/121825752013) and [plugin runtime](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40394518914/job/121823901145) checks also pass. The check runs and the re-read PR head match this exact commit.

- **Current local validation (2026-10-26):** Tested `90baa4e0b822dbee54e51d870e3f902c1143f073` (tree `36d89052034e3d2e1230835aa09da6146bb678c8`) on macOS arm64 with rustc/cargo 1.97.1, default crate features and default test threading. The isolated checkout used its own `target/` directory with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0` and `CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0`. All 1,549 selected tests passed; formatting and strict Clippy exited 0.

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0; no output
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra --lib
# zeroclaw-api: 321 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
# zeroclaw-infra: 319 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::
# 870 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 5023 filtered out
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib live_config_authority::
# 39 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 5854 filtered out
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
# exit 0; no Clippy diagnostics
# Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized] target(s) in 1m 54s
```

- **Historical hosted validation (not current-head evidence):** On `1688a026cb7dff7c8ef9a54a9e73128c3258cb8a`, [Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39728651042/job/119658338409), [Parallel Runtime Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39728651042/job/119658474359), [Lint](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39728651042/job/119658338391) and the [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39728651042/job/119661634575) pass. Test runs the RPC regressions listed below, including the transcript remote-TUI recheck.
- **Transcript remote-TUI recheck (68c8228891, b350fcec00):** `commit_session_messages` also checks the remote TUI owner after reserving writer capacity, under the same session-map guard as the send, as `replay_session_plan` does. `messages_frame_capacity_wait_rechecks_remote_tui_owner` rebinds the owner through a trusted-local `session/new` during the capacity wait and asserts that the old remote TUI gets no transcript; current-owner and trusted-local controls still read it. The test fails without the fix.
- **Historical local validation (not current-head evidence):** `d72bab13cd71f1fa31e0028668a2ee471a88f9fc` (tree `0cb5396b9b114b24801ab91e4a87f00e433c7974`), macOS arm64, rustc 1.97.1; default crate features and eight test threads. All 1,094 focused tests passed, with no Clippy diagnostics.

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0; no output
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc:: -- --test-threads=8
# 862 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 4919 filtered out
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-infra --lib session -- --test-threads=8
# 207 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 107 filtered out
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib live_config_authority:: -- --test-threads=8
# 25 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 5756 filtered out
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
# Finished dev profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 19s
```

- **Current local linker diagnostic and historical baseline:** The current runtime test link emitted `ld: __eh_frame section too large (max 16MB) to encode dwarf unwind offsets in compact unwind table, performance of exception handling might be affected`; the binary linked and all selected tests passed. The warning concerns the large test binary's unwind table. Earlier validation reproduced the same diagnostic on clean master `ceb1e11176b7ee86ca3007cb7f6110ae94ff6ecb` with `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib --no-run` (exit 0). That is historical baseline evidence; the current pinned master was not separately rebuilt for this warning.

- **Historical CI on the previous PR head (not current-head evidence):** On `d5df4214cad96bfc6bfbdea13a64767b116ac1df`, [Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36751197781/job/110009962176), [Parallel Runtime Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36751197781/job/110010144453), Lint, the plugin-backend Check legs, and the [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/36751197781/job/110014127332) pass. The Test log explicitly records the admission/provider, final-effect, storage-lock and outbound-backpressure regressions below passing; its main suite reports 19,059 passed and 39 skipped. These results cover only that older revision; the refreshed head has a separate run.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local evidence exercises synthetic principals, in-process RPC handlers, existing local/WSS transport tests and real session stores on macOS; no live daemon against a real identity provider was tested. Hosted Windows compile and service-smoke jobs passed, but the advisory Windows nextest workflow and targeted Windows Clippy job were skipped by workflow selection. Full Windows runtime-suite coverage is not claimed.
- **Regression coverage:**
  - `append_rechecks_authority_after_admitted_lookup` (prepared-repair regression): demotion cannot preserve a foreign-session append, and revoking an owner's update grant prevents both durable and live writes; a demoted owner who retains update authority can still append.
  - `queued_operations_lose_the_admin_bypass_when_the_administrator_is_demoted` (new): alice holds `member` session grants plus an `administrator` profile, and bob owns an ACP session. For each of prompt, close, delete and kill against bob's live session, delete and kill when its live incarnation is reaped during the wait, and prompt (the rehydration path) and messages against the reaped session, alice's request passes its pre-check as administrator and parks on the admission permit; the profile loses `admin` (her `member` grants stay) and the permit is released. Each request gets `FORBIDDEN` with the uniform denial, each refused prompt ends the client's turn with a failed `TurnComplete` on alice's connection, bob's live generation is unchanged (or the session stays reaped, not revived), and his durable row still exists, is not killed, keeps his owner and gains no messages. Configure parked on the provider-update lock is refused the same way and bob's overrides are unchanged. Positive control: alice, demoted while her delete of her own session waits, deletes it.
  - `queued_prompt_rechecks_ownership_after_its_provider_waits` (new): alice's prompt on bob's live session passes the post-admission ownership check as administrator and then parks, once on the provider-update lock and once on a pending provider binding; she is demoted and the wait is released. Both prompts get `FORBIDDEN` with the uniform denial and a failed `TurnComplete`, bob's provider receives no call, and his incarnation and durable row are unchanged.
  - `demoted_administrator_cannot_resume_a_foreign_session_with_a_stale_stamp` (new): `handle_session_new_for_test` skips the gate, so alice's connection keeps its administrator stamp after the demotion; `session/new` naming bob's live session is refused and his generation is unchanged, while the same stale connection still rebinds a session of her own. Resumes of bob's reaped ACP and chat sessions queued behind the permit when the demotion lands are refused and nothing is restored; bob's ACP row keeps an interrupted-turn checkpoint unrecovered and his chat row keeps its owner. Positive control: her own reaped ACP session, resumed the same way, is restored.
  - The direct `resume_existing_authorized` tests accept the owner argument and returned authorization guard.
  - `final_prompt_effect_waits_recheck_current_authority`, `removal_effect_waits_preserve_foreign_session_after_demotion`, `restore_effect_waits_preserve_retained_checkpoint_after_demotion`, and `deferred_approval_install_rechecks_after_agent_wait` cover the later execution, mutation and channel-install boundaries.
  - `messages_frame_capacity_wait_rechecks_authority_before_disclosure` and `resume_plan_capacity_wait_rechecks_authority_and_incarnation` exercise actual dispatcher responses and backpressure. The plan test covers live/restored resume, prompt rehydration, demotion, replacement, own-session and unchanged-administrator controls. Empty-plan and closed-writer cases also pass.
  - `guarded_effects_reauthorize_after_store_lock_without_partial_writes` and `guarded_state_and_delete_recheck_owner_and_authority_after_connection_wait` verify post-lock authorization and preserved durable data on denial. `history_wait_releases_map_and_refuses_replaced_incarnation` covers the changed history lock order.
  - `remote_resume_admission_wait_uses_current_principal` covers remote demotion with an own-session control. `remote_resume_rechecks_channels_at_final_agent_install` checks capability changes during the final Agent wait. The plan-backpressure matrix now includes remote live and cross-mode resume and checks their intended admission-permit lifetimes.
- **Commands run and tail output** (author-reported historical local evidence on b0879527d3, macOS arm64, rustc 1.98.0; not a claim of new local runs on the integrated head):
  - `cargo nextest run -p zeroclaw-runtime -E 'test(/admitted|demot|owner|resume|queued/)'`: `114 tests run: 114 passed, 5169 skipped`.
  - `TMPDIR=/private/tmp cargo nextest run -p zeroclaw-runtime -E 'test(/rpc::/)'`: `660 tests run: 660 passed, 4623 skipped`.
  - `./scripts/ci/rust_quality_gate.sh --strict`: fmt passes; clippy stops on its only error, `unused import: std::sync::mpsc` at `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/service/mod.rs:15`, which unmodified `master` also reports on macOS (the import is used only by Windows and Linux code). The script's provider-dispatch section, run on its own: `provider dispatch gate clean`.
  - `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets --features ci-all -- -D warnings -A unused_imports`: `Finished`, no diagnostics.
  - `cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`: `Finished`, no warnings.
  - `./scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh`: `Comment hygiene gate passed.`

No live deployment or rendered-interface run is claimed.

The remote-TUI rebind regression asserts `SESSION_NOT_OWNED` and that the private transcript marker is not sent. These are distinct refusal paths; no claim is made that every regression has the same message.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** A demoted administrator's queued prompt, close, delete, kill, configure, messages or resume of another principal's session is refused at the covered waits, with the foreign session's state preserved. Positive controls explicitly cover deletion and live/reaped resume of the caller's own sessions.

The exact-head hosted run supplies the broader Linux tests, Windows compile/service smoke, macOS compile and selected plugin checks named above. The older local plugin skips remain historical. No live identity-provider/deployment test was run. Docs gates were not run because this PR changes no documentation.

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Wire/config shapes remain compatible; requests that lose authority while waiting are refused. Rust APIs add guarded `SessionBackend` methods and a generation field to `ResumedRpcSession`. The changed `resume_existing_authorized` callback is crate-private, not a public closure API.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

The guarded state default has no persistent effect and authorizes the locked live owner; a backend that persists state must override it and read the stored owner under its mutation lock. In-tree SQLite and JSONL behavior is covered by the added tests. No wire or config migration is required.

- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None

prs.title: feat(tools): add opt-in subprocess memory watchdog
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Add `runtime_profiles.<alias>.shell_max_memory_mb`, measured in MiB and disabled by default, for native shell and skill subprocesses.
  - Sample the command's resident memory plus its visible descendants. Stop the owned command group or Windows Job Object when a sample exceeds the threshold, and return a failed `ToolResult` with the threshold and observed memory.
  - Share the existing capped-output execution path between shell and skill tools. Stop the command on monitoring failure, preserve capped partial output with truncation markers, and bound cleanup waiting after timeout or failure.
  - Check zero RSS readings through the operating system's process API. Accept a confirmed zero for the same observed process identity and skip descendants confirmed to have exited after the snapshot. Unreadable live processes and incomplete responses remain monitoring errors.
  - Carry the threshold through the existing runtime-profile policy. Explicit child policies cannot raise or disable a finite parent threshold.
- **Scope boundary:** No `RLIMIT_AS`, default memory cap, hard allocation ceiling, cgroup implementation, or guarantee against host OOM. Detached or reparented processes can escape sampling. Docker keeps its existing container memory controls.
- **Blast radius:** Native shell and skill execution, runtime-profile policy construction, explicit child-policy validation, and Windows process ownership. Existing tool admission, environment filtering, and sandbox authorization remain in place.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #6916. The original strict OOM-prevention requirements remain open. #7937 introduced the earlier implementation, which #8417 reverted; this PR uses resident-memory sampling instead of restoring it.
- **Runtime placement:** The bounded native shell/skill RSS scope was approved by @tidux and recorded in merged #11436. Merged #11697 widens its catalogue coverage to all five locale files used here.

### What this does, simply

The shell and skill tools let an agent run programs on your machine. Their timeout and output cap limit how long a command runs and how much text ZeroClaw stores, but they do not limit the memory used by the program itself.

This adds an optional watcher. You choose a memory threshold in the agent's runtime profile. While its command runs, ZeroClaw samples the physical memory used by that command and its visible children. If the total crosses the threshold, ZeroClaw stops the owned command group and tells the agent why it failed. A zero reading is checked directly with the operating system so an unavailable measurement is not mistaken for no memory use. A child that exits between the snapshot and that check no longer causes an otherwise healthy command to be stopped. If output was capped before a command failed, its partial output says it was truncated.

The watcher is off unless configured. It reacts after observing memory use, so a command can exceed the threshold between samples. It does not reserve memory, impose a kernel allocation ceiling, or guarantee that an out-of-memory event cannot happen. Virtual-address reservations alone do not count, avoiding the earlier virtual-memory-limit approach.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

Both tool entry points need the same child ownership, bounded output capture, timeout, and memory-failure handling. Sharing the existing shell runner avoids implementing those lifecycles twice. The new sampler uses the existing `sysinfo` dependency; Windows containment and failed-spawn cleanup reuse the existing `process-wrap` dependency and service guard.

The essential new work is per-command process ancestry and RSS sampling, plus platform-specific ownership on Windows. Three small native readers resolve zero readings without adding another process cache or dependency. They compare the returned process identity at the existing whole-second precision; this does not eliminate every descendant PID-reuse race. There is no global process cache, new dependency, polling scheduler, or sandbox backend. Sampling runs about every 100 ms plus observation time. Its metadata work scales with host process count and concurrent monitored commands; disabled monitoring starts no sampler. Shared resident pages may count more than once.

Monitoring follows the root command's lifetime. On Windows, dropping the enabled command's owner explicitly terminates its Job Object before closing the handle, stopping remaining job descendants even after root completion. Non-native runtimes, Docker sandboxes, and unsupported operating systems reject an enabled watchdog before spawning; Docker deployments should use their existing container memory limits.

The bounded runtime placement exception is recorded by merged #11436.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. Focused tests spawn real subprocesses and exercise resident allocation, descendant aggregation, virtual reservation, and tool-result conversion without requiring a provider or changing a live agent's configuration.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [Required CI](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38010558146) passes on `73db3b5cae818a5d45d9f5676f69643d8ee48007`, including Linux Test, Parallel Runtime Test, Lint, Format, Windows compilation and task-owner recovery. The same head ran in [hosted macOS](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39163181716/job/117780719339) and [hosted Windows](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39163181716/job/117780719366) jobs. All 12 macOS and 11 Windows subprocess-memory tests passed, including `descendant_departure_after_snapshot_is_not_a_monitor_failure` and `failed_native_read_does_not_accept_sysinfo_zero` on both platforms, the complete native-record check on macOS, and `root_exit_closes_owned_job_descendants` on Windows. Both platforms also pass the resident-memory tool diagnostic, shell/skill container rejection and policy non-escalation tests. macOS passes terminal detachment, timeout/cancellation descendant cleanup and all three truncation tests. Both hosted jobs ran `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --no-fail-fast`.
- **Current head `de78ac7c0f81`** (`73db3b5ca`, a clean merge of `master` `1c1cd118a`, and `de78ac7c0`): the new commit is documentation only. It adds one sentence to the `shell_max_memory_mb` doc comment and to `docs/book/src/tools/python-skills.md`. The sentence says that on macOS a command that starts a descendant under another user (`sudo`, a setuid helper) is stopped with a monitoring failure, because that process's memory can't be read. On Linux x86_64, `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-config --lib` gave `5910 passed; 0 failed; 9 ignored` for runtime and `1819 passed; 0 failed` for config. `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-api --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. CI for this head is pending. The Security job may fail on the new wasmtime advisories (RUSTSEC-2026-0420 to 0424) until #12129 lands.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The new departure regression has now executed on both macOS and Windows at the current head. The full platform suites remain red: macOS ran 19,490 tests with 19,484 passed, six failed and 39 skipped; Windows ran 19,043 tests with 19,034 passed, nine failed and 36 skipped. The six macOS failures exactly match the [earlier macOS run](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38000741090/job/114058025862), covering Telegram prompt timing, a filesystem spelling fixture, Hailo-Ollama and Serply connection classification, RPC session-method grants and Tailscale probe timing. No clean-master macOS execution baseline was run. The nine Windows failures exactly match both the [earlier Windows run](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/actions/runs/38000741090/job/114058025868) and the [clean-master Windows run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37880263821/job/113658218149). The previously identified fixes in #11361, #11362, #11363, #11365, #11366 and #11630 remain separate from this branch.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

The integrated head `73db3b5cae818a5d45d9f5676f69643d8ee48007` passes the focused macOS watchdog, terminal-detachment and descendant-cleanup checks:

```text
cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -E 'test(tools::subprocess_memory::tests) | test(shell_child_cannot_open_owners_controlling_terminal) | test(shell_reaps_descendants_after_timeout_or_cancellation)' --test-threads=1
Summary: 14 tests run, 14 passed.

cargo fmt --all -- --check
Passed.

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.

git diff --check
Passed.
```

The departure repair at `a42774653cd4f1458707854863228f3e5d6594ef` passes the focused macOS watchdog suite, formatting, diff integrity and comment hygiene:

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::subprocess_memory::tests -- --test-threads=1
12 passed; 0 failed on macOS, including descendant departure and live read-failure controls.

cargo fmt --all
Passed.
```

The following results are from earlier implementation and repair candidates:

```text
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::subprocess_memory::tests -- --test-threads=1
11 passed; 0 failed on the repaired candidate.

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib tools::shell::tests::shell_marks
3 passed; 0 failed, including capped stdout/stderr on timeout.

cargo fmt --all
Passed on the repaired candidate.

Earlier implementation validation:
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- from_profiles_ ensure_no_escalation_
27 passed; 0 failed.

cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- tools::subprocess_memory:: tools::shell::tests:: tools::skill_tool::tests::
110 passed; 0 failed; completed in 2.86 seconds after compilation.

cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-runtime
Passed.

bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
Comment hygiene gate passed.

git diff --check
Passed.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source comparison confirms that shell and skill tools use the same runner, enabled monitoring is rejected before unsupported execution, and bounded delegates retain their parent-owned tool policy. No real-account or live-agent exercise was needed for the subprocess contract.
- **Build warning:** The macOS linker reported that the debug test executable's `__eh_frame` section exceeds its 16 MiB compact-unwind encoding limit. All selected tests completed. Existing clean-master validation also records this linker warning; no new source warning was reported.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. This changes subprocess enforcement rather than visual presentation. The shell regression observes the returned failed tool result and memory diagnostic.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Head `de78ac7c0f81` (the macOS evidence below ran at `73db3b5ca`, and later commits change only docs and the `master` merge); native subprocess execution and `ToolResult`, exercised by `tools::subprocess_memory::tests`, `tools::shell::tests`, `tools::skill_tool::tests`, and the config policy tests.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `shell_memory_failure_surfaces_resident_cause` checks that the failed tool result identifies the resident-memory threshold.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The process fixtures distinguish touched resident pages from a large untouched virtual reservation, aggregate two descendants, and preserve completion when monitoring is disabled or memory stays below the threshold. Focused regressions distinguish successful zero measurements from failed reads and identity changes, and confirm truncation markers on both captured streams after a timeout. The departure regression discovers a live child, deliberately kills and reaps it before the native fallback, and confirms that sampling continues; its live-process read-denial control remains an error. The integrated master regressions confirm the child cannot open its owner's controlling terminal and descendants stop after timeout or cancellation. Policy tests parse the setting and reject child escalation.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No duplicate local full-workspace run. Hosted macOS and Windows execution now covers the changed native process paths on the current head, alongside the focused local macOS checks and required Linux CI. The remaining full-platform failures are recorded above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Memory failure adds a localized diagnostic to the existing tool result. Its threshold and RSS values are numeric, and it grants no authority. Existing command output remains untrusted and capped.
- **Risk and mitigation:** A configured watchdog can stop a legitimate memory-heavy command. Shared pages can inflate the total, and polling can miss short spikes. Only owned process groups or Job Objects are signaled; sampled descendant PIDs are never termination targets. Samples remain in memory for the invocation and are not persisted.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for existing configuration. The new setting defaults to `0`. Sharing the shell runner also bounds skill output during collection and applies owned-process cleanup on skill timeout or cancellation.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. Adds `runtime_profiles.<alias>.shell_max_memory_mb`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- **Upgrade steps:** None for existing users. To opt in, set `shell_max_memory_mb` in the runtime profile selected by the agent. Use `0` to disable it. For Docker runtime limits, use `runtime.docker.memory_limit_mb` instead of this native watchdog.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Set the selected runtime profile's `shell_max_memory_mb` to `0` and recreate the affected agent/session. Revert the merge commit to remove the implementation and shared skill-runner change entirely.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `runtime_profiles.<alias>.shell_max_memory_mb = 0` disables sampling.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Failed tool results containing `resident-memory threshold`, `resident-memory monitoring failed`, or the unsupported-native-runtime diagnostic. Legitimate commands terminating early indicate a threshold that is too low or a monitoring failure.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A. This does not supersede an open PR or incorporate contributor code from the reverted implementation.

prs.title: fix(providers): use the shared stream idle bound for Anthropic
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Anthropic streaming used a fixed 90-second byte-idle timeout. OpenAI Responses and OpenAI-compatible streams already use the shared 300-second floor introduced by #10886.
  - Gateways that route Claude requests through Bedrock can stay silent during large tool inputs. The original investigation reported failures when that silence exceeded 90 seconds.
  - Anthropic now uses `stream_idle_timeout(timeout_secs)`: 300 seconds by default, raised by a larger configured timeout. The schema field description and both provider guides describe the same policy.
  - Body-read timeout errors name the effective bound and the `timeout_secs` setting instead of reporting only reqwest's decoding error.
- **Scope boundary:** This PR changes Anthropic stream-idle enforcement, diagnostics, tests and documentation. Request payloads, authentication, retry policy and non-streaming timeouts retain their existing behavior. It adds no configuration key.
- **Blast radius:** Anthropic-family streaming and its operator-facing timeout description. A genuinely stalled stream now waits 300 seconds, or a higher configured bound, before failing. Consumer cancellation still aborts the parser immediately.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10886, Related #10884. Depends on #11541. Per the maintainer's review, land #11541 first, then refresh and recheck this branch with its extra-header and redirect protections preserved.

### What this does, simply

When a Claude stream stops sending data, ZeroClaw waits for a limited time before ending the turn. The Anthropic adapter allowed only 90 seconds. Some gateways send no keep-alive events while the model prepares a large tool input, so a working generation could exceed that limit and fail with a vague error.

Anthropic streams now use the same 300-second floor as the two OpenAI streaming paths. Setting the provider's existing `timeout_secs` above 300 extends that window. Each body read resets the idle timer; this is not a deadline for the whole generation. A read timeout now explains which limit fired.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. Real-interface evidence for the changed configuration description and timeout diagnostic is still needed. A controlled endpoint can demonstrate the timeout change without a paid provider call.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli` for an interactive streamed request, and `surface=tui` for the Zerocode configuration editor. Messaging channel: N/A, this recipe uses no messaging channel.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use synthetic configuration and a local Anthropic-protocol mock that returns successful SSE headers and an initial text event, stays silent for 100 seconds, then sends a terminal event. Configure an Anthropic profile with `timeout_secs = 120` and an agent named `idle-proof` that uses it. Use the same configuration and mock on captured master 5a51398dd5 and this branch. Do not use production credentials.
- **Steps to run:** Start the mock, select its Anthropic profile, and run `zeroclaw agent -a idle-proof`, then enter `Reply with the mock response` at the prompt. Use interactive mode so the CLI supplies the streaming sink. Record the emitted text, completion or interruption, and elapsed silence. Restart the mock for each revision. In Zerocode, open that provider's `timeout_secs` description and capture the full rendered description. For the named-error case, repeat with the endpoint silent beyond 300 seconds and capture the actual supported-interface error output. A larger configured bound needs its own elapsed-time check if claimed as wire-tested.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The 100-second silence completes successfully. The configuration description includes Anthropic. A body timeout names the 300-second bound and advises raising `timeout_secs` above that bound.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The same 100-second silence reaches Anthropic's fixed 90-second read timeout. The configuration description omits Anthropic, and a stalled body lacks the shared named-bound diagnostic.

### How I tested

The earlier published head 107783d22773242936e78ae93317507ca4ef178d has passing hosted CI. The refreshed revision 70009f64d6cd31261dec9e978c73537f1156d895 merges master 5a51398dd52469644f2c2a017296b4ff89c8e02a. Its full diff and overlapping master changes were inspected. The docs style and links gates and `git diff --check origin/master...HEAD` pass on that refreshed revision. Rust compilation and execution results for that revision are pending.

The PR adds `anthropic::tests::stream_idle_bound_uses_shared_floor_and_timeout_secs` for the 300-second floor and a 900-second override, and `anthropic::tests::sse_read_timeout_names_idle_bound` for the parser diagnostic. The latter uses a 100 ms test client with a supplied 300-second diagnostic bound. It verifies the error path and text, not elapsed-time agreement or the production client's configured deadline. Production client/parser wiring was checked separately in source.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Historical [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37471074798/job/112299840714), [Test](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37471074798/job/112294405441), Format, Lint and Docs Style pass for published head 107783d227. They cover the original provider/config changes and Markdown, but do not certify the refreshed revision or the future #11541 integration.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Fresh CI runs on the pushed head `70009f64d`. The timeout-message test does not measure the production 300/900-second client deadline. Combined header/redirect/timeout validation after #11541 lands is still needed.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  Run on head `70009f64d` (master merge), Mac mini, `zc-cargo-narrow`, `-j2`, `--test-threads=2`:

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                    ok
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets -- -D warnings   ok
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers -p zeroclaw-config
    zeroclaw_config     1817 passed; 1 failed
    zeroclaw_providers  1980 passed; 1 failed; 4 ignored
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers openai::tool_round_policy_tests             ok (rerun)
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-providers anthropic                                   ok
  ```

  `policy::tests::unix_foreign_null_spellings_get_no_filesystem_exception` also fails on clean master `5a51398dd` on this machine. `openai::tool_round_policy_tests::native_tool_round_flags_reach_stream_and_chat_wires_without_changing_defaults` failed once with connection refused and passed on rerun. Neither is touched by this PR.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Inspected the shared timeout helper, factory forwarding, streaming client, parser error mapping, cancellation guard and master integration. A read-only merge preview with #11541 finds conflicts requiring preservation of both changes. The original author reported timestamped probes: Anthropic direct, 2 pings and 30.0 seconds maximum silence; a header-authenticated gateway pool, 2 pings and 30.1 seconds; Bedrock via gateway, no pings and 51.2 seconds. Those are historical reports, with no attached raw capture verified in this pass. The live Bedrock request was not rerun on this branch.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real screenshots pending.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Real screenshots pending.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Real screenshots pending.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Source and tests show Anthropic using the shared floor and configurable increase, with the corrected description and named-bound diagnostic. The real-interface A/B observations described above have not been collected on the refreshed revision.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Live provider probes were not run; no current gateway credentials were used. Workspace-wide tests were skipped; the change is limited to the providers and config crates.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No. Existing Anthropic calls can remain open longer while idle.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. #11541 owns the separate header/redirect work and is not incorporated here yet.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A, all answers above are No. The longer resource-holding interval is documented under blast radius and rollback.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The existing setting gains the same stream-idle semantics for Anthropic as for the two OpenAI paths.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. The existing `timeout_secs` setting now raises Anthropic's stream-idle bound above 300 seconds; its config-editor description and timeout diagnostic reflect that behavior. No key, flag or environment variable is added.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: No migration is required. Keep existing configuration for the 300-second floor. Set `timeout_secs` above 300 on the Anthropic profile only when a longer idle wait is needed, then apply the provider configuration through the existing configuration workflow.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

prs.title: feat(zerocode): reopen open sessions when zerocode restarts
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - zerocode's sidebar list of open sessions lived only in memory. The daemon keeps every transcript, but quitting zerocode lost which sessions were open, so each launch started from an empty sidebar.
  - The list (session ids, agent aliases, order, focus, and the last Chat/Code pane on screen) is now saved whenever it changes, as an owner-only JSON file per connection target under `<config-dir>/open-sessions/`.
  - At launch the saved list goes to the existing reconnect resume path (`set_resume_sessions`), so restored sessions reattach by id exactly as they do after a daemon reconnect: focused first, the rest in the background.
  - On by default (`[sidebar] restore_sessions = true`). `zerocode --fresh` starts one launch with an empty sidebar and still saves its own list.
  - Each zerocode window on a daemon keeps its own list in a numbered slot, held by an OS file lock. A window takes the lowest free slot, so closing a second window and opening it again while the first runs reopens the second window's sessions. At restore, sessions another running window has in its list are skipped with a notice. Without that, two windows would reattach the same live session, and either window could cancel the other's turn. That stale-session and multi-tab hazard is why #8911 (silent auto-resume, for #8653) was closed in favour of the #8922 picker. The lock is released when the owning window exits, including on a crash.
  - Each window publishes the list it is about to reopen before its panes start (an empty list on `--fresh`), so other windows never judge by the previous occupant's stale list.
  - Saved Code sessions the daemon no longer lists, and saved Chat sessions with no stored history (for example deleted), are dropped with one notice.
  - When the daemon refuses to reattach a restored session because this terminal's environment differs from the one the session started in (FORBIDDEN `-32012`, "Session environment differs" or "Session retains a local operator environment"), the entry stays where it was, with the same order and focus. Its pane shows a translated notice that the saved session can't be reattached from this terminal environment and that the daemon still keeps the old conversation, plus an explicit "start a new conversation" action (the existing new-session key, Ctrl+N by default). Only that action opens a fresh session in the same slot, with the same agent and mode, and the saved list then tracks the new id. If creating it fails, the refused entry and its notice stay. Switching from the notice to another session moves the refused entry to the background, and closing it while a live session is focused closes only that row, so the live session stays on screen. Nothing is replaced automatically, other errors behave as before, and the daemon's environment check is unchanged.
  - Fully resuming the old conversation in that case is left to upstream #11921 (history persistence so tasks can resume after restart).
  - Local daemon connections only. Over WSS the daemon admits a resume only from the client identity that owns the session (`capture_session_access`), and a relaunched window connects with a new one, so a saved remote list could only produce failed rows. Reclaiming a remote identity per window slot is a follow-up.
- **Scope boundary:** Local connections only; remote (`--connect`) windows are unchanged. Client only (`apps/zerocode`); no daemon, RPC or runtime change. Queued messages, unsent drafts and attachments are not saved. A turn that was running when zerocode quit is not resumed or rerun.
- **Blast radius:** zerocode startup (one extra `session/list-acp` call and/or one `session/messages` probe per saved Chat session on a local connection when a saved list exists) and the per-frame sidebar derivation (a cheap comparison; the file is written only when the list changes, and never while disconnected).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #8653, #8911, #8922.

### What this does, simply

When you quit zerocode and start it again, the sessions you had open in the sidebar come back: same order, same one focused, on the pane you were using. The conversations themselves were always kept by the daemon. What was lost was the list of which ones you had open. If a saved session has since been deleted, it is skipped with a short notice. If a saved session can't be reattached from the terminal you relaunched in, it stays in its place with a notice and an option to start a new conversation there. Each zerocode window keeps its own list: close a second window and open it again, and it gets its own sessions back. A session already open in another window is not opened twice. Use `zerocode --fresh` to start one launch with an empty sidebar, or set `restore_sessions = false` under `[sidebar]` to turn the feature off.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `tui` (zerocode Chat and Code panes)
- **Setup / preconditions:** A local daemon with at least two agents.
- **Steps to run:** Open two Code sessions and one Chat session from the sidebar, focus the second Code session, quit zerocode, start it again. Then quit and start once more with `zerocode --fresh`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** With one `zerocode` open, open a second window, add a session there, close it and reopen it: it comes back with that session, and the first window is unchanged. The second launch opens on the Code pane with the same three sidebar rows in the same order and the second Code session focused, transcripts loaded. The `--fresh` launch starts with an empty sidebar.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Every launch starts with an empty sidebar (or the recent-session picker); the previous launch's open sessions must be reopened one by one.

### How I tested

- **Current head:** `214a73cc5` (`8628b342c` plus the fix for Greptile 4429702542: if switching from a refused restore notice to another retained session fails, the refused entry stays focused, so its notice and "start a new conversation" still work). Linux x86_64, rustc 1.98.0, in its own target dir (the log shows zerocode compiled from this tree): `cargo test --locked -p zerocode --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4` → library 52 passed; binary 1,599 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored, including the new `chat::tests::a_failed_switch_from_a_refused_notice_keeps_the_refused_entry_focused` (Chat and Code panes). `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` are clean.
- **Previous head:** `8628b342c` (the fix for Greptile 4429144032: closing a refused restore row after switching to a live session no longer replaces that session; test `closing_a_refused_entry_after_switching_away_keeps_the_working_session`).
- **Previous head:** `b8f816f436`, a merge of master `1c1cd118a` into `d05cdf055c`. The merge conflicted only in `apps/zerocode/src/chat.rs`: master added `cleanup_notice` to `ResumeEntry` and this branch added `environment_refused`, so the struct and its constructors keep both fields. On a Linux x86_64 build host (rustc 1.99.1): `cargo test --locked -p zerocode -- --test-threads=4` → library 52 passed; binary 1,596 passed, 1 failed (the known `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`); `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passed.
- **Previous tested revision:** `d05cdf055cb2a9a61f343643619abe730dc78b4c` on the Mac mini, with the results below.
- **Formatting:** `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passed.
- **Clippy:** `cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
- **Package suite:** `cargo test -p zerocode`, through `zc-cargo-narrow` with `-j2` for compilation and two test threads: library 54 passed; binary 1,600 passed, 1 failed (the known failure below). The TestBackend evidence-frame tests were removed in this revision; the behaviour tests stay.
- **Deleted-Chat regressions (new or updated, all pass):** `open_sessions::tests::deleted_chat_session_is_skipped_at_restore`, `open_sessions::tests::chat_sessions_survive_startup_without_a_complete_daemon_listing`, `open_sessions::tests::chat_restore_drops_only_the_specific_missing_session_refusal`, `open_sessions::tests::mixed_restore_prunes_code_by_list_and_chat_by_history_in_order`. Each saved Chat entry is probed with `session/messages` (limit 1): no stored history, or the daemon's "Session not found or not owned by this principal" refusal, drops it with the existing notice; any other error keeps it for the normal resume path. I ran the first test against `409b7725ef` and it fails there (`dropped` is 0, expected 1), because that head kept every saved Chat ID.
- **Environment-refusal regressions (all pass):** `chat::tests::focused_restored_environment_refusal_keeps_slot_focus_and_notice`, `chat::tests::background_restored_environment_refusal_keeps_slot_and_opens_notice_on_focus`, `chat::tests::restored_environment_refusal_new_conversation_replaces_only_the_selected_slot`, `chat::tests::failed_refused_session_replacement_keeps_saved_id_and_notice`, `chat::tests::unrelated_forbidden_restore_keeps_existing_error_behaviour`, `chat::tests::session_picker_environment_refusal_keeps_selected_entry_and_notice`, `chat::tests::chat_entry_retry_adopts_restored_environment_refusal_action`, `chat::tests::restored_environment_refusal_requires_typed_code_and_specific_message`. On `c4f45eb508` the focused-refusal case promotes the background session over the refused one and shows no notice, so the first test's focus and notice assertions fail there.
- **Known failures:** `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` also fails on clean master `f2b432db` on this Mini (it passes when run alone). `app::tests::input_wait_returns_early_for_pending_transport_events` is a known timing flake (it passed in this run).
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** That both guards are load-bearing: with the local-only gate removed, `remote_connections_neither_save_nor_restore` fails; with the early publish removed, both `*_publishes_*` tests fail; with the live-window check removed, `sessions_open_in_another_running_window_are_not_restored` fails. Not yet verified: a real launch against a live daemon (see Screenshots below).
- **Intentionally skipped:** Full workspace tests; this change is confined to `apps/zerocode` and its docs page.

### Screenshots

Real screenshots pending.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? Yes: zerocode writes one new file plus an empty lock file per window slot and connection target under its own config directory. It is written owner-only (`0600`) and atomically, through the same `secure_file::write_private_atomic` funnel as `zerocode-config.toml`.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. The file holds session ids, agent aliases and the connection label (socket path or WSS URL). The label is already shown on the dashboard. Credentials are not stored.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: see the first item.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. A config file without `restore_sessions` restores (default on); a missing, damaged or newer-format list file is ignored.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: `[sidebar] restore_sessions` (env `ZEROCODE_sidebar__restore_sessions`) and the `--fresh` flag. Documented in `docs/book/src/zerocode/config.md`.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: nothing to do on upgrade. To keep the old behavior, set `restore_sessions = false` under `[sidebar]`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert the squash commit. Without a revert, set `[sidebar] restore_sessions = false` or launch with `--fresh`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `[sidebar] restore_sessions`, `--fresh`.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a launch that reopens sessions the user closed, or the toast "Could not save the open-session list".

prs.title: fix(channels): honor Telegram 429 retry_after via shared per-token flood gate
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Telegram Bot API 429 responses were treated like formatting failures: `sendMessage` retried immediately as plain text (a markdown→plain double-hit), draft edits kept their cadence, and the typing loop never noticed — so a rate-limited token got hammered, its penalty escalated, and finalized replies were lost (issue #11615).
  - This adds a flood-control gate (`TelegramRateLimiter`) shared **by the clones of one channel instance** (channel fields, spawned typing loop, approval paths) — it is *not* a registry keyed by bot token: separately constructed channels on the same token, including repeated one-off announcement factories, keep independent windows. Gated surface: the channel's text traffic — `sendMessage` (final answers, draft creation, approval prompts), `editMessageText` (draft updates, finalize), and `sendChatAction` in the recurring typing loop. Initial inbound typing hints, model-picker sends and text/markup edits, approval-resolution text edits, acknowledgement reactions, media uploads, `deleteMessage`, and `answerCallbackQuery` still post directly and are not covered by this gate.
  - Droppable calls (typing, draft edits) skip silently while the window is open. Deliver calls wait the window out bounded by a caller-side budget (`rate_limit_max_wait_secs`), **re-check the shared gate after sleeping**, and stop with a distinguishable budget-exhausted outcome if the window is still active — the budget bounds how long the caller waits, never the server deadline, so nothing is sent into an active window. On a fresh 429 a Deliver call retries once; a second 429 contributes its own (possibly longer) `retry_after` to the shared window and stops the formatting/resume/resend fallbacks — a 429 is not a formatting failure.
  - The recorded deadline keeps the later of the active and new values, so out-of-order concurrent 429 responses cannot shorten the window; an unrepresentable delay is rejected rather than clamped into permission to send sooner.
  - Honors `retry_after` from the JSON envelope (`parameters.retry_after`), with a `retry after <N>` description fallback and a 5s fallback when nothing is parseable.
  - Partial deliveries still suppress the orchestrator's full-answer resend via `FinalizePartialDelivery`, and flood-control exhaustion now stops the chunk-resume path as well instead of burning the wait budget twice. The pending-narration loop in multi-message finalization also stops on the terminal gate outcome: instead of burning three narration retries plus a final-answer wait on fresh budgets, it propagates the gate error, so the outer resend is suppressed without reporting an undelivered final answer as delivered.
  - Two new optional telegram channel config keys: `rate_limit_max_wait_secs` (default 60; `0` restores the default — it is not a disable switch) and `typing_refresh_interval_secs` (default 4, previously hardcoded). Both resolve from the live config authority at each use, including per-tick in the typing loop, so a published change applies to a running channel without a rebuild.
- **Scope boundary:** adaptive draft throttling and any listener-side changes are explicitly out of scope (per maintainer triage on #11615); no behavior change when no 429 occurs — the pre-send gate is a no-op on `Clear`.
- **Blast radius:** Outbound paths of the Telegram channel only (`send_text_chunks`, `send_draft`, `update_draft`, `finalize_draft`, `start_typing`, approval send) plus one guard in the orchestrator's finalize-fallback arm. No change to inbound/listener logic, other channels, or the agent loop. Defaults keep today's behavior for well-behaved tokens.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #11615. Related #11608.

### What this does, simply

Telegram tells throttled bots exactly when to come back (`retry_after` in the 429 body), but the channel ignored that and fired again immediately — markdown attempt, then plain attempt, then more draft edits and typing ticks. Each ignored window made the next one longer, and when the final reply finally hit the limit it was dropped: users saw drafts vanish mid-sentence. Now the channel records "blocked until N seconds" per channel instance (shared by its clones) the moment a gated call sees a 429, keeping the longest active deadline. Gated cosmetic traffic (recurring typing indicator, live draft edits) stays silent during the window; user-visible sends wait out the server-directed window up to a bounded caller budget and try again once. When the window clears within budget, the reply is late instead of dropped. When the window outlasts the budget, nothing is sent into it: the answer is held and an error is returned — this slice has no durable delivery queue or automatic later redelivery, so such a reply can go undelivered (WARN-logged) until the sender retries; the gated callers stop retrying inside the recorded window and suppress blind resends of accepted chunks. The direct-call exclusions listed above still apply.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — the rate-limit interaction is fully covered by mock-server tests (429-then-success, repeated limiting with escalating deadlines, blocked-window skipping, budget expiry without resend, mid-wait window extension, cancelled waiter, cross-chat window sharing, gated draft creation, live-config resolution, pending-narration finalize stop with zero and nonzero accepted prefixes); a live 429 cannot be induced reliably without flooding a real bot token.

### How I tested

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
env -u HTTP_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY -u ALL_PROXY cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels telegram
env -u HTTP_PROXY -u HTTPS_PROXY -u ALL_PROXY cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels finalize
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** channels/config unit and integration tests cover the changed surface (telegram channel + config schema).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` at workspace level shows pre-existing warnings in platform-conditional code outside this diff (unix-gated code on a Windows host, Windows-only service code); none originate from this change, and the channels crate itself is `-D warnings` clean. Two pre-existing `zeroclaw-config` test failures reproduce on unpatched master (`agent_bundle::…outside_shared_is_dropped_with_its_content`, `platform::native::…powershell_full_scripts_execute_with_native_semantics`).
- **Commands run and tail output (head `fe42c5d30`):** `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels telegram` → `test result: ok. 429 passed; 0 failed`; `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels finalize` → `test result: ok. 23 passed; 0 failed` (including the two new `finalize_stops_on_flood_gate_with_{zero,nonzero}_accepted_narration_prefix` regressions and the retained transient-retry controls).
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Author-reported live observation (distinct from CI signals): ran an earlier revision of this change as a production Windows service against live Telegram for 24h — 3 real 429s observed (previously 7+ per incident), zero `failed to reply` events, every post-429 turn delivered after the gate window. This predates the review-round semantics tightening; the current head's budget/no-resend and pending-narration-stop behavior is covered by the mock-server regressions above, not by live observation.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no presentation change.
