prs.title: feat(zerocode): configure per-pane session cap
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A ZeroCode pane could track at most 8 sessions (focused, background, and retained reconnect entries), fixed by a compile-time constant. Workloads that keep one session per worktree hit it quickly, and the daemon's own ACP `max_sessions` setting does not affect it.
  - A new `[sessions].max_tracked_per_pane` setting replaces the constant. The default stays 8; valid values are 1 through 32, so two panes at the maximum still fit the daemon's 64-session store.
  - The value is resolved once at startup. An out-of-range or malformed value stops startup with an error naming `[sessions]` instead of being silently normalized, as the issue asks for validation. The `ZEROCODE_sessions__max_tracked_per_pane` env override goes through the same check.
  - Every admission path uses it: the sidebar "+", Change directory, opening an existing session, and reconnect resume. The `zc-chat-session-cap` notice shows the configured value. The entry-retry pane carries the value so a retry does not reset it to 8.
  - The three per-session result channels are sized by the configured cap, as they were by the constant.
- **Scope boundary:** no daemon, RPC or runtime change; no Config-pane control yet (file and env only, documented as such); no sidebar UI change.
- **Blast radius:** `apps/zerocode` only (config loading, the two chat-like panes, the config reference page). Existing config files load unchanged; without `[sessions]` the limit is 8 as before.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10665. Supersedes #11729 (same feature as `[chat].max_sessions_per_pane` with clamping; closed in favour of this one).

### What this does, simply

Each ZeroCode window side can keep a limited number of conversations open at once. That limit was fixed at 8. This adds a setting for it. Nothing changes unless you set it: the default is still 8 and the highest allowed value is 32. A value outside that range is reported at startup rather than quietly changed.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface`: `tui`
- **Setup / preconditions:** a running daemon; in `zerocode-config.toml` add `[sessions]` with `max_tracked_per_pane = 3`.
- **Steps to run:** start ZeroCode, press the sidebar "+" until it stops adding sessions. Then set the value to `0` and start again.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the fourth press shows "Session limit for this pane reached (3)" and the focused session stays as it was. With `0`, startup fails with `max_tracked_per_pane must be between 1 and 32`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the setting is ignored; the limit is reached at 8.

### How I tested

```sh
rustfmt --edition 2024 --check apps/zerocode/src/{acp,app,chat}.rs apps/zerocode/src/config/mod.rs
cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zerocode
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the zerocode build, clippy and test jobs cover the changed crate; `Docs Style` covers the config reference page.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none known.
- **Commands run and tail output:** fmt, clippy and the hygiene gate clean. `cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode`: 1462 passed, 1 failed, 2 ignored; lib tests 52 passed. The one failure, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, also fails on untouched master on my build host and is unrelated.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Coverage:
  - config: default 8 and round trip; `[sessions]` written in the default file; 0 and 33 rejected; a non-integer rejected; env override wins over the file
  - pane: a cap of 2 refuses the sidebar "+" and the notice shows 2; a cap of 1 refuses attaching an existing session and keeps the focused one; channel capacity follows the cap; reconnect resume at a cap of 2 reattaches the background session
  - the existing cap tests (retained resume entries, Change directory at the cap) now read the pane's configured value
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: no layout change; the only visible difference is the number in an existing notice. I'm verifying this in the experiment build, which already carries this setting: https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261014T043851Z-2fb8b5092a60 (dogfood base https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/commit/0341618f9d69e31bf38300d134ba86e98491d49d).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** head `1dcb827ef8` (the reconnect-cap fix for @tidux's `>` finding); CI Required Gate green on it. The suite above first ran on `f0ab7cd30b28`. It was rerun on head `1dcb827ef8` on Linux x86_64 (Rust 1.98.0, 2026-10-30): `cargo test -p zerocode --no-fail-fast` gave lib 52 passed, bin 1564 passed / 0 failed / 2 ignored, and `terminal_disconnect` 3 passed. `insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` failed in the first full run and passed on rerun, in the full suite and alone. prs.title: fix(runtime): keep identity sections at the head of direct-path system prompts
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why.** Two independent system-prompt builders order their invariant sections differently. The session builder (`SystemPromptBuilder`) places the identity block (`## Project Context` — the AGENTS/SOUL/IDENTITY/USER bootstrap files) near the head, so it survives the head-retaining truncation in `finalize_system_prompt`. The direct builder (`build_system_prompt_with_mode_and_effective_tools`, used by cron `JobType::Agent` runs, CLI one-shots, headless/delegate surfaces, and channel startup) placed the same identity block after tools in compact mode and after tools, skills and workspace in full mode. Because budget truncation cuts the tail, an oversized direct-builder prompt can lose part or all of its identity content, depending on the retained prefix. Which builder is used and how much text is assembled determine the result.
- **Real incident that exposed it.** A production agent (telegram channel; ~45K chars of bootstrap workspace plus a skill bundle rendered in full mode) exceeded its 50K prompt cap. Channel conversations stayed in persona; every cron turn — including its weekly self-review — ran with none of the bootstrap files present. The failure is silent: no error, no warning; the agent simply stops being itself behind one of the two doors into the runtime.
- **Fix.** Move `append_project_context` to the head of the direct builder (before tools/skills/workspace), mirroring the session builder's order for both values of `compact_context`; emit a trace WARN (`error_key: agent.system_prompt_identity_truncated`, with retained/total/zone diagnostics) when truncation still cuts the identity zone, so silent persona loss becomes observable; regression tests cover identity survival under a small prompt cap through the real turn path, section-order parity between the two builders, and the WARN in partial/full-cut scenarios.
- **Why not unify the two builders in this PR.** Consumer-specific shells (interaction context, channel handles, tool advertising) legitimately differ between conversational and one-shot surfaces. What must not diverge is the survival contract of the invariant core. A shared layout module for invariant sections is the right follow-up and deliberately out of scope — this PR is the minimal, reviewable step that stops the bleeding.
- **Blast radius.** Any agent whose *assembled* prompt exceeds its cap and that runs through cron / CLI / headless paths. Channel startup also calls the direct builder, so channel-only agents can be affected. Prompts that fit the cap retain their section contents but receive the new ordering. One existing test's section-priority expectation updated to the new (identity-first) priority — a deliberate priority change, not a budget-check weakening (the exact unicode budget assertion is retained).
- **Linked issues:** none found. Related: the prompt-budget floor accounting in #11910 counts the floor; this fix ensures the floor actually reaches the request.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw has two prompt builders. One already places the agent’s identity before tools and skills; the other placed it later, where a prompt-size limit could cut it away first. This PR puts identity earlier in that builder too, including its background-task and channel-startup uses. It also warns when the limit cuts identity, although a matching heading inside a workspace file can still hide that warning.

## Testing (required)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — mechanics covered by unit tests; the A/B story is in the summary.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** required CI (Test, Lint, Format, clippy) — touches `zeroclaw-runtime` prompt assembly, covered by the workspace matrix.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none known.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  ```sh
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                 # OK
  cargo check -p zeroclaw-runtime --tests    # exit 0
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-runtime           # exit 0 (pre-existing warnings only)
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib agent::   # 1409 passed; 0 failed
  ```
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The new order was compared against the channel builder's `with_defaults` (identity second there — unchanged); the failing-then-passing boundary test proves identity was previously cut. Not verified: full-workspace `cargo test` / `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` (untouched crates go through the same functions; targeted `agent::` suite covers the changed surfaces).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** branch head; tests `turn_prompt_budget_truncation_retains_identity_bootstrap`, `identity_precedes_tools_and_skills_in_channel_and_direct_builders`, `identity_zone_truncation_warn_reaches_the_log_pipeline`.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** see above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No** — ordering change plus an operator-facing WARN; no new model-visible content beyond what the workspace already authored.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes** for prompts within budget (byte-identical sections, new order). For over-budget prompts, behavior changes intentionally: identity now survives at the expense of later sections — that is the fix.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No**
- Note: `zeroclaw-runtime` is a holding crate; this is a bugfix to an existing subsystem (no new functionality). Flagging per the crate guide in case a recorded exception row is required all the same.

## Rollback

`git revert <sha>` — additive ordering change plus tests; revert restores the previous (buggy) ordering.

## Summary
Windows `default_forbidden_paths()` previously mirrored the Unix secret homes (`~/.gnupg`, `~/.config`) and hard-coded English `C:\Windows` / `Program Files` spellings. Those Unix paths usually do not exist on Windows, and relocated system or profile directories were unprotected.

- Document the Windows defaults next to the Unix list in `docs/book/src/security/model.md`.
- Unit-test relocated env values and missing-env fallbacks via an injectable getenv helper.

Fixes #12124

prs.title: fix(setup.bat): persist user PATH without setx merge/crop
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Replaced both `setx PATH "%PATH%;%USERPROFILE%\.zeroclaw\bin"` call sites with `:add_zeroclaw_bin_to_user_path`, which reads/writes only the HKCU user Path via PowerShell `[Environment]::Get/SetEnvironmentVariable`.
  - Stops copying the merged process (machine+user) PATH into the user value and avoids setx’s 1024-character truncation that dropped the new bin entry and any prior user tail.
  - Fixed the `Expand-Archive` fallback to use `Join-Path` / `$env:USERPROFILE` instead of embedding `%USERPROFILE%` inside PowerShell single quotes (apostrophe-safe).
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change `install.sh`, Scoop, the documented PowerShell one-liner in `docs/book/src/setup/windows.md`, or non-PATH installer steps.
- **Blast radius:** Windows `setup.bat` prebuilt and source install routes only; future terminals get the user Path update via standard environment broadcast from `SetEnvironmentVariable`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12121

### What this does, simply

On Windows, `setup.bat` used to call `setx` with the current process `%PATH%`. That string already includes the machine PATH, so writing it back into the *user* Path duplicated machine entries and, when the combined length exceeded 1024 characters, silently cropped the value—often losing `%USERPROFILE%\.zeroclaw\bin` itself. The script now mirrors the maintained PowerShell install route: read the user Path only, prepend the bin dir when missing, write user Path only, and still update the current session’s PATH for immediate use.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (Windows installer script `setup.bat`)
- **Setup / preconditions:** Windows machine (or VM) where combined process Path length can be inspected; optional long user Path to reproduce the crop.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Note current user Path: `reg query HKCU\Environment /v Path`
  2. On `master`, run `setup.bat --prebuilt` (or a dry exercise of the PATH block) and re-query — observe merge/crop when Path is long.
  3. On this branch, run the same install path; re-query HKCU Path.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** User Path gains `%USERPROFILE%\.zeroclaw\bin` (or equivalent expanded form) only when absent; length can exceed 1024; value does not start with a dump of the machine Path. Current session can resolve `zeroclaw` after the session PATH prepend.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `setx` wrote the merged process Path into the user value and could truncate at 1024 chars so the bin dir never persisted.

### How I tested

- Static invariants on the changed script: no remaining `setx PATH`; both prebuilt and source routes call `:add_zeroclaw_bin_to_user_path`; Expand-Archive uses `Join-Path`/`$env:USERPROFILE`; helper uses `GetEnvironmentVariable`/`SetEnvironmentVariable` with `'User'` target.
- Pure logic self-check of the membership/join rules (empty user Path, already-present, long >1024 user Path) confirming append without truncation and without injecting a machine Path prefix.
- No Windows host in this environment, so end-to-end `setup.bat` / live registry write was not executed here; reviewer Windows smoke is requested above.
- AI-assisted change; human (submitter account) reviewed the diff before opening this PR.

```sh
# Invariants checked locally (Linux agent host):
python3 -c "t=open('setup.bat').read(); assert 'setx PATH' not in t; assert t.count('call :add_zeroclaw_bin_to_user_path')==2"
# Membership/join self-check for >1024 user Path (no registry writes)
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Default PR CI for the repo; script-only change, no Rust surface.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No Windows runner exercise of `setup.bat` PATH persistence in this PR’s local environment.
- **Commands run and tail output:** See above; self-check printed `self-check OK` / `setup.bat invariants OK`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Diff review of both former `setx` sites and the Expand-Archive quoting fix. Did **not** verify on a real Windows registry.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — installer script / env persistence only; no UI layout change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `9c70b15` / `setup.bat` / logic self-check on agent host.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A (no live Windows run)

prs.title: fix(channels): classify telegram transcription failures and bound transient retries
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - Every error from `manager.transcribe` in the Telegram voice path became `UpdateDisposition::RetryTransient`, so a terminally rejected voice update pinned the long-poll offset and head-of-line blocked every later message until an operator intervened (#10863; production incident reported in #10640, where an ASR endpoint's persistent HTTP 413 wedged the channel for ~8 minutes and survived restarts).
  - Transcription providers now classify failures: substantiated payload-specific terminal rejections (HTTP 413/415, plus local pre-flight byte-cap and format rejections) are `Permanent`; credential (401/403), rate-limit, 5xx, transport, and unrecognised failures stay `Transient` — the same conservative philosophy as the `getFile` classifier (#9314/#9315): retrying a recoverable failure is safe, skipping a recoverable one loses a message.
  - The Telegram voice parser acknowledges terminal rejections with a new sender notice (`VoiceDropReason::TranscriptionRejected`, Fluent key added in en/es/fr/ja/zh-CN) instead of retrying forever — the same contract as the existing duration and file-lookup drops.
  - A bounded transient budget (10 consecutive attempts per update) acknowledges a persistently failing update with a loud ERROR (update id + attempt count) instead of retrying it forever, so failures that can never be classified as permanent but never recover either (e.g. an endpoint returning 500 for one corrupted file) cannot wedge the channel indefinitely. Giving up is explicit and observable, never silent.
- Deepgram, AssemblyAI (upload step), and Google STT now check `!status.is_success()` before JSON deserialization, so a proxy/gateway 413/415 with a plain-text or HTML body classifies as `Permanent` instead of falling into an untyped JSON-parse failure (misread as retryable `Transient`). Error bodies are read as text, extracting the vendor JSON message when present. AssemblyAI `create`/`poll` carry no audio bytes, so their non-success statuses stay explicitly `Transient` instead of masquerading as a payload rejection.
- **Scope boundary:** media-group batch retry machinery unchanged; `getFile`/download classification unchanged; other channels' transcription call sites unchanged (they do not acknowledge vendor offsets); no config, CLI, or schema changes; `TranscriptionProvider` trait signature unchanged (classification rides inside the `anyhow` chain).
- **Blast radius:** Telegram channel update-disposition path (voice parse + single-update retry gate); transcription error construction sites in `zeroclaw-channels/src/transcription.rs`; one new Fluent key in runtime locale catalogs.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10863. Related #10640, #9314, #9315.

### What this does, simply

When someone sends a voice note, the Telegram channel downloads the audio and hands it to a transcription endpoint. If that call fails, the channel used to retry the update forever — including failures that could never succeed, like the endpoint rejecting the recording as too long. Because Telegram redelivers unacknowledged updates first, one poisoned voice note blocked every message behind it, for every chat of the bot, and restarts did not help.

This PR makes the failure handling distinguish two cases. If the endpoint rejected *this recording* (too large, unsupported format), retrying is pointless: the channel now tells the sender why their voice note was dropped and moves on — the same way it already handles over-duration recordings and expired files. If the failure might recover (endpoint down, rate limit, bad credentials awaiting an operator fix), the update is still retried as before. As a safety net for failures that claim to be recoverable but never actually recover, an update is given up loudly after 10 consecutive attempts: an ERROR log names the update id and attempt count, so the message loss is explicit and observable rather than silent — which is the recovery policy the issue asks for.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A` — the behavior boundary is covered by new wiremock-driven listener tests that replay the production incident shape (persistent 413) and the recovery shape (500 then 200); no manual Telegram setup adds signal beyond them.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` = `telegram` (voice transcription path)
- **Setup / preconditions:** N/A
- **Steps to run:** N/A
- **Expected on this branch (after):** N/A
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** N/A

### How I tested

New focused tests, all at the real behavior boundary:

- `listen_terminally_rejected_transcription_does_not_block_later_updates` — the incident replay: voice update, ASR endpoint consistently answers 413 `audio duration exceeds limit`; the voice update is acknowledged with exactly one sender notice, and the text update behind it is delivered with the offset advancing past both.
- `listen_recoverable_transcription_failure_retries_and_delivers` — 500 once, then 200: the same update is retried at the same offset and delivered as `[Voice] recovered words`.
- `process_update_acknowledges_update_after_transient_budget_exhausted` — the transient budget gate: an update at the attempt cap is acknowledged with no further I/O; below the cap or for a different update id, routing is unchanged.
- `try_parse_voice_message_terminally_rejected_transcription_notifies_sender` — the sender notice carries the new dedicated wording to the right chat.
- `transcription.rs` unit tests: status classification (only 413/415 permanent; 400/401/403/408/409/422/425/429/451/5xx transient), local validation rejections classified permanent, `failure_kind` recovery through `anyhow` context layers and its transient default, and a wiremock pass over the Groq provider proving 413 → permanent while 500/429 → transient.
- Provider-path regressions (wiremock, added with the review fix): `deepgram_non_json_413_is_classified_permanent` (HTML 413 body → `Permanent`; vendor-JSON 413 keeps the readable message), `assemblyai_upload_413_is_permanent_but_metadata_413_stays_transient` (upload-step 413 → `Permanent`; create-step 413 → `Transient`), `google_stt_non_json_413_is_classified_permanent`.

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-telegram
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** workspace `fmt` / `clippy` / test jobs cover `zeroclaw-channels` and the locale catalogs; the new tests run in the standard channels suite.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** 5 `link_enricher` tests fail in this Windows/localhost/VPN environment — pre-existing on clean `master` (localhost networking restriction), unrelated to this diff. CI (Linux) is expected green.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → clean (after one `cargo fmt --all` normalization pass over the new tests).
  - `cargo +1.98.0 clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-telegram --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` → `Finished dev profile` (no lints in the crate; `--no-deps` because path-dependency `zeroclaw-config` trips pre-existing Windows-only `collapsible_if` lints on this host that Linux CI never compiles).
  - `cargo +1.98.0 test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-telegram` → `test result: FAILED. 1958 passed; 5 failed` — the 5 failures are the pre-existing `link_enricher` localhost cases above; every telegram/transcription test passes.
  - Filtered re-runs of the 9 new tests (`terminally_rejected`, `recoverable_transcription`, `transient_budget`, `failure_kind`, `http_status_classification`, `local_validation`, `whisper_style_http`) → all `ok`.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The classification mirrors the existing `FileLookupError::classify` philosophy and the voice-drop notice plumbing (`notify_voice_drop`, bounded notice timeout) is shared with the three existing drop reasons. Not verified: a live Telegram bot end-to-end run (covered instead by the wiremock listener tests at the same boundary the existing offset tests use).
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` — no user-visible interface state changed; the only new user-facing string is a chat notice delivered through the existing `sendMessage` path, asserted by exact text in tests.

- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A

- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full `cargo test` workspace run — the change is contained to `zeroclaw-channels` (+ one locale key); focused crate suite plus CI covers the rest.

milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(config)!: forbid /mnt,/media,/run/media and Windows drive/UNC defaults
prs.body:
## Summary
Fixes #12134.

Under Full autonomy (`workspace_only = false`), the default denylist stopped at OS directories and left WSL DrvFs (`/mnt/c/...`), `/media`, `/run/media`, non-system Windows drives, and UNC shares open while the matching Linux/Windows system homes were refused.

- **Unix defaults:** add `/mnt`, `/media`, `/run/media`.
- **Windows defaults:** deny every drive-letter root (`A:\`…`Z:\`) in addition to the existing `C:\Windows` / Program Files spellings; refuse UNC shares in the path checkers when no allow entry matched.
- **Most-specific-match unchanged:** a workspace or `allowed_roots` entry under those trees (common WSL layout) still wins by depth.
- **Filesystem channel:** reject single-letter `/mnt/<x>` watches unless `allow_broad_roots = true`; named binds such as `/mnt/inbox` stay allowed.
- **Docs:** `docs/book/src/security/model.md` lists the new defaults.

This is a deliberate behavior change for operators who relied on Full autonomy to roam those trees; `allowed_roots` remains the opt-in.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --test mnt_forbidden_paths`
- [x] `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib checklist_default_forbidden`
- [x] `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib filesystem_validate_rejects_drvfs`
- [x] `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib filesystem_validate_allows_named_mnt`

## AI disclosure
Prepared with AI assistance. I reviewed the diff, ran the tests listed above, and take responsibility for the change.

prs.title: feat(gateway): bind each core connection to its caller's credential
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. **Stacked on #11186** and contains its commits: #11186's branch lives on a fork, so a PR here cannot target it. Review only the last three commits, `feat(gateway): bind each core connection to its caller's credential`, `fix(gateway): keep pooled core connections bound, bounded and truthful about refusals` and `fix(gateway): let a capacity waiter take a connection a request lets go of`, until #11186 merges.
- **What changed and why:**
  - #11186 gave the in-process gateway one `RpcClient` to the core. It dialed at startup with no credential, so the core refused it and the seam stayed idle. One shared client also could not carry each caller's identity. This replaces it with a pool of connections keyed by `(auth provider, SHA-256 of the bearer)` over #11186's `InprocConnector`. Each HTTP request uses the connection its own credential opened and no other, so routes can move onto RPC with the caller's own principal (#11280 and #11331).
  - **No credential-less core connection, ever.** A request whose credential is absent, blank, malformed, over-long, or names a provider that cannot verify a bearer gets `401 auth_required` before any connection is opened or reused. Every handshake the pool sends carries `auth_token` and `auth_provider`. The pool has no probe, heartbeat or background reconnect: it dials only for a request, with that request's credential. This matters beyond the in-process transport, which already refuses an anonymous `initialize`. On a Unix socket the core admits a same-uid peer that presents nothing as the shared operator, and with no `[users]` roster any local peer gets in through local compatibility. When the gateway later dials the real socket, a tokenless path would not fail, it would escalate.
  - **Only the pool initializes a connection**, always with the credential its key came from. `CoreCall::request` refuses `initialize` locally, so a request cannot rebind a pooled connection to another credential or send a tokenless handshake.
  - **Local checks are shape only.** The gateway refuses an absent, blank, malformed or over-long bearer, or a provider that cannot verify a bearer, before any dial. Whether a well-formed bearer is valid, and whether a well-formed `oidc.<alias>` is a configured provider, is the core's call. It is made on one dial that presents the credential; a refusal answers `401` and nothing stays pooled. While the core is unreachable, a well-formed credential cannot be judged and answers `503`.
  - A credential the core refuses, at the handshake or later (revoked, expired, re-verification due), answers `401`, and its connection is discarded and closed. `FORBIDDEN` answers `403` and the connection leaves the pool. **A core reply stands even if the connection closes right after it:** only the client's locally synthesized `INTERNAL_ERROR` (request undeliverable, connection dropped before a reply) is read as a lost connection. The request is never retried without the credential or with another one. An unreachable or lost core answers `503 core_unavailable`. A request that times out answers `504 core_timeout`, and its connection is not reused.
  - **Bounds are on open connections, not on map entries.** At most 64 core connections are open at once. A connection takes its capacity before it is dialed and gives it back only when it closes, so connections being dialed and connections a request still holds after leaving the pool both count. When the pool is full, the least recently used connection no request holds is closed to make room (ended ones first). If every connection is in use, the request waits up to 5 seconds and is then answered `503 core_busy`. While it waits, a request that lets go of its connection wakes it, so it can close that now-idle connection instead of waiting out the deadline. The wake-up is sent only after the finished request has released its hold, so a waiter that re-checks immediately on another worker finds the connection evictable. A connection idle for 10 minutes leaves the pool, unless a request still holds it.
  - `CoreAccess` is an axum extractor over `Authorization` and `X-ZeroClaw-Auth-Provider`. A route that lacks the handle fails closed with `503` rather than falling back to the in-process path.
- **Scope boundary:** no route is ported; nothing calls `CoreAccess` yet (#11280 and #11331 do). No change to #11186's client, connector or transport. No endpoint verification: that is handled by #11274, and it must run before any credential is written once the gateway dials a real socket. The pool's dialer today returns an in-memory duplex. One connection per credential for now; the contract's split into a stream connection and a request connection comes with the first streaming route.
- **Blast radius:** `zeroclaw-gateway` only: `core_rpc.rs` and the seam's wiring in `run_gateway_with_plugin_webhooks`. #11186's startup dial is removed, so a supervised gateway no longer opens a core connection at startup; the pool dials on demand. Nothing else in the workspace uses `CoreRpc` (checked, including the root crate's integration tests).
- **Linked issue(s):** Part of #11002. Depends on #11186.
- **Labels:** `release:v0.9.0`

### Decision pending (authentication for routes served through the core)

With `gateway.require_pairing = false`, an HTTP caller presents no credential by design. This PR implements the recommended default: **ported routes require a bearer; a pairing-disabled install keeps the route's in-process body** (`CoreAccess::InProcess`). Each request asks the same pairing authority the in-process routes check. That authority fixes the setting for its daemon generation, and a reload brings a new one. A caller that selects a provider with `X-ZeroClaw-Auth-Provider` is still authenticated (or refused) even when pairing is off. It is never waved through. The bearer requirement and the fallback when pairing is disabled are pending with the maintainer. If the ruling differs, the change is confined to `CoreRpc::access`.

### Known limits and follow-ups (review Lows not changed here)

- **`FORBIDDEN` discards the connection**, as contract ID-4 reads today. For a scoped OIDC principal that polls a denied panel, that means a fresh dial and token verification per poll. Raised for the contract: whether `-32012` should keep the connection. If it changes, it is one arm in `CoreCall::request`.
- **The bearer length ceiling is 8 KiB.** Some identity providers mint larger access tokens (large group claims). This needs confirming against the gateway's header limits and the OIDC deployments in scope before the first OIDC-reachable route is ported.
- **The streaming connection (ID-6's second connection per credential) is not here.** When it lands, a live subscription must count as use for the idle sweep, as a held request already does.
- A `risk:*` label is for a maintainer to apply; the risk-report job was cancelled on the first run.

### What this does, simply

The web gateway is being turned into a separate program that talks to the ZeroClaw core over a local connection. For that to be safe, each web user's requests must reach the core as that user, and nothing may reach the core as "nobody". On a local socket, "nobody" is often treated as the machine's owner. This PR adds the gateway's connection manager: it opens one core connection per user token, never shares a connection between tokens, turns away requests with missing or bad tokens before touching the core, and drops a user's connection as soon as the core says the token is no longer valid. No web page uses it yet. Moving pages onto it is the next step.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. No route uses the pool yet, so there is no user-visible behaviour to click through; the unit tests below drive the extractor through a real axum router and the daemon's real in-process connector.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` runs the gateway unit tests (the new `core_rpc` suite), clippy and the build over the changed crate.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none for this change; a real-socket dial is out of scope until endpoint verification (#11274) and the gateway binary land.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
At 93e0f32cba (third commit): the same suite, 30 passed, including
test core_rpc::tests::a_waiter_takes_the_capacity_a_request_lets_go_of ... ok
test core_rpc::tests::a_waiter_woken_by_a_release_finds_the_connection_evictable ... ok
clippy --all-targets -D warnings, rustdoc -D warnings, fmt and the comment hygiene gate pass.
The second test polls the waiting reservation inside the wake-up itself, the
ordering another worker can hit. With the wake-up moved ahead of the release
of the request's hold, it fails: "an idle connection existed before the
deadline, but reserve answered Some(Err(Busy))".

At 485ce0b0e1:
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                               → exit 0
cargo check --all-targets -p zeroclaw-gateway                            → exit 0

RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p zeroclaw-gateway --no-deps       → exit 0
cargo check -p zeroclaw --tests                                          → exit 0
scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                                       → Comment hygiene gate passed.

cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib core_rpc
```

The review regressions are live. With three mutations applied together (the `initialize` guard disabled, replies judged by connection state again, and capacity taken from an unbounded semaphore), 7 of the 28 fail, one or more per defect:

```text

test core_rpc::tests::a_pooled_connection_cannot_be_rebound_to_keep_a_revoked_bearer_working ... FAILED
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The invariant tests are live. With one line changed so that an unusable credential falls through to a dial with an empty token (`bearer(headers).unwrap_or("")`), 5 of the original 17 failed at 2d757926eb, including the test against the daemon's real in-process connector:

  ```text

  ```

  Also checked by hand:
  - The removed `CoreRpc` API (`attach_inproc`, `client`, `is_connected`) has no callers outside this module and the gateway's wiring. That includes the root crate's integration tests.
  - No log line carries a bearer: the pool logs the provider and the error code only.

  Not verified: a real socket or named-pipe dial, which waits on endpoint verification (#11274) and the gateway binary.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no user-visible interface state changed)
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 485ce0b0e1 and 93e0f32cba, `core_rpc` unit tests (fake core over an in-memory duplex, plus the daemon's real `InprocConnector`)
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** the test output above
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** see the test list
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:**
  - The full workspace test suite runs in CI.
  - Clippy runs with `--no-deps`: the local toolchain is older than CI's pinned 1.98 and flags an existing lint in the untouched `zeroclaw-infra`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:
  - The gateway now forwards an HTTP caller's bearer to the core, inside `initialize` only, on an in-process connection.
  - The pool keeps only the bearer's SHA-256 as its key. The bearer itself lives in the request that presented it and in the handshake frame, never in pool state or logs. Log lines carry the provider and the error code only.
  - The risk this closes is the reverse: a credential-less connection resolving to the shared operator. The invariant tests assert that no handshake without `auth_token` ever reaches the core, across every refusal path.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. No route changes behaviour. The removed startup dial was refused by the core anyway and served nothing.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>` restores #11186's idle seam. No route depends on the pool yet.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** once routes use it, a `401 auth_required` for a caller whose bearer the core accepts, or a `503 core_unavailable` while the daemon runs. The gateway logs `core refused a gateway caller's handshake` (INFO, with provider and code) and `gateway could not open a core connection` (WARN).

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(runtime): enforce the system prompt size budget (fail closed)
prs.body:
Fixes #11908.

## What

The `max_system_prompt_chars` runtime-profile limit was advisory only. This makes it a hard gate and removes the unlimited default:

- **Fail closed in the turn gate** (`turn/mod.rs`): when the assembled system-prompt floor reaches/exceeds the context budget, the turn returns a typed `SystemPromptFloorExceedsBudget` error **before dispatch** — the over-budget request no longer reaches the provider. The historical WARN keeps its `error_key: context_floor_exceeds_budget` so existing trace dashboards still match.
- **Finite safe default** (`schema.rs`): `default_max_system_prompt_chars()` 0 → 50000. An explicit `= 0` in a profile keeps opt-in unlimited.
- **Workspace bootstrap respects the cap** for `compact_context = false` sessions (oversized-bootstrap regression test: 5×200K files under a 50000 cap).

## What this is NOT

The budget is resolved atomically with the rest of the profile from one generation-stamped config snapshot (`resolved_agent_config`), and the new gate measures the provider-bound request — the suspected snapshot-race and history-vs-request divergence paths were inspected and do not reproduce as independent defects; the gate now rejects any such bypass regardless.

## Tests

New regression tests (prefix `prompt_budget_cap_`): gate trip conditions, typed+localized refusal, capped workspace bootstrap with `compact_context = false`, finite schema default.

## Notes for reviewers

- Behavior change: a turn that would previously dispatch with a flooded system prompt now fails with a clear, localized error. Operators see the remediation text instead of a silent confabulated reply.
- `turn/mod.rs`/`outcome.rs` touched — happy to add the ADR-016 exception row if required (per #11578/#11625 precedent).

prs.title: fix(runtime): restore agent_alias attribution on cron/gateway agent runs
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** cron- and gateway-triggered agent runs emitted the tool/provider/turn records of the run body without `agent_alias` (only `cron_job_id` / `risk_profile` survived). Root cause: `agent::run` and `process_message_inner` build the run body as `body.instrument(scope_span).instrument(attribution_span)`, but the log layer walks *recorded span parents* — the scope span is created eagerly in the prologue, so it records the caller context as its parent and the agent attribution span never enters the walked chain.
- Fix: name the attribution span as the scope span's parent (`parent: &__zc_attribution_span`) in both call sites, with a comment explaining the mechanism so the pattern is not reintroduced.
- Regression test `run_body_scope_span_keeps_agent_attribution_reachable` mirrors the production wiring and asserts `agent_alias` + `risk_profile` reach an event emitted from a nested tool span.
- **Scope boundary:** no change to span creation in the channel orchestrator (its lazily-entered scope spans are correct); no changes to cron scheduling/delivery or to the log merge algorithm itself.
- **Blast radius:** observability consumers only. Cron-run events now carry `zc_role: "agent"` (nearest attribution wins by design) alongside the preserved `cron_job_id`; consumers that filter cron runs by `zc_role == "cron"` should filter by presence of `cron_job_id` instead.
- **Linked issues:** none open for this exact defect.

### What this does, simply

Every log event is signed with the agent that produced it by walking the chain of recorded span parents, leaf to root, and merging attribution found along the way. Cron and gateway runs assembled their span stack in a way that silently cut the agent label out of that chain: the "small" scope span was stamped with the caller as its parent before the "big" agent-attribution span was placed around the body, so events emitted under the scope span walked past the agent label and found only the outer cron label. The result was fully anonymous cron runs — tool failures no monitoring rule could attribute to an agent, per-agent metrics missing for every non-channel run. The fix stamps the scope span with the attribution span as its parent at creation, so the walked chain is whole: events carry the agent alias again, and the cron job id is retained next to it.

Verified in production A/B on our own deployment: pre-fix cron run of a worker agent — ~200 events, none with `agent_alias`; post-fix run — all 52 events carry `agent_alias` + `cron_job_id`, including a failed tool call that previously would have been an anonymous failure record.

## Testing (required)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — the regression test covers the wiring; the change is invisible to interactive surfaces and the pre/post delta is shown by the regression test and the A/B evidence above.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** required CI (`Test`, `Lint`, `Format`, clippy) — the changed surface is zeroclaw-runtime, covered by the workspace test matrix.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** none known.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  ```sh
  cargo fmt --all -- --check
  cargo check -p zeroclaw-runtime --tests   # exit 0 (pre-existing unrelated warnings only)
  ```
  Additionally, a standalone probe against the real `zeroclaw-log`/`zeroclaw-api` path dependencies reproduced the defect on the old wiring (`agent_alias: null`) and confirmed attribution on the fixed wiring (`{"agent_alias":"probe_agent","risk_profile":"probe-risk","tool":"probe_tool","zc_role":"agent"}`).
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Production A/B before/after deploying the patch: cron-run events of a live worker agent transitioned from fully anonymous to fully attributed, with `cron_job_id` preserved. Not verified: channel-path regression (its span wiring is untouched and covered by existing tests).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** revision `039287065`; evidence: JSONL runtime trace events of a cron-spawned agent run.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** full `cargo test` of zeroclaw-runtime not run locally (long compile); the new regression test is exercised by required CI.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No**
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**

## Compatibility (required)

prs.title: fix(desktop): refuse in-app self-upgrade of a desktop-bundled kernel
prs.body:
> Implements the recommended refusal of in-app upgrades for a desktop-bundled kernel, which is pending with the maintainer; not for merge until decided.

## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - **The problem.** Every ZeroClaw Desktop package installs its kernel sidecar in the same directory as the `zeroclaw-desktop` app executable. I checked this against the installers the desktop bundle dry run produced:
    - macOS: `ZeroClaw.app/Contents/MacOS/{zeroclaw, zeroclaw-desktop}`
    - Linux `.deb`: `/usr/bin/{zeroclaw, zeroclaw-desktop}` (the AppImage uses the same `usr/bin` layout)
    - Windows MSI: `zeroclaw.exe` and `zeroclaw-desktop.exe` in the install directory. The MSI also adds that directory to `PATH`.

    With `gateway.allow_self_upgrade` enabled, the dashboard's in-app upgrade ran `zeroclaw update` against that sidecar and swapped it in place. The desktop app and its kernel then run different versions. On macOS the swap also modifies a signed, notarized bundle. The next desktop update overwrites the swapped kernel anyway.
  - **Ownership rule** (revised after review; the first head keyed on co-location alone, which a `zeroclaw-desktop` launcher symlink in a shared `bin` directory could fake). A kernel is package-owned only when both hold:
    1. **It was built as a sidecar.** `scripts/desktop/prepare-kernel.sh`, the only step that builds the desktop sidecar (release jobs and the bundle dry run), now builds with `ZEROCLAW_DESKTOP_SIDECAR=1`, and the kernel reads that marker at compile time. Homebrew, cargo, `install.sh`, the release archives and workspace builds never carry it.
    2. **It still sits in its package.** The directory the kernel really lives in (resolving a symlink *to* the kernel) holds `zeroclaw-desktop` (`zeroclaw-desktop.exe` on Windows) as a regular file. A symlink *named* like the app does not count, because symlinks there are not followed. A sidecar copied out of its package therefore keeps its own upgrade path.

    The check lives in `zeroclaw_runtime::restart::desktop_bundled_kernel`, the runtime owner of the desktop-supervised contracts. The gateway delegates to it, so a later runtime-side upgrade path can apply the same guard.
  - **Refusal.** `POST /api/version/upgrade` refuses a package-owned kernel with 403: "this ZeroClaw was installed by ZeroClaw Desktop; update the desktop app to upgrade it". The existing `allow_self_upgrade` gate is still checked first.
  - **Status and dashboard.** `/api/status` gains `desktop_bundled`. The upgrade dialog shows "This ZeroClaw was installed with ZeroClaw Desktop. Update the desktop app to upgrade it." in place of the Upgrade button.
  - **What decides ownership.** How the kernel was built and where it lives decide, not whether the process is desktop-supervised. A kernel installed separately (Homebrew, cargo, `install.sh`) that the desktop app finds on `PATH` and supervises keeps both the in-app upgrade and the desktop-supervised restart. That holds even when a `zeroclaw-desktop` launcher sits beside it.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Not changed: the CLI `zeroclaw update`, `allow_self_upgrade` semantics (still the config value), restart classification, and the desktop app itself.
  - Only the English dashboard string is added. Other locales fall back to English until the next catalog fill.
- **Blast radius:**
  - The dashboard's in-app upgrade for kernels shipped inside a desktop package.
  - `/api/status` gains one boolean field. The status contract test is updated.
  - `ZEROCLAW_KERNEL_PATH` (reusing a prebuilt kernel in `prepare-kernel.sh`) now also requires that kernel to have been built with `ZEROCLAW_DESKTOP_SIDECAR=1`, or the package will not refuse its self-upgrade. The release workflow does not use it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Part of #11004
- **Labels:** `release:v0.9.0` (path and size labels are applied by the labelers)

### What this does, simply

When ZeroClaw Desktop is installed, it brings its own copy of ZeroClaw along with it. If someone had turned on "upgrade from the dashboard", clicking Upgrade replaced that bundled copy with a newer one. The desktop app was left running with a ZeroClaw it wasn't shipped with, and on a Mac the app's signed bundle was modified.

Now ZeroClaw recognizes when it is the copy that came with the desktop app, because the desktop app's program sits right next to it. In that case the dashboard says to update the desktop app instead of offering the Upgrade button. A ZeroClaw installed some other way, even if the desktop app is running it, upgrades from the dashboard exactly as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, optional. This needs a desktop package plus `gateway.allow_self_upgrade = true` and a newer release available.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web` (dashboard upgrade dialog); `/api/status`, `/api/version/upgrade`
- **Setup / preconditions:**
  - A kernel directory containing both `zeroclaw` and a file named `zeroclaw-desktop`, for example an installed desktop package or a copy of a built `zeroclaw` next to an empty `zeroclaw-desktop`.
  - `gateway.allow_self_upgrade = true`.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Start `zeroclaw daemon` from that directory.
  2. Open the dashboard's version badge.
  3. `curl -X POST` `/api/version/upgrade` with a bearer token.
- **Expected on this branch (after):**
  - `/api/status` has `"desktop_bundled": true`.
  - The dialog shows the desktop-app message and no Upgrade button.
  - The POST returns 403 with the desktop hint.
  - Remove `zeroclaw-desktop` and restart: `desktop_bundled` is `false` and upgrade behaves as before.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the Upgrade button shows, and the POST returns 202 and swaps the kernel in the package directory.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:**
  - The `Quality Gate` gateway tests and lint cover the Rust.
  - The web checks (`cargo web check`, `npm run test:permissions`) cover the dialog.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No CI job runs an installed desktop package against a live release feed. The ownership rule is tested against temporary install directories, and the layouts were checked against real installers from the bundle dry run.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

Ownership rule, at the revised head:

```text
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- restart::
test restart::tests::sidecar_beside_its_desktop_app_is_package_owned ... ok
test restart::tests::kernel_not_built_as_a_sidecar_is_never_package_owned ... ok
test restart::tests::sidecar_copied_out_of_its_package_is_not_package_owned ... ok
test restart::tests::desktop_app_name_must_be_a_regular_file ... ok
test restart::tests::path_kernel_beside_a_desktop_launcher_symlink_is_not_package_owned ... ok
test restart::tests::path_symlink_to_a_packaged_sidecar_is_package_owned ... ok
test restart::tests::test_builds_are_not_desktop_sidecars ... ok
test restart::tests::the_desktop_packaging_step_builds_sidecars_with_the_marker ... ok
test restart::tests::desktop_app_executable_matches_the_tauri_package ... ok
test result: ok. 12 passed; 0 failed

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib -- version:: api_status_contract
test version::tests::self_upgrade_refusal_keeps_the_config_gate_first ... ok
test version::tests::self_upgrade_refusal_blocks_only_desktop_package_kernels ... ok
test version::tests::a_kernel_not_built_as_a_desktop_sidecar_keeps_its_self_upgrade ... ok
test result: ok. 15 passed; 0 failed
```

Mutation check. Each edit was applied, the tests were run, and the file was restored. Every mutant fails:

| Mutant | Failing test(s) |
|---|---|
| follow symlinks when looking for the app (`metadata` instead of `symlink_metadata`) | `path_kernel_beside_a_desktop_launcher_symlink_is_not_package_owned` |
| ignore the sidecar marker | `kernel_not_built_as_a_sidecar_is_never_package_owned` |
| do not resolve a symlink to the kernel | `path_symlink_to_a_packaged_sidecar_is_package_owned` |
| the first head's predicate (no marker, `is_file()` beside either path) | `kernel_not_built_as_a_sidecar_is_never_package_owned`, `path_kernel_beside_a_desktop_launcher_symlink_is_not_package_owned` |
| refusal ignores `desktop_bundled` (from the first head) | `self_upgrade_refusal_blocks_only_desktop_package_kernels` |

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                -> EXIT:0
$ cargo clippy --locked --no-deps -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings   -> EXIT:0 (first head)
$ cargo check --locked -p zeroclaw --tests                                   -> Finished (first head)
$ cargo web check          (regenerated TS client includes `desktop_bundled: boolean`; tsc -b) -> EXIT:0
$ npm run test:permissions (includes the UpgradeDialog logic tests)          -> # fail 0 across all suites
$ scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh crates/zeroclaw-gateway/src             -> Comment hygiene gate passed.
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - The installed layouts listed above, by inspecting the macOS `.dmg`, Linux `.deb` and Windows `.msi` produced by the desktop bundle dry run.
  - `desktop_app_executable_matches_the_tauri_package` fails if the desktop crate is renamed or a Tauri `mainBinaryName` is introduced, since either would change the installed app name.
  - `the_desktop_packaging_step_builds_sidecars_with_the_marker` fails if a `cargo build` in `prepare-kernel.sh` stops setting `ZEROCLAW_DESKTOP_SIDECAR=1`.
  - **Not verified:** a live upgrade attempt against a real release on an installed desktop package.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A: the change adds one conditional line of existing muted-text styling in place of the disabled note, with no layout change. Covered by the dialog logic tests.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The revision's clippy pass is left to the required Lint job. The shared host was below its disk floor for another build; the revision's test builds compiled the touched code with no new warnings. No workspace-wide build.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. It reads whether a file exists beside the running executable.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A. The change narrows an existing opt-in binary-replacement surface.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for every install except the desktop-bundled kernel with `allow_self_upgrade = true`. That case now refuses the in-app upgrade by design and points at the desktop app's update.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. The API adds the `desktop_bundled` status field.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert <sha>`.

prs.title: fix(providers): honor Ollama and llama.cpp thinking controls
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Ollama and llama.cpp collected the alias `think` setting and global `runtime.reasoning_enabled` switch but dropped them when constructing compatible requests. The factories now forward explicit on/off controls across text, tool, and streaming requests, including llama.cpp Responses.
- **Scope boundary:** This repairs forwarding and clarifies the existing settings. Models and templates must support an off mode for generation to stop.
- **Blast radius:** Local provider construction and config descriptions. Other compatible families keep their current behavior; regression tests check that boundary.
- **Linked issue(s):** No existing issue identified for this exact omission.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `docs`, `config`, `provider`, `distinguished contributor`, `risk:medium`, `size:L`.

### What this does, simply

Saving `think = false` on an Ollama or llama.cpp alias previously left the backend's mode unchanged. The alias now sends the backend's off request. When `think` is unset, these providers inherit the global runtime switch; when both switches are unset, backend defaults remain in effect.

Ollama receives `reasoning_effort`. llama.cpp Chat Completions also receives the boolean `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`, while llama.cpp Responses receives `reasoning.effort`. An explicit alias setting wins over the global switch. Chat Completions overrides conflicting manual reasoning fields while preserving unrelated request options. For enabled thinking, effort is selected from `provider_extra.reasoning_effort`, then `provider_extra.reasoning.effort`, then `runtime.reasoning_effort`; the first non-empty, non-`none` string wins, otherwise `"medium"` is used. llama.cpp Responses uses that selected effort but does not forward other `provider_extra` fields or `chat_template_kwargs`.

The config descriptions distinguish these mode controls from native thinking budgets and Anthropic's display option. Disabling an added budget or leaving a display option unset does not disable a model's own reasoning.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for a live backend smoke check.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli`; provider HTTP requests. No messaging channel changes.
- **Setup / preconditions:** A test ZeroClaw instance and agent using llama.cpp with Gemma 4 26B A4B and its current chat template.
- **Steps to run:** Set the provider alias's `think = false`, rebuild, restart/reload the test instance, and start a fresh chat. Ask `What is 17 multiplied by 23? Reply with only the number.` Repeat with `think = true`, then unset the alias value and test `runtime.reasoning_enabled = false`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The off Chat request contains `reasoning_effort="none"` and `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false`. A supporting Gemma template generates the answer without a reasoning trace. The alias overrides the global switch.
- **Prior behavior on master (before):** The same boolean settings supply no off control to the compatible request.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The previous-head [CI run 37055617698](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37055617698) passed on `e6276f970389b84a6a12914e2f2dea6f94689054` on **2026-10-02 at 19:50:59 UTC**. That is historical evidence. The **2026-10-04** review fixes advance this PR to `ca582f75b26597e69d39e1097a3fb9e300d864c3`; new-head CI is pending and is not yet claimed as passing. Current-head local provider tests, scoped Clippy, formatting, and changed-docs gates pass. The provider tests exercise the real config/factory-to-HTTP boundary; dated live backend checks below cover the model/template behavior that fixtures cannot prove.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Live checks called the backend APIs directly with the control fields verified by the config-to-HTTP regressions; they were not a live rebuilt ZeroClaw CLI run. Generation suppression is confirmed for the tested Gemma/llama.cpp artifact and prompt. The tested Ollama/Qwen3 artifact continued generating reasoning under off controls.
- **Commands run and tail output:** The following checks ran on **2026-10-04 (UTC)** for review-fix head `ca582f75b26597e69d39e1097a3fb9e300d864c3`. The new nested-effort HTTP regression was first run against the unchanged resolver and failed with configured nested `"low"` overwritten by runtime `"high"`; it passes after the fix.

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
passed

cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-providers --lib local_thinking
9 passed; 0 failed

cargo test --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-providers --lib
1925 passed; 0 failed; 4 ignored

cargo clippy --locked --offline -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings
Finished dev profile
```

Dependency-inclusive Clippy was also attempted during the original **2026-10-02** validation. It fails on the unchanged `zeroclaw-infra/src/acp_session_store.rs:1648` expression with `clippy::nonminimal_bool` on Rust 1.96. The changed-package check passes; this PR does not include that separate cleanup.

On **2026-10-04**, `scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh` and `scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh` ran with `BASE_SHA=e6276f970389b84a6a12914e2f2dea6f94689054` and `DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/providers/configuration.md`. The quality gate found no blocking issues on changed lines. Full-file lint also identified an existing duplicate `See also` heading outside this patch; both headings are present on the parent revision. The links gate passed its six collector tests and found zero added links.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Original live verification on **2026-10-02 (UTC)**, repeated on **2026-10-04 (UTC)**. Both used the prompt `What is 17 multiplied by 23? Reply with only the number.` with temperature 0.

  **llama.cpp / Gemma:** Gemma 4 26B A4B instruction-tuned Q4_0 GGUF from ggml-org, with its original template, on llama.cpp commit `6f4f53f` and an RTX 3090. The downloaded GGUF was verified against its published SHA-256: `d208665ab1cd3a69f7a9a4bc59430e8448c8093d9b06334f566ac59d6d504a03`. The repeat used the same cached artifact and backend binary.

| Test date (UTC) | Thinking mode | Generated tokens | Reasoning characters | Final answer |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| 2026-10-02 | On | 157 | 280 | `391` |
| 2026-10-02 | Off | 4 | 0 | `391` |
| 2026-10-04 | On | 157 | 280 | `391` |
| 2026-10-04 | Off | 4 | 0 | `391` |

  Off requests sent `reasoning_effort="none"` and `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false`. `/apply-template` confirmed the off prompt omitted `<|think|>` and used the empty thought prefill. The answer-only content and four generated tokens confirm generation suppression for this case; an empty reasoning field alone would not establish that. This is one prompt, not a general quality or speed benchmark.

  **Ollama / Qwen3:** The live Ollama 0.35.0 `qwen3:4b` check on **2026-10-02** found that native `think=false` and compatible `reasoning_effort="none"` still generated reasoning in ordinary `content`. The **2026-10-04** repeat used an isolated Ollama server, the same cached model, and a 256-token cap:

| Request on 2026-10-04 (UTC) | Generated tokens | Separate reasoning characters | Ordinary content characters | Thinking generation disabled? |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Native `think=true` | 256 | 707 | 0 | No |
| Native `think=false` | 256 | 0 | 707 | No |
| Compatible `reasoning_effort="none"` | 256 | 0 | 707 | No |

  Both off requests produced identical visible reasoning and reached the token cap. The artifact's metadata advertises `thinking.values=[true]`, with `default=true`, and its stored template includes `<think>`. **Thinking was not disabled for this Ollama/Qwen3 artifact.** The PR repairs forwarding; it cannot guarantee generation suppression for a model/template without a working off mode. Temporary test servers were stopped after both checks.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A. No interface layout, styling, or interaction behavior changed; descriptions and documentation were clarified.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Review-fix head `ca582f75b26597e69d39e1097a3fb9e300d864c3`, **2026-10-04**. Config resolution and real factories were exercised against protocol-accurate HTTP fixtures for text, tools, streaming, and Responses. The live API checks above were captured for the original `e6276f9703` forwarding patch. The review fix changes enabled-thinking effort lookup and docs; explicit off still returns `"none"` before effort lookup, and current-head off regressions pass. The dated API checks remain model/template evidence, not a live rebuilt CLI run on this new head.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** Current-head local test tails above; dated live comparisons above. The **2026-10-04** Gemma repeat again returned exactly `391` in off mode with four generated tokens and no reasoning. Ollama off mode still returned a reasoning paragraph in ordinary content.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Nine regressions cover alias/global precedence, manual-field conflicts, defaults, preserved unrelated Chat options, local model names, Gemma's template flag, and unaffected compatible families. The added regression checks nested-only effort, flat-versus-nested precedence, empty/`"none"`/non-string fallbacks, and explicit off across Ollama Chat, llama.cpp Chat, and llama.cpp Responses, including text, tools, and both streaming paths.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No duplicate full-workspace Cargo run: public Rust signatures are unchanged and the full provider package was exercised. `graph_changed` could not enumerate symbols because the fresh worktree has no SCIP index; factory callers were checked directly and crate impact was inspected.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No; existing requests gain control fields.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No. Fixtures use synthetic messages, keys, model identifiers, and loopback endpoints.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. Mode selection comes from operator configuration; this patch adds no untrusted prompt text.
- If any Yes, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for unset controls. Explicit switches now take effect, including precedence over conflicting manual reasoning overrides.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes: existing controls gain working behavior and clearer descriptions; no new keys or syntax.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Exact upgrade steps: Rebuild/update the binary, retain the existing config, restart/reload the test instance, and start a fresh chat. Explicit typed switches now override contradictory manual workarounds.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <landed-fix-commit>` and reinstall/rebuild the prior binary.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Unset alias `think` and global `runtime.reasoning_enabled` to restore backend defaults.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** A backend rejects the control fields, or a model/template without an off mode continues generating reasoning. The latter is not evidence of missing forwarding.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A; no existing contribution is superseded.

prs.title: fix(channels/lark): parse image elements in Feishu post messages
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:** Feishu/Lark **post** (rich-text) messages that contain an image were silently dropped before reaching the agent, so the bot never answered them. Two gaps in `crates/zeroclaw-channels/src/lark.rs`: `parse_post_content_details` required a `zh_cn`/`en_us` locale wrapper (flat bodies that keep `title`/`content` at the top level returned `None`), and `img` elements were never converted into image markers. The change accepts flat bodies and downloads each `img` element through the existing `download_image_as_marker` path in both receive modes.
- **Scope boundary:** Only the Lark/Feishu channel implementation. No other channel, provider, config schema, or CLI surface changes. Plain image messages (`msg_type = "image"`) and file messages are untouched.
- **Blast radius:** Feishu/Lark posts that previously produced no inbound message now reach the agent, carrying an `[IMAGE:data:...]` marker per downloaded image. This reuses the marker format from plain image messages. Wrapped text-only posts keep their existing behavior; flat text-only posts are also newly accepted.
- **Linked issue(s):** No tracker entry yet (reported out-of-band from a live deployment); happy to link or file one if that is preferred.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `channel`, `channel:lark`, `risk:medium`, `size:S`.

### What this does, simply

Feishu clients can send one message that mixes text and a picture (the "图文" composer). ZeroClaw read those bodies only in the shape some clients produce (a `zh_cn`/`en_us` wrapper), and it never looked at the picture element at all. The result was the worst possible failure mode: the message was skipped without a reply and without an error.

This PR teaches the post reader the flat body shape, collects the `image_key`s of `img` elements, and hands each image to the channel's existing download helper so the agent receives the picture as a normal image marker, exactly like a plain image message does today.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes — this is channel-level behavior that needs a live Feishu app.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` `lark` (Feishu endpoint), WebSocket receive mode.
- **Setup / preconditions:** `[channels.lark.<alias>]` with `use_feishu = true` and default `receive_mode = "websocket"`, an agent bound to that channel, and a Feishu app subscribed to `im.message.receive_v1` with the `im:resource` scope.
- **Steps to run:** Send **one** message that contains both an image and text.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the agent receives the post (image marker + text) and answers it.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** the same message produces no inbound event at all — no reply, no error.

### How I tested

- `cargo test -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-lark --lib flat_post_with_image` — new unit test using a real flat post payload (image + text): `test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed`.
- `cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-channels --features channel-lark --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` — clean.
- `cargo fmt -p zeroclaw-channels -- --check` — clean.
- Manual smoke on a live Feishu bot (v0.8.5 source plus this patch): before the change a mixed image+text message left no inbound trace and no reply; after the change the same message reaches the agent and the reply describes the picture.
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** the `zeroclaw-channels` unit tests plus the workspace fmt/clippy gates.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** webhook receive mode was patched to match the WebSocket path but was not exercised against a live Feishu webhook.
- **Beyond CI, what did I manually verify?** Live WebSocket receive on a Feishu tenant (image+text post answered). I did **not** verify webhook mode end to end.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `N/A` (no rendered-interface change).

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? `No`
- New external network calls? `Yes`. Post images now trigger resource downloads through the existing `GET /open-apis/im/v1/messages/{message_id}/resources/{file_key}?type=image` endpoint already used for `msg_type = "image"` messages.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? `No`
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? `No` — the test uses a synthetic `image_key`.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? `Yes`. Content that used to be silently discarded (post text and images) is now delivered to the agent, matching the existing trust boundary for `text`/`image`/`file` messages. `LARK_IMAGE_MAX_BYTES` limits each accepted image to 10 MiB; `[multimodal]` limits apply during downstream provider preparation and do not bound aggregate channel download work.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: no new trust boundary or endpoint is introduced; posts are the same operator-visible channel input as other message types. Downloads retain the existing authentication, MIME checks and per-image byte guard. Posts with several images can increase receive latency and temporary memory because there is no post-level download budget.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? `No`
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? `No`

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <squash-sha>` (single-file change; no data migration).
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** `None`
- **Observable failure symptoms:** image posts stop producing inbound messages again, or trace logs show `failed to download image in post` (WARN) alongside `[IMAGE:<key> | download failed]` bodies.

---

## 中文说明

**问题：** 飞书「图文」消息（`msg_type = "post"`，一条消息里同时有图片和文字）会被**静默丢弃**——机器人既不回复也不报错。原因是 Lark 频道的 post 解析器要求内容带 `zh_cn`/`en_us` 语言包裹层，而这类消息的内容是平铺结构（`title`/`content` 在顶层），解析直接返回 `None`；即使解析成功，`img` 元素也从未被转换成图片标记。

**修复：** 接受平铺格式的 post 内容；从 `img` 元素提取 `image_key`，并复用频道已有的 `download_image_as_marker` 下载路径，把图片作为 `[IMAGE:data:...]` 标记交给 agent。WebSocket 与 webhook 两条接收路径都做了同样处理，下载失败的兜底标记与既有 image 分支保持一致。

**测试：** 新增单元测试（使用真实的平铺 post 报文，含图片与文字）通过；改动 crate 的 `clippy -D warnings` 与 `fmt --check` 干净；并在真实飞书机器人上做了手工验证——修改前图文消息无任何入站记录、无回复，修改后同一条消息能正常到达 agent 并回答图片内容。webhook 模式仅代码对齐，未做线上验证。

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.
