prs.title: feat(security): block direct spellings of irreversible destructive commands
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:** the allowlist screen returns `true` immediately when `allowed_commands` contains `*` and `block_high_risk_commands` is `false`. That short-circuit is intentional — it is how an operator opts out of the subshell/expansion guard in a trusted environment — but it also opts out for the handful of operations that leave no system to recover on. This puts a floor under the common accident and the lazy spelling.
- **Covers**, per chain segment and ahead of the wildcard opt-out: `mkfs` and every `mkfs.<fstype>` variant; `dd` with `of=` naming a raw block device; `rm` naming the filesystem root; the classic fork bomb. `validate_command_execution` reports a distinct error, so an operator can tell "screening is off but this is still denied" apart from "your allowlist rejected this".
- **Linked issue(s):** N/A
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `config`, `distinguished contributor`, `security:policy`, `domain:security`, `risk:high`, `size:L`, `needs-author-action`

### ⚠️ Scope: best-effort hardening, not a security boundary

**This does not bound the wildcard posture, and nothing in this PR claims it does.** An earlier revision did claim it, in the title, the error text, and the doc comment. @Audacity88 and @tidux both blocked on that, correctly, and this revision narrows the contract to what the mechanism can actually enforce.

The matcher is lexical: it reads the first word of each outer shell segment. The native runtime then passes the accepted string to `<shell> -c` unchanged. So under `allowed_commands = ["*"]` with `block_high_risk_commands = false`, all of these still reach the shell:

```
sh -c 'mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda1'       bash -c "mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda1"
env mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda1           sudo mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda1
echo /dev/sda1 | xargs mkfs.ext4  rm -rf /tmp/..
```

…as does any equivalent through `nohup`, `timeout`, `find -exec`, or a language interpreter. This is structural. A lexical scan of the outer token cannot constrain arbitrary shell execution, and no amount of added patterns changes that; closing the class requires enforcement at a layer that can constrain execution (sandbox/runtime), which is a much larger change than this PR.

`catastrophic_deny_does_not_bound_the_wildcard_posture` pins those bypasses as **permitted**. A test asserting that a dangerous command is allowed looks alarming, which is the point: it writes the boundary down, and makes any future change that closes the class an explicit edit to that test rather than a silent widening of the claim.

### Coverage fixes from review

- **`dd` device prefixes** — added `loop*`, `md*`, `mapper/*`, `dm-*` to the physical families. On an LVM or RAID host `/dev/mapper/vg-root` *is* the system disk, so omitting them left the common server case open.
- **`rm` path spellings** — `/`, `//`, `/.`, `/..`, and `/*` all name or expand to the same directory; the literal `== "/"` comparison caught only the first. Now normalized: an absolute path is the root when every component is empty, `.`, `..`, or a bare glob. Still lexical, so `/tmp/..` is not matched — pinned as a known gap in the boundary test above.

### Deliberate exclusions

`/dev/null` and `/dev/zero` are character devices and stay valid `dd` targets, so output suppression keeps working. The fork-bomb matcher strips quoted spans first, so `echo ':(){ :|:& };:'` is not captured. Both are regression tests.

### Scope boundary

No change to the allowlist, to `command_risk_level`, to approval flow, or to what `block_high_risk_commands` does for anything else. This is **not** general shell-syntax normalization — the existing guards already reject backticks, `$()`, process substitution, unsafe redirects, `tee`, and background `&` outside the wildcard path, and that design is untouched.

**Blast radius:** every caller of the allowlist screen and `validate_command_execution`, i.e. the shell tool and anything reusing the policy gate. Behavior changes only for the patterns above; a negative test pins the ordinary cases.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface` = `cli` (shell tool via the security policy)
- **Setup / preconditions:** `allowed_commands = ["*"]`, `block_high_risk_commands = false`, `autonomy = "full"` — the most permissive posture configurable.
- **Steps to run:** ask the agent to run `mkfs.ext4 /dev/sdb1` (name a device that does not exist if you would rather not find out). Then ask it to run `sh -c 'mkfs.ext4 /dev/sdb1'`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** the first is refused with "direct spelling of an irreversible destructive operation". The second is **permitted** — that is the documented boundary, not a bug.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** both are permitted and reach the shell.

### How I tested

- `catastrophic_direct_spellings_are_denied_in_the_most_permissive_posture` — 18 variants including the four new device families and four new root spellings, asserting both the refusal and the distinct error text
- `catastrophic_deny_does_not_bound_the_wildcard_posture` — the six bypasses above, asserted **permitted**
- `catastrophic_deny_does_not_capture_ordinary_work` — `dd if=input.iso of=output.img`, `dd of=./disk.img`, `rm -rf ./build`, `rm -rf /tmp/scratch`, `echo` of a quoted fork bomb, `grep -r mkfs docs/`
- `catastrophic_deny_survives_a_high_risk_command_being_explicitly_listed` — listing `dd` unlocks `of=b.img` but not `of=/dev/sda`
- `catastrophic_deny_applies_to_every_segment_of_a_chain`

```sh
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config    # 1294 passed; 0 failed (+ 90, 9, 8, 5, 1, 1 in other targets)
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime   # 3737 passed; 0 failed, 3 ignored
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                     # clean
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets -- -D warnings   # clean
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                        # passed
bash scripts/check-pr-title.sh "<title>"                       # passed
```

The shell-quoting fix is on 373168200c, which merges current `master` (0 behind). Validated on that head:

```sh
cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib    # 1676 passed; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib   # 4672 passed; 3 failed, 6 ignored
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets -- -D warnings   # clean
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                     # clean
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh                        # passed
```

The three `zeroclaw-runtime` failures are `tools::delegate` background-task timing tests (`did not finish before timeout`). They fail identically on current `master` (1f12418cc0) in the same checkout, so they are not caused by this change. New regressions: `shell_quoting_does_not_hide_a_direct_spelling` and `shell_quoting_awareness_leaves_ordinary_commands_allowed`. With the old whitespace splitting restored, the first fails.

I ran the full `zeroclaw-runtime` suite rather than a filtered subset this time. The error-text CI failure on the first revision happened because the shell tool's tests live in `zeroclaw-runtime` while I had validated with `cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib shell`.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Quality Gate over `zeroclaw-config`, which owns the policy gate, plus the dependent `zeroclaw-runtime` suite that consumes the error text.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `strip_windows_exe_suffix` is a no-op off Windows, so `mkfs` name matching is validated on Unix naming only. The patterns are Unix-shaped by nature.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** That quoted text is not captured, and that the raw-block-device prefix list excludes `/dev/null` and `/dev/zero`. I did NOT run any of these commands against real hardware.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No** — this removes capability
- New external network calls? **No**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No**
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A.

The trade-off, stated plainly: an operator who deliberately set `["*"]` loses the ability to run a specific set of direct spellings, and the error text says so. The risk this revision exists to remove is the *opposite* one — an operator reading "denied in every posture" and concluding the wildcard posture is bounded when it is not. That belief is more dangerous than not having the tier, which is why the contract now matches the mechanism everywhere it is stated.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes, with one intended narrowing.** Commands that are direct spellings of `mkfs`, `mkfs.<fstype>`, `dd of=<raw block device>`, `rm` of the filesystem root, or the classic fork bomb are now refused in every posture, including `allowed_commands = ["*"]` with `block_high_risk_commands = false`. That includes the same spellings written with shell quoting or escapes, such as `FOO='a b' rm -rf /` or `r\m -rf /`. Every other command is decided exactly as before.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No.** No new keys, and no existing key changes meaning. There is no setting that re-enables the covered spellings.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- Upgrade steps: none. An operator who relies on running one of the covered spellings directly through the agent will now get the refusal below and must run it outside the agent.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert the squash-merge commit (`git revert <merge-sha>`). The change is confined to `crates/zeroclaw-config/src/policy.rs` and has no persisted state or migration, so a revert restores prior behavior on the next build.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None. The deny runs ahead of the wildcard opt-out by design, and adding a toggle would recreate the posture this exists to put a floor under.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** shell-tool calls failing with `Command not allowed: direct spelling of an irreversible destructive operation` on a command the operator expected to run. A false positive would show that message on a command that is not one of the covered spellings. Grep tool-call results and agent logs for that exact string.

Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Tests only: `crates/zeroclaw-gateway/tests/router_limits.rs` (+609). The 64 KB request-body cap and the cron-run timeout exemption were asserted only at the constant level; the actual router wiring (`RequestBodyLimitLayer` on both routers, the long-running sub-router's separate `TimeoutLayer`) had zero coverage, so a wiring regression on a DoS-shaped boundary would have passed CI silently.
  - Seven tests boot the real gateway and speak raw HTTP/1.1: 413 over the limit on both routers, exactly-at-limit reaching the handler with the full body parsed, 408 at the default budget on ordinary routes, and — the load-bearing pair — the **same** 5-second cron job completing under `long_running_request_timeout_secs = 10` and being cut off under `= 3`. The pair checks that the long-running route responds to both configured budgets.
  - Port assignment uses `run_gateway`'s own port-0 + `GatewayReadinessReporter` path (no reserve-and-rebind race); the shell-dependent cron tests are `#[cfg(unix)]`-gated (the native Windows path shells through `cmd.exe`, which has no `sleep`), with the sub-router's timeout still covered on all platforms via its `/a2a/{alias}` sibling.
- **Scope boundary:** zero production changes — `src/lib.rs` is byte-identical to master (checksummed). No new dependencies.
- **Blast radius:** the `zeroclaw-gateway` test target only. Answers the tracker question: the cron-run wiring is **correct** on master.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #7692. Related #7685 (this was its last open row).
- **Labels:** `distinguished contributor`, `needs-author-action`, `risk:low`, `size:M`, `type:test`

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — the change is itself tests; CI executes them.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** required Rust CI runs the gateway integration targets.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** required CI does not run this target under `--no-default-features` (that row omits `--all-targets`); verified manually below.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check → exit 0
cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings → exit 0
cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway → 458 lib + 9 + 7 router_limits; 0 failed
cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --no-default-features --test router_limits → 6 passed
flake check: 3× standalone → 7/7 at 6.13s each; full-suite and no-default runs consistent
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Discrimination was proven with temporary production mutations (applied, observed red, restored byte-identical, final suite green): lifting the main router's body limit to `usize::MAX` fails the 413 test in 0.10s; swapping the sub-router's timeout to the default budget fails `cron_run_route_completes_when_the_budget_exceeds_the_job` in ~2s. A simulated non-unix compile (`cfg` flip) runs clippy clean, so the Unix gating cannot break Windows CI via dead-code warnings. Those passing runs do not establish load-proof timing margins; the earlier review recorded a successful response that failed the success-path elapsed ceiling under package-suite load. Known residual: a regression hard-coding exactly 5 s is a knife-edge race against the 5 s job and is not excluded.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** N/A

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No — all sockets are loopback within the tests
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk (tests only): `git revert e9598f317`.

prs.title: fix(zerocode): answer dropped elicitations and record them in the transcript
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A pending `ask_user` / `poll` prompt could be cleared on the client with no reply. The daemon then waited out the tool's own timeout (600 s for `ask_user`) while the user saw nothing. Every clear that isn't the user's answer now goes through `withdraw_pending_elicitation`. `Chat::answer_withdrawn_elicitations` (run each transport tick, after the resync drain) sends the `cancel` and notes it in the transcript.
  - A modal that outlives its turn is closed on `TurnComplete` and recorded as expired.
  - The `ask_user` / `poll` tool card now leads with `question:` and lists the choices. Before, the collapsed card showed the first 120 bytes of key-sorted input JSON, so `channel` and `choices` came first and the question was cut off. The card is the one record of the question.
  - The expanded (`Full`) `ask_user` / `poll` card shows each choice whole, inside the card's shared byte and line limits. Multi-line choices continue indented under their bullet, and the list stops with the usual show-less footer when the shared limit is reached. The collapsed card keeps the 200-byte, one-line preview per choice.
  - The card's `result:` is the record of the outcome. For `ask_user` / `poll`, the pick (or the `DISMISSED` marker from #11815) is shown in the warn colour the old outcome line used. An outcome line (answered, dismissed, withdrawn, expired) is written only when no matching `ask_user` / `poll` card is on screen, such as an older history or a card that never arrived. In dogfooding, a line under the card repeated its `result:`. That fallback line names the question (`<outcome> (Question: <question>)`, new key `zc-chat-elicitation-outcome-note` in all five catalogues), because no card shows it.
- **Scope boundary:** Client only (`apps/zerocode`). No daemon or wire change. Overlay placement and the sidebar needs-input dot are unchanged; the dot already exists (`ChatState::sidebar_status`). Free-form `ask_user` on the Code tab is still unsupported.
- **Blast radius:** The ZeroCode Code and Chat panes' elicitation path, and how the `ask_user` / `poll` tool cards render. A dropped prompt now gets a `cancel` reply where before it got none. The daemon already handles `cancel` (`Ok(None)` → "user cancelled").
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11623. Related #11117 (durable human-question primitive; it scopes ACP elicitation out). Companion #11815 makes `ask_user` return a `DISMISSED` result rather than an error when the user presses Esc, so the card's `result:` reads as a dismissal.

### What this does, simply

When an agent asks you a multiple-choice question in ZeroCode, a box pops up with the options. If the pane reloaded while that box was up (which happens when the client falls behind the live stream) or you started a new session in place, the box disappeared and nobody told the agent. The agent sat waiting for up to ten minutes and then failed with a timeout. Nothing about the question stayed on screen either, so afterwards you couldn't tell what had been asked.

Now the agent is told "cancelled" right away whenever the box goes away without your answer. The `ask_user` tool card shows the question, its options and what happened. A separate note appears only if the card isn't on screen.

**Why the record is client-side.** The prompt asked whether the record belongs in the daemon so it survives reload. It already partly does: the daemon persists the `ask_user` tool call with its full input, and with this change that card shows the question and choices. So after a reload the question is still on screen. The card's `result:` carries the answer or the cancel, and it is persisted with the card. Making the outcome durable means a new daemon event and storage, which is the job of the #11117 durable-question primitive. I kept this PR to the client.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The failing path needs a notification-lag reload to land while a prompt is up, which is hard to trigger by hand. The regression test drives it directly.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (ZeroCode Code pane)

### How I tested

**Current head `b28702328`** (`8c7f6f54de` plus the fallback-note fix for Greptile 4429142227), on a Linux x86_64 build host with rustc 1.98.0, in its own target dir (the log shows zerocode compiled from this tree):

- `cargo test --locked -p zerocode --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4` → library `52 passed; 0 failed`; binary `1570 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored`. The one failure is the known `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` (see below). The four tests that check a fallback note now expect the question in it. The reload-withdrawal test also asserts that the withdrawn line contains `Pick one`.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → `Finished`, no warnings. `cargo fmt -p zerocode -- --check` → clean.

**Previous head `8c7f6f54de`** (`59b0cd500` on `7996a8193b`, then a clean merge of master `1c1cd118a`), on a Linux x86_64 build host with rustc 1.99.1:

- `cargo test --locked -p zerocode -- --test-threads=4` → library `52 passed; 0 failed`; binary `1570 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored`. The one failure is the known `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` (see below). The two new tests pass: `expanded_ask_user_card_shows_whole_choices_within_shared_limits` (a 300-byte choice and a two-line choice render whole when expanded, with the second line indented under its bullet, and the collapsed card still cuts both) and `expanded_ask_user_choices_stop_at_the_shared_line_limit` (a poll with 100 two-line options renders 100 choice rows and then the show-less footer).
- `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → `Finished`, no warnings. `cargo fmt --all -- --check` → clean.

Earlier commits, all through the remote wrapper (`scripts/zc-cargo`) on the build host:

- `zc-cargo test -p zerocode elicitation` → `test result: ok. 19 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1410 filtered out` (at the third commit)
- `zc-cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` → `Finished `dev` profile`, no warnings
- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check apps/zerocode/src/chat.rs` → clean
- Full `zc-cargo test -p zerocode` → `1426 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored` at the second and third commits (first commit: 1425/1). The one failure is `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` ("SIGINT was swallowed while the insecure-TLS prompt was blocked", `main.rs`). It fails the same way on unmodified `origin/master` 05f9fe95d4 on the same host (`0 passed; 1 failed; 1422 filtered out`), so it's environmental on that host, not this change.

**Mutation check, third commit.** `elicitation_question_choices_and_answer_are_recorded` now applies the card's result and asserts no outcome line; `elicitation_with_a_card_adds_no_outcome_line` (renamed from `elicitation_outcome_sits_under_its_card_inside_the_agent_turn`) asserts the entries stay `agent, tool:ask_user, tool:shell` after Esc and the browse cursor is untouched. Writing the line even when a card exists: `17 passed; 2 failed`, both tests. Restored → 19 passed.

**Mutation check, second commit (placement since superseded by the third).** `elicitation_question_choices_and_answer_are_recorded` now streams the agent turn and asserts no line on arrival, one outcome line, and the question exactly once in the rendered transcript. The new `elicitation_outcome_sits_under_its_card_inside_the_agent_turn` delivers the request before the turn streams in (the router order), adds a parallel `shell` call, presses Esc, and asserts the entry order `agent, tool:ask_user, system:dismissed, tool:shell`, the rendered order agent label < `question:` < outcome < shell card, and that the browse cursor follows the shift.
- Asked line restored on arrival: `18 passed; 2 failed`. Both tests fail; the order assertion shows `["system:The agent asked: Pick one…", "agent", "tool:ask_user", …]`, which is what my screenshot shows.
- Outcome appended instead of placed: `19 passed; 1 failed`, with `["agent", "tool:ask_user", "tool:shell", "system:You dismissed…"]`.
- Index shift removed: fails with "the browse cursor stays on the shell card" (`Some(2)` vs `Some(3)`).
Restored → 20 passed.

**Mutation check, first commit.** I reverted each piece of the fix in one mutant (reload clears silently again, no asked-record, no `TurnComplete` close, card arm disabled, `reset_for_session` clears silently): `14 passed; 5 failed`. All five new tests failed:
`elicitation_installed_during_reload_is_answered_not_dropped`, `reset_for_session_queues_a_cancel_for_the_dropped_elicitation`, `elicitation_question_choices_and_answer_are_recorded`, `turn_complete_closes_a_stale_elicitation_and_records_it`, `ask_user_card_leads_with_the_question_and_lists_choices`. Restored → 19 passed.

- **CI checks relied on:** the zerocode test and clippy jobs.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** none for this surface.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real screenshots: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11624#issuecomment-6233889542 (experiment build, picked result and dismissed). Real screenshots of the current head pending. I dogfooded the second commit on 2026-10-17: the question showed once, but the answer was repeated, which the third commit fixes.
- **Not verified:** a live reproduction of the lag-reload race against a daemon.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The question text was already rendered (in the modal); it's now also rendered in the transcript through the same terminal-safe path as tool input. Nothing new reaches the model.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** revert the squash commit. The change is client-only, with no config, state or wire change to undo.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** none.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** an `ask_user` / `poll` prompt that disappears without a `cancel` reaching the daemon (the turn then waits out the tool's timeout), a prompt answered twice, or an `ask_user` card missing its question, choices or `result:`.

prs.title: fix(zerocode): use local Linux clipboard writers and report copy outcomes
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Try an optional local Linux clipboard writer so Copy can work when the terminal ignores OSC 52.
  - Report successful local writes, unconfirmed terminal requests, and errors distinctly across Chat, Code, Logs, queued messages, links, and composer copy/cut.
  - Bound native input delivery and process completion, retain selected text on known failures, and consume failed composer copy keys before quit handling.
  - Preserve the first copy badge when the bottom notice resizes the transcript, and translate the new feedback in all five shipped catalogues.
- **Scope boundary:** ZeroCode text clipboard delivery and feedback. No daemon, RPC, configuration schema, clipboard-image cleanup, native macOS/Windows writer, dependency, lockfile, or CI changes.
- **Blast radius:** Explicit user copy/cut actions, transient feedback, and transcript feedback invalidation during redraw.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11418.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode is the terminal interface for chatting with agents. Its Copy actions previously asked the terminal to update the clipboard and immediately showed "Copied." The reporter confirmed that GNOME Terminal ignored both that request and a direct OSC 52 probe, while Alacritty worked.

This PR tries `wl-copy` or `xclip` on a local Linux desktop. A successful writer reports "Copied." SSH sessions, macOS, Windows, and Linux sessions without an installed compatible writer keep terminal copying, with "Requested" feedback because the terminal does not acknowledge delivery. Known write failures show an error and preserve selected text. Composer Cut keeps its existing undoable behavior after a terminal request.

The result belongs to the existing clipboard module and existing transient feedback. There is no new configuration setting, dependency, persistent state, or daemon call. One deadline covers pipe backpressure and helper completion. The helper is killed and reaped on failure. Copy badges survive the notice-driven viewport change when captured content still matches; width and content changes invalidate them.

The relatively large diff covers the shared writer, each existing copy consumer, and tests in their owning modules. A writer-only change would leave misleading feedback; a feedback-only change would leave the local GNOME clipboard failure.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. Final-head desktop feedback and clipboard delivery need real-interface verification.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface:tui`, ZeroCode Chat/Code, composer, and Logs. N/A for messaging channel; these are local terminal panes.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Use the same Ubuntu GNOME Terminal desktop and daemon configuration for `master` and this branch. Use `wl-copy` on Wayland or `xclip` on X11. Use an OSC 52-capable terminal for the separate SSH case. Record the binary's source revision. No provider changes are required.
- **Steps to run:** On each revision, launch `zerocode`; click a message Copy target once and paste into another application; repeat for a code block. Select composer text, press Ctrl+X, paste elsewhere, then Ctrl+Z to Undo. Repeat Copy without a compatible helper on PATH. Repeat through SSH in an OSC 52-capable terminal. In a disposable test environment, use a failing clipboard helper and copy a Logs selection; record the visible error and retained selection. Capture the first-click badge and Logs error with surrounding TUI context. Also repeat with enough history to scroll, so opening the bottom notice changes the viewport.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** A successful local writer copies the intended text and shows Copied on the first action. Without a helper, or over SSH, feedback says Requested; terminal support determines delivery. Known writer errors report failure and retain selected text. Cut after an emitted terminal request remains undoable. The new regression targets first-action badge retention during notice resize; real-interface confirmation is still needed.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Copy always requests OSC 52 and reports Copied even when GNOME Terminal ignores it. There is no local Linux text writer. The copy badge can disappear when the bottom notice changes the viewport. Cut removes text after an unconfirmed terminal request.

### How I tested

Local Cargo results for the pushed head `caa009b0b` are below.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [CI Required Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39024301235/job/117373409734) passed for published head `f607e1b8ee6d187a538f82d0b914a3cdca841d4a`. Its Test, Lint, Format, MSRV, platform checks, and ZeroCode RPC boundary jobs supply historical compilation/test evidence for the original implementation. They do not cover local merge `033df206f` or the subsequent working-tree fixes.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The [Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40999699368) passed on head `caa009b0b`. CI does not prove real desktop clipboard delivery, terminal presentation or SSH behavior.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Run on head `caa009b0b` (master merge `033df206f` + `561a4c75b` badge fix + `df1434917` clipboard cfg fix + `caa009b0b` translations), Mac mini, `zc-cargo-narrow`, `-j2`, `--test-threads=2`:

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                  ok
  cargo clippy -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings        ok
  cargo test -p zerocode
    zerocode (lib)       54 passed; 0 failed
    zerocode (bin)       1579 passed; 2 failed; 2 ignored
    terminal_disconnect  3 passed
  ```

  `chat::tests::first_copy_badge_survives_app_notice_resize` passes. Both failures also fail on clean master `5a51398dd` on this machine (1561 passed; same 2 failed) and are not touched by this PR: `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` and `app::tests::input_wait_returns_early_for_pending_transport_events`.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Inspected every copy consumer and the upstream changes to overlapping modules. Direct rustfmt, whitespace checks, comment hygiene, the ZeroCode dependency-boundary gate, and catalogue key/argument checks passed locally. No live clipboard or terminal smoke was run during this refresh. The reporter's [GNOME results](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/11418#issuecomment-6257700422) show correct message, code-block, and composer paste; the reporter also [confirmed either helper works](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/11418#issuecomment-6257745658). Their tested revision is unstated.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real xfce4-terminal 1.1.4 captures (VTE 0.80.1, the terminal library GNOME Terminal uses; it ignores OSC 52) on Linux X11. Each copy was read back with `xclip -o`. Before, master `5a51398dd5` with xclip installed: ["Copied to clipboard" but the clipboard is unchanged](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11529/live-caa009b0b/B01-master-5a51398dd-says-copied-clipboard-unchanged.png). After, this PR: [xclip copy delivered](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11529/live-caa009b0b/A02-pr-xclip-copied-clipboard-has-text.png), [no helper: Requested/unconfirmed, clipboard unchanged](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11529/live-caa009b0b/A03-pr-no-helper-requested-unconfirmed.png), [failing helper: Could not copy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11529/live-caa009b0b/A04-pr-failing-helper-could-not-copy.png), [composer Ctrl+X, then Ctrl+Z](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/evidence-screenshots/pr-11529/live-caa009b0b/A05-pr-composer-cut-then-undo.png).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `zerocode` and the daemon built from head `caa009b0bd0e` on Debian 13 x86_64, X11, with xclip 0.13-4. Before: `zerocode` from master `5a51398dd5`, the merge base. Setup, stub provider and clipboard read-backs: https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/blob/evidence-screenshots/pr-11529/live-caa009b0b/MANIFEST.txt
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/blob/evidence-screenshots/pr-11529/live-caa009b0b/ (B01, A01 to A05). Clipboard read-backs: master `[UNCHANGED-SENTINEL-MASTER]` after "Copied"; PR with xclip `[Answer to: Name one use of a clipboard]`; PR with no helper `[UNCHANGED-SENTINEL]`; PR with a failing helper `[UNCHANGED-SENTINEL-2]`; PR composer cut `[draft line to cut]`.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** The reporter observed correct paste with local helpers, and unconfirmed requests with unchanged clipboard contents after removing both. prs.title: feat(zerocode): show message times in the transcript
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - The ZeroCode transcript never showed when anything happened. When an automated prompt, a refused queued message and a long tool call overlap in one session, there was no way to tell the order or the durations from the screen. A time on every message proved to be too much (an earlier revision of this PR did that). The transcript now shows time context in two places only:
    - a dim, centered divider (`── Today 01:00 ──`, `── Yesterday 22:20 ──`, or a date) before a prompt that starts the transcript, comes 15 minutes or more after the previous activity, or starts a new day. A quick back-and-forth gets no dividers.
    - a dim footer (`─── 01:00 → 01:31 · 31m 40s`) under a turn that ran for a minute or more. Short turns get none.
  - `session/messages` entries gain an optional `created_at` (RFC 3339) wherever the store has one: ACP full loads, ACP cursor pages, and the Chat backend via `load_with_timestamps`. It is skipped when absent and `#[serde(default)]` on the client, so either side can be older.
  - **Store fix underneath.** Checkpointed ACP turns write all their visible rows at finalization with one timestamp, so a turn's prompt read as the time the turn **ended**. A divider or footer built on that would be wrong by the whole length of the turn. The checkpoint row now records `started_at` (a nullable column, added on upgrade), and finalization and crash recovery stamp the turn's prompt row with it. The other rows of the turn keep the finalization time, which is the turn's end: exactly what the footer needs.
  - Live turns: entries are stamped on receipt, and the footer is placed when the turn settles. A later terminal frame for the same turn does not move it. A history load taken mid-turn hands the footer to the live settle.
  - A reloaded turn that ends in a recovery marker gets no footer, because recovery stamps its rows when it runs, which can be hours after the turn stopped.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Individual tool calls and replies in ACP history still share the turn's finish time. Giving each its own time would need a time on every checkpoint journal event; it isn't needed for dividers and footers.
  - No toggle. The only existing display toggle is thoughts; a timestamp toggle would need a new action, keybinding and help text.
  - The Chat-backend path (gateway SQLite) is affected by #11420, which rewrites every row's `created_at` on each turn. This PR passes through what that store holds.
- **Blast radius:** the ACP store's write path for checkpointed turns (only the prompt row's `created_at`) and one additive column on `acp_turn_checkpoints`; the `session/messages` wire shape (additive, optional); ZeroCode transcript layout (divider and footer rows drawn outside each entry's line range, with the tail re-render accounting for them).
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11620. Related #11420.
- **Holding-crate exception:** the `zeroclaw-runtime` part (`created_at` on `session/messages`, confined to `handle_session_messages` and the entry builder) is covered by the row added in #11697 (merged).

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode now shows a small grey date-and-time line when you come back to a conversation after a break or on a new day, and a small grey line under any turn that took more than a minute, saying when it started, when it finished and how long it took. Quick exchanges look exactly as before. Under the hood, the daemon's database used to record every message of a turn as happening when the turn finished; this PR records when the prompt was sent, so those lines are right after a reload too.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `tui` (ZeroCode over the daemon socket)
- **Setup / preconditions:** a daemon and ZeroCode built from this branch; any agent.
- **Steps to run:** send a prompt that runs a tool and takes over a minute. Then send a quick follow-up. Wait 15 minutes (or reload a session from yesterday) and send another. Switch away from the session and back to force a `session/messages` reload.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** a `── Today HH:MM ──` divider above the first prompt; a `─── start → end · duration` footer under the long turn; nothing around the quick follow-up; a new divider after the gap. The same marks after the reload. A session from an older daemon shows no marks rather than wrong ones.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** no times anywhere.

### How I tested

All builds and tests ran through `scripts/zc-cargo` on the remote build host.

- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on the touched files: clean.
- `zc-cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-infra -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
Results below are for head `c57119d62da9` (rebased on `master` 2026-10-17) unless marked.

- `zc-cargo test -p zerocode`: `test result: FAILED. 1537 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored`. The one failure, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, fails the same way on unmodified `master` on the same host.
- `zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-infra acp_session_store`: `test result: ok. 88 passed; 0 failed`.
- `zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib rpc::`: `test result: ok. 850 passed; 0 failed`.
- `zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib`: `5627 passed; 4 failed` at the earlier head. The 4 (`relay::local_dial_tests` x2, `new_session_methods_are_denied_without_their_grants`, `peer_turn_cost_scope_through_execute_boundary_attributes_recipient_and_shares_budget`) fail the same way on unmodified `master` on the same host. The runtime diff is unchanged since.

Each new test fails with its fix reverted and passes with it restored:

- Store: `finalized_turn_prompt_keeps_turn_start_time_and_reply_keeps_finalization_time`, `recovered_turn_prompt_keeps_turn_start_time` (fail when the prompt keeps the finalization time); `turn_checkpoint_start_column_is_added_to_an_existing_database` (fails without the migration).
- RPC: `conversation_message_entries_carry_each_source_message_time` (fails when the projection drops times).
- Rules (`chat::entry_time`): `dividers_mark_the_first_prompt_gaps_and_day_changes_only` (fails when every prompt divides), `a_day_change_divides_even_after_a_short_gap` (fails without the day check), `footers_follow_finished_turns_of_a_minute_or_more` (fails without the one-minute floor), plus label and parsing tests.
- Transcript: `transcript_shows_gap_dividers_and_long_turn_footers_not_message_times` and `a_live_turn_gets_its_footer_when_it_settles` (fail when the layout drops the footer row, when a settle doesn't invalidate the tail, or when a later frame may move the end); `a_history_load_taken_mid_turn_hands_the_footer_to_the_live_settle` (fails when a moved footer doesn't force a full rebuild); `a_footer_on_a_divided_entry_keeps_one_divider` (fails when the tail re-render ignores the divider row); `a_recovered_turn_gets_no_footer_from_its_recovery_time`.

`rpc::dispatch::tests::cursor_pages_equal_legacy_projection_for_valid_tool_groups` was updated: cursor pages now carry times, so its full-load reference uses the timed projection.

- **CI checks relied on:** the Rust lanes for the three crates.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** no end-to-end daemon+TUI run in CI for this.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The divider and footer rows were checked in a live ZeroCode pane against a scratch daemon (seeded history plus a live turn), by reading the terminal's text.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real screenshots: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11622#issuecomment-6232571932 (experiment build, taken before the current head). Real screenshots of the current head pending. Daemon/store verification is also pending.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** none.

### Screenshots

Real screenshots: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11622#issuecomment-6232571932 (experiment build, taken before the current head). Real screenshots of the current head pending.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. Times are display-only and never reach the model.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The new wire field is optional both ways. The new column is nullable and added on open; an older binary ignores it (its inserts name their columns). A checkpoint begun by an older binary has no start time, and its prompt keeps the finalization time as before.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert` the PR's commits. The added `acp_turn_checkpoints.started_at` column is harmless to the reverted code and needs no down-migration.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** no dividers or footers (old daemon or missing `created_at`), or a footer whose start is later than expected (start time not recorded).

prs.title: feat(zerocode): expose settings actions and filter keybindings
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:** Client settings now show contextual action hints using the effective keymap. Keybindings can be searched by action name, action identifier, or effective key without executing settings actions while typing.
- **Scope boundary:** Existing settings writes, preset application, and modified global shortcuts keep their existing behavior. Effective-key collision handling and Shift+Tab normalization remain separate work.
- **Blast radius:** The ZeroCode client settings pane, its Config footer and input routing, and its English Fluent catalogue. No daemon, RPC, configuration schema, or dependency changes.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11492.

### What this does, simply

ZeroCode's Config screen lets you change client preferences such as themes, keybindings, and connection settings. Several pages previously left their action hints blank, and some instructions named Enter or Esc even when those keys had been overridden. Finding an action to rebind also required scrolling through the whole list.

The footer now identifies the current client-settings page and active pane and shows the controls that can actually reach it. The Keybindings page adds a search field. Typing edits the query; confirming it lets you browse the matching actions, and a separate activation starts rebinding. Searching, clearing, and cancelling do not save a binding. Rebind and reset still operate on the action displayed in the selected row.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The change reuses the existing action registry, resolved bindings, search controls, Config footer, and locale loader. The full binding list remains authoritative; search derives visible row indices from it. Config and global routing yield ordinary query text so characters cannot accidentally reset a binding or switch sections. Modified global shortcuts retain their established priority, and hints omit local keys those shortcuts intercept.

The source and catalogue changes are accompanied by tests at the pane, Config, and global input boundaries. No new persistence owner, API, registry, or dependency is introduced.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, for actual terminal presentation and focus.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Config client settings.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Build this revision and use your existing compatible daemon, client profile, and keybindings. No additional feature settings are needed.
- **Steps to run:** Open Config, switch the outer section to ZeroCode, and select Keybindings. Open detail, start search with the resolved search key, and enter an action name such as `clear input` or a key such as `Ctrl+z`. Confirm the query, select a result, and activate it. Cancel capture, clear the filter, and return to the section list. Inspect the other settings pages and Connection editing. Use the same steps on `master` for comparison.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Contextual controls reflect your effective bindings. The filter narrows the actions; query confirmation does not start capture. Capture/reset target the displayed action. Clearing preserves useful selection. Mouse or keyboard departure stops query editing while retaining its text.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Keybindings has no filter; client-settings footers generally lack contextual controls, and some titles/editor instructions use fixed keys.

### How I tested

The original implementation was validated on `c75f24e832eb1437b6614bbaeddd2d537814d7e1`:

- `cargo test --locked -p zerocode --bin zerocode`: 1,431 passed, 0 failed, 2 existing ignored tests. This includes filtering, correct capture/reset targets, empty results, cancellation, repeated search selection, typing without config writes, mouse list/query geometry, paste isolation, effective hints, locale fallback, and narrow footer rendering.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Touched-file rustfmt, `git diff --check`, comment hygiene, and the ZeroCode RPC-only dependency gate passed.
- The [Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40998818887) passed on the current head `ef584933c420c951c5e249cb737865a7327f427c`, including workspace nextest, lint, cross-platform checks, and the ZeroCode RPC boundary. All applicable checks passed; conditional checks were skipped. Earlier: [Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37142730934) on `c75f24e832`. Real terminal captures of `fd1b0623d6` are in https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11505#issuecomment-6511701389. `ef584933c` only deletes `#[cfg(test)]` code, so they still match.

Subsequent updates preserve those behaviors and correct effective hints during Connection text editing. Three existing standalone settings tests passed for that correction. The existing `keymap::guard::tests::no_hardcoded_chords_in_handlers` test passes after documenting the printable-editor-input classification; that annotation changes no runtime behavior.

Historical CI on `ad847fb32fbf6b9104b09079daeb24e0acf4f013`: [Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/37826288701) passed, including the Test job, lint, cross-platform checks and RPC boundary. Workspace nextest passed 19,371 tests with 39 skipped; the keymap guard passed in both ZeroCode test targets. The hardware-feature suite passed 189 tests with 1 skipped. All applicable checks succeeded; conditional checks were skipped.

Rebased onto `master` at `4e82ce46e9c6` (head `0723ca1a67b1`). The rebase needed one adaptation: master added a layout row to the Config view, so the client-settings footer now renders into the last row. `config_manager::tests::client_binding_query_owns_printable_outer_keys_and_paste` caught the misplaced footer before the fix. On the new head, `cargo clippy --locked -p zerocode --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed and `cargo test --locked -p zerocode --bin zerocode` passed 1,535 tests. The one failure, `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, also fails on `master` on my test machine and is unrelated. Touched-file rustfmt, `git diff --check` and comment hygiene passed.

### Screenshots

Real screenshots: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11505#issuecomment-6511701389 (macOS Terminal.app captures of this head, `fd1b0623d6`). Earlier screenshot from my experiment build: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11505#issuecomment-6232477525.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions / trust boundaries? No.
- Secrets / sensitive data handling changed? No. Connection-setting persistence is unchanged.
- Network / filesystem access changed? No. Filtering is transient; existing explicit settings actions retain their write paths.
- Any real identities, secrets, tokens, credentials, personal emails, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- Upgrade steps: None. New client strings use the existing English fallback until translated catalogues include them.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After merge, run `git revert <merge-commit>` for this PR's merge commit.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** Query text invokes a shortcut, capture/reset targets a different action, or a footer advertises a key intercepted by another control. Existing configuration remains readable after reverting the UI change.

prs.title: feat(zerocode): show readable Config labels and full field details
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Config field rows use readable labels and bounded value previews so long arrays do not consume the visible row.
  - The selected field's Help view starts with its exact path, complete description, and current masked value. It follows the selected row on regular field tabs, including filtered results.
  - Shared help prose uses the existing Unicode-aware text wrapper so long paths and array items wrap and remain reachable by scrolling.
- **Scope boundary:** Presentation and field help only; configuration keys, defaults, validation, registry, and save behavior are unchanged.
- **Blast radius:** ZeroCode Config rendering, prose wrapping in the shared Help overlay, and Config documentation.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #11489. Related #9363 for localization completeness and #8062 for structured JSON editing.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `risk:medium`, `size:M`, `zerocode`, `docs`.

### What this does, simply

Config currently shows raw setting names and clips descriptions into a small fixed area. This PR makes the rows easier to scan and lets you open Help to read the full setting information, including its exact configuration path and long value. Secrets stay hidden. Unset values and environment overrides remain distinguishable; unit and default explanations come from the schema description, without inferring how a current value was configured.

### Scope and maintenance tradeoff

The change reuses the existing Config descriptors, Fluent catalogue, Help overlay, and text-input wrapping. It adds no metadata registry, RPC method, dependency, or persisted state. One-line rows preserve existing list and mouse geometry. The inline Enter-to-edit hint is removed to leave room for the label and preview; the existing edit binding remains available. The supporting shared-help change is needed because whitespace-only wrapping permanently clipped long unbroken paths and values.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Config and Help.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Connect ZeroCode to your existing daemon. Use an existing agent with a precheck timeout or a risk profile with a long command/path list; no configuration change is needed.
- **Steps to run:** Open Config and select a field with a long value (for example a risk profile's command list). Inspect its label and preview, then press `?` (or Ctrl+G) to open Help and scroll through the complete path, description, and value. Close Help, open the filter, type part of a setting path, move to a match with the arrow keys, and press Ctrl+G; while the filter box is focused, `?` is typed into the filter and Enter opens the editor. Help should describe the highlighted match. Repeat on a secret field. Run the same steps on `master` to compare. The filter matches setting paths, not values.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Readable labels, an ellipsis on clipped previews, the highlighted field's exact path and full description/value accessible through scrolling, and hidden secret contents.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Raw path labels, clipped long row values, and descriptions limited to one or two rows. Field information is absent from Help; long unbroken help prose can be clipped.

Tested revision: `8ad24910fa88e7ac0a68e7ac017e208ceee8d3ee` on the Mac mini. The current head `bd96063d64` only removes the `evidence_frame_` TestBackend render tests (`#[cfg(test)]` code). The [Quality Gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40998641260) passed on it.

### Screenshots

Real screenshots: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11501#issuecomment-6511701866 (macOS Terminal.app captures of `8ad24910fa`), and the before/after comparison against `master` in comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11501#issuecomment-6514496680. Earlier screenshots from my experiment build: see comment https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11501#issuecomment-6232358551.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No.
- New external network calls? No.

- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No.

- If any Yes, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A.

## Compatibility (required)

- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - A foreground agentic delegate ran its tool loop with an inert observer, so while it worked the parent turn, the RPC stream and ZeroCode showed nothing until the child answered. A long delegate looked the same whether it was working, looping or stuck.
  - Each tool execution in a turn that streams events now scopes the turn's event sender and the call id (`agent/tool_execution.rs`, next to #11298's cancellation scope). A foreground agentic delegate gives its child loop an observer (`tools/delegate_activity.rs`) that turns each child tool start and finish into one new live turn event, `TurnEvent::DelegateActivity` in `zeroclaw-api`: the tool name, a secret-redacted argument summary (`approval::summarize_args`), and a 400-character output preview of the already-scrubbed result. Parallel workers carry the scope across their spawn. A delegate inside the child reports one level deeper (`depth`) against the same parent call.
  - The observer sends with `try_send`, so a full parent channel drops activity instead of slowing the child or the parent turn.
  - RPC forwards it as a `delegate_activity` `session/update` (`rpc/{dispatch,types}.rs`). ZeroCode shows a child-call count and the running tool under the delegate card, and the call list when the card is expanded.
  - A tool's own `approved` input is left out of child summaries: under a successful call, `approved: false` read as a refusal.
  - While the delegate's turn runs, its card's Response line now says "Waiting for response" instead of "Result not recorded". The card only says that for a call this pane saw start in the running turn; restored history and calls a finished or cancelled turn left without a result keep the neutral wording from #11446.
- **Scope boundary:** no persistence: the event isn't written to the turn checkpoint or session history, so restored sessions look as before. Background delegates don't forward (their turn may be gone; #11292's `check_result` progress covers them). The child's text, reasoning, usage and approvals aren't forwarded. No config key and no opt-in. Other channels (ACP server, gateway WS, chat channels) ignore the new variant through their existing fall-through arms.
- **Blast radius:** the tool-execution scope wraps every tool's `execute` when the turn streams events, but only the delegate tool reads it. Foreground agentic delegates now run with a forwarding observer instead of the no-op one. RPC clients get a new `session/update` type; older ZeroCode builds ignore it.
- **Linked issue(s):** Part of #10531 (its observer-forwarding piece; #11292 shipped the first piece). Related #8763 (live half of the ZeroCode subagent view), #11446 (the neutral wording kept for restored cards). Holding-crate exception row: #11697 (merged).

### What this does, simply

When one agent hands work to a helper agent and waits for the answer, you used to see nothing until the helper was done. Now the waiting card in ZeroCode shows how many tools the helper has used and which one it's running right now, and expanding the card lists each of them. Only the tool names and a short, secret-stripped summary of each call are shown, never the helper's full inputs or outputs. Nothing is saved; reopening the session shows the card as before.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `N/A`: I ran it live in the experiment build; the tests below drive the delegate path end to end with a scripted provider.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, ZeroCode Chat with an agent that has an agentic delegate target.

### How I tested

```bash
zc-cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zerocode -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings
zc-cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- tools::delegate agent::tool_execution rpc::dispatch::tests::delegate rpc::types
zc-cargo test -p zerocode --bin zerocode
RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" zc-cargo doc -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-runtime --no-deps
rustfmt --edition 2024 --check <changed files>
bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh
bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
```

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Test and Parallel Runtime Test run the new runtime and ZeroCode tests; Lint covers clippy, rustdoc and comment hygiene; Docs Style covers the `rpc-socket.md` addition.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** no test drives a real daemon and ZeroCode together; the RPC mapping and the ZeroCode handler are tested on each side of the wire.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Latest local run on `9f3090ee37` (the head `db3d91e2f9` since then only removes TestBackend evidence tests): fmt and clippy clean; `zeroclaw-runtime` + `zerocode` suites 7916 passed, 3 failed: `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` and two `relay::local_dial_tests` tests, which fail on master on the same machine. CI Required Gate green on `db3d91e2f9`. @tidux's points are fixed in `563ed8555` (id-less results paired by arguments), `c6fb85a71` (reused child ids, neutral unfinished rows) and `035aa48f4` (checkpoint-exclusion test, `output_preview` documented in `rpc-socket.md`). Earlier run: clippy clean (exit 0). Runtime filter: `318 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored`. ZeroCode: `1459 passed; 1 failed` — the failure is `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint`, which also fails on master on the machine I ran it on. Rustdoc exit 0, fmt clean, hygiene gate passed, docs gate `0 error(s)`.
- New tests:
  - `foreground_agentic_delegate_reports_child_tool_calls_to_the_parent_turn`: a scripted agentic child calls `echo_tool`; the parent sink gets exactly one start and one finish with the parent call id, agent, child call id, a summary and an `echo:` preview.
  - `background_delegate_does_not_report_to_the_parent_turn`: same child with a progress sink (the background shape) runs its tool and sends nothing to the parent.
  - `tools_see_the_parent_event_sink_only_in_a_streaming_turn`: the scope is visible inside `execute` with the call id, absent without an event sender, and gone afterwards.
  - `delegate_activity::tests`: secret argument redacted, preview bounded, id-less calls get one id shared by start and finish, a full parent channel drops instead of blocking.
  - `delegate_activity_notification_is_flat_and_round_trips` (RPC), `parses_delegate_activity_update` and `delegate_card_shows_child_activity_while_running_and_keeps_it_after` (ZeroCode).
  - `subagent_card_says_waiting_only_while_its_turn_runs`: a live delegate card says "Waiting for response"; after its turn settles without a result it says "Result not recorded". The existing `subagent_card_restored_missing_result_does_not_claim_live_work` passes unchanged.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Swapping the forwarder back to the no-op observer makes the foreground test fail and leaves the background one passing; forcing the card's waiting flag off makes the waiting test fail. Both restored afterwards. Live run in the experiment build ([branch](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d), dogfood base `0341618f9d69`): a foreground delegate to another agent running four slow read-only tool calls; the parent's card counted the calls, showed the running one, said "Waiting for response" until the child answered, and kept the list afterwards.
- **Visual interface evidence:** `Screenshot`: real macOS Terminal.app captures of the current head `db3d91e2f9`, at https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11730#issuecomment-6534712777
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** Tests: `9f3090ee37` (above) and CI on `db3d91e2f9`. Interface: ZeroCode TUI, debug build of `db3d91e2f9` (daemon and ZeroCode from the same build), captured in https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11730#issuecomment-6534712777. Earlier captures from experiment build [20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d](https://github.com/Audacity88/zeroclaw/tree/experiment/zerocode-builds/20261015T062922Z-af67956b5e9d) are in 6232092560.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11730#issuecomment-6534712777 (current head `db3d91e2f9`; earlier: 6232092560)
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** asked the agent to delegate in the foreground to a helper agent that runs several slow tool calls. While it runs, the card shows the call count, the running tool and "Waiting for response"; expanded, it lists each call with its redacted summary; after the helper answers, the list stays and the result replaces the waiting line.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** the full `zeroclaw-runtime` suite; I ran the delegate, tool-execution and RPC-type filters, which hold every test touching the changed code.

### Screenshots

Real screenshots of the current head `db3d91e2f9`: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11730#issuecomment-6534712777 (the delegate is running with live child-call counts, and the card expands to the child call list). Earlier captures from the experiment build: https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11730#issuecomment-6232092560.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No. Child arguments go through the same redacting summarizer as approval prompts, and the output preview comes from the result the loop has already credential-scrubbed. Tested with an `api_key` argument.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No. The activity goes to the client only; it never enters a model request. ZeroCode renders it through the existing terminal-safe text path.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: n/a

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. The `session/update` type is additive; older clients fall through their unknown-type arms.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** After squash merge, `git revert <squash-commit>`.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:** a delegate card without a child-call line while its child runs tools, or child calls shown under the wrong card.
